_childDocuments_.review: Disgaea 6 feels like a game where the company ran out of budget halfway through development, so they decided to put out a half-finished product that at least worked. I am gonna start with the bad points of the game and you will hopefully understand why it feels like that to me. Disgaea 6 has the most predictable story out of all the Disgaea games I have played so far. It took me 2 chapters to predict how the next 6 chapters would go. 3 chapters to figure out what the God of Destruction was. I didn't see something that subverted my expectations until Chapter 9. I was actually excited to see where they were gonna go with that. I was crushed when I saw how they squandered the opportunity, because the execution was simply too lazy. What about the post-game story?!? Remember how in Disgaea 5 they had this whole thing with the Carnage Dimension? Remember how exciting and cool that was?!?Well Disgaea 6 does have a post-game story. But it's abysmal. It's just a series of battles with characters fighting for trivial comedic reasons. It's something you would see in a DLC. Only here it goes on and on and on, and it's boring. Speaking of the Carnage Dimension, that makes a return in this game once again. But wait, there's more. This time after you beat the Carnage Dimension, you unlock the Rakshasa Dimension with even stronger, higher level, enemies to fight. Oooooohhh. Scaaaaaryyyy.  No reaction from the characters, no cutscenes, nothing. It's just a multiplier that's being thrown here to increase the difficulty of the game and prolong its duration. It's not that much different from the LoC Mode cheat shop option in Disgaea D2. Could you please not do that? I know Disgaea has always been a series about huge numbers, but this is too much. At the end of the day, they are just numbers. In Disgaea 6 it drags on for too long. More on that below. Just less numbers, and more features please. So let's talk a little about Rakshasa, the Auto-battle system, and the late game in general. You see how I have 350+ hours in this game and how I have earned all of the achievements. The majority of the hours you see were from Auto-Battle.  So why is that?? I originally went into this game blind. It's how I approach Disgaea games. I try to enjoy them first before I rush for the achievements. And that was a mistake here. Sure, cleaning the story was nothing hard. But making it into the late game felt like it was taking for ever. The game makes a HUGE deal about its Karma system, D-Merits, the Juice bar, and Super Reincarnation. Sure, lvling up the weapon mastery and classes becomes a breeze with the juice bar. In fact things like innocents that increase MANA and class mastery and weapon mastery become obsolete very quickly.On the other hand, increasing levels and stats through the Juice Bar requires a TREMENDOUS amount of gold. And you also have to unlock D-Merits in order to increase karma caps, earn karma, earn bonuses, evilities, and items. And you also need to Super Reincarnate to further increase level caps, increase stat caps, increase your stats, etc. And you also need to level up to lvl99,999,999. And you also need to farm for gold for the Juice Bar. And you need to do that for every character you wanna use. And if you are like me and you wanna try several different characters, all in all it feels like a ton of busy work rather than a reward. I spent so many hours auto-battling, eventually I started wondering "When do I get to play the game?"And it's all Rakshasa's fault. No, I don't mean the dimension or the enemies. I mean the Evility. Rakshasa enemies have it, and it increases their stats AND damage. It's a huge increase. Rakshasa Lv 12, which most Rakshasa enemies have, will increase their damage by 1600%. That means even if an enemy has way lower stats than you, they can still do significant damage to you. This evility was a mistake. You cannot fight Rakshasa enemies unless you either cheese them, or be significantly stronger than them. Having a fair lvl won't work. Your skills need to be lvled up to do enough damage, and if they are lvled up, they cost an insane amount of mp, and how do you get mp?? Being high lvl. And you need to grind a lot to get a high lvl.......unless you cheese it."You keep talking about 'cheese'. What nonsense are you mumbling about??" So in the end I gave up, and looked up some video guides. So it's at that point I learned all characters that participated in a battle earn exp, so I could level up from lvl1 to 99,999,999 by having 110 characters equipped with Recycle Spirit explode, and then hog all the exp with one character. It was then I learned I could cheese the Rakshasa V stage with a War Lady equipped with a Witch Doctor innocent. Sure, I could grind things manually. But what would you rather do?? Grind for thousands of hours the old fashioned way in order to tackle the insane post-game, or auto-battle your way to lvl99,999,999 in just a few minutes? Even with that, you still gotta do it several times due to Super Reincarnation, mind you. "But what about items?? They should help in increasing your stats and make things easier." Items in this game are completely obsolete!!!............sort of. It's true you can increase your stats with items even in this game. But you need to beat Rakshasa V first, and then you need to reincarnate to increase the stat limit of the character you wanna equip said items. If you don't do that, a character that has 999,999,999,999 Attack with a Normal Legendary weapon is STILL gonna have the same Attack with a Rakshasa one. it's not that items do not help, it's just that you have to go through the hoops before you can make proper use of them. Which leads us to the Item World. Oh boy. This is the biggest sin in all of the Disgaea series. The Item World was the one thing I was most excited for in every Disgaea game. In Disgaea 6, not only lvling up items before you beat Rakshasa V is pointless, but the Item World itself is abysmal. Pirates? Gone. Invasion? Gone. Geo puzzles? Remember how cool it was to have geo symbols explode and how that could help you beat hard stages in the Item World? That's ALMOST gone here. The grand majority of the time you don't get enough geo symbols to have a geo chain, and the geo symbols you get are not impactful at all. Not that it matters much, as you are not gonna get anything useful from the Bonus List. It's filled to the brim with useless consumables and divers. You no longer can get rare items from it.The layout itself is very simplistic. The maps are always very short and easy to traverse. I guess it makes things easier, but I wouldn't mind a little variety.All in all, the Item World in Disgaea 6 is just boring.I.....actually reached the text limit. I am gonna continue my review in the comments.

_childDocuments_.review: Note: I got 160+ hours on Disgaea 6 for the switch, so I've explored the majority of the game. Alongside platting Disgaea 1, Disgaea 2, Disgaea 4 & Disgaea 5 which has given me time to get adjusted to practically all the mechanics offered in the Disgaea series. This is probably the only Disgaea game I can not recommend, there's a few reasons for it. 1st being the auto battle mechanic, I am not against it but am against the way they implemented it into this game. Normal story mode you can progress without, but you do need to use it for post game otherwise the progress becomes so unbearingly slow that you'll get burned out. I hypothesise that the developers tried to extend the grind out with auto battle in mind to try and reach the 100s of hours playtime counter. But this comes at the cost of the people who like to play the game manually. If you dislike auto battle mechanic, then I highly encourage you to miss out on this entry. Primal Liquid (Disgaea YouTuber) left his switch on for 3 weeks (Demo) + 1 month (Full game) 24/7 to complete all of the post game under auto grinding constantly. This amounts to over 1,000 hours which is beyond unacceptable for the amount of end-game content offered (It's pretty bare bones). Keep in mind this is with auto battle constantly enabled, you'd be looking at more playtime then this if you were to play exclusively manually. This is the biggest issue with Disgaea 6. Since this is an auto battle game after story mode, it's hard to give a justification for a £65/$70 price tag. Especially for a mixed review game (At the time of writing). In comparison to previous Disgaea games, this entry is lacking. Mechanics such as weapon skills, magichange, toss & receive etc. are removed. This kills a ton of variability in terms of how you can approach battles, it's pretty 1 dimensional now in terms of how you can approach fights. The mechanics/features that are missing stack up, Disgaea 5 a £30 game has much more features/mechanics then Disgaea 6, a £65 game. Even if you're a new player who won't miss these features since you've never experienced them, you will probably feel like at times that Disgaea 6 feels a little bare bones in terms of what it offers. You're justified in thinking that way, especially since this game is more expensive then games such as Elden Ring & Persona 5 Royal which smash this game out in the ball park in terms of content that is offered. The only DLC included in Disgaea 6 is reskinned characters/weapons with some new skills/passive skills, not enough to justify a next gen price. Especially since you won't even be looking at these characters' skill animations after a certain point due to constantly using auto battle. Most games charge £40-£50 for a complete edition, not stack the price up post release. The reception for Disgaea 6 was already bad to begin with, but over charging for this game as well is the equivalent of just spitting on the grave. _childDocuments_.review: Do Not Purchase This Game.I've written deep guides and thoughtful reviews in the past, but all this game deserves is a rant.I am a newer fan to the Disgaea franchise, joining during the lifespan on 5. I played through the entire main series from 1 to 5, getting more and more into the late game with each game in preparation for the release of 6. Unfortunately, Disgaea 6 isn't a real Disgaea game. It plays like a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ mobile or auto-clicker game.There are two reasons to play Disgaea, the quirky and zany stories, and the great strategy gameplay. This game fails on both ends. The story is mediocre, with members of the cast missing the fun energy of previous games. Instead, the characters are fairly boring and offer little enjoyment for the story.But most egregious is THE ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ GAMEPLAY. Nippoin Ichi boasts an insane increase to the level cap in this game, but don't let that marketing fool you. All they did was inflate the numbers. While each previous game did see an increase in player levels for players when they reached end game... hitting level 200+ accross the board during the tutorial is just crazy. Leveling up feels meaningless now, as the game's experience system is seeing more inflation than the current economy. So playing the game doesn't feel rewarding.Good news though, as the solution for unfulfilling rewards is already in the game. Thats right ENJOY MEANINGLESS COMBAT. Did you buy this game for Strategy? TOO BAD. The game now can play itself. I understand the idea of automating grind, but this turns this game into a mobile gacha or an autoclicker game. I repeat... THE GAME PLAYS ITSELF. There is no reason on your way to end game to even bother with strategic decisions. Just setting your party on auto-battle will defeat any problem. Too low level? Well you can also add Auto-Repeat onto Auto-Battle to let the game overlevel the ♥♥♥♥ out of you while you go to work (or play a real game like Disgaea 5).This game is a major step-back for the series. The QoL improvements are not worth the complete degeneration of gameplay. Do yourself a favor. If you want a strategic game, buy a different entry in the series. And if you want a game that plays itself, there are plenty of autoclickers on Steam that are way cheaper than the $70 asking point for this game.Show yourself some respect, and do not buy this terrible game.

Here's why: --Adds a new feature that largely automates the game and cuts down on the grind--Adds a customizable ai to assist in the formerly mentioned automation, this can be fun to program if you like little logic games--Even higher and insaner caps on things like levels, stats, and damage--Simpler and easier systems to power-up and grow your characters that are more forgiving then previous games--Great humorous storyline you would come to expect from a Disgaea game --Adds a new feature that largely automates the game--Higher numbers on things like levels, stats, damage, and exp gain give the game a false sense of grandiose--Dumbed down or removed a lot of the old systems for powering up your characters like chara world--Way less character classes then previous games--Way less DLC characters then previous games--Seems like there is less story and content then previous games (that could be my imagination since everything is so automated)You may have noticed that several things are listed as both a Pro and a Con. _childDocuments_.review: This is one of those times that I wish I could give a neutral rating, but as it stands it is a thumbs down.Really wanted to give this game a thumbs up, as I like the characters and the story.The thing that hurts this is the game plays itself.  Now there is nothing wrong with that, but for $70 dollars I want to have some input.When I heard that this game had an autoplay feature, I was excited, as this would allow me to grind easy battles to build up my squad.  I was also excited to hear that you could program each troop and how they would act, similar to Final Fantasy XII.  The problem is that this is completely unnecessary.   All of the battles in the story, save one, can be won by simply setting all of your troops to attack and overwhelming the enemy.  Most of the main campaign stages do not have geo tiles, or hazards so any reason to manually control your troops is gone.  The computer will handle everything for you.  Simply have you party grind while you sleep at night, wake up and clear a few chapters, then repeat and you will be good.You may say, well don't auto grind and that will make the game better, but the game is designed with the idea that you will auto grind in mind.  The game is balanced around this concept, and to not do it would handicap you.  The content after you beat the game is also designed around grinding and using auto battles.  At no time did I feel like I was using strategy, which is important in a strategy RPG.Really like this series, have played them all but this is the weakest, not due to story or characters, but the game playing itself for you.This game also does not have as many features as the more recent Disgaea games.  I know that games sometimes get bloated and things need to be trimmed back, but this game is missing classes and other customization options that were in the other games.  Features that were fun and are sorely missed.Looking forward to Disgaea 7 as I hear that they will have auto battles, but that you have to do regular battles to do auto battles.  This seems like it may be a good tradeoff and make the game more balanced, we will see.

_childDocuments_.review: [THIS REVIEW CONTAINS VAGUE SPOILERS] TLDR at the endDisgaea 6 feels like an attempt was made by a different company to make a Disgaea game, and somehow mimicked the character artstyle. The translation to 3D was clunky, and has made the attack animations look awkward and not well done. There's usually some degree of story for character growth in Disgaea games, but this one just had a bunch of one-dimensional characters in a vacuum, with some interactions in the hub that you can absolutely miss. There's much less humor in the entire game than any other entry, and it's only ever better in the one post-game chapter featuring characters from other games. You know, developed ones. And even when characters get "development", it's handled in the same arc that it starts. Within 5 chapters you see a character fully grow, and then fight the SAME EXACT BOSS FROM BEFORE. EVERY CHAPTER.Another big part of Disgaea is its maps, which this game seemed to decide to reuse assets/styles for constantly. There's a loose explanation in canon, and then you are forced to look at the same worlds in the same order, more than twice. The inflated numbers didn't really seem like an issue at the start, but when you get to the difficulty changes you begin to realize that there's no standard like in the other games. You have to regrind gear, go back through maps you've seen a million times to do so, and then do it all again for the next difficulty level. If you're a long-time Disgaea fan, you're probably used to doing level grinding. But do you know about grinding the same old bad items, this time a different color to represent they're from THIS difficulty?And that's where auto-battle and auto-repeat come in.You'd think, wow, i don't want to do all that multiple times, right? If you're new, that's what you'll think immediately. If you're a long time fan like me, this probably seems like heresy.But when you're running the same map over a thousand times to reincarnate AGAIN, because you need to do so at least 60 times to get to some of the second difficulty content, it becomes more appealing.And then, suddenly the joy of getting to the next tier is gone. The number's gotten bigger, but you weren't even involved!And don't even think about turning on auto-save. Did you know if your power goes out, ALL your saves get corrupted? I didn't until it happened two days ago. The straw that broke the camel's back, because I definitely would not re-do 86 hours of this game, especially when now even new saves won't work. I literally can't play it anymore! It just won't save now!TLDR: 3D looks bad in this game, Maps are repetitive, You are at some point FORCED to auto-battle if you want to make it anywhere, Story's bad and the humor's hard to come by. You WILL fight the same exact guy literally every chapter at the end, and then multiple of them later on. Number bloating in this one actually becomes a problem progression wise if you're an old head, and not as satisfying if you're new. Play one of the other entries if you can, I promise you'll have a better time.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm buying this game at full price to support NIS. As a fan of the Disgaea series, and to save a company that nearly went bankrupt. Outside that, this isn't a good Disgaea game. The auto battle feature is introduced to early, a measly 100 mana to unlock. That's super early game. Honestly it should've been a feature that was to be implemented after you beat the main story. Maybe around the time you hit Carnage. You know, when the actual grinding sets in. The speed multiplier is too fast as well, x32. Really? It so fast that that it's not even enjoyable to passively watch. It makes the gap between manually playing the game and auto battle so incredibly large it is impossible to get anywhere in the post game without auto battle.I have over 100 hrs in this game and I promise. Active hours is probably 3% of that, and 97% is just letting the game run. Auto battle has no engagement for the player. It wouldn't be a problem if the game was designed around people able to run at x32 speed all day and all night. It takes hours, days, weeks in the best grinding spot to get anywhere in this game. Some playing causally 5-6 hours a day (that's not casual) will probably take a half a year to beat post game. Again its designed around people who will leave there console/pc running all day and all night at ludicrous speeds. Which will cause physically wear and tear on your electronic components, great!Now because NIS almost went under this game is stripped down in terms of normal systems and content of a normal Disgaea game. Less than HALF the classes. NO weapon skills. No Magichange for monsters. I don't blame simplification of design for this. When you have only so much resources (money), you have to allocate it to the most important stuff. Sometimes you have to make cuts so the product actually comes out.Buy and play Disgaea 5 instead. It's a superior game.Things Disgaea 6 did right? Research item world is nice. Juice Bar is awesome. I like the 3D sprites (not everybody shares that opinion). I really like Zed as a character.In conclusion, if your a fan of Disgaea, buy it to support NIS. If you just like or are interested in Disgaea, buy the older games or wait for a supreme sale. Otherwise it's sadly a skip.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR... Buy Disgaea 5 and enjoy it. This game is not worth your time, or money. Maybe on sale.Disgaea 6 is a sad and weak clone of its former glory. Compared to 1-5, which I have a combined over 3000 hours on, this game does not even hold an ember to the burning sun of previous titles. The core failure is substituting the fun mechanics and fresh new ideas that previous games introduced (to grind up the ranks) with a "demonic intelligence" system that serves to turn the game into something less than cookie clicker. The change to 3D models (instead of typical well drawn 2D) was a major red flag.The good:Story may have started out weak but got interesting toward the midgameJuice bar addition is nice for quickly leveling up new people and stat boostingNew quick access features helped out in base for avoiding the "run everywhere" syndromeThe Bad:The darkest assembly (meant to be a place to pass bills on changing the game/making characters stronger) was turned into a small assembly hall with nearly zero detail to admire.   ^ on that note, there is a larger and better designed one, but they didn't use it... for some reason???The story randomly falls off at climatic points leaving you to "talk" to your party in the lobby with no voice acting, making it cut clean through the tensionThe main hub was scrubbed down to a very tiny area with no purpose to exploration except for 1 hidden chestThe Ugly:The game went from it's height as a strategy RPG to this low as a cheap knockoff with cheap expressionless 3D models, cheap set design, and worst of all, micro transactionsPrevious glory as a grind RPG through fun mechanics was replaced with a "program your troops" system and an auto-battle/auto-repeat system. They literally suggest "walking away to do chores" while your troops fightsThe game's primary features (compared with previous titles) are lackluster. Item world is just plain old Disgaea 1 style item world Squads were reduced to just a single shop instead of an actual system/buildings All unique introductions of previous titles were removed (magichange, character dungeons, world building, ship building, etc)By itself, without consideration of previous titles, this game is an overpriced grind arcade game where you occasionally pop in to perform administrative work to manage your band of heroes as they slay 4 people in the same location 800,000 times until they are level 99,999,999 so they can reset to level 1 so their stats can get a little higher each time.2/10. Nippon Ichi Software should be ashamed to have released such an underdeveloped product. The story was decent, but the characters were poorly designed and hard to associate with, the grind was taken from being fun to being a chore, the micro-transactions on top of a 70 dollar game are a slap to the face to even include, and the lack of features just goes to show that this brand name game is now a second shelf knockoff.After playing since 2005 when I first picked up Disgaea 1, I'm setting this series aside as another cash grab using nostalgia as bait.

_childDocuments_.review: I'd give it a hesitant thumbs-up if it wasn't for the inclusion of microtransactions, which have no place whatsoever in a $60 (previously $70) game.Overall, it's really painfully obvious that the transition to full 3D meant that this game was incredibly rushed coming out. It's a story as old as time- you make a new engine, you get a bad game out of it. Executives are never flexible enough with release dates, and honestly I don't think this series in particular needed the full 3D treatment. But the suits think they know best, so we got... This.This is one game in a long series, so it is inevitable that I must compare them to previous titles. There are some good changes to the Disgaea formula here, so let's go over them first. First, the introduction of Demonic Intelligence, custom AI for your team, is both an obvious and necessary QoL addition, considering how repetitive the series always has been, and something that shifts the genre of the game fundamentally. Overall, I like it, believe it or not! Sure, it makes the game lean far harder into "idle game" territory, but on the other hand, I got an RSI from grinding in the last game, so maybe it's for the better. I've played more than one game with custom AI scripting mechanics, and this one is on the better end of them. There are some things I can't figure out how to code in, and the D.I. UI could use some more QoL features, but they give you enough tools to properly use the skills in your arsenal for the most part.Another change I liked is how they treated monster units. Monster weapons, magi-change, etc. are gone. Monsters now work just live every other class. This makes monsters actually viable to use in your teams! Because wow, most monsters sucked in past games. Limited weapon pool, the inability to lift/throw, and generally poor opportunities for skill acquisition meant monsters were always a tier lower than most humanoid units. Unfortunately, I suspect this positive change is simply because they couldn't code monster stuff in in time, but removing features can be good! Monster mechanics were bad! They're good now!Some new features were generally forgettable, like 5-tile large units and the juice bar. That's okay. Not everything can be a winner.The biggest issue with the game is what they cut. A whole lot of classes, revenge skills, capturing, Item World invaders, the list goes on. The game feels a bit more bare-bones than previously. The main plot combat scenarios even suffer from this- You literally fight the exact same boss 4 times in a row for 4 missions in a final section of the game, for example. A notable mention is that, other than the main antagonist, there are no non-protagonist characters with a unique sprite. The cast of characters has never been more sparse.They also felt the indeed to inflate stats. The maximum level went from 9 thousand to 99 million, for example. I guess they really wanted to punch up how broken you feel endgame, but otherwise only serves to make it feel even more like an idle game. I've played a lot of idle games, don't get me wrong, but these days idle games have been overrun by free to play cash grabs, considering how viable it is to monetize games in that genre, so it is Not a good look. Of course, the executives probably did this for that exact reason- they want in on the cash grab.The writing is as bad as ever for a Disgaea game. Casual sexism! Paper-thin and aggressively unlikable characters! Things too Japanese for me to understand! At least Zed was a good protagonist. I liked him at least. Anyways Disgaea writing continues to make me cringe, but I still play them and read all the text that comes my way, so I guess that's on me.Anyways, despite all that... I still had fun. All I did was fast forward through the entire plot I hated reading with auto-battle in 20 hours, and that was it, and I somehow still had fun. I'm beginning to question my taste in video games! But regardless, despite being the weakest Disgaea game in a long while, it's not actually a bad game. I wouldn't blame you if you waited for Disgaea 7, but I also wouldn't blame you if you gave this title a shot.

_childDocuments_.review: Reconsider Disgaea 4, 5, or D2 before touching this one. As much as I love all the Disgaea games in the series, I cannot recommend this one for folks starting the series or with a tight budget.- Decent story/characters, ported well to PC, lots of QOL features (auto battle/save, retries, dark assembly, reincarnations, etc), and cute chibi 3D-Models.- Playing through to the story is very easy, and a bit repetitive. Does have some decent twists for events, but nothing spectacular.- The 3D-Models can be a miss for some, but I also like the previous HD and SD sprites.- Lots of variety of play since there are a lot of strong characters, including DLC ones. So there's a decent balance between character roster strengths for builds/teams.- Price tag was $89.99 CAD for me. For what the game's worth, no.- For the story-game you start off super strong and you get stronger. There's not much of a 'growth' to show. Previous Disgaea games you start off weak and eventually grow strong. You are just earning a new letter for the damage you're doing, similar to a Cookie Clicker.- After beating the story is post-game for those that want to pursue huge stats, a lot of things are dependant on the auto-battle system they implemented. Sure it is great but the way they balanced it, entirely depends on it for grinding. Almost all parts of the game (item levels/stats, reincarnations, extracts, HL) require the auto battle.- Skills and classes are too generic. You can't pass a Warriors skills onto another character like before, generic character skills are locked per class. Certain skills are also simplified where as Braveheart/MagicBoost/TargetLock/SpeedLock are into one skill for a character to 'do more damage'.- A lot less classes to create (compared to other Disgaeas), the amount of auto-battle padding for grinding, the skill animations of the 3D-Models during combat, repetitive story-segments, all together feel really rushed. Game is merely an auto-chess/cookie clicker or something mobile like.The game itself overall isn't terrible, but it does not justify the high price tag for what other Disgaea games offer. I get the developers tried to get 'new players' into the franchise but this is not the way to do it. Huge numbers into trillions are cool and all, but oversimplification and padding doesn't teach or help new players into the series. This Disgaea has lost its' core and become into a grinding chore.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR - Not recommended at full price for ANYBODY, and only recommended on large sale for big fans of the Disgaea series. This is the worst game in the entire series and has so little content it feels like it was supposed to be a MOBILE game, that's how bad it is.Story - It's fine, pretty standard Disgaea story, standard cliche characters and the 2 big 'twists' are obvious a mile away, but overall it was decently executed and fine. Not fantastic but not terrible.Graphics - Terrible. I don't mind the idea of the 3D chibi sprites, but they seem to have used that as an excuse for cutting out a huge amount of the animations. 95% of the story 'animations' are the standard Disgaea 2D graphic talking heads, and almost the only animation is some enemies popping up. A huge amount of the battle animations are either GONE (combos), or significantly stripped down.Content - HORRIFIC. Huge amounts of content from previous games is completely gone or significantly reduced. By far the worst offender is the weapon skills - customizing your characters is the entire reason people PLAY this series, people!!! ALL weapon skills are completely gone, which means that there is no longer any point at all other than stats to using different weapons, and weapon mastery is now just a stupid damage bonus. Every character is limited to the skills of their current class - and unique characters CAN NEVER GET any other weapon skills. And yet for some reason, you can still teach them any magic! Chara World? GONE. Item stat proficiency bonuses? GONE (now its just a blind modifier based on level) Magichange and monster items? GONE. Items/weapons? MASSIVELY reduced to only fist/sword/axe/gun/bow/staff/emblem/glasses/armor/belt/shoes/healing. Everything else is gone.  Character classes? Disregarding unique units in both games, its cut all the way from 47 in Disgaea 5 to 22 here, LESS THAN HALF - and since you can't get their skills on the characters mastery is just another dumb stat modifier anyway. Endgame content? Outside DLC its just Laharl/Etna/Flonne (which they tried to pad by just making you fight them 8x times), and Baal.And the balancing is HORRIFIC. They clearly decided very late in the development cycle that they were going to massively increase the level cap, but they never bothered to GO BACK and balance everything with the significantly increased stats and levels - so you're in Carnage dimension and still getting repeatable quests for a few hundred mana, most of the items even at extremely high level only give a tiny fraction of the stats your level 1 reincarnated character has, or you finally finish 100 weapon mastery D-Merit and get... the NORMAL version of the highest level item, which is utterly worthless compared to Carnage items. And at a certain point it becomes obvious that it doesn't really matter that you can't get skills, because your standard attack does EXPONENTIALLY more damage than your skills, even if you massively stack the level on it! Your autoattack is literally doing more damage than an alleged SS single target skill leveled to the point that it takes 100% of your SP to use, because apparently a lot of the +damage calculations simply aren't applying to your skills!They try to cover this horrific balance with the Juice Bar, but it just serves as a cover for their horrible balance. Using Zed as main character and finishing the entire story basically solo and he only has ~20 weapon mastery on his weapon. Meanwhile doing the 100x D-Merit quest, which you usually get pretty early, gives you enough money that you can instantly max to 100 proficiency in Juice Bar.A lot of their calculations DO NOT WORK correctly. Setting the game to 4x speed RUNS SLOWER THAN AT 2X (and no, its not my comp, I have a supercomputer, when you set it to 8x, then it actually DOES speed up again). Oh, and the 'skip voting' in the Dark Assembly DOESN'T WORK because it requires you to hold down a button while selecting 'Begin Vote', BUT THE GAME DOESN'T LET YOU ACTUALLY SELECT IT WHILE HOLDING IT DOWN (tried 5x different buttons). A lot of the in-game calculations are also messed up - for instance, using the assembly for max XP by hogging XP, triple XP, welcome party, and set Cheat to max, but setting the difficulty to 20 stars on some levels GIVES LESS XP THAN LEVEL 0. (A level 1 clearing Martial Level 1 with this setup and difficulty 0 boosts you to level ~60k. Same setup at difficulty 20 only boosts the same character to level ~45k!!! WTF!?!?!?).The whole auto-battle thing makes the late game effectively just a stupid idle game. The bar for Carnage and Rakshasa is so much higher that forces you to significantly grind, but they've so cut down the content that there's very little to actually grind except levels and Karma! Why the heck would you design a game in a way that the most efficient way to play it is to NOT PLAY IT!?!?!Overall its just an incredibly poorly balanced mess missing a huge amount of content from previous games, with a lot of bugs that feels like an early beta build of an intended mobile game. Worst game in the entire series, highly disappointing after the great game that was Disgaea 5.

_childDocuments_.review: The PC releases for the Disgaea series has finally caught up, Disgaea 6 Complete launched on the PS5 and Steam on the same day, this has resulted in a bit of a price shock for many of the newer PC fans of the games and is largely responsible for the unfortunate mixed reviews. Disgaea has always been a full priced game for it's initial core console release, and usually loaded with like $30-50 of additional DLC, with the PS5 generation Sony is pushing for a new $70 price tag on all games and releasing a game for significantly less on another platform at the same time is surely against their rules. So here we are, a series on Steam where the previous entries have all released at $20-40 because they were many years old at that point, suddenly the latest release is $70, the negative reception there is pretty understandable. That said with the Disgaea Dood Bundle you can grab it for $59, and Disgaea 6 Complete does include all of the DLC, so this is still going to be the cheapest place to get the complete game. In a couple years or so I'm sure it will have a 50% off sale, so since PC fans are already used to waiting years for the next game it might be worthwhile for some to wait a bit and get it at a more recognizable price.The game itself is great, full of new QoL mechanics and the most polished iteration of the classic Disgaea formula yet. The higher starting stats and quickly escalating levels is a bit jarring at first, but turns out to be a fairly brilliant change that solves a lot of the balance issues the previous games had. You might go from level 1 to 300 very quickly, but each individual level is about as meaningful as in past games while character starting stats and initial equipment stats are about 1000 times higher than normal, this means those 300 levels don't do a whole lot for increasing your overall power. Levels still do something and you can feel their effect, but what this means is a single trip to the item world or repeating a stage a couple times no longer skyrockets your character power to the point where the campaign becomes trivial. The campaign balance is a lot tighter, you can't accidentally ruin the challenge or nullify the level design, those +50% enemy strength geo panels still hurt after diving down to floor 30 in an early piece of equipment. For the first time I can remember I've actually had a gameover during a normal campaign stage because I tried to ignore the map layout and brute force it, it's great.New mechanics like the Juice Bar that stores a pool of exp/mana you can apply to any characters you want, and D-Merits which reward characters for reaching certain milestones give you a lot more control over character progression. Reincarnation has been redone with a Karma point system which makes things much more clear and controllable, allowing you to purchase various upgrades for karma points while reincarnating. The switch to 3D was worrying when I first heard about it, but it's done flawlessly. At their default idle stance classes from previous games look like their old hand drawn 2D sprites in HD, you can't even tell they are 3D until you start rotating the model. What this really enhances are animations, no longer restricted to the same few animation frames used in every skill, each animation is very fluid and looks a lot better. The downside of this is the amount of work required to recreate all the old classes and characters in 3D was obviously a bit beyond the scope of a single game, so in the end there are about half the generic classes as in Disgaea 5, though still a very large number of unique characters from previous games.A controversial addition is an auto battle system, but the reality is this is a really amazing and deep addition to the game that makes perfect sense. It functions similar to like the gambit system from FF12, you can create a series of conditions and actions to allow certain characters to act in ways you want during auto combat, from hunting down chests to healing allies in certain conditions. You get a large grid you can fill with many conditions and actions and can spend a lot of time making a fairly complicated AI routine for a character. It ends up being pretty amazing for zooming through low level item world stages, telling certain characters to beeline to innocents or chests before dashing for the gate, or for grinding exp stages on repeat, tasks that have always been fairly mindless and repetitive. The system doesn't really allow you to tackle challenging content though as there aren't considerations for things like geopanels or enemy strengths/weaknesses, positioning, throwing, or any of the important combat mechanics in the game. If you just try to go through the main story using only the auto battle feature you are going to struggle immensely and deal with frequent gameovers. Disgaea 6 is not some idle game that plays itself like some of the negative reviews mention, it just has a tool you can use in specific situations to help with the grind, if you want.The story I can't really judge yet, I may edit this review later once I've completed it, but from seeing the first few chapters it seems to be fairly average, much better than D3, probably not as good as D1, just somewhere in the middle. The main character isn't annoying or entirely unhinged, it's been giving me D2 vibes so far. Edit: I've finished the main story, it starts off a bit slow and meh, but gets a lot more interesting later and most of the characters become really enjoyable. I'm still not sure I would say it's better than the D1 story, but I enjoyed the D6 story more than most other Disgaea games.Overall Disgaea 6 is a great addition to the series, and as somebody who has spent hundreds of dollars over the past 20 years buying all the games and all the DLC on consoles and again more recently on Steam, I would say it's fully worth the $60-70 asking price. That said I can easily understand that might be a bit high for many fans, and I'm sure there will be a generous sale within the next year or two to bring it down to something more in line with previous Steam releases of the series.

_childDocuments_.review: This is easily the worst entry in the series and I didn't even finish 3.  Every good thing about Disgaea, the madcap mechanics, the crazy variety of units, the silly character abilities, has been scraped out and dumbed down to the point where it feels more like a Gacha.  Of the 483 hours I have spent "playing" this game, the majority has been on Autofight with short stints of unsatisfying Item Worlding.There are a few interesting concepts in here, don't get me wrong, but there's miles of empty calorie game play between each one.  Evilities are more versatile than ever, since you can convert 99% of them to scrolls and pass them around like party favors to create truly ridiculous builds.  Unique Innocents with quirky effects on your gameplay can be found with a lot of effort.  But in the end, no amount of clever building will defeat the secret final boss, Numbers.  Numbers, formerly known as Super Overlord Baal, has the very unique and interesting ability to have lots of high numbers, and to defeat him you must gather all your wit, all your cunning, and all your guts to grind for literally days until your numbers are higher than his.  If you don't, he will hit you very hard and you will die.There's no other way to say it than they maxed out the grinding aspect of this game at the expense of all else.  The soul of Disgaea to me is that there's always a way to use cunning and trickery to cheat your way to the top, but here all you can do is leave the game on Autofight overnight, then come back, Reincarnate everyone, and do it again.  As for the plot, it has one or two solid moments that surprised me, but it still feels... Formulaic in a lot of places, to the point where even the characters in the game start to mention it.  The characters are one dimensional to the point they can, and do, simply shout their one character trait in lieu of saying anything interesting.    Marjorie is the only one who seems to be able to pry herself out of this routine, and is usually the only one saying anything useful at any given time, with her personality gimmick being more of a side dish that compliments the overall experience (The voice actor is also excellent.  I bust a gut laughing every time I call Marjorie out of the base and get "CAN WE DO SOMETHING ABOUT THIS SKIRT??")The run time also feels padded out, with situations that in previous games would have occurred over the course of one stage being stretched out to fill an entire world. TOO LONG, DIDN'T READ - Disgaea 6 is an attempt to condense Disgaea to a serum that you can inject into your veins with minimal effort.   It might as well be a Gacha.

_childDocuments_.review: There is a deceptive amount that is new in Disgaea 6.You can see the new art style, the new level cap(s), a Karma system that streamlines growth from Reincarnation, monster units equipping weapons and throwing characters like humanoids, the Juice Bar, removing weapon-bound skills, no stat proficiencies, EXP and Mana being earned by everyone in the party instead of just the characters dealing the final blow (a fantastic design decision), and of course the Auto Battle feature.Stat-scaling is also very different.  Most enemies, at least in the early levels, have worse stats than players even when they're at the same level, and stats increase much more gradually with level (at least in the early going).  You can even defeat the level 99 Chapter 1 boss with full level 1 squad with low-rank equipment.  You'll find yourself cranking up monster difficulty *because you can*, and it just allows you to ramp up your levels even faster.  You will need to disable Auto Battle for a few maps because they have Geo Panels that punish you for facerolling, but you can usually sit back.Equipment power follows a similar growth curve, so if you're ramping up your core stats to crazy levels through overleveling and copious reincarnations, your equipment is basically an afterthought outside of (1) selecting the right weapon type so you use your best stats and (2) equipping shoes for their movement.  Characters can still enjoy a nice dose of power exploring the Item World or getting some Rank 39-40 Equipment from completing D-Merits, but it's generally not worth investing the effort to make the equipment a major contributor to one's production until reaching Rakshasa in the post-game.  But if you do power up some equipment in the Item World, it can make the Super Reincarnation grind substantially faster.Is Disgaea 6 worth playing (and buying)?The Auto Battle feature drastically changes your experience with the game.  Disgaea 1-5 gameplay predominately involves managing individual character actions.  In the main game, it plays closer to conventional grid-based RPG with the occasional trap/puzzle map, but Disgaea 1-5 postgame involves repetitive player actions and is a huge time sink.  Disgaea 6 has a faster story if you're Auto Battle-ing, but the mid-to-late postgame takes roughly as long but puts you in a manager role where you leave your game playing on its own for long stretches instead of compelling you to enter in the actions itself.  This AI will struggle navigating the Item World without periodic checks from the player, but it will handle plenty of (static) maps you can Auto Repeat for hours of growth.  I don't know if it's ~200 hours well spent getting to the end of postgame, but it's much better than manually entering in repetitive commands for that long.  But as a huge plus, it's a very DIFFERENT gameplay experience, so if you think having a different relationship with the game is good (particularly in this way), that is almost enough by itself to make the game worth playing.  I have not experimented with Demon Intelligence, but it allows a player to customize each character's AI, potentially making the Auto Battle feature better and more-interesting.I do have some quibbles.The small roster is not as harsh as many reviews make it out to be, as there is still a great variety of evilities to unlock.  Still, I miss having Valkyrie and a second designated Spear user, especially since we get the designated Spear-user so late in the story.  Not that weapon proficiency is very important in Disgaea 6, but I would have preferred more balance in weapon proficiencies to represent all weapons more-equally (for comparison, we've got three Fist mains).  And even just having male-female variants of the same class would give the game more aesthetic diversity, which can be a goal for Disgaea 7 (when NIS isn't starting from scratch graphics-wise).For whatever philosophy that justified stripping away weapon skills and making characters more-sharply defined by their class skills, I would have expected magic (Fire/Ice/Wind/Star/Heal spells, as well as Espoir) to have been revamped and pared down as well.  Spells probably shouldn't max out at a Range of 10, and with the way players can upgrade skills and spells, there isn't a need to have spells of different tiers anymore -- the game could safely remove the Mega/Giga/Omega/Tera spells.  Alternatively, the game could give each tier the same power but lock each tier to a specific target size (Base could be single target, Mega could target a 3-row, Giga can do the 5-cross, Omega could do a 7-spread, and Tera can be the 9-box), which would make spells handle more like skills.  Even then, this might still be too much versatility for players, given how much they're constrained by class skills.Kill Bonus scales poorly with Item Rank.  You can kill enemies with a level sum of 100k to multiply the item's stats by 5.  This is too slow for low rank items and too fast for medium-to-high rank items.Axes still get OP in the Item World (its minuses turn into positives), and Guns (unlike every other weapon) still allow a player to dump two stats.Still, for these complaints, I think overhauling the graphics, sharing EXP and Mana with the whole party, and delivering a very different gameplay experience (managing instead of micromanaging) is a valiant effort on the developer's part.  The $70 price tag isn't surprising given the original Switch release only happened one year earlier (unlike with other Disgaea Steam releases) and that the Steam version is bundled with DLC.  If that price gives you heartburn, then wait for a discount to your liking -- whatever you feel like paying, it'll be worth it when the time comes.

_childDocuments_.review: Played this primarily on the Switch originally, and purchased just to see performance improvements (which thankfully is great here). Not keeping due to price. Will pick it up later depending on the mod scene and a sale. I don't think Disgaea 6 was worth the original sticker price, and the DLC is largely just a few characters which amount to the price point of entire games you can find here.If you're a Disgaea fan, how much you like this entry or not will depend on what you values most from previous entries. For myself I enjoyed picking away at item worlds as enemies escalated rapidly in strength. D5 did away with that with weakened enemies and slowed leveling rates. D6 goes a step further and makes geo-panels a non-factor in the item world. You will frequently encounter floors with geo-blocks with no panels, and floors with panels and no geo-blocks. Whether this was due to complications related to the auto-battle AI system (called D.I) I don't know. Either way, weaker enemies and item floors with no concern for positioning makes it a no-go for me.The classes have been pared down heavily. I don't mind this in principle, but there is nothing particularly robust to leverage this against. They have limited movesets to make positioning more important, but positioning is less important now thanks to terrain and enemy positions being less of an obstacle compared to previous entries.There are some other things that are head scratchers. Why cut weapon skills but keep weapon mastery? Why not go back to weapon fortes and maybe flavour the class differently depending which favourite they use? Seems a bit disjointed and half baked.You will probably hear a lot about the auto-battle system. It's nice in that it can help automate grindy elements for you. Many will say it's optional, and it's true. But keep in mind that many of the grindy aspects have been increased in response to having this system now available. So if you don't want to use this system, keep in mind the grind is far far worse than ever before without it. Maybe to push people towards micro-transactions that are available within the game?Most of this is just rambling to put something down before I refund the title, as there are more odd thoughts on the design. My final thought would be that past Disgaea entries were somewhat flexible on allowing you to play how you want and giving you something in return. Here, in Disgaea 6, they've given all these great QoL aspects without as much to play around with.

_childDocuments_.review: So this PC port not only contains the DLC from the Switch and PS4 release (Without charging a ton for DLC that is sold separately), but contains basically every PC oriented feature you'd want from a modern PC release in 2022, and then some. My expectations were set pretty high after the Labyrinth of Refrain port being extremely solid at launch (and not needing anything to really be modded in, outside of PS button prompts and ultrawide support, the ladder of which I was able to get working anyways with a centered UI by adjusting three float values in Cheat Engine), but they've exceeded those expectations here by a ton:+ Unlocked Framerates (Including an option to cap at the display refresh rate) and a separate VSync toggle.+ Ultrawide support up to 32:9 during gameplay (Special abilities and cutscenes are pillarboxed, but regular gameplay works fine without major problems).+ Support for automatic controller prompt switching (The game has Steam Controller, Xbox, PlayStation, Nintendo Switch, generic DirectInput, and Keyboard/Mouse prompts), and user enforced prompts (if you're using an analog keypad like the Razer Tartarus or software like DS4Windows/DualSenseX to use a PlayStation controller outside of Steam)+ Steam Deck support (Outside of the lack of 16:10 support, which is letterboxed and sadly is noticeable due to the Steam Deck not having an OLED display) runs at a rock solid 60FPS for me with the correct button prompts.+ Using plenty of 10 and 11 bit render passes, so using HDR retrofitting with Special K makes this game look absolutely fantastic on an OLED display. Bonus points for using Flip composition (and NOT Copy to GPU GDI composition), which makes rendering and input latency just as good as exclusive fullscreen (minus the lenthy resolution switching when booting or alt-tabbing).+ Not having me open a debugging tool during playing to fix problems. This absolutely deserves a standing ovation and an award from me, considering how many modern Steam releases of games completely fail on the front of UX.+ Not hardcoding resolution options, instead grabbing all of the available resolutions from the display. This is something many Atlus, Koei Tecmo, and IdeaFactory PC ports consistently fail at, and I feel like this is absolutely worth mentioning.+ Dynamic Resolution Scaling (outside of lacking a framerate target option for it to engage, so how it works currently is a bit of a mystery), and supersampling (for anti-aliasing)/upsampling (for when you are running on lower-end hardware but still want a sharp UI) options are here. I do wish that the game opted for a Temporal Anti-Aliasing solution (instead of an on/off toggle FXAA) alongside having the options of FSR 2.0 and DLSS for upscaling (as the current upscaling lacks a temporal solution and can cause extra aliasing), but what's already here is rock solid for those that think aliasing is a huge concern, and that don't want to mess with NVIDIA's DSR and having to use Fullscreen Exclusive mode to run the game at a higher internal resolution.The only notable flaw that I can think of is the lack of 16:10 support as noted on my findings on Steam Deck support, and CPU/GPU utilization being extremely weird (There's times where the game will dip to 90FPS or so on my RTX 3070 and Ryzen 5 5600X, but after adjusting the rendering resolution, the game goes back to a consistent framerate cap of my screen refresh rate (144Hz)). I'd imagine these things could be addressed in a patch. That and some of the localization decisions made, but I do admit that's more of a subjective thing, as NISA is known to take some creative liberties when it comes to the Disgaea games.This should be the new standard for JRPG game launches on Steam (and PC in general), and I think that most JRPG developers putting their games on Steam really should take notes from everything this game release does right. It's not a Mary Skelter 2, Demon Gaze, Elden Ring, Final Fantasy 7 Remake, Shin Megami Tensei III, PD MegaMix+, Persona 5 Strikers, or Deadly Premonition 2 situation, and after the many bad game launches I've experienced in this year alone, I'm glad that I was able to look forward to a new release without being promptly disappointed from a bad game launch with no patches on the horizon to fix any withstanding problems. This is probably the best way to play the game (as the Nintendo Switch version has performance issues, and the polish on this PC port is many magnitudes better than what running the Switch version unofficially on PC could ever provide), and I urge anyone who is interested in the Disgaea series or supporting good business practices (not dumping buggy unfinished debug builds of games on Steam at full price and promptly never patching them, which is something Valve and Epic Games are apathetic towards) to be a dood and support this release.NISA absolutely did a bang up job and went above expectations when it came to delivering a PC port that actually supports a wide range of configurations. Both them (as of their latest releases) and PH3 Games (Keep in mind, they work closely with NISA on the Trails games, and it's entirely possible that they consulted on this release) are the best in class when it comes to PC ports of JRPGs. Thank you for doing a fantastic job!EDIT: As I've played through a good chunk of the game's main story already, I can say that there's a problem on my main desktop where the game will cap out at 70-72FPS or so in the hub area, while alt-tabbing out of the game makes it suddenly go to 120FPS or so. Same thing with the pause menu, runs at 100FPS or so while focused, but alt-tabbing makes it hit a rock solid 144FPS. There's definitely something really funky going on with how the framelimiter (and more specifically the alt-tabbing behavior of the game) is working at the moment. Based on my findings, I found that disabling the in-game VSync option, and then using Special K or NVCP to force VSync actually fixed the problem. If NISA could get a patch out to address this problem, that would be fantastic.

_childDocuments_.review: The story, the characters, the animation of the skills, the voice acting, all those are tip top!I really enjoyed going through the story, even if the auto-battler made it a bit too easy, and the bosses were repetitive. Still, I had fun. It was like a long movie with wacky characters.Took me 18h to do the story, so if you get the game around 10e, I would say you got a great deal.I dont recommend the game though because I dont want to encourage devs to create this kind of game for the price they ask. For 70e, I am expecting at least 140h+ of good gameplay, or at least 90h of memorable fun... So what is past the story (20h mark)? A bot simulator. Not fun to me.I never did the post-game in the previous Disgaea I played, so I went through the experience with this one, to see what it was about (and to get some for my money). Very poor design: it s about figthing the same boss, several times, with better stats. I did my best to avoid as much grinding as possible and it took me 80+ hours to beat the secret boss at max difficulty. And it felt lame.Here is the "gameplay" of the post-game: 4 min passed in different menus, 30 sec in automated combat, and you get a little drop of improvment on one character. Then you have to repeat that 100 times to unlock the next step. 1000 times for the step after that. Etc. Finally you unlock the secret boss. And then more grind to beat it. Several times, with more grind, to "finish the game". 95% of the time in menus and 5% in automated combat. That s what D6 has to offer: you can experience being a bot.For a "tactical" game, it lacks a lot of the basics. You dont have access to the formula to do damage. If you hit a mob with your sword, you dont know exactly how much damage you ll deal. Some mechanics are not explained in the game (for exemple, you cant boost your stat above 100% in battle), some mechanics are inaccurate (in-game wording is "each turn" but the actual effect is "each battle") and some mechanics are just missing (most buffing spells give buffs with no description).Between D4, D5 and D6, there was no change to the UI, the design of the maps, the basic mechanics or 80% of the classes, so I am wondering how are they using the 70e they are asking for the game. There is almost no innovation in terms of gameplay.If the auto-battler was the innovation, it is not actually that well designed. I regularly had to intervene to put it back on track. Usually I was just turning one character to the side so that the spell actually hit someone instead of whiffing.If the "visual upgrade" was the innovation, it s NOT gameplay. When it is better for the sanity of the player to skip all cinematics and play at x32 speed, who cares about the visual upgrade. D5 visuals were good enough already. What are the priorities for the devs?Outside the gameplay, even the UI is outdated. Having to go through 3 different menus to put an evility (passive bonus) from one character to another is just plain stupid. It s even more stupid to realise it s the case for at least 3 games in the row. The UI is not scaling with what is required for the late-game. Switching from a combat setup to an EXP farming setup takes 8 min. 8 min in different menus, achieving nothing. Why is it still the case after 6 games that are basically the same, with just a different story? How come no one improved on that?So should you buy? Easiest "HELL NO!" unless you play for the story and you get it for less than 12e.I m happy I ll went through it. Never again. And I ll wait for D7 to drop below 12e to consider it.Cheers,

_childDocuments_.review: You want super inflated numbers which make it difficult to gauge power?A mediocre story that has terrible life lessons?Maybe you want a game that plays itself?Perhaps a game which launched at $70 USD when it's only worth $40 at most?If the answer is yes, then this is the game for you!The pros to the game are that the QoL is through the roof, and that the grinding isn't nearly as grindy, but you're sacrificing a lot in return.The D.I. and auto-battle don't necessarily need to be bad things, but it leads to the problem of removing too much challenge leaving you unsatisfied when everything either dies like a limp noodle, or you are instantly destroyed. Perhaps they could have made it so you don't earn exp while auto battling or something, I don't know.The juice bar is one thing I can praise, because it allows you to use units you want to use instead of the units you want to level, but I think they made it a little TOO convenient in that you can use it to level class and weapon mastery. This takes ALL of the grind out when you reach later stages.The Demerit system is a unit achievement system which rewards characters for milestones, but WATCH OUT, karma, which is the currency used to allocate stat bonuses, when collected using the collect all button, will not be saved above the cap. This means you can lose out on massive amounts a vital currency for your units individual power because of the arbitrary karma cap limitations. There is no warning when you use collect all if you'd exceed the character's cap on Karma.Auto-sell is useful, as long as you don't auto sell your Mr. Gency exits in the item world.They keep a few useful things like the cheat shop and evilities. That's the end of my positive points.If you have enjoyed previous Disgaea games, go back and replay the ones you enjoy most. This game has FEWER classes than ANY other entry. A unengaging story which starts out ok but wanes drastically as time goes on. Items and item world being practically useless before postgame with few exceptions. Inflated numbers FROM THE START OF THE GAME making the UI frankly messy to the point it is hard to read. Not-so-subtle culture war politic analogs in the US localization (Zombies are discriminated against for being zombies) hammered over and over. There were a couple audio related bugs (even though they were supposedly worked out). The item world this time has no real surprises like random bosses, pirates, or anything outside of mystery gates keeping it lively. Every system which makes a comeback is stripped down for the most part.This game wan't made for fans of the series and it shows.As a fan of the series, if you want to play disgaea, play literally any other entry and you will have far more fun.If you aren't a fan but want to enter the series, there are still better options even if the mechanics can be overwhelming.If I were to give it a rating I'd have to give it two separate ratings. One for Disgaea fans and one for Non-Disgaea fans.Disgaea fan rating: 2/10 - They cut out much of what you probably like and did so to expressly say that you, as a fanbase, are not who they're appealing to with this entry.Non-fan rating: 5/10 - Mediocre and nothing to keep you playing.If you absolutely MUST play this game wait until it's 90% off.

Everything about this game seems rushed.  The animations are very stiff and lack polish.  The story is the worst, and they pad the game heavily with you fighting the same antagonist over and over again.  There is a whole chapter where that's all you fight in all 5 parts.Don't get me started on the DLC.  At the very least, it seems they could have used clips from previous games for voicing for these characters, but instead use voice actors that don't sound anything like their counter parts (outside of Laharl, Etna, and Flonne obviously.)I really want to like this game.  I like the idea behind it, I enjoyed the characters, it's just missing so much of what makes a Disgaea game Disgaea.With that being said, it's not all bad. _childDocuments_.review: Finally got around to playing this as i got the itch to play a digaea game while 7 was coming in the mail. I DO own this on the switch but i tend to like to have the add-ons for a game and if i wanted to get it all on the system it would cost me 45$.... or i could just buy it here while its on sale for 50$, which is what i did instead. The only thing that im missing out on is the hololive dlc which my switch version has, but the complete version has everything else so i can live without it. ¯\_(ツ)_/¯As for the game itself, if my 32 hours of playtime is anything to go by i did in fact beat the normal route and just starting the post game (I inflated my units since i let my team DI level for a day in the back while i did other things, S reincarnating once and getting a team to lvl 5000 after that is more then enough to steamroll the story). I do know what to expect in post and am unsure if i want to take it right to the end but ill be playing it all the same. Story wise, much better then expected since it follows the Disgaea formula almost as well as 4 did, good pacing, fun concept of dying at the end of every chapter, good character development for everyone involved in a miss-matched group, the twists were a little off putting but the end result was nice.The conversion from 2d to 3d does bother some people as well as myself initially, but I got over it pretty quick since it plays just like a usual Disgaea game.Gameplay wise, - Things like magi-change that was introduced in 3 and monster combinations that was introduced in 4 were removed. It's good in a way since it removes issues in lower levels of the item world where you would sometimes run into an un-killable enemy that has a lvl9999 mothman become a gun weapon for a lvl9999 gunner with boosted stats and all of a sudden be harder to kill then baal. (Especially with the Carnage and Rakshasa difficulties and the boosted level caps). Also monster weapons were removed, its something i got used to since Disgaea 1, and its something i got over eventually, but its still weird give monsters normal weapons (Albeit it cuts out 2 weapons for item world grinding min-maxing so it doenst bother me THAT much).- Item warehouse was removed so now you just get a 1500 base inventory limit, its nice that you don't have to worry about clogging the inventory when on an item world run but it alternatively gets clogged and hard to manage if you keep item drops on (cheat shop allows you to turn them off), Items bought from the shop can no longer have innocents on them but they retain the level of weapons you boosted so getting a lvl 50 kitchen knife also means you can buy a lvl 50 kitchen knife going forward.- i do like the addition of the D.I system which made leveling tolerable even if you aren't a seasonal player of the series. Though it is evident on how unpolished it is, not so much in how you can set it up since you can make it do as much as you want long as the grid space allows for it, but more that it seems to put a tole on the game's memory as it would sometimes lag or lock up the game at the start of fights (ran fine after that though). - Game numbers are evidently inflated where in older Disgaea games you start out in 3 digit stats and weapons are a nice boost to stats and damage as you go up the ranks, in D6 you start out in the 5 digit stats and weapons are only boosting 4-5 digits up to rank 33 where you finally see useful upgrades, but all in all you can equip a rank 2-5 weapon and just sit on it till the end of the main game, boots are also stagnant until rank 32 when you finally get a new one that boosts movement by 2 instead of 1. Your reliance on damage is solely dependent on the juicebar, which is very Disgaea-like but at the same time makes gear pointless until you get closer to rank 40 gear where you begin seeing massive gains (also stat boosting innocents become equally useless as a drop in the bucket).- For units, there are a decent amount of story characters to obtain, as well with the complete version of the game you also get all the dlc if you want to use it (i decided not to since i didn't want to clog up my unit list since you can have up to 130). All classes are story locked so unlike older games you cant just run across them in the item world and then unlock them in the dark assembly after you defeat them, you have to just wait for a mission to pop up that has it's unlock as a prize every chapter. Also with how little options there are for creatable units, granted its still a lot but if you played older Digaea games it leaves a lot to be desired. I did like how heavy monster classes took up a 5 block space instead of a 1 now, they cant fit into small areas but its neat how they use them as blockades to protect the rangers behind them. All in all and the TLDR is that i like it, Though chopped down a lot in areas it is the same Disgaea that people enjoy. The Qol additions makes it easy to get into and make you feel powerful until you get to post game where the hard grinding and min-maxing completely opens up. Good if all you want to do is finish the story to be done, and good if you like to farm your brains out to max the stats on everyone. A lot of the downsides I complained about apparently get fixed in Disgaea 7, so ill look forward to playing that when I'm done here. Can recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: My recommendation is dependent upon a discount.In-depth review from a huge disgaea fan(TLDR at bottom) Disgaea is my favorite game series and NIS is my favorite developer. Currently, i have 359 hours on Disgaea 5 and i put about double that into Disgaea 4 and D2. I bought this game at full price which is an honor i only give out about once per year. I watched many reviews on youtube about this game before the pc release and everyone was saying that 5 is better but never really properly explained why. I aim to do that now as concisely as possible.Graphics: This game did not need to be 3D. I'm sure they did it because they thought less people would play the 2D version. Characters still do the same poses they did in the 2D games but in 3D some of them look very strange. However, this accounts for a very small amount of gameplay. The graphics overall are pleasant to look at though.Audio: Most of this games audio is ripped from previous games. Do you like 4,5 and D2's music? Its literally the same for the most part. Take that as you will. The juice shop song is a BOP though! Voice acting was adequate.Story: Not good. I started skipping towards the end. I didn't expect much and i didn't receive much. Out of the ones i played i would order them 4,5,D2, and 6 from best to worst. However the story has never been the draw for me.Gameplay: This part more than others depends on you having played D5 or D2 to understand. The gameplay is very similar to Disgaea 5 so instead of covering every little minutia of D6 im going to cover the changes from D5 to D6Drink Shop: Great idea in theory. At the end of every battle you get mana and exp from battle and depending on the amount you get, a separate amount is added to your drink shop. You can use exp to and HL (currency) to raise individual stats of characters such as ATK, DEF, RES, ect. However the balance for this feature is all out of wack. On one hand, raising base stats with the drink bar is a noob trap. It is nice that the stats you gain are maintained through reincarnation but it is SO COSTLY to level your base stats in this way, you are WAAAAAAY better off just grinding levels. However for things like Class proficiency, and weapon mastery, its the reverse. You would be stupid to not use the drink bar to level these as doing it through grinding levels can take hours while the drink bar can do it instantly, at high cost but not so high that its not easily done in the post-game. Once you level these, you will have almost no reason to use this other than dumping mana into a character to reincarnate easier.Classes: There are 22 classes in this game and many of their unique evilities are sorta inconsequential. The same goes for the unique story characters. Shout out to Misedor. I'm not sure if this is less classes than D5 but it sure feels like it. It also feels like what class you choose matters less in any given situation now. It still matters, just less.Abilities: Generic weapon abilities are gone. No longer will you learn new axe skills the higher your axe mastery becomes. Each character has between about 2 and 4 unique abilities and you can also teach anyone magical spells. However thats it. Melee builds have been left out to dry in this aspect. No Braveheart, or Poison. Only fire, ice, wind, star and the 4 different versions of each.Item World: Through my entire playthrough, i never had a peice of equipment that raised a character's stats by a consequential amount. The stats from weapons are a drop in the ocean compared to my character's base stats. I have just NOW reached the point where im going to need to level items to get stronger but im in the late post-game farming Raksasha 20 star enemies (Sometimes). Most people won't even make it to this stage. As a consequence, i havent done a single mystery room in the item world yet as farming the story is just more efficient.Auto-Battling: Yes now Disgaea is basically an idle game. Now i like idle games. I can enjoy them and i am still able to enjoy this game. However there are some things that are noticeably lacking. Your units move based on AI that you set called "Demonic Intelligence". This tool is good but i quickly discovered things it was missing. For example i cant tell someone to look for a skip gate starting at round 5 and for every turn after. I also have not discovered how to make my units automatically use Espoir on any ally with any status effect. So if im auto battling, they just have to deal with it i suppose.And so ends the gameplay sectionThis Port: I didn't play the switch version, however i can tell very little love went into this port. I play with a controller but button prompts are always for the keyboard. This can make things confusing. I still dont know how to rearrange auto-battling parties without using the keyboard. There is also one thing i definitely can't do with the controller and that's enter names. When reincarnating, if i accidentally choose to change a character's name (Which is easy to do) I have to walk over to my keyboard to change the name or even just to close the text box in order to continue. Also manuevering your cursor during battle is . . . weird. It hard to get the cursor to go where you want it to even after turning on snapping. I never had this issue in D5. Not once, This incentivizes just auto battling which i did 99.9% of the time.TLDR: I was able to enjoy this game even if i was disappointed at points. The people who said D5 was better are not wrong. However i think there are some good ideas that could be incorporated into future releases quite well. Its hard to say if i recommend this game. I'm glad i played it. I'm not glad i spent $70.00. I thought Disgaea 5 would be dead to me as soon as this came out but i may go back to it. I'm also not done with this yet though. I just want Disgaea to be better and for NIS to be successful and i think this game may have hurt that. Its complicated.
