_childDocuments_.review: A retro-themed visual novel with a few puzzles/minigames scattered throughout.  The characters were well written, and I thought the story had a pretty interesting spin on the whole Mothman legend.  I really liked the overall art style as well.Some of the sounds are a little sharp/grating, but I have overly sensitive hearing anyway, so it may not be that bad for most everyone else.Didn't notice any bugs or other performance hiccups.Recommending for casual players and fans of visual novels.
_childDocuments_.name: Mothmen 1966

_childDocuments_.review: As there aren't many reviews atm, I decided to make a review about this game. It's a short game that can be finished in 1-2 hours hence the lower price. For me this is a good thing, I have less time and find short games to be great to play then. The art is really good, nice monochromatic colors which give some really nice shadow effects and give a spooky feeling. I remember this game from a time ago in a article of PCGamer, so really wanted to give it a try. The game also has some sound effects for dramatic effects which work pretty good. It has an interesting story. There are multiple minigames throughout the game. There is also a minigame called Solitaire which is fun to play. You keep on playing this minigame, I actually had to snap out of it. ^^In the game you get multiple options in the story but I still find it to be 1 story and if you choose the wrong path you die. Technically you can play this game with 1 playthrough.This game has mainly good points but some bugs. I advice to save in the game by pressing the right below button. This game does seem to miss a 'Quit Game' option, so your sorta stuck into it and have to go task manager to exit it. Unless I really overlooked. Also when I went to save the game and went back in the game, the top screen was missing or the text seem to copy itself. I had to reset the game to play again. Also the game seemed to crash 1 time for me. For me this wasn't a biggie though as long as you make some saves. I'm an older game and are used to games crashing sometimes. The good old days.. ^^ For the ultrawide users. I have an 3440x1440 screen. This game didnt support ultrawide, but tbh I didnt expect this. It wasnt even noticable. Now should you buy this game? Yes! Games like these are kinda rare and the price is really nice. Also the small shortcomings are neglectable compared to the overall feel of the game. It's nostalgic with a great story and really great art. Support this developer.
_childDocuments_.name: Mothmen 1966

_childDocuments_.review: Choose your own adventure stories haven't really piqued my interest since I was in middle school.  Mothmen 1966, however, made me feel very nostalgic for the genre and I really enjoyed the handful of different scenarios and outcomes (deaths).  I don't feel like the game is too short, it's a comfortable length and doesn't get too lost in the camp and silliness of the plot.I do wish there were more endings than the death options and the post credit ending.  However, I do think the ending provided is fun.The artwork is enjoyable to look at and lead you through the story.  I felt like the characters had sensible motivations and character background so that even if I found their plights a bit nonsensical I could understand the context behind their actions/feelings.  Really glad I sat down this weekend to play the game and 100% it.  I felt easily drawn into the world and enjoyed it as a nod to the absurdity of traditional choose your own adventure novels.  May not be for everyone, but it scratched the itch I was hoping it would.
_childDocuments_.name: Mothmen 1966

_childDocuments_.review: Well... I haven't played it much, but as for now I'm kind of amuzed by the quality of the Pixel art. The story is appealing too. The retro vibe plus the X-files or Monster of the week (Why not) vibe complemets itself really great. The tone of the story and the pacing are well made. The only thing I kind of don't like is the chance to retry when you make a mistake, dunno, for me it takes the stakes away, but that is just a personal preference. It dosn't rest anything to the game or the story at all.
_childDocuments_.name: Mothmen 1966

_childDocuments_.review: WARNING:, can I start this off by saying I'm flabbergasted by layers of framework that were implemented into the game down to the texture, lighting, shading, model, colour grading, and many more. I must have over 50 screenshots for this game .....I checked I have exactly 100 screenshots. Mothmen 1996 or LCB Game Studio in general has style and nails it throughout. Now that's out of the way, time to get to the nitty-gritty.Mothmen 1996 is mostly a linear Gameboy VNs with some choices that could lead to death and some fun mini-game sections to keep things interesting and retro. In this game, we play as a group of strangers escaping from the invasion of mothmen, more so about part human and part animal, as well as a secondary story I feel some players may not be satisfied with towards the end as you don't take a whole like this story. As for me, if there’s one I've taken from this game I learned how to play solitaire (it's not as hard as I had thought it would be), but in all honesty, I really had a blast experiencing this weird adventure game about a mythical beast I'm not familiar with. I wish we will get more games exploring this horror concept of other cryptos like the Jersey Devil or kaiju like King Kong, just something players could see in other medians, rather than just in movies. But, whatever  LCB Game Studio releases from now on, I'll be inclined and intrigued to play it, because their games are so unique and different so far. P.S. If you're still on the fence about this game, check out LCB Game Studio's other games on itch.io (preferably Jolly Laughter) which is free.
_childDocuments_.name: Mothmen 1966

_childDocuments_.review: I have mixed feelings about this game. I heard about this game on the Drabblecast, but it was a while before I purchased it for myself.It's a short game. I made it through twice in about 3 hours. This is not necessarily a bad thing. Only one ending (that I can tell).I liked the mini games. The solitaire  game that relies on precognition (or dumb luck) is just wild. I would prefer it if I could play it in the menu without having it hook back into the main game when I'm done. The final fight game was also a favorite.The pixel artwork was also great. That being said, I would have liked a little more polish in the story.  A good story is really important for me in game play. While a short story is not bad, I really would have liked more, and some parts felt really abrupt and didn't necessarily mesh, especially the part about shrunken bear head. Just *blam* character thinks in his head about the story.  I also would appreciate the ability to turn the text sound down or off without turning down/off the rest of the sound on effects. I'm getting up there in years and old school computer text noise grates on the eardrums.Overall, I think I would recommend this game, but maybe wait for a sale. 2.5 out of 5 cat treats
_childDocuments_.name: Mothmen 1966

_childDocuments_.review: Mothmen is such a creative retro comic book inspired piece of interactive fiction. It's charming and never overstays its welcome. The color palette is beautiful and fits the vibe it wants to portray excellently. The NES inspired soundscape is fun, it gives everything a little extra depth that i appreciated and it only helped further the vibe. The death screens were easily my favorite part, specifically the death sound is PERFECT. The story is fun and you're swapping between three different characters. None of them are very deeply developed but for the playtime it works very well and hits that comic book aspect. Overall Mothmen does exactly what it wanted to be perfectly. The price of $4.50 on sale is well worth what you're getting.- I don't know if i would recommend this game at the full price of $9 for that amount of content that's in it BUT I will say that money is absolutely worth being spent and sent to the developers pockets for future endeavors. Can't wait to try Varney Lake.
_childDocuments_.name: Mothmen 1966

_childDocuments_.review: Great, albeit short, visual novel with a retro style and interesting subject matter. Writing and characters are solid and develop interestingly through the story. This will take you about an hour to beat and possibly up to two hours to get all of the achievements if you get lucky with the solitaire mini game.
_childDocuments_.name: Mothmen 1966

_childDocuments_.review: This is a perfect, atmospheric, fun pixel adventure with choose your own-adventure mechanics, some cool puzzles, and a story that is worth the ride. Seriously, the “Pulp” in the game description is no lie, go in with no expectations and enjoy the ride. You get to play as three different - very distinct - characters and interact with each other to uncover a X-Files-like mystery. The visuals are gorgeous, I love the neon greens and the old school comic style. The game also knows how to use the old rickety PC game soundtrack as well as sound effects. Those who are old (like me) and remember ye olden adventure games, you’ll be delighted by the sound effects. For the young kids: enjoy, it’s highly atmospheric. The game takes about 90 - 120 minutes and it’s worth the price. The pacing is great, nothing is drawn out, there is a mini game in there to play and quite possibly multiple endings (I only played it through once but suspect that there’s ways to lead the characters in different directions). For 8 bucks, this is a steal, given that you get unique visuals, a great and very smooth gameplay, a unique soundtrack, a mini game, AND honestly one of the greatest plots your pulpy heart could want. Take a peak:
_childDocuments_.name: Mothmen 1966

_childDocuments_.review: While the aesthetics of Mothman 1966 are charming at first, I found myself disappointed having kept an eye on this game since its original announcement. It's extremely short, to the point that even $9 seems a tad much, and the puzzles were tedious at best. The story is fine until a specific point near the end, where it takes a completely out-of-nowhere turn that made me say out loud, "wait, what the ♥♥♥♥ just happened?" The ending is extremely unsatisfying, and is more a point where the story decides to stop than an actual ending. And as far as I can tell from the achievements, there is only one ending, so I doubt that I just didn't get the TRUE ending with a more satisfying conclusion.If you're dead-set on playing this, I'd suggest waiting until a sale, if that ever happens.
_childDocuments_.name: Mothmen 1966

_childDocuments_.review: Just completed this and ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, what a game! And that ending lol. The whole thing is just a truly chill experience, bringing to mind a Tales of The Crypt style comic I used to read here in the UK as a kid called Scream! The setting, the story, the music and fun little mini games, the pixel art aesthetics (I grew up with a Commodore 64 so I love it)... I honestly can't recommend this enough. And although I don't think it's officially verified for Steam Deck, it plays perfectly on it. Been playing this one a lot in bed at night and it's been seriously brilliant. You really do feel like a kid again reading a horror comic by torch light under the covers! Very happy I have these guys other two games still to play now! Well done to everyone involved, you guys have a new fan!
_childDocuments_.name: Mothmen 1966

_childDocuments_.review: A 2 hours visual novel with a few short puzzles sprinkled in-between. If you fail, you can instantly retry, so the experience wasn't frustrating at all. The art is delightful & the mystery is quite interesting! The writing itself is decent, but nothing amazing, it's a pulp after all. I liked most of the characters besides - spoiler: If you're looking for a short experience for a weekend or an evening with some spooky 1960s vibes, I definitely recommend it! Check out the other games from these devs too! They have two other similar games with completely different mysteries & story! (Varney Lake & Bahsen Knights)
_childDocuments_.name: Mothmen 1966

_childDocuments_.review: Been playing this since the demo came out, played the other pixel pulps too, even the Christmas special, and all of them are like those choose your own adventure books with a touch of tales from the crypt, it is awesome, super engaging and filled to the brim with replayability, i can't recommend this enough!!! PLAY IT!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Mothmen 1966

_childDocuments_.review: One of those cases where I wish steam had a mixed review option. This game tries a lot and doesn't really succeed. Some of the puzzles and minigames are interesting, but because they all use the same menus as the dialogue options, some of them end up being ridiculously cumbersome to play through. There's one in particular where you're rotating puzzle pieces on a grid and it's like 4 menus to rotate one piece. It just doesn't work.The story feels like it has to check off some boxes to hit the Mothman Prophecies inspiration quota (mothmen, check. men in black, check. weird writer asking everyone questions, check.) but then doesn't really engage with the material seriously. It ends up feeling dismissive and a little too ironically detached for my tastes. The climax of the game ends up feeling lazy and unearned, and the ending itself just doesn't make sense given what we know about these characters. The little characterization we get over the course of the game is largely thrown out. Generally I like shorter games, but this one feels like it meanders around for a little while and then just abruptly ends. With all that said, the art's good and they did a really nice job with the game's engine. It looks and feels great. I just wish the game itself was better.
_childDocuments_.name: Mothmen 1966

_childDocuments_.review: There’s a startlingly down-to-earth sensibility Mothmen glows in that the devs seem ready to defend to the death! And I get it. It’s a lazy critique of pulp stories, and stories in general - wahhh, these characters are ‘flat.’ That word does an astonishing bit of legwork. It’s this want for a very specific kind of story couched in a pretend offhand remark. There’s a humanity in everything that can (and can’t) be presupposed about an imprecise archetype - and that’s every character in Mothmen. Something that feels precise, but not enough to put your finger on.I think the characters here mostly accomplish that. There’re extraordinary things on ordinary edges that feel very human. I think the actual problem is the game’s insistence on putting these characters through a ‘fast-paced’ story that doesn’t have enough time to respect their normality.  There’s a certain point where these characters seemingly lose everything that makes them charming almost-cliches so they can just become cliches. Who have a lot of lore to tell you. It makes me hate the mothmen for eating through the story. Like moths. I hate that this game shakes out into something that doesn’t quite work because it has the foundation of something revolutionary. If the next installment in this series keeps at the same breakneck pace, I hope the devs look for more pauses in the action to consider how their characters, in all their normalities and abnormalities, would really react.
_childDocuments_.name: Mothmen 1966

_childDocuments_.review: This game has the same energy as those weird sci fi horror anthology Goosebumps rip offs you'd find in the school library about the killer Komodo dragons of kentucky or some ♥♥♥♥ . Would def recommend for those who are a fan of weird anthology short fiction and the pixel art is very nice and retro. I will note there are not multiple endings beyond some CYOA style deaths. I do kind of wish there were more weird and absurd deaths like you'd see in those Goosebumps CYOA books, but thats a nit pick.

_childDocuments_.review: Really like the concept and design of this game. Classic Apple IIe type horror with PC speaker-styled sound effects, a great story (awesome writing), and a number of unlocks. Though there have been some complaints about an auto-save feature (which the devs claim they want to implement) it's really not an issue because you can quick pass earlier stuff to get your unlocks or back to where you want to be. _childDocuments_.name: Mothmen 1966

_childDocuments_.review: This game is more like an interactive comic. It is short, but it doesn't feel like it should be longer. There are some mini-games and choices to make it interactive, but they don't feel very closely tied to the narrative. The story is interesting, and it combines the Mothman, men-in-black, the Civil War, and lots of others things. I don't know if it all fits together neatly, but there is a lot of lore packed in here. The artwork looks GREAT!
_childDocuments_.name: Mothmen 1966

_childDocuments_.review: This game is trying to do some interesting things, but it really just fails at most of them. The art style is interesting, and it's a throwback to classic games, but the interactivity of the menus and interfaces suffer because of that retro-style. In the modern day, creating an interface that lets you interact with the puzzles more intuitively should not be compromised because of art style. You can have both.The story is weird. The characters are all basically unlikable, the relationships are needlessly complicated, and the plot itself is hanging on by a thread.My biggest issue, though, regardless of interface or story, is the way that there appears to only be one right path most of the time, and choosing the other options will either get you killed (over and over again, especially with some of the unintuitive puzzles) or will just funnel you back into the "correct" path and basically call you stupid for trying something different.I can tell this game was made with passion. The dev(s) definitely seem to be familiar with the Mothman mythology - at least in passing - but the story takes on insanely convoluted and downright silly turns, for seemingly no reason. It's a game that is simultaneously trying to present genuine drama and complex character interactions while also using some of the goofiest nonsense storytelling I've ever seen.If you're in for a laugh and you don't mind replaying the same sections over and over (because of dying to things while you try to figure out the correct option to click), give it a shot. Don't expect it to be interesting or fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Mothmen 1966

_childDocuments_.review: The good- Amazing visuals in green, cyan and black colors. Each frame is an artistic masterpiece.- Mysterious, trippy atmosphere that gets you immersed right from the beginning. It has something surreal in it, like having hallucinations.- Well written. Every line is interesting and you never get bored of reading.-  Nicely designed characters with well shaped personalities. Also, visually they're awesome and you can feel their emotions by looking at their facial expressions.- Good sound design with 8 bit electronic sounds and a mix of white noise that enhance the mysterious atmosphere.- "Impossible Solitaire" is a fun game to play.- It has some cool extras on the main menu. There is a gallery with nice images and you can play solitaire whenever you want.The bad- Minimum, shallow gameplay. It's more of an interactive graphic novel than an actual video game.- The few puzzles that it has are unimaginative and clunky. Interacting with their pieces via text instead of directly clicking on them is annoying.- Small duration without much of a story or proper climax. It just describes a weird situation. Ending is abrupt and leaves a lot of unanswered questions.- It's gorgeous visually but the images could be less static.
_childDocuments_.name: Mothmen 1966

_childDocuments_.review: After watching the trailer I really wanted to like this game. Its dripping with aesthetic and charm and there is a surprisingly dense amount of characterization given to the main cast in the short span of the game. However, a handful of things bog this game down for me. The story takes some interesting turns but leaves too many unanswered questions for my taste. You're faced with many decisions but very few of them have impact on the overall story, minus the ones that just lead to an instant death. Finally, the lack of an autosave feature meant that I accidentally had to replay certain parts of the story after exiting to the main menu partway through.
_childDocuments_.name: Mothmen 1966

_childDocuments_.review: Like a night a drive-in movie, and about the same price. Strong, clear writing with great character insight. Good pacing. The navigation for some of the puzzles is a little old-school, but that also fit and it didn't get too much in the way. For how much lore they packed into this, it all went together surprisingly well! Stay after for the credits and get a little bonus. :)
_childDocuments_.name: Mothmen 1966

_childDocuments_.review: Just an interactive episode of the twilight zone.Really well polished game with a unique narrative for a Cryptid that usually gets some uninspired storylines, potential for 1-3 hours of content if you don't use a guide for achievements. If you ♥♥♥♥ with late 20th century mystery shows this is your vibe for certain.
_childDocuments_.name: Mothmen 1966

_childDocuments_.review: "Mothmen 1966" is a short horror-mystery visual-novel with puzzle elements that is competently written and a charming bow to the pulp-genre. The design, palette and visual style is gorgeous, but sometimes the sounds/ambience differ somewhat in volume and theUI can get tedious in some passages.Nonetheless a great experience that can be 100% in around 1,5~2 hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Mothmen 1966

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed the art, the atmosphere and the story, even if it's a short game. It has nice minigame-like mechanics that allow the gameplay to vary and you can also play a cool solitaire directly from the menu screen. I would have liked it to be longer as I was really getting into it, but I enjoyed it anyways. I'm looking forward to these devs' future projects!
_childDocuments_.name: Mothmen 1966

_childDocuments_.review: I admit I wasn't sure about the graphics at first and there are also some issues with the technical side on an ultra-wide screen (opening the menu froze the pictures and a restart was necessary; after beating the game the "EXIT" option was outside of the view window). That aside, the actual story of the game was engaging all the way and short enough to finish comfortably in one sitting. The story is simple enough, but moves fast and the characters grow on you, despite their cliched 60s stereotypical behaviour. There are some puzzle sections, but fortunately failing does not mean that you have to restart everything -- only the particular puzzle or part of it. Overall, really good and I would actually love to see a sequel (not necessarily the same story, but another game with this style and story -- there are enough cryptids to make hundreds of games of anyway). I do recommend to wait for a sale, though. I got the game for ~2 €, which I would consider fair. 9 € is too much for what is available here.
_childDocuments_.name: Mothmen 1966

_childDocuments_.review: Super solid visual novel! Highly recommend! Could be boasting their claim of being well-written but it really is! First came across this when trying to find VN that were not FMV/acted and not dating sims (there are so few!). If you are looking for something well-written (Disco Elysium spoiled me--I've become pickier about writing) or are a horror fan, you'll definitely not be disappointed. Will definitely be picking up all subsequent titles from the same series. It also helps that the art and presentation/UI are super well-done.
_childDocuments_.name: Mothmen 1966

_childDocuments_.review: Mothmen 1966 is about the struggles of playing solitaire. It is also a cool visual novel! What is amazing is how they managed to create such a creepy atmosphere by only using like 5 colours and a few bleeps and bloops. I won't spoil the story here, but even though it is brief, there is enough material to make your imagination run wild.What does not work so well are the puzzles. Using typical visual novel style dialogue selection system to solve simple puzzles is cumbersome. Runtime could have been longer as well, because it is possible to finish the game in about an hour.Overall, Mothmen 1966 is a good way to lose a night's sleep. I am interested to see what LCB Game Studio does next. 4 mothmen out of 5.
_childDocuments_.name: Mothmen 1966

_childDocuments_.review: I feel like I'm in whatever microaudience that this game and the entire Pixel Pulp series is for. Strong, lurid CGA-esque graphics and wild horror fiction that harkens back to some horror books by some horror authors of yesteryear. Praising the graphics is obvious enough: if you like what you see, there's a lot more of it inside, and it all looks great. It's moody and carries a lot of the game's tone and is like a bath for my eyeballs. The story is harder to put my finger on. It does a good job of building an ominous atmosphere where what is going on and where it's going is hard to pin down. On top of that is this mountain of intense character stuff, where there is always at least one person quietly grinding their teeth with absolutely loathing for someone else, with the pettiest, most poisonous thoughts swirling around them. There are moments where a few of them are truly hard to be around.So then on top of  is how the story develops, where it keeps piling on new and crazy developments that just get weirder and weirder and weirder. By the end, it's hard what to make of it all except that I wish it all hung together more tightly (thematically?). That, and an appreciation of just how ludicrous the piling on of elements is. I don't want to list them because the surprises are fun, but if you've read The Mothman Prophecies, then where it takes those already absurd elements is even more absurd. Initially I was on the fence about the writing overall, but in the end I like it. It's a weird little story and for that I appreciate where it ends up. I do hope that future games have stronger writing, with a more cohesive narrative, stronger sentences, and a bit more time given to making the characters, uh, not so completely grating. As it is, for an inaugural game where the crime is perhaps a bit too much absurd craziness too quickly, it's promising to see and makes me eager for what a steadier hand will deliver. And, I mean, it's supposed to be a pulp story, which it delivers on in spades.My only real criticism is the sound and music, which lean way too hard into the CGA-era PC internal beeper aesthetic. Straight up: it sounds flat. If they can break CGA visual rules enough to do this amazing, rich art, then they can and should break the beeper rules and add some more timbre. The sounds have to be fatter, folks. Don't die on this hill.
_childDocuments_.name: Mothmen 1966

_childDocuments_.review: I've been having this game sit in my Steam Library for a bit now, but I am glad I finally got around to playing this lovely looking game! The art was absolutely gorgeous and super cool to have the story told with! Plus, once I got a hang of the mini games I almost wished there was a quick way to play them through the main menu. Anywho, I really appreciate this game for it's art, music, overall story, and really loved how the almost nondescript look the art had made the cryptids creeper! Would definitely recommend this one while all cozy with blankets and a nice cup of (insert preferred beverage here).
_childDocuments_.name: Mothmen 1966

_childDocuments_.review: Rounding everything it's a recommended experience.The story leaves some loose ends and the ending it's not that satysfing. Don't know if it happens because it's a "pulp story".The gameplay has some interesting puzzles and action sequences. The best thing of this game are the graphics; beautiful art style, almost like paintings, and the color palette it's really captivating.
_childDocuments_.name: Mothmen 1966

_childDocuments_.review: Overall I enjoyed this game! The art was beautiful and I really enjoyed the concept. I felt as though the characters could have had a little more depth and as other reviews have mentioned I felt some frustration with the puzzles/combat, some of them felt like I couldn't solve them without just brute forcing it. I think the puzzles would have been better if you received some kind of hint or help after dying the first (or third) time. If the concept interests you, I think its worth picking up, especially if its on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Mothmen 1966

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic.  Mothmen 1966 incorporates a myriad of concepts and ideas on top of a rarely used foundation.  Few if any games have utilized the Mothman legends and even fewer have expanded upon the source material.  The absurdity of it all stays true to the inspiration taken from old pulp fiction magazines, expanding upon them by introducing several interactive sections in addition to multiple choices to make in dialogue.  I loved it and I look forward to whatever comes next, both new titles and merchandise.  Best of luck to the devs!
_childDocuments_.name: Mothmen 1966

_childDocuments_.review: I really adore the art and the color palette for this game. It really sets the mood and vibes. The story feels so short though, I hope there's a sequel sometime in the future! I blinked and it was over--just when I was getting immersed haha! I was hoping for another ending, but even without  one I can see myself replaying it sometime down the line just to revisit the characters. It's an enjoyable novel and worth the money! 😊⭐
_childDocuments_.name: Mothmen 1966

_childDocuments_.review: My only complaint with this game is that it should have been longer since it was throwing us a lot of plot hooks to latch onto and I wanted more time to explore them. Other than that, I liked the old-school graphics, the mothman, and the "tactical" section which I think could have been a longer minigame.
_childDocuments_.name: Mothmen 1966

_childDocuments_.review: Neat little horror story with choose your own adventure elements about cryptids and other mysterious sightings featuring a cast of surprisingly human characters (Victoria gang WYA), totally recommend it if you dig this stuff even a little bit. Great art, too.(That being said, who's the demon at the dev team behind 50/50 Solitaire? I just wanna talk)Sudden Spanish PS: Es lindo ver cosas así de devs de tu país, no sé :)
_childDocuments_.name: Mothmen 1966

_childDocuments_.review: An interesting visual novel with a gorgeous CGA art style. The tale is very pulpy and you'll either like that kind of story or not. My main gripe is that the puzzles are frustrating to play because it's all done with clunky menus and they demand one solution only. There are also no branching paths and alternate choices just result in a slight amount of different dialogue.I did enjoy this but at full price, I think it's a bit steep, given the short length and lack of replayability. I'd recommend getting on a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Mothmen 1966

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not a visual novel player, but Mothmen really catch my eye since day one. And i'm trully happy after finished the game. The history was really good, the art, mechanics, I really loved the game. My only complaing is that i'm not a big fan of "you fail, try again". Not sure how that can be changed, but a few times I thought that it might be good to the story continue without that player. Besides this tiny thing, this made me travel back in time.
_childDocuments_.name: Mothmen 1966

_childDocuments_.review: If you like the aesthetic from the screenshots, just buy the game. Believe me, it only gets better.Short little visual novel type game, with a few "gameplay" elements (choosing through text options to get through puzzles, nothing too hard).Story is decent, atmosphere is 11/10.It takes an hour and a half to finish the game. It has 3 endings.
_childDocuments_.name: Mothmen 1966

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this game with some reservations. The good: The pixel aesthetic is well done, the music is sparse but effective, and the writing is very good, the story is both creepy and makes you want to read more of it, and all the characters are surprisingly well drawn for such a short game.The bad, is that this game is *very* short. I don't wanna spoil anything, and I assure you that the story is interesting, but the ending is extremely sudden and there are a LOT of unanswered questions, in fact game didn't seem to answer any of the questions the player/reader might have, although from what I understand this is just the first part of a series. Even so, I managed to get to the end in under an hour, which is arguably not worth the 8 dollars I paid for this given how a Kindle novel of the same price could keep me occupied for much longer. Still, the quality of the writing and the inventiveness of the premise made it worth it for me, so I'd recommend it in the end. Nice horror!
_childDocuments_.name: Mothmen 1966

_childDocuments_.review: Good, pulpy visual novel with well-executed retro pixel graphics. It's a bit short (a couple hours at most) but it's punchy and doesn't waste a lot of words. The writing is good, and I look forward to future releases of this style from LCB. Hope this becomes the first of many "pixel-pulps". If you like this, look up the LCB site and check out their debut "Shark Riders".
_childDocuments_.name: Mothmen 1966

_childDocuments_.review: It's a short (~1.5-2 hours read) but enjoyable visual novel also with solitaire that the devil forces people to play in the darkest pits of Hell. Your local 7-11 in the backwoods populated only by mysterious writers emerging from bushes and mutants that should not be is the perfect place for a romantic dinner with your girlfriend. Even if coyotes and mothmen want to try and ruin the evening.
_childDocuments_.name: Mothmen 1966

_childDocuments_.review: "Your feel your heart pounding." (Appears in chapter 2's car scene, I believe.)A grammatical error? Unforgivable! In all seriousness, Mothmen 1966 is an interesting albeit short graphic novel with a fun aesthetic, in both visuals and plot. Obviously, it's not the deepest or most emotional, but it's enough to entertain and get you invested. I'm glad the devs are working on some more "Pixel Pulps". Bought for Mothmen, stayed for camp horror.
_childDocuments_.name: Mothmen 1966

_childDocuments_.review: Good little horror visual novel.It's a recommended but with some conditions.If you expect a lot of content, take in count I played a least a good 30 minutes on the solitaire mini-game alone to get some achievements, so it's more of a 1 hour and a half experience, not 2 hours.If you want to play the game just to see the characters die in gruesome ways in the different endings don't get it there is no gore.Apart from that I just wish the game would use the cursor to it's fullest potential in the mini-games.A good example is the solitaire mini-game, you have to click on buttons to move a cursor to select cards, let me just use my mouse.I really don't see the need for something like that except to lengthen the playtime slightly and it make the mini-games more annoying to play on top for no good reason.
_childDocuments_.name: Mothmen 1966

_childDocuments_.review: Good game but painfully short. If most games are movies this felt like a comic book. The whole thing feels like a great intro to a much longer game. The demo was maybe 1/4th of the game.With that said, it's good though, interesting story, some fun and interesting minigames mixed in. Some great bits of choose your own adventure vibes while the story really only plays out one way, but even that fits back into the narrative which was cool.Overall a good game but left me wanting so much more even though I enjoyed what is there.P.S.: If you're able to win the Impossible Solitaire, I'd love to take you on a trip to Vegas.
_childDocuments_.name: Mothmen 1966

_childDocuments_.review: Mothmen 1966 feels like a game that would have been perfect for a X-Files fan back in the 90s. That's very much me; an X-files fan stuck on Vector 13 comics and found footage mockumentaries about boggy creaks and mothmen. The low-fi nature of it Mothmen 1966, coupled with the intriguing story makes it feel like you're taking a deep dive into some old, unsolved mystery.
_childDocuments_.name: Mothmen 1966

_childDocuments_.review: Mothmen 1966 is a 'Pixel Pulp' - a visual novel featuring a fusion of exceptional writing and stunning illustration, inspired by mid-20th century pulp fiction and 80s home computer graphics - set amongst the strange occurrences of the Leonid meteor shower of 1966.
_childDocuments_.name: Mothmen 1966

name: The Last Clockwinder
detailed_description: Tucked away inside a colossal tree, discover a pair of gloves that allow you to turn anything you do into a looping clockwork clone. Use your new power to repair the clocktower and uncover the ancient secrets it protects. Use the Clockwinder’s gloves to recreate the actions you take with clockwork clones, known as the gardeners. From growing to harvesting to tossing plants through the air, you’ll need to get creative in order to solve each of the puzzles put before you. Using the gardeners, create an interconnected system to grow plants, harvest resources, and work together to save the clocktower! Automate everything! Perform simple tasks by hand, and then use the gloves to loop each task on repeat. Team up with yourself! Coordinate your clones to create marvels of precision teamwork or hare-brained Rube Goldberg machines. A cozy sci-fi world! Tackle things at your own pace in a gorgeous setting inspired by watchmaking, sci-fi, and the natural world. Rediscover your connection to the Clocktower: Piece together your complicated past as you work to save your childhood home.

_childDocuments_.review: runs really well, is super satisfying to play, the story and art direction are great, and it's a really unique idea for a VR game. love it overall. a must-play for me. has single-handedly restored my faith in unique ideas coming to VRedit: now that I've finished it, this is one of the best VR games I've ever played. my only complaint is I wish it was longer, but the difficulty curve is so perfect that maybe making it longer would have not been a good idea. I hope a sequel or DLC is released someday, and I'm very glad the devs released this on SteamVR and not only as a Quest exclusive or I never would have gotten to enjoy it. amazing game
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: This is exactly the kind of game that needs more recognition: it's something that couldn't have been done without VR. So not only did they put together a new mechanic, they also wrapped it in a touching story with great art and music and top-notch voice acting. On top of that, the interaction with world is better than almost anything else I've played that uses physics in VR. You move things in an intuitive, satisfying way, and things are never janky. Well done, and I hope to see more like this!
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: I'm giving this a recommendation because it's a good game damnit. Automation in VR, such a cool and unique idea! It's like a physics based cookie clicker or adventure capitalist with puzzles and a pretty good voice acted story.1. For some reason the inventory is locked behind picking up a resource object that looks like any other resource object and there's no hints that tell you picking it up will unlock the inventory, leading me to reach the third area without an inventory. Not great.2. No. Smooth. Movement. Not even smooth turning. Why every VR dev decides Teleport and snap turn are good enough for launch is beyond my understanding but it's annoying as hell and makes me not want to play. In this game though I've made an exception because it's truly a gem apart from that.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: The game feels good.  Grabbing.  Interacting.  Heck, just listening to the great voice acting or music.  It feels "right" in VR, which is still a challenge for most games.  Think Factorio, except YOU are the machines, and whether it's throwing or cutting or catching in time with the previous "you" you set in motion, creating an assembly line of your little guys is satisfying.  Worth it!
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: At its heart, it's a physical programming game, with a colorful and tactile presentation that serves as a pleasant backdrop.  There's nothing terribly difficult, mostly requiring methodical problem-solving, but it's still very satisfying to meet the efficiency challenges in each room.  The story is unobtrusive but well-written and well-voiced.Took me about 8 hours to hit 100%.Once you've beaten all the challenges, there's not much in the way of replay value.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: I have so far played three VR games with this exact mechanic, and I have to say, this game uses it better than either of the others by a wide margin. This is by no means a perfect game, but it has a fantastic charm and style to it that is very difficult to successfully capture, and I've experienced very few bugs thus far. All in all, I think this game is a must for anybody with a VR headset.Also, after interacting with myself for three hours, I have concluded that I hate myself.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: Really great game that you owe yourself to play. Took me five hours, probably take you less.You can tell a lot of thought was put into how to make this game in every aspect, this is really great work.Levels were thoroughly thought through, are fun and to start just playing around until you find a solution. They never frustrated me and I never got bored or wanted to move on. There's a long ass list of playtesters in the credits, you can tell that they used their feedback for more than QA.Art direction is really great. Finally! Bright, well lit environments that feel great in VR, are fun to navigate and are visually appealing. The only minor quirks (on the off chance the team read these, consumers shouldn't care) are that the smoke effects rotate with the HMD, I think you should be able to set that they rotate on the Y axis towards the HMD but not x or z (is unity Y up?) but I only noticed it because I tilted my head on purpose. Also I really wish these beautiful assets had slightly higher res bakes, but I get that it would be pretty high cost to fix that for so few users with higher res displays.The grabbing, fruit collision and throwing feel really great. You do a lot of throwing and grabbing in this game, thankfully those systems feel really robust - they won't frustrate you. Only you and your feeble human arms will frustrate you.The story and voice acting are great! It's all thought voice-over and at first I sat around while it was playing, but you can keep puzzling if you want. I thought that Edea sounded like Delilah from Firewatch and oh ♥♥♥♥, it is Cissy Jones! (Had no clue she was Olga (civie at the start of the game) in Half Life Alyx, rip that whole first part they apparently cut (nested parentheticals, great)). Levi and Jules were also great - at first the dynamic didn't really sell but I got into it around halfway.Played on the WMR HP Reverb G2, which isn't offically supported but worked great with literally no adjustments. My only thing (very minor, only bugged me for five minutes and then I didn't care) was that the text looks really blurry and like it's straight out of Windows 8. There has to be a better way to render that, it was never hard to read, but it was rarely pretty among these enviroments that deserve better.Really excited to see what this studio does, they clearly understand what kind of games VR desperately needs!
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: To be honest I was skeptical. I played Transpose which has a similar concept and it was disappointing. So, my expectations weren’t too high. But this one is so much better in every possible way. The puzzles are much better and stays fair until the end. Some of them requires accuracy and speed if you are trying to get the best score but first this is optional and second it still never gets frustrating hard. The next one is of course very subjective, but the presentation is so much better. The clocktower is very relaxing place to be unlike the futuristic world in Transpose. This makes the puzzles so much more fun and relaxing, at least for me. Even standing there, listening to the fantastic background music, and thinking about the next puzzle is just relaxing. Last but not least I didn’t expect the story to be so good. The voice acting and story telling is fantastic. Just listening to the recordings and dialogs makes you connected to the characters. You really care about them. As you might have guessed already, I loved this game. I have nothing bad to say about it. I had no bugs, no performance issues or anything negative. This one is an easy recommendation!
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: As a VR veteran, I am happy to say that this is easily one of my favorite VR titles to date.To summarize it; the game is kind analogous to Opus Magnum (for all you Zachtronics fans); you're challenged to solve production puzzles by using the fewest amount of looping recorded clones of yourself. Your movements and actions are recorded and looped to create one of the "Gardeners", robots that mimic your actions over a set loop of time. By strategically placing yourself and planning ahead, you can set up an assembly line of your past selves to produce whatever goal item that specific puzzle demands. The game really forces you to think creatively about efficiency in a way that pushes a boundary for this type of game. There's a level of out-of-the-box thinking required that scratches the same itch as a lot of other 'production' genre games, but in a unique way that feels totally refreshing and fun to wrap your head around. Fans of Factorio and other factory genre games will feel familiar concepts but explored in a new light. The planning required is different from those games - instead of being restrained by space/layout or by technology, your production is limited by how efficient you can be with your own body. Later levels will have you planning out where to throw tools and such to get the most out of your time for each loop. It's not perfect, and there are a handful of things that feel a little rough around the edges, but that's almost a given for any VR game and this one feels like a true breath of fresh air.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: This is an absolute must have game for anyone with VR. Fantastic story, environment, visuals, and the most enjoyable mechanics/gameplay i have experience in VR. It feels as if there is a near infinite number of ways to solve every puzzle, and it doesn't require you to figure out the most skill intensive complex solution to beat the game. It still tests your skills and mind but if you aren't going for the Fruit Per Minute and # of Bots goal in the applicable rooms it's a modest challenge, and that's good. However the challenges in each room, even if they are inconsequential are an absolute blast to figure out and perform. The pacing of gameplay to story elements is done really really well. Every moment where i've found myself a bit strained after solving a puzzle I find a new room with some recordings of Edea or end up having a chat with levi before getting back into puzzle solving action with a clear head.All in all a very very fun VR environment and puzzle game, with a really cute and moving story, and i wouldd highly recommend you give it a shot.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: I greatly enjoyed this factory-puzzler... ? It's basically robotic automation, to manufacture fruit. While it felt like a lot of trial & error, the iterative process is quick enough to make it quite enjoyable indeed.My play-time is from completing the whole game, as well as spending time perfecting it, getting all achievements. The whole game revolves around creating clones of yourself, recording your motions, and collaborating with yourself in variable time loops.Most interactions are physical, meaning you get to reach out, grab, list, push, press; things, buttons, fruits, seeds, machines. I love this kind of hands on interaction model, it makes me feel like it's an actual world to a higher degree.On that topic, the environment is crazy well designed, gorgeous and interesting. A lot of the surrounding environment is static, but the game doesn't suffer much from it, as the main game mechanics offer up a lot of interaction instead. I also enjoyed most of the audio and music, although without any clones out it is silent, which is a bit annoying but only happens when starting fresh or resetting.I'd say the only thing I didn't care much for was the story, the game could have worked just as well with no story at all, in my opinion. It felt more like a chore to listen to the dialog than anything, but maybe that is a testament to how much I enjoyed the actual game. That said, the story does leave a door open for future games, so I guess there's that!Would I recommend this? Absolutely, especially if you enjoy automation simulations and sequencing. I'd class it more like a factory game rather than puzzle game, although I guess they share aspects.

_childDocuments_.review: A whole lot of fun, until the moment it suddenly isn't.The premise is great, it's a lot of fun to get started with, but later in the game you constantly run into the issues of the game and they just take away the fun.The two big issues:1) The "clones" don't often successfully repeat the actions you did. Their hands might get stuck in some position yours weren't in, or when they try to grab something it fails when it worked fine for you.2) The physics changes randomly whenever you add new things. This is particularly annoying because a few of the objects you interact with are very physics heavy floaty things you can't interact with easily. So you e.g. try to push these balloon like things around, you set up the perfect chain of clones to push them to where you need, then you just add the one last clone to lift up a lid and capture them and .. wait, why are there no more floaty things coming this way? Oh, one of the things that was already working fine for 5 minutes decided to change how it interacts with the physics and now the things are floating some other direction and failing to get to you.There's only so many times you want to rebuild the complex chain of intricately detailed actions just hoping that this time it won't glitch and get ruined at the end.This is the kind of system that would provide infinite fun for all kinds of sandboxy experiences, but it looks like as it is, it will fail provide that kind of fun for long term, even if these issues are fixed. You can try to optimize your creations a bit, but there doesn't seem to be much reward in doing that, and each of them is pretty tightly limited to their own small areas.At 2.5 hours it seemed like a ton of fun and like it will provide seemingly endless fun, and at 4 hours I'm pretty much done unless the dev decides to at the very least fix the physics that the game so heavily relies on.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: Easily the best VR game of 2022. This game is being slept on. The core mechanic is unique and really, really satisfying. Graphics and music are beautiful and relaxing. The story is good and the pacing is perfect. It took me 10 hours to complete the game with all achievements but I was really taking my time, leaning back and just watching my clones work for a couple of minutes after completing a room (it never gets old watching a perfect production line in action).One complaint that I have is that the clones abruptly reset to their starting position each cycle unless you confirmed your recorded movements before the time ran out. It doesn't look good and makes it less satisfying, so I played the game by always confirming my movements a bit early so the clones movements were smooth and continious. I wish the game would reserve some time in each cycle just for resetting the animation.Also some later levels require high precision movements, meaning you'll be re-doing the same task very often until you get a good recording. Though this only really becomes a problem if you are trying to 100% the game.And I am nitpicking here, because otherwise I have nothing to complain about. It's a phenomenal game, I wish there were a hundred more rooms to automate.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: When they say best game they ain't joking, this is great fun. Very well designed and paced too, I could go on about how design and technically it's good but the core is this is a really fun VR game that you should play. Decent length too, you can squeeze a decent amount of juice out of this by optimising the levels and getting the challenges, or just trying to find inventive ways to cheese it or get really good at throwing.I ask for DLC, modding support, etc, though because the mechanics are really fun and some kind of level editor or similar would put this game into the next level. Please add index finger tracking support too, low priority but it's nice to have.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: A very charming little puzzle game. The game is short as most VR games are, I was able to beat it in a single session of playtime around 3 hours. The only complaint I have is the difficulty curve of some of the late game puzzles being too extreme. I'd give it a solid 9/10 overall, wish it was longer as the puzzles are really fun with a multitude of solving methods.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: A beautifully conceived, designed puzzle game that is savvy about how to mesh the story, setting and puzzles. It's not without its frustrations: while it does throwing in VR better than pretty much any other game I've played where you need to throw things, you still have to be an okay thrower and catcher. The minimum requirements per puzzle mean that you don't have to be more than mediocre, but it remains frustrating to know how you could solve one of the puzzles (or solve it better, i.e. more efficiently) but you miss your throws or catches over and over. However, by the end I understood that even my imperfect solutions rather fit the overall themes of the game. And finally, let's not forget that this is definitely one of the VR games that makes very good use of the medium: The Last Clockwinder would be a very different game without VR. A definite recommendation, unless you are really, really bad at throwing and/or you have the teensiest of VR spaces only.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a big fan of automation, puzzle and story-rich games, but it turns out The Last Clockwinder is better described as a basketball free throw simulator. The initial hour is great because recording multiple movements to chain them together is a great idea. Unfortunately, the game rarely does something interesting beyond that.There are  5 kinds of plants, some of which you can grab directly and other you can't. You farm each fruit a room and to make plant seeds with them in another room. Making seeds involves making "molecules" out of fruits and spiky stick. That's about all there is to this game.Each room plays similarly. You arrive, you figure out what you need to do and then record the chain of movements needed. There are 3-4 room where you need to think for a minute or two, but the real challenge is figuring out how to do it efficiently. This should be the fun part but it isn't for two reasons:* Efficient movement requires you to record and re-record a ton a of time until you pull it off.* Any change downstream means re-recording every movement upstream.What I ended up doing most of the time was spending 15 minutes of trial and error to adjust my throws and do complicated moves quickly. Once finished, there was clearly room for improvement but that would mean restarting from scratch so I proceeded to the next part. There is not much incentive to optimise except for achievements.The game rewards precision too much and there is not much content. Not recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: This is the kind of game that can only exist in VR. Thus far I have played very few games like that, so this one is a standout. It's an innovative puzzle game with a great art style and a moving--if simple--story.It's short (I finished it in ~6 hours), so I would look for it on sale, but I fully recommend playing it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: Great puzzle game where you make duplicates of your movements to accomplish a variety of tasks. In the end creating a "production line" with the duplicate robots.These tasks are determined by the fruit you are harvesting or any combination with others... And each fruit is special in some way, and their characteristics will mean youll have to handle them differently... The way the game combines them and how you handle their various traots at the same time, is what these puzzles are all about.  Graphics are nice and fit well with the theme of the game, voice acting is outstanding! none of that flat audio lines with no feeling, the story is shortish (took me ~4hrs to finish the game) but i still have to go back and finesse the efficiency.The only problems i ran into are some spikes that made the game choppy, that was sometimes solved by restarting the game, and sometimes the levers are all wonky, also a temporary problem.I dont know, but despite the small issues, by the end of the game i had a sense of... satisfaction? accomplishment maybe? lol The puzzles have a nice logical progression and some of the later ones are challenging.This is an easy game to recommend to any puzzle loving person, original mechanics and overall above average, with only little issues.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best VR games and possibly THE best VR puzzle game.I was thrilled at the discovery of every new element in this game, finding what fresh way the devs had invented to use VR controls. Your performance as the little gardener robots infuses them with personality that makes surveying your completed works as fun as creating them in the first place.The game is packed with little bits of finesse and talented design; clever transitions and fun interactive elements where lesser devs would have a hard cut and a simple point and click menu.I can't wait to spend more time with my funky little guys, and to play whatever Pontoco come up with next.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fantastic. The puzzles are great, not too hard - besides, there are hints available if you need them. The base mechanic is super fun, and the game introduces new twists regularly, you can tell they are not trying to pad the game. There is a nice story along with it, it's just a pleasure.The only thing that doesn't work is Steam's tracking of my play time. I finished the game, and it took much longer than the 10 minutes it shows here. Achievements also don't seem to show (I am using Virtual Desktop),
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyed this, and I place it among my top VR puzzle games of all time. Great story telling integrated with such clever level design. I get that it was optimised for mobile first, my PC performance doesn't get taxed at any point. But I love changing the smallest amount of each level, getting stuck in to solving the task at hand, and having it feel so different from the last. Regardless of design genesis, it's clever, and offers great progression and sense of accomplishment. Art style gives us a lovely space to be, in VR. The puzzle mechanic is solid. Time skips, repeats, conveyor line creation. The Satisfactory builder in me appreciated it. It's a physical puzzle where creative solutions apply. I'd happily go back to optimise some of my earlier attempts. Could be a good one to 100% on the achievements too.Story is trying soooo hard to be wholesome, but there's a time and place for it. Great VA. Pacing is solid. It gets away with its wholesomeness. Definitely a cozy game to pick up if you're in the mood for that sort of thing, and a great puzzle experience with the narration turned down if you're not.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really fun little game that involves a bit of planning, dexterity and timing. It has a rich story that gets told along the rooms you solve. It's not really a puzzle game because the puzzle challenges (produce certain amounts with limited number of clones) are optional. I didn't finish the game yet, but I estimate that it'll take me roughly 5 hours in total, so that would be around 4€/hour on the first playthrough.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game with amazing central gameplay and idea. This is what VR games should be: Not just clunky versions of flat games, but something that cannot even be conceived without VR. The only knock I can think of is that it is, as it's often the case with great concept VR games, far too short. How much 6 hours of great VR fun is worth to you will vary from person to person but it was well worth it for me - hopefully we get a DLC or a sequel to this gem.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: The Last Clockwinder is a fantastic game and truly one of the most creative applications of VR out there. The gameplay revolves around recording clones of yourself whose actions loop in order to automate fruit plant harvesting. So, for example, you might record one clone that cuts a badgertail off of its plant and then tosses it across the room—and then go across the room and record another clone that catches it and sticks it to a bomb berry before putting it in the press. It’s extremely satisfying building these automated chains of control, and the process of recording interactions between several versions is yourself is a gimmick uniquely possible in VR. Despite being a relatively short game, there’s tons of room for creativity and problem-solving as you seek the most efficient ways to automate each mechanism. The lore is pretty well-done; it contributes nicely to the atmosphere of the game, as do the music and visual style. It also has options for smooth locomotion vs teleporting and smooth rotation vs rotating at customizable intervals (e.g. 30°, 45°, etc.), which is great for accommodating different levels of player comfort in VR. I would love to see The Last Clockwinder discussed in the same breath as Beat Saber, Superhot VR, or even Half-Life: Alyx as a must-play VR title presenting a unique, immersive gameplay experience that genuinely makes the most of VR capabilities. 10/10.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: Only wish it was longer.Very fun and whimsical atmosphere with good sound design.My favorite part was looking back at a room and realizing that I recorded every single step. Its a little surreal.The game could use some longer puzzles or bigger areas to play with, but really enjoyed it and looking forward to any other installments.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: A lovely short puzzle game with fun and novel interactions. 5 hours to complete but I took my time and optimized some puzzles where I didn't need to advance the story. I hope there will be a sequel.Pros:* A fresh take on a factory puzzle game* Good use of VR as an interactive media* Lovely art style and audio design* Quality voice acting and writing* Runs well (VR physics ain't easy)Cons:* Heights. If you are acrophobic or just don't like heights the ending puzzles are very anxiety inducing. I nearly quit!* Ending puzzles are frustrating and some behaviors are not tutorialized* Some interactions don't make sense and break game rules.Bugs* Inaccurate physics interactions. In particular often the gardeners only successfully grab a handle 50% of the time. Exactly 50%.* Doesn't recenter correctly in Steam VR. Game always started me facing backwards and wouldn't recenter.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really unique vr game. For the most part vr puzzle games haven’t really appealed to me but this one really utilises the benefits of vr to make a really interesting game.The basic concept is that you need to pick fruit and get it to a shoot on the other side of a room. This gets more complex with fruits that explode when you hold them for too long or ones that float. Then later you have to combine them together too. To get them around though you have to press record and act out an action. When the recording finishes a clone of you will repeat the action forever. This allows you to have these clones create conveyors all doing different actions to achieve your goal.In addition to this unique cloning aspect, the puzzles are varied. They can be difficult but I never found them frustrating. You have the option to just solve a room or there’s also an optimisation goal where you use less than a set number of clones and produce at least a certain amount of fruit per minute. These can be a lot more challenging but are also fun to figure out.I did have a few small issues. When I was in a position I wasn’t supposed to be, like in a wall, the whole screen would go black. This happens in a lot of vr games and usually you just move your head back and you are okay. In this game, I found that I’d have to walk around the room for a few minutes before it worked again very occasionally. I was playing using a wireless link from the quest 2 so this may not be the same for people who don’t do that. Also, you could beat the optimisation problems by stockpiling up a load of fruit next to the shoot and repeatedly throwing it in until it said you’d beat it. These two issues are very minor though and shouldn’t put you off playing it.All in all, an incredible vr puzzle game. I’d highly recommend it even to people who don’t usually like vr puzzle games. The game is engaging, has fun puzzles and is just the right length for what it has to offer.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: I can see why this was voted as Meta's best VR game of 2022. It's a short and sweet puzzle automation game that really takes advantage of it being in VR - you wouldn't be able to play this on a flat screen. Figuring out the best way to automate every fruit farm feels great and I really couldn't think of any downtime in this game. There's a decent story here too, not groundbreaking by any means but it added to the great experience that I was already having. The music is lovely, the visuals are nice, and the game doesn't overstay its welcome (it takes ~10 hours to 100%).Overall, totally worth buying, even at full price. So what are you waiting for?!
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: It's like a zachtronics game meets a puppet show??  You have to do optimization puzzles by recording copies of yourself in the room, until they all play out all the necessary steps, in sync with each other...It can be a lot of fun coming up with optimized solutions, though honestly, there are a couple of things I should warn if you're looking forward to that:1) it gets almost cheatingly easier if you have a big enough playspace (you can't teleport while recording, but there's no radius limit on walking around in *real life*, so being able to walk from point A to point B during a recording can spare you from having to throw the item to a second copy -- the number of copies used is one of the toughest optimization criteria)2) the most optimal solutions often involve throwing an item really far across the room, which typically just means a boring amount of recording attempts until one of them happens to successfully land in the target...  it's one thing to re-record until you nail a complex interaction, but re-recording until you happen to nail a three-pointer just gets dull...Of course, the game never *requires* you to do either of these things -- but if you were specifically going in hoping to pull off clever optimizations, just bear in mind that that aspect of the experience isn't quite what you might hope it to be...  but there's still a lot of fun to be had here, learning and experimenting and theorizing.  And I wound up getting into optimizing even with those caveats!
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: This one was a pleasant surprise to find in the VR store list! The music is phenomenal, the voice acting felt natural and well written, and the art direction is excellent.The puzzles weren't too tough to solve (I never felt like I had to look something up), and I kind of wished there were more complicated "lab" challenges, but that's okay. This is a game about automation, you can pass each level with fairly basic designs, though the game offers challenges that encourages the player to maximize efficiency. It's an elegant way to engage with the automation/puzzle mechanics to whatever degree the player wants, and doesn't shame the player for how they want to play.I had some issues with my Index grips being too sensitive, and grabbing/holding things when I mean to throw them. It became kind of annoying. You can manually turn that off in the Index settings menu, which I would recommend, and just rely on the trigger button for grabbing things. This is a pretty common issue in most VR games and is by no means unique to The Last Clockwinder, so I definitely wouldn't begrudge them for the Index being sensitive. Again, this can easily be fixed in the index settings. All in all, I would highly recommend. One of my favorite VR purchases to date!
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: A very fun and super satisfying problem solving game where your athletics and brain are both needed in order to achieve maximum efficiency. I find myself playing until I hit all of the efficiency goals in the level and have been having a blast. It is very fun to see versions of yourself running and throwing things around to accomplish tasks of varying complexity.Solid sound track, controls, voice acting, and art style. One of the most creative uses of VR I have been able to play.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: The Last Clockwinder is such a special game in my heart because this game reminds me of those "clone yourself" flash game puzzles I used to play when I was a kid. Except in this one I get to whip and nae nae. The puzzles are super interesting and forces you to think in a space where the only moves you can do are basic movements in real life. The simplicity of everything makes everything super clear to understand and so fun to mess around in. I find myself not even going for efficiency and just making really elaborate machines that involve me doing trick shots with myself.The art is beautiful and blends super well together. It genuinely feels like I'm being placed this comfy small space that I can sit down and vibe in. The amount of care that's put in with the small details of each room and each section of this game is fantastic. The music being reactive to how many clones you have really gives you a sense of scale and complexity and it becomes more and more beautiful.The story is so adorable with a character having a reflection of their time there. The voice actors do an AMAZING job as well.This game is super charming and so innovative for VR and it's one of the few VR games in a long time that have caught my attention I am so happy for this game finally being release. Congrats Pontoco!
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: This is an absolutely amazing game, It has amazing mechanics, visuals, and story. The cloning mechanic was done amazingly with you being able to use different timers for different clones to make things as fast and efficent as possible, the only bug I encountured with it is that with alot of clones in one area you will have to look at them to make them work as intended. The puzzles were done nicely slowy increasing the difficulty and having a satisfying end result. The visuals were done nicley, it had a steampunk mythical kinda theme that was implemented amazingly. Lastly the story is amazing, it was heart touching and had a satisfying ending. The game is around 4 hours to complete but you can go back and try to make everything at maxium efficency if you are an achievement hunter. I would rate this game 10/10.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: This is an early review but loving it so far. Not entirely sure how much content there is but the puzzles are interesting and it seems good depending on full length of the game im concerned about content as I have reached plant 3 out of 5 seeds slots. Will look at updating review once finished but so far loving it. Concept is very interesting and enjoyable. Exited to see where this leads.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: A great game with a very solid core, utilizing the strengths of VR with good physics and plenty of throwing action, while still providing a decent, if not difficult challenge in how to solve and especially optimize the puzzles it provides. The characters are like-able and relatable flawed. The environment and interaction visuals are pleasant to look at and the music adjusts dynamically based on what is happening. The weakest point are the short completion time (Roughly 5 hours completion for me) and the lack of more difficult content for those who want to invest more. On a last highpoint, game does not prevent you from mucking about with the mechanic, experimenting different ways to exploit and have fun with it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: Very cool concept thats executed well.  Finding the most efficient way to automate a room is really satisfying, especially when you manage to pull tricky stuff like passing a fruit *back* to a previous recording.  Even just the little robot guys you make are fun to goof around with.  Dancing when you have some downtime between loops, or even just creating clones for the heck of it.  Its a very cool mechanic and I think they got alot out of it with the puzzles.The story was really touching too.  You communicate with a ship captain who brought you to the tree, and find old tapes of your character talking with Edea "the clockwinder."  I wont give much anyway but it was very touching, especially with the ending.  The biggest issue I would say comes with the recordings sometimes 'glitching' when you close the game down and come back.  I've returned to rooms I've completed in last play sessions and the recordings are suddenly desynced, ruining the automation.  Luckily you dont usually have reason to go back to previous rooms since it just calculates the rate of fruit you harvested, but I feel like just returning to a previous room would be enough to change that calculation, so you'd have to fix it.  I assume this is just cause VR is tricky to program and this didnt happen with EVERY SINGLE ROOM or anything; most still worked fine.  .  There will also be times when you record something and it goes perfect, but then the gardener ends up not grabbing something or not throwing the thing the same way you did, but that can just be chopped up to how it was recorded.  Annoying, but thats 100% on you.Highly recommended if you have a VR headset.  Its a must buy as far as im concerned
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: Easily the best VR game I've played. Such a simple premise executed flawlessly and with so much style. The environments are gorgeous the writing and designs are adorable and the gameplay perfectly delivers a feeling I've imagined since I was five years old. Stands head and shoulders above any competition for VR puzzlers.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: DOES NOT SUPPORT VIRTUAL DESKTOP!! Quest 2 controllers don't work in VD with this game so you are forced to use inferior Air Link with washed out muted colors and insane aliasing even at max resolution. if you tried VD it wont work in Air Link unless you Delete the Save file from within the game (click new game and then delete save). it's perplexing they don't support Virtual Desktop since probably 90% of us on Steam use VD with the Q2.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: Nice game concept with looping riddles.Difficulty ★★☆☆☆☆☆☆☆☆ * I like the artstyle and the atmosphere* looping riddles are pretty nice* every loop will work, whatever crazy thing you do - so creativity pays off* challenge board available to make you solve riddles more effectively* their seems to be a rare chance that you can softlock yourself by despawning critical story / riddle items* if you set the game to smooth walking you cannot leave the balcony when you start the game (switch temperarily back to telpeortation)* game is too shortIt is a nice little riddle game to kill some time and it has a high potential to add more crazy stuff to it.I accidentally softlocked myself by perma-despawning some of my critical seeds to produce things and the auto-save function kicked already in. The devs are alreeady aware about the issue and try to build in additional safety mechanism that this kind of issue will not happen again anytime soon. Big kudos from my side.Unfortunetally I already refunded the game due to less of 2 hours playtime, but I will consider returning at some point again when I feel in the mood again to do so. It seems that this bug was a one in a thousand situation that usually does not happen. So I can still recommend this game for people interested in an unique VR riddle game :)
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: This game was a delight. It ran flawlessly.It's well-designed (except ladders, and sometimes getting stuck on things, but it resets you to a safe place nearby).It's clever, warm, comfortable to play, feels deeply cosy and is satisfying, while leaving plenty of room for creative problem-solving and feeling like you're solving problems in a way somewhat unique to you.Don't wait as long as I did to play this, it's wonderful.If I have a criticism, it's that the game is short. This is much better than being too long, but I did still want more come the end.Have fun =)
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder
