_childDocuments_.review: A super fun factory optimization puzzle game, but only in VR can you high-five your past self to celebrate, or throw a knife across the room to cut a plant and then strike a ninja pose ... all for your actions to be recorded and played back so you can see how awesome you are.Took me nine hours to beat the game, a further four to master all the puzzles and get all the achievements. Well, except for the piano one ...
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: I don't think I've ever written a review for a game on Steam before.This game is short and very sweet, though. This game's mechanics are a perfect fit for VR, and the story is very well done. I'm going to be thinking about this game for a very long time, and recommending it to my friends longer still.Bravo.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: Exremely frustrating simulator of precise throwing.When I first saw this game I expected some logical puzzle game that would test my skills in optimizing production chains, not unlike Factorio, or Satisfactory. Something where the your task is to plan a series of short manual actions and merge them into something greater.Meanwhile, 80-90% of this game is just repeatedly throwing stuff and hoping that this time it will go to the right place. Between VR's latency that's around 30-90ms and the fact that throws are calculated based on position of controllers, not our hands, aiming your throws is really hard. I would often plan the steps pretty quickly, then spend dozens of minutes just trying to make sure the fruits and gems go where I want them to. The game pairs very poorly with sitting, small real life spaces, and poorly with playing wired. The amount of moving required is surprisingly high, as you try to extend around in order to achieve as much as possible in your loops.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, I am legit in love with this game.  I bought a copy on the quest store as well and switched to that so I can play without airlink. I have now played through the game 4 times (a 100% run and a couple of any% speed runs).  The gameplay is both relaxing and frustrating, as a good puzzle should be.  The art style and mechanic of the "floor switching" is well doen to keep you immersed.Original Review:  This is a love letter to VR.  Only played 1.1 hrs so far cuz my battery died
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: I do not understand why this game has such a high rating. It is extremely repetitive. Throwing things in VR is not a great experience ever, I'm a very careful player, but still managed to bump TV a bit (no damage).You can walk while recording a clone sequence (it is not possible to teleport or walk using joystick while recording), meaning that having a huge open space is very beneficial, or you can try to throw things, both are frustrating, because timings are extremely tight.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: easily one of the best vr gamesthe only things that are not perfect in this game are1. the ui looks like the default unity ui2. no full body3. not enough(maybe add a sandbox for replayablility)4. the piano doesent perfectly replay when making a clone play it(and is a bit buggy in total)thats it! i didnt encounter anything else unlike other games...
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I liked this game! It can be fun at first, but it's quite buggy and feels really half-baked.- When I cam back to the game for a second session my saves loaded with all the robots starting their cycles at the wrong time. Maybe broken by an update?- The physics is not fully deterministic, which it really should be for a game like this.- Interactions in general are more fiddly than they should be. Throwing objects is less consistent compared to other VR games, the colliders on the hands are large and don't match their visual model, and the hands have no physics of their own (I'm guess they're probably kinematic bodies that are exactly tracking the hand pose?) which leads to objects glitching out when you try to touch them with both hands or push them into static geometry, and it makes pushing objects feel weightless and inconsistent. This is especially bad with the luftapples in later levels. Overall it means you spend a lot of time repeatedly re-recording actions that should be easy. With better physics, I can imagine interacting with the luftapples could be fun, but it just sucks.- The framerate drops more than it should when looking towards the main play area, even with nothing going on.- The levels are frankly too similar, so it quickly gets boring doing more or less the same kinds of solutions several times, especially with the aforementioned jank that makes recording solutions take longer than it should.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: Appreciated the solarpunk aesthetic and themes.I found this game to be a simplified version of Transpose. While Clockwinder had better graphics and an actual story that Transpose lacked, Transpose had more depth, creative perspectives, and had more challenging puzzles. I went 'not recommend' here because I didn't particularly care for this game - I didn't find it engaging and puzzle were too easy. But I do recognize quality puzzle design here. The Clockwinder puzzles have intuitive rules, allows the player to design solutions, and watching your own design-solution is part of the reward. I love the cloning mechanic as it expands your perspective to consider the time element, not just space. Despite Steam only recording 83 minutes played and not triggering any Steam achievements, I did finish the game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like it, but throwing things around gets really annoying really fast.Current VR control just dosnt offer enough feedback for weight and velocity to be able to throw things perfectly accurately, so most puzzles are 10x harder than they should be, so you end up repeating the same thing 100 times, failing a throw by 5 cm, getting more and more frustrated, so any enjoyment gets killed by any hard puzzle even if you know how to solve it.Also Medicine 2 puzzle alone would make me subtract few stars from any rating, the wonky physics arent accurate enough for entire room throws and object interactions.Other than that it would be a fun VR game even with its mobile Quest2 graphics.Still, the controls would need a complete redesign for me to recommend this game to anybody, it needs some alternative throwing method to be an enjoyable experience.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: Really nice game story and visuals wise, but calling it puzzle game is tall order - it's way more precision throwing on timer thing than puzzle solving... if anything this is physical exercise if you want to get all achievements.In my opinion it's 7.5/10, but for 8 or 9 out of 10 it would need some more variation in game play - though plants have various mechanics, precision throwing on timer is all you really do.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I could give this a positive review however there is a soft-lock that make me unable to recommend this game to anyone that is playing with meta quest link as the room selector has a 50% chance of not appearing and if you ever make a mistake and let go of it while it is not on a room. for this reason I have refunded and cannot recommend this game to anyone that is using a Meta Quest headset and it also apparently effects people using Pico headsets.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: This is not a good VR experience.The game is about throwing things to solve puzzles. Yet the throwing physics don't work well (Most VR games get throwing wrong though, here is a video explaining the core issue: . It's very clear if you compare the throwing feel in Half Life Alyx to this game, but it's particularly awful for a game that relies so heavily on throwing things. In terms of accessibility, the game also leaves a lot to be desire, for instance, it severely lacks good left handed support.The robots and environments are cute though.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: It's a well made game with few bugs and average performance but honestly fails to deliver an interesting experience. It is utterly barebones and very clean, to the point that it's two steps from being a game for children. In a single word, it is boring. I genuinely have no significant memories of the 6 hours I played and have no reason to touch the game again.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game, even after only 30 minutes in the clock tower, it begins to feel like your home, and once you understand the base mechanics you can get a true production line going, you don't even need to progress in the story you can just chill and watch your cute little droid pals amass vast amounts of plants in a synchronized dance orchestrated by you in your quest to find the last clock-winder
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game!It's just that it can't be played with Virtual Desktop, when doing so the record button never registers. I'll update my review to positive once Virtual Desktop is supported.Additionally smooth locomotion could be supported but not necessary.Devs posted a workaround for VD users, I change my rating back to positive, thanks!
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: I thought this was an automation game.IT IS NOT AN AUTOMATION GAME.It is playing catch with yourself the game.You are basically back in gym class with the teacher screaming at you to try again to throw the ball to your classmate after you have failed for the 100th time and you are simultaneously the gym teacher you and your friend at the same time and everything is super frustrating.So unless you are some super athlete with great ball handling I would give this a pass.Oh also you need a future not invented vr headset with perfect hand tracking to make the throws not a matter of chance.Also needs a huge space, I managed to destroy my ceiling lamp with this.Story was cute and heartwarming though, but not enough for me to ever play this again.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: This is probably one of my favorite VR games that I've played. It's game play is pretty straight-forward and the story is sweet but not super deep. Despite this however the game feels very well put together and consistently challenges you to make better and better contraptions with your clones. The game took me about 5 hours on my first play through and while that is a little short it feels very meaty compared to the other VR games on the market. I played through it a second time because I found it to be that good. In the end, The Last Clockwinder is a good, short VR game that won't leave you wanting or disappointed. If it looks like a game you would enjoy, you likely will enjoy playing it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: Overall thumbs up. Cute story, great visuals, and wonderful voice acting to drive the short tale. The game play loop is interesting and solving the puzzles is satisfying and open ended. Sometimes the clones don't do exactly what you record yourself doing which can lead to you thinking something is working only having to go back and re-do it. This doesn't break the game by any means. However, completionists beware, this can make getting some of the more difficult achievements much more frustrating. It took me about 5 hours to complete. I got it on sale and I'd say it was worth the sale price. Regulrar price may be too high for some. Your call.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: What an amazing game! The Last Clockwinder combines the system-design puzzling of a game like Factorio with the precise, complex body movements only feasible with VR, a simple yet powerful story, and likable, well-acted characters, all within a whimsical, mysterious setting.My 8-year-old and I had tons of fun beating this game together.. we didn't want it to end! Kudos to Pontoco for creating this innovative, well-rounded game. I can't wait to see what they come up with next!
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very unique VR experience and I enjoyed it very much.There are a few issues I should mention though. First of all, turning. Most levels are roughly grid based, meaning that snap turn, which is on by default, works great. However, the level change console in the corner turns you to face it, which means you are now off grid. In practice this can be mitigated by turning on smooth turning, but it is something you should be aware of.The other, much bigger issue is inconsistent physics. I saw a bit of this with the water droplets and a lot with luft apples. The variance might not be much, but you don't need much for the clones to mess up. Doesn't matter much for casual play, but to reach the production challenges it is rather annoying.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: I don't say this often but in the best possible way, there were parts of this game that made me feel like a kid again in how strangeness would turn to wonder. Specifically there was a puzzle where you have to make a floating plant get weighed down and as I saw it coming towards me, I just was completely immersed, in the 'I momentarily forgot I was playing a game' kind of sense. The only critique, I think the main game is the right amount of length, it does have replayability if you want to be obsessed with optimizing your sequences, but I would like a New Game+ mode where it would be the same exact game but just with WAY HARDER puzzles, give people like me something to chew on. Other than that, I mean, come on, a game that is played using motion capture? It really makes me feel like I'm living in the future. This would've been borderline unthinkable ten years ago.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: What a wonderfully wholesome, cute and relaxing puzzle experience with nice characters and just the right amount of good story to immerse you in this little world of mechanized tree-gardens.I would so, so love it if they would expand on this idea, because there is a lot that still could be done with it in a sequel. IF there is anything "bad" about this game, then that it is rather short. That also has its upsides - for example the fact, that every room, every puzzle feels unique and fresh. There is little to no repetition - but repetition would have been perfectly fine, because I was really enjoying my time there planting fruits and instructing my gardener robots.This game never pushed it's envelope and simply tried, and succeeded(!!!) to provide a wholesome, fun puzzle experience with great visuals.Really wish the game was "bigger". But what is there... is absolutely great. 10/10 fun experience! (And it is cheap. Really got my moneys worth here. No regrets.)
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: In short if you like artsy, puzzle, automation, VR games and a nice little story you will love this game. The long version.The art style is quite nice and easy on the eyes and quite colorful unlike most VR games and combination of puzzle automation and VR works really well together. The story is relatively short and simple but it's quite nice and fits the theme very well. It only took me about 4 hours to finish the game but that being said most of my solutions were very inefficient and there is replayability and going back and optimizing. For $25 I'm not disappointed I've spent more going to movies that being said if you can get it on a sale even better. Games like this make me optimistic with the future of VR and I do hope more games of a similar nature come out. And remember vote with your wallet
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderful game with an interesting little story, cozy atmosphere and unique puzzle mechanic that makes you feel... very accomplished? Best word i can think of right now. You'll stand there looking back at your solved puzzle room and say to yourself: "Damn i'm good :D". Good length to it where it doesnt overstay its welcome and introduces new aspects to the puzzles at a good pace. Finished the whole thing in about 4 hour-long play sessions.NOTE: Played via Virtual Desktop which for some reason doesnt seem to have registered playtime on steam or achievements... Weird.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best VR games. Very creative idea. Do you like automation like Satisfactory. Then play this game. It's about automation, but instead of machines, you are creating recordings of yourself that repeat the action over and over endlessly and you must create a production line out of these clones. If you just want to beat the game, then it can be done very quickly, but if you like to optimize, then you'll spend a lot of time. Mainly because not only do you need logical thinking of how to make something, you also need to be agile enough to pull of the action that you came up with. But you can try endlessly and once you get it right, then just keep that clone and it will keep repeating endlessly.My only complaint is that how short this felt. Well, not that it's short in a bad way, but just it's so amazing that I want MORE! I hope the devs continue with this idea.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: while a bit on the shorter side of games, the last clockwinder has to be one of the most fun vr puzzle games I have played so far. Story and voiceacting are great, the graphics are charming and the game mechanic is very unique and an absolut blast to play. Absolutely woth its price, even if not on a sale!
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: The Last Clockwinder’s core mechanic is one of the most unique uses of VR in any game, taking full advantage of the medium. The game uses this mechanic in its excellent time-management puzzles in repeatedly interesting ways, creating an incredibly engaging experience. And set with charming visuals and a nicely intertwined narrative, the game is simply delightful and basically perfect.I do think the throughput goals should be mandatory though, as going for them created an incredibly satisfying challenge. As they are not, I will strongly recommend all players go for their associated achievements.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: Loved this game. Nice story, beautiful aesthetic and design, and the puzzle mechanics utilize VR in a very unique and satisfying way. The only con was that the game doesn't support cloud saves. I lost a few hours of progress because I didn't realize this before I decided to rebuild my PC. It's not a big deal since it's a short experience, but just be aware.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: This game is probably the best game I've ever played in VR and I'm less than two hours in. I very rarely review games and I don't think I've ever reviewed a game so quickly.I love automation games where you can tweak the efficiency to work perfectly. Satisfactory, Automachef and, more recently, Techtonica have scratched that itch. This game is more organic in how it manages it and is on much less grand a scale but it is no less satisfying when you get there.I was initially worried it would be a 'complete a level, move on' linear type thing, but I am thrilled to report I was wrong!Your previous levels continue producing the resource as you progress, and you can go back with new gear and tweak the efficiency even further!The game does a lot of 'show, don't tell' and I honestly love that. The controls are simple to get the hang of and intuitive, the aesthetic is adorable. I played until my headset ran out of battery and I cannot wait to play it again once it's charged.Hats off to you, devs. This game is excellent.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: Maximise efficiency through trick-shots! I was left with my elbow sore from trying to streamline the process of harvesting fruit by throwing them as far as I could across the room... Nevertheless, the aching arm didn't deter me from wanting to play more. This is a beautiful, fun, and challenging game with very unique mechanics which pair excellently with VR. I found myself wanting to explore every spot of each area and listen to each piece of the story which was nice and interesting. I can say without a doubt this was one of my favourite VR games to play. Short and sweet.I also made the gardeners do rude gestures so bonus points.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most rewarding VR experiences I have ever played. I really enjoyed the mechanics off the game. It were a great 5 hours.  The puzzles had a nice increase in difficulty. It was never to difficult to win the level. Maxing out each puzzle was also a blast. This will be a game I will keep recommending to everyone with a VR for years to come. Also amazing story and voice acting!
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: odd game, not my usual type, but fun. kinda relaxing, not too sure what to think of it. less than 2 hours in at time of posing and i am invested in the story being told here, i want to keep playing. but alas, my headset needs to recharge. honestly i am looking forward to the puzzles i have yet to face. definitely worth the 14.99 i paid on sale, and (probably) worth the 24.99 standard but too soon to tell.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: Basically the title. I love the puzzles and automation, definitely tests my hand-eye coordination. My only gripe so far has been that the game doesn't seem to respect your physical space very well. I find myself having to reorient to my play area quite often, because I will be turning weirdly to set up an automation, or the worst offender: Teleporting to the room selector console, which turns me to face the console, often a 180 degree turn.Basically, it's a lot of fun, I'm just tired of knocking into things in my living room. Still recommended though!
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: 8/10 - Greatthe Good,Good puzzles, hard to completely finish, but it's only an option to do so.Nice visuals and music but what makes this game even better is the excellent story & voice acting.the Bad,About 5 hrs to finish the game.Wish it had longer story to progress, Rather then useless achievements, gimmicks to lengthen the game time.the Ugly,Using Meta Quest 2 & Quest 3 to play, 1) via Virtual Desktop Streamer, the game play time & steam achievement doesn't work, but plays fine in 120 fps.2) via Steam Link, the play time & achievement works, shows 120fps on PC screen, but VR fps on Quest is way Low (30fps). ...Overall, A Must try VR game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: An absolutely amazing VR game, most VR games are more similar to tech demos, The Last Clockwinder feels much more like an actual game that doesn't rely on a gimmick of VR to be fun.It's a great puzzle game that controls super well, the story that you unlock as you go is wonderful, and everything feels super smooth and polished.I just wish it was longer, I completed the game while 100%ing the achievements in just 6 hours, I wish it wasn't over.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely fun! I've never seen this sort of mechanic in other VR games (though I'm sure there's some out there).The story is interesting and easy to follow along with since it's fully voiced and you can complete other activities while listening to dialogue. I can't seem to get into a story if it's just words after words after words and all you can do is listen. This game doesn't make you sit there while you listen; you can continue on with your exploration while the story plays in the background. Honestly, more games should do that.But back to the gameplay, the concept of making clones that mimic your movements to create an automated system is super fun. My boyfriend and I just sat and watched the little guys throw things to each other for a good five minutes.In only my second play session, I've almost completely changed my mind about this game. Don't get me wrong, it's very well-made and fun. But I discovered a bug that disrupted the main mechanic so much that I couldn't bare to play it anymore. This bug, however it was triggered, would make some of my throws, catches, or sticking fruits together completely miss and make a whole cycle useless. It got to the point where it would be perfect for the first few, then never again.For a game that's all about consistency and looping, this inability to keep consistent physics makes it incredibly difficult to enjoy this game. I don't know if this is a one-time thing or a consistent bug, but I'm personally not going to be playing this game for a while. I'm keeping my review as recommended still, since it's a great game and I had a wonderful time in my first session. Hopefully the next time I play, I can verify whether or not the bug is a consistent issue or not.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: Basically a Factorio-light in VR. Unique in its gameplay and pleasantly short. A fantastic puzzler that forces you to become more efficient (and better at throwing).I can't recommend the Steam Index controllers, as they are very imprecise in grip controls.Also I was unfortunate to have multiple almost game breaking bugs, but I saw nobody else have similar issues.It speaks to the game that I can still highly recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game that understands how to incorporate VR mechanics into the puzzle-automation genre. The game didn't force me to optimise the fruit production process too excessively, but the challenges provided enough flexibility for me to experiment and work out a solution that always felt satisfying to accomplish.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: A game which I thought would not be too interesting from the trailers became incredibly addicting and an extremely fun game to play! There is one small simple thing which makes this game great and it is the challenges section on each puzzle. Without those challenges this game would be a walk in the park and it is fun to be able to choose your own difficulty. All the puzzles were very rewarding to complete and aim for the top challenge goal, although the final two were too difficult for me to complete. Overall it is an easy recommendation and a super fun experience!
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: I think this is a good game. I like the audio logs giving context for the story, they sound good. The way you automate stuff is engaging and it feels good to "solve" a room's puzzle.However, I did not realize quite how much throwing there would be which IS entirely my fault, but it's exhausting and I needed to redo some throws dozens of times because you do need to be pretty accurate to achieve certain goals. You can realistically likely use as many robots as you want but I really wanted to achieve those goals for using under a certain amount for a room.I know it's not the most descriptive review, but I do recommend it. Just be prepared for a lot of throwing and physical activity. As of writing this review I have only played an hour and a half so I don't know how long the game is, but trying to achieve the goals I mentioned would likely extend the playtime by a good amount.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: The concept of this game is brilliant, and it captivated me the moment I saw the trailer in my feed.I loved how such a foreign and absurd idea was perfectly implemented in a believable world and story, both of which I quickly fell in love with.It was annoying how, when I reloaded the  room, 1 clone wasn't doing the same things anymore, breaking the "assembly line"
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: It starts off good with clear understanding of what you need to do to progress. It is just getting positioning and throwing items to correct places which can take a while to get right. Then the game progresses to a 2nd set of areas and beyond all have broken demonstrations showing nothing of importance. I had several time no clue what I was supposed to do and had to watch playthrough videos to find out what I needed to do, this really needs to be improved upon. Also the game is missing a clear indication of where to put those 3 unblocking capsules you make and when I saw a video of where to put them that makes no sense as thats not where the blockage is.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: At first i was questioning if it was worth the money but it truly was a fun an interesting game there is about 3.5-5 hours of game play now the story is interesting and fun, but is it worth 24.99 not really(GET IT WHILE ITS ON SALE) however if you want to kill some time in an immersive engineering type game this is it:)
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: Having done what seems to be about a fifth of the game so far, I am loving it. Sure, you need to re-record a bunch of times for perfect movement, but the game never punishes you for not being perfect, and you can always just add another clone. I would absolutely love to see a game like this with more intricate automation, like the Create mod for minecraft. But this is still a fantastic game so far.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: + It's a surprisingly simple concept, but somehow felt amazing and engaging.+ Mechanics such as time looping drones repeating recorded actions are not new but not often used in games so it feels new or unique combined with...- Having to move around and deal with physics objects can sometimes be infuriating if you repeat the same recording attempt over and over, but... + Regardless it feels fun and satisfying when you get a good assembly line going.TL;DR: This game is basically role-playing the inserters from Factorio but with physics xDEdit 1: I haven't beaten the game yet, I'm progressing slowly with small sessions due to VR eye strain hangover
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: This is an absolutely great and, even more so, unique VR-Game. The Gameplay Mechanics are one of its Kind and i dont think there is another Game thats coming close. The Feeling is great, Visuals are pretty nice, Voiceplay is good, and i havent came across a single Bug.Overall a great Experience, and even if im no begginer, i think this is very very beginner friendly Game to get People into VR.The only Thing that bothers me about this otherwise great Game, is the length.I´ve completed the main story in about 3,5 Hours. If you are a beginner in VR or even gaming in general, i think you will need about twice that long. (i gotta add i didnt go for maximum troughput in every Level, as im not that into min-maxing i just went for the minimum required amount to advance the story. If you max out every Level i think youre looking at about 6-7 Hours for an experienced player)If you see this Game in Sale, dont even hesitate to buy, if not on Sale it´s still a good Value in my OpinionI really hope the Dev´s will drop a Content Update or even a DLC for a few Bucks with more Levels, new Fruit and or mechanics.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: Great game!Minor things that I missed are a bit more realistic graphics and a more interactive game world: More things to pick up, look at etc. BUT:Other than that, this game is absolutely wonderful! The gameplay feels fresh and if you want to max the levels it gives you a nice challenge. The actions you record are captured perfectly and throwing things at your future self just doesn’t get old... This game is a catch!
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: Great game thus far, I am loving the story and the challenges of each area. 10/10 amazing puzzle game with a great story!Edit: Just finished the story of the game. I'm gonna change my score to a 15/10. This is a must play. Loved the story and watching the automation of the gardeners makes my ADHD go burrrrrtt. On the real, highly recommend and plan to play again!
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: I have played this game for 2 hours so far and will DEFINITELY update my review when I'm done, but first impressions having gotten through 4 rooms, this game is fantastic. The main puzzle mechanic is recording your movements and then using that to play basketball with yourself, using fruit as the balls. It is VERY active for a puzzle game, and it's a concept that only really works in VR. The way the music builds up as you create more clones to automate each room just adds on to the great feeling you get for solving a puzzle in the most efficient manner you can.Between the fun mechanics of the game, the charming story, and the wonderful voice acting, this is one of the best VR titles I've played. One thing I'd like to single out is that the player character has both an androgynous name and voice - something I'm never too bothered about in flat screen games, but when in VR the androgyny makes it far more comfortable and immersive for me to step into that role.I got this game for $15, but I easily would've felt like it was worth my money at full price.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: Nice puzzle game, loved the automation concept. The last puzzle(whale p.2) didn't really read great to me, but other than that it was great. Took ~5 hours to play through the story, but would've been longer if you take the time to hit all the optimization goals(did on a couple I felt were really cool).
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: This is honestly the most engaged I've been with a VR game in a long time. The mechanics are so simple and yet so clever. In the beginning it is mainly about nailing the obvious solution, but later levels will really make you think about the most efficient way to solve them. The music is fantastic, too. The story is a bit underdeveloped, but heartfelt.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: "How could I forget Silgar!(...) Oh! I saw a bit of fruit earlier that kinda looked like him."- Quite a masterpiece in department of task automation in VR. You record your own moves for clones that do the job.- Very nice art with a bit of mobile quality, but for me it goes as stylized.- Narrative is the strongest part with fabulous voice acting and dialogue. It just lives its own life. Quite warm story.- Perfect classical soundtrack.- There are some higher bars of productivity, quite challenging, so there is replayability.- On a few occasions, some small errors/inaccuracies happens with your recorded moves, especially with lighter elements falling (sometimes after you revisit the room)- First playthrough took me 6h, with some maxing out (2/3 of achievements)Generally very enjoyable and highly recommended, 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: Cozy environment with pretty lighting and very pleasant atmosphere overall. You record your steps, then sit down and watch your clones work in perfect sync. Flawless so far.The game is quite short and simple though: first playthrough took me only 5 hours and that's because I was taking a lot of time on improving the rooms and did not immediately figure out how you're supposed to solve the last task. For the full price I'd expect more content/playtime and replayability.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: hi im a random dude who plays factorio, minecraft, COD warzone 2... this game was a total suprise. ive played other VR on my rift S and many have some cool visual or whatever, but this had a nice smooth gameplay loop that engaged me. this wasnt a large game, it could be a tech demo, but it was well rounded in its simple scope. its a nice VR game
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: An absolutely charming VR game with a unique means to solving puzzles. Well worth a try, plus it has an engaging storyline and good voice acting that really draws you in.It's worth taking the time to figure out the puzzles of each room, and the best way to optimise the various steps, but make sure you have enough room around you when recording each step, as it is far too easy to forget you have limited space due to the immersion!
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: Heartfelt little game about the impossible path to perfection - basically an assembly / factory game a la factorio where the automation comes from yourself. I'm dumb as hell and had to look up a walkthrough to know what to do at the very beginning (you have to press a switch that's heavily obscured) but the rest of the game is very freeform challenge-wise. Feel free to do as much or as little as you want, as long as you get the bare minimum production quota.It's great! Definitely something you can only do in VR.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed this game more than I thought I would. It's a great mix of challenge to your mind and body. You may think you have a solution in mind, but when it comes time to physically act it out in a timeframe then you run into problems that you didn't expect. And then you think of a new solution and try to implement that. The rules are so simple, and lead to such complex problem solving, that this is an easy recommendation.This is also a rare game that could not be done in regular gaming. Using your whole body is core to the experience. You have to solve 3D puzzles in a 3D space with your 3D body. If you like automation games at all, and enjoy the unique gameplay experiences that only VR can deliver, then definitely pick this up.It is a bit short for its price tag (I'm about 2/3 through at the time of writing) but it's up to you how to spend your money. I'd recommend spending at least some of it on this game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the best VR games I have seen so far. The pacing is just perfect and kept me hooked for several hours straight. It's just a lot of fun to create choreographies with lots of clones throwing items around to solve or optimize one problem.Also, the game's setting is just cozy with lots of nice details.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: Same review as just about everyone else: the central mechanic of this game is SUPER fun, very refreshing, and totally unique to VR. I enjoyed The Last Clockwinder all the way through. What’s funny is it’s near-impossible to explain the appeal to someone who hasn’t seen the game. (“So it’s a gardening game where you power a giant clock with fruit, but you have to use robots that record the way you move, and…”)To address the few negative reviews, I’ll touch on the only minor negatives:1) There’s a fair amount of tossing physics objects, so be careful about whacking hands and elbows in real life! (On the plus side though, you’ll definitely get some exercise.)2) I hit an occasional bug where one of the clones suddenly stopped reproducing its actions accurately. This was a bit frustrating because I had to redo key parts of the puzzle. However, the bug was rare enough (and the game short enough) that it wasn’t a big deal for me.Neither of those caveats spoiled my experience. I’d play a sequel or expansion in a heartbeat.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really fun game with a very chill atmosphere and an enticing story, I fully recommend playing this. i have completed the main game, but i still haven't figured out how to do all of the puzzles as efficient as possible, so there is still more than enough for me to do. And the stylised graphics are also just amazing, as is the sound and background music. This is a must have.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: It was honestly really fun! Seeing arrangements of your own movements come to life in perfectly repeating motions is quite satisfying, the story is pleasant, the graphics are alright for a Quest title, and I like that there's adaptive music depending on which stage you're on and how many clones are at work.Just one thing, I had to give up on the more late-game achievements because sometimes optimal puzzle solutions require extensive perfecting of rapid movements and that can make for some really exhausting puzzle-solving. I would've liked more puzzles centered around complexity rather than about acting fast and precise.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: This is my favorite VR game of all time (so far, anyway). Wonderful use of the medium, excellent sound design, super immersive world (that I would love to explore more of!), and some really fun puzzles.Oh, and the story was so touching it *literally* made me cry. Bonked myself in the headset trying to wipe my eyes.If you have a VR headset, you really owe it to yourself to give this one a try. Cannot recommend this enough.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: When you get down to it, "The Last Clockwinder" is a simple game with a simple concept: an automation puzzle game in VR. But what makes this stand out as one of my favorite VR games is how that simple concept was expanded upon to create unique puzzles, beautiful environments, and an engaging narrative. With you literally being all of the individual parts that create the assembly line, you have free reign to do whatever you're physically capable of in order to get the fruit to the goal, allowing for infinite possibilities and no one correct solution. My only real critique is a big bug I ran into while playing, which is the plug that moves you between rooms occasionally disappearing, though returning to the main menu and resuming the game fixed it. Overall, I had a blast exploring the Clock Tower and learning about Jules and Edea's story, and if you love automation games, I feel you will, too.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: I was hesitant to buy this; don't make my mistake! It's worth it!To me, the trailer looked a lot like A Fisherman's Tale, which didn't really blow me away. I thought this would be a slow story-driven game with various puzzles. Also, the trailer kind of chaotic & overwhelming; and while I understood the premise of recording my actions to make 'clones' of myself to carry out tasks, I was afraid it would be a tedious battle trying to avoid bugs of minutia.I'm happy to report it was not overwhelming or tedious in the least! The coding of the clones just works like, well, clockwork. I was quite surprised how easy it was to make clones and how everything just fits. It was very satisfying.As for the chaos, the game starts off at the perfect slow pace, and does a great job of easing you into, but without being boring/tedious. Typically with these kinds of games, I just go through once, but the satisfaction of setting up a little assembly line like this has more replayability value than I'd expected, especially since each level has various challenge (more production per minute and/or fewer clones) -- but really, the drive to go back and redo things is just for the joy of creating a efficient system.I was very surprised by how much I enjoyed this game, and it fits into my top 10 and I would say is a must-play for VR players. The clone assembly line mechanic is not one to miss!
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: In this game you record your movements and leave behind clones that you'll use to help yourself solve a series of puzzles. Looking down at a room full of my clones after a solve and marveling at my creation put a smile on my face every time. Especially because I kept making my clones dance at the end of every recording. I played through this with my wife and it was fun taking turns doing the rooms and watching how my wife's solution to problems differs from mine. The mechanics are intuitive and easy to understand. The puzzles are fairly open ended, allowing for some creative liberty in solving them. They also progress nicely and are often very satisfying once you put everything together. As a musician I also appreciated the rhythmic and musical quality to the game, especially in the dewshot room. I highly recommend you give this game a shot, one of my favorites!
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best VR games ever released. Such a fun and unique concept that makes me feel like I'm playing a Zachtronics game, with all the mindbending puzzles and off-the-wall solutions. I'd consider it a must-buy for anyone with a headest. Over Boneworks, over H3, even over Beat Saber. It's that good.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: A really fun game with a great atmosphere and cute story. Took about 5 hours to completely finish on top of seeing how far maximized I could get some of the throughput for some of the rooms (well beyond the listed amount for some rooms). A decent challenge in the last few levels and overall I had fun from start to finish.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: A relaxing game with very innovative VR gameplay and mechanics; the puzzles are more on the fun side and not too challenging. The art style is simple, soothing, and enchanting, the story lovely. The music ranges from great to hauntingly beautiful - I had to look up the composer (Joel Corelitz). Gameplay is smooth and well-polished. I look forward to more games from the developers.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing!! I legit haven't had this fun in a solo game in YEARS! It runs wonderfully on my oculus quest 2, the graphics are nice and cozy, the enviorment is great, love the way to switch rooms, and it's really fun!! I don't think im even halfway through yet but it's been great so far :)If you like; Nice graphics, playing at your own pace, puzzle solving, optimizing and working with yourself this is definetly reccomended! I mean you don't have to optimize but i like doing that, and this game lets me do that without pushing me to move forward. Oh and the robot clones are supper cute, it's weird to say since im the one doing the movement but the way they end up working togheter is adorable and brings me so much joy. Like a proud mom looking att her kids lol <3
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: an excellent game that makes really novel use of the VRmy only complaint is there's not enough of it. Its an automation game at the core but it really just doesn't built it up enough. there's no reward for improving efficiency since rooms don't effect each other and infinite seeds is pretty trivial to get with a bit of time.if it were more involved, like using 1 fruit to feed another make something to grow something else it'd be perfect.still a great game, just wish there was more to it
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: Addictive, yet not pushing you anywhere.Relaxing, but optionally thrilling (doing XYZ in a self-set timeframe can be a rush!)Happy and warm, but a tear almost dropped.Its a bit on the shorter side, I'm still missing 10 achievs and want to hunt them afterwards (EFFICIENCY++!!) but i feel like if the game was much longer, it'd be a drag. This way, every stage brings on new challenges, new way of thinking, every plant is a different kind of quirky and levels with combined plants later on will test your knowledge on each one! Only thing is i dont think you can play this in Oculus PCVR like some other games and only SteamVR runtime is supported (i feel like the first one has slightly better tracking)
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: Perfect example of a perfect VR game. Everything in this game is made for and can only work in VR. 10/10 recommend. Intriguing story, acceptable graphics, and great music. One minor con. Text becomes quickly unreadable from a slight distance, most likely some holdover from the quest version. Still, a minor issue, rest is pretty damn good.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: The Last Clockwinder is a beautiful, if short, VR puzzle game about the stewardship of nature, automation, and passing along the torch.Jules is a young woman who received a distress call from a place she once called home, a massive tree-machine called the Clock Tower.  When she arrives, the Clockwinder, the steward of the Clock Tower, is no where to be found.  The Clock Tower is sinking into the ocean world it was left.  You play as Jules as she moves from room to room in the Clock Tower, rediscovering her past with the Clockwinder, as well as repairing the great machine using Gardeners, simple robots that mimic her movements, to pick and move the fruit that powers the Clock Tower.These robots will mimic her (and by that, I mean your) movements exactly.  This means you can pick a fruit, and then lob it towards where it needs to go, and the gardener mimicking you will keep on lobbing fruit that direction.  If you're accurate enough to make it in, great!  The throwing feels much better than pretty much any other VR game I've played, but its still not amazing.  So you'll probably want another version of yourself to be there to field any wayward fruit.  It's like factorio meets basket ball.Each of the 5 fruit all require different means of harvesting.  Some need to be cut off the vine, some are shot out of a slingshot, and some float away at the merest touch.  The harvest levels tend to be simple affairs, just about maximizing how much fruit goes into the goal, with as few gardeners as possible.  The Laboratory levels are trickier, and these levels are required to make new seeds for your harvesting levels.  The labs find you making simple "molecules" of different kinds of fruit.  Figuring out the best way to stick together fruit is a fun business, and being especially efficient will allow you to pick up infinite seed bags.I wouldn't have minded the game going on a few more levels, though only if they found new and more interesting fruit.  The five in the game are more than good enough for me to recommend it.  It somehow scratches that Zachtronics itch of trying to make the machine more efficient by just a tiny bit more, while still being a very open ended VR game.  You are the machine, so how efficient you are is only limited by your patience and skill in getting a perfect throw here, or moving your arms quick enough to put the molecules together.This being a VR title, some weirdness with geometry was expected, and encountered.  Some ledges felt difficult to get over with the sliding controls (as opposed to teleportation).  Some times when moving exceptionally quick, fruit would behave unexpectedly, or the knife would fail to cut stems.  It's understandable, and you lose at most 4 seconds of attempting to make a proper loop.My rig played the game without jitter, freeze, or slowdown.  I'm not running top of the line gear, so I imagine most VR setups should handle it just fine.  The style is the pseudo-cartoony rendering that is common in indie 3d titles, but each model you can find was very lovingly designed, the robots are charming, and the fruit wobble satisfyingly.  I wish there were more interactable toys around the rooms without puzzles, but there was only one room like that that I can recall.It's the only real thing I was disappointed in: the music room.  It's a side room, where you can use looping robots to play a 4 second jingle on a piano and harp.  However, the game only seems to have 3 or 4 sound channels for these sounds, so if you have more than that, they get glitchy and cut out.  It's a very minor gripe, but I went from extremely excited by the possibilities to mildly disappointed in the realities.I really do recommend The Last Clockwinder to puzzle fans looking to try something fresh and interesting in VR.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic game!Really interesting mechanics that are very well implemented (at least with an Index controller it is really astonishing how a game based on physics and vr motion can be this precise).It also helps that the game never demands this precision (outside of achievements) so it can only get frustrating if you let it (because you are just absolutely sure that you could do it a little bit more efficient with a perfectly timed throw across the whole room!).Besides this the puzzles are interesting, the setting is really refreshing, even the story is pretty nice for a puzzle game and the presentation is also very well done.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: I usually like automation games but this takes it in a direction I never imagined. You're basically automating processes by recording your movements and having robot clones carry them out. It is an uncanny sensation to watch tens of your own clones undertake actions you yourself invented moments prior. Such a clever and beautiful game and something that really flexes VR as a medium. 10/10 buy it right now.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun little game! I'd actually played another game called The Under Presents that had a similar time-clone minigame in it, and always wanted to see someone make a game entirely around this mechanic!The story and environment are beautiful as well! Finally, I really liked the way you switch between rooms in the tree, the interactive switchboard-like globe is really fun to use!Overall a fun and innovative VR game, would definitely recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: this is now my all time favorite vr game, i just wish there was more to do, please developers add more content bc im addicted to this gameplay, in the whale room i have just a party of gardeners all reacting to each other, its so fun using the mechanics and watching your creation work in perfect symphony, its more satisfying than power wash simulator
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: I wish there was more VR games that weren't just punching and shooting simulators. They're great for that but it takes a truly creative and innovative team to put together a game like this that takes advantage of the hardware in a new way. If I ever heard someone compare a game to this one with a similar level of polish I would likely be buying it soon. The game is short but I wish it followed up on the story a bit more. I understand the reason for using the tape recorders and radio for running the story along but I was really disappointed when at the end there was no Edea to be seen. It's pretty sad to not get the satisfaction of seeing that to the end. Especially when the story really felt like it had ended. At least that was the only thing that disappointed me when playing this game.The only finicky thing is figuring out how to handle all the fruits in the game. It's very obvious how to deal with the first three. The last two made me scratch my head. I never really figured out Dewshots and Luftapples came to me at the very end. I'm sure that was just a personal issue with me. The bell puzzle also stumped me briefly but I think a good puzzle shouldn't come to anyone right away. Sadly, I did look up a solution. Though, again, it adds to the value of the puzzle when it feels like there could be multiple ways of approaching it.If you're on the fence about the game, go for it. It's probably not longer than a 4 hour play. Likely no more than a few gaming sessions if you have trouble wrapping your head around what the game wants you to do.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: The Last Clockwinder was an incredibly fun game to play through, I’m shocked I haven’t heard about this game until now. It's one of my new favourite games! :)The main mechanic of recording your movements and interacting with your ‘past selves’ is very cool and weird to wrap your head around. The story was cute and the way the characters talk felt incredibly natural. Unfortunately, it only took me a few hours to 100% and it doesn’t have much for replayability other than trying to perfect previous rooms. It would be nice for there to be extra challenges after beating the game or have some sort of endless mode to mix things up.I highly recommend trying this game, just don’t forget to stay hydrated! You can work up a sweat if you don't take breaks.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best VR puzzle and story games I have played thus far. The physics are fantastic, the aesthetic of this world is beautiful, and it was a lot of fun making these Rube Goldberg style automation sequences. The soundtrack is great and I love how it progresses as you solve the puzzles. This is a must have for sure.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: Easily the best VR puzzle game I've ever played, with one of the most ingenious and satisfying uses of mechanics that I've played in a long while. The constant moments of discovery as you creep closer to your goal, culminating in the wonderful feeling of stepping back and admiring your effort is incredibly rewarding. This game's mechanics are a perfect synthesis of physics, interaction, precision, timing, and spacial reasoning the likes of which I've not personally experienced since Portal. Like Portal, The Last Clockwinder gives you a unique mechanic paired with a novel concept and allows you the freedom to explore at your own pace. Like Portal, it is friendly to beginners who are just learning the mechanics as well as returning players trying to push the system to it's limits. A game that makes full use of the medium it's in, The Last Clockwinder is a must-play VR title that offers a glimpse into the vast and untapped world of mechanics that VR can offer!
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: Great idea, lovely story, awesome game mechanics.Everything here works like a cogs in a clock :) Story, visual style, game mechanics, a lot of freedom.Game will force you to use your brain to make things more efficient.You can make it simple (yeet stuff ) or complicated (yeet multiple stuff at once,combine it mid-air, do multiple things at once ,yeet stuff faster) 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: Such a simple concept, but there is lots of fun to be had here. Imagine the fun of automation games like factorio or satisfactory, but instead of being limited by the tools available to you and your ability to combine them for efficiency/speed, you are instead limited by your ability to complete a task within a time limit. Creating a room full of robot copies of yourself that all work together in perfect harmony to harvest resources is just *muah*, I spent quite a bit of time just watching my room full of bots and feeling satisfied with a job well done. Unfortunately, this game only lasted 5 hours, and only the first 3 of those were satisfying and fun.The latter 2 hours introduced two new resources to collect, dewdrops and balloon fruit. I had no issues with the previous resources, every time I recorded a robot to repeat my actions it would repeat them flawlessly as they happened. But these new resources are *heavily* reliant on physics and extremely precise movements of your hands. It seems that this emphasized all of the tiny inconsistencies within your robot copies. I rapidly went from trying to fully optimize every room to getting extremely frustrated just trying to get any amount of resource collection automated. I'd make a robot copy that moved the resource to exactly where I wanted it, but it would only work when I did it and on the first cycle of the robot, then the physics would bug out and, despite the robot following the *exact* same movements every time, the resources would end up being thrown in wildly different directions.This lead to far more issues with the fact that these new resources weren't even slowly introduced to you. As soon as you get them you're expected to use them in areas requiring a dozen or more robots to complete, and if any single one of those robots decided to stop working consistently then your ENTIRE assembly line was ruined and you had to restart from scratch. I got so frustrated that I just got each room done and stopped caring about making anything even slightly efficient. And there were even a couple times when I got a room working well and producing a good amount of resources, and I got an urge to go back and try to make it better, but as soon as I loaded back into the room my production dropped, half of the robots in the room weren't working properly when they were at the time I had left the room. It left a very sour taste in my mouth from a game I was quite enjoying.I think the devs have a great base here, small tweaks can fix my major complaints, and then I think the game ought to have a non-story mode, playable after the story is completed, that lets you take more advantage of the fun mechanics that are here.At the end of the day, this game is definitely worth playing and I recommend you get it, not at full price though, there's simply not enough content to justify it's base price.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, this is a prime example of an almost perfect indie VR game. The story and gameplay may not be the best ever but they are damn tight and beautiful. This is a great game for everyone no matter how much of a gamer or VR vet you are. Note to the devs, I had a persistent and annoying bug where certain levers (knife and seed dispensers) would randomly stop working and exiting to the menu and reloading was the only thing that fixed it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed this little gem. The game's mechanics of cloning your actions to efficiently accomplish a task is well done. The narrative arch is all conveyed through audio recordings and the scene doesn't change much as you stay in one room the entire game. The music and tone is calming (especially given it is about cranking out the most refined machine built entirely of your collective recorded actions). Challenges get harder over time, but the underlying dynamic is the same. If you like games like Transpose, you'll probably like this (and vice versa).
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: What a fantastic little game. I absolutely adored this game and everything about it. The story it tells can be a bit on the nose with its allegory but it makes sense given the subject matter. The voice acting was fantastic, the music was whimsical, the visuals were cosy and very fitting, and the mechanics just work perfectly. Above everything, it's just fun as hell and show what VR can do. Worth every penny and I'd love to see what these devs do next.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: Straight up Best VR design ive seen to date. It uses exactly what VR is good at perfectly 10/10 game for me. Narrative is short but sweet, some challenges are hard others not so much but even if a problem is hard you can brute force it easily so the difficulty is ultimately up to you. This game is must buy from me even if you don't like puzzle games.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a very unique answer to a question I had never thought to ask: How would you implement an automation mechanic in VR? Between the simple controls and the elegant design of each puzzle, this is a quick and fun experiment. The storyline in the game was short, simple, and sweet, which paired well with the atmosphere of the game. I would certainly recommend any one who enjoys automation games to give this a shot.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best VR puzzles of all time. It takes the idea of using clones in VR from Transpose and adds Zachtonics-lite conveyor planning. The result is satisfying to play and mesmerizing to watch after optimizing puzzle solution.Controls are easy and intuitive, throwing is very responsive. Puzzle difficulty(including optional production quotas) is a bit low, but still challenging enough to be fun.Visuals are good but could have used much better textures for PC version. Story and characters are interesting and voice acting is great.Works on Reverb G2.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: A fun little game that i enjoyed the whole way. The story was also kinda sweet. My only complaint is that it feels a little too short, HOWEVER I still feel a drive to complete the various puzzles at a better par which softens the length issue (which is a credit to the game vs other puzzle games I've played). If they released a expansion or something that had new puzzles with more ways to interact with the fruits I would absolutely buy it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: Just from the description alone for this game, I was already intrigued. Actually playing the game was even better. This is such a unique idea for a game, I don't think I've seen anything similar on the store thus far. The gameplay is fun, trying to experiment with ways to solve the 'puzzles' and make your processes more efficient. I'm the kind of guy who skips cutscenes all the time, but this game just plays audio recordings and calls which you can have in the background to listen to while you solve your puzzles. The story itself is actually quite cute also! Overall I would definitely recommend this game, it's quite cheap, it offers a lot, and it's definitely worth giving a shot.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: This is a new type of not just vr game but game in general. Its not the most mind challenging puzzle solver but it does make you think very creativly and feels rewarding to progress or even to go back to old areas to do it even better. I will safely safe this is a vr must experience to those who bored of vr shooters/beat sabor.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: Playtime around 3h. Feels really polished and while the puzzels arn't really difficult, the mechanics make them feel really unique and the visuals and storry are great. The pacing ist also well done, nothing feels like a grind - but you are left with space to put the extra efford in, if you feel like it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: Played fine with Airlink on Meta Quest 2. Not exactly a puzzle game since you need to make the right moves with the right timing, but you have as many tries as you want, and it's pretty forgiving. Both the game mechanics and the puzzles are nice. At no point do you feel like "well that's just the same puzzle with just a small difference", puzzles have great variance. Heck, I wish they made it longer by just re-using mechanics.I really liked the story line, even though it was only voice.I made the full story in 4 hours. You can probably spend maybe 4 additional hours trying to optimize your lines and get most achievements. Overall, strong recommend, even though 20$ might be a bit high for 4 hours of play time.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: A great puzzle game with only one true flaw: The list of things that you interact with is very limited. The premise of the game is that you're simultaneously investigating the disappearance of an old friend, while also trying to restore function to a complex system by using "clones" of yourself to perform simple tasks in sequence. The execution of the story and the mechanics is awesome! But if that's all that any game ever was, then we'd have a lot more 5-star hits out there.When it comes to most games- especially VR games, the ones that stand out and shine are the ones that have polish due to "the little things" that give the virtual world life. Something as simple as interacting with the objects present in a room, if not all of them, then just the ones within reach that draw curious games to them. In this game there are plenty of interesting books and plants throughout the levels- none of which you can interact with, unless they specifically are designed to progress the game. This flaw in the gameplay isn't a flaw that "matters" to the story, but it definitely matters to the immersion. What the point of world building if you can't interact with that world?  The story is fantastic, the puzzles are terrific, but there's a bit to be desired left over. I'm glad to have played it though, and I look forward to more games like this one, albeit a bit more interactive.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good little title, albeit a little short like most VR games. I got it on sale for 18 bucks and beat it in about 4 hours. And honestly, considering that's about how much I'd pay to go see a movie when factoring in ticket+food, this is a perfectly fine deal. Full price of 25 bucks is a bit of a different story imo but that's your call to make. While it can be beaten in 4 hours, probably even less if you're quick with puzzle solving, you can easily get more time out of it by trying to get all achievements or optimizing the automation as much as possible. The story in here is okay, nothing mind-blowing but by no means bad and it even tugged at my heartstrings a bit. Overall, good buy, especially if you can get it on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: Probably the most refreshing VR puzzle experience I've ever had. I was a little hesitant to pick up this game at first but since there was a sale I figured why not. After roughly 4-5 hours of game play, I can comfortably say that this game is worth every penny, and wont disappoint if puzzle games are your bread and butter. Give it a shot.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: A very nice VR automation game where you record your movements for bots to repeat. Nice visuals, okay story, not too complex and a bit on the shorter side with a regular playthrough clocking in at 4ish hours. But then you also are challenged to optimise your automation with throughput and number of bots, so there is a bit more to play.The physics at some times could be a bit better - sometimes your throws won't work the way you expect, or a recorded movement won't have 100% the same result, but it's nothing major.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: I'm only a few hours in but this has become my new favorite VR game.It has very interesting mechanics that would only be possible in VR. The graphics are great. Stylized, but simple enough to run without a hitch even with a ton of robots running. The physics system is reliable enough that so long as you're nor bouncing something off of a surface you should be able to repeat your results perfectly every time.I didn't get motion sick once while I was playing.Puzzles are simple enough to solve, but making them more efficient adds a good level of challenge.I'll update this if my opinion changes, but so far I REALLY love this game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I played this earlier in the year. This is easily one of my GOTY choices, great idea with a beautiful and smooth execution. Even the story and overall atmosphere feels exceptional. This to me feels like one of the most polished and enjoyable VR experiences, I can't wait to keep playing and finish it, it feels similar to the satisfaction of a game like factorio, but with the monkey part of my brain loving throwing things around and feeling more playful.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: I would classify this as a game up there with Beat Saber in the category of "If you have the ability to play this game, you very much should, and it helps justify the investment". Just the right amount of complexity, just the right amount of wiggle room. It takes dexterity and multiple attempts to set up those perfectly choreographed throws and movements, but you have an infinite amount of time and attempts to get it just right. No other game, not even VR Chat or Alyx, has so thoroughly displaced me in my physical room because of how immersed I was in moving about in the virtual space. This is the game I'm having my friends and family try out if they visit and want to see what you can do with VR.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: The game takes a fun mechanic (making cloned recordings of yourself) and explores it in a few interesting ways. The game ends at the perfect moment before outstaying its welcome.It has a simple but endearing narrative pulling you through the various levels. The art design is spot on.I took some time in the early - mid challenges to achieve optimal automation. Overall took 7 hours. I might revisit sometime and optimise some of the later challenges when the format will feel less repetitive.Certainly recommend if the premise appeals to you!
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: I like automation, juggling, and puzzles, so this game is a good fit for me. No, you don't need to juggle, but there can be a lot of throwing and catching.It's very satisfying to see all the recorded versions of yourself working together. I had some performance issues. Even though the VR performance graph showed plenty of headroom, I'd get some inconsistent stuttering, which could make it hard to do that throwing and catching.There are some bugs with the smooth locomotion mode, but it looks like the developers are responsive to feedback and are working on fixing those issues,I'd like to see a game with a bigger variety of actions and more challenging puzzles. Some of the later puzzles are difficult more due to inconsistent physics rather than the complexity of the puzzles.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: I definitely enjoyed the game! The main mechanic of the game is well executed and I absolutely love it, the graphics were nice and the audio & voice overs were great. I finished the story in about 5 to 6 hours while playing with the Valve Index and after a bit of a break came back to get all the achievements which took around 10 to 11 hours.My biggest "problem" with the game is that the additional content, such as optimizing the throughput for certain levels to gain achievements, often felt extremely tedious. Let me explain:You need to use a maximum amount of clones to get a certain production amount, this could for example be 'using at most 5 clones to get 20 berries per minute' but could also be combining several resources and then feeding those into a machine. Because of this limitation you will likely need to rebuild your clone setup a few times, which isn't bad with 5 clones, but certain levels require more than 10 clones at the same time.. I absolutely did not enjoy those achievements and just cheesed them by manually feeding resources into the machines as I didn't want to spend the time on several of those giant levels, I really wish they were done differently.Achievements and optional content aside the game is still great. I received it as a gift from a friend (hence the "I received this for free" tag) and overall would highly recommend it!
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: It's an assembly factory puzzle game in the vein of SpaceChem, Opus Magnum, Infinifactory, etc. If you liked those, then you'll probably enjoy this.Fun while it lasted, but fairly short (about 8 hours to completion + min/max challenges.) Still, good enough value for the price point. Devs have no plans for a level editor or custom Workshop challenges at present, but that would certainly be a welcome addition to extend the life of the game.Just make sure you have plenty of room to swing your arms; I accidentally smacked my desk and monitor several times.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: The first VR game I've completed within one sitting. Making npcs copy your movement is a very creative and well executed concept and it allows just enough freedom for you to do about anything without making it too un-approachable.However, there are some issues.- The game will sometimes just... die? It's just not exactly as stable as I'd like it to be.- Some items (especially fruit chains) can just disappear/rubber-band if I push them too hard.- The game died right after I finished the last  "puzzle" (just before the credits, in the final room) and it really broke the overall experience. Sure it didn't destroy it, but the fact I had to re-launch the game, enter my save, and watch the credits again just to realize there's nothing after was pretty infuriating. - The story started off interesting, but quickly got stale. By the time I was at the final levels it feels like it's just "another story" instead of something your character is going through.Overall I'd give this a 9/10 for the game itself but a 7/10 for stability & bugs. Definitely worth a play if you own a VR headset, and if you don't, it's a somewhat okay reason to get one.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing Game.1. really cool and unique mechanic with the robot coping your movements really fun to use. 2. the story is very cute and its fun to find all the tapes to uncover the whole story. amazing voice acting. wholesome characters with a little bit of mystery. 3. the puzzles are really fun to figure out. then with the challenges in each room it give a way to add replay-ability to the rooms. 4. runs GREAT. i never had performance issues and only had one glitch issue that was fixed with a quick restart. 5. my ONLY complaint is that its a little short but it is priced  accordingly. 6. love this game they deserve your money. gota support the amazing VR games when they come along.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: A fascinating problem solving game that utilizes VR capabilities in a unique way.I recommend any puzzle-enjoyer to give it a try, whether they are looking to solve a problem in a relaxed way or want to optimize every move so they can watch a highly efficient team of robots throw around fruits like crazy and reach the maximum possible output of a desired product.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder
