I'm too drunk to remember what I pair right now, but it was probably less than $30 cause I rarely pay more than that for any game!  It's nice to take my Steam Deck into the John for a #2 and I can give a game a shot for 10-20 minutes!
_childDocuments_.name: Capcom Arcade 2nd Stadium

_childDocuments_.review: For me, both Capcom Arcade Stadiums worked well without any issues. Both have a good collection of classic games to choose from with many cool additional features (e.g. rewinding). The only two things that I didn't like:1. Why are there two almost exactly similar Arcade Stadiums existing? Why aren't they merged into one?2. Buying games as DLCs is rather expensive if you want to get all of them. I would prefer a package that would contain all games from scratch without any messing with DLCs, just like e.g. Disney Afternoon Collection.
_childDocuments_.name: Capcom Arcade 2nd Stadium

_childDocuments_.review: It's very simple.You bought Street Fighter 30th Anniversary Collection and you have no idea why they only gave you the bugged American version of Super Turbo.So you get Arcade Stadium 2, you buy HYPER STREET FIGHTER 2 for 2 dollars and now you have an awesome version of the game to practice for your online matches with. Also, as a bonus you can get the best fighting game ever, STREET FIGHTER ALPHA 2, for another two dollars.The rest of this package could be nothing and 4 bucks investment for two arcade perfect ports of the best SF games is an easy thumbs up.
_childDocuments_.name: Capcom Arcade 2nd Stadium

_childDocuments_.review: This is a pretty good collection. One of the positives is that achievements aren't really tied to a specific game. This makes it to where you can buy only the games that you actually want and still 100% the collection. The CASPO rating has bonus weeks for the games that you own. It will rotate every three weeks so you can rack up higher CASPO scores. That said, there are some very obvious cheaters in the CASPO ranking, you'll see what I'm talking about if you pick this collection up. It's pretty frustrating in my opinion when someone works hard and is tenacious enough at the game to rank highly only to have some clown with 10 hours of gameplay magically rack up 4 billion points. My best advice is try not to let it bother you too much. The collection will be a trip down memory lane for a lot of older players and it's a great way for younger players to get exposed to some classic titles.
_childDocuments_.name: Capcom Arcade 2nd Stadium

_childDocuments_.review: I don't think we needed a whole new game; they could've easily just added the new games as DLC to the first Stadium game. Still, I gotta hand it to Capcom for keeping these games alive and accessible. I don't see many other companies doing the same and investing this amount of work, there was even a free game to get started. I ended up buying the whole thing at a massive discount, and it was totally worth it for me. Keep them coming Capcom!
_childDocuments_.name: Capcom Arcade 2nd Stadium

_childDocuments_.review: If you're seeking a nice collection of quality arcade games without the hassle associated with downloading emulators, configuring them & downloading roms from questionable sources this may be what you're looking for. It works flawless & offers a nice variety of titles which allow old school gamers like myself to revisit their childhood, re-discover retro games & share their love for gaming with their family & friends.I purchased both Capcom Arcade Stadium 1 & 2 on sale which include all games. I like Capcom Arcade Stadium 1 more than version 2 but both offer a nice value in retro gaming entertainment. The layout is pretty much the same for both versions but obviously the games are different for each. I find that the 2nd version is more focused on fighters whereas the first version is more varied in game style.I recommend you pick up both to have the complete collection but only if you can get it on sale. There were about 11 games I liked from each collection so there are a minimum of 22 titles that made it worth my while. Although I do have a Tankstick arcade I haven't had a chance to test it out yet. I'm sure it would give these titles a more authentic feel like back in the 80's arcade days.Works great with an XBOX ONE S controller!
_childDocuments_.name: Capcom Arcade 2nd Stadium

_childDocuments_.review: Well, this is a mixed review, and it will be the same one that I will give to Capcom Arcade Stadium 1... first things first, this game is not free even though it claims to be, it is just the platform for you to buy the real games in form of dlc, on the other hand, the interface of the platform is beautiful, with the appearance of an arcade bar, in addition each and every one of the games that you can buy are a gem and the settings and filters they have are the ones indicated, the emulator of roms is very good compared to other retro games that I have bought here on Steam with frame drops and horrible input lag, and for that reason alone I give it my full approval, it is very good that they have added achievements, the only bad thing is that It has 1 achievement for 100 hours of play in which after 1 year and only around 30-40 hours of play, I had to leave the game open in the background to get it.
_childDocuments_.name: Capcom Arcade 2nd Stadium

_childDocuments_.review: well done, good challenges(time attack, special -hardest, 1cc- challenge, score challenge), rankings..very good.made for players to enjoy in more than one way those gems.CapcomSportsClub is at last available.unfortunately for a 2nd game it's just a game list swap. you cant have a 3d arcade room you could visit on foot.beside those things & the limited choice in cabinets(there s only one game-specific cabinet: darkstalkers & ONE at that)i hope the next salvo of games wont summon a CAStadium THREE.might just happen

_childDocuments_.review: It is actually quite good for replaying all the retro games of yesteryear (including the Street Fighter 2 games) the fast forward and speed up buttons are kinda annoying though otherwise this is a good and cheap ways of getting the Capcom games you want, just be aware that this and the previous Arcade Stadium cover all the Capcom retro games on Steam so the specific genre releases like the Fighting Collection are not worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: Not a bad game selection.  But there's a ton of overlap with past offerings here on Steam.  So your mileage may vary for the price.  Please add Giga Wing, Mars Matrix, Alien vs Predator, Cadillacs and Dinosaurs, and The Punisher if at all possible.  I know Capcom re-licensed Alien vs Predator for their arcade stick.  Just add it here too.  It's easy money.
_childDocuments_.name: Capcom Arcade 2nd Stadium

_childDocuments_.review: So, I like Capcom Arcade Stadium 2. I liked the 1st one as well. I don't need more than 15 minutes to know that much. It does more of what I liked about the 1st iteration. That said, I'm worried about the overall reviews that'll be incoming for this one for two reasons. 1st off, the free hub download followed by optional transactions for games removed the main barrier of entry keeping pretty much every game from getting review bombed. It's not something people pay to do. 2nd, and more importantly, a very significant portion of this game's releases are also in prior collections. Most notoriously, the overlap between this collection and the Fighting Collection (the Dark Stalkers collection) defies reason, considering they're only a few weeks apart in release. I like this title, and I've purchased and liked all of Capcom's retro bundles, from Mega Man to Beatemups to here. If Capcom keeps making preventable mistakes that keep their releases from performing well, we might not see more, and that's probably the worst thing about the Arcade Stadiums - that Capcom will draw the wrong conclusion from all the red thumbs.
_childDocuments_.name: Capcom Arcade 2nd Stadium

_childDocuments_.review: Great collection of classic Capcom arcade games. There's so much to enjoy here!The highlight for me is Black Tiger (Black Dragon / JP). This is easily one of the best 2D platformers ever created. The art and game design is still mostly unmatched to this day. A timeless classic.I own the Capcom Beat 'Em Up Bundle, so there's a few titles in this collection that overlap. But it's not a big deal to me as there's so many great games here and having the Beat 'Em Ups included here is nice for the convenience of staying in the same UI.The collection works and performs flawlessly on my desktop PC.At this time of writing the game doesn't work on the Steam Deck though - it just crashes on startup. The first collection works fine, so hopefully Capcom will fix this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Capcom Arcade 2nd Stadium

_childDocuments_.review: 8,5/10 Great collection.This collection is much better than Capcom Arcade 1st Stadium in my opinion.And it's good to know that we have the option to buy games individually or in bundles.The free game in this collection is "SonSon" which is pretty good. I will definitely buy this collection so I can play these Mega Man games. ^^Unfortunately, Capcom's marketing is pretty bad. Why actually?Last month Capcom Fighting Game was released and this collection contains all Darkstalker games, as well as the two Street Fighter Puzzle Fighters, etc.We shouldn't forget that Street Fighter 1, all Street Fighter Alpha games are also in Capcom Arcade Stadium 2.Now I wonder if buying Street Fighter 30th Anniversary was a good decision or not.Apart from this problem, I would like to thank Capcom for releasing this collection on Steam.Overall:Anyway, many thanks to Capcom for this collection. I'm really looking forward to a Capcom VS SNK and Marvel VS Capcom Collection.(I really want to play these games!) ^^

name: Time Commando
detailed_description: For retro gaming lovers, discover a jewel from 1996: TIME COMMANDO A deadly virus has invaded a top secret military super computer. Its catastrophic time-warping effects now threaten to overtake the computer systems of the world. If you cannot restore its memory in time, the growing virus will cause the world's collapse. You must journey through the corridors of history to stop this technological demon. But vicious warriors await with lethal purpose. Instinct will be your only ally. All-out combat, your only choice. Time Commando will take you on a journey in time and space that you will never forget. With plenty of weapon types, stylized visuals, and diversified gameplay it should keep you entertained for many hours. This title is very unique and it should be a part of every serious game collection. 9 Worlds to explore, each in a different time and place: prehistoric, Roman, feudal Japan, Medieval, Conquistador, the Wild West, and the modern wars. Impressive arsenal of weapons, from Katanas through rifles and spells to a technologically advanced combat yo-yo. Entertaining and challenging puzzle-solving elements, stylized visuals, and an original story. Disclaimer 1: this game uses DosBox Disclaimer 2: this is the european version of the game. The introduction has no voice over. Disclaimer 3: start with the easy mode ;)

_childDocuments_.review: I used to play this game as a kid and remember it with pleasure.SUMMARY OF THE PLOTBecause the game was released in 1996, the story takes place in the near future (in 2020). The military has, with help from Historical Tactical Center, developed an advanced AI-system that allows every combat technique through history. One day, a person from a rival company breaks in and install a predator-virus in the main computer, which causes that the whole mankind are sucked into a vortex.Stanley Opar, the game protagonist, works as a S.A.V.E. (Special Action for Virus Elimination) and is the only hope to save the world. When he is sucked into the vortex, he must travel through different time eras, starting in Prehistoric and ending in the era of Beyond time where he must fight the virus, which is a big blue shark.The different time eras are: Prehistoric, Roman Empire, Feudal Japan, Medivel Europe, Conquistador, Wild West, Modern Wars (WW 1 and probably WW 3), Future (Stanley's future) and Beyond Time.GRAPHICThe game was, for it's time, very detailed and realistic. In the beginning, Stanley are shaved, but gets beard further in the game. The cutscenes are good for it's time.GAMEPLAYYou play in a 3rd person perspective. In 1996 it was unusual to turn around in 360º; when you klicked to the right, the character went right and don't  right. This was something new for it's time. You can attack with kicks and melee attacks. You can also jump to the left, the right and forward. In each time era you will have typical weapon arsenal for that era, i.e. in prehistoric you'll have stones, club and a spear while you in the Modern Wars have rifles and handgranades. Every era offers five different weapons.There are various hidden room and places where you could find power-ups, weapons or other things. Every era includes two stages. In some stages, it's a boss, in others there's no boss fight.The camera angle is better now than in 1996. Great work, Steam!MUSICEvery stage has it's own music. In the menu, there is two soundtracks. CONCLUSIONLike anything from the 1990s, this game is just for nostalgia, nothing more. If you are a new player, don't buy it because you will not find it satisfying. For me, and those who played it as kids, it's a pleasure to see it on Steam!

_childDocuments_.review: I've been playing this game since I was about three years old. It's most likely the first video game I ever played.I have no idea where my parents got the disk but it made me love computers and programming for the rest of my life.It also had an effect on my perception of history. Here's how:- I permanently and irreversibly believe that Neanderthals looked like Batman but with orange-ish clothes - I'm afraid of women because the first person you meet in the Roman Ages- I will forever believe friendly knights will duel each other if their opponent tricks them into it- Wizards are annoying and can teleport.- Black belt martial artists got nothing on an unarmed Stanley Opar- If I see ever a clay pot next to a statue, you'd best believe I'm gonna turn the lid 360 degrees just to be sure- The American Civil War was fought by standing in one place and pretending to be a statue- The more recent wars were fought by guys with roller blades and grenades- Beyond Time is probably what it's like to do DMTAll-in-all, this game was way ahead of its time, and games are no longer made to the quality they were back in 1996. Seeing it appear on Steam with a new studio backing it has made me a happy man.I disagree with another reviewer that the game serves exclusively for nostalgia, it's still fun and challenging.Would rather play TC than Call of Duty. Would love to see a sequel or remake.
_childDocuments_.name: Time Commando

_childDocuments_.review: The year is 1996. I am 6. The disc for Time Commando comes free with Windows 95. I have never played a videogame before. My mind... is blown. Almost 30 years later, this game still goes hard. Soundtrack? Slaps. Stanley's skin-tight yellow future suit? Baller. Punching and kicking cavemen and Conquistadors to death? Absolute aces. I no longer have to call in my dad to play the level with the space zombies (because they don't scare the peepee outta me anymore), so that's a bonus. However, I do NOT remember this game being this difficult. Dark Souls? Don't know her
_childDocuments_.name: Time Commando

_childDocuments_.review: This game reminds me of my late father. He introduced me to gaming with this, Heretic, MDK, Duke Nukem 3D and Descent. Extremely nostalgic.Anyways, if you are planning on playing this for the first time you're probably a retro gamer and you probably know you'll be playing a 90's game, which comes with all the limitations from that time.Aside from that, Time Commando offers:Great exploration gameplay. Every stage will reward you for finding hidden objects and rooms.Great concept. The game will make you travel trough time, starting from pre history going all way to the future. To me this is the selling point of this game.Each era will set you with weapons from that time, so the gameplay will always be changing.Don't forget to use the code COMMANDO after finishing the game for an extra stage. (guess this is the only code I'll never forget lol)

_childDocuments_.review: Time Commando is a great game for those who want to revisit the past and see what gaming was like back in the early 1990s for 3D Action titles. The game's concept is simple enough: you are a Time Commando who has been dispatched to go through different periods of time to defeat a virus that was inserted in a Time Machine by an evil scientist. You go through multiple time periods, fighting and killing whatever is in your path. Apparently, Time Commandos don't think about what kind of repercussions come from killing so many in each time period, because the game ends the same way, no matter how you play it. The weirdest design choice of this game has got to be controls though. For some reason, they decided to make this adventure play just like Resident Evil, which is jarring considering they never use a Zombie or Demon. Pros:+ The Weapon Variety makes each Time Period have a different feel in combat.+ The graphics and music are actually nice pieces of history.+ It plays great on the Steam Deck!+ It's a very fast-loading title to just sit down and play+ It can be challengingCons:- The controls are very dated and sluggish. This will turn off modern gamers.- While the weapons change, the combat can get boring after a bit. It's good that they don't stay in each time period too long.- The story is simple and almost non-existent. If you are here for good plots, move along.Overall, I recommend the game for those who enjoy old-school games at this point or would love to replay it on their Steam Deck. On another note: This game is ripe for a remake (if done correctly).
_childDocuments_.name: Time Commando

_childDocuments_.review: Recommended only for people who played this 27 years ago :DPlayed this as a kid in 1996 and finished it multiple times. Except for the camera movement being very choppy (was it like that in 96? Probably was...) and the initial cutscene not playing for me for some reason - the gameplay and music still have this magic!I remembver that even in 1996 this games graphics were a bit weird, a little bit sub-par (when you compare it to Tomb Raider 1 that released in the same year, which aged a bit better). Super interesting premise though - from fighting cavemen through knighs, WW1, to science fiction. Fascinating, I don't recall any fighting game doing that.

_childDocuments_.review: Some of the best use of pre-rendered image in a game. For a 1996 game, the effect is really impressive. Specially at the later stages. The combat is a bit clunky, but the theme variety and enemies make it a better experience than I tought I would have.Go with a retro-focused-mind and you can have a blast. The difficulty is unforgiven in the early stages, but for those who remain the good part is really at the end.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game of an era from the good old days of 2000s. I tried this game back in 2000 as a kid but couldn't finish it. I got to second level then stuck.  This is a hard game. Finally able to finish this game with walk through  help. The biggest constraint is the time so it helps to use walk through to collect all the clean circuits or run out of time and die.  Keep the first life so the health bar is always 4 bars. and collect all the hidden items. It'll easier to finish the game. A well made game.
_childDocuments_.name: Time Commando

_childDocuments_.review: Wow. I was only 7 the last time I had ever touched this game, that was all the way back in 2009. I got frustrated with Time Commando because of how difficult it was, never being able to finish the game after already halfway through it and eventually gave up. I ended up losing the disc somehow and when I did decide to give it another try I never found it again nor could I find another copy anywhere else, so I gave up looking and eventually forgot the game even existed.Then LO AND BEHOLD, 12 years later and I stumble across this game again on Steam. Words cannot express how absolutely THRILLED I was to be able to play Time Commando again!After all these years, I can finally bring myself some closure and finish this damn game once and for all.Thank you Adeline Software for such an amazing game, and an awesome childhood!
_childDocuments_.name: Time Commando

_childDocuments_.review: Very charming old DOS game with amusing animations, enjoyable soundtrack and variety of levels. Gameplay can be clunky and camera angle is not like modern games, but the animations make up for it imo.Does not include extra goodies like the GOG version, namely some artwork, wallpaper/avatars, reference card.
_childDocuments_.name: Time Commando

_childDocuments_.review: Ah, yes, Time Commando. A game that only left a small tiny portion to my childhood - due to my cousin owning it instead of me and he was already in a gameplay (at the first Wild West level, no less), I couldn't even find the game's name out - but said portion still left an impression on me of how I didn't know how to play it and just fiddling around like the 5-6 year old I was. After seeing a 6 parter review of the game 10 years ago, I got flashbacks of that game and made me wish I could own it somehow. 10 years after that, I finally got the chance and had a great blast with this game! Definitely could recommend for anyone who also played this in their childhood in one way or another, or are looking for a challenging retro game!

name: Bandle Tale: A League of Legends Story
detailed_description: Digital Deluxe Edition Bandle Tale: A League of Legends Story™ Deluxe Edition includes the following: Poro Closet : Dress up your fluffy little poro pal in two exclusive (and ultra-cute) outfits. Stand Behind Poro! Buzzy Poro Home Sweet Backpack : Two eye-catching exteriors for your bigger-on-the-inside backpack home. Honeycomb Hive Purple Prism Bungalow Strut with Style : Three pathway effects for your character. Busy Bee Zip-Zap! Full Speed Ahead Secret Menu : Order up! Fresh out of the oven, three additional recipes to add to your cookbook. Rainbow Egg Almost-Perilous Pie Poro Snax About the Game One little Yordle, one humongous problem. From Lazy Bear, the studio that brought you Graveyard Keeper, comes Bandle Tale: A League of Legends Story™. Jump into this delightful crafting RPG set in the magical world of Bandle City, home of the furry and fun-loving yordles. You are a shy yordle living in Yarnville, a cozy but isolated island obsessed with all things knitting. When your 101-year-long apprenticeship ends, you want nothing more than to see what lies beyond the portals that connect the rest of Bandle City. But when a party you attend goes horribly wrong, the portals collapse and everything is thrown into chaos! With your unique knitting magic and unflappable spirit, enlist the help of new friends, restore the portals, and reunite Bandle City once more! BEYOND THE BANDLEWOODS In Bandle Tale, experience a never-before-seen look at life beyond the bandlewoods. Encounter curious critters, gather materials to make impossible crafts, and awaken magical portals as you move between five unforgettable new islands. PARTY ON, BANDLE CITY! A good life in Bandle City hinges on one thing: beet soup! Wait, no, having fun! Throw festivals to ensure that your fellow yordles are happy and entertained. Cultivate your green thumb and cook farm-to-table dishes for your guests, or flex your engineering prowess and build gadgets to delight them. MEET THE CHAMPIONS Befriend colorful characters and make League of Legends Champions your allies as you unravel the mysteries around you and mend your community, one magical stitch at a time.

_childDocuments_.review: It suggested if you like story games that make you run around the entire time following a quest, crafting stuff for that quest, and gathering materials. This is the game for you.!!Don't expect Stardew Valley. you dont have the free will to not to quest if you don't want to, you have to do the quests and its not replayable after you finish the game, unless you wanna just experience the entire story again ( i dont judge, you do you.)This is how the game is it's like this (without spoilers)-A quest needs materials -you run around to gather them (get "XP")-craft them (get "XP")-give it to them-you level up-you use your ("XP" points to  buy level up )-you are now leveled up, you have access to more materials to craftand it starts all over againYour mission is to help the Yordles in anyway you can thats it, thats the basics.You do not need to know league of legend bandle city lore, but to be honest it does help me enjoy the game wayyy more.Example:-There are jokes/mentions of other yordles that are not in here example: Gnar is mentioned as a joke, i found the joke funny because I knew about gnar. -The personality of the Yordles who are present in League of legends, I know the way they act so it feels more personal when I read their dialog and I understand them more.-You'll get material that belongs to the Yordles who are not mentioned here like an item that belongs to Hemindinger or Themed decor that belong to amumu, poppy, gnar etcPlay this game is you love -endlessly crafting and gathering.-veigar!- yordle foods-yordle parties -having your small house where you can do your crafts and more-veigar!-adorable cute graphics you can look at forever,- learn about the yordle world and embrace the story,- be a cute yordle who helps other yordles,-have a great humble sense of humor!, -veigar!- 40+hour of gameplay!

_childDocuments_.review: Don't get fooled by all the negative reviews from players with 1 hour on the clock.Some of them complain about the diminishing rewards of the XP system, while curiously the XP system isn't be the main way to level up.People who get stuck or complain about slow progress didn't figure out the core gameplay yet. The tutorial is barebones, so at some points you will need to stop and think about the mechanics the game offers to you. During my playthrough I had a lot of 'Aha' Moments while figuring out untold bits about how the mechanics and minigames work. If you don't mindlessly rush through the game it'll all come together naturally and smoothly. This contributes to the feeling of exploration while getting to know the yordle world.This is first and foremost a story driven game but it keeps a good balance between story telling and a standard 'crafting game'-trope.The colorful and cute art used to portray the yordle universe makes traveling very enjoyable. There are so many eye-candies. I very much enjoy the minigames, which are an essential part for making progress through the game. I can not recommend the Deluxe Edition unless you are a Poro connoisseur for life or feel a particular need to support the Publisher/Developer. Completed the game with all side tasks and quests in about 35 hours (posting this for someone else) while keeping a fast pace. _childDocuments_.review: I have played this game for almost 24 hours since release and close to the end. It is  a farming sim like stardew valley: it is all about collecting resources to craft things so you can collect more resources. If this is not a genre/game-play loop that you enjoy, then this game is likely not going to be for you.  this is a very cozy crafting simulator. If you like laid back games with a specific game play loop then this is for you. If you don't like repetition and running around, then don't. The game is good, but it's a very specific genre/style.  open up your quest menu and do quests. Go to the different islands and do the food stand and parties. This is your main source of gold & EXP. Don't rely on gathering and crafting alone.‎ ‎ ◉ The game runs pretty smoothly. There was a few stutters here or there but it didn't impact my experience. ‎‎  ◉ The pixel art is very beautiful with creative and unique settings. It is very whimsical and fantastical. If you like cozy pixel games then I highly recommend this ‎‎  ◉ The writing is pretty good with funny jokes and fun characters. I am a League player so I am familiar with the cast, but there is a lot of prominent "original" characters to Bandle Tale. I don't think you need to be familiar with the lore since the game explains the setting and plot well enough. ‎‎  ◉ The quests are very enjoyable! Not too difficult but not too easy.‎‎  ◉ The game-play loop: it is quite repetitive but I did enjoy the grind. You run around collecting the basic resources so you can craft items necessary for quests or to build new machines. There is a lot to unlock and find which I find enjoyable.‎‎  ◉ Side-games: I am counting the food stand and the parties as the sort of "side" games that you play. You unlock new recipes, parties, and "furniture" for both through the skill-tree. They're both fun but I find the food stand more enjoyable as the food recipes get more complex. .‎‎  ◉ The tutorials: some of them aren't as clear as they should be‎‎  ◉ UI: the readability for the skill tree can be rather confusing. Pair this with just the sheer size of how big it is, it's easy to get lost. I have been stumped 2-3 times because I had no idea what I had to do and there wasn't much clarification.‎‎  ◉ Running Around: you will have to do this A LOT. I recommend just using the portals, you won't run out of thread easily but it can be tedious when you start running low on sources. ‎‎  ◉ Item Recipes: it can be so easy to forget what you need to craft and what  need to be crafted. It would be nice to have a recipe book for craftable items in the menu to remedy this. ‎‎  ◉ Vending: it isn't really well explained and it takes much longer to generate money through it versus the food stand. It's better to just stick items into it to sell (be careful that they aren't necessary for quests/crafting) and check it periodically.

_childDocuments_.review: {final review}⭐️ 5/10 ⭐️Surprisingly disappointed with the end to this game. I completed all of the achievements with the main story and honestly... the end felt SO rushed. There are still side things I never explored, people with requests, incomplete badges, nodes I never unlocked, crafts I never made. Of course I could do all of that on my own but for the game to suddenly complete without forcing you to do most of those higher level crafts is, to me, bizarre. It's also weird that the end game has no save file where Bandle City is back to normal, it just forces you to replay your last save file before the finale.For a large portion of the game I avoided going to bed to force crafts to complete. But after needing so many of certain things and having certain items take 5+ minutes to craft it kind of became necessary to sleep over and over again which felt like cheating. It feels weird having no punishment for dreaming repeatedly. I still recommend playing it because it did have moments of fun and unique cozy crafting. But, dang, I wish the game wanted me to play more instead of seemingly rushing me out. {mid-playthrough review}⭐️ 6.5/10 ⭐️I have yet to finish this but what a SLOW build this game is. I found the beginning incredibly frustrating with not enough explanation given on how parties and cooking worked, ended up wasting a lot of resources learning while doing. But, it's also fun to not have your hand held so tightly and messing up felt kinda part of the game - it just felt unintentional. After 7-10 hours I finally felt like I got the hang of auras and filling my emotion orbs quickly, that's when it became really fun. I actually equate the crafting to those "merge" games where a lot of items building upon smaller building blocks to more complex things. Before being able to craft a hefty pile of Portal Yarn and project auras, walking everywhere and remembering which towns had which auras was long drab. My biggest advice to new players is to not skimp on your Portal Yarn, make your life easier and USE IT - a lot of the festivals give it to you as a reward. Also, using your quest log is a huge help to see where people are or what talent node is needed (blue text is clickable!) As others have mentioned, the inventory management is a hot mess. . I did  how crafting grabs items from your chests; a really big convenience that not many cozy crafting games allow. Though, turn-in quests don't tell you when you have the required items if your chests.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm trying to like this game, really I am. I am struggling to push myself to continue often at times. The game will open SEVERAL quests are once, but you can only do them in a certain order because you have to open up badges to progress further through the skill trees to get to the skills needed to complete the other open quests... Add in the 'aura' mechanic and you're constantly picking up your backpack to move (and also need to have it on you to teleport..) back and forth constantly from other regions. I don't know who decided the order of the skill trees, but certainly not someone familiar with these types of games. The overall vibe is cute, the music is nice, the humor is my brand of humor! ....but it really needs some quality of life/rearranging of quests (or even LOCKING/not even showing the ones you can't do until previous quests are completed). And by grind, I mean do literally ANYTHING and EVERYTHING you can because the game will decrease awarded exp (even go to 0!) if you do the same thing over and over again so be prepared to craft items, plant food, harvest foragables, host food stalls, host parties, and generally do everything short of pulling your in-game character's hair out to try to rectify your mishap.I'd highly suggest finding a guide just to use as a roadmap for 'what to do next' if you're not a fan of endless grinding. _childDocuments_.review: It hurts to say this, but this is a great crafting game held back by some really unnecessary roadblocks, I'll probably finish it just because, but right now I'm severely fed up.The visuals are beautiful, with just the right mix of cute and quirky. Same goes for the characters. I love Graveyard Keeper from the same dev, but have only the faintest notion of League of Legends. This didn't seem to hurt, I feel that the game tells me everything I need to know about the Yordles. Just like GK, especially with the DLCs, the game has a vast bouquet of parallel game mechanics. Some intricately interlock, others don't, but you always have  to do.Sounds good, so what's the problem?  And I'm saying that as someone who has a high tolerance for that. When others complain about the grind, my fun is usually just getting started. But judging by the stats, I'm only about halfway through and I can't take it anymore. And looking at the achievement list, I'm not alone. Purely based on the unmissable story achievements, not even 20% of the players make it to the point I'm at after roughly 20 hours.The island maps are manageably small, but they have lots of corners and tight meandering walkways. Sprinting is a b*tch, on top of a series of leg prosthetics with questionable perks. Yet, you constantly have to run from one end of the maps to the others, always using the same godforsaken paths. There is some portaling, but it costs resources and the portal locations are barely useful. You also can't portal without packing up your base, ostensibly so you don't get stuck if you run out of portal resource. The constraint stays in place though . Adding an otherwise useless stamina bar to that should be downright illegal.What's really killing the fun for me is the  though. It has a ton of cool skills and recipes, and it is somewhat gated by progression, but not prohibitively so. But it takes a good long while to make sense of what the abilities need and do. I constantly chose stuff I couldn't yet use. On the other hand, you get no info on what skills you will need to progress the different questlines.  that I spent points on stuff I wanted only to learn 5 minutes later that I should have spent them on skill X instead. As far as I can see, there is no way to reset the different trees.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're only looking at the reviews to check if the price is worth it: yes, it is. This is a huge game. There's a crazy amount of quests and skills to unlock. This is not a 20-hour game, and you will easily get $35 out of it.This is not a Stardew Valley clone. This game is much more akin to Wytchwood, with the gameplay loop being picking up quests, having to craft things or unlock new skills to craft things, and completing those tasks then unlocks more quests. It's an RPG, not a sandbox-lite farming simulator. It's sad people are leaving negative reviews here because they thought this was going to be like Stardew or Harvest Moon - take this as your warning that it isn't.That being said, this is a really great game for what it /actually/ is. The graphics and music are both top-tier, I'm continually awed by how stunning the graphics are. The writing is witty and oozes charm, there are so many moments that have made me smile. I watched my friend play for about 10 hours so far and we've had so many good laughs over the things that have happened thus far.I wouldn't say the game is grindy, at least not at the part we're at, but it does require paying attention to your resources. Resources don't fall into your lap; you need to go and gather them, which obviously takes time. If you play this game with the understanding that the genre is by nature quite slow and chill, you'll have a better time slowly working through all the tasks. If your goal is to finish the game in 20 hours, you're going to get impatient and burn out. For the negatives: the UI is poorly explained and the game desperately needs better tooltips, though it does feel nice to figure stuff out on your own. Playing with a controller feels good, but sometimes movement animations can feel sluggish. I have minor beef with the fact you can't mash A through dialogue because it'll end up repeating the same dialogue choice. That being said, these negatives do not outweigh the positives.I'm saddened by the fact Riot Forge is closing - it really feels like they didn't market this game properly, as most of the "cozy game" fans I know didn't even know this game existed - but I'm glad they're going out with such a great final game.

_childDocuments_.review: After playing through the entire story and getting all the badges, I think I can finally give my review. The art and the music was super cute and I loved it all. The story itself is fairly simple and quirky. I like that the game doesn't take itself too seriously and it's nice to meet all the yordles from League of Legends and collect all the Easter eggs sprinkled throughout the game. The cooking, crafting and party mechanics are fun and it doesn't get super repetitive. The only things I don't like is that there is no post-game content and for $25 dollars I expected a little bit more. I also didn't like the storage mechanic because you aren't able to throw away or discard items, so your inventory fills up pretty quickly. I understand that it was probably necessary since you get experience from crafting and harvesting, so they can't just let players craft hundreds of items and throw them away to farm exp. Overall, very cute game but I might recommend that you wait for it to be on sale in order to purchase!

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot tell you strongly enough how much I ABHOR this game! I was so excited for this game, preordering it as soon as I could because I love the yordles and the game appeared to be targeted towards a 'cosy' gamer, but now I see why they never released any actual gameplay before the game was released...The first 2 hours, albeit cute, are immensely confusing because you are overloaded with information. It's fun for about 30 minutes when you arrive at Bandle University, but as soon as you unlock the other 3 places it becomes completely insufferable as you have to jump from place to place doing the most mind-numbingly boring 'grinding' activities in order to move forward with your skills.It feels like they overload you with the tutorial and figuring out how to play the game for 2 hours just so you play enough of the game to be ineligible for a refund. It's really unfortunate that this game had so much potential but bombed so hard... I can see why Riot Forge doesn't want to make any more games.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't get fooled by all the positive reviews from players with 1 hour on the clock. This game starts out great with fast progress and seemingly straightforward and interesting skill tree. However, around the time you've unlocked all the islands and have to throw parties for each, you hit a wall and progressing becomes an unbearable chore. The way the XP system works in this game is you get diminishing XP returns from activities you repeat. So you eventually hit a point in the game where every action you perform have already been performed so many times it yields little to no XP, or "emotion orbs", anymore. Too bad since I loved the game and its cute artwork at the start.

_childDocuments_.review: I'd like to pre-emptively state that I have literally been counting down the days to release. I was so excited for it! It's not really what I was expecting, however.The art style is beautiful, and the world is colourful, carefully-constructed, and interesting to explore. Beyond that, though, the game feels a bit soulless. It's like they had a solid vision for the aesthetics and story, but didn't really put the same amount of planning into the actual gameplay.Gathering is holding a button, and then waiting for it to respawn. Crafting is choosing your wanted item and then holding a button down, or waiting for it to finish. Most quests are craft and/or fetch quests.Beyond the cute aesthetics, decent sound design, and nods to other titles in the "LoL Universe," I don't think this title has much lasting power, as is, and little to no replay value. It is also definitely not worth full-price, IMO.

_childDocuments_.review: I sought this game out because I played Graveyard Keeper and I loved it, and I wanted something similar. Bandle Tales is Graveyard Keeper mixed with League of Legends, which is perfect for me but not for everyone. Both Bandle Tales and Graveyard Keeper are just grinding simulators. The whole game is crafting to make upgrades to make more crafting. The atmosphere is great, story is engaging, and mechanics are smooth. Good amount of playtime - I finished the game with 100% achievements in 30 hours.No game is without its downsides, and I'd say the downsides are very similar to Graveyard Keeper so I was expecting them. Since this game is very grindy with multiple, long skill trees, you may find yourself a little lost in what you need to craft something. Or you work to get somewhere in the skill tree only to find out you need something else from another skill tree that you are very far away from. I did find myself in that place a couple times, There were also a couple visual bugs that I couldn't find a way to report. Overall, very positive experience. I loved this game, it was a treat!

_childDocuments_.review: I have never reviewed a game on Steam before, but I felt the need to with this title because I think it has not been given its fair shake.I *love* this game, and part of why I love it so much is that it defies expectations. What you think will be a laidback, cozy, crafting adventure turns into one of the most indepth titles I've explored in the genre.While the world itself is gorgeous and cutesy, the underlying systems are complex and puzzling and not for the faint of heart, particularly if you're not interested in figuring out how everything works in conjunction.There is some ingenuity and experimentation that the developers have instilled in this game that is not intuitive, and that can certainly be frustrating when you're uncertain what or how to do something. But I found puzzling everything through ultimately very rewarding and satisfying and by the end of the game I was sad it was over, and will now be in search of another title that is equal parts adorable and challenging.

Especially when the controls themselves don't get mentioned.Also got basically stuck in a very early quest on my first playthrough and had to restart as I used most of my Firefly Bulbs for fuel while experimenting with food. After I used 1 of my firefly bulbs I went to buy something from the store, so I spent most of my stars (money) there.  Game then forced me to continue on with quests since it seems more of a story game than anything like a chill crafter with any degree of freedom.As I continue with the quest I'm tasked with throwing a party, so I throw the first party but fail, because my 2nd Firefly bulb turns off midway through. So, we try again, I succesfully complete the party the 2nd go around, so I go to buy the button (goal of the quest). Turns out, the party doesn't give me enough money to be able to afford it, though I would've had enough if I hadn't spent my stars beforehand.Now I have no more stars, no more firefly bulbs and no way to get new firefly bulbs, this in turn making it impossible to throw another party (dishes require to be cooked), which in turn makes it impossible to make any more money, since it's impossible to make money, it's now impossible for me to progress further into the game since I cannot afford the button which is needed to progress.As far as i can tell, at the only maps you have access to at the point above, there's no way to collect more firefly bulbs.Game is gorgeous and looks really cozy and friendly (though Yuumi looks like a nightmare of herself). Conversations are pretty cute but not very diverse.Corki's plane goes down the first time you ride it, gotta wonder how he keeps it up in the Summoner's rift.A little dissapointed when coming from the creators of Graveyard keeper combined with the larger than life lore of League of legends and the summoners rift. Especially as graveyard keeper was such an amazing addition to this genre.would recommend this game at a 15eur price point, I think 25 is too much for the game as it stands.(love the art though, it's really great).It's basically a fetch quest with pretty environments simulator.

_childDocuments_.review: Short review if you are too lazy or busy to read the entire thing:Play it if you want to experience a story in Runeterras aka LoLs universe.Otherwise dont play it, its a really bad entry in its genreBeside it´s cute artstyle and characters the gameplay is just not up to parSo, I finished Bandle Tale maxing out all badges and finishing the story. So I feel qualified to give a proper review now.Let´s start with the positives:- The game is really cute- The story might not be the deepest but is fun to experience- The areas are well designed on an artistic level - The game expands upon the world of RuneterraSadly thats about everything that is really good about this gmae.So what was bad/unfun?- You are bombarded with information in the tutorial (this is because the game introduces all of its mechanics at the very start which feels really overwheliming and like bad pacing)- Auras (Auras are extremly important for crafting but unless you want to burn resources generating them with a building you permanently need to travel trough the world up to the point where you travel over 10 minutes for one item. This is because certain Auras are only available in certain areas which feels like it just exists to lengthen game time. I get that you dont have access to every Aura from the start and need to unlock some through story progression but not beeing able to make them resource free afterwards with the designated item feels just counterintuitiv.)- Certain mechanics are completly useless or feel like a drag (This revers primarly to cooking, which is forced upon you for story progresion, fishing, which is really good for nothing tbh, the university which is also definitly out of place and the vending machine which you maybe use one or two times if even. )- Achievments (You get blasted with them throughout the tutorial and the story gives you some on the way. Some you get for using the previously mentioned mechanics excessivly. And some for upgrading certain things like the house or the sprint to its maximum. So about 90% of "achievments" are "You played the game the intended way".)But one problem is the biggest for me: LATE GAMEWhy is it a problem? Quite simple it does not exist.After you throw the last party the game shows you the last 2 missions that you now completed, which are not saved and neither the reward for the party nor the rewards for the quests are given to you. I realised after the credits that I only used about half the skilltree, which makes me wonder why some of these skills even exist in the first place. As the game doesnt hand out any reward not even a achievment for maxing out the skilltrees, throwing every party once, holding every lecture, or maxing out your building capabilities it feels just useless to do these things. And it´s not like there were no possibilities for a late game either. Heimerdingers Labratory or Veigars Lair could have done something, or make a quest to repair the 4 big bridges, give the portal in the backpack an actual use, but sadly no effort was taken to even try to implement any form of late game or completion intuitiv. The game just goes "complete the story and leave" which is fine dont get me wrong, but why implement so many posibilities and not use them?Overall the game is mostly played for it´s connection to Runeterra but is fairly bad beyond that. It comes nowhere near games like stardew valley, graveyard keeper or forager. A lot of potential was in this game but sadly none of it was really put to use. Most of the gametime you are either stressed about routing or sleep skiping time for your craftings. Actual gameplay is miniscule and repetitive.So to put it in numbers:ART: 8/10MUSIC: 7/10STORY: 6/10GAMEPLAY: 2/10OVERALL: 3.5/10 which equivaltes to: mediocre at best

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, so here's a few things to get out the way:- If you've played Graveyard Keeper before, expect many of the same mechanics, with a different "look". If you really enjoyed it for the humour and not for the grindyness, this game is not for you.- If you hate the feel of "factory" games, in which items have a big production chain, this game is not for you.- If you expect anything related to League of Legends lore or extensive character development, this game is not for you.Essentially, the game has good visuals, interesting details with a multi-purpose base and some great ideas but the lack of instructions on a very complex game leads to a very frustrating experience. Even things like finding an NPC can be a chore and not clear on the map. Simple things like "I can buy from this vendor, but won't let me sell despite saying the item has sell value" could be explained from the get go, but don't. You have to stumble across those details. This happens over and over in this game.And don't bother looking online because at this point in time, there's barely any help/guides out there.The game does a good job with gameplay diversity in the sense that you have a few activities you can do within it, but then it "forces" you do to them to progress, which I disliked.Overall, the game can be enjoyable if you go in with the right mentality but for me, the grindyness and lack of direction on how to achieve something that seems simple just don't make much sense. For instance, the game has no combat and you are forced to upgrade your character's speed/stamina because... reasons. These kind of details feel like they are there just to enforce the grind.In the end, I wouldn't call it a "bad game" in any sense of the word but it is wasn't the experience I thought I would have when I bought.PS: Played it all the way through with 100% achievements... because I wanted to like it and had played too much to refund it to begin with :)

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not a fan.The first 10 hours were horrible. _childDocuments_.review: I teetered back and forth about buying this game due to some of the negative reviews. I bit the bullet when it was on sale and I do not regret it at all. It only took me about 24 hours to complete the main story and earn all achievements so it's not super long. This is made by the same team who made Graveyard Keeper and it shows. It is a grindy experience (though not as grindy as GK) but I enjoyed it.Bandle Tale is a very simple system of progression through four tech trees. Your character earns points by collecting (which only receives a substantial amount early on), crafting, and throwing parties. When you go to sleep, you will claim the points and be able to use them to unlock nodes in the tech trees. It personally took me a few hours to figure out that crafting and collecting was a terrible way to earn points. The best way is to throw parties. To do that, you need full bars of happiness and community. Best way to do that is through a food stand, though you can also get some points from vending. Once you have enough, you can throw a party. I saw some reviews criticizing the end game for forcing you to run to characters on opposite ends of the map and heavily relying on different auras to craft things. In my opinion... it really wasn't that bad. Travelling is made much easier by having an upgraded leg and stabilizing the portals so you can travel without a backpack and pay 0 portal yarn. Another tip - put your backpack in strategic locations that have pre-exisiting auras. You can also stack auras. Two Motion I auras in Bandle Center will make a Motion II aura. If I had to make some criticisms of Bandle Tale, one is that I never had to unlock all the tech. For example, I never unlocked the mech bugs or ice cream/freezer tech and was able to complete the game. I'm not sure what they were even for. And this isn't a criticism per say, but there are SO many parties you can throw and you will never throw most of them. And while I don't think the end game was hard or annoying, I did find it to be a bit lackluster. In any case, it's a great game on sale or not, and people who enjoyed GK will definitely enjoy this (except you might miss the superior humor of the GK characters lol).

_childDocuments_.review: It's a cute little game where you play as a yordle. Charming little Pixel graphics, the game isn't very difficult by any real stretch. _childDocuments_.review: Pros:* Fun and cute* Focus on crafting and quest progressionCons:* Bugs galore* Skill tree is really imbalanced - many skills you unlock require LATER skills in order to use * Grindy* No automation* Hope you like pressing ESummary:Fun cute game that would be so much better if bugs were fixed and the skill tree rebalanced correctly.This is NOT what I would consider a slow life "Stardew Valley" like game. This game is actually quest progression focused with a story and consists of a lot of gathering and crafting to progress.  That's not a bad thing at all - except the lack of automation really starts to become apparent. There's not enough space to create a "proper" layout (even after upgrades) to allow all machines all functionality, so you constantly have to demolish/move/rebuild stations in order to make the crafts needed. This is also on top of having to pick up your home and move it around - often times to gain access to certain auras needed that don't exist in certain zones. This means there's just a ton of time spent prepping just to make things, which is what the game is all about.There's a ton of display bugs in the skill tree that make progression confusing at times. But that's the least of its problems. The skill tree balance is really bad. There are 4 main "trees", and it doesn't take long before you start unlocking skills that require other skills much deeper in the other trees. It's not bad to have related skills, but many of these are behind "gates" that are further in the main questline than others. For a simple analogy, it would be like unlocking a level 10 craft that requires a skill you don't unlock until you do a level 20 quest. It can be frustrating but overall it's still fun. But the game would be so much better with just a bit more quality control and balancing of the game, along with some ways to make it a bit less grindy and/or constant E clicking.
_childDocuments_.name: Bandle Tale: A League of Legends Story

_childDocuments_.review: Very cute game from developers with a unique and good sense of humour, I love their other game graveyard keeper. It has a complicated crafting and skill system that I like a lot. However, this is a game that comes from an indie developer who could use more playtesting with actual players to streamline systems. This is evident in the way they've set up festivals and how to serve food, its hard to understand what to do and how to do it the first time. I had to start over to be able to understand how the system works (hint: get two ovens to make food) To navigate the character between areas there are often small bridges and the amount of times my character gets stuck behind a little unnecessary design is frustrating but its not a 60 euro game so I can live with it.

_childDocuments_.review: To say this was a good game would be an understatement. This game is a testament that Riot for years has been sitting on lots of potential, but refused to act upon it, instead working on another game that barely got them anywhere. For years I've loved the yordles due to their natural ability to be social, to be friends and to despite all odds, be able to live among each other without the human concepts that would ruin the whole yordle society.Humanity needs to learn from this game that we could had been better. But sadly, a pipe dream that will never be accomplished. With years wishing to see and wonder the life of these adorable happy creatures, I finally found a game I can truly call home. A game that gives me joy and wonder. To go beyond the miniscule requirements for achievements.Just wish this game had more, or even a modding option. But with Riot Forge dead, this is as far as we'll get.So if you want several hours of peace in crafting, look no further than this game. I actually was able to smile for the first time in years, playing this game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is SO much fun it is shocking to me that it isn't more popular. _childDocuments_.review: I wanted to give this one some time based on some of the other reviews. I love it so far but there are definitely critiques that I would make. Getting XP during some points is difficult, but I don't think it's impossible or like you need to grind for it for an extended time. The skill trees frustrate me sometimes because you need have certain things unlocked in order to use certain skills but they can't be unlocked until much later which if you aren't paying attention can really screw you over. Main recommendations:Sleep and bank your XP as often as you can.Lectures and Fishing are a great way to get more XP.If you are short on XP for a skill tree unlock try preping materials you might need once you have it unlocked.Make sure you see if there are other skills you might need on other trees before you unlock a new skill.Invest in every part of the game - farming, cooking, vending, lectures, parties, etc.Bring your bag with you - I can't tell you how many times I have just wandered away to do one little thing and ended up having to run back to grab it so I can hop to 3 different spots.Main disappointments:I wish there was more side quests that you could unlock without cooking (just on the map exploring or in other ways).No Romance is kind of a bummer but I get that not every cozy game needs it.Main loves:Progression is not always linear - (which could be a con for some people) I enjoy having to think about what I want to work towards that seems fun and also what I should work towards for story progression.No timer - I am not stuck two islands away from my bed and only minutes from passing out and losing money or things.It is easy to expand storage/send things to a drop box if you are out of space.Over all I think they made some QOL improvements to the standard cozy game format. There are some aspects that I miss, like a romance element. I think the people who stated they struggled with having enough XP are valid, but I think taking your time and investing in each aspect of the "economy," for lack of a better term, would make that feel like less of an issue. I partially wish that the skill tree was a little more thought out maybe even just one big one rather than 4 smaller ones, since they do relate in occasionally frustrating ways. However, I am still having a lot of fun with it and I still look forward to having time to play it at the end of the day.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, I wanted to like this. Graveyard keeper is one of my favourite games. But I just can't. Let's break this down:1. Craft system on its own is very good and interesting. There are some flaws, e.g. recharging a battery/ribbon on a billionth time is tad bit boring. But with some polishing it could be very good. It is literally the only part of the game that has some improvements over graveyard keeper.2. There is just too much intermediate items and too few interconnected space for crafting machines. You have to move them around constantly for arrangements that would allow to do the crafting. Basically it turns into an annoying minigame.3. On that matter, minigames. They are an essential and annoying part of the game-play loop. There are several of them. Party, feeding, fishing and moving the ♥♥♥♥ around your house. Each is annoying and dumb. Game has a dedicated mechanic that forces you to repeat feed-party loop as it is an optimal way to farm research.4. Late-game is ultra-grind. Virtually nothing is automatable or optimizable. You just have to repeat the same trivial actions for a thousand times in a row to achieve something.5. Dialogues are completely idiotic. It feels like they are targeted at preschoolers. I did expect that since it is a LoL game, but it is still annoying. Characters are bland and forgettable. None of them is interesting or unique. Just a lot of boring phrases copied all over the place.6. You have to walk around for what feels like an eternity. Walking around can feel nice when it happens in huge area full of content. This game offers 5 tiny maze-like islands, where NPCs constantly send you to talk to someone in another part of the map.7. Visual design is full of some abstract art, which is very strange for a game targeting four year olds. I just do not get it and it annoys me on its own. Personally I also find it extremely ugly overall, but that is not an objective critique.

_childDocuments_.review: To start off, this is a lovely game that comes out to about 30 hours of playtime if you focus on the story and do the side quests along the way.This game has a cute art style and I love all of the characters and how each one was an important part of the story! It does have similar vibes to Stardew Valley as far as being a cozy game, but it is not a game where you can keep farming as long as you want. It's an RPG, so the whole basis will be the quests which are driven by fetch quests and gathering/crafting certain items. I would recommend it to anyone who enjoys League of Legends lore and characters from the game, but also just general cozy gamers who love a cute story. There are times where the game felt "challenging" but the core part of the game are throwing festivals/food stands, so as long as you focus on that, you'll always have enough points to go through the skill trees. Biggest piece of advice I can give is to ALWAYS take your backpack with you everywhere and collect items along the way as you see them, upgrading the inventory for me early was a huge help. If you feel like you're struggling to succeed in the parties/food stands, look into upgrading your Leg and your festival decorations. Also selling items for Stars will give you a huge help as there are vendors that sell various items that can be helpful.I hope everyone enjoys the game as much as I did <3

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game for Teemo and after 5 hours there is still no TeemoIn all seriousness, this game starts out really cute. The art style is fun and whimsical, the characters cute, and the game-play feels very cozy and lighthearted. However, this starts to wear off. The story dialogue gets long and tedious, and I find myself just speed clicking to get through it. The crafting isn't entirely intuitive, and I have spent too much time in the menus trying to figure out where the heck the thing I need for the mission is. It feels like I have to unlock multiple things for each quest objective, and to unlock those things you need to sit and grind meaningless days. This was not the case in the beginning, where things felt much faster paced. But now at a bit over 5 hours and being maybe? close to done with the second island everything feels like a chore. Some items take a while to craft, and when you are crafting 5+ things to do everything it gets tiring. The game is starting to feel cluttered as the amount of workbenches needed keep going up, and I am running around to each one trying to find what I need. Overall, it is a very cute game with some subpar UI and too much grinding once you get past the beginning. I would still recommend it, but with the forewarning that it will get a bit tedious.

_childDocuments_.review: I've never played League of Legends but I love cozy non-combat games. Bandle Tale has adorable graphics and no combat so thought I'd give it a try.  It's unlike any other farming/sim game I've played so far. It's definitely not Stardew Valley! There is farming, but it is only one part of the game. This is a narrative driven linear style crafting game. It has a few mini games too. One is a more relaxed version of popular cooking games where you serve customers what they order. It's one of the ways you can get skill points. There's a large skill tree where you spend these points to unlock new recipes and abilities as you progress. There's tons to do, see, and discover. The world is beautiful and I am very much enjoying everything so far. Looking forward to what is yet to come.

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this game so much that I purchased the physical collector’s edition from Riot for my birthday! I can’t wait to receive it! So I bought it on Steam summer sale and another copy, that’s how much i love it!This is a very repetitive manual labor farming system with fetch quests. You won’t learn everything in a hour gameplay, but everything makes sense the longer you play. No need for guides. It won’t hold your hand. _childDocuments_.review: Ever since this game was announced to be in the works, I have been waiting for its release. I am somewhat disappointed with the game. I was enjoying it at first, but eventually I was just speedrunning to the end because I wanted 100% steam achievements. The main issues I have with this game are as follows:1. It's poorly explained how to make progression in the early stages. There's so much information being dumped all at the beginning and there's no way to access it after reading, so if you can't remember it then you're stuck. 2. It gets very repetitive very quickly. There's so much grinding and running back and forth. The one thing that would have improved this game dramatically is the use of an item checklist or a better way to view which materials are required for crafting. Otherwise, you're just running in circles between islands because there's bound to be one material you forgot.3. Quests are all the same. You talk to NPC, they ask you to craft an ever increasing list of items / workstations, host a party, progress to next story stage. A greater variety of tasks would have been nice, Overall, the game is cute and there were some funny one-liners. It's chill but gets boring very fast, and it's no surprise that only 1.6% of people have completed the story so far.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR; I like the game overall but it feels a little rough around the edges in many ways that I don't think ruin the game for me but definitely impede gameplay and can ruin the game for others. It is not sandbox but it's not also completely railroaded where you can only do the current task and nothing else. The Yordle lore and personalities are enjoyable to see as an LoL player and I imagine they'll be good for non-LoL players. Overall, the game feels inviting to play and once you understand the gameplay loop it can be a game where you kinda turn your brain off and just enjoy it, but it isn't the easiest to get there because the instructions and UI are rather clunky. I do recommend it to anyone who likes "cozy games" because it feels good to exist in Bandle City with the combined graphics and art style--just be warned that it may have a learning curve.~~I've already played through about half the game based on skill tree and achievement progression. I really like the game but there are some glaring issues that I just can't look past.Overall, the game lacks clarity. I'm not the sharpest tool in the shed but the game seems to enjoy not helping you learn its mechanics. Most tutorials are given very early on during your first instance of doing something and they are rarely expanded upon after. You can replay the tutorials but more intricate parts of the gameplay are not explained in them nor is it explained how some of the gameplay features interact. I started to realize the more I played that I was only going through the motions and didn't really know what half the UI meant or how to raise the level of a meter in the bottom of the screen. I didn't fully understand the gameplay loop until about ~12 hrs in, and not for a lack of trying. I think the choppiness of the story (the main feature of the game) also added to it. I'd fully read dialogue and then complete a task and then be completely confused at how the next couple parts of the quest made any sense. I believe good quest design is rooted in a functional flow the player can follow along with and partially predict but some of these made zero sense to me. While it feels like I pointed out a large portion of the game as being red flags, I still think it is a very fun game.The storyline itself is cute and makes sense for the most part and is incentive enough for me to continue playing. The dialogue is fun and witty and not too long in the tooth. Coming from LoL, all the characters look, feel, and sound like their LoL counterparts; though the game does lack VA in everything but the cinematics and I think more inclusion of it would have benefited the overall feel of the game. The art style is perfectly whimsical and all the character sprites, even of basically unnamed NPCs, look fantastic and full of personality. I'm personally pretty happy with how Veigar turned out because he looks more like a whimsical evil Yordle than a ball of evil energy in a coat and hat. Despite how good the full body sprites are, I think most of the portraits for the LoL characters are horrifying. They have too much detail in the wrong places and characters like Tristana wind up looking old and sleep deprived. The MC looks perfectly unremarkable though which makes for a better focus on storyline though I wish there were some more creative customization options. The set design is also some of my favorite in gaming. The worlds seem to exist in a vast expanse of sky which just feels so cozy to me--it's like a surrealist painting where you feel distinctly somewhere but don't know where that is exactly. There's a great sense of space and no area feels too full or too empty. One of my favorite design features is the use of optical illusions in the terrain and I will forever want that in more games. I'm not that invested in the soundtrack of most games but this one definitely has great ambiance and fitting tracks of each game feature/task. I wouldn't rank it among games like Nier Automata or Outer Wilds but it does its job and really enhances the experience.I will for sure be playing this to completion but I do want to give some running feedback to any potential buyers who are on the fence. I can definitely see how this game could be frustrating to learn for some and not worth it but I do think the world, characters, and story are worth giving a whirl.

_childDocuments_.review: Despite being very excited for the game, I ended up requesting a refund. I was just expecting a lot more for a game that is $25 at full price and I was foolish to think that this game would instantly be good for an official League of Legends game created by the people behind Graveyard Keeper.The pixel art is beautiful. The story and worldbuilding has a lot of charm to it.However, Bandle Tale is an empty game that lacks player freedom.My biggest criticisms that lead to me refunding:- The grind is too much, not fun, and a straight path that you can't meander from. There is no player freedom when it comes to finishing quests. When you hobble around Bandle Tale to accomplish your fetch quest, there is nothing to do except to walk painfully slow from one side of the island to the other to try and find the materials you need. The biggest problem is that it's all a straight shot. There is no secret paths to wander off to and explore, all NPCs you encounter only have a SINGLE line of dialogue, and the beautifully drawn world is just so empty.- It is counter intuitive to have a game that is relaxing 99% of the time but also has the most stressful cooking minigame with the tightest timer in the world. - Lack of player freedom. I think a simulation game can be boring and can be slow-paced so long as there is player freedom. A slow game can be excellent if you just let your player meander and take their time building or customizing. Beyond the initial character customization, there is nothing to customize or really do in Bandle Tale. You can choose where to put down stuff in your home/shops but not only are there predetermined spots to put things down, but everything you put down has a function. There are "correct" places to put them down to maximize efficiency. It's not really customization from a base/house building point of view.- Resources having respawn time was just not a fun choice in a game where there is nothing to do but the main quest. There is nothing for players to do during respawn time except to wait. Players don't have side quests or secrets to go find during this time.Overall, this might be the game for you if you LOVE Yordles and you don't mind a game that is slow and lacks freedom.No matter who you are, I would definitely wait for a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to enjoy this game, but it really isn't fun at all. There are so many problems.The story is straight up bad, with caricature character and long written dialogues every few minutes.The main mechanic of this game you will experience is walking. You need a resource? Be ready waste an entire minute just walking back and forth to harvest it. Need to get some item from the shop? No problem, it's just placed in the most inconvenient place possible. Need to progress in a quest? That's your lucky day, you will have to talk to several characters on the opposite side of the map! Want to get XP you worked for? Come back to your home for no reason. Just waste more time to get your XP you have already worked for. Yes, I know there is a fast travel, but it's not free and you have to farm to use it, which defeats the whole point of fast travel. Oh you want to gather resources faster? Just waste more time to save a little bit of time in the future.The game feels very raw and unfinished from the gameplay side. Map should have been more concentrated, timers shorter and sleep mechanic could have been skipped completely, inventory management is a joke, everything is slowing you down in the most boring way possible. I feel like Snake climbing the ladder every time I have to harvest some remote resource.I like "job games", I have 1000 hours on Warframe after all, but this game doesn't let me play it, it instead makes all the fun things locked behind timewasting activities. Timers, walking, having to manage my inventory, having to save XP, having to wait for the event to be available again. If a mechanic is completely pointless, why putting it in the first place? It would be so much better if there was no inventory, no need to sleep every two minutes and long timers on things.On the positive side, I like the art-style and the game itself doesn't seem to have any bugs and is decently coded

The cutscenes have very awkward pauses, usually between the actions or at the start where you just watch a character walk slowly for a few seconds. And why do you need to press and hold to get the item from the machine? It already has been crafted! At first I treated this game like Stardew as "open world", free play, farming/crafting game - and found myself VERY frustrated with the grinding halt the game came too... the second save I played as an XP farm making unlocking the skill tree a priority.. and the progression of the game went fast. Personally, I found that this course took away from the story and made the adventure feel flat. Partying and Catering are pretty important aspects of the game, but the small internal room you get for food production is ample for supporting your magical food craft... If you are looking for a Stardew clone, this is probably not what you are looking for as it had a very "closed/railroaded feel" .. but if you are interested in Graveyard Keeper... this is a cute intro into what to expect for gameplay.
