_childDocuments_.review: Bandle Tale is a good game and it's disheartening to see that it hasn't attracted more players.Seeing that more than 90% of the people who bought it played it, but less than 10% have seen the end of it makes me think that maybe they were not ready for such a mind-boggling game (I wasn't).First and foremost, this is my first time playing this type of game. There are a few walls throughout the game, and if you're not ready and don't really understand how this all work, they're steep and hard to climb. Ngl, I used a guide to get through the most mind-boggling parts of the game. At the beginning, Bandle Tale holds your hand very tightly and keeps somewhat holding it throughout the adventure, and this is maybe worse than letting us strive for ourselves. Since I didn't need to understand all the mechanics of the game to progress, I breezed through it until a wall spawned before me and prevented me from going forward. And in front of this wall, I was left alone, there wasn't much guidance provided (if any). Still, I managed (thank you unknown person who took the time to write a guide) to see the end of it, and it's probably entirely due to how cute and soothing the game is otherwise. There is no time pressure, you're free to go at your own pace, enjoy side activities, talk to any and ever yordle around, it's really enjoyable. The story is simple, it conveys all the goodness expected from yordles. The different parts of Bandle all have their own identity and atmosphere, and they're all likable. The pixel art design and the colours used also fit well together.In the last 20% or so, I've felt as if the game was overall less polished, a few typos, things that would not update immediately, etc., but nothing game-breaking, really mere inconveniences.I would have liked some free play after the final cutscene, I still had much more to do and it would have felt better to not have to reload a previous save to finish it.Someone experienced in this type of games may take less than 20h to finish it, but as a newcomer to the genre, it took me a bit more.

_childDocuments_.review: [bold]Basically a whimsical Graveyard Keeper 2.0[/bold]This game was created by the same team that made Graveyard Keeper, and it really shows. Big improvements have been made in terms of getting around more easily and managing your inventory, both of which were lacking the GK series. An effort was made to make things more intuitive, as well.I never had to look anything up in a wiki, but I did spend quite a bit of time scrolling through talent trees to try to find the one thing I needed to progress. It also took a little bit of time to figure out how to reliable gain skill points, but once you get the hang of it, this is handled in a better way than the similar mechanic used in GK.The game took me about 30 hours to complete the game, which I feel is worth what I paid for it. The aura system makes the crafting system more interesting, and it's fun to try to create a "chain" of machines that interact appropriately with each other.The only downside for me is the ending, which is abrupt and impermanent. By that I mean that after the ending credits, you're returned to the title screen and have to reload from your last save point, which means you can never actually complete the game and check off that final quest. There are also a few endgame threads that feel unfinished. Overall, I'd say if you like games like Stardew Valley, Graveyard Keeper, etc., you'll like this one, too.

_childDocuments_.review: As a league of legends player, and cozy game enthusiast I was very excited to try this game. After completing the game I personally felt I got my money's worth. $25 USD for 34 hours, and while I definitely could have been faster I took my time and enjoyed the game. There were a couple times where I had to look for a guide to progress and I feel like there could have been clearer tutorials or quest markers built in game. There is 0 end game or replayability in this game. I had no trouble getting every achievement and didn't need to go out of my way to pursue any. However I don't think that's really a bad thing. It was cute and I'd love to keep playing but it's also nice to have an end to the game and to not have to remember to check back in or spend money on new content.Personally I don't have an issue with the price of the game, it felt absolutely worth the money and the art style is amazing and reminds me of old pixel art games of the past. However, because it's a completed singleplayer game you can wait for a sale anytime.I would recommend this game to anyone. _childDocuments_.review: If you like crafting games (especially cozy crafting games), you will likely enjoy this game. The first time I played this game, I didn't set it down for 9 hours. It is very engaging if you like to craft and explore. However, if you want automation or city management, this is not the game for you. this is about crafting.  There are some puzzles / order of operations issues, and PLENTY of exploration as well.  And a tech tree that would make Civilization fans salivate. But this game is ultimately about crafting/exploring with some quirky social mechanics (you throw parties and have to set up the party correctly to have good vibes....yeah, game was obvi made by Gen Z, let's be real xD).  It has good length (about 25 hours for the main story, maybe 35-40 for all side quests and 100%ing the game). I love the game. There are lots of achievements to hunt for, LOTS of fun and engaging crafting mechanics, and the NPC humor is very Yordle. If you have an itch to craft and explore, check out the game!Gamplay: 8.5/10Visuals: 8/10Sound/Music: 9/10Overall: 8.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: i like it. it's fun and relaxing and super cute. i heard most people complained it's grindy but i never have a problem because i spend way too much time over gathering supplies and trying to craft like 20 of everything before moving forward with the story. so when i DO move forward with the story i get like 50 unlocks in the skill trees easy peasy xDYou get to make your own yordle character instead of playing as an existing character in the League of Legends universe, which I thought was a nice touch.I think it's very genre specific. If you're not into cozy, slow games that are mostly just cutesy, this might not be for you. If you're into League of Legends lore, and really want to be immersed in the Runeterra universe, this one is a cute peek into the mystical yordle world. It's very reminiscent of what the fey realm could be like if you're into D&D. There's easter eggs and some yordle cameos.I also heard people complain about the full price of the game. I personally supported it on release because I was sad that this is the last game that Riot Forge will ever release. The size of the world and the game itself makes up for the price, and since it's definitely my favorite game genre, the price wasn't a big deal to me personally. But I understand that since League of Legends itself is a free to play game [skin purchases aside] some of the people coming from the client advertisements might balk at the price.I haven't finished the game yet or explored all of the map areas, but I liked it enough to review it and recommend it.Post game review:It was fun, I liked the story. My only gripe is that after you finish the game it sets you back to whenever the last time you saved the game was before the "final party."So make sure you save right before ending I guess? Also, you can get all achievements without having to unlock all the skill trees and badges, but to me that feels like it's not actually a completionist game lol.Even taking my time and crafting a lot of everything I could, I still needed 103 more purple orbs to completely finish all skill trees. And even though the final quest gives you 100 orbs as a reward, since you don't get to save after the final cutscene, it never actually gives it to you.I don't think there's any post game. Nothing changes after you "beat" it and from what I can tell there's a few portals [one in a backpack pocket, and one near Dr. Nestor's hideout] that are never really used. In the map it looks like bandle center has a section you can never explore. So there's that.Uncertain if Riot Forge just pulled the plug slightly early on it, or if LazyBeargames just didn't get to do everything they wanted to with the time they were given, but it was still a worthwhile game with 40+ hours of play.

_childDocuments_.review: Strap in, folks, because  is the crafting RPG that's here to tickle your funny bone, test your patience, and maybe, just maybe, steal your heart—assuming you can get past the crafting conundrum that'll have you questioning your life choices. 🤔✨ The game's art is so stunning, it'll make your eyes pop out of your head—and not in a horror movie way. We're talking pixel perfection that'll have you screenshotting every two minutes because "OMG, look how cute that Yordle is!" 📸 Imagine needing a thingamajig to create a whatchamacallit to finally craft that doohickey you've always wanted. Welcome to Crafting 101 in Bandle Tale, where the crafting chain is longer than your grocery list during quarantine. 📝 Ever dreamed of being an adorable creature with customizable fur and ears that defy gravity? Dream no more! Bandle Tale lets you live out your fluffiest fantasies, complete with sparkly trails as you sprint. Because if you're going to save the world, you might as well do it with style. 💃 The dialogue is so witty, you'll find yourself chuckling at references only the truest of League of Legends fans would understand. It's like being part of an exclusive club, but with more Yordles and less secret handshakes. 🤝 Just when you thought you'd crafted it all, Bandle Tale says, "Hold my beer." You'll craft, and craft, and then craft some more, until you start dreaming in crafting recipes. It's the Inception of crafting games, with more layers than a lasagna. 🍝 Imagine planning a party that's more stressful than your actual day job. You've got a countdown timer, a list of demands, and a crowd of Yordles who are hard to please. If you thought your last birthday party was a logistical nightmare, Bandle Tale's party system is here to say, "Hold my elixir." 🍹 Sometimes, you'll find yourself on a quest for a specific item that feels like searching for a needle in a haystack. Except the haystack is made of needles, and you're not entirely sure the needle you're looking for even exists. 🌾🔍If you're the kind of gamer who thrives on crafting, loves a good lore-filled laugh, and doesn't mind getting lost in a rabbit hole of resource gathering, then  is your ticket to a magical world you won't want to leave.But, if the thought of more crafting makes you want to craft a letter of resignation to the gaming gods, then you might want to sit this one out. Or, dive in for the dialogue and stay for the sheer absurdity of it all. 🎭In the end,  is a rollercoaster ride of emotions, packed with enough charm, challenge, and chortles to keep you hooked. Just remember, in Bandle City, the biggest adventure might just be figuring out how to craft that next item on your list. Happy crafting, Yordles! 🚀✨

_childDocuments_.review: This game isn’t for everyone, and perhaps the cozy game advertisement wasn’t the best angle to promote it with; regardless, if you’re the same type of gamer as me, I recommend it. Contrary to initial impressions, Bandle Tale is more a game about “management” than a social sim, so don’t enter expecting something like an endless farming sim. It has clear objectives and everything in core gameplay centers around management, be it of skill points, resources, or “events” (planning your parties and your food stands). If you’re a nerd like me and draw enjoyment from trying to make everything as efficient as possible, you’ll have fun with this aspect. Another way you can enjoy it is if you don’t stress and don’t mind that things are slow to make, just playing the game easy-going.The food stand and party events are hectic, working similarly to those waitress simulation flash games of yore; you have to prepare food and serve it real-time, and need to account for your inventory before even starting (run out of plates and it throws you off balance). With more complex recipes, it can get frantic fast; during parties, you’re supposed to take… happiness? Fun? From your guests, as a number of points, with you needing to meet a threshold within a time limit. Again, this too can get hectic with bigger parties. I personally enjoyed the decision process of checking what my party guests want and how to make the decorations, dishes, etc. Plenty.The rest, the resource management aspect, is all about you improving your skills, machines, and processes to get materials for the party and food stand events, and for quests. A lot of it boils down to decisions; which skill to improve? You must review your skill tree constantly and adjust and better your equipment. Again, a lot of the enjoyment here is derived from you trying to make the process as streamlined as possible and it all “clicking” together with a sequence of decisions. I will give the game criticism that some of the difficulty feels more like wanting to pad the game for more gameplay time than organically building up on the mechanics. Fast travel requires currency, which is kind of annoying in a game so dependent on you going from one place to the other to gather materials for different crafts; unless you have a lot of this currency, you’ll feel like you’re wasting time just walking; so if you enjoy the game I suggest you throw the first party, which rewards you with portal yarn (the aforementioned currency), every so often. The game later gives you a way to permanently “stabilise” portals, removing this requisite, but at that point you’re close to the end game, which leaves you disappointed it wasn’t introduced earlier on. And some of the later crafts, machine improvements, and items for quests have several steps and pre requisites, some of which involve waiting. And though the game lets you sleep, which passes time and expedits the wait for several of these processes, later on some take even longer than your “naps”. This can be frustrating. Another criticism is the learning curve. Your first hours with the game involve many tutorials, some of which are just text with diagrams, and many of which I feel could be more detailed, especially when you’re being introduced to new mechanics. I have noticed several people in the Steam Discussion pages have questions I myself had and had to re-check (the game, fortunately, gives you a Tutorials tab in the pause menu where you can return and check them). I feel like the game could be more specific with the descriptions of certain quests and the introductions to new mechanics. My suggestion to make your time with it easier is to check the Steam Discussion page. On the visual and auditory level, this game is gorgeous. The spritework is detailed and colorful, the shaders when your character walks around illuminated areas are beautiful, the backgrounds change in unique and pretty ways when you move region to region and weather changes (sunset and dawn, rain) and though the soundtrack has plenty of the same leitmotif, this is so that the music changes diegetically when you move from one environment to the other, day becomes night, weather conditions change and events happen. The animations are surprisingly meticulous considering the pixel art style, and have a great amount of character; lots of key NPCs as well as all the League of Legends champions have distinct dance animations and a jump animation you see in parties when you collect their “happiness points”. I also found the noises and visuals of making things, operating machines, and brushing your poro very satisfying. The game highlights its visuals with a mechanic where your character takes a moment to breathe and observe a pretty landscape in Bandle City. These moments are really pleasant.Character customization is a bit more limited than I’d want, but not bad. House customization also offers beautifully rendered options. The game also has accessibility with colors for several types of colour blindness. No complaints on this regard.I got this game as a present because I’m a massive yordle fan, big enough I got gifted the Collector’s Edition. Learning more about the very overlooked region of Bandle and interacting with the champions was basically my core motivation to get the game, And I’m simultaneously pleased with it and not…? The game, joyously, has more story than I expected it to. There’s a surprising amount of turns, and even some red herrings! It’s packed with humor and wholesomeness but doesn’t shy away from a bit of mystery. It keeps in line with the generally bright tone of Bandle City that Riot has established; the champions are written in a really charming way, and their interactions between themselves and your character are pure joy to watch if you’re like me and love them. Though I was very happy about that, something that irked me was that the champions aren’t very interactable outside of quest objectives which was especially disappointing precisely because when they interact, it’s so fun to watch, and I was left craving a bit more. I wish more rotating “filler” lines were incorporated, cause it did get a little monotonous when NPCs would repeat the exact same line from when you finished a quest hours ago. One or two other lines to alternate with would have been nicer. I also wish there was more interactability with them in the matter of side quests; the entire game really centers around doing favours for your friends, it would have been nice to be able to do additional quests for your favorite champions, or befriend them a bit closer. I also think that could have added some replayability. I, however, have no complaints with the writing itself.  Honestly, as a yordle fan who enjoys management, I enjoyed this game. I enjoyed the developments of the story and seeing my backpack house grow and my skills improve, I really enjoyed the party and food stand mechanics, I loved the champion interactions and think this game is a great glimpse into Bandle City. It’s just definitely geared toward a specific type of gamer, and could use a bit more polish. I’d recommend it to other people in my same page. If you don’t really care about the characters previously, it may not be for you. Not because the story makes no sense if you don’t know about League, but because arriving to it with previous knowledge of the characters makes it more enjoyable.

_childDocuments_.review: If you want a cozy game with pixel graphics and like games like Stardew Valley, this is a good choice. The story is good, you have to do various things and it keeps you quite busy.The game has a playtime of about 25-30 hours, especially if you want to unlock all the achievements (which you can get in one playthrough, because most of them are unlocked through the story anyway).Those who complain about the grinding and XP are only partly right. Yes, sometimes it feels that way, but if you skill the things you need for the quests first (they're labelled with a little question mark) and then stick to the story and diligently collect everything and craft things until you run out of XP (purple orbs), you'll be fine. If you complete the readings at the fountain in Bandle City, organise parties (for which you get skill points) and cook for the Yordels, you'll make very good progress. I ended up with over 130 skill points and a fully unlocked skill tree. I also recommend always making sure that the skill orbs are not completely full, as you can lose skill points if you keep collecting them because the orbs are already fully charged. So always go back to sleep to collect them and only then continue looting.

_childDocuments_.review: I have played League of Legends since it first came out and did not buy any of the other Riot Forge games. This one appealed to me because I'm an avid fan of farm & crafting sims... plus, just look at it! It's adorable. Overall, I have a lot of criticisms of the game, but honestly - I liked it. I liked being able to play a light hearted game about some of my favorite Yordles and learn a little more about Bandle City. I had fun with the fishing, cooking, and party mini-games, but most of all I had fun trying to break my brain on crafting - since it's not always apparent how to get the appropriate combination of things you need, especially early on. There are some different avenues, that make it a bit puzzle like... for example, should you go to THIS map for THIS aura to help with THAT item, or should you instead craft that other item which gives you that aura, go to this other location to get the thing needed for THAT aura, and well.. you get it. It's an endless rabbit hole, with some twists and turns. I'm not saying it's super complicated, but you will need to use some brain power at times to get a certain craft done. If you enjoy casual, crafting type grindy games, you will definitely enjoy this title.I will say that if I had no past knowledge of League of Legends... well, I'd still probably buy this - though maybe not for full price.- Again... adorable!- Environment details are rich and exciting. It feels like a lot of love went into the map designs. They're sprinkled with little creatures, unique plants, and stunning backgrounds.- Character models are eh... The unique characters from League of Legends look true to their name and are well designed; however, I cannot say the same for the regular townsfolk and the player character. You get to customize your character at the start (and can do so again by visiting your bed), but the options are uninspired and bland. I would have loved more choices (there were only about 4 ear shapes, maybe 8 hair styles, and then the rest of the options are color only). If you are going to give the option to customize your character, please make it count or instead offer us a visually interesting design that cannot be customized. I sometimes find myself losing my character amongst the rest of the NPCs visually. There are a very few NPCs that have a slightly unique hairstyle, facial hair, or height outside of the original League of Legend yordles.- Even though the visuals for the league characters were on point, I was disappointed in the writing of them. Very little lore seemed tied in, even though there is a plethora of it. Their personalities also just didn't shine through for me, except for maybe Veiger and Lulu slightly.- Beautiful music!- A little lackluster on ambiance sounds- I wish they'd used some of the voice lines from the league characters to give them more life and personality. I understand this may be something that Riot would not allow them to do.The game is super chill, relaxing, and cute, but that does come at a price. Repetitiveness. Your days mostly consist of:- Performing crafting, gathering, or "event" type actions until your EXP orbs are full- Sleeping to consume the EXP orbs and unlock skills within the various skill trees (which typically unlock more crafting, gathering, or "event" type actions with some exceptions)- Rinse & repeatThe crafting itself is not interactive. Check what items and ingredients you need for a quest, check which skills in your tree need to be unlocked to proceed with said crafting, grind experience as needed, craft your item (no mini games for crafting, only cooking, fishing & parties), complete your quest and move to the next one. I will say though, that it hasn't become boring to me yet and for some reason I enjoy the monotony - and, strangely enough, I got super into trying to be as efficient as possible when crafting higher level recipes. For example, you need auras to craft certain things. Sometimes, these only appear on specific maps and you'll need to go there to utilize the aura to craft. Other times, you'll need to craft an item to create the aura you need, in conjunction with a different aura. It's like doing simple quantum physics. OK, well, maybe not exactly like that, but you get my drift hopefully. You can also choose to expend you hard earned stars to acquire some of the materials you'll need, or a specific map might have crafting equipment you can utilize to be even MORE efficient!I won't go into much detail for the parties, fishing, or cooking - they're simple, fun mini games that you've probably experienced in mobile games at one point. I was actually wondering if they were intending to port this to mobile.Could have been better, but isn't terrible by any means and I truly love the knitting theme. The story mostly makes sense and is easy to follow along to. I feel like the target audience was far younger than I was expecting from a League of Legends based game (and from the creators of Grave Keeper). This threw me off a bit. The writing level goes anywhere from 7/8 year olds to early teens. Being 34 years old, this was a little unsettling at first, but kind of reminded me of Little Big Planet. Its been a wholesome, family friendly ride so far.- UI is pretty! But sometimes lacking in detail for player comprehension- Quests containing linked out words to needed skills is very helpful- Please... PLEASE give us some more options for utilizing the mouse AND keyboard instead of only the keyboard for much of the game. My left hand gets so tired, and sometimes I want to keep playing while taking a swig of a drink or eating a snack, but I can't, because you can only move & interact with WASD+E, but only click through dialogue with the mouse (that I know of). - Speaking of the dialogue... it seems to have no rhyme or reason. It seems to, by default, automatically proceed without the user having to left click; however, sometimes it just stops and never continues on to the next bit of text. There is also no option to TURN OFF auto-dialogue, so I can't like... turn my eyes away from the screen while talking to ANYONE because I'll miss text if I do.- Give me some flipping way to sort my inventory. For a game with a  massive amount of ingredients and crafts, please give me bigger chests (maybe there are some later? Iunno, I'm 20 hours in right now) and a way to sort my inventory into chests and out of chests. This is a huge pain point for me. I've currently got like 10 chests, no idea what's in what, and I run around just trying to shift click everything in my inventory on every single chest to make some space because MY INVENTORY IS ALWAYS FULL AND I'M A HOARDER.
_childDocuments_.name: Bandle Tale: A League of Legends Story

_childDocuments_.review: Bandle Tale offers a brief escape into the enchanting world of Bandle City. With its charming visuals and lovable characters, it's a cozy journey for any player. Plus, the inclusion of puzzles adds an extra layer of engagement, making you think while you explore this whimsical universe. Its such a fun and lovely game and I can't put it down! Some of the puzzles just make you think. highly RECOMMEND!
_childDocuments_.name: Bandle Tale: A League of Legends Story

_childDocuments_.review: MIXED.....VERY MIXED. But would still recommend.As someone who had never played a "Cozy" game before (I had no idea that was a thing before looking into and fully playing Bandle Tale) I'm mixed on it, but I still enjoyed it enough to complete it.What I enjoyed:The story. Nothing too grand or big. Simple.The pixel graphics, everything is colorful and cuteThe Yordles. Personal the best, and most interesting faction in the League Of Legends universeThe Cooking (Semi-mixed on). It's fun to cook the weird variety of food you can unlock. And you don't even need to unlock everything.Mixed on:One of the things, was the "Aha" moments VS and thee, "Oh, well I've got to travel to 3 different locations to make this ONE thing. Craft it, then realize you have to make 4 more of that one thing" moment.Despite thee "Aha" moments, being far and in between, there was still fun and satisfaction that was had despite that feeling.Another one, was the different ways to use the Elements or Magic Aura. For me, I would get the blueprint to make something, but you'd never make, or barley use for it. Unless the game asked for some Elements or Magic aura 2 or higherI'd also talk about the Kitchen EQUIPMENT here, but only used the bare minimum of the supplies and equipment. I didn't feel the need to make anything or use anything new. Unless there was a mission or badge requirement. Which I didn't really mind.Done Poorly:Personally, I think the beginning was VERY confusing. The game tries to tell you what to do, but you're given so much info at the beginning you can get lost trying to understand what to do. I had to look up a few things before I could get the ball rolling. But once I did I started to enjoy the game a lot more.I'd still recommend the game. It is a fun, linear, cozy adventure game. Unsure if this a selling point or not, but you don't need to know anything about League Of Legends to enjoy the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Bandle Tale: A League of Legends Story

_childDocuments_.review: Game is nice, loop satisfying, art super cute.The tone is REALLY wholesome, to an excess in my opinion, but this is a question of taste, absolutely fitting for every ages, but UX may require some help/support for some players.The UI and UX is a little rough however, took me a while to understand there are tabs and how to properly understand quest steps.The gameplay is not super deep, there is mostly only progression path (unlock trees is very linear, you need to unlock everything to progress, so there is almost no agency) but the duration is just right for it. A good experience while it lasts.Recommended for lovers of wholesome crafting games.
_childDocuments_.name: Bandle Tale: A League of Legends Story

_childDocuments_.review: The game has cute graphics and great music, but not much else, unfortunately. It starts off strong with a quirky story and cute characters, but it's slowed down with mechanics that are bogged down by too many factors. There's certain 'auras' you have to get to craft different items, many of which can either a) only be found on one island that you either have to teleport too (after throwing a party to get the material to do so each time) or b) walk there yourself.It isn't clear how to get the 'artifact' for creating the auras yourself besides fishing in the 1 portal spots on each island and hoping for the best. The other reviews aren't wrong when they say that the XP system with diminishing returns doesn't work for this game. You have to constantly find different ways of doing reskins of the same grindy tasks (cooking food for yourself, picking up items, etc) and it's just not worth it. Even the cooking system is extremely fast paced and even if you quickly prepare the food, the yordle's wait timer will time out and they leave as soon as you reach them or accidentally throw it away. It's a mix-match of frenzied grindfest that isn't fun in the long run. After the first 2-3 hours I was pretty much over it and could't be bothered anymore. Not to mention some factors aren't explained, you need certain items with specific traits to be able to throw specific parties and then you need X amount of guests who also want X items. To make matters worse, there's a cap of what you can place so it becomes a mini strategy game.I'm not sure what Bandle Tales wants to be, but as it is now, I can't recommend it. It might be fun for a die hard League of Legends fan, if even that.
_childDocuments_.name: Bandle Tale: A League of Legends Story

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so cute! It's definitely more of an adventure RPG game with farming/crafting elements in it than a farming sim game. I love the artwork, the characters, and story so far.I think my biggest complaint with this game is that progressing through the quests gets very repetitive and frustrating. You get a quest, you have to go gather mats to make the item for the quest but you might struggle to figure out how to make said item so you browse your skill tree to find how to make it and then finally go get what you need and make the item and turn it in. Rinse and repeat. It honestly might be the reason why I don't finish the game and just watch a playthrough of it.
_childDocuments_.name: Bandle Tale: A League of Legends Story

_childDocuments_.review: Great Game, very entertaining and has fun references to League of Legends, I probably did it the hard way. My only thing is if you are going for the Achievements make sure you get the first one because for some reason I have all of the final half of the achievements and have none of the first half (Most you HAVE to have to continue like first yarn crafted)
_childDocuments_.name: Bandle Tale: A League of Legends Story

_childDocuments_.review: This is like any other cozy game with quests where you are time gated by your resources and skill levels. The game will tell you what MAIN quest you need to achieve, but doesn't give directions for the smaller in between tasks. Overall it's a cute game and it's been fun to see the Yordles from LoL. I enjoyed the story and don't mind the grinding of materials/crafting to level up.
_childDocuments_.name: Bandle Tale: A League of Legends Story

_childDocuments_.review: Starting with the bad, as it's a major problem. The tutorial system is either bugged or non-existent with some aspects of the game, leaving you unable to progress the story. You can try and figure out what the game is looking for by burning through resources or look online for answers. Neither should be required for a RIOT game nor any game at this price point. The good, a League of Legends story for those familiar with the characters. A potentially cozy game once the systems are figured out or bugs/tutorials improved.Cheers.
_childDocuments_.name: Bandle Tale: A League of Legends Story

_childDocuments_.review: If you are a Stardew Valley and League of Legends fan, this game is a must.The narrative is well written and knits itself very well into the game style and lore. _childDocuments_.name: Bandle Tale: A League of Legends Story

_childDocuments_.review: This game was extremely unique in how it ended up playing out. I figured it would just be another farming simulator but with LoL characters, but the crafting, cookouts, and parties were made up most of the game and they were all really fun. It also had a pretty cute story, if a bit predictable, but I enjoyed it nonetheless.There were some reviews here saying that you hit a wall of no progress after a specific point, but that was never the case for me. As long as you don't screw up the parties you throw, you get a bunch of skill XP to get what you need to progress.I do think that making it so that locking teleportation without your backpack behind stabilizing all the portals is not a good design choice. It just makes going between islands more tedious since you always have to pack your house before tping. Aside from that and that a small portal should've been put in the knitter's island, Everything else felt fine though.
_childDocuments_.name: Bandle Tale: A League of Legends Story

_childDocuments_.review: Since the announcement I was super hyped for this game.I loved Graveyard Keeper but didn’t really like the theme and love the LoL universe.After playing for almost 10 hours now I’m super invested and can’t really put it down. Theres a lot do to and its start to get a bit overwhelming now with so many different items available.But if you want to enjoy it, you really need to like crafting and item management :) otherwise the game is not for you, this is NOT gameplay like Stardew Valley, also no combat, just collecting, crafting and a few mini game mechanics, for example restaurant simulator cooking (very small part of the game tho)Really sad that Riotforge closed down now and the game probably wont get any DLCs or something.The one thing that’s a bit annoying in the gameplay is the mechanic to take the house with you, there’s no shortcut or anything so you need to go to bench and do it manually.
_childDocuments_.name: Bandle Tale: A League of Legends Story

_childDocuments_.review: This game has very adorable graphics. The writing is nice and the story is well written. My only complaint is that while some things are over-explained, there are other things that are under explained. I spent a lot of time wandering and trying to figure out how to do certain things to progress or get to certain places. Beyond what is normal gameplay. I had to google the solution which should have been obvious, but wasn't.Overall, however I highly recommend this. There's plenty to do and the story has lovely characters.
_childDocuments_.name: Bandle Tale: A League of Legends Story

_childDocuments_.review: If you like grindy but cozy crafting, resource gathering, completing quests based on those things, and/or LoL/LoL lore, then it should be a good game for you! I love a cozy, cutesy pixel game and I also love LoL lore. I pre-ordered Bandle Tale because 1) Yordles 2) Adorable pixel art and 3) I've played Lazy Bear Games' Graveyard Keeper and the resource gathering, XP/Skill progression style and saving the town from problems scratches my itch. The skill tree style from GK transfers into Bandle Tale which was exciting for me because it gave me a good idea of what to look forward to in this game in terms of progression and game length (cost : gameplay and length - good).Notes: - Good story, can be tedious at times with blabber but at 6.7 hours I've met Lulu, Corki, Veigar, Tristana, and I'm assuming Teemo eventually. There's some jokes sprinkled in that can keep you going as you learn about the different regions of Bandle City to keep you interested but most of the dialogue really highlights the quirkiness of our beloved yordles. There are mentions of Heimerdinger, Gnar, Poppy, and additional elements that include Gragas, Blitzcrank, and more. - Super cute pixel art and lots of stylistic customizations for your backpack home which I personally really enjoy switching up time to time (you do have to earn certain materials to unlock them). - You have your own Poro, they don't do much, but they're super cute sittin' in the corner of your house. You can pet and feed them, hell yeah.  - Once hitting about 4 or 5 hours in, there is a noticeable decline in XP gathering from resources because your yordle essentially gets "bored" at doing the same task repetitively (understandable). It's not unbearable though. I'm expecting as you progress in the story and quests that the new introductions of tools and materials will make up for that, but you still need those base resources that won't give you XP anymore which might feel bad to some. - You have to do the quests to progress. There is a lack of freedom and you can get stuck on a quest if you used up skill points that aren't the skill that is required to progress in a quest, so I recommend always having some skill points banked in case you come across that barrier. I'll probably update and adjust once I've progressed a bit more in the game for those contemplating if its worth getting.
_childDocuments_.name: Bandle Tale: A League of Legends Story

_childDocuments_.review: I play league of legends but I mostly bought this because I love lazy bear's other games. I recommend it simply because it's not bad by any means, but you have to go in with the right expectations or end up disappointed.This isn't what I was expecting. It's an rpg with crafting instead of combat, it is absolutely not a simulator. It's closer to the atelier series than it is to graveyard keeper or punch club. That would be fine if it weren't for the fact that the games story seems like it's made for a light weight simulation game. If it was sort of just 'there' existing as a reason for a simulation game to exist, it would be fine, but that's not the case. The story is front and center and that ends up putting it in a position that it doesn't feel designed to fulfill. It's not a bad story, but it's very airy and silly, and the dialog is not as witty as I expect from this developer. They're usually a lot better at dialog, and I wonder if maybe riot was making them dial back the sarcastic meta humor. The visuals are great, lazy bear has always had phenomenal pixel art, and the yordle setting is really fun. If you're playing the game strictly for the tristana, teemo, and league stuff I'm sure there's a lot to like. The game isn't very expensive but, as a fan of this developer and the source material, I honestly don't think it's worth the money unless you're super into yordles. All in all, it honestly seems like a big missed opportunity to give people a proper yordle life sim. Absolutely baffling that they didn't do this, especially when the developer is known for making simulators, and the colorful yordle setting would have been the perfect way to do that. It's like riot had cake mix and frosting, and decided to try to make a pizza with it instead of a cake.
_childDocuments_.name: Bandle Tale: A League of Legends Story

_childDocuments_.review: A relaxing little cosy game in a pixelated style with cute and funny interactions, lovely critters and of course, your favourite champion, TEEMO.So far, the story, music and artstyle have been impressive and are the key factors. I can farm, pop up my restaurant, be a party planner, teach... and of course knit! Thanks to my 101 year internship with my grampsYou don't actually have to know anything about LOL itself, but it has obvious references ofc

_childDocuments_.review: I usually don't write negative reviews, but this game tried to waste my time, so I refunded it. It had jaw-dropping pixel art but nothing else positive going on. I got sent to help a cook and I couldn't make any progress due to the constant and not-easy-to-learn tutorials. I rage quit as it was not what I expected unfortunately. _childDocuments_.name: Bandle Tale: A League of Legends Story

_childDocuments_.review: If you know or playef Graveyard Keeper you will find some similarities here!I love this game, im almos 10 hrs. in and the only thing I wish there was, is a search bar in the skill tree cuz I get lost scrolling. A story driven crafting sim. where you can carry your house around, and the placement of your machines matters cuz AURAS.I've seen some people not like it because they find it a little too complex for a cozy game, but for me it keeps me thinking about what my next move will be!
_childDocuments_.name: Bandle Tale: A League of Legends Story

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely love this so far. Graveyard Keeper was a fantastic game but never enough time in a day for amount of grinding to be done and it was massive, this one takes off any kind of time pressure stress that you can just enjoy. Its adorable, story is good so far. Love how you can customize your backpack home. This is honestly the most relaxing and enjoyable grind game I've played which is a nice change of pace since I always go full tilt on similar games trying to make currency quickly and advance story. No stamina to deal with. No rushing back to home for end of day. Just all your own pace. I think it has good replay-ability, definitely will be playing for a long time to come. Thanks devs
_childDocuments_.name: Bandle Tale: A League of Legends Story

_childDocuments_.review: Enjoying story with fun and unique quest lines. The adaptive game progression allows you to change the task you want to do at any given moment. It also provides multiple ways to earn skill points, whether through emotion, friendship, satisfaction, or other means. The instructions and tutorial are simple, yet you can still always optimize your gameplay to gain more progression (Food Stand). Characters from the main game League of Legends maintain their personalities. Veigar is a good example of that with his stubborn, truly evil motivations still intact.
_childDocuments_.name: Bandle Tale: A League of Legends Story

_childDocuments_.review: If you remotely liked Graveyard Keeper and aren't turned off by the lighter theme in the screenshots then buying this is a no brainer. I was hopelessly addicted almost immediately, and there are subtle improvements over Graveyard Keeper that make it much more enjoyable to play, such as not having strict time limits and a strict day/night cycle. I'm enjoying it... immensely.
_childDocuments_.name: Bandle Tale: A League of Legends Story

_childDocuments_.review: I have no idea who any of these League of Legends peeps are, but this is still a lot of fun if you like these kinds of games.  Which I somehow do even tho it's just 'go here and do this' type of quests with some story dialog in between.  I really liked Graveyard Keeper because it was such a fun/different subject matter.  This is also weird and fun and also less time pressure like in that game (actually no time pressure yet, 3 hrs in).
_childDocuments_.name: Bandle Tale: A League of Legends Story

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game. My friend and I have been streaming it to each other from the moment we got home from work. The world is cute and feels right for yordles. Every time we enter a new place there is something extremely cute for us to gush over. I can really tell where they have improved on some of the pain points of Graveyard keeper. The onboarding is so much easier to understand. The crafting is fun and just the right level of grindy for me. Resources are easy to come by but you need to figure out what unlocks will let you use them.
_childDocuments_.name: Bandle Tale: A League of Legends Story

_childDocuments_.review: Such an adorable game! What could be cozier than a game where you save the day by the power of knitting? I love it. So fun to see Bandle City and explore it, and meet all of the Yordles. It's especially fun to see the characters that are in League of Legends itself. I love the game-play, I think having your house also serve as a backpack and having the ability to transport my home to wherever I want is a really really nice aspect of the game.And the cooking is like a mini-game! I was pleasantly surprised by this, I knew we would be able to make and sell food, but the way it is implemented makes it extra engaging and fun. I'm super excited to play the game more and see where the story goes!
_childDocuments_.name: Bandle Tale: A League of Legends Story

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game.It is super fun feels a bit like stardew valley mixed with minecraft and some magic league of legends fun. Characters are funny, locales are pretty, the skill trees are exciting etcI suggest this game for a laidback fun timeOnly issues I would say is teleporting being money is bit annoying, and it can be tiring running around everywhere but thankfully there are ways to move faster and eventually get free teleporting!
_childDocuments_.name: Bandle Tale: A League of Legends Story

_childDocuments_.review:
From Lazy Bear, the studio that brought you Graveyard Keeper, comes Bandle Tale: A League of Legends Story. Jump into this delightful crafting RPG set in the magical world of Bandle City, home of the furry and fun-loving yordles.

You are a shy yordle living in Yarnville, a cozy but isolated island obsessed with all things knitting. When your 101-year-long apprenticeship ends, you want nothing more than to see what lies beyond the portals that connect the rest of Bandle City. But when a party you attend goes horribly wrong, the portals collapse and everything is thrown into chaos!

With your unique knitting magic and unflappable spirit, enlist the help of new friends, restore the portals, and reunite Bandle City once more!
_childDocuments_.name: Bandle Tale: A League of Legends Story

name: Madden NFL 23
detailed_description: GET THE LATEST VERSION OF MADDEN About the Game Play your way into the history books in Madden NFL 23. Control your impact with every decision in all-new ways. Call the shots in Franchise with free agency and trade logic updates, play your way into the history books in Face of the Franchise: The League, and assemble the most powerful roster in all of Madden Ultimate Team™. Face of the Franchise: The League The League drops you into your fifth NFL season at a skill position of your choice (QB, WR, RB, CB, MLB), and you’re seeking a fresh start with a new team. Negotiate a 1-year “prove-it” contract with one of 32 NFL teams, and show out with great on-field performance to earn rewards and level up. The addition of New Drive Goals and Drive Summaries allows you to tweak your experience throughout a game and get feedback and rewards based on how well you play. Get performance boosts from weekly activities and training between games while Madden Ratings Adjustor Chad Johnson guides your career development by providing ratings updates as you strive for the highest level of prestige on your Road to 99. Will your NFL career rank among the all-time greats? It’s up to you. Franchise Plan and strategize like an NFL head coach with refined scouting, staff management, and weekly strategy features to take your Franchise to the top. New athlete motivations like team location and salary demands factor into contract negotiations and add to the drama of NFL free agency within Franchise. Updated Trade Logic AI represents the value of star players more accurately for fair and more realistic offers. Madden Ultimate Team Develop your dream fantasy roster of current NFL superstars, Hall of Fame legends, and more. Always have something to play for with the first-ever Field Pass challenge and reward tracker in Madden Ultimate Team. Play to earn MUT Champions entry tokens and choose to compete at your convenience. Simplified Set building lets you navigate your content binder more effectively so you can focus on improving your Ultimate Team roster all season. This game includes optional in-game purchases of virtual currency that can be used to acquire virtual in-game items, including a random selection of virtual in-game items.

_childDocuments_.review: First Madden game for me in about 5ish years, got this on sale, didn't expect much to have changed, not much has. That being the case, I can't recommend this game at any price.Obviously the focus is still on ultimate team as it is a cash cow for this franchise, but I'd like to see them improve on other facets such as be a pro mode, graphics, player movement and just realism in general.Be a pro is really a husk of what it should be. The NFL is a multi billion dollar franchise. At the very least, try and incorporate some hall of fame careers into this mode, let us play out a season as a prime Barry Sanders with voice acting and the like, or prime Dan Marino. Obviously the rights are there to have these guys in the game, why not capitalize on it other than having them in ultimate team. That being said, it's probably a pipe dream for something like that, but please, at least add some decent acting and fun moments to the awfully drab face of the franchise mode.Graphics, player movement and realism are generally tied together, so I'll just compare the graphics to NBA 2K. Most of the players in 2K have facial scans, why not have full body scans in Madden. Lineman look morbidly obese, linebackers look like lineman should and it just doesn't look right across the board from head to toe. Player movement is as robotic as it was 5 years ago. All of this attributes to the lack of realism in this game.Overall, I'm just disappointed. 2/5

_childDocuments_.review: I played from Madden '98 to Madden 2004 and loved the franchise. Grew up with it. Since this is my first Madden since 2004, you can imagine that I was happy with how far it had come. I know a lot of people hate this game because it is no different than the last 5 years of Madden, but I didn't experience those last 5 years. So I'm the best case scenario customer for this game. Very easy and happy to please.With that said... this game is 50/50 for me. I'm addicted to the gameplay and love the feeling I get when I pull off a great play. But I DESPISE how the majority of online players win in this community. There are small exploits that I feel experienced players target for easy wins. Wanna hear me rant for a minute? Here we go (if you want the short TL;DR version, scroll to the bottom):Are you picking cover plays and predicting a pass in your audibles? Too bad. They're going to throw a deep pass and its going to get caught even though the receiver has 3 of your players covering. Go ahead and try to intercept. It's your best chance. It's pretty much a 50/50 dice roll. If it doesn't work, you're screwed. I've literally seen players catch a ball without ever turning back to look at it. I've also watched my own players run AWAY from someone they're supposed to be covering, which lead to that player getting the ball and running it to the endzone. Do you have the other player at 4th down on their own half of the field? Too bad. They're not punting once. They're going to, instead, pick a passing play and throw it deep. It succeeds more than half the time, too. Want a tactical experience where every yard has to be earned? That's rarely going to happen. They're going to pick a running play and you're going to sit and watch helplessly while the entirety of your defense freezes up and BACKS AWAY from the runner half the time. Want to take control of them and tackle? Great idea! Too bad there's still going to be times where you tackle someone with three separate guys at full speed and the runner still manages to truck 5-10 yards with ease. That's if you don't experience THIS kind of gameplay first when the opponent has the ball:RUNNING PLAY. 5 yard gain. NO HUDDLE. RUNNING PLAY. 8 yards. NO HUDDLE. RUNNING PLAY. 4 yards. NO HUDDLE. PASSING PLAY. DEEP PASS. Touchdown.The worst part is... I had the above happen to me in a game just last night and I predicted every single play and picked the best counter for each one. I even knew when they were going to switch it up to a passing play. Predicted it. Picked a coverage play. Had three guys covering the receiver who was running deep. He bullet passed it to that receiver and the ball went THROUGH my three covering players right into the receiver's hands. 50 yards gained for the other player.TL;DR:It seems to me no matter how accurate your play predictions are and how calculated the plays are that you selected... your success is determined by the AI and the AI is extremely unpredictable. No matter how well you plan and how accurately you predict the opponent's play, they'll still leave massive openings half the time and you'll pay the price.Like I said, I'm practically new to this franchise, having not played since Madden 2004. For some reason, I feel like Madden 2004 was a better game. When I search online, it turns out people agree with me... even down to the mechanics.Madden 23 is currently on sale for $17.99 and I've seen it at that price before. I'd say that's a worthwhile price... That's what I bought it for. But $59.99? Not worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: I will say I love this game and will play it until the end of time, and I admit it may be Stockholm Syndrome. With that being said, I truly don't get how EA can get away with selling a video game labeled "Madden 23" knowing it is literally a copy-paste from the year prior. I wish I could use Free Form passing as well as have the updated UI and faster loading screens. Seriously, it feels like you're streaming the game on Dial-Up. Bugs and General Annoyances I've found/experienced:If there is a dog pile at the LoS as the HB carries for an inside run, there is a chance that as long as defenders who are on the ground either via being taken down, missed a tackle, etc., that if the HB gets tackled on top of those defenders, the game will not register a down, the character model will bug and he will be getting up as his character model shifts off of the defender while floating, allowing an unfair chance for more yards.Terrible Booth Reviews and Play Challenge decisions. There have been multiple times where I've done secure catches on corner routes in order to toe touch, and have been ruled incomplete, after a challenge the ruling stands but when going into Instant replay, it is incredibly evident that the character models are in bounds visually. This bug was weird, I can't explain it. I took a punt return. Visually, my receiver cushioned the ball and took off. I did hear the sound queue of the ball bouncing off of hands, however. Followed by the commentator team mentioning how I "recovered my own fumble". Okay, sure no problem. Starting the drive I noticed that, even while on my own 30, my down and yards were 1st & Goal... I threw three straight 10yd-15yd passes resulting in what should've been 3 first downs. Only to find myself of 4th & Goal at opponents ~40. Forced to punt or FG attempt. I truly love Ultimate Team. The challenges are exciting at first, the cards and players you can unlock are a dopamine rush. I just wish they would allow more single player battles weekly, or add a Character Skill Based matchmaking. The challenges do get repetitive and boring, and when you want a change, you can battle 5 AI weekly OR go H2H against other players. Going H2H with a team average below 85 has been basically an auto L. Almost everyone I've gone up against has had a team average of 93+ and the stat disadvantages with your players feels the same as NCAA vs. NFL. Really a bummer that until I wait and grind to gain that average, or P2W, I essential have an imbalanced mode I won't touch. With all that being said, if you want the most popular American Football Simulator, well here ya' go. As I said at the beginning I love this game, I just have no hope that EA will care enough about the fan base or community to create a product that is more than 50% enjoyable.

_childDocuments_.review: The game let me play it for free for a few days, and I planned on buying it on sale if I liked it.  Long story short, I will not be buying it on sale.  The last Madden I played was '08, so I was excited to see how the game had changed in 15 years, even if I knew it didn't change much year over year.  The first thing I noticed is that the movement was incredibly familiar.  In fact, it felt the exact same as '08.  This isn't the end of the world, but that is somewhat concerning that no meaningful improvements have been made.  I decided to play Face of the Franchise, and I'm glad I did, as it showcased the worst parts of the game.  In FothF you choose a skill position, and you have some light RPG upgrades you can work toward.  The problem?  The game glitched in week 2 and suddenly told me my WR was a level 1 QB with the QB tree, except it still lined up at WR.  Then when I created a new WR it started me at the beginning again, but with all my exp and perks unlocked.  I played this new WR to week 7, when it did the same thing to me again, effectively killing the character.  Also, there is no way to get the cpu to choose the plays, so I was deciding every offensive play we did as the WR.  Very realistic.  I then went to franchise mode.  And I didn't get far before my RB complained about not getting enough touches, and wanted 10 touches and 100 yards the next game.  So I gave him 18 touches, 162 rushing yards, and 45 receiving yards.  And then I get another complaint that "he can't do anything if he only touches the ball once per drive" and a debuff.Other annoying things that wouldn't normally be deal breakers for me, but are still annoying:To summarize, I didn't expect a lot from this game, but I was still dissapointed.

_childDocuments_.review: Couple of things right off the bat, i barely ever leave reviews and the only other ones i have done are positive. Not played Madden since the 21 version. I don't play the MUT just offline.The onfield play actually seems slightly better than the last time i played, still needs some tinkering with the sliders. The downsides of the play is the weird chunky player characters. Everything else feels similarOne time i loaded into a game in franchise mode and it had actually loaded as a game but under practice rules with no game clock lol. I scored a couple of TD's, exited the game and it let me keep my score.Background in Franchise Mode and the menu buttons are so flat and generic. Looks like something that is 15+ years old. When i was playing 21 you had the coach in the background at his desk more dynamic menu changes. Here you have a flat colour background and the menu's and buttons look like they have been done with the absolute minimum effort required. Not a big thing, but just makes playing the game feel so unappealing right off the bat, especially when you know what they had a few years ago.New Scouting system. I kinda get the changes they are going for here. You basically hire scouts who can focus on a couple of positions and put them in a region of the US and you will start to accumulate information on all players, with a focus on the scouts specialization. Decent enough idea but the execution, again relating to the menus make this absolutely tedious. For example the combine scores come out, you have to go into the player card to view, ok, but then if you want to view the next players stats you have to exit then select the next player then enter his stats card. Takes forever! No reason at all while in the player card you can't move onto the next player to go through and compare stats. Manually going in and out takes so long, and its the only way as very few stats are available on the list of prospects. With tweaking could work wellPlayer motivations, with player tags and salary cap rollover are all here now. The player motivations especially remind me of of the last NCAA game. Right now everyone pretty much hates my team, (if you want to get FA's on the cheap seems like you need to be in a hot state lol) Only thing is that even with these tags and motivations, a good offer still seems to be the way forward. You can add points into your talent tree to make it easier to sign free agents. Again its got the beginnings of a decent system, just seems a little unrealistic at the moment.The talent tree for coaches and coordinators is ok, so far through my play through seems pretty easy to accumulate points, and like the rest of the game the visuals for this are dull with minimum effort.Relocation is exactly the same as it has been for several years now, only difference is no conquistadors or marshals because that must have been clearly triggering people lol. Nothing new to report here.Training and player progression. Still pretty much the same, training seems to be set up to be done automatically unlike before when it encouraged player participation and the player progression is done by choosing a role and getting points allocated based on which role you picked as before.Still have scenario's and media questions which is fair enough, they work ok for what they are. The transition/loading screens look poor as well like there is something wrong with them or just lack of effort.So overall its still Madden and yes there are a couple of new features but ones which need tweaking and developing before they can be implemented properly. But honestly and maybe this is partly because of how unappealing the game looks when you actually get into it, but it feels like one step forward two steps back and as if there is less now than a couple of years ago.

_childDocuments_.review: I get Madden every 3-5 years as it's a reskin at this point. Played Madden 20 before this one, mainly as created players. I don't interact with MUT because why would I fork over that much time/money to a company that won't put time or money into improving these games? My review below is comparing this game to Madden 20.The Good (What they added)-added an actual pass rushing system as a DE. It makes sense and is coherent and I feel like it's a solid baseline.-create a character has FINALLY sped up rating adjustments and it doesn't take forever to create characters.-adjusted the X-Factor system so that it feels like taking different skills impacts the game.The Bad (What they removed)-How can I not see the NFL STANDINGS at a quick glance from the main page of Franchise mode!? I don't think I've even seen a Standings option. Like if your going to copy/paste the game every year, at least remember to hit ALT-V because I have to skip thru the week's games to get a quick glance of everyone's record and its stupid.-Why is EA so insistent on doing the same thing every few years where they mess up camera angles so when I'm playing as a player I have to cycle the angles instead of like Madden 20 where if I'm a player, I get the player camera angle. I'm calling it: in 2 years they'll have a "new and improved" Face of the Franchise and bring back the camera angle as "AN ALL NEW IMMERSIVE CAMERA". And speaking of Face of the Franchise...-I didn't play this mode more than a few games, so I don't have too much knowledge, but in a few games it felt like Face of the Franchise is basically just Franchise mode with cut scenes. I'm glad they actually got rid of contracts and replaced it with a currency you want to level, but if the end goal is to be like 2K then I'm good. I don't need grind in this game, especially when I have the option to play as players in Franchise Mode. -The $60 price tag because YES, this game was listed at $70 if u didn't get it on sale, and this is apparently not the next gen edition. Not that I'd notice because I still play NCAA 14 a lot and the drop off in graphic quality is minimal compared to the gaming experience you get.The only remaining thing I'll talk about is just the product in general. We as a community want a realistic football sim to play, whether it's to pretend we are living the dream of a football player, or just to kill time until the next game. Animation based gameplay is not the move to get realism. When I see 3 players on defense do the exact same animation pre snap every play, I cry a little inside. When I hit a dude but he gets a stumble animation and falls forwards 10 more yards glitching thru 4 of my teammates, I get frustrated. While X-Factor is better this iteration, I still hate the whole system as it relates to realistic football. If they had to remove all the cutscenes from Face of the Franchise and give me blocks of text to read, but I get a functioning Senior year of college, Combine, Draft, and Story, then stop wasting money on cutscenes with Shirley your agent or Stan your football coach before practice and start putting in basic features to make me feel immersed. Baseball Superstars is an anime/baseball mobile game and that can get me immersed into the life of a baseball player better than this franchise has in over a decade, and I HATE watching baseball! Football Manager lets me play as a coach or owner of a soccer organization, and I HATE watching soccer! Other sports have games that I enjoy playing despite not following the sport because they give you *something* to enjoy when you play it. We have to look towards A or AA developers making games like Axis Football where they give us a game that's like football but can't use anything NFL related and they don't have nearly the budget they need to do what they want, but they're STILL trying to give us a real football experience.By the time you read this, I may have triple digit hours put into this game. I play it to get my football fix for the NFL. But I can promise you that this is the last Madden I buy, because the only other football game I want to buy will be one made by a different company if EA ever lets the monopoly on simulation football expire (they won't). This game has a free to play pay structure with Madden Ultimate Team, but we're all stupid enough to pay upwards of $70 every year for them to give us the same game, and in the case of MUT, we pay $70 for them to wipe our progress and copy paste the year-long release schedule for their cards.

_childDocuments_.review: OK, I get all the hate for this game, especially for us PC users, and the criticism is fair. I don't think you should ever purchase this game at full price.  I picked it up at the $18.00 price and it is worth that price. Here is what I find the most different, (this is after 10 hours of play) the DEFENSE and Star Players.  The defense is so improved.  Running drag routes for first downs is now contested.  You no longer can throw any old receiver out there and they make catches and plays or any running back and get 100 yards.  These guys don't get open and they can't punch thru holes.  You need a good offense line or you will get wrecked!   You need your star players.  I now have to actually worry about the pass rush.  I played against Micah Parsons and he was wrecking shop on me.  I actually had to run plays to counter him! You just can't run the ball and get 5 yards a carry.  I use to run the ball on 3rd and 5 and always get a 1st down.  Trap plays were like stealing.  When your on defense you have to cover their stars or they will ruin your day.  The computer doesn't let you trick them into making bad trades, well at least not as bad. You can still trick them but it is harder.  I had to give up more picks.  I actually have to punt the ball!  Well I am only 10 hours into the game but I find myself actually having to plan out my strategy.  If I call a bad defensive play they will eat my lunch.  If I don't pick up the blitz I am going to get sacked,  In Madden 22, I went game after game never getting sacked.    Well that is all for now, I hope this review sheds some light on Madden 23.  It is worth 18 bucks.

_childDocuments_.review: Madden 2023 is an absolute train wreck of a video game. It's a testament to how a once-beloved franchise can be reduced to a pile of digital garbage. Electronic Arts (EA) has outdone themselves in delivering a Madden experience that is not only subpar but also infuriatingly unplayable.Let's start with the most glaring issue: the AI. In Madden 2023, the AI is nothing short of laughable. It's as if the developers decided to take a massive step backward in terms of artificial intelligence. Your CPU-controlled teammates seem to have the intelligence of a particularly dimwitted toddler. They frequently make baffling decisions, like running out of bounds when they should be heading for a touchdown or throwing interceptions that defy all logic. It's not just bad; it's insulting to anyone who's ever watched or played football.But wait, it gets worse. Glitches are as commonplace as touchdowns in this mess of a game. You can't go a single match without encountering some infuriating bug or visual glitch. Players frequently warp through each other, the physics engine is utterly broken, and the game often freezes or crashes, leaving you staring at a loading screen as if it's mocking your decision to buy this abomination.One would expect a AAA game like Madden 2023 to be polished and refined, but it's anything but. It's clear that EA rushed this title out the door to meet their annual release schedule, and it shows. From the clunky menus to the uninspired graphics and animations, it's painfully evident that this game was not given the time or care it needed to be a worthwhile addition to the series.The sad truth is that Madden 2023 feels like a soulless cash grab by EA, a company that seems more interested in squeezing every last penny out of its loyal fanbase than delivering a quality gaming experience. It's a shame that they continue to ignore the pleas of their community for meaningful improvements and innovations.In conclusion, Madden 2023 is an unmitigated disaster. The AI is a joke, glitches are everywhere, and the game is a slap in the face to anyone who's ever enjoyed the franchise. Save your money, save your sanity, and avoid this travesty of a game at all costs. EA should be ashamed of themselves for releasing such a half-baked product and expecting fans to swallow it.

_childDocuments_.review: Madden 23 is very much like Madden 22. The biggest changes feel like steps in the right direction (Free Agency, Career Progression) however, there is still so much bad about this game that makes it downright unbearable at times. I typically only play franchise mode as it is where I feel you can have the most customization and impact on the game you want to play. With all Madden games though I try the career mode (Face of the Franchise) at least once. So this review will focus on those aspects.Franchise Mode:The good thing about franchise mode much like previous Madden modes is the ability to customize the league as you see fit. Though the customization is still lacking in some areas, there is not much difference between Madden's Franchise Modes of the past and this year. The biggest difference that I have found is the Free Agency period. This is where Franchise Mode has taken a great step forward. Adding features like player interest, and various factors in to what kind of career they want to have is a great addition. This feature makes sense given that EA is trying to revamp their NCAA video game and recruiting is going to be a factor in that game. I quite enjoyed this feature as it adds a lot of necessary depth that previous games have been missing since EA severely trimmed back their Madden games over a decade ago. Another necessary addition to free agency was the eval button which made free agency feel like more of an ongoing process and prevents issues such as player stacking so that the user has so much depth that the rest of the league is at a severe disadvantage.This leads me to the complaints about free agency that I have which is that it is still spread out over multiple weeks. With the addition of the eval button, this process could be trimmed down to one week with more evals added. Thus cutting down the loading times between weeks, and trimming the amount of time of the Off-season period. This doesn't mean I dislike the off-season, in fact it is the opposite. It is where you can really build your team but at a certain point for myself time is the most valuable thing, and with the eval button feature, it feels even more wasteful to have free agency spread out like it is still. The other complaint about free agency that I have is that searching for players you have signed for is less intuitive this year, not a big complaint. All that to say though that I really did like free agency this year compared to previous Madden games.The rest of franchise mode feels pretty much the same as previous additions. The menus could be far more user friendly than they are. The News section this time around still makes absolutely no sense. The stats & awards of the ongoing year should be far easier to access than they are. The league schedule should be more easily accessible. Also, the sack stat & record is still so broken based on simulated stats. The record is still broken nearly every year. MVP award winners seem better balanced (it's no longer Lamar Jackson because he rushes for like 4,000 yards and passes for a 100 every year), but I think more time will need to be spent in franchise mode to get a good feel for MVP. The simulated W/L records of each team is still crazy unrealistic and it seems like there are at least three teams who go on magic runs every year (This could happen in real life but the chances of a team making it to a conference championship, not losing a lot of pieces, having no injuries, and then suddenly becoming the worse team in the league is about 1% in real life but in franchise mode it seems like this happens nearly every year).The best fix to franchise that I have noticed is through the draft. From the simulated drafts that I have seen, teams have actually drafted according to their needs. Unlike last year, and previous years where the first players taken off the board for the first ten picks was ninety percent of the time quarterbacks, like 6/10 were always quarterbacks for literally no reason. Speaking on the draft, scouting still has a ways to go before it becomes really useful. They have added some more level of depth but it feels like the scouting system won't be fully complete until 2030 lol.Face of the Franchise:This years face of the franchise took one step forward and ten steps backward. The progression system, and side activities this year are all way better than previous versions. The opening contract choices were very good. The biggest issue and main complaint about face of the franchise is that it still does not feel like your own career. I say this because instead of having you be a potential undrafted free agent rookie or anything like that, instead you miss out on the first four years <--read that again 4 YEARS of your career. I don't mind if we as a player skip the college nonsense of previous years but missing the first 4 years of your career is ludicrous.A good thing about face of the franchise that I really like was the camera angle. For some reason I loved playing the game with that angle but you can't use that angle in other game modes or other games which is disappointing.The Game:Even with the positive additions to this years franchise and face of franchise, if the on-field gameplay is not good, then the game is not good. Which in this case, the on-field gameplay is still just as terrible as previous versions. Especially since the PC version does not have the same capabilities as the supposedly "Next-gen" versions which is astounding. Maybe the on-field product would be better if the PC version did have the so-called intellisense feature. Still this does not detract from the fact that receivers randomly break their routes to allow for the corner to jump the route especially on slant routes. It also does not detract from the fact that the QB can get random inaccurate passes or pressured passes even when there is no pressure or any defender within five yards of your player. It also does not detract from the fact that when player switching on defense to make a tackle, you are almost always never switched to the guy closest to making the play. This happens a lot especially when a scripted animation triggers such as the WR using a juke move but your defender just stands there and has to go through the animation with no chance of breaking through it.I play Madden games on All-Madden and the amount of utter uselessness of non-player controlled characters is astounding. Defensive coverages are still greatly lacking, even when all of the possible adjustments are made, the opposing quarterback is almost always able to find someone to throw it to and that player always makes the first person miss which is incredibly frustrating. The amount of fumbles is incredibly astounding. On base sliders, I had back-to-back games where there were at least 7 fumbles each game. This is terrible for base sliders and I don't know how it passed a quality assurance test.The only real way to play this game with an authentic experience is to get some really good gameplay sliders or figure out your own gameplay sliders that you like to play with that makes the bugs less frustrating. I am still trying to figure out good sliders, as the ones that I used for last years game seem to be a little off do to the few and probably very few changes made to the on-field gameplay. FINAL THOUGHT:If you are going to buy this game (which I strongly recommend against), I can only hope and pray that you find gameplay sliders that make it fun for you.
