_childDocuments_.review: Why I fell for it this year is beyond me. I knew going into it this was going to happen, and yet I bought two copies. One for myself and one for my brother. It's a nostalgia thing, my brother and I grew up on Madden. We breathed football gaming and we battled for three decades now. We played all matter of football, Techno Bowl, and more. We loved ESPN 2K5, and then All Pro Football. Then came NCAA titles, it felt like EA actually made some effort with the NCAA games. Then of course that came to an end over money. Now Madden is the only so-called REAL football game, and it's sad. Madden 2012 had physics-based game play and so did Madden 2013. It had the effect of feeling more realistic, but it had some goofy things happen with the rag doll animations. It didn't feel cheap when an interception happened because the player physically had to be there. The presentation was better back in the day, more like a CBS broadcast with actual announcers in the booth! Actual halftime shows with highlights. I could create an actual team with my own designed logo and build my stadium with a lot of preset sections I could use to customize it. Franchise felt as if I was controlling my team! I recently played NCAA 2K3 for the GameCube (I still have it). While I can tell graphically Madden is better, the sad reality is that it's not that graphically far off. 2K3 players are blocker for sure, but the stadiums, field, and overall presentation is well animated to this day. Madden 23 graphically is no different than Madden 2019, and that is sad. That is the last Madden I had purchased before this game and it feels like there is no difference. So, what is wrong with Madden 23?No difference in the last four years, this game is the same game with a roster update as Madden 2019.Lack of real physics and animation algorithms make for an inconsistent football experience. Players warp to to intercept the ball and running backs always fall forward 3 to 4 extra yards when tackled. Even if tackled in the backfield, it's rare you get a running back down for a loss.Presentation is very sad. Half time simply is this, "The two teams are battling it out, and now they are back on the field to resume the 2nd half". I swear that is all! No effort put into it at all! Superbowl animations are the SAME as 2019. The only difference is camera angels are changed, but the animations are not different.Pushing Ultimate team constantly, always in your face. Wonder why Madden has gone downhill? In 2011 ultimate team came into the picture and people bought it up. You think it's because they have exclusive rights to the NFL? Nope, it's ultimate team. People spend billions on that product and I guarantee you 2K would have followed if allowed to make football games still. Look at their Basketball games, same deal. Quality has gone down and monetization has gone up. While having exclusive rights makes it easier to put out a roaster update every year and people purchasing it. It's the ultimate team mode that is really killing this franchise.Bring back Physics based game play. Make a great presentation, and put things back into the game that has been in older games. Franchise mode and create a team with my own logos and colors. Bring back all the customization we use to have in games from the PS2 era! I want Madden to be great, I want it to succeed and make EA a ton of money! I think if they made this game with a lot of old features put back in and physics instead of animation football, the game could easily be one of the greatest sports games of all time!PC version does not have field sense, but from what I have seen from others playing on the PS5 or Xbox, it really makes no difference. Same boring copy and paste game! If you have not bought this game, DON'T. It's too late for me my friends. I have already contributed to EA making this game the same every single year because idiot's buy it. I am one of the Idiots!

_childDocuments_.review: The overall gaming experience is better when there is a solid sense of team and a modest amount of sportsmanship required for that game to be successful.  While there is a lot of complaints about the PC version, it's up to the individual to access the level of immersion they require to be happy.  Madden '23 not only allows the player to feel the emotional impact of failure, but the true nature of achieving a well deserved victory.  If you are looking to a quick game for self-satisfaction, Madden '23 may not be the game your looking for.  Practice and dedication to the basic principles of Football are still required, even though it has been simulated for the computer.  You probably will not just step into this game and be the next greatest sensation.  Take some time to learn and understand the rules and how to play the game.  Football is an American tradition, and the Madden line of games from EA Sports is the only viable solution.  Get with the program and play today!!  Come join us online.

_childDocuments_.review: I thought people calling this game trash were being hyperbolic. They are not.First, I had to click Steam’s PLAY button at least 3 times before the game would launch. I believe the first time was to update EA’s app. The second was to “log in” to EA’s app. The third was to “prepare the game”. And the fourth (I think) finally loaded the game itself. Wow.Then the game loads. Vsync is not working so my PC starts chugging out 150+ fps on my 60hz TV for no good reason. Because Vsync isn’t on, the game looks buggy and glitchy as hell even in its initial (unattractive) attract mode, screen tearing and asset-rattling occurring everywhere at once. Gross.Then the game asks me to configure settings. What sticks out to me most about this part of the experience? Being asked THREE TIMES what difficulty and mechanics I want, and having to repeatedly confirm I want Pro and Simulation. Once would’ve been enough, y’know. Ugh.The celebration of Coach Madden and the intro matchup of AFC v NFC seems cool and all, but I’m rushing through looking for a pause and settings menu. Finally the first kickoff play selector comes up, and the pause menu takes me to a settings menu that doesn’t have graphics options. So, I exit this cool ceremonial intro, presumably missing out on playing it forever. All because Vsync was disabled by default. Wonderful.Eventually I’ve ended up at the main menu. Settings > graphics > enable Vsync. Framerate drops to 30 mysteriously even though 60 should be no problem on my GTX 1080Ti on the main menu, regardless of resolution. I fiddle with it for a minute and then give up to move on. Turns out, luckily, gameplay still manages to be 60fps. Phew.I decide to go to Learn How To Play, to brush up. Even this portion is half-assed. It says “press B to select the Fullback”, and I press B once or twice. Having highlighted the Fullback, I then press B a few too many more times. The Fullback isn’t selected. Still, the game congratulates me and passes me on to the next tutorial as if I’d selected the correct player position.The soundtrack is almost entirely cringey rap and hip hop.I haven’t given up yet, I’ve only just begun. Still, do not buy. Thanks again for the Christmas gift, friend from EA!

_childDocuments_.review: The fact that EA has an exclusive license to make simulation NFL games is a joke. As long as Ultimate Team keeps printing them money, they don't care. The game was better 15 years ago. A short list of my biggest gripes:* Last gen version on PC?!?! My PC is more powerful then new gen consoles, but I'm treated like a second class citizen. Granted, 2k does the same thing, but these are multi-billion dollar companies. Do better* No cross-play. Every other major game franchise outside of sports allows cross-play, Madden should as well* Outdated positional terminology: Everyone refers to players by group like edge, ILB, or IOL. Once on a team and in a set playbook, sure players can have defined positions. But in FA and the draft, players should be listed by the position group they belong to, not just limited to a specific position. Don't arbitrarily limit if a player is a Right guard or Edge or left. and for ♥♥♥♥♥ sake, if I see Khalil Mack as a stand up linebacker again I'm gonna hurl.* Contract Inflexibility: Contracts in Madden are a mysterious hole that we don't get insight into. Why does a 7 year contract only have half the average AAV in the final year? How does it scale? You never know until you sign them. At least give us what 2k has, being able to back or front-load a contract

_childDocuments_.review: What if I were to tell you that almost every single criticism I had for NBA 2K23 ALSO applies to Madden 23? Would that surprise you? It sure doesn't surprise me. Despite this being an EA title not a 2K title, Madden 23 manages to fail to function on just about every level that it matters.First and foremost, there are quite literally ADS if you change menus. I'm not kidding. There's popup ads in a fully priced game that you purchased advertising for you to buy packs or different microtransaction bullsh*t. If sports weren't such a universal thing, meaning if the franchise had no real world tie in? All of the current sports franchises besides *maybe* FIFA would have lost their entire playerbase years ago. Even for the people that don't care about online or franchise mode or any of the typical things you might buy Madden for and just want a singleplayer experience should be warned. Face of the Franchise currently has a bug that is impossible to avoid and inevitably happens to your savefile where it will at random completely reset your career progress and default to making you a Quarterback. There is no way to salvage the save file, and while you can restart your season and it will keep your upgrades, you have to start on a new team all over again from the preseason. Just made the Superbowl when the glitch hits? Oh well. I got this game on sale for 18 bucks because I enjoy watching football and have enjoyed playing both in real life and the game my whole life, since Madden 06. The worst part about this is that the game is kinda fun when it works, you just have to jump through hoops to get there. I did mostly face of the franchise so far as a middle linebacker and playing defense is super fun, but again, you have to fight to play the game.There's still all the weird unskippable stuff, like cutscenes that I'm positive are written by AI. Seriously, just pay like one f*cking writer at this point because jesus christ these are painful to sit through and unskippable. At one point, your agent(?) named Sosa just... buys you an apartment? Like imagine if that happened in real life. Your agent, without telling you, buys you a luxury apartment you haven't seen before. That's grounds for suing the hell out of them lmaoThere's even this stupid line they had the announcers record where if you skip the halftime animations they get offended? Yeah, no sh*t I don't wanna watch your stupid little halftime walk off/walk on animation. The immersion is broken 10000 different ways, so forgive me for not buying into the whole "realistic football simulation" aspect of this game. You kinda lost me when the QB got sacked and clipped half of their character model into the ground.There's no good place to put this tidbit either, but theres this really weird cutscene thing that happens a bunch with Chad Ochocinco? He says like 2 lines then it goes back to the game. Very weird but glad he got a paycheck I guess.Its painfully obvious that just like 2K, the ultimate team and other modes that allow microtransactions are the real reason these games are still being made. I used to love Ultimate team when it first came out because it was pretty easy to get good cards without spending money and have a fun team to play with against your friends. Now you need to spend in the 100$ range on microtransactions that only last for that version of Madden to be competitive. I feel very bad for the people who are addicted to these games and the game modes that require spending more money, and genuinely, I hope you find other games that are kinder on your wallet. If you have played past madden games like me, you would remember many times when you press the button of an open receiver, only for the quarterback to throw it right to the defense. When I saw that they were advertising more control when you though the ball, I felt that the must frustrating part of the gameplay would be fixed. Ultimate team:I haven't touched ultimate team for years because I know EA will just take more of my moneyFace of the franchise: Imma keep it 100 with you guys I didn't even know this gamemode existed until I relaunched the game for the review. Its hard to notice anything but ultimate team with how much they try to shove it down your face. Franchise mode:Only new feature that is worth anything comes during the free agency period, the coaching tree thing is boring, and not even hard to max out even with the xp on the slowest setting. No matter how realistic you try to make this mode feel, it will never reach it. CPU trade logic is still stupid, the draft is still boring (its good that you cant see rookies overalls during the draft, but why can you see how good they are one second after the draft is done? what if you draft a bust in the first round, or find a steal in the fifth? In real life, no one really knows how good drafted players will be until they get on the feild ina real game. A cool feature that EA should add (for next madden) would be that you learn the overall of the rookies as they play snaps throughout their rookie year, not just what DEV trait they have. what happened to rookie mini camp? this can actually be a great time to learn about a rookie's stats, and maybe force you to make a decision on how much game time you give him. But it's EA, why would I expect realism from a game with the "Immersive Sim" tag."Just a roster update":I wish I could say that this was just a $60 roster update, but I disagree with most of the player ratings so much that I ended up spending over 8 hours (in the past week alone as of writing this review *I have only got through 12 teams at this point*) changing the players overalls and skills to what *in my opinion* better suits them in real life. With the base madden roster, the real star players don't feel like stars (to me) and you can get good / similar performance from guys who are practice squad level in real life. I could have wrote the whole review on why I dislike the madden ratings and why *in my opinion* my ratings are better. For example, the "Official" roster with live updates has Jonathan Taylor as the 6th best running back in the league (as of 12/12/2022) No matter what metric you look at, at the current time he is not even top 10. My roster brings him down to a cluster of players from 10 ~ 16, which is where he is performing at in real life as of this review. I do this for most players in almost every position, so star players are noticeable and replacement level guys feel like they should be replaced. The only positions I haven't touched are Kicker/Punter (i can't be bothered) and *most* Quarterbacks - I feel this is the only position group that EA graded well.Conclusion:If you have any of the other madden games, do not buy this one. I should've learnt my lesson, but I didn't.If you really like football and don't have madden 21 or 22, and only have a pc to play it on, then buy it if it goes on sale. I would highly recommend not paying full price for this game, 1. EA doesn't deserve your money, 2. It isn't worth $60.I hope you make the right decision for yourself, and also thank you for reading this review.

I know Madden is a buggy game, but up until now, I didn't mind it. So here's the reason I don't recommend this game:You can't play it. I did a full season of franchise mode with no bumps, got to the Super Bowl, won, and started a new one. I'm not sure what happened in the new one, but no matter where I leave off, the progress doesn't save, and yes, I've troubleshooted (troubleshot?) all of the different things that could be hindering it, and can only conclude that it's an EA problem. And, hey, Madden is buggy. I tried to accept that and move on. This wouldn't compel me to write a review and actually take action if not for where I'm sent back and the frequency of these send-backs. I played through to week 13 in my farthest attempt, and was sent all the way back to pick 8 of that year's draft when I logged back on. This happened 6 different times (with my making it to week 13, week 8, week 8, week 3, week 1, and postdraft before it sent me back), and that's when my patience ran out. I have yet to open the game again, and I don't plan on doing so until I get some kind of confirmation that this bug is fixed. If you only play nonstop on weekends or only ever play an entire season from draft to draft, you might not have this issue. But there's a reason I say "might," as I don't commit that level of time to just playing Madden, so I have no idea if the bug persists past that. It very well could, for all I know.Anyway. I'm not overly-affected by the monetary loss, so I'm keeping the game in my library in the hopes that EA figures out how to fix things, but I absolutely encourage everyone to avoid this game until it gets fixed. I've always thought the community can be pretty harsh on the developers, and I've tried to stay away from those levels of toxicity, but now I do believe that the game isn't just frustrating, but that it's unacceptable, intolerable, and ultimately unplayable.

_childDocuments_.review: So first thing to notice about all the negative reviews is that hardly anyone actually refunded their purchase. A second interesting observation is that many people don't seem to enjoy the game because they also have Madden '22: they feel they didn't get enough new features. But if that's the case... then why would you still buy this? After all, in the end all a game publisher is interested in is revenue. And that's exactly what all those nay-sayers are giving them.And not just that: a version which pays respect to the late John Madden by not only featuring him on the cover of the game, we now  get so called "Madden legacy games" where none other than John Madden himself is coaching the team(s) that are on the field: both a younger version as well as an older version of John are facing each other and if you pay attention to the playbooks that are in use then you  going to notice differences in strategy,  in comparison to the playbooks used by modern teams.What I also deeply respect is that EA's standard opening sequence ("") is  voiced by none other than John Madden. In my opinion this is quite a big deal because... EA is said to be pretty picky about their intros.The first thing you're going to notice is that the menu options are much more clear; instead of vague "Exhibition" modes and such we now have clear to the point options such as "Play now", "Ultimate Team", "Franchise", etc. making it really clear what kind of game you're about to start. What I personal also enjoy much better in Madden '23 is that training and practice options are easier to access. Hard to miss "Learn to play", eh? ;)Of course there's also a roster update: at the time of writing we're in the NFL pre-season for the superbowl and as always the active roster is accessible within Madden '23, meaning that you can (re)play games which are on the official NFL agenda, but also that the teams on the roster have also been updated. After all, players tend to come and go.You'll also notice that the matches themselves are more optimized. In Madden '22 you could basically walk across the whole field if you kept spamming the "turn around" option enough, that has been changed. In fact, the AI has also gotten an update because I clearly noticed that if I kept repeating a certain move then the AI would be more eager to counter that.For example: the first time I faked an attempt to kick the ball and instead passed it the opposing team seemed surprised. But the  time I did this (in a row) they were waiting and went straight for the quarterback. That didn't happen in Madden '22, not like this... and I really enjoy it.And finally... Madden '23 will notice if you already own Madden '22 and if it detects as much it'll pick up all your preferences and appy them automatically for you. The game even welcomes you back :)  you need to keep in mind that if you follow releases of sports games then obviously the developers aren't going to release a completely different game every single season because... why take the risks? At best they will add improvements, bugfixes and general cosmetic updates but in the end you should expect to play the same kind of game you did before.This is really  new... Somewhat offtopic but: 10 years ago I bought myself wrestling games, and guess what? Most of the changes ... were roster updates, and at best a few new storylines. But that was roughly it. Same thing happened with F1 games... a new roster and at best some new circuits got added.So if you already own Madden '22 then I  suggest that you look up some YouTube videos which demonstrate the gameplay on PC, and then make up your mind if that's what you'd might enjoy. I know I do but... yeah.If you're new to the Madden franchise and you're interested in picking up a sports game about American Football then this is a very solid title to grab. It can teach you the game of American football, you can customize just about everything, you can set up games the way  want them to be and of course... the commentary. I  the commentary in this game, it's so dynamic. Commentators in this game can actually notice  mistakes which you might be making. Remember me mentioning wrestling games above? Yah, their commentating doesn't even come close to this!However, if you already have Madden '22 then you need to keep in mind that while you'll be getting a new game, it will also have plenty of overlap. Generally speaking you'll be getting more of the same, but updated, optimized and with the legendary John Madden added to the game as well.Yes, it's true: there are features which are available on gaming consoles (XBox & Playstation) but which  included in the PC version. The reason for that - as far as I can tell - has everything to do with control. Gaming consoles use controllers which can detect pretty much any kind of movement and that kind of control is just not necessarily a thing on PC. After all: some players swear by using their keyboard & mouse, others use things like a Steam controller (myself included) whereas others rely on controllers from other brands. Heck, some even use the XBox or DualShock gaming controllers.But this  means that it's pretty much impossible for EA to rely on the same kind of game control which the consoles provide. And someting tells me that gamers will probably get even more upset should EA decide to provide these features on PC anyway, but  if you're going to buy a specific controller in addition to the game to make it all work.Each to their own but I'd rather focus myself on the stuff which IS included with the game; even on PC there's plenty of new stuff to find. I may be a casual gamer, fair enough, but I  notice changes in behavior where the AI is concerned in comparison to Madden '22.In the end all I care about is one thing: am I having fun with the game?  Guess what?  I do.  TOUCHDOWN!!!!

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not going to go on about next-gen graphics, because that's a dead horse, and frankly I'm not a graphics ♥♥♥♥♥.However...let's talk gameplay. I last played Madden '08, before purchasing this game. It is still a better game. Franchises were better, Superstar/FotF mode was better, and most importantly, the AI was better, somehow. I have literally ran in CIRCLES while on a route, 3 times, before my QB finally threw the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ball. It's like the AI chooses the worst possible outcome about 30% of the time. It waits until you reach the sideline so you can't gain YAC yards, despite you being open for the last 10 ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ steps. It throws ONLY to the primary receiver named in the playbook, even if they are covered by 3 dudes...unless YOU are that receiver, then it will throw a no-gain swing pass every single play, no matter how open you are. Your blockers will STARE at the opponent running past them to tackle you.My HB in FotF is actually too fast for the AI players, so I have to deliberately NOT sprint in order for the play to actually unfold properly, which is especially asinine since my HB is built for power, not speed. The player ratings do not matter, Josh Allen with a 95 rating is just as trash when controlled by the AI as Taigavailoa is with a 78 rating. The absolute worst part is that it makes any position that ISN'T HB a nightmare to progress in FotF. You have to rely on idiot AI to catch your passes and block for you as QB, and once the ball is out of your hands, it's all RNG. Play defense and watch even the best offenses in the NFL fail to score and capitalize on your good defensive plays. Play WR and get the ball thrown to you about 7% of the time it should be, the other 93% of the time you get to watch the AI perform like your teammates are crippled. Mentally. HB is the only somewhat palatable choice because, no matter how stupid the AI gets, I can just hand myself the ball and truck people until it all evens out again.The physics are OK, but the players fall all over themselves like drunken toddlers from the smallest nudges, even by your own teammates, which, with the pathetic AI, happens far more than is acceptable. Changing direction is a stat now, because apparently only the top 1% of athletes in the world know how to turn around, leading to instances where your character SHOULD just turn, but instead runs a circle with a 5 yard radius. Whoever had that idea should not breed.I get it's EA, and subpar is what they do...but how the actual ♥♥♥♥ did they go THIS far backwards? Everything else about the game aside, how the HELL is the AI significantly stupider that it was over 15 years ago?

_childDocuments_.review: After playing the last years Madden on Xbox one the PC version of Madden 23 is a graphical upgrade. If you are looking for a completely new experience compared to last years last gen Madden this game will not be that. EA has made some noticeable improvements especially defensively, the AI man and zone coverage logic seems like an upgrade from last year. Franchise mode has an upgraded player interest system that adds a new dynamic to roster happiness. Don’t get me wrong the tackle animations are virtually the same from last year, your running back with plow into a stout defensive line to be not gang tackled but glitched into a single man tackle. Sometimes hilariously falling forward through players for 8 yards! But that’s Madden right! Madden needs a physics based system to create NFL simulation realism when it comes to game physics and mechanics. Overall I’m not overly disappointed by this years Madden, but is it worth the price tag of 59.99? Again I would say nay, all in all this game could have been released for half the price as a Madden 22 DLC. Personally I do like playing Madden 23, especially the connected franchise mode though the experience does lack immersion in some areas, a system that included player hold outs during training camp, 5th year contract options, offseason Free agency drama, and random retirements would go a long way to the immersion of this game. What Madden consistently fails at capturing is the excitement of the NFL off the field as well, previous Maddens during the early 2000’s achieved this feat well. Maybe, the day will come again when Madden reigns supreme as the best dynasty experience, but today it doesn’t live it up to its predecessors. Finally, I would buy this game but wait till it’s on sale, because the features offered are not a large enough leap for the price tag.

name: Noreya: The Gold Project
detailed_description: Wishlist now! About the Game Noreya: The Gold Project is a 2D pixel-art metroidvania game set in a dark fantasy universe. The game offers players a choice between allegiance to the God of Light and Shadow or the God of Greed! But be careful! Decisions made in the game affect your progression by changing the available paths and abilities. The game's key art creates a unique experience for gamers with no run being the same as others, this duality encourages players to explore both paths. Salluste, the God of Greed, took power over the city of Lemia after imprisoning the Goddess of Light. Kali, a fighter who lost everything at the hands of the gods, sets out for the city to verify the rumors surrounding this new god who corrupts and subjugates humans in exchange for wealth. Explore the City of Gold and its cathedral, confront the creatures of shadow and gold, pledge allegiance to the God of your choice to embody their power, or detach yourself from the Gods and suffer their wrath. Game features Meticulously crafted pixel art 2 Unique persistent worlds that evolve according to your chosen allegiance to the gods (The Path of Gold or The Path of Light) A skill tree with over 50 abilities! ⚔️12 memorable bosses you can face in any order Over 25 totally unique monsters with innovative gameplay surrounding each monster. Easy-to-play, hard-to-master controls. Smooth, pleasant platforming. Fast, dynamic gameplay. Pixel-perfect combat, subtle and accessible. Several possible endings. An original, epic soundtrack by Sarys and Xavier Dang (MisterMV), which evolves according to your allegiance. An original storyline scattered around the world: find all the steles in the game to understand the history and mysteries surrounding the gods (optional storyline). A non-linear World: discover the world as you please Backstory: The world of Noreya In time immemorial, seven deities joined forces to shape the land we know today as Noreya. Such was the power of the Seven that Men, as a sign of respect but also out of fear, began to worship them. Some sinners, however, strayed from the path, bringing out the most maliciously treacherous parts of themselves. From this malice came new deities, gaining their powers from the servitude of their subjects. In the lands of Lemia, home of the primordial Goddess of Light, an endless famine persisted. The poor inhabitants' desire for wealth benefited the God of Avarice, who in turn promised an end to their misery. The god everyone now calls the 'God of Gold' transformed all his followers into shapeless, tormented creatures: the golden shadows. Lemia, once so luminous, now gives way to unhealthy greed. Duality: Pledge allegiance and receive the power of the gods! With a skill tree containing over 50 skills, you can evolve according to your allegiance to the Goddess of Light or the God of Gold. You can also play double duty, but in this case you won't have access to the most powerful spells. It's up to you to find the best balance for your style of play. A world for every god. No more metroidvania with a single map to discover. In the world of Noreya, the world changes according to your allegiance. Are you familiar with the Golden World and have now decided to worship the Light? Get ready for a whole new experience, forge ahead as you discover which areas have changed and discover which parts of the game are no longer accessible! However, in turn get ready to explore other new adventures that now await the servant of the Light! Each version of the world conceals secrets and exclusive bonuses. Can you find the artifacts hidden in the depths of the world? Only time will tell! The soundtrack Signed by the incredible duo Sarys / MisterMV, enjoy an original soundtrack that will accompany you throughout your adventure. Switch allegiance, and the music will change and evolve with you. A game for arachnophobes: Initially, we had planned to include spiders in the game, but we realized that many players are arachnophobic. WIth this in mind, we worked on coming up with an alternative that works and retains the feel of the underground environments. But who knows, maybe one day the spiders of Noreya will be released. But that's a tale for another time. Read more on : Recent Events & Announcements

_childDocuments_.review: I wish so badly that I could recommend this game because its presentation is really quite striking: the pixel art is gorgeous and I love the way the art design makes use of color, light, shadow, foreground and background. The soundtrack is also incredible, it's lush and atmospheric, and the production values are super high. The story setup contains a lot of promise: you're a warrior caught in a struggle between two warring gods, with each offering you power and dominion if you pledge your allegiance to them. There's a skill tree with branching paths, and who you choose to ally yourself with will grant you unique abilities and unlock certain paths in the game world. I love the inclusion of RPG elements like this, and I think the potential replay value for this title is quite high.This game is a joy to look at, a joy to listen to, and it's clear that there is a lot of creativity on offer here, but ultimately I cannot recommend it for the simple reason that it is just no fun to *play*. Movement is clunky, it's a beautiful world but it feels like a chore to traverse. Combat...hoo boy...combat is *borderline non-functional*. There is no block, no dodge, and your sword has an absolutely pathetic reach. The first boss, Crawley, clings to walls and jumps all over the arena. Because you have no ranged attack and your sword's reach is so short, your only hope of defeating him is to just get in close and swing wildly, but it's nearly impossible to do that without taking damage yourself because touching the boss hurts you. Oh and did I mention, the boss has no visible health bar, so you can try the fight over and over again without knowing if you've made any meaningful progress whatsoever. That's what this fight boils down to: run in, mash the X button, and just HOPE that you kill the boss before it kills you, 3 hits and you're dead. That is just absolutely inexcusable, and when the rest of the game is as strong as it is, it is just such a shame that the combat completely sinks the experience.Don't get me wrong, I love difficult games! Blasphemous I and II are two of my favorite games of all time, and those games are absolutely *white-knuckle* difficult, the difference is that those games have such rock-solid fundamentals that the challenge always feels fair, even if it can be extremely brutal. In this game, I feel like I'm getting my ass kicked over and over again, not because the game is offering any kind of legitimate challenge, but because I keep falling victim to this clunky combat system and bad game design. This game has so much going for it, but unless the combat receives a complete overhaul before release, I can't recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Noreya: The Gold Project

_childDocuments_.review: I'm incredibly torn as to whether to recommend this game. My first 10-15 or so hours with Noreya were an absolute joy, it felt like a really solid little metroidvania, with some really delightful pixel art, a clear visual style throughout. The level designs were nice, the unlocks and expansion of traversal all felt good, and I was having a great time exploring the world. I especially enjoyed the mechanics requiring switching the world between states, and would've loved to see it featured a bit more prominently, and for the switching to be less clunky (teleporting around to find the statue I needed to alternate was a bit tedious). The story was light, but present, and the writing, although not exceptional, was perfectly serviceable. The controls and combat felt fairly snappy and enjoyable. I thoroughly enjoyed the forgiving nature of the game, with saves per room, nigh-infinite healing using a meagre amount of currency (even if it is a little _too_ slow), and quick resets at either the current room or the last hub. Unfortunately, the deeper I got, the more the rough edges started to grate away at me. It started with the odd little quirk, a lack of polish here and there. Random use of soft particle effects, in an otherwise beautiful pixel art setting (the moths and hit effects). The annoying pulsing shadows when left on one health. The repetitive sound design of the enemies (I ruthlessly murder the bats ASAP just to stop the damn flapping). An angry worm moving in unpredictable ways. A bugged room transition that consistently placed me inside the floor. Pixelated text rendering and a myriad of fonts. Odd bugs, like things not spawning occasionally, or things happening out of sync. Confusing menu behaviour (just let me press B to close the dang thing).These weren't really enough to sway my feelings though. I was still having fun, and I can forgive a recent release from a small team a lot of issues. The bigger problems really started showing as I progressed deeper into the game, and it's with the enemy behaviour design.Some of this is apparent earlier in the game, although it's not very problematic. Little things, like enemies that will endless walk towards the nearest edge of a platform attempting to reach you, making it almost impossible to safely jump to the platform without defeating them first. This is exacerbated by enemy attack patterns, which often have very little telegraphing before the attack occurs, and can have deceptively long range.This became more egregious the deeper I got. There's a moth type enemy that will attempt to float above you, maintaining a fixed distance, and drop projectiles in a fixed pattern. This can make it almost impossible to deal with them by regular means, unless you can very quickly scale something faster than they will float, or before they aggro. There's a reaper style of enemy, with scissors and a blade you encounter mid gameish. They have an incredibly repetitive attack pattern, that offers little room for rebuttal, and absolutely zero opportunity for using your combo attacks without tanking some damage.This is the general issue that persists amongst the enemies in Noreya - they're overly aggressive, especially when confronted with many at once. Despite attempting to minimise the amount of hits I'd take, after a while I began to accept there were two options for dealing with most enemies. Either cheese them, by finding a location you could avoid their attacks, while still attacking them and get them stuck there until they died. Or, accept that in most encounters, you're probably going to lose some health. This problem is exacerbated by the size of enemy hitboxes, and their desire to endlessly run at you. Many times I felt like I was taking damage when I hadn't made contact with the enemy. For the most part, this is fine. By no means game breaking. A bit tiring and oft disappointing, but manageable. I'm still having fun.The bosses in Noreya are all so very close to being excellent. Most of them have a nicely designed arena to fight in, and a unique set of attack patterns and puzzles to solve. Unfortunately, they mostly suffer from the same problems as the enemies, only far worse.- hitboxes on their attacks are often poorly represented, leading to regularly being hit when you feel you should've avoided damage- hitboxes on the enemies themselves being hard to understand, again leading to regularly taking damage from contact with the boss- bosses being very large, and arenas offering little space to manoeuvre around the bosses without taking damage. Combine this with their propensity to push you into corners, and you guaranteed to lose some health. (side note: dodges seemingly have no iframes, and many of the bosses are larger than your jump height, or float obnoxiously around head height, leaving you no room to get around them)- poorly telegraphed attacks (this is particularly prevalent on the sword and mage bosses in the cathedral)- randomised attack patterns (the lack of telegraphing could be manageable if you could learn the order of attacks. from my tests, you can't)- incredibly dodgy homing behaviour. Lots of the bosses use attacks with some degree of tracking, which often leaves you with nowhere to go. Hyper aggressive tracking combined with oversized hitboxes and small arenas with limited mobility leads to frustration. (Sword guy and Worm both absolutely sucked for this)In the end, I found the most effective way to handle most of the bosses was just... to stop trying to avoid attacks, and just absolutely wail on them, using my oversized health pool and the few seconds of invulnerability from taking damage to beat them into submission before I died. This was completely unsatisfying and let me feeling disappointed instead of victorious.And now I've landed at finally fighting Greed. And I am not having any fun. Sadly, I fear this is where my journey ends. The combination of tight platforming combined with inconsistent, unpredictable attack patterns is just frustrating. Once again, I'm just crutching on my health pool instead of trying to do better, because it feels more like fluke than skill. And then you get to the actual fight, and once again, you're backed into a corner - this fight even introduces walls you can't wall jump off, completely pinning you into corners with the oversized boss and his infinite ads. The thing that upsets me the most is I can see so clearly the vision for these encounters, and they're great. There is just so much potential packed into this, that is just falling short by lacklustre execution. Despite all this, I really want to say give it a go. I still have 20 hours of mostly good times from this game. All the earlier content felt really solid, and really enjoyable. I cannot stress that enough. Even the earlier bosses felt good. And the developers are still actively patching and fixing things, so I'm sure it's going to get better. For that alone, I want to recommend it. But I recommend it with a big dose of caution. My problems could well just be a skill issue, you might have a great time. EDIT: I left Greed alone, had dinner, and continued my exploration. 100%'d the map, found all the items, and basically did everything else I possibly could. Had a great time. Came back after getting beefy, wailed on Greed first try. Turns out bosses are hard when you're hangry. The game is good, although I still think the sword guy and mage guy were both kinda bad compared to everything else. The enemy behaviour and hitboxes are still a little rough, but nothing so severe as to tarnish the gold project. Certain enemy behaviours got easier to deal with after unlocking certain tools, but were ultimately still a bit of a pain. I'm going to rewrite this review tomorrow to sound a little less negative, because I really have enjoyed this game <3

_childDocuments_.review: I have a lot of little complaints about this game that I can excuse from a small studio. The one thing I can't forgive is how bad and unpolished the combat is. Enemies are far too mobile compared to the player, at least in the early stages of the game. Many attacks are also not telegraphed so you are best off avoiding anything but the most basic enemies or resort to tedious hit and run tactics. Game difficulty should come from complex mechanics not cheap tricks.Also, the currency you use to purchase skills is also used to heal which is just strange and unrewarding. I shouldn't have to choose between healing and progressing my character.The simplest change to make this game more tolerable would be adding basic knockback/stun to enemies from player attacks. Without that I consider this game simply unplayable.

_childDocuments_.review: An amazing metroidvania!**The good:**- The story was very interesting, ignore the first 5 story messages that include the tutorial, the rest of the writing is pretty good- Combat is simple but fast and if it's too hard, you can explore further to make it easier. The skills are way more helpful than I expected.- The exploration in this game is top-notch! The map is enormous, possibly bigger than Hollow Knight. Full of secrets. There are a few harder platforming sections**Neutral**- The first 5 bosses were disappointing, while the last 2 were very entertaining and challenging.- The soundtrack is small (in number of songs), given how big the map is, it gets repetitive unfortunately (even if it's a good fit for the game)**Bad**- The early game is poor and does this game a disservice by pushing people away. I'd argue wait until you get the first "story skill", that's when the game picks up. Also the writing looked bad early, but became really interesting later on**8/10. I highly recommend it.** I was struggling to find something to play after DOOMBLADE and Nine Sols, I tried Deviator (huge disappointment), Biomorph which I tried hard to get into, but the combat, movement and plot just aren't there. Then somebody on reddit recommended this and I was hooked. Finished in 3 days (20 hours).

_childDocuments_.review: A promising metroidvania with a potential to become great!The art and music are amazing as it is.The gameplay is fluid with the character becoming more versatile as more powers are unlocked as you progress, similar to classic metroidvanias, reminding me quite much Hollow Knight.The skill tree is nice but in the balance between gold and light does not seem ideal at the early access. Similarly, the impact of the allegiance to the world is quite small and the map changes seem to buggy, unless it is voluntary for some rooms to not become visible, especially in the light allegiance. I would have hoped to see more impact from allegiances on the gameplay.Looking forward to the final version of the game !

I am recommending because the developer seems very responsive and hopefully these issues will be fixed quickly. I waited patiently for this game for quite some time because I prefer to wait for the finished product rather than play early access. I expect a newly released indie to have some issues, and the game crashed a few times in my overall play, but my progress loss was minimal. For $25 it would be nice if controller support did not require a workaround, but was an easy enough fix. My main issue was that in large rooms with bosses (looking at you giant worm) there was screen stutter. This also affected platforming at times. Maybe this is only on steam deck, if this is not an issue on windows then I recommend the game. Otherwise wait for a couple patches.

_childDocuments_.review: I personally loved this game. I waited to complete the game before commenting. I also was a backer of this project.I really loved the art, the music, the level design, the puzzles, and most of all the lore; I truly found the lore very interesting, where you follow pieces of the journey of a human in a world of deities, and you fight to restore your life.While a lot of people could complaint about the challenges, such as the early and general difficulties of the game and some awful bosses, the best advice I can give you is to aim beyond those obstacles. Yes there is a lot of monsters in every room which will put a threat in your exploration, and at the early game they will be the main issue, but don’t judge the game only on this mechanism.Take time to apprehend the gameplay, play with the move and skill sets of your character. The game gets easier once you start to understand how to explore and earn some useful abilities. There is more than one way to do a lot of stuff in this game. And in late game, they don’t pose a threat anymore.For a MetroidVania-like game, this is my first experience where platforming is this important, and I kind of like it (I mostly played Metroid games and I don’t recall so much platforming gameplay).For a few negative points, the game has some coding issues (performance issue, some crashes, exceptions) (note: I also played on Linux but it’s not specific to this platform), but the devs truly worked on fixing those, bringing support, so maybe I should say "had"? And nothing to break your experience. Well except when I got a corrupted save file, but I decided to still play the game, so I started again and I noticed how I much improved from my first run. Don’t give up.I also got sometimes frustrated by some bosses (oh boy I spent a lot of time on one of the first boss and endgame ones), because they require to be steady and have player stamina, but it gets easier with experience and a bit of dedication. Advice: maybe try to explore more when stuck in front of a tedious fight so you can find some welcomed powerups.A new update with boss health bar is in process of being released, so I guess it makes fights easier when you can see where you reach.The game is not too long, 15 to 20 hours top, for a full run while discovering, which is nice.I look further to see more games from the same studio and publisher. Thanks for such a nice gameplay experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Noreya: The Gold Project

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very good metroidvania, I've been waiting since early access for this and it definitely didn't disappoint. _childDocuments_.review: Noreya the gold project had me hooked from start to finish over the course of it's respectable 15 hours runtime. I was thoroughly impressed by nearly everything the game had to offer with my only minor complaints being that the achievements are annoying and that it's a bit unbalanced. I have literally no other complaints about this game so it's a real standout metroidvania of this year for me alongside ultros, because both brought something new to the table. In Noreya's case this is the dual nature of devoting yourself to one god or the other which not only affects your skill tree but also the actual map! Depending on your allegiance to gold/light some rooms of the map will change and you can swap this around to explore both worlds. Said map is the real highlight of the game for me with utterly brilliant level design paired with perfect controls providing an exhilirating mix of combat, puzzling and platforming.The platforming in this game sticks pretty close to the classics like wall jump and air dash, which all handle exactly how you want them to, but also innovates with the spirit mechanic. A few hours into the game you unlock the ability to project your spirit outside of your body which allows you to fight certain enemies but more importantly changes the platforming. There's platforms that only have collision for your spirit as well as obstacles that are either dangerous to your spirit or your body. The excellent controls and this brilliant spirit mechanic allowed the devs to make some really clever and fun platforming sections/puzzles. Some of these span several rooms across both worlds! So going back and forth to gradually unlock a key item is engaging and rewarding. This comes into play mostly for getting the true ending which was one of the most fun paths to a true ending i've done in a metroidvania in a while.I cannot overstate how cool the level design was, each room felt so unique and biomes each have their own mechanics. They're also of respectable size and look downright incredible. This game has some S-tier pixel art, with each environment bursting with detail and colour. I took MANY screenshots playing this game and was constantly glued to my screen looking at all the beautiful backgrounds. The biomes are wonderfully complemented by a captivating OST that i wish they sold seperately. Said soundtrack also changes dynamically when you are in combat although this is over pretty fast since the radius is rather small. Still this element which i normally don't like was executed very well, never breaking the pace as the combat tunes were additive to the OST instead of distracting from it. Unfortunately the sound effects are a bit lacking but that's not all too uncommon for an indie game. Combat still felt satisfying despite the lack of impact coming from the SFX, mainly thanks to the aforementioned tight controls. It started of moderately challenging on the medium difficulty but gradually got a LOT easier. This is because there's tons of upgrades to find and the skill tree which gives you very powerful perks. Said skill tree is dependant on your allegiance and can also be respecced at will which is very  much appreciated. You can only upgrade your skill tree at god statues which are properly spread around the map in right places. One of the first perks you can pick up is a fast travel between god statues which is once again very much appreciated. The whole game has so many quality of life features that just made it non frustrating. Respawning for example happens on a per room basis (not on hard mode though) so you can quickly get back in the action should you fall in battle which won't happen that much but is always possible.This is because the game is rather quite easy going in terms of combat. Healing takes a while if you channel your heal that costs gold, of which you will have a LOT laying around since enemies drop quite a bit. There's other ways to heal in the skill tree which is where the game felt a bit unbalanced. There's a lifesteal perk that is quite literally overpowered and allows you to brute force bosses but no one is forcing you to take this perk so you can challenge yourself accordingly. Only the true final boss served as a BIG leap in difficulty but like the bosses before it, this fight was very well designed and fun. Every boss felt unique and fair which also counts for regular enemies. Sure the combat could have been more engaging but there's so many soulsvania's with tediously difficult combat that it was fun to have one that kept the pace. Especially with the fast paced movement mechanics!Performance or bugs won't slow you down either as this game runs smooth all the way through with no bugs or crashes to tarnish the experience. It's a wonderfully made game and it even delivers on, the in my opinion least important aspect of a metroidvania, which is story. Scattered around the world are short pieces of text left behind by an important character that gradually piece together to tell a compelling narrative with a very satisfying conclusion. There were some grammar/spelling mistakes but as a whole it worked very well. Sometimes it even gave hints for cool mechanics such as using enemies to activate switches out of reach. You need to use all these tricks at the end to fully explore the map so for completionists such as myself it's a blast to 100% both maps. Only the achievements are a bit annoying, some requiring very specific replays but most being kill 100/200/300 of each enemy type. Getting these is a grind but I myself am perfectly content with my one 100% playthrough and i think you could be to. Play this game! :)

_childDocuments_.review: Solid little puzzle platformer/metroidvania. Pros: - Movement silky smooth, really it's fantastic and responsive. I'd like a longer dash and maybe a double jump but everything works- Areas distinctive and visually rich. It's beautiful execution of a pixel art style.- sound track ok- lots of interesting lore- Plenty of skills and unlockables (4 main movement/progression skills and many more game inhancers)Cons- Balance issues, early game is tricky end game is a total cake walk when you have enough health and damage to go toe to toe with the last 3-4 bosses including the end boss- Exp/Gold acquisition falls off. Early game you'll be buying new skills and upgrades all the time. Late game you'll be grinding loops to spend thousands of gold per skill point - Story is told in disjointed text dumps and some of the world mechanics aren't hugely clear (light/gold switching for example)This game is value for money. I would have happily paid twice as much for it. I enjoyed it and i'd strongly recommend it to anyone who loves a good puzzle platformer.

_childDocuments_.review: An unexpected metroidvania gem, that requires a little appetite for punishment.Noreya is unusual as far as the genre goes. There's very little telegraphing what abilities you'll get and some are quite surprising. Enemies will seem very unfair until getting a chunk of these but it balances with a nice restart level/area option or just going back to your last resting place with all your coins so you can upgrade and come back. The 1.1 rework helped a great deal as well, you have some more traditional iframes now, less tedium and boss health bars at last.The game's real weakness isn't from the game itself in my opinion. It's the lack of information around it. You'll typically find at least blogspam sites with guides on areas, abilities, tricky puzzles and enemies but for some reason Noreya hasn't spawned any of those. So finding the True Ending will be leg work, reading and some brute forcing for example. Hopefully this will change in time as the game gets picked up by more people as it deserves to.

name: The Last Hero of Nostalgaia
detailed_description: The Last Hero of Nostalgaia is a satirical action-adventure, driven by a dark story, set in an incredibly rich and complex world. Nostalgaia, the world of videogames, is collapsing backwards into a mysterious pixelation, with every particle of fidelity bleeding away. Oblivion seemingly awaits even our most cherished gaming memories. But as the lighting dims and frames diminish, with the world on the brink of extinction, hope emerges to fight back. As the most hideous pixelated hero to ever spawn in Nostalgaia, you must fight through an army of its mindless inhabitants, while being jeered by a cynical narrator who despises your very existence. Featuring hard but fair combat that fans of the genre will relish, along with *full character customization, unique battle armor and engaging narrative mechanics rich in lore, The Last Hero of Nostalgaia’s twisted and wicked tale is prepared to send you headfirst into almost certain death around its every vertex. Set in a world celebrating video game nostalgia, The Last Hero of Nostalgaia features hard but fair souls-like exploration and combat, combined with a twisted, wicked tale told by a cynical narrator Play together through online co-op and brave the pixelization together! Uncover various suits of armor and weapons, each with their own unique lore and attributes

_childDocuments_.review: Iron Pineapple is probably going to like this one.Overall, the standout feature is the nicely interwoven world / level design. Although enemy density is a little inconsistent - sometimes there's a bit too many, sometimes a bit too few - the way the map loops back around on itself really has a Demon's Souls / Dark Souls 1 vibe. I am very impressed.Combat is just what you'd expect, it's literally Dark Souls sans a separate parry button. You can rebind controls for both controller and mouse/keyboard, which is a very nice touch. I've noticed a bit of jankiness with the camera - as always, it's the hardest boss. Sometimes even when locked on I can miss a target that, by rights, I should have hit. Not the end of the world but definitely slightly less polished than a typical Souls game. Will hopefully get better with new patches.The lighthearted theme is a welcome change of pace from the now somewhat tiresome "the flame is fading and the world is rotting" ethos that the Souls series is defined by.Enemies can become a bit repetitive within an area, but probably no worse than a Souls game in this regard. There's decent enemy diversity overall, at least from what I've played so far (estimated to be roughly half the game).All in all, a very nice Souls-like with a great, lighthearted theme. I'm enjoying it quite a lot.

_childDocuments_.review: Finished the game a few minutes ago and really enjoyed it. The game keeps the style of the average souls-like game but gives it the fresh twist of not taking itself too seriously, the areas, the bosses and the items are all filled with references to classic games that will make any gamer chuckle.The gameplay itself is not the greatest, it's slow (similar to Dark Souls 1 and 2) and that made some portions feel unfair or tedious to get through (the train portion in specific) but overall the game is not more challenging than any of the souls games.I had a lot of fun with the boss fights given they are mostly references to souls bosses or other game characters.Also really liked the remembering system looking for the lore of the weapons in order to reach their full potential really gave the game some extra contente and stuff to be done, and seeing the blend of 2d and 3d in the artstyle really gave it a unique look.It's a great game and i had a lot of fun with it.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely!This game is amazing, with a unique story, great combat, and fun mechanics that give a great twist to meta-games and souls-like games. But these bugs are ruining my experience for sure.Sure, there's a few immersion-breaking issues with the game's targeting, tracking, and collisions, but those almost add to the charm of this game. Especially when you see the player messages floating in mid-air and you try to figure out how to find and read them! lolThis game is definitely a gem that everyone who enjoys a good story and a souls-like experience should add to their collection.I will say that my previous review called out a number of missing map areas, NPCs, and similar, and it turns out that simply uninstalling then reinstalling the game was all it took to fix it. Likely one of the files got corrupted causing this issue, but in such a way that Steam's verification check wouldn't notice anything. So if you consistently are missing areas of the map that should definitely be there and resting at a shrine, killing some enemies, or reloading the game after saving it doesn't work, then simply uninstall then reinstall.I will also say that the devs are amazing and very responsive! They were a great help in the process of figuring out what was going on, and it was definitely a pleasure interacting with them. Thankfully we were able to figure out this solution even if we weren't able to determine the initial cause. And now that my game's working, I think I'll start a new play-through to see what I missed due to corrupted files the first time around! :)

_childDocuments_.review: The gameplay of Dark Souls + the humour of The Stanley Parable + the style of Medievil.This is as Souls-like as you can get while still being unique in its own way. This is a much simpler game that doesn't bog the player down with obtuse mechanics and useless filler items. The game's tongue and cheek humour is bound get get at least a few laughs while not overstaying its welcome. The combat is snappy and overall feels very smooth to handle, but some of the weapons have deceptive ranges-- a sword's sweeping attack looks like it would be good for crowd control but actually doesn't reach as far as you would think. The level up stats are easy to grasp which allows for quick character building without paragraphs of explanation. Overall, a great Souls-like for beginners and a fun, less stressful adventure for series veterans.

STEAM Game Normal, lazy✅	Unique world and story✅	Satire sense of humor that I enjoyed✅	Gameplay feels for most part like dark souls 1✅	Plenty of unique features✅	World is fairly fun✅	Unique visual design and pretty enjoyable✅	Enjoyable 4th wall breaking and various references/parodies✅	NPC dialogues and voice acting is pretty good❌	Lazy world interconnection design❌	Quest progression is even more obscure than any souls game❌	No NG+ for easier achieve hunting❌	Combat feels like DS1 but weapons are fairly weightless❌	Fast travel system is lacking❌	A lot of back-forwards running for completionist run❌	As for writing review date game has bunch of technical issues and mishaps that need to be polishedFairly unique soulslike. _childDocuments_.review: Unironically one of the best Non-FromSoftware souls-like games out there. Keeps to tradition, using mechanics that are found in all three Dark Souls games, while also introducing new mechanics that fit really well within the genre. Surprisingly detailed, with great level-design. The gimmick of reintroducing resolution to the world and items is well done and makes loot more exciting.Some enemy and boss attacks are a little wonky, and can sometimes be frustrating to navigate, but overall combat and movement feel solid. Takes some getting used to however.The game supports online co-op with one other person as well. I haven't personally tried the co-op, but I imagine it uses a peer-to-peer connection, so be wary of that. Also, if you do want to co-op with friend, ensure you don't play too far ahead, as both players must be at the same spot in the story in order to play together.8/10 The pop-culture references and easter eggs are great.

_childDocuments_.review: Hearing this very quote is rather tiresome nowadays, as this uninformative and vague phrase is overused for every second action role-playing experience that dares to borrow one or two minor mechanics, and in worse cases, just because it is harder to play… as if  invented the difficulty itself. And yet here I am, baiting myself for yet another title that declares to have such an allegiance.But somehow, in its own twisted way,  can claim that it truly is a – and I despise that term – . How so? With its satirical approach, it parodies this stereotyped subgenre, purposefully trying to replicate it, and then it proceeds to jab at other games as well (unless they were all  and we, mere mortals, were not ready for such a truth just yet).It sounds like a recipe for disaster, right?Well, even with its shortcomings, its respective qualities pleasantly surprised me!Let us start from the beginning, though. You spawn as a bunch of pixelated sticks in humanoid form, whose purpose is to stop the pixelation of the video-gaming world of Nostalgaia. Yet, a vicious Narrator stands in your way; not only that he humorously describes your whole journey, but he also actively influences both the story and gameplay, which can bring sudden unexpected twists. That reminded me of , albeit there it was crazier. Nevertheless, the narrative became my favourite part, as it managed to entertain me from start to finish; do not be afraid, though, as even if it throws a lot of quips at you, it also lets you play in peace for a bit, so it does not overstay its welcome.Thus, the audiovisual spectacle naturally goes hand in hand with the plot, not only in the form of environmental storytelling but due to the interventions of the Narrator, as well.  constantly fiddles with its visual presentation, mixing both two and three-dimensional environments that are portrayed by modern, charming visuals as well as by intentionally dated 8-bit ones; even enemies abide by such changes. Unfortunately, the soundtrack undermines it a bit in my eyes, as I can only think of like two tracks that stuck with me.Now, the gameplay – namely the movement and combat – is straight up like the first . I mean, even some animations look the same! It is much slower, especially when compared to most of the modern, fast-paced , but that is the point! To make you crawl for those good ol’ days. Well, if  can get away with reusing a lot of stuff while pretending to be a new shining title, then why should I scold this one for trying to bring a bit of nostalgia for satirical purposes? And as I said, it spreads its wings and jabs at other – even totally different – subgenres, as you can find stuff like armour from , for example.So, as the gameplay loop is just like the one from older  instalments, you will galavant around the world without a map, trying to figure out where to go next while encountering various aggressive foes to fight with. And while it seems like your regular linear experience at first, it opens up after a few hours, letting you taste its wonderfully interconnected places with tons of shortcuts. That bewitched me! I mean, even newer  games abandoned this approach, yet this unknown indie title went full in and did so! And I am not pulling your leg now, but level design-wise, it did a splendid job.Moreover, in later parts, it also brings numerous environmental gimmicks that spice up your journey. Thus, a deadly fog might appear while you walk through the woods, or you have to form a path by interacting with moving staircases, as in . I adored locations like these, as they always brought a breath of fresh air, changing the gameplay loop a bit.It also tries to push you into exploring more by adding brief riddles to items’ descriptions—in order to unlock their full power, like increasing their stats or gaining an additional passive bonus, you need to find the place of their origin or importance. While I love mechanics like these, they are (un)fortunately not crucial for completing your playthrough. Not that I would want to prolong the playtime in an artificial way, but I still think it could have had more of an impact. And I would honestly wish to see this more in some of the upcoming titles.When it comes to the enemies, they get more interesting once you progress a bit, as well. At first, they are basic and pretty much defenceless against your rain of light attacks or well-timed heavy strikes. Yet, some get more aggressive later on, punishing your cocky approach. And even though the game lasts for about fourteen hours, it has a sweet variety of foes to fight, constantly revealing new types in each location. But, I had this issue in a few instances: some spots felt a bit crowded while others were a bit empty. Mind you, it is not like that all the time, but when it happens, it is noticeable enough.The bosses would be the most ambivalent aspect, though. On the one hand, I appreciate their references or hilarious ideas that enliven them, even if just visually. On the other hand, their encounters are not that thrilling, sadly. Not even that difficult, if I am being honest. Still, I would not call them terrible, as there are other contenders for that , but they are just mediocre. So, if I could improve only one part, it would be this!Nevertheless, if you would have any difficulties, then there are both non-playable characters and even real players at your disposal. And as it is custom, anyone can share those infamous messages, and I feel most of their respective options are present just because of the meme potential that  unintentionally created. I get that they are there because the community loves them, but seeing  at every second corpse got old for me after all these years. Maybe I expected something unique, but if we are supposed to be nostalgic, we should go full in, I guess.Yet, even with some of these shortcomings,  is still a captivating and humorous experience from start to finish, as its light-hearted approach to the narrative, playful visuals and excellent level design, as well as a bunch of references, make it a solid indie title that I can recommend. But, if you are specifically looking for another  with a superb or even just fast-paced combat system, then it might not be for you.

_childDocuments_.review: I had a lot of fun for the first 1/3 of the game, but as time went on it started seeping in how un-polished this game is. Level design, bosses, hit detection, a lot of it just started to unravel for me.And by the time I was 2/3 into the game I genuinely thought the game was over. But it kept going. Then it kept going more.Also the attempt of having the narrator be an antithesis to us is a neat concept, but it gets wasted. Most of the game you'll forget he's there, and even when he does talk it's so try-hard, hammy, and not funny at all. They tried really hard to capture the wit and charm of the narrator from The Stanley Parable, but it just feels so flat and annoying, even.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Hero of Nostalgaia

_childDocuments_.review: A soulslike is a hilarious genre to pick for your post modern self-aware narrated adventure game about player agency. The Last Hero of Nostalgaia uses iconic video game symbols like blue shells and buster swords as carrots on sticks to move you through a world that’s fundamentally soulsian with a sprinkle of Stanley Parable.That blend isn’t always perfect: a narrator who doesn’t even try to keep up with your exploring prevents the satire from being as biting as it could be, and an inelegant “souls at home” combat system gets a little tired by the end…but Nostalgaia has wheat for its chaff. It manages to squeeze beauty out of its intentionally low-fidelity aesthetic in surprising ways, and it has the courage to look at its inspirations and successfully identify some cool new ways to play with them.It’s never quite the timeless classic the games it’s sourcing from are, but it creates fun in its own way.SoulsLOVE might be a more appropriate term for this one than soulslike. From Dark Souls It doesn’t just borrow some key mechanics and a tough but fair difficulty, but wholesale lifts animations, a selfish selfless binary final choice, and even literal locations. There’s near 1:1 recreations of both Firelink Shrine and the entrance to the Demon Ruins here. There’s an earnest admiration for the games that cane before here in a way that’s more transparent than you’d usually expect; I’m the first to roll my eyes whenever “it’s dangerous to go alone, take this!” Appears as a ‘gamer cameo’’’…in a media landscape that’s increasingly cross-promotional, more and more games are coming out of the least glamorous third of a media centipede.I had my hesitations about a game within which referential humor and nostalgic pandering were the driving force, and yet “the last hero of Nostalgaia”, sold me on the idea because it did so in a way that’s mechanically significant.What unifies all of the games disparate Easter eggs and reference based equipment is the gamification of Dark Souls lore text. Every item and weapon you pick up is both an homage to some classic gaming hero but also a riddle to be solved. Open up your inventory and read the associated description to find a clue that prods you towards some landmark out in the world, the association to which will grant that item a visual upgrade, some bonus stats, and even progression towards a character wide unlock system that benefits you beyond that individual item being equipped.It’s not the only mechanism that handles your power ups but it is the most interesting, and for me it was damn effective. It serves a few different purposes, not the least of which is an extra bit of diligence I had while exploring: making mental lists of significant places that seemed to be the lock for a key I didn’t have yet.But it was also a fun way to play with the intertextuality of gaming. If you pick up a crowbar and recognize it not just as a tool but this emblem of gamings past, you’ll have a leg up in playing the association game it asks of you.It’s a method of handling Easter eggs that allow those who are plugged in to be rewarded with more than just a smirk, but also an exploration meta-game.The Last Hero of Nostalgaia is fun for as long as that meta game entertains you, because outside of that it doesn’t give much reason to not play one of its muses instead.Combat is never anything more than exactly what it looks like: it’s a servicable and blatant homage to Soulsss…, and any enjoyment you extract from it can be owed to the formula itself rather than anything meaningful Nostalgaia does with it.A self aware narrator who taunts you and postulates about whether you’re going to be a jerk or a not jerk when you reach the climax didn’t add to the game as much as I thought it would, partly because of how static he was.For as self aware as his writing is and as much as he seems to chirp endlessly about player agency, he seems to lack awareness to respond to you exerting it. Wander off the beaten path and you’ll typically just be met with silence, get stuck on a boss and the narrator will lose his tongue until you eventually beat itt…rather than using the opportunity to jeer you.For better or worse he’s also a compass. Don’t know if you’re going the right way? Keep trying random paths until the commentary returns, then you’ll know.It’s never a truly gripping satire for this reason, because for as much as it seems to verbally encourage you to break the chains of game linearity, sometimes literally, it seldom felt like it was responsive to that happening.It’s not without its moments though: the premise of bringing Nostalgaia back to its nostalgic peak involves some cool visual flourishes, like the world shifting from pixels to 3D and sometimes the gradient in betweenn. Strong art direction and lighting even manage to give you the butterflies of coming up on a new vista, despite an art style that doesn’t exactly lend itself to powerful imagery.It also manages to nail the interconnectedness of its world, albeit with some needed budget shortcuts to make that happen. A long series of tunnels and elevators run parallel to and underneath most of the levels, acting as a ‘backstage’ to the main stage that is the game and support rapid transit and shortcutting. The overusage of the same elevators as opposed to more organically themed shortcuts can make it easy to forget which one leads where, but there are otherwise plenty of distinguished visual landmarks that make navigation without a map possible.But really Nostalgaias biggest hurdle to overcome is something it may have unintentionally borrowed from Dark Souls 1: a dip in quality at the halfway point.The Last Hero of Nostalgaia doesn’t backload blatantly unfinished levels, but it does run out of steam: the halfway mark was right around the time the basic souls-template combat got boring, which is also right around the time levels started throwing in copious backtracking and cheesy traps that are oblivious to how stiffly the game controls, which is ALSO right around the time the game had like 2 fake out endings and kept dragging itself on.I was surprised to see that my end hour count after rolling credits was only 15, it felt like way more and not necessarily in a good way.  Which isn’t to say that I don’t recommend The Last Hero of Nostalgaia: I actually found it quite compelling, just maybe not as compelling as it’s multiple climaxes demanded. Among games that involve circle strafing and fishing for cheesy backstabs, you’ll find titles with both grander scope, and tighter execution…even if you deviate from From Softwares catalogue.But you’ll find few that commit to a novel gameplay idea quite as hard as Nostalgaia does: one that rewards your curiosity and encourages you to look at your environment in new ways. It’s at times inelegant, but it is worthwhile for its own reasons, and it gets all the easier to recommend if you’re willing to engage in one of the most profound acts of player agency possible: putting the controller down when you get bored.
