_childDocuments_.review: After seeing this game on Iron Pineapple's video I figured I would give it a try. Little did I know how well put together this game actually was. I went in thinking it would be like "Stanley Parable mixed with Souls", and it is like that in a sense, but it is also so much more and stands itself out as a very solid game in its own right. I've experienced a couple bugs/glitches but nothing game breaking and nothing I bothered to report. The game is very self-aware and breaks the fourth wall in a way that isn't jarring, but entertaining and all part of the plot. You follow stories in a land once dedicated to the generic "hero's quest",  coming from the perspective of NPCs and items that were active during the golden age of these heroes, and some that may have witnessed it's downfall.This is starting to sound like a review article, but It's not. I thoroughly enjoyed the game (with 34.3 hours in 1 play-through). It has great lore, told via classic Souls style environmental storytelling. I truly felt nostalgic through the whole thing, and enjoyed the feeling of once again dungeon crawling through gauntlets, not knowing what's around the next corner.Highly recommend this game to anyone who is looking for something to do until the next Elden Ring DLC drops.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Hero of Nostalgaia

_childDocuments_.review: It's clear from developer commentary that this game was trying to make a Soulslike whose defining quality is making an artistic statement about the cultural obsession with nostalgia. The problem is that while doing so, the developers made a nearly one-to-one imitation of the gameplay systems of Dark Souls but didn't put enough attention into how the polish of those games elevates their mechanics. What this results in is a game that occasionally might have something interesting to say that is too often stifled by gameplay systems, poor quality control, and general lack of attention to detail. It's really difficult for the player to engage in a mirror held up to their consumption of nostalgia when the camera shoots their perspective into the sky because half the bosses have a jump attack, or when your attacks simply don't register because of poor hitbox detection, or when the player is taken out of the game by the fact that almost no areas have music, or when the frontloaded narrator disappears for about 80% of the game, or the many many many bugs including but not limited to the game simply forgetting where your souls (memory) were left. All of these - and many more - simply break any cohesive point the game could have been making, leaving the player with an okay-at-best-but-usually-very-subpar Soulslike that will every once in awhile make a joke.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Hero of Nostalgaia

_childDocuments_.review: A first glance at the trailer might give you the impression that this is another game just trying to cash in on retro graphics- Do not be mistaken! The Last Hero of Nostalgaia is an incredibly well designed soulslike game, and it makes really good use of it's artstyle to tell an interesting story. Let me break it down;First of all, Gameplay! As a big fan of the genre, I have yet to find a soulslike game that isn't made by Fromsoft that nails the dark-souls feel as well as this game does. Combat is weighty and tense- Mashing the attack button is rarely the best choice, as your swings need time to follow through and could leave you open for attack if you aren't careful, and this is true for the enemies as well! Combat feels like a dance, putting you on your toes to dodge attacks and find openings to attack or heal, and this is especially true for the bosses, most of which are really well-designed and really fun to fight. The devs put a lot of effort into making sure everything is balanced just right, and you can really tell.Second of all, level design! The map is cohesively connected and really feels like a whole world, rivaling the original dark souls in how interconnected it is. At the start of the game, the world feels vast and unfamiliar, everything miles apart, each area a journey to get through- by the end of the game, you know the layout like the back of your hand, dozens of shortcuts opening up to give you free reign of the world, and it's an utter joy to explore, lots of little nooks and crannies to find stuff in. Third of all, Story and Puzzles! There aren't really puzzles to block your progression, but there's plenty in the Remembrance system! Items lore will give you hints pointing to landmarks in the world, and going there will let you upgrade your items, making them more powerful and giving them special abilities, as well as revealing more of the story surrounding the world. And the story is really interesting! The writers weren't lazy in the slightest- They've developed an interesting, self-consistent world with a wide number of characters who's stories all intersect- both past and present, with dozens of long-gone characters developing the backstory of the world and explaining it's current state, and characters you meet on your all have their own quirks and personalities, their questlines weaving in and out of each other. And while the story is comedic, it's a DARK comedy, the game mixing humor and tragedy masterfully.And finally, Yes, the fanservice. I know there are people out there who would get a bitter taste in their mouth from it, but honestly, I really enjoyed it. The games artstyle is not simply retro for the sake of retro- It's an active participant in the story, and wouldn't be the same without it. The games items and lore also make a lot of references to other video games- pulling inspiration from triple A games and small indie games alike, and they do so in a way thats both faithful to the originals while having their own unique twists to fit into the world of the game. Picking up items clearly inspired by some of my favorite indie games was really nice.In short; The Last Hero of Nostalgaia is a really well-designed soulslike game, and it's got a very interesting story to tell, about not just video games, but the game industry and our relationship with video games as well. It's funny and sad and I really, really recommend you give it a shot.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Hero of Nostalgaia

_childDocuments_.review: The Last Hero of Nostalgaia is definitely a unique Soulslike RPG. You play as a stick figure (made from ASCII art aka symbols) and have to venture forth into the fading world of Nostalgaia, a videogame running out of memory since someone overstayed their welcome as a hero... and encouraged others to do the same. As a result of which, NPC's hate our pixel-perfect hero and will gladly curbstomp them into oblivion. Other heroic figures stalk the land, halfbaked or worse and the land itself is drifting apart.It'll be easy for you to see just how many videogames, player tropes and more besides are referenced in this game. The most blatant one? Hard to pick, but Heartflow Altar is basically a major nod to Firelink Shrine from Dark Souls. You can find a Keyblade, something something Earthbound and so many other things. I especially like the faded Astoria armour, the Forgotten Knight armour and the equally faded torch (useful)This is a Soulslike, so prepare to die a lot, run back to where you died to get your souls... erh... memory, and then hoof it back to the beacon to level up. Controls are pretty good, if a bit standard. You played DS1? Then you know how to play this one. Especially as MP is Access in this game and... welp, better farm that consumable. You'll also want to farm enemy weapons and armour, and for that you need to beef up that Luck stat asap. Unlike in other games, here Luck has so many, many uses. Other stats tend to cap around 16, not all though, but you don't need much more to make it through the game. Restoring the memory of pixellated weapons and such also gives bonusses.With most games you can see a plot twist coming, if you've been playing for some time. You see an area that looks empty, you think it may be a boss room. Nostalgaia otoh tends to take your expectations (the devs obviously being gamers) and tossing them out the window in a spectacular fashion. Heavy spoiler alert, but this one I did not see coming:  I'd expected a fight, but not that reveal. And that's just one of the unexpected ways this game lowballs you.As much fun as Nostalgaia is, I do have a few gripes with it. Major one is the fact that you can get stablocked when facing multiple enemies. You can't roll away until you've stood back up after a stab, your swings have lower priority than enemies' do and they do have block/stun moves. Also, you can't warp between beacons, just between the only one tethered at a time and whatever you currently are resting at. One way btw. Given how big the world is and how easy it is to get turned around it gets frustrating.If you like Soulslikes, or just videogame nostalgia, definitely pick this one up. I recommend it fully. Our Stick Figure Hero is like OPM's Saitama: the best hero, but nobody acknowledges them.

_childDocuments_.review: I played through the entire game, which means its good enough, but overall it is not ready.  3x I fell through a floor into an area which had not yet loaded, meaning I wasn't able to leave.  Could not die because no enemies were there.   I had to run around until I found a place without a wall and attempt to fall to my death, I say attempt, because 2x I fell into a void.  Secondly, sometimes hits simply do not register.  My blade went right through an enemy more times than I can count, without doing any damage only to be hit right back and my next hit connect.   Game needs some major polish before I can recommend it to anyone.

_childDocuments_.review: Its a very good game. Me and my friend were able to beat it in about 18.4 hours. We did spend a lot of time finding the riddles so you could subtract about 3-4 hours from that, if you wanted to play straight through.The riddles started out pretty easy and near the end turned extremely difficult.It was a very rewarding way of getting upgrades to your items. The game play is exactly what it says it is: A dark souls clone. The multiplayer feels exactly like what you'd want dark Souls to be like: Co-op from spawn in to the end of the game (obviously From Soft has there reasons for doing it, and they do it well). The story is fantastic, and honestly one of my favorite parts of the game. There were a lot of funny moments, twists, and turns, and very funny characters.I'm writing this 4 days after release, so there are some bugs, but nothing shutting the game down and turning it back on wont fix. My only complaint has to do with the ending.SPOILERS: There were a lot of B story lines that weren't wrapped up. This might of been our fault, because we missed something or couldn't go back. The corrupted woman who just had eyes just disappeared, and nothing was explained. The essence of suffering had my friend and I constantly going back and forth as to whether or not to trust him, and I didn't wan't to feed him any weapons because I though it would make him stronger. He fed the NPC that was becoming conscious to him, and we didn't notice any real consequences. I thought that He might of been the final boss, ect ect ect. He was such an interesting character, and then he just disappeared after the final boss fight. The Defeated Hero in the cage on the Scrooge McDuck stage just disappeared. I guess what I'm trying to say is if I failed, let me know somehow.  I have no idea if what happened to any of them, and chances are, if i found out I messed up I probably would be more willing to run through the game again and get it right. That brings me to the ending of the game. There is nothing said as to what happened to The Land of Nostalgaia. You get a brief cut scene if you choose the bad ending and based on what you know about the story, you can make an inference that you messed stuff up (Okay Good), but if you choose the good ending, nothing is said. There is not even a black screen saying "peace was restored", It just cuts right to the credits. For a game that has such a funny interesting story as one of the major selling points, the end didn't feel satisfying. Does the shop keeper become normal again? Do our friends become Heros even though there corrupted (besides that one a**hole)? Will the old man or someone else take the place as King? Am I talking out my A** and just wasn't paying attention? Only the Devs know (at least at this point). If the Devs read this: thanks for the awesome Game. Criticism aside, I had a lot of fun with my friend and and was pulled into the story from start to finish. Damn Good job Fellas.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Hero of Nostalgaia

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunate Softlock after 90% CompletionCombat is not fun, tries to emulate the souls-like feel, but ends up being super clunky as some weapon attacks just do not connect for... some reason. Enemies tends to move back when you try to attack them most of the time, so you need to bait an attack to MAYBE hit them, but then they dodge back all of the time, so fights with basic enemies are just annoying after the first run through of the area.The boss fights were... okay? They had somewhat interesting boss ideas, but due to clunky game mechanics it falls on its face. Going from a spawn beacon to the Boss room would always take a few minutes due to going up elevators, dodging onslaughts of enemies, or just long pathways just to get to the boss. And when you finally got to the boss room, most boss fights were too easy or absolutely dreadful to fight. Luck seemed to be the main factor of completing boss fights than skill, and it just was not an enjoyable experience.I ended up sticking through it all because I enjoyed the visuals and concept of the game itself, just to see all of the different areas and design elements when it came to the areas of the game. I think they did a fantastic job on that, and the theme of it all fit very well together.The final nail in the coffin for me was after completing most of the Unreachable Maw, I wanted to go back and collect any items I may have missed previously. There is a fast travel system, although only usuable once you complete most of the game, that I used to travel to an earlier section of the game. This caused the game to crash. Each time I now relaunch the game and load my save, I fall through the floor, perish, and the game crashes.Unfortunately, I will not be completing this game nor looking at playing the DLC. If you want a true souls-like game, look elsewhere.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to love this game but the mechanics and game feel drag this game from an 8 to a 4 imo. The art style is great and story seemed alright from what I could manage. People love souls-likes because the gameplay is difficult to learn but rewarding to master. The difficulty in The Last Hero of Nostalgaia isn't due to the game but the unpolished mechanics, the enemies can attack seemingly as fast as they want while you have a 2-3 second delay between yours. That alongside how hard even the weakest enemies hit is a recipe for disaster, you rarely feel like the deaths are your own fault.

_childDocuments_.review: Really really good made soulslike. From the look and feel it gave me dark souls 1 vibes. The artstyle is amazing. The worldbuilding is amazing. I didn’t really care much for the story but the storyteller design was nice. If you play soulslikes then you get the hang of lt pretty fast. _childDocuments_.review: Played through this game with my wife as her first souls-like and she had a good experience. Honestly it's one of the better souls games out there and is fairly polished and has nice humor. A few bugs here and there and occasionally it felt like hitboxes were inconsistent but not terrible. It's a relatively short experience especially if you don't spend a lot of time backtracking. Clearly it takes a lot of inspiration from DS1.Multiplayer was mostly seamless and you can do it from the very start. Players must have the same story progress, but it will progress both players at the same time. No need to play the areas twice!The game has a unique mechanic where your armor and weapons have memories and by being in the correct location you can unlock the memories. Doing so gives a stat buff to the equipment, but additionally it also buffs the player as you reach certain milestones. Game is really just missing a NG+.

_childDocuments_.review: Ever since I played the first Dark Souls, one of my favorite activities is to find other games that can satiate my hunger for Dark Souls. Beyond the Dark Souls sequels and Elden Ring, I have tried a lot of titles that draw on the dynamics of this type of game, but rarely finding products that fully satisfied my taste. But, if until yesterday the only title unbranded From Software that had unreservedly convinced me for its atmosphere, its melancholy flavor, and its effective mechanics (a little less so for its faces) was Salt And Sanctuary, one of the demonstrations that a few people can create great games, as of today I can count among the titles I love The Last Hero Of Nostalgaia.The game is clearly a declaration of love to Dark Souls, both in terms of mechanics and atmosphere and settings. True, the game's calling card is evidently its ironic, often demented, reading of soulslike, causing me plenty of moments of hilarity. But to stop at that would be reductive because, as the game takes you in for slaps and jokes, an increasingly developed storyline will unfold before your eyes, showing you the scope of the epic of Nostalgaia, a land of heroes. And where there are great heroes, there are necessarily great tragedies. You will get a lot of laughs, but you will see that sometimes they will be bitter laughs. And all this while you're going at it with that hammer you like so much.The game, while clearly indebted to Dark Souls, shows a clear personality, with a well-executed balance between serious and facetious. There are also some interesting mechanics among which the one related to the memory of items stands out: many pieces of equipment keep within them a shred of memory that gives a clue as to where you should go to blossom its potential, both in terms of parameters, and the memory itself, which will expand by giving you new clues about the game world and the characters who have traveled it before you.I appreciated some gameplay choices, which bring The Last Hero Of Nostalgaia closer to the first Dark Souls than to its successors: the game pace is slow, the Bosses have their own characterization without resorting to frantic combos and narrow attack windows. TLHON manages to be an interesting challenge without looking for difficulty at all costs, but offering the player stimulating but not frustrating situations, rather focusing on the construction of compelling scenarios and gradually increasing the player's interest in the history of the world of Nostalgaia.In short, if you too are here because you are in a constant crisis of withdrawal from Dark Souls and don't disdain those who combine seriousness and facetiousness, book your ticket to Nostalgaia now!
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Hero of Nostalgaia

_childDocuments_.review: If you like Dark Souls at all, you owe it to yourself to play this game. The Last Hero of Nostalgaia was a wonderful little adventure that was both a solid souls-like and a a wonderful ode to video games as a whole. I even ended up enjoying the story immensely. Please buy this game, the developers really deserve it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Hero of Nostalgaia

_childDocuments_.review: The Last Hero of Nostalgaia caught my eye with its intriguing “pixelated” style and interesting concept, so I decided to give it a shot. It’s not a game I hear talked about much, so I wanted to try it out and share my experience.The game is set in Nostalgaia, a world collapsing into pixelation as its heroes and memories fade away. The humour really stands out too. Plenty of witty dialogue and cheeky nods that made me chuckle. There are some familiar looking areas like the fire link shrine as a main hub, which I really enjoyed!The world design is another strong point with limited fast travel, you’re forced to pay attention to the layout and interconnectedness of the areas, which I really liked. It makes exploration feel meaningful, having to remember places, unlocking shortcuts and not mindlessly teleporting from point A to B. That said, the game is riddled with glitches. I’m still not sure if they’re intentional or not, but sometimes they worked to the game’s quirky charm… other times they were just frustrating.Unfortunately, the combat left a lot to be desired. It doesn’t feel smooth or satisfying. Same goes for the bosses-kind of a letdown-too easy and lacking the punch you’d expect from a “Souls-like”. The storytelling takes a major turn at one point and I have to admit it caught me off guard in a good way. It's an interesting twist that adds depth to the narrative.As for the price? I’d say wait for a sale. While the game has its moments and offers a unique experience, it doesn’t feel worth the full price given its shortcomings. If you’re looking for something humorous and a little offbeat, it’s definitely worth checking out.

_childDocuments_.review: I decided to write this rewiev because this is one of those games that you can end up falling in love with (like I did), or hate with every fibre of your heart.Let's start saying that the amount of love the developers put into this game it's clear, and it shows. It's a project with a great Soul (ahah) that tells a story that in the beginning may seem just parodistic but has a lot of meaning behind its idiotic cover.This game is clearly inspired by the first Dark Souls game, with all of his clunkiness but a lot of his good qualities.There are a couple of really intelligent mechanics, expecially the remembering of the equipments, that can be very fun if you like riddles.The graphic style is pleasant and very well thought, with the mixing of 2D and 3D parts (and I like that it's tied to the world building too).BUT for the sake of the review I'm going to give you two examples of the mixed bag that this game can be sometimes:- POSITIVE: there is some of the best level design that I've ever seen in an indie soulslike, with shortcuts everywhere that make travelling from one end of the world to the other easy and a game of remembering which lift takes you where. - NEGATIVE: these shortcuts are exaggerated and most of the times don't make sense in terms of the world building, and because of this incoherence it's very hard sometimes to remember in which area you have to go to reach another one.- POSITIVE: some of the sidequests tells great stories of very interesting npcs, with a great voice active and writing.- NEGATIVE: to progress in some of these quests you literally need to follow a guide. It's a design choice that I understand but that I don't fully approve since the real final boss is locked behind the most convoluted quest of the game. I really hope for a sequel or a new game that can learn from the rough parts of this one.

_childDocuments_.review: The Last Hero of Nostalgaia" is a game that will undoubtedly resonate with fans of the Dark Souls series. From the moody, atmospheric environments to the challenging combat mechanics, there are plenty of similarities to be found here.One of the most striking connections between the two games is the design of the game world. Much like Dark Souls, "The Last Hero of Nostalgaia" features interconnected environments that can be navigated in a non-linear fashion. The game also makes great use of shortcuts and hidden paths, which will be familiar to anyone who has spent time exploring the world of Dark Souls.The game's visual design is also reminiscent of the Dark Souls series. From the crumbling ruins of Firelink Shrine to the twisted streets of the Bloodborne-inspired city, the environments are beautifully detailed and filled with atmosphere.Of course, the combat in "The Last Hero of Nostalgaia" is also heavily inspired by Dark Souls. The game features a similar stamina-based system, where each attack and dodge depletes your character's stamina bar. Timing and positioning are crucial, and each encounter requires careful consideration and skill to overcome.But while "The Last Hero of Nostalgaia" certainly borrows heavily from Dark Souls, it also brings plenty of its own unique ideas to the table. The game's storyline, characters, and world-building are all original and engaging, making for a game that stands on its own merits.In conclusion, "The Last Hero of Nostalgaia" is a game that will appeal to anyone who loves the challenging, atmospheric worlds of Dark Souls. But it's also a game that has plenty of its own ideas and identity, making it a must-play for fans of the RPG genre.

_childDocuments_.review: Last Hero of Nostalgaia is a pretty close recreation of Dark Souls, while also being a meta commentary of Video Games.The gameplay is very close to DS1 to me, its kind of clunky, and missing a few things Dark Souls has, but it the closest I've seen from a non-souls game. It has the a great interconnected world just like DS1, every place has multiple meaningful shortcuts. It even does some new stuff, like changing how you interact with reading item descriptions. Most weapons/armours need to be remembered, which involves bringing them to specific places so they can, and they will give a little blurb that hints about this. Once this is done, most weapons will unlock a weapon art, some other bonus, and a damage bonus. I find this mechanic neat because it actively leads you to interact with lore.This is one of those "I get the reference, I clapped!", but ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ I love it, I did ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ clap. The game has a bunch of fun references like an area just called "Player Housing", and the big bosses are so neat. Most weapons/armours are just references (i.e one weapon is just the Soul Edge, or you can get Master Chief armour). I'm gonna describe one of the bosses here to the end of the paragraph just so I can describe the fun designs to match the original character, if you dont want that spoiler skip. One of the big bosses is the Moogle from FF6, he backstabbed Terra and Locke because he was greedy. When you go to face him, he looks like Smough with a little moogle head. His boss fight his him dancing around, casting blue magic, and using his Dragoon lance. Other bosses also have very fun interpretations of their origin, just very well put together.Game does have some stuff I don't really like. I think the weapon hitboxes on Big Weapons either don't last long enough, or the hitboxes are too small, also felt wrong when I missed enemies. You won't get any fast travel ability, this isn't really a fault, since there are a bunch of shortcuts, just be aware of backtracking this involves. The main thing I don't like is this game has Dark Soul quests. Time sensitive quest triggers that if you walk too far into another zone, you are ♥♥♥♥♥♥ over. I missed all but 1 quest (and missed out on the true final boss) because of that crap. I really just hate that they are time sensitive, it really doesn't make much sense why they are besides emulating the dumb ass Quests in Dark Souls. There isn't even a New Game+ (at the time I wrote) so I can speed through the game again to attempt quests again.Besides these very minor complaints, I love this ♥♥♥♥. Its Dark Souls (I love that game!) and it shows huge love to Video Games (I love Video Games!), hugely recommend to anyone who loves these two things.

_childDocuments_.review: I have played A LOT of indie souls over the years. From Salt and Sanctuary, to Thymesia, i've been with the genre since birth, and have seen the best and the worst the genre offers. That being said, Nostalgaia is shockingly good. Like, REALLY REALLY GOOD, for one simple fact. It doesn't try anything new. Its Dark Souls 1 to a T in terms of world design, and thats a VERY good thing to accomplish. Dark Souls 1 has the best overall world design of any souls game to date, the world is expertly crafted with shortcuts, and exploration can lead you down very long and very complex paths, but always seem to lead you back to where it all started. Nostalgaia does something very similar, but in its own fun way.Nostalgaia doesn't try to shoehorn new or ridiculous mechanics into an already perfect genre, instead, it simply adds its own theme to a genre littered with attempts, to improve what is already perfected. Strength, dex, and "magic" builds are here, R1 spam is here, Charge attacks are here, if you played Dark Souls, non of what this game offers is new, but the theme is where the game shines incredibly brightly.The overall concept is enough of a draw that the gameplay doesn't need to shine. A story centered around a crumbling video game world, where heroes are seen as cancers, and even the narrator hates the hero enough to cause random and deadly events. Combine that with stellar voice acting, nods to franchises big and small, and a combat formula that works fantastically, you have a legitimately great experience... For the most part.Combat great when you find a weapon you like, kinda lacking when you have a weapon you dislike. Hitboxes are NOT generous in the least, and certain move sets straight up can't hit enemies on slopes or smaller enemies. Near the last stretch of the game, the enemy variety goes full Farum Azula on us, with enemies that are obscenely difficult, and WAY too frequent. "cough" nerf werewolves "cough". Some bosses are just too difficult, and maybe im just bad (my ego says otherwise), but i feel like some bosses are best dealt with, with full heavy armor and R1 spam, rather than learning move sets or counters.Nostalgaia is probably the best indiesouls i've played in a very long time. A lot of work went into this, and i think the devs smashed it out of the park. I would love to see this game get a sequel, or at the very least get some more eyes on it. Its a very well done game, and i love the tone and theme the game is going for. Very much worth the price if you like anything soulsey.

_childDocuments_.review: The Last Hero of Nostalgaia is Stanley Parable meets Dark Souls. Good concept, horribly executed. There is a huge lack of music, stale gameplay, bugs galore, and too many interesting ideas that failed to realize its full potential. The lack of Music makes the game incredibly quiet and boring as you slosh through Paper Mario enemies who range from Green looking zombie to Red Looking Vampire and a few armor clad enemies. On the rare occasion enemies are 3D, they have a 50/50 chance of looking amazing or just awful. The Narrator has more speaking parts in the tutorial and the first zone than the rest of the game, and I understand voice acting is expensive, but make the narrator have a taunt, have him make fun of me for dying, have him astonished that I killed a boss on my first attempt or make fun of me for dying to it over 10 times before clearing it and just have it on a 5-7 different voice line loop. ANYTHING is better than those long pauses of quietness that happen when someone comes out during Thanksgiving dinner. The second boss is the only "well" designed boss. All the other bosses only have 1 phase and a small gimmick that makes you go "Oh yeah, thats from that one game" and the second boss was also the only relatively difficult one. It really just felt like they threw all their plans into the first quarter of the game, then just said "Ah good enough to get us our $25 from steam!" and let the rest play out in the most uninteresting way possible. The last thing that they should of really done nicely with the game was "Beat this Area Boss, go from Pixel to 3D!" or something along those lines.  I'd avoid this and live curiously through any youtuber who was willing to play through from start to finish.

_childDocuments_.review: This game starts off very well for a low cost souls-like: nice humor at the start, the combat isn't too bad and the weapon, armour and rememberance systems aren't too bad. In fact, the game's pretty fun...!Until you reach the Mines in Oreshaft village. It's around that point that things become ridiculous, with enemies having skills that are almost impossible to counter or dodge, such as the vampire like guys in Festivity Row forcefully pulling you out of blocking or attacking and stunlocking while attacking you and healing themselves, the mine overseers making whole swarms of enemies attack you while also being strong themselves and, of course, the teleporting Ender man-like figures in the stage after NPC city. Luck is a stat that half works if you don't play as any class aside from the game's rogue class. If I invest 23 levels worth of stats in Luck, I expect my chances of the enemies dropping double Memory to be higher than 1 ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ percent. If I spend 16 levels in equipment load and unlock the weight load buff from remembering weapons, I expect myself not to fat roll while wearing mid weight armor and wield a mid weight shield and one of the lighter greatswords. The bosses after the first one are a joke: a three phase gank boss for the second boss in the game when you still haven't gined nearly enough levels and items? A fat guy who literally never stops sommersaulting around an indoor football field sized arena for more than 2 seconds while also throwing random spells at you which still keep firing after he charges you again and then goes full Darkluker attacking you while his phantom at the same time spams spells at you and is invincible, and lags after the fight finishes and keeps firing spells at you no matter how far away you are. The third boss isn't bad, but if you have a 100% physical shield and at least 120 stamina you can just hold it up and trade hits after rebuffing. I kept the boss stunlocked by changing my build to hold the Legeneric and just spammed L1 while turtling her attacks. The game, as a whole is not bad mechanically aside from some small flaws. The humor at first is okay but gets annoying when the same joke gets repeated again and again with small changes. But the worst is the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ enemy design that you can somewhat mitigate with skills but still cannot and will never be able to completely counter even if you have the best reaction time and items because when you have two, three or four teleporting enemies that teleport behind you and attack, no matter which direction you turn to you will be ganked, stunlocked and killed.I have played every Dark Souls game, with my favourite being Ds2 in which I have easily over 5k hours by now, and I have done most common challenge runs and some more uncommon ones. I have finished Demon's Souls in the ps3 version on RPCS3 on a laptop, which means I had to use WASD to move, R T E Q to attack and the num pad to move the camera. And it was still good and fun. But this game is like it's trying to gradually get you annoyed with it so it makes you to quit eventually so it can claim it's hard and not all players finish it. Imagine if you go to a restaurant and order a giant pizza, but the waiters start stopping by your table more and more frequently to ask if you need anything, bump on your chair and table and generally keep escalating until they outright bring out the 12 gauge millitary shotgun and shoot out your kneecaps before nailing your testes on the chair you sit on with a hammer and nail so you are forced to get out of the restaurant and they can keep claiming no one finishes that pizza. This is how more and more annoying the enemies get. When you design an enemy to be unfair due to some bs abillity that you cannot respond to and you spam the enemy in one closed area, you know exactly what you're doing.If I had writen this review two to five hours in, I would most definitely have had recommended this game; but not anymore. Not for full price at least.

_childDocuments_.review: The Last Hero of Nostalgaia is nothing short of a work of art.The combat is methodical, requiring you to observe and react to your enemy's attacks, and use your own attacks in moments where you will not get hit. There are a wealth of weapons available: from fast-hitting daggers, to slow, high-damage giant swords, there's plenty to experiment with and almost certainly something to fit your playstyle. There are also plenty of defensive options with shields: shields that let you parry enemy attacks and leave them open to attack, shields that let you use your weapon's special abilities, and shields that can let you block almost every enemy attack with a well-timed release of the block button after blocking an attack. The combat takes the best aspects of its predecessors in the genre and puts them all in one neat package.The world design is also excellent. Every area in the game is connected to other areas, which makes navigating intuitive and rewards you for exploring; the entire world feels like an actual world rather than distinct zones that happen to sit next to each other. The world design also plays into the "remembrance" mechanic.The Remembrance mechanic allows you to power up items that you collect by solving a riddle tied to the specific item. Solving this riddle requires you to go to a specific part of the world and "remember" the item, which not only increases its stats, but also provides a lore entry for that item to tell you about its history. I found nearly every riddle to be clear about where I was supposed to go - just make sure you're paying attention to the world design and other item's lore entries as they'll help you a lot when trying to remember certain items. You don't have to engage with this system if you don't want to, though, as it's completely optional.What really makes TLHON excellent is the complimentary nature of the narrative and gameplay genres. The overall narrative talks about the importance of remembering the past, as it informs our decisions in the future; but, at the same time, we shouldn't cling to the past as that causes stagnation and prevents new stories from being told. The gameplay teaches you this exact same lesson as you might get stuck fighting the same boss over and over again. If you focus too much on your past mistakes, then it can be difficult to move forward and triumph over your enemy. Inversely, if you fail to learn from your past mistakes, you will continue to make the same errors and fail. Learn from the errors you make and have them shape your actions in the future, and you will be able to overcome any challenges thrown your way!I'd also like to briefly mention how good the music is. A Shell In The Pit has really captured the essence of each boss in their theme, and each theme is incredibly distinct and memorable.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is honestly really cool in concept, but its executed rather poorly especially in the realm of gameplay. The combat is stiff and clunky in a way that makes the "souls-like" tag feel a bit audacious, you're constantly gonna be fighting the lock-on system and rigid input cues for any control during a fight with a single enemy, and a lot of the game seems to boil down to DS2 style gank fights so you can imagine how hellish it feels I'm sure. Honestly it made me go back and appreciate dark souls 2 for having at least a functional enough combat system to make it's gank fights somewhat fun a times. Here, the enemies have poorly telegraphed moves, there's way more of them in certain areas than there needs to be, and while i love exploring and witnessing the game's level design and character designs, the core combat sucks way too hard for me to wholeheartedly recommend it unless you're a real patient person with nothin else to play.

_childDocuments_.review: Whilst it is an amazing game, concept and I love the narrator.What the devs didn't do is learn from DS2's Adaptability.Great concept, terrible design.In a game genre where combos and attacks are incredibly vital, why the hell do you make THAT A STAT?!Momentum Should not exist and serves to make the game incredibly frustrating because it never applies to enemy weapons. They stagger you, but you can't stagger them. What the actual hell are you thinking? Adaptability was at least a stat you could increase in DS2, but this? Momentum is tied to weapons and never increase.Whats that? you chose rogue and wanted to go crits.. guess you're incredibly squishy with weapons that barely ever stagger, meaning enemies can attack you whilst you hit them. Not fun, but out of spite I'm completing this game but I severely do not reccomend this SoulsLike

_childDocuments_.review: Thus far I have loved almost everything about this game. It's a fantastic soulslike that is parodying the story premises of the Dark Souls series (kill those stopping the cycle and also sacrifice yourself to keep the cycle going). Good things: The story is phenomenal, the routing is extremely well planned, the bosses are great and I love every last one of them, and the areas are beautiful in their own, pixelated way. The humor is on point, the narrator is adorable (in a sinister way), and the characters are really easy to like. The fighting feels good and works really well.Bad things: It has a few issues, such as having Equipment Load being tied to its own stat and not being influenced by any other stat which causes you to spend way too many points on something that doesn't give you any other bonus than a marginally better roll. Strength, Dex, and Stamina should instead affect equip load in different ways. Like, strength and stamina give a bigger bonus to it than dex does since a dex build is more likely to use light armor anyway.The weapons desperately need to have their ability scaling explained in more depth than just "this weapon scales off strength and dexterity" so that the damage numbers can actually make sense. They do explain the scaling but, it's not very well explained and doesn't match up with the numbers you've got.At least one area (the quest reward vault) really needs a beacon at the beginning of it. Otherwise it's just a chore to fight your way back to it, even with the shortcut in The Depths.Dual wielding is not really a thing despite the Resolutionary featuring dual swords for their class icon. You *can* equip two weapons, and *can* swing both but, not as part of a unique attack animation like it should be. You have to equip two weapons, press to attack with your right handed weapon, then use the button combo that lets you attack with your left handed item. This swings each weapon separately, using their own individual attack animations, instead of combining them into a dual wielding attack.On a more personal note: It's not exactly what I would call 'challenging'. It has some challenging parts, for sure. But up until the Quest Reward Vault I was mostly just breezing through enemies with a few hits. Even groups weren't really challenging. That's not to say the enemies weren't cool, or the encounters weren't well thought out. It just wasn't all that challenging. Maybe I have too much experience with soulslikes? XDOver all the game is fantastic! I highly suggest getting it, and don't wait for a sale if you can afford it now!

_childDocuments_.review: Despite its tongue-in-cheek nature, this game offers some exciting and creative ideas. Throughout the game, Easter eggs and references to other games are cleverly incorporated into the narrative beyond just a 'hey, I remember that!' motif. There is a fun, light-hearted, creative sense of storytelling here that pulls from various sources. No doubt, this tale will resonate with many because of its varied references and its themes, which are almost sure to elicit discussion. The story is about a video game world in desperate need of saving by resetting it by you, the hero. Its overarching plot manages to incorporate the previously mentioned Easter eggs from other games (and nostalgia in general) to show how memories over time can become messy, distorting what we once loved and the eventual need to let go of newer adventures and memories to take place. It's a world split between the old and the new, figuratively and literally.It sometimes feels like Dark Souls almost to a fault regarding story and gameplay. Regardless, it offers a practical, strategic approach to combat similar to those titles, giving it a solid gameplay foundation, which I enjoyed. World and level design also ring identical to a Souls-like structure but with the game's world in disarray as the world shifts between the old and the new. You'll find yourself exploring typical and unexpected locations with equally similar enemies, though with a few added twists. Even though the enemy and boss designs aren't mind-blowing, they are creative and fit the game's comedic, irreverent style.While the game may borrow similar themes and narrative elements from Dark Souls (rebirth, heroes refusing to do their jobs, prolonging a world beyond its intended end), they do so with taste and humor that gives the game its identity. The whole experience of Last Hero of Nostalgaia was gratifying as it ended up being a comedic Souls-like with some interesting surprises and funny moments to be had, especially if you're an avid video game player. This experience I'll remember fondly and is worth checking out.Recommended. Now, get out there and become a hero!

_childDocuments_.review: If you are interested in the game because you want a kinda fun lower budget game be warned that parts of this game are on par with dark souls. Personally I have mixed feelings. the art style is neat, but I haven't come across anything that actually lets you restore large sections of the world as the trailers seem to imply, only specific items and small areas around safe points.The biggest problem with this game is it's combat just isn't accurate enough for how difficult they've made some of the bosses. Tracking and hit boxes when dodging is sketchy so often moves will completely miss enemies right in front of you. They will sometimes miss too when I'm too close but this is less reliable. Some of the enemy and world design also doesnt properly prepare you for certain bosses. The big golden guy in the screenshots is a great example - before him increasing stamina seems unnecessary but he moves far quicker than anything else in the game to that point. This isnt the biggest issue but it isnt ideal game design either. Having said that, your stats are listed in plain text in the save file so you could easily max your stats and reload the game if you're not looking for that kind of experience.Some may not have an issue with the combat issues I mentioned but I was looking at this as more of a meme game than a serious soulslike and the issues I mentioned really hurt the experience for me. Beyond that I appreciate some of the NPCs and the narrator and similar humor (NPC staging areas are amusing), the art style is fun and levels enjoyable to explore, the memory mechanic is neat, and in fairness the dodge mechanic is far more lenient with its invincibility than the soulsborne games.Overall I'd recommend the game if the humor and art style seems fun to you. Worst cases you can just make some quick save file edits (no real technical knowledge needed) to work around the difficulty.

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine Dark Souls 1 combat but clunkier, Dark Souls 3 poise, and, towards the midpoint, enemies that require Bloodborne-level evasion. The absence of fast travel in a nearly purely linear world that requires backtracking to the main city to return items becomes grating after the first boss, leaving only the story and world to hold the player's interest. Both are great but sparse and held together by the combat, which, as mentioned, needs improvement to feel functional. Maybe good if you like the first Surge game.

_childDocuments_.review: It's funny Dark Souls.In reality, it's not a bad game, just not the greatest. If you can deal with a somewhat janky game and have fun with that, it's pretty good. Reminds me of budget games you could get back in the day. _childDocuments_.review: Every single time this game introduces a mechanic or idea, it quickly becomes annoying. I ended up hating this fast travel system of "tethering" a single location to warp to. The remembering mechanic is a cruel tedium. The "staging rooms", were such an interesting idea to me when I realized they kind of work like shortcuts from area to area, but after just a couple new areas it's equally as confusing. The Staging rooms just become another length of empty space to sprint through, while that ironic elevator muzak becomes exactly what it's parodying in the first place. When I first saw a weapon ability that was a buff for faster rolling I became excited that there would be other cool weapon abilities. haha, there are 4 weapon abilities spread out among all the weapons, if there are actually 5 or 6, they're just forgettable or I couldn't find the remembrance locations, because you have to drag the weapon to a specific spot on the map and use it in your inventory (seperate from equipment menu) and "remember" it which is also a memory (souls) sink and only THEN do you learn that it's special ability is just exact same as the 8 other "spin slash" weapons in your inventory. After 12 hours into this I'm just sick of trying to find these spots to remember weapons through this increasingly convoluted map. That's this game, you will like it at first, while it still has that NEW CAR smell, but all it's little ideas are half done. It's like a game of constantly getting you excited for something that's underwhelming. There's a lot of little things that seem like a little patch could iron them out, that's not a real worry of mine, games are never perfect. However if your game is made to be near identical to another game, it seems real lazy for something to be missed or done as if you were uninspired. Heavy attacks button queue very sensitively, so if you full charge one, you will accidentally button queue another heavy attack immediately after. You can't switch weapons while sprinting (which you have to backtrack and sprint a lot) you can't even stance switch while sprinting. You cannot hold stance switch to your offhand at all. Off handed weapons are held upside down in the characters left hand. These tiny things just read like lazy oversights.

_childDocuments_.review: A love letter to Dark Souls and gaming as a whole. It references Dark Souls 1, 2, 3, Bloodborne and Demon's Souls as well as a multitude of other classics such as Minecraft, Mario, Zelda, Metroid, Castlevania and many more.For me personally, this is probably one of the games that comes closest to the "feeling" of Dark Souls 1, not counting other FromSoftware games. I don't necessarily mean atmospherically, it's  a very different (although still very charming) setting of course, but gameplay wise instead. The world is very interconnected with many paths leading back to previous areas, which you'll need to make use of until you're allowed to teleport between Bonfires (Beacons) later on. I just wish it was larger. There are actually quite a bunch of very distinct areas in the game, with enough complexity so that exploration always stays interesting and just enough Beacons so that it remains dangerous but rewarding to explore. Unfortunately the game doesn't have a lot of boss fights and most of them happen towards the end, so you'll be going through multiple different areas in a row without fighting anything big. And as far as progression goes, the game is also very linear from start to finish, excluding the DLC. That adds some much needed branching pathways to the game, but I'll write a separate review for it on its store page.There's a decent amount of weapon diversity, with this unique gimmick that equipment in this game wants you to "remember" it, making it stronger. For most items you need to go to a specific location somewhere in the world in order to be able to remember them, and you're given clues as to where that is. It's pretty fun. I also like that no matter what build you go for, even if it's very niche, there are always multiple weapons designed to be used for such a build, meaning you always have some variety. Like, say a build that equally focuses on all 3 main damage stats (strength, dexterity & source), there are 4 weapons for that. You can also infuse weapons like in Dark Souls, so technically most weapons could be used on most builds, just not optimally.The combat feels pretty good overall, however here is where the game shows its one biggest flaw, which is that the hitboxes of your weapons can be very janky. Every once in a while an attack will completely miss an enemy, even when your weapon's model is physically going through the enemies body, and even when you're standing directly in front of the enemy and are locked on. It sometimes looks like the protagonist isn't the only thing made out of one dimensional sticks. And it happens to all kinds of weapons, from daggers to great clubs, but at least it mostly just happens against human-sized or smaller enemies. Very annoying when you get hit because you were relying on an enemy to die/stagger from your next attack, but then that attack just whiffs for no reason. Eventually you'll just get used to using attacks less prone to missing.Another, minor critique I have is the performance in some areas. The FPS is pretty inconsistant and one area in particular (Start of Sequence) causes lots of stutters and small freezes, which is really annoying. But it's nothing game breaking.Anyway, highly recommend anyone who ever enjoyed a Souls-like to at least give the demo a try, it's free after all. If you end up buying the game, your demo character even gets transferred to the full game automatically (although idk if that messes with achievements in some way, I ended up just making a new character to be safe). I'm currently on my 4th character, hunting the last few achievements I have left, and I'm having a great time with it. I can definitely see myself coming back to the game at some point in the future just to make even more characters/builds.

_childDocuments_.review: A perfectly fine Souls-Like game that wears a skin of retro throwback and modern trends.++PROS+++ Lots of gear and build potential, 2 things that get skipped in a lot of other indie souls-likes.+ Interesting, unique world that, while it is filled with game references, is it's own stand-alone thing with it's own lore. Nostalgaia is, by and large it's own thing and so it doesn't just blend down into meaningless game references, which is a thing I really like.+ Speaking of game references, they go all the way from known figures like Link from Legend of Zelda and Mario to Lester the Unlikely for the NES and Duke from Dragon's Lair for arcades.+ On it's own world each character you meet have lore-drops you can learn about them in item form and they are written well with good voice actors. If you want to immerse yourself into this world as it's own unique thing you can!+ Graphically the game is consistent in it's style which is good. Audio wise there's some banger tracks in here and the sound design is fine overall.+ It's really charming that NPC backareas are the big shortcuts between areas. It helps flesh out this world where NPCs do need rest and food so they have these expansive backrooms they go and rest, train, etc.+ Powers for your character take advantage of the fact you're just a stick hero which I really liked. It really ties into the story with gameplay.+ "Remembering" items as the main way to power them up and give them graphical fidelity is awesome honestly. I love how it makes you interact and remember the world, gives you lore, is optional but simultaneously the powerups can be massive. It's uniquely Nostalgaia and I love it!??MIXED??? Dark Souls 1 styled gameplay, including weird pauses in animations. I got used to it pretty quickly, but it makes combat VERY tedious at points. Similar to DS1 the slower weapons are way too hard to use consistently unless they are near one-shotting enemies so if you're having trouble I actually reccommend just using the daggers you find as they go through enemies just as fast as the slower ones due to the animations.--CONS--- The trailers don't show the latter areas, especially in the leadup to the final hero, and that makes a ton of sense due to the fact that the enemies no longer make as much sense in terms of WHY they are there, but also areas are just far bigger and filled with the same guy 9 times. You can tell that a lot of the love and care in this game went towards the first 3 to 4 areas, but once you hit the 2nd-tutorial section the game quickly drops in quality in terms of level design and overall gameplay, as you'll just be facing swarms and swarms of enemies with a little bit too much health and forced waiting sequences.- Enemies stop being inventive around the same section as well, which is just a shame. They become very cookie-cutter to accommodate how you'll only be fighting hordes of the same guy from now on.- The bossfights, like the enemies, end up feeling all the same as they lose all the interesting gimmicks and fighting styles in favor of spamming the same 3 or 4 moves on loop. This is VERY notable in the Minecraft-DLC area where it's boss just spams the same 3 or 4 attacks with minimal cooldown while summoning enemies to chase you down, turning the entire fight into hit-and-run gameplay style.- Shortcuts are cool in terms of lore, but overall are ridiculously inconvenient and don't even feel worth it when so many of latter areas are just MASSIVE, LONG hallways. Mercucio's Lair is just a gauntlet of trap-rooms, then lava-rooms filled with one enemy and one status effect traps which is probably why you see the drop off in people actually beating him despite being near the end of the game: It just loses it's charm and slows down to such a slog that the only way I made it through was just to sprint past the hordes of singular-type enemies which felt awful.- Exploration drops in fun and value by the end as well as enemy quality, boss quality and level quality. A lot of the spare rooms you'll find by then exist solely to remember set items you may or may not have found and offer nothing of value otherwise. Two rooms I found, back to back in Mercucio's Lair had nothing in them except for static props for world building and an obvious location for remembering weapons. The!!OVERALL!!Honestly, for 25 bucks this is a game that I feel is worth it with the DLC being more mixed. You're spending roughly a dollar per hour if you try and be as completionist as possible, a thing I wouldn't recommend, but exploring is where a lot of the fun is and the game will reward you... Until those final sections. Even then I was loving the game, however I don't see myself beating it despite being right next to the final cutscene cause I had my fill. The fact it has Co-Op is great, and there's still messages flying around for extra guidance for anyone playing the game fresh. It's a fun, indie soulslike and if you really like games, gaming history, etc you'll end up finding lots to love and giggle at. Can't wait to see what the devs make next as this was lovely.

Lots of love put into this game and it consistently provides exciting exploration and fun shenanigans with friends. _childDocuments_.review: There are probably lots of great reviews for this game so I will just say it’s basically dark souls 1 with a stick figure. The highlights are the interconnected world that rivals or maybe even exceeds DS1’s world layout, and the memories mechanism. Basically just about every weapon and chest armor piece* can be remembered to unlock further potential. These are also the cons as the remembering function is a little clunky in practice and could be improved and I still think the devs should enable fast travel between beacons (bonfires) for qol fixes.

_childDocuments_.review: Is really hard for a game to get that souls feel right and this game gets it all the way. The combat and weapons feel really well tuned, the bosses and enemies have really fun attack patterns and the way the map is designed and the way it connects is just masterful.The unique gimmick of making the items remember in certain spots to make them more powerful, uprez and get the lore really makes you interact with the world more and it made me actually read those and all the references to other videogames in those.Can't comment on coop since the friend that got the game with me is busy atm and we can't do that yet but from trailers it being a full on no disconnect 2 player campaign progression coop is totally a selling point as well to me.This is easily my favorite game of the year and only way I can see that change is if somehow Silksong comes out this year as well.The only complaints I have are really minor with only one actually mattering is that the lock on can be a bit jank sometimes and not lock on on stuff right in front of you.The other is more that I'd really love a way to make the forgotten relics be restored somehow as well and that the maid version of haunted armor is something you can't get as drop is just a totally missed opportunity.Only thing left to say is Luivanni of the Abyss DLC when?

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great time if you're looking for a Co-op souls-like game. The enemies and environments are interesting and varied with a good amount of challenge. There are only a few problems that if the devs fixed, would make the game much better:- Boss aggressiveness seems to be easily cheesable because they usually go after 1 player the whole time. Making the boss switch aggro would make the fights MUCH more challenging. The boss designs were cool but since every boss endlessly chased me, my partner just hit them in the back until we won.- Kicking the other player every time we lose. Its hella annoying and I don't know what purpose this serves. Would be a nice QoL change- Killing both players when one of us dies. It doesn't feel like a fair system. Maybe if my partner dies I have to go to a checkpoint to revive them instead (Remnant had this system and it worked well enough)- Bad UI while trying to 'Use Multiple' makes me misclick on other items and use the wrong item. The box that opens when I click on an item can instead be moved over the item's picture instead of to the right of it where the constant misclicking happensOverall, this game is pretty good. Even with the issues mentioned above this game is well worth the money

There is plenty of room for improvement, but for its price and what it offers, it should only get better with new updates.

_childDocuments_.review: An Experience of a Souls-like while still having enough of its own uniqueness to be its own series, The game tries to mix both seriousness and absolute downright silly in Random Encounters, The animations of the swings and the quantity of how many unique looking tools there is really makes you want to find and unlock each tool.The Co-op is seemless as one can join at any moment when you want them too, by simply using an item in your inventory and summoning or being summoned.But be warned as you can not hurt each other with hack and slashing, magic can still hit team members and cause stunlocking if you are not careful.The game is quite enjoyable so far and it has a good bit of content for  it.

_childDocuments_.review: I-frames are very delayed; hit boxes are questionable; recovery frames are obtuse and unrefined; enemy aggro is inconsistent, often having enemies attack before even turning or finishing previous animations; lock on is really only a suggestion, and good luck switching to another target if they aren't in front of the first target; stamina drain is overbearing, god help you if you block an attack,(when entering ankle deep water there is the risk of dying of old age before making it across); and there is a pretty annoying amount of times where the character attacks/ attacks an extra time without any input (probably a 10% chance).If you are onboard for a souls ripoff with an admittedly interesting story; cool ideas;  a lot of cheek; pretty decent graphics; good ol' indy concept design;  and none of Fromsoft's quality; , then try this out. _childDocuments_.review: TL:DR: Buy this on sale, it's a good game but with poorly implemented ideas.A good game with horribly implemented ideas and poor balance. There's things in the game I love, such as the references, weapons, armor sets, and build variety (though luck builds are insanely overpowered). However, the bad implementation screws most of those ideas... The average HP you'll have in the endgame is around 1300, maybe more if you dump points in vitality, and there's enemies that can take 600+ hp off you in a single combo, while you have some pretty heavy armor on. Mind you, the enemy I speak of (werewolf), is not a miniboss or a rare foe, it's a regular enemy that's spread about in the game world like if it was regular cannon fodder. Another thing that SUCKS in this game is the fact that most weapon animations, especially if you do a combo, do not allow you to roll away from an attack, forcing you to either equip daggers (which have decent frame data to allow you a dodge), or just trade attacks until you eventually die because you do not have enough HP to do that against every enemy. The combat could be really improved if there was a rework on poise, because for the most part, one of two things will happen. You'll poise break enemies in every hit, stunning them in place on every attack, making combat so easy you'll snore, or, against stronger enemies such as the God forsaken Werewolves, you'll either have to use a great weapon to sort of be able to counter them, or pray you can DPS them before they melt your entire life bar away.The huge damage basically any enemy can do causes another issue, which is not rewarding combat, if this wants to be a soulslike, combat/confrontation has to be rewarded, such as for example elden ring giving you flask recharges ocasionally, also, another issue is that this makes it so sprinting away from enemies is just more rewarding, because with the damage and hitstun they do, it's easier to book it and hit the next checkpoint at times, then, come back and explore at your leisure, since most enemies get stuck in map geometry and get their position reset.I do recommend this game, just grab it on sale because you'll not be having a smooth ride the whole game, and many times you'll have to cheese combat encounters to make them possible, such as two or more werewolves trying to attack you.

_childDocuments_.review: An amusing souls-like that was overall really fun to play. I did not go into the game expecting much, but I was pleasantly surprised in finding more depth to it. Overall a 20 - 30 hour journey through several different interconnected regions, unlocking short-cuts between them as I progressed.The remembering system of restoring the lore to the equipment was a novel mechanic that I liked, though others may find tedious as it requires some backtracking. I generally breezed through most bosses, not really using much in the way of consumables nor grinding levels ahead of time.There are NPC summons available for the bosses if following the quest-lines, standard souls-fare. There are also a couple different endings both of which I played through and enjoyed. In true Dark Souls style, at least one of the big NPC quests can be completely missed and requires some backtracking.Pros:+ I enjoyed the voice-over by the narrator, but this is very subjective+ Lore storytelling, multiple endings, and item collect-athon gives some replayability.+ The underlying story about the dangers of nostalgia and hero worship were an unexpected bonus+ Interesting map design with short-cuts+ Plays pretty smoothly on the Steam DeckCons:- Narrator has a lot to say in the beginning but commentary drops off mid-game- if you are looking for From-Soft's hyper-tuned mechanics and pixel-perfect hit boxes you will be disappointed- Not really much of a sound-track (I fixed this by playing the Crypt of the NecroDancer soundtrack in the background)Mixed:- Wonky textures sometimes on the maps, lamp-shading the "retro-ness" of the world. Depending on how forgiving you are, this is humorous or "bad-game-design".- DLC is pretty optional, only for those who want to answer the question: "what would this game's version of Blighttown play like?"

_childDocuments_.review: Ever felt like Dark Souls needed a bit of humor injected into the formula? Well this game will help you find out what you've been missing! The Last Hero of Nostalgaia is an unapologetic satirical adventure filled to the brim with a gorgeous changing world, unique enemies, and a combat system reminiscent of the souls-like genre. This is all packed on top of a dark story with a narrator that is actively hating you and making your life harder since you were created.Combat wise, you can expect the usual souls-like combat of timed rolling and attacking. The enemies are relentless, but Nostalgaia offers some interesting features that sets it apart. The world is a celebration of video games, which means a bunch of easter eggs and items influenced by other franchises (like the green herb from Resident Evil). Armor and weapons also have their own lore which, if you go to specific spots, you can help them remember the past memories which can power up the weapons! Mix this with a humorous outlook and online co-op and you have a recipe for a very enjoyable game. But, of course, we have to see how this game runs on the Steam Deck.When set to max settings, Nostalgaia can actually perform decently, but it has a major issue with lighting that is casting shadows. For whatever reason, it is very taxing on the system, so going into any spot with too many lights caused major slowdowns and battery drain. This typically went to 20W while framerate droppped to 33 FPS. While these framerate drops can't be avoided completely while saving any battery, there are ways to make gameplay significantly better.After my testing of The Last Hero of Nostalgaia, I came across a couple conclusions. I found that 55 FPS helps negate some of the minor frame drops while keeping smoothness, 1024x576 with FSR looks great with these kinds of visuals, and the lighting causes some issues regardless of settings. With these in mind, I found that 55 FPS was stable in the most important parts of the game, the fights.With this, there was still some minor slowdowns at some points, but it stuck above 51 and returned to 55 soon after. This didn't impact gameplay at all and the batter lasted around 3 - 3.5 hours! If you want to play at the highest quality settings, there will be some sacrifices for stability in bigger areas. Getting rid of Volumetric Lighting helped, but it fluctuates wildly in some areas with drains going from 11W to 19W. Playing at 40 still felt good, but the bigger drain made it hard to justify.There really wasn't any major bugs in the game and was actually pretty smooth through and through. There were a couple of little things I noticed like Vsync not working in the main menu and then starting up in-game, but this didn't affect the game. My biggest issue would be the slowdowns caused by the lighting, but with the recommended settings, I was able to minimize it to almost nothing!I truly believed the souls-like genre was good as it is with some incredible and unique games there, but I didn't expect to enjoy this one as much as I did. On the surface, The Last Hero of Nostalgaia seems like a generic souls game, but the humor that is injected into the formula, with the video game nostalgia influences, feels like a breath of fresh air. I actually laughed out loud when the narrator threw a cow at me. With the recommended settings, this game is wonderful on Deck and definitely worth your time!

_childDocuments_.review: While The Last Hero of Nostalgaia starts on good premises, the experience is quickly dimmed due to a poor execution.Let's start with the goods : the writing and world-building. It has great visuals (no need for high-end graphics!), a few good level design and very often rides on references. The game also has a "remember" system which allows to unlock an upgrade for your weapon/armor if you find a very specific place in the world. Some just asks for money, though. This also unlocks a weapon arts for your weapon, but most are just useless. As for the resources to use those WA and spells, it can be bought really cheap at the start of the game (100 were enough). On the other hand, you can sacrifice this memory, and its weapon art, to "unburden" your weapon, increasing its damage. Turns out dealing big damage is more than enough to steamroll the gameAnd that's all folks! The combat is terribly dull. It feels like a prototype of demon souls (ps3) : there are many hits that will just whiff, because your enemy is a foot below or above. Your hit-boxes are very inconsistent, and your character doesn't respond well. You can't even lock/unlock during an attack : even when the enemy is just dead, you are still locked until your attack has entirely stopped . And sometimes, your attack will just stop out of nowhere (especially using great hammers!). Plunging attacks are completely bugged : only your weapon hass a tiny hit-box, you will either miss, or land on top of the enemy, without even damaging it. You can then move while staying on his head...Queing is also very annoying : when you spam a spell, hit "use"then switch to another item during the animation, the game will still launch the next item even two seconds after your previous input. The same goes for light attacks, be careful of spammingThere was one boss that was cool, the vast majority were complete push-overs.It is a bad game for whoever seaks challenge (unless you impose some on yourself), but for anyone looking for their first "souls-like", this might be just the game for you (but really cheap!)

_childDocuments_.review: At a base, completely fundamental level there's nothing wrong with this game. It's a Dark Souls clone, and that's meant with complete sincerity. It's not a soulslike, but a one to one copy that does a good job of aping DS1. Good weapons, an interesting system for upgrading them via geolocational riddles, a stat system that isn't actually that confusing. But then there's the checkpoint system. It sucks. It's terrible, it's downright ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ awful. Very few games have a single opulent mechanic that drags the rest of the game so deeply through the mud it's formulated a wet grave, but oh boy this game has done it. In the early game, the idea of locking a point you can always teleport to might just pass over your head, but it's a sinister little ♥♥♥♥ that turns the MC Escher map into an endeavor most foul. Wanna go back to an area because there's a good weapon or armor set there? Hope you have your rinky dink little anchor beacon set exactly there that you only get one of, because otherwise you can pound sand. I'll replay this game from the start every couple of months like some pilgrimage to a mountainous peak of realizing that I actually hate playing it because of this. Of course Dark Souls 1 didn't have exactly fast travel, but it had it. This is like if Fast Travel got hit by a bus being carriaged by rhinos, this is the type of design decision that baffles the mind to think about how it passed prepro, design, and testing. If that doesn't bother you, you'll probably like it, if it does, tell this game to eat dirt.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a shame that the game is on the state that it is because you can see that they truly tried, there's a lot of creativity and passion poured into this game.The main thing that drags the entire game down is the amount of bugs and how horribly implemented the hitboxes are.Enemy's hitboxes are horribly implemented in a favorable (for them) way, you may take damage before, during or after the enemy swings it's attack depending on the enemy plus the weapon may completely miss and you will still take damage.Meanwhile, the player's hitboxes are horribly implemented in a unfavorable (for yourself) way, the amount of times I impaled or crushed an enemy with an attack and absolutely nothing happened is just disastrous, plus, since the enemy doesn't get staggered, since the hit counted as missed, now they get a free hit on you, so you better spend a lot of levels on health.Bugs range from falling through terrain and dying to the void, enemys suddenly taking zero damage from all sources and getting stuck at the beacon in multiplayer leaving you no option but to force quit the game. The only favourable bug is when rarely an enemy's AI breaks and they stand still so you get a free kill, everything else will either make you die or make you force quit the game.There's also a handful of game design problems but it wouldn't matter if they were fixed because the bugs and hitboxes alone make the entire game a missery to play.

_childDocuments_.review: The best thing about this game is the story and world building in it.  The game play, however, is very unpolished.  The dodging is very lenient and the fact that you can block one hundred percent of physical damage, from the start of the game, is absurd.  The target switching between enemies is horrendous as it switches about a tenth of the time.  The targeting is also very poorly made, with weapons that had long reach you still needed to be basically inside the enemy to hit them.  The progression of bosses was very anti-climatic, Mercucio was probably one of, if not, the easiest of the bosses in the game.  The dlc also has the problem where, to complete it, you had to have done a quest line, which isn't really that much of a problem, but more of an annoyance if you already finished the game, or gotten past the cutoff point of the quest.  Overall I like this game's world a lot, but the game play is just completely lacking.  From unimaginative and boring bosses, to basic mechanics that fail to work properly, the game is so insanely easy, even compared to a game like DS3 where I first tried more than half the bosses.  The story is finished, but the game play to me, is still early access.

_childDocuments_.review: This game seems extremely promising at first. Offering a funny narrator and the possibility for a new souls-like cooperative romp through a decaying land. The narrator's witty and on the nose banter is enjoyable. Negatives:- The narrator which was a major selling point just seemingly disappears for long lengths of time past the first quarter of the game- There are major hitbox issues which bring unneeded difficulty (your swings should connect but they won't. Or vice versa. But more often than not they will miss)- Multiplayer is VERY restrictive (I had to restart a save because I went ahead a little on my own and it de-synced my save from my friend's which made it so we could no longer connect unless we restarted.)- There are some other things I've probably forgotten considering how long it's been since I played this game. But whatever you do. Don't buy this game unless you have run out of any other souls games to get your fix. It will entice you with it's charm and variety. But it will turn into a horrendous slog.
