_childDocuments_.review: Edited: 1/26/23 - I want everyone who hasn't read this to understand, my review is buried for some reason. If you go and search negative reviews and select "most helpful" my review is no where in sight! WTF?! There is something whacky going on here. Steam DOES NOT want you to read my review. I've been looking forward to Choo-Choo Charles since I saw some screen shots for it a year or so ago. I didn't have high expectations knowing full well this was pretty much a one person project. However, I have seen some wonderful horror games that have also be done with small teams that have easily surpassed all my expectations. I want to start off by saying I have a lot of respect for the creator of CCC and I hope to see them do more projects as well as to continue to improve this game. Now let's get into the pros and cons!Pros:* Completely unique concept, a demented train that attacks you and terrorizes the island and your own mode of transportation is a train* The environment looks pretty good, constant rain and thunderstorms, makes you feel uneasy. Always worried when will Charles attack?!* I can tell a lot thought and time went into this game * Big map can be explored on foot or with the train* PicklesCons:* It's a short game. I took my time because I'm a slow player when it comes to these types of games, I love to explore.  * Classified as horror but it's too hokey. I'm not talking about Charles he actually looks freaky, however nothing about this game has made me think "yep, that scared my socks off"* I hate to say it, but it's boring. The overall story is boring, the game play is boring it's not keeping me very interested or invested* All the missions might as well be the same thing, and are SUPER quick and simple. Collect item for NPC, NPC rewards you with scrap, the only truly unique mission is the ghost mission * 95% of the map is empty and not worth exploring, when the only thing to collect is a few paint cans and scrap (which will become worthless) it's really not worth looking around* I can only collect so much scrap before I'm ready to go play another game, sorry but there isn't much to do after you've upgraded your train* I RARELY saw Charles and that is a huge turn off for me. He's the golden goose in this game and he's rarely in it until the end, and the end for me was such a pain in the ass compared to rest of the game that it was actually frustrating  * Some guns need a cross-hair* You need to be able to mark on the map places you've been so you can look at what places you've thoroughly searched for scrap or paint cans, really not interested in trying to remember what places had lock boxes. I don't see myself playing until I've found all the paint cans* Other than Charles, you and a few NPCs the world is pretty lifeless* The Charles cultists or whatever they are, are another wasted opportunity, you can't do anything to them unless you have them follow you back to your train so you can gun them down. This to me, is utterly annoying, because the sneak mechanic is uninteresting and worthless. It's just easier to run from them and ignore them.* Charles is glitchy, especially when you are on foot. He'll get stuck on things, he'll get stuck inside buildings and he is so damn glitchy for the final fight that you'll probably have to do it multiple times because he'll get stuck on something and then suddenly appear practically inside your train hitting you* ZERO replay-ability, massive let down for such a short gameI don't like giving a thumbs down when I want to see the game sell well and do well, but in good conscious I can't give the game a thumbs up because I want those things. I have to be honest or my reviews are worth nothing. As it sits, this game has TONS of potential and I think the creator has TONS of potential, but it's just not a good game YET. I'm hoping more things will be added, multiplayer would be great but I doubt that happens. Bug fixes, more content in general would really add to CCC.  I will happily change my opinion if I continue to see improvement. But for now, there are better games in the horror genre for $20 USD. I think for as short as this game is it might be a little too much money for a 2-3 hour game, but I'll leave that up to you to decide.P.S. I want to say something, I'm seeing a lot of positive reviews that tell you to ignore the negative reviews and just people blatantly ignoring what this game is offering BECAUSE this was created by one person. I don't care if 1 million people or 1 person made a game, if the game costs money and isn't free there SHOULD be criticism. So keep that in mind if you are going to only look at the positive reviews.

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoy and find the review helpful, please follow my curator StarsDeck! I heard about the title before and was interested due to its controversy. Journalists and companies seem to dislike it, while most players praised it, so I was invested in seeing the fuss. The game gives you a train to ride across the map during the first minutes, and you better take care of that train because that train is family now. During my half hour, I noticed the game was low-budget, but I thought it was a diamond in the dirt.I like trains; you like trains; everyone likes trains. The vehicle is customizable, allowing you to give it your flair, and I decided to focus exclusively on speed during my first hour with the title. The extra speed allowed me to move across the locations with less risk of Charles finding me and kept the experience less tedious. I love the weapons, as they can be obtained by doing side quests that take five minutes each and have different uses. For example, the bazooka is excellent for getting rid of Charles quickly in open-world encounters, while the default gun is excellent for stunning in boss fights.I would have appreciated some on-foot weapons, mainly due to the stealth aspect needing to be fixed when you are on foot. I would visit a cave to find the game's main objective, only for enemies to bother me. As I could not get past these foes stealthily, I would lead them out of the caves to kill them with my weapon on the train. That resulted in a tedious section of back and forth in which I asked myself why are the cultist a thing in this game. It would have been better to include on-foot weapons or remove these enemies altogether as they downplayed the experience.Another thing that bothered me is that quests are marked as either mandatory or optional-yet you have to do a lot of optional missions if you want to beat the game due to the last main objective requiring upgrades to the vehicle. While that is annoying, I enjoyed the side quest due to their simplicity and fun mini-games, such as playing a slender man section or delivering pickles to a lady that loves pickles.The originality is there, but the developer could have added more meaning in effectiveness. For example, a quest where a bridge is broken and must be repaired would have been an exciting challenge to the player. There is not a lot of danger when moving around on foot, as Charles will stay on the rails mostly. While that downplays Charles, it allows for a better time exploring the world and discussing with the island's people without too many hassles.The strong point of the title is that it is a no compromised experience. Choo-Choo Charles is a fun game that lets you beat it in one or two sittings. It stays within its welcome and is rewarding enough to keep you invested as you gradually upgrade your train. The side quests are funny and straight, the locations look great, and so does Charles, a menacing demon roaming around. The scraps needed to develop your upgrades further add a layer of being like a gremlin hunting for scraps like a maniac!The weak point here is that the developer made some questionable choices. Why add stealth if it won't work and it's not a central focus? In addition, objectives on the map sometimes won't update halfway in, meaning you can get a letter, and the map will still think you need the letter. These issues keep the game from reaching greatness and could have been through more before making the final cut.My specs are RTX 2060, 36 GB of ram, Intel Core i7-11700K - Core i7 11th Gen Rocket Lake 8-Core 3.6 GHz LGA 1200.Running the game on max settings, the FPS ranges between 50 to 65; I recommend setting the graphics high instead if you have a rig similar to mine for a more consistent experience above 60 FPS. The game would sometimes forcibly despawn an enemy for no reason, while other times, I would get shot by a foe and was sent flying into the air to my doom. These issues were rare and did not appear to be consistent as I only suffered each only one time.Choo-Choo Charles is a game that you can pick and finish in one sitting. The asking price might be a bit much as it would be better priced at 12-15, but it is an enjoyable ride nonetheless. A survival horror that oozes originality and rewarding gameplay keeps the player invested from start to end despite some erroneous game design decisions. Is it worth your time and money? Overall, this is a good pick for most gamers out there. Do note that this is a survival horror, not a Horror game, as it lacks jumpscares and is more action-oriented. If you have money to spare, get it for the total price; otherwise, wait for a sale to drop it to 12-15 bucks.8/10  GREAT

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a solo developer having fun with a goofy concept and taking feature suggestions from commenters on TikTok over the course of a year. As long as you engage with Choo Choo Charles from that understanding, you'll likely have a fun time. As of editing this review I have 3.4 hours of playtime. Discounting goofing-around or backtracking because I was streaming while playing and also wanted to 100% the game, I probably 'played' the game for two hours tops. I find that perfectly reasonable for a $20 indie game someone made by themselves, but I see some people in the reviews unnecessarily upsetti spaghetti about the run time, so there's some data for you.Most mechanics in the game are jankily-implemented sketches of something the game would be very cool if it had the full, finished version. Stealth segments SOUND interesting. In practice the detection is instantaneous and that enemy will eternally follow you. The fix? You can sprint as fast as them for infinity, and they have jank pathing and almost never actually shoot at you. The shotguns function more as melee weapons than guns. You can sprint through every single stealth section without letting go of Shift and never die. Charles himself clearly had the most design put into him. The rest of the game is peppered with goofy NPCs without lip syncs. An early version of the game had every NPC as a cardboard cutout, which fit the (genuinely amazing) hand-drawn textures of everything built in the environment. Then at some point some Unity Asset Store-lookin' human models were plopped in and it actively detracts from the game's style and atmosphere. Choo Choo Charles is the video game equivalent of watching a good director's first student film. You can see all the little details that will mark their style in future, but they didn't have the funds, practice, or time to fully develop that into what they want. Fully worth your $20. Just know it's a three-hour-at-most story and the flamethrower is literally worthless. Never need to fire it once.

_childDocuments_.review: This was a game that I swore I wouldn't play... and then my friend gifted it to me.Choo-Choo Charles is a game that I saw the trailer for about a year ago and intended to never try out, but I still thought it looked super interesting! I'm glad to say that I played through it today and loved every second of it.Choo-Choo Charles has it's own charm. Charles can get stuck in some valleys, and it's quite hilarious—until he unsticks himself and comes chugging down towards you alarmingly fast, then it's not so hilarious. The map is absolutely massive and way larger than I expected it to be. I had so much fun running around and exploring new areas. There are quite a few quests located throughout the map for the player to complete; most aren't required but are pretty fun to complete anyway, especially the quests that unlock new weapons for you to use against Charles. Most, if not all, of the quests are fetch-style quests, which I don't mind too much because it just feels right in this kind of atmosphere. If you're someone who enjoys lore in games, Choo-Choo Charles has notes that you can find throughout exploring, and they actually provide a bit of lore on some of the characters, like Warren Charles III! I enjoyed reading a lot of them :) The visuals are appealing; I found it to be very beautiful, and the game runs fairly well, which is always a huge plus.The only thing I wish this game could've had was a crouch mode. There is a way to "stealth" and it's by leaning over the edges of walls to look out for enemies, but I really wanted a crouch mode to be able to actually feel like I was being quiet and to ensure I wasn't being seen by an enemy. Besides that, this game is amazingly polished and was an absolutely amazing play.In terms of replay value, I was able to complete 100% of the game in under 4 hours on my first playthrough. This was with me taking my time as well. If you just want to run around and fight Charles multiple times, you could probably get more than 4 hours logged, but there isn't much replay value for me. It's a relatively short game for the normal price of $20, but I really enjoyed it, so I think it's well worth it. It's also a very easy 100% game for my completionists out there!All in all, I definitely recommend trying out Choo-Choo Charles. It's extremely well done and will get your heart pumping at times. I enjoyed every minute of it and hope there will be a sequel or even DLC (the ending hints at one? LET'S HOPE!)Thanks for reading my review and have a fantastic day! :)Rating: 9.3/10

_childDocuments_.review: To clarify, I enjoyed Choo-Choo Charles. I just don't think it's worth the asking price. Get it on a sale where it's at least half the cost.I remember finding C-CC as many others did, as part of its zany train-spider pitch that captured the imaginations of many with its decidedly nuts teaser trailer. I didn't stay up to speed with the game's development so its release was a sudden but pleasant surprise. I only wish Two Star Games had given it more time, as there's simply a lot of missed opportunities to do so much more with its premise, setting, gameplay and characters. It wasn't quite all that to find that the unique selling point of the game, the pursuit by Charles, really is the game's only unique selling point. All else around it is rather bland.The atmosphere is, in some ways, a big plus. It's simple but oddly homely, exploring a lonely, grey, rainy island in your little refuge of a train. It really does make you feel like you're an explorer on a mission. Equally simple, but appealing, are the upgrades to your train. That said, it does make you feel a bit useless when you're on foot to do quests. I would've appreciated some meaningful use of the inventory system or items to facilitate this, especially when dealing with the island's cultists (we'll get to them later). Scrap is the main currency and it's essentially everywhere: you won't be in short supply in any instance and it's easy to outstrip the upgrades with the amount you have. In the final confrontation, I was practically swimming in scrap.That said, it's only in the later game that a real sense of vulnerability arises, namely that Charles might appear when you're away from your only point of defence. It's moody, sure, hearing the howling train whistle in the distance. But there's not much beyond that to add to the atmosphere beyond some light soundscaping. If you like it, you like it. If you don't, it'll miss you completely. Even the rain falling through the roof of your train breaks that thin layer of immersion quite easily.On this, the world is relatively big, but a bit too empty. As a result, the side quests and challenges of them also feel that way. There's some fun ones, a slender reference and a slightly tense but more annoying struggle against a swamp monster. For a lot of it you're simply going on a simple fetch quest or to place something in a position not far away. Nothing too tough. The hardest challenges you'll face in C-CC are finding the two locked away paint cans for your train. But that's mostly down to the cultist AI being bad. They're the enemies you'll encounter and all function in the same way: chasing after you to get close, then firing a shotgun. Think basic AI, running after you in a straight line, easy to get stuck on objects. That sort of thing.The game just feels overly simple. And not in that kind of indie-dev, one-central-killer-idea-makes-the-game kind of way. Nothing you do feels particularly substantial. One of the earliest side quests you'll do is walking up a set of stairs, opening a door and then grabbing the supplies you need anyway from that room. There's a couple of fun ideas, but nothing that feels more engaging than the eccentric personalities that dot the game: pickle lady, the witch and, I guess, the lighthouse keeper? Small, novel locations are the highlight, an abandoned bunker and a watchtower in the middle of a haunted valley, but again - nothing that feels particularly impactful or memorable. In the end, all you're trying to do is up your scrap count and there's a good chance you'll maximise your train upgrades 1/2 to 2/3 of the way through the game, depending on how completionist your run is.I guess one of the biggest reflections of the empty feeling of the world is the through the characters. None of the activities feel substantial, partly because there's a pretty weak lore behind the concept. You do favours here and there, but none of them further developments on the island. They don't add into any ongoing missions, disputes or activities the islanders are engaged in. They all want to help you, but don't feel like people living with the struggle of cultist uprising or meandering train-spider. Yes, there's written documents that detail the past, but none of is meaningfully realised in the events of the game as you complete quest after quest. Instead, it's just a to-do list of things to get done, without a meaningful structure or sense of progression. Little makes this more clear than the underwhelming arrival of "Warren", the human big-bad who doesn't have any motives that feel actualised by what you're doing, other than characters mentioning his name when you go over to retrieve some item for them. It's all half-baked and simply undercooked. The cultists themselves are promising secondary antagonists, but they too don't seem to have much personality beside their change of masks. They have generic lines and threats more in line with a mugger than a devoted cultist to a train-spider. Where did they come from and where's the imagination? Where's the conflict with islanders considering giving up the fight to go and join them? The feeling you get, instead, is more in line with an easy use of assets than well-spent development time.There's just a lot of missed opportunities for flavour here. The islanders all seem to have knowledge to take down Charles, so why are none of them acting on it? Where are the divides in perspective after all this time of living with Charles? Where are there disagreements and antagonists, heroes and villains creating alternate plans that fail, forcing you down a path of retrieving the eggs to then finally confront the fortress on the island? As aformentioned, it's all unstructured. Things happen in order, but don't increase or decrease the stakes accordingly, it's all fairly weightless.I wanted to like Choo-Choo Charles much more than I did. I enjoyed my time with it and, ultimately, I'm glad there's a hook for a sequel, because it's a chance for Two Star Games to really make better on this foundation. But, at this price point, there's no justifying nearly £17 for a game I got less than three hours gameplay out of (including 100% completion). It's just a shame that from the time since I first saw the game and now, very little effort was seemingly made to flesh out the world of the game and it feels all the more lifeless as a result.TL;DR - Game is fun but underdeveloped and short, not worth the asking price.

_childDocuments_.review: Like everyone's saying, game's too short for for the $20 price tag or $14 sale tag. Before you look at my played hours and go "b-but", I have a habit of leaving games running tabbed. Actual criticisms: Stealth feels a little janky. Your weapon is perma-mounted to the back of your train and Charles can come at you from the front. Charles himself is fast and the game can more or less randomly decide to end you if he happens to spawn while you're on foot and not 5-10 seconds away from shelter. If you find shelter he can hover around the area indefinitely and zero in on you when you leave (happened to me once). World feels bare and lifeless, and the NPCs don't help with that. The threadbare story is very curt and shallow. The ending was..... an ending.I've given a lot of complaints above..... but I  regret my time playing. The game's jank, but it's decent stupid fun and I can tell some heart went into this. It was an enjoyable 100%. But everything mentioned  that steep price tag for what this game is, no. There's plenty of both better polished and cheaper horror games out there. This is one of those occasions where an "eh" option on Steam reviews would be more precise than a "yes" or a "no". 4/10Edit:I  like to see a sequel to this made, with perhaps a bit more budget and polish. While the execution could use work, I like what's presented here, and I think a sequel would do it well if things were learned from this game. Would totally buy a Part 2.

_childDocuments_.review: For a 3D game made by one person this was really impressive. Short game (only about three hours) but it kept my attention from start to finish, and it does a fantastic job of making Charles a omnipresent threat; without spoiling too much, the final battle against him is SUPER satisfying. Definitely made the whole experience worth it, but the game was still really fun overall. I think my only real criticism of the game is the character models; the kooky NPCs that populate the island never move their mouths when talking (and they only have one facial expression at all times), and their movements are stiff. The lack of proper rigging and modelling for the human characters is very apparent with the player character; you don't even have hands, so don't expect to be able to use weapons or do stealth takedowns of enemies; running and hiding are your only skills when you leave your train. This is most definitely because of the minuscule budget, so hopefully for Two Star's next offering they'll have more money (and people) to make something even better. I enjoyed Choo Choo Charles for what it is and I can't wait for more from the developers!

_childDocuments_.review: Blind positivity doesn't bring improvement. With all the respect to Two Star this game could have used more time in the oven.I have the feeling this is going to be one of those games that cannot be criticised because it was made by one person.I refunded the game when i realised the state it was in.And with that here is the review:Spoiler warning I was really looking forward to this game. I like the idea of traveling around with a train as your savehaven.And on top of that having to venture out on foot to explore and collect loot to survive on the rails.With that said there isn't much to loot. Only scraps.And sometimes there is just a breadcrumb trail of scraps leading to places. When you take dmg your HP regenerates by itself so no healing items. The train runs on infinite fuel so no fuel.Only scrap. And there is sooo many scraps that you will be able to fully upgrade your train before you are even close to getting the second egg. (The main story items that you need 3 of.)The Quests. The first quest i did gave me this bad feeling. "I don't trust you go picklock this chest then i will trust you."The chest is like 2 steps away next to the building. The picklock minigame.. i didn't like it that much. Usually the circles were really close to the start point of the "click now" circle so i had to wait for it to go all the way around.but that's fine. When i got to the next quest is where i lost hope. Burning house where you get the flamethrower.Dude set his house on fire and he is like "Yep it's burning down, if the fire dies out you can take the weapon." so naturally i looked around his house to see if there is stuff to collect. Then above the house i found this Water Container that has a red valve. Well you just needed to turn the valve with no issues to put the fire out. That's it. And after this all the quests were the same. Go here get that for me you get scraps. The map has NPCs highlighted so there is no exploring to find people.Same goes for the quest items. They will be marked so you don't have to explore for them.Let's talk about Charles a bit. He is the main figure of this show after all. If the game wasn't so short his presence would be actually nice. He appears in your area every now and then. You can hear his trainhorn in the distance and it's great.He is pretty buggy on the other hand. When he charges at you he will send you flying sometimes. This caused me to land on top of a building and Charles was unable to get to me but he wouldn't leave me alone either.I also watched the final fight againts him when a certean someone streamed it. The whole putting in the eggs at the temple then running back to your train to fight charles is a cutscene. You literally don't get to run away from charles before you two fight. The game takes care of that for you.The final fight with charles is also uhh.. just a regular encounter with him but the world is more dramatic about it. Charles multiple times seems to enter a new phase but it just makes him.. teleport?.. oh you also get scraps for some reason when you damage charles. So your supply of scraps matters even less so you don't have to worry about running out as long as you don't stop shooting.Stealth vs the dudes with shotguns. They have really good eyes. They will see you from pretty far away then chase you all the way back to your train. You can only kill them with your train's guns. ( or running them over but that rarely happens.)They will always run straight at you and try to shoot you with their shotguns. There is a few area with a couple of them inside like the caves or the temple.Let's talk about the other train. It's really comfy to go around with your own train. Sadly with how short the game is it won't last long. There isn't much to explore either. As i said fully upgrading the train takes no effort. You can collect paint cans to customize the color of your train. That's the only extra content as well as of now that pushes the game's playtime a little bit further.The weapons are okay. But it really doesn't matter in the end. You can beat charles with only the base weapon and the flamethrower. Spray fire on charles to slow him down switch to the gun shoot a bit then switch back to flamethrower.Charles won't be able to touch the train like that. And from what i saw the dps of the machinegun and the flames are up there with BOB the ultimate weapon. That said the combat againts Charles is intense. It's just a shame that Charles only tries to peck at the train. He doesn't have anything that you need to counter. Here are my ideas of how combat could have been better.(these are not in the game.)Imagine it like this. Charles has a charge attack deals insane dmg to your train if it connects you have to use the flamethrower to make him slow down and stop to prevent the dmg. Or Charles pulls out his own gun on top of his train that you need to gun down with the machine gun or else Charles will start shooting your train. Idk Charles becomes armored and immune to dmg while comboing with other attacks he can do but if you use the rocket launcher his defense shatters and you can do dmg to him again. BOB the ultimate weapon.. i can't think of anything right now that could be fun to counter with it.There are other things that could make this game absolutely worth it. Two Star clearly wanted to make a good horror game. But it's not exactly scary either. The only scary parts are when you are not on your train and you hear charles which is great. But there are soooo few things to explore on foot and sooo little time as well since the game is short.I went to the lighthouse thinking i could get trapped there if Charles decides to be around. But he just didn't come at that time and that dread was kind of wasted. Barry the water monster. I am afraid of water monsters or deep waters. But even that part didn't make me hesitate to go into the water. It was just an amnesia water monster that you could beat by standing still.Please don't take this as a hate review. The only reason why i decided to write a review was to give feedback. I think this game needed more time before it was released. Maybe our dear developer felt rushed or who knows. _childDocuments_.review: Alright. Choo-Choo Charles is done and dusted. This was a pretty fast paced sandbox action horror set on an island isolated from the rest of the world ATM. I don’t think I’d really call it survival horror since there’s really only one resource (scrap) to collect, which is quite plentiful; and the only penalty for dying is losing a couple scrap. Anyway, it was a fun little game.The aforementioned scrap is used to upgrade your train’s damage, armor, and speed; and can be used to repair your train as well. Speaking of trains, you ride one around the map, leaving it to investigate locations, meet people, and fulfill quests on foot.Each quest will offer you something relevant to trying to survive long enough to kill Choo-Choo Charlie, a half train half giant demon spider (or giga spider as one NPC calls it lol) rampaging about the island you’re on. For your efforts in completing quests, you’ll receive scrap and weapons you can interchangeably install to the back of your train. You start out with a machine gun, but quickly get a small array of much cooler weapons. I used the flamethrower for the final boss fight, personally.Many times throughout the adventure, Choo-Choo Charles will show up to try to chase you down. When you’re on the train, doing enough damage will scare him off temporarily. On foot, you’ll need to hoof it into a building or back to your train to avoid getting eaten. Fortunately, you can run pretty fast.There are also sequences where you’ll need to sneak past enemy NPCs. They’re armed, but you’re not, so stealth and running for your life are the proper tactics. Although you can bait them onto the train tracks and run them over if you so desire, lol.There are collectibles in the form of paint cans used to give your train a make-over; and notes which offer expanded lore about the island, its inhabitants, and of course Choo-Choo Charles.Graphically, this is a nice looking game with the highlight obviously being Choo-Choo Charles himself. A funny thing with the the quest giving NPCs. They’re voice acted well, and are generally fun and funny characters, and they stand in whatever pose they’re given initially, their lips don’t move, and it basically makes them intentionally even more comical. Plus the writing generally leans heavily into being campy B movie horror/comedy. Enemy NPCs tend to whistle while they work. The audio in this game is exceptional in every way, from the OST to the in-game sounds to the voice acting.And that’s it in a nutshell. Not a particularly difficult game, although the final boss battle with Choo-Choo Charles was somewhat challenging. Pro tip. Make sure you have spare scrap going into that sequence.This is fully Steam Deck compatible.Choo-Choo Charles took me about four hours to complete and I bought it on sale, but in reality, cost vs value is there at retail price. I enjoyed the game and there’s a solid chance that you will as well.

_childDocuments_.review: I get it's a meme game, but save your money, you're not getting your $20 worth. I didn't come into this expecting AAA quality, I know it was made by one guy, but when you ask people to drop 1/3 the price of a AAA game, I expect more than this.-Unless you go out of your way to do literally everything available to you, the game MIGHT take around 2 hours to complete.-Any difficulty in "surviving" against Charles can be negated within the first 10 minutes, the moment you acquire your second weapon, which in turn renders the other 3 weapons basically pointless.-Stealth sections only require use of the game's extremely scuffed stealth mechanics if you don't want to get magdumped by enemies while trying to loot scrap and collectibles. In general, these sections (which are the entirety of mandatory missions) are extremely unfun.-AI cultist enemies are more annoying than anything. Basically, if they spot you (which is REALLY poorly telegraphed whether they can or not) they will almost never get off your nuts until you bait them ALL the way back to your train and mow them down.-Charles himself is EXTREMELY wonky when not chasing your train, and has a knack for either mauling you instantly or getting stuck if he catches you in the open world, it's one or the other. As for when he DOES end up chasing you on your train, it's more annoying than anything since he's probably chasing you a good distance away from where you wanted to be, forcing you to backtrack after making him run away.-For a game that is this big of a meme, it really doesn't capitalize on it. I honestly didn't find anything here particularly funny, as the writing weirdly tries to take itself seriously for most of the game. The only instance of actual comedy I found felt extremely forced and out of place, and if you've played the game you know exactly what I'm talking about.-Quests are extremely samey, mostly consisting of "go here, grab this, come back". Aside from one extremely janky reference that I actually kinda liked, there wasn't much creativity there and felt like they only exist to bloat the runtime above the 2 hour mark.For a game that I initially thought would just be a funny little $5 adventure against the goofy spider train, I'm unfortunately disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: While Choo Choo Charles does a few things right but it also misses the mark, with around 3 hours of playtime I had collected everything, completed all the side quests, maxed out my train upgrades, Explored all there was and defeated Charles, all at the cost of $29 Canadian dollars. With little to no replayability I'm not sure if this is worth that much but here's what I thought of the game.I was very hyped to play this game since it's announcement, it had so much new going for it and interesting mechanics.Pros: Train gameplay is well done and works well, it's fun to travel around the map and not having to worry about steering and being able to enjoy the scenery as well as check the map. Atmosphere is good with the added rain effect giving a sense of unease. The cinematics and story are interesting with little clues dotted around the map giving you an idea of what happened and who the villains are. In the beginning there is a sense of horrible dread as soon as you hear that train whistle.Now the bad...-The game just feels lacking, train combat feels easy once you are fully upgraded within the first hour and the sense of dread I mentioned above is suddenly more like "oh here we go again". -The enemy npc's or train cultists(?) aren't fun to encounter due to the lack of a good sneaking mechanic, I don't think I've ever played a sneaking game without a crouch however you can peak around corners. Enemies only see you when facing you directly, sound doesn't seem to tip them off and they can literally see you from a mile away and will FOLLOW YOU until the ends of the earth leaving your only option to run a mile back to your train and use the gun to kill them. It'd be nice if there was at least a small self defense mechanic like a stun attack or that if they lose sight they won't follow, even reducing their run speed so you could possibly break line of sight would make the game a little more forgiving. -Friendly NPCs feel strange in this game, It's hard to take a horror game seriously when it has a crazy pickle lady (yes kinda like a crazy cat lady but pickles), and a witch in a swamp? There are some good ones don't get me wrong, there's a small nod to Slenderman and the water monster from Amnesia which I enjoyed. Others seem to fit well into the game like the lighthouse woman, the conspiracy theorist, and others. There are a few bugs which I'm sure will be patched (fall damage occurs too easily, even when you literally have to fall for a puzzle onto platforms and a wind noise that just grows in certain areas to point it blows your eardrums) and while I am a little critical of the game it did do quite a few things right but just fell short in others. If the game would include a new difficulty or mechanics to customize your playthrough (damage multipliers, frequency of Charles showing, less scrap) then I feel like it'd at least have some replayability or reason to play again. As it stands I wouldn't recommend this game yet, maybe on sale or if changes are made but for now I'm afraid I just can't endorse this game.

_childDocuments_.review: 11/8/23 This review has been edited to include commentary on the new Nightmare Mode.Man, this game has figured out a fairly simple, but REALLY fun gameplay loop. I love getting to drive a train, I love having to (mildly) maintain it, defending it is mildly stressful and enjoyable, and as silly as Charles is, he makes a great villain and good nightmare fuel. The movement of the train, the sounds, the experience of using it is all VERY pleasing. It can take a good while to stop depending on your speed, you've got some basic customization options you unlock, and getting to speed around the island as directed by the railway loop just... really works. You're often revisiting locations and exploration is really encouraged. The gameplay with the train is a lot of fun and it's clear some time was put into making it as fun as it is. And I love the stress of briefly leaving it to explore the island-- Charles can be ANYWHERE.You made my childhood model train set into a real place and let me run around it being chased by a childhood monster. This is AWESOME, I love it.A word on the game's problems, though. Up front, I want to make clear that this is an unabashed endorsement of the game, I really do recommend it. But there are a number of ways it could be improved upon. The character animation is very rudimentary, the story leaves a number of secondary story threads unresolved, and while I LOVED the additional monster sequences, there are only 2 of them. The "stealth" system is extremely bare bones, and more often then not, I ended up luring human enemies back to my train and mowing them down with the mounted gun.One of the challenges of developing with a very, very small team is that you HAVE to cut corners in places to actually produce a game. Animations can't all be AAA quality, you have to cap the number of locations you have, and your expectations need to be kept scaled to the resources you have. You actually have get the game made, tested, refined, and then released. This game is rife with these (necessary and correct) cut corners. And despite how enjoyable the basic gameplay loop is, you can really feel it. UPDATE: Let's talk about the new Nightmare Mode. I've spent a few days trying it and doing my best to learn the ins and outs, I can only conclude it's not very well designed. It is, as it promises, very difficult, but not because you need to learn how to utilize the gameplay loop effectively, but because you need a great deal of luck as well as an ACTIVE AVOIDANCE of the game's central gameplay features. Driving your train is extremely dangerous and you quickly become motivated to hunker down in buildings until Charles goes away. Sitting around, doing nothing, and hoping Charles goes away, isn't fun. And you die/restart so often, that the game starts to feel like a rogue-like, just without the benefits to dying and starting again that any smart rogue-like includes. In short, Nightmare mode is extremely frustrating, not because it's challenging but because it's boring. Offering up a warning that "This is designed to make you rage quit" doesn't excuse the poor design. I'll stick to the original version, thanks.TL;DR: This game is fun, I loved it, I just wish it hadn't taken me 3.2 hours to finish. I would have liked to stay here longer. Nightmare mode is frustrating not because it's challenging, but because it's boring.

I'll break it down into pros and cons for ease of reading.Pros:Interesting conceptReally cool movement (diagonal strafing bunny-hops are the most efficient form of movement)An actually roaming enemy instead of pre-loaded cut scenes add an awesome level of suspense and randomnessA couple interesting characters and side-missionsCons:Complete lack of replayabilityExtremely boring at timesMassive lack of backstory, almost entirely left to speculationHorrendous optimization, you'll need a pretty good computer for max graphicsCharacter models look gross, for lack of better wordDid I mention that this game is VERY BORING?Maybe 2 hours of playtime if you are mentally handicappedAlmost a complete lack of consequence from dying,To sum this up, I wouldn't call it a game as much as I'd call it an experience. _childDocuments_.review: This isn't necessarily a bad game, but it isn't necessarily a good game either. There are a number of design decisions that make playing the game tedious more than terrifying and tense - which I assume is what they're going for.The game plays the concept fairly straight - there's little attention drawn to the fact that there is an inherent goofiness in the design of a train with a creepy face and spider legs. The non-train enemies (humans in masks resembling Charles) are likewise a funny concept, but not much is drawn from their presence, beyond stealth sections which are more tedious than anything. Whilst not in the train, the player has no weapons or ways to defend themselves, meaning that any failed stealth attempts are best solved by running back to the train to your gun, or even out of the area entirely if you left your train a fair way away.The side-quests in the game feel like a scatter-shot approach to designs that *could* work in this kind of game, but they're mostly unique in their designs. Some of them, including one in a swamp, and one seemingly inspired by Slender are the worst offenders of the poor design - with these two quests alone being responsible for the majority of the deaths in my play session. In the first, the player is made to enter the water of the swamp to retrieve something as part of a side quest, but they will be chased by a creature within the lake. The problem comes from the fact that the only cues which indicate how close the swamp creature is are the splashes (both visual and auditory). However both of these get lost easily in the player's own movement, which likewise generates the splashing cues.The second of the two quests has the player run around a gorge collecting 8 pages with children's scribbling - only they're being chased by a ghost which seems to move faster than the player, and when caught, will teleport the player to the outskirts of the quest area - which is frustrating, but more frustrating is that it can also teleport you directly next to Charles, away from the player's train, and away from anywhere to take shelter.The game is very generous with its currency - the scrap that you use to upgrade your train. If you do all of the side quests, collecting scrap quickly becomes irrelevant - once you reach level 10 in each of the Train's attributes (speed, damage, armour), the only thing left to spend your scrap on is repairs.There's a really good feature with the map - it seems to generate a real-time view of the low LOD map - and you can zoom right in to and see what certain structures are. There's a fair amount of good ideas in here that maybe aren't quite executed as well as they could be.

_childDocuments_.review: Let's do a super honest review of this game because so many people seem to be upset about this game for one reason or another. It took me about 4 hours to beat this game 100%. Some people just sped through it and are saying they are beating it in 1.5 - 2 hours. Everyone is going to have a different time just due to how much they are exploring and holding down the sprint button. I believe the dev had said that the average completion time will be 2 - 3 hours and I believe that to be accurate.There's a lot of people in the forums complaining about the price. This is a tough one as everyone's money is worth something different, kind of a "to each their own" sort of deal. I paid the 20$ just like everyone else and did I have fun for 4 hours? Yes I did. I played a game about a train that you upgrade while avoiding a giga spider train on an island and I had fun. I just finished playing The Callisto Protocol a few days ago and you know what? I'd gladly pay the 20$ again for this game before I spend another 60$ on some BS "AAA" title like Callisto again. The indie horror / adventure sphere is so dense with garbage titles that are all free assets of the same lady / zombie / monster that just zoom towards the camera in a dark hallway that this game was an honest breath of fresh air in an otherwise stale genre. Here's what you get in this game: 1. Your own battle train to upgrade. You can upgrade the speed, damage and armor of your train to fight against Charles when you encounter him in the wild.2. Missions / Sidequests: Some people will just reward you with scrap to upgrade your train and some will give you fancier weapons to use against Charles. 3. A small island to explore to collect even more scrap and paint, so you can customize your train's color.That's really it. It is a very simple gameplay loop mechanic. You hop in your train and visit all of the NPCs and get ready for the final fight with Charles at the end of the game. The more you upgrade your train the easier it'll be to beat him at the end. Whether or not that gameplay loop is fun to you is really up to the individual. I had a great time but I love the idea of riding around in a train. Also the game is just so silly and walks the line between silly and fun that I had a great time. I'd rather be chased around an island by a giant spider train than some overused ghost asset from the Unity or Unreal store.You'll also run into guards around the island that just want to murder you. You don't have any way to REALLY fight back at the moment unless you park your train close by and mow them down with the guns you have available. You can also run them over with your train which is VERY satisfying. You will be dying a fair amount when you get caught by the guards with guns but for the most part you just run away and you're good.A lot of people are upset about the price and the length of the game and that's okay. They don't need to buy it. If you really beat it in an hour then you probably rushed through the game and did minimal exploring and that's okay too. If you didn't see any of the information from the dev who worked on the game and told you ahead of time how long it would be I am sorry, but it is what it is. It sounds like the dev has plans to add more to the game and probably DLC in the future. I for one already got my moneys worth playing through it but not everyone agrees.At the end of the day you're playing a game about a zombie spider train that chases you around an island and you battle it from your battle train. I am not sure what you thought you were getting, but that's what you're getting. Yes, the game is very silly and yes, it's also fun. Read the reviews and make your own decision.tl;dr - It's a silly game that is a lot of fun if you don't take it too seriously and just enjoy it. Yes the game is shorter at 2 - 4 hours but it's 2 - 4 hours of fun. If you REALLY want to talk about wasted money go buy The Callisto Protocol and come back and tell me it was worth it while you spend 10 minutes hopping back and forth over a window ledge in the final boss.

_childDocuments_.review: Super-early review, with only an hour-and-a-half under my belt, and the game far from "beaten". I try to avoid such things, but when in Rome...and Steam is looking more and more like Ancient Italy by the day...!      I bought this game Day One on a complete whim, since: a. The Callisto Protocol sounded potentially disappointing, especially for such a mighty price, and b. this certainly looked and sounded a wee bit "different"...      My first two thoughts as the opening cutscene started up: thirty bucks Australian is a pretty high price tag for on-screen characters talking with their mouths closed (!)...but hey, at least the voice acting's pretty good. Ah well...here goes nuthin'...      By all reports it was made by a solo developer, and that's certainly impressive; but again, has me a wee bit worried about that price tag. But wow...it's certainly a big ol' open world for one itty-bitty person to have realised, even if the human character models sure are ! But at least the rest of the graphics are generally pleasing (one part realism, one part Bendy and the Ink Machine cartoon surrealism).      The atmosphere is quite unusual for a horror game: spooky and ominous, but obviously action-packed whenever Charles the half-spider, half-train shows up! And your own train's handling is as smooth as you would hope it would be - considering how much of the game is based on it - without being overly complicated: it's really just three levers and an upgrade list dependant on how much "scrap" you collect (often via "side missions" given to you by other humans on the island; or simply by exiting your vehicle and exploring off the beaten path).      And that's really all the early section of the game, as far as I've played, seems to be: upgrading the capacity of your train-with-a-machine-gun so you can better tackle Charles on the infrequent (though thoroughly unpredictable) occasions that he attacks you...       And the combat itself? I'm pleased to report it works pretty nicely; though I wouldn't go expecting a great deal of "strategy". The single biggest mistake I made was to stop my train at  the wrong time - through no fault of my own that I could perceive - just as Charles decided to attack me. You're much better off fighting him while you're moving, and keeping safely  of him - since your gun is at your train's rear - and the whole game's based on an ongoing autosave, so, well...you can screw yourself pretty good if you choose to park prematurely. Though there's always, luckily, more scrap to be found, and it's mighty useful for repairing your train after it's been unceremoniously "derailed" (you don't get a "game over", just a "you have lost some scrap, and now have to look for more to repair yourself with")!      Oh, and beware: not all NPC humans that you encounter are "friendly"...      It's clearly a much more imaginative take on an open world-ish "survive-and-upgrade" game than, say, your garden-variety zombie apocalypse. Though it does play out reasonably similarly, with the exceptions of the fights being far more infrequent but more "boss fight"-ish when they do occur (I haven't yet found a way to defend myself against hostile humans, beyond running like heck...but I guess we'll see with time)! Oh, and the epic "zoom up and out" thing the game does when you hit the Map button is very nifty and novel indeed...      So, in conclusion: I'm enjoying it so far, but don't feel I can give a particularly definitive appraisal until I've progressed a bit further. Which is really why people shouldn't review certain types of games long before they've "beaten" them, but...that Roman thing again. Guess I thought I'd try something different to my usual...both gameplay-  review-wise...      I'll update when I have something further to opine!Verdict: 8/10.(PS If you enjoyed this review, feel free to check out my two Curator pages: Cheers!)

_childDocuments_.review: Game looks great, it has a good concept, voice acting is mostly good and there are like 3 fun/interesting quests.Otherwise almost all of the quests are very simple fetch quests with little to no substance, having the worst stealth I've played in a game and being incredibly short for its price tag.There is not much to say about the quests, an npc will tell you to go somewhere, mark it on the map and when you come back they either give you scrap or a weapon. Theres 3 quests that require little more than just walking.The stealth boils down to enemies walking in the same circle pattern making an extremely loud sound. If they see you, you have to either run 5 minutes away from the dungeon, lure them to the train to shoot them or simply run past them.They deal 10% of your health bar in a single shot, have to stand still for multiple seconds to shoot and you'll regen your health back faster than they can generally damage you. So after the first dungeon and being stopped in the second one I just ran through all remaining dungeons without any risk.You fight Charles only a couple of times (mostly because the length of the game) and its just firing at him until he leaves, you can keep changing weapons, but that's pretty much how far the strategy goes in this game. The game is also optimized very poorly from what I've heard, personally I was lucky enough not to have run any frame drops, other than opening the map tanking my frames into oblivion each and every time I opened it.It's a shame because I absolutely adore the concept (being the reason I bought this in the first place), having a mobile base that's your only real safe heaven that you have to venture away from to upgrade and manage it. I think the game suffers from having only one big bad since you never have to learn to adapt or do stuff like weapon switching.It's pretty clear some aspects of this game are meant to be satire and the game doesn't take itself seriously, I dont like calling things unfunny, but there wasn't any actual attempts at jokes in the game, everything felt like the dev was trying to be as absurdist as possible.While I don't think the game was meant to be a cash grab, its just barely long enough to be pushed out of steams refund policy, released before giving it enough proper development time for the scope, costing way too much, getting increasingly less and smaller updates and having a plushie announced of charlie almost immediately after the games release.

_childDocuments_.review: Choo Choo Charles isn't a bad game, and while it has its moments and succeeds in pulling off a scary train spider monster, it doesn't succeed at much else.Story-critical missions rely on stealth, and this is the worst stealth system I've played. We're given no tools to sneak, enemies need only glance you to chase you forever, and WHEN you are seen, it's the same thing every time--run back to the train and awkwardly use it to kill the guy that chased you hundreds of meters from a cave. I did this a dozen times, and it really dampened the experience.As for Charles himself, the game does succeed at making him a presence to be feared. The game forces you away from your train enough that when you're warned he's on the prowl nearby, the fear is palpable. The shame here is combat encounters with Charles on the train is 100% solved. One weapon in particular is a remarkably hard counter on him, and it seems like the only price we pay is the chase becomes a slog. There are multiple weapons in the game, but I never felt like my choice in weapon had any real impact--the irony here is I found more uses for these guns on goons than I did Charles, and I don't think that's what this game was shooting for.The exploration in this game is decent. The open world is small with now traditional quest markers telling you where points of interest are, but the game does care enough about a sense of discovery to not point you toward everything and let you use your head to make your way. A short study of the map shows places out of the way that are worth your time to investigate, but this does start to wear off--short of collectible paint cans to reskin your train, the basic loot system of this game very quickly becomes boring. Scrap is your money, and while it's vital, its implementation is very basic. Scrap loses what allure it ever had halfway through this game.Speaking of game time, this is a very short game--I finished it in about three hours. Short games absolutely can live up to their price tag, but I don't think Choo Choo Charles does. $20 is too high a base price for this game, and I'm not sure I feel great about even $15. It doesn't do enough right to justify a short and sweet experience, and I think the short game time ought to be considered more of a mercy than a feature given how flat the game becomes in its latter half.If this game drops to a $10 price tag, this thumb flips. Choo Choo Charles has a good theme, and I just wish there was more meat on this piece to make it more satisying.

_childDocuments_.review: Just played through the game in a single sitting. While I am going to mark this as a recommend, I do think the price should probably be a bit lower (I got it on a sale myself) for what is on offer here. Its less about the length of the game - as personally I don't think the length of a game is a good way to judge value, and more about the fact that the game has quite a few misteps IMO. That said, I did have a fun time overall and would welcome a followup title that explored the world/lore more so still recommending it.I do think the game could be improved in a number of ways though, so going to list them here in no particular order.- The world map lets you place a waypoint but you can't remove it... For a game that focuses so much on crafting atmosphere, its a HUGE oversight (IMO) that you cannot remove the giant on-screen widget showing you where the waypoint is. Just let us remove the waypoint in the map by clicking on a placed waypoint.- Forced stealth sections are fine to me... but I just wish I could crouch. Crouching doesn't even have to do anything mechanically, but not being able to crouch behind cover in a stealth section just feels bad after years of being conditioned to crouch. It would help these sections feel a bit more tense IMO.- Cultists are annoying... the best way I found to deal with them, if I did get caught, was to run around so that they were all chasing me then kite them back to my train and just kill them. Having no way to counter them if they DO spot you, coupled with the fact that they run about the same speed as you and chase you for a VERY long time just makes them feel bad. I like difficult enemies and so on, but it just feels like you have to perfect the stealth everytime the first time, or too bad.- Charles randomly turning up was great the first couple of times... but after that it got a bit annoying. Most of the time he would turn up at incredibly frustrating points - like when I was stealthing through areas with cultists and such. Meaning that my best option was to just run away and hide in a building or let him or the cultists kill me to get it over with. Similarly, the best way to deal with Charles, if you aren't in your train moving, is to just wait until he's there, jump inside a building, and wait him out - which is very boring. Sometimes he would leave after 10-20 seconds, other times it would take minutes. He even glitched into the building and killed me once lol. A few little checks to ensure that he isn't going to turn up at particularly frustrating moments would go a long way IMO. Likewise - the fact that he DIDN'T come attack when did things that were very loud or whatever (like blowing up dynamite or turning on a lighthouse) feels like a missed opportunity to me.- Dying feels like a bit of a missed opportunity for stakes. I only died a handful of times and each time I did I lost single digit amounts of scrap... I had completely upgraded my train in less than 80 minutes of playtime, so losing 1-3 pieces of scrap for dying really didn't matter. In general the game has a bit of an economy problem - its way too easy to get scrap.As I said - I still enjoyed the game. I just feel like the price of entry is a bit high when there are quite a few issues and annoyances hurting the overall experience. I absolutely adore the atmosphere in the game, and the music (while barely playing) was wonderful. Obviously Charles' design is sick as well. Again - I'd LOVE to see the developer revisit the idea and expand on the lore, polish it up, etc. in a future title!

_childDocuments_.review: Truly one of the best experiences in gaming i've ever had even though I hate horror games. (Spoilers Ahead)PROS: 1- Great hype! game was a hype train since day one (get it?), For about a year me and my friend's never stopped talking about it, we were there for the pre-launch stream and made sure to keep updated so it was a really great feeling knowing that what was delivered exceeded our expectations!2- Story, I really didn't think I would write a review for how good of a story choo choo charles has but here I am. The build up was great, having all the NPCs point to warren really made me excited for the end and it payed off really well making a great cut-scene that felt extremely fitting.3- End boss battle, This really and I mean REALLY took me by surprise, such an amazing end for an incredible game, the boss battle was fun and had a few surprises sprinkled in. The gun play in this game fells great! hard hitting and effective. But the final teaser cut-scene at the very end has set up for an amazing sequel!CONS:1- Missions, this does not apply to Required missions OR Weapon missions and they are easy and straight forward. I am talking about some of the side quests, some/most of them being fetch quests (Journal man, Pickle lady, Blue case Bloke) These I found were boring and just there as filler, BUT some of the side quests (The witch, Ghost papers, Parkour man) added something just a bit different, I liked the idea of having a secondary chase mini game that added a bit of action if Charles didn't appear (such as the ghost or swamp monster).2- NPCs, character models with mouths that move in action to the voice, maybe some more complicated dialog or dialog options, more animations just even moving around the room or being able to see them do an action (writing, building, thinking) stuff like that would make it feel more complete (In My Opinion)MIXED: 1- Time, I finished this games main story and all side quests (Except paint collection) in just under 2 and a half hours, I understand that its a one man team working on developing this game so i'm not willing to mark this as a con since that seems unfair, however even just mini games like fishing, tic-tac-toe or other random things would've been nice to see. 2- Price, Being Australian this game set me back around $30 and since I was so hyped I didn't really care how much it cost. But looking back considering I paid 30 dollars I feel like there was still a bit missing (refer to CONS: and MIXED: for reasons) I basically paid 10 dollars per hour and the replay-ability of this game isn't huge because once you've done every mission there is not much to go back and do except find paint and after that even less.TLDR: This delivered on my expectations and I would HIGHLY suggest it! extremely memorable and I cant wait to see what is made next!Final Score - 8.3/10

_childDocuments_.review: I feel really bad about this, as i've played it quite a bit (as you can see), and i respect the game and the developer. it's an indie horror game that ties something different, and has heart. but all things considered, i can't recommend this game.first, i know this may get some flack, but this game is wayy too expensive for the amount of actual (good) content it gives you. i can't imagine buying this game at full price before the nightmare update, i would have been able to refund it with how long it took me to beat normal mode. i'm not normally one to complain about game prices, but this did really feel like a lot for what it gives.the game doesn't look bad at all, at higher settings the atmosphere is pretty good, and charles is a really awesome design. unfortunately, the island is boring as hell. everything kinda looks the same, the character designs are.......... interesting. it kind of feels like it was slapped together with pre-made assets, which i know some were used - not saying this is bad, but it is very dissonant with the rest of the game. This is suuuuuper striking to the player as actually most unique textures are hand-drawn - if this was made more clear with ALL the objects in the game, it could be a really unique style! unfortunately, it falls flat and looks like there's objects with personality shoved into a "nintendo hire this man" looking game. I will say though, if the entire game went with the realistic looking style and just having the goofy no-mouth-moving characters, it would be a lot less charming. the combination of the two is kind of fun to look at, but i feel it could be more unique if it fully leaned into that "hand-drawn texture" style.map design and quests are boring. I'm really sorry, but there's only so much go here -> get thing -> go back i can take. There are some really interesting or funny quests like the pickle one, or the slender one, but most are just kinda lame. the quests don't even involve charles, and we'll get to that later. the cultists are my least favorite enemies in a game i've seen in a long time, they are annoying, uncreative, and have broken ass AI that barely works with the stealth system. by far the worst part of the game.charles, the by far coolest part of the game, is also underwhelming. you only encounter him randomly, and only on chases is he actually interesting. he's only scripted in the intro, and in the ending. it's a really lame usage of a great design. i wish he had more neat and actual skill based interactions instead of "hope he doesn't spawn" and "if he does, wait for him to go away or fight." there needs to be more interaction, more actual you know, gameplay instead of running, waiting, or the same chase scene.speaking of the chase sections where charles is running behind you, they're awesome! it's fun, exciting, and spooky! i wish there was more of that! but like unique versions of that, and not just that same scene recycled. I want this game to more content, but that content needs to be unique. lastly, i'll talk about nightmare mode. I really gave this my best shot, as you can see i've given about 14 hours of attempts into it. it's just not fun. it's not skill based, there is no skill in it. it's really just luck of hoping charles will work with you. along with that, it does the classic videogame "harder mode just enemies faster and stronger!!!!!!" which is super duper lame. the scenery and music is nice, but that doesn't replace the fact that the mode is incredibly poorly designed. It completely not only ruins the chase scenes by making you stall charles out with the flamethrower, but even that won't work 100% of the time for some reason (don't ask me, ask the broken ass AI.) the enemies all kill you in about 2 hits, which is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ridiculous, but wouldn't be that much of a problem if the mode wasn't permadeath. the permadeath makes this mode absolutely insufferable. it's completely luck based, takes ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ forever not only to get through a run but to even get through the intro that you have to replay EVERY time. i understand it's a hard mode that's supposed to make you "rage quit lmaooooooo!" and ♥♥♥♥, i know it's a free update, but it's wasted potential on something that could be an actual, well designed challenge instead of the "turn the sliders all up" challenge we got. and yes, i know, i know, skill issue. you try saying that ♥♥♥♥ when you get a random supersonic charles attack that kills you when on a 50m sprint.that's what i feel this game is really, just an awesome idea with a lot of wasted potential in execution, which makes it middle of the road. this sucks because i really love the idea and the dev. twostar has been one of my favorite indie devs as of late! I think that a Choo-Choo Charles 2 or a spinoff or whatever could be super dope, there's so much you could do with it. I don't recommend that you buy Choo-Choo Charles, but i am really looking forward to what's coming next from this series or twostar.

_childDocuments_.review: I can understand the hype around this game however I will go ahead and say that if you are planning on getting this game definitely wait for a sale, don’t buy it at full price like I did because I don’t think it’s worth the twenty. There are three main issues that I had with this game during my playthrough.1. Charles doesn’t feel like that big of a threat: Throughout my whole playthrough I never felt that worried about Charles because he never showed up that often for me. Even when he did show up he wasn’t that hard to ward off, especially when you upgrade your train a whole bunch and you get better weapons. He doesn’t really cause that much of a threat to you until the final time you fight him.2: Most of the side quests are to easy: A majority of the side quests in the game I feel like are way to easy. Some of them literally just involve you walking ten feet away from the quest giver and pressing a button. There was one side quest that I really liked, but there’s another one that’s really aggravating. ( I won’t go into details due to spoilers. )3: The hostile NPC's are way to annoying: The way the game wants you to handle these guys is by sneaking around them, but there’s no stealth in the game at all. The second the AI sees you they immediately chase after you, and the only way to deal with them is to make them chase all the way back to your train just so you can shoot them. This is made even worse when you go into the mines as it’s a long way back to your train. ( I also had 2 moments where the AI saw me through a wall. )Other then these three things I did enjoy my playthrough, and the ending is definitely worth it. However I feel like these three things really hold the game back. Overall I’d give it a 5, maybe 6 out of 10.( I do recommend this game, but only if it is on sale for 15 dollars or lower. )

I'm hoping that in the future we get a second game that expands on this concept as there are very good elements in this game.Adding a Nightmare mode added to the replay ability of this game. Nightmare mode is no joke, the atmosphere is significantly darker, Charles is incredibly more aggressive, and will hunt you down faster. There is a lot more strategy that goes into this game mode as you almost have to pre-plan your route to a certain degree. A lot of what you do in this game mode is dictated by Charles and one wrong step spells the end of the run. Having one-life makes it that much harder. After getting my ass kicked 3 times right out of the gate by Charles I finally planned my route and BARELY beat Charles in the end.

_childDocuments_.review: Last year I was watching the development videos of the game and now I finally got to play and finished it. I was absolutely eager to try it since I loved the idea that was behind this game.  -Alright even if the game is so enjoyable it's literally too small. Side stories are little to none even tho I completed them all it took me 2h to finish the game. Takes an hour or two to finish it without any pre knowledge and if you know the game you may well finish it less than an hour. .-It's not openworld there are invisible walls all around the island and around the rivers inside mines. Probably devs didn't wanna spend their time to make a swimming animation or something so they just put invisible walls instead.-Side characters' mouth don't open man. Like they ain't even talking it's the figure standing there and using telepathy to tell you what they wanna say. Again devs didn't wanna spend making mouth movements so yea you are stuck with that and they didn't fix it since the release.-The railway points (where you get to change the road by using a lever to go whichever way you wanna go) don't have any animations for rails. I tried it all with all the graphic settings thought it may be about it but it wasn't. There simply isn't anything there. And once we use lever and head out to road there is a point which it checks where the lever is facing and sends us that way but makes us go offroad a little bit which makes the game kinda odd.-Brakes on the train don't have any effects or animations. I was actually expecting some sparks or something but none at all.-Character designs were awful, it didn't fit with the environment or the atmosphere that we were in at all. -I loved the way that we could operate the train so simply. Enjoyed it's mechanics.-When you zoomed on the map you could see the live actions in it like trees shaking, birds going around, lighthouse lighting around itself, people sitting at porches and so on.-The design of the trains were appealing to me.-Weather changes; rains, storms, foggy and the last boss fight one.-Atmosphere of the game(in epic graphics, it isn't as enjoyable as in epic if you have a low built pc(sorry))-Seeing your train's armor change by each level was a great touch which made me wanna check what is new everytime I upgraded it. -Upgrading your train by scavenging and collecting suplies here and there then having a boss fight was fun. It's a small game for it's price and has lot's of quirks but since I used to watch the development videos of this game I enjoyed it a lot. I would suggest you to give it a go and have fun.

_childDocuments_.review: After the Hardcore Mode Update, theres at least some replayability with a challenge now.Such a mode was exactly what i was hoping to find.Yet, theres still so much left and some to be desired.The gameplay itself remains solid although lacking, showing the low budget at every corner (like stealth sections with some cultists i dont feel were necessary to the plot anyway, missing ways to actually deal with them, like hidingspots or distractions (they know where you are, even if you break line of sight and get some distance)).Its still a non-scarry ok-ish proof of concept.Because of the addition of a hardcore mode, it however now gets a partial positive review, under the condition that you grab it at least at 50% off.For about 8-9€ this is a solid experience providing enough. Still not great quality, but fun enough to warrant a price under 10€, for the about 4 hours you get (if you also do all collectibles and explore a bit).The foundation is there, but it seems content light.I was going through the forums to see whether my experience met up with others and it did.It started solid, it had the mood and setting, the story premise felt a bit manufactured and weird, let alone "scarry", but ok.Graphics were going from solid, to placeholder-ish. I could have interpreted that as a stylistic choice in some cases, so no hard feelings about some weird or outright bad textures.Well, to the core problem: The foundation is there, but apparently im already halfway through and it played that way.The game threw tons of scrap for upgrades at me and that felt weird at first.But i assumed i was just upgrading my first train and its first 3 stats (weapon, speed and health), and i will unlock new trains or trainsystems, maybe a wagon or whatever later and need the loads of scrap for that stuff (because maybe the scrap distribution was not just for my starter train, but also meant for later unlocks).But it turns out, the game went for a bit of a rush there.I played 25 minutes and already did like 15 upgrades or more.I had seen Charles only twice at that point.My assumption also sadly didnt turn out true.It will be that one train you control, with these 3 upgrades and only two functions (drive and shoot).No specialities, no new trains with unique abilities, loadouts or designs.Why? I dont know.Not even more modes than the standard story mode it seems.No Hardcore Mode without saves.No survival mode (stay alive with your train as long as you can, constant looting is necessary, locations reset their contents after some time or random loot chests spawn etc.).Another problem i had, was that Charles wasnt at all providing scare or a lot of tension.He should be a deadly, scary murder machine.And i assumed the main protagonist would be the island, as the island is the core setpiece that could make him scary.You know, like driving through a dark underground tunnel, possibly into a dead end (mines) and he could follow you anywhere.Turns out, he cant.I was sitting in a lake, kneedeep into water in the open. A sound indicated hes on the run (why is there a warning anyway), but he somehow had problems reaching me.Same is true for any other structure. Get into a dumb shack, your are save.So the game idea was good.The gameplay while super simple, was fun.Story: CheesyGraphics: Retro or outright bad, but not a focus point. (performance however is a bit bad for how ugly the game looks)Mapdesign: Generic and boring, missing out potential (especially the reuse of textures everywhere by just copy pasting makes it far worse, you literally see that when using the map).Combat: Blant and somehow lacking the use of normal guns. A solid double barrel shotgun and very limited ammo would have been an actually deeper solution to enhance the gameplay.Im not fond of the inclusion of the cultists anyway, they feel like bloat. But the stealth that isnt really stealth makes it even worse.One gun with very limited ammo and you needing to explore interesting places to find some more, while also being able to use the gun on open field to stagger charles away from you, so you can get some distance (basically a last resort when you run to your train and he catches you), would have been a much better idea.Content: Nothing to do, beat after roughly 3 hours top, no additional modes, not enough quests or sidemissions, no unique and different ways to beat Charles or just escape him (i mean, the story premise could change from "kill him" to "dude, just clear the way through that tunnel so we can all escape).Unlocks: Only colours for your train and a few weapons.People ask for coop and that would be cool.But im dead honest, what would you want to do in the game with one person more?Beat it in 50 minutes instead of 3 hours?The game needs a ton more content and replayability.Especially randomized contents (loot drops) and unlocks plus gamemodes that give twists to the games premise.Add mutators on top and we have something going on.Disclaimer:I grabbed the game for about 8€ (bundle discount on top of normal discount). I started a new run (on top of my already existing 1 hour) and got through it in about 3,75 hours, including collecting all paints, exploring the entire island and all locations i could find (even without quests).I then spent about 20 minutes on hardcore mode, before eventually dying.If you dont go for 100% achievements, you can finish the quests and story in about 3 hours.I encountered Charles in my entire playthrough about 5 times, often playing half an hour without even hearing or seeing him.Make of that what you want.
