_childDocuments_.review: This is a pretty solid game, at least the first time around. I've only been through it once, but I am curious about how it will be after a few runs. It's definitely a bit shorter than I thought (this run was around 3 hours), and while I didn't do much research on it before buying it (other than reading the tags and brief parts of the description), it seemed a bit different than what I expected. I was kind of thinking you'd go through and help solve multiple cases, and just keep going that way with increasing difficulty and depth as you continue playing. It's not that. It sort of starts that way, but doesn't stay that way for long. It's VERY linear as far as I can tell, and while I think there are different outcomes based on player inputs, I have yet to try that. It's not the investigation game it's labeled as. It's still well put together and thought out, but I felt a little bit misled, as there is really only one single "case" that you're working on as the player, it just happens to include a few other cases that you work on in the tutorial stages. Without spoiling it, I think it's a good game, though I don't know if I would pay full price for it. I think if you could get it for under $10 USD it would be a much better value, personally. But, we'll see how it goes on the replay-ability of the game and that might change. I'm curious how different actions and responses affect the outcome of the game for sure. Soundtrack really buffed this game a lot too, it was really well timed and well orchestrated. My main complaint is some of the cutscenes are ridiculously long for what their substance is. There is basically no substance to most of them, it's just some sound effects and maybe the occasional spot of dialogue.As someone else said in their review, it scratched an itch I didn't know I had, but I would've been much more excited to see some real investigating. Like phasmophobia, but you're the computer geek at this government intelligence agency. If you play through the first hour or so, you'll see sort of what I mean by that.

_childDocuments_.review: The Operator is a very short (3 to 4 hours at best) interactive visual novel with good production value. The interface looks clean and easy to use, the voice acting is good, and the interactive elements are pretty decent. For a visual novel. It is presented, however, as a game of deduction and puzzle solving. The puzzles and deductions are shallow with too much handholding. As you progress new mechanics are introduced, and then discarded immediately after. This gives the mistaken impression that much more content is waiting for you and puzzles will get more difficult. And then the game is over.The story is equally shallow. The opening scene reveals too much, making the big reveal at the end something you can piece together within a few minutes of playing the game. The ending is a cliffhanger of sorts, but it makes this game feel like the opening chapter of a larger story that has not been written. Worse is that none of the conspiracy is ever explained, leaving you with many questions that are unlikely to be answered. There are no divergent paths, only one ending, and zero replay value.If you go into this game expecting a visual novel, you will have an entertaining few hours with an okay story and underwhelming finale. If you go into this game expecting deduction, investigation, and puzzle solving, you will find only disappointment. This ultimately leads to my negative review. For a visual novel it is too short with an unresolved story, and for an investigation game the puzzles are too simple. The Operator has a lot of unmet potential, which is a shame.

_childDocuments_.review: (This review contains information that might be considered spoilers for some, so read with caution!)TL; DR:It holds your hand throughout the game. The investigative puzzles are immersive, but simple and provides very little challenge. It's short, but you might possible still like it for it's presentation and story. If there was a "lukewarm" rating, I would pick that. But since it's clearly a labor of love, I'm inclined to rate positively.The longer review:When I heard of The Operator a few days before launch, I was hoping for something to scratch that Obra Dinn / Curse of the Golden Idol itch. Not very many games manage to make you feel like a proper investigator or makes you feel super clever when you progress, and those two games are the gold standard.The Operator - unfortunately - is not that game.The immersion is great. You definitely feel like an operator, scanning photos for details that you then input into various databases to yield result. The interface is exactly how you'd imagine a 90's 'hacker' terminal to look like, complete with a terminal and an official looking 'FBI' interface. The majority of the game is fully voiced with competent actors (for the budget).Although a very polished and - for its medium - a cinematic experience, gameplay-wise it falls into many of the same pitfalls as other "investigative" games like it. The puzzles are - for the most part, but with notable exceptions - simple, requiring few steps to solve. Your hand is woefully held through each of them and the freedom to make your own deductions are sorely lacking. For the most part the tools required to solve a certain puzzle will appear when needed, and disappear when not needed anymore.The story is decent and very on-par for such a game. It doesn't fully manage to suck you into the world, however. For one, the main plot felt rushed. You're a new operator working cases, and the very first case you receive is a part of a brewing conspiracy. Every case following that is connected in some way. In my opinion, the game doesn't take it's time to build up the world or the characters before placing you front and center into the main plot thread. Some of the major plot twists are extremely predictable, and some of what is presented as a major plot development honestly really isn't. We don't know the involved characters enough to care when the revelation is given to us.The game also makes the cardinal sin of ending abruptly with no real resolution, most questions left unanswered and a feeling that your actions throughout the game had little impact.A lot of this comes down to personal tastes, hopes and expectations, however. Chances are you'll like this game for it's good presentation and decent enough puzzles. It's not particularly expensive (though maybe a bit pricey for the estimated game time).

_childDocuments_.review: I have to say I was absolutely hooked with the concept of  One watch of the trailer will tell you why; an operator helping with government investigations, analyzing clues, basically being the man-in-the-chair? It's all awesome! But what killed the mood for me was the cliche writing, amateur voice acting, and the simplistic puzzles. First of all the writing. Who TALKS like this?! Every person you meet is quippy, chippy, or clever with their line delivery. These don't sound like professional field agents, they sound like cartoon characters. A man has been killed, TAKE THIS SERIOUSLY! They should be more realistic, a bit grittier, more direct. And why am I doing everything? What exactly is your job here??Next are the puzzles. They are already simple enough, but I feel babied and talked down to by the characters we meet. The game would make itself so much more compelling if there were harder applications! Something I had to grill through to find what my agent needed. So far, I can click two buttons and get the answer to the riddle. I don't  like a secret agent, which is what I bought the game for. And not to mention the game's animations for security footage, which are taken so seriously for how poor in quality they are. The tone simply doesn't match. Finally, I had a sincerely hard time caring about the story of the game. The plot was mildly interesting, conspiracies and hackers and whatnot, but it didn't land. Mainly because it meant wading through monologues from the characters, which drove me insane. If the game was harder, there would be much more to invest in. I would feel accomplished! But after completing the first two days, I feel like there was no other option but to succeed. There was never any risk of me failing, which made it hard for me to connect to the game at all. In the end it was not the experience I was expecting, and if you're looking to be a tech-savvy sleuth, look elsewhere.

_childDocuments_.review: It's worth playing as it isn't very long. The gameplay concept and execution are really good. The voice acting is pretty decent and makes the visual novel style content engaging to consume in addition to the gameplay mechanics. They have some pretty good tricks to flesh out the experience and make it feel more "real" while still managing to keeping the game very lo-fi...I think it had a lot more potential than it tapped into. A very common criticism will be linearity and lack of player choice or replayability. There are a few moments where you can alter the outcome of an event that feels like it should have a more meaningful impact on the story, but the impact on the overall narrative is actually very little.  I also feel they were very close to allowing you to play the detective by doing your own extracurricular investigating, but then they sort of throw that out by having a character just be like "I bet you didn't notice THIS!" It's like... actually I did notice it and I wanted to have my moment of feeling like a genius. I think this is something that the Ace Attorney games do a little better.... while still railroading you into a very specific solution and solution path, they at least make you feel like you figured things out and make it feel rewarding. I think this game could have done at least more of that if not going as far as to actually add in more optional discovery and unprompted use of the information you gathered.I'll also say that while this is a pretty good standalone narrative game concept, it feels like something I'd like to see integrated into a bigger game that doesn't play exclusively like this.

_childDocuments_.review: I would prefer to give this game a 5/10, but unfortunately, that's not possible on Steam, so I’m rating it negatively for interested buyers to see.I bought the game to unravel mysteries as an FBI operative—a game I could play for several hours. The gameplay mechanics are exactly what I was hoping for, but unfortunately, some of them are only used once throughout the entire game.The story is extremely short, with a plot that becomes obvious within the first 40 minutes of gameplay. Seriously, 2 hours of gameplay for 14€? Not to meantion an "Original Soundtrack" for another 10€. If players could skip some dialogues and cutscenes, the game would only last 30 minutes. The story feels more like a detective TV show where everything is "weird," "doesn't make sense," and "everything is interconnected."In summary:+ The game mechanics are awesome! - Unfortunately, their potential is wasted on a simplistic story with a soap-opera-like plot seen more than thousands of times on TV.+ The soundtrack (not bought), sound effects, and voice acting are excellent.- The story is simple and feels rather sloppy (95% of the ideas went into coding and mechanics, 5% into the story). Perhaps it's due to the potential for a speedrunning community?- When I calculate the "price per hour" of the main story, this game is undoubtedly the worst in my entire game library (7€ per hour (almost 12€ if you buy the "original soundtrack"), including cutscenes and dialogues).- The game has unskippable cutscenes (returning home), dialogues (the tutorial), and end credits, likely so that you can’t get a refund within the 2-hour Steam policy.? If the sequel to this game will also be only 2 hours long, the developers might as well not even bother. It’s not worth the money.If the game was a bit longer (at least 4 hours of a decent story), I would recommend it, but unfortunately, I can't.Definitely buy it during a sale, just not now.

There is only one case that you work, and for all the manuals you only tend to use it for whatever task once or twice. Now, even though it isn't like it described it was a great story game. Some of the twists were predictable and others were not. It is a short game, and there isn't a replayability factor to it but the tasks were fun to complete, and the story was nice to follow. I do recommend it, but try to go into it without looking anything up.
_childDocuments_.name: The Operator

_childDocuments_.review: Fun and interesting, The Operator brings the vibes of conspiracy and mystery that is very much along the lines of X-Files. The puzzles are interesting and varied, and all hook together into the narrative. Its not a long game by any means, but the price reflects it. I'd recommend this for any fans of detective style games.
_childDocuments_.name: The Operator

_childDocuments_.review: A very interesting idea. I picked this up after having played the Home Safety Hotline game. I feel this genre of Computer Screen based narrative is an up and coming format for storytelling that has a lot of potential. In the case of The Operator, we see a well thought out concept of an intelligence bureau, agents who need help in the field and yourself as the operator tasked with helping them correlate information remotely. Quickly the game establishes the breadcrumbs of an overarching mystery that slowly unravels over the course of your investigation.I found the narrative to be quite gripping from the start and the gameplay to be endearing, the use of the computer screen and phone conversations feels very personal and the side characters you encounter are given enough personality to be endearing as you assist their investigations.I'd say if this is your type of game then it is 100% worth a go. And for such a reasonable price I'd say give it a chance if you are on the fence.I will be eagerly awaiting any possible follow up to this story and world.

_childDocuments_.review: Very short game, so bad time per value. The gameplay involved had very simple and unengaging puzzles (but the bomb defusal was fun). The story was rudimentary and uninspired as the level of detail in which the clues are presented to the player is astounding with a lack of fundamental complexity present in even the most simple of detective novel, this disastrous combination results in the player being able to piece together the gist of the story within the first ten minutes of the game if they have an IQ above room temperature. Overall, Meh.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good game, and I enjoyed it. It's clear it was made with love, but unfortunately, it's very linear for me. The game practically holds your hand through the story, leaving you no room to make your own choices. You're forced to do things you might not want to do. For example, at the beginning, I tried to resist and wanted to shout, "Catch Hal!" I even tried making unauthorized ip-calls to my superiors to report Hal via the terminal, but the game didn't allow such actions. This is a big downside for me. I want to make my own decisions rather than choosing from a set of predetermined responses. The game doesn't even offer the illusion of choice.I won't lie – I had to look up a walkthrough on Google to solve the bomb puzzle, and I hate puzzles. _childDocuments_.name: The Operator

_childDocuments_.review: If you are looking for a good puzzle/detective guy in the chair game to scratch that itch made by an indie developer to entertain you for 3 hours with great gameplay, great puzzles that don't hold your hand and are satisfying to solve, great voice acting, introducing a couple of interesting game mechanics beyond "click face and search for name here" and a pretty good linear story, then this is the game for you. I bought it at 10% off and really enjoyed it, will definitely be on the look out for the next game this developer makes, and would recommend it to anyone with the expectation that its a good indie game.  If you are looking for a deep, multi ending detective game where choices matter and there's endless replayability, this is not the game for you. I think the two critiques I see the most of is that fact the game is short and doesn't have multiple endings. For the length side, I think complaining that a game isn't long enough is a pretty good complaint to have. The game isn't perfect, but its entertaining and I hope the developer makes a longer game in the future using the success from this game to better utilize some of the interesting game mechanics that get introduced but then not used again (there's a few). Whether it's worth the price is subjective. The developer gave the reasoning that it's about the length of a movie, around the price of similar games, and so that's why it's at the price that it is. I don't know how much that justifies the price for this game, which I feel is a few dollars more expensive than similar games, but since I liked the demo, the movie comparison seemed reasonable enough for me (at least given some reason instead of no reason at all) and I wanted to support the developer, so I went for it when it first released. Overall, I am very satisfied with the game, had a good time, and would buy it again. Not having multiple endings doesn't bother me much. If the "choices" are scattered throughout the game, I'm not replaying, solving puzzles I already know the answers too, just to change a couple of dialogue options. The same thing for if the choice is at the end and there's no individual save feature for me to go back to. I think it's fair to expect an indie developer to just make a game that's fun to play once. There's dialogue options that don't really matter, but I found the characters you interact with the most really endearing and felt connected very quickly.
_childDocuments_.name: The Operator

_childDocuments_.review: The game is fine, but I wouldn't recommend it. The twist is fairly obvious due to environmental effects. None of the puzzles are particularly difficult. _childDocuments_.name: The Operator

_childDocuments_.review: "The Operator" is an incredibly enjoyable experience that draws you deep into the world of digital investigation and conspiracy. As an operator for the FDI, I found myself thoroughly engrossed in solving complex cases, and the game kept me on the edge of my seat from start to finish.Pros:Engaging Mechanics: The investigative tools are a highlight of the game. Analyzing evidence, digging through databases, and assisting field agents in real-time was so satisfying that I often wished I had more time to use these tools.Gripping Narrative: Each case is a well-crafted story with twists and turns that kept me hooked. Although I figured out the major twist halfway through, it was set up nicely and added to the overall tension rather than detracting from it.Atmospheric Tension: The game excels at creating a sense of paranoia and urgency. The mysterious presence of the cyber criminal HAL and the cryptic messages to "trust no one" added layers of psychological depth that kept me fully engaged. There's one part of the game that had me sweating buckets because it was so tense, but I won’t spoil anything—just be prepared!Cons:Not Enough Time with the Tools: My only real gripe is that the game could have given us more opportunities to dive deeper into the mechanics. The tools are so well-designed that I wanted to spend even more time exploring their capabilities.A Bit Short: The game is on the shorter side, but considering it was developed by a very small team (possibly just one or two people), what they’ve created is nothing short of incredible. I sincerely hope to see more from them in the future.Anyone who appreciates immersive narratives and detective games should definitely play this one. The game provides an exciting experience with tough puzzles and a gripping narrative that will keep you wondering. Although some may find the twist predictable, it's skillfully done and doesn't take away from the overall experience. Even with its length, it's an amazing accomplishment for such a small team, and I can't wait to see what they come up with next.
_childDocuments_.name: The Operator

_childDocuments_.review: The Operator is a great narrative game which brings back all the feelings of the X-Files and Millenium as you play as a Federal agent or operator helping Agents in the field examine evidence and uncover a mystery (I dont want to say too much but the intro really puts you in mind of the X-Files from the get go!) A lovely, entertaining, puzzling and at times blood racing game! Totally worth it and I loved it! The  section was particularly awesome! Love it!I received a key for the game although I already had it in my wishlist and was intending to buy it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Operator

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished playing through this game and rushed straight over here to write my review.Hands down, this is one of the BEST Terminal-centric games that I've played in recent memory.  If you're looking for an experience filled with mystery, suspense, and unexpected twists (plot-wise and gameplay-wise) then this is the game for you!There's one specific section of the game that literally had my jaw dropping at what I was being tasked with, and I know it'll be a memory that sticks with me whenever I think about this game.I'm so glad that I tried out the demo for this game.  If you enjoyed it too, then pick the game up right now because it has  much more up its sleeves.Absolutely recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: The Operator

_childDocuments_.review: Despite this game being 4 hours long and with a rather depressing ending, I still enjoyed it a lotThe story feels very much inspired by X-Files, while the gameplay, it seems, took inspiration from the game Orwell. All the logical puzzles were straightforward and I never even needed to click the "?" button. There was one very stressful moment, but since I resolved the situation it was a good kind of stress. The music changes in dramatic moments were perfect. Most of the plot elements were actually rather predictable, but there were definitely some pleasant surprises.
_childDocuments_.name: The Operator

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very fun investigative game. A bit short, I completed it in just under 7 hours, but it has good plot and keeps your attention the entire time. There were several times when I told myself I needed to take a break, but I just couldn't pull myself away. I enjoyed pulling apart the mysteries and using the various tools at your disposal the solve the conspiracy. I wish there more cases to solve, but it's a small team that worked on the game, so it's understandable. The audio does a pretty great job of keeping you on the edge of your seat and aware of what's going on as well. Well worth the price tag, and I would absolutely play another title from the devs!
_childDocuments_.name: The Operator

_childDocuments_.review: This game scratched an itch that I sorta didn't know I had. Made me feel like an actual secret service agent from the comfort of my own home. It also surprised me with some of the story. At one point I gasped so loud, people came to check I was ok. I appreciate that there was choice in the conversations and it was reasonably forgiving if you made a "oopsie". My one wish is that it was a tad bit longer... but I'm going to hold out hope for a DLC. Honestly, I'm super pleased with the game and if you like puzzles/mysteries this will definitely bring you some joy! I'll be going back to get those last 3 achievements...
_childDocuments_.name: The Operator

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR:"The Operator" is a captivating detective and story game with meticulous attention to detail, featuring thoughtful mechanics, excellent voice acting, and an atmospheric soundtrack. It's a unique and immersive experience perfect for fans of detective stories and puzzles, well worth the full price.###"The Operator" offers a captivating and immersive gameplay experience, masterfully capturing a mysterious atmosphere. It skillfully combines elements of detective and story games, impressing with its attention to detail. The developers' meticulous care is evident in every aspect, resulting in a seamless and highly enjoyable gaming experience. Thoughtful game mechanics, a user-friendly interface, top-notch voice acting, and a moody soundtrack draw players deep into the gripping narrative.The storyline is intriguing, though not particularly long. Hopefully, future expansions or DLCs will conclude the story, as it currently feels like a cliffhanger, especially if you watch the credits until the end. ;)The reactive music significantly enhances the game's atmosphere, contributing to the immersive experience.For fans of detective stories, puzzles, and theories, "The Operator" is a true gem. You take on the role of an FDI operator, assisting field agents in solving cases.Along the way, you uncover peculiarities that add an extra layer of excitement."The Operator" feels unique and fresh, supported by its step-by-step storytelling approach. Overall, "The Operator" is definitely worth the full price and is highly recommended for anyone seeking a well-thought-out and gripping game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Operator

_childDocuments_.review: Reading the review, a common complaint I see is directed at the length of the experience. Don't let that dissuade you, it's a gripping, one-of-a-kind experience that had me glued throughout the whole experience!The presentation is superb, with great voice acting, tense music and fantastic art direction. The story is tight, and admittedly, it left me wanting more. But I see that as an indication of how incredibly much I enjoyed the experience!It almost feels like an Annapurna-release in how tight and refreshing it all felt and played.Obvious "thumbs up" from me.

_childDocuments_.review: An extremely solid game with fantastic voice acting, music, atmosphere, and cinematics. I'm particularly partial to the camera feeds which mask lower fidelity models (and occasionally wonky animation if you really look for it) through camera filters that made me guess multiple times if I was viewing real footage until I caught on to the trickery.It has a controversial ending, especially due to the short length of the game. Personally I respected it, but it would've landed much better if there were more things to do. It lacks a lot of the exploration that you can do in a similar title, Hypnospace Outlaw. The game is broadly very linear, with a few choices and decisions that change things up, but you can't uncover hidden optional content like in HSO. The execution of being an operator ends up playing closer to Phoenix Wright (story over mechanics) than HSO. I very particularly remember feeling disappointed when I assumed control of  and was hoping I could at least play a day (if not campaign) of that. Also the  mechanic was pretty fun. If they made it a side mode (non voiced of course, it only has one correct answer as of now) I'd probably play that for a good bit.That said, I quite enjoyed it, and it's pretty unique. I hope they build upon this solid base in a future title, there's real potential for something I'd really fall in love with. Unfortunately, they delisted the demo (cringe) but if you liked the demo, it's like 20% of the game but you'd definitely like the game. If you're skeptical or broke, probably better to wait for a sale for ~$10.
_childDocuments_.name: The Operator

_childDocuments_.review: I have real mixed feelings about this one, but in the end, I came away feeling disappointed so I'm giving this one a thumbs down. There just isn't enough here. The game needs more build up, more time spent getting to know the main character and his friends and coworkers while doing "normal" cases before being dropped into investigating the big conspiracy that the game centers around.When certain twists and betrayals happen in the storyline, they didn't really land for me because I didn't really care much about the characters.Additionally, in terms of puzzles, they are all fairly straight forward and don't really make much use of the tools the game introduces. Aside from the tool you use to look up people, most of the programs and documents introduced in the game are used a single time.Also, to make one particular nitpick, I didn't appreciate it when a character in the game insulted my intelligence because they told me to type a command into a "chat window" and i entered it into the text chat i was having with that character instead of into the PHONE CALL window I was having with another character.
_childDocuments_.name: The Operator

_childDocuments_.review: It's short. It's easy. Half of the game is a tutorial. It didn't really feel like I was investigating anything. The things you can examine are very limited. And you're basically told what is going on, instead of being allowed to figure things out by yourself. It's very lineair and at all times I felt I was just being pushed into a very narrow direction. The ending was really disappointing too. I did like the story, until the ending.. I'm not going to spoil it, but this game feels like it should have been a casefile to investigate in a different game. It felt like three rooms of information from a Deus Ex game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Operator

_childDocuments_.review: Very positive experience. Yes, it's a very "on the rails" linear story line. However, it allows you imagination to run wild and feel like you are in a movie a bit. I really dug the puzzles. If you spent some time with the files and mechanics, you might discover some things before they are part of the story, but that's okay, it makes you feel really smart! Would it be cool if there were some branching story lines with different endings or character development as you choose different dialogue choices? Sure. But it doesn't take away from the overall experience. And I think it was really fun. It was reminding me a little of "Majestic" from the early 00s. Does anyone remember that game/experience? Overall, if you did linear story-telling, feeling like a boss detective, this is a fun 5-hour game. I definitely had some nail-biting moments in it. Great job, devs! Look forward to more!
_childDocuments_.name: The Operator

_childDocuments_.review: fun game, but definitely too short. and some plot-bumps if not plot-holes.you are given lots of decisions to make, but upon replaying, none of them matter. on my second playthrough i immediately reached a dialogue option where i say "no", and then the person im talking to says "ok but say yes", and then im no longer able to say no. the story they tell throughout isnt bad, and i really enjoyed the few puzzles there are to solve. but there is no replay-ability. would have been nice to at least have the option to play the goodie-two-shoes who tattles constantly and maybe get one new puzzle and a different ending.the people criticizing the ending we got are kind of right. its not that i mind the outcome of the story, its that the way that outcome is reached isnt very believable. spoilers ahead because its impossible to discuss without spoiling. ///one guy, maybe two if you count the director, somehow manage to k*ll two armed FDI agents, and the main character, and escape without any consequence, inside the FDI headquarters which we know to be decently secure, as we have just spent an entire mission infiltrating it. as well as cover it all up, and catch and frame an FDI agent who had been hiding in the server room we just infiltrated, despite them having had no way of knowing she was in there or involved as far as i could tell. /////end of spoilersi think the asking price is close to fair. ten dollars would probably have been better, but its not way off. im still recommending the game because despite my criticisms, it was fun and i think people should play it.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is unique and one of the most interesting experiences I had with a PC Game for a long time. This is NOT a simulation game, it is more of a point and click adventure game in front of a console. And it does that great, the storytelling is top notch and if you liked the old X-Files TV Show you know the general feel of everything. Still it is SHORT, VERY SHORT! I completed it through 3 or 4 sittings, just when you think now its picking up and here is a huge plottwist... Poof Credits roll. I hope there will be more but I also hope this time it will be longer, 5 or so Episodes like the classic Telltale games would have been a sweet spot for this. Nonetheless its original enough to recommend if you like narrated experiences. Just do not expect a simulation game.

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely good, the content in it is of high quality, it is well acted and well written-even if archetypal, the different techniques are entertaining. _childDocuments_.review: I don't write many reviews and this one is more of a warning in some ways. This is much more of a click along adventure with a couple of mini games. I haven't replayed the game to see if the solutions to the mini games are random or fixed. But i purchased the game after playing the demo and that definitely felt like the game would involve much more gameplay and hard work, perhaps some red herrings and a chance to fail.It is hard to give a proper review of the game without ruining it for people, but it is very short. The slow delivery of text communications or waiting on videos to play pads it out considerably at times and it does feel deliberate to lengthen the game especially at times when there is tension and i personally felt i would be doing things much faster if i had been allowed.Now don't take that the wrong way, i suspect most people who complain it is short were wanting more. Even if you work out the twists before they come it is worth getting to the end, though it does feel a bit disappointing when you already worked out the big reveals early on. And yes if you look carefully you will at least suspect very early in the game what some outcomes will be. Over all the game concept and execution is good, i would have preferred more puzzles or having to dig a bit more for solutions to problems, you are given tools you use exactly once and then never have to use again. It feels set up for a sequel and i hope that they do make one with a longer story.If you are looking for a click along movie and enjoy that type of game then it may be worth full price to you.If you are looking for a complex puzzle game where you are the one solving things wait till it is on sale but still get it.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall enjoyable. Decent interface and storyline, good variety of puzzle mechanics, low to medium difficulty and complexity.I'm usually not a fan of dialogue choices and multiple endings, so I didn't know how to feel when I found out this game  have alternative endings.  Like another user put it, it really felt like I had reached the "bad ending", and that I was supposed to make different choices.  But playing through a second time did not change the outcomes aside from slightly different dialogue, and seeing one or two subtle hints I had missed the first time around.And the developer has confirmed that it's not intended to be replayable (see the dev's )The interface is quite well done, with a variety of technical mechanics.  The in-game documents and user manuals are quite impressively believable in style, while staying relevant to the gameplay, and to the storyline.  I quite enjoyed the  style puzzle.I was a little disappointed that the terminal was so limited, but given this is a relatively small game, that's understandable.At times, especially at the start, it felt like a bit of information overwhelm moving too quickly, but it generally seems to be quite forgiving (though I haven't tested what happens if you don't answer a call, or fail to ).Often it felt a bit too heavy on the handholding.  .  Most of the big reveals were heavily hinted at early on so I knew long before the characters themselves knew.  There were a couple that surprised me though.The voice acting was quite good.  As was the sound design, and animations.  There's quite a few unskippable animations but they're generally done quite well and relevant to the storyline or puzzles.Overall decent little game.  First playthrough took me just about under ~6hrs at a meandering pace (and not keeping track of breaks).  Would play a sequel if it's ever made.

_childDocuments_.review: "Wow just WOW!" were my first words when I finished this game. Like its simple but super effective until the very very end of the game but that's just my lil nitpick and the game is short. _childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for an engaging narrative that you can follow along with interactive elements, I highly recommend The Operator. I felt genuine emotion throughout my gameplay, which is always a hallmark of a successful story. However, I struggle to define The Operator as an actual GAME, given its extreme linearity. It's a series of puzzles (none of which are all that difficult) which separate story scenes when you get down to it, even though it's pretty good at distracting you from that fact. I also feel the need to say, in the least spoiler-y way possible, that this is not at all a lighthearted feel-good game. That's fairly obvious from the marketing, but it REALLY goes out of its way to be as bleak and depressing as possible sometimes, which may or may not be what you're looking for.

_childDocuments_.review: The premise is fantastic and absolutely soaked in old X-Files vibes. _childDocuments_.review: I'm giving this game a 'recommended' because my overall feelings are more positive than negative, but I definitely feel like the price doesn't match the value. The few puzzles aren't very challenging, and you spend as much time reading manuals for them as doing them because you generally do each type once without getting to test your skills further. The conversations are very casual and not nearly carefully worded enough for cloak and dagger operations, which feels out of place for the severity of the events. Everybody constantly name drops each other, though I'm sure this is so you can research characters in the database as a curious player.As for the plot itself, it foreshadows and delivers, using linear conversations with dialog choices that affect nothing, and while I found most of it predictable, I still enjoyed the ride. This is because while I've listed so many negatives just now, The interfaces, animations, and voice acting all contribute to a fantastic game-feel that kept me enjoying my time. The experience of playing this game was precisely what I wanted from it,  Making me walk away from a game that objectively failed to meet most of my expectations with such a positive outlook for future releases is an impressive trick.I wish this game delivered on the day to day cases your department is supposed to handle, the way the store page pitches it. What we got is this wild thriller-movie theme park ride that revolves around a case that destroys the status quo before we even got to be a part of it. I'm invested though! Bring me more of this world, before and after the events of this game.

_childDocuments_.review: The Operator is one of the games that show the limitations of Steam's "Yes/No" model for review. It's a good game, it's solid, but it's got its limitations that you need to understand before you buy.To put it briefly: The Operator is the videogame equivalent of a good B-movie thriller. As a puzzle game and narrative experience it "does the job". You will get about four hours worth of puzzles that are just difficult enough to make you feel smart, but nothing that is designed to resist you too long either. You'll get a scenario that follows the codes of the conspiracy thriller, but is strongly linear and doesn't do anything you haven't seen at least a few times before...There are puzzle games out there that will make you forever regret that you aren't able to experience them for the first time once more. Obra Dinn, There is No Game, Chants of Sennaar...The Operator is not one of those. It hits all the right notes, but the performance isn't inspiring.If you like the genre of puzzle and thriller, then by all means go for it. It is a good, solid game for those gamers whose expectations are appropriately set. But if you haven't played puzzle games for a while and are looking for an amazing, unforgettable experience? Try the others first and come back here when you're hooked to the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a tough one for me to review. On the one hand, this is a very cool concept, and I think it’s executed very well. On the other, it feels very much like a proof of concept for a bigger game. I don’t want to get into spoilers, but I will say that I would’ve liked a few more “normal” cases to solve before jumping into the government conspiracy aspect. I feel like it would’ve made some of the later reveals stand out more. As it stands, you start the game immediately suspecting something is fishy. Your very first case kicks off the game-long mystery. Also, I feel like some of the reveals were done more for the immediate shock value than they were for actual plot reasons. As in, you uncover a number of secrets that feel like they don’t actually go anywhere, beyond the initial stomach-dropping “oh ♥♥♥♥” moment. I would love to see this expanded upon in a sequel, which is why I’m ultimately recommending this game. The fact that my biggest complaint is that “I wanted more” should ultimately speak to the quality of the experience. Like I said, it’s got good bones. I just wish it had been fleshed out more.

_childDocuments_.review: "The Operator" is a good game, except it isn't actually a game... It is more of an interactive film, where your choice doesn't actually matter, for example, despite several attempts to play for the agency, I couldn't do so, you always have to side with some renegade hacker("HAL"). The game just locks in dialogue options, so you can only comply to progress further in the game. When she reveals her identity, you can't report her, which proves how choice doesn't matter in this game, even the dialogue options aren't that much of a choice, as the respondents largely react similarly. Also, many actions in it don't have consequences, like you can mess up all the tasks hundreds of times, and the game just tells you you are wrong, not the characters, the game, like, you can (in some cases) just blindly click the screen and eventually you will get it right. Or with how you can mess up the bomb diffusal and subsequently kill a federal agent, with no consequences. Generally, the game is well made, and I have not found any bugs, but the crippling lack of player agency, and no consequences for wrong choices just make the game unplayable, and I would, therefore, not recommend it to other people, as a game at least. As I said, this isn't a game it is an interactive activity, that uses the mechanics of a game.

_childDocuments_.review: My recommendation is heavily conditional. If you are into conspiracies and point-and-click games with simple puzzle elements, I would recommend this at around $10. If you don't fall into those categories, then you aren't the target demographic and I can't recommend it. Overall Operator is not a bad game - in fact, I would really like to see more content for this, or perhaps even more games like it - but it's held back by a few flaws.First, The Good:Next, The Bad:I did enjoy my time with Operator; if you're like me, and enjoy the thought of playing detective and uncovering government conspiracies, you probably will too. Ultimately I think this is a decent game with a solid concept behind it, but the problems I listed above hold me back from recommending this unconditionally. In particular, I feel that Operator is slightly overpriced when measured against the amount of gameplay time you're likely to get out of it. This seems to be the developer's first game, so I'm hoping that they take the lessons learned from Operator and continue to improve on this formula.

_childDocuments_.review: First and foremost, I really enjoyed the characters, dialogue, puzzles, and story. I saw many comments saying that the twist was unexpected and, after having played the game myself, I'm going to have to agree that I ALSO did not see that coming! I feel it is worth mentioning that, one of the more unforgiving elements of this game is that you are unable to save and restart at the beginning of a chapter/day. Therefore, if you miss an achievement, you have to start the game all over again. This brings me to the next unforgiving aspect of this game which is that no dialogue or cut scene is skippable or able to be fast-forwarded (e.g. clicking to make dialogue scroll faster). Despite the fact that these elements made the game a little more frustrating, I welcome the challenge. It doesn't take away from my positive review nor my recommendation for others to check this game out. If anything, it makes the achievements feel earned. Additionally, the game is not very long. So, a few restarts shouldn't lock the player into an unrelenting commitment of innumerable hours. I put just 6.5 hours into the game and, to put my point into perspective, I restarted the game twice -- to get all 13 achievements.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a shame this game is so short because I really liked what it did offer. The voice acting was superb, the soundtrack was a mix of nice ambient music and great tense tracks for specific moments, the suspense, mystery and narrative all kept me hooked, and I was really looking forward to how things would play out. Gameplay wise you basically do some light detective puzzling work, mostly just advance dialogue but it was still intriguing enough for me. But just when I thought there was going to be this big shift in the game and things would really get ratcheted up to 11...the game just ends. I thought I got a bad ending and that I'd have to replay the game to see more, but looking at the achievements that is just the ending of the game. If this were an experience that lasted even a few more hours it'd be an easy recommend, but with how abruptly the game ends I wish Steam had a Mixed or Neutral option. I'll still leave the game a positive review as I think it did more right than wrong but just be aware that this is a *very* short game that unfortunately doesn't quite stick the landing at the end.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is short around 3-4 hours, but it's very memorable. Reminds me of Orwell (the first one, which was just amazing).The interface is retro and stilted, but you can tell that it's a design choice by the author. Behind the retro graphics of what is essentially a conspiratorial work simulator, the game stands out as a very polished experience. I have experienced no bugs. Once I knew the basic game mechanics, I didn't feel cheated in anyway by the game. If I made a mistake during gameplay, it was because I was distracted, not because the game didn't provide enough clues.The polish of the game also stands out with the brilliant sound design. The music is spot-on with some Tool-like guitars like the song Rosetta Stoned blended with futuristic suspense tunes.Moreover, the game has its audio cues timed to the millisecond; they don't feel like jump scares but like actual sound design choices. The audio cues ALWAYS enhance the experience in this game, which was fascinating to experience.The twists can be bland, but you still end up wanting to know more about the story. The first thing I did after finishing the game was checking out if a sequel is planned.PS: I am a scientist by education and I was thrilled to see that the developer researched science and some real-life conspiracy history in surprising depth.

_childDocuments_.review: *spoiler free*A very enjoyable detective thriller that's spent mostly looking at the same computer screen, tastefully emulating a simple, proprietary FBI desktop you'd see in the background of 90s movies. Even so, the gameplay is varied, as you gain access to more and more tools and programs to use in your cases, and the tasks or cases themselves vary a lot. One particular case that involves a manual was one of the most memorable gaming experiences I've had recently. It was very tense and had me fully immersed in my current task. You'll know it when you get to it.Speaking of immersion, you occasionally get breaks from the screen (as you should in real life as well) as your character steps away to end the day and get home, or walk to a nearby destination. These intermissions are very well done and put you in the character's shoes, not to mention let the both of you unwind before the next day of cracking cases.The mystery is engaging and gives you just enough clues at just the right pace to let you put the puzzle pieces together yourself. Don't take this as a negative, this is the game rewarding you for paying attention, using your notepad and attempting to connect the dots yourself.For the price of one movie ticket and a box of popcorn you'll get much more than the average flick and support a great developer. I hope to see more in the future.Editing because I forgot to mention:The soundtrack and audio work is FANTASTIC, listening to it now.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has an interesting premise and it has been made well. The graphics are good and the audio is top notch in my books.But unfortunately it's... hmm, how should I say it... easy? Or not even that, hand-heldy! Like, it doesn't really let you do much anything of worth outside of one high stakes scene that is timed. But that it not what 99% of the game is.It's kinda like this game is backwards from what you would expect from a logic puzzle game. It's the Agents or other people that call you aka the NPC's aka the game itself that do most of the detective work. And you, the player, are the computer whose job is to do the tedious work of checking. You get one single question to answer from the field agent and the answer is never that hard to find. In fact it's almost never necessary to collect and compile information as an active researcher and there's basically no need to take notes. Most of the times you just click on the right, kinda obvious document and do the thing and then answer so the plot may thiccen.And it's not like the setting of the game, you being the computer guy helping detectives in the field means it has to be boring. There could have been more you could do. But most of the intrigue in this game comes from chat interactions, not from actual action you get to do.Like for example, there are two things that could have been so fun to get to use as active participant, as part of a larger puzzle YOU need to solve yourself, the chemical analysis software and the bomb defusing manual, that only get one use. And also, no love for the vehicle database, just for people database. But like, just being able to do more than to just find out an answer to one question at a time, being able to take notes and to make actual deductions? Would have been fun. Think of Mainlining as an example.It's just that, there is so much promise. This game was instant purchase for me as soon as I found out about it, as a fan of mystery and "hacking" genre of games. But it just didn't really deliver what I hoped for. And I'm kinda bummed about it.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, I adored this game.  I struggle with this next phrase because i don't fully mean it and understand why it is the way it is... but I'm glad I bought it on sale and not full price as it's not quite worth the full price.  I mostly say this due to game length and lack of choice in endings.  I took a look and it looks like this might be a first time game from this dev, who I'm guessing is solo or very small which is VERY exciting to see if this is their freshman showing.Things I LOVED:-Dynamic story telling.  There was a clear storyline running through from start to finish.  Not overly convoluted, not too cliche or simple.  Were the twists a little predictable?  Maybe a few.  But that didn't take away from the impact when they hit anyway.  The pacing of those drops were excellently done.-Style was lovely.  I REALLY dug the overall look of the game.  The various tools you got to us, the puzzles you go to solve... all from a single terminal.  It made me think of a hacking game from the early 00s of gaming sites that I loved to play over and over.-The voice acting was excellent.  Really stellar work.-The game itself.  It's just really enjoyable.  It was well paced, the mystery was fun, the story was easy to follow, the puzzles were a bit easy but a few had some real challenges in there.  One puzzle was a bit too much of a lateral thinking puzzle, BUT that was one of the best twists of the whole game so I can overlook it. Things I wish were different (not bad, just things I wanted more of):-it's far too short.  It took me about 4 hours to complete and that was going very slow and taking my time, looking at my phone a lot and doing a few other things at the same time. (thanks ADHD)  The story telling and plot that the game is driving could easily have been a full scale game.  And I'd pay good money for it, too.  This is top notch story telling from a new dev and I hope we see more.-Lack of use of cool tools.  You're introduced to several cool mini puzzles throughout the game like a car analyzer, a bomb diffuser, and chemical component analyzer.  All of them have robust rules and options with them.  And they're all used only once.  You gave us so many cool toys.. let us play with them!!-No story diversity with a .  While the story they have given is lovely, your choices don't matter.  There is just that ending.  I wanted more options, i wanted to affect the story with how i played and wanted the game reward cleverness (i.e. if you found a certain name on a certain list before you were told to.)All that being said, if you like mystery games, if you like hack style games, this is a great choice.  I am very excited to see what this dev does in the future.  If this is their first showing, we are in for some real gems in the future!!

_childDocuments_.review: I am the fan of the stories in games, and "The Operator" has just reached the top with this engaging storyline. What made it so cool is that the plot was very catchy, so it kept me playing. I could only wish for more depth in some storylines, making them way more complicated and detailed. Just a few more levels of detail in the story would make the experience even more puzzling and immersive. The game needs the possibility of side tasks that would help to. It would provide depth to the experience and variety of mundaneness, because otherwise, having some really mundane cases that are not related to the main story might make it feel more real and alive. The game mechanics were great! Simple and comprehensible, suitable for many players. My only complaint is that the game felt a bit too short.Something like statistics about what choices I made would be great; for instance, what percentage of the other players made the same decisions. That would be a great addition concerning interactive replay. The user interface in the game, especially the terminal interface, was so awkward in the context of the end of the 1990s since it felt very modern. A more period-appropriate design would add to the overall sense of immersion and give a more authentic feeling to the game. All in all, "The Operator" is quite a compelling game with a good story and intuitive mechanics.

_childDocuments_.review: A good cinematic visual novel. Hits the right notes over the course of the game, but be forewarned the game is short (3 hours) and linear. Big props to the music direction and voice acting, which is genuinely top notch. Puzzle aspect is alright but a little too straightforward and easy for my tastes. Plot is, unfortunately, just sort of silly - lots of plot holes, a twist that's reasonably easy to predict, and suffers from the aforementioned linearity.Overall the experience is pretty good for a game at this price point, as long as you don't expect a bunch of different endings or replay value. This is a direct line visual novel with good-to-great production values and a goofy story with relatively unconvincing worldbuilding, but executed very competently.

The puzzles are either simple or downright pathetic. Anyone who enjoys mysteries and has read a couple of detective novels could finish the game in under 3 hours. There's a part in the game that's quite exciting and was my favorite, but it ends quickly, leaving a bittersweet feeling.If this game had followed in the footsteps of similar games like Hacknet, it could have been a masterpiece in the genre. Instead, it turned into an interactive movie, like a typical Sony game.I'd recommend it if you find it for under 5 euros, as it only offers about 4 hours of gameplay at most.

_childDocuments_.review: kinda wish i could leave a "mixed" review because i don't hate this game - it does a lot of cool and interesting things and scratches a little bit at an itch left by hypnospace outlaw and home safety hotline, however the game is extremely short (a casual run through is about 3 hours, i can imagine someone who understands and quickly solves all the puzzles immediately on their first playthrough could potentially complete it in half that time,) the game introduces multiple puzzle mechanics that it uses exactly once and never returns to, and it has zero replayability - there is only one ending, the nature of which i imagine many will find unsatisfying due to the negative outcome for the player character and his allies. this is in spite of the player SEEMINGLY having some control over the events that take place, but ultimately have no impact on the end of the game. the feeling i got by the end of the post-credits sequence was that i had just paid 16 bucks for just the prologue to the "real game" which doesn't exist.speaking of prologues, if you played the demo and were drawn to the game due to the extraterrestrial / ufo themes that dominate that portion of the game, you'll be disappointed to know that this entire element is dropped immediately after the portion of the game covered by the demo ends, and never comes back. i'm not going to call this intentionally misleading, but i imagine a non-zero number of people who bought the game will walk away disappointed due to this fact.finally, the game is a bit buggy and softlocks in multiple places - i recommend you follow what the game expects you to do in the exact order it likes, as getting ahead of yourself, either through experimentation or actual foreknowledge, can potentially end your entire run and you'll have to start over.

_childDocuments_.review: Hi, I'm arko, I can give a little bit of backstory;When I was a younger kid, I always loved the idea of discovering a crime, investigating, solving cases, it just scratched an itch and ideas I had for my brain.Almost a decade later and I still enjoy such, I love ARG's, and such, and whenever I find one, I try my absolute HARDEST to solve.I started off with the Kaigan Games, Games, Sara is Missing, popularized in the late 2010's, you take perspective as a person who has found Sara's phone, and tries to investigate by asking her friends, family, and debunk cultist relations. Later on, I moved onto the SIMULACRA series, though not totally investigative games, they follow a similar principle, I loved SIMULACRA 1, and replayed it 4 times. It just satisfied me a way other games have not.I found out about this game way before release, I became excited to purchase it, though I did not buy it day one, I bought it extremely early. This game, scratched an itch no other games I listed prior and ARG's that I didn't even know existed. The way the game functions, the calls, everything that's in this game, is great. I love the operating system, and I think this is by far one of the best interpretations of a call center in the 80's-2000's. Everything from the keyboard sounds, the ambiance behind you, the mouse clicking, the computer effect, is so immersive, and I believe this is one of the most immersive games, I have ever played.-----------------------------------------------------My opinions on the story, there will be spoilers.You start off the game with a cutscene, you are being questioned by someone in an absurdly bright white room, there's nothing there but white. At first, you will think this cutscene means nothing, and is useless, but at the end, it will totally blow your mind, I won't say it here, as I want YOU to experience the thrill and twists this game has to offer. The immersive and keep you on your toes gameplay, especially with the bomb you have to deal with to make sure an Agent doesn't die, the back and forth with the notepad, manual, call, commands, is extremely thrilling, and keeps you nervous and anxious, as one wrong move, will kill the person you are trying to save.The use of a system that has a database, is great, scanning cars, people, places, and objects to help solve cases is amazing, and I believe it is the best yet.-------------------------------------Overall reviewGameplay: 6.5/10Story: 11/10Graphics: 5/10Cinematics: 5.5/10Sound Design: 10/10Soundtrack: 10/10This game has practically confirmed others are planned, due to the end credits and the last thing you do, so I really expect and hope for another installment.Good luck, Operators.

_childDocuments_.review: Played the demo and got really hooked, so I bought the game the next day full price.AFTER the demo I expected it to be very similar to Orville and Cyber Manhunt, with the primary focus on using the game's mechanics to solve multiple criminal cases, most unrelated or maybe filler and some interconnected into a bigger picture.It was... kinda like that? But instead of a focus on multiple cases and the solving mechanics, it focuses solely on one storyline.Which to me was actually really sad I guess because the gameplay mechanics were really well implemented and would have made for a super nice gameplay loop but instead got used once to advance the plot and then got discarded (e.g. the lab analysis or manually unlocking files). Also, the game is probably 75% dialogue, in which you are given choices that lead nowhere. You feel like your choices should matter, maybe in resulting in different endings but there is only one ending implemented. It actually made me compare it more to a visual novel than a detective game.The lack of "filler cases" is also more of a negative in this particular storyline. I've read that the developer wanted to focus more on the main story instead of filler but I think some filler would've helped the player to immerse themselves better into their role, made better usage of the well-implemented mechanics and would've allowed the player to connect with the characters better, settle mentally on the twists and turns of the main story and process them before the next thing gets thrown at them. It felt very fast-paced with no breathing time from basically the get-go and if I'm not mistaken the story takes place within only a couple of days in-game which also does not seem realistic.Conclusion:+ well-made from a technical point of view+ well implemented mechanics+ good soundtrack- poor use of mechanics- unclear advertisement (detective game vs. very story-driven, more of a visual novel)- no actual choices made by the player even though it feels like they should have mattered- lack of cases with a rather short gameplay time as a result- lots of dialogue with comparatively little gameplayIf you're looking for somethin akin to Orville, Cyber Manhunt or even Her Story, this is not it.I considered requesting a refund but I believe that if I buy a product, receive it and use it, there is no reason in refunding it, even if it was not what I expected

_childDocuments_.review: I did enjoy The Operator, but it's very much one of those titles I wish I could give a sideways thumb to. I can't explain why without spoilers, so I'll tag that section.This is one of those games that takes place entirely in menus, but still manages to have a compelling story with some puzzling that keeps you engaged in relatively simple game play systems by making you use the analytical parts of your brain. Taking place in a fictional early 1990s where people have cell phones and wireless Internet access, you're playing as a remote operator at the Not FBI who is tasked with helping field agents analyze data relevant to their cases. As you progress, you'll start to become embroiled in a huge conspiracy that goes through many elements of the agency and other places as well. The interface is nice, the music is good and the voice acting of the characters is actually great. If you like stuff that's more action focused, this might not be for you, but I was kept engaged throughout.Non-specific spoilers and attached criticisms below:

_childDocuments_.review: Like everything, there’s the good, the bad and the ugly.The good is that it’s quite a good experience, even if the puzzles are simple and intuitive, they’re not repetitive, and there’s some variety to it. The plot is extremely well written and serves well the thematics of the game.The bad is that I feel like somethings were underdeveloped. I’m referring specifically to the puzzles, I think like at least the chemical compound/molecules breaking could have appeared a couple more times. Not only that, I think the puzzles could experience a little bit more of variety, like 1-2 more types of puzzles. Although the plot was great, it also could have dived a bit further.The ugly is how the story breaks on the climax to an open ending. The story was just building up throughout the first two hours. During the 3rd hour, it was building the suspense to the climax, and then it’s just ends abruptly. The game could be double its playtime and still have room for a sequel, if the developers/publishers wanted to sell more content later on, during the next couple months (through a DLC) or down the road. However, the story is unfinished. It does leave mixed feelings like many are referring down on the comments and on their reviews.The game is incomplete as it is. The endgame was too soon and didn’t develop where it should.Nonetheless, this is common in movies and books, and I see where the developer can come from, as it may take a lot of time to put a game, even with this size, on the market and well polished.I will do this: I’ll leave a positive review on this game, but if there is a sequel, which I expect it will have, and if the game isn’t finished by then, cuts again abruptly and is the same length, I will leave a negative review on the next one.

_childDocuments_.review: Very cool game. In the same vein as " Papers Please" but a bit more tactful, and different.The game is engaging, and interesting overall, though for those who don't enjoy reading, or aren't very apt for it, this may feel like a slog, so  buyer be warned, reading at a moderate skill level is a must.I think the blurred scenes of you going home, aren't needed but I guess they do add something to the experience. I also wish we had a list of names to choose from, that were pre-recorded, instead of being agent tanner. This is a very minor nitpick but would've added to the experience even more. I'll settle with being tanner though since recorded hundreds of last names would've been a nightmare for the devs!The puzzles can be VERY hard at some points but it feels incredible to solve them without clicking the option for help! And figuring out how to use the supplied operator applications, such as the chemical analyzer, felt great!Very Satisfying game, scratches the exact same itch as papers please does, but in an oddly different way. Would recommend this even at full price because of how well thought out the experience is!

_childDocuments_.review: Firstly, I'd like to preface my review, by saying if you are interested in this game. Do not watch a play through of it, try the demo, see if your engaged and then buy the game. This review is spoiler free.A lovely crafted indie detective thriller, with a fantastic narrative story provided me with a very enjoyable and gripping 3/4 hours of game play on my first play through. The game has been painstakingly crafted down to every individual element, and it really shows, but this love creates a gripping, edge of your seat experience which will make you truly engage with every character and feel every emotion in a short space of time. The time setting is fantastic, blending a feel of early 2000 technology, with modern software and interface feel. When the game says use headphones, I usually disagree. But this is one of the rare examples which playing with headphones or a decent speaker set-up takes this from a game to a true experience.The game has got an excellent blend of mixed media, cinematic and a truly atmospheric score that intertwines with the narrative in a beautiful way to create this experience. Throughout the game it makes you constantly think, am I making the right choices, is this how I solve this puzzle, and gives you everything you need to figure these out in a well executed manner without holding your hand too much. Even the achievements have been carefully thought out to provide you just enough information that your inquisitive brain wants to fully unravel and unlock each one.Do I wish the game was longer? Yes. Am I disappointing by this? No, I loved every second of my playtime and strongly look forward to what the developer and his talented contributors bring next. Would I consider buying a future DLC expansion? Easily, this has been the most engaged with a game I've been for a very long time, and I would love to see what the developer brings to the operative universe next. This game is truly, one of those rare indie gems, that brings the passion and story into an over saturated gaming market, and really makes you wish more development companies (Especially AAA) had the same mentality and craft.

_childDocuments_.review: Insanely good. In something of a trend started last week by my playthrough of Anger Foot, "this could have been an email, but you wrote an essay, and an excellent one at that". In other words: What could have been a simple gimmick indie that's fun and gone in one hour is turned upside down by excellent production value, which includes: great direction, engaging narrative, amazing atmosphere and voice acting. I couldn't believe how much stuff *goes on* in this game and by the end it felt like taking part in a conspiration-themed deep state thriller and not playing a puzzle solver, and that's despite spending most of the time (*most*) staring at computer screens.I guess my only complaint is that the story is *only* good and you can see some twists coming from a mile away, but it more than makes up for that with excellent characters and being, well, engaging on a surprising level. The Operator is also not as open-ended as it seems to be, and could use a few more notable decisions and alernate endings.Give this a go, there's much more to this title than meets the eye. Heck, if nothing else comes up this can be my personal GOTY.

In the shadows, a war between the Yatagarasu and the Phantom Society is brewing, Devil Summoners who harness the otherworldly powers of “Demons”. Existing in the secret sea of humanity’s data, a digital hivemind has evolved into sentience: Aion. Observing humankind from afar, Aion calculates that a world-ending disaster is imminent and creates two agents to combat against it: Ringo and Figue. Together, these agents of Aion must investigate and prevent a butterfly effect that will lead to the end of the world. _childDocuments_.review: I have two really major problems with this game. The story, and the Sabbath system but they are so fundemental that I cannot bring myself to recommend this game. The story is easily the worst of ATLUS's games I ever played - and I played a bunch: SH1, SMT 3-4 + 4:Apo, Strange Journey, Devil Survivor 1-2, Persona 1-5. You'll be rolling your eyes pretty much every cutscene be that from extremly big plot holes or character over-reactions. The titular Soul Hack from the first game, was brought down from mystique, epheral to convenient ressurection switch - which can be turned on or off whenever the plot needs to somehow push forward.Characters themselves are good, though they are at their lowest during the main story events, and are at their best during the hangouts scenes. Now onto the second issue - the Sabbath system. This system is basically an equivalent to "win more", that is if you are winning by exploting enemy weakness you will hit again at the end of player turn. The problem is, that this system doesn't work well with any other battle system mechanic. First, if you setup your team correctly and have a wide spread of elemental skills you will pretty much wipe the enemies even before Sabbath will have a chance to hit. Ok, you can utilize it by not using your last character's turn if you have a big stack count enough to save some MP - but that's it. In comparision, in Strange Journey we had a similar system, but one with very important difference - that attack was immediate, and was also connected to demons alignment system which enemy could counter. I won't go into details how Persona or SMT systems perfectly blend their mechanics into their own battle systems - but one thing that connects them is that the mechanics can also be used by enemy, therefore making their mechanics integral part of the whole battle systems that player needs to play with.All in all, it's sad because the game really has some good music and interesting aesthetic but is brought down by some fundamental flaws. The way the game was published wasn't really helping it either. For most people it was a new franchise which they weren't sure about. Yet the developer/publisher decided to move content into Day 1 DLC. The situation is even worse because the game itself is very short compared to other ATLUS's games, and the price tag is set to AAA games standards - initial price was the same as Xenoblade 3 - released a month prior - which has a lot more substance and content.

_childDocuments_.review: I've only grasped the first few dungeons, so I'll give my review out so far.I have not played the previous Soul Hackers title, only Persona and SMT titles, but from what I've seen so far: You play as Ringo, an AI agent created to prevent apocalypse, maybe that's why it seemed like the plot feels a little too rushed. Right after the prologue, Ringo would automatically thrown to a dungeon in order to start her mission of saving the world from the apocalypse. The goal is to save a certain someone whom later joined in on her party, Arrow.Meeting Arrow would give the player the mechanics of the 'Soul Hack'ーWhich is a skill unique to Ringo where she could 'hack' a soul in order to revive them from death. Once Ringo saved Arrow, it was then revealed Arrow had a connection to the other characters that later became the rest of the party members. This would all be done in just It is unbelievably fast if compared to Persona series in general.So far, I don't really see the appeal of the character dynamics other than Ringo and Saizo's (And when Ringo picked the Saizo's preferred options)ーThe quirky answers are amusing. But then again, it's mostly because it reminds me a lot of the quirky answers Persona series has.As for the party's dynamics (as far as this review goes), the current atmosphere feels like they're only characters bound by the same reason of "being revived by Ringo" and currently shares the same goal. But other than that, I have yet to see connection between each of the party members.Now onto Ringo and the other AI agent called "Figue". Again, for me, their dynamic felt a little too rushed for my comfort. They are both AI that was born on the same moment, with different personalities. In-game, they should only know each other a day or two, but the game made it seemed like Figue had known Ringo for a long time by worrying every each one of Ringo's actions like a doting parent. For me, it seemed incredibly stupid. So it's a bit hard to have attachments as of this time of writing.The graphics are phenomenal, especially the character models and designsーI fell in love the moment I first saw the trailer (esp. knowing Shirow Miwa is the character designer. I have loved sensei's design since 7th Dragon 2020), and it was actually the reason I bought the game in the first place.The UI is clean and attractive as well. However, my only complaint so far would be the design for each dungeons. It felt so empty if you compared them to the Persona series.The gameplay felt a little bit too repetitive with no real consequences (I play in Normal difficulty).With no in-game days mechanics, you can go back and forth between the dungeons and the safehouse with no consequences other than your meal buff effects wore off the moment you leave a dungeon.Again, I have not put in enough hours to give an overall verdict, but putting all my impressions so farーI would say only to get them if the game is on a discounted price (I bought the Digital Deluxe edition and for me it's honestly pricey. I would not say it if the game is otherwise worth the money). Just buy Persona if you want a much more fun ATLUS game experience with that much amount of money.
