_childDocuments_.review: (Non Spoiler Review of base game no DLC quest)*Disclaimer I completed the game on Normal, unlike these sub 10hr playtime reviews.* *The last Atlus game I played was SMTV*Graphics are clean, this is probably the same engine as SMTV on Switch. It looks like a sharper version of that game with some cool cyberpunk flair nothing too fancy but its still pretty. (This is an HD switch game imo). Game supports ultrawide which is nice the character designs and art are awesome imo.Story was a pretty fun ride for me, I was recently playing Death Stranding and the story kinda shares similar man vs a.i issues. If you played Nier or something similar you get the idea for this games general story which i personally enjoy. Dialog was good with the plot dancing around goofy and serious things. Acting was great (played with JP VO) all I gotta say about that is "Mu,mu,mu-mu-mu-mu". I saw alot of people saying this is missing x or y features, not enough to do with the party members etc. This is Soul Hackers not persona guys. That said its hyper focused story, demons, dungeons and I think it fills a nice spot in Atlus current lineup. SMTV having semi open world* with enemy patrols, traversal and exploration, Persona with its more indepth social and sim features. And now Soul Hackers with its focused story and dungeons, its a good time as always building up ur roster of demonic pokemon.For sound the opening OST kills it imo, def a jammer not many memorable tracks in this one. The last boss track gives me Nier vibes and is pretty epic. I do still enjoy the break in the battle music even now so yeah like always Atlus battle BGM is good.Overall Id recommend this, Best to try the game urself if only the price of admission wasent so high GL.(Possible Spoilers MY THEORY ON WHY THIS IS ON A TIMELINE AFTER THE EVENTS and INFLUENCE OF PERSONA5 /STRIKERS with possible ties to PERSONA 4?(*WARNING* STOP READING IF UR WORRIED ABOUT SPOILERS KEEP READING IF U LIKE LORE AND COMPLETED THE GAME)If anyone here's played persona 5, you may be interested in this. (who am I kidding lol) You eventually encounter a dungeon helper that looks strikingly similar to one very popular cat. From color layout to eyes and even ear style and placement, that got me thinking could it be? No way. Another member of the party carries himself very similar to Yuuske wearing white with the hair covering his eye and dons a fox tail pattern scarf.Basically if you play this game u will encounter 1 too many coincidences for them to be coincidences. There's a group of people called "The phantom society" and the leader wears a mask and touts fighting for good.The game asks you whats the difference between humans, demons and a.i. Which makes me think back to P4 where Adachi turns into an Aion esc contruct (complete with rainbow style LEDs implying he has control over all colors of covenants in his world / server? I think no one in this game is "human", because even devil summoners when damaged break apart into shapes.And the baby cocoons also bear resemblance to things we've seen in other atlus titles I think SMT nocturne (not sure been a min). With the last boss sharing similar shape to those "babies" in the pods u see in the bone zone.This game is an altered server / timeline sometime after the influence of the events in persona5's world / server is what I'm coming up with after 1st clear with nearly all side quests complete outside of DLC.Gunna take sometime before I jump back into to NG+ and see if they hid anything, was one long enjoyable ride.

_childDocuments_.review: ***SOFT RECOMMENDATION // WAIT FOR A SALE***Pros:-Fun combat. While I miss Press Turn & One More from other sub-franchises, Sabbaths are fun. I just wish critical adds weren't locked behind upgrades and were in the system by default. Demon inheritance is a thing, but not every demon can learn every element. It's a shame, because the attribute system in SMTV seemed like the most fun way to balance demon builds. Beyond that, if you like MegaTen combat, you'll like it here too.-Great characters. With how goofy most of the cast looked, I wasn't expecting much; perhaps that's why was blown away by the quality of the character writing. Each character has a unique perspective and character traits while still feeling reasonable why they'd help Ringo and without feeling one-note.Cons:-Ringo moves very slowly through dungeons. There is a speed boost skill you can get early on, but it doesn't last very long and is tedious to repeatedly activate.-The dungeons are boring and repetitive. There aren't many dungeons in this game, and the ones that are feel very short and bland. There are two in particular that I consistently had to check against quest and demon locations because I could not tell them apart visually. MegaTen games typically have some interesting dungeon puzzles; there are only two of such in this game, and calling them puzzles feels like an overreach. They can be bruteforced very easily, and don't feel satisfying. I'm not asking for Nocturne-level warp dungeons, but a little more content would have gone a long way.-The story is apparent within the first half-hour of gameplay. The character writing carries the entire game on its back.-This game only feels loosely connected to Soul Hackers. There are a couple of character references and Soul Hacking happens. That's it.-The music is serviceable. Disappointing when compared to Persona 5 and SMTV, the latest entries in the other two major Megaten franchises under Atlus' belt.All in all, if Atlus was attempting to make Devil Summoner the third pillar in their roster, they failed. This game was underfunded, lacking in distinct content, and generally feels like it could have used more time in the oven.DLC Rating:-I have no opinion on costumes. It's pricey, but honestly changing the battle theme to the original Soul Hackers one was worth it to me.-Demons being such expensive DLC-- ON LAUNCH-- is criminal. _childDocuments_.review: I want to point the fact that this was a positive review. Then around the 40th hour in the game I simply broke down because this game is a complete waste of time. every single mechanic of this game is made to waste your time for nothing and story and background environment, as every npc, are basically nothing and there is no worth to go on with the story.For reference, I played EVERY smt\persona game into existence, yes included the old famcom megami tensei, so I know what I am doing here.This is not a good SMT game. It’s a bad entry point for a newbie of the series, it has NOTHING to do with the original Soul Hacker except some citations all around and it’s the worst story and npc.Regarding the setting I will never understand why they put the "2" here considering the original soul hacker game is the ending chapters of two old series (the raidou games and the devil summoners). If you don't want to explain everything it's relatively fine, but this is an entry point in a story that goes on from FOUR games in two different series. Atlus simply solved this excluding everything coming from the original game and putting the name just for marketing purposes. Just reading till this if you are a SMT fan you have your full for not buying the game.Now back to the game.The dungeon design is the WORST I’ve ever seen. The dungeons are all the same and the soul matrix is simply the worst thing that they could ever thought of. Instead of a single labyrinth they decided to split in three parts, and every part has four enormous floors. Too bad that those parts are the same empty space with only the floor to walk into. The floors have the same monsters and object, the only difference are the minibosses. You will stay A LOT around here for mmo fetch tier quest with no interesting rewards, the miniboss sometimes unlock some fusions but nothing more. The normal dungeons are subway, offices or dock area, recycled every time. The shop hubs are tiny and poor designed. This game coming after Persona 5 and in 2022 this dryness of environment is terrifying lazy. It’s like playing into a beta version or some modeling kit.The battle mechanics is classic SMT with come late persona’s qol, but there is no progression nor new mechanics. The thing you do in the tutorial dungeon is the same thing you are doing for all the 40-50 hours needed to end this pain. There is absolutely NOTHING as progression, only numbers that go up. The MC carries the game like Atlas, but the other npcs are NOTHING. Their personal stories are really lazy and predictable but the worst experience is doing hours of the same labyrinth, the same four demons, running and running spamming assassin’s steps cause you are TIRED, just to have two or three lines of conversation and that's all. The game tries to build mystery but in the end the characters story and the general story is NOTHING. I know perfectly that the SMT games take a while to gear up but this takes the consideration to an insane extreme. This is why I decided to put a negative review. I sit through the immense NOTHING of the personal stories, boring side\fetch quests with two or three dialogues and nothing else, hoping there was something better in the end.Well, there isn’t. All the situations are solved with some stupid deus ex machina (yeah I know that that’s basically what the two MCs are but it’s SO LAZY), personal motivations fall behind and everything turns to I have to find a thing to find a thing to find a thing. They put some kind of bait and switch in the fourth floor of every NPC labyrinth but to reach it you have passed 30 to 40 hours in game hungry for more, and that’s basically the only surprise\reveal you can expect because all the other stuff you can easily predict or they are so phoned in that it’s offensive, from a narrative standpoint.The plot starts to gear up in the LAST dungeon and it's solved like it's late for work. It's not the hardest plot in the world but hte pacing is horribile, everything in the beginning, nothing during the midgame (30-40 hours), the rest over the last minutes. Awful, really.All the background story of the characters are given to you by breadcrumbs, like a couple of lines after 2-3 hours of dungeon exploring, the hangout events are interesting but they are so cheap and some of them are just useless filler, you can easily see where the dev teams run out of ideas. I think, if you remove the farming\running around parts, this game has less than an hour of dialogues, reading very slowly.This game is a slogfest and I am playing with the cheat dlc which increases your exp and money and I barely keep in par with the dungeons. I don’t even want to know how bad is when you have to honestly grind money and exp. It’s just not worth. Watch a playtrough if you want to know about the story but the game is just not fun or interesting.No, this is not acceptable. This is the laziest SMT I’ve ever seen and it's insulting coming in this year and walking into the footsteps of Soul Hacker.Don’t buy this, you aren’t missing anything.

_childDocuments_.review: I'd somewhat recommend Soul Hackers 2, but with many caveats. I've played every single Persona game and almost every SMT game ever released. I've played games made by Atlus for a long time, and after the resoundingly high note that was SMT V, I had really, really high expectations for Soul Hackers 2. What I got was a very middling JRPG that's stuck between being an SMT game and a Persona game but is good at being neither. This game is a prime example of style over substance. It looks really, really nice. It has one of the best presentation out of any megaten game. However, the gameplay, dungeons, and quality of life aspects just aren't there. Pros:-Great artstyle. Everything just looks very aesthetically pleasing, from the characters to the environments, the demons, the visual effects, etc... The colors really pop and look vibrant no matter what is happening on screen. The character models are not only very sharp and expressive, but they also move really well. From a presentation perspective, I can't fault Soul Hackers 2 at all. It just looks really good.-Interesting story with solid characters. Midway through the game, the only thing that pushed me forward was the story. It shared some loose connections with the original Devil Summoner and Soul Hackers that I appreciated, and it was nostalgic to see the world of these games again after so long.-Great atmosphere and setting. The writers really kept the atmosphere of the original Devil Summoner games alive in this game, portraying this gritty, dangerous world full of demons and intrigue. Again, this may be because I've played the original Devil Summoner and Soul Hacker games, but I instantly liked the world of Soul Hackers 2. -I like Ringo a lot. Cons:-The gameplay is noticeably worse than the most recent Atlus entires. It's like we've regressed 10 years since Persona 5 and Shin Megami Tensei 5 came out. This game feels like a PS2-era game that was released in 2022. Gone are press turns or anything that makes megaten combat remotely enjoyable post-nocturne. The combat in this game trying to be more like Persona's combat but it's somehow much slower paced, less complex, and less satisfying. It plays like a very generic JRPG combat system, which is already a dealbreaker for me when it comes to JRPGs, but even more so when it's a megaten game. In addition, demon negotiation has been completely gutted. You can no longer even talk to demons in battles. The only way to recruit them now is through an RNG mechanic that occurs when roaming the dungeon, and when you do get to talk to them they ask you for only one thing and will always join you if you give it to them. It's like they only included demon negotiation for the sake of having it, and only put in only the minimum amount of effort to make it functional. It's a very gimped version of a very long-standing megaten mechanic, and I have no idea why they made it this way when even games released 10 years ago had it down pat. -The dungeon crawling is really, really tedious. Ringo moves really, really ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ slowly and the dungeons mostly consist of very barebones corridors that you run straight down to get to the next boss or story moment. There are barely any gimmicks or variations in scenery. These are some of the laziest, most tedious """"""dungeons""""" I've seen Atlus put out. Hell, even Megami Tensei I and II on the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ NES had some dungeons with more variety than Soul Hackers 2. The game also only has 2 tracks that it reuses for every dungeon in the game. 2 tracks. You remember how each dungeon from any Persona game, or even each dungeon from the first Soul Hackers game had a unique theme? None of that is here. In fact, the dungeon music in this game became so mind-numbing after 20 hours in that I just turned the music off and played my own music. I almost dropped this game a few times because of how unbelievably ass the dungeons were. All my above complaints wouldn't even be so bad if only Ringo had a sprint button that I could use to speed through it all, but they decided to make her jog like my grandma after she just had a stroke. After having played through the sprawling maps of SMT V or the complex, multi-layered dungeons of Persona 5, it's really, really hard to slog through this game's sorry excuses for dungeons.-The loading screens are atrocious. You get a 5 second loading screen every time you change locations. It may not sound much but keep in mind that this happens every. single. time. you. change. locations. If you need to go shopping at 3 different stores, go grab some quests from the quest lady, then go fuse some demons, then go back to base to rest up, then go back to the dungeon to keep exploring, that's 7 loading screens in the span of 5 minutes. How is this even a thing? SMT V had massive open levels that were like 30 times the size of any one map in Soul Hackers 2, and there were barely any loading screens at all in that game. Conclusion: I'll give Soul Hackers 2 a 6/10, and I'm being generous. I wanted to like this game. I liked its presentation, its world and story, but if you strip away all those things, it's a very clumsy and mediocre JRPG sitting on the shoulders of giants. It's not even sitting properly up there; it's just half-heartedly dangling one leg off the side like it doesn't fully know what it's doing. My main problem with this game isn't that it's not Persona 6 or SMT 6, but rather, it executes some of the most basic aspects of being an Atlus game quite poorly. I'd only recommend you get it when it's on sale or if you're a big fan of Atlus and their games. Even then, set your expectations somewhere around the middle of the pack. Then you'll enjoy this game much more than I did.EDIT: After I've finished the game and sat on it for a while, I'll knock the score down to a 5. The story was actually quite good right up until the very end, where it went straight to ♥♥♥♥. The final dungeon was also like a final ♥♥♥♥ you to the player. The enemies suddenly got a massive level spike, forcing you to go back and grind, and the """""gimmicks""""" that they threw in were, as with any other gimmicks in this game, thrown in for the sake of having gimmicks and padding the dungeon out rather than being a fun or interesting challenge. The DLC mission is also a joke. It's one of the most barebones Atlus DLC I've ever played. SMTIV Apocalypse and SMTV had some of the coolest DLC the franchise has ever seen, so Soul Hackers 2 once again is the lame child in Atlus' family of games.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a weird one for me to review. It's basically the most "meh" JRPG in recent memorie for me, one that might just edge out into a fun but likely forgettable romp if you're a fan of Atlus's style of JRPGs like I am. Also, this game basically has nothing to do with devil summoners (likely why they removed the subtitle) or even Soul Hackers 1 (a devil summoners game) despite the concept of devil summoners existing in-world, as this is mostly subverted from the very get-go and your devil summoners even react to how they're not really acting like normal devil summoners anymore... most of your human opponents do, but it's ultimately kind of pointless fluff the way enemies are presented, though.That's okay, I guess. but I kind of wish it was a true devil summoner game... the other characters aren't all that interesting and imo it would have been better to have Ringo (the MC) be a classic devil summoner on her lonesome, summon demons directly, and just have her use soul hack to resurrect whatever character is to become the current story arc's central figure. Instead, you stick with a 4-man team forever and much of the game focuses on them while very lightly touching on stuff like what a human soul really is and what it means to be human.Unfortunately, it regards to that, there's just a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ of wasted potential so far that has me really frustrated. This isn't new for JRPGs, which usually take a pretty shallow approach to concepts like good and evil. It's by intent; a lot of JRPGs share tropes with anime (specifically stuff like Naruto, Demon Slayer, Dragon Ball Z, etc), and shōnen, which is what that genre is called, is literally targeted at young boys. That's why a lot of JRPG MCs are young teenage boys, and why the stories never touch on darker or more mature themes like many western RPGs commonly do.But Soul Hackers 2 has an entire cast of adults exploring what it means to be human as well as the nature of death and the human soul... Not a child in sight (technically), and yet the game immediately and forever shies away from any meaningful engagement with those concepts. There's even an early joke about getting addicted to soul hacking (the supposedly emotional process that brings the dead back to life), so it's all shallow and lighthearted. Anyway, the game's leads are the same guys who did Tokyo Mirage and you can really tell... so yeah. At least the story premise here isn't laughably ridiculous from the start as it was in their last game.While not outright terrible (writing is fine, voice acting is good), it all adds up to a kind of meh storyline and you never really end up caring about any of the characters. The game also looks pretty simplistic and doesn't have very extensive scenery or dungeons, though the individual character models are well-done. I've never once been awed upon entering a new area or dungeon.Combat remains Atlus's best strength. It's probably what you'll enjoy the most, and there is a crapton of it. Unfortunately, there's a really repetitive, drab Mementos-like area (for those who come from Persona 5) that doesn't really add many twists (looks the same, pretty linear, all the quests involve just killing enemies or boss versions of normal enemies, etc), and boy does it get old and tedious after 5 seconds.Overall, it's a decent JRPG that I think true fans of JRPGs will view as a game with more positives than negatives, as most of those negatives are also things JRPG gamers have long dealt with. It's not an outright terrible game, and can serve to fill in time gaps in between what I would consider far better JRPGs (Persona 5, The first Crossbell Arc Trails game, etc), and if you play western RPGs too, there's probably a lot better upcoming options out there too depending on tastes.I'm going to give it a thumbs up, but I'm going to finish by saying this will never be a must-play and will probably be forgotten by the end of the year, and it's definitely never going to be considered one of Atlus's best games.

_childDocuments_.review: Two cyborg waifus created by a super secret artificial intelligence attempt to stop a culturally stagnant humanity from killing itself via demons. The setup is more exciting than the actual plot itself. The twists and turns follow your typical JRPG playbook with every  coming from a mile away. One noteworthy inclusion is that the MC, Ringo, is fully voiced. While not the worst thing in the world it's hardly anything special and Ringo herself can be funny despite some of the cringe writing. You'd think a sequel to Soul Hackers would have demon summoning and recruitment, well you're wrong bucko! The series is now a persona spinoff complete with lack of demon party members and recruitment. Instead you equip one of your four human party members with a demon and they use the inherited spells and abilities. Recruitment is handled in the most brain dead way possible, you walk around and find them randomly. You simply give them what they ask for and if your level is high enough they're yours. You'll be hunting for demons randomly placed in dungeon maps so boring and empty you'll get persona 3/4 flashbacks and they aren't even randomly generated maps! Combat is one of the worst in the series thus far! Instead of the one more time system where a strike with an enemies weakness you get build your "Sabbath" charge. Some hits can add more than 1 per attack if you hit hard enough or use a commander skill to boost them. At the end of your turn your demons come out to smack the enemy. You or your enemies hitting weaknesses do not give/take away turns unless it's status related which makes the combat extremely easy and boring. In an attempt rectify this they added the commander skills from SMT strange journey REDUX . There's also social links, but they're for the party members only and suck.Actually nearly fully featured other than lack of ultrawide because Japanese indie devu pwease understandu. Might be worth it on sale if you really want to play every mid JRPG ever made. I'd personally avoid if I was you tbh.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're familiar with smt games, you will be familiar with certain parts of the game like contracting demons, fusing them, and most of the skills available. This game was fun to play, however it feels like it made some decisions that negatively impacted the game. I'm not sure if it's due to limited budget, but the dungeon design in general was quite mediocre. The visual aspect for most dungeons aside from the final dungeon was bland, and maps themselves went back to old persona game designs, but what's worse is that one of the dungeons which you have to go through for at least 3 x 4 floors if you want the true ending, is designed so you have to go through an ever growing teleporter maze, which makes going through it and finishing quests tedious.  you often get item collection quests and these items actually have fixed location spawns in spite of spawning similar to the random items you get otherwise, and if you miss a small portion of the large map, you could be going in circles for a while before you can finish  the quest.I'm not familiar with the first soul hackers game, but for this second one when it comes to combat, unlike smt games and persona, hitting a weakness does not give extra turns, which has meant that the game basically gives every boss in the game a skill that gives them extra turns instead, while you get a stacking "all out attack" or sabbath as they call it,  based on the number of stacks for that turn.there are other small things seemingly missing here and there like lack of skill mutation.This game feels like it was held back by minor stuff + the biggest problem, dungeon design.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good game not only as a SMT game but as a JRPG as well. The story and characters are pretty well done and I love how the the four main characters relationship evolves as the game plays out. The Bar Heidrun is a location you can go to to have "hangout events" with some of the squad and you can learn more about them as people and see them interact with each other on a more personal level (some times) outside of the main story. The game is quite easy actually (and I played on hard) as it's designed to make sure you don't really have to worry about dying and you can freely grind  for the levels and macca you need and honestly calling it "grinding" is a bit of a stretch as the game sort of throws exp at you. Battle System itself is simple and has enough mechanics to make it interesting but I wish certain elements were either still there or done better. Personally though I found that the battle system kind of dragged until mid close to late game phase when the demons became more interesting in their skill slots and having certain upgrades for your COMP and passives your characters can learn from the Soul Matrix. Dungeons are awful and boring as all hell (especially the Soul Matrix my god) and the lack of variety in regards to the dungeon music is a sin but the OST itself is good (well I like it at least). DO NOT BUY THE LOST NUMBERS DLC it's low effort and a scam tbh I didn't even finish nor do I really care to because it has what is the worst boss I fought in that game. The boss is bad not because of poor design but because there is a sheer lack of putting any effort in it's design to begin with and the main game has some interesting bosses. For PC performance I had no hiccups at all while playing this and it was a smooth 10/10 experience for me personally so maybe Atlus can port they're other games with better success in the future.Overall for me I recommend this game whether you are a megaten fan or even if it is your first game in the franchise it has enough elements you keep you a engaged and due to the game designed around making sure you can comfortably  level up, fuse and upgrade your COMP as necessary people shouldn't really have to much of a difficult time with the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I love Megaten games and have played nearly everything that's been released since Devil Survivor 1 on the original DS + most of the PS2 games. This review is my first impression after getting through the first 3 story dungeons.Playing the game on Very Hard for my first playthrough and I'll say I'm enjoying the challenge it offers that restricts you from using items (although it is very trial and error not knowing any of the bosses the first time around) with just enough customization to help you prepare and enough side-content in between if you find yourself struggling/underleveled. Battle system is not press turn, but there's enough customization to compensate and make things a bit more interesting (equipment/comp upgrades/demon fusion/Mistiques that boost parameters of a certain type of move/etc). The characters are interesting and consist of adults that act like adults (elevated by the voice acting, the English VA's did a great job). The banter between the party members and the battles are probably the most enjoyable aspect of the game for me. Music is good overall.Onto the bad stuff, the dungeon crawling is incredibly bland and sluggish. I don't get why they had to tie many mechanics of dungeon crawling like finding item chests/heal spots/and especially demon negotiation to demon recon (where monsters in your stock just stand in random spots of the map to offer you one of the 3) it makes discovery/finding things a whole lot less interesting. Figue as a navigator seems really unnecessary with how simple encounters in this game work (the monster is 3 feet in front of me I don't need a navigator to tell me what's right in front of me) The Soul Matrix dungeon (of which there are 3 of the same dungeon for each of your party members aside from Ringo) is tedious/boring, it's like Shin Megami Tensei IV Apocalypses final dungeon times 3 with a lot of nothing and is a major missed opportunity. These things alone dampen the experience a pretty good amount and makes it kind of difficult to recommend to everyone kind of player.Despite being pretty mixed on this game and a little hard on it, I'm still finding enjoyment from the game. The cyberpunk setting and the battle system/characters are what help's this game stand out. I can only recommend it if you're craving something that isn't Persona or Shin Megami Tensei (though borrows things from both games), are looking for a JRPG with an adult cast, and are piqued by the cyberpunk setting/theme while not too peeved by the underwhelming dungeon crawling.

_childDocuments_.review: Buy it on saleSoul Hackers 2 is overall subpar for an SMT entry: plot and worldbuilding details are glazed over without serious consideration or development, dialogue is repetitive and shallow, and the characters feel hollow and unlikable. Serious themes such as death, sexuality, and divinity are handled callously and the cutscenes depicting them are often slow and lifeless. The environments are repetitive and boring, npcs and quests feel uninspired, and the dungeons don't feel worth exploring. Characters and demons themselves LOOK good, I just can't understand the gap between their looking straight out of Persona 5 while running around environments that look ripped from SMT 3 Nocturne.The combat is worthwhile, but the Sabbath system feels gimmicky and the dialogue between characters makes me cringe. I would rather have a team of just demons over these gloomy losers. The leveling feels really off: unless you're stopping to fight every mob, you're going to be super under-leveled while progressing at an organic pace. The Soul Matrix is straight-up a bad time. The side-quests feel like content for the sake of content, which I would expect from a lesser JRPG. It's like a checklist to clean out these horrible teammates' souls by witnessing their trauma and having a conversation like "that was messed up but I see why you wanna get the bad guy" over and over. It makes me more claustrophobic than Mementos from P5 or Tartarus from P3, and might stop me from ever finishing this game. Lastly, a matter of personal preference: I usually play SMT games in Japanese, but the subtitles are really lacking in this one so I'm playing with the English dub so I understand what my loser teammates are whining about in battle. If you're a Subs > Dubs guy like me, you understand it's a bad time.

_childDocuments_.review: Soul Hackers 2, itself as a game, does not deserve the review beating it has taken. As a bridge between social sim Persona and Hardcore JRPG SMT, it does quite well. A solid 8, not groundbreaking but a fun time.The main focus of the story is Ringo and her crew travailing a horrible stagnant and stale corporate future, in order to save mankind from causing its own destruction.The gameplay is standard SMT/Persona fair, turn based combat plus creature collection. Its not particularly hard if you have any JRPG experience and tends to border on being too easy.The world and dungeon design is not that good tbh. granted it sets the tone of living in a corporate and stagnant city , with a thin veneer of glamour masking the hollowed out reality of a post industrial city. Yet this boils down to a lot of corridors in train tunnels and empty corporate buildings when dungeon diving. Except the Soul matrix part of the game, which is more like long pathways in "cyber space" and teleporter puzzles. I enjoyed the soul matrix until I ran into those puzzles. I wish that they were just number/colour coded. My advise is save before you jump.On the down sides, its a bit short, the teleporter puzzles suck and thats about it. I even liked the music , even if it was limited it wasn't grating. HOWEVER the DLC practices are obscene. If it wasn't for the high prices it could almost be forgiven, but locking away series regular demons was too much, it felt like whaling. Costumes and extra missions are one thing (not great behaviour, but all too common ) but that was a step too far.Other notes is that this port runs ok. You will get stutter on your first battle of that play session, but other then that its not too noticeable, when running around and such.Overall I did enjoy my time with it and 100% completed it. I liked the combat chatter from team mates and the enemies making the characters have bags of personality. I enjoyed the style of the character design and the music. The story is So-so to good, with great character moments thrown in and some good voice acting from Ringo and Milady's VA in particular. I look forward to any sequels that may come.I would say that this game is easily worth its money at £30 or about that. I wouldn't bother with the DLCs at all. The challenge battles arn't worth it, though the character introduced is fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Soul Hackers 2 is another title in the long line of the Shin Megami Tensai umbrella collection of games and another entry in ATLUS's commitment to bringing the games over to the PC market overtime for past releases and same day release for newer content.The immediate comparison people will attempt to make with it being a SMT title is to Persona 5/5 Royal. The only real comparisons you can make are the demons you can summon/recruit and a giant stretch to the hangouts you get with each party member at the bar in the city and the occasional dialogue choice that gives bonus points to their relationship level. The "Soul level" of your party member is required to delve deeper into their own personal dungeons, which are sort of just bland and uninspired grey looking "mindscapes" with no differentiation between your three party members. As you progress you unlock gates, as long as you have the required soul level for them, which gives you a little more backstory into that character and gives them an unique passive or usable ability.Your party is limited and small, four total, and you get all members around 15-20 minutes. You really only do one very small dungeon with two people and meet the third at the end of that and the fourth immediately after in the city you visit. While it's a staple for most RPGs to have bigger parties that you end up getting new members well into the game and have to switch out members if you want to level them but Soul Hackers confines its story into these four protagonists and their involvement in the storyline.The overall story is basic. Make sure the big bads don't summon their big angry god to rewrite humanity. Anyone who has played a SMT title knows that's just how things go. Where you get involved is how the characters flow into the story. The ideals they hold, their different paths they took in the Summoner world and how/why they're working together now. It does delve into some serious stuff, but that's par for the course for a SMT title.The gameplay is standard SMT fair. Turn based combat, use demon abilities to hit weaknesses, weaknesses build up a gauge which stacks up and at the end of your turn does damage based on the stacks and resets. You explore fairly simple, cityscape type dungeons for the most part and they're not too hard to go through. The only real challenge/annoying aspects is the last dungeon and certain floors of the protagonists personal dungeons that have warp elements to them which, if I'm being honest, had me looking for a map after 15 minutes of getting nowhere. While in the dungeons, your demons will be in random areas with something to give you. You can recruit demons from them, they can give you items (and notably key items that unlock more hangouts to get more Soul Points for certain party members), or heal you a bit. Depending on the difficulty you play on, you can burn through the game in probably 40-50 hours while still exploring all the areas to try and get everything."Well that sounds like a very neutral and bland sounding game, so why recommended it?" Thank you for asking, random internet person.It's not a really a bad game. Nor is it a great game. It's a 7. It's just a generally good, relatively simple RPG. Being a SMT fan as a whole, from the mainline # series to all of their spinoffs on varying consoles and handhelds, it satisfied the itch of a SMT title. For what it does and tries to do, it does it well. If you jump into this because you finally got to play Persona 5 Royal, or even Persona 4 Golden, expecting all SMT titles to be that way then yeah you'll probably be disappointed. Soul Hackers 2 is its own thing, as is the other spinoffs like Persona, Raidou, Devil Survivors, Digital Devil Saga, the mainline #'d series, Strange Journey, etc. You also don't need to play the original Soul Hackers because this has nothing to do with that one at all.The latest patch added some much needed quality of life elements as well, most notably faster dungeon movement and battles.

_childDocuments_.review: I think this game gets an unfair comparison to Atlus' giant franchises like SMT and Persona. I personally like the story, the characters and their motivations. The dystopian cyberpunk atmosphere was done right. The music is a bop (special mention to COMP Smith and Battle of Devil Summoners). Character and Demon designs are beautiful and very stylish. Sabbath system doesn't bother me that much, in fact, I like it and it's a breath of fresh air from SMT's Press Turn system and Persona's 1-more system.Now the actual downsides of this game, for me, are the dungeon designs. They're... boring. They're just hallways, nothing very special. There's teleporters but that's it. Soul Matrix's dungeons were the worst, especially on floors 4-5. Lots of teleporters to teleport you on God knows where. You gotta memorize where they go or write it down, else you're going to be stuck to that floor for a while to the point that it gets frustrating. For Lost Numbers DLC, it was alright, I guess. I liked Nana and her story. However, the DLC Dungeon is once again, the worst. Every floor was basically almost the same. Also, same as the other dungeons in the base game, there's nothing very special with it. It was a drag all the way down to the last floor.As for other DLCs, they offer nothing except some "conveniences" and fan-service to other Atlus games. If you like costumes and custom battle BGMs, then get them, otherwise they're not really essential.Overall, I have issues with the game, mainly on dungeon design, but still, I really like it.8/10

_childDocuments_.review: Update:  Having played to the end, I will say that it gets *better*, but I wouldn't say it ever truly becomes more than "adequate."  The plot does eventually pick up, and the dungeons get a bit more interesting towards the end...  but it's still a bland and watered-down MegaTen experience which is hurt by having a budget that was clearly too small for the scope of the title.  And it's still very hard to forgive just how interminably boring the first 20-30 hours are.  Die-hard MegaTen fans will undoubtedly want to play this sooner or later, but if that's not you, go play one of the better games in the franchise instead.******************************************************My disappointment is immeasurable and my day is ruined.I know some of the Atlus fans out there are trying to put a good face on this, but the reality is that this is a mediocre MegaTen game *at best.*  I can even accept that the gameplay has been simplified to the point of being welcoming to newcomers, because I don't blame Atlus for wanting to bring in new players.  What I can't accept is how ungodly crushingly BORING this game has been so far.I'm 22 hours in, and - I'm not exaggerating - at least half of that time has been spent wandering around an endless, endless set of subway tunnels and utility corridors.  And every time I beat a boss and I think I'm finally done with this section, ANOTHER set of subway tunnels opens up.  It's like Mementos in P5, except so much worse because I don't even have the catbus to speed up exploration.  This is one of the most miserable grinds I've been put through since the PS2 days.  Just the same tunnels repeated over and over and over.And for funsies, occasionally I'm given a side quest which forces me to go back to other sections of this endless set of tunnels, for even more of the same. It's like Atlus outsourced an SMT game to Idea Factory.Likewise, the plot has been dull as dishwater too.  It's been pretty much nothing except the characters sitting around talking about  the plot.  Apparently there's some big war going on between multiple factions of Demon Summoners, and an apocalypse is on the horizon, but I've been shown almost none of it.  Just endless cutscenes of the crew expositing at each other at the home base.  Nor are the characters particularly interesting either.  Main character Ringo has some sparks of personality, but otherwise, even the supposedly flamboyant outgoing character seems like he's on too much prozac.  And, of course, the combat being easy and streamlined just adds to the underwhelming.I really can't recommend it to anyone, not unless it magically gets so much better later on.   If you're already a MegaTen fan, you'll probably play it anyway - but don't get your hopes up.  If you aren't a MegaTen fan, just wait for Persona 5 Royale to hit Steam in a couple months.  It's so much better.  Or play Shin Megami Tensei V on Switch if you'd prefer a *good* dungeon crawl.  But don't start with this.

_childDocuments_.review: I was very excited and hopeful for Soul Hackers 2 since it was the first time in a long time we got a brand new Shin Megami Tensei series spinoff, and could be the title that would bring forth new / revive some old SMT subseries. While the game is good in some aspects, it's tainted by some very glaring cons that make it a drag to play at points. It's hard to give it a positive rating, so I'm going to say I'm very mixed. Here's why: The game itself visually looks well with the vibrant color palette and character designs, especially Ringo and Figue who serve as the main character and sidekick, who look very well done with the cyberpunk-ish look and style.This game's cast, which is an adult cast this time around instead of younger teenagers like the Persona series, is a good bunch with their own distinct backgrounds, personalities, motives, etc. Each character is perfectly fine, and I had no complaints on how they handled them. It's not one I would vaguely remember many years from now, but they were an interesting bunch. The main character Ringo, she is easily the best part of this game. They actually went with a protagonist who isn't silent this time around, and I hope it's not the last time due to this games' mixed reception. She was very like-able from the beginning, and is easily the best character by a landslide.The story itself was alright as well, with the different side characters this game offers and events. The antagonists were very bland though IMO and weren't nothing to write home about. I will throw in a big con about the story however here. The biggest gut punch about party's backstories (Arrow, Milady & Saizo) if you want to learn them, you have to go through the 'Soul Matrix', which is the most bland and uninspired dungeon I have probably ever witnessed in an JRPG. More on this later on exploration. Now time for the points I am either mixed on, or very much despise about the game: The combat itself at first is okay, the sabbath system is essentially the "All-Out Attacks" from the Persona series, except some demons can acquire skills called "sabbath skills", that usually tack on extra damage or ailments to the enemy. The skill variety is what you can expect from an SMT game, but certain demons have their own unique skills that are just not in the game at all. The biggest one being Yoshitsune, who's unique skill is 'Hassou Tobi' which is a big part of why he is a sought after demon to recruit/fuse, is just not there. This was a slap in the face when I realized this, and is very jarring since we just got SMT V less than a year ago and these skills including that one are all there in that game? The combat after a while becomes a cake walk, especially since it isn't the press turn system and you can hit enemies that resist/null certain affinities and not get penalized for it. The COMP skills however, I can say I thought was a good addition and made it a bit more interesting and made you want to go after since they can increase damage and affinities which are huge to have for later. The OST is nothing too special, certainly not even close to touching Shoji Meguro or Ryota Kozuka works by any means, but it was fine. They let MONACA, who have made the music for the Nier series, handle the soundtrack instead and while there are some tracks that are good, they aren't any that would stand out that I would listen to over time after playing. The best piece I would say is the game's main theme "Hopeless Call". I wouldn't say there are any BAD battle themes, they are all decent but not too memorable like mentioned. Now finally for the exploration / dungeon layout - which is BY FAR the WORST part of this game. The dungeons are very linear and get to be a drag to get through, especially since there isn't a dedicated DASH BUTTON. A bit later on, you start to acquire these skills called "Map Skills", which can make these more bearable but still a chore since you spend a bit of MP to activate them and have to constantly refresh them. One of these skills is "Assassin's Footsteps" I believe it's called which served as this game's run button for dungeons / open areas, which runs out after a short while and costs 10 MP each time to use. Why would this be locked behind a skill for crying out loud? Persona 5 had a dash button for dungeons and that game came out years before this. At the time of me typing this, they announced on October 3rd 2022 they are releasing a patch for the game that adds a dash button and other fixes that will be released sometime in November I believe. I can respect them for at least going back to correct it, but it's too late for many who have already played it and moved on, myself included. The demon negotiating, which is a big staple of the franchise, has been completely watered down here. Within dungeons you send out the demons in your current stock to "recon" the area, which they usually turn up with an item either for restorative purposes or for a quest, or just straight up restore your HP/MP. It's completely randomized, and these recon demons are also how you recruit new demons to your party. Again, it's COMPLETELY randomized which demon it selects, but it usually is according to the current dungeon difficulty/level. The thing is, instead of the demon asking you questions unique to itself, as well as asking for either Macca or items, it only asks for either ONE item or Macca and it joins you simple as that. Recruiting this way that's completely randomized as well as brain dead frankly was very uninteresting. Continuing from my last point about dungeon layouts... The 'Soul Matrix' I mentioned earlier, which is required to go through for the main story to an extent, but further if you want to learn more about the party members, is the main culprit with awfully linear and repetitive these dungeons can be. Each floor for each character looks the EXACT SAME, but are laid out differently and end up getting more complex with random warps and such as you progress further up. These are so bad that I started to believe they were auto generated with how straight forward and boring these got. This itself is the biggest con of the game for myself and many others I can see. And to wrap it up, this game brings back more "Day 1 DLC", similar to the sort SMT V had, but it is infinitely worse here. The biggest part of being an ENTIRE SEPARATE STORY ARC locked behind it. The game itself it pretty short for an SMT title, so why would they cut this out and not leave it in to add some more depth and side quests, when the side quests in this game for the most part are just fetching something and skipping dialogue just to get to the reward? The DLC also includes bonus demons as well, including Satan and Mara. The other two are costume packs and booster items, which are okay and should've been the only two. The costume packs are different outfits for the party you will recognize from older Megaten titles, and include some unique music tracks depending on which you wear. You cannot see these costumes outside of battle however. I own the DLC, which I regret greatly after playing. I went and spent my time getting all the achievements the game has to offer to get my moneys worth at least. If you are interested in buying the game as a Megaten series fan, or even just a fan of JRPGs, please wait until this game is discounted to AT LEAST half off. Looks like it's currently at $45 USD at the time of my review, and the highest tier, the "Digital Premium" edition listed at $58.49 instead of $90 USD retail. At least the highest tier which includes everything is under $60, but it's still not worth it even for that price.

_childDocuments_.review: Personally, I don't really understand the large amount of negative English reviews that I'm seeing so far. A lot of vague nonsense about being a "budget title" without bothering to mention how, saying a game is bad because you don't like the DLC practices (which should be considered review-bombing, as it has no bearing whatsoever on the quality of the game), one person saying it's a good game but not as good as some other RPG they played, so it's not recommended (one guess if comments are allowed on THAT one), and other such nonsense with no expansion whatsoever on the point. Just words vomited onto a review and posted for the world to see. Though I haven't been able to finish the game yet due to work and other personal issues, so far, I've had a pretty fun time. +Sabbaths are a pretty cool mechanic in lieu of press turns, which makes enemies having skills like Beast Eye far less painful. +The AI seems pretty smart for the most part, and difficulty is fairly well balanced on Normal. Combat itself is fun and crisp, which given Atlus's track record shouldn't surprise anyone.+The characters are all pretty believable and interact well with one another, matching the chemistry of Persona 4 Golden, in my humble opinion.+Adults being the focus of the story is a HUGE plus for me. Actual adult concerns and issues are brought up and dealt with, which is a nice change of pace from teenagers solving everything. +Good voice acting, music (mostly), and audio mixing, though Atlus is almost always good at these, so that's a bit of a given.+Story seems pretty good so far. It feels like there are actual stakes and the threat actually beats the heroes to the punch far more often than not. You're playing catch-up the entire time, and you can really feel it.-The DLC is mostly superfluous, though I like the anti-grinding DLC personally, as my limited time isn't conducive to long grind session. I actually like the DLC story so far, so that one was also worth it.-Character dungeons are a good idea, but boringly designed, and NOBODY likes teleporter puzzles. They were bad in Pokemon two decades ago, they're bad now. Stop it. Get some help.-The navigator. I like navigators in Atlus games, most of the time. This is not one of those times. -The "Dangerous" enemies have weird level scaling and appear far too often when I'm exploring character dungeons. Tone it down a little bit, maybe.-I can only hear the do-♥♥♥ theme in one store. I love that theme, Atlus. Let me play it anywhere.

_childDocuments_.review: There are a lot to complain in this game, but I'll be somewhat brief by focusing myself on the major thing that can at least allow you to endure the rest of the game. Like, for example, their previous game: Shin Megami Tensei V; which had an enjoyable (but still flawed) battle system, while having a mediocre (if not nonexistant) story. A disappointing game, yet not one I dropped. For your information, I played a fair share of Shin Megami Tensei and Persona titles already; my review will be based on these standards and knowledge. Let's talk "battle mechanics".Shin Megami Tensei/Persona games are reknowned for their iteration of the PressTurn system, be it variations of it, or unique branches like the OneMore system in Persona. Mechanics that allow you, AND your enemy, to accentuate the need of utilizing weakness to capitalize the number of turns. Discovering weaknesses, focusing on them, multiplying turns, disabling theirs of the adversary, but also available for your enemies... In short, a double-edged, (variably) complex but rewarding system, that can be used by you OR your foes; an equal foot for everyone.Now, Soul Hackers 2, and the Sabbath mechanic: hit weaknesses to boost an obligatory "big" attack at the end of *every* turn. That is all. No real variation, nor an enemy version. Not something to plan, but something automatic, and one-sided. A sadly simple and boringly linear mechanic that becomes uninteresting and impressively repetitive by the 10th fight. Adding to that the (pretty cool but) annoyingly long animation —and I repeat: EVERY turn— that you will start to —by the 10th fight— to skip. And that, is why I can't bring myself to continue this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Soul Hackers 2 is probably the most derivative megaten game that I've played. There's not much to set it apart from any other title in the franchise, and while it does do everything somewhat competently, it doesn't do anything particularly outstanding. The sabbath mechanic is similar to demon co-op from strange journey, map navigation is similar to Tokyo Mirage Sessions, you control humans with demons attached like in Persona, it has a set of dungeons similar to Mementos in Persona 5 that I literally thought were randomly generated because of how boring and samey their aesthetic was. The most unique thing about Soul Hackers 2 is the story which is fine? I do really like the characters but for whatever reason the overarching narrative just wasn't that gripping to me. At around 40 hours long this game is one of the shorter games in the megaten franchise that I've played.My three main gripes with the game are the Soul Matrix, the character voice lines and the DLC.As I said before the Soul Matrix dungeons are literally identical to one another and they are astoundingly boring. There's a billion side missions to do in here so that you keep trudging around the same endless gray platforms for hours. The game's skill unlocks are also partially tied to it. If you want to be more effective in combat and get cool skills, you MUST do this dungeon regularly. I can't exaggerate how ludicrous the character voice line play rate is. The navigator will tell you every single time that an enemy has appeared "An enemy!," that they're running at you "Be careful!." and that you're safe after you hit them "Now we can relax." It happens EVERY SINGLE TIME. Once you get into a battle the fun doesn't end, because nearly every action you take or button you press in the battle screen will trigger a voice line. Sometimes multiple characters saying lines on top of each other! For me, using the menu in a quick and efficient way is one of the most satisfying parts of a JRPG, and it really gets on your nerves constantly hearing voice lines play. It was so egregious that I actually just muted voices altogether a couple hours into the game. If you can have fun without voice acting and let the music carry battles and scenes, then I highly reccommend playing this way as well unless you can somehow withstand the barrage of voices telling you what to do.The last thing I want to touch on is the day 1 dlc for this game. ♥♥♥♥ you Atlus. The dlc issues that plague this company are downright insulting. SMT V had a superboss and iconic demons locked behind dlc, and Soul Hackers 2 has extra story and dungeon content PLUS demons, seemingly picked at random, also locked behind a paywall. If you decide to buy this game, don't buy the DLC. Please don't support this anti-consumer ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.Putting that aside, overall Soul Hackers 2 is a very okay game. It could have literally any other name and still be a good Atlus JRPG, but for some reason they went with the soul hackers branding. If you have played basically every other megaten game then pick this up and you'll probably enjoy it, but the rest of Atlus's catalogue far exceeds Soul Hackers 2.

_childDocuments_.review: Sometimes changing an established formal can be good, other times it's annoying. Soul Hackers 2 is a strange mix of both. For new-new comers to the series, many of the changes may seem weird, but nothing annoying. For anyone else whose coming off the heels of SMTV/any other SMT game, they can put a real damper on your enjoyment.For starters, you can't recruit demons via talking anymore, only through demon recon and it's random too. This means that 8/10 any time you recruit a demon it's one that you already have. With how rare demon recruit nords are, it's a MASSIVE waste of time. Even more so when you're trying to farm.Fusion skills have also changed, now skills can only be passed down if the new demon has an affinity for it.  Which, the game does a poor job of telling. But the biggest change is the (lack of) press turn, this changes battles on a fundamental level. In other games, you would avoid hitting a demon's resistance because it would mean losing you're extra turns. Now? It doesn't matter! Not only does hitting a demon's resistance not affect turns, it still does a good bit of damage. Thankfully, the characters, music, and setting more than make up for all this. This is not a game you buy at full price, this a game you get on sale. Oh, and the DLC is terrible, all of it full stop. Don't pay for demons that are main stays of the series and the exp items break the game. The costumes don't even show up in the overworld.

_childDocuments_.review: As far as I’m concerned, it always feels like a special occasion when an Atlus JRPG comes out on PC as I really like their  franchise. With that said, I’ve never had the chance to play any of the titles in the  line, so basically  was kind of an entry point for me.In general, I wasn’t disappointed, although it would feel more appropriate to give this one a so-so hand sign instead of a thumbs up if it was available. The whole time it felt like I was somewhere halfway between the  and  games I’ve had the chance to play so far, in a sense that the story, the characters and the art style was closer to the former, whereas the dungeons and actual gameplay reminded me of the latter. The turn-based battle system is more or less as you would expect if you’re familiar with any of the aforementioned series, focusing on using demons and exploiting element weaknesses. It’s fun, but still, I would have loved a bit more innovation here to shake things up sometimes, at least during boss fights. Also, be prepared for a loooot of running around in similar-looking, monotonous corridors and subway tunnels… Unfortunately, there’s not much variety when it comes to level designs, which is a shame.What I genuinely loved, however, were the characters, especially the protagonist, who is not a mute, blank slate that requires others to communicate for her, which is quite often the case in these games. Between battles and cutscenes you also have a chance to get to know your party members better, but don’t expect as much social interaction between them as in . And, of course, we also have the Demon Compendium, the absolute essential part of any title in the franchise, so catch and fuse ‘em all, if you can, I guess.All in all, I didn’t regret the time I spent with , even if its content feels much lighter than what I expected. There’s just not enough of anything, but what we have is OK. Nothing to write home about, though.

_childDocuments_.review: Many small issues and a few bigger issues.As of 2022/09/11, several game crashes are still in the game with no word I've found on fixing them or acknowledging them.If you have loading tips on, especially on auto, it significantly increases your load time.Game is not optimized well. (Whether or not Denuvo has a part is unknown). The game has an abnormally long starting load. This seems to be mitigated somewhat by disabling tips on load screens, oddly.Premium Costume DLC and Preorder DLC was broken for several days.Some missing QoL, such as the ability to cancel fast travel if you accidentally activate it and the inability to fast travel to certain locations.Not a huge minus, but some content is locked behind NG+Certain things are tedious, such as clearing "New" quest marks.Recruiting new demons feels a bit too much RNG based, particularly at the start. This is mitigated later in the game, but initially, you can kill 100 of a demon and end up getting a different demon that you've never encountered before despite the game suggesting that more kills = higher chance. This is on top of recruitment events already being somewhat random. Limited battle music options. (You can choose one song or random, you can't select which ones you want).Game auto-pauses when you switch windows, so you can't even do things during load screens.Some QoL stuff is locked behind active skills with relatively short durations and cost MP.Some of the keyboard controls are somewhat awkward and seem to be designed for controller, such as scrollbars not acting as scrollbars.Minimap options are somewhat limited as you have zoom in, zoom out, or disabled. There is no partial minimap option or real minimap transparency options.There are times where the text log just doesn't work.Battle speedup is locked behind Auto-Battle and only works if activated before the attack. There is no visible option to have the speedup activated separately.In one section of the game, you have forced camera angles. In one spot, because of camera angle swapping, it is very difficult to move as the controls keep changing due to the angle swapping.And more.

_childDocuments_.review: The game looks great and Ringo is a great protagonist, however the gameplay itself is extremely boring. The lack of press turns of even the 1-more system and being replaced with sabbaths hurts the game as there is no turn manipulation like the other games, leading to just hit weakness for more damage. Having no way to get Demons through battle is another bad choice as it leaves the only purpose for battles to gain exp which complied with the bosses being very easy leads to the player skipping most battles. Replacing chests with Demons is cool but most of the time it's not useful as it's either a demon you own or is too high level or healing which you can teleport away and any time to do.The dungeons all feel very samey and boring, just long hallways and turns filled with the exact same shadow enemy every 2 seconds and Mimi screaming the same quotes again and again incessantly with no option to turn her off. The teleporting dungeons in the Soul Matrix 3/4 are god awful and only exist to waste time. I have no idea why they kept the exact same colour scheme for all character's soul matrix and didn't even bother to change the colour like Red/Purple/Green. The Day-1 DLC is atrociously overpriced for almost nothing of value. The new dungeon is just as boring as the rest, most of the side quests are "go back to area and beat a reskinned boss". The costumes, music and regular demons like Satan and Mara should have just been a part of the base game. The grinding DLC is the worst offender and I'm almost sure they added it just so you could stand a chance against the overleveled DLC final boss that you stand no chance of beating at the level you should actually be at the time you fight it or because they knew how dull fighting felt and minimised it when there is actually a rare hard boss.I would also like to mention how the "demon affinity" system just kinda sucks and doesn't add anything to the game other than making fusing more annoying because the closest 7 demons to your level all can't learn a Force skill so you're stuck using a subpar demon or losing that element. SMT V's system where they could learn it but with higher MP cost and lower damage was much better and the feel of everything being done better in SMT V lingers on throughout the whole game.Misc notes: I really like the portraits lip syncing and faces changing mid sentence along with the 3D models also matching. Walking is slow as hell and complied with the dungeons that feel worse than even Persona 3/4's makes it feel like even more of a chore. No High or even Medium damage Ruin skills make them completely fall off mid/late game as not only is the damage bad but almost all the bosses are immune to the effects. I'm not sure why bosses even bother using Beast Eye and don't just have 2 moves flat out like the some of the DLC Bosses or the Final Boss having 3. All the enemies in the dungeon having the same shadowy glitchy model is confusing considering how they already had overworld chasing models for 95% of the Demons in SMT V. The side quest are some of the worst I have experienced with them all being either a fetch quest or beat up X guys but only after you finish the area and give terrible rewards. Meals are a neat addition but the game never feels like you need them.The story, music and characters are mostly all just okay apart from Saizo and especially Ringo who carries the game. While the game isn't bad it is a huge let down comparing it to what came before making the game feel empty and boring.

_childDocuments_.review: Guess I´ll keep this short. The overall experience was around 6/10 in my opinion.After finally getting my hands on and devouring Persona 4, I decided to check and see what else Atlus has been up to. I´d never even hear d of Soul Hackers before this and from the demo footage it looked kinda cool. Now it´s 60 something hours later, and my opinion boils down to a resounding ''meh''. The story itself starts of well enough, introducing interesting concepts and showing a fair bit of promise. Unfortunately it seems content to never really explore some plot points, there are a fair few cases of loose threads just being left hanging, and by the halfway point it seems as if the story was being rushed violently to it´s conclusion. The characters likewise show a lot of promise, and in true Atlus style there are a few systems in place to help the player spend time with and get to know them better. Unfortunately I never found myself becoming invested in any of them, and any character motivations came of as fairly dull at best. There are a fair few things to enjoy about them on the surface, but when you begin to dig there really isn´t to much to find.As for the gameplay itself it should be nothing to unfamiliar from Persona, although it felt more akin to Shin Megami Tensei. You have a fairly decent hub world to explore, various NPCs to interact with, quests to complete, it´s all here. the demon summoning allows for a fair bit of customization, depending on the situation at hand and a persons playstyle. Each character has strengths and weaknesses that can be offset to a degree, but never enough as to remove their individual identities. There is a bit of an issue of character dialogue getting quite repetitive, and that problem unfortunately persists throughout the entire game. I found myself playing the game more with the sound turned off during the more grindy sections, with the final boss suffering badly from this problem.Main story line is relatively straightforward and easy to track. Most all of the plot twists that occurred are anything but subtle, although I will give the game props for one or two that did catch me by surprise. The side quests are your standard fair for these kinds of games, but I will give props for the NPC´s actually being given character development. A fair few will give multiple side quests of similar nature, but with an overarching story all of their own the progresses along with the main story.I could speak of this game further, but as a whole this feels as though it is one is a hit-or-miss kind of situation. I can´t say I enjoyed it particularly, but that does no mean the game has no redeemable qualities. Far from it. I would say if you´re a fan of Atlus´ other work, I´d say you should think about giving this one a look. Definitely not one I would recommend paying full price for, but do pick it up when it goes on sale and give it a whirl. I can´t in good conscience recommend going out of your way to complete it, but if you just stick to the main story and a few side quests, I believe it should help to kill a few hours.It by no means should be compared to it´s siblings, but taken as it´s own thing. An interesting venture into exciting waters, but ultimately it seems more interested in floating on stagnating waters, rather than raising the sails and catching it´s wind.I would love to see what this series could become with some time and a fair bit of polish.

_childDocuments_.review: this is a good game. i like all of the characters, the dialogue is good, i'm a fan of the gameplay systems the music is very solid. soul hackers 2 is a game between the styles of persona and mainline SMT, but while it does lean quite a bit more into the mainline end of things, i think if you're using this as a bridge between the series, it's much easier to cross it starting from the persona side. there's a lot of little exclusive things its missing from a mainline game that a persona players wouldn't pay much mind to being missing, such as demon negotiation and more in-depth dungeons. as someone who stems much more from the persona side, while i can't say that those systems were replaced by anything more interesting, i will say i didn't mind as much that they weren't present. the characters are definitely the best part of the game for me. there's only 4 party members, but all of them get generous amounts of attention, are expanded upon in an interesting way, have actual conflict between them, and don't get neglected as their arc passes. the 'hangout' system to interact with your party members outside of the main story also feels satisfying and paced well. ringo as the main, fully voiced protagonist was done fantastically, and i never felt like she did or said anything a player would disapprove of, while also staying interesting and multi-faceted. the main cast being all adults also served and improved the story, and its refreshing to not have to play as a bunch of high schoolers in a jrpg.i did enjoy the story a lot, i think it played very well into the characters backgrounds and over the course of the game, had an interesting message and made the game more memorable to me. there were motifs throughout that constantly developed the characters even more, showing different sides of them as the story struck their nerves. i'll concede that the overall story was pretty predictable, but there were moments that did genuinely surprise me without being ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. speaking of which, the story did not rely on an "i have amnesia but i will suddenly be able to remember an important plot detail in the third act" moment, which is a plus.there were some definite downsides of the game though, some that i sympathise with, and others that didn't affect me much but i understand. one of the bigger ones is a DLC with a "bonus story arc", which i genuinely cannot defend. the arc itself i believe is great, but the fact that it's day 1 DLC with a significant amount of story content is a bit ridiculous. granted, it is just a side quest that isn't directly mandatory for the main story, but it is by far the most in depth side quest in the game. the dungeons seem like the biggest complaint, as they don't have many grand set pieces, can be repetitive and even maze-like. while i believe all of those aspects, it didn't impact my experience as much, as that's usually something i'm not too interested in anyways. this combined with the demon negotiations being absent is probably more ignorable if you're predominantly a persona player (tartarus moment). i will defend the sabbath system to the death though, it's fun as ♥♥♥♥ and gets expanded upon with skills, it's awesome. overall, i love this game a lot. i played it a while ago and it's still lingering in my mind. it's small scale comparing to other jrpgs (even by atlus alone) but its style and lack of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ moments makes it both memorable and respectable (and fun) enough to recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: -first impressions-First of all I got the $89 version because I know I will pour enough time into it personally to justify the price. I am recommending this as a game on its own and not the major issues surrounding its release trust me I will tell you how stupid it is. Here is the quick version of what I want to say. Maybe I'll add more to this later but I got ♥♥♥♥ to do and so do you.   -Soul Hackers 2 is an absolute must play if and only if you are a fan of Megaten games there is subtle and not so subtle fan service to the og Soul hackers and devil summoners -If you aren't super involved and interested in the franchise some mechanics will take you a minute to fully grasp (as a Megaten game it is easy, as a normal turn based JRPG it's probably around average to a little above average in terms of difficulty)-if you have only ever played a persona game please please PLEASE temper your expectations. This is not persona the scope of this game isn't and wasn't ever meant to be on the same level of persona. (hence why its dumb to price it as such from a PR perspective)  -it’s a 7.5/10-story is good, combat is great, OST character design and art style is orgasmic-dungeons don’t have a whole lot of window dressing much in the same vein of a classic Megaten game. The star of the show is what you're doing, not where you are doing it. there isn't a whole lot going on in the dungeons themselves. enemies are frequent and will always be riding youNow unrelated to the game but the issues surrounding its release.-ATLUS fumbled the bag with the collectors edition of this release through Shop ATLUS. fact of the matter is a lot of us never got a chance but it honestly is a blessing in disguise -Day one DLC for a triple A priced game that isn’t supposed to be on the same scope of one of their major titles such as SMT V or P5R is total ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and is on par for ATLUS as many of us should know by now. -this game should not be priced at $60 in any universe if you want my opinion on what this should be priced at. $40 for a standard edition $50 maybe $60 if you really have to have the Day one DLCThe day one DLC itself is nothing special. The items are helpful for busting out grinding but should honestly be free. The demons are very nice. Overpriced at $12.99 but nice, the models  for them are wonderful and they are all packaged as one. I would have no complaints (especially because ATLUS tends to package extra demons like this) except for the fact Namissa is locked behind the paywall. Someone who should already be a character we interact with in the story anyways and could've been someone we battle to recruit I.E Demi fiend and Ruido/Dante style, that's when they bust out the OG soul hackers battle music could've been ♥♥♥♥♥♥ sick. Speaking of music we have the worst offender. The music and costume pack, $12.99 ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ batman! The music is enjoyable and the costumes look nice but $12.99? I was born at night, not last night. The lost numbers is supposedly Inconsequential to the story which is probably more of a good thing I mean, you'd be pissed if important plot related details were locked behind a $10 paywall  Overall the Day one DLC sucks but ATLUS is a business and the winning faction inside the company right now is on the side of “make the most amount of money” and they know they can get away with it -edit #1- ATLUS has further fumbled the bag even more with breaking the DLC if you happened to get it through a 3rd party key seller in some cases. I don’t have this issue because I bought the $90 version but the issue needs to be addressed and also reflected upon in this section of my review until such a time passes where ATLUS resolves the issue. -end of edit #1-If you are gonna refund and wait for it to get cheaper I wouldn't count on it getting super low %15 off max knowing how reluctant ATLUS is to push it super low.
