_childDocuments_.review: The more I play the more the flaws annoy me. There is nothing outright terrible about the game but also nothing great. It's a solid 3/5 game and worth a pick up once it has a deeper sale. Steam just has no neutral rating.The combat is simple. I like the sabbath idea but it's weird that critical hits don't naturally build it up. You also rarely actually kill enemies with it which is the how you effect negotiations. Enemies don't have their own sabbath system and there is no penalty for hitting or being hit for a weakness or immunity. Just feels like babies first SMT game. Damage scaling is annoying since you just do less damage to things higher leveled to you and they'll just wipe the floor with you. Usually you can tactically work around this with null/absorb to waste turns but nope game over.Each of the four characters specializes in certain things IF you bother to go through the soul matrix (essentially Tartarus or Mementos) While that is a good idea in theory the majority of these things take until the end of the game to fully develop. Most of which directly effect the sabbath system leading to just an overall lackluster system. The characters naturally have no abilities so you need demons to take advantage of this. Starting on the 3rd floor I believe it goes full troll and has all teleporters and only gets worse on each floor. Not fun or challenging just annoying.The fusion system can be extremely annoying to pass on certain skills. The game tells you demons that are weak to something can never inherent those skills. But the game has hidden stuff that won't allow you to transfer some things no matter what. Since our characters need certain skills to be most useful this just leads me to not always fusing new demons since I can't pass on what I want. Strangely enough it's like the developers knew this and your demons level up pretty fast and aren't outclassed easily like normal.Demon negotiations being RNG on the map is annoying. One you have no control over when it happens and two they seem to always give me demons I already have when I want to restock to fuse. You can kind of get around this by eating a specific meal to boost the rate. I liked when you demons would sometimes just give up and try and join you in past games but that doesn't happen here. They don't troll you and take your stuff if you say yes they will join every time. The movement speed is unbelievably slow. There is an ability later in the game to move faster but it isn't a passive and doesn't last long. Near the end of the game this isn't that big of a deal when you have tons of MP and can passively restore it. Moving around the map is dumb you have multiple stores you can warp to but it doesn't just go into the store just right in front of it. You have to go to Axis then inside it to get to the soul matrix. Why not just have a tab for the matrix since there is nothing in Axis 95% of the time?The sidequests are almost all pointless from a narrative perspective and for the rewards. The only ones worth doing are the ones that give you hangout events but you don't know that until after you complete them. I would suggest looking at a guide if you aren't feeling it.The lore/world building for the game is also pretty lacking. No build up for either faction and it pretty much is summoner=bad no matter how you look at it.The only real positive is Ringo is voiced and has a bit of an actual personality. The drawback is none of the characters (including her) are that memorable. The only decent thing is two of the characters just don't like each other for most of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Soul Hackers 2 is definitely the most polarizing entry in Atlus' JRPG lineup that I've personally played. There's a lot of good here but also a fair amount of bad. I'm going to get the parts of the game I do not like out of the way first so anyone reading this knows what the sour parts of the game were for me personally and then can weigh it against the later positives in order to make a decision on whether or not to buy it.- ConsThe dungeon design in this game is abysmal. Dungeon's like these would have been expected back in the early Playstation 1 days but nowadays? No. Dungeons are linear, boring, and repetitive. The biggest offender of it for me is the "Soul Matrix" side dungeon that allows you to unlock skills for members of your party. The rewards for getting through it are worth it, but it's a slog every step of the way. Genuinely would rather go through Tartarus in P3 again instead of dealing with another obnoxious teleporter "puzzle".The story is painfully short. I beat the entire game in just under 50 hours and that's with me doing every request, getting 91% on the compendium, upgrading my weapons to the max etc. Point is, I did almost everything. I really wish there was a bit more of the main story present in this game as it is the more interesting part of the game. The requests are all basically boiled down to "go here, do one of three things, go back." Very few of the requests are unique and the ones that are do not stand out at all.Lastly, day 1 DLC. While I didn't buy the game on day 1, the fact that DLC was released for it on its release date that added a decent chunk of story and content is extremely cringe. Atlus please stop cutting content just to resell it as DLC. - ProsThe soundtrack for this game goes hard. Really hard. Unsurprising considering most of the music Atlus does goes hard, but it should be stated nonetheless. Characters are all well written and fun. While my opinion of some characters at the start was a bit mixed, towards the end of the game I genuinely really liked and cared for all of them. Ringo in particular is by far my favorite protag Atlus has made so far. I really like the snarky personality she was given, she's fun to listen to and I like how she interacts with the other members of the party a lot.Story while short is good, I just wish there was more of it like I said before. It has some really good twists I wasn't expecting and some pretty good story beats. Genuinely one of the better written stories Atlus has made in recent years.

Don't use them unless you wanna ruin the first playthrough of your game being overpowered.The bonus story pack should have just been apart of the base game, I don't know why it isn't and its locked behind a garbage 13.49$ CAD for how little it adds to the actual game. the content itself is fine. _childDocuments_.review: Having played the game for another 20 hours, I just wanted to add a little more detail on how I felt about the game now that I've gotten both endings, and beat everything in the DLC.  Overall, I still can't recommend the game in its current state.  That being said, some things got better and some things got worse as the game went on -- I've left my original review below.What got better: the party/demon composition customization.  As the game progresses, you get access to more demons with sabbath abilities.  This means that when the demon joins the stack -- that ability can trigger.  Having these abilities is a MUST (in my opinion) for one of the DLC bosses, and allows for a lot more customization in terms of having demons in your stock you don't plan on using directly.  In addition, as time goes on you unlock more Mystiques and more Mystique slots.  Again, this allows your attacks to target specific features of each fight, allowing for tons of customization before going into battle.  For example, some mystiques make your attacks more effective against enemy weaknesses, so if there are some enemies you need to take out fast, you might want to equip these instead of mystiques that increase overall power.What felt the same: the story.  If anything, I think it ran out of steam a bit as I got to the end of the game.  And I did all the grinding (which got way worse) after getting the "endings" (i.e., I just left the DLC until the end), so I don't think my loss of momentum on the story came from the massive grind to beat the DLC superboss.What got worse: the grinding (this is really a problem for the DLC superboss -- for the base game, I didn't really do any grinding).  Holy moly.  If you want to get all the materials upgrading your COMP, you're going to have to hunt down specific demons in specific locations.  And these might be low level demons you just didn't fight in some early game dungeon.  Thankfully, there's a comp upgrade that lets you target certain demons, but this can be just beyond tedious.  Further, I tried fighting the DLC superboss at level 95 and felt like I had no hope.  After grinding to level 97 it felt close, and it was beatable at level 98 (with my possibly flawed strategy).  I did this without going to new game plus -- and maybe that would make it less painful -- but the long grind up to level 98 was just not fun in any way shape or form, fighting the same risky enemies over and over again... and the final set of risky enemies have stat debuffing effects.  This doesn't make the fight too hard, but just makes it drag on as if you don't remove your accuracy debuffs you can't hit them, and if you don't remove your attack debuffs it takes forever to bring them down.I was playing on Hard mode, but maybe on normal the grinding is less necessary?  Overall, this was the worst part of the game for me.  Especially because I paid extra for it!-------Original review: I really wanted to like this game -- but overall I just find it a bit boring -- maybe the issue is that I'm holding it to the standard of other Atlas games which I've liked a lot more (P2, P3, P4, P5, SMT III, SMT V), but I didn't have fun with it, and that's enough for me to not recommend.  First, the good: The art is appealing. The character design and voice acting is great -- I like how Ringo is an actual character instead of a silent protagonist.  The music has some high points.  There's a lot of ways to set up your team (demons, affinities and equipment can be swapped) and the sabbath system is emphasizes different tactics than the press-turn/one-more systems.  So, where did it go wrong?  In no particular order:A) The city -- there's just nothing going on.  Compare to e.g., persona 5, where you can go to the batting cages, play darts, fish, etc.  Or compare to persona 3 where you get to watch everything change as more of the lost show up.  B) The dungeons -- they are super linear, especially the soul matrix.  Just run around until you go to every possible spot and you're done.  I think the SMT games have better puzzles and the Persona games have better style.   Also, I don't like how Ringo's character model takes up ~30% of the screen when you're running around (compare again to other SMT games where the character models are much smaller and therefore it's easier to see what's going on).C) The combat -- I played on hard mode and still didn't find much of a challenge here.  Compare to SMT III remaster where you're regularly going to have some really tough fights.  The fact that you can warp out at any time to refresh hp/mp means you don't need to do resource management like in the persona games where you want to finish everything in one day.  And there's some just plain annoying things like that mothman who drains your MP when you run into him (and again, you can just warp out to refresh, so this is more of an inconvenience than a difficulty spike).D) The main story -- I don't want to add any spoilers here, but I just found it uninspired.  The individual character arcs are more interesting, but the soul matrix is so boring it's almost not worth grinding through it to get there. E) DLC story -- I also didn't find the lost numbers story interesting.  But, if you want to fight the superboss, you're going to have to get through it.For way less $$ you can get P3 portable or SMT III.  I'd say go for those instead.

_childDocuments_.review: This game does so many things right that it's a shame that the final product is weighed down by bad decisions and poor performance. Story and characters are interesting, voice-acting is great, art direction is cool, but the gameplay is too thin and a step back from more recent SMT games. Taking away the extra turns from hitting weaknesses and replacing it with the Sabbath system has dumbed down the strategy greatly. It's just hit weaknesses, get free damage at end of turn, repeat. Add to that the limited move list for every demon, little variation in enemy encounters, and it just feels like a mobile game; a far cry from the strategy and careful balancing in the core SMT or Persona games. Beyond that there are the side quests, which are MMO-style fetch or kill affairs. Boring, uninteresting slogs, every single one. Under-cooked is the term that came to mind. Occasionally a dungeon will spawn an elite or treasure enemy, which are basically pointless because the elite enemies are just regular demons that are 5+ levels higher than the party and the treasure monsters were regular demons that you can't ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ hit no matter how much you buff your aim. To top this off there are strange quality of life issues. When moving around town protagonist Ringo will take a few slow-down steps after the player releases the stick like she just sprinted the hundred meters. Navigating to the world map can not be cancelled, a selection must be made, and from there a load screen. And the load times for a game that has smaller maps and poorer graphics than SMT5 on the Switch are longer than they really should be. Overall this is not a horrible game, but a decent one done poorly, something I don't expect from the series or publisher and will probably be my most disappointing game of the year.

_childDocuments_.review: I am a big fan of the Persona series so Soul Hacker being another spin off of the Megami Tensei games peeked my interest. The cyberpunk aesthetic is well done and the main cast is interesting enough. But the dungeons are boring,grindy, drawn out and feel dated. It feels like a chore to get through. The boss battles are actually quiet tough and engaging but I found myself not wanting to come back to this based on the dungeon design alone. I'm not sure I will even finish this game, let alone recommend it to anyone else.-Update after Further Play: I've come to the conclusion that this is a 10 hour game that the higher ups said needed to be 30+ hours. This game does so many things to waste your time. By default there's a 5-10 second loading screen between each area that can be turned off in the options and suddenly everything loads instantly. Exp and money gain from combat feels like they are about half of what they should be in order to force you to fight a ton of encounters just to stay leveled near what you should be. Dungeons have lengthy paths that serve no purpose and there seems to be very little unique items or rewards for exploring. The dungeons themselves are the most bland things I've seen in a while and the repetitive audio every time you see an enemy is enough to mute the whole game.  The story is decent but not worth it unless you love grinding turn based fights for the sake of it. The only good aspects of the game are the combat & fusion systems that exists in other SMT/Persona games. Do yourself a favor and just go play Persona 5.

_childDocuments_.review: First off, I'm using the version of the game including all DLCs. Like I usually would have done, I cheesed it and level grinded my party to 99 early on, so I've been able to auto-battle most stuff. This was made easier by the fact that one of the DLCs lets you toggle the dropping of level-boosting items from each encounter, but I would have done the same thing even if it took me longer, so it was really just a timesaver. A friend who's also playing it has taken about the same amount of playtime to reach where I am now while barely using the DLC content, so I imagine it must not be that difficult of a game compared to mainline SMT.Story, and especially characters, are top-notch. I never want to play a silent SMT protag again after this. In contrast to Persona (except P2:EP), all the main cast are adults and have adult problems and deal with them in a mostly-adult manner. I played with the English dub, which was excellent, although I'm planning to do NG+ with Japenese audio to compare. The graphics are also excellent, in my personal, amateurish evaluation. The music - done by MONACA, the people who did the music for the Nier series and Drakengard 3 - is also great, aside from one or two tracks that I felt were repetitive. The weakest point is probably the mostly-optional side-dungeon design, which is very same-y. The layouts of the dungeons are fixed, and early dungeons are pretty straightforward, but later dungeons have gimmicks. All in all, although I haven't beaten it to 100% completion yet, I like the game a lot and would definitely recommend it!If you're starting out, however, you'll want to adjust certain options in the config menu from the title screen before you start, since you won't be able to actually access the in-game menu until partway through the tutorial level. Namely:-Set Ringo to center instead of left screen-Make the camera distance further from her-Set Loading Screen Tips to display (button advance), which will remove 90% of load screen time

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyed the game. Had a few issues but overall a good game that does a lot of things better than a lot of other recent Atlus games. First off, the graphics. I love the visual style of this game. Its like P5 with its comic book aesthetic, but dialed to 100. The colors pop out very well. All the characters look extremely vibrant. My greatest praise goes to the demons. While using the same models as P5 and SMTV, with the use of colors and textures the demons look better then they ever have been. Going back to P5 after this makes that game look kinda dull. One thing this game does worse than P5 though is the UI design. P5 still clears this game in that sense, but the UI is still miles better than SMTV. The music is also very good. Its not as good as the previous atlus game, but there still are a lot of good songs. The jewelery shop theme, all three of the boss themes, and the hideout theme come to mind the most. The reason for lack of songs is probably budget. Now for gameplay. I am going to get the negatives out of the way first. The dungeons suck. But, they arent as bad as people say. People went through p3 and p4's dungeons, and never complained, even though they were way worse. And do not tell me those games are old so its okay, all the Atlus games that preceded p3 and p4 had way better dungeons. While the dungeons in this game are bland mazes, they function as a place to do combat, which imo is amazing. The combat in this game is amazing. I know people complained about human party members, but this game does them perfectly. Demons in this game function like Personas. You equip them to party members and they give you stat boosts, skills, and elemental affinities. How this is different than the modern Persona games is that finally every party member can change out their demon. In P3 having mc being the only one with more than one persona worked because of the AI party members, in p4 and p5 it sucked. All the party members might as well not be there as there is zero customization to them while the mc just does everything. It is so lame. Instead SH2 works like the older persona games, where you only have four party members who are all extremely customizable. Not only can each member freely use any demon, you can also customize them by increasing their elemental affinities and giving them accessories so each party member feels different. This customization goes into the gameplay as it really does have that SMT feel of making the perfect party to fight the boss, making it very satisfying. Managing your demons by fusing them is as fun as ever, especially since they brought back smtiv's fusion search functions. Ringo's Aion skills also add a lot of strategy. They allow fast swapping out of demons like in Persona, but puts a limit on it so its not OP. Another Aion skill is increasing stacks, which segways into the main battle mechanic. The Sabbath system. In this system when you get a weakness you build a stack. At the end of your turns you summon a demon for each stack and you can do an all out attack for a lot of damage. I really like this system since it becomes a puzzle for getting the most stacks. Later on you will unlock Aion skills and passive upgrades which give more stacks depending on if certain conditions are met. It becomes a puzzle to see how high you can get the stack. Now for story, I will keeo it brief to avoid spoilers. I really liked it. Its simple, has good twists, and is very personable to the characters. The characters are all interesting with their motives, and the writing quality is a leaps better than P5's (p5's writing is doo doo so ig its not a high bar). This game avoids p5's writing pitfalls by not having mean spirited humor, making all characters equally shine, and also being more concise. Characters mostly do not repeat the same plot points a million times. I also find the plot point of most people yearning the apocalypse interesting. Is it the best story ever told: no. But imo the plot still clears smtv, and persona 3-5.Overall I recommend this game. My only issues are the dungeons, and I guess the lack of budget. The side content also has that feeling but it still reinforces the satisfying gameplay loop. Another issue is the dlc, which is disgusting I agree. I still think the base game is good enough though, also p5 had 80 dollars worth of dlc which had even more overly priced costumes and op personas but no one cared for some reason. In short, if you like the gameplay side of smt with fun battles, and if you like simple but satisfying stories, you will probablt like this game. Most of the issues are budget issues, and overall I was able to look past them. The hate is overblown for this game, reminds me of the TLOU2 hate, where people were more mad because the game wasnt what they were expecting. If this game interests you, please play it.

_childDocuments_.review: A handful of flaws, but a solid game otherwise.If you go into this game with the lens of it's not gonna be as great as mainline SMT or Persona, it's actually quite fun. I loved the characters, thought the camera work and animation were wonderful (on top of the fact that, according to what I've seen, this is the first game where ATLUS ACTUALLY ANIMATED ENGLISH LIP SYNCING, HELL FREAKING YES), enjoyed the combat (though some of it needs work, namely enemy balance and the amount of grinding you need to to), and the story was nice and had plenty of good writing in it.HOWEVERIt is far from glorious. Some of the dungeons (especially in the endgame) are horribly designed and made me legit look up a guide just to navigate through them, which for basic map design with zero puzzles should not happen. The game forces you to grind a lot, which is thankfully easier to do with the character Axes areas, but it's still a drag. And I played this game before they released the QoL update, which took over TWO MONTHS to come out and adds damn near necessities for a JRPG, like a freaking RUN BUTTON.It has its flaws, major and minor. But the people who say it's the worst thing ever are very much exaggerating it. I enjoyed the game as a fresh, new experience, using the demons I loved from SMT and the gameplay design of ATLUS I've known for years. I think it could've been great, but some of the decisions they made regarding endgame stuff and the flow not really having a hook to it (I lost motivation to play this game 4 times over the course of 2 months, most good games I finish I only lose motivation to do so one time, if at all) shot the game down in the end. Again, it's still good, but could be a lot better. 7/10.

_childDocuments_.review: I think this is a great game and is very much worth buying. Not for kids unless they are older and pretty jaded. Gameplay is Persona and SMT style and very enjoyable. Some of the DLC is good, but it is not must buy and with the exception of the cosmetics, can be attained in game. The game is rated Mature for violence, partial nudity, strong language, and blood and gore. The violence is characters laying in pools of blood, a character getting impaled through the chest, and a dismembered body part. There are scenes with on of the main characters with no clothing covered with a sheet, and scantily clad female demons. One of the demons is a phallic H.R. Geiger-esque monster. They drop the F-bomb and other words in the game as well. Lastly you do summon and contract demons in the game. They are based on all of the current and past mythologies of the world. In towns and dungeons you have the freedom to run around and interact like most modern JRPGs, and inn dungeons you have a diablo-esque overlay map. Random encounters pop up on the map, and you can "slice" them to avoid the encounter, which is a feature that is very nice. There are also checkpoints, or gates, in the dungeon that allow fast travel to various points in the dungeon. The battle menu has the Persona feel, meaning every action is linked to a button rather than choosing from a menu. The enemies (and you) have resistances and weaknesses that you can exploit to do massive damage, and add stacks for an end of round attack called a "Sabbath" that attacks with the demons the character that exploited the weakness summoned and does pretty good damage to all enemies. Let's begin with saying that the DLC is absolutely not necessary. In fact, I daresay play the game through without it and then get the DLC. I willl break down the DLCs and what they add to the game:  This gives you the ability to turn on items that boost your stats and abilities in the game. After you turn them on in the gameplay menu, you get items that sell at a high price to the vendors, Items that allow you to buy stat raising items from a vendor, and items that each one boosts you a level and ove that boosts your demons a level. You get one of each of these items after you defeat an enemy in combat.  This gives you access to a new  summoner, and an extra dungeon and an extremely difficult boss fight. The Story is pretty good, and the dungeon is enjoyable, and the boss fight will rock your world. Definitely wait until you have mastered the game for this one.  This will add 8  demons to the compendium, once you unlock it. You will be able to summon them for free the first time, and they are stupidly powerful. This and the boost item pack has the potential to make the game too easy on normal difficulty, unless you fight a risky enemy.  adds costumes from Persona 4 and 5, SMT4, Soul Hackers 1, Devil Summoner, and swimsuits. It also adds a BGM that you can change in the menu. Get it if you are into that kind of thing, but this one is definitely skippable.  This one give you 2 of a few items that will help out in the beginning of the game, most notably original flames  which will prevent a wipe on normal difficulty. This is assuredly not a must have, and the extra difficulty is only if you want a challenge beyond hard. The bonus is that as of the time of this review, it is free.  I have thoroughly enjoyed this game and will wholeheartedly recommend it to anyone. I love the controls and the battle system, though the dungeons can be a little grindy. the ability to avoid battles and the gate system mitigates that a bit. I think this is a great addition to the SMT universe.

_childDocuments_.review: I think it's a shame that I cannot give this game a “mixed” review because even though the game looks eye-catching, I don’t think that Soul Hackers 2 sets a good example for either series (SMT or Persona) nor does it feel fulfilling to play as a game after Soul Hackers (3DS), despite not needing to play it beforehand.There’s a few things I really appreciate that were done well with this game:- Leading is Ringo and Figue’s designs. Matching suits with altered personal touches: a cybernetic jacket for Ringo and leggings for Figue. It sets them apart as main characters for sure (or rather main character and sidekick but we’ll get to that later), because no one else is an AI overlord turned humanoid. - Another thing I think was handled well was the character's individual skills through the usage of Mistiques and COMP Upgrades. Each character has an affinity the game starts them with but the game gives you free reign on switching that around and crafting the team as you see fit, granted you have the materials.- The final thing I want to praise, is more of a Quality of Life thing, but it's the ability to essentially Demon Search when out in the field. I got about two thirds of the way through the game before I realised it was a thing but it saves so much time. By going through the menu and into enemies list, if you have the demon you need to fight for a request there, you can hit them with the “search settings”.  Now when you’re out in the field, if the demon you’re looking for is in the encounter that's appeared, that encounter will get a little target mark over it. The bigger bonus is that you can assign more than one demon with the search setting at the same time which is amazing for people who like to bulk complete quests.The big gripes that I have with the game are as follows:- Dungeon design is beyond bland and the Soul Matrix is the biggest offender. Endless blue/purple sea of platforms. They change the puzzle design per person and per floor, but not the look or the musical style of somewhere that is supposed to represent your party members. If Aion can literally make Figue and Ringo, then the place that’s supposed to be the soul of a person can look a little more interesting than some floating platforms and broken stairs. This point also leads into another minor annoyance I had with the game, the map. Or rather the lack of a dedicated screen for a map that I can interact with, while yes, if nothing has spawned I can stand for an indefinite amount of time and look at the map, I don’t want to do that. I want to look at the map in a way where I can see it all and not have to keep fiddling with it so I can see what I’m running into and not have my entire screen obscured. Additionally, why can’t I pin points of interest on the map? There have been some Aion directives I wanted to go back to later but because of the amount of teleporting bullshittery, it's hard to get to and from certain locations or even memorise the route to get there. Green teleporters are one thing but the red ones really take the cake and admittedly, ended up with me putting the game down for an entire week before I reluctantly picked it up to finish the main story. You fixed this issue with Strange Journey Redux (3DS), and backtracked here. Why?- Why do I have to pay with MP to run faster? At the time of writing this it was announced on Oct 3 that there will be a dash introduced and Assassin Steps will be shifted into the role of Estoma+ essentially. Why does it take a patch for this to be implemented?- The load times have been a point of contention for a lot of people and I agree. God forbid you’re upgrading your party and you forget to buy equipment and you have to back out of one place and go somewhere else? Why not have most, if not all, of these available Karakucho? Another big offender with time wasting is going to the Axis. Why is there not an option to go straight to the Soul Matrix as opposed to having to go through the notions of walking past Flamma every. single. time. - Battling is so SLOW. Again, also going to be patched in, but in a game where you have long animations, constant fighting and possibly grinding, whether it be for levels or items from certain demons, speed up buttons should be the norm at this point. Again, you did this in Tokyo Mirage Sessions (Switch) with speeding up the session mechanic, but decided against it here with the sole exception of being able to skip sabbath animations. On that note,- Sabbaths are also beyond underwhelming too. You lose out on Persona’s “All-Out Attack” feature or SMT’s “Press-Turn” system. Literally either of these would have worked better in this game than sabbaths and I think Press Turn would have been the way to go, as it would have added far more difficulty to the game as opposed to making every enemy HP sponges. - You have NG+, but are still required to sit through the tutorials despite having completed the game at least once already. Who decided that?TLDR: I don’t think this is a good game to start with for people new to the whole franchise because it does too much of both sides (Persona and Shin Megami Tensei) and does neither half as good. It’s an alright play for those familiar to the franchise, and a roundabout decent game for those just looking to play for fun.

_childDocuments_.review: After finishing the first Soul Hackers about a month ago, I'm somewhat conflicted and underwhelmed. There was so much potential I have imagined with the direction they could have taken this series in, but in the end, this is a half-baked SMT game that was not given nearly as much budget and attention as it needed (and it shows), despite being sold as a full priced 60 EUR game.Now for context, my experience with the SMT franchise as of writing this review is having played the entirety of IV, a bit of IV:A, around 3/4 of V, the first Soul Hackers recently, Tokyo Mirage Sessions #FE, and Persona 3 and 4.The sabbath mechanic doesn't add much depth to combat, "1 More" from Persona and Press Turn from SMT3 onwards works much better and gives the player much more choice, this is simply just "more damage at the end of the turn with an optional bonus if one of the demons chosen for sabbath has a sabbath special skill". The fusion animation is very disappointing, and the fusion system in general seems fairly limited in terms of inheritance. Dungeon design, oh god the dungeon design, someone fire the guy that made these atrocities, most of the "dungeons" in this game is literally endless empty copypasted corridors with 0 atmosphere with nothing in them, and Ringo moves so damn SLOW through them until you get Milady's sprint ability. Going through Soul Matrix in this game over and over again to get your companions new abilities and find out more about their backstories is torture, the environment is so bland. Only the last dungeon in this game looks like someone put at least a little bit of care into the actual design of it, but it's still kinda meh.Main story writing is nothing special, although it gets the job done, I guess the companion conversations are one of the few redeeming things that make this game enticing, although for that alone you could just look at a youtube compilation of these.Side quests are horrendously boring generic MMO fetch quest grind, but honestly, this is the case for every Atlus game ever, including P3/4.The OST has a few standout pieces, but is fairly weak to the other SMT games I've played.Also, there is absolutely no demon negotiation which is really an SMT staple, and that's very disappointing, only being changed into I want your money/item/HP/MP - Yes/No selection.It might be worth it to get this game on sale, but definitely not for the full price, if you've already played all the better SMT games and are still looking for more.Personally I would recommend IV as a nice introduction to the series instead (V is more accessible because Switch, but imo has horrible writing and terrible level scaling in combat implicitly forcing you to grind and eventually me quitting halfway), the first Soul Hackers once you get into how the mechanics usually work, because even despite its age, it feels surprisingly modern, especially the 3DS port. And if you want more of the mushy Social Links stuff, obviously go for Persona instead, 4 Golden has been out for years, and 5 Royal is just around the corner for PC.

_childDocuments_.review: My expectations were low due to people getting mad about this game but it's...not bad? Kind of good, even? It's obviously very very underbudgeted but there's a decent game here and the skeleton of a great one if they were just willing to commit to it. The story's somewhat abridged and to-the-point but it works well enough and the VAs put in a herculean effort to make the most out of it.The dungeons are bad but battle-wise it tries quite a few new things with mixed results. Moving the damage boost skills to a new accessory slot is a great idea that cuts a lot of the busywork out of fusion and opens the door to some new strategies and being without Press Turn means that you fundamentally have to approach battles differently from the usual, but being stuck with a 4-man party rather than (turn-based) Devil Summoner's usual 6 makes the lack of Press Turn hit harder.  Demon skillsets being completely customizable(including their starting skills, which was reserved for the end of endgame in SMT V) is a double-edged sword, once you have everyone's roles sorted out there's not much reason to change them and the skill slot crunch hurts quite a bit even with boosters-as-accessories taking some of the load off there. There's a lot of interesting new skills that you won't really be able to make use of unless you're constantly switching demons which has it's own limitations. On the bright side the game's actually fairly generous with money(which is an SMT rarity) so you have more room to experiment.Overall I think it's pretty decent and worth your time if you're an SMT fan, and worth a go for anyone if you get it on sale.

Incredibly slow, tutorial heavy and railroady. You don't even get to sprint in this game. Around 5 hours in you could potentially unlock a slight jog as a skill but that's the best you'll get. Also the biggest issue for me is how some elemental affinities have been removed. This makes the majority of demons feel the same, which has always been an issue with the Shin Megami Tensei games.Even with these issues though I would still recommend playing Soul Hackers 2 however you will need a little patience in the first couple of hours.For my full Review of Soul Hackers 2 check out my video here:

_childDocuments_.review: Soul Hackers 2 is a great spin-off. It isn’t as long or ambitious as other Shin Megami Tensei titles, but it’s clearly made with the same quality. While the reduced number of demons and the simpler mechanics can be a negative for veterans, this game proves to be a much friendlier starting point for newcomers. Fans of the franchise will likely enjoy this installment, even if it lacks the complexity of other titles in the series.PROS:✓ A distinctive art style✓ Story and characters are enjoyable✓ Two endings for players to unlock✓ Excellent PC port full of modern options✓ Fantastic voice acting ✓ Enjoyable fighting mechanics✓ Few new demons never seen in the seriesCONS:- Side quests don’t add much colour to the world and are quite shallow- Dungeons are basic and repetitive- Selling some demons through DLC- No normal demon negotiations- Devil Summoner game, that, just doesn't have it in the title

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: I beat it. More on that below. The main paragraph here still applies.Buy on sale if you really need an SMT hit. It's not bad, but they brought in a lot of persona influence and it feels like some weird middle ground between mainline and persona. Nothing wrong with the core gameplay loop, just a bunch of small things that drag the whole experience down. I wouldn't pick this as someone's first SMT game either.No way Atlus looks at this, but Fog Breath's description is wrong. It says it lowers all stats, it actually only lowers attack/accuracy.Good news: looks good, combat is surprisingly interesting (although I'm at level 20 so who knows about later), battle transitions in dungeons are snappy. A lot of Raidou love (PC port where).Things I would love options for but don't expect: Remove the danger alert owl in the top right, he clashes with the background, is real noisy, and provides little useful information. I can hear when the demons spawn in...Lower the amount of in battle dialogue, they are giving xenoblade a run for it's money and I've already given up and muted character voices.Let me walk faster. Please.Let me just warp into shops and save a load screen. Even on PC, on an SSD, it's ~5-10 seconds to load the area the shop is in, then enter the shop, buy my items and another load screen to leave. God help switch players.Similarly, let me use safehouse functions from the map field. Spare me the load screen to heal.Major whine: Main cast is main girl and 3 walking anime tropes. That wouldn't be a problem except a fair amount of this game is running their social links and helping them through their trope issues. So you know how their characters will work out, it's just waiting for the plot to catch up, and until then angst. --- I have now beaten this. I'll keep it basically spoiler free.This was a surprisingly short SMT game. My profile says 55, I'd peg more around 45, I got distracted and idled a fair bit. That is also ignoring the 5 hours I spent wandering around quest locations looking for a doohickey, and the hours I spent half awake in teleporter mazes.Not sure how I feel about that, it didn't feel like the game got compressed or anything, it's just a shorter game. Except one way teleporter mazes where I can't mark the map, those suck. I hold by my original opinion: buy if you really need an SMT hit. Skip the DLC, even the extra story DLC, I assure you the extra story isn't worth 10 bucks.Things that fixed themselves: You can unlock an ability to run faster. Shame you get it pretty deep in the game, it lasts for maybe a minute, and costs 10 mp. It also requires some very specific ability choices.The cast's anime character tropes get resolved pretty fast all things considered. Mostly because the game moves fast but still.You also get an "instantly leave the dungeon" spell. Very good.Things I am now confused about:You can get equipable items that buff damage types, IE +50% fire damage. No such items for physical/gun damage... Why?It has the SMT5 thing where you are constantly low on mana, but the game really wants you to spam spells to activate sabbaths. So lots of safehouse trips to top up...DLC demons get 1 free compendium summon, so you could just grab Satan from level 1 and steamroll.The mistique thing is a real cool concept, to make you specialize what spells people are using. In practice to optimize sabbaths you want to zap the enemy with what they are weak against, so everyone is blasting the same spell type. So besides when you're farming the risky spawns for XP, or you die to a boss and are party rejigging, it doesn't see much play.Things I really grew to dislike:There is a final alignment choice. I thought it would be determined by which party member has the highest soul link. It's actually SMT5 where they just ask you in the final dungeon which ending you want. It also appears to be 1 of 2 options, although I didn't reload to find out. I'm not even sure why the choices I picked gave me my ending, or why I should care.I wasn't exactly enthralled with the plot, but I was actually expecting a twist at the end, just because it felt like nothing happened. Nope, that was it.You can only recruit demons by fighting them, then hoping you have a map event to recruit them. Makes it a PITA to drum up fusion fodder. Certain items and killing them with sabbath damage helps but you still don't get to pick who you want.Fusing demons is also a pain, because demons have at max 6 skill slots, and are very restrictive as to what skills they will take. Not only are you trying to optimize the end result, you're also optimizing the intermediate demons so you can actually pass on skills you want.The mind dungeon/Tartarus is... real dull. All the objectives in there, also real dull. Long, same looking, and teleport mazes.A real lack of scenery variety. You go to the docks twice, the sewers twice, and the office building twice. Only the last dungeon looks even remotely interesting.Big whine: some sidequests are basically: go to location X, find dude Y, do something. They don't mark where dude Y is on your map. Those 5 hours looking around dungeons to find dudes? I am not kidding. My advice, is look in the box rooms near teleporters, or when available use a guide.

For a dungeon crawler, there is a distinct lack of different environments, but when you think about it there isn't much difference in how things look so it is more a veneer of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ keeping you engaged.  I think that if you aren't an SMT simp you will probably not like this game, which is a shame because it feels like the most user-friendly SMT game ever. It tries to appease everyone and yet it only pleases simp types.  If you want the extreme challenge of patients that SMT 3 dishes out you will not find it here.  If you want the interesting dungeons of the first soul hackers you will not find it here.  If you want the characters of persona you will not find it here.  If you don't want denuvo, look elsewhere.  I like it, but that means you will probably not.  Then again I don't speak for you, decide for yourself. _childDocuments_.review: EDIT: So apparently Ringo's walk cycle is tied to FPS. Which is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ bonkers. After switching FPS from unlimited to 75 or 60, her walk cycle doesn't feel like I'm running around a pokemon ice cave. I still would only recommend this game if it's on sale. I played about 10 hours of the original on emulator, so I can't say I have a solid baseline for comparison other than  SMT and Persona games I've played/watched playthroughs of. Fair warning: Received this game as a birthday gift from my partner. I would only recommend getting this if it's on sale. Devs if you're reading, please consider adding patches to alter Ringo's absurd walk/run movements and a way to turn off "sabbaths."I desperately want to love this game. The voice acting is amazing, the art design is fabulous, and ....that might be where it ends? It has the standard play of an SMT game where you battle after making contracts with demons and adding them to your array. The story so far is fine and kind of generic - end of the world is coming. Gotta stop it. High stakes. Fun characters with their own motivations - very ragtag. I'm only a few hours in, so nothing huge storywise to report on. The battle system is ALMOST what you'd expect from an SMT game, but you don't get to have demons fighting in the field. You basically just take on the powers of whatever demon you have equipped. Which honestly isn't that big of a deal since P5R didn't have the demons out in the field, the personas just hopped out during attack rounds when used. However, I really do miss the in-battle bargaining system where you could win them over and recruit them through chatting, bribes, and items. Being able to send out your demons to do "recon" for you and having them simultaneously used in battles is nice and all, but there feels like no risk is involved. Kind of wish that you had to send one out for recon and had to choose one or two to keep behind for defense. Like another player mentioned, there's a battle-breaking sequence where Ringo conducts a special attack at the end of the player turn where if one [or several] demon's weakness[es] is[are] exploited. It's annoying to keep watching and you can't turn it off to just keep fighting a battle. It feels super lazy and makes the fight system too easy thus far. Outside of the battle system, moving Ringo in the real world is a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ nightmare. When you stop moving a character, you expect them to stop moving, not continue a walk cycle to go another 10 feet. Devs cared more about Ringo's walk cycle looking good because "leggy femme character" than actually feeling enjoyable to move around. I shouldn't feel like I'm playing an old pokemon game and skidding around ice when I'm just trying to move around when there are enemies nearby I'd like to sneak up on. This should absolutely be something a player can turn off in the menu and it isn't. The camera angles are ridiculous when starting the game, and it took about an hour of cutscenes/play to actually get to a spot where I was allowed in the menu to change those settings. Again, if you like SMT games, I hope you'll enjoy this, but seriously only buy this if it's on sale, because they hit the wall instead of anywhere on the dartboard.

_childDocuments_.review: as of 20 hours into the gameStory/Character: 5/5Aesthetic/Graphics: 4/5Combat/Gameplay: 3.5/5I personally love this game. It fits nicely into what I was looking for and my experience with the SMT series but I can see the caveats a lot of players have with it. so I think it's best served to just say who I think will enjoy this game. Who I think would enjoy this game: Soul Hackers 2 seems to be ATLAS targeting new adult fans of Persona. The story is less shy about treating you like an adult and all of the characters are adults themselves. So I think the person that is going to get the most out of this title are people looking for something a bit more mature than Persona 5 but are relatively new fans of the franchise. Explanation of scores:ATLAS at this point has a reputation for love-able and memorable characters, and Soul Hackers 2 is no exception. The characters all have endearing chemistry and great well written banter that makes it easy to get attached. The most standout example of the characters and writing is our protagonist Ringo who is just as active and well, if not better, written a character as any other in the game, a notable and welcome departure from the silent and self-insert protagonists we see so often in RPGs in general. Aesthetics wise Soul Hackers 2 delivers on what it offers. A bright and colorful cyberpunk world with a high quality soundtrack. The set pieces and aesthetics of the game are clean, well constructed, and have a memorable identity and flare. Meanwhile the soundtrack delivers on the style we're used to in the Persona franchise, albeit without the catchy vocal tracks. The only draw back for the looks and aesthetics of this game is the volume of aesthetics. Soul Hackers 2 shows its more limited budget in stretching the assets it has, however those same Assets are not wanting for quality.Soul Hackers 2 is a distinct flavor of the SMT franchise while also borrowing elements of the persona series specifically with it's social gameplay elements exploring side character stories. As far as SMT games go the combat is familiar and different enough that newcomers to the SMT style of games will find a distinct different flavor of combat vs recent entries such as Persona 5 but veterans of the SMT franchise may feel it doesn't stand out compared to other games from the series.

_childDocuments_.review: First off, the PC version is excellent. With an RTX 2070, you probably can run the game in 2K with DLDSR 2.25 enabled and still get 60 FPS, resulting in a very clean looking game, easily competing with the PS5 version.I do that with an RTX 3080ti (system specs at the end) and get 120-144 FPS. Doing the same with 4K on my TV (6144 x 3456px in DLDSR), I get a stable 60 FPS. If Persona 5 Strikers runs fine with you, so does this title.Soul Hackers 2 is a good game, but no equal to Persona 5 - not in content, nor in production value. Take away the time management, the narration-heavy level design of the main story chapters and it leaves you with the core combat system (collecting, leveling and fusing demons while exploiting the enemy's weakness as good as you can) and dungeon design as boring as the subway levels in Persona 5.Technically, it's a solid performing game. You have plenty of graphic options and it should run great on medium level PCs. Without side activities as in Persona 5, it's leaning more towards the grindy aspects of the game. While there are side quests ("requests"), they're usually but very simple fetch quests. Social interaction with the other group characters is restricted to drinking at the bar or unlocking parts of your mates' subconciousness (a construct in form of a dungeon, you basically enter new area when your friendship has reached a new level). There is no social management needed, in certain dialogues you simply pick answers in order to keep your standings as equal as you can (or not, your choice).The game focuses on the combat and collection aspect of the series. Everything is streamlined to it: fast travel to every location and shop, no lengthy side activities, extremely simplistic dungeons, no time management.With a price tag of 60 bucks for the base game, it's a bit lacking. Total game time should be around 40-50h. If you're in love with Persona 5: this is far less game for the buck. Best to wait for a sale.my system:i7-8700k, 32 GB, RTX 3080ti

_childDocuments_.review: Soul Hackers 2 feels like an Atlus game from 15-20 years ago, not a brand new game that just released in 2022 at full price AND with a day one DLC.The story has been okay so far. A nice mix of sci-fi + SMT esoteric fantasy stuff. It's not been anything too interesting so far, but that might change later. Characters are fine for the most part, with Ringo being a major standout with how great she is (especially with Japanese VA). In terms of storytelling and character development it's a major step above SMT, but (aside from Ringo) never quite reaches the heights of Persona or Atlus other story focused works.The aesthetic is great. The neon cyberpunk styles and city is a cool setting. The OST is good overall (but again, still falls a bit short of Persona or SMT) and the cutscenes are all really well doneThe gameplay is simplistic yet fun. The big twist with the game is that with every weakness you hit on an enemy, you get a "stack". At the end of your turn, you unleash every "stack" as a massive attack. It's very satisfying. If you're an experienced megaten fan you'll probably find it way too easy, as enemies never take opportunity attacks on you, nor can they build stacks like you can. This makes SH2 a good entry into the overall series, but might leave experienced fans a little bored.Now, the issuesFirst, Soul Hackers 2's dungeons are AWFUL. Genuinely some of the worst dungeons I've had to suffer in a JRPG in a long time and it feels like a massive step back for Atlus. Remember Persona 5's amazing palaces? Or SMTV's open world design? Well, SH2 goes back to old Atlus dungeon design: long, narrow hallways with no decorations, no interactable items or treasure chests, no puzzles and LOTS of dead ends and backtracking. It's terrible and mind numbingly boring.On top of that, Ringo moves so, so slowly through these hallway dungeons so not only are you bored out of your mind because there is nothing in the dungeon besides you and some easy enemies, but it takes twice as long to get through as it should.It actually blows my mind. I've seen 30 year old games with better dungeons than Soul Hackers 2. I've seen DS games with better dungeons than Soul Hackers 2. The fact that they just threw in maze like, dull empty hallways and decided to call them "dungeons", then charge 60 dollars for it is an insult.Which brings me to the second major issue: the price. Soul Hackers 2 is not a 60 dollar game (70 dollars if you decide to buy the day one DLC), nor is it anywhere near the quality of other Atlus titles. This is very much a throwaway game made by Atlus' C team (supposedly the same guys that made TMS) while the rest of Atlus works on Persona 6.If I had paid 30 or 40 dollars for this, I would have likely been willing to overlook it's issues. But I paid 70 dollars for the deluxe edition because I was expecting the general quality and polish you expect when you buy a game with the "Atlus" logo. This isn't even in the same dimension as ANY of the Personas or SMT's. It feels cheap and half-assed. It's the first Atlus game I genuinely regret buying.Overall, it's not a bad game, but its really not great either. Maybe worth it if you can get it at a steep discount, or if you're really hungry for more megaten, but I wouldn't recommend it otherwise

_childDocuments_.review: I'm just a few hours into the game but, so far. I get this strong sense of the game being mostly handled by Atlus's B team while the A team works on an unannounced P6. This game was built on Unity which, at least seems to offer a little more stability than UE4 did for Shin Megami Tensei V. Still, it leaves a product that feels less crafted and polished than P5 with it's proprietary engine did. The textures, effects, lighting shadows, etc. Seem fine enough but they all have an early Ps4 game feel to them rather than a game that just released. No idea how long the development was on this title. Ultimately, I am enjoying the game and will probably finish it. However, for anyone with a medium to low income, I'd say wait for a sale because this game doesn't seem to do anything to warrant a triple A price tag.Edit September 5, 2022:I have now finished the main game and the little DLC completing *most little side stuff and achievements along the way. In my opinion the worst part of this game by a wide margin is the Soul Matrix. If you're at all interested in completing all 5 floors for each character you're very likely to spend more time in the Soul Matrix then the rest of the entire game combined. Considering that it basically looks the same on all 5 floors, with the addition of teleport pads on the higher floors, it is very, very tedious. The second worst part of the game is the DLC dungeon "Hachigaya Training Field". This, much like the Soul Matrix but arguably worse since it's most the exact same floor duplicated over an over is extremely tedious. The actual Lost Numbers story and the character Nana is pretty fun and adds to the game but, this dungeon was super lazy. It could have all but 1 of it's floors removed and would pretty much be the same dungeon. In a nutshell, those 2 dungeons feel like pitiful attempts to add playtime bulk to a rather thin game that is asking a triple A price. The actual characters imo, are somewhat endearing however, 2 of them--I won't spoil much--just grow too quickly and end up acting about as off the rails stupid as I could imagine. The whole game feels like it takes place over the course of just a few weeks and it just doesn't track at all with the character progression for those 2. There needs to be like a whole middle of the game added to this game.For people complaining about it being compared to Persona or Shin Megami Tensei get real... Even Atlus immediately threw Persona content into this game. Besides that, as far as the genre goes the easiest other games in the genre to compare it to are Atlus's other IPs. While this shouldn't be another Persona or SMT it should be comparable in detail quality or superior even now that Atlus is a much more successful studio than when they were developing P5. The Joker costume for Ringo imo, is the way to go, I super dislike her vanilla outfit. Some of the Persona 5 music is being reused here but, that's not a bad thing, frankly the original music for Soul Hackers for me personally is a let down. Otherwise, it's a fun if a bit generic JRPG that feels like an early PS4 release despite being a 2022 release. If you've played hundreds or even just dozens of games in the genre you'll see tropes everywhere some bad some fine. I'd say wait for a sell unless you're a big JRPG fan that has money burning a hole in your account and you've already exhausted Steam's list of JRPGs that are better than this game.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is pretty good, it introduces some very much needed quality of life that Megaten games were severely lacking. So why the negative review?This game has a very serious flaw that could erase your entire progress - I had a power outage and ALL 20 of my saves were corrupted. Not the auto save that the game might have attempted at the time of outage, but hard saves that were made way before the incident. After rebooting the PC, the corrupt save files were immediately uploaded to the Steam Cloud. Miraculously, the autosave was actually the only one that didn't get corrupted and I was able to salvage my run with only 20 minutes of gameplay lost.While I'm complaining, there's also two minor issues that really get on my nerves.First of all, each cutscene is full of awkward pauses and unnecessarily long cut and paste generic animations of characters gesticulating, which add up to half of the cutscenes' run time, if not more. Instead of moving and making gestures during speech, the character will end their line and stop to perform a gesture for several seconds before resuming. There's a fast forward button, which doesn't speed the game up much anyway, but it's almost impossible to use it without skipping some of the dialogue with the awkward way the cutscenes are structured. Every single cutscene starts with a painfully slow fade in and fade out animation of a character walking or making a vague, miniscule motion and you have to stop fast forwarding before the fade out or you're guaranteed to skip at least a line of dialogue.Another terrible design choice is that equipped costumes appear only in battle. They don't appear on Ringo in dungeons or in cutscenes, even though all the cutscenes are in-engine. There's actually some cutscenes that happen during battle, so it's clearly possible to use those models in every other cutscene as well.All in all it's a good game that improves on the Megaten formula.The visual design is beautiful, voice acting is high quality, the sabbath system is fun.However, the fatal save corruption issue, which should have been patched ASAP, is simply unacceptable.

_childDocuments_.review: This isn't exactly what I would've had in mind for a new entry in the Devil Summoner franchise, but that's not a bad thing. This game has its faults, such as: dungeon themes, dumb DLC, the Soul Matrix, and quite a few not too interesting side quests, but I firmly believe that the pros in this game outweigh the cons. The story is great, the characters are excellent, the combat is a new unique take on the standard SMT combat system that is really fun, and the soundtrack is amazing. I'm hesitant to say that the game is worth the full $60 asking price, especially when you factor in the DLC and just how much it adds, but if you happen to see the game and all its DLC on sale I would definitely recommend picking it up

_childDocuments_.review: The game has quite an ambivalent response and somewhat negative reviews. But if you know what you are getting into, it is probably worth the time to its audience.The characters are well-written and the English voice cast was quite good. The main character Ringo is quite quirky and memorable. The core mechanics of turn based RPG combat are as solid as any SMT/Persona game. However the rest of the game is quite bare bones when compared to other modern RPGs. Dungeon design is plain and repetitive, the main plot is a bit of the standard search for the five triangle pieces to save the world. The social interaction system is extremely simple and streamlined compared to the Persona series.The game feels like it was originally scoped for something like the 3DS and not the PS5 generation of console. If it was priced like a 3DS game I don't think the complaints would be so vocal. So I'd say if you like turn based RPG /SMT games this one is worth it if you pick it up during a sale like i did. I think I got it 60-65% off the original price.

_childDocuments_.review: I waited for this game for months and I got what I wanted.There is a lot of things to say about this game, before you even get interested in the story, characters or anything else, you will probably end up seeing people getting mad about Day 1 DLC's.I can understand some people think of it like a "greedy" way of making people pay for games, but you have to remember ATLUS is probably one of the most honest company.Yes they make Day 1 DLC's, but it's just bonus content that you DON'T have to pay if you don't want to. Also, compared to a lot of other companies, ATLUS is just beginning to make profit of the SMT franchise, which exists for about 35 years, and the cost of making all these games is not cheaper than before, so if you have to pay 70$ for the full game + bonus content, which is now starting to get translated in a lot of other languages than Japanese and English only before, I don't think it's a bad thing, considering the qualities, and the time you can spend on the title too.I have played the 3DS version of the first Soul Hackers game, and I loved it, I have played a few other SMT games, SMT 5 being the last one I've played, not my favorite at all, but still cool.When this game got announced, I haven't played the first one before but it got me interested because I loved the cyeberpunk aesthetic of the game.I've only played 10hrs at the time I'm writing this review, but ATLUS killed it with this one, the story isn't the most impressive or innovative I've seen but it's really well written, which makes it interesting and makes you want to know more about the characters, the city etc...Talking about the characters, I really like them, the fact you can get to know them more when doing their Soul Matrix is really cool (btw the camera angle in dungeons being right on Ringo's ass is the best thing lol)For the gameplay, I like how they managed to reuse Persona 5 mechanics but still changed them a bit to make it unique for SH2, it's smooth, really well animated, nothing else to say.I'm playing in hard difficulty and I honestly think I'm gonna try to complete the game at 100%If you want a good SMT game before Persona 5 Royal coming this October 21st, do not hesitate to purchase this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought the most expensive edition on PS4 at launch and had mixed feelings after finishing the game. I do like the game a lot, but I felt that the game has a much lower budget than most games that sell around this price.   So, a few years later, I gave this game a second chance on this platform since it had a big discount. I felt much more satisfied with the price I got.   I don’t really want to compare this game to the Persona series, but it can’t be helped because the game itself did use an awfully similar system like equipping demons or hanging out with teammates to increase relationship points akin to the social links. [Positives]   + Interactions between the cast are interesting, to me at least. We get to see a group of misfits saving the world together. I feel like we don’t get to see that often.   + The story is compelling for the most part. Particularly the battle of acquiring the Covenants.   + The battle system is simple but fun. I like how I had to keep switching demons in the battle to exploit the enemy’s weakness(es) while covering my own.+ The number of demons is high, and some are even ones that we don’t usually see in recent games.+ Splendid art direction, music, and voice acting for both languages.[Negatives]   - Several bosses have difficulty spikes. Forcing you to level grind for a few extra mins/hours.   - The dungeon designs are so bad. Even worse with the one that has puzzle gimmicks.   - The ending arc has a rushed feeling to it.[Summary]Recommended for those who are familiar with SMT or Persona “AT DISCOUNT”.P.S. The game’s acronym is SH2 which is the same as some certain survivor horror game lol.

_childDocuments_.review: What a disappointment. I mean, a JRPG with cyberpunk anime aesthetics that seemingly implements some social mechanics, as a Persona enthusiast how possibly could this not be appealing after all? Well sadly, it turns out this game doesn't live up to my prior excitement.There's actually not much to say tbh. Soul Hackers 2 isn't especially bad imho, but it isn't exactly good either. Getting straight to the point, Ringo is an amazing character, but that's about the only good thing - in fact, she pretty much carries the entire run and ended up being my sole motivation for actually finishing the game. Aside from that, this game is basically sheer blandness as you will go back and forth between a very few enclosed areas, going through corridor "dungeons" (as in actual corridors...) and completing your typical boring sidequests. Characters excluding Ringo are decent enough, but the very limited social aspect didn't quite lay the ground for actually empathizing with them - well, you certainly will at some point, but in regard to storytelling and character development, Persona 3 did it 10 times better 16 years prior. There's indeed no such thing as social links in this game, rather you will encounter occasional hangout events at the usual place which will eventually allow you to unlock combat skills for each member of your party - and tbh, while this will still give you some hints of lore about them, it's much more the foresight of that end objective that made me actually hangout with my party. As for the story itself, it is very timid in its intentions, thus very predictable.Fortunately though (or maybe not), Soul Hackers 2 is an SMT entry so it has inherited from the series' good old mechanics, namely turn-based combats and demon fusions which are both as effective as ever. To be fair, someone who isn't familiar with SMT would probably be able to show more appreciation towards this game since said mechanics are overall well thought out. Then again, I wouldn't even recommend this to newcomers as there are far better options available out there if you're willing to dive into the SMT series.So yeah, Soul Hackers 2 basically is a very lacking game and comes off as a lazy attempt at making something refreshing. While I still enjoyed it at some point, I just can't help thinking that Ringo just didn't deserve that game.Edit: typo.

_childDocuments_.review: Objectively speaking, Soul Hackers 2 probably isn't a good game... But I just can't get myself to give it a negative review...Soul Hackers 2, has some great characters, an interesting setting, and a pretty interesting premise for a story! Plus the soundtrack in my opinion is a solid A tier! Not quite up to the Atlus standard in my opinion, but still has a lot of bangers that I listed to very often even after I've finished the game!But the dungeons man... The They gotta be THE most boring and mechanically frustrating things I've had to play in a looooong time. Which is a shame since you're gonna spend most of your time in them...They all look basically identical, and most of them have the same song, and then you have the navigator constantly making noises about enemy statuses, that you have no option to mute (as far as I know).And the Soul Matrix, each party members "unique" dungeon, is the worst example of that. Each floor, for each character looks and functions the exact same, and then later they also throw in portals into the mix, that you don't know where they will teleport you to, making traversing them even more frustrating. But the worst thing is that they are not really optional, since, to get the true ending, one of the things you need to do, is to complete each characters dungeon. But at the end of each dungeon, you get some honestly really cool and challenging boss battles! Which in my opinion are solid highlights of this game, making the dungeons kind of worth it in my opinion!As mentioned previously, this game has some good characters! And those boss battles are usually pretty personal for them, making them feel very climactic! Or, maybe good concepts for characters...?Since, I like them, but also feel like they are very underdeveloped? Either way, I enjoy them! But really wished they where given more time and attention, since the game is kind of about them? Anyways, I was first very skeptical on Arrow and Figue, but Figue ended up being one of my favorites! Not to mention the protagonist herself, Ringo! Ringo is such a treat, and is super entertaining! And her dynamic with all the party members is very fun to watch.And the story is cool at first, as long you don't give it that much thought, because as soon as you do, the logic starts to crumble and fall apart real fast.Another thing that I like in this game though, that I personally haven't seen done that much before, is that as you finish some side quests, the party members can actually comment and talk to you about what their opinion on that matter was, as you unlock a conversation with them about it at the bar, once the quest is finished. It makes the side quests a bit more worth it in my opinion, as it fleshes out the characters a little more, and makes them feel like their own individual people.The side quests themselves on the other hand, aren't that great... I mean, some of them have their little side plot going on, which is fun to follow up upon as you get more quests from those characters, and can even meet them in the overworld, and hear their opinions on the recent story events. But most of the side quests basically boil down to "find the thingamajig" or "fight someone somewhere", meaning that yet again you have to go out to the right dungeon, and mess around until you by some mere chance find the thing you where looking for. It takes so much timmmeee, and is not very fun! The "collect this amount of this item" quests are by far the worst though in my opinion. because one time, I was either doing something wrong, or I had THE worst luck imaginable as I had 5/6 items I needed, but couldn't find the 6th one for literally 2 HOURS. Since the chance to get that item was random. Plus, the game overall lacked a lot of polish in my opinion... Small things like, the main menu theme not looping correctly, everyone spamming voice lines for each little move they do in combat, or the foot step noises not being synced to the animations (Since, sometimes the sound doesn't match the visuals), or when story events aren't being reflected by the music, like, when something sad happened/is happening, and the characters are sad because of it, but the music is still happy and funky in the background. I know they are all super small things, but they add up, and kind of break the immersion quite a lot. As you can see, my opinion on this game is a very mixed bag. Plus, I haven't written a review before either, so, I apologize that this is kind of a rambled mess. But, despite everything, if this game has sparked your interest, I'd say give it a shot! But please, spare yourself, and use a guide or something to just get the dungeons (and quests if you wanna) done and over with faster, and I hope you will enjoy the characters, boss fights, and the music! Because as I said, I'm really glad that I sticked with it! I had some great moments playing it, and Ringo, Figue and Saizo will be living in my head rent free for quite some time I think!So yeah! Here's hoping that Atlus doesn't get too discouraged by this games performance, and tries to make more games outside of the mainline SMT and Persona series in the future!
