_childDocuments_.review: It's like Persona except you're all adults so the only time you get to hang out is over a beer between work shifts.Okay now for the actual review:This game's combat system is heavily based on that of the most recent Persona games, there are no rows, alignments or temperaments to think about when assembling your party, instead there are four fixed party members who are essentially all given the ability of a Persona protagonist to "equip" a demon in order to use its moveset. Each party member has an affinity for a specific element and so pairs up better with some demons over others.The combat itself is even more persona-like rather than resembling the original Soul Hackers, with the initial combat interface being instantly recognisable as the one from Persona 5. The main gimmick of this game's combat system is the Stack system which grants you a extra attack at the end of each turn whose damage is determined by how much you can exploit enemy weaknesses. Unlike systems from previous games in the series, enemies cannot use this system against you, leading to the combat system being balanced in the player's favour.Older SMT games will allow for demon negotiation during combat, the replacement for this system is something I will go into as part of the next section.Fans of older SMT will be happy to see that maps quickly become fairly complex, they are by far not the most intricate in the series but in later areas are satisfactory. Dungeon crawling consists of free 3d movement of your character rather than tile-based first person movement of older SMT games, as a result moon phases and magnetite "demon rent" systems have been scrapped.The traversal in Soul Hackers 2 has been made to be very streamlined and forgiving, to begin with, encounters are no longer at random, instead taking another feature that recent Persona is known for (yes I know they didn't invent this) where encounters are visible in a dungeon and can be avoided. There are also a number of field abilities that you are able to unlock including one that I missed on my original playthrough which allows for sprinting. Since finishing the game I have learned that this is now a default ability after an update, thank god.Saving is allowed at any time in any location and fixed terminals allow warping between different points in each dungeon, An early field ability allows instant escape from a dungeon to the map screen in exchange for 1mp, this eliminates concerns of managing your resources while deep into a dungeon as you can leave to restore your stats at any time with little consequence.Rather than chests or much of anything else to discover for yourself in dungeons you will instead encounter demons that you have recruited standing around, speaking to them will allow you to claim either an item, or recruitable demon. While unique, this is quite a shallow system.Item discovery is randomised, with a chance of being consumables or upgrade materials of common and rare varieties. The locations of quest items are mostly randomised, goals often being "collect X item in area Y" requiring you to walk around aimlessly talking to demons until you find the required number of quest items.The negotiation system in this game is a negotiation in name alone, there is no real failure state to recruiting a demon; you speak with them, they name their price, you say yes to recruit them, or no and then they leave.This game has a very modern interface, as mentioned previously the basic battle controls you will be interfacing with are pretty optimal, making use of all of a controller's face buttons rather than a tedious linear menu like other SMT games.It is clear that Atlus learned some lessons from their HD port of SMT3 to Unity, the resulting game is quite a decent PC port supporting high resolutions, framerate capping options up to unlimited, and many options for graphical settings.Affecting their PC ports since P5 Strikers is poorly implemented anti-aliasing, I substituted this for the AA from nvidia's control panel and it looks fine.Loading screens are almost nonexistent, but a pause was added to loading screens so that the tips can still be read. this pause can be disabled in the settings menu.One major port issue is that running above 60fps can cause running acceleration to bug out, this does not affect balance but can feel odd. - Present (English and Japanese) - Atlus game (good) - Atlus game (very good)While overall I would rate the music of this game highly, I am at least a bit disappointed that it does not quite feel like a successor to the style that Soul Hackers 1 went for, what we have instead still sounds great but is a bit closer to something from Ryota Kozuka's work on SMTV. That said I hope we get some high quality uploads on streaming platforms soon as I am a big fan of some tracks. - BadThere is some great music in this game, and each area you visit of the city when picking up quests, upgrades, or items in between dungeon runs has you encountering a number of them which never got old for me, the majority of your time however is spent in dungeons which - with a mere two exceptions, all share the same dungeon theme.While the dungeon themes are dynamic in that they transition to a more tense version of the theme when an enemy is in pursuit, this still means that this long dungeon crawler is spent mostly listening to the same song on repeat, this is especially a problem when the theme starts from the beginning after every battle encounter.Speaking of battle themes, there are a few different boss themes, but for regular encounters we only get the one, and due to the lack of demon negotiations within battles, there is no negotiation theme either. Given that the regular battle theme is by far the one that will play the most, this makes the DLC which adds music from previous SMT games something I would strongly recommend.Possibly my most controversial opinion on this game is that of the character designs for the main cast, which I have strongly disliked from the moment they were first revealed, they do however grow on you after a while of playing, and once again with DLCs the cast can be dressed as characters from other SMT games in order to fix their goofy outfits.The visuals are otherwise great, demons are high quality and environments are very stylised even if the dungeons are repeated tilesets.The story was alright, better than SMTV but nothing special. The main cast are fleshed out a lot with lot of scenes of dialogue explaining their backgrounds, there are some plot heavy sections, these can be skipped easily on repeat playthroughs.There is some connection to the Devil Summoner series (mostly some names and the use of COMPs to summon demons), there is little to directly tie this to SH1 plot-wise. The nature of Demons and COMPs existing is never really a focus unlike the last game.I think this game easily could have been named Devil Summoner: Aion instead of SH2 and might have been more successful for it, no knowledge of SH1 is needed to enjoy this game.Gameplay = Simplistic and easy but excusable due to being streamlined and satisfying.World = Pretty and sounds good, fleshed out by a ton of dialogue.Plot = Mid-tier for a SMT game, good enough.Recommended for fans of dungeon crawlers & monster collector games.Not as convoluted as other series entries but main mechanics like battles, exploration, and demon fusion are present. This is a decent first entry for someone trying to get into SMT.Game is quite expensive for what it is, relies on DLCs to cover up flaws that would be more of a pain otherwise. I would suggest picking up the deluxe edition from a key site if possible, or wait for a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: First impressions:+ Story, while starting off somewhat slowly and quietly, has my attention.+ Runs smoothly.+ UNCAPPED frame rate! This genuinely surprised me. I was expecting it to lock at 60.+ Half decent graphics options.- Built in anti-aliasing option not very effective. I use a 1440p monitor so I rendered at 4K using DSR, and..- While DSR works, changing resolution takes a second or two longer than it should, potentially leading less patient players to think it's soft-locking.     Obviously one person's positive experience doesn't mean no one will have issues but if you're worried about a janky port, so far that has not been my experience.     I'm averaging ~220fps @ 1440p and ~100 @ 4K with a RTX 2070 super.      So Atlus probably isn't kidding when they claim you only need a GTX 760 or Radeon HD 7870 to get 1080p/60 so long as you have a 6-core CPU.

_childDocuments_.review: The hate I hear from the game because it doesn't compare from the first Soul Hackers game. after completing hard difficulty first walkthrough because a challenge is always fun. I did have fun however noticing its flaws, played few other well known Shin Megami Tensei titles, Soul Hackers 2 didn't exactly grasped me like the first Soul Hackers. What makes Soul Hackers unique from other SMT titles and Persona? Firstly, we all know Status Aliments is a common thing however one Aliment "Bomb" is only in Soul Hackers. To see it back in Soul Hackers 2 made it exciting, as well for demons in a unique race name "Zomas" that was later mention in the story. However I knew the "Demon Compendium" didn't have a whole lot of demons like SMTV, not even ONE "Zoma" to fuse for. The hype for it died down for it. A returning character from the first Soul Hackers, and Devil Summoner came in and that was "Madame Ginko" but in all honestly, I just wasn't hype for it unfortunately, same applies for Yatagarasu and Phantom Society. Vision Quests are back but I find first Soul Hackers to be more entertaining. The characters from your party are great, the voice acting is fantastic. Saizo has relationship problems and shows how being a devil summoner messes/changes your life, which made me love a lot. Milady is cold, hides information from the group, eventually later gets expose on some stuff but all of that would've been solve if she just opens up to them a little more, especially since the dire situation everyone is in. Arrow is average, don't hate him, don't love him either. Couple moments where I was hype for him. Ringo has amazing personality and succeeds serving as a protagonist that always puts a smile on my face. Picking out choices as her is great to see her reaction. Voice acting amazing. Figue unfortunately didn't get enough screen time until the climax happens, eventually making me dislike her. Other adversaries that oppose Ringo and the gang are good, Iron Mask and his Zenon was good, both of their looks awesome. Without spoiling much, his writing could've use some work, but I love seeing him whenever I got the chance too. Story felt/is repetitive since the first person that died, and this kept going throughout. It was horrible because I'd really love to see more about the characters, how they got there, how they die ETC. If they did this, it probably would make me care about the characters lot more and get an understanding what sort of motive they wanted to aim at. Ichiro onda for example since the beginning, his slight shown of Braze made me want to know more about him, along with Arrows Sensei. The Developers love having their characters say "Soul Hackers". The day one DLC was a disaster, especially when they announced DLC from previous Soul Hackers cosmetics, a favorite character, and well known demons that SHOULD'VE already been in the game BASE. So no thank you. Gameplay; unfortunately it wasn't challenging. Hit a weakness, hit more weaknesses, you deal more damage from what's known as "Sabbaths" or "Stacks" if you're only a persona fan, basically an "All Out-Attack!" move. Yes, the battle is that of Persona look, you get four party members equip with demons with little stuff. Landing a improper move in battle, they don't punish you for it unlike SMT or even PERSONA games. You just get rewarded for it as long as you have a demon to block that move incase the enemy reflects on it. You don't lose a Stack, the enemy doesn't get stronger, NOTHING like that, so then the battles just feels.. well.. boring. Sometimes I wish it was just Ringo or with Arrow and Four/Three other demons which you don't see in battle unless its a Sabbath. If it had more actual team building, it would've been more fun, but Soul Hackers 2 just didn't have any sadly. No momentum/flow at all. If it were to have first Soul Hackers battle system, battles would've been NUTS. Little interaction with characters like reviving an ally, making jokes during battle was entertaining. Some may find it annoying, it can get old but I personally didn't mind. Customizing your COMPS was actually really fun for me! Dungeons; My god where do I begin. It was very repetitive, boring, last dungeon looked appealing. I disliked the Soul Axis dungeons, the portals were disgusting. I had to look up a guide online in order to pick which portal that would lead me to a gate. This made SMTV exploration look like a masterpiece to be honest. The Matrix doesn't chance at all, not even giving a little personality base around the character you wish to visit. Heck if they even add a red color in the background, I'd notice a little difference. The Music was the same thing, Matrix, if an enemy ambushes you, regular battle theme, EVEN when facing the bosses. I really wish it was different, R.S maybe having a hip hop battle theme, those bosses have the same music, god even Iron Mask bro. Missed Opportunity like how? It's a SIN. Dungeons hardly have any traps, and not enough puzzles. It sucks. Navigator to warn you enemies near by was super annoying. If they just left it out and keep a signal on right corner that changes colors showing you're on the clear or not, I'd be happy for cause I can see game, thank you. Anyways, lots of repetitive stuff in this game. I feel little emotional by characters but wasn't enough. I knew not to expect much from Atlus making 3D. I don't know how they didn't do it well on this one despite making great sellers in the past SMT that are 2D. I'm more emotional on that than the game itself. Please do better Atlus, I know you can, it's just not this one sadly. 6/10

_childDocuments_.review: Interesting exploration and deviation from other SMT titles. Evidently made on a tighter budget, but the smaller scope helps the character-driven story and makes sure it doesn't stay too long past its welcome. The style and presentation carries it if you enjoy this type of glitzy dystopia. Battles are a bit longer due to less reliance on instant kills, which helps make everything more important but can be a bit sloggy if played in long sessions. Recommended on a sale if you're tenative, particularly after the recent QoL patch.

_childDocuments_.review: I will give this game a thumbs up, as the game is not "bad" and I did have fun, just taking a step back and looking at things objectively.Really disliked how rushed the story was.  It was dungeon after dungeon without any breaks for proper character developments or subplots (excluding soul matrix and requests).  Character moments, while I did find them really enjoyable and heartwarming, were too short and too few.As the main story is extremely rushed, there is no time or incentive to fully utilize items such as the augment/arcana mystiques because by the time you grinded enough to get them, you would already be reaching the end. Combat is okay.  I preferred the old press turn systems from older SMT games.  Delivers more of a challenge and a reason to fuse properly.  Without enemies being able to gain extra turns from exploiting ally weaknesses, there really is no point in stressing trying to get coverage because you can just heal the next turn.On a technical level, the game runs smooth on my laptop, but I noticed that Ringo's hair tended to spaz out when she runs.  I've checked with many other users and they also said the same thing.  This isn't a major problem as some players did not have it happen to them.Dungeon design is really disappointing.  For a "cyberpunk" world, the dungeons revolved around dark, gloomy, old installations.  Dungeons also have the same old puzzles most of you guys know such as, collecting keys to unlock doors, defeating mid-bosses to get items and teleporting through portals. Speaking about cyberpunk theme, despite the main city being designed nicely, you are unable to really explore the city.  When you're in the city, the game becomes a "side scroller" where you just run back and fourth to the store you want to visit, and that's all.  No exploration within the stores or whatever, it just shows up an item screen.The soul matrix is really a slow burn, it does look good however.  If you aren't a fan of backtracking or running a long distance, you would probably find yourself skipping alot.DLC review:-Lost numbers is alright.  It's really just a few more quests.-DLC demons are alright.  They have unique skills, but you can't pass them on via fusion. -Costumes are beautiful, just that you can't wear them outside of battles.  Not even while traversing dungeons.-Stat boost items are sort of a waste because you can grind for highest stats, but once again if the main story is so short, what's the point?To end the "review", I would just encourage future players to wait for sale to get this game, because it is not worth the SGD$120 I paid for.  The game has good moments, but the moments are quickly taken away due to how rushed everything is.  There were many promising character developments wasted.  Mini spoiler:The man you see in the trailers, only really appears for a few quick battles and that is all.

_childDocuments_.review: Atlus resurrected the cult classic 90s MegaTen game, Soul Hackers, for a sequel which is perhaps the most by-the-numbers, and predictable RPG they've released in fifteen years.At its core Soul Hackers 2 revolves around traversing some of the most thematically bland and uninspired dungeons, defeating enemies in a so-so variation of Press Turn combat and making your way over to the next round of story dialogue, much of which tends to be filled with unnecessary exposition. Throw in some half-hearted MMO sidequests too - the game has to rely on this as a crutch to make the dull dungeon crawling more palatable. The above would be digestible if the narrative was actually interesting, but it isn't. Soul Hackers presented the writers' bold 90s vision for what a connected future might mean for society. While I don't mind the loss of the hard boiled detective atmosphere that permeated its predecessor, Soul Hackers 2 is meant to be set in an era where data-driven AI has become sentient, but it does almost nothing interesting with it, at least in the 13 hours I've played so far. The world itself might as well be set in the present day. If you're going to spend your precious time on an RPG, or even an Atlus game, you can do much better than this. There are simply more interesting, more memorable games by the esteemed RPG developer which are worth your time over this uninspired sequel.

And last but not least, RINGO BESTO WAIFU

_childDocuments_.review: While this isn't a perfect game by any means, it's still an enjoyable experience, and more than anything I'm glad Atlus finally started paying attention to PC players... even if it's just for a spin off.The biggest positive in this game are the characters themselves and the setting. I can't emphasize enough how happy I am they actually created a cast of adult characters with a sassy female lead who is not a silent blank slate. Ringo is actually one of the best Atlus characters around, but it's a shame she doesn't get a fully fleshed out development. It's also unfortunate that bad sales or reviews will be correlated with the idea that "games with female characters don't sell" or "this didn't do well because it wasn't set in a high school".Dungeons are repetitive, but then again I wasn't exactly expecting a SMT V semi-open world experience here to begin with. The closest thing I could compare them to is P5 Mementos, which personally I don't mind too much. Soul Matrix leaves much to be desired but it's fun to play idly. Battles feel like standard SMT experience but I'm glad they at least tried to innovate it somewhat, rather than just slap on the SMT V system. I know people miss press turn system, but I can do without if it means getting to develop different strategies with familiar demons and skills.The UI and environments (especially the city) look good, in line with what I've come to expect from a modern Atlus game. Maybe it didn't get a high enough budget or as much love as Persona game would but that didn't stop the devs from doing the best they could with the aesthetics.With all that said, I think this game's biggest problem is the price point and evil DLC practices. At a reasonable price this could have done so well, especially for people who wanted to play something casual before P5R gets ported. I can see a lot of players being disappointed that they aren't getting a full SMT/ Persona experience at a full price. This game was never meant to be a mainline entry and it is disappointing to see it suffer from being treated as one because when we put all that aside, I genuinely like it.

_childDocuments_.review: I am going to make a review on mechanics and make a comparison strictly in comparison to other Devil Summoner and SMT games, and I think it's the absolute most essential thing for the game developers themselves to read.Talk and Demon Dialogue is an absolute love hate I have for the series. This game addresses that relationship and did what I always wanted them to do, remove Talking from combat and incorporate it in other ways. I really enjoyed the Demon Auction from Devil Survivor; and wished they would implement that instead of the Talk feature.GO AGAIN! Is my absolute least favorite mechanic in all of SMT. It is iconic, I love weakness/resist/block, I love everything about it, except there are better ways to do it. Say what you want about Sabbath, but it's quick, it's clean, and it removes 1 Hit Party Wipe Lucifer wombos, and having to GAMEFAQ a specific linear boss strategy.The game works the way Persona Works, but all characters are Joker. The powers are borrowed, but a persona is owned.  Invoker vs Evoker; One Summons and borrows, one creates and is locked into that power. They can exist simultaneously in the SMT-Verse. This game shows very clearly what a Devil Summoner is, in other games the exposition is murky even in SMT Core Games.So in short, the gameplay is exemplary and removes the stagnation of GO AGAIN! and keeps the TEAM ATTACK! from Persona games but makes it into a core mechanic and breaks it into pieces.Mechanically the game is smooth, and the TEMPO of the grind is nice so it creates a buffer against monotony. I have yet to feel like I need to run around in a circle and fight for no reason like I did in Soul Hackers, or Another Journey; Instead I feel like I'm running through Pokemon Sword and Shield Zones.Soul Hackers in a Nutshell - The Story is very Soul Hackers - Cyber Themes, in the same way Devil Survivor was. It is very true to SMT, but finally we have a game that FEELS LIKE PERSONA QUALITY OF LIFE, that DROPS THE EXCESSIVE SOCIAL EXPOSITION, and FEELS LIKE A DEVIL SUMMONER GAME, NOT A PERSONA GAME. My only request to new players is to not immediately cancel the game because of the rapping boss. This is a real canonic thing in the SMT Verse; it makes sense only because it's in Devil Summoner. The cyberpunk version uses a Saxophone and a Synthesizer to make Music; This guy is just straight up a bard from DND.And finally, I played through both versions of Nocturne. Dante was a lame sell out capcom ad, but I understand why you used him for the American Audience. SMT V felt like Nocturne in all the wrong ways. It was going back and rebuilding an old mistake and not bringing anything new to the genre. Where is the Quality.I feel like this game would have been a much better game for the MAIN STORY, not the sub story. If you pick one to play if you want to explore SMT, Pick Soul Hackers 2, Do Not Pick SMT V.  Will absolutely recommend the DS games as well to newbies. PS1-PS2 love of SMT is the same fake Love Diablo II fans have.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me say it from the start: The thumbs down is purely because the company decided to separate important parts of the game into day 1 DLC, which includes a side mission with (apparently) quite a bit of context to the story and the ability for enemies to drop certain helpful items and an extra difficulty option (seriously?). Not to mention locking out demons, for whatever reason.The game itself is fairly good. Characters are interesting, each one with a decent personality and backstory you can explore. The combat feels like any Person / Shin Megami Tensei game, just a little bit easier somehow. For those who have not played any of those titles, it is turn based fights that heavily rely on identifying and exploiting your enemies weaknesses, with a big part of the game being mix and matching (or merging) demons to get the upper hand.Overall (so far, at least), the game feels a little worse than the latest entries of the other series, but is still an entertaining game. The only thing i find annoying so far is the multitude of loading screens involved to jump from point A to point B.

_childDocuments_.review: Good musics, good story and interesting characters, nice visuals, new spin on the Atlus gameplay that I do enjoy a lot.Only bug I got is some weird inertia in character control when going over 60 fps, and some few, rare, crashes on startup.A month after release still no fix from Atlus. On github an awesome person named Lyall made a simple mod to fix that. so you should give it a try since it does improve control responsivity a whole lot even at just 60fps.I have finished the game with basically 100% completion.I had a fun time overall, but ... not the best coming from Atlus. It wasn't super long, and like everyone else is saying, yes the dungeons are actually boring except the last one which is probably too short.Not enough variety in the overworld music (to not say no variety at all)Mimi can get really annoying.TLDR : A Good game, but clearly not a great game, just a bit disappointing coming from Atlus.

_childDocuments_.review: This is probably the worst game that I have ever convinced myself to complete.A solid 4-5 / 10 that aggressively wastes your time with rng based puzzles (good luck picking the right teleporter or go back to the beginning), slow movement that then forces you to pay mp to walk faster than a crawl, and large empty paths that force you to struggle through your two-year-old levels of speed. _childDocuments_.review: There is a somewhat decent core of a game here, however I feel like the negatives outweigh the positives so I can't really recommend it.Starting with the battle system, I have to say that it's merely alright. It's the standard "hit weakness, do more damage" fare that you'd see in most other modern MegaTen games, but the press turn system is replaced by the pretty boring Sabbath mechanic that lets you do damage at the end of your turn depending on how many weakness you hit during it. Seems decent on paper, until you realize that it doesn't really do that much, and it's actually pretty useless against boss fights.The COMP upgrade system is rather unimpressive, and all it does is encourage grinding enemies for the necessary materials to buy your upgrades. The upgrades themselves are also pretty boring, and the most exciting thing you can unlock is Commander Skills which are special abilities you can use every few turns in battle that do useful things for ya, like increase your Sabbath stacks, swap demons etc. Every other upgrade is generic "do more damage" or "you can now equip higher tier upgrades". Overall very underwhelming.The story is very average and predictable. The characters are very barebones, and the ending is so basic you can see it coming 10 hours into the game. The first Soul Hackers game at least had great characters to carry the story, while this one doesn't even have that. There's really nothing special to write about here, the story is kinda just... there. The side quests are on par with the main story, and kinda just exist. In a way they're worse than the main story, because you will often find yourself getting asked to go back to the same dungeon you were asked to go to 5 times already to fetch yet another item from yet another random demon. There's 2 particular dungeons, both of which are almost identical looking subway lines, that you are constantly asked to go back to over and over again because the game just doesn't have anywhere else to send you.Finally, what I think is the worst part of the game: the dungeon crawling. 80% of the action takes place in what's called the Soul Matrix, which is a set of 3 dungeons of 5 floors each, which are . It's literally a series of almost untextured corridors floating in a void of nothing where you constantly get spammed by enemies every 2 steps of your way, and your reward for beating each floor is a tiny bit of story dialogue that they could've easily fit anywhere else. I think a good comparison to the Soul Matrix would be the final dungeon of SMT4 Apocalypse, for folks who have played that one. Just a large section of literal nothing that takes needlessly long to complete.I kinda focused on the bad here, but there  things to enjoy here. The combat, despite being simple, is still fun. The boss encounters are mostly enjoyable. The fusion system is as fun as ever.Unfortunately, for every little good thing the game does it does 5 other things poorly, so it's just not worth the time.Play Soul Hackers 1 instead, as this game has nothing to do with it anyways other than share a title.

_childDocuments_.review: **Important**: Make sure to go into the Gameplay section of Config and change Loading Screen Tips to Display (Button advance), this will reduce loading times immensely. Also, you can change the small FoV so that the main character doesn't take 1/4 of the screen. And no, you do not need to play the original Soul Hackers to get the full experience out of this game.This is a lower budget title so keep that in-mind going in. It's not going to blow you away like Atlus's major titles Shin Megami Tensei or Persona. Though it is a good game that you should try if you're an Atlus fan, and the PC version is actually well made -apart from lacking ultrawide support but that's kinda expected-.

_childDocuments_.review: If you are coming from a Persona series perspective, here's what I can tell you. The gameplay is closer to P4, but slightly simpler. There is no schedule mechanics, so if anything is similar with P5 Strikers in that aspect. You can and should build relationships with your party which is easy. Overall the game is good.If you are wondering about negatives, there are few in my opinion. The party doesn't grow beyond a total of 4 members. The dungeon(s) that are dedicated to party members are generic in design (literally all look the same). You acquire the full party pretty quickly at the start since the story depends on having all 4 during the whole time (this may be seen as a negative to some).In terms of DLC it is mainly cosmetic with 3 exceptions. 1. is a side mission DLC. 2. is a demons pack DLC which is probably the one that annoys people the most. 3. is a boost pack, which doesn't automatically break the game since every boost is actually an item so you have full control over when to use it. It can be useful if you are stuck, but generally the money boost is the one that may make the most difference without actually breaking the game.

_childDocuments_.review: The game experience focuses on the characters, story and game play and less on the exploration of game locations and questing; all of which is typical of Atlus games.  The elements the game focuses on it do so well, delivering an engaging experience.  Refreshingly the game is technically sound, which in these days is a seemingly difficult accomplishment to get a quality working game launched.  Our main protagonist is not the typical blank insert, she has personality which is brought to life with a competent script and good voice acting.  This holds true for all of the main cast of characters. I found the combat system akin to Toyko Sessions, but instead of your team landing combo attacks when weakness are hit on your enemy, Soul Hackers 2 uses Sabbaths which initially are stacked by hitting weaknesses (later there are alternative ways to add "stacks" to this feature), which will unleash demons in the stack in an all out attack at the end of the player's attack phase.  All in all a good game experience.

_childDocuments_.review: It's decent. 7.5/10Its decent, but playing this right after Persona 5 hurts its score.Persona 5 had fast combat animations, great soundtracks, good pacing, and interesting maps.Soul Hackers 2 combat feels slower, soundtrack not memorable, a lot of side quests, and the 'soul' dungeons are all the same maze like style. Pros:The world is a futuristic japan with demons summoning being the normal.Main characters are fairly cool and their story unravels as you play.The shops owners are like side characters with their own side quests and stories.Side quests are quite interesting for lore, world builder, and store owner stories. There are defeat or collect x amount of item requests, but you can usually do them alongside the main story/more interesting side quests.Japanese and English voice included. The japanese sounds more impactful to me, but you do miss out on battle dialogues not being shown as subtitles.The sprites/artwork are nice and animated to talk and blink.The camera work during cut scenes are quite nice and have more effort put into it. Con:Combat is not snappy and feels slow. There is a speed up option that doesn't feel nice to watch, but it does help.Initiating combat is odd. You need to swing at the enemies model and then walk up to it to start combat. I get its there so you can skip battles (swing but don't touch), but feels odd.Map list is ehh. Its gets long, and theres not indents to help quickly locate city or store options.Weird default settings. Like character purposely being off center, insanely zoom in camera, voice actors speaks before the text is able to appear. All can be fix in settings, but just weird choices to have as their default.Dungeons gets boring quick. It just reused dungeons with long branches paths where you either hit a dead end or go the right path.Overall:Its a decent JRPG, don't recommend for full price. If you haven't played Persona 5 yet, choose that instead. Soul Hackers 2 is if you just want more SMT/Persona style game.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a shame this game's catching so much venom!From my perspective, as a willing supporter of those who create and publish works like this, Soul Hackers 2 is a slick, fresh, modern take on the long running Shin Megami Tensei / Persona Universe. The characters are compelling, the Japanese voice acting is superb, the localization has done a fine job with the challenges faced by translators. The art work and style are excellent, consistent, and well-used in conveying the tricky bits involved in AI personalities interacting with Human Beings.Any experience you've had with all those previous games in the SMT/P series carries over well into finding your way around this piece of world building. And yet, remarkably, it feels fresh. Well done, authors, artists, and Atlus! My own time with SMT goes back to the PS Vita and Nintendo products of that era. I'm thoroughly enjoying this game! One thing I've noticed with this particular battle system; in many turn-based team battle settings it often feels optimal for your team members to gang up on opposing targets, eliminating them one by one - for each one quickly eliminated, that's one less source of incoming fire.Not so here! Instead, it seems to be preferable to spread the damage across as many in the enemy group as possible, to bring their HP count down across the board, so that when Ringo lets go with a Stack Attack you can wipe out multiple targets in one swipe. Very interesting. Battles in Soul Hackers 2 take on a completely different dynamic from a lot of other turn-based battle system games. It feels fresh and interesting.Now, there are technical aspects to the Denuvo Digital Rights Management (DRM) solution that some folks object to as a matter, to them, of principle. Perhaps they feel they should have the right to copy and redistribute software freely, despite that specifically being prohibited by the Terms of Use they've agreed to by installing and starting the software. What we purchase is not the software, but the limited and specific rights to use it, under license. Copyright laws vary by nation but are established with consistent intent to protect the rights of authors and publishers of creative works. Those rights are not cancelled simply because someone doesn't agree with them, any more than your right to speak would be cancelled if I didn't agree with you.Like the game? Want to try the game? Buy the game. if you're offended by the DRM implementation, then return the game under Valve's Terms of Use and get your refund. But please don't tear down or trash-talk a game or a game publisher simply because they've taken steps to protect their rights to a creative work.Does this trash-talking happen to every game that employs Denuvo DRM? If so, that's an injustice against the authors and artists. And while we're at it, the level of piracy in the present world is a plague upon any creative house trying to produce and publish copyrighted work in a sustainable way. Want less noxious DRM? Stop downloading copyrighted works from piracy sites.And none of this has any bearing on the merits of this work as a game. I've been enjoying it very much, and feel anyone who's enjoyed previous excursions into this universe will probably enjoy this one as well!So thanks again, authors, artists, composers, musicians, and publishers! My life is enriched by your creative efforts, and I'm glad to support them!Addin, now at  65 game-hours,,,Still a strong recommend for this one! I'm actually playing it in parallel with Persona 4, 5, and Soul Hackers 1 on the 3DS. It's turning into quite the late Autumn/early Winter binge here, and I'm thoroughly enjoying it!Some folks say the Soul Matrix levels are tedious, or overly plain: Bah! Look at them on a decent monitor, they're a nice rendering of the idea of a synthetic reality - and their design from a game architecture standpoint is just fine. The stairs come along when they need to, the gates are well-placed, the story-reveals are meaningful and significant, if you just let the story do its thing on you; there's really no problem here.So in sum, at this stage, this is a game that belongs in the SMT Universe. There's room in the world for Golf, Croquet, and Frisbee Golf, too!

_childDocuments_.review: As far as Jrpgs go this is a very good game. I love all the SMT and Persona games and I think if you go into this expecting that you might be disappointed Atlus have delivered much better. The majority of hate and mixed reviews I feel like has stemmed from hardcore SMT fans expecting another big budget game.The character development I really liked and warmed up to all the teammates. Ringo is a very good protagonist I much preferred her over the persona main characters for the most part. The story was as you'd expect its a cookie cutter Atlus experience but the game did have some amazing moments I just wished some parts of the game were more fleshed out and other bits should have been streamlined, the pacing was a little iffy at times but peak moments were amazing.The demon fusion and character customisation is amazing as expected and the game has its own unique twists not offered in the other games so even if you're tired of the same Megaten stuff you can build your team and strategise differently.The ost was pretty good especially the event and boss themes, unfortunately you'll likely get sick of hearing it by the end.My main problem with the game is the dungeons, they get extremely repetitive and by the end I just ran through avoiding all battles and the final area was pretty disappointing to me I almost couldn't be bothered to finish it, the battling and story overstayed its welcome which was sad because I felt like I did want more of the game, just not what I was given.I still suggest if you've not played any Atlus game before, play a different one first, this is not the best they can do. If you want a challenge I'd play SMT instead the game got easy even while being underlevelled on hard. But if you're more there for the story and not dungeon crawling I'd definitely recommend! Just pick it up on sale if you can it's gone 50% off a few times.

_childDocuments_.review: I’m a big MegaTen fan, but I just couldn’t do this one. Soul Hackers 2 has some good ideas and has some of the aspects that I love from this series, but ultimately, I was unable to finish the game and it felt like a chore to get as far as I did.The game starts with an almost forty minute cutscene sequence and that kinda sets the tone for the pacing here. It is slow, monotonous, and one of the laziest JRPGs I have played in a while which really hurts to say given the studio that it’s coming from.The dungeons are quite literally just connected hallways and small rooms, there is VERY little actual variety there and the devs couldn’t even be bothered to include chests or other physical treasure to find. The exploration is limited to dead ends that sometimes have one of your demons standing by to hand you an item.It doesn’t even take that long to get that bad, because by the second dungeon you are literally walking on floating hallways and rooms in cyberspace. It is the most basic of JRPG dungeon designs and is something I would expect from a student project, not a full-fledged AAA production from a respected studio.I wouldn’t say the story has been terrible so far, but it has hardly done anything to hold my interest. It’s your typical JRPG sci-fi with just a bit of edge to it, kinda reminiscent of Scarlet Nexus, but a bit more narrow in its focus. This is good in some ways, but given the already slow pacing, it’s a bit of a pain as you wait for things to build up and the sheer number of cutscenes included here does not do it any favors.The only thing I outright enjoyed here would be the combat. It’s your usual turn-based combat, elemental attack types, strengths, weaknesses, bunch of items to use and upgrades to equip, and my favorite element from this series - the ability to recruit demons and fuse them together into stronger ones.All of that is some good stuff. Granted, it doesn’t really do much to elevate it further than that, but at this point I will take what I can get from this game.Outside of that, there’s nothing else really to note here. It’s a roughly 30 hour JRPG with okay graphics, okay music, and fun combat, but absolutely awful dungeon design, a monotonous gameplay loop, and a story that leans more towards boring than interesting. I had planned to finish this one up for a full review, but honestly, I just can’t see myself burning any more time than I already have here.Follow my  for more reviews + videos!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is disappointing.It's stylish. It's "the sequel" to one of the weirdest SMT spinoffs, giving it a lot of room to experiment without being bound by past titles. If I were to describe to you the story or some of the events, it has a really, really interesting concept, and the cutscenes and characters are visually distinct and fun, with solid performances. It also has a few incredibly nice quality of life features (props to whoever decided to have an icon pop up over enemies in the field you need to take on for quests! That saved me so much time!).But this game feels like it was made on a budget of about $50 and all the coffee the team could ask for, Long stretches of the game are running through multiple "separate" dungeons which consist of the same tilesets. (Two of them are the most egregious, feeling straight up identical, including reusing their opening area.) The vast majority of gameplay is technically optional, being identical gray voids which will ask you to rerun the same three quests no less than FIFTEEN TIMES (this sounds like a joke, this is not a joke), but for the power curve or having any kind of money on hand, you'll want to take these on. Just using the demon compendium is massively grindy and more expensive than ever, and if you try to go without it, recruiting demons is more RNG-based than the series runs on*. I hate saying it, but the GAMEPLAY portion of this game feels unfinished and cobbled together from the assets they had on hand when deadline struck.I completed this game, I even got the "good" ending, but I feel like nothing sums up how soul-sucking this game is that the content was so bare-bones, and the cast dwindles so fast with named character deaths, that I kept thinking I was coming up on the final dungeon over and over for the last 12 hours of my 33 total runtime, because I didn't see how they could draw anything more out of what remained. (The fact that the final chapter is basically only hinted at in one scene and then actually contained more lead-up in the DLC campaign makes me suspect that the DLC was content removed from this base game to have ANYTHING to sell.) I will never call anyone who says they enjoyed this a liar, but I'm cautioning any single person reading to stay the hell away.Also I just realized at the end of this I literally cannot recall the soundtrack to this game. Not a single track.* Oh, you think I'm joking, or this is hyperbole? You need to do the following to recruit a demon. 1. Find one of YOUR demons in the preset 'search' points in the dungeon. 2. Hope that the demon has the recruitment icon over their head, not "key item", "item search", or "healing" instead. 3. Talk to them and hope that it's a demon you want or haven't already got, a thing you can't tell from a distance or until you engage. 4. There's one final bit of RNG in that now you have to do the bargaining step from other games, taking their requests until satisfied as usual. If any of these steps fail, return to 1. Have fun filling out a team.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: I would not recommend this for someone getting into the SMT genre because it is a bad representation. If you've played other SMT games and are expecting something similar to those I would also not recommend it (DO MORE RESEARCH). For the truly brave that want something different (perhaps worse imo) then I think you could consider this game it just feels very unfinished to me. I have not played Soul Hackers 1, I played a bit of the remaster and it didn't really interest me so I do not know if it's a good successor to that game.Just for some background, I've played a bit of SMTIII Nocturne, finished SMTIVA, SMTV, Devil Survivor 1, Devil Survivor 2, the upgraded versions of those games as well, Persona 4 Golden, Persona 5, Persona 5R, Persona 5S and I am near the end of this game and I don't know if I can finish it. I consider myself in between a casual and hardcore for this genre at least the modern version.For a modern game it feels really bad, more specifically unfinished. I'll try to not go into the specifics of the story, but most of the game play is mapping around the dungeon, fetch quest via talking to demons, and talking to your teammates. I struggled coming up with a third point cause it's mostly the first two. The dungeon experience is straight out of Persona 4 or SMT4A but worse because they make you do more with the same movement and those games came out in 2008 and 2016 respectively. The puzzles in Soul Hackers 2 are just infuriating and inconvenient, the maps are plain, and walking around just feels like a chore. The movement and attacks also feel clunky, while it's not important in a game like this I thought I should point it. All this just screams to me that it was rushed because there is practically 0 depth to the dungeons.Another issue I have with this game is the overworld. It feels so empty. It's pretty much the shops to get items, interact with teammates, demon fusion, quest shop, and restaurants for food. A lot of things are tied to character interactions which honestly they are all pretty bland.Moving on to the combat... it feels unrewarding. The press turn battle system has evolved into sabbath attacks which replace bonus turns for more damage at the end of your turn, which can be modified with different abilities but most of them suck imo. I feel like this is move is bad because it restricts a player's choice. It only allows you to get more damage down as opposed to healing or buffing yourself again which feels worse to me. It's not like this helps with resource management either because your MP pool is so big plus you can always just leave, heal, and come back.Another issue for me personally is demon fusion. You are restricted to 6 skill slots with I think 0 amps for specific elements, although these come in the forms of augments for your comp which can be debated on whether this is good or bad. I think this discourages you from swapping demons too often as you only have so many augment slots and they are also linked to farmable materials + money. There are also far fewer elements in this game than say Persona or even SMT which means easier element coverage but also demon variety seems lower. Also money is painful to farm, I have the DLC and it's still rough fusing demons, so I couldn't imagine what it's like for people without.Side Note: RIP Hassou Tobi you will be missedAs someone else said in their review it's like a mix between a Persona game and SMT except it does both poorly.End of gameplay stuffPOTENTIAL SPOILERS MAINLY JUST TALKING ABOUT CHARACTERS AND HOW BAD THE STORY IS IGNORE IF YOU DON'T WANT TO KNOW ANYTHING Characters:StorySide Note/Rant (PROBABLY A SPOILER)Idk this was a rant cause I was really excited for this game, it looked cool like Persona 5, SMTV had some great combat imo, and I had an itch for a new SMT game and this just didn't scratch it at all.

_childDocuments_.review: 8/10 - The SMT (Shin Megami Tensei) series may not be for everyone, but as a fan of turn-based JRPGs, I thoroughly enjoyed this game. If you're also a fan of the genre, it's definitely worth purchasing, especially when it's on sale. The game boasts a solid story, which seems like it draws inspiration from The Ghost in the Shell series. The characters each have their own personal traumas, which can be explored through the Axis, similar to Persona 5's Momentos level design. The game's artwork and sound are both exceptional, and the battle system, while different from previous SMT games, is still enjoyable, particularly with the addition of Sabbath actions that allow for customization and special actions that can be taken per turn that require some planning to make the most of out in boss battles. The character customization is a highlight, with the combination of augments and demons allowing for individual strengths to be maximized, individual characters affinity to be increased, and accessories and meals to buff the team.However, the level design is lackluster, with poorly thought-out mazes that feel tedious to navigate. Boss battles are particularly punishing (as expected, I played the game on hard), requiring grinding that can disrupt the pacing of the story, although this is typical of SMT games. Overall, the game offers a challenging and enjoyable experience, with its art, story, characters, battle system, and customization all impressing. While the level design may not be the best, it's a great follow-up to the original game and references it in subtle ways, but falls short in similar ways the original did.

_childDocuments_.review: I liked Soul Hackers 2, the visuals are stylish, the story is pretty well written with some cool philosophical stuff, the music is stellar, the animated art that emotes along with the conversation is soooo coool and immersive. The characters in the game are all pretty well written and Ringo is a great example of an interesting Main Character. I really hope that the MC in future games can be an actual character instead of a card board cut out going forward! If you just want a good looking game with a solid story then it's pretty good. This issues with the game come from the fact that it's an ATLUS game and has some siblings that are hard to be compared to.This is NOT a Persona game, so if you are coming off of that Persona 5 PC release looking for a fix, you won't find it here. There's no life sim, and no dating. I honestly kind of feel the same can be said for Shin Megami fans looking for their next fix too, as this game lacks the press turn systems that create challenging but fair combat in that side of the franchise.Instead it uses a new system called the Stack that I think is interesting and forces you to utilize items more, but has some issues. The stack instead of giving you extra turns for exploiting a weakness creates a stack of damage that will be dealt at the end of your teams round, and there will sometimes be additional effects added to that depending on the demons you have. You will unlock more ways to make the stack stronger as the game progresses as well. Ultimately while I find the stack interesting it does not pair well with the typical difficulty of a Shin Megami game. I originally started playing on Hard, but had to switch it down to normal just because I felt the stack didn't give me enough agency to deal with the deadly enemies I was facing. Even on normal a lot of the fights didn't feel like the stack contributed enough to give me any sort of advantage or survivability. Overall I don't think this game is a bad game, but it's not your typical Shin Megami game. If you are aware of that I think you can come in and enjoy it for being a game with a good story, good characters, and great music. Though honestly I'd turn down the difficulty and just focus on the story.

_childDocuments_.review: This game feels like it was made by whoever was leftover from working on the persona ports at the atlus offices.Soul Hackers 2 is probably the easiest megaten game out there from my experience, but if you're unfamiliar with megaten games as a whole, it might give you some challenge. That said, I don't recommend this as your first outing as it'll give you a bad first impression on what to expect going forwards.The good:The setting and presentation are nice, lots of style to be had if you're a sci-fi nerd and need a change of pace from your average cyberpunk dystopia. (Not that the dystopian aspect isn't explored at all)Character design is stellar, especially for the important shop keepers you return to throughout the game.The voice acting well done for the human characters and the jack frost monsters.And the story is by far the games best strong suit.The bad:Simply put, this game overstays its welcome by a long shot.If you're B lining it for the story you might not feel anything beyond the occasional grind wall for neglecting side content.However, being a completionist, or 80%ist, the game is littered with busy work that can feel more time wasting than interesting.by the 30 hour mark, you've already seen all there is aside from the stories conclusion.Dungeons easily feel like stretches of land with nothing to do in them aside from fight, but you'll start to avoid combat after a while as the only time the game tests you is through the "target" series of side missions.These missions start out fun, helping you come up with clever ways to beat the fight like a puzzle, but eventually feel like a gotcha for not investing in a monster who can use a particular skill. made worse by the fact, the hardest target missions, require abilities you don't "need" for anything in the base game.its not hard because you can't use your head, its hard because you happen to not have the answer with you, and you'll have to then spend the time to go bad and rebuild a particular monster to have the move.The sad thing is, these will be the things that get you killed in almost every circumstance. the fights run on a timer where if you take too long, they'll throw out a move that insta kills the party. I can still count on two hands the amount of times I died to fights normally.On the target of dungeons, the thing that finally got me to write them off, almost every late game dungeon relies on putting long hallways with rooms that have multiple teleporters everywhere. one or two, ok. but when five dungeons do the same thing back to back, thats not challenging. thats mind numming. made worse by the fact they all look the same.Demon negotiation is all but nonexistent in this. Now you just find you monsters throughout the dungeon, the demon will show up, ask for something slightly more demanding depending on how many of the said demon you've killed. they then join you no question.the voices for the demons outside of the jack bros series aren't fitting either. recent game gave them good voices, but now suddenly ones who normally sound refined and calculated sound crazy and silly.what version should you get?either the deluxe or ultimate edition. get them on sale. don't pay full price for any version.the inclusions either version provide make the overall game easier to swallow, especially with how low the price point has been getting on sales lately.Final verdict: 6/10TLDR: its OK. but thats it. don't bother trying to 100% it. Don't make this your first megaten game either.

_childDocuments_.review: Initial impressions: The trailer art style is semi deceiving. Initial impressions set my expectations to something close to Tokyo Mirage Session however the lighting and shading work lends it somewhere closer to a noir comic book like style. If you enjoyed PS2 Megaten games (like I do) the game navigates kinda similar, in a close up 3rd person view. The controls are a bit difficult and throw you off but they aren't intolerable. The combat system is highly controversial, and I can't say for late game, but initial impressions are interesting to say the least.People are disappointed that Press Turn isn't the system that Atlus went with, and while I also enjoy press turn this was to be expected even before the games release. Devil Summoner games (which this game should fall under) tends to be Atlus's test bed for different combat systems. Devil Summoner 1 and Soul Hacker has its loyalty system, Raidou Kuzunoha has its real-time battle system, and Soul Hacker 2 has the Sabbath system. Its sort of like 5's essence system and 3's magatama system. The player character gains the affinity of the demons they have selected and use demon skills during their turn. The player doesn't summon the demon to the field, rather they use the demons skill directly, and if the skill is especially effective against a foe the demon will stick around till the end of the round. At the end of a combat round the demons engage in a Sabbath and inflict extra damage against the enemy party. The side effect of this system is characters can only summon 1 demon each, a maximum of 4 per party. Its a far cry from the 4+ party characters and I can see it leading to less complex party set ups compared to Soul Hacker 1, but once again this isn't the first time Devil Summoner has limited the active demons in a player party. It's not the worst combat system but I can see why many don't like it compared to the other games. I enjoy it (as of writing this) but it's worth knowing this is the main gameplay for this game. The combat animations are exceptional, all characters have a stylish aura and demeanor (yes even the guy in the hoody, he looks cooler in person than in the trailer).People often ask why Soul Hacker 2, rather than Devil Summoner: Aion or whatever. Besides Soul Hacking being a main story mechanic it probably has to do with its themes being directly connected to Soul Hacker's. Where Soul Hacker's main themes and setting was all about the exponential growth of technological capability and how the explosion of tech in the 90s was rapidly changing the living standards of all people, Soul Hackers 2 directly follows it up with modern days continued technological growth and yet somehow the stagnation of human living standards. Even if tech is still getting better as the years have gone on we as people haven't been greatly changed. Not in any utopian way that the 90s had envisioned it atleast. Only time will tell if this theme is fully realized but I can at least understand the Soul Hacker 2 monicure.TLDR/Conclusion;I'm not saying this is the best game or even one of the best. Its probably not going to break new ground in the SMT fandom in terms of story or gameplay, as many have pointed out in there own Reviews. However I see very little reason as of now to not recommend it to people who enjoy SMT and Atlus games in general. If you set your expectations to that of a decent, if simpler take on Devil Summoner I doubt you will be disappointed. I see very little reason to by the game full priced and with DLC. I only did it because I like to support Atlus's game developers. I honestly have never played a bad Atlus game. Many tedious and some that were kinda boring, but never bad. Play on Hard if you are familiar with Atlus games (its closer to other Atlus games Normal, and remember there is a Very Hard that should be closer to the expected Hard mode).

_childDocuments_.review: Probably the least engaging megaten game.Story feels rushed. It's just moving from point A to point B, and at point B a big story moment happens, nothing happens in-between. Even SMT5, the game with THE HAT SCENE, has a better spine.And it really surprises me how so many people claim that the characters in this game are good. While they get their development, it's extremely predictable. In the end it's not like their beliefs actually matter, there is so little conflict they might as well just make all the characters best friends who always agree. And when it comes to picking a dialogue option the game literally tells you who likes your answer, not even persona does that.Oh and it's not a sequel to soul hackers. It does not have the world building, characters, art direction, gameplay, themes or anything even in the style of soul hackers. It doesn't matter if they have soul hacking or name a character Kuzunoha, it is clear this was not made as a follow up to any devil summoner game, especially not soul hackers, and all the terms were just shoehorned in.The gameplay is so bare bones it's not even worth trying to learn the details. It's literally just hit enemy weaknesses and get an all out attack. Didn't hit a weakness? Well you're gonna deal 5 damage, even with high stats. Because demons don't matter half of the time. Fusion should only be used to get the next level of elemental spells for your party, no need to think about stats or costs. I got past the halfway point of the game I'm pretty sure, and I barely fused any demons, because they don't do anything. 90% of your stats are tied to your character, the rest 10% is from your demon, they get added up, so it ends up just like SMT5, only your character level matters for scaling. And the dungeons are just hallways. Just dark tunnels, rarely any quirks, and no secrets at all. You could argue that is what dungeon crawling is, but actual fun videogames have engaging events and reward exploration. In this game you just walk into a bunch of dead ends until you get on the correct path. It's actually insane how much detail they put into shopping areas you rarely visit with a bunch of NPCs and stuff that serve absolutely no purpose. Yet they can't make the player interact with a dungeon environment. Hell, they literally had to add the option to sprint in an update since the dungeons are such big snoozefests.It's not as bad as persona 3, but it's still a disgrace to soul hackers and the megaten franchise.

Gonna write short review/impressions after playing for 12 hours: I hate to admit this, but the story of this game even at the beginning already beating SMT V one, SMT V bland and forgetful cast with no exposition is easily beaten by Soul Hackers 2. PC performance and controls are flawless, no complaints (just make sure to change in-menu loading screen settings to hide or advance with a button so load times are instant instead of 10 seconds). _childDocuments_.review: I am a longtime fan of the Megami Tensei series. I've played nearly every game since I started with Persona 2 on the PS1. While I am not yet finished this game, I am really enjoying my time with the game so far, and I am fairly confident that other fans of the series will find something to enjoy here as well.First, the gameplay. This game evokes a similar feeling to older entries in the series. Press turn is notably absent, replaced with a more traditional turn-based combat system. Your team takes their actions, hitting enemy weaknesses to gain stacks, which are consumed at the end of your turn to deal extra damage to the entire enemy team. There is not much strategy beyond just hitting weaknesses for some extra bonuses, but some skills and abilities unlocked later in the game provide some stack interactions that add some much needed texture into the combat. Navigation of the combat system uses a similar menu layout as found in Persona 5, and it feels snappy and responsive. Combat is surprisingly fast paced due to the ease of menu navigation, coupled with short animations, and there is almost a musical rhythm to it that feels very satisfying. Overall, while I would prefer that the combat simply used the press turn system, it is more than a serviceable combat system as it is.The next core part of any Megaten game is the demons. Unlike a more traditional Megaten title, your demons do not join you in battle. Rather, they are equipped to your human party members in a manner similar to how it works for the main characters in the Persona series. During fusion, you have the ability to reassign any skill in the skill pool, including a demon's base kit. This means that you get quite a bit of flexibility when fusing. It seems that demons in this game only have a maximum of 6 skill slots. While that may seem like it reduces the overall possibilities for a build, that ends up basically not being that relevant. Your party members each are able to equip passive skills that affect various properties, so the end result is that you will still have access to at least 8 skill slots that affect your combat prowess.I actually quite like the exploration and dungeon design as well. There are a few clever contextual mechanics and puzzles sprinkled throughout. There is one dungeon where its unchanging aesthetic makes it visually boring after a while, but I think it is a relatively minor complaint. I liked how you basically never need to bother with combat unless you want to, and can just focus on exploration. I found myself simply knocking enemies away in the dungeons with my sword and running past them, then catching myself up by using the rubberbanding exp gains to level myself up right before a boss by doing some side content. Yes, the dungeons have been more interesting before. I personally think the design of SMT dungeons probably peaked in Strange Journey, but what we have here is still more than enjoyable, if just a touch on the easy side.The fusion interface is one of my favourites ever in terms of both ease of use and presentation of information. There is a fusion search feature with many search options, including a compendium fusion option that allows you to automatically summon and fuse a fodder demon from your compendium. It also allows you the choice of summoning either the base demon for cheap, or your customized entry for the full price. I've already spent a solid chunk of time just fusing things for fun, and I imagine I will spend quite a bit more.This game is also beautiful to look at. Just like Persona 5, it oozes charm. Rather than a picareseque roguish style, this game draws its art direction from its more cyberpunk oriented roots. Characters are visually distinct and really stand out, thanks to some brilliant designs from artist Shirow Miwa. Coupled with the outstanding art direction, the music is also impeccable. The soundtrack blends a variety of genres, from dubstep to power metal, once again highlighting the techno roots of the cyberpunk aesthetic. I particularly enjoyed the COMP Smith track. The guitar riff in that track calls back to Digital Devil Saga, making for a nostalgic trip back in time.I tried to stay away from much in the way of trailers ahead of time, and I was expecting that the protagonist, Ringo, would be an emotionless doll like so many other AI characters in anime-adjacent media. That is surprisingly not the case, as she is a lovable ball of sass and sarcasm. Alongside Ringo, the other cast members are all likeable as well, gradually opening up their backstories over the course of the game, and their constant banter is both believable and adds some levity to an otherwise dark story. I am playing the game using the English dub after having forgotten to change it before I started the game. I ended up being pleasantly surprised by the voice acting and delivery of lines, and have been largely happy to keep it on English voices.So far, the story is fine. There is nothing head-turning here, but what is here is done competently. There is a plot about some secret conspiracy to destroy the world and remake it using the power of some MacGuffins. Pretty typical Megaten faire. I assert that plot has never really been the strong suit of the series anyway, and that so long as it is inoffensive, it serves its purpose well enough as a means to an end to move us from dungeon to dungeon, where the real fun takes place.Overall, I really have been enjoying my time with the game. I don't think it's perfect by any means, but I take comfort in its relative simplicity. I also accept that this game is not going to be everyone's cup of tea. If you became interested in the Megaten franchise through Persona 5, this game probably doesn't have much of what drew you in. If you're someone who really just likes a classic JRPG, this is like a Dragon Quest game with a splash of Megaten paint on it. I know people are hungering for anything at all like Persona and getting disappointed that this isn't it, but games like this are great too. It's comforting and beautiful in its simplicity, and a genuine love letter to days past and the games of old.

_childDocuments_.review: Persona 5 + SMTV with an identity crisis and a $15 budget. Not very good to say the least. Not terrible but not good either, very much a 6/10 game. In terms of it being an SMT Game its like a 3/10 for me. Simplifies most of the core gameplay and appeal of Both Mainline SMT and Persona to the point of it being completely dumbed down and losing most depth. Not to mention the game honestly feel kinda janky and somewhat lacking an identity. This was definitely made by Atlus' C team who couldn't decide what the game was supposed to be and focused too hard on blending SMT and Persona to the point that they forgot the core concepts and appeal of both, giving us a game that doesn't match the appeal of either. It has some things to like like character designs of an alright cyberpunk aesthetic but all of it is bogged down by some of the worst dungeon designs and combat I've seen in an SMT game. I hope you like running through empty corridors with no variation and hearing your party members speak literally any time you open any menu in combat (Seriously i don't know how that made it into the final game the way it is) plus the whole "Sabbath" System isn't nearly as fun or engaging as something like the press turn system or the 1 more system. Atlus tried to reinvent the wheel when they already have combat and dungeon designs mastered. I don't being negative as SMT and Persona are some of my favorite franchises ever but with this trying to be a hybrid of both it has massive expectations to live up to, even without those expectations this is still just a very meh game at best. If you are Persona fan reading this and you are looking to get into Mainline SMT this is NOT the game. Play either Nocturne or SMTV, I'd also recommend SMTIV and SMTIV:A if you have a 3DS still. All of those game are significantly better first entries into mainline SMT imo. If you are are a Persona fan looking for more Persona you will be disappointed. If you are an SMT fan or a fan of the OG Soul Hackers you will probably be even more disappointed. Overall i sadly wouldn't really recommend it to anyone and doubt this game will even be mentioned a few years from now. Hope Atlus can learn from this and this flop doesn't discourage us getting more SMT spin off games but i'm not super confident considering Persona being the money printer that it is.P.S. Haven't beaten the game myself but watched a friend of mine play through the whole game past where i was because i really couldn't be bothered. 7 hours was more than enough for me because the same blue-grey boxy dungeons gave me a headache.P.P.S. ATLUS ♥♥♥♥ OF WITH ♥♥♥♥♥♥ DAY 1 DLC LIKE THIS. It doesn't get much lower than locking fan favorite demons behind a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ paywall. _childDocuments_.review: This is a tough one to recommend. If you're going into it for the story experience with some nice characters and voice acting with a serviceable battle system and a decent-to-good presentation, I would recommend this game. However, if you asked me to describe what I did for most of my 40 hour play through, most of what I describe would sound mediocre and not worth sinking time into. It rides that middle line really hard between recommending and not recommending.I'll get the bad stuff out of the way first. As many people have mentioned already, dungeon crawling in this game is repetitive, and frankly, bad. It feels tedious going through both the main story areas and the Soul Matrix (which is this games Tartarus or Mementos), and you are often expected to go through each of these areas several times to complete side quests or to level up your characters/fill out your demon collection.  I always have to put something on in the background, whether it's music or Youtube videos, because these dungeons are so mindless and boring. What's worse is that the further you get in, the more that dungeons incorporate new mechanics that only serve to waste more of your time, such as teleporters that don't function how you would expect them to that often times teleport you in the opposite direction of your goal. Unfortunately, this is where most of my play time came from, and what you have heard about the dungeon crawling experience from everyone else is true. Dungeon crawling is punctuated by the battle system of the game, which is perfectly acceptable, if a little boring. In my time with such games as Shin Megami Tensei 3 and Persona 5, the combat in Soul Hackers 2 feels far simpler, and mostly boils down to "use attacks that are good against weaknesses". It honestly feels a lot like modern Pokemon games, except more challenging. I was able to get through the entire story and most of the Soul Matrix with this strategy in mind on normal difficulty, though I wouldn't be surprised if the harder difficulties required you to incorporate more 4D chess into your strategies. It's an inoffensive combat system, but it's hardly something that's a main draw for this game. If you have played any SMT or Persona game, you will feel right at home, but don't expect anything revolutionary or progressive about itThe worst part about this game? The DLC, and how much it actually affects your experience. In the final few hours of my play time, I decided to purchase the BGM and Costume pack, as well as the "Booster Item Pack". Neither of these pieces of DLC were worth it, especially in the case of the BGM pack (how are you going to charge 13 dollars for music that already exists and a few costumes?). For the booster pack, this DLC is basically a god mode, allowing you to max out all your characters, AND demons, AND your in game wallet, and all you have to do is give 5 dollars to Atlus. I thought it was bad when Ubisoft added XP boosters to Assassin's Creed, but the booster pack for Soul Hackers 2 compromises every challenging encounter in this game and makes an already mindless game EVEN MORE mindless. This alone was getting me close to not recommending this game; it's obvious they cut out content from this game to sell it back to consumers on day 1, and Atlus (along with every other large video game company) needs to stop this crap.However, after thinking about my experience after playing this game for 40 hours across about 10 days, I realized that I enjoyed myself enough to warrant being satisfied with my experience once the credits started rolling. For those that wanted more of a Shin Megami Tensei story experience that revolves around adults as opposed to high school kids, I have to say that this was a nice, engaging story with a good cast of characters. Of course, this is mostly subjective, so it's difficult to sell this game to someone on just narrative alone. I will say, if you are into melodramatic anime-style JRPG's, you will really like the story, characters, setting, and just about everything that surrounds this game aesthetically. In particular, I want to give kudos to the voice cast for this game; most of the dialogue in this game is fully voice, and the English voice actors do a great job (gold stickers for both Ringo and Milady's voice actresses).Ultimately, my conclusion is that I do recommend this for those that want to see a cool story in a cool setting. If you don't think that you can stomach hours and hours of dungeon crawling, don't pick this up. Either way, I would highly recommend picking this up on sale and NOT buying the DLC. Another caveat on that: if you've never played any other SMT or Persona games, play those first. Persona 4 Golden is also on Steam, is way less expensive, and way better in general. Once you're balls deep into Shin Megami Tensei, then you should give this a shot. I know the optics around this game aren't exactly glowing, but I still had a good time going through the main game and helping Jack Frost kill a bunch of random demons 5 different times.
