_childDocuments_.review: I hate this rating system.It's hard to give this game a "not recommended" when in fact, the truth is somewhere in the middle. It's not a bad game at all. It's also not spectacular if you've played other games in the SMT universe. This game is a Cyberpunk interpretation of a SMT game. The world is quite interesting and the characters are well written. But just not enough time and effort was put into the game that it needed.To summarize, the game seems like it had a great blueprint with a lot of potential on paper, but due to a shoestring budget or other reasons, the game was never given the chance to blossom. The world while interesting, is bare bones. You are not told enough about the events that led up to the world you are now inhabiting. There aren't any Social Links/Confidants (Persona) to flesh out the world. Instead, you have one place that you can meet with your party members where you accumulate "Soul Points" in order to unlock gates in their respective mini-dungeons. The mini-dungeons of each character are repetitive and predictable.  Speaking of the dungeons, they are also mundane. Each dungeon plays the same, and while they might have small differences in size and scope, they are essentially the same kind of place and suffer from severe repetition.The story had potential but felt incomplete. The story, which is good on paper and could have had some really compelling moments, was held back by some instances of clumsy writing and the main event scripting which felt a bit rushed.The only place the game shines is the gameplay. It's good ol' SMT Devil Summoner gameplay. The gameplay does all the heavy lifting for the game because otherwise, I would have gotten bored and stopped around the 20th hour. So much potential wasted. If you have never played a SMT or Persona game and can get it on discount, then you should pick it up. Otherwise, save your money and wait for the next Persona game.

_childDocuments_.review: Really wish there was a neutral option on Steam, but since there isn't, I'll just settle for a recommend only because I did find myself having more fun than not. That being said, this game just doesn't feel complete. Not in the way of playability (bugs, glicthes, etc.), but more in a sense where it doesn't really have enough polish.I've played plenty of the other SMT games, so honestly I just bought this game because I'm waiting for P5R to release on Steam and I had already beaten P4G this year. With comparisons in mind, I really like the difference in combat in this game, the main difference being that attacking weaknesses won't stun enemies, but instead adds up to extra damage at the end of your turn, which itself can be modified in a bunch of different ways. As a result, getting hit is guaranteed, and it forces you to choose between offense and defense more than before. Other than that, its essentially the same, but for me, that was really just what I was looking for anyway. Upgrading weapons is a tad too grind-reliant, as it requires materials on top of the currency. All the options do allow for making more specialized builds with each character, but unfortunately they don't amount to much more than more damage for particular types, just first of the reasons why it doesn't feel like it had gotten the full polish treatment. As far as plot and characters go, the game does a fine job. I actually really like the characters, as they really aren't as morally cut and dry as the other games, so seeing them interact with not only each other but with your dialogue options is a pretty fresh feeling. Ringo is genuinely really funny, and even if the other characters are kind of tropey, I thought it was not really distractedly so. The story is just okay, its main problem being far too predictable (and at the time of this review, I'm a little more than halfway through it). It feels more like a plot you would get when your in your second draft; you've got the basic premise, maybe some things to spice it up, but you haven't reached the point where anything truly engaging has been added. The absolute BIGGEST problem with the game are the levels (or dungeons, whatever you might call them). Straight up, they are bad. Compared to other SMT games, they are incredibly uninspired, with them being simple mazes at best to infuriatingly gimmicky at its worst. They aren't even interesting on a aesthetic level either (other than the Soul Matrix, which acts as each companions side-quest dungeons). TWO of them are just subway systems with literally nothing going on. This was definitely the biggest problem with the game, and it is actually disruptive at time considering its not only the way to actually progress, but as mentioned before, they want you to actively grind for upgrades, too, so coming back to them is bound to happen. Even worse, for some reason you can't see the missions you accept in the Soul Matrix, so you either have to remember, look up what they were, or get lucky. The levels were CLEARLY not thought out enough, and its kind of baffling at times. All in all, its a fine game, but its unfortunately marred by potential not seen through completely. The fact that the main story on average takes somewhere near 30 hours to finish compared to the near 100 the others have says a lot. In a weird yet disappointing way, Soul Hackers 2 feels like the side game to the side game, and while I would love for them to come back to this, they have to put in more effort. Overall, like a 7/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Soul Hackers 2 is the definition of unfulfilled potential.This game is what you get if you take the modern Atlus formula and boil the elements down to their most barebones, basic forms.  Demon negotiation is here, but instead of being able to talk to demons in combat and persuade them to join you, you'll get the chance to recruit them occasionally in dungeons by just talking to one of your demons who found them for you.  And instead of having to discuss things with the demons, they just state a price up front (sometimes that price is free) and you can pay it and they'll always join you, or you can say no and they leave.  There is no way to mess up or fail negotiations, and the demons are always 100% honest.Remember social links from the Persona games?  Well, what you have here is "soul level", which is a number that can go up to 100 (200 in NG+) which you can increase by making dialogue choices during the story or during hangouts at the local bar.  It doesn't matter which dialogue choices you pick, the only thing that happens is that one of your party member's soul level will increase.  Your party members are supposed to have opposed philosophies but there's never any friction outside of what's already scripted.  Not even a "X didn't like that" message.  The bar hangouts are likewise disappointing.  They are mostly inane chitchat.  There just isn't much narrative meat to them.The press turn system is here... mostly.  But it's been simplified too.  This part is a bit of a mixed bag.  The hama and mudo instant death skills are gone, replaced with the "ruin" element that deals status effects.  This could be an interesting shakeup to the formula.  But combat is too easy for it make much different.  Instead of getting extra turns for hitting weaknesses, or knocking down enemies and preventing them from acting, what you get is a mechanic called the stack counter.  As you hit more weaknesses, your stack counter goes up, and at the end of the turn your demons pull of a big attack called a sabbath that does damage to the enemies based on how high your stack meter is.  It's kind of like an all-out attack ala Persona 5, but without the strategy.  It's basically free damage at the end of your turn.  There are some tough optional bosses that make good use of this mechanic but otherwise it trivializes combat entirely and offers nothing in return.That's the story of Soul Hackers 2.  Everything has been simplified to the point that the game doesn't really feel like an Atlus game.  It feels like a generic JRPG with a sprinkling of Atlus's usual elements here and there.  All the rough edges of an the Atlus formula have been smoothed away, leaving behind something bland and not that interesting.  This isn't a bad game per se but if you're played a few SMT or Persona games in the past this is going to feel lackluster in comparison.  I would recommend this primarily as an introduction to the series, or maybe even JRPGs in general.  Otherwise, though, Soul Hackers 2 doesn't have enough to leave a veteran player satsified.

_childDocuments_.review: I've finished this game twice now, once on the PS5 version and once on PC. Obtained true ending on both.For context, Megaten has been my favorite video game franchise since 2015, and Devil Summoner: Soul Hackers is one of my favorite games in the entire franchise. When Soul Hackers 2 was announced in early 2022, I felt a combination of optimism and skepticism going into this game. On one hand, I was so happy that ATLUS was making a new Megaten game that wasn't Mainline SMT or Persona, which still gives me hope that there will be future games for other Megaten spinoffs (devil survivor 3 PLEASE)On the other... this game looked like a very big departure from the first game. It took awhile to *somewhat* get over that hurdle for me, but once I did (and after going through the game twice), I can say that - while flawed from a dungeon crawling perspective, I really enjoyed my time with Soul Hackers 2.In my opinion, I think that the best part of this game is the story, which might just be the best Megaten story since SMT IV. The main party of this game are some of the most charming characters I've seen from ATLUS, and Ringo might just be my favorite protagonist in all of Megaten. She's wonderful. The plot is simple, but works very well throughout most of the game due to solid writing and great voice acting. Furthermore, I appreciate the emphasis of Detective Work throughout the game, which is seen throughout all of Devil Summoner. While this doesn't feel like a Soul Hackers sequel in my opinion, I think this game works great as a Devil Summoner title (should've called it Devil Summoner: Aion)The combat system called "Sabbath" is similar to the demon coop system in Strange Journey, and while it starts of slow, it really does open up greatly the more you progress through the game. While I don't think it's the best combat in Megaten, I find it to be very solid on its own and remains fun through the rest of the game.The same cannot be said for the Dungeon Crawling. As a whole, these might be some of the worst dungeons in all of Megaten. The Soul Matrix (the game's optional dungeon which provides very powerful upgrades and additional story for the party) is the biggest offender to this. Boring designs, repetitive music and visual design, large amounts of dead/open space, etc. The main story dungeons also suffer from these issues, although as the game progresses, there is slightly more variety in both music and visual design. After the November Patch, dungeon crawling is less annoying with the addition of a sprint button, but this only mitigates the bad dungeon crawling. Coming directly after SMT V (where the open areas of Da'at had really incredible level design), it's crazy how much of a stepback this game was.Overall, I really enjoyed my time with this game. Soul Hackers 2 goes on sale often, so if you're a fan of ATLUS or are just looking for a solid JRPG, I do recommend buying it! Although reception and sales were middling for this game, I do hope for future titles in Megaten that aren't Mainline SMT and Persona. Personally, I think it's likely with how well SMT V and the P5R ports sold, so I'm looking forward to what's next from ATLUS.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is for 0.01% of people. It's been lambasted and given mixed reviews by basically everyone, including MegaTen fans.While I understand their opinion and can see where they're coming from - I'm here to tell you that this game... is actually good (if you fall into that 0.01%)Essentially, this title is a strange hodgepodge of classic SMT and more modern Persona-like character interactions.If you came here for Persona, you'll be sorely disappointed when you find a different battle system and significantly less side "activities" and social links. If you're here for SMT? The battle system seems simplified at first and might scare you away from the lack of press turn (but is actually harder than SMTV on hard and Nocturne, excluding BS encounters), and some anime-isms might irk you.What really makes this enjoyable is that classic "average rating game" nostalgia that those familiar with Dreamcast/PS2/1, etc era are familiar with. When dungeons were total BS mazes and you could get hardstuck on fights if you weren't prepared. Lower difficulties unfortunately do this game a disservice. It's bizarre to me that the designers would make a game with classic dungeons designed to troll you and throw in "easy" mode combat and other things to try to get non-rpg gamers, when none of those people would EVER enjoy this dungeon design. You have to be a very specific type of person to enjoy these "monotonous", labyrinthine, teleport-heavy, one-way door dungeons. If you're that 0.01% that likes mapping and being trolled? This one's for you. The combat on Very Hard is surprisingly good. You'll get your ass beat far more frequently on bosses than SMTV hard, etc. Going in blind, you're forced to get your ♥♥♥♥ rocked, learn the mechanics. rebuild your team, and repeat quite often on bosses. It's arduous and annoying, but satisfying once you make a full party and get the rhythm going.  Every turn, you're swapping demons on your party members, issuing commands, holding sabbaths, and so on with little room for error. Normally, during SMT games, you eventually become absolutely broken and steamroll the game. This doesn't really happen on Very Hard, as the lack of items, exp falloff, and high difficulty forces you to constantly change strategy and team members/builds.The story is average and fairly predictable, but Ringo as the MC makes for a refreshing change of pace. (it definitely feels like Arrow was supposed to be the MC at some point and the story was hastily rewritten).If you're here because you liked Soul Hackers 1 (or the rest of the Devil Summoner series) - unfortunately, this has very little to do with those outside references, NPCs, etc.If you happen to be the extremely rare type of gamer that likes difficult RPG combat that challenges your teambuilding, and don't mind essentially doing the same dungeons for hours repeatedly, or revel in traditional teleport troll dungeons (a la Strange Journey, but less visually interesting), this one's for you. This one's all about the boss battles and classic bs dungeons. If you're anyone else... this game will probably be an unfun, painful experience (and that's ok because game variety is good and not everything is for everyone).

_childDocuments_.review: A great game whose shortcomings can be heavy to some.Important context: I picked up and played this game after the Quality of Life patch was added.I feel this is important as I believe a lot of negative experiences stem from things the patch addressed and fixed.This includes things such as:1. The Dash Button.   The dungeon designs are "dated" and very hallway-esque. This isn't a problem for an older person like myself who grew up on hallway-rpg designs from the PS2 era but it's worth mentioning all the same. Without the speed-up from the dash feature, I can see why the hallway designs would be annoying. This also allows you to more easily avoid random encounters when you're just trying to go from point A to B.2. The Fast Battle feature.  Animations at normal speed can last a bit longer than needed, especially the unusually long delays after an attack has finished. After you've seen everything so many times you just want to get through the battle as fast as you can without pausing for every animation, which is fixed with this addition.As for the actual shortcomings of the game as mentioned in the header, it all really just comes down to the DLC.The DLC questline is an entire story that supplements the main-story in a way that feels incredibly impossible to just separate and sell as an individual dlc. Between the new character, the added lvl 95~99 fight and leveling area, and the story itself being as important for context as the nibelheim flashbacks were for FF7, it's hard to recommend this game without the story DLC, which then leads to me saying:Wait for a sale. Not for the quality of the game itself, but because the the extra story DLC is important and I highly recommend you wait for a sale to justify the price of the main game + the dlc.Another minor issue is that the other iconic demons are in another DLC pack- and a major character from Soul Hackers 1 is in that dlc pack. This feels like a major step back from other SMT and SMT-Spinoff games which have better ways of including the previous games' protagonists.With that out of the way, I'm going to just end this review with a Pros and Cons list for simplicity.+Solid JRPG Story+Stylistic Design+Character Design and Character Personalities +Pacing and Flow of both story and gameplay(leveling, upgrades) is smooth.+Sabbaths are an interesting eye-candy mechanic that's both quick and satisfying to stack up.-Terrible DLC decisions-Overall Demon List is Lacking-Because they ripped the DLC story from the main game, there's a massive waste of opportunity with the DLC character who should have been integrated into the main story.-/+ If you have any idea what you're doing with fusion, you'll have an omni-negate demon for every member that covers everything they need by level 60 if not earlier. This could be a positive or a negative depending on who you ask so I figured it was worth mentioning.Either way: Get this game, it's great. Just wait for a sale because the dlc story is important.

_childDocuments_.review: Soul Hackers 2 is a pretty good entry into the ever expanding library of the SMT series. It'd definitely following the trend of becoming more "Persona" than previous SMT games, but still manages to deliver a worthwhile experience.First off, and the biggest draw of the game to me, the characters. Most of the time, SMT doesn't really focus on its cast, they serve their purpose, and have their quirks to them, but generally, SMT is about the gameplay. Soul Hackers 2 is not like that. While the non-essential story characters are incredibly flat and forgettable, the core party and those close to them are incredibly memorable and fun to watch. The chemistry between Ringo, Arrow, Milady, and Saizo works really well, and every scene they're in is a joy to watch. The story is more interesting than your standard apocalypse scenario because of how well the characters are all written, and it makes you feel for everyone on all sides. It's hard to make all of your characters likeable like this, and you can tell a lot of effort went into making the cast a lot more three dimensional than your standard SMT cast. However, the writing only gets you so far in an RPG like this, hows the gameplay? Well, its definitely a lot more simple than most other Atlus RPGs, this isn't too terrible, and allows the game to be a lot more accessible to new players, but if you're a hardcore SMT gatekeeper, you'll likely be disappointed. The move pool is drastically smaller than even Persona's, and demon move slots are limited to 6. Fusion is super streamlined, similarly to SMT V, with compendium fusions being carried over, reducing the tedium of filling out the compendium again. Dungeon exploration is standard enough, with one major problem. At the time of writing my original review, RINGO WAS SLOW AS ♥♥♥♥. They mercifully added a run button a few months after the game released, and while I'm sure its a nice quality of life booster, it doesn't save the frankly boring and generic levels. With the exception of the FINAL AREA, the levels are the same 3 recycled subways, office buildings, and blank voids repeated over and over and over again, making it a huge drag to get from one story beat to the next. I really like the story here, but I'm not going to lie, some of the mid points made it really hard to continue. Luckily, these dungeons tend to be short, but with them composing most of the game, and feeling twice as long with the lack of anything interesting, they are definitely the games biggest weakness.Now, lets say you've read my little textwall, and the game sounds interesting to you. As you scroll back up to the buy button, you might notice this game has a lot of DLC. Now you're thinking "Hmm... should I buy the deluxe edition???"No.The DLC is a total waste of money. At best, you get a couple side missions that are a nice distraction from the main game for a little bit, and at worst you're spending an addition 50% of the main game's cost to completely ruin the game by instantly being able to hit level 99 with infinite money, and getting a couple neat (but totally useless) costumes. If this is like your favorite game ever and you just really wanna show your love for it, go for it I guess? But really, these are nothing more than a scummy attempt to scrape more money away from you by ripping content from the game day one that really has no business being DLC to begin with.Overall? I had a good time with Soul Hackers 2. The gameplay is pretty lacking for an SMT game, and the DLC is pretty lame, but the characters and story are such a great time, and the general aesthetic being so appealing and easy to get sucked into, that it almost carries the rest of the games weakpoints. I think this makes a great first SMT game, especially if you're looking something closer to Persona. If you're a bit more of an SMT veteran, this may be a bit harder of a sell. If the story looks cool, or you just wanna see everything this series has to offer, it's far from a terrible game, but other games in this series significantly outshine it. 6/10.

_childDocuments_.review: I rate this game a 7.5/10. If you expect something of persona or mainline SMT quality, this game is not it.Overall I enjoyed my time with this game but it has some major flaws keeping it from being a 8/10 for me.This game is supposed to be a budget title and you can see it ingame, which is why I don't recommend buying this game at 60 dollars if you're not a huge Shin Megami Tensei fans (Go grab P5R instead if you haven't played it).What I like:- The characters. Ringo is a great main character with actual personalities- Progression system is fun with a lot of customization opportunities- Sabbath and commander skills are neat ideas- Stress-free combat for casual players like me (but it can be too way easy at times)- The game respects your time by allowing you to save and quit anywhere- A few great tracks with huge Nier vibes, as expected from Monaca- Good story, not great but it's a breath of fresh air from Persona and SMT games- 40 hours main story, a good length for this gameWhat I don't like- The dungeons. Even though I'm used to navigating bad dungeon designs (looking at you Tales of Berseria) it doesn't mean that I give them a pass, especially for a 60 dollars game. By the end of the game I just spam Assassin Steps to rush through dungeons.- The lack of variety. This one is the biggest flaw for me. In Persona games, the randomly generated dungeons change overtime in terms of soundtrack and overall theme. In Soul Hackers 2, there's only 1 track for Story dungeons, 1 other track for Soul Matrix, 1 track for every single story boss, etc.- Combat is too easy with every single enemy advantages removed from hitting your weak points- Demons and some materials require a lot of running around and pray that RNGesus will give you what you actually want- Skill inheritance isn't explained very clearly. I still don't know how they pick which skills to inherit by the end of the game.- ♥♥♥♥♥♥ DLC practices. Atlus keeps trying to hammer in the worst DLCs possible in their games and I don't support this one bit.

_childDocuments_.review: Starting this off with the fact that I normally enjoy Atlus RPGs and will defiantly be picking up Persona 5 and 3 when released with my previous experience being with Persona 3,4 and Shin Megami 2 which were amazing games that I got hooked on instantly. Saying that soul hackers 2 wasn’t the case from the beginning and is now the same if not worse 30 hours in.The first key point for these types of games for me is generally the story and characters with a mix of good combat mechanics that come together for an enjoyable experience. With this game, the biggest problem is, that it all feels stale and bland with the story being simple boring and overall super predictable from the base story or the side story from learning the characters' pasts through the dungeons. The characters in this game also fit the story point of being one-dimensional and just not interesting at all not keeping me there, with this being one of the few games where I was just skipping through the conversations. Dungeon design is extremely simple which is honestly the case for Persona 3/4, but these games stem from the generation of the ps2 while this game is a 2022 release a lot of the dungeons feel the same as walking down a tunnel or corridor and being generally outdated. The graphics are ok for this type of game but seem very pixelated even at max setting at 1440p but are passable, I guess as the game's performance seems good across the board using a 3080 and on the steam deck (do not change the resolution or get locked out for 24 hours recommended to play at high for best overall experience).The one point of the game that stands out over everything else would be the combat that again is like previous games which were good anyway but includes a stacking system that isn’t partially new or amazing but is a nice addition. Demons and monster collecting is enjoyable and fusing but again is something they’ve done well through their franchises and as such is good in this.After getting to the 30-hour point heading into the last arc with all the side quests to this point done apart from the 4th-floor matrix collection quests that are honestly unenjoyable I’ve decided to drop this game as overall it’s just extremely boring and hasn’t grabbed me at any points, so I honestly wouldn’t recommend this game even at £30 which is what I spent and not at full asking price with the day one DLC implementation being embarrassing (if you haven't just go and buy persona 4 or wait for 3/5).

_childDocuments_.review: After plaything almost 2 whole playthroughs and getting all but 5 achievments, I feel like I can finally take the time to review this gameI'll give a summarized version, and an extended version of this reviewSummarized: It has good visual presentation and voicework, but falls short in every other categoryMAJOR MAJOR SPOILERS BELOWExtended review:Oh man where do I start...? I'll start with the positives I guess.Pros:-Soul Hackers 2 has some really nice visual designs and presentation, I really liked the aesthetic overall, the whole cybery futuristic dystopia is nice, as well as the character designs themselves, be it the main cast or the extra shop owner characters like Victor or the quest giver Madam Ginko, the designs are top notch-Demon Fusion is still fun to do, although it feels pretty much unchanged from other games, so nothing too interesting, but at least it still works as intended-Game doesn't have any massive bugs (that I'm aware of) and runs fairly smoothly-Music is alright, nothing too spectacular given ATLUS's track record, but passable-Voice work was really good in this game, in both English and Japanese-Saizo is kinda based sometimesNow onto the bad...we're gonna be here for a whileCons:-Small nitpick to start, the default game options are godawful, the default camera angle and FOV make exploring dungeons a nightmare but thankfully you can change that. Same goes for loading screen tips artificially inflating load times, they can be disabled thankfully-Characters are really boring in this game, genuinely some of the most forgettable characters in any game I've played recently except Saizo, and he's just alright at best, the only memorable part about Arrow, Milady, Figue, Ringo, Raven, and so on, are their visual designs, otherwise they have nothing that makes them stand out, Arrow being generic anime good guy, and Milady being the "tough girl who refuses to open up, but has a soft spot for children" as her entire character, Raven ends up being a "morally grey" villain who wants to save these orphans by...destroying the world?!?! It doesn't make sense and is hardly morally grey, it's just bland-Story is very very VERY generic anime, and very very forgettable, starts with standard megaten "apocalypse" plot, but it tells you everything important within the first 2 hours, like Yatagarasu, Phantom Society, the Covenants, summoning the Great One, yadayada, it shows its hand right away and then barely builds on it at all, the numerous plot twists are all predictable and fail to make me care about what happens next. Like, the whole Soul Hacking thing barely even comes into play throughout the entire game, only like 6 times in the ENTIRE story is Soul Hacking even used, 3 times for your party members, 1 time for Arrow to give the purple covenant, 1 time failed with Figue and Raven, and 1 time to rescue Figue on one of the endings.All the story exposition happens in one of two locations, the safehouse, or the orphanage, and very rarely in the Axis itself.The whole story revolves around gathering the covenants to stop the end of the world...that's it. The individual character stories are pretty bland as well or just handled poorly, and speaking of being handled poorly, character stories happen in the Soul Matrix or during the hangout scenes at the bar. The Soul Matrix sucks major ass, and the hangout scenes aren't engaging enough to be memorable, which only further hurts the memorability of the characters. The game has 2 endings, both are similar and neither of them are very interesting, effectively leaving things off virtually unchanged from the start of the game. -Gameplay: I'm gonna split this one into two parts, Dungeon Crawling and Combat.    -Dungeon crawling: Oh man this is by FAR the worst aspect of this game, having to explore and return to the various "dungeons" as they barely qualify as.This game has multiple boring dungeons, between the shipping areas, the subway lines, the towers, and the Soul Matrix, the only one that felt even slightly different was the final dungeon, and it still sucked hard.The shipping districts are just small containted areas, nothing special about either of them, West or East shipping districts.The Subway lines are just that, abandoned subway lines with almost nothing of interest except for this one door puzzle that goes away after you beat it, and there are 2 of these identical subway dungeons for you to mindlessly roam around in.The Ozaki Hope towers are a smidge more interesting, with the elevator puzzle, but that's about it, otherwise it's the same mindless roaming around, aside from this one segment where you go through the vents as Mimi, the little owl navigator bot, which is extremely slow and still have to deal with enemies while doing so.....it sucks, plain and simpleThe Municipal tower is this weirdish dungeon with doors and "teleporters" that transport you either up or down depending on the flow of the water...and that's it.Soul Matrix, the dungeon you revisit the most because there's 1 for each character except ringo, so you have 3 identical dungeons, that boil down to doors, telporters, and a second version of teleporters....yay....I just listed eveything unique between all of the dungeons, now here's the flaws they all share.All of them are enormous, long, spiraling empty halls with nothing to do except fight or run past enemies....which makes exploring them not only very tedious over the course of the roughly 60 hours of main story progression, but very boring as well.On top of having boring empty halls for every dungeon, enemies spawn every two seconds, forcing you to stop and swat them away, wasting time.Actually progressing through these dungeons really sucks when you realize that Ringo moves slower than a paralytic grandma who just got shot in the knees, and the only way to speed her up is by using a skill that costs 10 MP to speed you up for like 20ft worth of distance, which you can only unlock by progressing Milady's Soul Matrix....Also the navigator is insanely annoying, someone invented a mod just to shut the navigator up...that much should be self explanatory.Combat: BUCKLE UP ♥♥♥♥♥♥ BECAUSE THIS RANT IS GONNA BE MORE INTERESTING THAN THE BATTLE SYSTEM-Battling: You and your party members can each equip some gear, augment mistiques, and a demon eachcombat is turn based and lacks the fun aspects of other smt games, like the press turn system, or even the baton pass from Persona 5, and 1more function from Persona 3 onwards. Instead you are rewarded with a Sabbath for hitting weaknesses....which is just damage at the end of your turn to all enemies....for doing the normal thing...so the gimmick with combat is a non interactive reward for playing the game normally....lame...and you can only upgrade it through having certain demon skills or stack bonuses applied, but it fundamentally remains the same.      There's no sabbaths for enemies either, so the enemies are always at a disadvantage to you, which is an oddity for SMT and Persona, as enemies could take advantage of both Press turns, and 1more in those games.      Light and Dark skills are gone entirely, replaced with Ruin, which is basically just ailment moves that also deal damage...      Without any sort of interactive gimmick, battles become really boring, especially with the removal of Demon Negotiation putting the final nail in the coffin, it just devolves to hitting the weakness and moving on, no strategy or tactics in any capacity.With a lack of strats, progression just becomes a boring grind.I have more I could say, but I can't fit much more into this steam review, so here's my final verdictGame has good visuals and presentation, everything else is ♥♥♥♥, and I can't recommend it, even if you're a longtime fan of the series. 2/10, don't buy it, even on a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: This is my favorite Atlus game I think. The combat finds a way to incorporate the idea of having a party of characters fighting together without being as repetitive as Persona thanks to the ability to actually change the demon associated with each party member. It mostly feels like an in-between of SMT and Persona, being both an ensemble narrative cast of protagonists and a game about making nice with demons so they'll help you in a fight. It's the same combat as most every Atlus game, once again being a little simpler than SMT V's additional turn system but more in-depth than Persona's All Out attacks.Mostly though this is the first Atlus game where I care about the characters and want to see them interact and develop as friends, including the protagonist, who has a distinct character as opposed to the blank slate types that you often see in Atlus rpgs. Oh also they're all adults and there's no weird adult/child romance stuff, so you know, that's a positive.Anyway I just think it's the best JRPG this company's ever made so it's a bummer that this might be the last one since it doesn't seem to have done well.

_childDocuments_.review: If you can get this game at a decent price then I can comfortably say you're in for an experience that, while somewhat flawed, is still very much worth your time.There are a few things that I must address before going in-depth:While I didn't encounter any bugs or glitches, myself,  Atlus announced there is a patch to add some general fixes and QoL updates coming in the near future, so these issues may be fixed by then. I did the following for the best personal experience:-Under "Loading Screen Tips" set it to either "Hide" or "Button Advance". For whatever reason this shortens load screen times drastically.-Lock the frame rate to 60fps, as apparently higher/uncapped rates can break some animations.-Adjust the camera settings so Ringo is focused in the center and the camera zoom is further away.-Lower analogue stick sensitivity, as Ringo can be a little slippery to control.Soul Hackers 2 is a game I can say I personally enjoyed, but I can completely understand why others may be underwhelmed or disappointed by the final product. The fact that the first Soul Hackers is such a cult classic among RPG fans may also play a role in this game's mixed reception. As far as Shin Megami Tensei games go, it is a very mellow experience that has a lot of the pieces the series is known for but doesn't necessarily go very far with them, and as a result the game lacks the sense of scope that players familiar with the series may come to expect.If there's one thing I'm certain Soul Hackers 2 does very well, it's the presentation. The game is incredibly stylish and beautiful with its futuristic city environments, character designs, UI and VFX, as one would expect from a modern SMT/Atlus title. The music is also great with the Opening Theme, Weapons Shop, and the multiple Battle Themes being the highlights for me. The voice cast is also full of very solid performances. Outside of looking and sounding great, it's the rest of the game, itself where one's mileage may vary.As far as writing goes, I found the interactions among the main cast to be very enjoyable. Each party member is well fleshed out and they play off of each other very well, with Ringo and Saizo being my personal favourites. The other major characters also have some good interactions with them as well when it's their turn in the spotlight. The actual story, though, is rather lacking as far as JRPGs go. It has the pieces there to be something great, and there are a lot of compelling elements, themes, and interesting ideas that SMT is known for, however it feels like for most of the game that the story progresses just for the sake of moving the plot along.For most of the game I was more compelled to see the interactions between party members and piecing together each of their backstories and how they weave together, rather than being attached to the main plot. It was only really after the major twist regarding the main antagonist that I began to feel like things were really picking up and felt engaged to continue the story, and that's roughly three quarters into the game. Fortunately I do believe the game had a satisfying enough finale and a great final boss to go with it.The other thing that I feel a lot of people will be hit or miss on is the gameplay. Soul Hackers 2 is, in all intents and purposes, a Megami Tensei game, but it's a relatively simple Megami Tensei game. The core gameplay loop that makes SMT so addictive is all there: you explore dungeons to recruit demons, and eventually fuse those demons together to create stronger demons, allowing you to explore more dangerous dungeons. The battle system also features the series' trademark affinity system, with each demon/enemy having their own strengths and weaknesses against the different damage types in the game. It's one of personal favourite systems as far as turn-based RPGs go.On top of these staple features, battles in Soul Hackers 2 features the addition of the "Stack" system. On top of dealing bonus damage, attacking an enemy with their weakness grants a Stack. At the end of the player's turn Ringo performs an AoE attack and deals damage based on the amount of stacks gained during their turn. It's a very simple system, though in comparison to other battle mechanics present in other SMT games, it can feel rather shallow by comparison. Even as you progress through the game and gradually unlock more perks and abilities, the Stack system doesn't provide as much strategy to battles as the "Press Turn" system in mainline SMT or the "One More" system in Persona.While the battle system can feel hit-or-miss based on your preferences, the layout and dungeon design is probably the game's lowest point in nearly every aspect. While not necessarily bad (for the most part) they are considerably boring. Dungeons in Soul Hackers 2 go back to the maze-like hallway design of older RPGs and don't really bring anything interesting to the table. Compared to other recent entries in the series like SMT V's sprawling environments and Persona 5's unique palaces, it leaves a lot to be desiredIt also doesn't help that the environments are rather bland. The Soul Matrix, the area where you will likely spend most of your time leveling up and grinding, features 15 different floors, each one with the exact same music and background visuals (not even a change in colour scheme) and it gets very samey, very quick. The main story dungeons don't fare much better either, as they all boil down to the same idea of "abandoned urban environment" (two of which are abandoned subway lines) and all share the same music track, which detracts from giving each one their own sense of identity. The only exception is the final dungeon, which feels very distinct and interesting and features a unique music track that adds a lot to the atmosphere.All in all, the best way I can describe Soul Hackers 2 is that it's a very good game to introduce newcomers to Megami Tensei as a series. It features all the core elements and gameplay loop in a way that's easy to get the gist of. It isn't brutally difficult like Mainline SMT, and it isn't a massive time sink like Persona. It's just enough to give players a taste of everything this truly unique franchise of RPGs has to offer. That being said, do I recommend getting this game at full price? No, not really. I would still say wait until it goes on sale for like half off. If you can get this game at a decent price then I can comfortably say you're in for an experience that, while somewhat flawed, is still very much worth your time.

_childDocuments_.review: 7 Hours of gameplay opinions and tips:     - Very approachable for newcomers, a good entry for veterans but may feel a little oversimplified at times if you're used to the difficulty curve for SMT/Persona/DS games     - English voiceover is okay, but Japanese audio will make the game feel less awkward     - Agreed. Day 1 DLC is a pain, bought the extra story DLC and so far it has made very little impact on gameplay. Would love to see Atlus/Sega atone for this sin ;)     - Default settings for the game are terrible, fix your camera, text speed, etc ASAP when you start the game     - Music is solid     - Demon merging system is nice and simple with the new "search fusion" filters     - Character upgrade elements are an interesting take on the "Glory" mechanic that SMT 5 intoduced to the franchise     - Dungeons haven't been anything special but they haven't been a pain either     - Story is actually pretty good. Cutscenes and dialogue are a lot more lengthy and slightly less interesting than SMT 5 in my opinion, but if you're the kind of person who likes long storylines you'll like this one.     - So far I think a $40-$50 price tag would have made more sense for this game on release day since it does feel a bit watered down for a SMT/Persona/DS game but honestly you can justify buying it for $60 if you're pretty diehard on the franchise and want to play it ASAP and want a solid PC option until P5R gets ported.Overall I do recommend playing this game but perhaps waiting for a sale or solid free DLC drop if you've been on the fence about buying it. It doesn't quite justify the price tag just yet.

_childDocuments_.review: I did a blind buy of this on release day. You win some, you lose some. And this time I lost some. I wouldn't recommend this. I got almost every achievement so here's my two cents.The long and the short of it: The best part of this game is basically the art style, characters, voice work, and the weapon shop and Mansei Realm music slaps! ...otherwise the music is a mixed bag. The story is unremarkable, but has a few twists to be enjoyable. Boss fights on hard mode are challenging and satisfying to beat. Speaking of boss fights the primary mechanic in this game, the sabbath attack, is actually still relevant during boss fights instead of completely thrown out like in the Persona games. While the worst of it was the extremely boring dungeon settings and design.The main protagonist Ringo is surprising charming and silly. The artwork had me thinking she'd be a cold leader type and since she's some kind of robot/AI/android, so I figured they might've leaned into that kind of trope. Then Saizo I thought seemed too tropey from the artwork, but I ended up liking him the most, besides Ringo, with how he developed. Because the voice work is done by proven talents, the characters come to life and their banter is enough to keep me going through these long dark endless hallways.The game's basic story premise you can read in this game's description page never really develops beyond that. Despite that there are some twists and turns towards the second half of the story. Even Saizo acknowledges the amount of twists at this point in the game. With that said, the story is nothing to write home about, but it has its moments and I enjoyed it enough.The gameplay loop essentially boils down to crawling these massive boring dungeons, getting to a checkpoint and leaving to rest, upgrade or do a hangout. Which to me is immersion  breaking because the game sets things in the main story thread to be urgent, but it feels weird to leave the dungeon to have a beer with your party mates. You just have to suspend disbelief here. Maybe I'm too used to the Persona dungeon and daily life cycle. Speaking of Persona, I fee like the party member hangouts here seem tacked on because of Persona's popularity.As far as gameplay systems go, the sabbath attack is basically a weaker all-out attack from Persona and hitting weaknesses doesn't stun enemies, but you can stack up the damage and it's actually relevant in boss fights unlike in Persona which is a plus. When you progress in a party member's soul matrix dungeon you learn abilities for them that can affect how these characters can add to the stack. However, it's pretty much on rails. You play the party members as they're designed to be. It's a beginners trap in thinking you can make Ringo a good ice user because her ice bonuses from mistique unlocks never go up that high and she doesn't get stack bonuses from them anyway.I played the game on hard right from the start and I will praise the game for its tight balancing. Boss fights are challenging and satisfying to beat. The soul matrix quest bosses can be very tricky especially because you often aren't allowed any items or commander skills and have a time limit. I always took these bosses at the recommended level and always eventually found some kind of combo to win. However, since you can, eventually, leave a dungeon and come back at any time and can skip random encounters as you please normal enemies don't pose the threat of attrition on your resources like in other JRPGs. They are just piñatas to beat for loot and XP. This further adds to the monotony of dungeons.I've been beating up the dungeons in this whole review so let's get to it. By now, many reviews pan this game's bland dungeons and that word really doesn't describe how bad they really are. They are all long dreary corridors with usually nothing of interest to see or do and they all have the same ambient piano track playing for all of them except for the soul matrix dungeons which has its own track that's shared between them.  if you don't mind spoilers all the dungeons are basically: , , and . This is in stark contrast to the rest of the environments which all share the neon future aesthetic so it really confuses me why they went this direction for the dungeons. Only the final dungeon has any interesting design to it. Now if you played Persona 4, you might be familiar with the long corridor dungeon design, but at least there at each stage of the game it had a different theme and music. Of course if you played and liked Persona 3 then you'll be right at home with the never ending dark corridors!Now the dungeons do sometimes have a puzzle to solve which helps break up the monotony. One dungeon has doors closing behind you and it was interesting enough to solve. Then a few soul matrix dungeons have a "pick a door" teleporter puzzle where if you pick the wrong one you're punished with being sent backwards and having to walk back to it. Game design nowadays have a lot of padding to prevent people from complaining a game is too short, but this is particularly egregious.Finally, this game's default camera is awful. I had to adjust the settings multiple times so I can see where I'm going.Overall, this game is a missed opportunity. It could've used some more time in the oven, but I feel like a resurrected 20+ year old franchise isn't going to get the funds to develop a more fleshed out game. However, if you think you might like the characters in a very anime-ish end-of-the-world story, then I'd recommend playing this on easy/normal and just getting to the story bits ASAP.

_childDocuments_.review: This game gets a lot of hate, some warranted and some not. It still has fun SMT gameplay and still has demons you can fuse, albeit they reduced the amount of demons in this game since SMT V. At the same time, this game has a lot of “one step forward, two steps back”.I believe a lot of hate from this game comes from it being so tonally different to the original Soul Hackers and from the graphics of this game not looking too great, which I would agree with to an extent.It still has many similarities they put in this game from the original, such as “Zomas” returning and it even the Bomb status ailment, which doesn’t appear in any other Persona or SMT games except Soul Hackers as well as Club Cretaceous returning with Madame Ginko who appeared in the original Devil Summoner and Soul Hackers 1. Devil summoner factions also return such as the Phantoms and Yatagarasu. Vision Quests return too, but the only issue is they’re not as exciting as in the original Soul Hackers.I wouldn’t be surprised if some of the developers who worked on Soul Hackers 2 played Soul Hackers 1 when they were young, but they couldn’t do much except for references due to a tight budget and the hand they were given.If you want to play Soul Hackers 2 for the SMT and Persona gameplay, I’d say go for it. But be aware that they heavily “persona-fied” the combat. So unlike the original Soul Hackers, you now control 4 human party members who equip demons that you can change at anytime (this was a big disappointment for many people especially since SMT V released and had demon party members). Why couldn’t we get the protagonist, 2 human characters, and 3 demons? Why did they do only human party members in a game spinoff where you always recruited the demons directly? They just made SMT V as well, why couldn’t they re-use those assets?Also, “zomas” return in this game (zomas are unique artificial demons, you fuse them with regular demons to create very unique demons), but unfortunately you cannot get one in this game – it’s enemy exclusive which was extremely disappointing. It’s worse that they made it enemy exclusive rather than just not including them to begin with. But you know why of course, it’s because it would take too much effort to make one nowadays. It’s so sad because they make many references to how zomas are made from the original games, such as showing Dolly Kadmon which was a vital ingredient for the creation of zomas, which only made me even more depressed.You don’t “knock down” enemies like in Persona, instead each time you hit a weakness a “Stack” counter goes up, and after the round of combat is over you unleash an all-out attack (called a Sabbath stack) which deals damage based on how high the counter got.You can upgrade your party members’ COMP weapons to deal more physical damage or to get other bonuses, such as making the stack counter go up for healing party members or for dealing critical damage. My criticism is that you can’t see demons attacking directly anymore unlike in SMT V or even Persona games but you can see them during the stack Sabbath attacks.The optional quests have fun optional bosses to fight too, but narratively the quests don’t have much substance to them. One criticism is that the quests don’t have objective markers, so you’ll have to wander through entire old dungeons to find who you’re looking for.The plot of this game is also, admittedly, very boring and dry! Again, it sounds like it’d be a fun game, you have all the factions of Devil Summoners fighting each other and demons, you need to save the world, and people control demons through computers! But the way they handle the narrative and exposition is just awful. There’s so many flashbacks that are not fun to watch and there’s a lot of repetition.As well, without spoiling specifics, they kill off so many characters as soon as they’re introduced (even off-screen) and then do flashbacks, but what’s the point anymore – the character is dead. And it’s not just once, they keep doing this numerous times in this game! There was one character that is heavily foreshadowed in the game who, if you played old Devil Summoner games, is a pretty big figure from a fancy devil summoning background, and guess what happens? Killed off-screen.I kept face-palming at the numerous bone-headed decisions they kept making, it’s as if they were intentionally trying to make their fanbase mad. It’s not even like the plot of the game was rushed – the plot of this game is detailed and they clearly spent a lot of time writing it and editing it, but it’s just bad and not entertaining at all, kind of like Fire Emblem: Fates’s horrible plot.All of the dialogue is voiced extremely well, but the actual lines of dialogues written are in such a long-winded way for some reason. At first, I laughed because I saw streamers who got codes for the game early skipping all of the cutscenes while they were livestreaming and I thought to myself “Damn, maybe these people stream FIFA all day or something and can’t get into JRPGs”, but when I played the game for myself I immediately understood why.Another criticism I have regarding dungeons is that there’s no treasure chests, so exploring doesn’t feel rewarding anymore. Sure you’ll find your demons who will give you money, items and introduce you to other demons, but you can actually grind these infinitely by running up and down, they don’t feel unique like treasure chests, it makes the game feel grindy and repetitive.The demons have material drops in this game compared to other SMTs, so you now need to grind and defeat thousands of demons to gather the materials needed to upgrade your COMP and get new skills for your party (these are on top of the skills the demons they equip give them, they’re not necessary at all but they can be helpful). I think I’d prefer just having COMP upgrades cost more money and having the demons drop money, rather than having to track down drops all over the place and having to grind a specific demon for hours just to get the one last material I need for an important upgrade.The navigator in this game is pretty annoying too and talks way too much. Having encounters on the map be “generic red monsters” also goes back to how SMT4 and SMT4A handled encounters (in fact it’s even worse because in those games they’d actually have different enemy models depending on if it was a giant demon, a dog demon, a male/female humanoid demon, etc, so you could tell which enemy you were facing, whereas in this title it’s always the same generic red monster chasing you or a powerful generic purple one).Another issue with this game is that although I agree that 30-40 hours needed to complete it is reasonable, but the pacing is odd and generally very slow. I won’t spoil anything, in the endgame area the plot really picks up, but as soon as it picks up steam it dies and ends the plot quickly. There’s two amazing bosses after the “sea dungeon” who have big plot significance, but they go out the window and you go to the final boss quickly after to wrap up the plot. The game had the potential to have an exciting plot, like having devil summoner factions fighting each other or having a bunch of devil summoner groups work together to defeat some big bad demons attacking the city, but they didn’t go for that route.So use this as your criteria if you want to decide whether this game is for you or not. I definitely wouldn’t recommend this game as your starting point into SMT games though because of the many criticisms I have with the game’s story. I do believe the game is just a tad underrated, but granted most of the hate is genuinely deserved. If you’d rather watch the game, I have a full playthrough of the game with all routes, all quests, NG+ quests included, Nana DLC, superbosses, and endings below on YouTube.

_childDocuments_.review: So far this game feels like it was meant to ease newcomers from Persona 5 into the wider Megaten franchise, but considering they didn't attach Shin Megami Tensei or Devil Summoner to the title and the marketing was non-existent, I really don't understand what ATLUS was thinking on that end. Sure, Shin Megami Tensei: Devil Summoner: Soul Hackers 2 is a long and ridiculous name, but at least it might get people who know about SMT interested in the first Soul Hackers, older Devil Summoner games or just Megaten in general.Highly enjoying it so far though. It feels like a cyberpunk coated SMT4 with some Persona elements and more dungeon crawler than city sprawler. The combat system is simple and satisfying which could be a positive or negative depending on your preference. I don't mind it, there are plenty of Megaten games I could play to quench my masochism. It's a refreshing change of pace and I wish it had been marketed better.

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of people really don't like this game, and I can see why. Soul Hackers 2 is far from perfect, but it has a lot going for it too. The setting is interesting, the graphics are great with a unique style to it, and there's lots of great character moments. The story does fall a bit flat at times, but there's plenty of great moments. Where this game fails the most is the gameplay. On higher difficulties it feels like you have to do all the optional content or grind, and in general just playing normally can feel like a grind as well due to how repetitive the dungeons are, especially the soul matrix. If you're in for the long haul though, and willing to put up with some issues, there's good times to be had for sure.

_childDocuments_.review: . but: If you've come from SMT or the Persona Series, you'll be very disappointed with Soul Hackers 2.- The combat starts slow and boring, but it gets good and interesting mid-late game.This game is also grindy as ♥♥♥♥, which wouldn't be a problem if the combat wasn't boring. The boss you are supposed to fight at the end of the first real dungeon (the Central Line one) is lvl 34. If you didn't grind, or just did a couple of fights and you are at hard difficulty, you'll face them at lvl 20. I'm not kidding, I've spent 10 hours griding to complete that fight, finished it and activated the DLC Forbidden Scriptures to gain levels without griding for the next dungeons. At hard you also get a pityfull amount of money, which makes it even harder to fuse demons. But activating the DLC items also feels awful, because within an hour of griding, you can reach lvl 99 with a character and have 5M yen to spend on whatever you like.I wouldn't mind the free lvl up demons, but the free lvl up summoners are straight up broken and unbalance the game very fast.Oh, and all non-story bosses have a hidden turn limit. If you don't kill them by their 5th turn, they will one shot you. Even if you can beat them by repeating a strategy over the course of 10 rounds. So not only you have to grind to be on level, you also have to be over-leveled to beat those bosses.- The Story is SMT meets Persona. Not espectacular, not bad either. Pretty mid. The characters are good tho.It's meh. It's the same quality as a the game itself. It gives a little bit more info about parts of the main plot tho, and it intertwines with it in a very good way. If the missions didn't have the "DLC" tag right next to their name, I wouldn't have noticed that that story line wasn't part of the main game.Really good. Had only 3 crashes which all happen after skipping the intro title, when loading the main screen. Idk what triggered them, but I didn't lose any progress, or time. I just alt+f4'd it and restarted the game.If you saved before a boss fight, quit the game, open it again, and imediatly fight the boss, there's a clear freezing frames issues because the game wasn't expecting to load a fight so fast after being loaded in.Ah, there's an option under the Gameplay settings. There are fake load screens. The game loads VERY, VERY fast, but if you have the "loading tips" option enabled, then between every load there'll be a 5-8 sec "load". If you disable it, the load times will be instant. This is an issue because you spend a lot of time running to and from different parts of the city, so disabling it does save A LOT of time.I LOVE THE FAST BATTLE OPTION. I WANT TO KEEP SEEING IT IN FOLLOWING GAMES.I missed and I love that Ringo (MC) has both a personality and agency. It is very refreshing to see. I wish future games do this as well.I love I don't go to a game over screen after the MC is killed. The MC has party members, let them revive them. I wish this was in future AND previous games.Why I ask myself is how are the party members able to use demons? According to the story, the summoners lost their ability to summon demons because now Ringo controls them, so they need her to summon their demons. But if Ringo dies, then they are still able to use them.I do think that the MC dying should impact the fight in some way because they are the heart of the team, and having your party members unable to use their demons is the perfect excuse to have an implicit timer to revive Ringo as soon as possible if she dies during combat.But, I like not instantly losing to a one shot ability that I couldn't predict.I bought it at a discount and I don't regret it, but don't pay full price for it.Copium that Atlus will see that people bought it, finished it, and they will choose to release P6 or SMT 6 the same day on PC and console.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit2: Well, the game is going to get an update which will speed up the game a bit. The run speed will still be the same (you just no longer go to a menu now and then), but being encouraged to fight more due to higher battle speed would solve both tedium and material grinding. So the main issues are (probably) gone and I'd be more eager to recommend this game. Well, if I actually got to TRY these changes. Too little too late, Atlus.Edit: I have beaten the game and am editing this review, but I'll keep the old one for anyone interested. I played on Hard from start to finish and have played the whole 3DS SMT library, as well as Personas 3-5 for any comparisons I'll be making. Also, I had to leave the game on a lot recently while playing, so the playtime is inflated by a few hours, and I didn't buy any of the DLC because Atlus is getting too greedy.This game was a rollercoaster. On one hand, most of the main and sidequest bosses as well Risky Enemies were great fights, and I think this game has some of the better gameplay design in the series. The difficulty slowly drops off, but not as much as some of the other games (like SMT4 or Persona 4G and 5, which just drop and keep dropping past the first few hours), and I think it was just enough for me to keep the postive review. Barely. On the other hand, the random encounters are as simple and boring as ever, which wouldn't be as much of a problem... if the battles weren't so slow, and you didn't fight so many of them. I know SMT5 added an option to skip animations by pressing the button again, why the hell is that absent here?You might be thinking to yourself, "Well I'll just avoid the battles", which is what I did most of the time. Well for one thing, you need materials for your COMP upgrades - in order to get "Skill II", you need "Skill I", so you'll need to go back and fight anyways, or be like me and just not have fun with the better Mystiques because you can't use them. Secondly, this is where the dungeon design comes into play - it's ♥♥♥♥. I mentioned it in the old review, and most people point it out, but nobody really points out WHY it's ♥♥♥♥. It's not just because it's linear with barely anything to interact with - Persona 3 and 4 also had that, and I didn't suffer nearly as much there. No, the problems are 1. There are only FOUR TRACKS in the whole game, two of which only play at the very ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ end of the game, while even Persona 3 at least had variations of one theme, and 2. Ringo is so S L O W, even when you get the speed increasing skill early on (which should've been the default, and it would still not be enough) Other games had the decency to make your character zoom pretty fast and/or have smaller, more compact dungeon design. This one doesn't.As for the story, it's about the same as I stated before. It's alright. There was a twist that I really enjoyed, and there were some good scenes with the main cast, but overall it's nothing special.Honestly, if Atlus fixed the tedious parts - dungeon movement speed and battle animations, primarly - or a mod addressing was released (I know somebody used Cheat Engine to speed up the game, which sounds like just the thing - but I learned too late to bother) I think this would be one of the better SMT games, and I'd recommend it at full price for fans, as before. Unfortunately, you're better off waiting for a discount, and maybe try another game in the series first if you have no prior experience with Megaten. OLD REVIEW:I WAS going to give this a negative review, but... eh, sure. It gets decent after the slow start.If you like JRPG gameplay and are fine with bland, very simplistic dungeon design, then this game is alright. If not, you'll want for discount, but it should still be ok if you want to try a Shin Megami Tensei game a bit closer to mainline than Persona, and SMT3 looks too aged for you. I'm still early into the story (will update this review if I remember) but it's enjoyable enough, if only for the main characters' banter and small talk. It's not good compared to other games I've played, including SMT, but it's not like Steam has many of the latter far. The combat is pretty good and challenging anyway, which is good enough for me. A lot of people miss Press Turns/One Mores from other games for hitting weaknesses, but in my eyes those mechanics negatively affected game balance or boss design if not handled right, so I'm fine with them gone in spinoffs. SMTIV lets you steamroll everything past the first 2 bosses by snowballing buffs while Persona bosses are boring and rarely do anything with elements.I will say the beggining of the game is boring as hell. I thought that maybe it was because it's too long and full of lore exposition, but in hindsight, I think it's the opposite: the game tries to show you all the main characters, their motives, positions, most of the town NPCs and what the main story will be about all within the first hour or two. As a result, a lot of the explaining and introductions feel half-assed. It helps get to the combat and gameplay faster but it just makes the early story unnatural. I feel like it's getting a bit better with its pacing later though.I also thought I'd hate the character design but it quickly grew on me. Saizo best boi.

_childDocuments_.review: I never posted a review for a game before because I feel like everyone is going to have a different opinion about a game regardless. However, I am going to have to make one just for this game in particular. So pardon my lackluster compositional skills. I feel like this game gets a lot more negative criticism than it deserves. So here's my take on it as someone who has recently gotten into the series starting with, of course, Persona 5. From there, I went on to play Persona 3, Persona 4, Persona 4 Golden, Persona 5 Strikers, and SMT3: Nocturne. I also played some of the non-RPG titles like all of the Persona dancing games and the fighting games. So that is where I am at in terms of the series. If you have been into the series for quite some time, then chances are that there are a lot of elements of this game that are going to turn you off and you are not going to like my review so may want to stop reading right about now. However, for those of you who are relatively new or are on the fence about this game due to negative reviews like I was, I feel that you should give this game a chance even if you have to wait for a sale. Gameplay: This game is actually pretty damn fun - mainly because it still has that addicting SMT gameplay. In terms of difficulty, this is probably the easiest out of any of the SMT games that I have played as it is pretty easy to get demons that can resist any element. There plenty of side quests in addition to the main quest even though they don't really get anywhere that interesting in the end, but offer additional combat and rewards that can help make the game even easier and unlock certain dungeons/maps. If anything, I think this adds accessibility to the game especially for those that are not familiar with the SMT series or are not fans of the difficulty spike in certain games of the series especially towards the end. Those of you looking for that challenging SMT gameplay may want to skip this one. I'm personally into both the challenging games and this accessible level of difficulty for this game. There is also new game+ available so that adds some replayability to the game too. I personally don't do new game+ stuff anymore since I have limited time for video games these days. Story: It is your typical JRPG trope-filled prevent the end of the world with the power of friendship kind of storyline. The characters are pretty likeable in my opinion although a bit flat. They help make the atmosphere feel pretty chill unlike Nocturne where everything feels empty and depressing (yeah, I know it is supposed to be post-apocalyptic) even though some people are into that. To each their own.Art Direction: I like it. Personally, not a fan of the other SMT games with the gothic doll-like artwork so it was not hard for me to like the artwork in this. Environment/Level Design: Other people seem to think that the dungeons are repetitive or tedious. If you think that the level design is repetitive, then you need to play Dragon Age 2. If you think that the maps in this game are tedious, then you need to play SMT: Nocturne. Music: Pretty good, but not Persona 3,4, or 5 level of good. Performance: This game never had any form of instability and it never crashed for me. I feel like it was optimized well for the PC and I had smooth frame rates the whole time. The game did not seem to be graphically demanding in the first place evidence being that my GPU fans did not activate when I played this game and I am rolling with a 5600xt with a Ryzen 7 3700X when I played it. If you are into ratings, then I would personally give this game an 8.5/10.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're into SMT or Persona, this game is for you--but let's be clear, it's NOT those games. Every SMT game is trying to do something different. The mainline Shin Megami Tensei games, like Nocturne, which is on Steam, are going for sort of these big, apocalyptic spaces, telling a story of how the world was ended and must be remade by killing God. Persona games--at least the ones that are on Steam or coming to Steam--are all about high schoolers getting into big stuff where you end up killing God.Soul Hackers--whether the original Saturn game, the PS1 game, or the 3DS remake--is more of your standard first person dungeon crawler. Think Grimrock or something, if you're not super familiar with Japanese dungeon crawlers (they share the same roots: the Wizardry games!). It dealt with the anxieties about technology leading up to the new millennium, so it was all "what if an MMO ate people?" and "what if spirits used technology to invade our world?" It was really cool, and if you have a 3DS, I think it's really neat.While the lineage is a bit nuts, Soul Hackers 2, which is technically Devil Summoner 3 (Soul Hackers 1 is Devil Summoner 2 basically lmao), is standardized into the third person of SMT and Persona now, like SMTV or Persona 5. It shares the same demons. It's not even exactly a followup to the technohorror of Soul Hackers. The budget's lower than Persona 5 or SMTV, and you can see that in the game.But it's FUN. Really awesome game, especially with the massive QOL patch they did that includes dashing while running! Cool story, interesting twist on the press turn system (though I still prefer press turn). But because it's LIKE the other games, it is not EXACTLY the other games. It's doing its own thing. Demon negotiation? Sorry, now your demons go find other demons for you to recruit. Victor's back with the compendium, and fusion is more like what you've come to expect from newer games of the series.Basically... it's... like, it's own thing. It's a cool, dark JRPG about preventing an apocalyptic event. It's a game where your friends eat pizza and for some reason have two massive jars of mayonnaise on the table. It's a game with some really good voice acting (Ringo is superb), great character designs, and so on.But like, hey, the budget's a bit lite. Expect most locations you visit to be relatively small--Kabuki-cho is represented here, but instead of Yakuza's Kamurocho, it's a single street with shops to visit. The Soul Matrix dungeon, which is absolutely massive, only has one aesthetic--even the much smaller SMT3 megadungeon had a mere five kalpas, and Persona 5's Mementos, while absolutely huge, was mostly procedurally generated mazes. I love them all, but these are more classic puzzle dungeons--deliberately designed and very specific. They just have... exactly one aesthetic. While there is story to them, and some fun fights to be found, don't expect a huge budget that would allow a ton of graphical variance.If you set your expectations correctly, you're going to have a great time.I'm getting near the end, and my current save has me at about 40 hours. I've done all the side content I could find--and the neoseeker guide got me thinking I have done ALL the side content. I haven't done the final DLC superboss yet, and I'm approaching the end of the story.Good game, fun time. Probably best for people who love SMT; I'd recommend you play Persona 5 first to dip your toes in, and then maybe SMTV on switch (or when it comes to steam, which will hopefully be soon).

_childDocuments_.review: >>****Game runs flawlessly on the Steam Deck on high > very high stable 50+ FPS using latest GE Proton version****<<Steam Deck Performance - 10/10PC Performance - 10/10Gameplay - 8/10Graphics - 5.5/10Style & Sound - 10/10Story - 7.5/10>>**To start off, this game is NOT Persona, and is not part of that series, despite being SMT.  This game is from a part of SMT that is far closer to its original incarnations as a dungeon crawler.  If you are expecting Persona, this isn't it. **<<Music and art style are really high points here and make up for  the otherwise rather basic graphics that this brings to the table. That being said, those basic graphics are also somewhat of a blessing, as it gives the game incredible performance on the Steam Deck and any middle-range PC system. On my main desktop with a 3080...not so much. Gameplay is about what you expect, though it has less emphasis on demon hunting than I expected of it, as most SMT games have a pretty heavy emphasis on the demons.  This game has a lot more emphasis on the characters themselves which is an interesting twist compared to other games from this branch of the series.  Combat is varied and tactical and is a real highlight. It is turn based but highly customizable. Storyline is heavy, with lots of cutscenes and voice acted dialogue. Characters are very colourful and charming, story is bright but with a side of strange nihilism, many of the characters you meet and recruit are people who were murdered, if that gives any indication of the tone of the world. Overall I recommend this game for fans of SMT, if you enjoy classic SMT and dungeon crawling you will enjoy this. If you're expecting the next gen game to max out your high end PC hardware with AAA big budget graphics and massive open worlds....well, you wont find that here. This is a JRPG through and through, so as long as you set your expectations properly you wont be disappointed.My biggest gripe with this game is that the DLC is sort of BS. Overpriced and silly. It's worth noting this game also has Denuvo anti-piracy, which I think is also unnecessary and punishes legitimate customers for buying games. If these things turn you off of the game, I wont blame you for it.A recommended buy when on sale or if you can find it for less than the $79.99 asking price elsewhere.

_childDocuments_.review: Now that I got  attention, I think this is a great SMT game, and, like every other entry in the series, have it's pros and cons.Let's start with the :- The gameplay is classic and that's a good thing, I love the weakness exploitations and with a great addition: the sabbats.- Ringo and Figue are the best IA protagonists, and at first I thought that this could be a bit cliché, but the more I get into the game, the more I liked them.- The game theme is a bit unclear but, once you get through the final steps, it gets more evident and I absolutely love it. I just wish it were a bit more clear, but I think that one is on me!But in every light, :- They try to make a group connection out of the members but they didn't feel like one. Maybe this approach is a bit more realistic than the classic JRPG where completely strangers come agross adversity and became friends. This group feels more like co-workers that tolerate the other one for the job's sake.- The Soul Matrix is, in my opinion, dull and empty. There's no use of it beside getting hacker's skills and learn just a bit more about the group.- And, the most irrelevant, but kinda in point with the game title: this is no sequel to the first one. There are no common elements, even if they trying to tell us that there are (and no, getting Nemissa as a demon with paid DLC is no connection at all). This could get a complete different name as the Devil Summoner saga and nothing would change.In general, I love the game's theme: . I just really would love that Atlus could've pour a bit more budget, but in general, this is a good start to revive the SMT flame and I hope they can play a bit less safe in later games in the saga, as once they did!
