_childDocuments_.review: Overpriced but still kinda fun. All the criticisms are valid. I barely recommend. If Soul Hackers was a riff on the earlier SMT formula, this is certainly based on SMT4. 3D environments, requests, etc. I couldn't help think of other games in the greater series when playing this.The core feeling I got was Tartarus from Persona 3. I remember many, many hours of running around and grinding and without the cheat DLC, I'd sure be grinding SH2 right now. Two major problems are it reminds me of P3P, where most of the fun exploration was replaced by menus, and that many of the dungeons end up being blind teleporter mazes. The story reminded me of Strange Journey not for any thematic reason, just it barely existed and the party members were basically "Stupidly selfless" good, "Rage Against the Machine" evil, and "I'm not getting involved" neutral. Similarly, the choice of endings (if there is one, I'm unsure) is a pick-a-path in the last 15 minutes of gameplay.Combat is overly simplified. Now weaknesses just add to a meter that does more damage at end of turn. It loses a lot of complexity and people interested in deep SMT tactical battles are out of luck.It is graphically very nice and the voice acting is above average. I can see where the money went, but this is very much Atlus' B series, with their A price. I guess I had almost 28 hours in it, but as the game went on, I needed more and more frequent breaks. That's not the way things should be. I don't want my time back, but this is "Pad playtime by grinding: The Game." Get it on sale, and be sure you're interested in grinding and obnoxious mazes. If you're expecting Persona 5, you'll be very disappointed. If you're expecting Strange Journey or Devil Summoner in 3D, that's less likely to end in heartbreak. But that price point.

_childDocuments_.review: This is how I like it. It's how I roll, okay? I enjoy crawling dungeons. I'm a dungeon-crawler kinda guy. I'm borderline and hypersensitive and what not, and thus I absolutely love miles upon miles of twisting and turning corridors, repeating similar battles ad nauseam, things that occupy my fingers and the ever-terrified lizard part of my brain so I can distract the mammal part of my brain with the music and finally let my human-brain ponder things almost the same way the normal people do. Having said that, Soul Hackers has actually managed to tire me out somewhere around the finale. And, mind you, some time ago I've spent 200 hours plus crawling Mary Skelter and loved nearly every second of it. And there was Legend of Grimrock just before that. And Vaporum. Have I already mentioned I was into dungeon crawlers?My problem with Soul Hackers is not that it involves an abundance of dungeoning. That's is one of the things  I came here for. The minor issue is that most of the locations are not particularly inspired. Shipping districts with lots of crates, abandoned construction sites, subway tunnels. All of these mercilessly recycled. There are at least two dungeons of each of those kinds, all of them consisting of multiple floors. But the absolute beast here is the Axis. It's a (mostly optional. But if you know your Shin Megamis then you must realize that skipping optionals is not an option) Gibson's cyberpunk virtual reality themed dungeon consisting of 12 (more on NG+!) mazelike floors that all look exactly the same. And if that wasn't enough, they employ an extensive use of portals when you reach the final levels. Not one or two portals per level but a sizable archipelago of islands interconnected by a network of teleporters that not necessarily make an immediate sense, require the memorization of where they lead and sometimes don't allow going back without taking a lengthy trek or teleporting entirely out of the dungeon and starting over. Luckily, there are a few fast travel points that somewhat remedy the situation. And as far as I know there is no separate map besides the mini-map projected onscreen as the party crawls.The thing is, I owe it to Shin Megamis a lot on lots of grounds and music is one of them. See, when it comes to such lengthy campaigns it is inevitable that sooner or later, and with the notable exception of Yakuzas, I will get bored with the soundtrack and switch to an external provider. And as fate would have it, it is always over the final dungeon of a Shin Megami game that I discover some of the best tunes. I've got Tanooki Suit from Persona4, Jess and the Ancient Ones while running kalpas in Nocturne, Sulfur Giants on a loop four or five hours straight, and Hackers had me discover Rave the Reqviem. But this was supposed to be a paragraph about Hacker's music, right? It's fine and dandy. Fits the mood, and stuff. Go, check Jess, Tanooki and Reqviem out. The characters are medium-lovable. Their backstories are the same old. There are also some heavily questionable, logic-bending actions towards the conclusion of the story, some unnecessarily theatrical screaming and some traditional JRPG exaggeration. But besides that, they are actually charming. During my 60 plus hours with Hackers, the way they interacted, hinted and commented each other's actions during the battles never got old. The little events in the local bar (the game has over 40 of those) while rather predictable, were still fun to witness. And the change and development they all undergo during the events of the game is - if you're willing to listen to their stories - actually quite impressive. Also there's Ringo, the game's protagonist and one of the better Shin Megami characters. First of all, she is not your typical SMT silent lead. She has both voice and personality. She is witty, upbeat and curious. She is also basically an anthropomorphized splinter of a macrocomputer superconsciousness overseering the humanity and there is a graceful explanation as to why such an entity would basically downgrade itself to meat and bone. L-l-look at you, Shodan, how the tables have turned...Also! The demons are really well written. There is this clever, little gimmick that instead of looking for the chests lying randomly around the dungeon, you send your demons out and they wait for you with items around the map. The Vile family deserves a special mention with their "Uhh, this thing will absolutely help the team.. W-w-wait how long have you been standing there listening?! DON'T tell anyone or I will have to kill you!" lines. You know, Viles? The evil guys.Also! Also! Most of the sidequests are of the standard go / kill / fetch variety but some of them are wrapped in a truly brilliant narration. Just forget the whole koala gig, it's better that way. I did. In all honesty, I have no idea what this koala business is all about. Found it in my notes for this review, reminding me to forget about it.            It's a Shin Megami, what did you expect? The mechanics are solid, there's hundreds of demons to be caught, and the usual rock-paper-scissors of the elements is present. If you know your SMTs you'll be at home and if you don't, you'd do best by starting somewhere else. P4 or 5 preferably, maybe Nocturne. Basically, any other main game. This one is for the folks who have drained all the other possibilities and still want more Atlusverse. Anyways. Hackers is slightly on a lite side. It's easier, more colorful and definitely less edgy than your usual SMT. Yes, of course there's the fate of humanity at the stake, but it's somewhere in the background. It's definitely not as soul - crushingly dark as Survivors or Nocturne. That is, if you find the complete extinction of humanity on a Biblical scale dark, I realize opinions may vary on this one. Nonetheless. The battles are significantly less challenging than I'd expected. Take the Sabbath mechanism. Every time a party member hits demon's weakness, it adds to the stack which in turn results in an all-out attack performed by the end of the turn which occurs when all of the party members finish their actions. Moreover, there is no similar punishment for enemies hitting the party's weaknesses. And, while I am far from calling it a hindrance, saving is available at all times outside of the battle.      Sixty hours plus cut short, Hackers is the definition of a mixed bag. Sure, it's only a solid Megami, but that's still a viable way of wasting some hundred hours of your lifetime away. Yes, it's not a legendary like Personas or Nocturne. Or Strange Journey. It has its ups and downs, but there are some really nice ideas and honest, heartfelt moments every now and then. Still, the DLCs are coldheartedly greedy and atrocious. If he was alive, Freud would definitely have had a thing or two to say about locking Mara inside a paywall cage like that. Best course of action, 60% discount or higher, no DLCs and only if you've already completed Nocturne and at least one Persona. I have spoken.      * had no idea for paragraph tiles, used the names of my playlists As always, thank you for reading this farand, as always,

_childDocuments_.review: Played just about every SMT Mainline and spinoff there is, such as DDS, Devil Summoner, including the first Soul Hackers, at least the 3DS port if not the Sega Saturn original. Knowing the first, I was pleasantly suprised. I was hoping they'd bring this sequel more up to speed with the other current titles, and so they did.The story is surprisingly compelling, though there will be a lot of dungeon crawling pretty soon into the game. More than some people might be used to. If I'd compare this title to any other in the SMT Universe it would actually be Persona Q probably.In a nutshell, I'm really having fun with this one, even though it is a little on the easy side. I like the traditional press turn system, which has unfortunately been replaced with the sabbath system. In a nutshell, for people familiar with Persona and SMT: Instead of getting extra (half) turns for exploiting weaknesses, the party collects "stacks", one per exploited weakness, later more possibly with some passive skills. If there is at least one stack at turn end, it will trigger sabbath, which is essentially an "All-out" attack, and it gets stronger the more stacks there are. This actually makes the game easier in a way, but it just feels a little less satisfying to me. It's not horrible though, and I think it's quite alright that they experiment with their combat system a little.For anyone who likes the SMT Franchise and doesn't mind doing a lot of dungeon crawling, they'll probably appreciate the title as I do.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm glad I waited for the QoL update so I could sprint through dungeons, because oh my god is the dungeon design tedious. I hope you like long, blue-tinted corridors because that's essentially all you're getting. You'll also be revisiting most areas multiple times if you plan to do all the sidequests/get the "good" ending.Battles are your standard Persona/SMT style turn-based combat, so unless you're very into those you won't get much else out of them.I mostly play JRPGs for the characters and the story though, so I'd have been able to forgive the lackluster dungeon design if I really loved those. But I didn't. Saizo, Arrow, and Milady were all fine. Not particularly exciting, although it was nice that they were adults who had adult lives. Ringo... was not as great as I was led to believe from all the reviews. Not offensive in any way, but not particularly great either.That's about all I can say for the characters. I loathed Figue, but that was almost a given. The story and worldbuilding made no sense. Everybody just blindly accepted the exposition dumps about an all-knowing AI, the conflict was basic and unnuanced, the final villain and their motivation made me roll my eyes (although the villain before that wasn't any better). It seems very clear to me that Arrow was meant to be the protagonist at one point, with how the story centered around him as much as it did, but he wasn't any more fleshed out than the others.I also wish I'd gone with my gut for the "normal" ending. Doing all the dungeons and sidequests just for that cheesy "good" ending was not worth it. It was actively worse than the normal ending for me. But I guess by the time I got to that point, I just so done with the game I wanted everything to burn. Incidentally, you can't do everything on the first run. You have to do a NG+. _childDocuments_.review: Not as bad as some people are making it out to be.Soul Hackers 2 is awkwardly sandwiched in between the release of SMT V, and the re-releases of the Persona games. It was never supposed to be a huge 70+hour JRPG, it's supposed to be a rather experimental, smaller JRPG for Atlus to see what works and what doesn't, similar to how they operated with the Raidou games, Strange Journey, DDS, and hell even the original Soul Hackers. I think a lot of people placed unrealistic expectations for SH2 to blow things out the water, when instead it's probably the most solid 7/10 game I have played in recent memory.It's essentially a Persona game with more stripped back combat, and it even tries to mimic the Social Link system with its own 'Soul Level' type of deal amongst the main cast. I think it's quite fun, and is a cool hybrid between SMT and Persona that feels like a 'lite' version of both series. Here lies the problem though, I think this game would be perfect if you have never played an Atlus JRPG before, but I don't think I would ever recommend it as someone's first game considering various other Atlus projects do it so much better. It's the Soul Hackers 2 paradox.If you're looking for SMT level of difficulty, unfortunately it's more on the Persona side of things, as the game itself is fairly easy. And due to it taking influence from Persona, the dungeon designs are rather bland and consist of you running down hallways to find the route to progression. It's confusing to me seeing people hate on the dungeon designs, and then recommending people to play Persona 3 or 4 instead. Are you alright? The dungeons in this game are very similar to those found in P3 & P4, and I feel like the emphasis on the dungeons being mid in this game is overblown.The OST could have been much better though, a lot of the tracks here are forgettable. I feel like a game with a futuristic aesthetic they could have had some off the walls type of music going on here, but instead it's rather mellow and reminiscent of things you've probably heard before. But regardless of that the game is still fun, and while I don't know if it's worth £50, I still feel like I can recommend it to anyone curious, or to fans of JRPGS. Maybe wait for a sale and you'll have yourself a fun game.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall: I'd rank this about a 4/10. Good characters, reasonable combat, barely adequate soundtrack, bad plot, terrible dungeons, infuriating navigator."Uninspired" would be the word I would use to summarize this game. The core concept was fine, but almost everything surrounding that concept ranged from bland to terrible to downright rage-inducing.I liked the individual characters. Ringo had just the right amount of sass, Saizo was cool without being a complete smarmodon, Milady wanted to set everything on fire, and Arrow had kind of a stick up his butt in a way that gave him a good contrast to the others. (Arrow's voice kind of reminded me of Yosuke from Persona 4, if Yosuke were a lot calmer and a bit older, which I liked.)Combat was fine. It was a pretty standard variation on the basic SMT/Persona/etc. system. The Sabbaths were an interesting halfway point between SMT V's press turn system and Persona's all-out attacks.Controls and menus were a little clunky. Ringo moves like she's on ice skates, with a large delay before she starts moving at her full speed and a large delay between no longer pressing forward on the controller and when she actually comes to a stop. It's funny when you run up to a demon or NPC and press the button to talk to them, then watch Ringo slide to a stop ten feet past them while the dialogue is going.Music was unmemorable. Coming from the entire Persona series before this, I was very disappointed in this.The dungeons were TERRIBLE. There were two dungeons in dark and visually unappealing shipping yards. Two in dark and visually unappealing subways. A DLC dungeon in a dark indoor treehouse that looked like it could have been built in vanilla Minecraft. Three dungeons where everything was just different shades of blue and the floors floated in blue nothingness. And one dungeon in a tower that was inexplicably half an undersea theme and half pathways made of bones with gestating fetuses in the sky.Those three blue dungeons were infuriating. Starting on floor 3 of each of them, they became mazes of one-way teleporters between short little bits of platforms. The teleporters largely had no discernible logic to them. One place, as far as I was able to tell from the single guide that exists in the entire Internet for this floor that was all in Japanese, had a set of teleporters that had to be entered in a specific order, with absolutely zero hint or guidance in-game to indicate that.The undersea dungeon was somehow more rage-inducing, possibly because I'd already spent hours with those stupid teleporters. Again, one-way teleporters, this time with a metric ton of backtracking in between each one. This isn't fun. This isn't interesting. This is just artificially inflating the play time.And while I'm on about the dungeons...Mimi. Oh my god, Mimi. Imagine Navi from Ocarina of Time, but turned up to 11. For every single enemy, she tells you there's an enemy, she tells you the enemy has spotted you, and she tells you when you've neutralized the enemy. EVERY. SINGLE. TIME. And her lines never vary! And the enemies make sound themselves when they spawn anyway! She never tells you anything you can't see for yourself literally right in front of you! Fortunately there's a mod to shut her up otherwise I would have given up on the game about ten hours in.The plot is paper-thin. Characters react to things in strange ways. There are multiple instances where one minute they're like "we've gotta hurry and do this thing!" and the next minute they're all "welp, we're tired, time to call it a day". At the start of the game, Ringo says "I can't just Soul Hack whenever I feel like it" and then proceeds to Soul Hack three times in short succession, so, so much for that, I guess?

_childDocuments_.review: Spoiler Free review.Let's be honest no one here has played the original soul hackers game and no one cares. What people care about is a good JRPG with great dungeons and even greater story. Sadly this ain't it chief. Soul hackers 2 is plagued by a predictable story, boring lazy dungeons that frankly just waste your time, static characters, and Cash grab DLC. The only saving grace of this game is the amazing characters designs and well built world, But you don't really get to explore the world so it doesn't matter. This game is pure cash grab that felt like there was some sense of passion earlier but quickly muddled by the need for money. If you had high hopes for this game like me, or was hoping for another amazing JRPG by Atlus, boy are you ready to be absolutely disappointed. So lets break open this baby.Dungeons and GameplayThe dungeons in this game are literally walking simulators with enemy encounters. If you thought death stranding was a boring walking sim, this is worse. Dungeons all look the same, either some sort of subway or the matrix. There is only 1 dungeon that's even some what appealing to look at and its the final dungeon. To be honest these dungeons are worse than P4. Large areas with loops and turns that take forever to get through and ringo walks like a slow ass grandma, yeah i fell asleep while exploring the dungeons. Puzzle don't seem to exist in the world of soul hackers because every dungeon is the same walking sim ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. What's worse is there's a section of a dungeon that becomes random encounters while not being able to see ♥♥♥♥ because camera controls are limited. enough is enough and i've said enough about these horrible dungeons, Battles and encounters on the other hand aren't that bad. It's your typical smt/persona TB battle system. Target weaknesses apply debuffs and buffs. The sabbath system, while a bit simple is really fun. Finding demons with unique sabbath only abilities is always fun. Commander skills feel a bit overpowered at times but being OP is fun. Difficulty doesn't really exist in this game. It's overall a very easy game with some systems that let you feel OP. The one Negative about battles is probably ruin. instead of having abilities that do specific debuffs, ruin abilities do damage while applying debuffs. Ruin kinda breaks the balancing of all area's excluding bosses(Bosses are usually resistant to ruin all together). So gameplay is fun.Story and Characterssince this is spoiler free i'm just gonna keep this section short. The story is predictable, BUT NOT BORING just predictable. Some aspects of the story don't make sense and character development is weak. some characters are ruined by events in the game and i don't like it. Saizo is the only saving grace of this game. The character I thought i'd absolutely hate is the most dynamic character. Most of the characters in this game are fairly static till the the last few hours of the game, and the ending feels rushed. Overall its a mediocre story about human emotion and the characters are fairly static till the last hour. Also the ending feels rushed and pacing is all over the place, like all JRPG's.ConclusionI don't have to tell you that the world of this game is amazing. I don't have to tell you that the character designs are amazing. That's probably why you're here. The overall game isn't that great. The dungeons are just walking sims with rpg battles, and the story is a weak one with static characters. Don't play this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, I think this is a solid entry in the SMT greater universe, though I have some issues with it that really hurt the experience. I love the main cast which have a lot of good moments/conversations, the soundtrack has some really solid tracks to listen to, and I think the general style is colorful and gives everything a nice look. I even chose to go through my first playthrough on Hard difficulty, and I definitely appreciated the challenge as well as having to sometimes completely remake my party to fit the situation and better equip them for any new bosses. One of my main issues is about the Soul Matrix, the main dungeon-esque area where you unlock abilities/backstory for your party members. The problem is, while neat in theory with the look, it's just extremely boring to see the same look of the dungeon, floor after floor, running around in a very visually unappealing area. It decides to make things worse later on by having a bunch of portals take you to different areas (without updating the map on which portal goes where of course), which pushed me to just look at a walkthrough to see where to get to the next gate I needed to unlock. My second main issue is while this game runs fine on Steam Deck, it only does so *if* you are able to get past the opening loading screen. Sometimes it will randomly freeze and never progress, so you have to close the game and re-launch and hope that it gets to the Atlus logo. This unfortunately also affects whenever you get a game over (which is easy when playing on Hard difficulty), because then the game could punish you even more for losing by just freezing the game. I'd have been lenient if the game just came out, but 4 months after release and seeing no real indication of the issue being fixed is a real bummer (with every "fix" being temporary at best, but then the DRM can kick in and cause problems there). Due to that, I've opted to not go all the way for all the possible content the game offers, since I'd be more comfortable playing it handheld rather than at my desk. While I did spend more time on my issues with the game, I did enjoy it and would recommend it with caveats, especially if you intend to only play it on a deck. If not, and you're not too bothered by the Soul Matrix issue (I ended up listening to podcasts while "exploring" it), then this is definitely another fun entry of befriending demons and using them to crush your enemies.

_childDocuments_.review: Soul Hackers 2 is a dungeon crawler, an old school dungeon crawler. It is similar to games Atlus released on the 3DS or maybe the PS2. If this sounds like a bad thing to you, stay away from this game because it is not the new big jRPG release by Atlus. It is not Persona or SMT6, it is not a big new shiny thing either.If you read the PS2 statement and it did not bother you AND the fact this is being sold as a full price release -which could buy you the big new shiny thing I mentioned earlier- isn't an issue for you, then this game is good. I enjoy it a lot.The story is good and delivered at a nice pace. The party members are very nice (they are very grounded, which to some might be boring) with different facets of personality and relationships to the enemies and each other. The dungeons are sprawling mazes, some of which really required me to pay attention to which warp led to what portion of the map and while grueling to explore sometimes gave me a real feat of accomplishment when completing them since it really feels like the dungeon is kinda fighting you back, making itself difficult to navigate through. Really wish we had more visual and music changes during the dungeons though.Combat is nice (please, play it on hard!! This game's hard is easier than SMTV's normal!!). The bosses have a puzzle approach to them with multiple phases, contrary to SMTV, which felt like every boss could be beaten by just tanking and hitting weaknesses and keeping buffs/debuffs up. The Sabbath at first seems lacking depth but as you get more COMP upgrades and Soul Matrix skills it shines quite a lot, making possible some strategies I couldn't see happening on normal Press Turn.tldr: Soul Hackers 2 is made for a very specific type of people that wants a dungeon crawler with grounded characters and a overall old school experience. It does not try to do anything really new. It was made within a budget and you can see it with the very samey dungeon designs, the fact that almost every dungeon or that every boss uses the same music track. It is still a good game in my opinion.♥♥♥♥ Atlus and their DLCs practices though. Also, a lot of the problems with this game come from its pricing. If it was being sold as a $40 title, everything would make sense. $60 could get you at least one of the upcoming Persona ports which are all better than this game. It could get you Xenoblade. It could get you the eventual SMTV port. Atlus and Square are really trying to get back to the old days, releasing a bunch of lower budget niche games which are all cool but almost never cool enough to justify the full price tag making the game compete with titles it can't win against, sending it to fail.

_childDocuments_.review: It’s alright. There is a part of the game where, once you complete a dungeon that takes place in a subway system, you have to go right back into another full length subway dungeon. This is just bad game design, plain and simple. Revisiting dungeons is fine when these visits are spaced out enough as to not make the player bored, but there was no effort made to space these dungeons out at all. Additionally, the Soul Matrix is bland and uninteresting. It’s just a sea of blue cubes meant to be all hacker themed, which is fine, but the Soul Matrix is meant to be done over the course of the game. Nothing about this dungeon changes at all between floors, or depending on whose Soul Matrix it is. This is only two dungeons I really had a problem with, sure the others weren’t super interesting but they were at least fine. I liked the dungeon where you kept getting into forced encounters that drained your MP, as it forced you to defeat the group of enemies with limited resources. In terms of combat, the combat system was fine. It was fun enough, but not as fun as mainline SMT or Persona. The main thing is Sabbath attacks that occur at the end of every player turn if you strike a weakness. Each attack that strikes a weakness adds a stack to this attack, and you can unlock ways to get more stacks depending on the element used or by certain commander skills. There is some satisfaction in getting very high stacks and dealing some massive damage, though the damage never seemed really significant to me, even when using every demon in my stock. Though maybe that’s just me, either way it’s still fun, but that’s all there really is to the combat. Other than that it’s SMT. The story was alright, definitely a step up from SMT V. I haven’t finished the story because frankly I got bored once I had to mandatorily revisit the Soul Matrix, so I can’t comment much on it. There are some twists and turns, the characters are enjoyable (except Mimi), and the English voice acting is aight. Again, haven’t finished the story because again, boring dungeon made me bored. Grinding in this game isn’t bad at all, as the meal system provides meals that can give you even more EXP from fighting higher level enemies. Meals can increase stats or buff your party in some way, and wear off when you leave whatever dungeon you enter. These meals aren’t hard to get, and you’ll likely end up with more than you need just from your allies giving them to you. The meal system is pretty neat and adds some level of strategization when preparing for a boss. There’s a hangout system where, after certain events or sidequests, you unlock a hangout event where you get to talk to one or some characters at the bar. These are kind of neat, but if you don’t care about them you don’t have to do them. Overall this game is just alright. Buy it on sale if you’re interested as this game isn’t really worth the $60. I haven’t covered every element of this game, mostly just the things that stood out to me as good or bad. It’s an alright game but it could have been better.

_childDocuments_.review: I both love and hate this game. 80% of this game you will spend upgrading your characters. Like similar Shin Megami Tensei style you get to use a variety of demons with each character, and customizing your characters is super easy and someways fun. But upgrading your characters sucks. Imagine in Persona 5 that you had to go through mementos to unlock the skills you get like "follow up" or "assist" BUT you had to go through all of mementos over and over again for EACH CHARACTER. That'd be super frustrating right? That's the reality that this game is. The graphics are great, the story is good, and the voice acting is good. But some of the choreography and sound effects just feel like they're missing or weirdly put together. Only really in cutscenes though. The characters are super likeable and i live for hanging out with them, because i love them a lot. But this game is NOT meant to be played unless you have a 2nd computer screen to watch anime, youtube, etc because the Axis = Mementos takes up a LOT of time. Keep in mind i've played 32 hours i'm pretty sure i'm near the end of the game, but i'm not doing side missions, BECAUSE it takes so long to do the Axis.The worst part of the side missions is that there are no map markers. Meaning you have to explore the dungeons you visit ALL OVER AGAIN and these maps are BIG. Think Shin Megami Tensei big. _childDocuments_.review: If you are  fan of PSP/PS Vita/DS/3DS style JRPGs you may like this. Its very small in scope like the portable JRPGs, small areas, a lot of transitions between those small areas. I'm sure a lot of the Demon models have been taken out of other Shin Megami Tensei (SMT) games as well as it seems they have the same animations. The game play is not that much different from those JRPGs too but it feels really good. This game was also mainly played on my Steam Deck too so that has helped.The world design reminds me a lot like Digimon Story Cyber Sleuth (DSCS), more so the way they designed the digital areas of the game, the rest is just your JRPG version of future Japan that has been in a lot of the portable era of games.Character design is fun and looks like a lot of Japanese sci-fi games that have to do with sci-fi  future, yet again reminding me of DSCS. Its the generic group of JRPG protagonists with flashy and flamboyant cyberpunky clothing. The voice acting in English is good but your standard fair from the portable era of games. I didn't play the original Devil Summoner: Soul Hackers so I can't compare. The battles are fun and flashy with great animations. They don't quite work the same as the other SMT games so it took a bit getting used to.  You don't use Demons as summons in this game the same way, you use them as essentially programs in your weapon which decides what attacks you can do and what your weakness and strengths are. The attacks are very similar to what the demons would do in the other SMT games. The demons in this game don't have the same weaknesses from other SMT though so I had to relearn some of what I knew from other SMT games. Demon fusion is here, and pretty much similar to the other SMT games. If you have played any of those portable are games the dungeon crawls are the same, a lot of back tracking a lot of small areas with a lot of transition. You see the demons in the world and can knock them down like other SMT games and get preemptive attacks. The dungeons are kind of bland like the portable era games.The main plot is a mystery story with your group mainly acting as detectives. You pick up cases from a few people in the world or from a quest giver that then will send you to people in the world. Most quest haver you returning to areas you have already traversed to find a glowing item, killing a certain demon or a certain amount then returning to the person you talked to then returning to the quest giver. The more you do, the higher you level up for the quest giver and get newer quests. It can get tedious and repetitious.

Dungeon design is SUPER boring; soul matrix is the biggest eyesore, but the fact that the only uniquely designed dungeon is the very last one is telling of how much this title needed more time in the oven.Story is forgettable, super predictable, and the main cast is not interesting enough to warrant the long-winded gameplay segments.Music slaps in its own right.Gameplay is boring, unbalanced, and disrespects your time. Main combat gimmick is super boring (more damage), and could be saved by the later introduction of sabbath skills. Elemental attacks are way stronger than its physical counterparts. _childDocuments_.review: Pretty good experience, especially post patch.The biggest selling point I'd say is the main cast of characters that is pretty refreshing for an Atlus RPG, a bit reminiscent of P2 Eternal Punishment. Great interactions both in battle and in quieter moments, all sold by extremely high-quality voicework in both japanese and english. Speaking of good points, the game looks great on all fronts, but especially the characters and demons. The Kaneko designs have never looked better, it's like I'm rediscovering them after many years, and the addition of the Doi designs is also greatly appreciated. Combat starts out boring, but quickly gets more interesting, Your mileage may vary on whether or not that's acceptable, but by the midgame it was decently varied and enjoyable, and stayed that way until the end. It kinda does its own thing separate from all recent SMT titles (no turn shenanigans), and it does it okay.Dungeon exploration is pretty bland, not helped by the lack of diversity in dungeon designs and soundtracks. The general direction of the game is a bit aimless in what it tries to convey about the state of the world. The plot fares much better as a personal story for the main cast than as a game with a broad message about society.The game is solid overall, but more so because it has a lot of uneven parts that balance themselves out, with the positives edging out the negatives in the end. I hope Atlus takes it as a first step to diversify the SMT catalogue beyond the mainline and Persona games, because there are a lot of good elements in there that deserve to be explored further. Don't expect to have your mind blown, but you'll probably have a good time.I just want a cool cast of characters like this one in all future Atlus games dammit.

_childDocuments_.review: Soul Hackers 2 is a tricky game to discuss in that it openly invites comparisons to another game it's very much not trying to be. The original Soul Hackers, so far as I can tell without having played it, was a fairly standard Shin Megami Tensei game, albeit with a more cyberpunk setting. Soul Hackers 2 sidelines SMT's trademark demons and most related mechanics, instead treating demons as equipment for the game's mostly human party members. This comparison ultimately does the game a disservice, as while a more conventional follow-up would perhaps be more welcome, it does a respectable if uneven job of standing up on its own. The human party members are endearing, the game's sabbath system is quite satisfying if not particularly deep, and while the new demon recon mechanic doesn't quite make up for the sidelining, it does function as a clever way to give those demons a greater presence. The game's biggest genuine fault is that the dungeons' designs are generally lackluster, in terms of both aesthetics and layout, and for a game that's spent mostly in dungeons, that can drag the game down considerably.Giving this game the Soul Hackers moniker may have been a misguided choice, but this is a fun if flawed JRPG. Maybe get it on sale, though.

I had to exit the game and reboot it every so often.-Dungeons can be a bit of a slog, especially the soul matrixMatter of personal taste-It didn't have any music tracks that REALLY slapped, like "One More God Rejected" from Shin Megami Tensei 3, but some people might enjoy the soundtrack anyway.-Sabbath system in my opinion, while fun, is not as enjoyable as the Press Turn system from Shin Megami Tensei, especially compared to SMT5 or SMT4A. However, once you learn how it works, team building around it ends up being pretty rewarding.Overall I'd say it's a B game, good not great.

_childDocuments_.review: very good and cooledit: thought i'd add more to my review considering that the above is kinda basicthe interactions between all the party members both inside and outside of combat are really refreshing for this kind of game, having party members comment of each others actions in game play and in story/hang out segments having their own conflicting beliefs but working together regardless is great as opposed to the average homogenised jrpg average of "yeah we're all really good friends trust me, we said so out right in dialogue". The main character of Ringo was a treat, despite the multi-choice dialogue it really feels like she's her own fleshed out character who exists to be more than just a self insert for the player.The story is you're average jrpg "save the world kill a god" kind of thing but mainly stands out with the theme of characters attempting to strive for the same goal via opposing means which comes together in multiple boss fights.gameplay wise, the sabbat system all though interesting, doesn't hold up as well as either the press turn or one more system of smt and persona respectively, all the idea of chaining weakness explanations for a bigger burst of damage was interesting kind of like the demon co-op attacks of strange journey, fails to really reach the same levels of depth as the other systems, really just summing up to "do more damage with weakness and crits = do more damage". Otherwise, i really appreciate the ability to fully customise the party's moveset and elemental affinities, allowing you to customise your parties' comp down to the buttons to rip that boss a new arseholeOverall, this is a great game though maybe not as unique as it's predecessor the OG Soul Hackers or other SMT entries, the story, characters and the customisation available for your party makes it a cut above your average JRPG.

_childDocuments_.review: I adore the Megami Tensei franchise. I love the sweet anime-like wholesomeness of the Persona series and can't get enough of the poetic hopelessness of the mainline SMT titles.Soul Hackers 2 is the first spin-off title in the franchise for the last decade that is not Persona. I can't emphasize how big that is. Every fan was over the moon when ATLUS announced that a sequel to the long-forgotten Devil Summoner: Soul Hackers is coming out soon.I truly wanted to love this game. Even if it wasn't up to par with P5 or SMTV, I still wanted it to perform well enough so we could get more spin-offs. However, it saddens me to say that Soul Hackers 2 feels like a game that predates P4 or any modern ATLUS title. The game has so many questionable design choices in the name of streamlining that it's no longer fun. For a game called Soul Hackers, very Little soul can be found in its dungeons and levels. I never went in expecting a meticulously designed game packed with content like P5, but I expected something that would make it stand out. So far, I haven't been able to find it, and I doubt I will ever be.I cannot recommend Soul Hackers 2.

_childDocuments_.review: I had quite some fun with this game. The game is no Persona, sure, but it got a lot of unwarranted hate. People didn't like the Sabbath system (I like it tbh) and people were complaining that the game is repetitive (But then they also complain that the game doesn't play out exactly like Persona or SMT??) The characters are all adults, which is a great change from Persona or SMT where they are a bunch of school kids. It has more adult themes and thus opens up the game a little bit more. I hope in future they make Persona games based on adults rather than school kids. There are some bad things about the game; like the soul matrix areas and the annoying puzzles you have to solve inside of them. Pro tip: Save before going through a teleporter, and reload if you need to. All in all, the game is in need of improvement, but it's still a really nice game.

_childDocuments_.review: It was ok, nothing special to me. Some plot twists here and there, but I didn't get caught up in it, something feels off. Maybe I felt like it was a standard anime, with some drama, characters fighting and then laughing together etc. I thought they were pretty generic from the trailers, they build up during the story though and Saizo is my favorite, I liked his story more but this is personal. Arrow got me at the beginning because I underestimated him a lot. Milady is ok aswell. Ringo is a MC with a fixed name and dubbed, which is great but I felt like something was off, maybe because she didn't have a background (explained story-wise but still..) and she's more self confident than the others, so I think I would have preferred a mute character like Joker. Figue seemed useless to me, even if she gets involved a lot in the story later on. It could be bigger, there are only a few small areas and some shops but it kind of works. I liked the night and futuristic atmosphere, specially the arts from the shops and the characters in there. Karakucho is my favorite area since it's bigger and you can feel the city. I also liked a lot the idea of the bar in Shinsando, you can meet your friends there and it resembles the social links in Persona but after a while it gets repetitive because it's limited to that, with the same animation of them taking a beer and drinking, while in Persona you can meet up in so many different areas of Tokyo and do different things. But I don't mean this game should have social links like Persona, it just does it way worse. Having played some other Atlus games, I think they did 2 great things through their games: the dungeons in Persona 5, where you get detailed palaces with parkour, air ducts, safe rooms etc and the ones in SMT3, labyrinths full of traps where you can get lost, with poisonous floors or no light and even some ingenious boss battles where you have to understand what's happening and think outside of the box to beat the enemies, aside from just weaknesses, strenghts and counter skills (EG: finding the only one enemy with a shadow on a full moon or the statue with no reflection). In this game, world dungeons are ok, more SMT like specially in the subway ones, where's a series of opened walls closing when you cross them and triggering others to open, and the ward municipal tower where there are some floors and a puzzle with elevators you can switch, but that's it. The rest of the world dungeons are just small and flat themed areas with some blind corridors. And you spend most of the time in the Axis dungeons, where you walk on squares suspended in the air and the only funny part about them is the area with random teleports where you get lost a lot and the challenge is to explore everything without getting lost. But that's something SMT3 did way better and SMT5 even worse in its only 2 dungeons, so I'm worried about that. I mean either do them well or don't put them in the game, otherwise it gets boring. It seemed pretty good to me. The comps upgrade system gives you all the passive abilities in exchange of money and materials found inside the dungeons; mystiques enhance your skills, halve mp costs or add ailments to normal skills, they are obtainable by leveling up demons or by scrapping the ones you don't need anymore. I didn't check if they were making an actual difference, but the numbers were there so they sure did. As always well done. I played it in english and the quality is the same of other Atlus games. Checking the game folders I also noticed they actually put lip sync folders for both english and japanese dubs. I expect a lot from Atlus soundtracks, I loved both the dancing vibes of the Persona series (that got me dancing on my chair for over 110 hours of gameplay) and the darker themes and ambient tracks featured in the SMT main series, that allowed me to better feel the apocalyptic atmosphere. Since MONACA was involved and they did a fantastic job in Nier, I was hyped a lot. But they obviously adapted their work to Soul Hackers 2 and there I lost the one thing I knew for sure I would find in an Atlus games. I mean, it fits well in the game's universe but I think their games are also unique for their soundtracks and I couldn't say the same about this one, with some exceptions. Leaving behind the awful experience with the missing costumes & bgm pack (digital premium editions in particular) that luckily has been fixed some days after release (I was almost getting through the end of the game without them), the only bug I noticed is the end walk animation being tied to the fps. If you cap fps to 30 it's how it's supposed to be, but with higher frames like 60, or 144 in my case, when you release the left stick Ringo keeps moving onwards by a lot. But it's not a big deal and the game should be otherwise bugs free. I have to mention though that there are still some rare cases of people that haven't got that dlc yet. Going through the Axis dungeons you unlock some background story scenes about Arrow, Milady and Saizo. But you just see the holograms of the characters involved like in Code Vein and I can't get to like this way of telling a story. It's an ok game, surely not great as it really feels it was a low budget production. But not that bad either. I recommend it to people without great expectations, but as a big Atlus fan I can't recommend it, they can and usually do way better than this. Since it has been produced by the same team from Tokyo Mirage Sessions, a game I avoided for the same reason, I guess it all makes sense.

_childDocuments_.review: Seems like a pretty solid middle ground between a more "traditional JRPG" approach like persona, and a mainline SMT game. The demon's as equipment approach provides more customization and Flexibility than you'd get in a persona game, while keeping a small, focused party of developed characters that an SMT game's mix and match monster party's have to rely on nonplayable story NPCs to have. Instead of the extra turn mechanics or knock down into all out attack combos of the other games, elemental weaknesses in this game build up an aoe attack that scales based off of each attack targeting a weakness, instead of an all or nothing approach. The enemies do not get this feature, but can still ambush you, which is a legitimate possibility based off of their spawning patterns.The dungeon system works pretty well, with your demons popping up around the map for a chat and a quick mid-dungeon recovery or gift, and the sword swing letting you knock down map enemies without starting a fight unless you intentionally run into them afterwards in case you just want to keep moving. This game also has "high risk" enemies (sort of like persona Q's FOEs), that cannot be knocked down, but can still be pushed away if you want to run past them.The bonuses for leveling a demon enough to learn all of their skills provide a nice little pseudo 'job' system, and I'm curious to see where this system goes later in the game.Non gameplay things: Pretty art, enjoyable characters, solid music. Animated portraits in dialogue is a nice touch. English voice acting is pretty good, though there's a kind of disconnect in RIngo's voice acting outside and inside of battle. Her battle line's seem higher pitched or something? Maybe I'll get used to it. Anyway I'm hoping for more PC releases of SMT games in the future, and this is a pretty good one so far.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not new to SMT games, but I've never played the original Soul Hackers, not have I played any of the Devil Summoner titles. The gameplay is okay, the demon encounters are.. frequent, the available demons and fusions are sufficient enough to make it through the game without major struggle. However, the story and it's pacing are far from perfect. I enjoyed the story, but there  is so much nothingness happening for the first half of the game, and then the story suddenly goes balls to the walls and gets interesting. Unfortunately, many players will probably lose interest before that point, especially when you consider that some of the dungeons are absolutely miserable. It's clear that some of them are designed to straight up waste your time and artificially prolong the game. If you can bear it until the end of the game, you will definitely be satisfied, as the story and everything does have a very good (and very Atlus-y) payoff.

_childDocuments_.review: Soul Hackers 2 may be one of the most disappointing games I've ever played. Developed by Atlus, most known for series like Shin Megami Tensei and Persona, these guys know how to make a good JRPG and even make someone like me who's not a fan of the genre interested in them. Soul Hackers 2 is not a step forward, its 20 steps back that comes with a price. First things first, this game is short. REALLY short. It took me 44.5 hours for 100% completion which also includes a second playthrough. This wouldn't have been a problem if game had a reasonable pricing, but for $90 dollars its straight up mental. What do you get with a full package? - You get few costumes, none of which can be worn outside of battles and don't tell me to download a mod because that's not an official part of the game. - You get battle soundtrack from other Atlus games which is whatever.- You get iconic demons from Megaten ser- wait, WHY THE HELL ARE DEMONS LOCKED BEHIND A PAYWALL!? And why is one of them only available in Premium Edition?- You get a "story expansion", but compared to the likes of Labyrinth Of Amala from SMT3, The Answer from P3FES, Marie and Kasumi from P4G/P5R this is a side mission quality expansion that's not connected with the main plot so its absolutely a filler. You don't even get to control the new party member, she's only available in missions related to her expansion, and even there you get to use her maybe 2 or 3 times in total. - You get boosters, in case you don't want to play a game you paid for.Why even bother? May as well just go out and buy other Megaten games on Steam, you could literally buy both P4G/P5R at once and still save $10 instead of buying SH2 Premium, not to mention both of which are bundled with all DLCs. Even Nocturne was a better deal.When people say dungeon design is bad, they're not being sincere enough. They're not bad. They're bloody awful. Terrible, TERRIBLE dungeons. After this game I doubt many will go back to P3 and complain at Tartarus. What makes them so bad?- Large, wide, empty, hollow. - They all reuse the same music. How. The. Hell. Did. This. Happen? Even Tartarus and Labyrinth of Amala had variations of their theme, but Soul Hackers 2 just plays the exact same song over and over again. These games usually have killer soundtracks, but this game can't even play a different dungeon music? Get out of here.- There are no puzzles whatsoever, you search for demons which hold key items you'll need to progress and that's as deep as it goes..... actually no, there's one much worse thing they could call a puzzle, it's.....-  I HATE TELEPORTERS. Someone thought it'd be really funny to sprinkle them across dungeons and teleport you all over the place, forcing you to run back and forward until you memorize which teleporter out of 50 is gonna take you to the right place. Speaking of running back and forward....- ...where's sprint button? Why is it a locked mechanic which you still gotta pay for per use and it lasts for 30 seconds? Who in their right mind would not implement a sprint button in a game that arguably needs one the most? Regular speed is super slow and would work if you were in tight corridors, but these are wide, open dungeons. The hell is wrong with you Atlus?No really, why would you buy this game over other ones? Is it because you think main protag is hot? Is it because you may be into cyberpunk setting? Is it because you're interested in the story? Because even if you said yes to all 3, there are way better choices out there that aren't as greedy and tedious as this. Story itself also isn't that good, as Ringo kinda carries it all while the rest is either beyond rushed or uninteresting. Not to mention the animations in non pre-rendered cutscenes are gut-bustingly atrocious.Worst game of 2022 for me, I'd much rather play a straight up bad game than something like Soul Hackers 2 which technically isn't the worst game of the year material, but its so underwhelming to the point where it just makes me angry. Ringo and her gang deserved better, and when my favorite thing about the game is a charming little stage play they set up for its announcement, then I have to question.... where is that passion in the game? Where's your SOUL Soul Hackers 2?

_childDocuments_.review: First thing I'd like to say - wait for a sale or buy key elsewhere. The game is heavily overpriced on steam.Second thing - there's ugly DLC practice involved. I'm talking about Day One DLC and clearly a cut content that could had being introduced in the base game. The only DLC I got was Lost Numbers Mission which I believe is fine as it gives access to extra realm with new bosses, loot and ''secret'' lvl99 boss. That area also contains materials required for extra upgrade which might become available for you only at New Game 2 and beyond. Now about the game itself.Graphics and Sound : These are at decent levels. You won't find them too cheap, although you might notice duplicate models and certain bosses appearing the same. Some VOs do repeat a bit too much, like ''navigator'' having 2 or 3 lines only, team mates saying the same stuff and so on. Guess these didn't have the highest priority in their budget list.Gameplay : I'd say it's a fine mix of SMT series and Persona. You control 4 Summoners who can have different demons and have different powers and weaknesses. Once you unlock special upgrades for main character Ringo, you can swap one or entire roster of demons mid-fight at the cost of ''turns''. There's no ''one more'' or pass system so every move does count, though Ringo can do two moves after certain upgrade purchase and if that skill does proc ( it's random ). There are many similarities between these games but also some new stand-alone changes to mechanics. It's certainly not a copy-pasta thing and has a stuff to keep you occupied.World, Dungeon, Exploration : These are probably the weakest parts of the game. Areas are small, dungeons look the same, the exploration is you running around and looking for own demons who you release at the entrance of the dungeon and who may find random stuff, help you recruit new demons or heal your HP and MP. Other than that - it's corridors that look the same with enemies spawning out of thin air and appearing as the same Red, Yellow or Purple ''robot-like'' figure until you and it do interact. Zones where you can walk and do stuff outside of combat are limited and usually contain few shops and some people to ''talk'' to. There's also the Club that gives you missions which will give you rewards ( sometimes useless ones ) but will also make you interact with people a bit more, creating an illusion that the city is a bit alive, while in reality it's just a small box with dummies inside.To sum it up - this is fine game to play if your expectations aren't too high, you can buy it cheaper and are waiting for Persona 5 Royal on Steam. If none of these three conditions are met, I'd strongly suggest watching few videos on youtube before making a purchase and then ending up disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: There have been issues with the DLC content based on where you have bought the game and/or DLC. Be advised that not all DLC may work correctly at the time of the writing. This game runs decently on Steam Deck but latest stable and Proton experimental will have effects displayed incorrectly or visual effects missing. The power draw for me was quite high so don’t expect long battery life at this point.I enjoyed the game, it’s fun Atlus rpg with pretty fun battle system. It’s not Atlus’ most expansive game but if you enjoy Persona series and other Atlus games it’s well worth the time. I recommend this game.Soul Hackers 2 is next in line of the Shin Megami Tensei: Devil Summoner: Soul Hackers series. The game’s story does not really connect to the first one’s story, but there are mentions here and there. You can jump in this game without feeling like a lot of things are missing. If you are familiar with other Shin Megami Tensei games or the Persona series, expect to see lot of familiar demons from the series.The game is typical Atlus dungeon JRPG. You advance the story, do sidequests and roam dungeons while defeating enemies in turn-based battles. The battles follow same principles as other Atlus RPGs, hit the enemy’s weakpoint to deal with them quickly. The difference this time is the Sabbath-system, where each time you hit enemy’s weakness, you gather “stacks”. After your team’s turn is over, you will unleash Sabbath attack based on those stacks. For run of the mill battles, you also have auto-battle feature.The story is pretty standard JRPG story, nothing exceptional, but for most part it will keep your interest up with side-quests and some interesting concepts. I for one enjoyed the different setting and more mature characters and lack of the usual high school shenanigans.The game runs quite well on PC. Your graphical options include the typical display modes, an FPS cap with 30,60, 120, 144 and unlimited varieties, vsync option and your average “low, medium, high, very high” settings. For Anti-aliasing and depth of Field you can either enable or disable the options. Unfortunately, the game does not offer clearer AA options. The sound options allow you to se volume levels, select sound device and change the voice over language from Japanese to English if for some reason you want to do so. The game allows you to set your key config and supports a wide range of symbols from different controllers from xbox controller to Dualsense controller as well as a keyboard + mouse controls. The game does not feature any accessibility features apart from subtitles and message speed, which is a shame.For gameplay options you have some basic options such as different difficulty levels and camera positions. You can also change the BGM options for battles.The DLC is mostly cheats and some regrettable choices. The Booster item Pack essentially is cheats and the accessories included with the costume DLC are very strong. Bonus Demon Pack includes some iconical demons from SMT series, such as Mara and they will be very high level and available for free. The Bonus Story Arc is a separate set of side quests with its own story that you go through alongside your main quest.

_childDocuments_.review: Soul Hackers 2 is a solid, enjoyable game worthy of the Atlus name, and while it suffers from too much mediocrity to be a fantastic game, it does offer a fun, focused, and accessible entry point to the storied Atlus catalogue. While there might be minor critical quibbles for Soul Hackers 2, there may be major content concerns for the conscious gamer.While sketching this review and listing my dislikes, I wrote, tongue-in-cheek, “It’s not Persona 5 Royal.” As much as I enjoyed Soul Hackers 2, it didn’t compare to Atlus’ pièce de resistance in many areas. It’s a good, fun game, but it’s not going to make anyone’s Game of the Year. The story was decent, with two or three twists, most of which I saw coming. The combat was basically identical to any other Atlus game, and, while it’s good turn-based combat, it didn’t really do anything different or unique. The music was always fitting to what was happening on-screen, but it was never attention-grabbing, unlike P5R’s OST, which has some absolutely banger tracks. To me, the most outstanding parts of Soul Hackers 2 were its character design and its pacing. Everything else was good, but not amazing.Everything about Soul Hackers 2 makes it a perfect choice for someone’s first Atlus game, and I highly recommend it as such. The game gives you a taste of what Atlus games are like, but without the commitment to a 60+ hour slog. Veteran JRPG fans or Atlus fans might find Soul Hackers 2 lacking in areas, but on its own, Soul Hackers 2 is a solid game

_childDocuments_.review: I was on the fence for reviewing this game for so long because I wanted it to succeed. But after months dreading to return to it, I just gotta get it off my chest. Atlus rushes a RPG to further boost sales. It seemed too good to be true that two Atlus games came out in the same year.Gameplay: Fun for the hardcore turn-based rpg players. For all others it will come off as a grueling dungeon crawl slug. I love a good grind but this game made me rethink that.Levels/Worlds: Very nice designs, just wish they were a bit shorter. After a point everything looks the same and there isn't any events to liven up the rest of the crawl.Characters: Ringo is obviously the strongest character, and it is nice to finally have a main character with their own personality. That being said at some points she's just too good? Too strong? It is clear they put all of their focus into the main character as the side characters are nothing but their tropes. Your side members exist just so you have the 4 party scheme of persona. Honestly you could go a more mainline SMT approach and that would take the bland characters out of the spotlight. Figue was my second favorite but the story reduces her to the sidelines for no reason other than a spoiler reason at the end of the game with very little pay off. ♥♥♥♥ the bird, easy to spot a cash grab mascot and this is the most bland attempt yet. It is just a drone for Figue and is tied to a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ mechanic.Voices: Being unable to turn off the notifications of enemy awareness is too taxing. I get the use, just let me turn it off. I played the game on mute after a point just to avoid it. YOU HAVE BEEN SPOTTED, YOU HAVE LOST SIGHT OF THE---, YOU HAVE BEEN SPOTTED. I played with the english dub voice acting and I'm sorry for them that they had to voice this game but at least they tried.Graphics: I thought this was the area the game would struggle in but this is where the game performs. Everything is visually appealing and smooth, I think the cell shading helps but I could see where someone who hates anime style with a passion would get tired. Atmosphere: The game really hits the bright neon notes and a striking visual backdrop, but after a while things start to look the same. I wish there were areas that weren't as future or fantasy to show just how much things have advanced but every square inch screams "FUTURE FUTURE FUTURE"Story: Interesting to a point. They really push the "technology has exceeded further than humans know what to do with and no new inventions will ever exist again" and then it just pretends we didn't discuss that for over half the game. For a society that has peaked, we don't see anything new from our world that could exist. It is a modern day world with a futuristic coat of pain and cyberpunk just ain't my thing.Grind: Too much without DLC, Too easy with DLC. I like a good grind but other than the numbers going up the battle abilities are story progression locked and you only get a certain amount. Hope for 30 hours you were planning ahead! Which is another thing, imagine if this game was over 30 hours long and you still had to grind just as much. Makes me shutter. If only they spaced it out to a 100 hour RPG with better pacing.DLC: Absolutely required. Can't beat the game without it. Shameless cash grab.

_childDocuments_.review: Soul Hackers 2 feels rushed under-cooked in almost every regard. The story is stretched paper thin, and the game time is padded to death due to difficulty spikes and ridiculously expensive upgrades that force grinding. The dungeons are vast hallways of emptiness, and what little unique designs exist are reused immediately.The combat system seemed interesting on the surface but it's incredibly shallow. You start with no ability to swap demons in battle and each demon can only use 3 moves. Eventually  you can be upgraded to allow swapping and up to 6 demon moves. You also end up with passive perks that end up funneling your party members into specific elements. Some of the passives can be used to fight more creatively, but its still not much. Saizo can be upgraded to have a chance of stunning enemies when he uses gun attacks. Ringo can have a chance of going twice. Milady can unlock a 0 sp almighty move that can restore sp. It's really not much.The most unique battle mechanic is the "sabbath" end of turn attack. You increase its power by hitting enemies weaknesses and then at the end of the turn it unleashes. But that's it. You have one unique mechanic at the cost of much better battle systems.There are 3 dungeons in the Axis that are all the same boring padded dungeons5 dungeons in the real world and 3 of them are slightly altered versions of the others.The dungeons themselves are shockingly empty. The only thing you MIGHT see is your demons sitting around offering items or negotiations for other demons to join you. The game is pure grind. Grind to level up because every stat point matters. Grind to get money because EVERY upgrade is outrageously expensive.Probably my biggest problem with the game is the disappointing story. I can't explain it all without spoiling it. It started off fine and had one good small twist but then it keeps going and gets really dumb. The jrpg genre is typically known for its really good stories so I don't know who dropped the ball here.I do not recommend this game unless it's on sale and you're out of other rpgs to play.

_childDocuments_.review: Way overpriced. The story is clichéd. Dungeons rely on multiple back and forth travelling to get "keys" or events to unlock inorder to proceed to the next floor. Characters' backstories feel lacklustre even though there are lot of "hangout events". True ending requires a specific condition to be met, for which players need to plan way ahead, or try again in subsequent playthroughs. Combat system is a little different compared to Persona series - you do not get additional turns if when you hit the enemy's weakness. Instead there is a "stack mechanism" which adds on for a cumulative attack at the end of the party's turn. This can be further upgraded or modified with different perks that you can unlock.There is a system called "soul matrix" which acts like a dungeon to train and upgarde your characters, but the high number of puzzles takes the fun out of it and makes it only a mind numbing grind-fest.In short, there are different mechanisms compared to Persona series (obviously) but they feel designed to deliver quantity rather than quality. I would recommen buying this at 50-60% discount.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: I don't think the game deserve its price tag and day one DLC which is quite minimal content, dungeons are uninteresting after some time, in game currency could've been managed better especially the devil summoning prices which are ridiculously expensive, bosses fight are not as fun because they give you one shot mechanic which pretty much force you to learn 'Sabbath' but then again after fusing demons, you pretty much want to avoid summoning them due to its price making it significantly difficult to have optimal devil lineupsI wish I can stay neutral in my review, I want to recommend this game but there are a lot of flaws that will keep people away, including myself. The gameplay itself was enjoyable at first, I was playing at hard mode for 20 hours or so but then I decided to go back to normal because how they treat some boss fight, especially some optional boss challenges. Some optional boss challenges have mechanics where they will one shot you after X turns, which is extremely frustrating if you face them under levelled. Pretty much every boss, you will need at least 1 heal bots and sometimes they get rid of 1 character on optional bosses, I find it almost impossible to beat boss on first try (unless you are over levelled) which is usually what I've always aim to do when playing Persona.Another incredibly frustrating things are economy in this game, I've been going through dungeons facing almost every single one enemy that I encountered and I only have barely enough for one or two accessories and upgrades leaving none to summon devils. On top of that, the price for summoning devils are ridiculous reaching up to 300k at level 20-ish, the more you levelled them up, the more severe the price hike gets. You can either choose to get a couple of weapon upgrades or one devil summon, I would always choose to upgrade my weapon because devil always ends up getting fused anyway.Dungeons are also very uninspiring, it's closer to what we had in Persona 3 and Persona 4 where dungeons are pretty much almost the same and I think we can also compare it to Mementors in Persona 5. _childDocuments_.review: Despite mixed reviews, I'm loving this game. It's just a really nice time. I can see where the negative comments are coming from, but for some reason or other, the lack of polish doesn't really bother me. I also bought it for 65% off with all the DLC, which I'd recommend.Soul Hackers 2 is in a weird place in between Persona 5 and SMT5, and having played and disliked both of those games, I find that Soul Hackers 2 gives me (personally) the exactly correct amount of character driven narrative to keep me moving forward, without getting itself in my way. The battle system is straightforward but the gameplay feels rewarding. It's less deep than both P5 and SMT5, at least it has been for the 30-ish hours I've played of it, but it feels nice to interact with the systems. The environments are repetitive and there is a lack of enemy variety, but I just kind of don't care? The game works for me.The thing that really makes me come back to it though, as opposed to Persona 5, is that when I boot up this game, I actually _play_ it. I get into combat, I explore areas, I fuse demons, I complete side quests. For the 30-ish hours I've played it, I actively played at least some 27h of those. Meanwhile, 30-ish hours into Persona 5 and I wasn't even halfway through the second dungeon and I'm pretty sure at least 20 of those hours were spent reading very well written teenagers being freaking annoying and stupid. I'm sure there is an audience for that, but that ain't me. Meanwhile, Ringo has been on Earth for 1 day and has already resorted to heavy drinking to cope with the amount of crap she has to deal with... and that might the most relatable bit of characterization I've ever seen in any Shin Megami Tensei game.Soul Hackers 2 also lets me actually listen to Last Surprise, which, bewilderingly, Persona 5 Royal refuses to.

_childDocuments_.review: Soul hackers 2 is just short of a masterpiece. I am an atlus shill, and I'll play anything they make, but I am not afraid to be critical of even their best games, but to be honest I have more complaints about persona 5 than this game. Let me start my praises with the fact that this is NOT a persona game. I'm so happy to see an actual devil summoner game in 2022, something I did not expect to see at the beginning of the year. I wouldn't have named it soul hackers, because it kinda limits the scope of the series moving forward to the cyber punk aesthetic but I'm not complaining. I excited for this new direction of the series, and I welcome a third flagship franchise in atlus' catalogue. I cannot praise the cast enough. I am elated that we get to play as ADULTS again, I am honestly so sick of the school setting that persona and smt keep using. I like the mature characters and themes this game brings to the table. The school theme does not make the other games not great (because they are) I just love the variety and change of pace from what we have been getting. Ringo is also a standout. I love that she has a cannon name. I love that she SPEAKS! I'm glad she has actual personality. The one thing I hate that atlus does is thr whole silent protagonist. I play jrpgs for the story and characters, not side characters doing info dumps and telling me what to do. Ringo takes charge, and brings more to soul hackers 2 than any atlus protagonist in a very long time.The story is actually very good, way better than I thought it was going to be. As previously stated the cast is great and they carry this game.  The plot stays interesting, and dosent overstay it's welcome. You aren't beat to death with never ending walls of text. The game gets to the point, says what it needs to and moves on. Not too much not to little, the story and pacing is just right.Gameplay is solid. They basically took everything good from tokyo mirage sessions and made it better. It's not as deep and interesting as smt v, but it's perfectly fine. It does what it needs to do and stays fun from beginning to end. I like how demons are used as equipment, it's honestly a great way to differentiate itself from the other games in its family. Sabbaths are just cool. A gang of 10 or more op demons swarming a boss is a sight to behold. Dlc sucks, I know. But I would rather get it day 1 while I'm playing it rather than 6 months later while I'm playing a different game. In an age where people drop 100s of dollars into forknife skins and gotcha gambling I don't see the issue of paying an extra 20$ for a game I'm going to drop 100 hours into. This is the game industry's problem not just atlus. If you don't like it just don't buy it. Like the costumes and the lost numbers. I don't like them and I wish I didn't buy them. Buy the game and the demons, maybe the grind easing dlc, but the costumes are worthless and the lost numbers isn't fun. Go read my individual reviews of those if you want more context. Take my word for it and just Skip em, youre welcome.I hope this game does well, because it's great and I want more like this from atlus. I'm an atlus faithful and it's games like this that keep me coming back day one no matter what. There's always a few bumps here and there, but I spend 95% of the time playing these legendary games with a smile on my face and sweat in my palms. If you love any other atlus game, jrpg, anime or adventure game check this one out. It's great for old head fans and newbies all the same.
