_childDocuments_.review: I was originally going to finish this game, but... ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ I just can't. The gameplay is so painfully unrewarding that I just couldn't stomach it anymore. It's a pretty standard SMT dungeon crawling turn-based battle kind of affair, but everything just feels slightly off, and it's very clear during the first battle. The animations are abysmal. Nothing has any impact, and nothing shows that off more than executing a regular attack against an enemy, at which point it becomes clear: these aren't two character hitting each other. These are two character models moving near each other. "Lack of impact" might not sound like much, but, after ten hours, it starts to feel very dull and bland. Magic attacks and skills feel the same, too. Unrewarding, unsatisfying, dull... They feel like special effects playing over a character model, rather than anything having an effect on an enemy itself. This might have been fine in the PS2 era, but this game was made in 2022. This does not fly.As for the story: it seems interesting. I actually like the characters, and the character designs, although I understand that most people... don't... And I guess I can understand that. Everything is very contemporary, and you might have heard people complain about the protagonist telling someone to "take the L" at some point. The protagonist is annoying, and has the personality of a perpetually unimpressed highschool girl. The rest of the cast is fine, except for Arrow who is bland as hell, but the main character, Ringo, is very grating.Speaking of grating, here's something I noticed. Nobody ever shuts. The ♥♥♥♥. Up. They talk when you buy things, when you change accessories, when you swap demons, when you swap outfits, when it's their turn, when you select an enemy, a skill, a target, a menu option in battle. When you select an enemy, they'll say something along the lines of "You gonna hit that one?", and they do this when you cycle to another target. Every. Single. Time. If you hold down left or right, you get treated to "You gonna hi- go for i- hit 'em h- that's risk- you gonna- go- hit- go for-", and it never stops. These people never shut the ♥♥♥♥ up, ever. They need to comment on everything. ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, just stop commenting on something for five minutes! I can't change equipment without Ringo making a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ quip, just let me ♥♥♥♥ with my inventory in peace!I might as well mention the DLC too, since it's the source of some controversy. First of all, I believe there are some outfits locked behind DLC. Persona game outfits, Raidou, Nemissa's outfit from SH1, and such. Also, changing outfits changes the main battle theme, which is pretty neat. Putting on the Persona 5 outfit has the P5 battle theme play, Nemissa's outfit has the original SH battle theme play, and so on. It's a neat addition. What is not a neat addition, however, as many people have pointed out already, is locking fan favourite demons behind paid DLC. Satan, Mara, Zaou-Gongen, Masakado, and several more, are all locked behind the "Bonus Demon Pack". ♥♥♥♥. That. That is so immensely insulting to your fanbase. I can understand maybe Nemissa being locked behind DLC, since she's essentially there as a cameo, but locking fan favourite fusions behind a paywall is garbage. How about you fuse my middle finger up your ass.I want to end by saying something good about the game. The music is good. Very good. It's good enough that it's what made me give this game a chance after listening to the soundtrack. It's a mix of traditional orchestral music, metal, dubstep, synthwave, and... some kind of weird chanting which I haven't been able to nail down the name of. I like it, though. The music is easily the best part of the game. If you're interested, the soundtrack is on YouTube and Spotify. I recommend checking out the opening theme: Hopeless Call, as well as the tracks: Into the Abyss, Soul Hack, Booting Up, and pretty much every battle theme, to give you an idea of what it's like.And that's Soul Hackers 2. Soundtrack's incredible. The game itself should take the L, as the protagonist would say, apparently.

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked PS2 era / pre PS2 era SMT games, its worth giving a shot. If you never did (and only have played Persona), hard to say if you will like this. That being said, as a somewhat big fan of mainline & spin off SMT games, was pretty disappointing overall. It does a lot of things, but doesn't do anything super well. At times, Soul Hackers 2 tries to be Persona a lot of I don't think it was executed very well. I have nothing against Persona but either go all the way or don't at all. Overall, it honestly feels like a 3DS era budgeted JRPG but for HD consoles & PC. Its not necessarily a bad thing, but it just feels empty because of it.I wish there was a neutral recommendation because thats where I would fall. I did not love this game nor hate it. I guess one positive note is that the sabbath & commander skill systems were very interesting. It actually led to some more interesting fights that way compared to what SMT usually is. A couple fights in particular were pretty difficult on hard. Final boss was extremely challenging on hard for me.The PC port was great, no issues. Kudos to Sega & Atlus on that. Big step up from the Nocturne Remaster. Soul Hackers 2 can run on Steam Deck for at least me. I did 800p medium settings, it hovered around 50-60 FPS. The latest stable build as of today won't let you get past animations at the start. I switched to an experimental build and it all started working. But a lot of the effects and animations were not being rendered.

_childDocuments_.review: I dunno whether to recommend this game or not! I have a love/hate relationship with this game.I personally really adore Ringo as a character (She's a fully written, full voiced character which is awesome and hopefully ATLUS does this with future protagonists) and I really like Saizo, Milady, and Arrow too. I like the soundtrack with the opening theme being my favorite song from this game and it's cool that Keiichi Okabe composed the soundtrack. I found the world itself to be interesting, but not as much as the original Soul Hackers' world. I like how this game has a full adult cast and I super enjoyed their many interactions between one another! These characters are not friends and it took until almost the end of the game for your group in-game to truly "be friends" or at least get along well, and I know throughout the game they'll sometimes have a nice chat but a lot of the times when they're together they will have arguments of some kind (Arrow and Milady are a big example of this) and this is because they these four characters have no choice but to stick together and stay as a team to get through this even though they don't want to! They basically aren't friends and are forced to be together and overtime these characters develop more, and I honestly love all this about these characters. They're nothing like the usual characters who join you on your adventure in jrpg's and rpg's where everyone in your group is just super nice and wants to help you on your quest without question, with everything being hunky-dory. However, as for the things I do NOT like about this game: Let's start with the Soul Matrix. It feels pretty bland and uninteresting, the music is always the exact same which is a real shame. I don't like how no matter how deep the places goes the Soul Matrix always looks the exact same and it doesn't have any sort of variety to it. I also feel it drags on for far too long as what also doesn't help is the fact there's import story stuff tied to it and the player is required to completely explore the entirety of each Soul Matrix to unlock everything the Soul Matrix has to offer, including the story stuff. When I mentioned "Each Soul Matrix" I mean that there's three Sectors in the Soul Matrix. There's the Arrow Sector, Milady Sector, and the Saizo Sector, and each look and play the exact same but the only differences between them is that each sector has it'd own story stuff like cutscenes etc (for example, Saizo's Sector is focused on Saizo) and while I do love these three characters (ESPECIALLY Saizo) I honestly feel the Soul Matrix drags on for far too long and according to some players, the Soul Matrix became too much for them overtime and they didn't want to do them anymore which is a shame because of the story stuff that's locked behind the Soul Matrix is actually good important stuff for these characters from what I remember experiencing but I fully understand these players decision. I personally did not mind the Soul Matrix too much but yeah I honestly understand other people's  criticism. Another thing I don't like about this game are the many dungeons (and not to be confused with the Soul Matrix. that too is a dungeon but it's a single overly large dungeon with randomly generated layouts). These dungeons are more bearable than the Soul Matrix, HOWEVER these dungeons are very uninspired, uninteresting, and boring but sure you could say the dungeons of the original Soul Hackers were "not good" however I truly believe those dungeons had much more thought put into them plus all those dungeons in the original Soul Hacker's had great interactions within them, and I feel Soul Hackers 2 is absolutely brought down not only by it's dungeons but also how all interactions within those dungeons work. Something I should also mention about Soul Hackers 2's dungeons that I didn't enjoy is that it's dungeons lack puzzles or at least any good puzzles.Overall, I have a love/hate relationship for this game. There's things I wish had more thought put into (like the soul matrix, dungeons, and puzzles) and things that I believe are fine the way they are (like the main characters the player is with throughout this game, and the voice acting) and plus it's a good game in my opinion but there are things which hold it back from being great and the dungeons/soul matrix may turn away other people from playing this game, especially with how much talk there is about them online and to be honest the soul matrix is the worst part about this game for me.For me this game is a 6-7/10 rating for me, at least! It has pros and it has cons, and because a lot of the time spent in this game is through the Soul Matrix and the many Dungeons explored in-game, It's a hard sell in my opinion. I feel this game is the perfect example as to why fun and overall great dungeon design in any game is super important and that bad uninspired dungeon design/dungeons is not good for any game.Even though my review says "I recommended this game" it's a review that's both positive and negative.

_childDocuments_.review: Soul Hackers 2 is a really solid cyberpunk JRPG. Its greatest strength are its characters, all of whom are very likable and have had their own traumas that made them grow into who they are, and they very frequently have an air of moral ambiguity to them, even when you wouldn't initially expect it. The dialogue is hip and modern, and yet, unlike Persona, which is hard not to compare this against, more adult to fit in line with its characters all of which are adults.Combat is your standard turn-based fair, but instead of the typical bonus turn from older Megaten press turn titles, you get a bonus attack of varying power depending upon how many times you exploit the enemies weaknesses. I appreciate its long winding dungeons; in some ways they're reminiscient of the dungeon crawlers in the series early titles, which could be very mazelike. This game is no different, though admittedly it takes a while for the dungeons to become more complicated and interesting. Eventually you get teleport puzzles and other environmental puzzles, but early on a lot of the maps will be very samey. Once you get past that though it really gets going.The game is very pretty and its music is pretty solid too. Animations during cutscenes can sometimes be very good, a step up from older Megaten titles.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR:  Don't hate this game for its creative or gameplay decisions. Hate it for its technical failure. In other words: this is a fun game until it stops working. All I get upon starting the game now is eternal loading. Not recommended unless the issue gets fixed.THE FULL REVIEW (spoiler-free)  Most of you have probably already got your info on this game from Megaten youtubers, so here I will mainly touch on things they didn't, or on points I have a different view on.THE GOODStory & Characters  You play as Ringo and three other party members to prevent the apocalypse in a futuristic and apparently stagnant but comfortable society. The plot has three major twists which I found engaging enough to keep me wanting to play. Ringo has a positive and playful personality, and I would love to befriend her IRL. Opinions on the other three party members vary across the playerbase, so make your own mind up. However, they still come across more alive in general than P3's cast (SEES); you can feel both the camaraderie and animosity in SH2. As for Figue, she is wife material; that is a fact!Art Style The game has a captivating art style and fresh character designs (within Megaten at least) and it pulls it off well.  The colours pop out very nicely in the whole game without being garish, whether it's on a bright environment like the hub worlds or sabbath attacks, or  the subtle specks of colour in the light signals and yellow lines in the dark subway tunnels. The menus are stylish but not overly so. I like the helpful skill type and weakness/resistance icons. Too bad the text is so small, and you cannot enlarge it in the config at all.Music  Most tracks are just fine, but there are a few bangers. They are: Mansei Realm, Safehouse, Battle, Boss, Soul Matrix Boss, and the opening theme Hopeless Call. See also Soul Matrix section. Combat  The battles are easy in random encounters, but harder during the bosses from the mid-game onwards, and hardest during risky (mauve) enemies. The latter category is used to grind for high sums of XP and money. A good balance in difficulty overall. (I played on Normal all the way.)The main principle in SH2 is the stack and sabbath system. Strike an enemy's weakness to add one of your demons to the stack. Once all your party members have their turn, all demons from the stack you made do a free, all-out attack on the enemy. The more demons in the stack, the more damage you do. This applies only to you; the enemy does not do stacks on you. Another important change is that aliments are now a big deal, while are buffs and debuffs less so, so you should take ailment skills, vulnerabilities and resistances seriously when making your demons and constructing your party. Learn to exploit this to your advantage and you'll have such fun!  Shield spells (as well as buffs ad debuffs) work on all allies/enemies (so, you know: properly!) which is a definite plus. Critical hits, unfortunately, do not result in extra turns, unit later in the game as an optional, unlockable, in-game upgrade to your comp weapons. Overall the stack and Sabbaths make for a fun combat system. I like the build-up to each sabbath with the demon silhouettes and increasingly thick mist and colours. The sabbath attack animations are thrilling and satisfying to watch. I've only ever skipped them twice out of over 100 times.Soul Matrix  This is a semi-optional dungeon you must complete if you want to unlock more character abilities (summoner skills). Many players have complained that the Soul Matrix is the same visually and musically throughout, and while I absolutely see their point, it's not all bad. The music and atmosphere are very serene outside of battle, and I love to admire the shimmering effect on the floor or background blocks. I advise you to stop and smell the roses. Admittedly, the blocks and BG could at least have been differently coloured for each character, and maybe the hue could have changed the further you progress. Nevertheless, I'll still gladly take the Soul Matrix over Persona 3's Tartarus any day for the positives I've mentioned.Demon Personalities  Atlus have always tried to flesh out the demons' personalities through their dialogue in the Megaten games I am aware of, and SH2 builds on this trend. The demons in SH2 have text archetypes and voice archetypes to give you an idea of their personalities. Some of the voice archetypes which stood out to me are: the Valley Girl (Mermaid, Apsaras), the cocky and mischievous male (Gremlin, Andras, Cu Chulain), gay male (Mokoi, Mothman), caring older sister or governess (Silky, Valkyrie) and scumbag male (Pazuzu). They did interesting things with Mothman and Pazuz. Info on them below in their own sections.Unfortunately, these are for flavour only. The excellent demon loyalty mechanic from SH1 is gone. I'm not joking. Demon loyalty was fun in SH1 and half-arsed in the Raidou games.Mothman (minor spoilers)A certain mothman stalks you throughout the apartment block dungeon to drain your party's MP before absconding to leave you fighting his increasingly tougher possy (nothing you shouldn't be able to handle by then). Mothman may use the gay voice archetype, but you know that one gets ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. He is a real player. God bless you, Mothman! When you finally catch up to him, he has three of his fellows with him. Throughout the dungeon I kept thinking you would take him/them out in a boss battle similar to, but even more satisfying than, the cat in Eternal Punishment's TV studio dungeon, but no. They are destroyed for you in a cutscene. [sigh] Never mind.PazuzuAtlus has always been good at writing downright scummy characters when they intend to, and in SH2 this honour goes to Pazuzu. He is the objective in a semi-optional sidequest from Aion. His lines are voiced and let you know that although he is powerful and speaks in a refined manner, he is nothing more than a bully. If you have a shred of decency in you, you'll make it your obligation to take him out. Great job, writers. Another Pazuzu appears in the Ash boss fight and uses the poison mist mechanic which was fun.THE BADDemon negotiation  It is overly-simplified. It works, but it's better in Nocturne. Then again, did any Megaten veterans complain about buying demons in an auction in Devil Survivor?Text Size  The text is much too small, and there is no way to change it. We went from nice and clear in P4G, to OK in Nocturne, to unreadable unless you put your spine into shrimp mode for the unvoiced dialogue in SH2. Please rectify this ASAP,  Atlus. I'm sure it would be much easier than sending Mr. Tomigawa round to fix my back every time.The technical problem  All I get upon starting the game now is eternal loading. I can't even get the title screen anymore. And this was all of a sudden after playing the game some 135 hours. The solution someone suggested on the Steam forum did not work for me at all even after verifying all of my local files. I cannot even say to wait for a sale, because this may happen to you at any time. Whether you buy it cheap or dear, what good is a game you cannot keep playing?CONCLUSIONWhat a shame. Apart form the one bug which makes the game unplayable, the good definitely outweighs the bad as long as you can play the game in the first place.

_childDocuments_.review: I found Soul Hackers 2 to be decently fun. I've played Nocturne, Devil Survivor 1-2, P3-5, a little of P2, and a bit of Soul Hackers 1 at this point of time. The combat is less fun than all of the aforementioned titles with the exception of Soul Hackers 1, but it's still genuinely fun. I actually liked the bonus damage mechanic that came with exploiting weaknesses, but the press-turn system is still a bit more engaging to me.The characters are well made, with superb voice acting. The art design's really neat. The gameplay/combat was really entertaining to me. I also really liked the demon fusing mechanic. My biggest gripe with the combat would be that the ruin moves are borderline useless. The game also wasn't particularly hard, and I played through the entire game and DLC on hard. The dialogue in the game is pretty good if I do say so myself. The boss battles are presented in a really cool way, but they're pretty damn easy.The story's pretty decent. The story mostly kept my interest all of the ways through, but it wasn't particularly great or anything, just a nice, serviceable 6/10 story. The story really needed to be fleshed out more, because it feels like there should've been more time given to develop the villains. The end is a bit too dramatic like a typical, anime-styled JRPG plot. Still, it ain't bad.My biggest complaint with the game would be the dungeons, especially the Soul Matrix. The Soul Matrix has super bland, boring, copy paste looking areas with sometimes annoying/boring pathways. The Soul Matrix areas are just walkways with an endless space of nothingness that are too damn long. They also have teleporter areas, which are VERY annoying to traverse through. The rest of the dungeons in the game are just kind of meh looking, with mostly straightforward paths. The dungeons aren't the worst thing ever; they're just the pure definition of MEH. Oh, and the DLC are 100% not worth it. The DLC are highly expensive nonsense. The only DLC I think that's worth getting is the Lost Numbers one, but it sure as ♥♥♥♥ ain't worth $10. I'd pay MAYBE 5 bucks for it.All in all, I think the game is a pretty damn solid JRPG, with some minor negatives, and ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ rip off DLC. I give it a 7/10.I recommend getting the game on sale. If you like Megami games, then you'll like this, but it ain't anything special. Nonetheless, it's a fun time.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game, but I just couldn't in the end.The premise and start of the game was interesting. I enjoyed Ringo immensely and how she interacted with Milady, Arrow and Saizo. I loved the cute little lines the demons tell you when they're out on recon in the dungeons. All of the dumb filler lines were great. The soundtrack for the last dungeon slaps hard. There were many different types of hee-hos. I really loved Milady. The EN and JP voice acting was amazing. That's all I really have to say that's positive.Now the negatives is just a long laundry list of stuff that really disappointed me as a longtime SMT fan. For one, the story was just so lacklustre and short. It only felt like the game was long because there was just so much filler. Everything related to the narrative picked up at the last dungeon and I got myself worked up only to find that it was the end. They could've done so much more with some of the characters and their backstories, especially Arrow. Throughout my playthrough of the game, all I could think about the entire time was "wow, Ishikawa Kaito really was typecasted for Arrow" because he was just so bland even with all of those later-game background revelations. The last dungeon could've easily been the midpoint of the game, but it just wasn't and I felt like my hype was for nothing. I hated the Soul Matrix designs and found myself immensely frustrated trying to figure out the 4F/5F of everyone's matrices. I felt that the game was really grindy and annoying, even though I was playing on not Hard Mode. I'm not a huge fan of whatever Persona-esque battle system is used (I'm a press turn stan). Overall, the game just felt rushed. I felt like I got half of a game and that they could've done a lot more with it. I'm not sure if it's even worth playing. If you played the original Soul Hackers, I think you'd be disappointed with this.

_childDocuments_.review: Remember back in the 90's when Square was trying something different with every new Final Fantasy? Set classes in IV with rigid party structure, back to the freeform classes of the Onion Knights in V, magic decoupled from characters first in magicite, then materia in VI and VII? That was, for me, an exciting time. Who knows what Square will do next? (Oh, Junctions. Oh well, IX will do something different!)This feels like that for Atlus, who have a habit of most of their games, really since the 90's, feeling kinda samey. Shin Megami Tensei will be apocalytpic explorathons (since V nixed dungeons mostly), Persona will be social sim with decent dungeon and a fun, dumbed down version of SMT's press turn. Catherine will be...  weird. Etrian Odyssey will be boring (sorry, guys), Trauma Center will be impossible to play in docked mode, and 13 Sentinels will be... developed by Vanillaware and just distributed by Atlus. (but seriously, play 13 Sentinels, guys)Since the one-two punch of Persona 3 and SMT Nocturne brought us One-More! and Press Turn, Atlus combat has mostly looked like variations on those. Which is fine. They're great. And every time they deviate from that in ostensibly a game in those series (Strange Journey's Demon Co-Op, TMS's Encores, and now Soul Hackers' Sabbaths), there's an outcry.So I'm going to be that weirdo who says I like Sabbaths. I don't think they're better than Press Turn (SMTV still has my favorite moment-to-moment combat from an Atlus game), but it's nice to see something different in an interesting way. It's less braindead than Encore and feels more satisfying along the lines of Demon Co-Op, especially as things get more complex later in the game (once you get 10+stack Sabbaths things are typically more interesting). And the way systems are spread out, between Mystiques, weapon upgrades, Soul Matrices, and demons, there's enough fun interlocking stuff to keep things interesting, and I can definitely see new game + being worth doing.The story is simple, straightforward, almost basic at times, but I haven't yet been absolutely insulted by it. What it mostly allows is for character interactions, which is the real bread-and-butter of the storytelling here, and which keeps me interested in what's happening. Grabbing a drink at the bar, sharing a meal at the safehouse, or digging into their secret, repressed traumatic memories are all opportunities to get to know these cast members and really feel like a part of the group. Even your navigator, Figue, and incidental side characters like Raven have piqued my interest enough that I pay attention to new info about them. Having onging questlines involving the shopkeepers is also a great idea, as it gives these potentially throwaway NPC's some staying power as characters (think the collector manikin from Nocturne). The world has stuff going on. It's a cyberpunk world, so a lot of what goes on really sucks. And it's glorious.The real let-down for me is dungeon design. If you count the three soul matrices as a single dungeon, since they all share a tileset, and the two subway lines as two different dungeons... which also share a tileset, there hasn't been much variety in dungeon designs. I'm not done yet, but I feel about 2/3 of the way through, and repetitive dungeons have taken up much of that time. Once I'm IN combat, or out of the dungeon, things are great, but wandering the hallways is a drab, repetitive, boring experience made somewhat worse by the semi-random placement of scouting demons (which replace item chests, healing points, and also allow you to recruit demons).Overall, the game is very fun, and despite its flaws, I definitely recommend it. Unless you're a real diehard fan of the sort of bright cyberpunk that feels like it's trying way too hard to bury its dystopia (but trust me, it's there), it may be worth waiting for a sale, especially given the absolutely predatory practices regarding DLC, but I am glad I preordered the game proper, if nothing else to let Atlus know that yes, some of us are interested in PC releases of their products.

_childDocuments_.review: Decent story with likable characters and a good battle system. It doesn't do anything too interesting though and the terrible environments often made to just waste your time, dull side activities, and continued series obsession with never trying to make the demons their own interesting characters outside of their appearance keep it in the more average territory. The overpriced launch DLC that includes some more iconic demon summons and story content also doesn't help.The end of the world is predicted by the artificial intelligence Aion who normally maintains neutrality to the events effecting the world as they watch over humanity. In order to prevent the worlds ending Aion creates two agents from parts of itself and puts them inside human bodies. You control one of these two agents and early on in her mission she soul hacks three recently killed devil summoners to help her with her assignment with each of them having their own ties to the events and factions surrounding the coming apocalypse.Gameplay wise it changes up what has become the normal battle system by removing the system of gaining extra turns or losing turns based on attacks hitting character or demon element weaknesses or strengths or getting critical hits. This system has been replaced by the Sabbath system where hitting weaknesses adds stacks throughout your party's turn, at the end of your turn the main character will summon a number of demons that you currently hold based on the number of stacks that will do damage to all enemies. As you play the system is expanded a bit by having characters gain twice as many stacks when using their favored element or physical attack type to hit a weakness, commander skills can change how the system works slightly by focusing attacks on one enemy or making gaining stacks easier for a turn, and some demons gain Sabbath skills and when they are part of a stack they might activate an ability that can heal you, do more damage, put enemies to sleep, steal items, etc. Like pretty much everything the franchise does it comes with its own positive and negatives. It's nice to see a change and it makes things a bit less punishing for both you (and your enemy) if you are unsure of opponent weaknesses, and because you aren't directly punished for hitting enemies strong to an element it means that for the first time in a long time skills that hit random enemies aren't as potentially dangerous and the skills that hit all enemies aren't worthless due to demon skill number limits. There really isn't all that much strategy to the system or interesting ways your demons react to it though, and the system does tend to cause to put less focus into using support skills or certain attack enhancing skills once characters unlock their passives that will gain you bonus stacks for just attacking with their elements. Like past games, items are still better used for status effect healing and resistance instead of wasting your 4-6 skill slots for demons with abilities that heal or prevent them. There are still odd decisions like giving some of the most powerful demons in the game useless final skill like healing the party after a battle.Characters also have their own upgradeable weapons that offer a few passive skills and affinity levels with each type of attack, support, and healing and raising those levels allows you to equip items that can enhance your power with a certain element, give elements bonus effects, reduce their cost, etc. Demons that you have in your party are also sent out to explore the map, not giving anything like using their abilities to interact with the environment or characters like in the Devil Summoner Raidou Kuzunoha games, but if you run into them on the field they will give you important material, side quest items, money, introduce you to demons you can get to join you, and they say a few lines based on their type.There is a slightly Persona element to the game where you are paired with a party of four characters that are together for the entire game and that join together probably faster than I've seen a cast come together in any other RPG. You get conversation choices every now and then that increases your bond with the other three characters, as well as hangout events at an outdoor bar where you will have conversations with different combinations of party members. Raising your bond allows to push further into each characters soul matrix where you view and discuss some of their memories and unlock new character skills for them. You can also eat a variety of meals at your safehouse for minor passive bonuses that are further influenced by how much each character likes the meal, though this is a pretty minor part of the gameplay each meal type does come with its own conversation.The main things holding back the game is the either dull or terrible dungeon design and the focus on backtracking or going back to find demon's for upgrade parts. The maps are either bland, generic, and simple to get through or when you go into the soul matrix for characters they become even blander and start adding elements solely to waste your time like teleporters that take you to random areas until you guess the correct patterns. They did at least make looking for upgrade parts easier by allowing you to see a list of enemies that shows where they are located and what they drop, and giving you the option to mark them so enemy figures on the field have a mark over them if their party includes one of those demons. The demons themselves aren't given much focus as they have a very limited number of spoken lines when ran into on the field, there is no conversation system to recruit them, and they did not keep one of the only good features of Shin Megami Tensei V where certain demons have unique skills with more detailed animations.Not long after the release of the game an update added a button that speeds up battle animations if used in a fight and that allows you to dash (not so much dashing as making a variety of things go faster) in the field. If I had played the game before the in field dash option was added, I probably would have stopped playing, or at the very least just rushed through the main story not wasting my time with sidequests or loot drops. Atlus has also done what has now become commonplace with the series and created massively overpriced DLC that should be free that includes certain series iconic demons to summon, multiple more story based side missions that are tied together for a new character, and the usual things to make the grind more bearable like summoner and demon level up items and high priced sellable items. If you are wanting to mess around creating new or all of the demons and getting upgrades, it's a massive waste of time to acquire that much money through normal means.Screenshots:

_childDocuments_.review: You're probably going to regret buying this at full price. I enjoyed the game, quite a bit, and I still regret buying it at full price. It starts off somewhat rocky, but after it lets you off the leash, the game becomes really fun. And then after a while, it just becomes disappointing. Although I have to admit, I was disappointed right at the get-go.If you were expecting a sequel to Soul Hackers 1, from the words 'Soul Hackers' and the number 2 in the title, then you'll be disappointed. This game owes more to persona 5 than any game in the devil summoner series. Whats the difference you might ask? Devil summoner games are usually first person dungeon crawlers where the player starts out weak and then evolve into a gun toting, sword swinging, demon summoning badass. Soul Hackers 2, meanwhile, is a 3rd person dungeon crawler where you fight demons as a party of 4 unique characters who deepen their friendship over the course of the story. Sound familiar? But that was only the start of my disappointments.The artstyle of the game is really good. Very pretty, good character designs, the works. The thing about it, though, and it might take you a while to realise this, when it comes to graphics, the game is pretty ♥♥♥♥. The environment looks pretty dated, character models don't emote very much, and they recycle almost all of the attack effects. Animation is pretty weak in general in this game, the most notable example being Ringo's walk cycle. It's rather stiff and somewhat awkward, and since she's the main character, this is probably going to end up bothering you a lot.Voice acting is pretty alright overall. The 4 leads have pretty decent voice acting, but Ringo's voice acting is just a bit off. Most of the time it'll be fine, but there's certain times where the quality dips. And again, since she's the main character, this is going to end up bothering you a lot. Music is alright too, not really any notable tracks.The gameplay is normal SMT fare, with the notable absence of light and dark instant kill spells. That means that random mobs won't randomly one-shot you, which is nice, I guess, and that's about it as far as gameplay differences go. Dark spells are debuffs, and they also do damage and exploit weaknesses so it's not bad. Building up the 4 characters is also pretty engaging, because the materials you need to upgrade them aren't always found in the same dungeon, so you'll upgrade different affinities at different times. You'll never really need to farm if you keep up with axis unlocks. The axis is the main side dungeon, basically, and you clear it out for some pretty nice character buffs. The issue with the axis, though, is that you'll be going there a lot, the scenery never changes, and it's used to pad out the rest of the game. The main issue with Soul Hackers 2 is that it's really not a long game, but it makes itself feel like it's much longer. I have just finished the game with 60 hours, 50% of which was spent in the axis, 25% I spent on loading screens, and probably 25% I spent in the actual story and story dungeons. There's just not a lot of content, and around the halfway mark, you'll notice things repeating themselves. As for the story itself, it's alright. There's a really actually quite solid (if somewhat cliche) twist in the lategame, sandwiched between 1 ok twist and another twist that's pretty poorly built up. The characters are alright and they get more fleshed out over the course of the plot, though they start off pretty one-dimensional. I'd give the story a passing grade, for whatever it's worth, considering you won't interact with it much. Though I should note that I almost didn't bother finishing the game because it was just so samey by the end dungeon, but I figured I might as well have just bitten the bullet.Overall, this is kind of a disappointing game for something that has the balls to say that it's full price. If you really want to play something like this you might as well just play Persona 4 Golden, which has more content AND a better story, and it's only about a 3rd of what Soul Hackers 2 is selling for. If you really, really, really want to play this, I'd wait for a sale. This isn't really a must-play game, especially considering P5R is coming out on PC in october.

_childDocuments_.review: I beat this game today so i'll review it before getting all the achievements and then come back and see if i made any errors.story:This is a very good generic RPG ("generic" doesn't mean "bad"). though, it felt more like "Soul Hackers 2 (part 1)" than "Soul Hackers 2". this game feels more like it only introduces and develops said introduced characters, and doesn't leave much outside of it. typical Atlus... can't do a game unless it's over 80 hours long full of meaningless fluff.the story at the last dungeon was ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ AWFUL. some "dude" influences "good girl" and "good girl" becomes "eeevil girl"... AND THE STORY EVEN ACKNOWLEDGED THAT AT THE ENDING!!gameplay:meh... it's an "SMT type" turn based game. though, i would be lying if i said i wasn't overjoyed to bypass this weakness shmeakness ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ with MEGIDOLAON!! when i finally got it. and the sabbath thing was also cool. shame i didn't get to use Ringo's command skills more often until the final boss. her command skills are basically your way of being a "boss character" in this game. seriously, free defense buff, and a turn extension? that's cool as hell! really sucks that you can't dismiss party members. they are stuck to you like glue (i mean, it fits story-wise, but come on...). also soul matrix sections were fine. people ♥♥♥♥♥ about it too much, floor 4 however... whomever designed these floors with the red teleporters? i wish you a very bad day.characters:Ringo is a sweetheart and i love her. she seems like a sass master, and she is sometimes, but the writers gave her serious moments here and there so she won't be the same static piece of ♥♥♥♥ you see in every RPG nowadays...thank goodness Arrow isn't the protagonist. he even got genshin's Aether VA and that generic look that somehow becomes chosen and yaddi yadda.milady is great. she spouts lots of empty threats most of the time due to having a nice twist of being a character from the opposing side, but i loved seeing her warm up to the crew despite her "circumstances"...Saizo is amazing. he is not important to the "main" story, but he was heavily affected by the "main" story, and that's great. he is the typical "jokester", or "funny man" you see in a lot of games, but the writers didn't overdo his shtick, so he managed to feel unique and expressive while still retaining his "jokester" persona.Ash should've been playable. that's all i'll say. gameplay lore be damned. very glad she got a happy ending.and Figue sucks, but it's the writers' fault for remembering she exists when the game is almost over.music i liked:COMP smith music and Cirque du Goumaden music.cool how the best music is found in the places you'd be spending most of your (non-combat) time in.TLDR: if you're looking for a generic turn-based RPG, be like me and buy this game at a 50% discount or lower. this game is NOT worth it's retail price.

_childDocuments_.review: Having finished Soul Hackers 2, I want to say I have mixed feelings on the game.To begin, It's clearly taking influence from SMT games while mixing in elements of Persona (Sabbath's being similar to All Out Attacks from Persona 5,  hang out events, etc.) but never fully commits to going the extra mile to make those features truly fulfilling imo. I think the strongest aspect of SH2 is the story and characters whilst the gameplay is a bit slow it also picks up towards the end when you have all your upgrades. The problem is some of the design choices that were made towards this game which felt like a massive slog for most parts of the game. For example, Ringo (The main character) does not have a designated run button but rather she just kinda lightly jogs around the field and that feels like a slog to me personally. (You get an ability to speed it up but if it's an ability which can only be unlocked by doing an optional dungeon). I think the other disappointing aspect is the level design as everything is flat and not very creative. There isn't much variety and when there is some change it all comes towards the end of the game and kind of is short in general. The lack of complexity for the dungeons kind of makes everything feel bogged down and there were times I felt really bored in the 50 hours I played. But I kinda dragged through it because the story and characters were really charismatic imo.So even with these caveats I'm giving it a recommend? Yes, because I had an evidently good time with it but at full price of $80 CAD I don't know if it's actually worth the full price of admission (Kinda wish Steam had a sideways thumbs in this case) but if you're looking for a solid JRPG when this does go down in price, keeping in mind with the downsides, I think it's a pretty good game.TL:DR Decent JRPG with a strong story and characters but falters with weird design choices that went towards the game. Recommend getting on a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: (Have not finished the game yet at time of writing)Soul Hackers 2 is a decent in-between of Persona 5 and Shin Megami Tensei 5. While the game tries to has social sim aspects similar to Persona 5 they are quite watered down and not as varied. And while the game is more strategic than Person 5 it doesn't quite hit the same customization and tough combat as Shin Megami Tensei 5.While it doesn't quite hit the sweet spot you might want straddling between the other latest Shin Megami line of games it gets about 80% of the way there. The combat is good, though not as many tough battles as I'd like. The story so far isn't anything amazing, but the characters are all fleshed out enough that they can carry it. The biggest issue is probably that the dungeons are uninspired and traversing them is a bit of a bore. If you enjoy the other Shin Megami series games then you'll probably find something to enjoy about this one.

_childDocuments_.review: This is not my ideal SMT game, but it is better than most of the series' historical titles.The music is great.  Normally I don't like voiced protagonists in RPGs, because my enjoyment of the game as a whole is marred by what the protagonist says.  I actively want Geralt, Eloi and Tiny Tina to die horribly in a hurricane with sharks,tigers and a nuclear bomb thrown in for good measure.  Ringo is enjoyable -- but I would still prefer silence. But I prefer gameplay over story, so take my opinion for what it's worth.As SMT titles go, the battle system here is "meh".  Not the best, but not overly tedious.  I miss the press turn system and feel like this system is a downgrade.  But it generally avoids the kinds of problems that could make Nocturne "the opposite of fun", where you have to spend 30 minutes incrementally grinding away at the health of a boss only to find out you lost the race and have to start over.What is an improvement over many of the titles is that you can swap out any of the main characters' demons both out of battle and during.  That opens up a lot of options for dealing with difficult situations.Overall, I'd give it a 7.5.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played Persona but not SMT, so my perspective comes from there. I've also never heard of Soul Hackers 1.Pros:- Genuine protagonist. Ringgo is great, especially when compared to Joker. Everything else in that world has so much personality it always felt weird the protag didn't. As I say, Ringgo is good fun.- Simplified mechanics. This isn't a Persona or SMT game and it didn't seem to be trying to be. It's essentially a new IP and an introduction into the way Atlus do things. It works really well with that mindset. It's also far less of a time investment than Persona.- The stuff Atlus usually nails. The world, shops, people. Yeah, they nail them as usual.- Persona 4-esque dungeons. I didn't really get on with the palaces and liked the re-grindable dungeons from 4. This is closer to that but without the demon of procedural generation. Being able to chill out and fight demons is nice.Cons:- Hardcore fans might be turned off by the simplified mechanics. The Persona/Demon fusing is barebones in particular.- Simplified soundtrack. The battle and dungeon track are both good, but I didn't miss an 'S' there. You get a song for every battle and a song for the dungeon, that repeat. - Default camera controls are DREADFUL. Change 'em.I enjoyed it in the same way I enjoyed Scarlet Nexus, but there are two sides to that coin. I recommend trying it if you want to try the Persona/SMT mechanics but don't want to jump into the massive rabbit hole those IP's represent. Also, please create actual protags in future Persona games Atlus! You've shown us you can do it!

No cats telling you to go to bed when you actually just want to go so something. _childDocuments_.review: Gameplay: 4.5 StarsThe game has a 5-8 hours tutorial depending on skill level, however towards the end of it combat and the Soul Matrix/Level system is an amazing upgrade to the Confidant system from persona, Soul Hackers 2 uses the Sabbath system which is an interesting evolution to the Press and One More system of previous games, your team can equip demon's similar to personas in Persona 2 and at the start of the game you earn "Stack" by hitting weakness similar to Press or One More however at the end of your entire turn the Stacks turn into an All-Out Attack called "Sabbath" where you summon demons for each stack earned (Pendulum Summon style from yugioh), as you progress the Soul Matrix and leveling your teams Soul Levels you earn more ways to gain stacks eventually gaining the benefits of the previous Press and One More systems, this makes it so you have to earn the overpowered exploits of the systems prior to top it off on Hard and in mid game, Elite and Boss fights start to use these systems against you as well.Story: 4 StarsTaking a classic of AI predicted the end of man and putting a really good twist on it, SH2 takes place about a decade after Soul Hackers and the events caused by Spookies story. Though unrelated to the previous game the world very much is the same world though we don't really address alot of the politica in SH1 that was setup in the World, Basically an Almighty AI calculated the world would end if 2 specific people are killed, your mission is to prevent their deaths and save the world. You end up being too late and have to Soul Hack Arrow to bring him back to life and from their you go on a Steel Ball Run chase to collect the corpse parts.....I mean to collect the Covenants to prevent the Antagonist from collecting all 5 and using them to summon the Great One and end the world.Graphics: 3.5Very basic Anime JRPG graphics of the 2020s the game offers very little customization and the antialiasing is kind of poor. (I run a 3060 GeForce RTX, with a Ryzen 7 5800x and 64GB of Ram) while i get a real stable 144+ FPS without needing vsync the lack of additional options makes me feel less in control of how the game looks.Audio: 4OST is pretty good, if you got the DLC though the new soundtracks added are alright (kinda sad I can't blast Mass Destruction during battle) also if you get the DLC unless Persona 5 or P5R you get to select the BGM during battle in gameplay settings and don't have to rely on what outfit Ringo has equipped.DLC: 1The day 1 DLC that has everyone in a fritz is honestly utterly optional the only major concerning one is the  Number's Chaser which adds a Side Story for you to progress side by side with the main story and due to Atlus' habit of Royal/Gold/FES editions not including DLC you will more than likely have to rebuy this DLC when this gets the Rerelease (if they even rerelease it considering the backlash they are unnecessarily getting.) The biggest reason i'm ranking it so low is you can tell all of it is just content that was not complete at the game going gold deadline and they had this content almost done so they decided to finish it between the Going Gold time and Release time to give us Day 1 DLC. The reason i strongly believe this is 2 series signature Demons/Personas are in the day 1 DLC Satan and Mara, the 2 have been in every base game to my recollection of an SMT title (outside of Digital Devil Saga) to date.Updated notes: Game is Persona 5 levels of easy and it is surprising a short campaign based on where I'm getting bored, the mystery and conclusion just doesn't feel great. While I enjoy returning to a standard story and gameplay for SMT, this is definitely leaving much to be desired, would recommend getting on discount as a bundle.

Sure you get some OP bonus-abilities for your party but those could easily just have been unlocked at certain levels.And yes, the DLC packs are atrocious and overpriced. _childDocuments_.review: This is a fun RPG with a nice battle system. I don't think any of the mechanics are as deep as some of the other Atlus games, but that is isn't a bad thing. The game is streamlined but not hand-holding or infantilizing. The story is very character focused but the characters are actually quite charming. It's also nice that each dungeon gives you something to pay attention to story wise-- that keeps the pacing tight.  The combat is generally fairly smooth and while the dungeons themselves are surprisingly plain, these are probably (overall) also the least annoying dungeons in SMT (or offshoot) game in a while. The game does a good job at keeping you focused on the story and advancing while also allowing you to grind if you'd like. It is an easy time if you are looking for a traditional (character) story focused JRPG.

_childDocuments_.review: As no doubt most reviews by now mention, when you first launch the game go to config -> gameplay and change the loading screen prompt either to button display if you want recaps or to none. None will change your loading screen times from roughly 8 to 10 seconds down to near instantly.Additionally worth mentioning is that the lack of costumes outside of battles can be fixed very quickly and easily with  mod. Keep in mind there are clipping issues here and there, but that's on Atlus. Not the modder!Now on to the actual review.If you are used to the length of Persona games you will be disappointed. Soul Hackers 2 takes as long to beat as your average mainline game. The game has 2 endings and a NG+ mode. Keep in mind, all NG+ does is add a few tougher quests and is intended for those that don't want to save scum to see the second ending or play the game on a tougher difficulty again.My first playthrough has been on  and while I enjoy the difficulty spike, some of the game's features don't account for the difficulty. You will find yourself biting your teeth out on Risky Enemies (always 10 levels higher than you) and foes going into enraged mode during challenge fights due to turn limits that don't take the lack of damage or HP sponges into consideration.Instead of the press turn system you are used to you are greeted by a stack system that deals damage at the end of your turn instead of letting you go again when you hit a weakness and depending on Ringo's abilities as well that of your demons unlocks additional perks such as free healing or applying status effects on enemies. I for one welcome the change in the formula and enjoyed my time with the system and trying to find ways to make full use of it.The story follows a more mature theme and unlike the depressingly lack of depth SMT5 had, the writing is servicable once again with characters being fleshed out. Albeit predictable at times, you will build an emotional connection not only with your party members but foes and temporary guests alike.The biggest downfall and gripe you should have with the product being sold to you comes no doubt from the atrocious DLC policy. Opposed to the claims Atlus made (companies lying, what's new?) the story dlc starts as early as you getting access to fusions and a recommended level of 8. The chain continues through the entirety of the game and is not limited to post game content at all.Not only does the boss demon pack break the balance of the game being readily available in your compendium without Macca charge or level restriction attached, it cuts out prominent and popular demons you normally find in any SMT game as of late. Nemissa being a part of it felt almost as dirty as seeing a stable meme like Mara being a selling point.Costumes should have been useable outside of combat by default and having to rely on a mod to fix the laziness of the developers isn't something to be happy about either.All things considered, the base game is well worth it's money especially if you bought it from one of Atlus' trusted partners. The premium edition is vastly overpriced and while I don't entirely regret shilling out for the DLC it will leave a lingering taste of salt and regret over cut content in my mouth for a while. Whether or not you speak with your wallet and avoid the dlc is your choice.

Holding a record for the longest-running video game storyline, the TEKKEN series begins a new chapter as TEKKEN 8 continues the tragic saga of the Mishima and Kazama bloodlines , and their world-shaking father-and-son grudge matches starting from 6 months after the closure of the last match. The story of Jin Kazama's growth and determination marks a new chapter in the timeless saga . • THRILLING OVER-THE-TOP BATTLES EMBODYING AGGRESSIVENESS & DESTRUCTION The new battle system, Heat , dials up the aggressive nature of battles , while maintaining the play feel and tactics unique to the TEKKEN series. The intensity of battles is greatly enhanced by the destructable stages. Unleashing super move-like Rage Arts is sure to enthrall both players and spectators alike. All of these hard-hitting mechanics come together to make TEKKEN 8 the most exciting installment in the series to date! • ENJOY YOUR TEKKEN LIFE! In the new single-player mode Arcade Quest , craft your own unique avatar and embark on your new TEKKEN life. Battle your way through a variety of rivals across multiple arcades as the story unfolds, all while mastering the basics and practical skills in TEKKEN 8. Unlock a variety of customization items for characters and avatars as you progress. *In addition to this edition, Deluxe Edition and Ultimate Edition are also available. Please be careful not to purchase the same content twice.

_childDocuments_.review: Without a doubt the worst Tekken ever made.Tekken 8 is a 50/50 slot machine mash-fest where using basic, fundamental Tekken skills that have carried the series for almost 20 years is a waste of time. Everything that Tekken 7 did wrong, Tekken 8 amplifies it one-thousand times worse.- Monetisation of EVERYTHING. Paid battle pass with stock unreal-engine assets as rewards, paid DLC characters, paid outfits. The cash shop was put into the game after launch to avoid any negative reviews and has predatory pricing (single outfit is 400 coins but you can only buy 500 at a time etc.) You're bombarded with ad's on the title screen whenever the cash-shop is updated with new things.- "Content creators" hiding that they have contracts or agreements with Namco and blatantly shilling products on streams (Nike trainers, Chipotle etc) or trying to suppress criticism of the game. High level players who were outspokenly critical of the game at launch all mysteriously went silent at the same time. One of them was asked his opinion of the game on a podcast, but he said he couldn't give it because it would damage his relationship with Namco.- Basic character tools have been re-purposed to just skip the neutral game and suck you into a 50/50 guessing blender which leads to even more guessing when you get it wrong. You BLOCKED a TWELVE FRAME MID from Reina? Too bad because it's time to guess. You BLOCKED a HALF SCREEN MID from Jin? Too bad, better guess. I could go on but you get the point.- Scrubby comeback 1-button rage-arts that do 50% of your life and stick you in a 10 second cut-scene for daring to do a basic poke, thus killing all momentum at the end of a round.- Armour moves that absorb ALL highs and mids which makes them TOTALLY SAFE ON BLOCK. Punish a King player for making a mistake and put him at a disadvantage? Better hope he doesn't mash his armour move that will absorb every followup and put YOU into a 50/50 guessing situation for 35% of your life.- "Heat" system that causes constant robberies. Push one button to activate your heat mode and get a heat burst, an armoured mid that causes time to freeze and absorbs all highs and mids. Once in heat, push the same single button for your heat smash, a move that can do 33% of someones life-bar that requires no brainpower to place, but will stick the opponent into a 50/50 guessing situation if they block it anyway.- When in heat, certain moves such as half-screen mids become one-time-use combo-starters which also leave the opponent in a guessing situation if they block it. These are frequently on characters with dangerous lows, so you have to just guess correctly twice in a row even when you block.- The oki system is somehow EVEN WORSE than Tekken 7. Literally EVERYTHING hits you on the ground. You can't just relax on the floor after eating a combo and take a moment to think about getting up correctly, because there is no "correct way" to get up anymore. You have to tech-roll up into the 50/50 blender because if you stay down, you just eat everything, even for staying still.- Awful balance, some characters are just blatantly unfair to play against (Dragunov, Feng, Yoshi, Alisa, Jin, King, Nina etc.) 90% of the people you run into online are meta-slave sweats playing as if their life depended on getting a win by any means necessary- Moronic exploits that ruin the game experience, such as;1) Idiots faking their location to bait you into accepting games which turn out to be a laggy mess.2) Idiots faking wi-fi connections as wired to bait you into accepting games which turn out to be a laggy mess.3) If the opponent has a potato PC that doesn't run the game properly, it lags YOU.4) You can mash print-screen mid game to artificially lag the game on both ends and force people to drop combos or make mistakes.5) People blatantly using scripts and macros to cheat (auto-block lows, auto-throw break etc.)The game is complete and utter garbage, filled to the brim with trash "comeback" mechanics to help scrubs mash their way out of situations rather than actually learning to play the game.This isn't a serious fighting game, it's a casual party-brawler with a Tekken skin designed to make idiots think they're good at something. Avoid at all costs.

_childDocuments_.review: Tekken 8 is a fun and great game in which you can break the skulls of enemies on the ground a lot, you can also side step a lot compared to 2D fighters. The game is complex and the LAB(practice) required hours could cause you to worry :). I'm writing this review from the point of view of a casual gamer that has Tekken 8 as their first Tekken game and finished almost everything in it after 70-80 hours in offline/online(rank 11)- Great graphics, combat looks cool, feels cool and brutal. Tekken 8 is the best version of Tekken- Winning online makes your laugh out loud, very satisfying- Good music options with Jukebox, can change to any Tekken music- Good Campaign that lasts for 3-4 hours and has incredible cut scenes that are gorgeous especially in the last hour of the game- Surprisingly funny 32 Story Episodes. Can try out moves for each of the 32 chars in these. Can take up to 5-6 hours- Good Arcade Quest that invites you to learn the basics of Tekken 8 while advancing a campaign through some social arcade places/stores/bars. Can take up to 5-6 hours- Strong Roster of 32 characters with around 10 characters that are really bad ass like: Jin, Kazuya, Devil Jin, Jun, Reina, Zafina, Paul Phoenix, Law(Bruce Lee), Raven(Blade), Hworang, Bryan, Victor and Lee- Minimum of 30-40 hours of gameplay to a casual player and easily 100+ hours if you would like to explore more than 1-2 characters and push the online ranks- Combat looks very cool, feels very brutal with the more heavy hitting characters like Jin and its satisfying to pull out a win in a stressful situation especially online- Unique combat mechanics and combat style, no fireball wars but you get grab wars and juggle wars- Unique mechanics like attacking your enemy on the ground a lot, side stepping attacks, auto blocking and blocking on Standing posture as the standard opposed to 2D fighting games where you block low as the standard- Easy mode exists that will allow you to juggle/air combo enemies with ease and perform other more complicated attacks- NetCode for Online pvp is great most of the times, no issues seen.- Multiple Online pvp modes like Quick Play, Ranked, PvP arcades which are all very populated- Combat seems fair and responsive both for single player and especially where it matters more -> for online pvp- Great practice mode where you can see the moves executed and then you get to practice them- Great combo challenges- Great replay system for your online matches, you can save your favourite matches, get improvment tips when you watch them and can actually execute the received tip on the spot -> totally new system which will help people improve a lot- A lot of customisation options for people that are into that stuff- Steam achievements are easy to get to 100% in around 25-30 hours as all of them are just integrated into the first hours of the single player and online journeys you go into. I don't view the negatives of this game as something very heavy, some people could also consider then negatives positives. Like a hard learning curve could be a positive or negative, a lot of mechanics same story etc- The story of the game is a bit generic, the graphics and the fights/explosions are amazing and save the campaign but the story itself is 'Power of Love and Friendship wins'. Maybe drop all the serious and granny like advice this story has and just make it funny like the Story Episodes are.- The music is a bit uninspired like techno music that is not very hard or doesn't drop some sick beat or anything but you can actually load your own playlist into the game or just any other Tekken sound track from the Jukebox so this point is saved but its worth mentioning- Even tho the game was simplified, i feel it could be simplified even more to attract the casual gamers. There are over 100+ moves(+1 stance and its moves) for each character(can be overwhelming) which denotes depth and variation but the execution skill needed to perform some of the moves i feel is still too much for a casual gamer- Execution skill needed for combos is too high -> especially online when you are getting hammered. There is a case that a player should struggle a bit a progress but when the struggle is too great(the execution skill for moves/combos is too high) people will just quit the online play because you would need to stay so many hours in the lab/practice mode and its not fun anymore at that point.- High end ranked games require a lot of lab hours(practice hours) which kills the fun of the game. If the moves could be easier, the lab hours would be lower. The lab hours need to be reduced for high end ranked play to include more people.- Please make this version of Tekken or the next Tekken more keyboard friendly. Most keyboards cant take 3 inputs at once and some moves are just not possible where 3 inputs are needed I wanted to point out that the negatives are small in this game and you will be able to play your character without issues(60-70% of the moves are accessible), there is an easy mode available for the more complicated stuff but it will feel like cheating and you wont feel so cool using it/winning with it. In conclusion i can say i had a blast with this game, its a great game, especially online when you fight some close games and you win. This will give you a minimum of 30 hours(25 hours to fully clear the single player + 5 hours for the casual online pvp push) and 100+ hours over a few years or if you want to try out new characters, its totally worth the money.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has received a lot of negative reviews recently and yes I also wrote a negative review before while still playing it up to now for easily over a thousand hours. I have played the entire series from the start since the arcade days so yes I have no intentions of not playing this game anytime soon. It's been almost a year(but still not) since the game launched and we've all gone a long way since then. I decided to revise my review because I truly believe that the game has improved since launch. This improvement has not been seen ( or perhaps people refuse to see it ) because of all the vocal hate the game is getting.  Has it improved a lot? No. Can it improve more? Definitely. It's not perfect and there are still a lot of things to fix. But that being said, the game has definitely come a long way since the casino gameplay at launch and the terrible balance issues. That's still not to say that it can't and still needs to be improved. But the hate it is getting now is ridiculous. And the monetization issues? Well here it is. A lot of other games milk their customers for a lot more money with more blatantly unfair practices. The Genmaji stage people were ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ about? It doesnt have any gimmicks and isn't a tight stage. It's very wide so yes you don't need to fully understand the staget to be a master at the game. And all the paid customs and DLC Shop? Well let me just put it into perspective.I've been playing this game since Tekken 1 and even during the times it was in the arcades. Back then balance was worse than what happened here. We had to play a broken game for YEARS before anything was done to fix it and it was usually done in consoles not in the arcades. And to play mind you we had to spend real money PER GAME. I would end up spending literally thousands of pesos a day just to rank up. I would spend money not eat neglect relationships and get into real financial problems just to play the game. With that in mind I can't see how or why these people are complaining so much about cosmetics and a stage that doesnt really impact the game. They're not required purchases and yes the game needs money to keep going. They can't publish the game and maintain the servers if they dont try and generate income. Is this the perfect way to generate income? Probably not. But comparing it to the arcade days where I literally had to steal from my mother and grandmother to play and starve well, you wouldn't want to experience that now would you?I don't love Harada. I still think he has made mistakes but I can respect him and his team. I can see that they are actually trying to make this game work and have actually made good steps to do so. I hope the haters can pause and really, really just reflect and see if the game is truly horrible and a product of Satan. Take a moment to critically think first before putting something out online or giving in to a strong emotion like anger. Think for a moment and really observe and question the game. Is it really that bad? Is it a good game? If you take time to pause and think about these things you might be surprised. I know I was surprised in the end.

I can now play against people who are about a state away from me without having to worry about inconsistent internet connection. I also believe that this game gives a lot of opportunity to new players to try and catch up with the more experienced group of tekken players. Tekken 8, from my personal experience and playtesting, has had by far the most in depth and well configured training mode which allows for so much more information which lets me improve during matches. Secondly, there is a replay system in which you can try to see where you could have punished on key moves, allowing you to learn matchups a little more easily. Furthermore, you can fight players and their ghosts, which can help you see and pick up new habits from higher tier players. However, we need to look at the negatives of this game.This may have changed since I last played the game, but why has cheaters consistently been so rampant in this game? I genuinely thought they would take a hard ban approach to these cheaters and yet I still see them happily playing. This is the first issue that needs to be addressed right away.Second of all, as someone who has played quite a bit of Asuka, why was she so unecessarily nerfed to the ground? I've noticed that the balancing of this game seems to be so much more wild comparatively to tekken 7, then again, it might just be because I'm not that good at this game lol. But it still does feel frustrating when you learn a character, only to find out you got stomped on by someone who was just mashing 2 button and you have to lab out against specific characters. While this is pretty normal, I feel like tekkens balancing was way too unbalanced initially (but I have no idea now).But the thing that truly bothered me was the focus on taking down users who like to utilize customization mods or skins to help incentive their own "shop". So what I'm understanding from this is that people who actively cheat and ruin the experience for everyone else is not prioritized and are only demoted which would allow them to climb back up while cheating again. Secondly, the crackdown of these mods at least makes me assume that they don't prioritize making the game enjoyable for everyone, furthering this idea for me that this game will die the moment it stops printing money. I don't exactly find it helpful as well that everyone in the Tekken community exalts Harada (Tekken game developer) as some modern genius who can do no wrong. This unconditional support without major criticism in my eyes has fostered an environment where Harada will never truly hear out anyone's criticisms and try to shut them down. I can barely imagine a better future for tekken, but if it does happen, I am always willing to give this game another chance.

_childDocuments_.review: I normally don't write reviews for fighting games but I really didn't expect T8's story mode to go so f***ing Hard..  By the end credits I felt compelled to share my praise and thanks for a series that has carried 3D fighting games for 30 years.T8 really feels like a love letter to the series. The story features callbacks to characters and events all the way back in the 90s, it has a banging soundtrack (and free alternate tracks for every previous tekken game), and the animations/visuals are a massive upgrade without being overly distracting to the gameplay.One issue that a lot of players seem to have is the heat system - much like rage drive it's a system that can be easily abused by 'scrubby, mashing gameplay'. I personally have little issue with it. Newer players will depend on it more and more experienced players will learn to adapt around it, like every new system in fighting games.The other issue is the in-game shop/battlepass. Thus far, only one in-game currency is used, and while the items seem overpriced it's nowhere near as exploitative as SF and MK. Does that make this acceptable? No. That said it's something I think should be taken into account, as we don't have to buy the 'new' stages like SF6.The 'premium' battle pass items are weak but fortunately the entry fee is 600 tokens -which can be earned back through the rewards.The unfortunate part about 'Live Service' titles is that this area can change over time, so if monetization does get better/worse I will update this section.Overall, I'm very happy with the offline portion of T8, and while I'm put off by the monetization of the online portion I am still enjoying ranked matches and messing around with the jukebox while labbing new characters. This is easily my favorite fighting game series and I'm glad T8 got so much love out the gate - hoping it only gets better from here.----EDIT SEPT 30th ----Well, with the new update we got 8 new chapters in storymode and some nice QOL changes... but the new stage isn't included with the season pass? Not a nice precedent that's being set. I still think the game is overall worth a purchase, but what a disappointing turn of events.

_childDocuments_.review: The core gameplay loop is pretty good, but not 70$ + battle pass + paid cosmetics good. And even the combat has a few flaws.The singe player content is barely existent, nothing more than a glorified tutorial. The story is garbage but nobody plays this for the story.The netcode is relatively mediocre, vastly inferior to SF6. The optimization is also pretty bad. SF6 can run perfectly on my rig, but Tekken will lose frames at random during rage arts in certain stages, which compels the game to auto destroy your configured graphic settings even though the fighting itself is not affected by the frame loss.The problems with the gameplay loop are that the game is fundamentally a casino simulator. Everyone just does 50/50s into 50-70 damage over and over. That's about it. Every light tap leads into nearly half your hp. You need a PhD in every character to even have half a chance of dealing with this nonsense. I suppose that's wonderful if you want to flex at tourneys and get paid to play but this is not a fighter you can just play casually.What will really infuriate you are all the little inconveniences this game foists upon you. Loading screen after loading screen... want to play ranked? Re confirm the settings you've reconfirmed 300 times, select the same side you've selected 300 times, pick your char, pick a random npc char, pick a stage, load the stage, and then, finally, the game starts searching. Which in and of itself can get annoying as you can't autofilter out things like wi-fis or high % disconnects. Even the rounds themselves are full of cutscenes - watch 2 players activate heat, watch a 10 second cutscene on every rage art, sit there and watch 10 seconds of combos every combo.Marvel as prowess matchmaking sends you against monsters while you are learning a brand new character.Rejoice as you play with the same cheaters you reported weeks ago on the most obvious auto low block and auto grab breaks in history.These devs don't even know how to punish people who dc. You gain no points and they lose none... something every other fighter has figured out. These people have the audacity to charge you for this mediocrity.The state of the modern day fighting game industry is abysmal overall and it is very sad that SoulCal and DOA are dead and this is all we've got for 3d fighting. SF6 seems the vastly superior product. I would not recommend this game to the average player, only to a Tekken hardcore or someone who just needs a 3d fighter like a heroin addict. All that being said, the overall fighting itself is relatively fun, barring a few things. With some tweaks and patches the game could be really good but I'm not a fan of both heat and rage arts in every single round.
