_childDocuments_.review: 60-70€ for an alpha/beta test build made by a predatory company. All the "feedback/critique" you give the devs don't matter as they'll do the opposite instead or continue whatever BS they had planned in the first place. I only got ~30 hours on the game due to the unfun nature + MANY issues with the game (excluding local gameplay hours at a friends place, VS mode) but still so few hours despite the game being out for some time now (should speak volumes of it's state). Most "positive" reviews you see the game get are from people who played the game during the "hype" phase. Either that or they are used to Alpha tests :D Jokes aside, it honestly confuses and shocks me to see the game have so many positive reviews.Pros:+ Fun singleplayer story mode (for fans)+ Training mode with lots of options (punishment training, replay etc)Cons: - Limited and poor customization choices compared to previous games.Lots of skins, costumes etc have been removed so that they can sell you it instead. You can also not mix-and-match full-body outfits the way you want with other pieces.The menu is horrible as you have to go through 10 different button clicks and loading screens just to preview an accessory. - Predatory (Content locked behind Paywall etc)70€ price tag yet sells u DLC characters, has an in-game Shop with Microtransations and a Battlepass. The shop btw sells you mostly re-used skins/assets that used to be FREE in Tekken 7 and some older costumes from previous games. They also decided to take down modders since they provided these "skins" for free before the shop was implemented, how else would they sell you the same content? What's funny too is that modded skins are client-sided so it's not the exact same as an actual ingame skin that you get to show-off vs other players... oh well. Oh and some items sold in the shop even have limited uses (such as fireworks ~10 time use). Moving on. You CAN NOT practice / replay-train / punishment-practice vs DLC characters UNLESS you've purchased and own them (this has been a thing since Tekken 7, they never learned). There is NO 600 coins option in the shop to buy the batlepass, you need to buy 500 coins minimum (twice). SCUMMY PRACTICES!- Bad Online / Versus gameplay (optimization, network, player-experience etc).While VS somewhat works, Online however DOES NOT work 70% of the time. Each match is a gamble on whether you'll have a lag-free match or not regardless if it's wifi, wired or 4 to 5-bar connection between you and your opponent. When you do find one, they usually quit mid-match or do not bother rematching having you spend a lot of time in loading screens and playing half matches. Every few other match lags which is intentionally caused by players using steams inbuilt screenshot feature (F12) to lag-switch you or unintentionally cause due to the opponents bad hardware or network connection. Oh and there is no permanent re-match option in-case you do find a decent match.- No Anti-Cheat or Anti-Plug (match leaving) punishment/system for Ranked or Normal online matches. People can cheat, leave a Ranked/online match whenever they want or do anything they want without any punishment at all. INFACT you are the one that gets punished since they DO NOT lose points when leaving a match, instead you get a "loss" or winstreak loss and they get to keep their points. - Dumbed-down Gameplay (Heat mechanic, new/old moves, aggression-gameplay focus aka game direction etc).You'd think they'd surpass Tekken 7s gameplay with new "better" gameplay, yet instead we get something much worse. For each added good change or new good addition to the game comes 10 worse ones introduced. While they did fix a few issues from Tekken 7 such as Side-step (dodging) not working properly. They also added more issues to the game.They claim to want to promote new-player experience and make the game available to everyone no matter the skill, yet the way they approach it is wrong on every front. There is an easy-mode button layout option in the game that has limited options and lots of downsides however it's an option for newer players to use instead of playing traditionally aka the way you're meant to play. BUT for some reason it shows EVERYONE in the match that you are using it, making new players face even more disadvantages and "shame". FEW characters have shortcut inputs to some "hard" moves that deal less damage in return, to help new players execute hard inputs. YET for some reason only VERY FEW characters have this. They clearly didn't know which direction to go when it came to helping new players get into Tekken or fighting games in general, hence leaving you with a bunch of half-assed options. Good luck new players, at least there's training mode haha... NOW let's talk old mechanics and moves. They removed Counter-hit options on many characters (magic 4 etc), nerfed Low-parry damage and few other things, which is fine btw and reasonable. BUT... then for some reason, they decided to buff normal combo/wall damage, LIMIT other gameplay options, and add in two Instant-click 50 damage options to the game. For some reason they removed Rage-drives (combo extender/starter special move) while keeping Rage-arts (one click, 50 dmg special moves) in the game. Most moves have become safer on block (rage arts, heat moves etc) and Rage arts especially got buffed (less -frames on miss/block) which means that you now have less options and weaker ones available if you manage to block one and there's almost no risk to using one now. Hyper armor on top of it almost being a safe move on miss/block = unbalanced and stupid. It's even worse since Rage-drives are gone now, leaving rage-arts as the only option meaning you'll use it almost always.Most moves/grabs track even though they shouldn't even though there are actual tracking moves in the game. Other moves JAIL which leaves you blocking more than evading moves, and moves now do CHIP damage on top of that. This results in harder/less Side-stepping, despite buffs, and other evasive options not being an option most of the time. Blocking now losses you the game.They introduced a new gameplay mechanic called Heat while also focusing on a more aggressive gameplay YET forgot to balance defensive/evasive options and defensive gameplay. Every match is now button mashing at it's finest and one or two 50 dmg (1 click) button spam. Aggression takes over the game as MOST moves and abilities now leave you in +frames, meaning you get to continue pressuring and spamming your opponent with moves while they get to spectate the match as they slowly die.Heat also helps on this front by enhancing your character with stronger versions of their moves/stances with more +frames, more damage, chip etc. While in HEAT you always have a 50 dmg (1-click) button to keep them on their toes and steal the match leaving little to no counterplay or exciting gameplay. Entering heat mode using a heat-engager move also heals you if you connect it, which heals "grey/chipped" health.Because of each of these "changes/additions" the gameplay ends up becoming repetitive, stale, boring and easy (easy in a bad way) as less skill is required, less options are available and things turning out the same almost every match (no variety or exciting different matches). Activate heat, button mash with your super boosted moves while chipping your opponent, hit one or two 50 dmg moves with Heat or Rage art and repeat.Charactes don't matter as much as each one play similarly due to the "new" mechanics forcing aggression down your throat. Weaknesses and strengths of a character don't matter either as each match relies on the same tools, every character is technically a "rushdown" now. It doesn't matter if you are new or a veteran, the gameplay plays similarly for both.3D is the new 2D apparently. Thanks for reading and Cya in 10-20 patches, perhaps the game is fixed by then. One can dream... :(

_childDocuments_.review: I'd love nothing more than to write a glowing review of Tekken 8. There's so much to love in the game, with the only caveats at time of writing being things possible to iron out post launch, such as; performance, character balance, cheat detection / a working report system and somewhat lacklustre character customisation choice.Unfortunately the game is due to get a post-launch and post-review period cash shop through which they intend to sell legacy costumes amongst other items as micro transactions. These costumes are set to cost 4$ each, where an entire playable character fit with multiple unique costumes in the last game would cost 6$.In their post release roadmap livestream, the cash shop was prominently featured and in my opinion brazenly called a "New Feature". This "new feature" is set to have pride and place on the main menu in a spot you cannot remove and feature in the tekken lounge game world where you go to hang out with friends. It is now quite clear that this was planned to be the solution to the relatively sparse character customisation well before launch and timed to land after the review period and critical success of their full priced game.The game gameplay-wise is very fun and truly a high point in the franchise in my opinion. With that said however, if you are sensitive to these kinds of business practices, know that you can no longer trust the dev team to stand with you in that regard. There is no walking back from this once added and seemingly nothing to stop them adding even more egregious 'new features' in future.It unfortunately undermines lots of the trust I had in the developers to ensure the game stayed as a safe haven from this type of business practice, as the game was at launch and certainly doesn't keep me feeling safe from other types psychological manipulation tactics being added in future.As I and my friends continue to play and support the game together, the version of the game without the cash shop won't be something we'll be able to play or have access to unfortunately. I'll of course update this review if that changes or the development team walk backwards on their decision to implement the shop in the way they plan to once they've seen the discomfort it has caused.Hope this review helps someone and happy gaming. ♥--- Edit 07/04/2024 ---The month following the release of the cash shop; a time limited battle pass system was added. It follows the same system of needing to spend Tekken Coins to obtain as the cosmetics which can only be topped up in inaccurate amounts. The update also has come in with a bevy of incredibly dubious balancing changes which broke far more than it amended.The team it would seem does not have the time to fix their game while they are spending so much time packing in and testing new monetisation methods. It's a huge shame, and I know of plenty of people whom this has upset immensely. I myself have pulled back from the game big time, my enthusiasm beyond matching close friends having been fully patched out.Tekken has always had mountains of depth which requires lots from you as a player in order to learn, explore and master, this isn't something they seem intent on respecting particularly well however. This applies to your money also as the cash shop items added to date, including the battle pass are not of significant originality or quality (not to mention the publisher's war on mod creators, a community which has been active and contributed to the franchise's growth since Tekken 7). I don't understand how they expect the players to spend their energy on the game or recommend it to others when the developers themselves have made effectively no positive changes to improve their community's health and enjoyment thus far.Once again, hope this review helps someone and happy gaming. ♥

_childDocuments_.review: First Impressions:Tekken 8 offers significantly more content than Tekken 7, particularly in story and offline modes—far more than Mortal Kombat 1. However, I do miss the Treasure Hunt mode.Arcade Quest:This mode seems valuable for newer players, thanks to its integrated tutorials as you progress. Personally, though, I found it a bit too slow-paced, with too much time between battles.Super Ghost Mode:The idea of training against an AI that learns from your playstyle is awesome. I'll definitely be using it to improve and learn more moves.Story:The story is excellent—much better than Tekken 7’s and many other recent fighting game stories. The two possible endings were unexpected but a great touch, adding some replayability.Character Stories:These are worth playing through, as they let you experience each character and figure out which ones you like best. Plus, you earn a million Fight Money, which can be used for character customization. The character stories are also more substantial than Tekken 7’s; instead of a quick one-and-done, you need to complete five battles to finish each character’s story.Overall Gameplay:The gameplay feels more refined than Tekken 7. The new Heat mechanic is interesting but disrupts some of the core gameplay fundamentals. Engaging Heat can break combos, which is useful but might get annoying in online matches. Heat and Rage together feel a bit over the top. Also, the game occasionally crashes.Comparison to Other Games:If you’re into offline modes like those in Mortal Kombat or Street Fighter, you’ll likely enjoy Tekken 8. Combos are easier to execute compared to both Street Fighter and Mortal Kombat. Compared to previous Tekken games, Tekken 8 does feel heavily monetized, with an £85 deluxe edition and an in-game battle pass. That said, it plays much better than Tekken 7 and does a better job of teaching you about combos.TL;DR:Tekken 8 has a lot more to do, introduces a new combo breaker mechanic, and offers better learning tools for players. It's also better than Mortal Kombat 1.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has quickly become one of my favorite games. Other games are hard for me to really get invested in and/or feel motivated to play. This game is such an amazing game because it gives you the motivation and inspiration to get better and continue playing. There are plenty of features and practice materials that advance your skill in such a fun and engaging way. I can confidently say this is my favorite game at the moment. Even never playing a Tekken game before, ever, i still feel like I'm able to be a solid player with friends and even in online random matches. The combo challenges, punishment practice, and the ghost battles are my most notable features. The combo challenges are fun and fairly simple. You can view the combo, watch the play through, and it even plays you the counts as the timing you should be doing the combos to. This is extremely helpful to me because it helps when I'm focusing on gaining the skill to use in battle, rather than just trying to beat the challenge and hoping i press the right buttons. The punishment practice is incredibly useful for learning how to block or move better around the arena. I love how it will keep you on your toes, expecting to be hit and having to find a  way to dodge a various amount of combos, they also have it to be adjustable. so you can have it set to regular difficulty or a harder difficulty, which i love because it allows room for improvement and it provides practice options for higher level/more experienced players. Lastly, my favorite feature is the ghost battles where you can battle your own ghost. Truthfully, i think this feature is insanely cool. It also allows you to keep fighting someone who is always constantly around or at your current level. It definitely has helped me improve by trying to hit new moves and also finding different ways to block. I also really enjoy the ghost feature because you can download other peoples ghost files!! This game is so lovable. There's just so much to love.

The last fighting game I even bothered to toss a lot of hours into and much more, was Street Fighter 4 on the Xbox 360 and I think Tekken 8 beats that game pretty fairly, maybe not for the singleplayer stuff alone, but as an overall package and what potential it has for the future with additional updates and DLC, it will surely replace SF4 as my "ye olde favourite".Obviously the game right now has some issues, but what AAA game these days doesn't on day one? _childDocuments_.review: TL;DR - One step forward but five steps back.The best looking in the series by a mile with fun new character and fantastic new moves across the returning cast.All of it sadly marred by the overuse of a far more aggressive, pressure-heavy gameplay that boils the cast down into and scummy monetization tactics BamCo employed that feel mobile game-y like cutting out more than half of the customization options from T7 just to sell them back to players a few weeks after launch. The dumbed-down execution is fine, letting new players get into the game without needing to know the complexities of the last entry, but the changes to grabs and the focus on rushdown make characters like Dragonov and King unbearable to play against, especially with the execution for chain-grab combos on King completely replaced with mashing your controller to complete the chain. The Heat system I think is a neat concept, giving your character more options for a short window each round, but with the focus on pressure and rushdown, it's not a defensive tool the game would have more benefited from.The gameplay is a wholly different beast from 7. Some like it, some don't. But the monetization is piss-boiling.$70 upwards to $300 for the Collector's, and a fighter pass that will add only four characters before needing to purchase the next pass, then an ingame shop that sells past outfits, THEN a seasonal battlepass to top it off. And both the shop and pass were added after launch to avoid the lovely ESRB tag of "In-Game Purchases".Also the fighter pass at the time of writing has three returning characters with no new cast members and arguably two of them, in both Eddy and Lidia, should have been in the default roster ( Eddy being a legacy character and Lidia being the last new character in T7, needing very little change ).All this to say I bought the Collector's because I like Tekken, but T8 ain't it, and it looks like it will never be. Go play T7; At least that game will give you a complete experience for a fraction of T8's cost.

_childDocuments_.review: Visually better than tekken 7, Story-Mode is kinda hype at times, otherwise it's just a downgrade of a game.Online is just as bad as before, however this time around you'll have to deal with opponents' potato PCs, on top of the usual poor connections and WIFI warriors. If your opponent drops FPS during the match, both of you will have to suffer with frequent stuttering and lag. It's a very common problem with Tekken 8 due to how demanding it can be on max settings.Ranked games are optional BO3-format, so there's no obligation to stick around for the full set (get used to the opponent leaving after their first loss). Also, no punishment for pluggers so you'll have to deal with people leaving just before losing every now and then too.Game also suffers from the modern disease of unnecessary amount of micro-transactions. As of right now there's a box price for the game, season pass, premium battle pass, cash-shop and in the future separate DLCs (if you're not willing to buy season passes). The cash shop requires you to buy Tekken coins, which come in set amounts. These are in inconvenient sizes, forcing you to buy more than you need for the item you are buying.The customization choices are a huge downgrade from Tekken 7 (which was already a downgrade from the previous games). The most basic customization options have been removed and they are now being added to the cash shop instead.Even when ignoring all of the micro-transaction headache, I still can't recommend the game due to the sheer amount of laggy players and pluggers. There are much better fighting games out there with proper online-modes.

_childDocuments_.review: 6 months in, and the game still crashes regularly. Netcode is trash, wifi players will autogrief you with poor connectivity, even if the game claims their connection is perfect. The game is peer-to-peer(no dedicated servers) and opponents will regularly have a frame advantage due to poor netcode, and moves will act weird and screw you over, because the game was designed for offline play. I'm native to europe 1 region, and have a better connection when fighting americans, than when I fight europeans. In tekken 7 you could edit your save file to choose your online rank and your play stats, I assume you can still do that since they didn't even bother with anti-cheat. I'm not sure why they felt the need to add ANOTHER cutscene move to all the characters, as if rage art wasn't bad enough. Also, they messed up the wake-up game completely. _childDocuments_.review: Despite being an arguably good game, Tekken 8 fails as software on multiple fronts. The netcode is questionable, the performance and optimisation are very lacklustre in a lot of ways, prone to crashing and causing frame drops and chugging on even high tier machines. For context, I have a 6750XT and sometimes the game stutters and even decides to randomly crash while stating I have run out of VRAM (I have 12GB)! Furthermore, there is a specific stage where you have to make a small prayer whether it will crash to desktop or not during the WHOLE match.Additionally, there is no anti-cheat behaviour in the game. Disconnecting to deny an opponent's win, cheating, and probably soon we will have people using scripts to auto low parry and macros for difficult inputs. If you "plug" someone, there is no repercussion for these actions leading to a very unpleasant online experience, even if you're just trying to casually run a few sets after a hard day's work.But wait, there's more! The community has alerted the developers to all these issues, on social media, in online chatrooms and even with game clips as hard evidence? What was their response?Adding microtransactions to the game, without fixing the previously stated problems, and they added this one month after the game released, without previous notice of such practices before the game launched, thus being purposefully misleading to bolster the game's review scores and fan reception.At the time of writing, despite liking this game and playing it almost daily, I can't recommend it to new and returning players alike. It pains me, but with the current climate, this product fails at honesty, performance and transparency. Stay away.

_childDocuments_.review: Coming from Tekken 7 - which, for transparency, was also gifted to me - I feel like this has been a chaotic undergrade.I don't consider myself a "good" player but some could say I fit the "decent" category.I'm specifying this to have the reader understand that this review is coming from the point of view of someone who doesn't really care about the plot, the skins, the collector edition with the action figures, what have you, but solely on the competitive aspect of the game.Brief detour: netcode, game stability, and general online experience are definetely better than what they used to be in Tekken 7.Back to the core of the review, the competitive aspect.After logging well over a thousand hours on said game, no doubt in my mind exists when I tell you that solid defense and quick decision making were two essential skills to possess as a player.Sure, characters had their gimmicks, they always have, they always will.However, in Tekken 8, the new heat mechanics themselves are entire gimmicks all playable characters have access to, and promote (yes, you've already read this in other reviews, because guess what, it's frustratingly true) extensive unrelenting aggression that just sucks the beauty out of the basics that Tekken 7 taught me were valuable.You are a glass cannon.Your opponent is a glass cannon.Everyone is a glass cannon, all the time.No, the extra health doesn't balance that out, nor does the regenerative ability that comes with bashing your opponent's kneecaps in.Combos are generally much more lethal, and also long, lengthy, interminable, endless, and every other synonym you can come up with.This is once again due to heat mechanics that allow everyone to extend almost every combo you can think of.Pair that with new stage gimmicks such as lava geysers and exploding walls, and the heat engager camera focus, and you have yourself a recipe for receiving a 15s combo after missing a jab.Not exaggerating: that used to be quite rare in Tekken 7 where you rolled your eyes after an Akuma/Geese with a full gauge started a combo on you, and in a few other cases.I got to "Tekken King" rank in a couple of sessions without knowing anything about any other character except the one I play, and even the one I play I didn't know much of, in terms of new moves and combos.This might register as a flex, but it's exclusively being stated to point out how easier and unrewarding this felt.Saying that the general lack of defensive skill and fundamental knowledge at that level is evident would be an understatement.Yet, people you play against make up for that in total aggression, and they have every right to do so.You should approach every fight like that as well, because the game wants you to do it, and is going to reward you for that.If that sounds marvelous to you, great, you're going to love Tekken 8, so go and press buttons.Personally, I already feel like uninstalling.

_childDocuments_.review: Playing Tekken 8 has really made me Appreciate Dota 2. Dota 2 nerfs the characters that are too strong and buffs the characters that are too weak. _childDocuments_.review: Excellent launch of a modern fighting game. Tekken 8 is visually gorgeous with a large roster of varied characters to thoroughly enjoy in both the most casual through pro level fighting. The storymode and other offline play is mashable for the newest of rookies while the skill ceiling is exceedingly high online for those looking for a challenge. Quite accessible for newbies too, for a fighting game. The very basics are taught well enough by the Arcade Quest, and the training mode is quite comprehensive. The movelists are as usual in Tekken very intimidating and long, but helped by the combo challenges and probably the best replay functionality I have ever seen this game provides every tool needed to get to grips with characters and mechanics. For everything else, there's always youtube guides. I can't say how it fares at high level, as I've barely gotten a bit over 17 hours in so far and maybe five or six of those went to Arcade Quest and the storymode, but I absolutely think it's worth the cost of entry. The matchmaking is generous and provides quite a lot of opponents with quite excellent connection quality, which has personally been a bit of a problem for me in SF6 due to living rurally and Capcom being far less generous with the matchmaking. If you're just after a singleplayer experience though... I don't know. The storymode has no challenge to it and while the production value is ridiculously high, the writing is hilariously bad. This story feels like a tween just tried to condense every Shonen anime arc into five-six hours of play, which I suspect is the intent. It's downright funny in its cheesiness. Highly recommended if you're looking for either a pro-level fighting game or just a casual masher. It's fun for everyone.

_childDocuments_.review: As a longtime fan of the Tekken series, I eagerly anticipated the release of Tekken 8, hoping for another exhilarating experience in the iconic fighting franchise. However, my excitement quickly turned into frustration as I delved into the game.One of the most glaring issues that significantly detracted from my enjoyment was the abysmal server performance. The laggy servers plagued my gameplay experience, causing frequent disruptions and making it nearly impossible to execute precise moves and combos. Whether I was playing online matches or attempting to enjoy the single-player modes, the lag persisted, creating an infuriating gameplay environment.The constant lag not only hindered my ability to fully immerse myself in the game but also made it challenging to compete against opponents effectively. It's disheartening to see such a fundamental aspect of the game, like server stability, fall short, ultimately detracting from the overall experience.Despite Tekken 8 boasting impressive graphics, diverse character roster, and engaging gameplay mechanics, the persistent server issues overshadow these positive aspects, leaving me deeply disappointed. Until the server performance is improved and the lag is addressed, I cannot recommend Tekken 8 to fellow gamers who value a smooth and enjoyable gaming experience.In conclusion, Tekken 8's potential is marred by its subpar server performance, resulting in a frustrating and ultimately unsatisfying gaming experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Well UE5, but consoles cant handle them. Expect forced framedrops in Crossplay matches 24/7.If someone is dropping frames (either their PC/Console cant handle the FPS which happens a lot or/and!!! their Internet sucks) the Person with the better Connection is ♥♥♥♥♥♥. How?Simply: Your Inputs will be eaten, sometimes you just hit them, they don't take damage and out of nowhere you're getting hit by a sped up version of their attack as Tekken doesn't know how to handle the fact you're both extremely offsync. Tarkov has less desync. That's not good. In General id say about 15 out of 100 Matches are fine, 50are okayish with only 6Frame Rollback (0.1 Second of lag FYI, still bad) the rest are unplayable at 16+ or just them dropping Frames as soon anything happens Stageffect / Ki wise. This happens so frequently i learnt to use moves with less groundplat/kieffects so its not as bad.Id say out of 100 Matches there's about 5 (i imagine its even worse at higher ranks) with someone using some kind of Script. Scripts are simple: They break everything, they CH everything etc. etc. They will just win, whatever.At more or less the same rate you will find people using Framelimiters. You're about to experience less FPS than a PowerPoint. They can change the FPS on their Side at will, forcing you to do the same. As soon as they start a combo it will be fine, once you're both neutral its back to 1/5th gamespeed. Tekken Devs have no idea how to handle this 6 Months after launch. Its been running rampart and there's no crazy cheatsoftware needed to do that. There's a plethora of options to do so.Losing a ranked match, 2-0 at 1 Health?Just close the game! No punishment whatsoever. Tekken calls it a draw and youre both thrown back to the main menu. No loss, no win for both of you. Interestingly enough the person that disconnected will keep their Winstreak. This leads to people roaming the matchmaking with a 999 Winstreak. Tekken sees no Problem here. There is a display showing you how often people disconnect before you accept, however its only for the past 20 Matches so its quite useless.As someone who played plenty of Tekken Tag 2/5/7 I am uncertain about it. Tekken always felt different from other Games as there's an insane Skillceiling for playing defensive. Yes you can play aggressive but staying cool under pressure was the name of the game. With Heat you can just mash out of anything and get + for free. Almost every other Fighting game has some kind off Resource/Ultbar/Armor whatsoever but Tekken adding this out of nowhere at this insane Scale? Not a big fan, but hey i get watching 2 Doods blocking everything for 30Seconds can be boring.79.90CHF (90USD wohoo Swiss) Basegame and you will not receive any DLC Characters. You have to buy them each at 7.90CHF(9USD).A Battlepass because that's whats in right now.A lot of useless, frilly accessories for a "lobby" where you can control a Mii Like Avatar that can be bought in an ingame store that no one wanted. To this day i have not used this "lobby" feature once so its quite obvious it has been added purely for monetization purposes. You will be reminded each time in the Mainmenu that you should unlock the Battlepass and you have to manually click the Popup away. Then another Popup follows with the uninteresting things you've unlocked from your previous Session. This again you have to close manually.If you're into Tekken sure buy it.For anyone else still interested: Play Tekken7 instead.

_childDocuments_.review: The game started off in a very good spot, with great gameplay with some easily fixable balance issues.Unfortunately, everything done since then with the game has been bad, if not catastrophic.They introduced an in-game shop after the initial review period for the game. Technically fine, you could ignore it. But it also comes with an in-game currency system where you can buy it in bundles of 500.After that, they introduced a battle pass model, with a paid battle pass option. In a 70$ game. I repeat - a paid battle pass in a 70€ game that already has a season pass and individual character DLC's, and an in-game store. There is a free battle pass version, but it may as well not exist.A reminder - Tekken 7 had periodic free cosmetic customization DLC.Coincidentally, the battle pass will cost you 600 coins. Remember how you could only buy coins in bundles of 500? So you'd have to spend 10$ for the battle pass. People will say "the battle pass pays for itself" - but you get 600 coins from it, not 1000, which is what the initial purchase would cost you if you didn't have any extra coins beforehand.As for the battle pass content - it's filled by assets that are straight out of Tekken 7, along with random avatar junk and even some stock Unreal engine assets. They put a round sphere in the battle pass. That's a reward, a sphere.As for the minor balance issues mentioned at the start of this?They're not so minor anymore. The devs claimed that they don't want to do major balance changes before the first major tournaments in Tekken 8.However, what they say and what they do is completely different. One character in particular, Devil Jin, required some adjusting to his damage in certain situations. Instead of them nerfing the move that caused it, they changed an entire mechanic related to it.This ended up impacting ALL characters and 90% of the stages in the game. As a result, a lot of characters got weaker, some got stronger and it all introduced a high level of uncertainty during matches.There's still the issue of pluggers in online modes too. The disconnect ratio still doesn't really do much. The devs try their best to ignore the whole issue when the solution is simple - if someone plugs/ragequits a match, the plugger should get a loss and the person remaining a win.But they won't even acknowledge that as an option, despite other modern fighting games doing it already.I might change my review if this all gets fixed, but for now just stay away from the game. It started off really good,  but every single thing since release has been bad.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a near Masterpiece. Unfortunately I've run into performances issues, including Several "Initialize error" messages and long load times. That could be my fault however as my CPU processor is old. Other than that this game has so much to over. The amazing fighting mechanics that Tekken has always been known for are present and over thirty characters in the base roster. This game has something to offer for every fighting game player. The Cinematic story mode titled The Dark Awakens is quite possibly the most ambitious, epic, and memorable fighting game story mode every produced. Its shorter than what you may be used to if you play MK and Injustice but it packs quite a punch. Jin Kazama goes through a tremendous character arc, one that brought genuine goosebumps and heartfelt moments. The final fight is beautifully choreographed and concludes the story with a bang. The ending leaves you wants more as expect and there are still loose ends to be tied up and explained but its good that we have a solid story arc to prop us into the next generation of Tekken after the somewhat lackluster Tekken 7 story mode.       Besides that there is a lot to do. The Arcade Quest is a fun little mini game reminiscent of old school Arcade play as well as a clever nod to Tekken world Tour competitive gaming. The new Replay and Tips feature adds so many tools to help player improve their skills and the New Super Ghost Battle ensures that you can play against anyone you want even when they are not available Online. You can even fight yourself. Its a brilliant feature and one I hope they will continue to build on in the future. The Presentation of this game is sublime. Namco really stepped it up with the visuals and this is apparent in the epic redesigns many of the characters have. I look forward to playing this for many years to come and to see the Tekken fandom and community grow after this new release. This is phenomenal and the best game to come out of this three decade old franchise since Tekken 5. What a time to be alive!

With the introduction of the Heat system allowing you to enhance your combos as well as provide very much needed chip damage onto blocking opponents the game provides much needed aggression in a game where previously, besides on-block frame traps, there was no punishment. There is one thing that is plaguing my experience with this game (and if anyone has any fixes for this please let me know) is that out of nowhere Unreal will just crash with no prior indication as to what could be causing it, and considering the research I have done online, I am not the only one affected by this problem. I do not think it is a graphics related issue as I have toned down the graphics to the lowest possible and have still been affected by this problem. With new fighters and returning fighters (and plausible guest characters) don't let this ultimately small hiccup dissuade you from experiencing one of, in my opinion, the best Tekken entries possibly in the entire series.TLDR; The game is very beginner friendly with a high skill ceiling but does have an issue with random crashes.

_childDocuments_.review: I have played Tekken on and off since I first encountered it in the arcade as a child. The variable characters, the 3d animations, the flashy hits, and the cool older kids doing weird stunts with a sword wielding ninja entranced me at first, but it was many years before I could actually identify the arcade game I had seen as tekken, when I discovered a copy of Tekken 4 at a friends house and played it while hungover.Years later, I played Tekken 7 and was impressed but found it a little sparse. The gameplay was deep but understanding it required a dedicated pursuit and the tools that were provided were not really up to the task. You had to do research and keep notes and build actual in-game experience against others - but the netcode wasn't that good, so online matches lagged and irl play, well, it wasn't long before all my friends refused to play me because the basic mechanics of this game (lows, armor moves, backdashing, throws, etc.) feel like unfair cheating to someone with little to no mechanical knowledge.Starved of good matches, I dropped Tekken 7, Now, Tekken 8 is here and it has arrived at a time when my schedule is open to it. Everything I could want is in the game - the core cast is essentially intact (though some will surely contest who is in the "canon") and the roster is an expansive 32 fighters with the promise of more to come (how many were in Tekken 4? 18-20? And I thought that was a lot to learn...). Animations and graphics generally have received a nice bump from 7 and the stages are beautiful, with multiple tiers to throw your opponents through (and now there are stage hazards as well). These stages are the best in Tekken history, visually fascinating and detailed enough that I have stopped in practice mode to admire the small details like the ongoing gunfight on the warzone level. The songs are all hypnotic bangers, and there is an option to use the soundtrack from any previous game.There are a lot of reviews out there that talk about how this is the Tekken to be initated with, with all the improved practice tools and tutorials and that is all true. The game does what it can to put you on a conveyor belt to competence which is great, since it has produced a bumper crop of new players for a franchise that richly deserves them. This however should not overshadow the fact that this is a great Tekken. I really enjoy the new heat system, it has added a new element of intensity to matches and meshes decently well with the older rage system. The special moves that each character has with heat really add speed and style to fights. I am not wild about the continued inclusion of rage arts but this could be personal bias - they are a cheap equalizer for less experienced players when a veteran forgets about them. I still think this game represents a further refinement of everything the devs learned from 7 and matches feel great to play, even after several hundred in a row.Also helping this tekken is the introduction of cross platform play and better netcode. Matches will still lag from time to time but it's almost always a more reliable experience than 7.This is the one to get if you are new and the one if you are old. Just pick it up, so we can all plaay together.

The whole bait-and-switch behind their monetization has left a really sour taste in the community and this practice should not be encouraged. Thumbs way down now.Original review follows below:Great version of the Tekken franchise. Has a large list of characters, feels really smooth, new systems that help players comeback / do cool combos, has options to make the game easier for people, practice modes, and lots of other things. Plus, in the story you're playing as Jin like 90% of the time instead of jumping around and learning about other characters and what they are doing. I think MK9 did it much better in terms of a playable fighting game story. Should have really focused on multiple characters and had more things than just the same few fights over and over (and the wonky fighting masses of 3D enemies).Either way, this is a great continuation of the Tekken franchise. Just wish it had more practice tools, macro setup, a few more characters (saving them for DLC, I guess), and more game modes (Tekken Ball is fun but give us more). Still think Tekken Tag Tournament is better because of the 2v2 dynamic, but this is very solid. Oh, and I wish they brought back Paul Phoenix's "Rapid Fire to Stone Breaker" move... _childDocuments_.review: A highly competent, frankly brilliant fighting game held back by a stubborn, intentionally archaic handling of online features and a cash shop introduced soon after all press reviews of the game were finalized to add insult to injury.The netcode is okay and usually playable, but it's the only fighting game of the current generation to not have rock solid rollback netcode.No PC stress test or PC performance indicator before going online means you'll regularly run into opponents who force you to play the game in slow motion. That's not including those who deliberately throttle their frame-rate when losing.The game's anti-cheat is a manually updated Excel sheet of cheaters names that the director of the game is personally demoting to beginner ranks, with no automated system to catch deliberate disconnects or cheaters.  You do not get a win if your opponent deliberately disconnects when losing, and they receive no punishment. The disconnect rate tracker in game is also not working, so you have no way of knowing if you've been matched with a plugger until you waste 5 minutes playing them. Those manually demoted by the devs will cheat/plug their way back to high ranks in a day or two. The devs are proud enough of this being their anti-cheat system that they boast about it on Twitter. When asked about introducing the above features, the devs have stated they are strictly against any kind of automated system for detecting or punishing foul play.I look forward to an update where I no longer have to wonder whether my opponent who seems weak for their rank is going to yoink their ethernet cable when they lose a couple of rounds.For now, I sadly can't recommend this otherwise solid fighting game.

_childDocuments_.review: I have only played the story so far and it took me about 4 hours to beat it on normal. It follows the trend that Mortal Kombat set some years ago, where you are basically watching a movie with fights to interrupt it. The story itself was okay, nothing amazing, but it progresses the narrative and has some interesting twists in there. One negative  thing about the story, is that some of the fights are way too drawn out and there needed to be more restraint shown by story director. You fight the same guy over and over and over again... and just when you think it is over... you fight again, gets a little tired. It is like watching a wrestling match where the combatants keep exchanging finisher moves over and over again, nullifying the dramatic impact intended by the finisher. Another negative is that there is some very out of place humor thrown in a certain points... I mean, you have someone saying that she is fighting for the bad guys because it would help sell her product; the sudden goofiness is not subtle and does take away from the tension the game is trying to build.The fighting itself is smooth as ever with how Tekken has always been. Very complex if you get beyond button mashing and try to learn the millions of things you can do with a character. I would  not consider Tekken to be a casual friendly franchise, so this is not surprising. Overall, I am having a fun time so far. I have been playing Tekken since the first one on the PSOne, so this is right up my alley. It doesn't do anything new that will replace my love for Street Fighter, but it is a good time.

_childDocuments_.review: This game had a strong start, but failed to retain it.Within 3 weeks of release, there was an announcement that a shop would be added to the game allowing users to buy items using a new in-game currency only obtainable using real life money. The incredibly convenient timing to do this after both the reviews were in and the refund policy was up for those who bought it within a week of launch is the main gripe I have with this. If it was at least part of the game from day 1 and mentioned on the store page or in trailers, I'd have less of an issue with it as because then I'd either completely avoid or wait to see if maybe it was a business model I saw worth buying in to.Just after 2 months after release, there was another announcement that a battle pass system would be added, where one of the items was a plain white sphere equipable as an accessory. If that wasn't bad enough, the parts of the update which actually altered the content of the game caused fighting game breaking issues like walls not breaking.Other than this, there's a consistent issue related to pluggers in the game which has been a thing since the beginning. Unlike a game like MK1 where someone plugging would result in a loss for the person plugging and a win for the other person, Tekken 8 has taken a different approach where no one loses or wins the match. Around a month after release, pluggers were being banned from the game, but the issue of the victim of the plugger not being awarded a win still persisted. Even so, I believe that banning people for plugging is insane.I can't help but think that if the developer's resources was being poured into what players were asking for rather than two monetisation systems, the game would be in a better state.So yes, other than the strong start, the only thing this game did right was teach me not to buy games until at least a month after release. Certainly a more extreme lesson than not pre-ordering like No Man's Sky taught me...(One thing to note, I am not interested in wasting my time playing games as a service where the base game is free, so there's no way (unless the content was special) I would be interested in that where the game is paid for).

_childDocuments_.review: As much as I love this franchise (I've grown up with just about every mainline Tekken game aside from 3 + 4), I can only recommend this game due to my own bias. Disregarding this however, Bandai here hasn't been doing very cool things with how they've been handling this game . Introducing a micro-transaction shop with its own currency system, along with a battle pass are all fine in most cases. But in this case, it's inexcusable as Tekken 8 is a ). The worst part of all of this is the fact this wasn't really revealed to us until  the game had been out for about a month. The shop doesn't need to exist; just sell legacy outfits as DLC for all I care along with removing the "Tekken Coins". Or maybe introduce a system where these Tekken coins are free and you gain these coins as you play the game? Meanwhile, the battle pass has no reason to exist in a full price game; it's not a F2P game that generates its revenue with its virtual shop and battle passes. Aside from the blatant monetization and Bandai's shady methods of introducing said monetization, there's been various complaints with people plugging in online matches, literal cheaters, and other crappy players disrupting gameplay in legitimately harmful ways. There should have already been measures taken into account on how to handle these types of players.Honestly, this game is relatively good. I've enjoyed playing the game so much,  in terms of unlockable achievements. I just hope Bandai listens to the outcry of its playerbase that do have legitimate concerns. They probably won't remove the battle pass and the microtransactions within the game. In my honest opinion, the shady monetization practices Bandai is engaging in will drive some, or even a good portion of its playerbase away from the game.I can only recommend this game if you're willing to excuse Bandai's monetization and ignore it regardless of what's added in the "Tekken Shop" or its Battlepass system.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best Tekken games, maybe even better than 5. A labour of love in every respect, with a great story that follows up on plot points from previous entries, individual character stories with fun (but not story-relevant, like they used to be) endings, and some of the most fun online play in the genre. I personally dislike the Arcade Quest mode and everything attached to it (especially because this game will never even reach arcades), but there are people who enjoy it so I guess I can see the value.However, the 'Tekken Shop' will be releasing soon, and you'll get to spend real money on Tekken Coins to buy cosmetic items. For your full-price triple-A game. Remember all those interviews where it was promised that they wouldn't do this kind of thing? Remember how they'd make fun of DOA for doing this? Can't wait to savour my 30 free inputs in Tekken 9.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a moment where I'm 50/50 with recommending this game to people. I play semi-competitively and also like to play casually as well, both provide wildly different experiences. From a competitive point of view, the game honestly is so frustrating at times due to how new mechanics affect the overall flow of a match. The new Heat Drive mechanic provides a variety of different moves for each character whereas in T7 it was just one powerful move. This mechanic is what leaves me 50/50 with this game as it does provide a new sense of gameplay, however it makes the game kinda stale to play at times and so often matches (especially at lower rank), just pops Heat Drive and their Heat move. Additionally to this mechanic certain characters have more than one powerful Heat move, the trade off being that other characters may have more moves provided to them while in Heat. The mechanic overall is not very balanced and I hope in future patches the mechanic becomes closer to provide a better match experience. From a Casual point of view, the game is crazy fun. It is a very fast pace game and majority of the characters reflect this new speed in Tekken. Characters like Reina for example and some returning characters really bring a "spectacle" factor to their kit which makes watching friends or playing with friends much more enjoyable. This is best Tekken game in terms of barrier of entry, but that's not to say the game is not difficult. This definitely fits into the easy to play, hard to master category of fighting games. Now the monetization to me doesn't concern me as I don't really care for it, however, this does create horrible business practices that forces players to pay for customization options for their characters and these options are not really great to begin with/ported from older games just retouched/a literal Ball. This is a tricky thing to discuss as some people do like it, but honestly go about it with your best judgement and just buy the game, if you don't want to spend money on cosmetics, it won't affect your gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: They changed everything I liked about Tekken 7 and doubled down on what I disliked. The only thing that is better are the visuals. Every game is the same; block something that leaves you in - frames and start guessing. This repeats until someone wins. Loosing doesn't feel like being outplayed and winning doesn't feel like outplaying. Some characters are really overpowered and almost every character has certain moves that needs nerfing. Ranked is the same 5 characters 90% of the time. They appealed to a more general audience and left the actual fans behind.All of this is personal opinion and expected, so I wouldn't give a negative review if that was all.Before fixing broken characters they added paid costumes and a battlepass. You can only purchase the battlepass with Tekken coins and the lowest amount you can buy is 500. Conveniently, the battlepass costs 600, so you have to buy 1000 to afford the battlepass. This is an old, greedy tactic that most companies have stopped doing, and we shouldn't accept it. It really makes the very limited costumization compared to older Tekkens feel really bitter, knowing they are releasing them for money later.They also added a character as DLC, which is fine, except it's a very strong one that's a notoriously hard matchup and you need to own it in order to lab him or even view replays with him in them. This qualifies as pay-to-win to me and is the single worst thing they could have done.The game was released without any consequenses for plugging and cheating. They have since fixed the plugging part by implimenting the solution they already had in T7. It's more disincentivizing it than actually fixing it, but it works. They are still not doing anything about the cheaters other than telling people to report them on twitter, which obviously isn't a solution at all. Not that they ever ban anyone anyway. Cheaters seem really rare, luckily, but you can't really know as it's all just guessing anyway.A lot of people are experiencing frequent crashes. The game can't distinguish between crashing and plugging, so that's a big technical problem that also makes the plugging solution worse.By turning on and off assisted mode during a combo, you can cause your opponent to lag and drop their combo. It has been reported many times and they really should have fixed it by now.I want to like this game, as we won't have Tekken 9 in many, many years, and if they address all of this, I will change my review. I'm not very hopeful though, as they have stated to want to move the series in this direction, and have a long history of ignoring technical issues.

_childDocuments_.review: Tekken 8 is the latest installment in the almost 30 year old franchise. It is on the surface a direct extension of Tekken 7 utilizing a lot of that versions mechanics with some key new additions that make Tekken 8 a unique experience, albeit an unbalanced one. The addition of the Heat mechanic encourages aggressive play, which unfortunately overshadows the meticulous footsie based gameplay the franchise has become known for. That's not saying Heat mechanic isnt fun, its just extremely unbalanced. Some characters really take advantage of it while others not so much and it shows. Expect this to become finetuned over Tekken 8's life span.The graphics are a major improvement over Tekken 7 in every way, if you can ignore eastern depictions of women still being extremely dated, the game looks beautiful.There are also some cash grab schemes at play with the battle pass, and tekken shop being added. A lot of the content so far seems very subpar for the price and even the price is pretty low (usually $5 for a costume). Outside of the new Mechanic, microtransactions and how the game looks, the gameplay is rather inconsistent. Some things work, but not all the time so if you intend on buying, expect a lot of patching to correct or change things going forward.Its important to remember Tekken 7 spent atleast 2 years in the arcades before it was ported to consoles where Tekken 8 had a couple weeks worth of beta testing that was meant to test connectivity quality. If Im going off of Tekken 7 as an example, give Tekken 8 1-2 years before it reaches a state of "balance".The reason I cant reccomend this game right now is because the state of the game is in such a flux, that the price tag just doesnt make sense. Theres not a lot of varied single player content to keep you busy outside of climbing the ranked ladder, and this game is also notoriously known for people "plugging" to preserve ranked points. lol theres a lot going on. If the chaos sounds fun im sure youll enjoy the game. Otherwise check back in a year and see how things are going. Ill prob update my remove a year from now and see whats changed.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I could give it a mixed rating.Editing my review for the third time now (14.04.2024).Look, I am a new player to the franchise, never played any other game before this one. I am as casual as it gets. Ugh. Some people say that the game is a one massive knowledge check. And maybe it is like that for the folks with that kind of mindset. ... *sigh* the game is fun. Extremely fun even. Kinda hard to get into for new players but very fun.Okay, let's count positives:1) Works on Steam Deck nicely (though with minimal settings);2) Gameplay is fantastic;3) Customization is great! At least for the MK fan such as I;4) Ranked is fun and casual friendly! Unlike MK there are no customization items hidden behind high ranks. You reach high ranks and you get... nothing! Well, nothing other than satisfaction of reaching it, I guess. In short, you don't lose anything for not reaching high ranks.5) Huge roster and the characters actually feel different;6) Beautiful soundtrack;7) Eeehhh.... Fight Pass isn't exactly predatory I guess...8) Somewhat easy to 100% the achievements.Now for negatives:1) Pluggers. Lots of pluggers. Especially in the higher ranks. And they are not punished. There are also cheaters with auto parry etc;2) Premium shop was added two months after the launch which is beyond scummy. They've changed the ESRB rating post launch. Many people have bought the game because it was not predatory, didn't have any premium shops or passes. And the players were duped by Bamco;3) While BP isn't exactly predatory, it's tied to only online modes. That's right people who aren't interested in online fights have received the middle finger. NOT COOL.4) While customization is great for the new players. Tekken veterans will agree that it is botched compared to predecessors. Probably it was made this way in order to place the customizations items in future BPs.5) No benchmark before going into online. Thus people with calculators can ruin the experience of others.6) Single player content is also extremely lacking in comparison to predecessors. Shame. I wanna see Tekken Force and Tekken Bowl in this one, also offline tournies.7) Bamco went after modders. Wow, not even WB and NRS do something like that.8) THE BALL.I really want to give it a neutral rating. Like really. But Bamco did their absolute best to tarnish the reputation and piss off the fans. And for the game that aspires to be not casual, but competetive the online problems like pluggers are absolutely inexcusable. Truly, a shame.

_childDocuments_.review: Been playing Tekken since I was a kid allll the way back in Tekken 3, Where one air combo would obliterate your health bar with no counter play. I love the direction this series is going. The heat bar has added more nuance and gives players a resource to create insane combos given time and practice. The tutorials are more thought out and give newer players a clear idea of what each mechanic is and how to use it. Even tailoring it to a specific character that you'd like to learn with the Arcade Story mode. Compared to Tekken 7's tutorial experience it actually feels like Bandai actually WANT people to pick up the game.The Story Mode actually took me by surprise. I found myself enjoying it more than I initially expected given how they handled it in 7 by telling it through the perspective of a reporter. But this time they actually had me hooked. Sure it was goofy at points but when has Tekken ever taken itself seriously? It progressed the story enough while still remembering it's roots and how insane and over the top the whole over arching plot is.All of the practice tools have seen a massive improvement since 7. My favourite feature is being able to look at specific replays from on or offline and be able to receive hints that are specific to what happened in that specific round. The game teaches you what to punish with, even giving you basic combos to get you started. Making this game easy to pick up but when you start putting time into it there is so much to dig into and master. The fighting in this game feels satisfying. All the sound effects are punchy and all the stages are visually stunning to look at. Haven't had any performance issues running on max graphics with my Nvidia 3070 Ti except for some slow loads at the start of stages when loading them for the first time but it smooths out quickly. Experienced one crash but it was a particularly hot day and it hasn't happened again since. Fighting online is insanely fun and addicting when you get a string of good opponents who are just down for a good time. There will always be spammers, button mashers and generally toxic players in any fighting game you play these days. I expect there to be a few people disconnecting every now and then or throwing out the same move on repeat because it has good plus frames. USUALLY there is always a counter play if you're patient and take the time to learn what moves your character has that are good to retaliate with. But when someone disconnects there is no punishment for the leaving party which is a little annoying. If someone leaves half way through a ranked battle, stop them from re entering the ranked queue for a while? Just something to make people think twice about doing and make it so that it's actively not worth doing. Aside from that a good chunk of the community is just down to have a good time and throw some fists. You can check player stats at anytime and players are rated on how fair they play so you can clearly see if someone is just going to annoy you before engaging with them. It will even show a players disconnection percentage on the screen before you accept the request for battle. So there are some measures in place to protect yourself but nothing in place to really punish straight up abandoning a ranked match. Yeah sure Tekken shop was a bit of weird addition. But it's completely optional. No one is forcing you to pay extra for cosmetics lol. The battle pass I see as a great way to reward people who are consistently playing the game and again it's completely optional to buy the premium version. Plus it rewards you with enough coins if you play enough where you can get the next one for free.THE SOUNDTRACK IS SO GOOD FOR THIS GAME! Every time a stage transitions into the final round music it makes things feel more tense. So happy that the Jukebox feature comes to PC instead of being a PS exclusive thing like with 7! Being able to go and listen to music from previous titles or even set it as the music that plays for the stages tickles my nostalgia nicely. Once you finish with story mode and all the character stories there isn't all that much to do offline except practice for online matches and.. Tekken Ball. I'm not all too mad at this myself as I mainly play to fight online but this may affect your decision in buying it. All in all this is my favourite entry to the Tekken series since Tag 2. Healthy sized cast with a wide variety of fighting styles to choose from. The new characters they added are fun and exciting to play and really fit into the roster. Excited to see what characters come as future DLC. With constant balancing updates it's only going to become a more stable and fun game to play. Find myself actually excited to pick up the controller and learn more ways to outplay my opponents with my favourite character. If you want a fighting game that you can really sink your teeth into and spend hours learning a character I cannot recommend this game enough.

_childDocuments_.review: As a loyal Tekken fan, Tekken 8 follows the same formula as it's predecessors; having an online/offline mode, gallery, jukebox, arcade mode and character specific endings. There are many things I love about Tekken 8, but these are the major selling points:- Multiple character specific intros & win poses- Good offline content (shame no team battle)- A great base roster- Matchmaking and loading times significantly lower in comparison to Tekken 7But there are two features that need to be highlighted individually. The first being the Fight Lounge. The reason I love it is because you can play with friends and strangers alike, but you have access to chat and the opportunity to meet so many great people. I genuinely feel like I'm in an arcade and it's a great place to hang out and play a few casual games.The second being the superb replay feature. The fact you can watch your own replays and train against something you may have struggled with, rewind to the exact moment to see what COULD have worked instead of what you did in real time. It's a fantastic feature which I hope is included in all future Tekken games. Now for the not so good:- Regular crashes occur, particularly in lobbies- The customisation  is lacklustre. Sure there's more options than Tekken 7, but Tekken 6 and Tag 2 had far superior features in this regard- Whilst the story was great, the story GAMEPLAY was nothing to write home about - They removed a great QoL feature they introduced in Tag 2 being online practiceOverall, veterans will enjoy this game and newcomers have lots of tools in-game to familiarise themselves with Tekken's mechanics and improve their play. A solid 8/10 from me.

_childDocuments_.review: Somehow each new Tekken game manages to be better than the previous one.And 8 is no exceptions. Unlike most fighting game franchises that "Reinvent the Wheel" whit each new iteration.Tekken as a series prefers to build upon the existing foundation. On one hand it makes new games in the series feel more like expansions than true sequels but then again some people prefer it this way.The game itself plays more or less similar to 7. But the most major 2 new additions to the core game-play are the Heat system, that basically, for a short while lets you do chip damage on each hit, empowers your characters specific moves, allows a single use of a super dash or a single use of a Super move that's similar to Rage Drive from Tekken 7 although its used as a pure source of damage instead of a combo extender.Surprisingly you can use the heat system any time during a round as it refills after each round. And it can be activated ether by using a armored move or unique attacks that lead in to it that follow up dash that lets you mix up your opponent after.Another new mahnick is above Chip damage. Unlike Tekken 7 where where doing powerful moves against a blocking opponent gave you no payoff here however it deals chip damage in form of gray life. This encourages more aggressive play. In fact the only way to recover gray life is deal damage yourself (Some character have alternate healing ways.)On top of this many classic characters have received a plethora of brand new moves. While the initial roster is somewhat smaller than the previous game, it makes up for it by having each character be more fleshed out ether by giving them unique mechanics or as above mentioned new moves.The series also offers a lot of Singlplayer options. In form of Arcade Qwest which is similar to SFVI world tour Although your avatar doesn't actually engage in fights but is instead supposed to represent a real world Tekken player. A decently fleshed out cinematic Story mode that is filled whit over the top situations. And also has character Episodes that give a but more story to characters that did not take part in the Main story. On top of this the game also has classic Arcade mode. Multiplayer on the other hand has classic matchmaking and a Avatar Hub whit virtual arcade cabinets similar to what SFVI also offers. The netcode is a huge improvement over Tekken 7 butt also seams to be more sensitive to unstable connections.Other notable features are the Jukebox that lets you customize the games soundtrack using songs from older titles.And Ghost battle that lets you train an AI to fight by learning your moves.

_childDocuments_.review: A Rare Gem Worthy Of ReviewI seldom find myself compelled to write reviews, but Tekken 8 has broken that pattern. This game is a rare gem that undeniably deserves recognition for its outstanding qualities. From the breathtaking visual design to the nostalgic callbacks and captivating narrative, Tekken 8 stands as a pinnacle in the world of fighting games.The meticulous attention to detail in character models, animations, and environments attests to the developers' commitment to excellence. Rarely do I encounter a game that not only raises the bar for modern graphics in the genre but also seamlessly integrates nostalgic elements and fun gameplay, making it a unique and enjoyable experience for long-time fans.What truly pushed me to share my thoughts is the game's story mode, a cinematic journey that prompted me to turn off the lights for an immersive experience—a rarity in my gaming habits. Tekken 8's compelling narrative is a testament to the effort invested in creating a truly memorable gaming experience.Now, as I wrap up this review, it's time to immerse myself in the next phase—some lab seshs to explore and find the character that resonates with me. With a game this exceptional, multiplayer awaits, and the quest to find the perfect main character for epic showdowns is the next thrilling chapter. Tekken 8 has not only earned its place in my library but has ignited a new enthusiasm for the journey that lies ahead.

_childDocuments_.review: Modern fighting game that keeps improvingFinal Score: 8/10+ Incredible graphics, art direction and effects+ While I think the PC version should be optimized further, it gets better and better+ Continuous support with life updates+ Incremental improvements in terms of matchmaking and balance changes+ Team Tekken Project are very responsive and adaptive when it comes to community feedback+ Players of all skill levels can get through the Dojo and Tekken Lounge arcades to learn the game step by step+ Improved practice and replay mode+ Faster matchmaking, respectively, improvements are made in that field+ Great roster with 3 new faces+ Quality single player content, i.e story mode with 4k quality cutscenes+ Amazing main menu+ Jukebox. You can change the music for all stages and different menus. This has to be the greatest feature ever for me+ The quality for paid costumes and items have improved. I'm talking specifically about new and T8 exclusive items. They usually come in a pack, in which you can buy them. For instance the Halloween pack and Samurai outfits are amazing. Simple but yet awesome. You don't need to buy them of course, completely up to you. - The game can get too aggressive and you will find yourself guessing a lot. 50/50 situations are very common.Generally speaking, the game made improvements compared to Tekken 7 but it also made some steps back.Tekken 8's emphasize lies on aggression. This results into fast, chaotic and energy draining gameplay. It can get very exhausting due to the aggressive nature. - The HEAT mechanics are way over the top. When people discuss about it, they often leave out the fact that both players, also experienced and pro players have access to this feature and of course they make use of it! Some characters have better heat signature moves than others. - Stage hazards deliver my body to the opponents silver platter and there is nothing I can do. (The developers have cut down the damage values but it is still very annoying). - A lot stages are simply too small. This results into "wall carries" and it is very difficult to get out of there. - The battle pass has to be one of the worst in the gaming industry, filled with filler items, simple stuff. Overall the quality is not there yet. - The customization seems limited compared to previous titles. A lot monetized and wearable items have been already featured in Tekken 7 etc, which were featured in the battle pass. - The overall balance need to improve and there is commitment from the developer to do that.I'm quite optimistic that things will improve over time. This game has a long time span and we can expect a lot of fixes, a lot new content and balance changes are on the way.Overall, give it a shot. New players or veterans of the series. You can enjoy a handful of modes and you're not restricted playing ranked mode only.

Broken gameplay & scummy MTX practices)(Tekken Rank - Fujin)Oh boy where do I even start...I was so fascinated by the game at launch & had loads of fun. 5 months pass by & I really started to realize how ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ♥♥♥♥ this game is. First things first, lets address the elephant in the room - the microtransactions. The fact that they had the NERVE to release a MTX shop like a month after launch gotta be one of the most scummy cash grab tactics I've ever seen in a videogame. It's a $70 game, mind you. There's no excuse in the book that could let this slide.Secondly, the horrendous gameplay. Like I said, I had a great time at launch. But then you start to realize how mash & panic friendly this game is. Heat is such a BROKEN mechanic that anyone can abuse at the start of the round for instant pressure by pressing one button. Oh, and it TRACKS. So you cannot sidestep it. You're forced to constantly block & block and hope to god one of the next moves are punishable on block. Why the ♥♥♥♥ do you have access to heat INSTANTLY? It literally acts like a comeback mechanic because it not only allows access to more powerful attacks (depending on the character, but also allows to do a special attack by pressing the heat button again which is PLUS frames, making it such a panic friendly button with little to no setbacks. The only good thing I can say about Heat is that you can extend combos with it. Going back to the point where I said this game is mash friendly. You can tell how beginner friendly this game is, hence the heat mechanic, but that's just part of it. Most characters have 1-2 button combo strings or jab strings you cannot escape, unless you power crush, press heat, or if you're lucky, sidestep. You're forced to play aggressive 24/7 & a player can just press random buttons to get a solid mixup on your opponent. It's so sad Harada made the game this way...the game just feels so unfun to play & probably the easiest fighting games to date....easier than Mortal Kombat and Smash Bros, no BS. No rental tickets like in Street Fighter 6, the replay tool doesn't let you take control of your character to practice against them. So you pay up, play against a friend/stranger that bought the character and lab against them or you just get destroyed, because Tekken is probably one of the knowledge check heaviest fighting games out there, so not being able to use the replay tool is scummy.Plugging has no real consequence either. You can just ALT+F4 if you lose your match to retain your rank. No Quitality type punishment like in Mortal Kombat, no yellow or red card queue like Street Figher 6. No forced loss for the plugger, no de-ranks, no loss on record, nothing. At least the disconnection rate display works now, so you can decline the match if the percentage is outrageous. Still there really needs to be a punishment for plugging, the integrity of ranked suffers immensely, because of the pluggers.The game itself plays really well, it's fun online and it has some nice tools to hand hold newcomers into the online experience. But it's still a fighting game, so if you have no prior competitive experience in the genre, be prepared for a steep learning curve. It's possible to improve at a decent pace though, if you play the game with a learning mindset. Balance is all over the place, but that doesn't matter for 95% of the playerbase, I wish I could actually recommend the game. Considering the MTX rugpull though, combined with the price tag of the base game, I just can't. Unless you're really desperate to play the newest Tekken, I'd either wait for a sale down the road or try one of the other fighting games out there, one that doesn't try to squeeze every single penny out of their playerbase.No MTX release score would've been a 8.5/10.My post launch MTX scum-score is a lenient 6/10.
