_childDocuments_.review: My negative review has nothing to do with the battle pass or the customization. The game in its current state just isn't worth playing. I guess this was to be expected given Namco's history of releasing the 1st version on arcade before bringing it to console but it feels like they learned nothing from the feedback people provided for T7. The balance in the game is a joke and despite a few patches, the developers still really haven't addressed any of the major offenders. The new Heat system is obnoxious and changes to pre-existing systems (ie: power crushes, throws, movement) have completely changed the gameplay for the worse. We complained about Rage Arts and Rage Drives in T7 so, instead of getting rid of these mechanics, what did Namco do? They effectively gave every character multiple Rage Drives and made Rage Arts safer on block. We asked for movement to be buffed back in T7 and what did Namco do? They nerfed backdashing, "buffed" lateral movement but then made all throws homing and changed multiple strings that were steppable in the past to no longer be steppable. We complained about power crushes in T7 and what did Namco do? They made the armor on these moves activate 2 frames faster and gave damn near every character a Heat engage power crush that is safe on block but high. The netcode is also a crapshoot. If you have crossplay turned on, prepare to play laggy matches against console players on wifi. If you turn crossplay off, prepare to play laggy matches against players with PCs that can't run the game properly. If you change the connection setting to only match you against 5 bars, prepare to see "Connection did not meet requirements" over and over and play against the same few players over and over. Did you like deathmatching in the previous games to assist with learning matchups or just because you wanted to play the same player again? Too bad. Everything is FT2, even in quick match. The only positive things in this game are the new replay features and the graphics (and the graphics are probably why the online feels like ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥). If the patch that is supposed to drop after Evo Japan does nothing to alleviate the issues this game has, then I guess we'll have to wait 2 years for the game to actually be in a decent state just like people did with Tekken 7's arcade release.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit:After a recent big Patch there has been a lot of positive changes that in my opinion really improve the overall feel of the game. Most command-grabs no longer being homing, Heat-Burst being less silly and overall nerfs of overly reliable moves like all the strongest powercrushes and neutral-dominating tools like the various demon-paws being adjusted in general really makes me optimistic about tekken 8 going forward. The game is in a really good place now overall. The annoying monetization is obviously still there, but the game is in a place know that it should have been in at release, so I can now actually recommend the game. I will still leave all my prior thoughts as a reminder of how the game was released and my thoughts on the first couple of terrible patches.Obviously not everything is perfect, some character-specific balance-choices might still be off, even though thats mostly subjective at the end of the day. I will state as an example at the time of writing this, Paul changes might have been too much and he might emerge as the new big bad of the game, but I still do not feel like its as silly as the top characters after the first few weeks. Perfect balance is not a goal one should strive for anyway. The most important part was figuring out how the heat-system needed to be adjusted and I feel like the developers nailed it for the most part. Heat still being character-specific will continue to be a hard problem to solve, but I believe in the devs to figure it out for the most part. Looking forward to really put in the time in tekken in the coming months.----old review----TLDR: Developer and publisher are messing up in a variety of ways. Can not recommend at the moment. Great at its core, foundation for a very good, if not the best entry into the series.First of all, if you really liked Tekken 7, you might not like Tekken 8 as much, as there have been sweeping system changes. But then again, in that case you most likely already bought the game.The gameplay can be frustrating at times with buffed throws and powerful armour-options being a big part of almost any match. This game is a lot about turn-stealing and offense. Particularly heat-bursts are way too powerful, as intended counterplay simply does not beat them a lot of the time.I am mostly on-board with the gameplay changes on paper. Tekken 7 was a non-interactive game at times. By buffing offense, this has been salvaged from being a boring turtle-fest to complex interactions when playing at a high level. This is a good thing in my opinion. You will not win by just backdashing in this game. Good stuff. Defense is still very strong and important, but its not the correct way to play at all times anymore. Tournaments will be wild.Other than that, balancing is quite off on the very best and very worst characters, but its not as bad as people say. The heat-system needs some adjusting. Some characters chip to much, some characters will run you over when in heat. Waiting to see if the balance patch in may brings the best characters down a notch and the worst up a bit to even the playing field, while adjusting the system-mechanics to not overly dominate the flow of the game in some matchups. Heat should matter, but its power is very unevenly distributed among the cast.The ranked mode has some problems. If you already own the game or are going to buy it in spite of all the bad reviews lately, I would recommend prioritizing custom lobbys with your friends or local events. Matchmaking in ranked has been recently messed with, in a bad way. You will be getting matched using the ominous Tekken-Prowess, which defeats the purpose of per-character rank and just make queue-times longer. It also is optimal now to play just one character to get to a high rank.Plugging is still quite rampant, even though there is an easy fix. This is not a problem in sf6, as leaving a match results in a loss. Bandai Namco are insentivising cheating by not implementing this. It would be better if that system is wrong(sometimes) than the current state of things.Overall, ranked can be pretty easily fixed, but so far, the developers approach has been baffling.Netcode is alright most of the time. Mostly good job! Bad delay-based Netcode made tekken 7 a pretty bad online-experience. This has been salvaged for the most part. Rollback is not implemented flawlessly here, but I get that in a game where you can cancel movement into all other movement at any time makes it harder.The Tekken-Community needs to fully emprace the ethernet cable though. Most issues come from wireless connections. Get a cable y'all.The developers also did a great job for training mode and the best replay feature in all FG's at the time of writing this. There are also pretty great learning ressources in-game when you check out the offline-modes. Good stuff. Not charging extra for frame-data anymore.I have also experienced a lot of crashes, though as of writing this, I have been playing for hours without any crash. Seems to be an issue in general with AMD GPU's.Biggest problem for me at the moment though has to be the downright insulting monetization thats taking place in tekken 8. They sneaked in a Tekken-Shop and a battlepass after getting good reviews for launch. After this they started releasing DLC-Characters at above industry-standard pricing. There is a kind of season pass when upgrading to a more costly version of the game, giving you early access but costing more than 4 characters when buying seperately. This is not okay. 9€ for a character with a 40€ "season-pass" is downright insulting (for 4 characters you pay EXTRA for early access and useless stuff essentially).I love playing the game but have not bought the first DLC. By not paying 9€, I am not able to go into training mode with eddy. Some of the amazing replay-features are also stripped away when looking at replays against DLC you do not own.Me not recommending the game mostly comes down to the choices made when it comes to monetization, as well as overall bad updates since launch. Patches have broken the parts of the game on several occasions since release, some things have been improved to be in an okay spot now.Quality-control needs to be figured out for this game to have a chance long-term. Hoping for the best as well as a 30€ season-pass.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: PSA for all PC players on keyboard, try mapping 1234 (punches and kicks) to keys on the same row, so you can use all 4 fingers at the same time without moving. Controllers will never make sense to me in a game that requires you to flow between button combinations.Ghost AI of other players. That's the best feature of the game. Even if you are shy and intimidated by the game's hardcore reputation, you can play alone in Acrade Quest and button mash in offline for hours of fun before the difficulty goes up and you start thinking about looking up and practicing normal combos. Then you notice walls are a problem so you look up wall combos. Then counter-hit combos etc. I am no serious fighting game player, but the gradual transition towards higher-level play, all while offline, was so smooth. Winning against ghosts gave me confidence as well, and by the time I joined ranked online play, apart from connection spikes, I was already winning. I recommend the youtube video called "Learning Any Character ~ Tekken 7" from Zug to understand the fundamentals of the series. 10 frames for a jab, ~15 frames for a launch, that kind of thing always seemed too intimidating to learn, but they come naturally with a well-featured Practice mode that lets you try punishing enemy moves, and a helpful Replay mode where you can review your mistakes and retry mid-replay. I am a convert.

name: Pine Hearts
detailed_description: Welcome to Pine Hearts Caravan Park! As Tyke, hop into your hiking boots and explore the paths and rivers of this cosy little world. Rummage around the park and find handy tools that will help you on your journey as you fill out your trusty hillwalking journal. Rediscover memories of Tyke's time in the park many summers ago and unearth the heartfelt story of his childhood. 👩‍🌾 Make new friends 🛠️ Unlock tools and abilities 🏕️ Rediscover memories 🐶 Pet cute dogs Every inch of the park has little surprises waiting for you to discover! A Touching Tale Pine Hearts is a warm, thoughtful game about love, life, memories, and family. It tells a story of the loss of a family member with tenderness and care, but please be aware of this subject matter before playing the game ❤️ Wholesome Classics Pine Hearts takes the item-based progression of Zelda, combines it with Souls-like level design and wraps it all up in a wholesome aesthetic with a focus on puzzles, not combat 🌳 No Barriers To Play We’ve worked hard to make Pine Hearts as accessible as possible. Some of the key Accessibility features include: Simplified Controls Colour Blocking Mode Black and White Mode High Contrast Mode Visual FX Toggles Font Scaling Full Controller/KB+M Remapping

_childDocuments_.review: is a short and cozy exploration game with a small emotional story to guide you along the way.From an isometric perspective, you control a cute and colorful nugget character as he wanders the tranquil world of Pine Hearts Caravan Park, meets various NPCs and helps them with their tasks. The map is rather vast and the game is heavily focused on exploring it, as there are no quest markers (neither to distinguish the NPCs that can give you a quest from the rest of the NPCs, nor for the items you are required to fetch), nor a detailed map of all paths possible. Available is only a top-level map of the game world that displays the regions, but not the connections between them or any other details such as paths or points of interest.However, the game is split into distinctive regions, and accessing them requires obtaining a specific ability, which is unlocked by gathering enough “droplets”. These can be obtained not only by completing quests but also by interacting with various objects in the game world or simply collecting them from your path, as you explore the maze-like environment. Without a map, navigating the world is not exactly trivial (especially for those without a clear sense of direction like me), as you have to project the zones visited in your mind and obviously remember their location, together with which NPC gives you which quest. Unfortunately, only the quests belonging to the main storyline are shown and not the side quests (which are encountered in much higher numbers than the former).While I could think of several QoL features that I would like to see in the game, I’m deeply appreciative of how much effort was put into accessibility options. There are several color palettes to choose from, and the interactable objects (including the NPCs) are brightly colored to distinguish them from the muted colors of the environment. To be honest, this was extremely helpful to me during the end game (even if I don’t have any disabilities) for gathering those last difficult-to-find droplets required for the hardest achievement of the game: gathering all 1500 of them. While roughly 1300 are obtained through quests and from wandering around, the last ~200 come from object interactions or other areas reachable only after unlocking all abilities. The map is also designed so that even the early zones contain areas accessible only with fully unlocked abilities, thus a full traversal through the entire map will be required for this achievement. I would have really liked to see from which of these zones I can still collect droplets, as opposed to wandering around aimlessly until I find something to interact with, but unfortunately, this information is not available to the player. The rest of the achievements are naturally unlocked as you play and complete quests. None of them are missable, as you can always return to the previous zones to obtain them and they’re color-coded based on the region they belong to, which is quite helpful.’ story is not the one that drives the gameplay forward, as it consists only of five miniature memories of the character and his father. However, they’re quite emotional and are bound to touch your heart, even if they’re short-lived. These memories, together with all the cute interactions that you can do with the objects in the environment and the colorful, positive visuals give the game a heartfelt, wholesome vibe.  is certainly a chill and enjoyable ride that will take you between five and seven hours to complete, depending on how much you like to dawdle, yet pretty expensive for the content that it offers.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not sure why  hasn't had more publicity. I was surprised to see that it only has 41 reviews so I wanted to write a nice review about it because I really enjoyed the game, and you will too if you like exploration and quests. Straight away from the train journey into Pine Hearts you will get cosy and heart-warming vibes just from the upbeat music and colourful graphics. Of course, everyone is super friendly in Pine Hearts and it is the sort of place where you would probably like to live, with camaraderie abundant to see, and loads of colourful characters to meet who are more than happy to lay all their chores on you. The game is very much quest based, performing tasks for people who have mislaid something, or want something delivered, or want you to collect items to fix something. You know how it goes. The characters are very interesting and you will spot connections between them which gives a nice community feel to the game. Often, you walk into situations where people are socialising or performing goofy stuff which will make you smile. Just interacting with everyone is fun because they will either give you a quest or have a humorous answer. It's definitely a feel-good game. Even though some characters do briefly show you where items are, with the camera shooting off to their location and back, you have to pay attention as there is no second chance, although occasionally characters will remind you of your task if you ask again. There’s also an active quest reminder in your journal but it just tells you what the quest is and gives no other information. Completing quests earns you equipment which is needed to progress and also gives you droplets which is sort of the currency in the game. You will need to collect enough droplets to unlock memories which in turn give you extra skills. There are four skills to collect and learn which open up areas which would have been previously inaccessible. The skills are climbing, jumping, moving blocks, and pushing trees to bridge gaps. All these skills are easy to perform but you will have to action a simple sequence of button pushes and thumb stick movement to do these. Personally, I would have just preferred pressing one button to action these skills as it felt a little frustrating going through the motions of pressing ‘A’ then ‘up’ on the thumb stick or similar. There was no challenge in doing the sequence so why bother? Game play is arranged so that early on quests are manageable with the equipment you already own but you will notice that lots of areas are inaccessible because they are blocked by rocks or chasms or need to be reached through climbing. These areas get unlocked by completing quests and earning enough droplets to unlock a memory which gives you a skill. Pine Hearts is reasonably big and although there is a very crude map there are no quest locators or any other help to aid you in finding characters or items you need. This means you will be doing a lot of backtracking, hitting brick walls, and getting lost. Your main tool will be your memory and remembering shortcuts and how areas fit together. There can be a lot of time saved through shortcuts, like a fallen tree saving you going around the long way, but there will always be a path to adjacent areas. Getting lost is a source of frustration but I guess if everything was laid out for you it would be too easy. There is a small story which plays out as you unlock memories and is quite poignant and sad. There are five memory clips, but because they are spaced out throughout the game they can be easily forgotten, but for such a brief story it leaves quite a powerful impression and ties together quests and stories you may have heard throughout the game and brings everything together. _childDocuments_.review: 7 hours 3/10 1 I wrote . No No Maybe the 1500 collectibles, finding the last ones you're missing can be a challenge No No No No No, you can use the accessibility features freely and still unlock everything NoSometimes you instantly fall in love with a game in the first 30 minutes. Pine Hearts did this for me! When the game starts and your first quest is to pet the dog, it is a great start! And after that, it only got better and better. However, I also want to mention that Pine Hearts has very emotional moments. It is based on the creative developer losing his dad in a very short time and while the game is wholesome it also touches on the sad feelings of losing your dad. The implementation of those feelings is done in such a beautiful way. I can imagine how challenging the development must have been with a project so close to his heart, but the love and beautiful memories he has shines through the game and I hope it also helped focus on those beautiful memories. So why did I fall in love so quickly? It starts with how cute this game looks and there went so much attention to detail. What I love about that is how they highlight all those little details by making it reward you with collectibles.  Do you see a crab with a crow? Pet it to get a collectible! Do you see a sea otter? wave at it to get a collectible. There are canons broken? Fix them to get a collectible. What is also implemented in a great way is the interactions you do with a controller for each interaction you want to do. There is a headlight and it can run out of battery, then you have to take it off your head and recharge it by rotating your left thumbstick. If you want to dig you pick up your shovel and first press the left thumbstick down and then press it up.  If you don't like this or can't do this, the accessibility settings have the option to turn this off and have simple controls. Speaking about the accessibility settings, there are so many great settings in this menu. For example, there is the option to standard run, or standard walk, or switch between them with a button press. There also is an option to highlight all the interactive things so it is easier to differentiate between things that are for show and things that are important to the game. It is so nice when a developer wants to include everybody and find ways to implement accessibility features to make the game playable for a wider audience.Another thing that I love about Pine Hearts is how it uses the Steam achievements to challenge you to do more and find more things to do than the main quest line. Almost every easter egg and little activity is tied to an achievement and this way a lot of people will get to see everything in the game. It is also done well how the achievements are color-coded and by seeing which color you're missing you can know in which area to look for it. And it gets major bonus points for not having missable achievements, so you really can just walk around and find everything for yourself without worrying about missing out on something. The only downside the game had for me is that there is an achievement to find all 1500 collectibles, without knowing in which area of the game you're missing some. I was lucky with this achievement. I had looked at most places, so I only missed 3 at the end of the game, and I could deduct which area I had not looked hard enough and quickly get them that way, but it can be such a struggle and annoyance to find those last ones without a clue where to look. luckily the accessibility feature to highlight interactive things is very helpful when walking around looking for those last few collectibles. I highly recommend Pine Hearts and give it a 4,5 out of 5 stars.

_childDocuments_.review: Another "wholesome adventure", similar in style to A short hike and Lil Gator Game, where you solve various problems for the people around you while you work towards your main goal (in this case it's actually the same as in A short Hike, to climb a mountain). It's a pleasant couple of hours (my playtime got a bit inflated due to having to restart), but i really enjoyed it.  But there where quite a few glitches that need to be resolved, nothing outright gamebreaking, and i'm sure they will be fixed in time, the game hasn't been out that long and the devs are active in the forums awnsering bug reports. 1) Some places where there is a hotspot where you interact with a tool are invisible. The key prompt is there, but the graphics for what you interact with isn't (for me it was a message in a bottle) it is marked on your map so you will be able to find it but it's stil anoying. 2) One minor quest in one area glitched out several times in a row, because i accidentally skiped a step and went directly to the solution, you have to restart the game and do the quest correctly and it will work. 3) The most significant one is that it's possible to sequence break the game. This only matters if you want to 100% the game, you are not locked out of finishing it. But if you start the quest in another area before finishing the one in your quest log you will not get a reward when you actually finish the quest, making it so that you will be short of the 1500 drops that you need for the completionist achievement. I'm not suire if this happens in more than one area, but it does in the Castle at least. That said, the glitches aside, this was a cute little adventure and I very much enjoyed my time with the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Pine Hearts is a cute and quaint little adventure game that reminded me of my childhood favourites such as Scooby doo Night of 100 frights for the PS2. which is ironic due to the nature of Pine Hearts narrative surrounding early-life memory's. I found the gameplay simple yet engaging, collecting different tools to unlock new areas for exploration and NPC's to discover provided more of a thrill than I was anticipating. Searching every nook and cranny for the necessary 1500 tears achievement was a little annoying, but nothing i'd deduct points for as I 100% Pine Hearts in about 7 hours of gameplay. (provided sitting in main menu doesn't register as steam playtime as I was AFK to do house chores.)The Main story of our protagonist Tyke is told through a series of Charming Animatics that convey to us the reason for tykes venture to the park and the emotional significance of his journey of which I won't spoil but will say that I thoroughly enjoyed and said story hit me in the feels. The Music Supplements the gameplay perfectly as each area of the Pine Hearts park has a unique song that play's on a loop during your questing. I worried that listening to such music for hours on end might irritate me but fortunately the music doesn't outstay its welcome, And of course, there is music that tugs on the heart strings during the games more serious moment's. If the developers of Pine Hearts ever attempted this type of game in the future I'd like to see more puzzles, riddles and perhaps some PG combat to spice up gameplay as though there were instances of gameplay diversity throughout pine hearts such as the lawnmower and sowing section the core gameplay loop of walking around to pick up items can get a bit repetitive. Overall Pine Hearts was a lovely experience that I recommend to anyone who desired a palate cleanser from real life woes and would grade this game an 85/100.

_childDocuments_.review: I played a demo of this game at EGX last year and have had it on my wishlist ever since - Tyke's waddle was the hook. So far I've been really surprised at how much more content there is than I expected, I've unlocked 4 areas of the map and the variety in scenery has been really nice, plus plenty of mini missions, lots of characters to talk to, and background animations that are funny if you take the time to stop and watch what the animals/characters/objects do when you're not directly interacting with them.The game is immediately charming and the main character (Tyke) so endearing that even though I've only unlocked 2 memories so far (about 50 droplets off the third) my heart broke seeing baby Tyke cry. Again, his waddle is also solid.I can see myself working through this game in 1 hour chunks over the next few weeks the same way I have so far. It's chill and casual and sometimes it's nice just to waddle around and enjoy the bright scenery.

_childDocuments_.review: I’ve written probably ten review drafts of this title and none of them seem to do it justice. So back to basics. Buy it. This is a beautiful game that manages to incorporate the complexity of losing someone into a wholesome, heartfelt narrative adventure game. Do tasks for the adorable people of Pine Hearts, grow emotionally and skill up. I am trying to avoid all spoilers with my wording here, because you must experience this beautiful story yourself. Technically speaking Pine Hearts feels crafted with love. The graphic design is cute and lighthearted, the music is just perfection, the story is a delight. It also has some clever accessibility options. A mix of mini games, light puzzles and NPC quests (the bulk of the game), Pine Hearts will take you on a relaxing, fun and at times, tear jerking adventure. Purchase it, it’s a rare gem of a game. Oh and I love how it leans into its Scottishness. I lived in Dundee for many years and this made me smile ear to ear. Bravo devs.

Your goal is to climb the mountain, but in order to even start your journey, you have to prove yourself. This game was wonderful from the sound track to the characters to the quests. I enjoyed everything about it. On top of that, the story was extremely touching as someone who has experienced loss before. Highly recommend!

(not for shortcuts)thise would be okay if it was just for shortcuts or get to a new area,but to get to a new area i had to first break a rock then climb 2 walls then cut a tree down then break another rock and then push a tree over. (and this is not the first time it seems to get worse the more powers you get)so while i do give it a positive i recomend if you buy it play with simple controlls.TLDR: good game, too many checks, play with simple controlls

_childDocuments_.review: Highly Recommend!!!Where to start when writing a review for Pine Hearts....In short: amazing looking game, smooth game play and great sounding soundtrack that hits you right in the feels.Longer version:What drew me to the game was the cute art style and the promise of a cosy experience (and ofc dogs to pet helps a lot too).This however did not prepare me for the gorgeously written story and the way it was brought. It was an emotional roller coaster based on one of the devs his story but it resonated deeply with me.Game play is fairly simple, lots of running back and forth collecting things and giving them to people. Pretty decent size map to do this on (don't be like me and not realise you have a zone map till almost the end of the game) with lots of extra's to find.Everything from the art style to the soundtrack, the story and the gameplay just made sense and made for a great experience so do yourself a favour and pick up this game!

_childDocuments_.review: Pine Hearts is a wonderful game teeming with personality. _childDocuments_.review: Pine Hearts A Cute and Emotional Adventure that is very charming and was a genuine joy to play. There are a total of seven areas of the map to discover and as you do you unlock memories of you past time in the Pine Hearts Park moving the main story forward. There are a ton of side quests in each area so I recommend you take the time to speak with everyone you meet and give them a hand.I very much enjoyed the art style of this game and found it really lended well to the relaxing cosy outdoor vibes. The soundtrack is very calming as well and changes for each area you can explore. Each area is also well designed and enjoyable to move through and don’t feel the same. Pine Hearts is an itsy-bitsy, open-world puzzle game! Explore the sleepy scenery of Pine Hearts Caravan Park as you uncover items, unlock new paths, and discover all the little secrets stuffed throughout the Park.

name: Promenade
detailed_description: In Promenade you have to collect golden cogs to fix the great elevator and unlock new worlds. To do so, you can engage with a bunch of diverse activities, like puzzles, races, cute NPCs, and many secrets scattered everywhere by using a dynamic moveset. Whether you like puzzles that require lateral thinking, technical platforming, or just wandering around, there's always something interesting awaiting for you around the corner. Use object's properties to your advantage : double jump by throwing an object down, glide when holding a chicken, run at insane speed with the rocket and a lot more to experiment ! And since you only need to collect some of the cogs to progress, you can follow your instinct and only engage with what interests you the most. Will it be platforming challenges ? Interacting with colorful characters ? Or facing the bosses that dwell in dungeons ? Wether you're a completionist, a cozy gamer, a speedrunner or a collectathon lover, you'll find your way to finish the game the way you like !

_childDocuments_.review: Promenade is a hidden gem amongst its platformer genre and its cute graphics should not be confused with it being a kids-only game.  Featuring extremely variable, challenging gameplay and smart puzzles with new mechanics introduced constantly, it always managed to keep me on the edge of my seat.There is not much of a story in the game. You fall into a watery cave and are saved by a cute octopus-like creature. This creature then joins you on your mission to repair the Great Elevator. Each time you repair a level, more cogs are scattered across the map for you to find.As I said in the introduction, Promenade is most definitely not just for kids, the gameplay is fairly challenging. Don’t let the cute aesthetic fool you! The core mechanic is that you can double jump once you’re holding something. This can be enemies or any random object that you can pick up. This will then propel the object down, thereby elevating you upwards. A double jump (when done in mid air). This simple, but unique premise evolves over time and there are constant new changes being introduced that help keep gameplay fresh and exciting. These jumps sometimes also need to be chained to reach high places, so grab something, jump, swing off a hook and then quickly grab another floating enemy in the air to propel yourself even higher. Falling does not result in any damage (as long as you land on the ground) but you will need to start climbing from the beginning again.While the protagonist does have a health bar, it refills at constant checkpoints and the game is fairly forgiving when you do die, or fall off the edge. Typically respawning you on the last solid ground you were at before.The main goal is to collect each of the parts of the cogs to be able to power up the elevator and get to the next phase. The cog parts can be found all over the place, with some easier to obtain than others. Some may be behind a large puzzle section and a boss fight, whereas others you may just be able to climb up a few obstacles to nab. Not all cog parts need to be done to progress the game, there are many extras here for completionists or achievement hunters to enjoy.I never knew what was around the corner in Promenade. Boost yourself through the level while riding a rocket, swing from chimpanzees hands, corral the chickens back in the coop, complete gravity puzzles or travel through space. The game is absolutely jam packed with creativity and many of the puzzles were exceptionally well designed and I could not help but admire the developers  ideas.This is the only part of the game that made me a tad frustrated but it is not necessarily a fault of the game. There are no indicators telling you where the remaining cog parts are, or where you have already been. There is a journal page that will tick off completed levels, but the universe is exceptionally large that I found it difficult to remember where things were, or how to get there again. I spent far too long aimlessly wandering around trying to find areas I hadn’t been to yet, or trying to find that one area by the beginning of the game that I need to return to. This is definitely a personal preference, or perhaps an accessibility feature, but it would be nice to be able to be shown some directions, or even a map when completely lost.The world of Promenade is undeniably wholesome, boasting its light, pastel aesthetic and cute creatures. There are no weapons, and you cannot kill any of the enemies. You can pick them up and throw them, but they will respawn shortly after and are the main way to traverse.There is no voice acting but the cheery upbeat soundtrack reminded me of older style platformers like Kirby. Each time you locate a cog, a little flute tune will play, representing a sort of congratulations, you did it! Did I mention the game was wholesome? 5 – 10 hours for a playthrough, but there is much content to discover to keep you going for double that. Yes, definitely. Yes, the game is brimming with things to do, especially for completionists.Promenade is a top-quality platformer that is bursting with creativity. From its smart puzzles, engaging and everchanging gameplay to its whimsical world, there is just so much to love here.  Its looks can be deceiving, and it is definitely more challenging than its cute graphics let on. I highly recommend this for all platformer fans.

_childDocuments_.review: The most wholesome puzzle platformer I've ever played. Calling it a platformer is totally dismissive of what the game is. Sure, there is a lot of platforming, tight precision trials that will take you to your wits' ends, and boss fights, but there is so much more! It has puzzling, platforming, exploring, adventure, all in a very beautiful, child-friendly presentation.So, you play as Nemo, a young boy who fell down a long tunnel into a fantastic realm. You are rescued by, and befriend a little poulp (baby octopus). The goal is to fix the big elevator to get back up into the real world. In order to do that, you must find cog pieces scattered throughout the world, awarded after accomplishing something.  And the tasks you can do are so diverse! You'll have to cook some food, learn to juggle, do a little dance, help two snails have a romantic lunch together, overcome your fear of darkness, play Breakout and Pong and other retro games, water the plants, gather the chickens, do a sneaky bank heist, race a penguin, catch ghosts, paint pretty pictures, look for hidden treasure, brave a thunderstorm... There are literally  more than a hundred things to do. Some of them are obvious and easy, some require good precision platforming, some require deep exploration, some require a lot of lateral thinking. There's nothing like that feeling you get after finally figuring out the secret recipe, or the hidden house, or the peculiar list, or if you're more into platforming than puzzling, beating a timed trial.The elevator goes through many floors, each with its own theme: a sandy beach, space, a flowery garden, a temple full of monkeys, a mountain, an office building, snow, a haunted house, a thunderstorm. And each level teaches you something new about what you can do, with a trial course focused on a specific mechanic, from simple moving and jumping, using paper airplanes or rockets to fly, using objects to double/triple jump... To me, these don't feel like obstacles to overcome, but more like lessons being taught. They aren't in the way, blocking all progress, but after you complete the trials, you can better navigate the rest of the game.Other than the game contents, the presentation is superb. The graphics are very nice, cartoony but beautiful, the different worlds are well designed, the controls and mechanics are well done, beautiful sounds and music, plus a lot of extra features that make it a good modern game. Moderate, not too hard but not too easy. To reach the first end, you only need to collect a little over half of the cogs, so you don't really have to do all the hard things, except that you must finish at least five boss levels to get to the end. Timed trials are optional, but reaching the second end requires collecting almost all cogs and beating a few really really tough trials. At least 10 hours. I've really enjoyed it for more than 30 hours already, and I didn't yet try to speedrun it. Superb! Excellent! Excellent presentation, good UX, plenty of settings, multiple save slots, good Steam integration with cloud save, excellent achievements (including a few for speedrunning), Steam Deck support. A few bugs encountered that are being patched. Yes. Looking for secrets. I'm not really a fan of precision platforming, so that would be  most negative aspect, but that's not a bad thing about the game itself.,  and their new remakes, which this game reminded me of with its jump and roll mechanics, and the hunt for secrets., beautiful platforming with a lot of focus on puzzles., beautiful platforming/metroidvania with a lot more fighting, but also clever exploration.

_childDocuments_.review: While researching to add the appropriate links to my youtube video I came across their website where it says; "4 enthusiasts who want to create a unique video game experience". _childDocuments_.review: Amazing puzzle platformer that is a joy to play due to constant influx of new things.The story start when a kid falls into a cavern filled with water. Before he drowns, a little octopus appears out of nowhere and rescues him. They quickly became buddies. Everything is seen rather than told, therefore the majority of the enjoyment stems from the wonderful cartoon-like animations.The overall goal of the game is to take the large elevator to the top. However, the kid's evil side is attempting to thwart you by destroying cogs. This occurs with each new floor you reach. So your task is to build a new cog by completing short puzzles and challenges that reward you with cog parts. One cog requires three little parts.Because the game takes place in a dream-like realm, you are able to go to many locations. It looks great in motion since there are just enough details on the screen to not detract from the gameplay. It never gets dull because you are continuously seeing new places and encountering new inhabitants of this world. Although the octopus will rescue you if you fall in the water, or you’ll reappear immediately if you drop into a hole, you can still fail. If the kid loses all five hearts, you will respawn at the beginning of the stage. But don't worry; there are hammocks everywhere that will heal you.This is a platformer with puzzle components, so expect a lot of jumping. Although the child's only abilities are to jump once and roll, his octopus companion can assist him with the most essential actions. This involves flinging your friend at opponents or items. Once you have the enemy in your hands, you can hurl it at something or use it to double jump. Of course, you aren't limited to a double jump because you can jump whenever you have something in your hands. Enemies respawn after two to three seconds, so you won’t waste time waiting for them. Another octopus’ strength you will gain later is the ability to grip onto hooks. The game focuses on challenges and riddles. The imagination and fun factor are high because you never know what you're going to have to do next. You might have to protect a snail from cannon fire so he can reach a bowl of spaghetti, carry a jigsaw puzzle to finish the picture, bring chickens to a pen, jump inside a painting and match colours, battle a boss, and so on. Obviously, the majority of challenges involve platforming, and there are some that repeat, like the penguin that wants to race.All possible challenges by location are listed in your notebook; but you need to find the page first. Some problems require some extra work, while others must be solved twice. One of them is trials, which require you to complete a normal and time challenge that will put even the most die-hard platforming enthusiast to the test.One small annoyance I noticed is that puzzles reset when you switch locations. So if you do two steps out of three, you’ll have to do everything all over again unless you finish it. Another one is that since you’re always going higher, you’re bound to fall down. In this case, you need to climb up or ride the elevator. In the end, this is a one of those titles why I like indie games. It's simple to play, visually appealing, and will keep you entertained for a long time. I think it might be a hidden gem that many will overlook and discover much later. One warning: if you go into the game blind, the game has a bunch of achievements that are easy to miss. This might bother achievement hunters that like to take time exploring.

_childDocuments_.review: I play a lot of platformers. I love the genre, but it can have a lot of duds. Either games with repetitive mechanics or cheap deaths, or ones where the controls don't feel quite right or tight enough for the dexterity they demand.And then you have Promenade, a game that came seemingly out of nowhere and is the single best platformer I've played in years.The fact that this has only 86 reviews on steam right now is very troubling to me, because I hope it doesn't mean that it sold poorly. This game is a masterpiece.So what sets it apart? First of all, it's not structured like a traditional 2D platformer, but as something much more open. Think less metroidvania (a genre I'm not a fan of personally) and more Super Mario Odyssey but in 2D. A collectathon full of mini open worlds where collecting enough gears will allow you to progress to the next mini open world.Each level is absolutely stuffed full of charming secrets, fun mini games and platforming challenges that range from simple and quick to totally sweaty palm fodder. It's never excruciatingly difficult but maintains a good balance and is no pushover.I won't go on too long, but just be aware that Promenade is one of those rare platformers that has *almost* no flaws. It is incredibly charming and wholesome, oozes creativity and passion at every turn, controls well and feels amazing to play.There are two tiny problems:1. A few frustrating moments of cheap deaths (could probably count them on one hand)2. A "Unity stutter" problem that is fixed by locking your frame rate to a multiple of 50 (cap it to 60 fps on steam deck and you're golden).Play Promenade. Buy it on sale, buy it full price, just buy it. The best $20 I spent all year, and at 10 hours for basic completion plus a few side things, has plenty of content.
_childDocuments_.name: Promenade

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked good ol' collectathons and you kinda miss them, Promenade is for you. Holy Cap Studio not only fully understood the biggest games of this genre, but they also somehow find multiple new ways to let you enjoy it. Add the very pleasant and progressive moveset and it will be a pleasure to move the main character and his octupus throught the entire game.The artistic direction is wonderful but don't get it wrong : even while looking shimmering, the 100%-run will sometimes challenges you more than the cute animation might suggest.A tiny game full of creativity.

_childDocuments_.review: i dont know how this gem of a game isnt more popular. it was a joy from start to finish. tight platforming, great art style and music, and all around one of the best 2d platformers i have ever played. huge thanks to the devs on this one, promenade deserves all the praise. buy it and tell your friends. more people need to play this.
_childDocuments_.name: Promenade

_childDocuments_.review: This game is truely charming !The overall ambiance is incredibly enjoyable, with each area meticulously designed and uniquely themed yet seamlessly blending into the overall joyful atmosphere. The musics is great, perfectly complementing each environment and significantly enhancing the overall experience.Traversing through young Nemo's imaginary world briefly transported me back to those tender moments when every cloud seemed nothing more than a giant cotton candy.Moreover, the name of the game is a stroke of brilliance; it encapsulates the essence of the experience - a period of time specificly designed to enjoy what is surrounding you without any other aim than simply having a good time.
_childDocuments_.name: Promenade

_childDocuments_.review: This game is one of the best platformers I've ever played, and a truly innovative experience!For casual players, it's a very pleasant ride, and for speedrunners, everything is done to make our task easier, and the challenge is really stimulating.The music is very pleasant, the art direction super refreshing. I really recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Promenade

_childDocuments_.review: 100% the first world and onto the next... already feel compelled to write a review. Others have already likened it to klonoa but more dynamic, and pointed out how unique the experience is and I must second both of those things. It's a 2d platformer game like you haven't played before, and if you like 2d platformers, puzzle platformers, or 3d platformers then it is a must play. It obviously isn't 3d but follows the design philosophy of 3d platformer collectathons more than it follows the typical 2d platformer design - explore the open levels and collect away! It's an itch I developed since I played a smw rom hack "demo" with a similar idea, and I finally get to scratch it! It really makes me wonder why more 2d platformers haven't explored this type of design

_childDocuments_.review: I've finished the 4 first level 100% and I really love it so far :)Great work :)EDIT :I've finished a 100% playthought (Still need few steam achivement tho)Honestly as far as platformer goes, close to a masterpiece.Gameplay 10/10- Perfect difficulty scaling, and well brought- The endgame content is very hard, but definitly doable- Extremy accurate input management (when you fail, you know it's your bad)Art: 9/10- Cute DAAudio: 8/10- I love the music- SFX prety nice
_childDocuments_.name: Promenade

_childDocuments_.review: This game does what good games used to do: gives you a few well-polished core mechanics, then turns you loose in a world to explore and experiment. There's so much to discover here, you'll feel overwhelmed. But the good kind of overwhelmed, as the sense of wonder and excitement at having another nook or cranny to stick your head into never goes away. I'm genuinely impressed by how engaging, charming, and deep this game is.P.S. Steam Deck compatibility is great. I haven't had a single issue.
_childDocuments_.name: Promenade

_childDocuments_.review: It's been a while since I've picked up something I'd consider a hidden gem or something I've beaten the algorithm to play (last was probably Helltaker). Sure I've played some less known games before in modern time but I had never seen any discussion of this and seeing the trailer and the reviews on steam being in the double digits, my curiosity was peaked.WI went in thinking would it would be a nice looking Braid equivalent game but the game plays way more like a good translation of a 3D platformer collectathon onto the 2D plane. A while I was slightly worried at the beginning the controls would be stiff, they really become quite fluid and the slow walk becomes more justified when time trials become relevant. Although I had to think a bit, I had no issues doing what I wanted and finishing up the game when I wanted to. The music is also nice and breezy, in the style of a David wise, and I'll be adding the soundtrack to my personal collection if it's available.I think the key thing here is the 2D collectathon. I'm always looking for good ones to fit in between bigger games so If you like classic 3D collectathon, I'd recommend at least keeping your eye on this for a sale as i don't think I've found a better translation in 2D. Exceeded expectations.
_childDocuments_.name: Promenade

_childDocuments_.review: This game is criminally underappreciated, not by the people who have played it (look at the reviews and you'll see many more like my own), but by the enormous number of people who haven't. If you like collectathons, platformers, puzzlers, or just good video games, then you will enjoy Promenade. Give it a try. There was not a single moment that I was bored during my 16 hours of playtime. There were a handful of times I was a little annoyed (specifically the maze in the haunted house...), but bored? Never. There is always something to do, and those somethings are always right within reach. All you need to do is roll a little to the right or left and you will find another item to collect, another gap to leap across, another puzzle to solve, and always another. This is the type of game that makes you want to play it, not only because of the amount of things to do, but because of how crisp doing all of those things feels. There isn't much higher praise I can give than that. If your game makes me scroll through my probably-too-long list of installations, past the games I've already poured dozens of hours into and would gladly and mindlessly pour more, past the dozen other new games I have yet to open up and maybe never will, to its page, with that big green button that reads "Play," and even then, when I still have the chance to say "screw it, I'm just going to play some more Risk of Rain 2," even then, if I plug in my controller and hit play to return to your world and explore every inch of it, beating all the objectives and clearing all the achievements in the process, then you have made a darn good game. Even better than that, you have made a fun game. People don't play enough of those these days. Hats off to you guys and gals over at Holy Cap. I hope to play more games from you in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Promenade

_childDocuments_.review: I am genuinely shocked this game hasn't got more attention since its release earlier this year. This game consistently gives out Nintendo developer vibes through it's innovative puzzles and platforming mechanics that are always involving. Completed in around 10 hours but will definitely be going back to find the remaining pieces.The only real issue I encountered during my play through was the lack of fast travel to previously explored areas. The great elevator is good for travelling between larger worlds but I sometimes had a hard time finding a sub level where I was missing several cog pieces.Do not hesitate on purchasing this game and giving it a try. Works great on Steam Deck as well!
_childDocuments_.name: Promenade

_childDocuments_.review: I honestly don't have too much to say about this game other than it's good. It has a nice aesthetic, movement feels fluid, and the environments are varied enough to keep you interested all throughout your playthrough. Progression is achieved by solving simple puzzles or overcoming individual challenges to get the game's collectibles, which is where its correlation to Mario Odyssey comes from. I do think that some of the collectibles are more annoying to get than others, but majority of them are straightforward enough to figure out. As a minor complaint, I don't really care about the game's story; in fact, it's so unimportant that it might as well not even be in the game. Ignoring that, though, this is a really solid platformer and if you're a fan of collectathons, you might want to give this game a try.
_childDocuments_.name: Promenade

_childDocuments_.review: Very chill platformer. Nothing is really difficult but the different mechanics feel fresh.You can see how the game also has been thought of for speedrunning with many shortcut in level design and animation cut mechanics. Not the best game of all time but a 10/10 for what is trying to achieve. I can only recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Promenade

_childDocuments_.review: Don't let Promenade fool you, behind it's cute and artsy graphics lies a challenging platforming and puzzle game. Get on an adventure and master the different tools at your disposal to collect gears and climb up the great Elevator. Promenade is an adventure game that rewards exploration with a ton of hidden secrets that you'll get clues for by fetching the lost pages of a journal. With multiple areas to explore, each bringing their new set of ideas and mechanics to platform will make your journey to the top an exciting experience to find out what mysteries lies in this world. If you love to explore, some challenging platforming and cute octopuses then this gem is for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Promenade

_childDocuments_.review: SHORT VERSION:Promenade is a beautiful 2D collectathon platformer that excels in the creativity of its objectives. It's not particularly difficult, but the novelty of many of its goals kept me engaged. While there are optional challenges that tested my dexterity, I definitely recommend this to people who enjoy relatively easy and calming action games.LONG VERSION:MY PROGRESS:I've completed every level and gotten every item in the game. I also beat the developer times in every time trial.STRENGTHS:- CREATIVITYThis game had a lot of surprising twists and clever uses of its simple and accessible mechanics. Examples include grabbing a planet from a mobile and placing it on a star map so that you can hop in a spaceship and visit, carrying a puzzle piece to the place it fits in the background, or climbing frozen cliffs by making snowballs and throwing them down.WEAKNESSES:- SLOW WALKINGThere is a roll that gets you around a lot faster so I'd advise getting used to that quickly. Otherwise the basic walk is too slow for my taste.OTHER POINTS OF INTEREST:- LOW DIFFICULTYThis game is relatively easy, so it is generally a relaxing journey. However, there are some later levels and optional challenges that bumped up the difficulty. That said, there are better options if you want to be overwhelmed by controller-snapping rage.OVERALL:- This is platformer manages to be really creative in offering a variety of goals without being particularly difficult. If you're fairly new to platformers or just want to chill this is a strong recommendation.
_childDocuments_.name: Promenade

_childDocuments_.review: A rather delightful platformer that progresses in challenges and introduces new mechanics as you rise up through the giant elevator.  There are a handful of locations that feel a bit more puzzle oriented, but overall it's an immensely enjoyable journey through the game as you run into so many different locations.The platforming captures some of the best parts of Super Mario World and the grappling mechanic made me think of the original Bionic Commando.  The way you grab enemies to progress through the levels reminds me of Kirby's Dreamland.  In short, the game manages to pull some of the best parts out of classic platformers to give us a fun time.Graphically the game feels like it's going to be pretty memorable many years from now.  It has a slight Adventure Time look to it, but I think the game stays pretty unique visually throughout.  There's a great amount of love and care put into this game, and it's a platformer that is absolutely worth playing.
_childDocuments_.name: Promenade

_childDocuments_.review: When I first played the demo, I was unimpressed by it. The art style was nice, and I liked the idea of a 2D platformer playing like a collectathon 3D platformer, but the moment to moment gameplay wasn’t amazing. The main character moved too slowly for my liking, the music of the pirate level was underwhelming, and I disliked how throwing enemies at enemies wasn’t as fun as in any of the Klonoa games. But given that the game was the only 2D platformer I ever played outside Klonoa to have a “pick up enemy and use them as a double jump” mechanic, I gave it a wishlist. I thought it could be better when fully released.After playing the game for a bit, I’m shocked by how clever it is. The puzzle design is way better than I expected and once you learn how to use the roll for speed (and unlock the grapple hook type ability), the platforming is fun to master. I would still like a pure run button (needing to do a roll for a speed boost is fine but feels more complex than I would like) because the default walk is slow.The level design is good, the platforming is fun, and the puzzles that require rethinking how to get one thing from one side of a level to another make me feel like I’m smart. Highly recommend to anyone who is a fan of 2D platformers. While I wasn’t impressed by the demo, I still highly recommend playing it to get a good idea on the type of game it is.
_childDocuments_.name: Promenade

_childDocuments_.review: I had LOTS of fun playing this game! It's full of surprises and secrets, and it is a good challenge to get all the cogs!If you liked the demo, it just gets better and better!It'd be really good though if the devs managed to fix the stuttering of the background when it moves. It required some concentration to kinda stop being annoyed by it.
_childDocuments_.name: Promenade

_childDocuments_.review: The game's art style gives me Yoshi's Island / Yoshi's Story kinda vibes. But the game play stands more on its own just as a great platformer. You go around levels collecting golden cogs which allow you to fix the great elevator and ascend to the next level/world.The music, the art, the movement are all fantastic. Some of the platforming challenges in the game are pretty tough despite the cutesy look.Neither of the bosses have been at all tough so far, so that would be the one downside. That could change as I continue to play.An absolute delight of a game. I really hope more people check it out
_childDocuments_.name: Promenade

_childDocuments_.review: Promenade is a charming, colourful, challenging and fun 2D platformer; as a lover of Platformer games, this is one of the best and most difficult games I've ever played!This soundtrack, sound design, level design and rhythm are so well thought out.The level design in particular encourages exploration, thinking outside the box, rewards you for persevering and doesn't punish you for getting something wrong.The level design is very intuitive, as you go through they introduce new mechanics, gives you some practice and then puts them all together in the main boss battles and challenges. There are some things that can be frustrating, but nothing that would make someone rage quit.The character design are also very cute and well deigned.If you love platformer/puzzle games you need this in your library, I would recommend getting the physical edition as well.
_childDocuments_.name: Promenade

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10I enjoyed every single one of the 10 hours it took me to 100% the game. The Holy Cap Team put an incredible amount of love and passion into this platformer. At the time of writing, there's not a SINGLE negative review for this game yet, and I hope it stays that way, because there's also not any significantly negative thing I can say about its design!In fact, I think this game's greatest strength is that you're never going to be bored while playing this. Throughout the entire experience Promenade constantly gives the player new environments, mechanics, and activities to accomplish. It gets gradually more challenging, but enjoyably so - I really felt like I was getting better at their systems, and there's no moments where I felt like the game became too easy or too hard with the tools I had. It's just pure fun.If you enjoy 2D collectathons, you really should be wishlisting or buying this, because this gem shouldn't stay hidden.
_childDocuments_.name: Promenade

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing puzzle platformer that follows the rule of adding a new design idea in every level, adding up to a beautiful and very creative "greater-than-the-sum-of-its-parts" gem of a game. Really cool art, atmosphere and sound design as well. A few sweaty fingers challenges after you reach the ending will help you stay longer in a world you won't want to leave.This is one that shouldn't fly under the radar ! Come join the Promenade :)
_childDocuments_.name: Promenade

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely adore this game. From the art style to the sound design to the physics/gamefeel to the creativity of the puzzles, it's a masterpiece in almost every conceivable way. Easily one of my favorite platformers, not just in recent memory but in general. I'm currently working on 100%-ing the game outside of my Twitch channel but have been asked to at least broadcast it on Discord by people who just can't get enough of it. This game is really something special and an experience I'll be talking about for quite a while.Feel free to check out my playthrough atIf I could pick one nit, it would be that it's possible to misinterpret a particularly anticlimactic moment as the end of the game, when the actual end of the game is wonderful and moving. If you feel a sense of "Uh, was that all?" consider the visual indications  to see how you might progress.
_childDocuments_.name: Promenade

_childDocuments_.review: I played this game during the beta and I played it again with pleasure when it was out.It is a good platform game, dynamic, well reacting to command, generous in game design and exploration.It is an independant game treated with a lot of care by a small relentless team. Musics are simple let enjoyable and adequat.The artistic direction is an obvious other strengh of this game.And last but not least, many easter eggs are present because it is a game which love other games and gamers. <3Delight yourself !
_childDocuments_.name: Promenade

_childDocuments_.review: Really unique and fun game. It's like they mixed a 3D platformer's goal based objectives with a 2D platformer and it works so well. The movement is also really fun and ranges from very basic running and jumping to chaining together combos and being able to do some really fancy stuff. Highly recommend to anyone that enjoys platformers of any kind.
_childDocuments_.name: Promenade

_childDocuments_.review: Such an incredible game!Every mechanic it introduces is fresh and polished, and there is no shortage of said mechanics either.The collectathon structure allows for so many different kinds of challenges that there is something for everyone, and the requirements are lenient enough that you can progress easily while skipping sections that don't appeal to you.Then the several creative steam achievements are the icing on the cake, it has been a while since I played a game that was so fun to 100%.
_childDocuments_.name: Promenade

_childDocuments_.review: Finished the game in about 7hrs with 135/180 cog pieces and the five octopuses freed. A very fun old-school platformer with gameplay similar to Klonoa mixed with collecting cog pieces similar to stars in mario 64. There are some fun new ideas for platforming and unlocking the other abilities completely changes the game, giving you new options for traversal. Some of the time trials can be quite difficult but not impossible. This game is for sure built with speedrunning in mind.
_childDocuments_.name: Promenade

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely worth the price. A beautiful collect-it-all puzzle-platformer in which you will appreciate the great freedom of approach given to the player in every situation, guaranteed by a varied and dynamic movement system that always rewards experimentation and refinement of the mechanics. If it plays like a cross between a faster Klonoa and a Super Mario Wonder, the design and cartoonish style might remind you of Scribblenauts.  Fans of the genre will definitely want to pick it up.
_childDocuments_.name: Promenade

_childDocuments_.review: Such an unexpected gem, has some definite Nintendo charm (maybe not Nintendo-level polish) but in terms of level design, platforming mechanics, clever gimmicks and thoughtful interactions, Promenade is top-notch.Despite having levels the world feels open and connected and the game has some really nice bail-out features like cancel the race, go back to home world, doesn't punish you for exploring or make you backtrack in a needless way but it could use a detailed map with markers.Also, I appreciate the fact that there are no words, no long drawn out backstory, no exposition through dialog, it shows the story in small which doesn't bog down the experience, bravo devs.Works well on Steam Deck with XBOX One controller, animations are fluid, if you liked DKC and Mario Galaxy then you'll probably like this.
_childDocuments_.name: Promenade

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing. It's like mario odyssey except 2D instead of 3D. I think it's better than mario odyssey too. It's extremely polished and feels great to play. The collectibles and levels are all a lot of fun. Promenade is in my top 5 indie games of all time, for sure.My play time:8.5 hours to beat the game the first time12.5 hours total to collect everything24 hours total for all the achievements (a lot of the extra time was for the 2.5h speedrun achievement)
_childDocuments_.name: Promenade

_childDocuments_.review: I was gifted this game by the Developers themselves, not sponsored at all. I didn’t expect much going into a free game from a new studio, but I was extremely pleasantly surprised. This game is full of charm and delight.You have very limited movement options, and the game knows this, using it to its advantage. Every single enemy you can bounce on, hook you can grab, is placed in such a way that getting from A to B becomes an interesting and fun puzzle in its own right. But once you understand the platforming, you can start the adventuring. This is a collectathon in 2D. And that might sound limited, but you’d be amazed at what you can do in the limited space. I’ve helped snails find love, raced penguins across the world, flown a ship in space and many many other things. It’s incredible and I never got bored.If you liked 3D collectathons like Mario Odyssey, or loved the 2D platforming of Celeste, I’d highly recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Promenade

_childDocuments_.review: I have played just a few minutes of the game (the tutorial and the first "level"), but first impression in really good. Great art style, controls and gameplay. The story seems interesting (but it's too soon to judge).Edit: I have finished the game. The gameplay gets even better, the story is really interesting and I really liked the way it's presented. The level design is incredible. It kind of feels like a 3d mario game (like super mario 64 and odissey) but in 2d and it works incredibly well. If you like platformers this is a must have, and even if you don't, this is still a great game.
_childDocuments_.name: Promenade

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent game and a refreshing experience from passionate developers who put their heart and soul into creating it.The game offers a wonderful gameplay, be it for casual players or hardcore gamers, thanks to jump mechanics that get gradually more complex.Led by beautiful graphics, the environment varies greatly from a level to an other while offering many hidden secrets to find.
_childDocuments_.name: Promenade

_childDocuments_.review: Go on an adventure in a world packed with secrets helped by your friend, a poulp with many abilities. Explore, solve puzzles, wander across dungeons, blast through races and much more in this game inspired by the best 3D platformers.
_childDocuments_.name: Promenade

name: ZERO Sievert
detailed_description: The world has ended. ZERO Sievert charges you with scavenging equipment across multiple areas, all set in an atmospheric fictitious post-apocalyptic Eastern Europe setting. Your base of operations, the bunker, is filled with traders, modding stations, and areas to make your own, providing you with progression across your excursions into the wild. Once you’re out in the wilds of the wasteland, however, the situation becomes a lot less secure. Across the five biomes of the game, you’ll initially be armed with little more than a gun and a bottle of water, after which point it’s up to you to recover items, take out bandits, and most importantly, get back alive. And be warned ; the nuclear fallout may have impacted some of the local wildlife… A wasteland to explore Procedurally generated maps make every journey different, with ever-changing hiding spots, loot locations, and layouts. With over five maps to explore, be sure to adapt and learn each one's secrets to get in, get out, and get better. Full weapon modification Hunt in a way that suits your playstyle, with over 35 unique guns and 150 mods that can be combined to make you the biggest threat in the wastes of ZERO Sievert. Create a weapon that suits your style or focus on stats to become the ultimate hunter. Looting and questing Multiple questlines guide you through the world of ZERO Sievert. Through talking with a range of characters you’ll slowly unravel information and lore about the world that’s been left behind. Alongside this, there are more than 100 different items to loot which can be used to craft new items, upgrade your own base, and trade.

short_description: ZERO Sievert is a tense top-down extraction shooter that challenges you to scavenge a procedurally-generated wasteland, loot gear, and explore what’s left of a devastated world. When the odds are stacked against you, you’ll need to do more than just survive...

_childDocuments_.review: This *could* be fun.If you haven't played Tarkov and know how that mission system works, you will be lost. If you have played Tarkov, you will likely be lost.Wander the bunker spawn to find quest givers, wander outside to eventually stumble on the train NPC to leave the map, and choose a level...then die. My gun's spray pattern seems to fly _everywhere_, while my enemies 2-3 tapped me with precision aim (enemies like random bandits and scientists who are secretly snipers). Animals were a little easier to deal with, but still horribly dangerous. The extraction zones are not pointed out in any way, and the deep green circles on the map blend in with the rest of the green. I had to google how to leave a map.PS: The dev responses to player complaints rubbed me the wrong way before I even started playing. "I don't like X change" is met with "well we changed Y and Z, hope you enjoy the update!" If you're going to ignore your players in your early access game, then just ignore them. Don't ignore them in a response.It overall just feels way too early. The premise is there, and this could be fun. However, there's currently way too much to google and there's a sharp barrier to entry.Ultimately, if I want to play Tarkov then I will just play Tarkov.
_childDocuments_.name: ZERO Sievert

_childDocuments_.review: ZERO Sievert manages to capture a lot of the STALKER and EFT magic in this tiny little addictive package. Random generation of stages every time you visit keeps you on your toes and makes every run feel a little fresh. The quest format and grind are extremely Tarkov-like, you'll be collecting junk like a combat hobo in exchange for money and different junk that you need. Being early access, there's some systems not fully implemented like faction relations, but what is here now is still quite substantial. STALKER is my favorite franchise of all time and I'd honestly say that of every game said to be inspired by or similar to it, ZERO is the absolute closest. I'm very excited to see it expand.
_childDocuments_.name: ZERO Sievert

_childDocuments_.review: Starts off as a punishing, brutal rogue-like that doesn't seem to make a great deal of sense and then... Bam! The loop and the grind kick in and the game is immensely fun. It's a game that rewards skill and caution. You will have times you feel cheated, but it's all the more rewarding when you get to the chopper after you've tried and failed several times over. Strong recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: ZERO Sievert

_childDocuments_.review: after watching a OperatorDrewski YT video on this game, i was hooked. 14 mins into his video and i had it downloading.. sooo much fun, well-rounded and sharp at the same time. i haven't had this much fun in a top-down/side-scrolling game since Fallout 1 & 2. and its still IN development with as much as it has to offer already.. this will go far and i'm here for it. ( also  don't come at me but nosin megant is the best starter weapon. hands down. almost like its inspired from another game. beautifully done. ONLY gripe i have is that you can accidentally ( and very easily) scrap your gun when  right clicking to unload its mag. and a random error that locks the screen. only way i've gotten around it was by using the expand screen key command, or sliding up on my track pad and using the arrow keys to select the game.  other than that, safe to say i'm going to put hours into this game.  100% recommend if your curious. ( plays similar to Tarkov, stalker, and a heavily modded Fallout NV/4 play through) READ THE TUTORIAL
_childDocuments_.name: ZERO Sievert

_childDocuments_.review: Gameplay is there. People who enjoy extraction shooters may enjoy this. It's the usual schtick, grind out missions to loot resources to improve the base or character. The game is intuitive from the get-go. I skipped the tutorial and managed just fine. Tutorial-wise, there were only two which is odd. Why not just develop a single tutorial stage that covers the basics? There are odd design choices sprinkled about. However, the UI and lack of QoL is going to be the reason why I'm refunding this game. UI is extremely chunky, with no option to scale it down. I don't need an item card that takes up a third of my screen, offering bare information. Additional information would be nice regarding certain statistics. For example, what is "Fragility"? What does the class armour number mean? Do higher numbers mean heavier weight class? There's so much space on item cards, it could have benefited from adding a little more to it.There's no comparison UI, often you will be moving the cursor back and forth between items. Moving items across, the norm is holding Shift and left-clicking. Here, it's Ctrl and left-clicking. Again, odd design choices. If it's worked in other games, there's no need to reinvent the wheel.That's what I've been able to pick up on in my short span of game time. As of writing this it is a short list, but the thing is I work in the interface and experience design industry and it irked me. People will enjoy this game, and I can recommend the gameplay to others. But it's a hard no for me and to others who appreciates more clarity and polish.
