_childDocuments_.review: TLDR- The game is one part Stalker and one part Escape from Tarkov, but in 2d pixelart. It has limited content and some issues making certain progression useless, but is not a bad 20-30hrs for the price. If you like STALKER or Tarkov, you will like this.The Game- If you have ever played STALKER or Tarkov, then you know what this is. You go into a map, loot up, complete quests, and extract back to your base. There are humans, environmental hazards, and monsters looking to murder your poor character. Unlike Tarkov, the only thing lost on death is time, and the game is completely singleplayer. While it may have a Tarkov theme, it is much closer to STALKER in terms of gameplay loop. When you die, you just reset to the beginning of your raid and do not lose anything but time.Aesthetics- The 2d pixelart is great. Simple enough to understand what everything is, but still stylish. The sound design kept me completely on edge, even though I was playing a giant-headed pixelman. Not me obviously, but when Jeff plays the game, he jumps when a monster screams across the map, especially if it is dark and rainy. Probably because he has sheet ammo and does not know how to run backwards.  The aesthetics are an A+ for me.Mechanics- The game has a lot of in-depth mechanics to fully explore. Each weapon can be upgraded to have better ergonomics, recoil, flashlights, lasers, accuracy, and even scope mechanics. The scope system is implemented well with advantages and disadvantages, despite it being a top-down game. Different bullets either have high damage/low recoil or high recoil/ high armor penetration. However, there is a ton of room for improvement/balance. Basically, you have to have knowledge of Tarkov's armor and penetration system to really understand wtf 45 pen means, and the game does not really give you much info. I tried to explain it to Jeff, and he just got lost, but that is not anything new. Just take the highest pen bullets you have when you go into the mall. Also, the recoil and ergo stats of the guns do not make a big difference. I more mod guns to look cooler on my character. Jeff said A, but I say B.Content and "story"- Well, this is where Jeff says I need to give the game a pass because it is in early-access. BUTTT, the game is obviously lacking a lot of content. I mean, I am at max trader level, and have the second best armor in the game at 18 hours. I need some more stuff to do and reason to progress, but it is early access and maybe there is a little more content ready to come my way. The content is a mixed bag. Many quests, just like Tarkov, are like "blah blah blah, collect 30 nails, 3 crystals, and the magic of Christmas." There are some great quests, like kill giant monster that keeps murdering everyone or defeat a horde of ghouls. But mostly, you are going to be roaming around to find the one stupid friggin golden zibbo that refuses to spawn. Jeff does not know my pain, but anyone who has played Tarkov does. C+ (the + is an early access handicap).The need to get more bling- After the first three hours, the game gets really easy on keeping your character alive and getting "chadded out" as the youngins say. I found the some of the best attachments randomly after defeating the easiest boss. The quest givers seem all too happy to give me full durability weapons. The game balances weapon progression by making all guns found on the map low durability, basically making them jam so your character dies with his wee wee in his hand. You can jump through a bunch of hoops to craft repair kits, but you never need to cause the quest givers just give you full durability weapons like its candy, and we stopped giving Jeff candy after the "incident". Good armor takes a minute to unlock, and it makes you feel powerful when you get it, probably the better part of the progression. C+Base Building- Well, I am 18 hrs in, and I have had zero want of building up my base. I have basically unlimited money, and at no point did I think it was worth to go through the tedious task of gathering junk to fix a problem I never had. Jeff says he likes to build the bed cause it looks cozy, but I think it is just cause his bed is crap IRL. Well, like why would I spend an hour to gather items to build a kitchen when food/water has never been a problem? The game needs an overhaul to make the base good. It tries to copy Tarkov, but it just makes zero sense to grind a copious mount of junk for a game where you lose nothing when you die. D-The Fighting- Okay, I have a confession. Jeff recommended the game to me because he saw a streamer play it for an hour. Apparently, most of them had no idea you could just run backwards away from wolves so you don't die. The monsters are simple, but all different. I won't spoil what they all do, but Jeff is super scared by them all, even more than the... and I quote "mean hunter dudes." Fighting people in the game feels like a tactical experience. You have to pie corners, jiggle peak, snipe, ect. Well, the enemy has good AI that will take cover, push, search for you, yell stuff when you ambush them. The only ♥♥♥♥♥♥ part is that monsters will spawn in walls, making it where you cannot see them, then just kill you when you get close enough to the wall of death. Besides that one bug which only really applies indoors, this is where the game shines. A-Areas to Improve- Jeff told me "If you know so much, why don you make a better game?" Well, Jeff, I am glad you asked for my opinion. I love to talk about all the amazing ideas for the perfect game, and let me share them. I really think the game needs to make quests a little less grindy for the "collect 200 items." Like, okay fine, I have to do some mundane stuff early on, but most of the quests are like that. I want to see more narrative driven content, which the game does well when it does it. Also, make the ergo and recoil stats actually matter. This is not a game where if I do not put my crosshair on the head of a tiny pixel controlled by another overweight gaming manchild, I die. Making the character have a bigger spread for full-auto bigboy guns makes sense for having attachments matter. Also, make clean food less common in-raid and with traders, make full durability guns a rare big reward for actually difficult quests, limit the 0-60% durability repair kits to rare crafts, basically, give me a reason to upgrade the hideout and craft. Make me care about more than maximizing roubles per raid. Make radiation an actual hazard. For the love of god, make the game co-op!.... I could see giving me a penalty on death as a way to balance it, but some might call that ImMeRsiOn bREaKinG. Just do something to make surviving a challenge. Lastly, grenades and rocket launchers would be nice, even Jeff agrees.I always hate playing single-player games in early access. I feel like I will play the half finished game, then never touch it again. The game seems to have a lot more content planned, and is fun enough where I might pick it up again after I get bored with Tarkov's next wipe. Give me a co-op mode, and if you would just give it to me, I'd be nicer to Jeff.Rant over

_childDocuments_.review: This genuinely used to be one of my favorite games, and I loved watching it come along through several patches, and despite its various quirks and flaws, it was challenging, fun to play and yet open and invited replay without rancor. Then this latest patch came along, and the devs duly warned us all that this would come with a save wipe, so I braced my end-of-content character for deletion and the starting of a new adventure. Several problems became rapidly apparent, some have already been mentioned by others, but this is my experience.-The disparity between the amount of reputation gain per quest and the amount of reputation to unlock what was before affordable gear at this point in my run is irritating. While I understand the intent and even the in-universe flavor reason for gatekeeping certain items, it's somewhat ridiculous that I'm going to be denied a backpack upgrade I could have easily bought twice over by now.- While I understand that in accordance with the new reputation system, the Green Army is no longer Neutral, but actively Hostile, this makes the early game MUCH more punishing than it was previously, when it might have been possible to rest among the green army soldiers like a clownfish in an anemone, or even lead enemies into them. Even as a fairly seasoned player, it was a frustrating start for this reason. Worse, the quests that presumably earn enough green army rep to make them stop shooting you likely comes well past the point you've stopped running from them, and being constantly shot at does not endear a faction to a player.-I personally have been unable to access the makeshift camp, even after jumping through several needless hoops in order to visit it at all, as the game simply hard crashes in a manner identical to the others. Which means I now have several quests that cannot be completed, and presumably am locked off from the reset of the levels forever. -In addition to this, not only do most of your quests now come from the Networker (which, whatever, but I had previously felt a connection with the barman and the Doctor and such as characters, so I was sad to see them lose that element.) and one of the initial quests immediately broke. For the quest Scientist Work 1, you're supposed to place an analyzer near a fire anomaly. Fine. Except, every time I tromp down to the big yellow circle on the map and find the big field of fire, there is no prompt for placing the device. At all. Anywhere inside or immediately around the circle. Anywhere. At all. I have searched, run through fire, died several times, all in an attempt to find the right place, but to no avail. Even with the other quests I've been able to complete, this has hampered my progress significantly.-For whatever reason, Blinks, an enemy previously seen several levels hence, are now in the Forest. Presumably, next patch will bring Big and ArminFor all of these reasons, Zero Sievert has lost a lot of the shine from its radioactive apple, at least for the moment. I have not lost faith in the devs, this game is still being developed, and sometimes missteps are made. Hopefully, they will listen to their fans, fix what wasn't broken before, and let us return to a freer Zarkov. I look forward to the day I can delete this review, and leave a positive one.

_childDocuments_.review: To begin with, this game is very poorly made, and its immediately apparent when you enter your first zone. there is nothing preventing your spawn from being right next to a hostile squad that instantly kills you, the train driving through radiation pockets that irradiate you before the game even starts, and also being dropped off right into a pile of car wrecks that also irradiate you. When finally leaving your spawn point and moving to points of interest you quickly learn that enemy human AI are INCREDIBLY over powered, requiring mag dumps of armor piercing ammo (and still not killing them) while they can kill you with a 9x18 machine pistol in half a second from the end of your screen. In the first area, the enemies spawn with the same level of gear as you or worse, yet they kill you almost instantly while you have to spend ridiculous amount of ammo to kill them. This is not helped by the fact that ammo is rare and the barkeep will only sell you small amounts of HP ammo (ammo with no armor penetration) at the start of the game. On top of incredibly unbalanced game play, this game is so poorly optimized that it drops below 10 fps on my high end computer, especially when bringing anomalies with artifacts onto my screen. This game is said to be like STALKER, yet fails entirely to be like it other than having "various loot" and anomalies that are flat out ripped from STALKER. While STALKER may be really difficult, especially with certain mods, it still has some balance to it where I don't have to empty an entire mag of armor piercing ammo into a bandit in the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ beginning area at the start of the game. The gun play in Zero Sievert is also incredibly painful and disappointing. The apparent "meta" is to quickly peak around a corner, shoot the enemy once or twice with your AK, then hide again before they instantly kill you (and they will hit you with their instant reflexes). _childDocuments_.review: If you came here for a review of this game you Will be let down but if you came for a good pie recipe you came to the right placeStep 1Make the custard: In a medium saucepan, whisk together egg yolks and sugar until well combined. Whisk in cornstarch and salt. In a slow, steady stream, whisk in milk and then the cream. Add butter. Cook mixture over medium-low heat, stirring constantly with a wooden spoon, just until it starts to thicken. Immediately whisk mixture until smooth, then continue to cook and stir custard until it has come to a very low boil for 2 minutes, about 6 to 8 minutes total. Strain custard through a fine mesh sieve into a small bowl, pushing it through with a small spatula. Stir in vanilla. Cover with plastic wrap, pressing the plastic directly onto the surface. Chill for at least 3 hours and up to 24 hours.Step 2Prepare the cake: Heat oven to 325 degrees. Butter a 9-by-2-inch round baking pan, generously greasing the sides, and line it with parchment paper. Butter parchment paper. In a medium bowl, whisk together flour, baking powder and salt.Step 3In a small saucepan, bring the milk and butter to a simmer over medium heat. When the butter is melted, remove pan from heat. In a large bowl, beat eggs and sugar with an electric mixer until pale and thick, about 4 to 6 minutes. With the mixer running on low, add the milk mixture and beat until combined. Then add flour mixture and vanilla and beat until combined.Step 4Transfer batter to the prepared pan and smooth the top. Bake until a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean, 30 to 35 minutes.Step 5Transfer to a rack and let cool 10 minutes. With a very thin knife, cut around the edge to release the cake from the side of the pan. Carefully flip the cake onto the rack, then turn it right-side-up to cool completely.Step 6Assemble the cake: Using a serrated knife, carefully cut the cake into two layers and place the bottom layer on a serving plate. Stir custard, and spread it onto the cut side of the bottom half. Replace the top half of the cake, cut side down.Step 7Prepare the glaze: In a small saucepan over medium-low, heat the cream to a simmer. Remove the pot from the heat and pour cream over the chocolate chips, oil, salt and let stand for 3 minutes. Whisk until smooth. Spread the glaze evenly over the top of the cake.INGREDIENTSYield: 10 servingsFor the Custard3 large egg yolks½ cup/100 grams granulated sugar2 tablespoons cornstarchPinch kosher salt1 cup/240 milliliters whole milk¼ cup/60 milliliters heavy cream1 tablespoon/14 grams unsalted butter1 teaspoon pure vanilla extractFor the Cake8 tablespoons/114 grams (1 stick) unsalted butter, cut into pieces, plus more for the pan1¾ cups/224 grams all-purpose flour1¾ teaspoons baking powder¾ teaspoon kosher salt¾ cup/180 milliliters whole milk3 large eggs, at room temperature1 cup/200 grams granulated sugar1 teaspoon pure vanilla extractFor the Glaze¼ cup/60 milliliters heavy cream4 ounces/113 grams semisweet chocolate chips1 teaspoon neutral oil, such as safflowerPinch kosher salt

Yes fixing bugs and balancing the game are very important, however there is almost no new content being added to the base game since its Kickstarter days.  5 maps in total and almost no new weapons or new quests except some holiday events. "The Bunker" or the game's main hub still has tons of unused space and placeholder assets.The devs fixing problems that never existed in the first place.The UI before the recent update worked perfectly, now they felt like a mobile game with very buggy inventory UI. Sometimes item can overlap each other in your stash, or sometimes you cant stack a stackable item.  The AI for some reason feels dumber and dumber each patch. I played on the Survivor difficulty but human enemy AI are not any smarter from Rookie difficulty since recently patch. On the other hand, monster AI is just unfair. Ever since Alpha the monster AI have a problem where they will sprint around the player in circles and snapping on to the player when they attack since most of the monsters are melee. This caused the player to just mag dump on them only to find out none of the shots connected and dies due to the need to reload. The devs never fixed this issue and seem to be fine with it even alot of people have requested to rework the monster AI in their discord.The devs seems to constantly tweaking core gameplay mechanics that should not be touched, because I literally feel like i am playing Enter the Gungeon, except with non of Gungeon's fluid movement.I really want to give this game a positive but i can't. if you plan on buying this thinking it is going to be a 2D tarkov, dont. _childDocuments_.review: EARLY ACCESS REVIEW (0.26.2)ZERO Sievert is a top down (slightly isometric) scavenger shooter heavily influenced by the S.T.A.L.K.E.R. series of games. You are a rookie "hunter" scavenging the the areas around Zakov after a nuclear plant explosion. You're assigned quests by various individual factions and individuals to build reputation and find out more of what happened.The Good:Gunplay can be difficult but rewarding. Combat is fluid with enemies using fairly smart AI to dodge attacks, use cover, and flank the player depending on his location. They will make use of long range attacks when possible and hide in wait for the player to ambush.There are a number of quests implemented, primarily mass killing, assassination, or part scavenging. While not overly complex they can pose challenges based on enemies present, anomalies, or radioactive areas.Areas are proceduraly generated each time the player enters the area. All loot, points of interest, and enemies are reset to provide fairly easy farming and grinding.There are numerous types of firearms and modifications, armor, and accessories, all which have their uses and may make minor or major changes to a player's playstyle. Most items provide small cosmetic changes to the player character.The bunker provides a safe home base where time still passes but hunger and thirst stops. The player has the option to expand on a "mini-base" inside the bunker to provide more storage, crafting, passive benefits, etc.The neutral:Currently there are no different difficulty settings, although there are a number of starting load outs which will change how hard the game is on starting.There is no manual saving; saves happen automatically and typically apply after the character returns to the bunker or exits the game. If a player exits in a map, they will be returned to the bunker on re-loading.Being early access, a number of the items are incomplete, such as some of the faction reputation, hardcore mode, some building options, etc.The bad:Most of this can be attributed to being early access, but I've had a number of crashes to desktop. On the upside, the game saves periodically and I've found myself "reset" at the bunker with some or all of the loot I had acquired.Sometimes areas that were previously cleared (or with no enemies present) may have some appear after exiting a point of interest, which can lead to some unfair combats or quick deaths.Verdict:If you're a fan of the S.T.A.L.K.E.R. universe and enjoy top down shooters, the game easily has an excellent dollar to time ratio in its current state. It is currently in early access but this is definitely a title that has seen a lot of love and will provide plenty of fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game in its current state, with an even more promising future as additional content or complexities are added.  As extraction shooters continue growing in popularity, ZS does an excellent job presenting the format from a top down perspective.  I love Tarkov, but the cheating situation in FPS games right now is untenable: this is PvE, so the only thing I need to worry about is procedural RNG and bag space.  As is typical of most PvE games, ZS allows you to choose your own unique play-through difficulty preferences.  To maximize replayability, I play on Hardcore mode losing all items on failed extract and making the gameplay more meaningful and immersive.  Message to the devs,Great job so far! Here are a few wishlist requests that I believe would push this game over the top:-Create urgency by making the raid extraction time-limited based on the player's radiation levels.  Each raid map would have a small but persistent radiation gain in addition to the other triggers that influence the radiation levels.  The player would be forced to consider the risk/rewards of extending the raid experience at the expense of not being healthy enough to reach extract, it would increase the importance of preraid preparedness, and create strategic considerations of item benefit trade-offs.  Most importantly, this simple modification immediately connects the gamer to the title of your game (0 Sv).-Make the maps larger in scale (x2) and apply a spawn probability % to all non-essential sites and non-active quest NPCs, so that the raids are more random and unique.  Add an additional, conditional extraction point nearer to the center of the map.-Hide the key sites on the unexplored portions of the map.  Only reveal contextual, or incomplete location data.-Modify the camps so that the number of  NPCs is somewhat random (instead of 3 NPCs all the time, make it at least 2 and up to 5).  -NPC bosses, should be rare, rich, and challenging.  Consider adding a countdown of days before a respawn after a boss kill to prevent boss farming, and maybe a less bountiful loot table.-Increase the probability of higher geared wondering "Hunters", with unique loot tables.-Add achievements, make several of them rare and challenging.  And finally...-Openly engage the modding community.  Some of my most memorable gaming experiences have come from modded games.  Your fans have great ideas, some of them enjoy programming games (for free).  Pick the best mods and include them as part of future releases/DLCs.Thank you.

I walk over to the wolf to loot and when I exitout of the inventory/loot screen I am stuck under the still living bunny.I try to press the ctrl/alt key + arrow keys to unstick myself and nothing worked.I had to exit and reload and well my run was gone. I was on the way out the door and I thought Id hunt a bit before going back to base.Then there are the minor bugs of dying randomly. I had full HP and I didnt see anyone attacking me but it just said I died.I was in full daylight so no mistakes on not seeing an enemy. I didnt see anything indicating to me I was going to die so I was like "whaaaaat?"But if you've gotten past all that and you dont mind the kinks being worked out while the game is still in EA then I would say you should still buy the game. _childDocuments_.review: It's really 3 different games, at least it feels so. It is solid 10 hours of fun, if you don't mind the grind it's more like 20-40 hours, which are unfortunately less intense than the start. It's a game based around intensity/action density, which by trying to prolong it's playtime lessens it's core aspect. It's sad, but I had fun and would therefore recommend it anyway.That artificial prolonging of the game divides it into 3 stages that feel and play different.First stage is "paranoic level". You know nothing, you have no equipment, you can die form 2 shots and you die half of the time when fighting grouped enemies. Your goal is to hide, to scrap all leftovers and jump paranoicly after any suspicious sound is made. Really intense, immersive, free and fun.Second stage is "Why, tell me why!? level". You're no longer paranoicly scared, you've learned most of key signals (sounds, enemy looks, location characteristics) and unfortunately reached the grind wall... You have all the money you can have, but you can't buy better armor, because you don't have exp, you can't enter most locations because they're locked after filler quest (you don't know even which ones). You grind, grind, grind in hopes to see what you dream of. Though some of that grind is not that bad, even fun sometimes, it's literally worst part of the game. You either end the game here or are pacient enough to reach third stage. This stage is little boring and repetitive, but at times also intense and fun.Third stage is "Am I a boss here? level". You've grinded your dream set, unlocked most of location quests and reached 4th experience level allowing you to access most of the game content. You know most of the game patterns, you have enough experience to know when to run and when to walk slowly, you can "finally" finish all the game content, which happens to be quite hard and new/not repetitive, which makes game once again intense, fun and either really satisfying or really tilting when you stupidly die. It's very similar to the first stage, but a little more tactical at it's core.

_childDocuments_.review: I played for 14 hours yesterday and I am violently obsessed. This is the STALKER sequel you never knew you needed. I am utterly obsessed. New fave. I'm really enjoying playing through this.One of my favorite parts is how the AI is aggressive. They'll push on you while you're healing instead of just letting you take pot shots at them while they cower in fear. That, in combination with the fact that even low-level enemies can kill you fairly easily if you're not careful, makes this game something you have to be slow and methodical about. But wait! If you're in rad-rain? If you're in a dangerous area? If nightfall is coming? You're in a race against time! If I could put anything on my wish-list for this game -- roving enemies that hunt you down a bit more aggressively than the existing Hunters and Bandits would be really awesome, and enhance the feeling of always being on edge in a hostile environment. I am, again, utterly obsessed. This is my current favorite game of the year so far, and I expect it'll stay top 5 as long as the devs keep hacking on it. Thank you, devs!

_childDocuments_.review: Sort of a rough experience.  The game's progression mechanics are... odd, IMO.  Gear quality scales upward linearly, unlocking new base facilities requires extracting with fairly random loot that is hard to specifically hunt for, and a lot of advancement seems to be based on the idea that you can unlock new gear for purchase from vendors (so dying sets you back less).  That's a poor choice on the dev's part, because the game does crash occasionally (~four times in 19 hours for me), and crashes count as deaths; playing without any hardcore options is basically cheating, but playing with them turned on will just screw you over if you crash.That all being said, the core gameplay is really good, and very well designed.  If you don't have hardcore settings on,  you'll probably only lose five minutes of progress on a crash, and you don't NEED to pursue base facility upgrades if you find the scavenger hunt annoying.  Zero Sievert reminds me a lot of mobile games, without the awful monetization that usually implies; it's amazing to just pick up and play for fifteen minutes to do a raid or two.

_childDocuments_.review: tldr: I don't think I've ever played a game that's pissed me off, yet made me want to come back as much as ZERO Sievert. The Long Version:This is definitely a game where your interest in the premise will greatly decide how much you like the game. If you want a 2d stalker-tarkov hybrid, then you'll probably enjoy it. However, if that style of game doesn't normally appeal to you, I don't see ZERO Sievert changing your mind either.  For the most part,  the game loop in ZERO Sievert is very similar to Tarkov. There are a few nods to stalker but primarily just enemies and atmosphere. You will mostly get quests, go to "the zone", and extract. The most significant change is there is no penalty to dying in "the zone" other than being reverted to just before you left. This means if you die you won't lose what you came in with, just what you gained while in the zone. This makes the game a little less grindy but the tension of early combat is practically non-existent. I personally prefer this but not everyone will. Where I find the game to be difficult is combat. One of the best features of this game is a line-of-sight mechanic that blocks out enemies in areas you couldn't realistically see. This makes the position of your character important beyond not getting hit by bullets. It can also make engaging multiple enemies particularly challenging. The TTK is relatively fast and combat feels very rewarding. However, it's very easy to think you're engaging only one or 2 enemies only to have 4-5 more buddies appear.Overall, I reccomend ZERO Sievert if this kind of game sounds interesting to you. I just haven't seen anything to make this game standout in the genre beyond being a 2-D game.
_childDocuments_.name: ZERO Sievert

_childDocuments_.review: Having sunk an additional 20 hours into the demo on top of what I currently have, I think it's pretty fair to say I  enjoy this game. I am particularly fond of the butt clenching early game and the moderate learning curve that comes with it. On regular difficulty you will die quite often but not enough to halt your gradual accumulation of good gear. Learning how to navigate the somewhat random maps and where to best find particular materials is helpful. Exploring new maps for the first time is (rightfully) terrifying.The gameplay is very tactical, methodical even. You'll spend a lot of time peering into the distance in order to secure your safety and prepare for the fast, lethal firefights. Range is your friend, but close quarters is often necessary to reach new objectives or better loot.This is the sort of game where a sufficiently skilled and knowledgeable player could rush end game gear. So, while there is a slow and useful skill grind, you aren't locked out of using anything you find. The story exists. I haven't really followed it because I just like fighting for gear. The game is also updated fairly regularly, the devs listen to feedback, and there is a very pleasant discord community. I don't know what else you could want from a small indy game, so if whatever you've already seen interests you, get this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Are you tired of all those boring, easy peasy shooter games? Look no further than ZERO Sievert! This game is so tense, you'll be sweating bullets (figuratively speaking, of course - we don't want anyone getting hurt). And if you thought looting was just for those pesky RPGs, think again! You'll be scavenging a procedurally-generated wasteland like it's your full-time job. Who needs real-life hobbies when you have ZERO Sievert?But wait, there's more! You'll also be exploring what's left of a devastated world. And if you're lucky, you might even find some cool gear to help you survive. But let's be real, the odds are probably stacked against you. That's why you'll need to do more than just survive - you'll need to channel your inner Rambo and shoot your way to victory.So what are you waiting for? Get ready for some heart-pumping, pulse-racing action in ZERO Sievert. And who knows, you might even learn a thing or two about surviving the apocalypse. Just don't try any of this at home, okay?

_childDocuments_.review: Don't listen to the hastily written reviews of others complaining about the gunplay and what not. The game comes with several sliders that you can use to adjust the game play to how you want it. Find that guns aren't doing the damage you want them to? Change the value in the games difficulty settings. The people that are leaving negative reviews have probably never played Tarkov or S.T.A.L.K.E.R before (which is what this game is based off of) and I think they are doing a phenomenal job with the game. The gunplay is fine. The ammo is what will make or break your guns damage just like in Tarkov or S.T.A.L.K.E.R . People complaining about how they "nerfed" guns seems biased. Every gun fills a role in a persons playstyle. Don't like a gun? Switch it up! :) They are balancing the guns to be more like there counterparts from the other game series' and I think that they are pretty accurate. The one gripe I will warn you about is to TURN OFF CLOUD SAVING. You can still save in the hideout by quickly returning to the menu and resuming the game. If you leave cloud saving on there is a chance that when you trade with an NPC it will revert your gamestate to the latest cloud save which will reset your progress. It happened to me about 10 times before I figured out that is what was happening. Until they fix that don't use cloud saving.Other than that this has turned out to be a very engaging and fun 2D tarky and S.T.A.L.K.E.R (gamma mod included) game.Good job devs :)

_childDocuments_.review: Early access review: basic game play loop is there. Go into the zone, engage enemies, scavenge supplies and extract. Skill tree improves item buffs and crafting but it a bit shallow. Lots of fetch quests with some decent gear rewards later on in the story.Early game play can be brutal. Evens out mid game with gear that blocks environmental hazards. AI mobs will charge, retreat, flank and group up. Different factions will also roam the map fighting. Leaving behind gear for patient players.Map layouts are randomly generated with POIs that have a fixed layout. Which is a little repetitive since there's only a handful of playable maps.Overall it's an interesting concept that draws inspiration from game play and story elements present in games like Tarkov, Dayz. STALKER, etc. Regular price seems a bit high for an early access title but it's worth picking up on a sale since it's being actively developed.

_childDocuments_.review: You're very limited on what you can do early game to survive and not waste resources. It's just not fun when ammo is scarce, meds are expensive and weapons you pick up are in the worst condition possible. You're forced to keep dying until you get that one run in the beginning that doesn't ruin your ammo supply or cash to get out of the newbie ditch. Even then you hardly make any cash to make up for the ammo/med/food/drinks you've spent. The weight limit also hinders how much you can bring back. The game saves as soon as you extract so if you left with no ammo left in your pockets, that's what your next run will be like. The bartender does sell ammo but he sells barely enough ammo to kill 2 enemies if you use a single type of ammo.I cannot recommend this game because the "fun" part of the game is locked behind an extreme resource management. If I was given a new loadout after dying, such as scavs in Tarkov or the beginner set of gear in Dark and Darker, I would have much more fun.

_childDocuments_.review: When the stars line up, this game is exactly what I want out of it: a top-down 2D stalker with weapon customization, inventory management and some fun fire fights. Putting together your guns is fun, you got plenty of options to experiment with different type of gunplay (though snipers have a clear advantage being able to shoot enemies before they can even see you.)But in the current balance of the game, it becomes a rather frustrating game the longer your play. Mid-to-late game enemies turn into bullet sponges that will absolutely shred your fancy armor (that you looted off a dead mob likely or bought) in seconds, despite it being identical to the enemy. Might as well wear paper to protect yourself cause your armor will break in a few hits and cost a lot to repair. And it happens a lot when exploring the Mall area and Zakov City. You turn the corner only to immediately die to a single salvo of guns from an enemy that requires basically an endless supply of grenades to kill efficiently. You kill a boss for a mission, only to be immediately gunned down by a sniper you can't see in the dark who uses a starter gun, yet it feels like they're shooting you with 120mm APFSDS rounds.After 30 hours on this game, I'm basically putting it down hoping for a balance pass on the armor of higher tier enemies & players.

_childDocuments_.review: Yes, Play this gameWe all play games that are generally developed by studios, we gripe over functionality, graphics, sound, lack their of and either continue playing or since there are so many games... we dont give others a chance based on peoples feedback.This game is made by 1 person and it has more choice than alot of AAA games do with depth in characters and world.Zero Sievert is a lite roguelike, top down pixel art shooter. It is harsh when it needs to be, has a slight learning curve and a gameplay loop that is relatively addicting. 11 hours in and I had more positive things to say about this game than most and it kept a smile on my face. Lets break it down.Sound Design: 8/10 - it does what it needs to, the rain, running on certain surfaces, guns, tactical devices etc all sound great and are appropriate for the world were in. It immerses you and does a great job not trying to overreach on what is necessary for the tone.Questing: 7/10 - I think there are too many quests (i know, shoot me), the main ones to progress faction reputation were great but the collect and bring back were a bit much, that being said. Still great quest design overall.Atmosphere: 9/10 - as with the sound design and partially because of it, you feel like youre in the biomes that you are exploring, a forest with rain feels cold and you dont need a cold monitor, it just feels right. When youre in a radioactive area, it makes you feel like somethings wrong with your character, its great!Enemy Variety: 9/10 - I think there are ~8 different enemy types, all with unique behaviours/pathing and approaches to combat, Without getting into details, they are all solid.Combat: 8/10 - the loop is great, armor helps reduce damage and has durability, you can visibly see what enemies are wearing for the most part and understand what weapons to use for that situation if youre going in with that intent and the guns are consistent in how you would expect them to perform. Solid combat, i would like to see some ways to use pistols as a personal preference, they are far too weak to progress but that is also appropriate for the setting.Weapons / Uniqueness - 9.5/10 - It is abundant and they all feel unique!Upgrade system: 9.5/10 - the attachments are amazing, they change the way your guns feel and there are alot of them. The added scope to extend your field of view is a great touch- Lighting is phenomenal at dark with a torch and the lasers look badass as they should Gameplay Loop: 8.5/10 - Loot, Extract, Hand in quests, upgrade your base, upgrade your character, go back in and loot some more - its exactly what you want in this type of game.Impressions: 8.9/10 - its amazing, dont let the art style deter you. This game should be played by all who like a challenging experience with a rewarding loop.

_childDocuments_.review: If you want a game that's very much a Tarkov/STALKER influenced top down pixel art shooter, then this is right up your alley, because even now there's plenty to recommend the experience simply due to the relatively low entry cost involved.But personally, I plan to come back later when it has had more updates. Because my entire time playing it so far was a whole bunch of "This could be really good, if..." because despite many of the core elements being in place and functional, just about every single one of them is enough to feel not jank, but all the same don't feel like the conversion from 3d first person to top down perspective worked that well.Basically, enjoy spending hours getting shot the nanosecond you come out from behind something because two AI were there and looking at that corner and you had zero way of knowing they were there. Enjoy dying in your inventory after clearing an area because your character has no spacial awareness, and enjoy having extremely short rounds because the hunger and thirst burns down way too quickly.Its still a perfectly good game, mind you, but if you came to it SPECIFICALLY because you like Tarkov and STALKER, temper your expectations. _childDocuments_.review: If you have huge fps drops, it's likely because your windows decided it's better to use your inbuilt mini intel card over your actual graphic card... another user already commented on how to fix it in windows 10, so here's for windows 11:    1.Right-click the Windows icon in the taskbar, then select Settings.   2. Click System > Display > Graphics.    3. Select your app, then click Options. If you don't see it, go to your steam, right click on Zero sievert>properties>browse local files (where you see the .exe file)> copy this path    Choose your graphic card    Click Save.(source: XDA developers website and my own experience)

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good game but still needs a lot of work. With a lot of the gunplay changes, I don't think they really have an idea of how to make combat work with this top down format. The bullet glancing system is straight up bad. And because you NEED an SMG/shotgun (probably SMG) to kill the melee enemies that repeatedly run through you and you NEED a sniper (or something with a scope and high damage) for when there's an enemy sniper 2-shotting you from off screen, that's your loadout end game. Sniper and smg. That's all you can bring with unless you want to run into no-win scenarios. It's very limiting. The irony is that the devs made these gunplay changes with the intent of increasing weapon diversity but they ended up decreasing it instead.Also still lots of just bugs with mission objectives spawning inside walls and whatnot. Like a lot. But hey, it's early access. Overall a pretty fun game but I feel like the changes made over the past year (other than just adding content) have been misguided and sometimes even made the game worse. Kinda getting worried about where the game is gonna end up but holding out hope that they can get it back on track. Worst case, it's still worth $20 for the ~100 hours of fun I've had with it so far. Ignore the people with 50 hours of playtime saying it wasn't worth $20 lolUPDATE: Per their update on June 4th, looks like they were working on multiplayer a lot for the past few months and have tabled it cause the engine doesn't easily support it. They'll be focusing more on core gameplay and content again which is great to hear. Still think the gunplay could use some work (an M4 does not have this much recoil guys, it's 5.56) and I hope they add an option to remove the bullet glancing/efficient range mechanics entirely for those that don't like them. But overall really excited for 1.0 and the new content.

_childDocuments_.review: Early Access:“Greed” would be a great alternative title for this game. I’m sure there are plenty of reviews comparing ZERO Sievert to a budget Tarkov with elements from Stalker but at it’s core it feels like a gambling simulator. You get tasks from various people littered throughout the bunker and you venture into one of several different maps to collect items to fulfill said tasks. Assuming you survive long enough to find the item or items a question crosses your mind, “Do I leave now or do I collect more loot?” Become the Rat Lord you always wanted to be. Carry a pistol with only 15% health and 10 rounds in hopes you can kill a bandit with a rifle with the same amount of health with little to no ammo. It doesn’t matter, like everything else you will just sell it when you get back. Constantly collecting rare items and money until you purchase some nice armor… and then do it all over again for the next upgrade. It’s Early Access and it isn’t perfect but it’s lots of fun.

_childDocuments_.review: It's not for everyone, and let's preface that with, I did finish the game, but I kinda enjoyed it? But also pretty much didn't. Doesn't make sense? I'll explain. What this game does great, is litter your early game with incredibly tense combat AND extremely satisfying victories. Combat itself is not difficult to pick up or master, and every early run will feel like a champion crawling back from a bloodstained pit clutching spoils torn from the viscera of whatever it is you've recently slain. It's great, it's satisfying, it doesn't last forever.What this game does poorly, is pretty much everything else. The AI on enemies will often flip flop wildly between, "Will run into their own thrown grenade" to "This mediocre bandit with an ill gotten sniper rifle has locked onto you in the dead of night without having night vision goggles, and will immediately two tap you once you scuttle out from that rock you hid behind." It's really not fun to have a suppressed weapon in the dead of night, shoot one guy, and suddenly the sniper that is beyond your field of vision has immediately locked onto you and is killing you from an area you quite literally cannot see. Speaking of, weapon balance is pretty poor, and most of your fighting will be done at the very edges of your screen. You 100% have to pick up a sniper rifle, because 95% of the fighting will happen at the edge of your screen. Subbing in an AR or an SMG just allows you to either waste stragglers when they charge you, or kill hordes of mutants when they get too close. All the guns feel same-samey, and you'll probably end up just picking the guns that have the highest armor penetration ammo. If you do pick up the game, the ZZ Vel will carry you throughout the entire game and can be acquired early. Loot balance AND faction reputation are pretty poor. There's an entire faction that quite literally cannot set up because they've been beset by mutants, so you single handedly go in and wipe all the mutants out, letting them proliferate across the maps. Oh but sorry, they won't let you buy the nicer weapons or high armor penetration ammo unless you officially join their faction, which will piss off another faction increasing the amount of danger per raid. But then, there will be random scavengers just out and about toting around full magazines said ammo, or just loose leaf ammo hanging around in boxes. Why? It's highly unlikely random scavs killed what was supposed to be an elite corporation of soldiers and scientists, but then again, they were dying to run of the mill irradiated cannibals. Regardless, joining a faction should offer benefits on price, free stockpiles of supplies, or free equipment every so often, it should not simply prevent players from getting to the equipment end-game.Difficulty is entirely artificial once you get into the meat and potatoes. At first, it'll seem difficult because you don't have nicer equipment, or full durability armor. Once you do, you'll realize the game is really only difficult cause everyone can die in 3 shots or 3 melee hits, but the game will spam 7-30 enemies at you all at once. Nothing says frustrating like having to repeat the same quest 6 or 7 times in a row because they want you to clear out an area filled with ranged units that can 3 tap you, while they hangout with the best protecting armor in the game, AND there's 30 of them in that area. Or earlier in the game, clear out this lab that has 4 mutant nests in it that spawn 10 mutants each, on top of the mutants that already live in the lab. It's just annoying. Doesn't help that melee attacks slow you, preventing your escape, AND all melee units will just sit on top of you hitting you over and over until you die. It also really doesn't help that said units are extremely fast, and all enemies offer basically 0 audio cues until they're right on top of you. Lastly, smaller mediocre gripes. Saving money is incredibly easy, and there's not really much to spend it on. At best you'll need repair kits, but those only cost like 4k each, and when you come home with 40-80k, you're not really making a dent. There's no point to offering an armor repair service if the guy can't repair any higher tier armor. Faction reputation AND skill levels need to be leveled up way faster than currently implemented. Higher tier armors could be more durable. The ending and overall story was really not satisfying or interesting at all. Some quest items being randomly generated instead of consistently lootable is complete nonsense. 50% faster loot speed perk should be the norm. Perks all in all seem tacked on rather than something useful. Why can't I shuffle stashes or at the very least rename them? How come when you're done with a questline it just cuts off rather than having any form of notice that says, "Hey this is the end of this questline."? What's the deal with weapon vendors selling you a weapon but not carrying all the attachments for it too? How come there's no mechanic to maintain your weapons? Why isn't penetration explained in "this bullet can pierce up to this armor class" instead of what we currently have, which is a random arbitrary value? All in all, it can be fun? But honestly it's still really, really jank for a "fully released" game, and there's a ton of areas that can be improved and expanded upon. For 20 dollars, it's an alright, "play it until it gets frustrating" game. I wouldn't recommend it to anyone that isn't super into Tarkov esque combat combined with Stalker vibes. 6/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Tl;dr: A solid game I have found enjoyable. There are a few flaws, but it's in early access.The premise of the game is to head out into a low-rez isometric environment filled with creatures and people that want to kill you, then return alive with loot to improve your equipment or quarters or to complete quests.Graphics: 3/10While this is a pixelated retro-styled game, there is a fair amount of detail to the those scenery sprites, especially the grasses. The characters are not great by retro-style pixel standards, so there is room for improvement without losing the feel of the game.Gameplay Loop: 7/10It can take a bit long to achieve anything notable, especially at the start. 'Breaking even' alone can be a bit tricky in middling difficulties simply because food and water is so expensive and the rewards for quest completion are considerably less. Despite this, each semi-randomly generated 'hunt' can feel brutal, a quick stop in the inventory screen can have you killed by a boar hiding behind a rock in no time, forcing you to start the hunt over. Making it to the extraction zone can feel like a relief. Audio: 4/10There's no music to speak of and the sound effects can be a bit bland. For example, using a Geiger counter crackle as a mouse-over sound. Music is only on the menu screen and is not good. Despite this, the sound does what it's supposed to.Story: 0/10There is no story save for the one you craft yourself.Verdict: 7/10While no single one of the above values is exceptional, the finished product is greater than the sum of its parts, and I look forward to seeing what is to come.Criticisms:The main one is that the game gets easier as you progress, rather than being more challenging.

_childDocuments_.review: Zero Sievert is a good game in its own right - mechanically sound, stupendous performance, incredible sound design, and impressive graphics for what it is. I really enjoyed my playthrough of the title. I particularly enjoyed the difficulty options that really let me pick how I wanted to play the game, as well as the feeling of growth and development as I slowly accrued wealth, skills, and better gear. The slow power creep that you get to enjoy, the finding of components and attachments for guns you have yet to unlock, playing with the various armors that the game offers to find out which one suits your playstyle best, fiddling with the different skills and specializations - all incredibly fun. I unabashedly enjoyed my time with the game and would recommend it to anyone who likes extraction shooters and doesn't mind playing them in singleplayer where Kibba is the only hacker you have to deal with. Twin stick shooter + extraction shooter = match made in heaven.The problem? Most of Zero Sievert's world building and mechanics are ripped from popular contemporaries. Whether it is coincidence or not, Zero Sievert *borrows* quite a bit from Stalker and Escape from Tarkov. Obviously given the russo-influences that is to be expected to an extent, but anomalies are really only found in Stalker and the variety of lootables from Tarkov are more or less 1:1 represented in Zero Sievert. Again, this is not really a problem given than Zero Sievert is more or less sold as a combination of those games with one less dimension. Food for thought for sure though.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely love the atmosphere and the tense extraction journey when you finally find that last item you need or a find a gun with some sick attachments. Especially while over encumbered which is like 90% of my time in this game. The sounds are wonderfully immersive, the gameplay is challenging but rewarding. I love that you can loot everything on enemies. Like his gun? Kill him and take it. Enemy using the same caliber as you? Kill him and steal his ammo. My two biggest gripes with the game:1) When I need an item and I can see it on a table but it's purely decoration. It has to be in a container to loot it. I can't pick up a power drill off of a table.2) No co-op. I'd absolutely love to scavenge with a friend or two. There could be co-op specific objectives that require teamwork to accomplish and extra enemies to compensate for the extra people. Of course friendly fire will have to be necessary to add to the mayhem. Sharing ammo and healing supplies or even having the ability to heal your friend would add so much to the game. I'm not sure PVP would work in a game like this. It'd be too easy to pick someone off with a scoped weapon and end their run. Last recommendation, have the option to have to load magazines for the weapons that support mags. The extra prep of having to load a couple mags before I head off on an adventure or having to hide out somewhere to reload the mags with some bullets would add an extra touch of realism. This also means collecting mags out of other weapons you find or purchasing extra mags to have on hand would be super useful. I really enjoyed it in Into the Radius. Collecting mags from weapons, filling them up and having to cycle through and keep track of how many I had left added a new dimension to combat.

_childDocuments_.review: So I first saw ZERO Sievert during Next Fest last year, while it looked good I skipped past it as I only had a Steam Deck and didn't think the game style would play well on such a device. Fast forward a few months, I received the game as a gift from a friend (thanks Alex) a decided to give it a go.  At first the gameplay was very difficult, almost too difficult but I still was in the beginning stages and trying to find a control scheme on Steam Deck that worked for me. I was using both thumb sticks and figuring out controls because at the time controller was not supported. I ended up making my own controller configuration and use the right track pad to aim and that has worked so much better for me. I've really enjoyed all of my time on here exclusively on Steam Deck. Ok back to gameplay, yes it was very difficult at first but it felt rewarding to extract from a zone with some loot and complete missions. Every extraction got a little easier as I was figuring out armor/weapons and enemies. Missions have been designed well and still feel rewarding finding what you need and trying to progress. Going to a new area for the first few times can feel nerve-wracking because you have no idea what you may face but overall is thrilling. Enemy movement seems to have been done really well, when in a shootout they'll peek out and shoot, take cover or even scout you out. Multiple play styles are supported as well, you can speed along or go slow and steady. Weapon tuning and attachments are pretty good and makes you feel like they can actually make a difference in gun play. At this point idk if I'm rambling or not I don't write many reviews but I'll try and close out. This has been a wonderful game to play and I'm still not done yet. Since release there have been several updates that fix bugs, introduce QOL features and even new events events overall. A lot of people say this is a STALKER/Tarkov mix and they're probably right about that (I have yet to play either unfortunately). I'd highly recommend anyone give this game a try who enjoys anything post-apocalyptic, extraction, top-down shooter, etc. The developer has really put a lot of time and effort into this game and you can tell how much they enjoy making it. Thanks again to Alex for the game, Cabo for all they're work they've put in and the ZERO Sievert community for help along the way.

_childDocuments_.review: While i really enjoy this game, i can't help but feel like its perspective is putting it at a massive disadvantage. The core gameplay is solid. Drop in one of several large areas, loot materials and quest items, get out alive, rinse repeat until you're a walking armory with more crackers than a limp bizkit concert. Its the first very solid extraction shooter out right now aside from Tarkov with its single player mod. The problem is hot infuriating the top-down perspective can be at times, and how many deaths are from simply walking into a boar or a mutant because you didn't 360 enough to see everything around you. Audio cues could fix this issue with proximity sounds around enemies, or even just more of a delay between "i see you" and "i attack you". I like the game, i really do, but i would LOVE the game if it was first person. A sequel with that perspective and same core gameplay would be amazing, maybe even Risk of Rain 2 levels of hype. Its great for the price and the dev is open to experimenting and adapting to feedback, so i can see this game being wildly different at 1.0 launch.

_childDocuments_.review: All in all, this is a problematic little game that has won me over with its charming pixel graphics. It's fun to play, but all these mechanics are just working against the player for no reason and it's bogging the game down as well. I think the devs just didn't have any game design experience, and if they do have it, then they have zero UX experience. You're making a product for the users, they should be having a good time using it, not being inconvenienced every step of the way, jumping hoops just to get to the gameplay.I wrote all the problems in detail but steam just decided to lose them. I'll just note the main points here. Inventory system is not as good as it could be. Combat feels good but there are some enemies (mainly boars) that are too overpowered if even one ever gets close to you (hitting with their asses and doing spins in place). Reputation system is good but it gets bogged down by enemies and friendlies being too hard to tell apart (you either risk your life getting close or kill friendlies and lose reputation). Base building makes zero sense. You should just be able to swap out modules without having to destroy the previous ones (what we just throw an entire gym away?). Also, for what reason do we need to have them as an item and then use the item but we have to install the module as a level 0 module first? What? Why can't I just click craft on the crafting table and it enables the installation of the module, and I can disable / enable them whenever? It's just adding unnecessary grind into the game and punishing the player for no reason.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright so lets hit the obvious points first:This game is Tarkov, with Stalker's environment, in singleplayer. Given the quantity of mods for STALKER, that should inform you about just how many people wanted to play something akin to this.This game is quite relaxing, while still having the high stress moments of Tarkov mixed in. You'll start looting a bandit only for his two friends to pull up and start shooting. The AI, while not relentless(mostly), will find advantageous positions and outflank your cover if you aren't aggressive enough. Mutants and animals are pretty lethal, you'll need to be both sparing with reloads and accurate with your shoots. The Art is appreciably unique. I quite enjoy the looks of the locations, and the little animations for healing/eating/shooting are *chefs kiss*.This is a game that will make you play slow. If you are a Hotheaded FPS junkie this game will repeatedly kill you, over and over. It rewards you for taking your time, for choosing your positions.TLDR: Singleplayer Tarkov with Stalker Elements, Excellent Gameplay, Excellent Artstyle, only missing component would be multiplayer(I can absolutely see this being S-tier if it arrives).

_childDocuments_.review: My current experience of the game:It feels like the game become worse and worse regarding game play, with each iteration. Latest changes made so the game went from playable where you could enjoy it, in the hunter mode, to an extremely hard mode, where everything will one tap you. I rather play games which have much better balance, which this game doesn't have. It's to difficult to make money after latest changes regarding the quests. It's not a fun game any more, as it also feels much more linear than before. The inventory managements is worst thing about this game. I much rather play the old Stalker Anomaly game.My old review was much more positive:It's a good game but it have some frustrated game mechanics like the inventory management and so on...Improvements I would like to see, for an otherwise fantastic fun game.1. Would be good if you changed so the durability of armor hold up much better. Right now the armor hold up equal good as paper. Sometimes one battle brings down the durability from 100% to 0%. For example in EFT and Stalker the armor don't get destroyed at all equal fast as in this game. Even higher tier armor is like paper.2. I feel also the night could be slightly shorter, like 2 hours or so. So 2h longer day time would be good to have.3. It would also be good if traders could have more money so you can at least sell everything from one raid. Give each trader an own economy with slightly higher average money than today or give traders higher total cash. Maybe bar keeper could have less average money than the green trader.4. The traders maybe could also sell some randomized stuffs. Because today you know exactly what they sell, making it little boring to check the traders what they sell. However some items should always be there like healing items for the doctor, etc... Maybe not the best stuffs should be there all the time.4. I feel like the inventory management is a night mare. Where it's hard to find items you are interested in. I would rather have less slots/tabs if you could stack many more items on each slot. So instead of 3-5 items you could stack like 10-20 items on each slot. For ammo it could be like 200-800 on each slot depending on ammo type.5. It would be good that you can check with a glance on your active mission if you can do the quest in the zone you currently are in. Today I need to read all text for each quest. For example by high lighting those mission with yellow color and beside the mission also write out the zone you need to go to.6. I also hope later on there will be new bases, which you can go to and rebuild your hide out at, who have more advanced traders and so (like Rostok in Stalker). _childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Robotron with Resource ManagementI dont understand all the positive reviews. This is NOT an excellent game... its barely a phone-game. I don't mind the simple graphics but everything about it is needlessly work intensive in an un-fun way. 30 different ammo types - ok - visually indistinguishable without mousing over for the popup - bad. And this trend continues to each of the hundreds of inventory items - can't tell what that splotch is? mouse over it - popup - its a sandwich which will restore a little hunger, but also add a little thirst... SO MANY MOUSEOVERS. Multiple statuses to maintain (rads, thirst, health, hunger, energy) with multiple resources particular to each - too much. Guns are not distinctive in use or effect, learning curve seems designed to be frustrating - not from difficulty but from making the interface and world difficult to interpret. Gunplay is NOT good - its just mouse pointing and clicking where visual obstacles may or may not deflect bullets, Enemy AI just charges as often as not. Need more resources to manage? Why not add in equipment maintenance, ammo manufacture, etc... the whole thing is just a lot of work to play. Basically the whole thing is a marginal game of Robotron with resource management.Convinced the positive reviews are the developers and buddies. This is not a good game.

_childDocuments_.review: **I wrote this as a note during beta release before I was able to post it here so some things might no longer be accurate**Zero Sievert is pretty fun and that's saying a lot for me because I don't normally enjoy 8-bit games. It's much like a top down, PvE version of Tarkov with some S.T.A.L.K.E.R-ish elements. First thing to get out of your head before playing is that it is not Tarkov and you don't lose what you bring in with you. If you loot and die, you lose the loot you gained from that raid only. Your inventory, health, etc is only affected if you extract. You have 5 stats to monitor in the game aside from stamina and item durability: health, energy, hunger, hydration, and radiation. My biggest complaint about the game is that you lose energy very quickly and your carry weight is dependent on two things: your equipped bag and your energy (UPDATE: I realize now that food and water affect carry weight slightly). The fact that energy drains so quickly means that you will never carry full capacity and at any moment you could be carrying things just fine, then get into a firefight and all of a sudden not be able to run or move because your energy went down. One more thing that's not great right now is how fast your hydration drains (I believe they may have fixed this). Hunger isn't so bad because there's lots of food in the maps and it's quite easy to craft. Hydration, however, is not very easy to bring back up. There aren't many vendors that sell drinks and vendor items are very, very limited and do not replenish until the next day cycle. You can sleep (which brings your energy back up) but when you wake you've lost even more hunger and hydration. The game has lots of potential and I will be playing the ♥♥♥♥ out of it.

_childDocuments_.review: Update:I've been a big defender of the developer but its become difficult to recommend this game without them addressing if they will change their mind about the weapon range damage system. Basically if your target is out of range the guns bullets will do no damage and in theory there may have been an interesting idea but now it has made the game less fun and the logic behind this system doesn't seem to be addressed.  The developers have kept working on adding content which I appreciate and see but the fact that this large vocal group of players and their dissatisfaction is not even acknowledged makes me worried they will never adjust or change the system. I'm still hopeful things can turn around but for now I can't recommend people to buy this EA game until there is a discussion for the range damage system.-----------------------------------------I'm usually a bit wary of early access games but after playing the beta I really wanted to support the developers to see this game come to completion. _childDocuments_.review: I'll review both the "exploration/fight" gameplay action and the "extraction" gameplay loop.- Action -I like topdown shooters a lot more than I like first person shooters. It comes down to my preference to know what's around me. It's not fun for me to get killed from enemies I didn't see from the side or back.This game's gunfight balance is closer to "Hotline Miami"'s style, where the fights are fast: you or your opponent usually take a few shots, that are too fast to dodge, to die. I really enjoy the hectic and fast and chaotic fights of hotline miami, it's a matter of taking cover until you are ready to come out a deliver your shot in under one second, or else you get shot instead.It's not comparable to other topdown shooters like "enter the gungeon" or "Nuclear throne", where bullets are slow enough for you to dodge. (The difference is that you'd would often fight 10 enemies at once with 20+ bullets at once).Long story short: you have to be careful. Advance slowly and pay attention so you're not caught off-guard, or you'll be dead or severly injured before you have the time to react. If you do pay attention, then you have a chance in taking the opponents offguard and kill them before they react.Yes it's exciting to be on your toes and advancing with care, but the map is big, 90% of the time you'll be walking alone with not much to do. When you encounter a house to loot, you'll be rewarded with some scraps material and rotten bread.So a particular run feel either:1) Boring because I spent 10 minutes walking slowly and kill offguard enemies2) Unfair because I get killed/injured without knowing what happened because I went to fast. - Extraction -I played in Hunter mode, which I believe is the "original extraction difficulty".In the Roguelike (you lose everything when you die, no progress cary over) to Roguelite (You make/keep some progress even when you die) spectrum, Zero Sievert sits in the middle.You lose everything you carry like in a Roguelike, so the punishement for death is high.You can start a run with gear that you previously collected, making a run easier because of previous progress, like a Roguelite.However there' one additional element that destroys any balance the game could have: You can go to the extraction site any time you want!Some other extraction games would require you to complete a mission before you are allowed to extract. But Zero Sievert allows to go for the exit at any time.Which means: If you get lucky and loot something good in a chest at the beginning, you can leave immediately.If you take on a fight a leave badly injured, you can call it quits and go for the extraction site.What an anti-climactic loop.It's at the same time: less exciting than a roguelike/lite, but also more punishing than a mission based shooter?Atleast in a roguelike/lite, you either win or die. So even if you only have 1HP left, you can't just quit. You have to start the next encounter and pray the gods will smile at you and allow you to survive or recover. Of course you might die, but atleast you died trying as hero with all your might.In Zero Sievert: cowardice is rewarded. Even if you only looted a few rabbit fur and other crap, well you don't want to lose your gun right? And you already took some hit with only 50% HP left... Well medkits are kinda expensive so wouldn't it best to just leave the map, get healing, and then come back?In a way Dark Souls could be considered an "extraction rpg", where you lose ALL your souls when you die. But atleast you still have one chance to regain them when you walk up to your corpse. So you could always take more risk and try to go for the homerun.It's a very strange balance to be able to choose your own risk and reduce it to close to zero.

_childDocuments_.review: If you like the vibe of Stalker and Tarkov, but like something that is a bit more relaxed and single player than Tarkov, then this game has you covered. It's a great looter-shooter / extract shooter in a top down perspective with a very enjoyable core gameplay loop. Go into a raid, grab what you can, complete missions, extract. I can highly recommend the Hunter difficulty (drop everything on death) because I think it makes the game last a lot longer and be more enjoyable with high stakes, but there is A LOT of options to the difficulty (think like Project Zomboid level difficulty options) so you can play how you want to. Also, the game is a masterclass in player-friendly design. At the home base you can instantly teleport between vendors so you don't have to walk everywhere. Carrying too much loot in missions will slow you down, but you can move normally even if overweight in the base. This game was perfect for me because I was looking for a less intense, single person Tarkov and that's basically exactly what it is, but it has it's own charm and some of the supernatural elements from something like STALKER. Best game of the year in my opinion.

_childDocuments_.review: I initially bought this game in early access a few days after the release of the .40 update. This was a controversial update because it altered the gunplay by causing bullets that land outside of your weapon's effective range to do less damage. It also added a deadzone for close-range shots in which they have a decreased chance to penetrate as well as an increased glancing shot chance. It also added recoil and bullet spread.However, the new skill system addresses most of the controversies with the .40 update, by adding skills which will eventually drastically increase the effective range of most weapons, as well as reduce the size and penalty of the close range deadzone. I would recommend anyone who quit because of the .40 update give the game another try.Now that the game is in 1.0, I can fairly confidently say it is in a (mostly) finished state, with an impressive amount of content and variety for a game developed by a solo developer. I write this review after spending a few raids in the new "Zakov" city map, which is massive and sprawling, with many indoor areas representing commercial, industrial, and residential areas. It is like the Mall map on crack.There are several new guns, further increasing the already impressive variety the early access version was host to. Both American and Eastern European firearms are represented, and there are more than a dozen guns belonging to both of these categories. As for the weapon types, the game has: Assault rifles, DMRs, SMGs, Shotguns, Pistols, Sniper Rifles, and one LMG as of 1.0. The variety is further increased by the whole host of attachments. The gun customization in this game is nutty, I don't think I have ever experienced a game with this much gun customization. With that being said, I don't know how it compares to other extraction shooters like Tarkov because I haven't played them.As for negatives, the game is still a bit rough around the edges in some places. Combat is very snappy and addictive but enemies can get stuck in walls and shoot you when you can't shoot them. Enemies with sniper rifles need to spot you from within the area covered by your screen, but they can shoot you from far offscreen, which can be very frustrating when you accidentally aggro an enemy and then get sniped by them from a place where you have no hope of seeing them. Rocks can also spawn in front of doorways and prevent access to locations, requiring you to restart a run to access key task areas. This makes playing on hardcore extremely frustrating. It doesn't matter on the easy "rookie" difficulty and the normal "survivor" difficulty, but but I lost multiple full gear sets to issues like this.As for non-bug issues, I think the greatest flaw with the game right now is the repair cost and fragility of max rank tier 5-6 armor. The most I have ever made from a raid is around 90k rubles. Getting shot 3-4 times will bring your tier 5-6 armor down to the 40-50% durability territory, which will cost a minimum of around 50-60k to repair. In addition, the fragility stat of max rank armors also means they get shredded extremely quickly, meaning they aren't that protective either. This discourages any playstyle apart from hanging back 200m away from enemies and slowly picking them off with a sniper rifle outside of their effective range. Any run & gun playstyle is heavily punished by the current armor repair costs.With that being said, the solo dev of the game recently made a post on the subreddit asking what issues with the game annoyed people most, and this issue was commented on the most by a long shot, so I suspect this issue will probably be fixed in future patches, as it is one of the most major gripes with the game and the solo dev is likely very aware of it at this point.

I can't wait to see the game get fleshed out as development continues!  definitely a big recommend for survival and extraction fans.  in the interest of being fair, I will point out the negatives.  there are some large indoor sections that are very same-y and mazelike where it is very easy to get lost, and some of the controls are unnecessarily confusing.  early on you'll probably have a few cheap deaths figuring out how to change fire mode and ammo type, and how to throw grenades.  fortunately there is currently a debug menu, so at least you can spawn yourself any items you lost unfairly.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: The developers have acknowledged what happened with the current update. Their plans going forward seem solid; the announcement is worth keeping in mind when deciding whether or not to buy "ZERO Sievert" in early access.As a preface, the game is in early access. I understand that it is not a complete product. However, the latest update completely breaks basic functionality.Half of the mechanics in the game do not work consistently; an entire section of the crafting station crashes to the desktop, you can become hard-locked due to main story quests being incompletable, and weapon attachments disappear without a trace.This update launched after the developers established a publicly accessible beta branch for testing game updates. It really makes you wonder if the developers even ran the game before pushing out the update, as all of the issues are immediately apparent and game-breaking.The mood around this update is strange. In the past, the developers had such great communication and even announced delays related to the update cycle. As a fellow developer, I understand being excited to share new content and features. However, the current release of the game is half-baked. With this release, the game took five steps forward and twenty steps back.As a request to the developers: please announce a delay if the update is not ready. Many great companies have released terrible products recently because they were forced to stick to a release date. I really enjoy this game, as evidenced by my playtime, and I don't want to see people (rightfully) toss it aside because it is a buggy mess.Building consumer trust back up is really hard. New players do not have the same understanding and background knowledge to see what the game is like when it works well. New consumers only experience what is present at the time.As much as I love the game, I cannot currently recommend Zero Sievert. I hope that this patch was a mistake rather than the start of a pattern. Even after all these game-breaking bugs are patched, I would be hesitant to recommend buying the game.As a consumer, wait until the developers show whether untested, bug-riddled updates become the norm.
