_childDocuments_.review: As an Escape from Tarkov and S.T.A.L.K.E.R. player, I came to this game with high hopes of playing something similar, even if it is at a much smaller scale. Sadly, I was rather disappointed by how promising it was, yet how many concepts were badly implemented.- There are factions in the game with which you need to build up reputation in order to access better gear and supplies. You gain reputation with these factions by doing repeatable quests that refresh every (in game) day. These quests are not inspired, they are generic and brings memories of MMO type of daily quests. These quests get stale really fast and they can vary a lot in difficulty which may slow down your faction reputation progress down to a slog if the RNG gods hate you.TLDR: Reputation quests are boring and RNG dependent.- The gunplay is.. not great. Weapons have a maximum and a minimum range. I presume this is in order to balance out the weapons types, but it doesn't really do that. Bullets have different armour piercing values which determines if your bullets actually go through the enemy armour or not. The highest AP on SMG bullets allows penetration of tier 3 ( out of 6 ) armour which is never going to be enough especially in the end game, which results in you still using the same weapon types in the end game but they just feel bad. I forgot to mention that these penalties do not apply to the enemy, which creates an unfair playing field.- Enemies most of the time have high armour piercing bullets which just shred you no matter what, This wouldn't be so bad if the AI had more than 2 states: Braindead and Perfect Aimbot. End game felt extremely cheesy due to this, as the best and safest way ( by far ) to engage soldiers was to sit as far as possible and shoot them with the sniper, otherwise you will be swarmed and peppered with bullets incredibly fast.- I've also encountered several bugs, but I am not going to list them all. The most frustrating was when terrain generation was acting up and blocked up certain entrances making it impossible to enter buildings required for quests or such.Overall, this game had an incredible amount of potential, yet the implementation has lead to a rather frustrating experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Early Access review, November 24th 2022.Holy crap this game is fantastic! When out on a hunt, Zero Sievert constantly has me on the edge of my seat. The gunplay is as good as it gets in a 2D game, and the sound effects are great. The game also has very clever details that make the experience even more immersive. For example, if after an intense gunfight your enemy's corpses are spread out in tall grass, they can be very hard to spot. But at some point I realised the birds would come eat from the corpses, telling me where to collect my loot! It might seem like a minor detail, but to me little things like this can really make a game. If the early access stamp worries you: the game seems very stable and in my first 12 hours of gameplay I have encountered no bugs (apart from some typos and grammatical errors). I very highly recommend this game!Disclaimer: like so many pixel art indie games, Zero Sievert is tough as nails. Don't expect to just walk around guns blazing, clearing levels. You need to think about when, if at all, to engage, and with what type of ammo. You will die a LOT. Don't buy the game if this is not your jam.Edit: November 26th, 2022: In the 10 or so hours after writing this review, I actually encountered quite a few bugs. For me personally it doesn't take away much of the fun, but I felt I had to mention it.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll admit it, when I looked at this game and saw the Tarkov-esque gameplay loop, I was scared. The idea that you make one wrong button press and you've lost 100% of what you brought in and grabbed Is what pushes me away from those types of games, but ZERO Sievert doesn't punish players that hard. Every time you load into a level, you will come out with the equipment you didn't use (or all of it, tbh I wasn't paying that much attention to my inventory). If you die, you simply pop back out by the conductor and are free to go back into it. If you escape, then you get to keep what you grabbed and make progress to expanding your capabilities. The game is willing to let you gut most weapons, and the modification system is straight and to the point, this part gives you x accuracy and y recoil, and that's it. And from what I've gotten and from the look of the screenshots, this game is willing to give you the pieces necessary to make your gun look like it came from terminator if you wanted it to. Granted, I only have 1 hour of playtime as of writing this, but this is honestly very fun! I seriously recommend giving this a look if your interested in a soviet apocalypse.

_childDocuments_.review: Zero Sievert is a post-apocalyptic survival game developed by indie game studio, Red Beat. The game is set in a world where a nuclear disaster has wiped out most of humanity, leaving only a few survivors struggling to survive in the wasteland.The game's main protagonist is a survivor who must navigate the dangerous and radioactive world in search of resources, shelter, and other survivors. The gameplay is a mix of exploration, resource management, and combat.The game's graphics are impressive, with a dark and atmospheric art style that perfectly captures the desolate post-apocalyptic setting. The sound design is equally impressive, with an eerie soundtrack that adds to the game's sense of dread and danger.Zero Sievert's gameplay is challenging, but not frustratingly difficult. Players must carefully manage their resources, including food, water, and medicine, as well as ammunition and other supplies. The game also features a crafting system that allows players to create useful items such as weapons, tools, and shelter.Combat in Zero Sievert is a mix of melee and ranged combat, with a variety of weapons available, including guns, melee weapons, and improvised weapons. The combat system is intuitive and responsive, allowing players to engage in exciting battles with the game's dangerous enemies.Overall, Zero Sievert is an excellent post-apocalyptic survival game that offers a challenging and immersive gameplay experience. With its impressive graphics, atmospheric soundtrack, and intuitive combat system, Zero Sievert is a must-play for fans of the survival genre.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who doesn't have the time or the stone-cold killer mindset to get into Tarkov, this game is amazing. It has the satisfaction of looting, selling, and gradually stockpiling a dragon's hoard of post-apocalyptic Eastern European treasure that I've always wanted, but in a top-down, pixel art, single player package.Despite its kind-of-cute presentation, ZERO Sievert is an ultra-deadly game with some impressive AI. Once alerted to your presence, enemies will spray you with suppressing fire before pushing or flanking. Even with decent armor, regular bandits can still pose a threat if you don't isolate and outmaneuver them. Then there are the S.T.A.L.K.E.R. inspired hazards: wild animals, mutants, radiation pockets, and anomalies.Nearly everything in the world of ZERO Sievert is trying to keep you from escaping the map with your hard-earned loot. But don't be discouraged if you're not into punishing games, because the difficulty is highly customizable. Every aspect of combat, looting, and even the economy can be adjusted to your liking, with additional hardcore options like losing your gear on death.In short, ZERO Sievert is like a lightweight, highly accessible single player version of Tarkov with elements of S.T.A.L.K.E.R. Play super hardcore with ironman mode turned on and a punishing economy, or chill with no threat of losing your stuff and enjoy mowing down bandits.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: The game is not bad, but I can't recommend it either as certain mechanics annoy me too much.The game tries to be a mix of stalker and Escape From Tarkov in 2d and does so reasonably well and the story was good imo. I had fun and the game certainly improved constantly during early access, though the final release felt more like a cut corner than a final leap. The gameplay loop and looting is fine and certain difficulty aspects will certainly appeal to an audience. However some mechanics are more on the edge of bad than on difficult:- most important: Having red–green color blindness i must say that i found it next to impossible to distinguish most of the faction-npcs you meet on your raids. Which really does suck when you don't want to damage your reputation needlessly but also don't know whether they will just shoot you up when you come closer. At least the scientists and bandits (and some late game faction) were easy to tell. Maybe there could have been some reputation-/faction-/indicator pop up after aiming at somebody for a couple seconds - enemies engaged in melee combat sometimes "move along", preventing you to be able to hit them back. Feels ill-designed and annoying but getting meleed with a gun usually does not end well either so there is at least a point.- the fog of war has no near radius so you can just walk past enemies. Again, learn to watch your corners but i would argue for being able to perceive somebody breathing right into my neck- there is one main quest which requires you to find 2 keys that are random drops from cabinets. Wasted a lot of time on the last one and eventually cheated it in (either rare or i was just unlucky). Imho there should be a way to progress with the story without getting stuck on random chance- the enemies view-range is equal in the horizontal and vertical axis while yours is not. So fighting left-to-right is both safer and easier while i often got hit and killed despite looking as far as i could into the upwards direction without being able to see the enemy. And yes, i got sniped despite looking as far as i could with the best scope in game (did see the muzzle flash so there is that i guess)- There is no mechanic of making sure that you don't end up in the middle of a group of enemies when entering buildings or using the spawns on the last map, leading to rather unfair deaths- In some cases random map-objects had been blocking the entrances to key map parts needed for missions, requiring to come back with another raidTo be clear: I don't mind dying in "hardcore" games as long as there is something that can be learned from it. And sadly this does not always seem to be the case, and that is not just me being bad (which to be honest I kind of am).In the end i found myself trying to get the game over with instead of looking forward to it.

_childDocuments_.review: Still in the first zone, but already feel like I can give this Early Access game a nice glowing review. I've been looking for single-player extraction shooters for years, since messing with the SP Tarkov mods. Recently picked up Hell Is Others, which while alright, botched a lot of things that Zero Sievert nails.First off, giving the player customized difficulty options is such a huge deal imho. It's always nice to find a developer who's chief goal is that the people playing their game have a fun time. If 1-hit kills, losing all of your gear on death,  and other extreme design elements that are so prevalent in other extraction shooters turn you off, you can mitigate those things easily here. Really love the focus on using stealth and setting up ambushes, as opposed to running into every encounter guns blazing. One other thing Iove is how generous the devs are with storage capacity, and you can even unlock some great perks that do things like increase your overall carrying capacity each time you level up.If you're on the fence about this one, I think it's an easy recommendation. Especially if you ever found joy in playing games like the S.T.A.L.K.E.R. series.-------------------------~ I am a former Quality Assurance Lead Tester, with over 20 years in the industry and nearly 40 years of PC and Console gaming experience. ~ Video Games are my lifeblood and I hope my reviews provide potential buyers with ample information to help them make a decision regarding their purchases.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't let the pixel graphics fool you, this game is intense because of the sound design, cone of vision, and rogue-lite design of the areas you deploy to for missions or to scavenge. The areas do not completely change; they only change the location of areas on the map each time you deploy to an area, which I think is great. I'm not even halfway done with the content in this game. And I haven't encountered any bugs yet, so that's a major plus. When it comes to the tasks/missions, though, especially if you accept a mission, don't play for a few days and come back, it's easy to forget where they actually want you to go. The mission overview is VERY barebones. And, the mission markers on the map are so random, because in some missions that have several goals to achieve, only parts of them are on the map and the other ones you have to figure out through trial and error or looking it up online.It's an 8/10 game for me. There's room for improvement, but the gameplay mechanic is very fun.And I love that it's a Game Maker game, which was the program I used to learn my first ever language.

_childDocuments_.review: I would have given this a lower positive recommendation as it is an intentionally HARD game, however the balancing and game design feels far too unfair.Human enemies are bullet sponges that can tank 30 rifle rounds to the face and two shot you in seconds even with high tier armour. Said armour is also too fragile and incredibly expensive to repair and even the basic ghoul can tear you to death in seconds.The Lab is the first dungeon in this game and a huge leap in difficulty - if you manage to get to the entrance without being mulched by a lone hunter, you have to fight through a large amount of super fast spiders, a ghoul infestation that spawns a large group of ghouls (sometimes repeatedly, other times only one group), and then there is finally the "Big" enemy which is the most tank-est enemy I've encountered so far. Still if you manage to get through all that you then have to make your way back out of the lab and to the nearest exit point. Hopefully a hunter won't pop out from a rock and murder you immediately.There are six locations although I only got up the five before I quit. Each map is randomly generated and although they look big on the map they are quite small and it doesn't take long to walk from one end to the next (the mall is an exception as it has a huge interior). The map generation is somewhat borked and will place static objects on top of interior entrances or block off small sections of the map. Sometimes NPCs and enemies will spawn on objects or in out of bound areas. Sometimes they will even do nothing while you shoot them. Fortunately they still die.There are main campaign missions and randomly generated daily missions that are basic kill and collect stuff, and sometimes go here and press F. The story is STALKER lite with no background information, your character is a nobody and there isn't an intro at the start of the game - your just standing outside of the bunker immediately after selecting difficulty and loadout.I played this on normal difficulty. I wish I played it on the beginner. You can't change the difficulty settings once you started a game. You can turn off the field of view limit in the options which completely negates one of the perks you can select when leveling up.This game feels unfinished.

_childDocuments_.review: At the current stage I can't really recommend it for $20.A few things are really unfortunate:No ultrawide support. The game runs on fixed resolutions in 16:9, that means on 21:9 or 16:10 screens (Steam Deck for example) you are stuck with ugly black bars. That's really not necessary with things like integer scaling being an option. Before you bring up "balance", it's a single player game and having enemy view distance be independent of screen width is possible. It's entirely understandable for a single dev to not bother with those, just not while asking 20€Missing complexity: The game emulates Tarkov to a degree, but there is not a lot of depth or breadth to weapons, ammo and gear stats. It falls into a trap that many tarkov clones fall into, the attempt of emulating the tetris without putting as much effort or thought into it. When you're going for the Tarkov clutter, you have to commit, otherwise it just doesn't feel the same. Again understandable for a single dev, not understandable for 20€.The game really doesn't look and feel good. The pixel art is too low fidelity, the colors and shapes clash with the game's feel and it's weird having a base full of clones. The interface is clunky and not very usable, splitting stacks and menuing is a hassle.In principle there is definitely something here, but right now I am considering a refund.

It does needs a bit of polish and tweaks on some stuff and it could turn into an even more amazing game than it already is.  Gun play and gun fights is honestly pretty solid and ♥♥♥♥♥♥ sweet for a game like this really gives me STALKER vibes when you get jumped by a pack of ghouls/boars/wolves and I got serious Tarkov vibes when I made it too the Mall and the CQB fights can get sweaty, plus the customization of weapons is truly awesome.  Now I will say some bullet damage re-works depending on caliber and bullet type and the pen/damage/recoil stats hopefully will be tweaked a bit, but also and more importantly the armor "fragility" stat and the armor degradation that happens depending on the armor level, as I understand this was done to tone down higher-tier gear to make it so you don't ever feel invincible, but if you get shot in a level 6 vest (Kibba Armor) which has a super high "fragility" stat (I think 70%), from bandits that when looted have 5.45HP's/PS, 7.62PS and even some pistol rounds absolutely KILLS the durability in around four or five shots occasionally it will tank a bit more but from my testing 7 shots with 9x18 pistol dropped a level 6 to 0% durability, yet a level 4 or 5 vest can tank 7 to 10, sometimes more, 5.45BT's, 7.62BP's, even 7.62x54rPS/SNB, and I understand the, "Don't be seen, you don't get hit, you don't take damage." but when you get into the more CQB fights it would be nice to not have to carry around armor repair kits, or before I got the repair bench I was shelling out so much money to the doc to repair my vest's or buy repair kits, I would like if they dropped the "fragility" stat altogether and just did it off bullet pen/flesh damage/type of bullet. _childDocuments_.review: I rarely review games on Steam, and it's even rarer that I wouldn't say anything constructive about the game itself and focus on aesthetic augmentations. However, this pixel-art game *deserves* the use of a scanline/ CRT-emulating shader used in conjunction to make it really pop. I've been using a free piece of software called ShaderGlass, and I highly recommend using it if you're playing on desktop. I use the 'crt-lottes-fast' shader at a pixel size setting of x4 for my 1080p panel, and with a bit of shader preference customisation, you can get a really nice Trinitron-style CRT overlay for this game. The hard edges are softened, and the dithering effects used in some of the graphics are rendered blurred and mixed the way games that used to look like this were on the display tech of 'their time'. Granted, I'm a bit of a CRT purist when it comes to archaic styles of graphical presentation, but it works so well I find it hard to believe anyone wouldn't prefer the overall image. It won't be for everyone to want to tinker with this kind of thing, I accept, but I urge you to try it. Great game; I can't add anything new that others haven't already said. Just add an extra step and an extra 5/ 10 minutes of tinkering and make it look the way it deserves to look. Caveat: a lot of these shaders require some GPU grunt, so you might need a significantly higher-end system than the minimum/ recommended specs advertised as necessary for only the game itself.

_childDocuments_.review: What can I say? I'm Hooked.I've heard this game described as a 2-D mashup of S.T.A.L.K.E.R, and Escape from Tarkov, which is pretty accurate.The style and flavor of S.T.A.L.K.E.R is there, you've got your post-apocalyptic zone, your anomalies and mutants, soldiers, scientists, 'hunters' and bandits. The general game-play loop will remind you of EFT: you bring whatever gear, ammo, and supplies you think you'll need into a mission on one of several maps in an attempt to loot and complete missions before extracting back to home-base. Mind you, you do not lose everything you brought in should you die. However, losing whatever you've gathered, or whatever quest progress you've made so far on that mission is plenty punishing enough.In this way, the game builds a lot of tension and forces you into some tough decisions: "Do I try to complete this quest before I leave, risking the precious loot I just picked up?"The S.T.A.L.K.E.R series is absolutely dear to my heart, but the 'survival game' shoe doesn't really fit on the vanilla games, where food and water become irrelevant after about two minutes. Food and water feel precious in this game as they should, and the survival elements stitch pretty seamlessly into the combat and overall game loop.The mechanics are likewise well-done and polished. Using good gear, ammo, positioning, tactics, and awareness will most often reward you with a successful run. The devs implemented a cover and line-of-sight system, and impressively dynamic enemy AI that make engagements even with enemies below your 'tier' engaging and non-trivial. There were only a handful of times that I've died on a mission and thrown up my hands as if "aw come on, you kidding me?" Most often I've had to admit to myself that I'd bungled my decision-making, execution, or both. _childDocuments_.review: Hidden GemThis is the best 2D Tarkov style PVE extraction shooter in fact I would say its way more fun than the greedy russian game itself. Why have you never heard of this game because its one guy with zero marketing making it and boy is it impressive considering. Many people have quit Tarkov and The Cycle and for those people you will love this game in fact its a great game for many.Game has a great foundation, the systems feel right, walking around gunning as you eat drink heal etc feels overall good without being too oppressive. The gameplay loop of getting home with your goodies feels good and makes you care about your runs. There are plenty of maps and content to explore here getting 100% will probably take you a long time if you care to. The enemy AI is very good overall the bosses especially react in a way that instills real fear into you as it suddenly feels like a human is trying to hunt you down. The graphics and sound are great I love the art style the scale of being a small cube helps to make you feel like an underdog against the odds of the apocalypse background. There's plenty of enemies and creatures to and lots of guns to fight them with all with punchy sound effects.All this said the game is NOT FINISHED maybe 60% of the way there 3 maps are missing and there is a significant amount of polish and clean up that is needed. Sadly game issues are x10 their weight when it comes to permadeath extraction shooters as you may invest significant time and skill into a run/mission only for some BS to ruin it. We accept this as players when making mistakes but alot of stuff in the game is silly/broken and I will list them hoping for changes;-Aliens they are straight busted 2 shot you in 1 second when turning a corner feels super cheap-Weather is just annoyin I get the realism attempt but walking around at 1mph feels trash get rid of all weather speed debuffs it doesnt improve the gameplay experince AT ALL!-Ghool nests once you learn the trick to them are super boring to play against get rid of them thanks-The base upgrade system needs a TOTAL REWORK it is awful I would actually get rid of it entirely and just let the player use them if they gather mats then scale the mats to quality of reward. WHY CANT I HAVE EVERY BASE WORKBENCH ! silly-Missions pacing is awful and needs totally streamlining made more clear with more ways to find where you are supposed to go many missions you will be on youtube trying to figure out why your mission has not triggered etc.-Upgrade system and weapons acquired pacing is awful I feel like once I got my 2nd gun I didnt get any improvement for a long time. Many weapons feel pointless other than for style hence I stuck to my rifle  90% of the time and mines and nades are super clunky to use.-Get rid of player upgrade books and just have it go up as you play the game and do those related actions thanks. -Costs of items/upgrades etc are insanely expensive one example is the lighting in the base, 24 bulbs took me 40 hours to get are you insane. Also I had no idea what it was I thought it was going to give me ability to make torches or something lol-Faction system is not finished I want more choices on who I can align with would be nice if all 4 could be chosen from and weapons were NOT related to that. I think the game would be more fun it every map had the 4 factions present maybe I could be a mad scientist or a bandit etc. Make the bartender sell any weapon once you sell it to him.-Day/Night cycle feels annoyin feels like you have to be perfectly awake at 8am everyday not fun-Food/Drink system is annoyin -Game needs more NPCs to interact with-Change the home base architecture its annoying to run around and looks bad.-WAY too much geo on many maps from cars to trees why am I always bumping into things it even blocks mission access sometimes as its procedural. Less density please.-Far too much radiation to the point all armor other than science hazmat feels pointless #amongus-Confusing weapon mods I never had a clue what mods are for what please add a system to know easily.-Item reveal time is far too slow and pointless get rid of it we not in a pvp game here-Add co op at some point the game would be great with others-The swamp map is awful change it-Change the mall to be not dark its cool to look and therefore graphics are wasted-There is no counter to acid rain and lightning storms total BS-More tracking tools please-Add Drones-More weapons not just guns-Add sound meter like BOTW-Crystals and inject buffs feel pointless and annoying to use and make-Finish the menu map system Overall there maybe many problems/bugs/QOL here but they are EASY to fix and I can easily invision this game being a 10 if they polish it up and finish the games vital features and hopefully give us some good endings to aim for hopefully one for each faction. Extraction shooters are a huge investment in time and skill but this is probably the easiest one to get into so I strongly recommend people try this game to get a feel for why this genre is great and will dominate the next few years in the gaming space.psWord of warning to the developers please do not make the mistake that valhiem made not hiring enough devs to make the game great, this game will fade into the past if it is not reinvested into with its profits. Also to the players this game is best on the biggest screen you have so if you are steamdeck user make sure you have a dock.

_childDocuments_.review: OVERALL EXPERIENCE: Zero Sievert is a really fun little shooter/looter/extraction game. I wasn't entirely sure how the game experience would be once I actually started playing it, but I ended up having a really good time.WARNING: If you are the type of person that gets frustrated easily or has to be an unstoppable force a.k.a God among men as soon as you start playing a new game then this probably isn't for you. However, if you enjoy a challenge/struggle and progression process then it'll be right up your alley. By NO means is there a hard learning curve to this game, it feels really natural, but you will get smoke'd by enemies, especially right off. GRAPHICS VS. DEPTH: Don't let the lo-fi pixel graphics fool you into thinking this is a arcade-like mobile game; the combat and systems have a bit of depth to them. When you created a new game there are 3 game types (standard easy, medium, hard) But the game allows for a lot of customization to make it easier or extremely punishing which is nice to see. EARLY ACCESS: Buying and playing EA games can always be a mixed bag, but my experience has been really good (game has been out for 1 year at the time of my buying/playing it).  I have come across 0 bugs while playing it, no lost saves or crashes to report.Once you progress a bit further into the game you start to see where the DEV team are working as it is still a work in progress (new levels, missions, etc.) but even as it is right now, you can easily get 30 or so fun hours of play as long as you don't put it on easy mode.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't let this games graphics fool you. This game may look simple however I have had plenty of heart pumping moments just by playing this game. Having 18 hours in the game I feel like I can talk about the game decently enough. Gameplay: General gameplay of the game is pretty easy to get the hang of. You can select from 3 different difficulties or manually change things to tailor the game to your liking. The gameplay is similar to Tarkov without the scummy cheaters. Hostile NPCs will use cover when engaging you. And they do put up a decent fight (Unless you ambush them. Then they don't stand much of a chance). I haven't fought any boss type characters yet but I generally try to avoid them until getting the proper gear.Difficulty:This game provides good difficulty choices for new and experienced players. You do however still need to play smart with firefights and when facing mutants. Even on the Rookie difficulty you can die pretty quick if your reckless. Like I mentioned above however. If you do not like any of the difficulty choice you can simply tailor the game to your liking.Quests:You can do quests in the game much like every other game. The quests aren't generally hard however I'd assume you'll get harder quests once you get more respect from the friendly NPCs. Some quests, such as the ones to find some items, may take a while to finish as your not always guaranteed to find the items quickly. You get good rewards from completing quests. And some quests allow you to pick your reward. Ammo:This game uses multiple types of ammo for it's guns. There isn't really a "Use this ammo it's amazing" type thing. It's more you have to pick the right ammo for the job. Ammo can be expensive or cheaper as dirt depending what you set your difficulty at. Guns And Gun Customisation: This game has plenty of guns that you can choose from to use. Some guns and all gun mods are locked at the beginning until you increase your respect with the friendly traders. The guns however feel really good to use. For example some guns work really well at medium to long range fighting but might suck at close range fighting. Other work for close range but suck at long range. The game does however allow you to bring a maximum of 2 guns with you. I'd recommend you bring one for medium to long range fighting (Assault rifle or Sniper) and something for close range (SMG, Shotgun, pistol). That way your able to fight regardless of range. (Pressing K will also give you a close up look at your gun in game. So you can get a closer look at your customised gun)Locations:The locations in the game are pretty big and fun to navigate. Lootable boxes are different each run due to the maps being randomly generated. Even though the maps are decently big their pretty easy to navigate once you learn their rough layout. Most quests take part in the Forest area but your free to go to any area you wish after completing a quest for the conductor.Conclusion:Reaching the end of this review my final view of this game is it's amazing. The game is addicting if you like it's type of gameplay. Trust me you'll always have the "Just one more run" itch. I know this game is still early access. So I cannot wait to see what the team brings to the game. Hopefully this overlooked gem will get more fun content in the future and hopefully the team make this game into something amazing

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a lot of fun, worth the price so far and with more content it will just get better an better.My only complaint is the load times for the maps, its not that its very long.. but considering you can die very very fast you can occasionally feel like you are spending more time waiting for the maps to load than you spend actually playing the game.  Especially when you died two or three times in a row in rather frustrating ways. That is not to say the game is RNG heavy or anything like that, it isnt. Its just very unforgiving.i want to point out though that i am playing on a laptop, not a gaming laptop just a laptop. Although the game is installed on an SSD.  Loading a map takes around 35 seconds depending on the map im sure. This might seem like a very minor complaint and it is, but its my biggest gripe with the game so far.Oh yeah another tip, if you are in a fire fight and you havent counted how many people were there initially, or maybe you didnt see em all. You think its all over and enter a building or something. They will be waiting outside for you when you exit, they will gun you down, you will die. So i realize this sounds a lot like, a non recommendation so i want to add some fun stuff at the end. The style in which you play the game matters a lot, making sure you count how many enemies there are before you engage is important so you can make sure to get them all and none of em circle around or hide out for you to relax. being careful and methodical is rewarded. And it feels very satisfying to progress in the game, as the game develops and matures im sure this feeling will only get amplified. The devs have done a great job with this one and im going to enjoy it a lot. Good job devs! hope it sells in the millions.

_childDocuments_.review: v1.0.4 has brought serious balancing for armor fragility that massively improves player economy. High-tier armor is no longer something that you acquire just to baby around because it breaks too easily and is costly to fix, but something you can truly rely on to protect you against the most serious of firepower.Overall, Zero Sievert has a lot of good thing going for it. It's a very charming game with beautiful artstyle. The weaponry it offers are more inspired rather than exact likeness to real-life examples e.g. guns have fake names that are instantly recognizable for what its inspired from, and appearance that approximates the real appearance rather than exact copy. There is/are mods made by players that make it look and named exactly for the real-life counterpart, but I think the original drawing and names are still my favorite by a large margin.Something I don't see mentioned a lot in reviews is sound effect design. I think it's right up there with the best shooters, so far I think with the exception to a suppressed FRD, which sounds unpleasant. Otherwise everything sounds amazing. The game does not neglect environmental sounds e.g. the sound of your shots hitting different surfaces are clearly distinguished, so that you can rely on audio cues on top of visual to determine if you hit your shots or if the shots that whiffed past you came from the east or south for example.Being a top-down shooter there are obvious limitations. One of the most obvious and impactful is the use of 16:9 display essentially boxing your vision (while not in ADS) to be more expansive in the diagonal directions, while north-south has the shortest range and east-west in the middle. This is something you should consider when maneuvering.The game is without question heavily inspired by STALKER and Tarkov. You could say it's a pixel love-child of the two.

_childDocuments_.review: Still early in, but getting rolling. Pretty fun thus far. Still rough around the edges, to be sure, but it's early access and is sorta expected. Dialogue has grammatical errors, some dialogue options don't function with specific NPC's despite being available, big ol' "IN DEVELOPMENT" stickers here and there, etc. It's all minor stuff though, and the game plays well. Definitely Tarkovey in a lot of ways that are apparent just looking at some gameplay. Notably, you don't lose stuff on death outside of what you nabbed in raid, however. Dunno what I think of that, as it makes death a little inconsequential, but in the same stride death comes so quickly that I can't decide whether it's a bad thing. One way or another, it does feel a touch underwhelming to lose nothing and just go right back in. My only other complaint is that the dialogue is a bit... off. I'm no literary expert, but if I had to pinpoint what the problem is, I'd say it's that it's a bit too open with its expository dialogue. It feels very mechanical and overly direct. I hope they improve it as they continue development, as the atmosphere present in games like Tarkov and Stalker is a significant reason why I love them so much, and this game has the visual and gameplay to back it up if the dialogue starts pulling its weight. (On that note, make the Scav group themes work for more than a second or two before fizzling. I really dig it!)Gameplay is solid though, and I think it does a good job at giving info to players. Tooltips on ammo types and meds relieve so much of the headache involved in learning the counterparts in Tarkov, Gunplay feels good and snappy, with quick deaths and mostly quick kills. Non-human creatures move fast and offer an interesting alternative hazard to worry about. Scopes feel a little janky, and I think they'd benefit from an indicator for when the "lock on" that turns the weapon hitscan happens, much like how the crosshair turns color when LOS is blocked. As for the map design, I haven't ventured out of forest quite yet, but the partial randomization of threats and locale position is good. I think anomalies and radiation could probably have a little more impact though, as they're almost a nonissue unless you're collecting crystals. I'll likely update this section as I continue on and see more of what's on offer. I imagine that I could have problems with the system if it ends up being a linear progression of levels. Overall, even in early access I think this could be worth a buy if you want an extraction shooter that is singleplayer and isn't quite as punishing as alternatives.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't expect a carbon copy of Tarkov or Stalker with this one. I really hope we get multiplayer in the future. If you're someone who enjoys a more methodical and slow pace, I highly recommend this game.Edit:I see lots of complaints about load times, though mine has never taken longer than 20 seconds to load into a game. Turning down dynamic grass in the settings should help a lot. After putting more time in, I can confidently say the gameplay loop is EXCELLENT. The use of the fog of war adds a gripping third dimension to an otherwise 2D game. You will get caught off guard often if you aren't careful. The game stays quite difficult into the endgame, with some enemies killing you almost instantly even when wearing top tier armor. It is extremely satisfying running around in top tier gear, instakilling foes that once gave you trouble. All in all a fantastic game and I can't wait to see where the devs take it next!

_childDocuments_.review: I want to like this game.  The first major and most glaring issue is the load times.  It’s open world but not really.  You have a base and you go to your missions via train. But you select what map you want to go to and they don’t intertwine so you can’t go forest then city.   So that limits you.  The next glaring issue is the grind is painful:1) get on train and wait for 1 minute load time2) get to forest, play for 10 minutes, die (and you will a lot) and then retry it, but it puts you back at the base and train and enter load time once again. It compounds frustration when you had sweet loot but lost it and do it all over again. 3) gamble every time. You do load time, kill a couple bandits and get loot. So go to exfil to save loot. But if you do that you’ll be back to do the mission but the dang load time is annoying so you stick out the fight and don’t go back then run into some pack of wolves that you kill, but wasted all your ammo and now you have to pass by some hunters who kill you and your loot is gone but the thought of a load screen again is too much so you shake your head and click on refund like me.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoy the game. The difficulty keeps me playing. I hope the Devs keep adding content as hinted and beyond.Some encounters you are toast no matter what. That's life in a procedurally generated hostile wasteland. If you just rolled into every map and mopped up no problem every time, it wouldnt be a game.For anyone complaining about combat or clunky ammo switching.. ENGAGE WISELY.. most human enemies will chill, eat or drink, turn their back and smoke a cig, hit them THEN. Have a plan for cover and/or flanking. Get good at shooting while flanking to cover. Just like real life, dont pop right back out where you were being fired at if you can help it. Find another angle the enemy didnt just see and shoot at you at. Try not to engage multiple human enemies at a time. Treat the situations with the same kind of caution and awareness you would in reality. Dont blame the game for your lack of planning or foresight. Its a you problem not the game.Think tactically and you'll have more fun. Rage quits will happen.. but the difficulty means your successes will taste sweet. At least they do for me. Happy wiser engaging.My pick for Best Game i Suck At in the 2022 Steam Awards

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR:I'm a teacher on Half-Term for a week. I wanted to catch up on my marking but spent 31 Hours playing this instead. No regrets. Longer Review:I bought Zero Sievert based on a Reddit post about alternatives to Tarkov, now that COD's DMZ is pretty much dead. I'm a really busy guy, I've got kids, I work a full week and I run a business on top of that. I like my few moments of gaming to be immersive but with the option to drop in/out for quick sessions. Zero Sievert totally scratches that itch. The gameplay loop is great, it's easy enough to get into and has just the right level of challenge to keep me interested without being overly difficult. At the moment, the game is in a very playable but definitely early-access state. Bugs are rare, there are a few typos in dialogue and some of the quests can be a bit glitchy. At about 30 hours in, I've maxed out all the stats, fully built my base, defeated all the bosses, collected most of the weapons/armour and finished the main Questline, so I'm probably going to swing back later down the line when we hit 1.0 for a fuller experience. Tips:The Scavenger Base Module is brilliant, it'll give you a constant supply of items to sell or craft with and will help build the other modules. A Stealth/Sniper build is really viable and works great at night once you have NVGs Your biggest expense early on will be Armor repairs, armor with lower 'Fragility', like the police armor will save you lots of money in the long run, as will crafting armor repair kits. The Radiation and Nourishment Injectors allow you to travel very light and basically remove the need to carry anti-rad or food/drink items (which are generally plentiful anyway). Do Ivor's Quest in the forest - it's worth it. You also do not have to kill him when asked.When you're strong enough - farm Lazar and his guards a few times and sell their weapons, you'll have enough money from there on to finance your expeditions. When you've max levelled a base stat (like stamina), you can choose a specilization by clicking on it in the journal.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: It's a good idea, and an "okay" game. Just overpriced for what you get, and I can't even recommend it to people with craptops since Stalker Anomaly exists, and Anomaly does everything this does better, *for free*.Zero Sievert attempts to make a S.T.A.L.K.E.R.-Tarkov hybrid rougelike set in a 2D space. This would be okay if you had room for tactics, but its a *2D* game. Meaning you're cutting a lot of the mechanics that make gunfights work in a 3D space, and by extension the life or death decisions that would normally decide your fate in the titles this game was inspired by are mostly thrown out the window. Couple that with the fact you can spend 20-30 minutes on the map trying to out-loot the attrition of spent ammo, meds, and food, just to die to a factor completely outside your control and you have a recipe for a frustrating game with a lackluster payoff.A few examples: -Elevation. No vertical space to work with means there are no advantageous positions to work with or take up before an engagement, its whatever open space you can catch the most enemies in before you open fire. No choke points or stairwells you can hold a good view on while you eat/drink/med. Its whoever turns the corner first and if you can out-prefire them or not. Thanks to instant reaction times on AI, this is more often, not.-Headshots and body damage multipliers. If you hit an enemy in Zero Sievert they take damage to their overall health, no modifiers for where they get hit to affect the damage they take, meaning enemies can eat a lot more damage even if you have the drop on them or have time to line up a shot. The guy you're shooting have good armor? You need to shoot him 5 more times before he dies and don't worry about his buddies who now have their guns up ready to dome you the second you try to get closer, all of whom will eat just as many shots.Grenades: Can't throw grenades because there is no "throwing" in a 2D playspace. Enemies dug into a position? Guy hiding around a corner you can't get an angle on? 2 dudes hanging out in a room with a good crossfire on the entrance? Sorry, no other option than rush them or wait until they come into your line of sight and hope the dice roll in your favor.You get the point. The style of gameplay its trying to achieve falls flat because of what the game is at its foundation. Dying to things you cannot counter is called artifical difficulty and Zero Sievert has a lot of it. No matter how careful you are, not matter how much you plan an engagement, no matter how outgunned you have your enemies, it comes down to a dice-roll. Thats the exact opposite of what you want in a game like this.As for the game loop: Its shallow, just loot and return. Crafting is RNG (materials), most buildings have a single lootable chest in them as a placeholder, you can't ID enemies in the beginning so you end up just shooting on sight because you can't tell whos friendly and who isn't, quests are just find X item or kill X enemies. Faction relations are non-existent and are "work in progress". Anomalies are obscure and checking with bolts is inconsistent (another thing you *really* don't want in a game like this). If you want the Tarkov experience, just go play Tarkov. If you want a better 2D shooter, play Synthetik. If you have a bad PC and want something with deep gunplay and much more fleshed out mechanics in a 3D space complete with a weather system, natural disasters, dynamic faction relations and with better variations on the quests with a full dynamic start for roleplaying and completely player-customized difficulty for even the biggest masochists or the easiest run-and-gun settings for the COD fanboy sick of Activision (Oh, AND ITS FREE!), go play Stalker Anomaly or Stalker Gamma. As a rougelike this is frustrating and doesn't provide a whole lot of payoff when you figure it out. This game isn't worth ~$20 USD. I'm not kidding when I say that everything this game does, S.T.A.L.K.E.R. does better.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been following the development for a fair while and I had played it in early access for a fair good while till it's recent 1.0 release and even before then it was a solid little game you could sink hours into. While promoting a strong favour for the styles of extraction shooters, this game is not based around PvP or PvPvE as most other extraction shooter games are categorised and is rather, a single player title. Being so this makes this game not forgiving or necessarily easy right off the bat but it allows you to enjoy shooter game a bit more of a relaxed state.There are customisation options to tuning the difficulty and making your play through how you want it but the default options are pretty solid with even balancing and it feels just as rewarding to successfully extract with your loot as it feels equally frustrating when you do fail an expedition. Either way however there are options to that if you do fail you restart to the previous point before taking on the raid so your progress is only momentarily halted.The shooting and inventory management as well the interactions with the surrounding world feel fluid and very smooth for the style and look of this game and translate into some very unique gameplay. The AI is only comprehensive enough to put up a challenge for the player in working out the best way to take on an enemy or gang if they stumble paths with you, I've had some good fights.It's quite a charming little game clearly inspired by numerous other titles in the apocalyptic and shooter genres but that doesn't stunt it's likeness but in fact I think it strengthens this game as a middle ground to fans amidst a broad genre alike. Also worth mentioning, this game is excellent on steam deck. Much like many games in this genre there's plenty of buttons and bindings a normal controller can't utilise like a keyboard can and so using the left touch pad I was able to make use of the virtual menu steam allows people to construct and it fitted beautifully in with the default config and it really makes the experience just as equal to playing on any kind of setup.

_childDocuments_.review: Normally i wouldnt write a Review this early, but i just had to share my first Impressions since this is the kind of Shooter i did never expect to be made.ZERO Sievert combines two of my fav Shooters of all time. Escape from Tarkov and Stalker. You have Stalker-like:-Radiation-Mutants-ArmorTarkov-like:-Hideout-Weapon customization-Crafting-Quests but with a bit more QoL-Raids and progressionand a mix of both in terms of:-Atmosphere-Sound (other than in Tarkov, you can really pinpoint the Location of Footsteps for example)Zero Sievert fully captures the Feeling of Risk vs Reward while in a Raid. You have to carefully manage your Ressources and make constant Decisions of what to loot, what to leave, when to engage in Combat, and ofcourse when to get the F out. It is also one of very few games that manage to make the night fun and scary to play in. TLDR: ZERO Sievert is brutally addicting so far. Just....one...more...Raid...

_childDocuments_.review: Having been keeping an eye out for a game that is reminiscent of such great games focusing on the post-apocalypse setting after a nuclear disaster, such as Battlestate Games' Escape from Tarkov coming to mind alongside the likes of GSC Game World's own S.T.A.L.K.E.R that bears a close resemblance to this indie title, ZERO Sievert takes places not in America but instead set somewhere in Eastern Europe as you are tasked with familiarizing yourself with once-friendly and peaceful lands now ravaged by all the dangerous elements that a nuclear apocalypse comes with it as well as the savage mutated monstrosities and ruthless bandits that roam the lands freely, slowly building up your reputation and ferocity as a 'Hunter' as you explore the various areas in this game which, as of the writing of this review, currently stands at 5 with a sixth soon to be on it's way!Before getting straight into the gameplay, no doubt it will intrigue some as to what comparisons this game has between Stalker/Tarkov here and, seeing how I am more familiar with Bethesda's works as far as these types of games go, I don't exactly have the gameplay knowledge to commentate on the big differences other than that ZERO Sievert, as an indie game, puts it's focus on a less technical and graphically-impressive world but rather sets it's eyes on a more 2D plane of exploration with decent 16-bit graphics to support a more retro-styled type of gameplay by building it's horror through it's atmosphere and monsters that you can't quite fully make out, which only deepens when you are dealing with them when it turns dark or when the weather becomes dangerous and actively harms your character by being exposed to it!With that being said though, how does one exactly 'progress' in ZERO Sievert anyhow? Seeing as the goals presented in these types of games vary from one game to the next but usually carry a theme of 'survival' and coming up against the odds, overwhelming as they may be at first, and coming out on top by the end of or near the end of the game whilst attempting to resolve the nuclear post-apocalypse conflicts and, perhaps, come to some form of understanding of what triggered such a catastrophic event and how to move forward from there.To start off, the very first mission entails a simple 'survival of the elements', whereby you are brought to somewhere in the middle of the map by a train seen at the entrance to your main base of operations (more on this later) to the chosen area of your choice, seeing as it is simple enough to getting there but, in order to leave, one must make their way towards one of two green flares that is visualized as a small green circle on the map to fully leave and return to base, taking with them whatever goods they were able to acquire on the field with them.No doubt though that is only a mere fraction of what this game entails though, seeing how surviving the first map is only one of two objectives as ZERO Sievert is a game that tends to not go easy on it's players, even during it's tutorial, as it also assigns you to kill at least 5 wolves to prove that you are prepared to face danger and come out alive as a Hunter, seeing how combat works purely on a gun basis, meaning that when your firearm runs out of ammo and you have nothing else to fall back on, you had best hope you don't run into any other danger or let it catch up to you, less you risk dying to either human or animal eager to rob you or eat you alive, possibly both depending on what you're dealing with!Also not even getting into the fact that, just because you may be adept at combat does not necessarily mean you are free from danger either as both the environment affected by the nuclear incident itself as well as your very own body present problems that one needs to be constantly aware of in order to survive for another day, with how the former can quickly change from harmless sunny weather into severe fog that hinders one's sight, radioactive rain that will increase your radiation depending on the severity of the weather and even bizarre 'emissions' that, if waiting out in the open for too long, will emit deadly plasma waves that quickly harm and kill both you and enemies alike!As for the latter, it is safe to say that this is a tradition as old as time itself as far as the survival genre goes, seeing how one must tend to their character's primal needs to sustain life itself, that being food to eat, liquids to drink and energy to rest alongside the aforementioned radiation which is kept preferably to a near bottom-low. These can be found lain across the dangerous areas through various human enemies holding them as well as many containers that can possess them, albeit most of them will be 'rotten', meaning eating or drinking them will pose a risk to you getting sick by receiving small boost to radiation that, with enough dosage of it, will ensure you throw up and become more hungry/thirsty as well as injuring you through nose-bleeds and the likes that require bandages to properly treat, something that becomes increasingly harder to avoid as later areas will be near enough like hotspots for various radioactive sources, of which the only key way to identify them (outside of static when too close to it) is by avoiding any vehicles and specific large objects as these seem to be the primary source of radiation from personal experience.Once you return to the main base of operations, aptly named the 'Zero Sievert Bunker' which essentially acts as your official Hideout for the entirety of the game, this is where you are assigned most of your quests during the game as well as being where several vendors offer both goods and services to ensure that you have a good use for Roubles, this game's currency, although bearing in mind that there exists multiple groups within the bunker, each with their own reputation that can only be increased by completing quests for them, as having too low a reputation means you will not be able to access their services or goods and, even for those you start off with, some of the more 'premium' goods will not be for sale until you prove yourself to them.Alongside a neat feature that allows one to customize their own little 'base' in the bottom-left corner of the bunker through various 'modules' that require a wide variety of resources to build, it's safe to say that there is plenty for one to do in ZERO Sievert as they slowly become more accustomed to the intense and scary atmosphere that this game brings with it, no doubt about that!However, to bring up some issues I had with playing this indie here, ZERO Sievert is a fairly challenging game, of which I personally enjoyed a great deal, and whilst it offers various difficulties to balance this out somewhat, it does little to resolve the problem of gathering resources for a certain type of activity, that being crafting your own items, seeing as the modules are one-and-done deals whereby you are granted the benefits permanently and can enjoy them whenever you like, whilst ammo, medicine, food and equipment repairs among others are quite resource-intensive for what little you get out of them, since some are fairly reasonable whilst others you get far too little from that it's better just to buy a brand new firearm or armour instead!Other nitpicks include certain enemy behaviours, mainly bandits equipped with powerful shotguns or rifles, are hard to counter at a higher difficulty as often they can one-hit you before you even have time to react as well as no melee alternatives, weak as they may be, means you are essentially helpless if you ever run out of ammo on the field, which is only made worse with a limited inventory coupled by a weight limit before it slows you down greatly.In conclusion, I'd safely say that ZERO Sievert is a pretty solid entry as far as indies go, given it's focus on the Eastern Europe landscape, and I look forward to seeing how it progresses as it leaves Early Access in the months to come!

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely fun, if unpolished. At the beginning you will die. A lot. But then you won’t. You’ll have the knowledge and resources to not only survive but  in the place you once found so lethal. Then you’ll feel comfortable enough to move on to the next area and the cycle will repeat, hopefully with fewer deaths than your first trip outside of the bunker. Sooner than you expect you’ll be raking in hundreds of XP and tens of thousands of roubles every time you go out. Oh, you’ll still see the K.I.A. screen from time to time because luck is as fickle as the Networker is with good-reward quests (if you get the game you’ll get that joke soon enough).For $20.00 US, as of the writing of this review, you get a lot for a relatively little amount of money. A perfect game out of the box (man, that idiom really doesn’t work, anymore)? Hardly. A developer at your beck-and-call? Pfft. Puppies and kittens and rainbows? Are you high?So no, you don’t get those things, but as long as you have reasonable expectations, what you do get is more than your money’s worth.One more word of caution: many or most of the available guides contain outdated information, so don’t count on them for everything. Oh, and stay out of the forums. There’s no good loot there. Plus an Infestation spawned and now it’s overrun with ghouls (another reference you’ll understand if you get the game).

_childDocuments_.review: It's a mix of:-S.T.A.L.K.E.R. Aesthetics (post-apocalyptic wasteland, scavengers, bandits, rivaling factions, mutants, hazardous environments, Slavic names) and its difficulty (bullets and hazards HURT so you're just as squishy as any other human NPCs)-Escape From Tarkov's gun customization (but pixelated)-Project Zomboid's visibility mechanics (you can only see enemies if you're facing them and if they're not behind a wall)As of game's current state of this review, you're just doing sidequests for NPCs and getting supplies to upgrade your room. I'll... recommend.  It's in a promising state currently AFAIK, as long as the devs keeps adding more content and iron out the bugs. If you want to play as a squishy scavenger looting a semi-randomly-generated area with danger lurking in who-knows-where while trying not to tire out / starve / dehydrate / get acute radiation poisoning, this is a game for you.

_childDocuments_.review: (Hardcore Hunter) ~700 hoursThis game's potential has so much head room, but we have a long, very long way to go. Currently with v.40 out it has divided the player base from what I've seen on reddit, and it is a tad concerning to me. For clarity I am pro v.40This game has helped me learn to focus and organize better, and has really helped my problem solving skills overall. With this new update, the game-play has slowed down immensely to what I have been accustomed to for months (and a year maybe?) and it's forcing me to slow down even more. I love it. However, the drastic change in pace is something I can see that has ultimately compromised the community and I'm going to try and fix that right here.The obvious changes now and what new players won't ever experience from the older versions is the grazing feature (enemy flashes red) where if the weapon you're currently using isn't being utilized at it's optimal distance, the hit will not register. For those of you just joining, you need to understand that everything that you once saw on the screen was a valid target, no matter the distance. The devs are obviously working extremely hard to provide more depth within the game and this new change has amplified that exponentially. This has caused me more anxiety, frustration, hair pulling, and desk smashing (consider grabbing yourself an XL mat to absorb some of the impact). This game is challenging me more and I welcome it. That being said, how we interpret the distance may not immediately make sense to use from a bird's-eye perspective at a glance. The gaps in which the weapons effective range respond to will take you HOURS to get comfortable with, and it will KICK - YOUR - ASS. I have a comfortable solution for this: an option for locking your cursor within the minimum and maximum diameters that your weapon's optimal range requires. This will EXTREMELY help those out that are on their Steam Decks with limited cursor movement.I would love to personally tell the staff that their hard work is not going unnoticed, and the vast majority of us appreciate the hard work that's going into this game. You guys rock!

_childDocuments_.review: It's a single-player top-down extraction shooter. Heavily inspired by Escape from Tarkov and Stalker. You go into one of the several maps, explore, kill, loot, and head to the extraction point to exit the map. In between expeditions, you mod weapons, pick up tasks from npcs, build up your hideout, and manage your stash.Unlike Tarkov, you don't lose anything when you die - you go back to where you were prior to loading the mission with everything intact (unless you play hardcore mode). To offset the fact that there are no human players or loss of progress, this game includes mutants, anomalies, radiation, and emissions inspired by the Stalker games. If you want to play a casual Escape From Tarkov with much less frustration, pick this game up.

_childDocuments_.review: This is Tarkov flavored Diablo. Surprisingly intuitive, unlike Tarkov, I never had to consult the wiki on any of the quests or anything.It's smooth, didn't experience a single crash, maybe a little lag on the woods village around the 8 hour mark, but that's it.The combat is easily the best part of the game, it's quick, lethal, and satisfying. My only complaint is the animals and mutants, once they get into melee range, you're pretty much dead. The heavy damage and bleeding early game is almost auto kill (hecking boars), but I feel like I wasn't actually able to shoot mutants or animals if they were right on top of me.The sound is good, very polished. I'm not sure if it plays into detection much though, like having a suppressor. I didn't really notice much difference before or after I started using suppressors.The art and animation is awesome. My highlight was the ghouls, fun little enemy with great design!The atmosphere is ok. It's not immersive by any means, but the sound and design complement the gameplay. The level design is overall very good. Map layout is mostly random and there's fun stuff to explore. Forest - Great map overall, hours of entertainment.Makeshift Camp - I also like this map, there's lots of cover so you don't know if there's bandits or boars around the corner of the junkyard. The issue with this one is that there's too many green army guys, they just kill all the stuff which is annoying when you're trying to do kill quests there.Industrial - Pretty cool map, but no reason to come here except for like one or two quests.Swamp - Parts of this map are real cool, like the sewers. It feels so empty though and there's not much reason to come here either.Mall - This feels like an end game map, tons of enemies, tons of loot, lots to explore. Has a lot going on for it, only reason to come here is to do The Stylish One quest.The quest system is a mixed bag. Killing stuff, cool that's fun, except killing hunters on makeshift camp - feels bad. The collecting random stuff for quests isn't fun on Tarkov and it isn't fun in this game either. It feels like chores and just sucks all around.The best quests are the objective quests, going into the sawmill full of bandits for a flash drive. An intense and fun adventure.The skill system is unexciting. It either needs a class system or a skill/perk tree or both. Trader rep works off overall level, which is ok, it should work off of tasks done for the vendors.The story. Meh. It's like Tarkov or Diablo, you're just gonna skip it to get back into the action.There are no consequences to death except losing your current progress. I think that's part of early access so that you can progress through the game at a quicker pace to give better feedback. However, it needs the Tarkov treatment where you lose your loadout when you die.The hideout is underwhelming. The only thing I used it for was making late game ammo and repairing weapons and there's items that do that, I just ended up selling those. You can heal, repair armor, and replenish food and water through vendors. I think that's fine, but I think the game needs to go full vendor or full hideout to work well. Personally, I think the hideout and crafting are a waste of time. Full vendor services is the way because it gets you back on the map faster.Like every other review mentions, this game needs co-op, that's a fact. As it stands, the game is a fun little diversion that I might revisit on updates and then go back to playing Tarkov. Co-op would extend the life of the game and I would badger more people to get it so we could play together, even in the current state of the game. Overall a fun but fleeting experience, we'll see how the updates go! I do think that the dev should lean more into the Diablo aspect than Tarkov.New Player TipsRat until you can Chad, then just rat faster.Money does everything in the game, earn more of it. The best way I found to earn money was selling guns. There are a few items that sell for a lot too, like the gameboys and they're not needed for a quest.The hunters usually have healing and/or food on them, helpful early game.

_childDocuments_.review: Is good.  And MAD respect for how fast you can get into the game.  From pressing start to being loaded in, you can click to skip every title screen and be loaded in in like literally under 10 seconds.  It's such a breath of fresh air from AC Valhalla where you have to sit through a minute of warnings and messages then have them "check for addons" then load into your game for another minute. Can't wait for more content and for it to be full release and see what it ends up as a finished product.  It's already quite enjoyable.

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent game in early access. It still seems somewhat unpolished due to bugs here and there (mostly with spawning npcs/structures inside one another in the environment) and occasional crashing (only once in my current 40hrs of gameplay). It is evident that the game is still in early access as there is no 'endgame' questline, but the gun play is in depth with the ability to add attachments and change bullet type, but still seems somewhat lackluster with customization options. It would be nice to be able to equip the weapons with more and there being more than just the single type of standard weapon mods but in different colors. A part of me wants to ask for a greater emphasis on the survival aspect of the game, namely the food/water/etc with more deathly options with water is not drunk or food is not eaten as the negative effects, although somewhat detrimental, are not horribly difficult to work around. However, the ability to turn off 'death from starvation/dehydration' would be excellent if the survival aspects were to be reworked.The gameplay besides the survival aspects and the modding of weapons involves either resource management or enemies. Let's start with the latter, enemies. The combat  is very tense throughout the game, although as of this version (0.40.23) the bandit faction are extremely easy in the late-game as they only have early- and mid-game counterparts and can be easily decimated. The ???/Watcher faction was an excellent addition to the game as it is interesting to see a new difficult type of enemy that is specifically in this iteration's final map. The monsters are terrifying as they will shred your health nearly as fast as the in game bosses do. Although they are squishy, they are fast, terrifying, and hit like a truck. Hoards of them genuinely send shivers down my spine. The Green Army and CC have an interesting feud, neither of which I would like to side with, but I am looking forward to a more in-depth questline, possibly returning us to previous maps with greater difficulty enemies. Overall, I just want more gameplay since I thoroughly enjoyed the game. Now onto the former, the resource management. Now  I do not mean the management as you open your inventory, but as in back at the base in the bunker(home location). I do wish that there was more substance to building yourself a home base and also I wish there was all around more to do with the modules that you build for the base. I feel as though I spent majority of my time in storage while in base then immediately leaving as there were no apparent benefits to using nearly any of the modules that you built. Final topic I will discuss is skills. Great addition allowing for more customization and allows me to really find my niche. Stealth sniper all the way baby!TL;DR, Great game, mildly lacking gun customization, great combat and gunplay, fair questline.(got bored and started procrastinating on hw)

_childDocuments_.review: I don't normally buy early access games, I review them even less, but I needed to leave this review. Is this game worth it in its current state of early access at its current price point? Yes.I already have over 20 hours into it and am just as excited to play it as I was 15 hours ago. The game certainly isn't finished and some of the criticisms that have been levied in these review are warranted, they just don't come close to outweighing the positives to me. First off difficulty: I have no issues with the difficulty. If you are impatient you will be punished. Take things slowly and at distance and choose your engagements. Survivability: Your armor has a condition percentage. Once that condition goes to zero it isn't functioning as armor. That's why you're suddenly dying more often. The DR will repair your amour for a fee, I would recommend doing that every time you come in from a raid, it appears to be cheaper that way. - Hydration is an issue early on. Prioritize drinks over all loot. Buy all the water you can from the Barman, this resets every day at 7:30. Ammo: The type of ammo you use is hugely important. Don't try and go against heavily armored foes with the low penetrating ammo, you will use an entire magazine before you kill them. The same is true for you though, if you have high tier armor you will sponge rounds from low caliber wielding bandits. Things I would like to see: More content: Quests, maps, guns, attachments. I would like to see some more attachments that aren't just clear upgrades, give us some that require tradeoffs that can lead down different playstyles. - Throwables would be great, maybe remove a med slot or two for grenade types.All-in-all I think the current spot the game is in is excellent given how close we are to early access release and I'm excited for future content updates, but I never recommend buying a game on what the future might bring and the game is worth it in its current form.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR - I strongly advise you to wait until release v1.0 before you buy this game. The game you're getting now may not be the game you want when released v1.0 eventually. Also, there's potential that this game will be in Early Access for a long time.Let me elaborate further.Based on the updates this game has been receiving, there's potential that the game mechanics will be constantly redesigned or maybe revamped. I'm not talking about changes like UI or QOL or minor stuff. It's about the core mechanics. Imagine a developer making an Action RPG, only for it to evolve to Active Battle System RPG. Or a Hold 'Em Poker turning into Draw Poker. Sure, it's still poker, or RPG with action in it., but now it's not what you wanted in the first place.The updates right now gives me an impression that the developer does not have a concrete idea or solid design specification / direction to the game. The development seems to be about throwing ideas at the wall and see what sticks. Or just throw it without seeing the results. This is not a good sign.Biggest example now is the recent update making changes to the core shooting mechanics. It is now the biggest source of contention of this game at this time. Expect lots of other things to change as it looks like the game design turns into a whack-a-mole session. i.e. Change something, and then try to change another thing in response to the previous change. Development hell.I bought this game to demo the first 2 hours. I liked it and had the impression that the development direction is already solid. I would have refunded it immediately if I knew otherwise. I stopped playing.Analogous to this, if you remember the Early Access period of this game called 'Starbound' ; Almost 10 years ago. The flip flop design where the mechanics (e.g. how the items stats work) kept changing to the point a number of people I know of got burned out and never touched the game again.Or AI Wars, where the core damage / RPS mechanics kept getting revamped, until I got tired from trying to relearn everything again.

_childDocuments_.review: Excited to see the full release product. Would love the devs to lean away from "only" making a Tarkov / STALKER clone. The ideas I see that are original are great, please do more of that! \steamapps\common\ZERO Sievert\ZS_vanilla\gamedata - open the file "weapon_glance_stat.json" in notepad. change the "eff_range" values more to your liking. [0, 0], [90, 1], [180, 0.5] The first value is range, the second is % damage. So between 0 and 90 "units", it will do 0 damage, between 90 and 180 units is 100% damage, and greater than 180 is 50% damage. If you dont want minimum ranges, just set the first one to [0,1] for each gun type.I agree that snipers having a minimum effective range of halfway across your screen is not ideal. I think a better way to balance the snipers and DMRs would be to nerf the ergo significantly on heavier weapons, nerf the recoil on heavier caliber weapons, make weapon mods harder to obtain but make them have a bigger impact on the stats. I think forcing people to use different guns through the game is great, but at the end of the game I should be able to use the gun I want, whatever it is, if I have all the mods for it

_childDocuments_.review:
ZERO Sievert is a post apocalyptic game set in a fictitious part of Russia.

The bunker ZERO Sievert: here you can accept new quests, talk to NPC, trade with vendors, manage your equipment and improve your base.

Maps are procedurally generated to ensure good replayability. The main points of interest will then be in a different location each time, but there is loot in everywhere in the map so be prepared to explore!

Weapons can be modified, it is up to the player to create a weapon he likes or to focus on statistics.

There are more than 100 different items to loot and you can use them to craft new items, upgrade your own base or sell them.

All this surrounded by a post-apocalyptic atmosphere that I will try to create as best I can.
