_childDocuments_.review: Beware: there is no Camila Giorgi in this game so only buy during a sale.Jokes aside, this is a game that deserves a mixed rating (when will Valve finally add this to reviews?!)The core gameplay is great with some very realistic tennis physics. It offers a huge variety of tennis courts to play at all over the world. It has a story mode in which you can play a custom made character to rise to the top and the character creator is decent enough. However, this leads to my first issue with the game: it leans heavily into stat distribution as in you can put skill points into different attribute such as forehand, stamina, serving, volley, etc. This means that matches often aren't really decided by the player skill but rather by stat distribution. A lower level player basically has no chance against a high level player by default.Visuals are okay though they do look rather dated. The quality of the models of IRL players is all over the place though they got the grunts right. If you ever wanted to play againt Scharapowa's obnoxious shrieking this is the game for you!Now for the main reason this game is getting a downvote rather than an upvote: microtransactions. Playing the game earns you VC (virtual currency) which can be spent on cosmetic items, level boosts, skipping tiers in the battle pass and few other things such as equipping different strings on your racket. Doesn't sound so bad, right? Well, you will quickly realize that you earn little to no XP and VC by playing the game while stuff costs a ton of VC. As a result you are encouraged to purchase VC in the shop which is exactly why MTX suck since they do affect gameplay even when or rather especially when you don't buy into them.TLDR: great tennis game, terrible monetization

_childDocuments_.review: TopSpin's gameplay is fluid and fun. It's easy to pick up, yet difficult to master. I set career mode to Very Hard and am getting my butt kicked as I get started. This makes the mode much more engaging and the payoff for a win very satisfying.I thought with the VC this game would be like NBA 2K, but no. The only way to level up your MyPlayer is to play and gain XP, which is a grind. But that grind is fun if you enjoy playing the game, and seeing as the career mode is pretty lightweight that grind is pretty much the whole point. So if that doesn't sound fun to you then perhaps mycareer isn't for you. The VC is only used for cosmetics and things like upgrading your coach, which, early on at least, happens pretty rarely so I actually feel like I earn enough VC to go buy the Yonex Ezone I use in real life and not run out of VC just when I need it. There does seem to be some physics missing from the hair and clothing as others have reported, which is definitely disappointing. While it doesn't look or play like a last-gen game by any means, it does seem like they're holding the game back a bit graphically on PC.I dislike 2K as much as the next person but at the end of the day I'm actually enjoying playing this game, so that's worth a recommendation to me regardless of who publishes it. Perhaps if 2K sees good sales on PC they'll pay a bit closer attention to it, but then again, maybe I'm just an optimist. Pick it up if you love tennis, like I do.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoy the 'arcade'? style Virtua Tennis series of games and wanted to try out this 'simulation' style tennis game.Unfortunately it seems like 'simulation sports' now-a-days are all about either a convoluted control scheme or player mechanic.Here, it is the player mechanic, being the 'timed meter' system. It influences all attributes of every single shot you make which can turn every rally and match into a drag. What's weird is that the 'timed meter' is not based on the distance of the player to the ball, or how long you have activated or readied your shot. The 'timed meter' just moves by itself. And there is no pattern to it, so you cannot get into a rhythm like with your usual 'time based rhythm games'.Apart from that, there are two are things that quickly deplete the enjoyment from this game;Firstly, the career mode is just the same three things over and over; training challenge, special match, tournament, each month for the whole year. And if you have already done the Tennis Academy training sessions then these training challenges only add extra tedium.Secondly, you can only play career mode with your player created character which begins with stats at 30. Except every opponent you will face will have stats that are two or three times higher than that. A kind of 'paper, rock, scissors' hit type hierarchy for the different types of shots you can make. This is enhanced by the location of the player on the court for the type of shot you are trying to make or receiving from the opposing player. Also, a stamina bar is added to the mix that not only pertains to the current point being contested, but can also carry into following points or sets being played. Then throw in how much power you put onto a shot, trying to get the right amount for the type of shot you are trying to pull off. And this all can be used in creating your own play tactics. creating your own combos of shot type variations and playstyle.

_childDocuments_.review: Topspin2k25: A Stellar Tennis Game Marred by Unwelcome MicrotransactionsTopspin2k25, initially a beacon of hope for gamers seeking a complete and immersive tennis experience without the dreaded intrusion of microtransactions, has sadly fallen victim to the allure of additional revenue streams. Developed by [Hanger13] and available on Steam, this PC game started off on the right foot but has stumbled along the way with the inclusion of microtransactions, leaving a bitter taste in the mouths of many players, myself included.When I first dove into Topspin2k25, I was enamored by its stunning visuals, satisfying gameplay mechanics, and comprehensive feature set. The game offered a breath of fresh air in an industry plagued by predatory monetization practices, providing everything a tennis enthusiast could want without any hidden costs or pay-to-win schemes. However, my enthusiasm quickly waned when news broke of the game's integration of microtransactions.The addition of microtransactions feels like a betrayal of the game's original ethos, tarnishing what could have been a standout title in the genre. Now, instead of focusing solely on enjoying the thrill of the game, players are constantly bombarded with prompts to spend more money on in-game content. Whether it's unlocking new characters, purchasing equipment upgrades, or accessing exclusive cosmetic items, the pressure to open our wallets is ever-present, detracting from the overall experience.What makes the inclusion of microtransactions even more disappointing is the fact that Topspin2k25 had all the makings of a modern classic without them. The gameplay remains solid, the graphics are still impressive, and the core mechanics are as engaging as ever. But these positives are overshadowed by the insidious specter of microtransactions lurking in the background, threatening to undermine the integrity of the game.It's disheartening to see a game with so much potential succumb to such scummy tactics in pursuit of profits. Instead of fostering a supportive and consumer-friendly environment, the developers have chosen to prioritize short-term gains over long-term player satisfaction. As a result, what could have been a beloved title that stood the test of time may end up relegated to the annals of gaming history as yet another cautionary tale of corporate greed.In conclusion, while Topspin2k25 still has its merits as a tennis game, the inclusion of microtransactions casts a dark shadow over its otherwise bright prospects. For those who value integrity and transparency in gaming, the presence of such predatory monetization practices may be enough to sour the experience entirely. Here's hoping that the developers reconsider their approach and prioritize the needs and desires of their player base moving forward.

_childDocuments_.review: Hangar 13 did a pretty decent job here. The game itself I found quite fun to play, pretty engaging. Obviously some tweaking to do but tennis games aren't exactly in huge supply, rights are a pain to secure and it was good to see another TopSpin. I enjoyed playing the demo for a weekend and it was greatly appreciated as I was stuck in a room sick.The publisher, 2k, not so much. Being forced to register for an account to play the game at all didn't impress.The game is absolutely rammed with microtransactions. Constant attempts to monetise and ad placements.The game is massively heavy with DRM. Presumably in part to ensure folks aren't getting those pay to win goodies for free.The main executable is over 600 MB in size, the largest executable file I've ever seen. It has both Denuvo Anti-Tamper with all the features active integrated and Denuvo Anti-Cheat further bloating it out. I haven't done any testing on frame rate in-game however loading is definitely considerably slower than it could be due to the obfuscation and the game is running checks at very least in between points.There is no 'offline' single player mode or mod use permitted - a career player may not be modified except by paying for it. The game is looking at active running programs for anything it doesn't like and will stop functioning properly should any scans return a positive.The game will not open if various programs are running, it will admonish the user to deactivate them.The game itself is quite fun. The intrusive and always-on nature of the anti-cheat is annoying. The lack of an offline mode is annoying. The mass of attempts to monetise having charged full price is annoying. This game is a massive cash grab that I cannot recommend: 2k's greed has killed Hangar 13's decent work.

_childDocuments_.review: As a high-level tennis player, I can't recommend this game to anyone. If you don't play tennis at all, you might like this game a bit more, but for me the gameplay is just too different from real life tennis. EDIT: This has nothing to do with how tennis works, I'm never playing this again.The things that bother me are: - The difference between flat balls and topspin balls is minimal. - Lack of content, I expect more from a 60 euros game. - Career mode isn't accessible when offline. - There are barely any real life pros in the game. - Movement can be quite clunky, especially when recovering to the middle, rushing the net and rushing back for a lob. - Your own MyCareer player starts with relatively low stats.* - Even if you constantly time and aim your shots perfectly, every player in the roster lacks precision. - Microtransaction, meh. Money printer go brrrr - Difference between difficulties is weird. If you're player is much worse in stats than the opponent, beating him on hard is relatively easy, but move the difficulty up and it becomes almost impossible.* For the progression, this is understandable, but I do expect a player who's participating in ATP-level tournaments to at least have more stamina and precision than the average 70 year old player in real life. And yes, even when timing and aiming perfectly, the precision of your career player is still terrible.I understand that the game has to be different from real life tennis, but it's just too far from reality to be enjoyable for me.

_childDocuments_.review: My experience with TopSpin 2K25 was the equivalent of retiring from a match after losing the first game at love on your serve and committing a double fault on the last point. The retirement wasn't because of injury but because you just didn't see the point in continuing to play, regardless of the outcome. 0 - 15: Mandatory 2K Games registration to play offline.0 - 30: Andy Murray's face in the opening sequence makes it look like he intentionally had extremely successful major facial reconstructive surgery to appear as terrifying as possible.0 - 40: The "advanced" graphics options are a joke for a PC game. The game looks like it was made in the PS3 era.Break point: You can turn off the timing meter in the settings but can't turn it off for the tutorial. I'm done with tennis games that force you to take your eyes off the ball to look at a power or timing meter. TopSpin 2K25 now has the honor of being the game I've played the least before requesting a refund. This game has no place even pretending that it's the result of a good faith effort to make a great modern tennis video game. I wasn't impressed by anything I saw in my short time with TopSpin 2K25. In my opinion, this game is nothing more than a low effort attempt to take advantage of tennis fans like myself who desperately want a modern tennis video game that's on par with the modern games being released for other sports.

_childDocuments_.review: Other than the crashes, the game is completely built around micro-transactions. When the servers go down, you're basically stuck to just Exhibition Mode. Even the WWE 2K games have more offline features than this.Game crashes on launch, when standard audio driver software are running in the background eg NahimicService. (this is preinstalled software found on ASUS motherboards), I suspect many will run into this issue. Thanks to the forums I was able to find a workaround to play the game. I would only recommend full price to tennis fanatics like me. I'm still going to play this to death.. or at least when 2K decides to turn off the servers.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who enjoyed TopSpin and TopSpin 2 back in the day, I was excited to see there was a new game coming out. My attempt to play the game, however, was cut short, as the moment I finished my first tournament in career mode, I received an error message saying I had lost connection to the 2K servers, and was swiftly booted back to the main menu with the career mode greyed out. As it turned out, the servers, perhaps unable to cope under the demand, had crashed, rendering the game all but useless, as most of its content is tied to the servers. At no point, to my knowledge, had the career mode ever been implied to be online-only before this, and for a single-player mode to require an internet connection is simply ridiculous under any circumstances, regardless of whether it's the new norm. Many people are reporting that their career progress has been wiped out after this server outage. I cannot speak to this, as I had already requested my refund well before the servers came back online, but if that is indeed the case, then it is merely another black mark against this mockery.Therefore, if you have a spotty internet connection, or are simply expecting the robust career mode of TopSpin titles past, DO NOT BUY THIS GAME. 2K has taken a beloved nostalgic series, gutted it, sewn its corpse back together, dressed it in a shiny new suit and is charging you exorbitant amounts of money to watch them puppet it about. And the cherry on top? Once 2K shuts off online support for the game--which it will, in a scant two years from the writing of this review--all that will be left is the exhibition mode. And that's certainly not worth full price, not now and probably not ever.If for some unholy reason you're willing to tolerate the 2K-ness of this affront to common sense, the gameplay is fine enough and the player customization is decent. But we deserve better. YOU deserve better.

_childDocuments_.review: Seeing the trailer, I thought "Topspin is back!" And thought that finally, after all these years, we would have a new tennis game made by a good game studio. Now, don't get me wrong, these physics and how the game handles are miles ahead of AO 2 and TWT2, and having played both I can confidently say that this game is the best currently out there. But, the game is practically Topspin 4 with better graphics and more licenses. In conclusion, I would really recommend not buying this IF you have topspin 4 available to play. _childDocuments_.review: Good core tennis gameplay that can create some really satisfying moments and tough back and forth matches. It's already a let down that you can only play one tournament a month even though in reality there is a tennis tournament almost every week but the real issue is the terrible stamina system.In theory a stamina value that is affected by travel and how much exertion you put into a match is a good idea. However when that stamina mechanic means that entering a 3 match 250 level tournament with 95+ stamina will leave you at less than 20 by the end with an injury to boot (meaning taking the next 1-2 months off) is frankly ridiculous.Don't get this is you're looking to experience a virtual tennis career on the pro tour. _childDocuments_.review: I have played for a few hours during the Free to Play weekend and I have had so much fun.Here are some of the positives that I have felt so far.- The gameplay is fantastic. Not overly realistic, but not overly arcadey either. It's really fun to play.- Graphics when playing is really good, especially the court. Some player models and your own created player should be better though.- The timing system.- TopSpin Academy. Great for getting into the game and learning the different mechanics.- Lots of customization for your created player.- Fun to play online matches (when playing against a similarly ranked player).- All four Grand Slams.Now, there are definitely some bad things about TopSpin 2K25. - The roster is pretty terrible for a game priced at 60 euros. 2K will add more players in the future for free, but we have no idea when. The communication needs to better here I think.- The career mode (MyCareer) needs an improvement. I have enjoyed it so far, but the energy system in particular is frustrating. You will have to rest pretty often (which has to be at least one whole month) to not get any minor or major injuries. - You start at rank 80 in MyCareer, which is the lowest possible rank. Would be much better if you would start at for example rank 250. 80 is not enough players to have in a career mode, especially when the game only has seven active male players in the roster.- I would have liked to see more game modes. The simplest would be that you could play through a Grand Slam tournament with a player from the roster. Quite a simple mode that would add a lot to the game.- Graphics up close could be better.- Some player models could be better. Most notably Alcaraz and Murray needs to be fixed in an update.- Microtransactions. Never liked it and never will. It's not as bad as other sports games though.All in all, I would recommend TopSpin 2K25 if you are really itching for a good tennis game. Honestly, I think the game is overpriced at full price (€59.99), but at the current price (€47.99) it is at least worth thinking about imo. If you are still not sure, wait for a bigger sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm gonna repeat a lot of what has already been said but this game is criminally bare bones. Although I will admit there is a good foundation which I'll explain below. I have not played any online mode either. Pros- to start the stadiums look great and I think the the gameplay feels good when working as intended. I like that at least for my career mode you're not top 10 of the world in the first year and have to grind and slowly work your way up. I like the broadcast and takes between sets/games but wish there could be more cut scenes, especially with the trophy ceremony which appears to only have one ceremony cut scene.Cons- the player models look horrendous and in a reddit AMA with the developers, the devs have stated they are happy with the look of the players (i refuse to belive theyre personally happy with the current models but are trying to publicly downplay this problem) and do not seem to have any intention on improving their looks. I think the hair, face, and clothing models all seem really awkward and reflect graphics of ps2 and Xbox 360 generations. The stands have the same few fan models which get stale after only a couple of matches although i tell myself theyre either tennis journalists or superfans to justify to myself why its the same people in the stands.  Although their roster has some top tennis players, it is severely laking in current players, including the likes of Djokovic and Nadal. They stated they will be adding more stars to the roster in future free dlc but the fact it was shipped out without these to seems unbelievable to me. One of the more criminal negatives is the fact that when the servers go down which is almost a daily thing since launch, the game becomes useless. I have have the servers drop st the last game of a match and all progress is deleted. You can not even play career mode and are limited to the tutorial and excebition matches as they have no way of tracking the micro transactions. I think the lowest tier version of the game is the most people should by and even then I recommend waiting until a discount is available because it is criminally overcharged at the current state. There are more cons as others have stated but to me these are the most egregious I have personally encountered. Do not buy in its current state

_childDocuments_.review: The game itself is solid. It feels fluid and the animations are phenomenal, unlike current other simulator games like Tennis Elbow. The only downside is that it is a 2K game, which means that your player needs to be grinded to level 30 to have similar stats to other players online. There is a mode though that plays online matches with pro players, making everything even. Otherwise, there are seasonal battle passes with a lot of equipment and animations that are of current used items. To me, this is a plus, but obviously that is polarizing. The character creator is nice, and you can even have multiple characters, which is dope.3 hours in and no performance issues or bugs. Running a 3070ti on 1440p max settings. I would always take people complaining about performance with their 4090 super systems with a grain of salt. The monetization doesn't seem that bad in it so far, mostly being cosmetics. All stat related boosts seem to be unlock-able through leveling and challenges. It seems mainly geared towards speeding up your progress and cosmetics, which is just fine for me, since there is a maximum skill cap anyhow. Pros:- Animations and Movement- Easy to pick up, but complex to master- Outfits and Equipment are real life equipment, nice if you are a tennis player- Audio and announcers (They're good quality!)- Runs buttery smooth for me.Cons:- It's a 2K game. That means your multiplayer experience is going to be deterred until you max your character- Lack of players. Honestly thought there would be more characters in it. The world tour only has 80 including you, but most are random generated. - McEnroe doesn't yell profanity at you :(- Pricing of the game is brutal for the higher editions- They sold on Fed's in game model somehow. Seriously, it's awful.- Denuvo can lock your account if you try to log into too many devices.Summary:Great game, audio and detail is all there as well as the animations. There doesn't seem to be any major performance issues that's affecting the majority of the player base. The game itself is amazing for a tennis simulator. The bad is that it is a 2K game, and that comes with all of those downsides.

_childDocuments_.review: Top Spin is back, and it's mostly glorious. My background with Top Spin: I've been playing since I got that free version of TS1 with NCAA Football 05. Top Spin 2/3 were played about as much as Madden or NBA 2K back in the day. Most people were grinding Call of Duty or Halo, and I was grinding out Top Spin 4. I have been playing Top Spin 4 on my xbox 360 from release, until literally 2 days ago, the day before I bought this game. Review: This is mostly what I have been waiting for. The gameplay is mostly the same, with some minor but necessary improvements. I could absolutely see where some people wanted more, but don't break what isn't broken, and this was not broken. This was exactly what I was hoping for. I found myself hooked all over again. I won't sit here and act like this game is perfect, but this makes me so happy to play. Roster doesnt have enough players, I'll admit that, but IMO, I would rather have good gameplay, over a good roster(looking at you Tiebreak). Both would be great, but this isnt a perfect world.  Another thing I have seen complaints about is online matchmaking. I'll admit, its a bit inconsistent as to who you're matched up against, but that was expected since I knew there were players who had been playing the past 3 days and objectively had better players, I have to assume this will get better when everyone has a maxed out character and comes down more to skill and strategy than a level 23 playing a level 4. Performance/Graphics: I have seen a ton of complains about this, and I can only speak for myself, with a 2070 Super, but I have not had even a slight glitch, hiccup, bug, or frame drop. This game runs a very smooth 93-97 FPS, max settings, 1440P. Graphics arent the best in today's market, but they're pretty darn good. I feel like I'm playing a different game than some of these reviews the way they're talking about how bad the graphics are. It's not as good looking as NBA 2K, but i also wasnt expecting it to. Last note: Career probably could be more in depth, but it's still pretty fleshed out and fun. There is going to be a long grind to be #1, and its nice to be back to doing coach objectives and having cool gear to grind for. MTX are not very welcome, but this is 2K in 2024,. we knew this was coming. I havent felt the need to buy anything, and everything can be earned for VC, though that is a LONG grind. I appreciate that you can earn them at all, as someone that has stopped playing CoD for their brutal MTX. This is somewhere on the worse side of the middle. MTX here suck at all, but if theyre going to be here, this is not terrrible. I don't plan on spending a cent on MTX outside of maybe the Battlepass if i find the gear to be worth it and im playing it that much. Overall: I'm hooked, and I think if you played at least Top Spin 4 and loved the gameplay, youre going to love this. It's not perfect, but its FUN, and isn't that why we play video games?

_childDocuments_.review: As a non-professional gamer, I’ve developed a knack for laughing at my own gaming mishaps—good thing, too, because Top Spin 2K25 has been a masterclass in testing my patience and sense of humor.Visually by today's standards, it’s not exactly eye candy—more like the candy you’d find in a discount bin after Halloween. But hey, it still gets the job done, even if it’s not winning any beauty contests. In a recent update the developers, bless their optimistic hearts, decided to tweak the serve mechanics, likely to force people to spend points in it and shake-up the stale meta: maxing out forehand and backhand power while camping at the baseline like it's Black Friday at Walmart. Sadly, this “improvement” has been as effective as a screen door on a submarine. Players now just opt for safer serves, ensuring we're still stuck in a baseline grindfest that’s about as fun as watching paint dry.In my ever-optimistic fashion, I tried to embrace several playstyles to avoid the meta including a serve-and-volley playstyle. Spoiler: it didn’t end well. The game clearly prefers that I conform to the baseline meta, much like society prefers I stop wearing pajama pants to the grocery store. The online experience? Let's just say it’s a bit like a trust fall where the person catching you is on their phone—laggy, unreliable, and occasionally hilarious in a masochistic way. With the servers set to be turned off in 2026, even the single-player mode will be stripped down, just like my hopes for this game.And then there's the grind. Oh, the grind! Earning VC feels like pulling teeth, except the dentist is also charging you by the minute. Whether you’re playing online or offline, gathering enough VC to respec your character or even just buy a new outfit takes time—lots of time. With the kind of earnings you make in online matches, you’ll be grinding longer than it takes for the game to be outdated.In today's tennis game landscape (which, let's be honest, isn’t exactly brimming with competition), Top Spin 2K25 might scrape by with a passable score—maybe a 5/10 on a generous day. But compared to classics like Top Spin 4? This game wouldn’t get more than a 3/10 from me. If you're hoping for something new and exciting, you might want to lower your expectations—or better yet, just pick up Top Spin 4 and pretend it’s 2011 again.Of course, this is just my experience, and I’m only one frustrated gamer who has a wife and kids, and have a limited amount of time for gaming. But judging by the echo chamber of complaints I’ve heard from others, I’m not alone in my gripes. If you’re looking for a game to make you feel like a pro, I don't think this is it. My gaming skills might be as elusive as a perfect serve, but hey, if there's a remote chance they might fix the flaws, I’ll be as shocked as when I finally managed to pull off a combo without accidentally hitting pause. Fingers crossed—though we both know I’ll be waiting longer than I do for my next victory.

_childDocuments_.review: TopSpin 2K25 initially impresses with some convincing animations and visuals, but ultimately fails to convert an opportunity to break through as the premier tennis game on the market. Developers of this latest iteration of TopSpin clearly have an appreciation for the skill and athleticism possessed by tennis professionals: Players actually slide on clay courts, can sprint to dig out a lob and return it with a flick of the wrist, and even dive on the ground for volleys. That's why I was disappointed to find that in spite of the appearances, the points in the game don't ever  like real tennis points. Players are able to stop on a dime and change directions much too easily, preventing you from "hitting behind them" after you've pulled them off the court with a wide serve. And despite not having to worry much about momentum, movement somehow still manages to feel sluggish, like you have to actively fight the controls to get your character to stand where you want them to. Moving to the net feels so unnatural, why can't I just push the thumbstick toward the net? Why do I have to press an additional button? Rallies can also grind on with neither player ever making an error, even if they opt to hit nonstop flat power shots.I was fortunate enough to try the game on a free weekend, because it's simply not worth a $60 price tag. Other games like Full Ace Tennis Simulator provide a much more true to life tennis experience at a fraction of the cost, and are actually possible to play with friends to boot.

From the moment you start, you’ll create your own player, design their appearance, and begin your ascent to the top of the tennis world. The progression system is well-balanced, offering a realistic sense of achievement as you improve your player’s stats and experience.One of the standout features of the career mode is the emphasis on both skill and strategy. Success in *TopSpin2K25* isn’t just about winning matches—it’s about managing your player's schedule, balancing training, and making smart decisions regarding your career path. _childDocuments_.review: For those who like tennis, TopSpin 2K25 is an excellent game. I especially recommend the career mode, where you can create your own player and customize him according to your preferences and play the most diverse tournaments of the ATP tour as well as the four grand slams and the Nitto ATP finals. With each match you will earn VC (currency used in the game to buy accessories for your player, such as shorts, t-shirts, rackets... and even different animations for serving, forehand and backhand). At the end of each match you will also earn experience points, which when accumulated will increase the level of your player. When you level up your player you will earn six AP points, which can be used to increase your player's attributes (serve, forehand, backhand, volley, power, speed, stamina and reflexes). If you want, you can also play the world tour, where you can play tournaments with your player against other online players of various other nationalities and earn points to fight for the top of the table. However, I only recommend this game mode to players who have reached level 30 (the maximum level that can be achieved), otherwise you will be at a disadvantage compared to other players in terms of attribute requirements. If you want, you can also play local or online matches with current tennis players or even great tennis legends such as (Roger Federer, André Agassi or Serena Williams).Positive points:Good gameplay, good graphics and a good customization system.Points for improvement:Fixing minor bugs, adding more players and props and greeting the opponent at the net at the end of an online match.

_childDocuments_.review: I used around 10 hours of the freeplay weekend.Is it a recommendation? Yes, with some "but"s:First the good stuff: The tennis gameplay itself is very good. It's demanding and challenging, especially the timing of shots and the services. So yes, you need to practise first. You won't win the Grand Slam without investing some hours into training and the lower level competitions. But that is a good thing. What about the microtransactions?The focus is on extra cosmetics, so some might think about a boycott just because of their existance. (I don't like MT, too). You earn your VC (ingame currency) with everything you play in the game from training sessions to online competitions. But for sure, the "extra" VC would come in handy, but is not needed.Tipp: Don't buy fancy outfits in the beginning. Stay focused on playing tennis instead of shopping. There are stepstones in the career that need an extra invest of VC (Trainers are affordable without any doubt, but later you surely want to buy Houses and a bunch of staff members that all cost a small amount.You don't HAVE TO pay for them, but I think you WANT to pay for them, because they give you big rewards concerning gameplay. More reasonable rewards than colored shirts and shoes can give you, Sir "Fashion Victim"! ;)May it be stamina/endurance boni for travelling around the world or VC boosts for certain competitions.What felt "not good"?- Player licences are not up-to-date. It seems, licensing was done when beginning the game production with Federer, Alcaraz or Medjedev as the Topstars (Germans will miss ANY famous player, male or female).You have Agassi, Graf, Sampras as legends, but Zverev, Nadal etc. are missing.On the other hand - unfortunately you don't miss them when starting a career. You won't be able to match the Superstars until reaching the second highest status level.- And this level is bound to missions, you have to fulfill, the world ranking isn't the key. You have to complete some challenges (win x TS250/500/1000 competitions, complete x Trainings in Bronze/Silver/Gold tier, etc.) to raise your status and be able to take part in higher/better competitions.- You don't feel like "playing tennis" in the tournaments, because you only play one Tie Break in the TS250 series, a Super Tie Break in the TS500 series and in the TS1000 series (with matching status) you can play a complete set of 3 games.I understand, that it would take way too much time, if you had to play every match with one set from the beginning, but just Tie Breaks feel a little awkward (I played over 50 matches in myCareer, I learned from an achievement, and still had no single "complete match" with a whole set).- I like the system how you level up trainers. You have to achieve a certain amount of certain shots or earn points from opponents mistakes - but also you sometimes have to win a point after 10 hits (= a rally of 20). But even if you try to play the ball easy for your opponent to return, he makes mistakes or misses easy balls. Good in the game, but bad for the next trainer level. I needed nearly a whole season for 15 "10 hit rallys") in the low level competition. Keep that in mind when choosing your trainer or else you play top tier competitions with a level 2 trainer...- Last thing: What firstly feels nice for progression in your career, evolves more to "grinding" for the levels. Every month you have the same routine of training, special event and competiton. There are different sub-missions in each, but you look to your status and choose the ones needed, even if you don't want to do them. So even with hitting the world Top10 ranking, you play the 40th TS250 Tie Break, because you need it for a raise in the status (to unlock the higher rated competitions).What did I miss?There have been Tennis games in the past, some good, some bad. Topspin2K25 is surely one of the better games. I would like to see e.g. "Sponsor Contracts" for a season. You could get outfits from the brand and goals to fulfill on the other hand. Some possibilities to earn some sxtra VC could be something like "Press Conferences" or Interviews (as known from other sports games like NBA2K or former FIFA series).Perhaps a little aaproach into a "Story Mode" direction could be a nice addition for offline players, because "MyCareer" is just plain menu-based gameplay between the matches.As a result of the freeplay weeken, I still want to buy the game - but not for the called price. Why? I'm not THE Tennis fan. I miss many players, I know (male and female, especially the actual famous German players) and I only was captured by the "MyCareer" mode (I'm more the Singleplayer-guy, don't play online much). So, I keep my eyes on the sales and some time, I'll get back to my started career and enjoy some rallies again.

_childDocuments_.review: I've never really played a tennis game before so thought I would try it with it being free over the weekend. Right away the game annoys you with a some need to update a 2k account, and you are stuck here till you do.  This could be something done once you get into the main menu.  So you get through this and then you are dumped right into a match(I personally hate when games do this). Having never played a tennis game, it was a bit of a put off initially, but as they give you a pro player to play as, it wasn't too hard to figure out the movement and buttons needed. I think there could a much better into to the game/series done here.You eventually get to main menu and can about setting things up to your liking. I found graphic options very basic and disappointing. Character creation is pretty good, lots of ways to customise your character. Of course, if you want to bling out, you are gunna have to go into the in-game store and use VC to do it. I'm assuming you can do some of this by grinding, You do get VC even just doing the tutorial.Once you get into the game the graphics are...OK, but seem dated to what can found nowadays. It's serviceable, and you have fun as long as you don't look too close. As a widescreen owner(there are lots of us), I'm used to menus and cut-scenes not being at the 21:9 ratio my monitor uses. In this game though, as you play a match, there are scenes that I guess are cut-scenes or something so you are back to a basic aspect ratio with black bars on each side during the game, this happens quite a lot. So jumping back and forth from 2 different aspect rations which is jarring, immersion breaking and annoying. If a game intends to make a cut-scenes a big part of the actually game play, the game SHOULD/MUST have versions of these that match aspect ratios for widescreen users. It's too annoying. The tutorial may be boring for anyone already familiar with tennis, but for a newbie like me it provided valuable information in getting up to speed with tennis. It's voiced by John McEnroe which is great. Even us non tennis players know who he is. I struggled during some of the lessons and expected him to get a little testy with me and it was disappointing when he didn't. Would have been a great laugh and just seems like a missed opportunity.Going into an exhibition game as my created player, i soon found out tennis won't be a simple as the exhibition game we are dumped into when starting the game. There is some skill and depth here and you ignore what you learned in the tutorials at your own peril. While the intro, graphics and continual aspect ratio switching during the game are lacklustre, it was nice to  see the core of the game can be fun and challenging. For me, I would recommend it, but not at the full price point. It's something I may actually pick up when it can found at a deep sale price and would recommend that path for anyone looking at this game. Not enough of the game is at a AAA  in 2024 game level to recommend otherwise.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a major disappointment. The core game play is good, as it is almost an exact replica of Top spin 4, and the updated graphics have some stunning courts and arenas. This is the only positive feedback I have for this game. The menu systems are clunky and very optimised for 1 thing. Promoting purchasing from the "Pro shop". While you can earn credits from playing the game, it would take a very long time to unlock a good number of cosmetic items to customise your character, and as such spending more money (over the already high $90 AUD) to unlock these items is encouraged as you also require these credits to play the game; hiring coaches, staff and player homes. I'm surprised you don't need to pay an entry fee to play tournaments! (2k do not take this as a suggestion)There exists some form of memory leak as each game gets progressively laggier resulting in requiring a game restart. The game stutters and the timing becomes much harder as a result, this ruins the gameplay and makes it near unplayable for longer sessions (30min+). Career mode has 80 other characters. I would have loved to have seen larger tournament draws, and wish more time would have been allocated to this side of things instead of microtransactions. I have seen a review here saying the devs have mentioned working on this for future? I think the game should have been released after that is finished, this is not an early access game.The multiplayer I've had a large amount of lag and rubber banding, my internet isn't the fastest but this hasn't been a major consistent issue in any other games but this one. On top of that in my limited experience online,  the meta for high power (Sharapova/Williams) does appear to be true. I don't have a large number of games but most of them I played against one of the aforementioned two.And to top it all off, while I myself haven't tried the console versions, I have seen it reported a couple of times that the PC port has lesser graphical quality compared to console versions.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all , I played the free demo and I royally suck at this game, so anything negative I say is a reflection of that. It seems that the entire game is based on the gauge, so if you get a perfect shot, then your opponent performs worse because of it...not because the shot was particularly well placed or timed.  Another problem with the gauge is that it's not consistent with its pace..sometimes the line moves fast and sometimes slow and that makes it impossible to gain any kind of muscle memory to hit the ball on your own.  You are tied to the gauge forever in this game it seems.  The game feels like it's controlling me and not the other way around...if that makes sense.  Graphics are nice and the motion seems real enough, the sound effects of the characters and the crowds is well done and overall the game looks polished.  I tried to give this a chance but the gauge especially ruined it for me.

_childDocuments_.review: It was great on the first day and a half. Now the controls will randomly stop responding as intended. It is like the game forgets that it is supposed to be using the left thumbstick input from the controller for aiming vs moving and what states the character model is in. My player will be mid back swing, and I will go to aim with the left stick on my Elite 2 controller and he just starts running in that direction rather than use that input for aim calculations. My character will also, at random times, split step on input like they should. But will then proceed to run in the exact opposite direction for 1-3 steps before shifting back to the intended path/direction. I have tried multiple controllers, multiple PCs, uninstalling and re-installing... nothing works. I actually found a solution for the input problem. I disabled Steam's Input handling for this game and I have not had the input issue since. How ever after recent updates the game's online play is terrible. There is far too much latency, and disconnects. Plus, far too many "meta" players that make online play so boring it is not even worth it when it is working properly. I have also found in recent updates has made volleys even more unnatural. I still do not recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: As I was a big fan of Top Spin 4 (back then on the Xbox 360) I was thrilled that the series was being continued, now finally on the PC. And what can I say? The surroundings are a little dull and sterile. Unfortunately, there aren't many pros as far as the player selection is concerned, so I hope that this will be improved. I would also describe the online part as rather rudimentary, a nice career would be really good here. Graphically, it's unfortunately not up to date but rather 10 to 15 years behind, which personally doesn't bother me too much as the actual gameplay is extremely good and motivating.All in all, there is a lot of potential here that has not (yet) been exploited by the devs. If you can overlook these shortcomings, Top Spin 2K25 is a very motivating tennis sim.

_childDocuments_.review: The best tennis game ever in terms of gameplay, along with Top Spin 4.The career mode is good but feels lacking of content. Graphics are not bad but could be better for a game published in 2024. There are a lot of licensed courts and different playtimes (day, evening and night). I think the worst aspect of this game is the lack of licensed players (only 11 WTA players, 7 ATP players, and 7 legends), and some of them are not even face-scanned... They said that they will add more players (as a free DLC), let's hope it's true... Playing as Federer feels so good, his character is really accurate.Even with these amount of negative points, the gameplay is incredibly amazing and realistic. The only bad thing about gameplay is that it's impossible to aim during the serve (at least with an XBOX controller), you can only aim in the middle or to the sides (in this case it always ends up with a fault).It's really fun to play, and the AI is not so predictable in the hardest difficulty levels. _childDocuments_.review: As a fan of the Top Spin series, the game play has been fun.It's been fun and addicting to work through the career mode. However, despite that, I've been regretting the purchase, for this full priced game with micro-transactions everywhere.I am concerned on how many micro-transactions there are for a full price game.Everything, all the gear, services in career mode, etc. cost "VC", which can be earned sloooowly in normal game play, or purchased with real money.The Season Passes are great, that can provide long term play and new items to unlock. But I am unwilling to pay for the premium passes, when I feel like many of the items should be unlocked by default (like player animations), like in past tennis games. Coming from Top Spin 4, to this new modern era of micro-transactions was jarring. If this is the trend for Top Spin going forward, I'll sit out.At least the other recent tennis games are not riddled with micro-transactions too.Also, it's been frustrating when online servers are down, that I can't play my career mode. It's the worst when the server disconnects at the end of the "offline" match. I don't think it saves rewards, despite winning the match.Why isn't it offline? All the features of the game go down if the servers are down. Only the exhibition mode remains. It does not feel like I actually own this game; I paid full-price for a portal to an online service, with micro-transactions. I don't play other recent 2k sports title, so I should have done more research if they are all like this beforehand. If that's the case, that is unfortunate though.Overall, the game play is good, but the micro-transactions and the persistent need for online turns me off.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is mostly an updated version of Top Spin 4, that released back in 2011.The gameplay is great (it already was in Top Spin 4), which is arguably the most important part.Some parts of the game are lacking (size of the player roster, quality of player faces, some mechanics of the career mode that have not been changed even though they were already criticized 13 years ago). There are some good things to note as well; for example, the courts look amazing, and there is a lot of them.The MAIN ISSUE is that an online connection is required to play offline game modes such as career mode. This is very wrong for several reasons :- Obviously, if your connection goes out, you can't play the game. Very stupid.- The quality of the servers is lacking. The game has been out for 3 days and we have already had two server crashes that lasted for several hours (again, when this happens, you can't play the game).- When the servers eventually get disabled (planned for 31 december 2026), the main modes of the game will not be playable anymore. This means that you don't really own the game, you just have access to it for a limited period of time.2K should allow us to play career mode offline. Until they do, I do not recommend buying this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I DO recommend this game for tennis fans. Get the standard edition. PROS1. The gameplay is the most addicting you can get from a tennis game. Its somehow better than TopSpin4 and I cannot tell you why. I think they just fine tuned it a lot better. Its fluid, looks great, feels even better. 2. The audio is great. The audio feel when playing on hard court especially, just absolutely sells the feeling that you're there.3. The visuals are good as well. YES, its not realistic or next gen. But the stadiums look absolutely ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ gorgeous. The color palette they chose is fantastic. Everything pops and stands out really well. 4. Online matches, if and when you get matched against players of your same level or around your same level, it feels so good to play toe to toe with them. Adrenaline pumping feeling. There are a lot of issues with the game tho.1. Career mode. It is copied and pasted from TS4 where you start from Top 80, have to do very DUMB objectives like "Play 3 of these tournaments and do 4 of these things to unlock "Star" level in order to play bigger tournaments". Artificial way to hold you back from progressing. I was hoping this game would've moved away from that but they doubled down on it instead.2.  Another issue with the career mode is the FATIGUE system. Its another artificial way to hold you back and make you grind more. And its VERY frustrating. 3. Lack of a big roster for sure is another issue. They did say they are adding more players but we don't know how many and when. 4. Right now, playing ranked with your player online is up in the air. The matchmaking can pit you against a level 30 player even when you're like level 10. And there are instances where you can almost beat those players cause they don't really understand tennis or have a large tennis IQ (bad positioning, shot selection etc) but you lose because they just have like 50 more points in their "power" attribute than you. I'm not adding 2K mtx stuff in the cons because its 2024 and its expected at this point that 2K would this nonsense. Honestly, this game right now for a tennis fan is anywhere from 7-8 out of 10. If it had fixed the career mode and had like 10 more players in each tour, it would've easily been a 10/10. I recommend this game because I want people to support this enough so that we can get a follow up that HOPEFULLY fixes all these issues.Keep in mind, the other BIG tennis game we have TIEBREAK and if you've seen its gameplay (or played any Big Ants other 3 tennis games) - you'd know how ♥♥♥♥♥ that is and how it wont live up to its potential.

name: Breakers Collection
detailed_description: Breakers Collection features both of the original games (Breakers and Breakers Revenge) and a brand new content for the cult-classic among the fans of Fighting Games, that was first released in 1996 for the Neogeo and Arcades and after released with a sequel in 1998 with additional playable characters, balance adjustments and new gameplay elements. Breakers Collection is a simple action-fighting game, with a roster with many playable characters (10 in Breakers Revenge), that were all known by the fans from around the world. The special actions are also similar to other fighting games from the same era, although the dashing and back-stepping techniques tend to differ between characters.

_childDocuments_.review: A really solid collection for a good price that showcases one of the simplest but addictingly fun fighting games from the NeoGeo's huge library of fighting games. The roster may be small, but it's a 90's fighting game, and the core gameplay is so much fun that it doesn't matter it's small. It's one of the easiest and fastest fighting games to learn but with so much depth to it, a fun roster of characters, a feel that immediately hooks you, so on so forth. I mean let's be real, who doesn't like Breakers Revenge? It's a classic that will always age well, simple but fun in the best way.Pros:+Solid emulation+Rollback netcode+Crossplay+Good training mode (could use some extra QOL features but as is is just fine)+Team Mode lets you play with a team of characters up to a 3v3 mode in a KOF style setup, restoring health in-between rounds and changing characters after the previous one falls+Nice extra content, good online features, online replays with various features, ranked, overall a strong package. Little bad to say about the game.Cons:-I had to limit my frame rate to 60fps in order to get rid of some emulation sound issues for playing offline, but even after the change it's only mostly fixed but not completely-No Breakers Revenge Extra Mode (a NeoGeo CD exclusive mode that makes this already wacky game even wackier, is absolutely worth playing in its own right)-Team Mode can't be played onlineI'm not entirely sure why I have sound issues with static, though I do use a sound card in my PC to listen to audio. My friend recommended limiting the frame rate (it is a fighting game after all) and it fixed the issue for the most part. Though bits of static are still there. Otherwise, give us Extra Mode and let us play Team Mode online and this collection is pretty much a steal. I mean c'mon, who DOESN'T want to play Extra Mode which lets you force draw games even after you die by stylishly murdering your opponent with a 50% combo that is impossible to do in vanilla otherwise?

_childDocuments_.review: Mekel Kasanova's TLDR ReviewsBreakers Collection is a compilation of two Neo Geo fighting games, Breakers and Breakers Revenge, which were originally released in 1996 and 1998 respectively. These games were never released outside of Japan, so this is an opportunity for players to experience them for the first time. The compilation offers players the opportunity to play the games with decent emulation, visual filters, and bonus features. The most important aspect of this release is the solid online play, which includes the rollback netcode functionality for smoother and fairer fights. This allows players to enjoy the game in its intended head-to-head versus play mode. Overall, the collection is a great way for players to experience these classic games legally and with added features for a more modern experience.The gameplay in Breakers Collection is smooth, with aerial supers and ground-slamming grab attacks that flow seamlessly from tap-combos. The game offers a wide range of options for approach and combo building, making it both deep and engaging for players. The game also comes with a variety of features such as screen filters, wallpapers, art galleries, training modes, full move lists, leaderboards, and options to adjust speeds and difficulty levels. QUByte Interactive has also added an all-new Team Battle Mode, which is similar to the King of Fighters series, allowing players to select a team of fighters and rotate through them as they are defeated. This mode is well-designed and makes the most of the diverse and interesting moves of the game's characters. However, players may feel that the ten-character roster is slightly limited compared to modern fighting games.One unique aspect of Breakers is that it gives separate identities and backstories to duplicate characters in mirror matches, which adds unexpected comedy to the game. For example, the flamboyant Italian character Pielle has a French counterpart named George who is said to consume Italians after being robbed on a trip to Italy. This level of creativity is not present in other fighting games like Street Fighter II.The gameplay of Breakers may seem simple at first glance, but it's actually quite complex, thanks to the ability to cancel super moves into a chain, and some unusual juggling potential. It's fast-paced and satisfying to play, and its visuals hold up well even today. The new team mode is similar to the King of Fighters series and allows players to regain a small amount of vitality after each win. The online crossplay and rollback netcode features in Breakers Collection are crucial aspects of the release, and have been implemented well. Players can also see ping and connection speed information, participate in ranked versus match-ups and download replays of their victories. The game's destiny was always in head-to-head versus play, and now with the opportunity to play online, it's time for players to get their fighting sticks ready.Graphically, Breakers Collection is excellent, featuring large, bold sprites, smooth animation, and bright, colorful backgrounds that take place in various locations around the world. The game's design is heavily influenced by Street Fighter, but the characters have their own unique styles and combo opportunities. For example, Condor is a strong grab character, Alsion III is a stretchy-limbed Egyptian god, and Pielle is a French-sounding Italian fencer. The game also features characters armed with weapons such as Sheik Maherl who wields a scimitar, and Tia, a spritely kickboxer from Thailand. The game's cast is well balanced and easy to pick up, but also offers a lot of depth for players to master over time.Although fun, the Breakers roster may be too small for the team mode in terms of variety and options. Online, the rollback netcode ensures smooth, lag-free battles, though the player may not be successful. The package may not have a lot of content, but it is as complete as it can be and is enjoyable to play. In retrospect, it is considered one of the best non-SNK fighting games released for the Neo Geo. Additionally, it is now more affordable to play the game with arcade-perfect quality. In conclusion, Breakers Collection feels like a passion project. It delivers a game that still feels modern and visceral to a new era of players. New players will be surprised by the high level of Visco's work, and the level of thought that went into its modernization with crucial up-to-date features is commendable. This kind of treatment should be standard when revisiting classic games, yet often it isn't. Breakers Collection gets it right.

_childDocuments_.review: A Neo-Geo arcade classic, the gameplay is buttery smooth and it's a great pickup and play experience. The collection has both the original Breakers and the updated version Breakers Revenge, with online rollback netcode, lobbies, ranked and casual matches, aswell as a training mode where you can see damage values, set the training dummy any way you like and see the hitboxes for each move.The only issue i've had is with the Replay function, which didn't match the actual game i had online. Other than that, this collection/port is very polished and i greatly recommend it for anyone who wants to get into the Fighting Game genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Breakers Collection

_childDocuments_.review:
Breakers Collection features both of the original games (Breakers and Breakers Revenge) and a brand new content for the cult-classic among the fans of Fighting Games, that was first released in 1996 for the Neogeo and Arcades and after released with a sequel in 1998 with additional playable characters, balance adjustments and new gameplay elements.

Breakers Collection is a simple action-fighting game, with a rooster with many playable characters (10 in Breakers Revenge), that were all known by the fans from around the world.

The collection version, the player will have more features and modes, like online versus mode - Rollback Netcode (GGPO) -, Art gallery and the most requested one, the training mode.

name: Song in the Smoke
detailed_description: Using the power of virtual reality, Song in the Smoke puts your survival directly in your own hands. Enter this dangerous world outside of time, where you must craft weapons, make clothes, build fires, and brew healing elixirs to steel yourself against its vicious predators. Whether you're either the hunter or the hunted, you can block, parry, and strike back with your club, or attack from a distance with your bow. True survivors will also need their wits to avoid some of the most lethal creatures that call this land their home. The world of Song in the Smoke holds equal parts salvation and danger. Use your senses to stalk prey: track their smell, follow their footprints, and plan your strike. When you’re ready, intuitive and responsive VR controls let you execute the perfect shot—a shot that could mean the difference between survival and death. The game uses a number of deeply-intertwined procedural systems, making every play-through unpredictable and unique. Animals seek water and shelter, while predators hunt for prey; as day transitions into night, the environment shifts and the creatures who inhabit it change their behaviors. A mystical narrative runs throughout the player’s journey as well, putting the experience into greater, transcendental context. Song in the Smoke is a beautiful and harrowing survival experience. How long will you last? Hunting : String bows to hunt your own prey, tracking their footprints and scents on the wind. Then hide among the ferns and bushes to line up the perfect shot, aiming naturally with your controllers before letting your handcrafted arrow fly. The player often takes the role of the hunted as well, requiring deft avoidance—or harrowing combat—to stay alive. Foraging : Find food, water, and the raw materials needed to build shelter and fire, as well as craft weapons and other items is essential for survival. Exploring : The wide open world of Song in the Smoke begs exploration, and moving through it requires curiosity and wit to unravel nature’s many mysteries. The song leads players forward, guiding them through this strange world and revealing a little more about the secret at its heart with each new discovery. Maximizing Resources : If you make the kill, make sure nothing is wasted. Stock up on meat, bones, and skins that you can use to keep yourself warm as you move through the world of Song in the Smoke, travelling from lush forests, through ancient valleys, to frozen glaciers. A deep crafting design allows players to build weapons, tools, shelter and fire from the raw materials nature provides. Total playthrough time: 12-20 hours REVIEWS Upload VR: “I am, if you couldn’t tell, quite in love with SitS ... An intoxicating trip, an experience directly connected to the beating heart of nature and acutely aware of the structure and interaction needed to make its survival gameplay work in VR.” Road to VR: 2021 PlayStation VR Game of the Year: 'In few words, Song in the Smoke is breathtaking, and definitely worth the tens of hours it will coax out of you.' USA Today: 'Top 5 VR Games of 2021.' Screenrant: “Song in the Smoke is an unrivaled VR survival game with horror elements, and it gives players complete freedom to explore, hunt in, and conquer the treacherous wilderness.' Shughead Gaming: “Maybe my biggest surprise of 2021. In the running for VR game of the year.” Gaming Nexus: “Excels with fantastic controls and VR mechanics, accomplishing some things that veteran VR developers still struggle with. Games like Song in the Smoke signal what VR games could be, which has restored a bit of my hope for the future of the format.” The VR Grid: “Song in the Smoke is an awesome blend of survival and fantasy” VR Focus: “Song in the Smoke looked like it was something special and it is, one of the best VR games of 2021.” Press Play Media: “A memorable experience the scope of which we’ve rarely seen on a headset like the Quest.” PSVR Without Parole: “GOTY. Best Survival Game in VR yet. Intuitive, Immersive, Incredible One of PlayStation VR's very best games.' PSVR Underground: “Game of the Year. A master class in survival.”
