_childDocuments_.review: The game feels unfinished. Visuals are the only saving grace. Characters mouth movements are as basic as sock puppets. All of the characters mouths move the same. We're using screenshots to describe most of the plot? Really?Combat is silly. If you charge your Ki max, and then use your signature final attack. The AI will then flee as far away from the map. This has happened multiple times. No Commentary guy, or any voice acting explaining the sequence in between plots. The Autoplay for cutscenes is super slow. No clue if there is a setting for it.  I honestly wish there was a commentary guy to verbally express what transpired inbetween plot points.  I don't mind reading. It's not the issue. My issue is that either you are reading and pushing the A button or you are reading and waiting for what I assume is 30 seconds for each scene and dialog. There is a handfull of cutscenes that are left out entirely. That or I just haven't unlocked them.  I guess I am supposed to select a different path to play as a different character to have that experience. Either way it's puzzling It would be nice to see what paths are for who. To me the build your own path let the gamer decide is just fluff.  I do like the create your own story. What I don't like is how I gotta character swap (Multi Menu) to experience a continuation of the story. And at times it's not even the path I was expecting. For example I picked Gohan, I was expecting Kid Gohan from Raditz to Vageta up to Namak, then lead into the Cell Games.  However I got Gohan going straight into Cell Games. The buildup was bland. And pales in comparison of how previous Budokai Tenkaichi games expressed one of the most epic fight scenes.  Dumbed down feels downplayed to a "oh that happened, Meh" doesn't leave as much of an impact when you out of the gate play as Teen Gohan and fight Cell.  Overall the game needs more polishing. Animation is a mixed bag, the AI is silly and flees as soon as you use your final special attack. Historical moments are either not there or hidden or just lost the hype it took to lead up to your favorite moment in the series. Story is mostly expressed through a voiceless dialog, with Screenshots. Actual cutscenes are okay in some areas. But really cursed in others specifically the character models and how they engage or interact during a cutscene with other characters. Honestly giving it a 6/10.

So you're watching a cutscene and before you know it the enemy is shooting a ki blast at your face, a timer that goes 3.2.1 or an announcer to start the fight would be amazing.-The AI do not feel fun at times, yes they are difficult but only because of the sheer randomness of their attacks. At times if you do nothing, the characters will just dash back and forth without rhyme or reason, just constantly spazzing out. Their difficulty really is the god mode of their parries and counters just knowing when to instant do them. Don't expect crazy combos and mechanics the AI will use on you that will make you feel you are fighting a high level player, just pure randomness and zoning that is questionable at times.-A lot of the fights in the story will take place on the same map multiple times getting really repetetive . If you're looking for online play however, I personally would not recommend it. Despite the game having such a huge roster of characters to choose from, you'll pretty much only see the same 5 or so characters in ranked online matches. Meanwhile, the unranked matchmaking system is absolutely horrible, and if it used the same matchmaking system that ranked used (select a preferred stage/bgm, select your character, queues you up to find an opponent) the online play would probably be miles better than it currently is, but as it stands right now if you try to go for unranked play, rather than queueing up, it puts you into a custom lobby as you wait for other people to join your lobby to play with. Sure you can just find someone else's room, but another problem is that usually there's more than just 2 slots in a room, so you're gonna be waiting for your turn to fight.Overall, taking the online play out of the equation, it's an amazing game, an absolute love letter to any Dragon Ball fan out there. But, if your main reason for getting it is the online play, unless they change some things, namely the unranked matchmaking system, I would not recommend this game for you.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR at the bottom.This game was fun for the first week, but I had to uninstall because people online prefer to cheese instead of just have fun. The game is deliberately unbalanced, which on paper, sounds fun - Until you understand that the playerbase can and will optimize the fun out of online play in favor of quick cheap wins with low skill ceiling fighters - And they have already done so at the time of this review. It goes to show how much gaming has changed since the last Budokai Tenkaichi, and how everyone has grown to prioritize virtual points over fun.You'd think that with a roster this enormous, there would be a huge diversity in the different fighters you'll be tackling. But if you buy this game with the intent to play online, you will go up against the same 12 characters, and your skilled plays will be punished with unskilled cheese (unblockable attacks, hyper armor, auto-dodge, stalling until the timer runs out and the person with the most health across their entire team wins by default).Oh, and I've never gotten a beam clash in Ranked. It's not meta to hit a beam attack with your own, apparently. It's fun to do with friends, it's extremely hype, but it's not optimal for quick and easy wins.Game design from 2007 with no online play doesn't translate well to an online setting who woulda thought.. Also no rollback servers...  Copied this Review because honestly i couldn't of said it better myself.

_childDocuments_.review: What I like:I have been playing DBZ games ever since 1997 when DBZ Legends, DB GT Final Bout and DBZ Ultimate Battle 22 were released for the first time on Playstation 1 and ever since I've been playing almost every single game released of this franchise. I also played all the DBZ Budokai, DBZ  Budokai Tenkaichi, Xenoverse 1 and 2, Kakarot and FighterZ as well and always enjoyed the Tenkaichi formula the most out of all of them ever since Budokai Tenkaichi 1 was released. With that being said, I personally consider DB Sparking Zero to be the king of all Tenkaichi games to almost perfect and definitely recommend it to everyone who loves DB/Z/GT/S/D.--What I dislike:But no matter how good a game can be there are still some issues and set backs and I will mention them next:The story mode at first it feels lacking in drama and narrator telling the story in the background but as you get into it you start to appreciate it specially after you play the story chapter of Vegeta. The first person angle in the stories could've been better if it gave more angles and freedom to look around but it was an interesting touch only that it feels very limited and rigid but it gives a new dimension to the story at least.I believe the reason the story mode is the way it is, is because of the customize mode where you can make your own story with a whole editing option which takes a lot of time to make something good and upload it in the online for other players to play your made up story and share it and so on. Really adds a lot of replay value to the game.The combat is the best of all games but if you expect that each character will fight different then this isnt the game for you as they all use the same formula for combos and combinations. The characters are semi unique on their own with the different special skills and passive skills and visually but in combat is really not that unique with all honesty. Expect the same as all the other Tenkaichi games only better. During the combat its really hard to learn it at first even with the tutorial that sadly it doesnt tell all specially the most important part of the game which is being able to be released from "back shots" which is when you get locked in a combo as you are being hit from your back. You need to master the Super Counter which is Up+Attack button. The problem is that the game doesnt explain anything in depth on how to do it correctly and this is where most players rage quit the game. And even knowing exactly how it works, the game doesnt seem to really respond as you would expect specially in online as there is discrepancy in the connection. Its a whole learning curve and its mandatory because both players and the computer in high lvls will always do backshots.My mayor let down of the game is the offline PVP as the devs gave the excuse of having only the hyperbolic time chamber to play with your local friends and its because they were not able to work on some elements about the stages involving destructions in offline pvp  which sounds like excuses to me. On top of that its very common getting knocked back to unfocus your opponent and makes it tedious and hard to find them again in such big stage that is only mostly white with myst making it way too hard to find your opponent to refocus. It was so much for my friends that their experience was mostly negative and it was very frustrating for me to admit they were right with their critics.The other issues is that whenever you play online, there is a bug which remaps your controller if you are using "classic controllers" vs someone using "standard controller" and it confused the game to change your buttons mapping to make the special attack be the same button making it almost impossible to play. So if you play classic, you will feel forced to get used to standard as its what the majority plays. Hopefuly this has been noticed and fix soon.The game is clear in about a week if you really dedicate to it and once you are done the only replay value is the online and farming dragonballs that can be found only as a random loot after finishing offline vs cpu mode making it very very tedious and boring to collect all the dragonballs. I would've loved if they used the same way it was done in Xenoverse but its what it is.My other issue is that the game offers a lot of slots for clothes and empty space for accesories making you thirsty to think there are many unlockables as you progress and having you wanting more and leaving you with a lot of expectations to the customization but the sad thing is that there is almost to nothing to these elements. The only unlocks are characters, music, and cpu a.i. gamestyles. If the devs would've added as much variety in customization as Xenoverse 2 it would've make this game way way more lasting.And last but not least, while the action and special abilities feels pretty good and solid, after playing games such as Kakarot, most of them feels lacking. You have no idea how soft the Kamehameha feels when they hit the opponent. Its a nice touch there are clouds of dust and smoke out of it but the impact and the boom you would expect are very bland and light. Meanwhile in Kakarot they look and feel a lot more close to the anime both visually and in sfx. But there are other skills such as the Big Bang Attack that does feels powerful and strong.  Its also strange and very lacking how there are no planet destructions after a huge explosion such as Majin Vegeta's Final Explosion, something everyone was expecting to see in this game.---However these things that bother me about this game isn't really that much of a big deal and the game is still amazing as it is. I just only hope the dev team actually add more to the game and also opens up to include more stages for offline pvp.--Overall Score:  8/10

_childDocuments_.review: Peak. It captures that same perfect energy BT3 did. It's what we all wanted the BT4 mod to be. I have very few negatives, but i'll list them before I glaze the game.- Character transformations are listed alongside the characters as opposed "click on character from 'x' time period, list transformations of character" style it had in BT3, this makes the roster VERY hard to navigate. VERY.- Instead of including all of the music with something like the ultimate edition, which, mind you, was over 100$, they're packaging it as two different music packs priced at 15$ each. Again, it's just music, but still. I want to be able to play head-cha-la while i'm in sparking WITHOUT dropping 15$.- The story mode is a touch lacking in certain areas, I found myself left wanting when certain pivotal moments just didn't have cutscenes. It was still fun, and I adored the "sparking episodes" so very much.- Maps. I just wish there were more. The maps that we DO have are very nice and very pretty, not to mention the map destruction is amazing, I just wish there were more maps.- A few OG dragonball fans will be a little disappointed when they see the roster, aswell as GT fans. I'm sure they'll package them later on as a DLC, but not being able to play as fan favorites like Mercenary Tao or Super 17 definitely sucks.- Wishes. I |WISH| there was more to wish for. As of writing this, you can only wish for 2 characters, and they can both be acquired by just leveling up.That aside, time for the pros.+ literally everything else.+ The game is just beautiful, so very beautiful. It's definitely the best looking anime game to date in my opinion.+ The combat is just as fluid as you'd expect from a successor to the series, and it didn't leave me wishing for more.+ The CUSTOM BATTLE CREATOR.... this game includes the most expansive mario maker-esque custom battle creator and I absolutely adore it. Also, yes, there are atleast 20 levels of Cabba vs SSJ4 Gogeta, and yes, I also made one.+ THE SPARKING EPISODES. I have only experienced Goku's sparking episodes as of writing this, and I won't spoil it for anyone reading this that hasn't seen them. They're incredible. I found myself, literally, screaming at around 11PM at night because of them.+ Online tournaments. Need I say more? You can do world tournaments ONLINE, with RANDOMS... it's peak.+ Ranked/Casual, I mean, it's got online matchmaking. Which, admittedly, in this day and age isn't that big of a deal, but having online matchmaking in a tenkaichi game is something I literally dreamed of. It's so nice to actually have it.+ Voice acting. In stark contrast to the lack of cutscenes leaving me wanting, some of the voice acting in this game left me with the exact opposite feeling. At first, I was kind of expecting the delivery of some lines to not live up to my expectations as the lack of cutscenes had dimmed my expectations, but when I heard that first "YOU FOOL!" I knew I was in for a treat. Overall, I was EXTREMELY satisfied with the voice acting in this game, some of the iconic one liners are just delivered so perfectly. Though, no UI Goku roar does make me sad.+ Story mode DOES have positives outside of the sparking episodes, you can also go down different character's story routes. It's a nice touch, in my opinion, though it's still dimmed by the lack of cutscenes.Overall? The best anime game to come out in YEARS. Easily one of, if not, my favorite release of this year, and a must buy for dragonball fans everywhere.9.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: I wasn't particularly looking forward to this game but once it was around the corner of getting released I decided to pick it up and try out to see if it was any fun.I ended up getting the game primarily for Episode battle so most of my impressions of the game are based around that, I did 100% the game to get a decent understanding of everything but I won't be talking about PvP as I don't care about it so if that's your bread and butter, I suggest looking at other reviews.Episode related- I think the game would benefit a lot from a joint episode map so you can choose to do them chronologically instead of per person as you end up skipping a lot of the story for certain characters. - Also resetting on a secret objective can get extremely tedious after a couple tries especially if you end up beating the enemy but not getting the secret route. This will mean waiting till the cutscene after the battle to hit pause then quit to go back to the episode select screen selecting the mission then skipping the cutscenes in order to then try again. This is made worse when the secret objective is time based but there's no dialogue to indicate you failed the challenge. - So few what if scenarios overall you'd expect there to be like a dozen or more for your main characters but there are very few "big" what if scenarios and a couple smaller what if scenarios that are just a cutscene.- On a similar note of skipping story there's just whole fights or scenes that get skipped or are these weird picture cutscene with text where instead of getting a narrator to voice over what's on the screen the game just has it up for a couple seconds before moving onto the next line of text.- There's a choice in "Chaos at the World Tournament" during Gohan's which is meaningless as it's just a whether or not you want to skip a fight. - During "Faint Unease" for Piccolo episode if you decide to help Goku you will get a regular cutscene then a text cutscene that will go over what the regular cutscene does which isn't a big issue but just a weird oversight.Gameplay related- Can't change your settings except for in the hub world??- Useless wish options, why are you able to wish for items that cost 15k zeni when just wishing for zeni gives you that much and more? - Can't play as certain what if characters from the story.- Grind to get dragon balls is mind numbing.Animation related- The transformations animations on characters can end up being lazy or seem unfinished? The former being Frieza going golden and the latter just being Jiren going full power.- The Mafuba animation just looks like a joke, special shout out to Gohan's.Bug related- After going to sparking mode or transforming my character will just refuse to do any ki related action until after I move which can get extremely irritating during harder fights- During certain cutscenes you can look through the eyes of the character you’re playing and it looks really dumb. Special shout out to Gohan on the ground in front of Cell. - There are times where the ai will just break and ki charge towards a wall.- It's possible for the enemy ai to fall through the map and lead to a reset on the fight, the map I found this to be extremely consistent is Rocky Land on ki attacks that move the enemy to certain positions that could be inside rocks when on ground level.The word for this game I'd pick is "Soulless" there's a couple things in this game I'd say are interesting but so much of it just seems like no one actually play tested to see if they managed to make something memorable, outside of the obvious what if character I doubt this game will be remembered in the long run without fixes and meaningful additions.If you read this far into my review and noticed I got something wrong, I'd appreciate a comment so I can correct it or if they update any of my complaints I'd also be happy to change it to reflect the current state of the game. Thank you for reading and I hope you have a nice day!Small edit for two things I forgot to mention regarding the what if content and if it is worth it at all and second being my experience with crashes with the game.- If you're curious as to what the what if content is I recommend just watching it on YouTube I do not believe it is at all worth it to buy the game to see the what ifs.- I forgot to mention this initially, but this game is also extremely unstable from my time playing it. I've had days where I have all the settings maxed with some other programs running in the background and had no crashes to having the most intensive settings at medium or low and I get hard crashes multiple times in a row with no other programs running at the same time. One of the worst crashes I experienced was during Buu Saga on Goku's story, I was about 7 hours into playing the game having done some of the other side content when the game hard crashed my PC upon launching the game back up my save was corrupted so I had to redo everything I did during those previous 7 hours, not exactly difficult after having learned the game but just annoying.

_childDocuments_.review: I paid 100 dollars for this game on a friend’s request.Dragon Ball: Sparking! Zero is a fighting game set in the Dragon Ball Universe, that thing that you watched when you were 8 and basically decided your entire life for you.Follow the journey of Goku, Vegeta, Piccolo, smaller Goku, Smallest Goku, Goku but blue, Goku but an ape man, and Goku’s son as they hone their strength and skill so that they can defend the Earth from the evils of the universe.Using Karate.Dragon Ball is a world wide phenomenon and has that same problem that 40k does, only instead of no one playing it, nobody these days seemed to have watched it. Nobody under the age of 28, at least. There’s a lot of memes and gushing about this abridged series, but actually sitting people down to watch Dragon Ball and Dragon Ball Z is like pulling teeth. But that’s not what we’re here for.Sparking! Zero is a third person fighting game where you take control of your favorite Goku and/or Vegeta and do battle in iconic battlefields from, mostly, Dragon ball Z and some Super. Not much Dragon Ball love in this one. You have a melee button, a ranged button, the button to power up, the button to move faster, a block, a counter, and a few other moves. Sparking! Zero is basically what I wanted Xenoverse and Xenoverse 2 to be, this all-out brawl that captures that essence of punching an idiot so hard that they go flying through mountains and buildings. Characters in Dragon Ball are strong. Like, really strong, and fast too, and also they shoot lasers from their hands. Even early in the series when Goku was just a little baby that hurt people that deserved it, people were moving at light speeds or blowing up the moon with their big muscular old man lasers. So capturing that in a video game is vital for that Dragon Ball experience. Sparking! Zero is the closest we’ve gotten to actually playing an anime episode or manga chapter since Budokai Tenkaichi 3. There was always something wrong with later games that, even if they were good or decent, they always lacked that pizass. Ultimate Tenkaichi was just a quick time simulator, Xenoverse was more focused on RPG and character building, and raging blast’s arenas were so small they may as well have just been wrestling rings. Sparking! Just kind of throws any kind of restraint to the wind. The arena gets demolished mid fights, if you kick a guy hard enough they just keep going if they don’t recover at all. Firing a beam of any kind will decimate basically any building in it’s way. Its basically a post-Canadian Hockey game simulator but with more Kung Fu.  And I love it, gets the blood pumping, makes me feel alive again. Story mode this time around is kind of like a big shenanigans event. You pick a character and then go through their life throughout the series. Only this time there are requirements you have to meet, and if you meet said requirements, you might go down a different path called a “Sparking! Event.” basically a what-if scenario. The early Goku ones, so far, have been the best to me. Stuff like going super Saiyan early or starting ♥♥♥♥ with Freiza because Vegeta asked you to. It does peter out near the Cell Arc, and sort of becomes lame after that, but I’ve only finished Goku’s story so far, so only time will tell, I guess.Outside of Story mode, you have your usual Budokai modes, or at least the ones you expect. No board game mode in this one, sorry. VS is where you can fight a friend or CPU or someone you just don’t like either locally or online, I’m like 100% sure there’s split screen, I don’t know I live alone. Other than that, there’s the MANDATORY CPU vs CPU mode that exists entirely for video game streaming blood sports and nothing else. People are also making their own what-ifs now, which is neat. Its nothing in depth, no one is making visual novel levels of story telling with the tools, it basically comes down to “Fight gogeta when you only have 10% health” or “What if Broly fought Broly”.Can you imagine a Dragon Ball story maker with RPG Maker levels of tools? I’d play the hell out of those.Sparking! Zero is exactly what it needs to be. Its Budokai Tenkaichi again, now with Online like the Wii port had for BT2, and a lot of people discovered on launch that they actually weren’t all that good at Budokai. Its a Dragon Ball game for Dragon Ball fans. Its about beam struggles and lightning fast exchange of punches, and punching dudes really hard and turning into a different form or changing your hair color. _childDocuments_.review: I am so happy this game exists, it is unreal. I am undoubtedly quite terrible but ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ is it good.Right in the childhood in the best of possible ways.And they gave SS3 Goku a badass extra rush instead of his super explosive wave and that ♥♥♥♥ is unfathomably cash.Update: "full" review below now that I'm almost finished (though will continue to play the custom battles people make and play the multiplayer tings.)***Tenkaichi: it is Tenkaichi, and it is beautifully Tenkaichi. This isn't for everyone, especially the Xenoverse fans, because I see some people criticise stuff like "long cutscenes for attacks" and "we don't need a cutscene for transformations." Nah. We do. That's Tenkaichi, that's in the genome of the game series, it wouldn't be part of that series otherwise. In fact, they've absolutely sped some things up - melee Trunks' Heat Dome ultimate used to have a bit of a cutscene showing the enemy blasting away and now doesn't, sadly - but all of this is Tenkaichi pedigree and it's wonderful that they kept it. I play Dragon Ball games for the cinema of them, I want to emulate the show, and the show is full of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ facial expressions and power ups and focussing on little details. It is perfectly fair to hate that, to want a fighting game that has a Dragon Ball skin, but it's not objective and it's certainly not, to my mind, a valid criticism of a series that has always done things a certain way. They made this entry authentic, and I am so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ glad that they did.Graphics: beautiful, exactly as I hoped. From the smoke effects, the energy effects, the explosions and destruction, the auras - Fused Zamasu got the sexy going on ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, and Dabura for some reason, what a king (literally) - they made it look amazing. On top of that, a lot of things that in the older Tenkaichi games were lacking - super explosive waves were always dull as hell, and certain abilities like Omega Shenron's Gigantic Blaze were basically geysers of detail-free red energy - are now actually beautiful and in some cases incredible. Super Buu's ultimate looks mad cool, as does Perfect Cell's, even though both are just named  super explosive waves. No complaints here, it looks great.Story: eh. I didn't dislike the story mode, but it is the weakest part of the game in many ways. I still have to finish Jiren's what-if (because UI Goku ain't using lube) but overall, I don't disagree with people who are upset because of the cutscenes and the odd choices of focus at times. The way Goku's SS transformation is kind of glossed over, for instance, or the lack of little battles in certain sagas, are obvious issues. At the same time, it is the same story of Dragon Ball that remains unchanged for decades now, and I've played it all before. I will say that the what-if stories are pretty great, and in some cases downright brilliant, but I won't spoil their contents here for those who read this and intend to play them. But that is clearly where the energy went, and I can't blame the devs for that. I will however say the biggest ♥♥♥♥-up is giving my boy Vegeta only a few sagas, because ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ hell the lad gets enough ♥♥♥♥♥ without games doing it as well! JUSTICE FOR THE PRINCE. Ah, well. At least he's great to play.Combat: ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ fantastic. Just a phenomenal upgrade over older Tenkaichi combat, it's lightning-fast, looks amazing, is intricate to the right degree, and while there are some issues - I think there needs to be either a narrowing window or an increased ki cost for repeated Z-counters (the dodge ones, I think they are?) - it is otherwise great. It feels like fighting a Dragon Ball fight, which is the whole damned point of the game, so...yeah. Great success. Plus moveset-wise almost all characters have interesting moves now, and it's a real nice upgrade from Tenkaichi 3. Still a few "super explosive waves" and "full-power energy volleys" but the visual upgrade and the general reduction in them helps. Also mad props to whoever decided Omega Shenron's Gigantic Blaze deserves to look identical to Syn Shenron's ultimate version, because that ♥♥♥♥ is fire and Omega is an easy favourite of mine just because of how he rocks so hard.Stages: this is a tricky area because I don't blame them for being light on the stages, and what stages are in are absolutely great, but there are distinctive absences which hurt the overall experience. People have found evidence that many are planned, and hopefully they will be free updates - be weird to split the user base because of DLC maps - but it is a shame that some key ones are missing. No ice continent stuff for some vital battles, including Super Broly which is odd because from what I gather that is the predominant influence on the art style. No Kame House, no Kami's Lookout, no Space! No ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ space map, what? We can play a Tournament of Destroyers without a map, we can play Otherworld Tournament without a map. Yeah. Probably the biggest area of iffiness, but thankfully it is a modern game and will receive updates (or mods, failing that!).Characters: obviously the roster is amazing but there are obviously holes, and some odd choices. With certain forms, like SSBE Vegeta, it gets fiddly because they technically can't use manga stuff and up to Super (anime) that form doesn't have a whole host of unique attacks (though I kinda wish they had done it this way just so that base blue Vegeta would have an ultimate that doesn't harm him, lel.) There's also stuff that is understandable but still a bit annoying, like Caulifla going straight to SS2, or Trunks (Super) only having SS Rage rather than 1 + 2 + Rage, but I imagine this is a moveset thing and trying to avoid too many of those aforementioned generic attacks (which have always been a criticism of the series, valid or not - some characters really do lack moves, hahah.)Custom Battles: these are great, if silly at times. I can see myself coming back to check in on them regularly just to play a variety of things from the absurd, to cool what-ifs, to recreations of movies or sagas that weren't the focus of the game. Really good, and I'm glad they added it. I definitely used to do my own "in-head" what-ifs when I was playing the older Tenkaichis as a kid, and it's just a proper game mode now, so great!Other thoughts: obviously, the game is not balanced. SS4 Gogeta will plough your fields if you are not ready for him, and in skilled hands he's probably terrifying. But this is, again, Tenkaichi stuff. It's fair to hate it, but it's just how the game is. I do think they need to fix the timer for picking your teams in pvp battles, as 45 seconds is frantic as ♥♥♥♥, so you basically have to know where people are in the rather ♥♥♥♥♥♥ select screen while also knowing who you want from the get-go. I don't think 2 minutes would be too long, especially as you can confirm your team early, anyway. In fact that character select is generally trash, I appreciate what they're going for, but still. Tenkaichi 3's was much better, the nested selection where you'd pick Goku (mid) and then pick his Super Saiyan for instance was much, much better.Final thoughts: I am in love with this game, and I am so glad it exists. I didn't think there would be a Tenkaichi 4, the last was in 2007 for those unfamiliar with the series, I was a mere child. And I never got into Xenoverse, they stripped away the cinematic side and I didn't give a ♥♥♥♥ about a create-a-character because I always want to play my favourites from the series. Already, people are modding this, and I'm sure once proper tools are available people will make some amazing things. (God, someone please make Baby Vegito Black, please God, please.)Anyway, if you like the Tenkaichi games, or want a proper cinematic crazy Dragon Ball game, this is the one. Play Kakarot if you want the full story, but play this is if you want superb in-depth battles with a massive roster of characters and doubtless many, many more to come.

_childDocuments_.review: Rewriting my review after 100%'ing and reaching Z rank: I still think the game is worth $30-$40 dollars at best, so if you can find it heavily discounted then definitely go for it. It's a weird thing; the developers definitely intended for the game to be couch co-op/online battle with your FRIENDS, but for whatever reason included Ranked matchmaking mode and intended it to be the driving factor in keeping consumers playing. I'll explain my reasoning later in this review. I'm a BT 2 and 3 player, I remember having a blast playing on the dinkiest TV with my friends back in the day. "No "I'll send you to the next world with this", it's disrespectful." Oh the days. Sparking Zero brought back that kind of nostalgia, and I am extremely grateful that my buddies and I got to re experience those days through this game.Let me clearly elaborate why I feel like you as a consumer should NOT purchase Sparking Zero at it's current price point or for the time being in general. The developers have made it crystal clear through their actions that they do NOT care about the game or the player base. Not releasing a day 1 patch for a game, or consistent patches for a fighting game is inexcusable behavior. No rage quitting penalties, no casual matchmaking search like ranked search, inactive lobbies not being cancelled after certain inactivity periods, players not getting points for their opponents disconnecting, and general character balance are some glaring issues with this game's online competitive scene. Story mode being a Microsoft powerpoint simulator with battles inserted in-between is lazy and uninspired. Skipping MAJOR plot points for main characters or using powerpoint to illustrate key moments is also pitiful. I'd like to think this game perfectly embodies " Pretty house, no one's home". The actual multiplayer balance of this game is straight up garbage can. For the players saying "BT wasn't meant to ever be balanced" and the devs saying they have no intention of balancing the game as it wasn't their intended vision: Previous entries weren't balanced because gameplay was more manageable at 30 FPS. Countering combos and vanishing was infinitely easier when everything was slowed down due to hardware limitations. There are moments where opponents will cast an ultimate ability and the cut scene won't even end; the 'hit' cut scene immediately initiates, giving you literally zero chance to vanish or block. Even when that exact scenario doesn't occur, sometimes ultimates will literally give you 1 frame to dodge and then the cut scene will start. In previous titles, at least you had a moment to breathe in order to react to what was happening, unless you were hard knock downed. There are multiple ultimates that are either or in game that desperately need their cut scenes shortened. The game is too fast to be making techniques fast AND unblockable, especially online. When we talk about balancing in a fighting game, we are mainly speaking on mechanics working in a manner that is fair and manageable across every player. Nobody is taking SSJ4 gogeta and nerfing his damage until he is built like Krillin. The players who speak against balancing are players who are abusing mechanics in game to cheese their way to victory; I'll die on that hill. These players will ki blast spam you, lag switch you to kill your vanish game and unblockable ult you, and in the same breath tell you "just get around it". I cannot for the life of me figure out WHY the devs decided to put abilities like instant spark, full power charge and afterimage strike on characters that quite simply should not have access to such things. Players being rewarded skill points for getting beat down just encourages these cheesers to choose a character with instant spark. Players will abuse these instant spark mechanics, and then just ki blast spam you until you have no health so they can spam their ultimate.There are multiple fixes for these issues. Make these utilities available for one time use during matches; they already time gate you out of ultimates in single player, it can't be that difficult. Make skill points charge infinitely slower, forcing matches to play out with actual fighting. Bring back ki sickness, time gate utilities, make vanishing cost more ki, make ki blasts do no damage when blocking. There are a number of ways around these issues and the devs simply refuse to do it. You are putting yourself at a major disadvantage which then encourages you to choose these characters to progress in online multiplayer. The devs are mainly at fault for encouraging this behavior which is actively killing the game. On WEEKENDS, the game drops down to 2900 players during the late evenings, and peaks somewhere around 7 or 8k average players daily. It's been out for almost 2 months and there has been what, almost 2 patches? I expect the december patch to be another "network stability" fix and the rage quitting penalties ( I.E. Time out for quitting, you won't get win points for your opponents leaving). The devs come out after a week and nerf YAJIROBI of all things, when all these other issues exist; then go radio silent. They aren't even doing the bare minimum, I fully believe they will kill support for the game sometime by the start of next if they don't consistently put out patches to rework the game.The input delay in this game is absolutely abysmal. It exists offline, and is greatly increased online. You will be infuriated, that's all I have to say about that. The game engine itself cannot handle the speed of the game. Often times you'll find yourself punching your enemy until you continuously move past them still punching. The casual lobby searching is borked and needs to operate exactly how ranked does. You'll find yourself going through all the search parameters just to have to choose a lobby, then when it says "lobby is full" you'll be transported back to the menu to research; EVEN IF the lobby says it has an open slot. There are so many connection errors, dropped matches, dropped lobby searches in this game, if I could go back in time and wait a few weeks before buying I would have saved my money.The actual UI navigation is convoluted and downright bad. Prime example is the store/customization. Why on God's green earth did they separate the actual shop from the customization menu. if you want to buy costumes, you have to purchase them all in the store one by one, exit to the MENU, and reselect the store/custom option and choose "customization" instead. And even that is useless, because once you go online you have to re-apply your costumes AGAIN; they don't auto apply after you do all that. They should have made the customization screen like this: You open up the character select, the costumes, items and accessories are locked where they show up at the bottom of the screen, and you can use zeni to unlock them right there before you apply.This game needed more time in the oven and it didn't get it. The developers got our money and ran off with it. No consistent patches, no addressing blatant broken cheese mechanics, no fixes for connection stability.. We did a disservice by giving them money for something that wasn't finished. I did a disservice by paying them $100 for a game that is worth $30. PLEASE, SAVE YOUR MONEY UNTIL JANUARY AND KEEP AN EYE OUT FOR ANY NEWS ABOUT THE GAME. If you end up seeing a bunch of news about patches for all the things I listed above, and the developers being more interactive with the community then go for it. If you can find the game on sale, go for it. If you just want to relive boxing with your friends like the old days, definitely go for it. If you want a fighting game where you can test your skills against other players, good servers, fair balanced matches, save your money and go buy tekken or something. _childDocuments_.review: I've played more out of rage and got all the way to S5. This game still has the same problems, and I have uninstalled it for good. This game will always be "wow this could have been super great" but never will be.After playing this game for multiple hours playing ranked online, my final review is that I would not recommend this game for multiple reasons and I preface this with playing 200+ fights in solo and got to rank B2. 1. A lot of people are saying this game as lot of depth to the gameplay and I would actually disagree with it significantly. The combos are to easy to pull off, your opponents stun time is so long, and the combos are literally xxy, xy,xxxy, xxx ^y, a, xxxx spam and charge enough to get 3 ki bars while they are falling and you got 2 health bars off. If you think this is a hard combo to pull off, you haven't played many fighting games, this is incredibly easy and simple to master in like 1 to 2 hours of practice mode. Yes people can "super counter" a 4 frame mechanic on an online game with ping problems in half the fights. You can revenge counter. For a fighting game, revenge counter is the worst combo breaker ever made, half the time, the enemy can just tp behind you and keep it going after you lost 2 skill bars or have so many more options than you to keep their attack going. So they need to rebalance revenge counters. 2. The game is intentionally imbalanced which I understand, but give more options for ranked play so I dont just play against the same 4 characters (Broly and some form of Gojeta). Yes people say play DP battle, but there is just another meta there that is another set of 4 characters. It's quicker to list the characters I have played against instead of have not.3. The story is LAZY to say the least. There really isn't much more to the game other than the online gameplay which again got stale really quickly4. I really dont understand the mechanic in a fighting game where you loose "sight" of your opponent and the best way to "refind them" is to literally stand still and try and face them and even though YOU CAN SEE THEM, your character can't. And by the way, most of the time why you can't see them is because they got their ult off on you, which already did 2 bars of health, why are you at the major disadvantage to NOT see them and gives them enough time to either respark, or just spam ki blast since you cant really block them to finish you. 6. The main mechanic of the game sparking mode is just to good. The fact that even if you stop someone from sparking, if they get just 1 super counter off and blast you away, they pulled off an easy spark. You have to be aggressive against them since they are trying to activate an auto sparking and they have to land 1 move to lock you into a frame where they have enough time to pull off sparking and then start pushing you (either ki spam or rush). Since sparking mode last so long, they have 3 chances to get you. And with how much damage everything does this game, If they get once with sparking, they did 50% of your health. Especially if they play characters were it's easy to land (unblockable). So overall, I WANT TO LIKE THIS GAME, but after playing it enough to really understand it, it's a shallow not fun fighting game that I spent 90 bucks on. So I am mad at this purchase and will play FighterZ instead.

_childDocuments_.review: As a longtime fan of Dragon Ball and Tenkaichi 3, Sparking Zero is a blast from the past with a modern twist (disclaimer: I don’t typically write reviews, but I genuinely wanted to write this to help people on the fence with making a purchase).If you grew up with the fast-paced, over-the-top battles of BT3, you’ll feel right at home here as Sparking Zero does a fantastic job of preserving the core mechanics and chaotic energy that made the Tenkaichi series so beloved. The roster is huge, with tons of characters and transformations, just like the old days, and the fights are even more intense and cinematic. The devs did a great job taking what worked previously and improving on it substantially.The controls and combat flow feel snappy, making it easy to jump back into that classic style of play and I love that they implemented the two control options for different play styles. The visuals and animations have been given a beautiful overhaul on the Unreal Engine while still maintaining the nostalgic look and feel of the older games. That said, it’s not without its rough edges. I’m finding the pace of the story mode, so far, to be very fast and newcomers of the series may be lost at certain points. On the technical side, the AI can be a bit unpredictable with difficulty spikes, and the camera isn’t always perfect, especially in tight spots. But if you’re here for the nostalgia and the over-the-top action, these issues are easy to overlook and this is a easy recommendation.Overall, Sparking Zero is a love letter to the Budokai Tenkaichi series, and to Dragon Ball. Again, as a fan of BT3, I couldn’t be happier to see this style of gameplay alive and kicking again in 2024. It’s surreal seeing this game on Steam and I wish Akira Toriyama could’ve lived longer to see this game’s massive success, but I’m satisfied with my purchase and hopefully if you’ve read this far, you will be too.It’s not a perfect experience, but it captures the spirit of what made those games great and to me, this is already the best entry in the series (now if we can just increase the numbers of maps). If you’re looking for epic, fast-paced battles with that classic Tenkaichi flair, Sparking Zero is worth picking up.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the best naturally cinematic games I have played, I say the same about Battlefield 1 but these are very different cases. I think Battlefield 1 creates it's moments using the sheer scale and destruction faced to show you how small you are and how triumphant you feel when you start to rack up kills. Here it feels cinematic in the sense of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ we're both transforming and we're about to clash the ♥♥♥♥ out of each other. I don't think I've played an anime fighter better besides when I emulated BT2 and even then this is so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ cool, I don't think a game has had me more hype as a massive Dragon Ball fan it's good to see they didn't shovel out absolute slop with the mindset of "Dragon Ball fans will eat it up" because this game is very lovingly made.I like this game a lot, I like how the movement feels, how the combat feels, the defensive options at play, it's exceptionally solid and every time I win a ranked singles with Bardock I feel like the legendary super saiyan herself. I love how unbalanced it can feel at times because yeah, Broly and Babadi won't be on the same level will they? of course not, but it genuinely feels good in this game if you're able to outsmart and outplay a higher power level opponent, like Dragon Ball you need not only strength but the technique and inventiveness to think on your feet during battles, reacting to what moves an enemy uses and countering with your own as there are MANY ways to counter play and turn the tables at the drop of a hat. With that being said I do have some grievances and things I wish to see added although I doubt they will because as it is right now missing some things from older BT games it also feels "finished" as in I doubt the developers feel the need to add new content outside of the upcoming DLC.More maps for one, just a little more variety, but with more maps I would like to see a better lock on as, very rarely, but occasionally I have stared at an opponent and had to wait until they noticed me and moved in to attack for them to even register. I would like there to be more customization and costumes besides just destroyed variants, maybe other single player/online modes like in the older BT titles. I don't really know who's OP and who isn't, I've fought 3 cheesers and while I won against each of them they all sucked to play against but I know that'll be a problem regardless of the game and the nerfs so there I have nothing to say really, what shouldn't be a problem is the aforementioned leaving penalties. I think if you leave a match there should be a ban limit on ranked for a while, not sure how long but something to prevent the SSJ4 Gogeta from rage quitting during my combo. What I don't think is coming are free character updates, as much as I would love every few months or so a new character appearing in the shop being unlockable and it's someone like Monaka, Nam, or any of the characters from the Super Dragon Ball Heroes hellscape, I feel like with the large roster as is it will be seen as an excuse to not "bloat" an already massive roster in the hopes of having so many characters will make people not expect minor things to be added like bit characters from Super or OGDB as they already do cover a large portion of Super with some OGDB thrown in there but not a lot. If they do this? I'll be shocked and #happy but @ the same time I also think that doing so would bring about even more outrage from an already wavering playerbase who still argue about who's broken and what's cheese and a character who on launch will be used to find ways to "break" the game would probably put people into a form of soyrage.Despite all of this including the lacking singleplayer modes I think the game is incredibly fun and the only game I've bought at full price where I haven't felt buyers remorse whatsoever as this is maybe the only game to renew my faith in it with every round of play, in short, go buy it if you're a dragon ball fan, one of the best experiences you could ask for.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DRDragon Ball Sparking Zero delivers stunning visuals and exhilarating combat, but it stumbles hard in story mode, feeling rushed and incomplete. If you’re here for PvP and fun online fights, you’ll enjoy it. But if, like me, you value a fleshed-out story mode, you might walk away disappointed.  ---I have mixed feelings about *Dragon Ball Sparking Zero*. On the one hand, the game looks absolutely stunning, and the mechanics are a blast to play around with. The fights are fast-paced and super fun, though the camera can get a bit janky at times, and in certain scenarios, button presses don't always seem to register as they should. Still, it captures that nostalgic Budokai Tenkaichi 3 feeling very well, which is a huge plus for me. And let me just say—PvP is really cool and something I’ve genuinely enjoyed.However, the story mode was a complete letdown. Without spoiling anything, it feels rushed, unfinished, and unloved. The only "What If" scenario that felt somewhat decent to me was Gohan's, but beyond that, it’s just disappointing. I can’t tell if they left content out to sell as DLC later or if the story mode just wasn’t their priority, but either way, it just doesn’t hit right. Much of the story is presented through basic slideshows, kind of like what *Ninja Storm Connections* did, which really takes away from the experience.I know this review might get a lot of hate because Sparking Zero is so well-received, and I can understand why. What the game does well, it really does well. But for someone like me who values a good story mode, especially for the "What If" scenarios, it was a big disappointment. Even Xenoverse 2 did the story better than this, in my opinion.I haven't tried custom battles yet since I’m waiting to see what other players come up with, but I’m definitely looking forward to seeing the community's creations in the coming weeks.So if you're someone who values what I value—mainly a rich story mode—then I wouldn't recommend this game right now. But if you just want a fun Dragon Ball game where you can enjoy online fights, then Sparking Zero will probably be perfect for you.

_childDocuments_.review: ★★★★ - Great  16 hours  Normal  		• The combat mechanics are fast-paced and fluid and flexible, allowing for high-speed aerial battles and powerful energy attacks similar to its predecessors in the 'Dragon ball Budokai Tenkaichi' series.		• The character roster is a standout feature, offering a wide range of characters, their variants and their many transformations (Approx 85 Characters, 182 including the variations).		• The controls are responsive, but the combo system may feel clunky until you've had more time learning the system.		• There are a few difficulty spikes in the episodes, sometimes making battles frustrating rather than challenging.  		• The Goku Episodic Battles story follows a fast-paced retelling of the original Dragon Ball Z and Dragon Ball Super arcs but with a few alternate what-if paths. The other Character Episodic Battles focus on a handful of arcs for each character.		• Episodic Battles skip over smaller story beats to focus on the main ones. But as someone who didn't watch all of Dragon Ball Super, I felt like I got the general gist of the story that played out.		• Custom Battles allows you to create and play other people's custom one-shot campaigns which gives almost unlimited replayability to recreate fights that aren't previewed in the standard episodes or to make fights that are completely different. 		• Dialogue can be hit or miss, sometimes in translation, sometimes repetitive due to repeating key moves but is overall passable.		• There are some fun interactions between less-featured characters, particularly in what-if scenarios, though these moments can be few and far between.  		• The cel-shaded art style and animation does justice to the anime, with explosive energy effects that mirror the show’s iconic moments.		• Character models are well-detailed, though environments can feel bland and repetitive.		• It would have been nice if the retelling cutscenes were also in-game rather than just flash cards however due to scope of the game, I can understand why it was downscaled.  		• When in Episodes, Pause the game and go into Battle details to check the objectives. Alternative Objectives (Only allowed on Normal Difficulty) will send you to what-if scenarios.		• Skill Points (Big Blue number) will let you charge Ki to Sparking! Mode or otherwise use numbered abilities. It is work using these tactically in your fights.		• If the Up Symbol appears on your character, hold up on the D-pad during a battle to give you a menu to transform.		• If the reset Symbol is fully charged, hold left on the D-pad to switch to a different team member. In Episodes, you want to do this where possible to prevent knockout; a single Knockout will cause you to fail mission.		• Pause battle and check Explanation of Controls for buffs and specific character skills.		• Spend time in the Super Training mode to get a keen eye on individual moves, blocking, combos and dodges to get full acquainted with the combat.		• Multiplayer is fun but not beginner-friendly. It’s advisable to brush up on single-player modes before jumping into online matches.		• The game has some balancing issues, so expect certain characters to feel much stronger than others in both PvE and PvP.		• If you haven't spent any money\zeni, completing all of the Goku Episode should give you enough money to buy all purchasable characters.		• When Summoning Super Shenron, you want to purchase Characters or Ability Items. As they cannot be gotten elsewhere.		• Shenron and Namekian\Potunga Shenron Balls can be farmed by playing Offline Battle with the CPU (5% chance per ball). 		• Super Shenron can only be accessed 3-4 times. 1 from completing Goku Campaign, 2 from Future Trunks Normal and Alternative endings respectively and 1 from purchasing the Ultimate Edition.

_childDocuments_.review: As a long-time fan of the Dragon Ball franchise, I grew up playing Dragon Ball Z: Budokai Tenkaichi 3, a game I absolutely adored. It’s hard to believe it’s been 17 years since that iconic title, and I never thought I’d see a sequel. Now, with Dragon Ball: Sparking Zero, we finally have a new installment that, while imperfect, has captured much of the essence of what made the original so special.Let’s address the elephant in the room: the game can feel unbalanced and at times a bit of a chaotic mess. The roster of characters is vast, but this comes at a cost. There are numerous transformations counted as separate characters, which can lead to confusion for people saying " OH WE HAVE 60 GOKUS! Yeah thats the beauty of the game. Additionally, the ranked mode has garnered criticism for being unfair. The amount of rage-quitting I've witnessed is disheartening—players quitting mid-match to avoid losing and subsequently preventing others from ranking up is incredibly frustrating. Yet, despite these issues, I can’t help but appreciate how much I’ve wanted a game that embraces this chaotic spirit. It feels like a worthy successor to Budokai Tenkaichi 3, and I genuinely love it for that.The story mode, however, leaves much to be desired. While it lacks depth and coherence, it shines in its inclusion of numerous "what if" battles. These alternate scenarios provide a refreshing twist on the familiar narrative and are undoubtedly one of the highlights of the game. They keep the experience interesting and allow for creativity in how the story unfolds.One major area where players seem to struggle is in their interaction with the game’s mechanics. There is a robust training mode available, yet many players seem hesitant to utilize it. Learning the intricacies of the combat system can significantly enhance gameplay and improve overall performance. I encourage everyone to take advantage of this feature—mastering the mechanics can make a world of difference.Regarding ranked matches, I believe a punishment system for rage quitting is essential. Implementing penalties for players who bail on matches would help create a fairer and more enjoyable competitive environment.On a more positive note, the custom battles feature is a standout aspect of Dragon Ball: Sparking Zero. It’s fantastic that fans can create and share their own unique battle scenarios, adding a layer of personalization and creativity that enhances the overall experience. This flexibility allows players to engage with the game in ways that resonate with their preferences, making for an even more dynamic gameplay experience.Dragon Ball: Sparking Zero is a game filled with potential and beauty. While it certainly has its flaws, the nostalgia it invokes and the opportunities it presents make it an exciting addition to the franchise. I’m genuinely thrilled about this game, and I can’t wait to see how it evolves. Here’s to hoping the developers continue to refine it and that the community embraces the spirit of Dragon Ball in all its Broken Messy nonsense!

_childDocuments_.review: Awful experience. The CPU on single player are psychic, but aren't actually intelligent. If you sit still at the start of an episode match, they'll spam dash and kick air. If you go in to deal any damage, they'll immediately read your inputs and perfect parry or counter. The only enjoyable way to reliably beat the AI is to spam sparking, spam x and vanish counter their perfect parries. Otherwise, you're in a sparring match with a robot that knows exactly what you're doing exactly when you do it.This is only after you get the game running consistently, which in itself is painful. The game-speed is tied to FPS, at around 40 FPS, everything is in slow motion. EVERYTHING is rendered in 3D. The UI on the main menu is a handful of options (usually one or two) over a 3D modeled, completely rendered and animated background running constantly. If you swap over to the left or right to view the other two options they let you at a time, Goku dashes off and the game renders a completely new scene. This killed my frames, which in-turn slowed the game down. I could hardly even open to options setting to lower my graphics.The general quality of the game is awful too. The sound design especially is so choppy and broken. As an example, during super saiyan blue Goku's ultimate, his kamehameha charges for a split second, then the game goes almost completely silent. The camera breaks constantly, getting stuck in walls or the floor. You can't see characters you're locked on to that are just slightly above you, and you can't move your camera up or down. On the maps with larger structures, like the city map, I also tended to get stuck in the buildings with no way out. There's also a pretty common bug where you get stuck charging ki and can't do anything else. It's like no one play tested this game.The single-player is disappointing. Some of the what-if scenarios are pretty cool, but the way it's portrayed to you is so incredibly lackluster, it's lost. The entire story is presented to you in either short, poorly animated clips or just a slideshow of the exact events of the show that are completely rendered in 3D for some reason, removing all soul even screenshots from the anime or manga might have and also, similar to the main menu, greatly lowering my framerate. It also takes place on the exact same maps. Fight different characters on Earth? Same exact field/canyon. Fight a character on Namek? Same exact spot on Namek in front of Frieza's ship (except for the Frieza-arc's specific destroyed Namek.) It's repetitive. There's an entire roster of 180 characters, but only 7 characters have a story and only 2 of those have any fleshed out alternative paths. Most what-ifs are just a single scene if you beat a boss quickly or don't use a special move.And on the 180 characters, most of them are just air. 100 of them are Goku and Vegeta and the others are so weak and boring, there's no reason to use them unless you're joking with friends. If you do want to joke around online, then the best way to do that is ranked, because the unranked matchmaking is awful. Instead of randomly connecting you to someone else who's trying to play, like ranked does, you have to connect to a room that could have dozens of different players, and wait in line for your turn to play your quick 5 minute match. The other players can't even challenge each other while they wait. It's ridiculous. Playing ranked is just as miserable, though. You aren't allowed to have any fun playing ranked, you're supposed to sweat until you win. Want to play anything lower than 9 DP in single battle? Go ♥♥♥♥ yourself, here's 20 SSJ4 Gogetas in a row. Want to play DP battle so you can make a balanced team of all your favorite characters? Time ran out because it takes years to kill a character with 8 health bars and a heal. Who knew? The combat isn't even enjoyable enough to overlook these things. It seems enticing, but you can't actually combo in this game. You have 2 attacking buttons, and 4 dedicated to blocking and countering and dodging. The entire game feels like a QTE. Vanish counters are the worst example of this. They cost nothing to do, and they can by countered by themselves. If you play against anyone familiar with this mechanic, a good 30% of the match will be spent hitting right bumper at the right time while neither of you take or receive damage. And on top of that, the ACTUAL QTE's, the clashes, go off so quickly you often do them wrong before you even see them. The dash clash is the worst example. The attack button is the same one used to fight clashes. If you dash towards an enemy that also dashes and attack before they can, you've already messed up the clash and are punished for it. I really wanted to like this game, and I spent a long time playing it, but it's not worth it. If you're thinking about buying it, don't. If you already did, refund it.

_childDocuments_.review: Rarely play a game so much during its launch period (43 hours in 8 days and got all Achievements) so decided to write a somewhat lengthy review for once:Roster: Despite me being a weird who thinks Red Ribbon Saga is the best Arc in all of Dragon Ball and thus obviously being disappointed in the rep we get from the first 16 Volumes, which is just pre-23rd Tenkaichi Budokai Goku and some outfits for characters like Yamcha and Roshi, i'm still very impressed with getting such a huge roster at launch, that's genuinely comparable to BT3, a game that had two previous games to build off of. Especially was surprising to see pre Battle of Gods movies and GT having a decent presence, i very much expected them as DLC bait but a Budokai Tenkaichi game isn't complete without SS4 Gogeta so i'm glad we got them in base roster even if i'd personally trade most of movie characters for characters from the earlier sagas.Visuals: Not to much say here tbh, it's based off Shintani's style from DBS Broly which i personally love and they did a great job translating it into 3D imo.Single-Player: Easily some of the most fun i had with a story mode in a DB fighter, really enjoy the CPU actually using the in-game mechanics properly, reminds me a lot of Infinite World's CPUs which i also adored. There are still obvious shortcomings though, the presentation in the canon routes is lackluster, luckily they tend to be much better in the What-If scenarios which are the story highlight here, especially loved Trunks and Gohan's What-If routes, Goku and Frieza also get some very fun ones too. Haven't touched player-made custom battles yet or tried creating them myself but i did enjoy the Bonus Battles the game comes with it, they're pretty short but still fun alternate scenarios.The way you do character unlocks is also nice, you can just outright buy them with Zeni if you don't wanna bother with certain content but unlocks can also be done via story paths or even bonus battles and some via Shenron wishes, and if you used Zeni to unlock a character/costume you get the amount refunded when you do the story or bonus battle that unlocks themMultiplayer: Primarily played online so this will be just focused on that and uhhh... unfortunately its not a good experience rlly. There doesn't seem to much punishing against rage quitters so it's very common, i had my first rage quitter in only 20 battles. There's other issues too like non-existent Anti-Cheat so nothing stopping cheating and the game unfortunately also lacks cross play even though by now it's a standard in AAA fighters. More than that though what probably annoys me the most is this game having the worst Ranked player base i have seen in a fighter, i did 100 matches so far in ranked and could genuinely count on one hand when players did a full set, people always quit after 1-0, 0-1, 1-1, doesn't matter which way it went, it feels extremely rare to get a proper Best of 3 even.At least connections on average felt decent, though when it gets even slightly bad it does feel terrible and you won't be able to do basic mechanics like Z-Counters at all with proper timing.The worst of all though is that atm there is a bug where with Classic Controls you can't use the first Blast 2 at all when facing someone using Standard, really hope it gets fixed soon.Gameplay: Well its Budokai Tenkaichi so expect unbalanced as ♥♥♥♥ over the top combat with occasional camera issues, not much to say, its very much what you'd expect from the series.and Afterimage Strike is hilariously busted this time, Super Vegetto feels almost like a cheat code with it lmao.Unfortunately though the game does have a pretty blatant issue on PC, which is the Shader Stuttering, it's not the worst example of it since the game seems to share effects for a lot of stuff so you can compile them decently fast but it does suck every game/driver update you have to prepare for initial stuttering unless they fix it in one of the patchesRanted a lot during this review so maybe surprising i still recommend it, but i do think its genuinely worth it for the roster and visuals alone, especially if you have someone to play it.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR- Not great for a newcomer- Controls and mechanics poorly explained in tutorial (or not at all in the beginning tutorial)- Not worth 70$If your new and unsure about getting this game, wait for a sale. Especially if your worried about about if you'd like it or not as it does not explain all the controls within the first 2 hours of play and that's about when you'd run of out of time to refund.For a newcomer to the sparking zero/budokai tenkaichi I wouldn't recommend this title. I've always liked Dragon Ball and have always wanted to have a game from the franchise to play like this, so when it came out I was excited to be able to play a game that would have the same flashy fights I love from the series but the new player experience left much to be desired. First off the game throws you into a tutorial which is a good start but it was short-lived as the tutorial itself was short-lived which really surprised me since it looked like the game had so many other different mechanics that weren't shown off which started to confuse me, not to mention how it didn't really explain certain things like how clashes work and whatnot, and so after that you are thrown into the story which made things worse. The first fight with Raditz was not enjoyable as although I just did the tutorial, with how short and vague it was I didn't really know what I was doing, or even what I could do. There were so many mechanics and moves the ai was pulling off that wasn't even in the tutorial which was a bit frustrating for the cool fights I was expecting from this game. Now I'm not saying or expecting to completely be a pro at the game right off the bat, but it would at least be nice to know how to play the game and its mechanics when it just throws me straight into gameplay after the tutorial, not to mention I was starting to have second thoughts about the game because of my experience feeling as if I should be on a time limit of 2 hours as I might just want to refund it. On to the next fight is the Vegeta and Great Ape Vegeta fights, which I heard online people had a lot of problems with, I didn't really mind their difficulty all too much, it was hard but doable. My main gripe was still not knowing how to do things like instant transmission, it never explained how to do that. After those fights I tried searching online for how to replay the tutorial or if there was somethings I missed until I found out that there's a separate area to learn the games mechanics which to me is a flawed system, why not incorporate those mechanics into the tutorial and have the training to practice instead of a short and minor tutorial and then immediately into the gameplay which I do get that yes this game series has long time fans who are the target audience who most likely already know how to play but it is a major oversight for new players. And with discovering the training area i felt more frustrated as it felt like the story fights I've been doing have been a waste of time as I would've rather learned how to play the game before getting into the meat of the game and by that time it near reached the 2 hour mark of me playing the game and I didn't know how to feel as, I didn't feel as I experienced the game enough to get a full read on if I liked it or not, but I also didn't feel like spending a couple dozens of hours to figure that out and not like the game and not be able to refund it because it is 70$ which to me is a bit ridiculous. the visuals look good but its nothing special, and they were a bit better in kakarot and the story is very lacking in terms of quality, not saying that I was expecting anything like kakarot but for 70 dollars? maybe don't make it a slideshow? I understand fighting games take a while to get the hang of and it takes putting time in to improve, but leaving out important mechanics in the tutorial of all things is just bad design. I really want to like this game and have cool flashy online battles with other people online, and improve but to me it does not feel like its worth the investment, or at least right now, and it's not that I can't afford it but there are just so many other games you can get at a fraction of this price and I just didn't feel like gambling on the idea of if i'd like this game in the long run or just having it forever sit in my library -70 dollars for nothing. I'd rather just wait for a sale and feel a little less guilty about buying this game. I know there are people that like the game and I'm happy for them but in my experience its a really hard sell for any newcomer.

_childDocuments_.review: If I could, I'd leave a neutral review, but as someone who hasn't played tenkaichi games in the past and was looking forward to online play, I'm leaning towards NEGATIVE review. And before someone says "it's meant to be unbalanced" "get good" "it's not competitive", the game has "RANKED" game mode. Also I'm fine with characters being stronger than others, however I am not fine with cheese meta ahh gameplay.So here goes:Pros:- Game looks stunning and the graphics/art is true to dragon ball. Ability and character animations for the most part are amazing. Few exceptions can be made, for example Jiren's transformation is scuffed.- Custom battle mode where people create their own scenarios and post it for others to play is quite fun. Although, when creating scenarios, it is a pain to find dialogue you're looking for, due to the fact that nothing is alphabetically sorted :/- Quite big roster, although it is inflated by character variations (like 8 different Goku's, Vegita's, although to be fair each one of them has unique abilities and combos for the most part). However, only 10 or so characters can be seen in online, due to them being meta.Cons:- Promised customization options are extremely limited, although this will probably be fixed in the future via some paid DLC (LOL). - Character select screen and menus are dog water.- If you're looking to play online (not with friends), do not bother. Game is plagued with cheesers who abuse broken meta characters/abilities like Giants unblockable rush attack, Afterimage strike, spammable supers (Roshi's lightning strike), Android 19 and Gero super armour grab, super armour and unblockable ults.- If looking past cheesers, online experience is lacking regardless. Many mechanics are kinda meh, for example: vanish wars which keep repeating until someone runs out of ki over and over again. Some mechanics never get used (e.g. Beam clashes). Also never seen Namek blow up, lol. Super counter is really inconsistent and shouldn't be a thing. Revenge counter should be used instead of Super counter to break out of combos.- Story mode is severely lacking and lackluster. All the story is told via slideshows and text, with occasional low budget cutscene. (I understand that there is DBZ Kakarot available for story exclusively, however it is still disappointing).- "What if's" as a concept in the story mode is great, however I don't think that it was executed well. Often it feels like the choices you make as a part of "What if" scenario doesn't change anything, because there is no explanation as to what conditions must be met following your choice. Basically, it felt really scuffed.- Movement feels limited sometimes, due to dashes costing a lot of KI. You always need to charge (this is a nitpick, just personal opinion).- Good soundtrack music is sold separately as a DLC... Not sure why, it's dumb, considering the game price. Atleast people are honest and bombed the DLC music pack with negative reviews.- Local play split screen limited to one map (hyperbolic time chamber).I hope some of these issues get addressed, however it's highly unlikely.

_childDocuments_.review: After spending over 30 hours with Dragon Ball Sparking Zero, I can confidently say this game delivers one of the most satisfying gameplay experiences I’ve had in a while. While the story mode might not be the game's strongest point it's decent but doesn't quite reach the epic heights you'd expect from a Dragon Ball game the rest of the game more than makes up for it.The gameplay, especially the battles, is a solid 10/10. The controls are smooth, the combat system is dynamic and engaging, and each fight feels like an intense, fast-paced showdown straight out of the anime. Whether it's the flashy combos, the use of ki, or the destructible environments, the game does a fantastic job of making you feel like you're in the middle of a Dragon Ball battle.Even with a story mode that's a bit underwhelming, I find myself coming back for more, purely for the thrill of the combat. If you're a fan of the series or just love action-packed, well-designed fighting games, Dragon Ball Sparking Zero is absolutely worth your time. I’m definitely going to keep playing just for the joy of the battles.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: What are you reading reviews for? Didn't you see the trailer? It's right at the top of the page. Click "Add to Cart" and join the fun!If you enjoyed the deep combat of the Budokai Tenkaichi games then this is gonna be one you wanna check out. It even has the option to use the OG control scheme. The game has a lot to offer. After about 20 hours I've barely made a dent in the main campaign because of how dense the game is. Just like the original Tenkaichi games there is a learning curve, so if you're looking for a pick-up-and-play experience, you might find the game frustrating. If you enjoy learning and getting good at a well designed and responsive fighting system then this is gonna be your jam. At default difficulty it is going to be more challenging than other titles like DBZ: Kakarot and Xenoverse, but that only makes it more rewarding when you finally do learn how to play.For returning veterans of Tenkaichi games this is gonna be an amazing, mind-blowing, experience. The combo chains are different from the older games, but that's not a bad thing in this case. The spectacle blows the game outta the water, and you can feel the genuine passion radiating from the game. It's very clear that everyone on the design team had a genuine passion for the game. Now if you'll excuse me, I gotta get back to the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Not much could be said that you probably havent heard. Its a modern Budokai Tenkaichi with Dragonball Super characters. The single player story is serviceable with new and fun what if splits from the cannon story, it doesnt have as much content as Xenoverse or as strong a retelling as Kakarot but as a showcase of the gameplay through the lense of the story it does more than enough to justify playing it through to the end. The main and most important component is the gameplay and the online features which are both fantastic. the gameplay is exactly what I believe most BT players were hoping for, its the same deceptively simple yet surprisingly in depth gameplay from the previous games but sped up and streamlined in a way that makes it feel as fast as most other 3d arena fighters in the genre like Naruto Storm. Its a no-brainer for fans of the older games in the franchise and I believe for most anyone who loves Kakarot or Xenoverse or any 3D arena fighter outside of Dragonball would love this game too. Only thing I feel its missing is co-op gameplay and a stronger singleplayer experience to come back to when you want a break from the online
