_childDocuments_.review: That is the best way I can write this. I can't say I have done everything yet: I have done all the Bonus missions in the game gives you and I've done Episodes that are applicable up the start of the Android saga to include  . I have beat every pre-built tournament setting once, dived into the training mode, and mostly have been screwing around without buying anything crazy out of the shop. So below is sort of the fresh review I can give after having not played a game like these since Raging Blast 2 (About 10 years for me)The game controls good and is quite a bit more fast paced than I am used to. That being said the controls are responsive to the random Xbox controller I was using (Though I do know some who plays Mouse and Keyboard and he enjoys it as well.) A small gripe I have and a piece of advice:  I have been seeing people online getting a little frustrated with a few missions in Episode story and the Customs I mentioned doing before. Having learned a few of the things from there (And maybe a little bit of patience and not throwing my head at a brick wall) it would have gone a lot better. I particularly enjoy the skill counter so that way if you need a counter-option, a buff, a transformation, or the new Sparking Mode, you can use it but you can't just pop into it all the time. Ki is relegated to a resource that is fairly limited and won't rise so quickly unless you are an Android or you use items to raise it. Inorganic lifeforms such as Androids cannot naturally charge key for blasts/dashes/super/etc so it's good to be aware of that.The game is beautiful, and I run a fairly old laptop as I travel a lot so sitting with a rig has been difficult. Even on this I have yet to have a crash at almost 15 hours of play. (A bit of an oxymoron with not being able to sit, I've had a lot of time away of work these past couple of days so I decided to get this.) The visuals are great - and the only things visually that bug me are slight nit-picks. Sometimes the camera freaks out a little when you dash - it can be a littler crazy on the senses if you are just dashing through obstacles but visually the game is . It's the craziest of modern graphics but the game oozes style that you don't need to have stupid crazy parts to run.The content available is a good chunk, and items can be unlocked through play or in the shop. I heard that some things in the shop are unavailable until you reach certain levels like SSJ4 Gogeta but Idk the exact validity of it. There's a big roster and when I am not messing around in modes that restrict to a certain character I've been playing around with Bardock just like the good ol' days. I haven't felt it get grindy at all during this time and considering more content is planning on being added I'm pretty excited for this game. In the shops you can buy Characters, Outfits, BGM, Items for you to use, Items for how the CPU behaves, even little customization stuff for your player card but even then you can get so much out of just playing. Money doesn't feel like an issue here.The bad? Like I said only a few nitpicky things. I don't want to share them because it's really just tiny things you'd have to look for and I don't want to throw that bias in your head. If you played the old games and like them, you'll love this  I don't typically rate on a number scale but I will here to show the magnitude of what I feel. I will repeat it is a love letter to fans of the old games, great for casual play and just really having a fun time with a flashy roster of characters.

_childDocuments_.review: Go ahead, laugh at my hour-in refund. I guess at 28 I'm growing out of my ability to keep up with the newer fighting games of this younger generation. I cannot follow the ADHD levels of reaction time needed and complexity of inputs; everything is timed, and a lot of the bundled buttons make zero sense to where I can't keep up with the story A.I. Looks great, sure, love the roster and stoked to see who else gets released and added to it. But, I cannot play this game, it's like fusing together input complexity similar to Street Fighter and Tekken, just 3D and Dragon Ball themed with awful button mapping.Dashing, boosts, and steps should be their own damn button, vanish follow-ups should just be the desired attack button and direction instead of requiring ANOTHER button to teleport. Blocking and defensive vanishing was fine, no qualms there. All of these counters should be a simpler input paired with the damn block button, not scattered across the controller.Maybe I'm too hard-wired to expect Raging Blast 2 or Xenoverse style simplicity, but it is what it is. Buy this game if you want to tear your hair out to play a complex Dragon Ball game and play for hours just learning. Also, my first time recommendation is to lower the story difficulty for the first run. Great Ape Vegeta is a damn menace, and has the mechanic of hyper armor that Bandai loved in the Budokai Tenkaichi series, which pushed me away from those games then, same as now.Good luck, praise to you who can actually keep up, and farewell!

_childDocuments_.review: This is a review exclusively for Sparking Zero multiplayer online. Offline mode and the rest are a 9/10. Since I only saw just positive reviews, I wanted to point out some issues for the worst part of the game, the ranked matches: - PD points are a very cool balance idea that gets ruined by those low PD characters with afterimage strike (vegito has that too) or armor like the androids (like dr gero) and this means that if you manage to do something and prove you are better, you are still not gonna win cause your opponent would have so many characters in his team that can escape easily or give you a hard time so you would still lose to the time limit;- so many players play fusions or very hard-to-counter characters that just win alone;- yajirobei is the best character in the game (and this alone says a lot);- too much tp abusing (even if you parry them, they can still tp and this ruins the gameplay quite a bit);- the blue energy with numbers (idk how is that called) grows so easily, making it impossible to play the game against afterimage strike or max power abilities (ultra istinct goku maxed his power 3/4 times in a row in a single match, making me play against spark all the time);- so many bugs, specially for classic controls;- unblockable ultimates (I still have to figure why it should be a thing in a fighting game but ok);- meta slaves people in a game that should have been fun for everyone (this is what happens when a game has a too big community unfortunately).This is my review for online ranked Sparking Zero gameplay. Final vote 3/10 TERRIBLE experience. Do I still enjoy playing? Yes, of course, offline mode is good, I can play with friends and I also play solitary matches online (a bit more balanced in my opinion but still trash). Someone has to talk about these problems and not just making positive reviews randomly in my opinion. I mean, I know we all waited years for this moment, but don't just ignore the problems just because of that.

_childDocuments_.review: The Budokai Tenkaichi games were some of my absolute favorite games during my adolescence; needless to say I was very excited about their revival with Dragon Ball: Sparking! ZERO. The combat system is outstanding with several layers to it and techniques to master, the graphics look amazing and each fight is exciting, not to mention the incredibly diverse roster of fighters. It's a slog to get through it all, with constant cuts and narrative structure that makes no sense (if you are not familiar with Dragon Ball's story, you will be lost), as well as cringy dialogue and over-exposition. But despite everything, it has some cool what-if scenarios and challenging fights that will test your abilities.

_childDocuments_.review: I hate that Steam makes me choose because this really is a thumbs sideways situation.When it's working well, it does a fantastic job replicating the unique insanity of Dragon Ball fights, and it's got an absolute ton of fanservice.  The truly bonkers roster, big story modes, scenario editor, all the love that went into the encyclopedia; this is a game with a lot of .But it's frustrating in all the ways it comes up short on .  It does a poor job teaching its mechanics, and even once you do get a grasp on them, controls can sometimes feel inconsistent or unresponsive (especially notable around character swaps), which isn't the greatest in a fighter.  And that's not to get into weird gameplay glitches like clipping out of the map, the AI bugging out and giving up, or online issues like controls suddenly changing to other styles (Though theoretically many of these can be addressed in the future)The animations and camera work can be fantastic for super attacks, but then story animations freeze up completely or the camera gets stuck in weird places in combat and that sucks.  That huge story with all the branching what-ifs sometimes impresses, but also sometimes skips things entirely while spending far too long on other beats.  The soundtrack is... fine, but as far as fighting game soundtracks go, really forgettable.Above all else, everyone is so tied to the core combat mechanics that it feels hard to find meaningful variety.  It's like Street Fighter if  character was a Shoto - sure, there  differences between Ryu and Ken and Akuma and Dan, but that's really the only playstyle you'll get, and that feels like a huge missed potential.I do enjoy the game, hell I kinda recommend it even if you're not a super huge DBZ fan, but I  in good faith recommend it at the full asking price.

It's really nice to experience the story of the manga/anime, especially with gameplay this good. The What-If's aren't just some one fight stories like I was worried about, they're thought out, and at some point have better writing than Super did. That's honestly my only gripe besides for some reason when I load into some online fights, I'm charging ki, I can fix this by holding R2/charge ki, and pausing. Fixable, but a little annoying. The game feels so clean, the animations are beautiful, this is the perfect sequel to Tenkachi 3, and I'm so excited to see more characters with the upcoming DLCs. Side note: The voice actors kill it, but Cell's VA is just flat out perfect, love my green beetle man. First time I've paid over 60 dollars for a game, and I don't regret it, I'd do it again. _childDocuments_.review: Sparking Zero is a game that feels like a warm embrace from an old friend. It's a neoclassical gem that seamlessly blends the nostalgia of the original Dragon Ball games with modern gameplay mechanics. The graphics are a visual treat, capturing the essence of the classic anime with stunning detail and vibrant colors.The gameplay is nothing short of exhilarating. Each match is a tense, nerve-wracking battle where every move counts. The characters feel incredibly responsive and powerful, allowing for fluid combos and devastating attacks. It's a game that rewards skill and strategy, but also leaves room for a bit of luck and intuition.What truly sets Sparking Zero apart is its ability to evoke a sense of familiarity while still feeling fresh and exciting. The characters are instantly recognizable, but they feel more alive and dynamic than ever before. The story is a love letter to the original Dragon Ball series (pretty short but consistant), filled with heartfelt moments and epic battles.In short, Sparking Zero is a must-play for any fan of the Dragon Ball franchise. It's a game that captures the spirit of the classic titles while offering a modern gameplay experience that is both challenging and rewarding.

_childDocuments_.review: To start off, I have to give credit to the game for how well it was developed and designed. It is too pretty, and maintains a similar design to that of Dragon Ball, with quick movement, environments that glow with beauty, making one feel like they're in the heat of the moment. Well-Known CharactersThe Character Models are well made and recognized as wellShowing The Unique features from Each FighterWhich Adds on to the Overall Experience as the Unique CharacterBut, as well made as it is, I think the game just hits a wall at a certain point. Though the mechanics are fun to begin with, they can end up feeling a little repetitive, and its story may not prove to be as deep and satisfying as some experienced veterans of the series may hope for. The combat system is fun, but it also quickly falls into predictable patterns where you can understand who is going to achieve victory. This can sap the excitement from combat once the novelty wears thin.In summary I think the game has a lot of potential, but it also has a lot of just straight bad. Longer, expanded storylines or more diverse gameplay mechanics could add replay value to keep players engaged. Secondly, introducing a wider range of different missions or side quests could help replace the monotony and enhance the experience.Overall, Dragon Ball Sparking Zero is a visually creative, technically sound title but one that its core concept lacked of depth and breadth. It is a fun time if you care about the series and I hope we get something a little less predictable next update or series of updates.

_childDocuments_.review: Dragon Ball: Sparking! ZERO is an excellent Dragonball game and worth every penny. is the game unbalanced? Yes.Is the game fun? YES!!I do agree Broly spammers are the scum of the earth but the thing that makes this game fun is the unbalanced fights and scenarios you can play out, the feeling you get when you outplay an Ultra Instinct Goku as Future Trunks is second to none. Mechanically the game is simple on the surface but mastering all the counter mechanics and sub movesets is where the game gets interesting, getting into a vanish or counter battle feels similar to hitting a perfect deflect streak on Sekiro. The campaign is good, the cutscenes are lackluster but the AI is fun to fight. Netcode is solid as well, anytime I lose I know it's usually from lack of skill and never feels like a lag issue. I highly recommend this game to any fan of Dragonball, 3D fighters, and to any fans of badass cataclysmic anime fights. 9/10 "Two Saiyan Thumbs Up!"

_childDocuments_.review: I really like this game, and I think it has potential!! I ,like many others, am a huge fan of it's predecessors. Tenkaichi 3 is still one of my favorite games ever made, and I think they did a decent job recapturing what made that game great. However, the game definitely has some warts, and numerous flaws. I think, if balanced correctly, it could be a highly competitive, and a viable game for tournaments and ranked play. It desperately needs to be balanced, and tweaked in several key ways though!!! There are a coupke characters that need some work as well. There are a handful of them that are blatantly and ridiculously overpowered, and the players who know how to use this handful of fighters have a massive advantage over the entire roster from the very start. These fighters need to be nerfed!!! Off the top of my head I know Z Broly, Android 19/20, Metal Cooler, and SS4 Gogeta need nerfs. Adjusting the counters would balance some of them so I would start with that, but they still need to work on this roster. I mentioned counters, and the priority/big fix should be the 5 counters. I think I have a way to balance all of them pretty easily. Super Counters are OP, mainly because it doesn't cost anything to preform them! Also, they cost some ki, but pretty much all of the vanishing moves are kinda broken.  However, if you 2X the ki cost of Vanishing, and make super counters cost 1-2 skill stocks, that would make the whole game play in a much more fair way. Also ki blast in general are an issue when facing certain characters. Which is why I would DECREASE the cost of revenge counters from two skill stocks to one, so that ki blasts can be countered more effectively, and the ki cost for them should be 2x as well. Implementing those changes as well as some other tweaks could make this game what it should be. The only other big thing I can think of at the moment is customization. To be frank I was offended when I saw the options for customization in this game🤣🤣 It is laughably pathetic!! Especially when you consider the options that you had in the predecessors to this game. I think that it can be fixed though and this game can be great just a couple of tweaks, and I think we could get there!! Solid 7 out of 10 game that could easily be an 8 and 1/2 maybe a 9 out of 10 if balanced correctly.

_childDocuments_.review: First let me say that I do not care for the online scene. I bought this game for the nostalgia and the hope to see interesting "what-if" scenarios that could lead into the Super timeline. If you are like me, honestly there are probably mods in Xenoverse that will give you that. The story mode and the branching arcs from the main timeline are so boring and not nearly as interesting as being the only thing of note to play if you are not trying to win online matches. From what I can tell, the want to give the community the ability to craft their own scenarios has hampered many instances of any creativity the "what-if" situations could have had as the story telling format of the scenes and goals for each fight makes it so that the game is just never engaging on how to get an alternate path. For about 90% of the alternate goals, it is just "beat this person/people quickly". There is not an ingame timer for any of these situations so it is either a guessing game if the condition has been met until the match is over and they deliver their dialogue. Another large negative to the story is the limited amount of battles for each of the characters. As an example, for Vegeta's story, you start on Namek, disallowing any changes from the fighting on Earth, Gohan starts in the Hyperbolic Time Chamber during the Cell Arc, and for some reason, the amount of fights per saga are very small skipping some fights, such as the Z-Figthers vs. Cell Jrs, most of the Ginyu Force fights, and many other tiny fights that help with pacing of the story and fights that allow for stuff other then the main encounters.I am hopeful that this is just a modern day game that will actually be decent to play through with updates and DLC that covers for most of the missing peices, but only because I have already purchased the game. Other then that, wait for discounts later down the road as right now, if you are here for some cool fan creations for fun what if stories, this is not the game.

_childDocuments_.review: As a major Budokai Tenkaichi 3 fan (as well as the fan-made Budokai Tenkaichi 4) I love this game. It met my expectations and has been a blast to play both the singleplayer campaigns and online with friends.There are some changes from BT3 that I dislike as of now and will take some getting used to, for example the super rush attacks miss *a lot* in this game vs in BT3 where they're a guaranteed hit unless blocked or dodged. This just means you have to set up for these attacks more now than you did previously, which to some might be a positive, but it just makes them feel a bit wimpy. Another is if you win a melee clash, your energy still drains, and that can often leave you winded and extremely vulnerable, which just doesn't feel right, and it seems like investing into that clash *less* than your opponent can be better (which is counter-intuitive). Also, what is so critically missing are the fine-tune controls for AI difficulty in battles (where you pick your character and your opponent and fight). You are basically choosing between dumb and dumber levels of AI, which is not how the AI feels in the singleplayer campaigns at all. It would be really nice if they could update the battles mode to include controls for the AI to bring them up to the same difficulty the campaigns have, otherwise players are going to get bored really quick. I did an AI vs AI battle of Beerus vs Whis, and it took about 10 minutes of them just being passive and bad at fighting to complete the match (on "super" difficulty, the highest), which is a huge contrast between some of the fights in the campaign (the concluding mission to Jiren's campaign is *insanely* difficult, and I want to be able to crank the AI up to this level with levels in between). You can't even do this in custom battles despite there being a completely different difficulty meter for the AI, which is confusing, and even cranking that up to the highest value (20) doesn't come close to some of the campaign battles. Let us enjoy the AI at it's fullest potential!Outside of those few shortcomings, this game is a blast and is leagues better than any 3D Dragon Ball fighting game since BT3. It feels like a game of that same era and I highly recommend it to anyone who is a fan of Dragon Ball.

_childDocuments_.review: I love dragon ball. I love fighting games. I originally came here after around 2000 cumulative hours in Dragon Ball FighterZ. A lot of people are dissing this game because of the AI and the story mode, but that is hardly the issue, and can easily be chalked up to skill issue, but what I don't see in these reviews is someone actually discussing how bad the gameplay mechanics actually are from a fighting game standpoint, let alone an enjoyable gameplay standpoint. I will change my review when they actually fix these issues i'm listing, but I'm sorry to say that I don't recommend this game because the gameplay mechanics are genuinely terribly designed and here's why:Certain characters are broken: Yajirobe is a good example. He does decent damage, and can heal back to full an infinite amount of times and it only takes him 2 seconds total to do so. Of course, he needs skill meter to do so, but in a game where you're constantly dishing damage and getting damage done to you, the skill meter charges insanely fast, and Yajirobe can just heal to full after every knockback/knockdown. The icing on the cake is that it only costs 2 DP to run Yajirobe, so you can pair him with an OP character like Gogeta SSJ4 and cheese the entire game. You may argue this is also a skill issue, but with how dumb the defensive mechanics are in this game, it's so easy to get at least one knockdown/knockback and heal to full. A lot of characters also have unblockable supers that you can't even block/dodge or react to, so people will just TP behind you and spam unblockables that almost one-shot your character.Ranked is unbalanced. The DP system is an attempt at making a balanced ranked system in a tenkaichi game, but does not work because of how much characters can heal while tagged out. There is no concept of 'blue' health or 'temp' health like from FighterZ, which limits how you can heal. So if someone were to run Gogeta SSJ4 and Yajirobe, they can easily just tag Gogeta out and swap to yajirobe, spam sensu beans for a couple of minutes, and bring Gogeta back out to full health. This is the basis for almost the entirety of higher level ranked games. Too many defensive mechanics, and they need to be heavily nerfed: To list from the top of my head, there's 5 main defensive mechanics. Guard, Perception, Revenge Counter, Super Counter, and High Speed Evasion (TP). This isn't even considering defensive skills like explosive wave or afterimage that some characters have which gives you a get out of jail free card essentially. Super Counter is the most OP one because it can be done at any point in anyone's combo, regardless of whether or not the opponent is hitting you from behind. It isn't hard to spam Left stick up + attack button to hit it as well. You will get a full reversal for free, and in high level gameplay, you will never get in a full 'combo'. The most annoying thing i've been dealing with in higher level gameplay is infinite TP encounters, where your opponent will TP, and then you will TP their TP in a nonstop cycle until one person runs out of ki. It's genuinely boring gameplay and is terribly designed. It's funny at first, but once you end up in 20 TP cycles it gets old really fast, and is genuinely frustrating to deal with. Perception is also an inherently flawed mechanic, because you can HOLD block, and react with perception while still holding block. That means you can SIMULTANEOUSLY block and perception at the SAME TIME. The only answer is side step or grab but you can just SUPER COUNTER to get out of the combo that you should be punished with. NOTHING IS TRUE IN THIS GAME. The only thing that is TRUE in this game is that your opponent will counter you, and you will counter your opponent. You are never safe, and it's for all the wrong reasons. This game genuinely punishes you for making the right decisions and it's trash. The guard mechanic doesn't work very well too, as I find myself holding block fairly often, and guard tends to be unresponsive, specially during supers that you could normally block. The controls in general for this game are jank. Combos aren't real and this game punishes you for them. In high level gameplay, opening your opponent up in this game is near impossible due to the amount of defense mechanics in this game, and if you just so happen to get one combo off, it doesn't matter because they can super counter or revenge counter out of your combo. It's BORING. The entire gameplay loop of high level gameplay in SPARKING ZERO is guard, chip, counter, trade, guard, chip, counter, trade.Knockbacks lasting more than 2-3 seconds is not real in this game. This means that if your opponent knows how to tech out of a specific knockdown or knockback, then you cannot follow up with a super. It isn't real. Last time I remember, in fighting games, a knockback should allow the player to get a special ability/super off but nah, not in this game. Nothing is real Ki system is flawed. In high level gameplay, you're not charging, the enemy is not charging. Ki blast beats most character's charges, so what we end up doing is spamming ki blast whenever a player charges. That means that neither player is building ki, and both players are spending ki to prevent players from gaining it. The main issue here is that 'combos' (if you're lucky to get one off and dont get super countered in it) do NOT build enough meter. The only way to get supers off is if your opponent is in a vegetative state and lets you charge, or if you have an ability like high tension that lets you instantly build meter. That means that characters that build instant meter immediately outclass those who cannot. It's boring and stupid. Stun lock mechanics. As I mentioned before, in high level gameplay, nobody is letting you charge up. This means a lot of the time, you're going to have around under 1 bar of ki, and if you just so happen to block a heavy smash or a super and it breaks your guard, you will be stun locked for around 20 seconds. This is enough time for your opponent to charge all the way into sparking and one shot you. It's genuinely stupid, and I don't understand why it lasts so long. You can chalk this up to skill issue & bad ki management, but just consider that one sonic sway (frame 1 perception) removes about 1-1.5 bars of ki. Sparking Mode. Sparking mode is awful. Some characters have abilities that instantly put them in sparking mode, some characters are forced to charge in order to get into it, which we've already discussed is almost impossible to do in high level gameplay. Additionally, sparking mode provides far too much damage for its semi-infinite 'combos', which can only be beaten by super counter or revenge counter (but is still hard to do for the former). Additionally, a lot of players in ranked abuse the movement mechanics in sparking mode to immediately TP/dash behind you and spam unblockable supers that almost one-shot you. It's not fun gameplay, and there is hardly an answer to beat it if the opponent does it right. Best example is Base Super goku, who has an instant transmission  and an unblockable spirit bomb you that will one shot youThe camera is awful. In this game, you can only adjust your camera to the left or right while  you're focused on your target. This means that you can not look up/down, additionally meaning that if you opponent fast flies up/down, your camera will break like crazy, and you won't be able to see your opponent. Additionally, there's some odd bug in this game that causes your camera to break and lose your opponent when they're right in front of you. This happens a lot during beam supers that you've blocked, as well as when the opponent instant transmissions in front of you. in certain cases, it can also happen during after image, and is genuinely annoying to fix, as sometimes even when you're staring directly at your opponent, your camera does not actually "see" them and lock back onto them. It's RNG af and is a game breaking issue.

_childDocuments_.review: The gameplay becomes too repetitive, with barely any distinction between enemies—there are no unique ways to approach or strategize combat against them. Every character's fighting style, whether hero or villain, essentially boils down to the same abilities: powering up, ki blasts, flight, and basic punching and kicking.This IP likely won’t survive much longer because it doesn’t appeal to modern audiences. The portrayal of female characters leans too heavily on stereotypes, making them appear weaker, which feels somewhat gender-biased. They should stop producing this type of repetitive content. It’s best to wait for a significant price drop, as it’s not worth the full price.This game should have received at least a 19+ rating from the ESRB, as it frequently uses language like "kill you," and treats resurrection casually, as if it’s taken for granted. Gore scenes, like Goku getting his belly pierced without any censoring, are somewhat alarming. Violence aside, it sets a bad example for kids, as achieving "super saiyan" physiques is unrealistic without steroids or illegal substances.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wish there was a middle option to the reviews because I really didn't dislike this game, I just feel that it lacks just about any level of customization that you see in other fighting games even of the same series.  Most characters don't have an alternate skin or even just recolors.  Instead of bloating the character roster with three different Base form and Super Saiyan Goku's and Vegeta's they could have opted to make the moves interchangeable like the Raging Blast games or even Naruto Ultimate Ninja Storm series.  Instead there are a few outfits that change moves on a character, such as Android 18 using Destructo Disk, or the Paid Goku Power-pole outfit.  Accessories also feel like they were just slashed at a late stage, why does every character show multiple accessory slots in the menu, just for scouter characters to be able to take them off, and halos for Goku, Vegeta, and Gogeta?  The game looks good, and returns to the series form, but that form fell out for a reason: People like at least a little balance in a fighting game. After you see all the moves and complete the story there's just the online PvP and nobody plays anything but ranked and abandons before it affects their rank.  If you didn't buy it already I would wait for a considerable sale and then enjoy the game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is insane. I went in pretty much blind aside from a few frames of a trailer. If you grew up on Budokai Tenkaichi this is that and more. It's beautiful. It's insane.I genuinely suggest any dragon ball fan get this game. It's HARD, it has DEPTH to its combat, and the storyline is not JUST cutting up the original story into pictures and dialogue, there's new animations, there's some fun alternate perspectives, there's even some non-canon alternate endings (the rewarding ones with depth require a lot of willpower but are so freaking cool!)Genuinely, if you like dragonball, if you like NUNS, Xenoverse, any type of arena fighter, you're going to love this game. If you haven't touched any of these or you're hesitant, there's the ability to play at a reduced difficulty to learn (I'm insane and didn't do this despite this being the first time I've ever played a Budokai-like game) and there's plenty of training informations and demos to help you learn how to play the game.Again, it's HARD, it's ANNOYING, but it's so WORTH it. When you beat a difficult fight you feel incredible. The game feels so good to play, and I'm so excited for the future.I hope this continues to get so much more love and attention from the devs and fans. It'd be amazing if it was the successor to Xenoverse 2 finally.The only main con I have, minus some minor issues with the budokai style that are inherent in the basics of the game, is that when you're doing training mode it's not terribly intuitive to swap through each specific lesson and sub lessons, it requires a lot of down time between menus and pressing an obnoxious button combo, aside from that, the difficulty is refreshing, the roster is INSANE, and the amount of love in this game is clear.Here's hoping to a bright future for Sparking Zero!

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, the game is fun if you like casual online PvP with scrambles and Dragon Ball in general; in that sense the game does deliver. But, if you were a seasoned player at any previous tenkaichi game (not raging blast) and you are looking to test your skills then this game is not for you and here's why (opinion might be biased considering I only played for 99 min):-The games looks too messy for how fast paced it is-Online connectivity is decent enough, but there's not much room for finesse-There's too much visual noise that doesn't allow you to see what's going on (particularly when charging and trying to see what your opponent does at the same time since your aura covers your opponent)-There's an inconsistency with some attacks that do not connect just cause (some rushes, specials that track, and vanishes that hit your opponent after you send them far away)-Some new game mechanics have that quality that DB Fighterz had where you can only counter them a certain way and one way only-All the characters feel much more like the "same character" than in previous tenkaichi games. The main thing that differs is how much damage they do-The game focuses a lot in reaching/using sparking mode, which makes it less flexible as a fighting gameI'm not saying don't buy it (I will refund since I did not like it and don't feel like getting better at a game I did not enjoy), but if you are looking for Tenkaichi 4, this is not it. This is clearly Sparking Zero (which feels more like a 3D arena Fighetrz)

_childDocuments_.review: Sparking Zero is an amazing successor to the original Budokai Tenkaichi trilogy and improves on it in every way, from graphics to gameplay. The new mechanics add depth to the combat while still maintaining a low entry level and high skill ceiling. If I were to complain about anything, it would be the map restriction for local multiplayer, rush attacks having poor tracking, and the lack of crossplay. Rush attacks now have to be used as a combo finisher for a guaranteed hit and will most likely not hit if done raw. The lack of crossplay is certainly upsetting, but the dev team has been very cooperative and have listened to fan feedback, so I have no doubt it will be added eventually. The map restriction can be fixed with a mod that I'm sure will be made available, but it is still unfortunate that you have to resort to mods to fix this issue. Overall Sparking Zero is still amazingly fun and the best 3D arena fighter probably ever.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is like a dream come true. Countless hours that we spent on Budokai Tenkaichi games seamlessly transfer to the way this game works and even though it has been more than a decade since I last played those games, this game feels natural to play and almost as if no time has passed since BT3 . If you haven't played the original series, the game might require some effort to learn due to a lot of it being sort of complicated. But I assume that going through the tutorial and battle training mode should get you up to speed and ready to play in no time. While it is not exactly a pure fighting game (at least, not in the traditional sense of the genre), this game is one of the best anime battle games that I have played. If you played the original series on PS2 then I doubt that there any reason for you to not immediately love everything about this game (except for FPS limit which I am really hoping they address after the early access period is over) and I would say that it is worth getting at full price. The presentation and graphics are top notch and the fighting feels fluid (for the most part but there are some stuttering issues and FPS is limited to 60). If you remember the story mode of BT games, the story mode here is pretty much the exact same thing but far more elaborate now with more branching narratives and what if scenarios which are fun. And while I prefer online modes in most fighting games, this is a really fun mode and you can spend hours into it especially considering that this covers everything up until the recent anime seasons (I don't watch anime so I don't know a whole lot about how much content that adds but it should be pretty substantial). In terms of online, I haven't gotten much experience here because it seems to take a while to get a game (probably because of my connection not being optimal for playing with other players who aren't in the same region). _childDocuments_.review: Can't recommend in the current state. The game desperately needs a significant update to improve stability, QOL, and input windows. It feels very inconsistent. Pros1) the game looks great. There's a lot of glitches as the maps load in, but the action itself is smooth and the animations are very satisfying. The art style was executed perfectlyCons1) there are two control schemes: classic and standard. There are significant advantages to using the Standard control scheme such as being able to trigger blocks and counters more effectively. If you're a classic player, you're going to find yourself at a disadvantage to players using standard controls. Very odd decision for a game that leans into being a casual fighter. The learning curve to switch from one to another is really tough as well. Not sure why they couldn't add an option to map your own controls. 2) Many controls are unresponsive both in single player and multiplayer. In single player, I don't think there's a problem with the game receiving inputs; rather that the input windows are too narrow. For comparison, the input windows for certain key counter commands is dramatically tighter than even From Soft games.Online is a different story. Lots of input lag, lots of failed connections, and no penalization for players dropping randomly. The poor connection quality creates input lag so you have to relearn all the timing for commands. It's very frustrating to finally tighten your counters only to get trashed online because the windows are different due to input lag. It's just not satisfying. You never feel like you're gaining mastery of the control set. Instead, it feels random and all about luck. The windows need to be adjusted immediately in a patch to make them more forgiving. 3) The story mode is not well executed. There are limited narratives, only a hand-full of what-if scenarios that are difficult to unlock because the criteria that must be met are not clear. Additionally, you have to play on the highest difficulty to unlock them. Why? For a casual game, I feel gate keeping the what if stories behind some arbitrary difficulty floor is not user friendly.  The difficulty also spikes randomly from battle to battle. For Goku the infamous Ape Vegeta battle might be the most difficult and must be cheesed to get beyond, but the Jiren fights are easy. Some narratives - like Gohan's - feel very rushed. You get one or two matches as child Gohan and are then thrust into the adult episodes. In sum it's only 5 or 6 fights. It's not like there's an absence of characters to setup canon fights for Teen Gohan: Garlic Jr, maybe Goku fights in the Time Chamber, etc. Very disappointing. Other characters suffer from this downside too. There are no fights from the movies, yet almost all of the movie characters are included in the base game. Why?4) There is almost no customization for characters. Only one character has an outfit that affects their move set. All other outfits are cosmetic, and most of them are recycled. Some variations are so subtle it's actually hard to tell what the difference is between the stock and unlocked outfit. There are only four accessories in the game, and they are only accessible by certain characters. 5) The game has a lot of characters but many of them feel the same because the move sets are essentially the same. There are multiple reskinned versions of the spirit bomb across several characters which makes them feel interchangeable.

_childDocuments_.review: I do NOT recommend this game in it's current state. BUYER BEWARE! MANY PLAYERS ARE UNABLE TO PLAY ONLINE!The "Communication Error" problem is preventing many players from being able to complete matches online, OR to even play  online AT ALL. It affects players on PC AND PlayStation, and seems to be caused by a large variety of things (including, but not limited to, BIOS version, windows version, windows update build, slightly older hardware, and others. The known causes are NOT consistent from player to player). Known fixes for the issue  include a long list of things, none of which work consistently for anyone. SOME people have managed to fix the issue on their own, however most are still screwed. The issue generally causes players to disconnect from a match the instant character intros complete (the moment the match begins), OR at some point mid-match.90% of the reason I even bought this game in the first place, was to play online with ONE person specifically, an IRL friend of mine. Together, he and I have put HUNDREDS of hours into Xenoverse 2, during which time we spent about 98% of our time doing nothing but fighting each other. For months we were both super hyped to do the same thing here.Although I have NO difficulty playing online with other people, my friend on the other hand cannot play at all. I personally do not care to play against random people online; it is toxic. Players consistently pick the meta characters and meta strategies, leading to boring, repetitive, and frustrating gameplay. I WANT to play against my friend, but cannot.The Dev team has offered only the barest MINIMUM of communication on the issue; only to acknowledge the issue, and nothing else. No timeline on a fix. No information on the issue. And any emails sent to support only get you a copy paste response essentially saying "we're sorry, we know its frustrating, your issue has been sent to the relevant team". Here on steam, in the discussion forums, there is a thread with over 1000 comments now, discussing this issue. But the devs refuse to pin the thread (overwhelmingly more comments than any of the other threads), or even acknowledge it.As of this writing it has been one month since release, and many players are still afflicted with this issue. And there are a LOT of them. Despite that, however, there seems to be very little acknowledgement of its existence online, or in the streamer community.This is also the same issue that essentially killed one of their previous titles, "Jump Force". It was never fixed, and the game was eventually de-listed from steam.The single player mode was fun, but lacks enough content to make my purchase worthwhile. I honestly would have paid $20 for that by itself.The UI is functional, but a chore to navigate.Gameplay wise the game is plenty fun. But since I cannot do the ONE thing I actually bought it for, I consider this game, in its current, broken state, a scam. IF this issue gets fixed, I will update my review.

_childDocuments_.review: I just want to say that I do like this game, it's really fun to go through the story and also extremely enjoyable to play PvP with friends, but the reason I can't recommend it is because there are a few very major issues that I think at least some of them need to be ironed out first.For the story missions, the game being hard is in no way a deterrent, in fact I love it; as frustrating as it can be, it's still really fun, and you can lower the difficulty if you want to. However a setting to skip the extremely long ultimate technique animations, or shorten them would be pretty nice if you're playing for hours at a time, because it just leads to the game suddenly stopping for 5 to 10 seconds in the middle of a fight. Another thing that needs to be possible is the ability to restart a mission as soon as you lose, not after watching the loss cut scene every single time. Furthermore, if you want to get an alternate win condition, you have to then wait for the cut scene, pause, quite back to the mission select and go back to the previous mission. It is absolutely insipid and I hate it.Another huge thing is how slow the menu system is, because every single transition has to have an animated cut scene, so it takes an annoying amount of time just to do anything.PvP in this game is literally the most insufferable thing ever. I can only recommend playing this with your friends so you can actually mess around and have fun with different characters. If you play online you will only see the absolute meta characters and very likely you'll be outmatched if you planned on having fun.For the fighting mechanics, I really like it, similar to Xenoverse 2 but with some more depth, but, and this is a big one. If you and the person you are fighting are actually somewhat good, this game is so lame. You'll both perfect counter or vanish back-to-back for seconds at a time, like two people with poor connection trying to backstab each other in Dark Souls III. I am literally begging, if nothing else, please add a limit to the amount of times this can happen. The Xenoverse 2 stamina system was literally perfect, do that again.Also personal gripe, I hate the way you lose sight of an enemy as if you lack object permanence, and must battle with the strongest of all enemies, the camera controls.If literally any of these things get fixed I will change my review to be positive.Or add 4 other Mr Satan's to the roster.

_childDocuments_.review: The best thing I can say about Sparking zero is that it looks nice. A lot of this game just looks great. The models look like a great adaptation from the Anime/Manga, the textures and colours pop especially on an OLED screen. Effects like the Supers or Ultimates look drop dead gorgeous with the lighting engine. Plus the roster is gigantic, with a lot of familiar faces, and some first timers for a Console/PC 3D Dragon Ball game.That's sadly where my like for this game ends... Sparking zero sufferers from style over sustain a lot of the time. Or in the worse cases, suffers from total consumer/player dissonance. The first major issue for Sparking zero is menu navigation, its the first thing you will encounter when playing the game after all. To go from the episode select menu, you have to press the right bumper on your controller of choice, watch an 3 second animation play, THEN, watch another 2 second animation as it transitions to the menu. You can-of course, spam the bumper and force it to move to the next menu quicker. Though the characters on screen will t-pose, or the camera will get a little buggy. Oh and of course your controls will get locked up for a micro second. I get , they did it, it looks nice and is unique. But using it feels not great, especially when you just want to quickly get to the store or something, and you've wasted seconds of your limited time on this mortal coil fighting a computer game menu.Once you win against the main menu selection and get into the story mode, you face even . You don't get one big story mode where you play as several characters throughout. You get to play specific characters like Goku, a little known background character you probably haven't heard of, in specific mission that are specific to them. Sounds great right? Kinda like how Budokai did it.You select the character, hit continue, and watch ANOTHER animation play out as your character rocks off to the sphere of 240 GIFs. Oh... and this is . You can skip it by choosing to go to that characters mission road map. And this road map is how you replay missions and view the clear conditions for certain missions. Good on paper right?.... Right? Well bad news for you ya goober, you want to replay the first mission when you are at the end of the road map? You have to scroll  This is more insanely worse when you have a character like Goku, who has alot of missions to play through so you're scrolling past mission after mission, past some Goku can't even play cause it's not for him. Or... OR. You press one of the bumpers, and you get a submenu of a mini road map condensed to JUST that characters missions.... You look at the screen and scream in a tongue you know not of "Hey, why wasn't this just the road map to begin with.". Till finally, finally, you get to the mission you want to replay, and look to see what the other clear condition is... Until your godless eyes gaze upon the devils best friend. "Defeat X/Y/X" and his partner in crime "???"That's right bucko, you have no conception of what the clear condition for a mission is until you either stumble upon it, or roleplay Cole Phelps and deduce it. That's... if you're lucky. There are certain what if mission that have such vague and absurd clear conditions to clear, that you would have no idea that they were even in the game. "Beat X/Y/Z in a certain amount of time", what amount of time? Yes!That then ties into the next glaring problem. The AI has dementia, and really should be taken to a home.The AI flops between the easiest pushovers on the schoolyard, to representations of fear and dread themselves. Sometimes the AI will stand completely still and stare at you, begging for you to end their life, or their laying on the ground not getting up wishing to return to dirt. To it's extreme twin brother, where the AI learns the concept of Where they will perform a 60 hit combo within 5 seconds, and you're stuck there, cause the breakout/vanish counter has decided it's not coming into work today. Oh, OH! When you are the one with the slick combo, suddenly Mr counter is back and is coming to collect names, cause the AI will counter vanish perfectly while you're fumbling to do the same. Though most apparent, is when you launch an ultimate that misses, and the AI decides its earned a vacation on the other side of the map as it super boosts into the invisible wall for 20 seconds.That's not even getting into how sometimes the skills will... just not work. The controls are slightly autistic, where you might of move onto hold down the trigger to trigger an ultimate or something, but it's still 10 paces back into convo talking about its special interest of ki blasts. Congrats, you've actually managed to trigger you skill and... it either misses point blank, or you speed past the other character and look like a muppet, hand up your crack and all. Super  inconsistent.The only other points I have against this game are kinda minor so I'll speed past them for your sanity and mine.- The shop where you buy your characters and alt costumes for said characters is fine, but I want to throttle the neck of Bulma who will not shut up while you are just browsing.- Some characters costumes are lacking/are missing outright, someone like Vegeta will have his Broly movie and Whis armour, but not his classic Z/Super one. Or someone like Jiren who's full power form has him shirtless, but it's not a costume for his base form, even though it was in the Anime.- Character forms being weird or wrong. Vegeta's Blue Evo isn't technically a form you can use, it's a power up that you can use, but sometimes you wouldn't even notice that he's in Blue evo, or that he has, which is annoying since Goku gets both UI-s and UI but you can't pair that up with Vegeta Blue evo outright. Future Super Trunks has Rage, BUT, has the wrong hair, the correct hair is on the boxart of the game, making it even more confusing why they've made this weird fusion of his SS2 and Rage.Overall (Yes, I'm wrapping this up don't worry)Sparking Zero, on paper, is a good game. But is brought all the way down by bad execution, and ideas that don't even sound that good when said aloud. It feels like this game was made in a lab, by people who THINK they know what the general consumer wants, but got so lost within their own wants. I don't dislike this game, far from it. I want to like it, but for every good thing I like about the game, I get ambushed in a back alley by jank or bad design.6/10, is the best I can give it. Good, but needs refined at the fundamental level. I wish I could give it a meh or a in-between rating on Steam, so I can only go negative.Oh, and to try and charge me almost 30 buckazoids for actually good music when I paid almost 100 smackers for the Ultimate edition is so not ok, not ok, you hear? Have the balls to slap me in the face next time.

_childDocuments_.review: Pre ordered this game the day pre orders were available because I am a huge Dragonball fan. Unfortunately it has some glaring and unacceptable issues that will keep its review negative forever for me.First, it is 2024 and I'm playing a PC game at 16:9 60hz locked on my 3440x1440 165hz monitor. At the very least, I was shocked to see good HDR support. Bandai has a habit of being stubborn with resolution and frame rate. Whatever old fart is in charge of making that decision, I hope they realize how stupid they are. This fact alone makes me feel cheated out of my money as I play on a very expensive setup and I should be able to leverage the power of that setup rather than have artificial black bars on my screen that were put there in post. Also, playing at 60 fps locked really sucks because when you encounter a scene that requires more power to render, your GPU is left playing catch up and you drop frames. At 60 fps locked, this sometimes means you drop to 30 and feels like garbage. If the game was allowed to run at say, 120, you would barely notice if the game dropped to 90 for a second to render a harder scene.Second, the story being told via index cards with text on them and very little animation was very tacky and some key animations from the story were omitted, such as Goku's first Super Saiyan transformation vs. Frieza. Based on my username, you could infer that I'm not happy with this as it's my favorite moment in the series.Third, frequently the cutscenes appear pixelated, almost as if they are loading in slowly while I'm watching them. Sometimes this goes away with time, sometimes it doesnt, and sometimes they aren't pixelated. It isn't my hardware because I'm on a very high end rig.Overall, it really sucks that such a great game is near perfection yet so far away due to neanderthal decision making by bandai. If you argue that ultrawide support doesn't matter because it's a small portion of gamers, you're clearly not that bright because the SUPPORT IS ALREADY IN ALL BANDAI'S GAMES. THEY PUT BLACK BARS ON IN POST BECAUSE THEY HAVE CANCER. Forced 16:9 60 fps gaming is unacceptable, but even more unacceptable when you're going out of your way to force it on people. I'm not sure why the Japanese are so obsessed with 16:9 60 fps, but they need to get the ♥♥♥♥ over it.

_childDocuments_.review: Cant recommend. It's not what I wanted out of a Tenkaichi game. Wanted a nostalgic arcade fighting game that I could casually play and just have fun rewatching old stories and new whatifs. The difficulty ended up being very wonky, where some enemies just stand there and let you beat on them, even ones that should be "stonger", but then there are enemies that are supposed to be "weaker" that just start perfect inputing and taking half your HP away in a few seconds.  In addition to all of that, while not a dealbreaker, the menus are terrible—all of them. Navigating the main menu is clunky and terrible, taking noticeable amount of time for animations to play to move from one screen to the next. In addition to there not being a consistent way to move through said menus, hit A or hold A, hit B or hold B. Navigating the episodes for arcs and characters is equally terrible. Since you are forced to play a single character rather than play arc to arc, you play sporadic fights, skipping most of the arc and then jumping to the next fight. Which is fine for certain characters and their arcs, but even then it can still be sporadic. Then actually navigating the menu to select the fights is bad; the "pretty" visual style to select a fight where it shows the arena you will fight on is clunky. Navigating and playing fights that are whatifs isn't better. There are unskipable cutscenes, so if you fail to meet the whatif requirement, it forces you to the next available story fight in the arc rather than letting you retry, so you have to go all the way back out to character select then back in navigating slow menus and unskippable cutscenes. There is more that is disappointing and frustrating, but these are the major sources of frustration. If you think these won't bother you, you should be fine, but it just kept taking me out of the moment having to deal with all of it.Edit: Learned that there is effectively no progression, it doesn't affect episodes at all. Which means there is just inherently very inconsistent difficulty for the story missions. Also it turns out that the CPU difficulty in story episodes are the hardest CPU's in the game. The battle CPU even on the highest difficulty is considerably weaker than the CPU in episodes. The story CPU can and will perfect chain combos on you while input reading and performing multiple perfectly timed inputs in a row. Which the hardest battle CPU gets none of that.

_childDocuments_.review: Dragon Ball Sparking Zero is a visually stunning and ambitious arena fighting game, serving as the long-awaited sequel to Budokai Tenkaichi 3, and it certainly delivers on fan expectations in many areas. With an impressive roster of 182 characters, the game offers a vast array of playable options that span the entire Dragon Ball universe, including "what if" scenarios and episodic battles that offer exciting alternate timelines for beloved characters. The depth and variety of modes—ranging from world tournament battles to custom battles that allow players to create and submit their own matchups—make this title one of the most replayable Dragon Ball games to date.One standout feature is the custom battle mode, which adds immense longevity to the game. The ability for users to design, upload, and share battles within the community creates a continuous stream of content that encourages creativity and competition. From fighting iconic series battles to completely new fan-created scenarios, it’s a Dragon Ball fan’s dream.However, while the single-player and offline modes shine, the game faces a significant issue in its online multiplayer functionality. Many players have reported struggles connecting to online matches due to connection issues. The frustration only grows when discovering that, according to Bandai Namco support, players may need to manually configure port forwarding to resolve communication problems, as seen in this Steam community discussion: In a time where seamless multiplayer experiences using NAT traversal and automatic UPnP configuration are common, this outdated requirement feels like a major step backward.Bottom Line:For fans of the Dragon Ball franchise who value offline play or are willing to tackle potential networking challenges, Dragon Ball Sparking Zero is a must-buy. The character variety and endless replayability make it a fantastic entry into the series. However, if online multiplayer is a priority, it may be worth waiting to see if future patches address the connection issues. Until then, the game’s technical shortcomings in multiplayer may be a dealbreaker for some.

Unless they win if you have beaten them they will inevitably 100% of the time rage quit it's honestly amazing my playtime in the game has diminished and diminished with each online session I do it's honestly beyond pathetic how everyone in S Rank and above just rage quits, I do not care about how unbalanced online is, it's fun.Giants are wonky lil guys who destroy anyone who is not stronk enough to break super armor? Funni.Yaji full heals on 5 skill counts which he can get in one single vanish exchange? Funni.Androids grab heals and steals ki and removes sparking? HILARIOUSAfterimage Strike gives you 15 secs of near immortality? PEAK CINEMA (And the main reason i see rage quitters, if you spam ki blasts when they activate their 15 secs of auto vanish attacks they get angry)All of that is fun, the game is unbalanced in a way where everyone is unbalanced tbh that makes it kinda balanced tbh.Giants? They fold to anyone beyond the power of a SSJ3 Goku, breaking their super armor with 1 hit and being so much faster than them makes em into a waste of DPYaji? Either don't engage in vanish exchanges or just, shoot a ki blast if he tries to heal, play safe so he doesn't throw you away or knocks you down and keep pressure so he has no time.Androids? Don't get grabbed bro.Afterimage Strike? Spam ki blasts, the ones who abuse it love it fr fr.The problem is, as I hope i've showcased, not the balance of the game, it's the fact that people will lose and then rage quit in the last second, it's honestly amazing how bad this is, if not for the rage quitters i would unironically be many ranks up if not a whole rank. _childDocuments_.review: This game is probably my biggest disappointment in gaming. I was really hyped to finally play this game but after playing it for about 3 weeks, I just couldn't take it anymore. The game has way too many problems to be playable. Most of the problems I find with this game probably wont even be fixed in the future. Here's all the problems I find with Sparking Zero :First of all, the lack of PvE content. Sure, the game's main focus is not the PvE. It relies much more on the PvP to maintain its lifetime. But still, it's just.. way too poor. The episode mode and custom battle modes are great. They allow us to enjoy the story with some plot twists that could lead up to entire story being changed. Goku surviving to Raditz and preventing the death of most of the Z squad from perishing against Vegeta and Nappa but also unlocking Super Saiyan against Vegeta after he killed Krillin was insane. And there are several sparking episodes (the what ifs) like this in the game. However, there's still a few problems like Vegeta's story line ending at Buu's Saga. Like.. what the ♥♥♥♥ ? But anyways, that's not the thing I want to point out, there's nothing wrong with these game modes. The main critique about PvE is the lack of extra game modes. In the previous BT games, there was a bunch of game modes to play which really made PvE enjoyable. But here.. well.. you've got arena and PvCOM ... but that's it. Which means that if you want more PvE content, you'll have to stick to Custom battle which is not a bad mode once again but you can quickly get bored.But my problems with PvE is the smallest issue here. The biggest one and probably the one where most of people will agree with me is clearly the PvP. Precisely online battles. At first i thought the game was going to be really fun online and maybe I could stick with to go as high as I can just to get a fancy letter next to my name and be proud of my ranking. But oh boy was I ignorant. The PvP in this game is probably one of the most infuriating PvP I ever played. PEOPLE.SPAM.CHEESE. At first, it's fine. From D5 to like.. B3 you'll have a pretty good time but once you've decided to go up in the rank, the real ♥♥♥♥ show begins. 80% of your online matches are going to be against a MUI Goku, SSJ4 Gogeta, Super Vegito, Jiren full power of pretty much any other strong ass character lore wise (Broly, Beerus, Whis..). And these guys.. oh boy.. These guys, they are so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ frustrating to fight.Even if you clearly have an advantage over your ennemy in terms of skill but also health, a single mistake will make you lose the match. If you let your opponent just breathe for about 2 seconds, they'll pop a sparking mode out of their ass, rush and make a combo. Of course, you'll start panicking and try to do a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ FRAME PERFECT COUNTER but you might fail and once they're done with their melee combo, they'll pop their UNBLOCKABLE ultimates and remove 2 of your health bars instantly. If we count their braindead combo before, you'll end up losing 3 bars which means that you are clearly dead.On top of this instant spark ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, these characters usually does a ♥♥♥♥ ton of damage melee wise and they have some crazy skills that either does 13000 damages or allows you to dodge any melee attacks for 15 WHOLE ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ SECONDS. Let's not forget that the devs had the brilliant idea to make thousands of ways to break out of your combo which includes the frame perfect ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ I talked about earlier and so, you end up playing a fight game where you simply can't combo and you have to deal with cheese strats that clearly requires the IQ of an oyster to pull and make it work.So yeah, sure, unbalanced mess is fun... when it's offline or with some buddies where you know that you'll have fun with. But outside from that, the PvP in this game is just unhealthy.And it's not like we can hope for some updates to fix these issues, Bandai is completely silent when it comes to talking about these issues and they completely ignore the community which is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ dumb because during the whole development of the game, they were really opened to feedbacks in order to fix issues fans had with the game and it was great. But now, it's dead silent. They fixed a problem which makes you unable to play classic controls correctly online and it took them 2 weeks to finally fix it. So I heavily doubt they will ever fix the issues concerning the balance and stats. The only one who got this treatment was Yajirobe. Even if it's a great change, lots of other problems are still here.I clearly don't want to hate this game. Just like a lot of Dragon Ball fans, I've been waiting for ages to finally play it and.. I can't say I get out of this experience positively. At first, it was enjoyable but my enjoyment for the game burnt out pretty quickly.So yeah, if you want to play this game with your friends and planned to spend hours beating each other in an arena dbz game, go for it. I heavily recommend this game when it comes to casual fun. But if you are more of a single player like me who prefers playing online and ranked, I simply can't recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: I really love the game and want it to thrive, Let me be clear that I do like it. the amount of defensive options are nice but a tad overwhelming at first, but I welcome some complexity in a simple(r) fighting format. I have no interest in competitive and so limiting local multiplayer to play EXCLUSIVELY on the white void of a map that is the Hyperbolic Time Chamber with a game that already has significantly LESS MAPS while also having MORE SOURCE MATERIAL than previous iterations makes me worried about the future of this game. I'm sorry that the current state of the gaming industry leaves me suspicious, but if they fixed the nonsensical exclusivity of maps during local, I'd trust and recommend this game more.local multiplayer shouldn't be restricted to the one map when the entire nostalgic foundation that made this sell game so successfully is THE LOCAL MULTIPLAYER!The Hyperbolic Time Chamber is literally a blank white void. It is no secret that players in any sort of fighting game in the broadest sense DO NOT ENJOY LOOKING AT TRAINING STAGES!!!Blank white room or boring blank grid doesn't make a difference, it sucks even worse to be forced into one map option, FOR WHY??? (please someone actually give me a reason, I can't think of one besides "oh in lore its a training room to prepare for the real fight!" I DO NOT CARE THIS SUCKS, IN A GAME WHERE THE STORY IS WHAT IF AND WHAT COULD HAVE HAPPEN WHY RESTRICT A PLAYERS FANTASY MATCH UP WITH HOMIES TO THE BLANK NOTHING MAP??? I know modern games push for online but this feels disrespectful, limiting player options in this fashion feels like the companies involved shot themselves in the foot and will act confused when players complain about this eventually.Make the easy fix and then I change my review, won't trust or recommend this game until then OR they truly do something so marvelous and mind blowing that makes me trust a corporation but that would need a real miracle.HOLD GAMES WE LOVE TO A HIGHER STANDARD, I BEG YOU ALL!

_childDocuments_.review: Having only played Sparking Meteor (bt3) and no other dragon ball games, Sparking Zero went above and beyond all my expectations.My only major complaint is the character select screen. In lobbies you only get 45 seconds to make a team, and you have to watch a 5 second animation every time you select a character, so with a 4 character team you really only get about 20 seconds to find all your characters. And because each transformation is its own character, you have to try and search through a list of over 180, which is virtually impossible. Each time you select a character the sort option is reset as well which makes it even more difficult.Minor complaint would be the music DLC that should've been included with the ultimate edition, major scam right there.The story mode also feels like it was originally supposed to be 1 map and was split up at some point, which leaves a bunch of dead nodes in the path and makes it hard to traverse. No GT in the story is also a bit disappointing.Anyone complaining about the slideshows are spoiled and should go back and play meteor to better appreciate how blessed we actually are.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:- The story is pretty good- Alternative paths develop in the right way- Combat and mechanics are fast paced, player ability is recommened at higher level- Some fights have a decent level of difficulty- Goku's story mode is huge and entertainingCons:- What If paths have very inconsistent conditions- Customization is none existent in story mode. Previous versions of Budokai Tenkaichi endorsed this for more varied gamepley- Customization is only relevant in Battle mode. Offline or Online, which really defeats the purpose of looking for stuff- The shop is genuinly badly constructed. By the third battle in Goku's Story mode, you pretty much unlock everything there and once you farm the Zeni, the shop is just a useless option in the menu- Dragon Ball wishes are fixed, you can only make a few relevant wish (1 more characters, and about 6 items) and everything else are titles or Zeni. Doesn't really encourage anyone to look for them- Sparkling Mode is just a spam option for dealing with AI- AI is very inconsistent, sometimes they can deal with every single attack and counter you, others they are just a punching bag. And I'm talking about the same level, not really in story progression- Some What Ifs path conditions are busted like: completely obliterate NPC in 40 seconds (it's a real challenge)- Aside from Goku's story mode, everyone elses is short and have arcs in which they do not appear or have 1 battle at most. Pretty boring arcs to be honest- GT character as well as Broly in roster, no story whatsoever which involves them. Fill in characters at mostFor the above reasons, this game is a 5.5/10 or 6/10 at most. Would not recommend unless on a 40% sale

_childDocuments_.review: There are a few issues with this game. There are plenty of performance drops on the story mode cutscenes which sucks as they're just basically powerpoints. I've tried the story mode out for different characters but unfortunately, every fight is the same. There's no noticeable difference when playing or fighting different characters  AI movements and combos are just the same, and beating them is essentially the same: go sparking, get behind them for a 20x combo, and activate ultimate. Attempting to fight differently really just ends up punishing you for not looking to defeat the AI asap.Storyline promises "What if" plotlines which are achieved through vague, undefined additional objectives like "beat xyz quickly" but no real definition of "quickly." Every "What if" only deviates from cannon slightly, and ultimately returns to it in order to progress the story further. I'd assume the online is probably more varied, but I don't think paying $70 for a multi-player game is worth it. Really feel ripped off considering the high price of this game, I feel like it would've been better to wait for it to go on sale for $30 in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: If you want to... relive the DBZ and part of DBS experience in a somewhat abridged format, broken into sections, from multiple different view points, with alternate story arcs, this game delivers on that in a really nice manner.I have never been very good at fighting games, but the combat is generally pretty fun. However what I do find frustrating is the bugginess of the combat. I've had multiple, upon multiple instances, of being in sparking mode, rapidly pressing X until I knock the opponent down. I will then try to use the ultimate attack and I start punching air instead of using the ultimate. Extremely frustrating, ya know? So let's say that's enough for you to just narrowly miss the timer for the alternate ending and the mission you're on is a timer. Wouldn't it be nice to be able to press start so you can back out to the main menu or show a retry feature? Sorry, you must wait till the programmers have deemed it necessary until you can use that feature. ALT+F4 is slower, so you're forced to wait. Ah, I know, I will hold in X to skip the cutscenes to make this annoying process faster! Ooooh, sorry, that too is buggy and sometimes it just won't work even though it is available (but it's not always available through the cutscenes).I can deal with bugginess, and I can deal with bad menus, but I can't deal with both in large doses. This becomes a real travesty when you consider the fun potential the story mode missions have for existing Dragonball fans.. On the other hand, once you understand how to get to most alternate story arcs is simply by "getting good and going fast", they all become trivial as long as the game decides to not get buggy on you.It's 2024 and developers still insist on ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ menu design and usability. We should be past this point.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was a colossal disappointment, mostly because of the lackluster story mode.  Too much focus on variety of characters, too little focus on substance.  Half of it is told through legitimate PowerPoint slides.  Story is VERY summarized - so much so that by summarizing they fundamentally change the story and its not very entertaining, very "on-the-rails", and only the core moments are true to the actual canon.  While it's nice to play as someone other than Goku (and in an interesting 1st person POV mode), the game falls short of so many expectations.  For example, Goku Black has his own story mode and while he is only present in one arc, I beat it in less than 30 minutes.  Goku's story mode took maybe 8 hours, but much of that is cutscene and PowerPoint slides.The Good:1. TON of characters, graphics feel smooth and clean2. You can play story mode in 1st person, which is so cool - story characters other than Goku are playable!3. Alternate scenarios in story mode provide cool "what-if?" scenarios to play out toThe Bad:  1.  Story mode is easy & shortly summarized rather than a true re-telling and half of game told through PowerPoint slides2.  Big META to the game, if you learn how to get behind your opponent you will win3.  Online ranked matches are XP based, so if you start to lose, get ready to lose more

_childDocuments_.review: It's imperfect, it's hugely unbalanced, the AI is broken (and sometimes flat-out cheats in What-if episodes), Episode battles has a very repetitive nature and the camera can be nauseating.The combat has a surprising amount of depth and variety, there's an incredible amount of customization, the animations and effects are superb and custom battles and tournaments offer fantastic variety, be it online or offline.It might miss a few things that BT3 had (more maps, loading screen minigames...) but all these things, including its negatives is exactly the reason why people are praising this game. It doesn't need to be perfect, it doesn't need to be meta, it just needs to be Dragon Ball. It's a gift to Dragon Ball and BT fans. If you never touched a DB game before or don't bother with DB at all, it's very hard to recommend Sparking! ZERO, it's going to be a 6/10 at max. If you are a DB fan or enjoyed any of the BT installments, Sparking ZERO! is an easy 9/10 or more. A love letter to fans and to the great Akira Toriyama.

name: Serious Sam: Siberian Mayhem
detailed_description: Welcome back to the world of Serious Sam in 'Siberian Mayhem' - a new standalone chapter in the adventures of 'Serious' Sam Stone. Make your way through the vast Russian landscapes on a quest to catch up with the traitorous General Brand, who remains one step ahead of Sam at every turn. The road is long, and there is oh so much to see. Co-developed by Timelock Studio and Croteam, 'Serious Sam: Siberian Mayhem' presents an expanded look at a familiar journey full of forgotten stories, unexplored places, and Sam's trademark guns-blazing battles against Mental's Horde. Join the fight, comrade! WELCOME TO SIBERIA ...the heart of Russia. This place is huge, cold, and so unpredictable even the alien invaders feel lost. Travel through five new levels set in a beautiful and dangerous world, from Arctic coastlines and desolate forests to abandoned villages and a chilling ghost town. Siberia is large enough for you to fight & explore for as much as you want. BEASTS OF THE APOCALYPSE Only the strongest souls survive in Siberia, and Mental knows it well. A new set of dangerous foes and bosses join the Horde in 'Siberian Mayhem'. Including some of the most advanced and intimidating creatures you never expected to see. TEMPERED STEEL There's only one thing that stands between Serious Sam and his enemies - a gun. Treat yourself with a deadly arsenal of new weapons, from the legendary AK to experimental 'Perun' crossbow, and more! Do you want to cause death from above or become one with 50 tons of first-class firepower? New gadgets and vehicles are locked, loaded, and ready to fulfill your most destructive dreams. AT HOME AMONG STRANGERS When you think the journey is over and there are no more stories to tell, the universe gives you a second chance. Meet a gang of new outcasts and unexpected characters who will help Sam on his journey to Tunguska. Complete side-missions in order to uncover new chronicles these wild places uphold. And pay attention to your surroundings - the world itself can tell you something you never expected to hear. SIBERIAN MYSTERIES The lands of Siberia are huge, desolate, and full of secrets. Useful, silly, weird, familiar... you name it. Can you find them all?
