_childDocuments_.review: Oh well... I will start this by saying, i did enjoy it but it's really short. Yes, i am aware it's just a stand-alone expansion, but still feels like there was so much more potential to it, potential that wasn't put into play.With some side missions and ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ around on the map i finished it in like 4 hours.If you're not a fan of the series or have some sort of attachment to the SS games, you might want wait for a discount on it.As an 'average winter enjoyer', i really loved the scenery, and i really wish the game had a photo mode, guess i will have to settle with some modding to take some captures from the game.Perun Crossbow is very powerful and satisfying to play with, it was probably my favorite weapon to play the game with (and finish it.. in like.. 4 hours...)The maps are big enough to strafe as much as your heart pleases, and fighting is awesome.Graphics seem slightly improved compared to SS4, BUT, the optimization is not very good.I like the idea of involving 'Tunguska' in the context of an alien invasion, because, in real life, there was a big explosion there in 1908, which sparked some interesting theories, even X-Files made an episode about it.What i am not happy about is that, in Serious Sam 4, there were huge problems with playing the game using DX12 (you'd get lots of annoying visual glitches), i was getting excited that maybe they fixed it in Siberian Mayhem (because trust me, there is a huge difference), but instead, they removed DX12 totally.They also added difficulty and multiplayer achievements again (Again with the ♥♥♥♥-measuring contests!)Cutscenes are too... cutty. Let me rephrase, in many cases there's no transition during dialogues, they're just cut suddenly, feels very amateurish.I'd say the game is good, but i expected some more, and it left me craving for more Sam.Am i happy or disappointed? Yes.
_childDocuments_.name: Serious Sam: Siberian Mayhem

_childDocuments_.review: Serious Sam 4 is great.  I will stand by that opinion.  Siberian Mayhem is more of the same, but even better.  It has snappier pacing, a far FAR better mech segment (one of the most fun mech levels in any FPS I've played honestly), a cooler sniper rifle, Roadside Picnic references, and a level that is basically Highway 17: Serious Sam Edition.  No, the performance hasn't been fixed, unfortunately, and if you really deeply hated SS4 this probably won't convince you otherwise.  But if like me you enjoyed SS4 a whole lot for what it was and want an expansion that takes the best elements and makes them better, definitely pick up Siberian Mayhem.
_childDocuments_.name: Serious Sam: Siberian Mayhem

_childDocuments_.review: The game has all the problems of Serious Sam 4, from performance to the absurd amount of overpowered things that make any balance impossible. Five levels isn't enough either, but now with survival missions and access to the workshop, lack of content should no longer be a problem.The level design, especially of the first two levels, has a quality level above Serious Sam 4. The first two levels are very interesting, they have varied situations and battles that remind you of the classic Serious Sam in the way they flow.The third level is more about exploration, as if it were a small "open world". I'm not a fan of this approach but it works well.The fourth and fifth levels are the more modern style where you use your overpowered tools to hold line against a bunch of enemies. In my opinion, this is the worst type of level Serious Sam has to offer and unfortunately it's the theme of the last two levels. Still, they aren't bad, they're just more on the braindead side of the action, but they're still fun with good moments.For fans of Serious Sam, it's another one of these imperfect games that has its charm and moments, so it's recommended. _childDocuments_.review: Serious Sam: Siberian Mayhem is an amazing game made by modders that are extremely talented and blessed by the original creators of Serious Sam - Croteam. This doesn't happen often in the gaming industry and I think that the game should be praised just for that even if it was bad. Since it turned out great though it deserves a double-praise, an Oscar even or at least a medal...I had a great time with SS: Siberian Mayhem. It looks, runs and feels just like SS4 (that can be both good or bad depending on your preference) and just like in SS4 the humour was on point for me. The gameplay remains untouched and only some weapons were replaced due to the setting - the AR assault rifle for example got replaced by the AK and the sniper rifle by a crossbow. New consumables were also introduced along with a death-ray laser gun which absolutely rocks. In some locations I even thought that the environments were more detailed than in SS4 and the love for this franchise on the modders part really shows here.Unfortunately it wasn't all sunshine and rainbows. SS: Siberiam Mayhem is still plagued by the same performance problems of SS4. It isn't well optimized. Even on my relatively competant pc it doesn't have a stable frame rate. Also, even though this might be subjective, the final boss is not satisfying to beat and quite unfair. I won't spoil anything but beware that the final boss doesn't play by the rules of SS games. Every defeat feels cheap even though it has the most complex AI in the entire series and the fight as a whole is supposed to be this bombastic climax. It simply didn't do the trick for me.All things considered, SS:SM is an experience that matches the game it draws its inspiration from (on which it's also heavily based) and in some cases even exceeds it. It might be shorter but it's just as if not more fun. On a sale this is an easy recommend and definitely worth the price. There is also co-op so I can imagine that playing this with friends is going to be even more of a mayhem but I can't comment on that since I played in single player.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: It's one of the best Serious Sam game and deliver an unique experience, although it has its flaws and somehow performs even worse than Serious Sam 4, the content really worth it.INTROSiberian Mayhem is a standalone expansion for Serious Sam 4, it has new mechanics, weapons, enemies and vehicles, but the core of the gameplay remains untouched. It's harder and some sections are really challenging, with a good balance overall, the game also knows how to be brutally unfair, especially on Serious difficulty. It's not something that will frustrate you, except maybe an overuse of snipers enemies in some sections or areas where you don't have room to fight with enemies spawning above you. In the moment of this review, I had a single session of 5 hours of gameplay on coop, playing on Serious difficulty and with enemy multiplier set to 2X, as a Serious Sam veteran player, I will describe my experience in this game.TECHNICAL ASPECTSSpeaking about the technical aspect of the game, I can't say I had a really good time. It performed much worse than Serious Sam 4, running the game on low or medium settings didn't made any difference, and all I got was a constant low FPS, especially on fights. However even with this issue, I had no crashes or major problems.The game also presents a brand new menu, faster level loadings and a way better loading screen. Everything else seems pretty much unchanged, it's still a Serious Sam game.LEVEL DESIGNThe level design was what made this game so special. Every level is unique, beautiful and well detailed. Probably the curse of the bad performance is also the blessing of the game, with lots of small details that benefits the immersion in a way we haven't seen before in any Serious Sam game. Mostly of sections are based on fantasy instead of real locations, as opposite to Serious Sam 4, which brought memories of previous titles, when the militarism wasn't the focus of the franchise. This is definitely one of the best thing this expansion has to offer. I personally loved the third level and it's my favorite.BALANCEA game made by Russians must have the well known "Russian Balance", right? Well, sort of. The balance is good, sometimes unfair, but it's Serious Sam, it's something that many fans were missing. I confess that I was worried about it being too easy like Serious Sam 4, especially on the beginning, when you only had a shotgun, a pistol, and lots of enemies to kill, but without the urge feeling of danger. That felling started to change after you get your AK-47 riffle, and the game start to show its colours. If you like a difficult game, this one was made for you.SECRETSYes.I could end this section just with that word, but let me elaborate a bit more: You want secrets? You'll have secrets. This game has more secrets and easter eggs than every Serious Sam game ever had, and not only the simple and generic parkour secret (don't worry, there's still parkour secrets for you) but the most crazy and creative ones. And a side joke for any Timelock Studio member who's reading this, you owe the idea of using classic levels as secrets to Cockatiel Studios, it's their NFT now.NEW FEATURESYou'll play with new gadgets, weapons, vehicles, mech, and unique mechanics for solving puzzles, I loved every new addition in this game, everything was planned and work very well with the campaign, including the usage of gadgets, something I avoided on Serious Sam 4 because I couldn't feel the need to do it, but in this title you'll be forced to use if you want to survive, which makes them so useful and fun. There are a few new enemies that are also a great addition to the game, and speaking about enemies, you'll love the final boss.FINAL VERDICT This is a must play for every fan of Serious Sam. It's not perfect, it's not TSE 2, but brings so many good things that it's already special in its own way.
_childDocuments_.name: Serious Sam: Siberian Mayhem

_childDocuments_.review: I'll be honest, going into this I had pretty low expectations considering how SS4 turned out, but after playing through it and beating it on Serious Difficulty I can confidently say this is the best modern Serious Sam game to date. There's a few negatives here and there which I'll be sure to touch on later, but let's talk about what makes Siberian Mayhem so great.First, the attention to detail is simply incredible. Arachnoids and Octanians will talk in their native language during combat, Octanians have a more significant military presence and genuinely feel like a key faction in Mental's horde, Technopolip Helicopters fall to the ground and explode violently on death, Harpies and Octanian Grenadiers have alternate attacks on higher difficulties to add to the challenge... and the list goes on.Secondly, the environments feel believable and help to serve the gameplay in a meaningful way. Ever since BFE, the series has struggled to balance out the more "modern" environments with Sam's classic gameplay, but Siberian Mayhem finally managed to strike a balance between the new and the old. During slower moments, you'll come across more detailed environments such as frozen over greenhouses, abandoned sheds with tractors still in them, fully furnished houses, orthodox churches, etc. However, when the combat starts to pick up, a lot of these environmental details are pushed off to the sides to allow for the combat to flourish. The combat arenas are still beautiful to look at, but they're functional above everything else, and I wouldn't have it any other way.Third, cool ideas that were introduced in SS4 are now fully fleshed out. Vehicles are back and better than ever, side objectives feel like self-contained levels with their own story and setting, gadgets are less frequent but are more varied, new and returning weapons feel good to use when dual wielding, etc.Fourth, da music. Do I really need to say anything? The main menu theme alone had me pumped to adjust my settings as quickly as possible so I could hop in and start playing. The OST for Siberian Mayhem is nothing short of legendary, it's short but oh so sweet to listen to.Fifth, the weapons! Most of SS4's arsenal returns but some of the more OP weapons/weapon mods have been replaced or removed (so long chainsaw launcher, nice to have known you). Luckily the new weapons more than make up for it, so let's talk about them.- First we have the crossbow. It straight up replaces the Sniper Rifle & Devastator by firing a hitscan beam that pierces through multiple targets and does heavy damage in addition to not having to reload. The downsides are it has a slow fire rate and low ammo capacity.- Next we have the AK which replaces the AR. It does more damage, has a tighter spread, and holds less ammo per mag. It looks good, sounds good, and shoots well; good gun.- Finally we have the Burner. It replaces the Laser Gun + Death Ray combo in a more balanced but equally gory way. It does pretty decent damage and on kill causes enemies to explode which in turn kills other enemies. It can absolutely shred through fields of fodder enemies and when dual wielded will cook through larger foes in seconds.Sixth, the new enemies! Not all of them are winners, but I hope to see them make a return in future Sam titles. - First up are Octanian Grenadiers which toss grenades and have an alternate attack where they toss out a rolling bomb that chases the player. They're not entirely new since they were planned for SS4 but still fun to fight nonetheless.- Next we have the Octanian Legionnaire. They're basically bulkier versions of Zealots but will sometimes be set up to guard other enemies, which is a neat mechanic I hope will return in the future.- Third up is the Draconian Burner. They're basically bulkier versions of Draconian Pyromaniacs that have better telegraphed attacks. In close range they'll slam the ground, at mid to long range they fire lasers that you either need to sidestep or jump over. They're a very cool addition to the enemy roster.- Fourth, the Aludran Microhopper. They're the first new enemy you'll encounter and are easily the worst. They appear in swarms, have unpredictable movement, and do loads of damage. I hate them with a passion.- Finally we have the best new enemy in the game, the Octanian Sentry Tower. They're one of the few area denial enemies in the game and serve as mini-bosses. They'll launch mortars, homing missiles, and have Miniguns to deter you from getting too close. They're actually pretty weak but can't be damaged until they overheat, where they expose their core for a few seconds. Their main purpose is to chip away at the player's health and create openings for other enemies to attack, and they're effective at keeping players mobile.So that's it for the positives, now let's talk about the negatives.First, performance is still an issue. Granted, the game runs much smoother than SS4, but there's still inexplicable lag spikes that pop up and there's a new performance issue that only Siberian Mayhem has where the game will literally freeze for a few seconds before playing normally again. This only seems to happen at certain points during the last 2 missions so hopefully someone at Timelock Studios or Croteam can fix this.Second, puzzles. I know what you're about to say, you only have to do a few puzzles and they're not required since they're only used for secret hunting, but they still don't belong in Serious Sam. They're kind of cool the first time you encounter them but on repeat playthroughs they grind the pacing to a halt.Third, invisible walls and death pits. Luckily there aren't many instances of these things but you'll still find yourself bumping into them from time to time.Fourth, inconsistent hitboxes. SS4 in general has really odd hitboxes for certain enemies such as Biomechs, Witch Brides, and Technopolip Helicopters where projectiles seemingly graze through their sides when it feels like it should have hit. Sadly this hasn't been fixed in Siberian Mayhem and the new Octanian Legionnaire enemy has hitbox issues where his armor effect seems to curve around to parts of his exposed back, making landing SSG shots needlessly difficult.And... That's it, wow. So yeah, if you can't tell I love Siberian Mayhem. It has some of the most enjoyable Serious Sam combat I've experienced in years and unlike SS4 the positives far outweigh the negatives. With that said I hope the negatives are at least looked into and that the performance issues are addressed in the future. I'd also love for cross workshop support with SS4 in the future and for SS4 to get some love in the performance department.It's immediately clear from the moment you boot up Siberian Mayhem that the people who worked on it genuinely love the Serious Sam franchise and have a keen eye for what made Serious Sam so memorable to fans in the first place. Everything from the secrets, combat, music, subtle world building, added details, weather effects, and map design are everything I could have asked for in a modern Serious Sam game, and Siberian Mayhem delivers it with such grace, integrity, and passion that I couldn't help but have a big dumb smile on my face the entire time I played it.Here's hoping improvements made to Siberian Mayhem get introduced to SS4 at some point in the future and cheers to the folks at Croteam and Timelock Studios that made this thing a reality!

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: I've nominated Serious Sam Siberian Mayhem for Game of the Year. Yup. It was that good.Well. Can't say I was expecting a Serious Sam game this year but here we are. It's fantastic too.Serious Sam Siberian Mayhem manages to fill in quite a few gaps that SS4 wasn't able to fulfill.One of the most notable things that comes to mind with this game is quite simply the amount of polish and care put into each and every one of these levels. The side quests for an example. On SS4 they were mostly simple. They usually consisted of a small detour where you would be rewarded with a gadget here and there. Sometimes a weapon. Nothing too substantial though. Siberian Mayhem's side quests absolutely BLEW my mind. The amount of length and quality that each side quest brought to the table almost felt like an entire level of it's own. To put it quite frank. Most of these side quests featured really unique scenarios and sometimes even boss battles. I would've NEVER expected such attention to these areas of the game but they did it incredibly well.Not only this but there's a lot of subtle improvements within the game itself that SS4 lacked. Such as better sounds. More destructible environments. Various UI improvements. VERY creative easter eggs (almost on par with TSE to be honest). LOTS of throwbacks to the classic Serious Sam formula. We're talking classic battle arenas (massive rooms filled with various platforms and launchers to help accommodate the space followed by waves of enemies you have to kill before progressing), Several nods to prior games such as bringing back (and sometimes even remixing) classic soundtracks, MUCH bigger areas to fight the waves upon waves of enemies, as well REALLY in depth boss battles.This game blew me away. If you're a fan of the classic Serious Sam games (TFE, TSE, maybe even SS2), there is definitely something here for you. However it does still give the same modern feel that SS3 and 4 captivates on. So really. If you're just a fan of the series. Definitely pick this one up. I had a really good time with this one.

_childDocuments_.review: I’ll tell you up front, I’m coming at this one from a weird angle. I am a Serious Sam enjoyer from the distant past, having spent plenty of time in the First and Second Encounters. I even knocked around in Serious Sam 2, the black sheep of the series, but that was the last one I played before Siberian Encounter. With that in mind, I can’t speak to the evolution of Sam between 3 and 4 (at least not yet), but I know a Serious Sam game when I see one and this has all the hallmarks. Ludicrously huge encounters, meaty guns, bizarre humor, and unexpected secrets are all here, along with some innovations I wasn’t expecting. This is easily the most fun I’ve had with a Serious game yet, which is remarkable seeing as how it hails from a totally different developer.Again, I can’t fill you in on the details of the story, because the last time I left Sam, he was planet-hopping across cartoonish worlds in pursuit of Mental. Here, he’s rolled up to the frozen climes of Siberia to check out a disturbance reported in the Tunguska area. Obviously, it’s a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ of monsters, and Sam’s here to kill them all and let the renderer sort them out. He’ll run across a few solid allies in his journey, and make a surprising discovery about one of his foes. There’s probably some other stuff going on, judging from the notes and audio logs scattered about, but if we can be real for a minute, I’m not running around in a Serious Sam game for the story.I’m here to gib as many enemies as the game is willing to throw at me, and hot damn does it throw out some enemies. Ramping up very quickly from the serene coastal opening, Sam has literally thousands of foes to mow down across icy tundra, frozen farmlands, precarious cliffs, ramshackle villages, towering refineries, and ominous warehouses. Timelock Studio, the collection of modders responsible for bringing Siberian Mayhem to life, absolutely understand why people play Serious Sam games, and have an admirable talent for composing surprising and creative encounters. This game feels like a greatest hits album of frenetic fights, challenging you with hallways choked with charging Kleers, plazas strafed with fire and harpies, and wide-open plains with more enemies than you can even imagine.Sam’s arsenal is up to the task of taking on this army, of course, with a collection of solid stand-bys like shotguns, launchers, and a beam cannon that makes enemies explode. There’s also an assortment of gadgets like on-demand healing, speed boosts, black holes, air strikes, and a portable combat hoverboard that come in very handy during the larger fights. Notably, there’s a skill point system here (apparently carried over from 4) that offers some absurdly powerful abilities like dual-wielding any two weapons and melee-executing even the largest foes. They’re so dramatic, in fact, that it seems odd they’re not just included in Sam’s standard repertoire. On the bright side, getting to dual wielding is easy enough through the freebie skill points you earn through normal progression, and once you’re toting around a minigun in one hand and a beam cannon in the other, you’ll wonder how you ever got on without them.The other notable feature of Siberian Mayhem (which may also have been in 4, I can’t say) is side objectives that help fill out the vast open spaces most levels have plenty of. Most of the game’s missions have a side objective that’s activated simply by approaching the area, and it usually rewards an extra skill point on top of the extra ammo and possible early weapons you’ll get along the way. These can get very involved, with one being a full-on quest into a secret bunker with one hell of a payoff. I really like this inclusion, because Serious Sam games have always valued and rewarded exploration, and having entire side missions to play through with their own setpieces is a really big bonus.It’s hard not to love the sheer volume and variety of action offered here, especially when you get to some of the more creative encounters and vehicle sections. The game is also broken up occasionally by cutscenes, most focusing on Sam himself but also introducing other characters like a rag-tag gang of stereotypical Russian crazies. I could knock the quality of the animations or voice acting in these bits, but again, story and drama are not what I’m plowing through a Serious Sam game for. I took around six hours to blow through the whole thing and do most of the side missions, which puts it somewhere between the good ol’ First and Second Encounters for length. And honestly, that’s about right for a Serious Sam game. You want these nice and punchy, so you can drink up the action and silliness before it wears out its welcome. Siberian Mayhem is just that, a fine figure of modern Serious Sam action, and one that I doubt will disappoint classic FPS fans.Did you enjoy this review? I certainly hope so, and I certainly hope you'll check out more of them at  or on my !

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, man, this series has really fallen off, hasn't it? To give Timelock Studio some credit, they're definitely better at making these games than Croteam is now, but they've inherited problems that Croteam introduced and it really is a killer.Simply put, Serious Sam was always reliant on conveying every shred of important information you'd need very quickly, both visually and audibly. SS3 was really where things took a turn in both of these, but especially visually. Now we're at the point where it's just impossible to quickly parse all the same information that you could in TFE, TSE, TNE, and SS2. The art direction is so focused on realistic lighting and effects that it obscures the colours and at times even the silhouettes of enemies. I can almost never determine what kind of beheaded I'm looking at (aside from kamikazes) by something as simple as shirt colour anymore. It used to be so stark. Green = grenadier. Red = rocket man. Purple = basic, weak projectile. This isn't helped by the enemy design itself, which likes to mute colours when they should really be popping. You can still have a game that looks good and is readable, as the new Doom games manage that just fine. But in Serious Sam's case especially, with the sheer number of enemies it wants to throw at you, you have to be even more aware of your art direction to inform players. The more enemies on screen, the more information you're tasking the player to process quickly, and this game does not succeed in helping give you that necessary information.The other absolute tragedy is the sound design. Unique enemy sounds aren't as distinctive or well-mixed. In the older games, if there was a Kleer skeleton within half the damn map from you, you'd know many moons before you ever saw it, for instance. Major and minor arachnoids made a passive sound for simply existing, especially good to know in regards to the minor, since it has a hitscan weapon. They also had a sound for detecting you, so you could duck back into cover real quick before it fired. Virtually every enemy had a very distinctive dying sound, so you'd know when that target was no longer an issue without having to watch their dying animation to be sure. Numerous enemies had pain sounds, like all the beheadeds, so you'd know if you stunned them for a brief second. If enemies fired a gun, you would ALWAYS know. You would never, ever be hit by biomechanoid lasers that you weren't aware of having been fired. The reptiloids with their homing projectiles ALWAYS used a very distinct sound for their quick charge animation, then a sound that it'd been released, and then the projectile itself had its own sound so you wouldn't forget it'd been fired. Then, if it exploded after running out of time, you'd hear it and know that projectile wasn't a threat.None of this is here. Or if it is, it's mixed so badly that you can't hear any of it. I even turned off the (unremarkable) music entirely just to try to hear these things better. It didn't help. It's just a weird, vague cacophony of noise that you're subjected to, rather than the intelligent layering of many different and seriously distinct noises, completely unique, to let you know the situation without even needing to see it. Boot up an old Serious Sam game, get into a fight, then close your eyes. You will know absolutely every single enemy in the battle and what they're doing at any given moment without needing to see a thing.Thing is, from what I played, these things didn't even really make the game harder, necessarily, as I didn't die. But as someone who really enjoys the earlier titles, and as someone who disliked SS3 and had no real expectations of this title except that it was better than SS4, I find myself not enjoying it at all and being disappointed by it. And again, I don't really blame Timelock. I blame Croteam. Even just thinking of what I've seen of SS4 and what I played of SS3 years ago, I can tell that anything that actually feels Serious Sam in this game is something Timelock managed to capture on their own. Nonetheless, if Serious Sam is perpetually going to continue leaning in a more realistic direction visually (despite the fact that every new game with realistic art direction is inherently having more problems with readability than games from 20 years ago that tried being realistic), and if the sound design isn't going to be reworked to be on par with a 22 year-old game, then I don't see any Serious Sam game managing to match the accomplishments of its earlier titles. Such a shame.

_childDocuments_.review: This review was written after finishing the game 3 times, including in Co-Op.I'm familiar with all the main titles in the series and have tackled Serious Sam 4 after Siberian Mayhem just to get a complete picture.The gun play feels just right. Punchy sound effects, animations that feel like they have weight to them, echoing explosions in the distance, enemies turning into a mess of giblets, splats of particles and smoke: all of this creates a satisfying experience. This particular installment features one of the more gratifying and fun arsenals in the series, while also having most of the "good old and tested" kind of gear, so the overall the package should be pleasing. Jumping into the game for both returning and new players should be a treat. Variety is back on the menu. I find it rather painfully exhausting to go through the same-looking areas of SS3:BFE, when the entirety of the game focuses on just one general location and/or setting. I felt completely burnt out when playing Serious Sam HD: TFE, especially with the additional more-of-the-same content. With The Second Encounter and SS2 being the more fun ones for me, Siberian Mayhem delivered in this department. The areas do not overstay their welcome, each location gets its own dedicated soundtrack, and the general scenery changes with each map. All Serious Sam games are filled with a variety of secrets and Easter Eggs and this game goes all out with those: fan-service, in-your-face references, memes, typical Serious Sam ambushes and even some trippy stuff is present. This is the first SS game that I've 100%ed in terms of secrets, and I would say that it was worth it. Combing through never ending trees and bushes ruins the pacing, so I wouldn't recommend on going all out with the secret search during your first run, instead, do that during a next run and save yourself a headache - use a guide. And no, most of the secrets aren't just L.I.F.E. gadgets placed in the most uninspired locations.After checking out Serious Sam 4 specifically for this review, I can say that, unsurprisingly, this game's framework is mostly made out of "building blocks" taken from the main entry. It does make sense, after all, it's a stand-alone expansion, rather than an outright new main entry. However, Siberian Mayhem is surprisingly more polished in terms of level design and does have a few "building blocks" of its own. It separates itself from the main game by having a distinct atmosphere that does not feel simply copied and pasted. Quality of life improvements and rebalancing, while might not be immediately noticeable, do make the game more enjoyable.A big, semi-open world means that there are going to be epic, large-scale battles. It also means that there's going to be absolutely nothing in between those combat segments.Siberian Mayhem most of the time is a tight, linear experience, but there are a few locations that turn into Alan Wake-esque open areas, that can be described at best as padding. If you do not care about exploration and secret hunting, then this will likely be a non-issue for you. However, if you do, then you'll experience the joys of traversing through seemingly auto-generated woods and bounce against invisible walls, loads of jarring brown bushes, find yourself in an automatic kill zone or run into a minefield.Yes, it's possible to tell where a playing field ends and where the map borders begin. You'd think that those areas are not worth any exploration, but that's not true. There are enough secrets hidden on the edges of a map, sometimes without any clear indication, like tracks leading off a main road.I do get that this is a returning formula that's been used in previous titles of the series, where maps can be seemingly "open and endless", but I would say that when it comes to Siberian Mayhem, there isn't much grand scale immersion when you see a bunch of brown bush lines that were put there in a level editor as a quick barrier.Same as in SS4, Siberian Mayhem has a mount mechanic, where it's possible to control an alien and use it as a vehicle and/or a weapon. It does sound fun on paper, but there is no easy or convenient way of mounting something. Not only you have to be standing almost point-blank to the target, but you also need to be behind it. In a game where most enemies will face you head-on. Trying out this mechanic during a battle usually means losing all your HP in the process. There are a few sequences where the enemies are patrolling unalerted, but making a mechanic viable only for a few limited opportunities doesn't sound fun to me.Serious Sam games are known to feature cheesy, low brow humor, and the franchise went through a few identity crises along the way: the polarizing cartoony SS2, then the more gloomy SS3:BFE that fills you with dread and sand. SS4 is leaning towards the cartoony side, with absolutely constant comedic relief. Siberian Mayhem leans towards cringe, and that's probably one of my least favorite aspects about it. The fake accents are just the icing on the cake, and make me wonder what kind of presentation it could've been with a different set of voice actors for the side cast (Gianni Matragrano did a good job, though).When it comes to performance, the game runs adequately even on an aging GPU. However, no matter which settings I choose, the frame times are never stable. This means, even though the game runs at 60 FPS, it never feels as smooth as it should be. Using external tools to cap the frame rate does not seem to help. On top of that, despite being installed on an SSD, I still experience constant (load-in?) stutters and texture pop-in. This seems to be inherited from SS4, where the game behaves similarly.Amongst other oddities, there are cases where the game shuffles between different texture LoD (level of detail), while the player is standing still.Loading times aren't as fast as I would hope. This could be explained by the fact that the levels in this game are gigantic. It takes around 35 seconds to load a new level, while it takes only 3 seconds to reload a save within the same stage.The game itself is stable, I didn't experience any crashes, and the overall visual fidelity is pleasing to look at. Croteam's engine is highly tweakable, but it lacks the necessary descriptions and visual examples to be user-friendly. One option that I would like to see is a photo mode. At least, offer a way of conveniently toggling the user interface off, since there's no setting to do so.Experience with Co-Op was mixed. Once I enabled an X4 enemy multiplier, the game began to freeze, where the game's audio would continue to play, while everything else stops. For the host, this meant that turning the camera in a particular direction in a seemingly random spot (even without any enemies nearby) would freeze the game for up to 5 seconds. For the client, this meant that all the entities in the game would stop moving, and you wouldn't do any damage to them. On top of that, the client would have freezes as well, even during cutscenes. It made no sense and there were no connection/ping abnormalities.Auto-saves are frequent, a certain amount of them is stored in case saving happens during a bad time. This is also an effective way of combatting save game corruption due to unexpected shutdowns or drive failures.Just the right amount of content, so it satisfies the need for more Serious Sam without watering down the experience. Strong gun play and polished level design invoke the classic game feel, while having a larger playing field. Variety is its strong point and the unstable technical performance is the weakness. If you're looking for more of SS4, but with better pacing, then Siberian Mayhem has got you covered.Review copy provided by Devolver Digital, Inc.

_childDocuments_.review: Serious Sam: Siberian Mayhem is a single player First Person Shooter, and follows on from the events of Serious Sam 4.•	Combat is fast paced and each encounter features a ridiculous number of enemies on screen, which is exactly what you’d expect from a Serious Sam game.•	Huge variety of different enemies with unique attack patterns. Colourful visual design of enemies helps to identify them within the chaos of battle.•	Lots of different weapons and gadgets, almost all of which feel fun to use, including shotgun, assault rifle, minigun, rocket launcher, crossbow, laser rifle, cannonball launcher, time warp, rage serum, hoverboard and more.•	Only took me 8 hours to finish on hard difficulty, which feels short, but at least the game is priced appropriately.•	First two levels are quite tough, mainly because the level design contains lots of small areas where you can get trapped in a dead end. Later the difficulty feels more balanced because the maps have more wide open space so you can actually move around and avoid enemies.•	There’s also a survival mode where you try to stay alive for as long as possible on six maps of endless waves of enemies. Not as fun as it sounds because the maps are too small for the amount of enemies thrown at you.•	Serious Sam games have never been focused on telling a good story, but even by those standards this was poor.•	I had a strange bug where the game won’t launch through the Steam client. When I click the green play button, nothing happens. I don’t even get an error message. Eventually I was able to get the game working by going to the install folder in file explorer and using the exe file.•	You’re going to need a powerful PC to get good performance. Mine is comfortably above the recommended spec shown on the store page (RTX 3080, i7 12700, 32GB RAM), and while most of the game was fine, I did have some framerate issues on the last level (playing in 1440p).•	Controls are fully rebindable and work well with mouse and keyboard.If you’re a fan of the Serious Sam games, or single player FPSes in general, you should enjoy Siberian Mayhem.

_childDocuments_.review: Serious Sam Siberian Mayhem is a fan-created expansion to Serious Sam 4, which has been given Croteam's blessing. It's pretty apparent that a lot of notes were taken from how SS4 turned out, as Timelock Studio really managed to focus on the best parts of SS4.Although it's a short six-hour experience, Siberian Mayhem shows just what the Serious Sam franchise is capable of. The pacing is quite excellent, and gets you into well-designed encounters very quickly. There's a ton of memorable moments throughout the five (quite long) levels. The environments are designed quite well, and feel realistic. Many of the levels have you weaving around the environment instead of just plowing forward through entire levels. It's quite a relief to be able to see where you're going, and where you've come from in a lot of these areas.While I feel there might be too much "heavy snow" areas early on, that quickly fades as you're taken through a variety of other really interesting environments. I really enjoyed the atmosphere of these levels and they felt like old Serious Sam games, as well as parts of Half-Life 2. The terrain also felt less flat than previous SS games, while still feeling realistic and adding some more strategy to combat. Exploring felt rewarding a lot of the time and secrets were hidden naturally and were enjoyable.The combat was consistently engaging, and the difficulty felt right when playing on normal. I think Serious Sam is at its best here, with some new enemies really putting pressure on you. My only real complaint is that they overload you with too many enemies at once, too often, in the later sections of the game. One level in particular gave me three back-to-back insane encounters. While the carnage was absolutely intense, the performance dropped and the game-play devolved into using the two most overpowered guns the entire time. Other than that, the game never got stingy with health or ammo, meaning you could always approach situations however you wanted, which is great.The bosses in this game were also incredible. The end-boss in particular made me feel something that I have not felt in shooters in a long time. I actually loved using gadgets during this fight, and I even felt that they were needed. I tended to stray away from using gadgets during normal game-play just due to being clunky and trivializing fights. Having said that, there are some new gadgets which are appreciated. The developers did a great job adding new content and having it fit. Some of the mechanics in Siberian Mayhem feel straight out of the original Serious Sam games, such as jump pads (which are used sparingly.)Some of the same issues from SS4 apply here, such as the perk system. I go back and forth on dual-wielding. Sometimes it's fun as hell (such as two shotguns), and other times it breaks the game and makes those in-between encounters trivial. When one sniper shot can take out a larger enemy, there's not a lot of threats unless you're overloaded with enemies. The AK is also insanely overpowered once you get it. I think having the guns feel overpowered is better than them feeling weak. This is probably why they throw so many enemies at you later in the game. Even with these weapons being insanely strong, pulling out the sniper rifle in a massive field during a huge encounter just to take out important targets feels GREAT.While the performance is generally on par or better than Serious Sam 4 itself, it can sometimes dip much harder with the sheer number of enemies thrown at you. It's pretty much CPU limited in this respect. There's also some other small issues like NPC dialogue being too low compared to Sam himself, and other sound effects.Serious Sam Siberian Mayhem is a must-play for any Serious Sam fan, and highly recommended to anyone that loves shooters. The only real downside (aside from potential performance issues on older PCs) is that it somewhat ties into SS4's story... and those elements wouldn't make sense to anyone who hasn't played SS4. I hope that future Serious Sam installments can follow Siberian Mayhem's design direction.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the best Serious Sam game yet, and a very competent modern shooter to rival the likes of the new Doom and Wolfenstien Games. It maintains Serious Sam's identity while taking lessons from other shooters on the market. Absolutely worth the asking price. I've heard this game has performance issues but it runs very well on my mediocre AMD machine. Easy recommend to fans of classic Serious Sam games and Shooter gamers.  The moment to moment combat is the best yet in the franchise. It took me a while to warm up to Serious Sprinting but it serves the absolutely huge combat arenas and because of the way Sams enemies work unlike most games it provides a tactical choice as I can choose to do the classic Serious S+M1 or I can sprint if I really need to get out at the cost of not being able to shoot. There is a huge enemy bestiary all of which are easily identifiable and fun to fight with one exception. The Kleer Skeleton makes a return and its in its its identical to it's previous versions though the changes to Sam's arsenal it is much less of a headache. Some weird inclusions are a pseudo glory kill system that doesn't work particularly well and feels out of place with the way the combat encounters are structures. Not enough reward to do a glory kill, they are are difficult to execute without taking damage. The one use powerups are powerful and fun to use exept the one that's just a portable health pack. I like the new artillery strike over the serious bomb.  New to the arsenal is the Grenade Launcher attachment, AK-47,  Crossbow, and Ray Gun. The grenade Launcher is much like the Doom 2016 grenade launcher. It is useful in the early game and can one shot Kleer Skeletons. The AK-47 is a pleasant surprise and favorite 'Assault Rifle' of any modern shooter. I don't approve of reloading but I can tolerate it for this high powered death machine at least it's the only weapon that reloads. It shoots fast, feels powerful and has a really meaty sound effect. It is useful for killing areal enemies and otherwise is a great all rounder. It also has ADS when not dual wielded. Shows a good sound effect can make me overlook everything I hate about modern shooters. The Crossbow is absurdly good. can oneshot most enemies with a headshot. Unlike the second encounter sniper, it does the same damage scoped as unscoped. The Raygun is just awesome. Its like the quake Lightning gun but much more powerful and requires a second to charge before firing. Makes enemies explode on death. Sam can duel wield now like the new Wolfenstien games. This changes everything. The Super Shotgun benefits tremendously as it can now do high burst damage from firing both at the same gun or alternating fire to increase fire rate vs the Kleer skeletons it one shots. It may be a bit too powerful when combined with the crossbow as anything can be quickly deleted by a few shots to the head.  This game is gorgeous. You're not in Egypt anymore. Its a wonderful change of pace for the franchise and is technically impressive. The visual effects in general are the best yet in the franchise and while a bit behind the curve and janky, I really can't complain. There are a few very welcome chill vehicle sections where you just drive though the countryside and throughout the game the scenery changes from snowy to green.   The weapon sounds are nice and punchy. The music is very good as well, and fits the action sequences and the exploration scenes. There is a sequence where you are piloting a mech while a rendition of Rasputin plays. Feels like a typical shooter soundtrack but with a bit of Russian influence. The writing is all over the place. Sam is Sam and plays the part.  The difficulty is well balanced and I have no complaints. Serious difficulty is hard but not completely frustrating like in the classic games. It is equivalent to the doom eternal Nightmare difficulty. One major issue is if you die more than a few times on one checkpoint the game prompts you to turn down the difficulty. It's very annoying to have to click though especially if you are struggling. Its a hard game by design, I know that by choosing Serious difficulty. There has to be a less obtrusive method of reminding the player they can change the difficulty.

_childDocuments_.review: Siberian Mayhem unfortunately gets a negative rating from me.Overall, the gameplay is still solid. Movement, dual wielding and the vehicle sections are all good fun. Bullet spread is still a thing sadly. The new weapons are extremely overpowered, which makes them extremely fun to use. The story is just present enough to give the game a slight nuance in stitching the levels together. Cutscenes are alright, adds some personality to Sam and his merry band of exterminators. The chemistry between the characters is much better in SM than in 4, much less cringey dialogue. The maps are of decent size and the item/enemy/area secrets and traps are very reminiscent of TFE/TSE. You can tell the mod team making SM were much in sync with Golden Era Sam games, and it really shows how Croteam has lost their personal touch. Some more interesting platforming sections would really put the icing on the cake. Of the new enemies, the Octanian Towers do a good job of putting pressure on the player amidst the other fodder, ultimately a pain in the ass to fight. They make the level less enjoyable. The other few additions are decent enough to fight.What prevents this game from being truly good and enjoyable is the performance. It's atrocious. Imagine having to crank every setting to minimal in a Croteam game (Slavic technosorcers that made games run on the most destitute 3rd world systems - and still function fantastically). It seems Alen Ladavec was the programming talent, and that talent has evaporated from Croteam when he left. The first and final levels run horribly - some areas are better than others throughout the game - but overall it's pure trash at maintaining a smooth and respectable framerate. What's astounding is the game looks serviceable; it's not pushing any boundaries as Croteam has unfortunately decided to pursue realism rather than the better stylized art direction in older Sam iterations. It performs much worse than Sam 4, well known for being poorly optimized. I doubt that SM will ever receive optimizations as that seems a fairly difficult task given a small team of modders and Croteam's seemingly apathetic attitude supporting Sam 4 (or Revolutions, or anything at this point).Another detriment is that like Sam 4, this does not have integral 16p coop, though likely will be supported via a mod like the former. This is another flag denoting Croteam losing touch with what made their games so good. Overall, a good attempt by Timelock that hits closer to old Serious Sam than 3 or 4, marred and rendered unenjoyable due to the complete and utter lack of engine optimization. Even 3 ran better than this, FPS-killing dust clouds included. Croteam needs to seriously™ buckle down and make this iteration of Serious Engine actually perform before pushing out Talos 2 or anything else.
_childDocuments_.name: Serious Sam: Siberian Mayhem

_childDocuments_.review: First things first. You might think "5 levels? For 20 bucks? What is this..". But do not despair, the levels are quite expansive. Expect most of them to take over an hour to finish, more if you do some exploration and secret hunting.Levels are action packed and very well designed. Closed spaces or large open areas, the variety should keep things from getting monotonous. There are several new enemies, and all of them feel unique and bring something new to the table. Did you hate Marsh Hoppers in the Encounter games? Well what if they did not die in one hit, had a ranged attack and actively dodged to the side from your shots? Siberian Mayhem has you covered. Besides new enemies, there are also several new weapons. All 3 of them quite powerful and fun to use. Overall, the difficulty can be quite high. Don't expect introductory levels with only a couple of enemies and slow pace. This expansion starts strong and never lets up. But considering the massive power increase Sam received in Serious Sam 4, I'd say that finally, the challenge corresponds to it.One slightly annoying technical issue is how the game handles texture streaming. It loads them only for what you are currently looking at. And most of the time, it is quite visible how the game constantly swaps from low resolution textures to the full resolution ones. In a cutscene, 2 characters talking with each other will be loading their textures every time the camera cuts away and back. In game, you could be standing in place, turn 180 degrees, wait 1 second, turn 180 degrees again and you will be looking at a blurry mess of a wall that takes a moment look as it is supposed to. And this happens pretty much everywhere. I can't imagine the nightmare it would be to have this installed on a non-SSD drive.And one minor gripe, I hated the ending. I was expecting something in the vein of Jewel of the Nile for Serious Sam 3, where it would tie into the main game, but the ending basically voids everything you do in this.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT:Not recommended but, i will modify it a bit to rectfiy post-release performance that the community kinda "worked-around"Its technically worse than Serious Sam 4. I managed to make it run acceptably (read: 60 with drops to 40) by changing a few settings (Terrain and Distance quality to Medium / Default and Pre-Baked lighting enabled instead of dynamic), but its not ideal, and far far FAR from acceptable for a game like it.As for the game itself: Its more Sam. Its fun, the campaign is open-ended, but has far more sense of direction than the old SS4, the new tools and weapons are cool, the secrets are nice, and the new additions are very welcome.If you are willing to risk the performance issues to play it, sure, its a recommend. But if you want a polished experience for the buck. Wait for patches, if they ever happen.

_childDocuments_.review: Probably one of the best standalone expansions I've played in a long while. It takes all the best parts of the original game and ditches everything that was setting it back. Unlike the full game, this expansion starts fast and hard, skipping walking and talking and getting to the essential part of the franchise — shooting lots of aliens in huge open spaces. And it continues to ramp things up as it goes, sometimes easily raising the bar above what was set by the main game.It is very important also to mention that this is not just a standalone expansion; this is a proper love letter to the franchise bridging the gap between a fan project and an official product. Syberian Mayhem was created by a small Russian team or modders turned developers in collaboration with Croteam. They even got the famous in the boomer shooter community voice actor Gianni Matragrano to act as a main supporting character Igor Ledov."Every Russian knows Serious Sam"						— Igor Ledov

_childDocuments_.review: These crazy Russian modder-f***ers did it. They've made an expansion for Serious Sam 4 that's better than the main game. Quite good, actually. At least this is my impression after my first playthrough.I'll be honest: the performance is very disappointing, and I almost want to give the game a negative review just for that. But since the weak engine isn't Timelock Studio's fault, I don't want to blame them too much for it. Just note that Siberian Mayhem doesn't run too well. I'm also not sure if the game is worth its full price for everybody. I'm a fan of the series, and even I hesitated.However, the game itself is quite fun and impressive. The levels can be huge with many varied environments, big and intense battles, good vehicle sections, and a bunch of side quests. The writing is actually pretty decent and funny, with lots of clever jokes and secrets making references to other Serious Sam games and Russian culture. Bonus points for a character quoting the song "Psycho Holiday" by Pantera.Overall, I'm pretty happy with the game. I'll probably come back and update the review when I've played through the game on Serious difficulty and unlocked all the achievements.Edit: I completed my Serious playthrough with all side quests and secrets last night, so I'm almost done with the game. I have to say, this is now one of my favorite Serious Sam titles, which I wasn't really expecting before playing it since SS3 and SS4 were big disappointments to me. They also released the first patch just three days after the game's launch, so a few issues have already been fixed, including the stuttering. Everything feels really smooth now (as long as the frame rate itself doesn't drop). Well done, Timelock Studio.Edit again: 100% after 20.1 hours of play time. Great game.

_childDocuments_.review: Siberian Mayhem is a lot like the old expansion packs you used to get on build engine games. The developers of the original game released the engine and a game with a solid foundation. Then a new team who have trained with it will release a much better campaign for that title with all the bells and whistles. Timelock Studio has had no issue coming up with an excellent campaign addition. While I do not enjoy the plot, I enjoy the gameplay and the side objectives are spectacular. Having no restrictions on having to create an engine from scratch has given the team the freedom and ability to put all of their talent, experience and creativity into one of the best campaigns Serious Sam has ever had. And perhaps will ever have.

_childDocuments_.review: You know, when I was playing through SS4, and being rather disappointed with that game, I kept thinking to myself "wouldn't it be nice if there was like, a DLC that fixed all of this?"It's ironic to saw, but that's exactly what Siberian Mayhem is.For a bit of context, the Russian part of SS4 was heavily cut due to, well, various development reasons.Likely being unfinished is one of them, and given that this project was spearheaded by modders, it's likely very different from what Croteam had cut anyways...Siberian Mayhem... Is what I feel SS4 would have been if it had been left in the oven to bake for another year or 2: it has so many better locations, fights, enemy variety, level design (indoor areas return, rejoice!), level ambience (you can just listen to the sounds, see snow drifts, the blizzards, and the scenic views, shoot barrels/pipes and see them leak/steam) that really set the tone heavily from things seemingly missing from SS4. There's alot of authentic steps taken to make this a believable Russia and a real place.Storywise, it's kinda, eh, but it gets more points since it takes place during SS4's climax, which I consider the best part of that game's story regardless, which I was rather disappointed with how short and anti-climatic that was. But Siberian Mayhem helps make it decent again with more backstory into things not explained in SS4. (also getting to meet characters you only heard on radios inperson is a nice touch)And the secrets... My god the SECRETS, it's a heaven sent gift straight from the classic-era (2002-2006) of custom maps! Which hits me very hard in all the right spots.Yeah if you felt that SS4 missed the mark, Siberian Mayhem will not disappoint you again. Really makes me happy again to know that this community still has devs/modders who can work magic just like the old classic days of Sam modders...Edit:Croteam, please continue to work with these devs, they give me hope again for this series

_childDocuments_.review: Serious Sam: Siberian Mayhem (SSSM) is a sneak-peak back into the potential of the Serious Sam franchise, and may be the best piece of Sam content since the 2nd Encounter, despite it being an expansion and not a full game.Regardless, SSSM is created by Timelock Studios, formed from many of the popular modders you see populating the workshop with content. It comes from a full understanding from what makes Serious Sam games fun: great encounters, well-crafted level design and pacing, as well as the wackiness mixed with realism.Serious Sam 4 had all the pieces of the puzzle, but never connected them. It felt like an incomplete and dated game, even if parts of it can be fun. Siberian Mayhem has more depth, both in the detail in each level, as well as how it delivers its content. The pacing is equivalent to the First Encounter, meaning that it allows fun gameplay at all areas, when you have less weapons, and when you have your full arsenal. To illustrate that point, picture how bad Serious Sam 3's first few Urban levels were with pacing, and how boring it was until you get to the Egyptian Ruin levels. SSSM starts at that level of fun. Acquiring the arsenal is fun, and the new weapons are great. Personally, the crossbow feels way more fun and satisfying than the sniper, and the Burner Gun is all around great for the crowd clearing.A few new enemies join the roster, while some like the hoppers are kinda meh, the Draconian Burner is an awesome, challenging addition that adds a level of strategy to the game akin to how the Reptiloids do.Serious Sam excels when the combat makes you switch between weapons regularly and prioritize different targets based on threat and current arsenal. This is done very well in SSSM.The levels themselves are easily better than any levels in SS4. Siberiade has become my favorite Serious Sam level ever created. It's placed right in the middle of the campaign, while you collect around half of your arms and get introduced to a quasi-open world (done much better than Breakfast in France due to proper use of borders, key points of interest, land marks, and not wasting space with kilometers of nothing). The openness is fun to explore and creates good swarm encounters. Additionally, secret hunting is my favorite part of the franchise, and this expansion does it the best.Some things I'd love to see in the franchise going forward:More unique movement opportunities: sprint is always a debate, but I think having enemies that really test the player's movement like the firecracker are good things to have. Stuff for encouraging jumping more, maybe dashes like the ones that already exist in the mechs we control in the game.Better upgrade trees: SSSM carries a slightly adjusted skill tree from SS4, and this tree could be a lot better to have some cool abilities, like having a robot arm automatically apply gadgets, new movement opportunities like a slide to go under hip-height projectiles, and cool features for weapon upgrades.New Game+ was added to SSSM, and would be a great feature going forward.Alternate Paths in levels. We kinda have that with the open level design in parts of Siberiade, but would be cool to see in more linear levels IF POSSIBLE in COOP.Bigger emphasis on Score: Fun screens at the end of a level for high scores like on Serious Sam Xbox, cool in game unlocks for high scores like weapon customization or player models. It would be fun if we could use score in the future for things like upgrade points or whatnot, just an idea, like all of these doesn't have to be a thing.Better COOP saves. It's kinda weird to understand how it works, would be nice if there was a full menu that can load COOP saves and keep track of player progress for others locally or something, maybe figure that out.

_childDocuments_.review: Really good entry into the SS franchise. Maps are better than SS4 and while it has a few flaws, for me it was close to TFE/TSE levels of quality - especially after the patch seems to have fixed most problems I had. I'd buy this if you're even slightly interested.Overall, map 1-2 are more like early maps in TFE/TSE, whereas map 3-5 are more like SS4. I didn't love map 3 - felt it had a bit too much open space in places, esp. when searching for secrets. However, overall level design was fantastic and on par with some of SS's best levels. _childDocuments_.review: [h]As a fan of the Serious Sam series and a russian at the same time i highly recommend this game to anyone who enjoys action shooters![/h]Even if you didn't enjoy Serious Sam 4, this game will make you cream all over yourself or a closest Gnaar female. Possibly multiple times. Everything in this game is made with love to classic installments like The Second Encounter, but with some very well made new features. New weapons feel good and authentic to the developing Sam universe. New enemies throw in new ways to move around the battlefield and fit well with the soul of the series.Secrets are really fun and sometimes hard to find and are also very usefull. There are many callbacks to classic games in these secrets as well. Can you imagine a good Serious Sam game without secret traps where you pick up an ammo stache just to be instantly ambushed by a horde of enemies just to waste all that ammo you just picked up SEVERAL times in a game? This game does it and it does so well ;)Great level design! There are all kinds of battles - big open areas to backpedal around and claustrofobic corridors filled with screaming meatbags to shoot your way through. Also very natural worldbulding. Gamedesigners made this Russia very believable to exist in Serious Sam universe. There's so much russian humor which is sadly hidden behind language and culture barriers, but this still fits, as Sam (and most players) are not that familiar with the Motherland. Don't take this game as multibillion-AAA-10-years-indevelopment one though, as it has some rough edges with some minor bugs here and there, simple animations and some sound and perfomance issues. But all of this always been a part of Serious Sam games and i can't blame John J. ♥♥♥♥ nor the developers for sounding like he was recorded inside Egyptian temple underground, as it always was like this and is kinda heartwarming :)    Voice actors did very good job too, all these thick accents are fun. Was surprised when i saw Gianni Matragranno voicing one of the main characters, his accent here is too believable.I completed the story on normal difficulty in about 8 hours pretty much strolling through the story without glancing over every corner for secrets and easter eggs and will come back for a 100% playthrough on hard probably. Very worth the price! Serious Sam: Siberian Mayhem is seriously serious game and you seriously should play it!

_childDocuments_.review: I'd argue that this game was better than it's predecessor, Serious Sam 4. There was one level in here that was similar to the France level(s) in SS4 but it wasn't as bad. However, all the systems and the like are in here so don't expect that to be changed. Same goes with multiplayer modes/etc. so nothing groundbreaking. You have vehicular battles, large scale battles, city battles, boss battles, and more.If you did like SS4 then you'll love this one. It's tighter and has a better direction that the other one, personally. The boss fights in it are on the same level as the previous one. For $20 (time of writing) this is a great buy. If you play on a lesser difficulty and aren't someone actively looking for secrets and the like I'd say that the game probably will run you about 4 - 6 hours. A friend and I had played the game searching for secrets in every level and we clocked in 7 1/2 hours of gameplay so your mileage will vary. We did play on Hard.We'll probably go back with another friend to play through on Serious mode (the hardest difficultly) and that probably will add a bit of time into there. Do note that if you didn't like SS4 then this may be a hit or miss. The one of the problems I had with the prior game was that there was just too much wide open space with nothing around. This one fixes most of those issues minus one level. Humor is still on point!
_childDocuments_.name: Serious Sam: Siberian Mayhem

_childDocuments_.review: Serious Sam: Siberian Mayhem is a surprisingly lengthy expandalone for Serious Sam 4, except is perhaps more polished, more focused and more fun than the game it's based on. That's not a knock against Serious Sam 4 though as I'm one of those who absolutely loves it despite its issues so getting more Sam action is very much appreciated.Everything the base game does well like the combat, this also does well and comes with some new enemies and weapons that are welcome additions to the action plus the crazy secrets we know and love are fully intact here. However there are some issues from Serious Sam 4 that did carry over such as the rocky performance, iffy animations and dated visuals so that is something to bear in mind before going in.Honestly it's well worth the money if you're a fan of Serious Sam and want more but if you're new to the series and want to jump into Siberian Mayhem then I definitely recommend bringing a buddy along for the ride as this gets far more hectic than 4. If you end up liking it and want more then definitely pick up the rest of the series after you're done, even the indie spin-offs since they're all great fun and go on big sales quite regularly.

_childDocuments_.review: I really honestly can't believe I'm saying this about a piece of modern Serious Sam content, but wow: what a great Serious Sam experience. While the engine is still very unoptimized, and very low frame rates are demonstrated when many enemies are on screen , as well as tons of delayed rendering of textures; the levels, assets, writing, and everything else are  This expansion does a really good job of showing the new Serious engine's graphical capabilities , and genuinely is the best looking game I've played in a while. Super impressive visuals are shown off at almost all times during the playthrough, and incredible attention to detail were put into ALL of the different environments, characters, weapons, and new enemies. This expansion basically feels like what Serious Sam 4 should've been:  And that's exactly what it is. to anyone that hasn't played any Serious Sam game before, and even more highly recommended to OG fans that have been waiting for a proper new Serious Sam experience for a long, long time.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a hard one to review. On one hand, this is probably the very best Serious Sam has ever been from a gameplay perspective. On the other hand, it is the absolute worst its ever been from a performance perspective. The performance does not even seem to use all of GPU processing available and is extremely CPU based. I respect the commitment to creating an entirely new from scratch engine instead of just using Unreal like everyone else, but it seems they bit off more than they can chew. If you're struggling with performance, I made a guide "how to fix stuttering" with some options that may help, but there are no guarantees. If you do end up playing the game, I would highly recommend also playing New Game +. The campaign is only around 7 hours, but the new game plus essentially remakes the entire campaign with all new enemy spawns where Sam starts off with all weapons and the early and mid levels have massive enemy counts that are not found in the first playthrough. Way more fun, but you probably shouldn't increase the difficulty as the massively increased enemy counts will increase the difficulty itself without having to change anything.P.s. If you don't unlock dual wielding first, you're playing the game wrong.

_childDocuments_.review: I wasn't a big fan of Serious Sam 4 so I went into this one with low expectations. However, Siberian Mayhem turned out to be a pretty serious game. I'd say I definitely enjoyed it more than the base SS4 and SS3 campaigns, which would for me put it still below TSE.What makes it good? I'd say the level design is a clear step up from SS4, the levels have more variety in them, and sidequests can take you to sections that feel like a different level. And the SECRETS ARE FINALLY CREATIVE! I'm all about the secrets. If a Sam game doesn't have good secrets it's not funky. There's a good amount of secrets that had a lot of effort put into them this time around, and the "classic" type secrets especially were my favorite. I went out of my way to explore every corner to make sure I found most of the secrets that I could. Last time I bothered to do that was probably with SS2.The new weapons and enemies are also solid and there's a fair amount of new gadgets and gameplay elements to set it apart from the base SS4. Also the levels definitely look prettier and more detailed than the base SS4 ones to me. There's also surprisingly good sound design, with a lot of ambient sounds all around adding to the mood (another thing that was missing from SS4 as far as I recall). The music is also pretty great, I liked pretty much all the level and battle themes. I could've sworn Sam's one liners were better too, there were a few I liked.Now the bad things; it's not a very long campaign, despite some of the levels being longer, it feels like halfway the length of SS4. Had the entirety of SS4 been made in this style, I think it would have been pretty good. Makes sense since it's a spinoff campaign made by a smaller team though. The story still follows Serious Sam 4's so a lot of stuff is already familiar from that game, along with the bad stereotypes etc, and it limits the scope of the levels. I played my playthrough on Hard difficulty, and I think there were some interior sections especially in the first levels that would have been quite annoying on Serious, since there isn't much room to dodge stuff and I felt like I had to tank hits sometimes. Otherwise difficulty felt pretty solid and by the end of the game I was all stocked up on unused gadgets.I think the quality of the campaign went up as it went on and my favorite level was probably Siberiade. There's still some stuff from SS4 that is still bad like completely massive (and empty) terrain areas that can make exploration annoying sometimes, but at least usually there isn't hidden stuff in every forest and you can clearly see if that's the way you're meant to be going in the first place. And you also get vehicles to make it a bit faster. But the vehicles can get stuck on tiny nooks on cliffs or the vegetation sometimes which was also annoying and cost me a couple reloads. The last level was allright but I preferred the ones before it, wasn't the biggest fan of the city sections with AI teammates. 4th level's tank section was actually pretty nice and one of the few vehicle sections that I liked.Also the last two levels and the final level especially had some weird heating issues on my machine. My fps overall was very good, 70 to 130 on Ultra settings in every level, but on the final level I actually had to limit my fps to 60 only because it was heating up my CPU so hard (up to 95 C while GPU was only 71 C), even on idle sections with no enemies. Another part that had fps drops / high CPU temps was the big fight at the end of the train station section in level 4. So maybe some optimization could be done there, at least on the final level, or then it's just the engine being weird (base SS4 also has way higher CPU temps than other games for me sometimes).TL;DRA significant step up from Serious Sam 4, but still limited by the base game with some of the same complaints. Would be nice to see a full length campaign in this style.

_childDocuments_.review: Whether or not you liked the base SS4, you have a high chance of loving this expansion. The only warning I would give is that it has all the same performance problems, so if you couldn't run SS4 well, you probably will have issues here.This campaign is SS4 concentrated, plus a bunch of things that people have been missing from it, such as more interesting level layouts or more unique fights. It's using SS4 as a solid base and asks, "now that we all know how SS4 works, and have experienced it fully, what interesting stuff can we do with it?". There's all sorts of cool situations, secrets, easter eggs, vistas, new enemies and weapons, new powerups, everything you could expect in a good Serious Sam game. If you thought SS4 was boring, you can expect to be pleasantly suprised with Siberian Mayhem. If you liked SS4, like I did, then all the more reason to play: this is more SS4, improved beyond what it already was.By the way, be sure to check out all the optional side missions, even if you don't use gadgets that they often reward you with: some of the best stuff is tucked away in optional paths. I'm serious: new locations, areas with unique music, very unique fights, secret bosses, all of that makes the optional objectives a must-play, so make sure to follow those cyan markers.In the interest of fairness, I want to say that the music, while good, I didn't think was on the level of SS4's soundtrack, and I did find myself missing the sunny warm locales of SS4; but Siberian Mayhem is not bleak and ugly - it's pretty, it's just got a different mood to it. And as already mentioned, the engine is still pretty slow and weird. My game had a habit of crahing upon trying to load a save, with upsetting regularity.Also, I wish the campaign was about two or three times longer. It goes by in such a flash. I suppose that's a testament to how enjoyable it is.TL;DRGameplay: much more creative and diverse than the main game, and just as solid;Graphics: quite often better than SS4's;Audio: the music is enjoyable, though arguably a bit less amazing than SS4's;Story: ??? Well, the ending is weird, and there are way less Rodriguez and Hellfire lines (none at all, actually), so...Recommended? Absolutely, beyond a shadow of a doubt.
