_childDocuments_.review: Serious Sam: Siberian Mayhem is an FPS that is a standalone expansion for Serious Sam 4 created by a new studio, Timelock Studios, that consists of veteran Russian Serious Sam modders.At its core, Siberian Mayhem plays like Serious Sam 4, so expect a lot of enemies on screen at once, a lot of firepower to take them down, and gadgets to give you a boost during battle. SS4 is one of the most solid entries in the series as far as gameplay goes, so Siberian Mayhem has a solid foundation. Siberian Mayhem contains new weapons:The game also has new enemies:Co-op is also included. Unfortunately, it caps the amount of players to four by default like Serious Sam 4 does. There is a mod that lets you bypass this.Like Serious Sam 4, the game has a skill system that lets you upgrade your character as you progress through the game, such as getting the ability to dual-wield various kinds of weapons. Skill points are found in special boxes in the game world, either normally or as secrets. The game takes Serious Sam 4’s skill level and improves it a little bit by having one of the early skills link to both the weapons and melee trees so you can invest in either tree easier. It’s a small but nice change that makes it easier to invest in a diverse set of skills instead of feeling like you’re fast-tracked to one part of the skill tree early on.Good levels are the lifeblood of a Serious Sam game, and Siberian Mayhem does not disappoint.The game consists of five levels, but these levels are long and packed with content. Levels will take around a minimum of 50 minutes to complete your first time around, and that’s for the shorter levels. Longer ones can easily take over an hour and a half to complete.Levels are a bit harder than the ones in SS4. The first level starts to throw large hordes at you a little bit before the halfway point and does not let up for the rest of the level. However, things really kick up in level 4, which is the most intense levels as far as combat goes. Right off the bat the game throws a huge horde at you on a mountainside and does not let up as you progress through the level. There are some breather fights later on to help you get your bearings, thankfully.There are also optional objectives that contain extra rewards and goodies at the end of them. You’ll want to do these because they contain a lot of great fights you’d otherwise miss. In fact, skipping the optional objective in the second level will make you miss a large area that has multiple fights in it! One of Serious Sam 4’s selling points was that it could handle gigantic levels. It did, but the large levels themselves really didn’t take advantage of the tech. Siberian Mayhem fixes this by adding a lot more enemies and adding enemy bases you can raid in that contain keycards that unlock a goodie at the end of the section. Level size combined with the enemies it throws at you makes going through huge levels feel like a journey instead of a tech demo, like SS4’s huge levels do.For secret lovers, this game is filled with all sorts of cool and useful secrets. The game’s secrets contain plenty of ammo and health this time around instead of being just gadgets over and over, like in Serious Sam 4, or boring parkour secrets with no good rewards, like in Serious Sam 3. There are also tons of wacky secrets, such as special mini-bosses that can’t be found anywhere else, a shine to a certain Serious Sam character, some throwback areas, and even a unique fight that pays homage to a game involving spirits and the sun! This game easily has the best secrets since The Second Encounter in both usefulness and humor.Some levels contain vehicle segments that are much improved over the ones in Serious Sam 4. The game’s sole mech section is vastly improved over the ones in Serious Sam 4 due to the fact that it’s much faster than the SS4 one and has a chainsaw melee weapon. The mech’s gun is a bit weaker than the ones the Serious Sam 4 mech has, but the mechs section throws far fewer strong enemies than the ones in SS4 did. The vastly increased speed makes SM’s mech section a blast. Running circles around enemies and hacking them up with a chainsaw is much more fun than slowly plodding forward and being forced to tank a ton of hits. Serious Sam: Siberian Mayhem is a fantastic entry in the Serious Sam franchise. The team that made it get what makes Serious Sam tick and know how to expand on the game in ways that Croteam didn’t with Serious Sam 4. It’s highly recommended for any FPS fan that loves high-octane action and/or has played SS4.

_childDocuments_.review: You know, when I heard a sudden Sam announcement being made by modders. I generally was not expecting anything good, having played and 100%'d Sam 4But having beat the game I can pretty much confidently say this is my Favourite of the main line series. and It pretty much improves on all the problems I had with Serious Sam 4The levels in Siberian Mayhem are some of the best designed in the whole series being both decently big while still interesting to explore. as well as have proper Enemy Encounter Designs where enemies feel like they properly compliment each other in each given encounter. (unlike Sam 4 where they were hastily slapped together).And even set pieces were generally improved like the Mech Section in the 2nd level which feels properly paced not out staying it's welcome before too long.The 2 new additional weapons (The crossbow and The Burner Ray Gun) are very fun to use, if not a bit overpowered. but they fortunately do not feel like a crutch and just another fun option for you to use.Now problems I have with the game is that at launch, it did perform a fair bit poorly. with some adjustments it ran alright but even then specific moments such as the final level still performed a fair bit poorly.The Devs have since updated the game and their most recent patch as of February 15th 2022 the game significantly performs better with some very minor hiccups during REALLY BIG Encounters.But something that is actually massively disappointing is that you do not get the Mini Gun till the VERY last level of the game and there is no secret to get it early like the other games. so you'll only ever get to use it near the end of the game, which does kinda suck imho. As well as far as I can tell, you can only get the Auto Shotgun only in a secret specifically near the end of Level 3 during it's optional objective, Which isn't nearly as disappointing cause it is a decent reward for exploring, as well as you pretty much have it for a good half of the game.But I think it's odd you have the auto shotgun for longer than you have the mini gun.and Personal disappointment which isn't too damning but is still saddening is the classic Laser Gun and Sniper do not make an appearance in the game at all. which I can understand the 2 new weapons are pretty much a replacement, least with the laser gun, I feel they still would've been fun option to have.But I feel this is an issue that will be mostly rectified once The Devs properly add workshop which I believe they've confirmed they're working on.Overall: I have no trouble personally recommending This game for it feels like a proper sequel to the Serious Sam games way more than Serious Sam 4, and Timelocks commitment to improving on the Performance Issues, as well as put genuinely time and effort into this game instead of shoving it out the door to make a profit much like Sam 4, shows that some Russian Modders care MORE about Serious Sam than Croteam themselves...Which is both funny and sad.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game! This takes Serious Sam 4, which was unfinished, and adds everything that was missing from it: good level design, good pacing, balance, additional vehicles and weapons, goofy secrets and gimmicks, and writing that isn't cringeworthy.You get 5 long levels packed with huge fights and the weapons you need to take care of all the enemies. There are old and new gadgets which are more balanced than just the "instant win button" that was the Black Hole in 4. The side objectives and secrets are fun and worth going for, and there is a subtle change to the skill tree that makes going for THAT one more viable.I didn't have any technical issues, except for the texture pop-in at the start of a cutscene.If you were turned off by the bad pacing in Serious Sam 3 or 4, give this one a try!

_childDocuments_.review: As a standalone game, it's difficult to rate this game since it felt more like a DLC for Serious Sam 4. I don't think it should have been released as its own game since there aren't many new things in terms of enemies or weapons. This lack of novelty could be why I didn't enjoy the game as much as I had hoped, especially since I started playing this shortly after I finished playing SS4. After dropping it and picking it up later I started to enjoy my time more.Although the visuals are a slight improvement from the previous game, the combat can feel repetitive and uninteresting due to the lack of new elements. However, one aspect that stood out to me was the variety of vehicles available and the multitude of creative secrets waiting to be discovered. The performance of the game still leaves something to be desired, which is disappointing given the game doesn’t look especially good. Overall, I would only recommend this game to those who have already played and enjoyed Serious Sam 4 and are hungry for more of the same.

_childDocuments_.review: Now, you either like Serious Sam games or you don't. If you do, this one is the game for you.Pros: - Well paced and fun gameplay - Ridiculous weapons, gadgets and vehicles - Much better visuals than previous same engine Serious Sam 4; at parts even stunning - Arctic setting in Siberia feels new and refreshing - Lot's of interesting bosses and easter eggs - Feels very full of content compared to Serious Sam 4 which was in parts empty - Voice acting is rather good, loved the voice of brand and the punsCons: - Animations are sometimes janky, especially in cinematics - Rather short (8 hours for me) - Texture popin and performance issues; only in cinematics for me, probably will be patchedLevels are challenging yet not frustrating; just right. Weapons are fun to use and vehicles ridiculous as they should be. Compared to Serious Sam 4 this one is much better paced and feels like it's full of content, everywhere you're able to you usually find something worthwhile.Easter eggs, while probably not exactly part of the game story and such itself, are also really top notch here. The dev team really put effort into those. Not everyone's cup of tea, but they really spiced up the experience for me.Visually this is much more appealing than Serious Sam 4 also. I felt the lighting was rushed in that previous game, but here they have perfected it, at parts making it even look stunning. Now graphically I wouldn't consider this game AAA quality, but it gets very close which is insane considering Croteam built the engine themselves.All in all I consider it to be one of the best installations in the whole series; I played through the whole game on one sitting.

_childDocuments_.review: While this game is technically intensive, and nowhere near as low end accessible as some of its Serious Sam predecessors, this game is outstanding. My original review was negative because of a launch bug that caused micro stuttering across low and high end rigs. The developers took this feedback seriously, and fixed the issue within a couple of days, so now I have almost nothing but praise to give. I'm personally sick of most modern games, and almost never have any excitement for new releases. SS3 was a disappointment, and I knew to skip SS4 entirely. I took a gamble and pre-orded this, and I am very pleased to say that I don't regret that choice. Serious Sam Siberian Mayhem might be the best Serious Sam game ever made, if not one of the best FPS games ever. Barring some small technical complaints, such as the awkward implementation of ladders, and some of the questionable handling choices made around vehicle control, this game is a master class in game design. The levels are scenic and extremely well designed. They heavily reward exploration, whilst having very straight forward objectives. They aren't confusing and look beautiful, even on low end settings. Especially if you are playing solo, you will notice that the enemy spawns have been very strategically placed to ♥♥♥♥ you up repeatedly, but there is a method to the madness which makes the difficulty satisfying to overcome. Even on Normal difficulty, you will encounter some level sections that provide a challenge, but if you aren't playing solo, the game is still a very satisfying co-op experience. Unlike other modern titles like Halo MCC made by AAA studios with Microsoft money, I have had no issues simply inviting a friend to my lobby and playing the game. The gun-play is excellent and only expands positively on the Serious Sam formula. The new guns feel extremely satisfying to use, and old weapons are complimented with a variety of alt fire modifications, which allow previously outclassed weapons like the single barrel shotgun to become a viable pick in a fight. The skill tree also allows for each player to mix up their play style and utilise weapons to become more effective in a variety of ways, suited to the players preferences. Everything sounds good looks good and feels good, with only the melee mechanics feeling occasionally dodgy, influenced by latency and the specific enemy types you engage with it. Without spoiling anything in specific, some of the new additions specific to each level don't overstay their welcome, and allow every level to provide a satisfying mix up of the expected Serious Sam formula. The idea of only getting five levels may seem off-putting on paper, but each level is very long and content rich, with optional side objectives and lovingly crafted secrets to discover. In addition, if this game is anything like its predecessors, it will support the Steam Workshop. At which point there is great potential for the community to expand the existing content in every way imaginable. If you have ever enjoyed Serious Sam and aren't on an incredibly low end rig, this is an absolute must buy. Every aspect of this game, down to niche environmental details of posters, features a great deal of love and flavor. It's extremely clear that the developers were passionate about this release, and its benefited heavily from Timelock having creative free reign over this title. Croteam should hand the Serious Sam reins over to Timelock and let them make every single Serious Sam release from now on. --------------------------------------------------------------------------

_childDocuments_.review: A great return to form after the somewhat disappointing Serious Sam 4! You can really see the passion that Timelock Studio has for this franchise and it definitely leaves you wanting for more by the end of this short adventure. The general game feel is way closer to the classic First and Second Encounter in terms of interesting and fun encounter design and the absolute abundance of ridiculous secrets to find, which I'd go as far as calling some of the best in the entire series! Some problems of the main game persist though, mostly the very poor optimization and the unbalanced nature of the gadgets, which make fights either way too easy when used or too frustrating when not. Though overall this is a really enjoyable FPS experience, especially if you're a fan of the classic games and don't mind some seriously shaky performance. I truly hope that Croteam is either taking notes or that they consider working with Timelock Studio again for a possible Serious Sam 5. (Also please consider ditching the gadgets for next time)

_childDocuments_.review: MIND BLOWN. WOW. For those unaware, I've put probably over 500 or so hours into the entire Serious Sam series, replaying the games constantly. It's my favourite series of all time and after hearing there was going to be a new game, a standalone expansion that is a mid-quel to SS4, I was super hyped. But wow, I had no clue how mind blowing and amazing this game was. In terms of the gameplay, Siberian Mayhem features yet again the same fantastic gunplay and carnage of Serious Sam 4, only dialed up to 11! There are WAY more enemies at points than in many points during SS4 and the game is seriously a great time if you just want to kill a bunch of things. The game visually is amazing at points especially with some of the weather effects that are in this game. The side quests in this game are absolutely brilliant, and there are so many moments that continue to humanize Sam which makes him so believable as a character. The performance Sam's voice actor gives might be the best of his entire career when voicing the character and I don't see how it can become any better.In terms of the story, it starts out as a mid-quel to SS4 as said, but things take a shocking, mind blowing turn at the end of the game, thus confirming the biggest twist in Serious Sam 4's climax that multiple timelines do in fact exist. This ending is so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ good, with it's high stakes emotions, massive major character deaths and excellent voice acting performances from the cast that it's hard not to love it. Every moment in my 4 Hour First Playthrough was just getting better and better and better, the characters they introduced I thought were awful and forgettable, made me warm up to them so much more like Carter did in SS4. The level design is masterful, Timelock Studios for their first project with Croteam did an absolutely incredible job with this game and these are some of the best levels the series has ever had.A MASTERPIECE. What else can I say? It might even outdo Serious Sam 4 in terms of my total enjoyment of the series. Serious Sam 4 had big twists and excellent gunplay and lovable characters, but the ending of this game absolutely blew my mind and I felt the emotions of all the characters in this game that it's hard not to recommend it. IT'S A MUST for fans of Old School Shooters and newcomers who have been playing Boomer Shooters as of recently. Here's hoping Timelock Studios does more Serious Sam games, because they might become the new masters if Croteam gives them the complete freedom to do whatever they want. Easily the best game I've played in 2022 and an early contender for my GOTY 2022. I love this series and this game showcases why.

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent expansion to an excellent game. I've seen comments that this is closer to the feel of  and  and I definitely feel that, but saying it's strictly a throwback would be misleading. It's more of a perfect blend of the old style and the  style, which itself was already a better blend of classic and new mechanics than  was. The first two levels definitely give you more of the  feel, where the levels in the main  campaign were more like punctuated bursts of action separated by exploration, the first few levels in  are tighter, more focused, and the action is pretty much always-on which will no doubt satiate fans of the older  titles. The third level and onward is more of a hybrid approach however, level 3 being an absolutely massive open sandbox that rewards exploration with multiple sidequests, and while later levels are tighter and more linear, they still have that big, exploratory feel with plenty of interesting diversions if you're willing to dig around. Generally the expansion puts more pressure on the player at a more consistent rate and makes for a good escalation from the main game.While the level  are strictly limted to what you can get in the areas around Siberia, the level  feels more diverse than perhaps any  game before this, verticality has never really been in Sam's repertoire, but the level designs here do a great job incorporating it in different spots and the design in a lot of places feels a bit more boomer-shooter-esque, particularly in the interiors where it feels very  or  inspired, albeit in a much larger capacity, and there are oldschool shooter staples like jump-pads to bounce you around in all sorts of fun ways.The arsenal also gets reworked and definitely feels more classical. The AK-47 operates a lot more like the Tommygun of old, and while my beloved Devastator is missing-in-action, you get a crossbow which is effectively identical to the  Sniper rifle and a laser flamethrower called the Burner which is possibly one of the most visceral and satisfying weapons I've used in an FPS.The story is smaller and simpler as it's meant to fill in part of 4, though by the end it gets a bit confusing. Still, Sam gets a lot of the same great human moments that I really enjoyed with 4 and has a new crew of wacky friends to accompany him. I think giving Sam allies to talk to is one of the best things 4 did for this character and while you don't have as long to fall in love with the supporting cast, the back-and-forth banter is still very welcome and the humor is still great.Both  and  have been excellent, and being finally done with the entire main-line  series my appetite is firmly whet for more. I think this franchise is in an incredibly good place and I can't wait to see what else is instore for good ol' Sam Stone.

_childDocuments_.review: This is hands down one of the best Serious Sam games. Surprisingly it wasn't even developed by main Croteam studio, but by the new developers Timelock Studio formed by long time Serious Sam modders. Let me tell you, they have some serious understanding of what makes a good Serious Sam game.Of course Siberian Mayhem couldn't be so good without strong foundations laid down by Serious Sam 4. It keeps all the great stuff from SS4 like dual wielding, vehicles, power items, big map and side quests, but learns from the missteps made by the main game. I think SS4 maps were too big and felt empty and unfinished at times, which I never felt was the case in Siberian Mayhem. Expansion's levels are very well designed and despite being big they are smartly "closed off" so you don't waste time looking for secrets in endless, empty map. On the topic of secrets, they are a lot of fun and thankfully include much less jumping puzzles. New secrets type include small, bonus stages cut out from classic Serious Sam games, retro graphics included. They are fun nostalgia bits, obviously inspired by the same type secrets included in new id Software games.Siberian Mayhem tones down the cutscenes and NPC interactions, which were overabundant in SS4. Instead, we get more cool one liners from Sam Stone himself, voiced as always by John J. ♥♥♥♥ (yes, he's killing it again). Talking about sound side of things, music in this expansion is great. It has the usual epic battle music Serious Sam series is known for, with a bit of Russian and Slavic influences thrown in. It goes together like vodka and pickles.I quite liked the graphics of Siberian Mayhem with its snowy wasteland, industrial complexes, abandoned villages and churches. Thankfully it doesn't go bore you with all the snow and keeps things varied and interesting all the way through, so expect more than just 50 shades of white color palette. It has quite a few amazing vistas, showing off snowy peaks and icy shores of Siberia. These are really nice moments of calm between all the mayhem.There are a few enemy and weapon variants added as well, with AK74 replacing M29 from SS4 and some enemies receiving reskins and reworks. We get to drive new vehicles as well, like portable hover scooter-turret and new mech with giant chainsaw attached. There are also a couple of new weapons including Crossbow and Raygun. While there are no major changes to the SS4 formula, these additions really help to freshen the experience.Performance wise Siberian Mayhem ran for me better than SS4, with pretty stable 60 FPS 1440p on GTX 1070. Still, I think this engine needs much better optimization. Doom Eternal is a gold standard in FPS games when it comes to performance and I hope Serious Engine reaches this level of polish with next installments.I wholeheartedly recommend buying Serious Sam: Siberian Mayhem. Its fairly priced, lengthy stand-alone expansion of SS4 that manages to improve on the original in many ways. This expansion reminds me of the olden days of gaming, when games were receiving these chunky, meaningful expansions instead of overpriced, worthless DLCs and Season Passes. I am all for this kind of quality content. Congratulations to Timelock Studios on their first commercial release! I'm looking forward to whatever you come up with next.

_childDocuments_.review: Croteam managed to redeem themselves. At least a little bit. Siberian Mayhem is definitely better than SS4 and in a way resembles the old titles. There are still some mistakes and weird decisions (e.g. where's the classic laser gun). Luckily the story and writing got much better. I still believe there shouldn't be any skill tree or gadgets since it ruins the gameplay. The point of SS always was to learn the rhythm of the fight, enemy patterns and fight hordes of enemies with guns. Where's the fun with using black hole or mini nuke? Some arenas are bit unbalanced and boring. The worst thing for me is the urban environment and setting in Russia. It feels boring, bland and uninspired. Especially in comparison to the amazingly unique and absolutely epic locations SS: FE and SS: SE. I can imagine SS5 - no ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ skills or gadgets. Every other game have something like that these days. Only focus to classics and fine tune it to perfection - shooting, epic fights and great locations (China, India, Japan can offer many interesting ideas). We could even visit some mystical lands like Shangri La. That could be really fun.

_childDocuments_.review: SS4 had some technical problems and some level design issues making the game feel flat and empty, hindering the pacing. _childDocuments_.review: Hard yes.This might be the best Serious Sam game I've ever played. It rights many of the wrongs that started to repeat themselves in Croteam's works following the original.The level design is top notch; open spaces are used thoughtfully, not just because Serious Sam tradition demands it. The sidetracking you can do in there helps fill out the spaces in the missions far better than the apocalyptically deserted deadzones of nothing that plagued 4. The look of areas is so distinct and fresh feeling compared to the usual Egyptian or urban decay looks that the series regularly wrapped itself in. The use of enemy variety and placement is some of the most fairly balanced I've seen. The new enemies really help flesh out the ranks and add extra layers of combat complexity in a challenging manner, enough that I'll probably miss fighting them.And grogs still suck, ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ grog rooms!If you liked Serious Sam and wished that it had produced something far better in the past decade than SS3 and SS4, then what are you waiting for? This feels like a labour of love and a proper fleshed out entry.Go get it! I haven't even finished yet and I can't wait to get back into the co-op run I'm on!

_childDocuments_.review: Short review - it is a more solid Serious Sam 4. Music is mostly fine, but I didn't find any tracks particularly banging. Plot is complete nonsense (especially if you consider ending). Engine still runs like sh#t (at least in maps 1 and 5, 2-4 seem to be pretty smooth), often stutters even on lowest graphics, framerate is inconsistent.But this thing is pretty much a love letter to old games with how levels are and I can't help but like it. Still more of the same, but it is good same. Really is what I'm looking for in Serious Sam games, so that would be something like 7.5/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Serious Sam: Siberian Mayhem

_childDocuments_.review: Serious Sam: Siberian Mayhem is not only one of the best games I have ever had the privilege of playing, but objectively one of the finest pieces of art humanity has ever produced. Every single element of this game has been masterfully constructed by the team of artisans at Croteam. The gameplay loop of running, shooting, running. shooting and running has never felt so refined. The Legion System has been so skillfully implemented that I can say with absolute confidence that gaming has been forever revolutionized. The music is so good, I swear to you I had an orgasm in my pants. CAME! The story is absolutely captivating, and I am without a doubt a better man, citizen and human being after witnessing it. I ran through the gambit of emotions connecting with Sam Stone: excitement, anger, fear, surprise, and true euphoria. The visuals were so advanced, that in many portions of the campaign I could not distinguish what was on screen from actual reality. This game is digital ecstasy.My final review: 10/10, better than sex, buy 4 copies and give them to others in the same way Christ spread the word of the lord. Praise be to God.

_childDocuments_.review: Definetely not recommended.Overall slightly better than just acceptable.A step forward from SS4 but still really bad.Poor optimiaztion, poor level designs, lacks balance, stupid final boss.Take it on a huge sale, speedrun on normal, probably with friends, may be fun that way.In more details:- Poor optimization but playable- you or enemies can sometimes stuck in textures, you can see through some walls etc but no much problems if you stick to the road and don't look in the corners searching for secrets- same stupid skills system as in SS4: skill tree suggests choice but you don't have because without dual wield you will be overwhelmed; monsters hordes size is adjusted so that you lack firepower even with dual wield- same stupid gadgets system as in SS4: there are tooo many of them and they are tooo powerful, so some battles are adjusted to force you to use them- new monsters: burner's attacks deal high damage while hard to spot and hard to dodge frequently resulting in being one-shot from nowhere; tower's rockets barrage is not fully dodgeable by sidestepping, turning aside and sprinting doesn't help either, although rockets looks same as those of large bio-mechanoid- level design: some levels are too big and wide, even with vehicles that are really extra to this game, sometimes you just have to spend several minutes to run to secret location and return back, in case if there is unexpected monster fight you don't get autosaved and have to run again, manually saving before the fight resulting in lower score or spend more time running in case of death. So the only thing you want is just run straight ahead till the end of level faster- level design - combat: while inside the buildings everything is pretty good; while outside, which is most of the game, especially last levels, you can fallback almost to the begging of the level, which you have to do because most of the weapons even with dual wield don't let you counter enemies, so mostly you just run backwards and you can do that so long that sometimes you have enough time to finish entire wave with dual pistols. Classic Sam is about fights in wide but limited space, forcing you to circle around and create space for yourself rather than just running backwards until the start of the level; allowing player to get back to gather items that were left while full is not a good idea either- final boss is horrible and is the only one (except secrets which are good) - attacks not fully dodgeable by sidestepping, so you may get hit if you did everything write; most attacks deal 100 damage on serious difficulty leaving no chance to make a mistake or even learn boss attacks mechanics; most gadgets don't really work on boss or have incredibly low effect, you have little time between attacks to activate them; the boss has relatively low hp with small arena and low number of pickups resulting in quite short fight- game is very short and I really doubt you will want to complete it again, try accomplish achievements that involve starting from the begging - e. g. find all secrets, read all notes, complete last level on serious difficulty without saves mid-battle or whatever; no extra content like challenges (survive as long as possible on small map with infinite waves of enemies)Good points:- the game starts very actively with decent fights even on the first level- story and other characters are simple but fun, Siberia layout and Russian comrades are atmospheric- good audio - effects, music both in-combat and outside of it- somewhat fun secrets

_childDocuments_.review: A sub 3-hour standalone DLC to Serious Sam 4, while trying to fix some of issues of the original, doesn't hold any better:- The technical aspect of the game hasn't changed at all. The graphics are still nothing amazing, while the performance is utterly ridiculous. It feels like every step you make, the engine pulls up an RNG to decide how much frames to draw. Whenever too many enemies spawn, the game can genuinely freeze for a whole second or two. - The gameplay is much worse than older SS games, on both visual and mechanical level. Sprinting makes you almost completely invincible, so most enemies have homing projectiles and lead their shots. What's the point of having 100+ enemies on the screen if the game can only process 10 blood decals and body parts at the same time? Blowing up a big crowd of gnaars just to see all the viscera fall through the floor and the bloodstains vanish in an instant is super cheap. Serious Sam HD remakes do this so much better, having come out whopping 13 years prior. Wow!Even more importantly, what's the point of having 100+ gnaars simultaneously on-screen, when it adds nothing to the gameplay beside freezes? - The level design sees a 50/50 split between huge empty swards or snowy fields, populated by at most a hundred odd enemies, most of which are low-tier trash that evaporates in a couple of cluster grenades, and rather tight industrial/urban corridors that are easy to get overwhelmed in. The russian hinterland aesthetic is slighly more exotic than SS4's generic vistas, but are nevertheless nothing to write home about.- The soundtrack is a quite a lot better, but whether or not it actually fits the visual theme of the game is debatable.- Most 'new' enemies are just varieties of the old ones seen in SS4, and some of them, notably the hoppers (frog-dogs) are incredibly annoying to fight against, instead of being fun.- The new weapons are, by and large, just reskins that replace the older ones: AKM for Tommy Gun, Perun Crossbow for Devastator and Beam Cannon is an XL2's free-standing Deathray mode. Nothing unique or particularly interesting.- The game still offers a few vehicle sections (why is there an Abrams tank in the Russian countryside?) and, albeit just one, another brain-dead W+M1 mech section, and even a modest assortment of pipe puzzles. Pipe puzzles in a Serious Sam game... uh-huh.- The final boss battle is actually pretty good, unlike the let-down that is SS4's bullet-spongling.- The cringey storyline is still in town, with even more second-rate puns and turn-of-the-century cutscene animations.Staying with and fixing SS4 would've been a better call for the dev. Better yet - figuring out what made the older games good and making the most of it.Not worth your money.

_childDocuments_.review: Since everyone has already forgotten about Serious Sam 4, a marketing decision was made to sell this product as a standalone.This is essentially a 5 level pack for Serious Sam 4 which is canon to the base game, sold as a seperate product. This is probably the single worst thing about Serious Sam: Siberian Mayhem.The actually levels are well made and in line with the quality Serious Sam 4 offers, but having this content as a seperate game is extremely inconvenient.I would have much rather paid the same exact price for a DLC which is integrated into the base game so the player can seamlessly experience the full game from start to finish.They'll probably release a "Fusion DLC" or "Gold Edition" down the line when eveyone has moved on with their lives, which will include the base SS4 game along with this expansion pack.2 seperate games means reconfiguring ALL your settings, not to mention redundant game assets which need to be downloaded twice if you have both games installed. It's just an annoying cash grab that was ultimately unnecessary.Further, as many others have mentioned, work needs to be done to optimize the game engine. You can have good hardware and still experience frame drops all over the place.Croteam seems to take great pride in their engine, but the fact of the matter is it has it's shortcomings. Unreal Engine would have simply been a better idea and would have yielded better performance across the board, among other things.With all this said, the game itself is fun and the levels are well designed as are the bosses and enemies. _childDocuments_.review: This review is written by someone who has enjoyed the Serious Sam experience since The First Encounter released in 2001. I love a good run through the HD remakes when I get the chance and several of my friends will play through the game in co-op when we all have the urge. But I just don't think this particular installment is ready for primetime.This entry in the Serious Sam catalog is a mere 5 levels and they are really more of a side quest for the events in Serious Sam 4. This would probably have been a better product if it were a $5 to $10 DLC instead. It feels similar in content and style to Jewel of the Nile for Serious Sam 3: BFE. As such, this follow the same newer art style as 3 and 4 as opposed to TFE and TSE. (Let's just continue to pretend that Serious Sam 2 never happened, shall we?) All of this adds up to a game that I feel was a little bit overpriced, though you get a discount if you own Serious Sam 4, as long as that deal doesn't expire. But that's not necessarily enough to warrant a "Not Recommended" review from me.The performance in the latter half of the game was unacceptable for me. As mentioned, there are 5 levels in this game. The first three played as you would expect, but the performance was horrible for the fourth and fifth levels. The game was constantly stuttering. Some modern games are plagued by micro-stutters due to the modern paradigm of "load in only what you need and only when you need it" causing constant loads to happen in the background. I can accept that to a point, but as an experiment, after multiple battles, I just sat idle. To test. The game wouldn't play for more than ten seconds or so before a "freeze" of up to an entire second. Sounds would continue to play in these periods if I were shooting or if enemies were attacking, but no movement, animations, or music would be playing at all. The computer I play on isn't terrible (AMD 8-core 3.9GHz, 32GB RAM, RTX2070 Super, game installed on a SSD separate from the OS SSD) and I don't have any problems with other games, which is why I'm so critical of the performance here. The experience went from a "Recommended with caveats" to an incredibly unenjoyable experience that I can't recommend in the game's current state.I'm always a fan of Serious Sam games. They're hectic and irreverent with enough action to keep those of us who grew up with fast-paced shooters like Ultimate Doom happy. But at the current time (Patch 1.03c), I recommend sitting this particular one out. I'd be happy to try again if there are any patches that mention fixing issues that sound like these, but for now, I'll head back to TFE and TSE.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all I have not personally played Serious Sam 4. My impressions are based on watching a review.But when people refer to this game as the superior version of SS4, they are pretty much saying that they prefer burning to death over drowing. Both are horrible.I might be biased since I have a soft spot for the original Serious Sam: The First and Second Encounters, but this game is nothing like old ones. But then again, neither are Serious Sam 3 or 4.Since SS3, the series has attempted to shift towards a more realistic approach, but losing much of what made the original games appealing in the process. This shift is most apparent when the game tries to create a serious atmosphere by relying on minute-long cutscenes immediately after or before absurd, comedic moments, such as spawning a holy kamikaze.This trend has continued into the latest entries, where the game borrows heavily from popular titles like Doom Eternal instead of sticking to its roots. The Serious Sam franchise once thrived on chaotic, mindless fun, but now seems intent on blending emotional storytelling and deeper character development—both of which feel out of place. Characters are introduced as if they’re meant to play a significant role in Sam’s life, only to be killed off within 30 minutes, rendering their presence meaningless and their emotional weight nonexistent.Gameplay elements have also taken a strange turn, with questionable weapon distribution that doesn't make much sense. Stronger weapons are often obtained early on, making the weaker ones obsolete. Ammo is abundant, so there’s no real challenge in resource management, and no reason to switch between different weapons to deal with specific enemy types. Instead, players can just use the most powerful weapon they have. There’s also a glaring mismatch in weapon variety relative to the game’s length—likely because the arsenal was borrowed from Serious Sam 4, which was a longer game where the number of weapons made more sense.The inclusion of a skill tree is another feature that feels entirely unnecessary. Many of the skills seem irrelevant or useless, with odd features like being able to pick up street signs and use them as melee weapons. It’s hard to understand why this mechanic was even implemented, as it doesn’t add anything to the gameplay. Similarly, the introduction of vehicles feels forced and out of place, often serving as nothing more than a way to traverse large, empty areas or move containers around, without contributing anything meaningful to the core experience.Another unwanted change is the addition of NPCs companions in certain sections. They cannot die and deal insignificant damage, making them feel like mere story props. This breaks the core appeal of Serious Sam, which has always been about Sam being a one-man army, single-handedly fighting off hordes of enemies.Sam’s third-person animations have never been a strong suit for the franchise, but now that the game places a heavier emphasis on story and cutscenes, these stiff and poorly executed animations are more noticeable than ever. The lack of polish extends to the game's combat as well—when enemies are gibbed, the aftermath is unsatisfying, with almost no blood decals spawned and blood clouds that vanish into thin air.Lastly, while there are no game-breaking bugs, numerous minor glitches throughout the experience add to the overall sense of the game feeling unpolished. Combined with the game's relatively short length.It is trying to be something it’s not. Serious Sam has lost much of what made it fun and distinct in the first place.

_childDocuments_.review: What many thought would be DLC actually turned out to be a full-blown standalone expansion, so here’s my quick review for Serious Sam: Siberian Mayhem.If you’ve ever played a Serious Sam game before, you know what to expect gameplay-wise. You get a bunch of guns and a bunch of enemies to shoot with those guns, oftentimes in big wide-open areas. Siberian Mayhem is pretty much more of the same with slight additions to this formula. The weapons are plentiful and fun to use, the enemy designs are varied, and there’s a nice sense of challenge behind it all even on normal difficulty.The core to a good Serious Sam game is there and all the bonuses like vehicles, gadgets, and side content to find only add to that. That said, not all of the new content lands. One of the big new enemies, for example, feels like a direct contrast to the run-and-gun nature of the gameplay. It’s called the sentry tower and it’s basically a giant orbital laser / homing missile tower hybrid that you cannot take down like a traditional enemy. Instead, you have to wait for it’s core to open after it finishes an attack cycle and only then can you attack it before it closes again and repeats the process.Whereas most (rather, all) enemies require you to run, jump, and swap around weapons constantly, this enemy requires you to stop, wait, and carefully target a weak spot - it’s a bit too slow for what I would normally expect from a Serious Sam game and easily my least favorite enemy to fight.The new weapons are at least cool though, the crossbow being a personal favorite. Otherwise it’s the same old gameplay. It can get a bit repetitive, but Siberian Mayhem is short enough that it didn’t at least go overboard. It took me just over three hours to clear all five levels - although that’s only with 30% achievement completion.My main complaints are actually with the technical side of things. Because while the gameplay is fine, I had so many smaller issues running the thing that it became rather frustrating. I have a brand new 5800x and 3080 Ti and the game installed on an NVMe drive, but that didn’t stop me from running into numerous massive frame drops, microstutters, and even outright freezes that lasted seconds at a time. I started at the highest settings, but found myself continuously dropping them lower as I played to try to accommodate for these technical issues.I would go from my fps cap of 155 fps all the way to 40 and then back constantly, especially during scenes where tons of enemies were on-screen (which happens a lot given this series). I still managed to clear the game, but I cannot deny that the constant technical issues really brought down the experience.The gameplay is fine (although not without issue), but I cannot in good faith recommend the game given all the technical issues I ran into. I can only imagine how much worse said issues would be on weaker hardware, so this is definitely one to wait for patches on or at least go in with tempered expectations.Follow my  for more reviews + videos!

For what it cost, it's a solid several-hour feast of blood, mayhem and silly stuff.I felt like the game design could've been improved; the last few weapons were either the best possible answer to all problems, or totally not worth spending time with, and the upgrade system should've given us more possible routes / tools to play with: double-jumps, speed increases, double shots, etc., would've really added some interesting endgame choices.  As it was, it felt like a bunch of the skill upgrades were mandatory and I couldn't get them all, so I took the ones that were obviously best.Overall, it did a great job confronting the player with massive hordes of enemies and varied the settings enough to keep from getting totally boring.  There are two sections where the player gets to use Very Special Powers, and they're both really fun; frankly, I would've enjoyed more of that, and less of just being Sam.But, after all the disappointing junk I've played in the last two years, it was genuinely nice to play a game that didn't try to be something it wasn't, didn't pander to <insert political crap here> and was straightforward fun.  Great job and I certainly hope Croteam works with these folks in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a long-time fan of the Serious Sam series, having played since the early pre-release Karnak demo of the original Serious Sam.  I would say I quite enjoyed the series up to and including even Serious Sam 2, despite it's wonky writing and aesthetic.  I even somewhat enjoyed Serious Sam 3 and 4, but I found 4 marred by technical issues that undermined my experience.I saw that this stand-alone release was getting good reviews from some outlets, so I decided to give it a try.  Not only are the technical issues of Serious Sam 4 present in this release, but they seem to be exacerbated and far worse than I remember from my experience with SS4.  Frame drops and stutters are near constant and severe, often doubling or tripling time between frame renders.  There has even been times where my 99th percentile frame rates drop from above 80 to 10 or single digits while my GPU and CPU aren't even being fully utilized.  To say that it is unoptimized would be an understatement.  To say that the technical issues completely ruins the experience is more accurate.  I played this literally months after the game originally released, making the prospect of anything resembling proper performance being patched in a delusion at best.  Don't waste your money or your time with this shoddy software.

_childDocuments_.review: A standalone DLC for Serious Sam 4 made by a team of Russian Serious Sam fans and honestly - it's not that good. Most of the positives about this game are just carried over from Serious Sam 4, and the people who say that the level design is "better than Croteam in SS4" are on crazy juice or just are biased because of all the Russia in the game.For almost as much as the original game costs you get 5 levels, which are longer than SS4, but kind of feel too long - because you only get like 4 environments with it (an oil plant, a forest, a village, and a city) and trying to make 5 levels feeling like an entire SS game means that like 40% of the game is just "opening segment" with very limited weapons and enemy variety. And anyone criticizing SS4 for some big, but empty levels should be trash-talking this one because they got a lot of that. You get 2 "new" weapons - the crossbow is just the sniper rifle and the new laser is kind of fun, but it's just a less powerful version of the original laser's alt fire - which is stupidly OP in tight spaces. You also don't get the Devastator and the Auto Shotgun at all."New enemies" are a scam. You get fanatics that are even more invinsible from the front and very idiotic stationary towers that kill the pacing. There are also a couple of minor new enemies like octavian grenadiers, the laser pyros, and the hopping frog-dog things that don't introduce anything new, gameplay-wise they're the same as existing enemies. There are also "boss enemies" that are just upgraded versions of regular enemies, which is the least creative design ever. The final boss is kind of cool, but it's like a character action boss in an FPS which means just circle-strafing him and throwing your inventory at him.The encounter design kind of sucks. A lot of the game is almost DOOM with smaller encounters in tight spaces and two straight-up DOOM arenas with jump-pads and such. That doesn't work in a Sam game. And not counting the overlong sections in OP vehicles (there are two) there are very few massive encounters with huge and interesting hordes. Most of it is corridors which are easily solved by the new laser's OP characteristics. Also, the cluttered design of the arenas constantly gets in the way, ever seen a cannonball bounce off a tree so small it's basically transparent?The story is summarized as "Russian fanboys write a Serious Sam filler fanfic", full of "boy, Russia sure is stereotypically Russia, but in a cool way", some Russian inside jokes, and a "definitely not a self-insert character".Overall, it's not horrible, just below average, and not worth its current price. But at least you get some unintentional comedy out of it because all those "Russia stronk memes" aged amazingly.

_childDocuments_.review: Full disclosure…I did not complete this game, nor did I even get that far into it.  I played about two hours and don’t think I even completed the first chapter before I rage-quit and uninstalled the game.  So, if there is a reasonably fun game beyond the first level I’ll never know, and I blame the designers 100% for creating one of the worst opening levels of any FPS game I’ve played…maybe ever.  The sheer imbalance of weapons, monsters, and pick-ups is ridiculous, combined with level design that totally breaks away from the openness of past games that encouraged lots of backpedaling and continuous fire to defeat wave after wave of enemies.  This might look like a Serious Sam game, but it sure doesn’t feel like it.It seems Serious Sam: Siberian Mayhem is trying to change up the core gameplay by creating more complex levels and stationary enemies that don’t come after you but would rather stand still and shoot or lob fire balls from a distance.  Admittedly, some enemies will still come at you including this new dog-frog hybrid that is nearly impossible to hit.  Backpedaling is much harder now since the levels are more complex and it’s easier to get hung up on the architecture; especially when you are running blind. Weird scripting issues prohibit monsters from entering the water, so you can simply escape into the surf and kill from relative safety as long as you don’t drown.  The first level was a mix of a lengthy beach section followed by a short hike up to a plateau where a major battle triggered, as I made my way to a communication tower.Once I entered the factory complex the game started going downhill fast.  The sheer number of enemies coming at me was so disproportional to the weapons and ammo I was being given I was often backpedaling completely out of the factory with only a pistol to defend myself.  Thankfully, enemies are finite, so I was eventually able to progress further into the facility, but the maze-like alleys between buildings, narrow corridors, bridges, and confining room-sized arenas had me giving up about the time I was put into a small area with about 50 Kleer and a shotgun.  After 30 minutes of trying to clear this room, I was scrambling for the uninstall button.  I simply didn’t care anymore.  I had pretty much gotten my fill of Sam in his previous game and couldn’t imagine this expansion offering me anything worth suffering through this frustration.Full review at More Steam reviews on our Curator page -

_childDocuments_.review: The fact that most players (92% of reviewers, at least) could be satisfied by such lazy level design when the old games were so tightly constructed is beyond me.  Did anyone even notice that most "idle" enemies (beheaded standing on roofs or enemies spawning behind the player in elevated spots) have broken AI and just stand there doing nothing? The carefully constructed "ganks" that existed in the old games are not present here (even though they were intended to occur) due to this ever-present technical issue.The old games made a point about smart and tongue-in-cheek level design by assaulting the player from interesting angles and presenting challenges in ways not confined to the number or type of enemies. You could feel the personality of the level designers coming through during many of the iconic and memorable moments in those games, and it was obvious that a lot of TLC was put into those sections. SM tries to recapture some of those moments, but every attempt to do so comes off as a poorly designed, semi-broken pale imitation.  A good example is SM's attempt to recreate the infamous "frog pit" from SS:FE.  In the old game, it was a tough-as nails gauntlet requiring you to have precise aim and movement since these little frogs were faster than the player and many in number. This was the only enemy type that spawned in this section, which allowed the player to focus on the unique challenge at hand, while generating a few laughs and some broken controllers. Even the way the frogs entered the arena by yeeting themselves off a platform added to the humorous personality of the section. In SM, the re-imagined "frog pit" is sparsely populated by a small number of large frogs that are slower than the player and easily kitable, while the real enemy-- some kleers and a few beheaded are thrown into the mix. There is nothing funny or iconic about this section in SM. The frogs are no longer the cute little imposing threats that they once were, removing the humor and tension from this section completely. They simply pop in at random on the floor of the arena are are best ignored for the first half of the fight. The addition of other enemies only serves to make the new "frog pit" feel more mundane and par for the course, rather than surprising, horrifying, hilarious and iconic.Enemy behavior used to be snappy, responsive and carefully scripted, but now the AI struggles to get its bearings straight for a few moments after spawning, leading to sloppy and random-feeling wave patterns.  This is exacerbated by the fact that the wave compositions themselves are now a hodgepodge of random enemy types haphazardly spawned around the player in an open field with no rhyme or reason.  One of the things that made the old games fun was how waves used to be clearly telegraphed and homogenized (think hearing a large group bulls spawn inside of a temple then come barreling down a hundred flights of stairs at the player in a neat wedge formation, followed some moments after by a line formation of kleers). Enemies reacted instantly and predictably upon spawning and did not really break formation until they reached the player.  This made arenas feel choreographed, deliberately designed and fun to learn.  This type of design has been eschewed for chaotic enemy vomit in an open field, which is lazy and thoughtless (anyone can mindlessly slap down a bunch of spawners in a big open square with no forethought as to how the flow of the game is affected).  Add in the fact that scripting and enemy pathing is a mess, and the results are levels that feel incredibly amateurish. And by god are those open levels downright as ugly as an old CS:S custom map.  And it's about as optimized as my friend's old high school Unity 1.0 project.The old Sam games were much smarter than many currently realize and can be used as a textbook case on how to create FPS maps that are intrinsically fun to play. SS4 and SM completely fail to understand how the source material's genius level design carried the experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Non original creators made better Serious Sam, but that's still not a "good" Serious Sam. My main complaint is still levels and locations - in FE and SE you had egyptian temples, pyramids, Karnak, indian temples, freakin Babylon, frozen lake, castles and so on. And here? Snowy plain, snowy plain, and then a plain without snow. Great level design, I can't wait to play more. And what's with the open areas all the time? Original Serious Sam had those mixed with closed locations where exploration was a little bit slower, but you had secrets, traps, and it wasn't all like "let's fight a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ of absolutely random enemies spawned all at once". I hate that. Literally I feel like every open-area fight is just randomized. You have snipers, drones, vampires, pyros and two damn helicopters spawned all at once. There's no tactic to that, no thought. I had to camp in a church and kill everyone one by one while going out and in all the time not to die in a mere second. That's not a good Serious Sam game, tho it's better than Serious Sam 4.

_childDocuments_.review: Serious Sam: Siberian Mayhem is, more or less, Serious Sam 4 set in Russia.It features the same gameplay mechanics, skill tree, weapon feel, and enemies (with 3 or 4 exceptions that you'll encounter only once each).However, there are some improvements.The graphics look okay now—no longer odd, unpolished, and incredibly buggy as they were in Serious Sam 4. No more textures randomly fading away or getting pixelated out of the blue.The game is stable, with no more crashes or random frame drops.And, unlike in some levels of Serious Sam 4, the objective marker points in the right direction this time.Level design is really nice and genuinely feels like Eastern Europe, which I really appreciate.Unfortunately (or fortunately, depending on one's point of view), the game is really short. At just under 5 hours, it feels more like a DLC than an actual standalone game. This didn’t really bother me, as I found Serious Sam 4 quite repetitive, boring, and a little too long for what it was, but it could have been 2-3 hours longer.Overall, it is indeed an improvement over Serious Sam 4.
_childDocuments_.name: Serious Sam: Siberian Mayhem

_childDocuments_.review: This was the usual boomer shooter I've come to expect, and although short in terms of episodes, it compensates for the length of each episode. The inclusion of puzzles to open chests (don't recall if previous SS iterations had that) was a pleasant distraction. Interestingly, the inclusion of NPCs fighting alongside you was unexpected, since I was so accustomed to winging it out by myself.One annoying thing about Serious Sam: Siberian Mayhem is that your vehicles can't pass through or demolish features like trees, which makes it annoying AF when trying to deal with enemies while driving. But I suppose it's to be expected, since nothing is ever easy in the series.True to the franchise's form, the Serious difficulty level is as described. It was pleasurable enough to blast, maim and sometimes stab my way through waves and waves of enemies. Plus the brief bit on the last level where you have to sort of ice-skate through mobs was unexpectedly fun.Now, for its drawbacks. Serious Sam: Siberian Mayhem's enemies, particularly the Kleer Skeletons, seem to have a noticeable problem with pathing, which is not too much of a hassle but is noticeable enough to speak of. But the most bizarre incident occurred on the fourth level.  Were it not for the fact that I ploughed through  I might have stopped playing altogether.Since I can say I got my money's worth, I won't downrate Serious Sam: Siberian Mayhem. But I just wish Steam had the option of leaving neutral reviews instead of either positive or negative only. The  certainly put a dampener on things.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: - Sam is back! - More straight forward run and gun type of fun - Abundant health and ammo to get the job done - More abundant upgrades points - Unique and enjoyable side missions - Fantastic environments and weather effects - New game+ - Drive a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ tank!Cons: - Huge, HUGE spike in difficulty with the final bossI hope I'm not biased because of the reviews I watched before playing, but Siberian Mayhem is a BIG improvement after Serious Sam 4. It's almost perfect actually. I had so much fun wiping out hoard after hoard of enemies. There were moments where I felt tremendous power and the confidence to push forward instead of running backwards for once. And then there were moments where I was surprised to have survived at all in the all the chaos and gore. And I think they ended it at the right time before the fighting could turn a little stale.My one gripe: the boss was waaaay too hard IMO. I played the game on normal up to this moment and died soooo many times trying to make it work. I tried learning the move sets, but it just felt like I couldn't dodge his hits and had didn't have any helpful artifacts to help. I finally relented and lowered the difficultly and still barely beat him after a couple more tries. I'll probably play it again though and give it another shot with new game+

_childDocuments_.review: Expansion pack or not. It's BETTER THAN SERIOUS SAM 4!!!I really like the campaign, although I don't think there was really a need of a story, like in SS4. Story could be something like SS3's. Whatever though, I ain't complaining. The new weapons are great. I love the crossbow and the Raygun, not to forget the AK 74! Which for some reason has a picatinny rail. There's a lot to explore compared to SS4. Really like the idea of Octanian Sentry towers, they're fun! Exploring was really fun for me too, considering how boring it is in SS4... atleast for me. The visuals are slightly better than SS4, primarily because of the use of various effects, but hell, the skybox is great. Workshop also consists of pretty good maps. Although still it's lacking quite a bit of content, but it's worth checking out. Definitely had more fun than SS4, I'd prefer this over SS4 any day of the week. SS4 is better in terms of Workshop though, some really great stuff in there, so I'd only prefer it if you really are into workshop content, if not, then Siberian Mayhem's campaign rocks. Don't get me wrong though, Siberian Mayhem's workshop is good too, but it's lacking quite a bit of content as said earlier, nonetheless, most of the maps are worth checking out. Overall recommended!

_childDocuments_.review: To be honest, I didn't expect much after how lame Serious Sam 4 turned out to be, but Siberian Mayhem managed to present much better performance, soundtrack, battles and probably two the best bosses of the entire franchise. The game remains true to itself, with all the one-liners, epic fights, "secret item traps" and adrenaline. The soundtrack is great, had a blast playing the base game and the survival mode as well. Side missions have become more creative and stressful but the rewards make taking these battles worthwhile.The only thing I personally think as a drawback from previous Serious Sam titles, from which 4 suffered as well, is the bad AI teammates that we get, to fight on our side, which definitely helps at times but they are just unnecessary. I may not win all the battles but that's one aspect of what makes me want to play Serious Sam. I played through the first 3 Serious Sam titles in Serious difficulty without having AI by my side and yes it was tough, yes it would have been helpful on a lot of occasions but for me, it just takes away from the experience. However, the developers improved almost every aspect of what made Serious Sam 4 a one-time and forgettable experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I never finished . I finished  and I had a blast but the almost jerk-like secrets spawning enemies right behind you and stripping away all the health and armour you had painstakingly stockpiled up to that point time and again wore away at me. Eventually, I got so fed up with it in  that I just put it down and never picked it back up.I was always curious about , though. Its smaller price point compared to  reminded me of , which I loved, and its similarly good reception on Steam raised my interests more. I eventually got it and, yeah, I love how much more friendly it feels compared to earlier games. In many ways,  does a lot to challenge the old ways of thinking with  in a fashion that makes it more surprising and fun to play while still being challenging and awe-inspiring with its hordes to shoot. Honestly, I don't think I can go back and play older s while this exists.The biggest illustration of differences in this regard is secrets.  games have always had creative secrets but  blows all previous entries out of the water. Well, the first two s, at any rate; I haven't played the others. But I like how the secrets in  actually feel like secrets that reward you with not just more ammo and inventory but actual jokes and funny moments that stick out in your mind, and exist to do more than just screw you over.In other ways than just secrets,  has always felt a bit cruel in a cheeky way.  is gruelling but in its own way and it feels a lot more fair, especially in terms of enemy placement. I've always hated Arachnoids in earlier games for being like "Hey, we're just going to throw these minigun-wielding hitscan jerks at you. Be sure to wipe them out before the battle really starts lest you get your health stripped away while those blasted Kleer jump you again, eh?" while, in , they're a lot more sparse, they spawn in places that are typically right in front of you, and they are often alone. They often do go down before they fire a shot, and I appreciate that because they are jerks. That said,  does carry over a lot of elements from older games that I'm not sure really work in the long run. I don't know why  needs to have three different shotguns because they're basically the same weapon but distinctly better and worse in ways that mean I really don't want to use that awful old shotgun when the coachgun actually one-shots those bastard Kleer. I would love to use the autoshotgun more but it bloody sucks; it's underpowered and ammo's too sparse. Why does it have its own ammo type, anyway? I reckon I darn well should be using regular shells with this thing. But this would all be solved by having new shotguns  the old ones and not take up more space on my gun selection wheel that I need to memorise. On that note, the minigun is something I want to use all the time; let me use the AK47's ammo for it because I do not want to use the AK while I have a perfectly good minigun right there.There's also a sniper weapon in this game and it runs into the typical problem that a precision weapon for hitting headshots against enemies doesn't work in a fast-paced boomer shooter, let alone one with as many enemies as . The distance of the maps gives it an excuse to be around but it just doesn't fit into the gameplay. It really only exists to deal with those blasted Octavian Snipers, who are almost as bad as early Arachnoids because the sniper is really the only way to reliably hit those small, distant targets without overkilling them.Having said that about the sniping weapon, the presence of alt-fire mechanics alongside dual wielding is an odd one. I think dual wielding is a fun concept that not only fits the visual style of  gameplay well—not to mention the personality of Serious Sam himself—but, strategically, it allows Sam to combine his different weapons to effectively have a primary fire and a secondary fire of his choosing against the mixed enemies of Mental's hordes... except dual wielding gives you a massive accuracy decrease for ballistic weapons  some of your weapons actually have cool alternative firing modes. Your multi-rocket launcher is able to load up to five rockets and lock onto up to five enemies, which is really cool for dispatching Major Biomechanoids, but you can't use alt-fire modes while dual wielding. You can't zoom in with your sniping weapon to accurately aim at distant targets and you can't lock on with your rocket launcher to fire and forget. I think the dual wielding mechanic needed to have been thought out some more alongside the alt-fires. Weapons getting upgrades is a neat idea but I'm not sure alt-fire is the way to go about it if dual wielding is still going to stick around.Speaking of weapons, the Raygun is an absolutely brilliant addition that is a masterful addition to Sam's arsenal. Being able to deal constant damage at range like the minigun is one thing. Making enemies blow up and deal damage to other enemies around them is a work of art, especially in this game series where enemies love to clump together in ways that maximise the explosive damage of the Raygun. So help me, it's even better than the minigun. I love this thing. The minigun should worry about being replaced by this thing because it deserves to stand next to the Serious Cannon as   weapons.Speaking of the Serious Cannon, one little nitpick: I do get we live in an era of incredible graphical potential and we can't just live on perfectly flat battlefields anymore but, as my cannonballs hit uneven terrain and go flying right over the Major Biomechanoid and six Sirian Werebulls I was hoping to squash like pins in bowling, I can't help but miss those innocent times. I'm not about to ask that the game take a bulldozer to those arenas but... ah, if only my beloved Cannon could work as it used to. One more more serious feedback. New Game+ is a nice feature that means I get to enjoy the juicy upgrades I get from prior playthroughs and make the most of them. However, weapons getting a truckload of points able to be allocated to them while I can only find up to ten in each playthrough means I feel empty. Not to mention each new plus to New Game+ makes enemies harder and harder and I just wish I could use all of my weapons to their full potential rather than just have so many empty upgrade slots.Finally,  games have a problem with just ending. The final boss is a great fight but it feels like it comes out of nowhere without a proper climactic buildup; it feels like it's interrupting something I was doing instead rather than be an ultimate goal I'm working towards. I remember feeling the same way about Ugh-Zan III in  and being perplexed that the game ended there. Mind you, these bosses are fantastic places to end a game; it's just that they forgot to actually write the games as if they were going to end there. Gotta construct the flow of your narrative to accommodate the highs and lows and help guide your audience to feeling satisfied with a good conclusion.Still, as I said, I love . It was a lot of fun and it rekindled my interest in . I hope Timelock get to make more games and levels like these for the series proper because it definitely needs their kind of perspective. I hope it keeps taking that kind of perspective in many fields and reconsiders more of its long-standing tropes that it takes for granted.

_childDocuments_.review: Serious Sam: Siberian Mayhem is a game developed by Croteam and published by the wonderful peeps at Devolver DigitalSerious Sam: Siberian Mayhem is a side-story from Serious Sam 4 and continues from Serious Sam: The First Encounter, Serious Sam: The Second Encounter, Serious Sam 2 and Serious Sam 3As Serious Sam, you get to travel across different places, fighting against creatures of all shapes and sizes. The gameplay is like that of old classic games, such as DOOM and Wolfenstein where you shoot enemies non-stop in huge arenas whilst getting keys, objects, health and ammoThe game runs on Croteam's very own engine and I must say the graphics were really nice. The arenas are huge and sprawling, full of sceneryThe music and sound effects are faithfully brought back from the original Serious Sam: The First and Second Encounter with new music and sound effects thrown into the mix. The sound effects are good but you can hear the difference in sound quality, sometimes poor to sub-par. Music too was the same, the music quality varied from poor to sub-parThe only thing that bugged me was the enemies, they were annoying to say the least. Always running towards, knocking down your health like there no tomorrow and Serious Sam runs so slow that even my late grandmother could run faster than him. The game doesn't feel as face paced as other arena shooter games I've playedSerious Sam: Siberian Mayhem takes a huge turn back from Serious Sam 2 and back to its roots from Serious Sam: The First, Second Encounter, Serious Sam 3 and Serious Sam 4, becoming more colourful and crazy from the first two games and not taking a more cartoony vibe that Serious Sam 2 had and taking the realistic vibe that Serious Sam: The First, Secound Encounter, Serious Sam 3 and Serious Sam 4 hadIn all honesty I prefer the realistic vibe from the previous two games rather than the cartoony vibe that was in Serious Sam 2. _childDocuments_.review: Siberian Mayhem is a perfect example of standalone DLC made right - it takes all the good parts of the base game and improves them, while also adding its own stuff on top. I liked Serious Sam 4, and I like Siberian Mayhem perhaps even more than the former. Gameplay is seriously fun: various combat scenarios test your skill and keep you on your toes, especially when playing on Serious difficulty. New additions to enemy roster spice up the gameplay, as well as three new guns(though one of them is basically a replacement for assault rifle) which are satisfying to use.Levels - which there are 5 of them - are pretty well designed. The environments are diverse and have lots of detail, which is surpising considering they are pretty big, though they are not as needlesly big as some levels in SS4 - base game suffered from  too vast level areas not being particularly full of interesting stuff(the biggest example is first levels in France). I also quite liked the level exploration aspect in Siberian Mayhem: not only do you get useful items like ammo and health pickups, but also find various pieces of lore through newsletter papers, various gags and jokes(some of which you can get if you know Russian, since you know, the game takes place in Russia) as well as cool easter eggs, some of which are direct references to previous games in Serious Sam. I won't spoil that these are exactly are, but if you played Doom 2016, I can say you can expect the same sort of secret stuff :)One of the things I love in Serious Sam games besides the gameplay is it's soundtrack, and Siberian Mayhem doesn't dissapoint. Both peaceful and combat themes, as well as various tracks are pretty beautiful and I personally like to listen to them both in game and outside of it.I didn't have any technical issues while playing Siberian Mayhem. Everything was pretty smooth and enjoyable.Overall, I suggest to play this game to every Serious Sam fan. If you didn't play Serious Sam 4, I would recommend playing base game first though, since Siberian Mayhem is after all an standalone expansion of it, and if you didn't like base game, chances are you may not like this one too.

Siberian Mayhem has enthralling game play, an incredible set of weapons that all have purpose, diverse enemy types, and massive battlefields with just hordes and hordes of enemies coming at you all at once.I think Croteam and Timelock are taking full advantage of going bonkers with Serious Sam's adventures, and I think this direction is perfectly suited for the series. _childDocuments_.review: It's hard to believe that this game is in fact made by modders, cause this game is a fully formed FPS with a badass campaign. Though I never touched Serious Sam 4 due to the complaints of the many that have. I'm glad that, due to the behest of many FPS youtubers, I went ahead and bought/ played through this one. The tagline for this game should definitely be: "Not your mommy and daddy's FPS," because this game is ridiculous. With a countless array of insanely cool weapons to the dozens of alien models in the game, you will very quickly find yourself overwhelmed by the hordes of hundreds of creatures that will fall at the hands of your Minigun, Laser Rifle, and Cannonball Gun.On Hard/Serious difficulty the game can get absurd with the amount of things thrown at you. Can't really complain though, because that is what Serious Sam is all about but I would say at certain points it can feel a bit unbearable.The story itself takes a backseat to the gameplay feeling little more than run of the mill, but that isn't always a bad thing. I love the Soviet/ Metal soundtrack quite a bit as it adds so much to the constant firefights and mood of the Siberian/ Russian setting. Performance can get a bit choppy but when you think about how many things can be on the screen at once, you kind of shut the hell up and just give in to the fun.Overall a genuinely great time with few things to complain about.8.5/10
