_childDocuments_.review: Now maybe it's just been a long time since I played the first Dusk diver but to start I wanna say it feels kinda slower? In combat I mean but not to it's detriment, so it's basically a lot like the first game but more, what do I mean? Well for starters characters from the prior game that were just essentially special attacks are now full on characters you can switch between in battle, there are more areas to choose from and walk around, attacks are more accurate than ever which I highly appreciate and it's just an all around good time and improvement, I said about the first one with certain things improved would make for a game I'd happily pay full price for, well they've done it and to make me feel a games worth full price is darn impressive in an era of quick heartless cash grab games with barely any real meat to them dood.Okay now onto the more detailed stuff, so the combat feels more refined now as I said, which is impressive with the addition of more playable characters I might add, the devs even did a great job of making them all unique, protag is a balanced melee fighter with a wide variety of attacks and the lightning element (This may stop an enemy from attacking) another is a defence/counter heavy fighter who's slow but high offence makes them an insane fighter if you play well, their element is fire which...oddly doesn't hurt enemies but instead makes them more susceptible to break, (Will explain that one in a bit) the third character has wider ranged hits and has essentially a bleed effect on their weapon but also timing to their attacks let's you do more damage and adds the bleed effect on normal strikes if you have good rhythm and finally you have a ranged character, very hard to master as the enemies love to counter long ranged attacks with rather nasty attacks of their own, they could have toned that down honestly but it's not the worst ever, their element is water, this slows enemies down both movement and attack wise dood.Combat flows nicely, it can be difficult at the start though and seem rather long as enemies seemingly have large health pools but as time goes on you get much stronger and you realise they wanted players to use their meter more (I'll get to that too) it also want's players to abuse the break mechanic, this can be activated from repeated hits or knocking enemies into a wall, you get a heavy, highly damaging attack in, free iframes (invincibility if ya don't know) and it even hurts enemies close by, essential for the more sturdy enemies if you want to end it quicker, enemies have decent variety too, even down to how some attack, one set of enemies truly terrified me to face off against every time I encountered them for their ferocity but also looked pretty cool, it made you play in very specific ways dood.Thought I was done with combat? Not yet! For you see I haven't mentioned special skills, there's a decent variety for each character, again all are quite handy and in fact all can also be set as a support attack, on top of that you have a burst meter that let's you power up and hit for some major damage, especially if you fill the new meter up to near full as it let's you then use a real cool ultimate attack, of which all characters have, the combat is real fun when ya get into it like that dood.Next onto food! So food gives you temporary buffs or even immediate effects at times but more importantly you have takeaway food, I think the idea is great! The execution less so, buffs last five encounters, typically you will have a few more than that in a non human world stage but you can only use them in a safe area, which you'd think means just out of combat which would have been ideal but instead meant save points or the human world, it's not like soul crushingly bad, it just feels wasteful in consideration to how many you can just stock up on and never use because you need to hit a save point, you already have a fullness meter stopping you from abusing it and the limit of three effects so it seemed a bit much dood.Next up is equipment and gems, they are a fun addition, armour can have up to three slots, as well as boosts to your stats, real basic but the slots let you put in gems that can substantially boost the players stats and give some handy effects, the only real issue being some are much better than others and often cheaper slot wise at that (some can take up to three slots) for instance 5% chance of not getting a status ailment is just plain wasteful, if it stacked like EXP or wafer (the alternate currency for other types of items) equipped to other characters it would be great but it doesn't so it sucks XD something to keep in mind for any dev 5% is rarely a good enough amount, that said the 3% health recovery on enemy down is great when there are so many enemies, weird they got that right but not the other dood.Music is great, nice variety to it but it could have done with one or two more tracks for particularly impactful moments of the story, although for the most important stuff they had some real good stuff for as every game should for their end game content, the story was interesting and the characters were very much themselves which is always a good thing dood.The costumes like before have an okay amount, recolours although for each character now and a few new outfits for each but you also get a few attachments now too, they aren't many but some are better than none I say and finally there is a new game plus, which actually adds a whole lot shockingly, I won't say what specifically due to spoils but rare is it that we get more stuff to have fun with in out NG+ of games, it does fall for that dark souls style no choice on the difficulty being raised though, I've always been against not giving the player the choice when a NG+ should be a reward, not a punishment dood.The last thing I wanna talk about though is levels, they are rather odd, some stats feel more worth it than others and with the right items you can get them all to max anyway but at first strength will seem weak then later it will be oddly powerful and worth it based on upgrades to your weapons, most stats up health even if it's not as much as the health stat, then other stats raise important effects, it left me feeling it was hard to choose, that said there is a refund item so no need to worry too much there dood.So to finish I wanna say I'm super happy to finally play and beat dusk diver 2, it was a fun time and I'd love to see the devs do more games in the future, even another dusk diver I'd be happy with and in a ways they do have a lot of possibilities to add more D.D games in the future, thank you for reading and I hope this helps you decide on buying the game or not dood!Edit: There is one thing I never delved into because I never needed to and the materials were rare enough to come by that I never used and that's gem creation, so the gems are a neat idea, I like them, the gem creation...is either straight up busted or the chances are terribly low, I got lucky to get a rank 5 one which I'm guessing was the meh experience boost but my point is if you are going to make the materials rare enough to be a hassle to get the game shouldn't make the chances for anything decent to be that Gods awful, even if it's just random versions of that rank it would have been acceptable but seeing me use rare materials only to constantly get rank 1 gems is a big nope from me, hope the devs realise that's an issue in the future dood.

name: Vampire Survivors
detailed_description: Vampire Survivors is a time survival game with minimalistic gameplay and roguelite elements. Hell is empty, the devils are here, and there's no place to run or hide. All you can do is survive as long as you can until death inevitably puts an end to your struggles. Gather gold in each run to buy upgrades and help the next survivor. The supernatural indie phenomenon that lets you be the bullet hell! Now with local co-op for up to 4 players! Supports mouse, keyboard, controller, and touch screen. Starting Tips Take your time to grab gems and items, they won't disappear. Get two or three offensive weapons at first, but focus on leveling them up one at a time. Armour and Luck are good starting power-ups to spend money on. Refund power-ups often, it's free, and try new upgrade paths. v0.1.0 release date: - itch: Mar 31, 2021 - Steam: Dec 17, 2021

_childDocuments_.review: So as you all can plainly see, I have played this game for 160+ hours. Is it a good game? Yes, and allow me to explain just how great a game this is.From the get-go, I loved the art direction of this game. Having grown up playing Castlevania and enjoying such classics like Symphony of the Night, Aria of Sorrow, Portrait of Ruin, and Dawn of Sorrow, it easily brought nostalgia to the days I was playing the games in the my room when I was a young lad. That being said this is not a Castlevania clone, this is a homage to the series and taken in a different direction: a roguelike Bullet Heaven. And that should be a new genre considering how well the creator of this game crafted it. For $2.99, you get a game that you can play for hours on end, moving around the map, collecting power-ups and items and smoking everything coming at you. The first few times I tried this, I lost but have gotten so much better that I can reasonably make the 30 minute mark... and yes, the goal of this game is to Survive for 30 minutes each playthrough. Not a significant amount of time but damn can time fly by when you are having fun.And that's really what this game is, just a continuous seratonin rush when you log into the game and just see how far you can go, what synergies you want to try this time, what crazy combinations can come into play with your builds and the weapons you take, and how you can best make it work. Coming from a Dungeons and Dragons background, this checks off the itch of just building a character multiple times to see how strong you can make them.And for the completionist, I have to give mad props to the creator. You have made a game that constantly has more and more stuff in it with each and every patch. More character, more weapons, more passive items, more levels, more challenges, more secrets, you name it and they just keep delivering.This is all to say that if you have the time and literally less money than to buy a bag of chips from a convenience store, you would not be making any mistakes picking up this game. It is a solid 10/10, hours of fun and replayability, and the fact that it is only in early access when there other games that have fully come out with a larger price and less finished, it is a necessary addition to anyone's library.This last note is to the creator. You are a phenomenal person and please keep kicking ass.

_childDocuments_.review: To explain this in popular-game terms: imagine Cookie Clicker developers creating a Crimsonland game, sprinkling a bit Binding of Isaac onto it, and polishing it into a good product that stands on its own feet.+ Instantly addicting, this will replace sleep and real life+ Gain up to 6 different weapons at once from the get-go+ Kill 100,000+ enemies per run+ Fight through literally screen-filling hordes and remain calm+ Get bombarded with new unlocks constantly+ There are so, so many secrets (16 secret characters alone!)+ Discover game-breaking combos where you just idle and everything dies+ Questionable artstyle overshadowed by all the crazy weapon effects+ Just really fun honestlyUnlocking all achievements, characters, weapons etc took me ~52 hours which is really not that long for a game that has idler/clicker genre in its roots. Most of it didn't feel like a grind although having a second monitor helps a lot. Because not only you can watch a movie (when you eventually get too OP to require inputs) but also the game runs better in exclusive fullscreen (it's true for most games really, it's just how the graphics card works, press Alt+Enter to toggle it).After you've unlocked everything you can play the game indefinitely. There's a very late-game method of infinitely leveling up your characters but it takes ridiculous amounts of coins, so you get to discover game-breaking money-making combos there too. It's cool.I did not like both DLCs though. They introduce "actual level design" but with no minimap and little to no point in exploring it kind of sucks. I was also exhausted by the game and wanted to just complete it at this point, so I did not pay nearly enough attention at the new characters' and weapons' strengths and potential combos. It was grindy at the end but it's probably my fault. UPD: they added minimaps to both levels!

The game's combat is challenging and rewarding, with a variety of enemy types and bosses that will test your skills and reflexes.One of the standout features of Vampire Survivors is its setting and atmosphere. The game takes place in a dark and eerie post-apocalyptic world, where vampires have taken over and humanity is on the brink of extinction. The game's graphics and sound design perfectly capture the game's tense and foreboding atmosphere, adding to the overall immersion of the game.The game also has a variety of different modes to play, including a story mode and survival mode. Each mode offers a unique gameplay experience, with different objectives and challenges to overcome.Overall, Vampire Survivors is a thrilling and entertaining game that offers a unique and immersive experience. Its fast-paced gameplay, challenging combat, and eerie atmosphere make it a must-play for fans of the shooter and survival horror genres.

_childDocuments_.review: At the time of writing, i have nearly 100% the game, only missing a DLC enemy kill threshold. Point is, i have engaged in all of its mechanics. While the game itself is a dopamine factory and the process of building up characters and figuring out map strategies is undeniably fun, there is one glaring issue that can detract from the long-term replayability: .Golden Eggs are incremental upgrades that you receive as a sort of prestige system, and while they may seem small, they provide permanent buffs to your characters. The problem is that there is  when it comes to selecting or limiting the buffs you receive. Since they are randomly generated, you switch between all of them or none of them, and it's impossible to fine-tune the buffs to your liking.By the time you notice a significant upgrade in a particular stat, your character is already so overpowered that the game becomes too easy. I wish there was a way to individually limit or set the size of the buffs so that you could get the fun bonuses without being stuck with overpowered stats that make the game a total cakewalk.Aside from this issue, the game itself is enjoyable, and the weapons (with the exception of the flower one) feel balanced and valid. However, the fun stuff and mechanics are mostly at the tail-end of progress. The power-up screen is only the beginning, and once you've filled it completely, you've barely scratched the surface. The early game can feel tedious and even frustrating until you get lucky with a good run and start to see what the game has to offer.Overall, I  this game if you have the patience to make it through the first level. But seriously, the lack of customization with the Golden Egg mechanic can make the long-term replayability suffer.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is basically as addictive as crack for reasons explained later. Gameplay is like:1) Low effort relaxation because it's an auto-shooter.2) You mostly just move around to avoid damage, maximize damage dealt, and gather up "xp" dots dropped by monsters as quickly as possible.3) After doing that for a while you try to pick the most optimal powerup to select next for the situation.4) Lastly, you try to get "unlocks" for new characters and more power-ups by finding "relics" on the level or fulfilling achievements.5) Even if you've effectively turned into god and everything that comes within half a screen radius of you now just dies instantly, the game will still kill you with an invincible monster at some point or keep upping the hp/defense of the mobs of monsters until they increasingly land blows on you.After that, you spend the gold you got during that game on unlocks/powerups for future games.Basically the "unlocks" is the main addictive reward mechanism in this.If you're looking for some sort of coherent story, rational worldbuilding, or clever content or something go elsewhere because the game basically makes no sense at all. I can't tell if you're supposed to be vampires, or if you're supposed to be vampire hunters, or where you're supposed to be or what you're trying to accomplish other than "unlocks" in some generic insane world full of mobs of monsters. Basically questions like "who, what, where,. when" and especially "why" don't seem to have answers provided within the game.But somehow it still seems to make more sense than Brotato.So some advantages:1) You're going to die anyway, so if you need to just walk away from the computer and let your character get killed then no big deal. Because of that it's a good thing to play to fill time when you may need to quit any moment.2) It works well on the steam deck (and probably a bunch of other handhelds and mobiles) so you can do this while waiting in waiting rooms in public if you need.Disadvantages:1) Most levels have little to no level design. Some are just big open floors with some random obstacles. Some are more like hallways with walls on two sides of the screen, but overall the procedural generation is rather weak.2) Ultimately there's not much to do but try to unlock everything. Unlike Hades, for example, there doesn't seem to be any final goal like "kill dracula", but maybe it's there and just not apparent to me yet.3) Also unlike other games, it's not possible to "win" a level and move on to the next one. You always die, but a new level will be unlocked if you manage to fulfill some achievement before that happens.Overall though this is good for when you need something that doesn't need to be taken seriously, and i've ended up playing it more than the other two most similar games I've bought recently (Brotato and Shape Shifter Formations).

_childDocuments_.review: Once upon a time, in a quaint village nestled between rolling hills and lush forests, there lived an old man named Poe. Poe was known far and wide for his love of garlic. He would sprinkle it generously on every meal, from his morning porridge to his evening stew. His cottage perpetually smelled of the pungent herb, and his neighbors often joked that they could tell when he was cooking from miles away.Despite the teasing, Poe continued to indulge in his garlic obsession, convinced of its many health benefits and its ability to ward off illness and evil spirits. But as time went on, Poe's consumption of garlic grew more and more excessive. He would eat entire cloves raw, oblivious to the protests of his taste buds and the concerns of those around him.As Poe's garlic intake reached unprecedented levels, something peculiar began to happen. His once pleasant aroma transformed into an overpowering stench that permeated the air wherever he went. Birds fell from the sky, flowers wilted, and even the hardiest of crops withered in his presence. Villagers held their noses as he passed by, and animals fled in terror from his foul scent.Despite the chaos he caused, Poe remained oblivious to the destruction he left in his wake. He continued to eat garlic with reckless abandon, unaware of the havoc he was wreaking on the world around him. But as his stench aura grew stronger and his presence more unbearable, something miraculous occurred.One fateful day, as Poe was out in his garden, surrounded by wilted plants and scorched earth, he felt a strange sensation coursing through his body. His skin tingled, and his bones seemed to ache with a newfound weight. Before his astonished eyes, he began to transform.His limbs stretched and twisted, his skin hardened into bark, and roots sprouted from his feet, anchoring him to the ground. In a matter of moments, Poe had been transformed into a towering tree, his branches reaching towards the sky like gnarled fingers.The villagers, initially shocked by the sudden transformation, soon came to see the beauty in the strange tree that now stood where Poe once did. They named it "Peppino," a combination of "Poe" and "peppermint," in a nod to the fresh, invigorating scent that now emanated from its branches.And so, Peppino stood as a reminder of the consequences of excess, a cautionary tale for those who dared to indulge their desires without restraint. Though Poe himself was gone, his legacy lived on in the form of a tree, a symbol of redemption and renewal for the village and all who passed through it.

_childDocuments_.review: Vampire Survivors brought bullet heaven (reverse bullet hell) games back to popularity, combining them with roguelite elements and charming pixel graphics to create an addictive experience. it's the kind of game where you keep saying "just one more run" and then hours have flown by before you know it.The gameplay is fairly simple: you start your run with a character and one weapon, while enemies begin to hunt you down. Your character attacks automatically, leaving you to focus on dodging and maneuvering to avoid getting killed. As you slay enemies, they drop experience points in the form of gems. When you level up, you can choose from three different options, which might include picking a new weapon, selecting a passive item, or leveling up one of your existing weapons or items. Boss monsters drop chests that contain up to 5 rewards. You can also evolve weapons into more powerful forms for even greater damage. The goal is to survive as long as possible—after 30 minutes, Death arrives to end your run. Gold earned during runs can be spent on permanent upgrades or unlocking new characters.There's an enormous variety of characters to unlock, each with unique starting weapons and bonuses, along with a great selection of weapons and maps. The game also allows you to modify your run with options like Hyper mode and Inverted mode, adding new layers of challenge and variety. Adventure mode and co-op play offer even more content to keep you coming back for more. The DLC are fairly priced and always offer a lot of new content, including maps, characters, and weapons.

_childDocuments_.review: I saw this title recommended on Splattercat's Youtube channel and I had to check it out.This is a Early Access title at the time of writing this quick review, however don't let this dissuade you!For the cheap price it offers, you're getting FAR more replay-ability and content in this challenging rouge like reverse bullet hell. The developer is consistently working on the title and is releasing micro updates with new features and constant balancing, keeping the title fresh, and fun to play!Graphics: Obviously we have a pixel art style, but it adds to the charm of the game, enough that it doesn't take away from the experience.Sound Design: The audio and music isn't over the top and could use some further development, but at this time it is pleasing and satisfying to listen to.UI: This is probably the biggest area that's lacking, there is no adjustable settings other than toggling some specific ones on or off. As well, the title does not have a screen size option and as such it must be letter-boxed on wide screen monitors, as well as causing some slight definition loss on ultra definitions. Many of these issues however are being addressed in future updates.Gameplay: Vampire Survivors is a fun twist on the bullet hell genre, mixed with a incremental progression system that allows for the player to gradually get stronger with each run. Weapons, and items are creative and make each run unique, while not killing a players run with poor RNG. The player always has a minimum of 3 choices when choosing what item to add to their arsenal as they battle the never ending swarm of foes. There's even a chest reward system that can drop from elite enemies and boss units, rewarding the player with 1-5 items. Things like whips, knives, pigeon bombers, magical wands and fireballs, and lightning from the skies can aide you as you quest from a new challenge. Overall I would grant this title a 7.5-8/10 in it's current state, and I eagerly look forward to the full release and fresh content to come!

_childDocuments_.review: I've had my eye on Vampire Survivors for some time now. Always from a distance, though - at first glance, it looked like some unholy combination of one of those idle phone games and a bullet hell shooter. I'm happy to report I was (mostly) mistaken. Vampire Survivors is actually more of a rogue-lite defense game where you are the bullet hell.The gameplay starts off pretty simple: you select one of the characters (each of whom has their own default weapon) and the stage you want to play. The goal is to help the character survive a set amount of time (usually 30 minutes) by moving them around while they automatically attack waves of incoming enemies.Most enemies you kill will drop experience gems. Collecting the gems fills your experience gauge, and at every level up, you get to pick one of the 3-4 random weapons and items. Each weapon has a different attack mode, and most can be combined with specific items to create even more powerful versions.Collecting and upgrading weapons and items like this is the key to a successful run. Your character can wield up to 6 weapons, letting you combine attacks with different ranges and firing modes. This is especially important in the final few minutes of a run, when an endless wave of tough enemies is almost guaranteed to overwhelm an unprepared player.As you play the game, you'll unlock more and more characters, weapons, and items. Beyond that, you can also unlock powerful relics that let you tweak the game experience, permanent upgrades that apply to every run, and tarot cards that add special effects to your character and the stage you're playing in.Each of these adds a layer of complexity and strategy to what at first looks like a game where you simply have to move the character out of harm's way. Once you have some experience and a few unlockables under your belt, the game practically explodes with all the interesting combinations of characters, weapons, items, and add-ons you can play with.At the same time, this is probably the game's biggest flaw. Some combinations of items, such as Unholy Vespers, Gorgeous Moon, Infinite Corridor, or Phieraggi are objectively superior to most other weapons, especially during the later stages of a run. As such, you'll always try to get them if at all possible, which ends up making every run feel the same.All in all, despite the deceptively simplistic look, Vampire Survivors is a ton of fun. It will probably work best for completionists (after all, there are almost 200 Steam achievements to unlock) and players who enjoy the feeling of mowing down entire armies of enemies single-handed. Run around, mow down enemies, and survive. Interesting and addictive gameplay. Can become repetitive after a while.

_childDocuments_.review: Rating: ★★★★☆"Vampire Survivors" is a bite-sized roguelike treasure that delivers intense gameplay and is complemented by the added incentive of Steam achievements.Visually, the game embraces pixel art aesthetics that suit the roguelike genre perfectly, creating a charming and nostalgic atmosphere.Gameplay-wise, "Vampire Survivors" offers fast-paced action as you navigate through procedurally generated levels, battling hordes of enemies while managing your vampire's unique abilities. The short play sessions make it easy to jump in for a quick gaming fix.One of the standout features is the inclusion of Steam achievements, which provide an extra layer of motivation for players to explore various strategies and experiment with different vampire builds. Achievements encourage both skillful gameplay and creative approaches to challenges.However, the game's difficulty can be punishing at times, and the procedurally generated nature may lead to some uneven runs, which could be a drawback for some players.In conclusion, "Vampire Survivors" is a delightful roguelike with the added bonus of Steam achievements that enhance the gameplay. It's perfect for those seeking a quick and satisfying gaming experience with plenty of replayability, earning it a solid four-star rating.

_childDocuments_.review: It's still in early access but, man, what a treat and find this early (pun intended) in the year. Vampire Survivors should run on a toaster so thankfully we can skip the technical details. It's a deceivingly 'simple' 2D autoattacker with a strong horror/monster movie theme drinking straight out of Castlevania and B-films of the era. Not much in the shape of story, it's pure mechanics. You're thrown into an arena and your goal is to survive up to 30 mins against increasingly brutal hordes of non-stop spawning mobs.You get a bunch of weapons at your disposal that you can upgrade as you level up, while randomly picking one each time you level up. That's where a rogue-like element shows up since you can mostly bet on getting the weapons and special effect items you get but it's all in that gacha/dice roll (props to the gacha theme since it's the embodiment of all gacha and you're not forced to pay real currency when you pick one chest!). You do get permanent upgrades that help you start in a stronger position but, still, it's not an easy task to reach the 30 mins mark. And what's your reward for doing so well? A swift death. Spoilers: death itself comes and takes you.There is a huge addicting and cathartic effect in planning a strategy as you desperately move around to position yourself and destroy some of the blatant Castlevania-like candles and flames for precious gold and items. Certainly a bit more entertaining than watching a cookie spin, right? The fact that it's compressed into 30 minutes sessions makes this an ideal pick up and play for those with little time to game. You're not demanded to sit through hours of non interactive cutscenes and dialogue, just pure raw, balls-to-the-wall auto-attacking.So, yeah, with that strong core of combining items and weapons to create your ultimate build, multiple characters to pick up from and the fact that it's still in development and is probably going to add even more content, yeah, surprise of the year and indie GOTY for sure. Gotta love when the stars align like this! Go get it now!

_childDocuments_.review: Vampire Survivor is one of the most recent innovation in video game history! Sure, it's probably inspired by a phone game that came before it (?), but nonetheless, I do believe it's the first of it's kind on Steam. That genre is one where you can move around and your weapons/skills are cast automatically.This lead to a game where you can focus on running away from monsters and dodging attacks, while you automatically shoot back at enemies. It's a roguelike, so every games you start, you begin at level 1. At first you're weak, but through various level-up, upgrades, tarot cards and weapon evolutions, you get progressively stronger. The monsters do so as well, of course. Eventually, when you reach the end-game or grind enough, you can absolutely obliterate the whole game, which feels really rewarding.At the same time, this brings on to the most negative point about this, sometimes it becomes an AFK-fest. If you care too much about how you build your character during a run, you become literally immortal. Some of the characters are so overpowered that you can literally AFK from level 1 as well, looting XP gems from time to time to level up and then go back to AFKing.I would still highly recommend this game, which now cost $4.99 at full price and is an absolute bargain considering how much content it offers. Many levels, an awesome soundtrack, retro graphics, hundreds of unlocks and much more. It is one of the only games I would ever recommend to buy even at full price!

_childDocuments_.review: This isn't usually the type of game I would go out of my way to get, so I'm thankful it was gifted to me. For three dollars, though, having played it now, I would have absolutely bought it myself.This game gives you a very simple objective, and it's built around a very simple formula: Don't die, get stronger, last as long as you can.The character you start off with is perhaps underwhelming at first, but he gives you a good idea of what you're supposed to be doing. He attacks enemies in front of him until he levels up. Now, level ups are really cool in how they function. You get to choose from three to four upgrades for your character. To a max of six weapons and six character buffs (which all have upgrades), your character continually gets better and better. There's a strategy element in choosing the best buffs of the three you get per level up, as they are RNG. There aren't really any that are bad, but there are some that are 100% better than others. And there are some that are better on different characters than others. While the whip is fine for the first character, you may not want it when you unlock the fourth character.I can firmly say that I haven't had as much fun with any new game in a long time as I have with this one. And it's only three bucks, likely with more content to come as (at the time of writing) it is still in early access.The exploration element is out of this world - I do not recommend looking at anyone's suggestions on "best builds" or anything like that. So much of the fun comes from finding out what YOU have the most fun with. Believe me, I was sitting here soyface'd to the extreme as I discovered new power ups and tried them out. Whisper-shouting "yooooo that's crazy" unlocking garlic, or just laughing at the insane amount of projectiles I could throw with the fourth character.Lovely game, absolutely recommend it. Whether you want something with strategy and depth or you just want to turn your brain off and chill with a game, this is the one for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Just One More Run... Oops, It's Morning!Have you ever wanted to feel like the ultimate vampire slayer without all the messy, real-life consequences of dealing with garlic breath? Welcome to Vampire Survivors, where you'll learn that pixelated bats are actually terrifying, and "just one more run" quickly turns into "wait, why is the sun rising?"This game is like a potato chip: you can’t stop at just one. Each round lasts about 30 minutes, but don't be fooled—time loses all meaning here. You'll find yourself strategically planning your life around your next power-up choice. Should you get the garlic aura to keep the undead at bay? Or maybe you’re feeling lucky and want to grab the magic wand for that sweet auto-aim?The controls are simple: move, survive, repeat. But the real magic is in the upgrades and evolutions. You’ll start off as a mere mortal, dodging everything in sight, but soon you’ll be a whirlwind of destruction, mowing down hordes of creatures while chuckling maniacally. The gameplay is addictive, with each run giving you a bit more to unlock, a new strategy to try, or a weapon to master.Graphically, it’s a throwback to the good ol’ days of gaming—pixel art that’s charming in its simplicity. But don’t let the retro visuals fool you. Underneath that nostalgic exterior is a game that’s deceptively deep. The soundtrack, by the way, will be stuck in your head for days. Prepare to hum battle tunes in the shower.In short, Vampire Survivors is dangerously addictive, ridiculously fun, and worth every penny (which is shockingly few for the amount of content).If you're not careful, this game might just bite you... and you’ll love every second of it. 🌒🦇Pros:Simple yet addictive gameplayEndless combinations of upgrades and weaponsPerfectly tuned difficulty curveRetro pixel art that hits all the right nostalgia notesCons:Time will disappear faster than your battery percentageGive this review a thumbs up if you’ve lost track of time slaying pixelated vampires!

_childDocuments_.review: It's like eating a bag of potato chips where multiple flavors are mixed together. It starts out simple. You eat a chip, obviously you can't stop at one. Then you slowly tell yourself you need to see all of the flavors the bag has to offer. It's too late you're addicted to the chips, you continue eating them until 3am and the result is massive slowdowns and diarrhea all over your screen. You've won, but at what cost? Winning rewards you with new flavors in your next bag.  You continue for days eating more and more. You no longer sleep. Eating, bathing working to provide for your family have all become optional.  There is only Vampire Survivors. Your wife can no longer watch the man she once loved turn into this creature she can't recognize. She leaves and takes the kid with, further plunging you into darkness. You are too far in. Normally you value your time more than to see absolutely everything something has to offer. This is different. You no longer care for this plane of existence, but only to have closure, to taste every flavor, discover every secret the bag has to offer. Finally you think you are done Achievement total 94/94. Relief wakes you up suddenly as if you were in a coma. You're done you reach for the phone to beg your wife to come back.  You get a notification, "New update available for Vampire Survivors". You discover the true meaning of early access. The manufacturer is continually updating and adding content until the final release. Weekly you are dragged back. Called in by the allure of new content, new and exciting ways to play. You spiral into madness every waking moment waiting to finally defeat the Vampire that will never come. After months of madness the it is complete the final release comes. You discover the rest of that there is, Achievements total 142/142. Finally, you can move on and rebuild the pieces of your life destroyed by obsession, no longer laying awake at night planning your next attack. After finishing I realized. It was me. There was no vampire in the game, because I was the vampire the whole time. I was transformed by my obsession into a creature of the night. The only hope for me now is to move on and rebuild my life. Deep inside I do not regret the time spent, but now is the time for healing, for relief. Some time passes you are sleeping peacefully next to your new wife. Your cat sleeping peacefully on your feet keeping you warm on a cold December night. You awake suddenly, feeling a disturbance. You have a notification on your steam app. "DLC for Vampire Survivors on sale now!" You check your achievements. 142/159. Your heart sinks, that darkness that you had once defeated is back again. You say goodbye to your wife, you pay the admission to your new madness of $1.50 and you dive back in headfirst. 10/10 Would neglect my health and family again. Insane value for the total 3.50 I paid for the game and DLC. Great job.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is unlike anything I've ever played.  Part bullet hell, part RPG, part rogue-like, and dare I say, part metroidvania in its approach to progression, I never thought I'd clock over 100 hours in it and still be eager to come back for more.  Not because I've done everything in the game and I just need to play more, but because as you are playing this game, you are slowly getting glimpses of what's under the hood.  Every time I think that I've reached endgame and I've completed the most difficult challenge the game has to offer, I find a new character, a new challenge, or a new strategy that changes how I think about progressing through a run.  Every time I think that I've found a character or a build that is the literal embodiment of pixelated apocalypse, I find a new character I didn't know existed and shatter the glass ceiling.  Case in point, I thought that the highest level you could achieve in a run was around 130.  Tonight, I found a character that scales Growth each level (experience earned per rank), and topped out around 400 and was outputting so much carnage that enemies couldn't even make it on to my screen.  In doing this, I learned about items you can purchase that permanently increase stats for the character you're playing on...but they require 10k gold for each 1%.  And here I was, thinking  money served no purpose because I'd bought almost all of the permanent power-ups.  Now I'm playing around with strategies on how to min/max characters for maximum gold potential per run, just to see how badly I can break this game.There is a reason this game blew up and is winning/being nominated for awards.  You have no excuse not to own this for its price point.12/10, would survive vampires again.

_childDocuments_.review: I've bought so many games in this years summer sale, but whenever I find time to play anything I just keep finding myself clicking Vampire Survivors like some kind of addict. The hundreds of enemies, the absolutely insane weapons that you can level up and evolve over the course of a run, the satisfying and flashy animations you witness when opening a chest... it all just makes me feel so good inside.The gameplay is fairly simple: Your character attacks automatically and you just walk around dodging enemies and vacuuming up XP gems, so you can get your next upgrade and make yourself even more powerful against the increasingly difficult thousands-strong waves coming at you from all angles. There's also some pretty nifty unlocks and pickups which help you progress the game, culminating in a mad dash to pickup and level-up 4 items so you can finally defeat Death, who will come in to try and ruin your day if you manage to survive a run. Doing so unlocks even more content, and you just want to keep playing.It also helps that the developer keeps adding more fun content with each update, and seems genuinely taken aback by just how well this little game he's made has done in terms of sales.Buy it, It's 3 bucks for a huge hit of dopamine.Update: So I've clocked in almost 40 hours now and I've unlocked everything there is in the game right now, including all of the secret characters like Toasty and Minnah, purchased all upgrades and maxed out curse, and 100%'d the achievements. Looking forward to the final few updates which bring an end to the game and I finally get to fight the elusive vampire, but I'll probably put this down for a while now as there isn't any other goal for me to aim for in the game.The recent limit break feature added does allow you to get even stronger after you've maxed out your upgrades, but the 30 minute limit that is imposed/guaranteed death if you manage to kill Death at the end of each stage really does kind of kill any real benefit you get from having it. I really hope that some kind of substantial endgame is added or even an endless mode without a time limit as right now, there doesn't seem to be much point in playing once you've done everything, the only thing left is to grind for golden eggs, which don't really make a difference when you end up being a walking death machine by the 30 minute mark regardless.It's still 3 bucks though - and I can't complain that I had this much fun for this amount of time for that amount of money.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has been incredible value for £2/$3 since it launched in early access.  I wanted to wait a while before reviewing the game, many people are skeptical about Early Access games in general and I wanted to see if it would be further developed at all, as many Early Access games are never finished and the Early Access system is frequently abused by many developers to make a quick buck and release a product that will never be finished.It’s been about 6 months since this launched, I have played it on and off since launch, and there have been consistent developments to the game!This game has grown substantially since the start of its early access launch, at the time of writing this review the game has 7 stages compared to the 2 it had on launch, 24 characters and over 60 items, new difficulties and new mechanics (Hypermode, Arcanas, Skip, Reroll, etc.) It is being updated and built upon frequently and a roadmap is listed on the storepage detailing the end goal for their content. A rare Early Access game that is actually worth it!TLDR: A great game at a shockingly low price, would highly recommend to fans of roguelites, consistent updates lots of fun!EDIT: voted for relaxing in the GOTY awards (+1 for next year!)

_childDocuments_.review: Vampire Survivors is an addicting single-screen bullet-hell shooter where you are the bullets. Play as various vampire hunters, slay hordes of enemies, get upgrades and become a screen-clearing terror- if you survive that long. Obtain achievements to unlock new characters, weapons and permanent upgrades, Use gold from your runs to purchase said new things, and try to find the perfect build. Based on my experience and existing guides, I highly suggest using the skeleton character Mortaccio and the King's Bible and Magic Wand weapons. Most weapons will, when fully upgraded and you also have the appropriate passive item, "evolve" into a more powerful form. To do this, you'll need to kill a boss and loot his treasure chest after the 10-minute mark in a run. 10 mins seems to be a cutoff point- if you can get the King's Bible weapon upgraded sufficiently at this point and evolve it into the Unholy Vespers, you'll have an easier time from then on, especially if you can also get the Holy Wand and Hellfire evolved weapons.VS reminds me of higher quality flash games you might find on Newgrounds or Kongregate and it has a very modest price. If you're looking for a simple game to kill some time and literally thousands of enemies per run, VS is a game to try.

_childDocuments_.review: - Pretty simple pixel art. Honestly, when I first bought the game, I thought it looked pretty bad, but it's grown on me over time- The sound effects, however, are awesome. It's like the dev had a folder of audio files called "dopamine triggers" and used them throughout the game- The soundtrack is another high point. I love that music is selectable at the outset of a run, too- Vampire Survivors is unique in its approach to a narrative: there isn't one, but it really seems like there should be one hidden there somewhere. All the pieces are in place--there are interesting looking characters, lore entries in the form of collections, settings and locations in levels, etc--but they don't really add up to a plot or story- It follows that the vibes are a little hard to figure. All the vaguely fantasy set dressing and absence of a narrative makes you feel more like you're playing with a toy than playing a video game- Here it is: the birth of a new subgenre. There are plenty of imitators, but this gameplay loop is the original. You walk around on an infinitely scrolling surface while autofiring your weapons at waves of enemies that fill the screen. You collect items and upgrades for your equipment that help you cope with the growing forces of bad guys- Eventually, the timer hits the limit specified in level select screen, Death comes out to claim you, and the run ends (...usually)- Vampire Survivors is packed with secrets, unlockables, and secret unlockables. You'll spend plenty of time looking through the collection and unlock menus to try and figure out how to get everything- Despite the lack of engagement offered by a gameplay loop like this one, it's highly addicting. It's like rewards and progress are spaced out at optimal intervals to keep you coming back for your next hit. That said, after nearly 40 hours, I feel like I need a break for a bit before coming back to try Adventure Mode and the DLC stuff- It always feels weird putting together a review for a game that's become a cultural phenomenon like Vampire Survivors. The word is out already: it's a fun game with broad appeal and a casual learning curve- I'm just so impressed with how addictive this game is. Poncle has a grasp of dopamine and reward timing that would put a neuroscientist to shame- . The market for so-called "bullet heavens" is saturated now, but you'd be doing yourself a service not to try the original. Pick it up and see what the fuss is about

_childDocuments_.review: As a player who has spent a few hours immersed in the dark, gothic world of Vampire Survivors, I can say without hesitation that this game is an absolute gem. From the hauntingly beautiful graphics to the gripping storyline, there's something truly special about this game that sets it apart from others in its genre.First and foremost, the atmosphere of Vampire Survivors is simply incredible. The moody, atmospheric visuals and haunting soundtrack really help to create a sense of tension and unease that keeps you on the edge of your seat. And the game's narrative is equally captivating, with an intriguing story that unfolds gradually over the course of the game.But where Vampire Survivors really shines is in its gameplay. The combat system is fast-paced and engaging, with a wide variety of weapons and abilities that keep things interesting. And the game's open-world design means that there are plenty of hidden secrets and unexpected encounters to be found, making exploration even more enjoyable than combat.All in all, I would highly recommend Vampire Survivors to anyone who enjoys dark, atmospheric games with an extremely engaging gameplay. It's a game that rewards exploration, challenges your skills in combat, and leaves you hungry for more. So grab your stakes and get ready to dive into a world of darkness, because this is one game you won't want to miss.

_childDocuments_.review: Vampire Survivors is a roguelike shoot 'em up video game developed and published by Luca Galante, also known as poncle. Following an early access period from December 17, 2021, it was released for macOS and Windows on October 20, 2022. Ports to Xbox One and Xbox Series X/S were released on November 10, 2022.The player controls an automatically attacking character while fighting against continuous waves of monsters, with the goal being to survive the onslaught for as long as possible and unlock additional characters, weapons, and relics for subsequent sessions. In spite of the game's name and key art, none of the variety of monsters encountered are vampires.The player selects one of multiple characters with different starting weapons and bonuses, and controls them on an endless stage with an auto-generated, repeating layout. The player's weapons attack automatically, and the goal is to survive as long as possible against constant waves of monsters that inflict damage when they come in contact with the player. Defeating monsters and exploring the stage allows the player to collect experience gems, which are used to level up, "floor chicken", which restores the player's health, and other helpful items. Each level increase provides the player the choice of three or four weapons and passive power-ups; once the player has collected six weapons and six power-ups and upgraded them all fully, any further levels they gain offer only gold coins or floor chicken. Another way to upgrade weapons and power-ups is to open chests, which are dropped by particularly powerful monsters and may contain one, three, or five random items. Most weapons have an ultimate form that can be attained by opening a chest after fully upgrading them and meeting other specific conditions.Sessions of Vampire Survivors have a soft time limit of 15 or 30 minutes, depending on the stage chosen. At the time limit, the stage is cleared of all enemies and a final, tremendously strong enemy named Death will spawn. One additional Death will appear every consecutive minute thereafter to ensure the player's eventual demise. A session that reaches or exceeds the stage's time limit is considered a successful completion and rewards bonus gold coins. In between sessions, accumulated gold coins can be spent to unlock new characters and persistent power-ups. Additionally, by completing challenges, the player can also unlock new stages, weapons, and characters.Vampire Survivors is nominally set in rural Italy in 2021. Hordes of monsters summoned by the evil Bisconte Draculó ravage the land, and the Belpaese family and other heroic survivors take it upon themselves to hunt down and defeat Draculó. This quest takes them through monster-infested locales such as a cursed forest, a haunted library, an abandoned dairy plant, an ominous tower, and an otherworldly chapel.Developer Luca "poncle" Galante explained that he created Vampire Survivors because he wanted to manage a community, based on his past experience as being an admin for an Ultima Online server. The game was inspired by Magic Survival, a mobile game that also consisted of a character automatically attacking enemies. Development of the initial early access version took around a year, with Galante spending around £1100 on assets, art, and music.The success of the game exceeded Galante's expectations and allowed him to quit his job in February 2022 to focus completely on development of the game. He was informally assisted by "a few friends" in their spare time. Planned content included additional weapons, characters, and stages, and an "endless mode". Galante's intent was to bring Vampire Survivors out of early access by the end of 2022. Galante hired multiple freelancers in March 2022 to expand the Vampire Survivors team and accelerate development. In addition to outlining the scope of the promised new content with a roadmap, Galante explained that a major milestone slated for mid-2022 would be porting Vampire Survivors to an "industry-standard" game engine to improve its overall performance.The full game was released for macOS and Windows on October 20, 2022. The game was also ported to Xbox One and Xbox Series X/S on November 10, 2022.While Vampire Survivors was initially obscure on release, by late January 2022 it became a hit and reached over 30,000 concurrent players on Steam. This number continued to climb, with the game reaching over 70,000 concurrent players the following month. While not the first game in its genre, Vampire Survivors led to several other games based on automatic gameplay and roguelike progression being released the following year, most released for a small price and in early access.Vampire Survivors received "generally favorable" reviews for Windows according to review aggregator Metacritic; the Xbox Series X/S version received "universal acclaim".Ian Walker of Kotaku and Graham Smith of Rock Paper Shotgun praised the game, both comparing the game to dopamine. Polygon's Nicole Carpenter noted the game's depth, with her saying "no one streamer I've watched played entirely the same". Aaron Zimmerman of Ars Technica named Vampire Survivors as his pick for game of the year.

_childDocuments_.review: Vampire Survivors is a pretty good game, and it is also a pharmaceutical formulation of mechanics and audiovisuals already proven by other games to "work". Absolutely nothing about it is original: it's a world you're already familiar with (Castlevania), with rules you're already familiar with (every smash-hit so-called "roguelike", e.g. Risk of Rain, that's been pervading the indie scene), and a dash of lootbox & iPad slot game key-jangling, all laid upon a gameplay foundation that can be fully described in one (or two!) three-word sentences. But does originality and human sensory abuse matter? You be the judge. The fact remains that all of these elements are combined well, and are used to provide an intriguing challenge - sometimes easy, sometimes hard, always requiring a modicum of creativity. There's a modestly respectable distance between how a beginner moves and builds and how an expert moves and builds, but no more than that. Balance is surprisingly "decent", with some outliers. 15 hours in (across two days of ownership), and I still have a small list of challenges left. I've seen just about everything, but I'm still looking forward to doing those challenges. The journey of unlocking everything is compelling. I do not believe that this game is worthy of mastery once you have unlocked everything. But it's a nice journey, so that isn't a complaint.There's a reason that the ratings are so high, and it is that it's possible to dislike this game only through contrarianism, principle, or unmet preconceived expectations. Without those things, you are just left with fun. So, have fun! I also recommend it as an EA game because this could be the final version and I would still be quite satisfied with the purchase. It feels like version .9 when really it's only about halfway done. Cool!One thought I have is that if half of the fun of the gameplay is picking your items, and the entire item picking process is predicated on evolution pairs, are the evolution pairs truly intelligently designed to serve the gameplay? In their current state, they're restrictive and force the player to make cookie-cutter decisions. The way they currently are is acceptable for now, but I imagine that as the game and the playerbase matures, people will get sick of having to always get the armor if they want the runetracer, or tired of feeling like their run is spoiled if they can't get one. Some items are useless without their evo pair, and some items are so good that their evo pair isn't necessary.Item evolution is one of the best features of the game, and its most special, so I hope it is developed with care!

_childDocuments_.review: I have never done a hard drug in my life. Growing up in a privileged, predominantly white neighbourhood with no small amount of wealth and with no likely consequences, that might come as a surprise. Despite having potential access to some incredible stuff, or so I'm imagining, it never crossed my mind why anyone in their right mind would want to inject the good ♥♥♥♥ into their veins. That was until the other day where I played Vampire Survivors.Vampire Survivors is a game that was unleashed into early access on the 17th of December, 2021, and is still in early access at the time of this writing. It is the single best example, in recent memory, as to what makes a video game video gamey. It is the pure, raw, and un-refined stuff that lays bare why kids and adults alike get hooked on the stuff. The game is amongst the simplest and easiest examples of what a game can be; a power fantasy, an arcade score smasher, and a constant wallop of positive reinforcement wrapped up in the skin of a 1990's Castlevania. Your character in Vampire Survivors begins weak, barely able to handle more than a dozen bats at a time. By the end of a 30 minute run, you have easily massacred tens of thousands of monsters, using nothing but a joystick. The monsters hardly matter in their numbers or behaviour, mechanically amounting to a slow and steady deluge of dumb idiots slamming themselves face-first into the attacks spewing from every angle of your little character. There are some cute tricks that the monsters can do, but not many, and this leaves the player with very few choices to make in the heat of the moment. This is an interesting choice seeing as the player can do one thing only: move. The rest of the game is automatic. Vampire Survivors is in essence a bullet hell, but the bullets are very slow and can be eliminated."It's a bullet hell, but you're the bullet hell" is the way I've heard this described. Although I agree the game is a bullet hell, I do find the way Vampire Survivors handles the tropes of the genre refreshing. As I said before, the bullets are literally waves of thousands of monsters headed your way. There are few intricacies to this, and dodging is simple so long as the monsters are dying. To kill them, the players needs to collect and co-ordinate a suite of weapons gained by leveling up and picking up treasure chests. These weapons are nearly all reskinned and appropriated Castlevania weapons: the knife, the axe, holy water, you name it. They can all be leveled up fairly quickly, and they get immensely more powerful as you do so. Alongside your up-to 6 weapons, you can choose a bunch of support abilities as well; these include increased movement speed, area of effect on weapons, or the incredibly powerful Duplicator that makes more projectiles. Although you don't get to push any buttons yourself, the number of bullets and effects spewing from your character sprite goes from a trickle to a torrent of spinning scythes, lasers, and fireballs in little time at all. If you choose the right weapon and support items combinations you can get even more powerful versions of your weapons, and this is where the heart of the choices in the game lead up to: a question. How fast can I kill these guys? The answer is yes, so long as you've chosen correctly and don't walk into enemies like a nimrod. This is the heart of the power fantasy in Vampure surivors, and part of the reason why it's so engrossing, though the game puts a hard cap on how powerful you're allowed to feel. I'll speak about this later on, so… put a pin in this for a few minutes.After a run, or when you die, the game tallies how much gold you've collected over the run. This is not the blue experience gems that eventually litter the field like a spilled glitter bomb, but the proper cold hard cash you get from opening treasure chests, finding coins on the ground, or leveling up so much that you can't upgrade your weapons anymore and are forced to choose between largely useless chicken or money.  This money is funneled into a meta-game progression which can boost your natural stats by a significant margin. It's fairly straightforward: you spend gold to be more powerful, get further into the game, and then get more powerful by spending more gold that you found by getting further into the game.  Coupled with the randomized item choices in-game, Vampire Survivors has the shadows of what it takes to be a roguelite. That said, the levels aren't random and the enemies come in the same waves, one after the other.The elements of a roguelite are there, but Vampire Survivors has less in common with the Binding of Isaac or Dead Cells than with Shoot-em ups and arcade booth coin slammers.So what does this game even do, then? It's easy, maybe too easy, and yet I find myself impelled to play rounds every couple of minutes. The only reason I can think of is dopamine, injected directly into the eyes and ears.As you mulch through hundreds of the little bastards on screen, the monsters drop little gems. These are your experience points. Every experience gem gives a handy little "ting" to let the player know they got the stuff. At first, it's just a couple of tings here and there. By the end of the game it's a roar of sound effects, beeps and boops and all that other junk that players have come to expect means "reward" in game terms. The game primes players by giving only a slow trickle of this positive reinforcement before overloading them with a high that is normally quite difficult to achieve in most other games. To call it a sensory overload, an overdose of pixelated glory, is an understatement. To have a game give success so easily, so readily and so quickly, is what forces Vampire Survivors to be not just a fun game, but an addicting one; a low barrier of entry to a cascade of power, a fantasy that relies on very little effort being put into the thing. It's a game that's perfect for the lazy gamer, and admittedly that's not a bad thing. Sometimes it's great to be lazy and relax.That said, the brain can only handle so much, and the game developers know that. First, after 30 minutes the game will end your run forcefully, sic'ing death itself to end you. To experience that kind of power again, to taste that proverbial dragon, you're going to have to play another run. Second, I've played 15 hours at the time of this writing, but now the irritation begins to set in. The boredom creeps up on me like the monsters in the game, slowly until the press of them overwhelms me and overpowers my sense of fun. Now when I play, it feels like doing a routine, like something that simply is done. It took me about 15 hours, but I have absolutely spent the game. I've wrung it out like a sopping rag, until it is dry and offers nothing more to me. That's when the developers drop another patch with new items and content, which is apparently going to keep happening on a weekly basis. Then I'm in for another couple of hours, finding the new novelties and doing my very best to break the game again.For $3, I'd say that's not a bad spend. The closest thing to a neighbour this game has is Deathstate. It's the same idea: the character automates your offense while the player controls all the movement, coupled with a deeper and more menacing game. If you've played Vampire Survivors,  maybe Deathstate can give you more of the same with a different vibe.

_childDocuments_.review: Vampire Survivors is a game I saw many people play and thought what the hell is the appeal to this? Especially once I learned that it is primarily just moving the character. You do not even aim the weapons in the game (well, most of them). Then I noticed it was an incredibly low priced game so I said what the hell and tried it out. Since trying it out, I have struggled to really describe what kind of game it is. It is this weird mishmash of a twin stick shooter with one stick, bullet hell, rouge-lite, horde mode game. And it's actually a blast? That is the biggest take away for me. Pinning a genre on it isnt needed because it's things like this that make new games fun. Its incredibly simplistic but very unique.It's so well paced too, the way it spaces out new weapons, levels, gameplay modes and such. Awesome Castslevania inspired sprites and music that is that perfect mix of catchy but not grating to listen to after repeat listens. It makes it hard to put down but at the same time easy to pick up because if you can control yourself its only a 30 minute run. I am not entirely sure if something like this existed before it, but even if that was the case it doesn't take away the fact the game is very good. And with a price tag like this? Just try it.I also must say, out of all the games I have played, this is probably the most amount of time I have gotten out of a game for the money that wasn’t on sale or I got for free in the first place. Insane value.Only criticism is that once you get maxed upgrades and most of everything unlocked you begin to max out in the x-teen minute mark, making the game a minimum 10 minute afk fest. Maybe in the final release it will be fixed, and its still satisfying to get to that state even if you are doing nothing. Hopefully this can get tweaked but even if it doesn't, you have already played several hours at this point to get that strong.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the most fun I've had in a game so far this year. Vampire Survivors blends charming retro RPG aesthetics with hack and slash intensity to create one of the best indie games I have ever laid my hands on. The loop of "Level up, kill collect, retry." is incredibly addicting and satisfying, and no two runs ever play out exactly the same. By far the most satisfying element of the game is the immediate power creep the game gives you, where you go from having to carefully considering your positioning and item picks, to simply emitting damage as you move side to side, hacking through huge waves of enemies. The game's intense visuals and wide variety of items is offset by the simplicity of the controls. Attacks are automatic, meaning all you ever use is the left stick and A button on your controller, or WSAD and space on your keyboard. The game manages to look and feel intense this way, without being confusing. At £2, or roughly $3, this game is one of the most fun games you can get on Steam at the moment, with one of the lowest entry fees for what it is. I would have been happy to pay more for such a great experience. If you're looking for a game to kill time, or even something you can play for hours on end without even noticing the time go by, this is your best choice right now.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Lots of fun, tons of unlockable things, learning curve is gentle, easily playable with one hand, lots of replay value, and it's dirt cheap!You don't control the firing of your weapons, only your characters' movement, which can be a bit strange at first, but adds a lot of depth for me, as weapon cooldown and which combinations of weapons/items you pick can make up for that lack of control.The first few levels can seem very difficult, especially with just the whip to start with, but keep at it, and remember, you don't have to win to unlock new things; even a failed run can earn you some really useful stuff.  The art style is fun, and my older machine (Xeon E5-2643 3.5ghz, GTX 1060 mini 6gb, 32gb ram) can run it just fine without any slowdown, even when the screen is completely full of monsters and projectiles.In my opinion, this game is just about perfect for parents or late night workers; the 30 minute time limit on levels is a perfect bite sized gaming experience, and won't keep you up all night.  Although the "one more run" factor is pretty high!Try to avoid watching or reading too much about it when first starting out; the game has built in clues, upgrade guides, and other reference stuff to help you out, but half the fun of it is trying new weapon/item/character/level combinations and seeing what you like best.  That said, some things can be a real bear to figure out without help, so it's good there is such a vibrant community for this game.The value for money on this one is out of this world, and I definitely recommend grabbing the DLCs, as they add a ton to the game.The castlevania feel of the whole thing is great, as a CV fan will spot lots of references to it, ranging from the subtle to blatant.  The 2d sprite style is also easy on the eyes.  HOWEVER, this is one game where I would take the epilepsy warning very seriously, once you become powerful, some weapons generate a LOT of flashing lights.As for downsides, some levels feel far harder than others, but with experimentation I've usually been able to find a build that works.  Some of the snowy levels still frustrate me, but that can be a positive thing too, keep me experimenting to find new ways to deal with them.I know I'm heaping praise on this game, and it may not be for everyone, but it really works well for me, and I think most all folks can get some enjoyment out of it.  I wish it was on the nintendo switch, that would really be awesome!

_childDocuments_.review: I expected to play this for like 45 minutes and be tired of it. "How could a twin stick shooter with only one stick be all that fun? You can't even aim anything!"33 hours later......Vampire Survivors is a fantastic example of devilishly simple interfaces leading to complex entertainment when built well. Luca and poncle oughta be REAL proud of what they've put together here.The roguelite/randomness elements aren't TOO random, so if you want a certain particular build, you will almost certainly end up with it most of the time. That's a complaint I have had with a lot of entries in this genre. If there's certain weapons or items that you entirely dislike using, you can (eventually) just ban them from the pool of items. A really good solution! I don't feel like I've needed to do any grinding, and my endgame is "collect and do and see pretty close to everything." Though if you're wanting to go beyond that, there's a lot of potential grinding awaiting you with golden eggs providing very tiny PERSISTENT stat boosts with no upper limit.Additionally, Italian isn't a language you see much in games, so that's neat.Small complaint: Near the end of level time limits when I'm doing fairly well, there's a LOT of lag/slowdown that happens, as there's a ton of elements going on at once with particles, enemies, animations, and various loot drops, all stacking and overlapping. Turning off damage numbers and flashing effects (in the pause menu options) helps a little. A limit of the engine, not the game's issue..

_childDocuments_.review: This game is dangerously addictive. Sunk 3 hours into it the moment I bought it and it felt like an hour at most. Be prepared to keep starting new runs with no regard to how much time has passed.On a more serious note, this game is incredibly fun for those who enjoy building up a character through various weapons and abilities. You'll unlock new things as you go, and be able to upgrade them each run. There are permanent upgrades that can be unlocked as well. No two runs ever pan out the same way, with some ending near the start, and some taking much longer (in a good way).The scaling of enemy difficulty in each run feels incredibly fair, more so than almost any other game I've played. You'll know when you made the wrong decision for item grabs/upgrades when this scaling happens, allowing you to learn from your mistakes and find solid upgrade paths that extend your runs.I've been on the hunt for games like this, where you enter a play area and have to deal with enemies, and then earn upgrades and gear that you can improve over time. I might get some backlash for this, but I equate this game to a more involved "idle game" where you actually have to take control of the character, but the upgrade paths mirror that style of play a lot. This is exactly what I've been looking for, as I've been playing multiple idle games recently but nothing has scratched the itch of being able to take more control of the game and feel more fulfilled in progressing into higher levels.All in all, I highly recommend this game. For the price, you won't find much else that feels as worthwhile to play in this genre (at least as far as I know). Fantastic game.

_childDocuments_.review: Vampire Survivors is an absolutely ugly mess of a ridiculously cheap indie one-stick auto shooter made by a single developer where you often lose where the hell you are on the screen and you don’t always have great control over where your character is firing. It’s cruelly punishing until it’s not, and then it’s so easy you become effectively immortal.Taking generic ghoulie baddies out means they drop gemeralds that give you more power. Collect enough power and you can choose an upgrade to make your puny weapon slightly less puny, pick another puny weapon to add to your arsenal, or a passive buff. Wander round aimlessly and more badsos appear, dropping more gemeralds for you to nip in and scoop up to get more power ups, trying to last as long as you possibly can as the waves get bigger and bigger and the badsos legitimately bad.So how am I credibly talking up this uninspiring sounding simple title as one taking its seat at the top table of gaming in 2022? Because the action is tight, frenetic, and astonishingly tactical and strategic, despite the rough-as-♥♥♥♥ presentation.There’s a real urgency to get the right powers to help you in the situation you’re in at that moment. The six weapons and passives you can pick up are locked in, no switching them out for something better, and you *have* to take from the list offered even if you don’t really like any of them - at least initially.Stick with it and you’re really rewarded as you find out that one of your weapons combines with one of your passives, and creates a brand new uber weapon.  New characters, weapons and maps unlock, and before you know it, previously impenetrable swarms of enemies can be proverbially ploughed through - and man, what swarms!Like so many games I love, it has twists and turns that you probably won’t expect. It has the stickiness and flow that make great games, with simple controls and a really stripped back concept mean it’s highly accessible. Vampire Survivors represents the vigour and energy that I love.I am sure that this sort of game existed in some form before, but the way it’s implemented here makes it a true genre builder. I genuinely believe that in years to come, we’ll look back at this $5 game as one that changed gaming not just for Indies, but also in AAAs learning from its less is more approach. A true classic, and I don’t say that lightly.

_childDocuments_.review: Vampire Survivors offers an addictive rogue-lite experience that will keep you coming back for more. As a fan of both rogue-lite games and vampire lore, I was intrigued by the premise of playing as a vampire surviving in a world filled with perilous enemies.The game features procedurally generated levels, ensuring that each playthrough feels fresh and unpredictable. I appreciated the variety of environments, enemies, and challenges that I encountered as I explored the game world. From battling hordes of undead minions to facing off against powerful bosses, Vampire Survivors kept me on my toes at every turn.One of the highlights of the game is the deep progression system, which allows you to unlock new abilities, weapons, and upgrades as you progress. Experimenting with different builds and strategies added a layer of depth to the gameplay, keeping me engaged for hours on end.Visually, Vampire Survivors impresses with its charming pixel art style and fluid animations. The soundtrack also deserves praise for setting the tone and atmosphere of the game perfectly.While Vampire Survivors offers a challenging experience, it never feels unfair thanks to tight controls and responsive gameplay mechanics. Even in moments of defeat, I found myself eager to jump back in and try again, knowing that each run brings new opportunities for success.Overall, Vampire Survivors is a must-play for fans of rogue-lite games and vampire-themed adventures. With its addictive gameplay, deep progression system, and charming presentation, it's a title that will sink its teeth into you and refuse to let go.
