_childDocuments_.review: Update #2: It's quite simply -still- one of the best games I've ever played. It's packed with content and unlocks. The DLC is great. The music is great. The gameplay mechanics are great, especially when you unlock the game-changing/breaking mechanics such as Limit Break, Golden Eggs (increase base stats of a character), and Arcanas (ability/run modifiers for the current run). Curse is an excellent mechanic for crafting the tailor-making to your liking depending on the build you want to try and the character.I'll never tire of the experimentation aspect of this game. It's like a sandbox filled with cool and interesting tools for me to use and combine to my satisfaction. Amazing work. Amazing game. Go find some vampires if you can and destroy thousands upon heaping thousands of undead. I've literally slayed tens of millions of monsters now at this point with the occasional boss here and there.Update: This game is quite simply one of the best games I've ever played. If you enjoy min/maxing and experimenting with different builds, you will naturally find yourself running clinical trials thinking, "Okay, but what if I mix this accessory to increase projectile speed with that bouncing weapon. And then add this accessory to do reduce cooldown... And then... And then..." endlessly. The recently introduced Limit Breaker game mechanic only makes experimentation that much more engrossing by letting you over-level specific aspects of weapons that could be the literal amount of projectiles per tick/cast, the area size of its effect, the speed at which it travels, and so on. It makes every run different and lets me set wildly different goals. Sometimes I just like to focus on one specific weapon to see how badly I can wreak havoc on the baddies. I've done things... terrible things... that turned them into dust before they could even approach the edge of the screen.It's awesome.--What an amazing game for less than a gallon of gas. If you like destroying thousands upon thousands of enemies, Vampire Survivors will be your jam. There's more fun packed in here than most "triple-A" releases.You can expect gratuitous pixel death, interesting weapon combinations and evolutions, hordes, more hordes, and different characters that can encourage different playstyles. The transformation to weak hero into a god of death and destruction is satisfying every time, every run.This is already a great game with the potential to become even better through content updates. Even if the game received no updates at all though, it's more than worth its price. Can you survive 30 minutes, hero?

_childDocuments_.review: For $3, this is one of the best games I have ever played.  If you like old school Castlevania games, this has the powerups from those games in a new bullet-hell rogue-like formula.  It has a lot of secrets to unlock and the gameplay loop is highly addictive.  Its simplicity at first glance belies the complexity that emerges the more you play.   The creator is also constantly adding updates.  Since I started playing, they have added 3 levels, 4 characters, 5 weapons and upgrades; vastly expanding player choice.  The speedrunning and world record setting scene is very active; and while many play styles are possible it takes skill and luck to really master this game. I would give this a 9/10.Coming back after a few expansions have been released to reinforce my earlier recommendation.  All the DLCs add significant content to the game and new mechanics.  Their collaboration with Konami on both the Contra and Castlevania franchises is especially worth noting.  Ode to Castlevania adds an extensive map with dozens of secrets, 80 characters to unlock, dozens of new weapons and powerups; it is truly staggering how much extra content you get for 4$.  The original DLCs are also excellent: Both Legacy of the Moonspell and Tides of the Foscari are great adding numerous new characters, a couple new maps, and several new weapons and powerups.  If you love the original game, then each of the DLCs are worth your investment.  Plus the development team continues to provide free updates outside of the DLCs.  This is a development team that values customer support and loyalty and rewards it.

_childDocuments_.review: Have you ever played a bullet hell and wanted to be the reason it was hell?Have you ever wanted to be the tower in a tower defense game?Are you the kind of person who has too many games but can never bring themselves to play any of them?If you say "yes" to any of these, then Vampire Survivors is for you! It's fun, it's easy to pick up, it's chaotic, and there's a good amount of depth to keep you coming back for more. It took me about 18 hours to get all the achievements, which is amazing for a game as small and cheap as this -- only $3 when I bought it! _childDocuments_.review: This thing is three dollars and terminally simple while also being a fantastic timesink with countless possibilities to reach the end of its 30 minute survival window. The mechanics and capabilities of the game actually stretch far deeper than you might believe on the surface level, and there's a degree of depth and planning ahead required to reach the 'end' of some of the secrets in store that you'd never believe unless you experienced it yourself.Put simply? I'd say this game's a time killer, if you've got a few hours to burn and want to make some progress? Fire it up, do a few runs, see what you can accomplish. With any luck, you might just encounter Death, or (spoilers) you might find a way to kill him instead.The concept is simple enough, pick a character, pick a level, and jump in, every character starts with a special weapon, kill enemies, level up, upgrade that weapon or acquire other weapons and items that increase your odds of survival. You'll go from having to carefully kite around entire crowds of foes to throwing out so many projectiles and death lasers that you'll feel like you're the boss of your own personal bullet hell.There are also plenty of ways to specialize. Maybe you want to deal damage at close range? What about far away? Single target or multitarget? Do you want to focus on AOE and massive damage zones or so much raw DPS put into a single projectile that even elite enemies can't survive a single hit? Do you want a regenerating forcefield or a zone of death around you that constantly damages and pushes away enemies? You've got choices, and these are just things you can make with the stuff you find starting out. There's a whole ton of locked areas, items, and characters, and the game is even so self-aware of its depth and complexity that it rewards people tech-savvy enough to crack and modify their save file with a secret character.The developer of this knows what they're doing, and it's still getting regularly updated, so this isn't some pump-and-dump asset flip.Sure, it might be $2.99, but I know some friends that've sunk enough time into it that they've gotten a better return on their purchase than Elden Ring, and I'm not making that up.

_childDocuments_.review: I am 37.My ex-wife and I have a daughter together, and adopted our son together. They are now both 4 years old.When we were going through our separation, I found myself lost and miserable. I was self destructive. I got so mad one day from everything spiralling out of my control that I punched some concrete in a moment of overwhelming emotion. That caused me to break my 5th metacarpal in my right hand... my working hand... my games hand.. the hand that I held and carried my children to bed with.. In fact, I may have only played this game a day or two.. With that being said, after doing so, I had a new found joy and hope for life. _childDocuments_.review: A marriage between garlic bread and challah...it's about time this happened!You can use your favorite challah recipe or the one I've included below. The main element is the garlic mixture which can be used on virtually any dough (although I would be cautious using it with a super sweet recipe.As you can see, I rolled out each strand and brushed it with the garlic mixture. It's a bit fiddly and time-consuming. The other option is to just brush each strand and then braid. The flavor won't be as intense and it can be hard to braid when the strands are oily and slippery (it's hard to keep the ends together). But sometimes it's worth the saved time.I baked mine on a sheet pan this time and they came out wider and flatter. If you use a loaf pan (or there are oval pans specifically for challah), you will get a higher fuller look. Good news - taste is unaffected!For more about baking challah in general, and for a larger challah recipe, please see my Traditional Soft Fluffy Challah.Challah Ingredients:2¼ tsp. dry yeast (0.25 oz. / 7 grams)1 tsp. sugar1 cup warm water1 egg¼ cup honey3 tbsp. oil1 tsp. saltApproximately 4 cups bread flour (as always, add the flour slowly towards the end and feel if the dough needs more or less)Garlic Oil Ingredients1/3 cup extra virgin olive oil6 cloves garlic, crushed1 tsp kosher salt1/3 cup flat-leaf parsley, choppedOptional: flaked salt for garnishDirections:Whisk garlic oil ingredients together. Set aside.Dissolve yeast and sugar in ¼ cup warm water in a medium-sized bowl. Let sit about 15 minutes until thick and frothy.Add the egg, honey, oil, salt, remaining ¾ cup of water, and 3 cups of the flour. Mix until a loose batter forms. Add the rest of the flour slowly. You may not need it all, so go slowly towards the end. Alternatively, you may need slightly more. The dough should be soft but not sticky. Once the dough has enough flour, knead it well. You can do this recipe by hand or with a mixer (using the dough hook). Let the mixer do the kneading for you if you’re using one.Cover the dough with a wet towel or plastic wrap and put it in a warm place to rise for about 1-1½ hours. Dough should double in size.Tip the dough out onto your work surface and let it rest for 10 minutes.Divide it into six evenly-sized pieces. Roll each piece into a strand. Then take a rolling pin and roll the strand lengthwise so that it forms a long rectangle. Brush with the garlic mixture and roll-up jelly-roll style so that it reforms a strand. Repeat with remaining strands. Braid each three strands together, yielding two challahs. Brush the top of the loaves with more of the garlic mixture and sprinkle lightly with flaked sea salt (optional).Transfer loaves to a baking sheet lined with parchment paper OR two loaf pans. Cover and let rise in a warm place for another 30-45 minutes. Brush gently with more of the garlic mixture and place in the oven. OPTIONAL: If you prefer a shiny finish on your challah, brush with a beaten egg and then add the second layer of garlic mixture.Bake at 400°F (200°C) for 20 minutes. Remove from oven and brush again with the garlic mixture. Return to oven, lower temperature to 350°F (180°C) and bake for another 20 minutes. NOTE: Time will fluctuate depending on your oven and the type of pans you used. I used disposable aluminum pans - for real bakeware you may want to lower the temperature and/or reduce the time slightly. Loaf should be golden on top, and firm on the bottom.Remove from oven and as soon as possible (if you try immediately, they may break, so wait 10-15 minutes) transfer to a cooling rack and brush again generously with the garlic oil. If you don't have a cooling rack, you risk the bottom of your challah going soggy (this is a risk in general, but particularly with the garlic oil we've been dousing the loaves with. If that happens, put your challah back in the oven for a few minutes, directly on the oven racks (no pan). That will crisp up any soggy spots very quickly.

All you do in this game is move around evading monsters.  You only control the movement.I wish - when you pick up an item - it hinted at what it's evolved form might do, and what other item would get you there.  For example:  The Cross evolves with the Clover.  I wish a message popped up after you pick up the Cross like, "I hope you get lucky with this item..." or "This item has brought many warriors luck."Also, I wish you could hit Escape to look at your stats, and mouse-over the weapons you have to see their individual damage or cooldown or area of effect stats.  You only found out the damage-per-second for each weapon when the run is over.There should be an achievement for getting the evolved forms of all 6 weapons, and an additional achievement for 7-out-of-6 (evolving Peachyone & Ebony Wings merges them together, giving you back a weapon slot).I wish you could abort a run.  Sometimes I've already put together the right combination of weapons so I'm unlikely to die for a while, but I know because of my loadout I won't be able to pickup the last weapon or powerup I need to evolve everything.  I need an easy way to Escape + Abort Run.Would love an endless mode.  :-)After a while you accumulate Gold to purchase modifiers from the main menu.  This is like, adding +10% speed for each rank.  One of those is Curse, improving the health/speed/etc of enemies to make the game harder again. _childDocuments_.review: You could spend your money on a coffee, but why caffeinate when you can turn yourself into an undead blender mowing down legions of monsters for hours on end? Vampire Survivors is dangerously addictive and costs less than a dollar menu item, yet it’s somehow more thrilling than most AAA games. The concept is simple: pick a character, grab some weapons, and become an unstoppable storm of garlic, holy water, and flying axes that annihilates anything daring enough to spawn on your screen.The gameplay loop goes like this: walk around, pick up upgrades, get more ridiculous powers, laugh maniacally as hordes of enemies melt around you. Rinse and repeat. Before you know it, you've spent three hours just perfecting your “whirling tornado of knives” build, and it’s 3 a.m. If you die, don't worry—just restart and make an even crazier loadout. There’s nothing to memorize, no combos to learn; just keep moving, grab everything that shines, and watch the chaos unfold. And for the price? It’s the best bad habit you’ll ever pick up.

_childDocuments_.review: This game blends something really intriguing between kind of bullet-hell 'screen full of enemies' games, the instant dopamine kick of leveling up once about every 20 seconds, and the casualness of an idle game.  I find the gameplay very satisfying in the way your power ramps, but all you're ever doing is moving your character around and making decisions about what weapons or abilities to acquire and upgrade.  And frankly, I love that it's a roguelike with a hard cap of 30 minutes.  For an adult gamer, it's kind of nice to be able to get something satisfying out of that short a period of play time.  I think the Castlevania nods throughout are fun and nostalgic, and the game being $3 for Early Access feels like a steal.  If there's more coming for this game, I can't wait to see what it'll look like.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is easily worth the $3 price tag.  It is casual but engaging.  Playing the game is easy and satisfying, and feels rewarding instantly.As you spend more time playing, you can exchange coins for power-ups at the start screen.  An assortment of characters gives you options to approach the game differently, as they start with different perks and weapons.Considering the price, and the fun to be had, I give Vampire Survivors a 9/10.  This game is perfect for when you want to slip a little gaming in and only have limited time.  I don't want to mislead though, once you start, you won't want to stop. With updates ongoing, I'm sure there will be more to enjoy in the future. I hope this gem gets the attention it deserves.Edit: I originally reviewed Vampire Survivors after about 90 minutes played. I loved it so much I couldn't help but recommend it to everyone I know (this is the best $3 I've spent in recent memory, possibly ever lol). I now have about 16 hours played.  I thought I would edit my review and share my even greater enthusiasm for the game.I recently beat Mad Forest! I unlocked the Inlaid Library a while ago, but stuck to Mad Forest because I wanted to finish that first. Wow, after the 20 minute mark things get really hairy... in absolutely spectacular fashion! This game gets better and better the more you experience and unlock. I wish I would've paid more attention to weapon upgrades - and unlocking all the weapons, items, and characters - earlier on.  I spent so much time just enjoying the early game, I didn't really pay attention to unlocking and upgrading things.With a greater understanding, I have a few tips for new players:First, you can refund your coins spent on power-ups at any time and re-build.  These apply to every character from then on.  Character's own perks get added on top of your main power-ups. Power ups cost more the more you unlock.  So if you want to max out "Luck" first, every upgrade to Luck after the first is more expensive, and all other power-ups become gradually more expensive as well. Just something to keep in mind as you try new things.Second, try to get multiple weapons as soon as possible.  After choosing weapons, check to see if they can be evolved, and actively try to evolve them. This process means getting a particular weapon to level 8, and also having in your possession the corresponding item needed to evolve the weapon.  Once these requirements are met, the next chest you pick up will drop the evolved weapon (you will get an achievement the first time you upgrade each weapon).  Most - but not all - weapons can be evolved presently, and the devs continue making great additions. I don't think it will be too long before all weapons have evolutions.Third, check the "Guides" section on Steam's Vampire Survivors screen after selecting the game in your library. There are a lot of super helpful guides.  I will include my favorite two below. Other than that, get in there and enjoy.  Survive the night, my friends! Good luck and have fun!My favorite guides:"Weapons and Power ups upgrade path" by Ocram"Item list with upgrades and unlock" by Sulca (this guide also contains a url that you can use to view the table in your browser.  I found this helpful.  I was able to quickly check my second screen for what weapons and items go together for evolutions, as well as how to unlock the weapons and items I didn't have. I pasted said url right under this).

_childDocuments_.review: It took me 38 hours to collect all the Achievements and most of the characters. I say most because I collected everything you can get from playing the game except the ones you need to input codes for.Short version, its a fun game. Its a bullet hell and if you are anything like me, enjoy flashing numbers and colors.Long version, the early game can feel like a bit of a grind. Each run you generally get something new. Survive 30 minutes here, level up weapons to 9 there, so on and so forth. After you get some things unlocked though, the game quickly opens up interesting builds and trying new things. Such as as much as I hate the cat, its great for farming gold so I made an entire build around it. Also sometimes you start a run and the RNG hates you so you just go with what you can and have fun.My only real tips for new players is keep an eye on the Cursed stat, I didn't realize what it was and kept boosting it, not realizing it was increasing difficulty till I started reading through everything. Second tip would be that at any time you can pause, go to Options, and end your run which KEEPS your progress. I could of saved a day probably if I'd known this simply for trying to max certain items and such and NOT keep trying to make it to the 30 minute mark.For a $3 game, I got a solid $20 of fun out it.

_childDocuments_.review: The indie scene is so strong for video games right now. For every complaint one might hear about predatory practices in AAA gaming, failed promises, broken launches, abuse of fear-of-missing-out mechanics, there's a small indie game which comes along that completely blows one's mind in its compelling simplicity. Vampire Survivors—which is basically Castlevania meets Cookie Clicker with some bullet hell aesthetics thrown in the mix—is a prime example of the golden age of indie games we're currently finding ourselves in.Vampire Survivors was probably never meant to be anything profound. Although surely the developer has labored a great deal over the balance, it's a relatively simple game. It appears to be a bullet hell, but in reality, there's very little twitch input required from the player. Your player character fires off their attacks automatically so you're tasked mostly with choosing which upgrades and build paths to pursue, while occasionally moving the player character around the map in order to avoid enemies. Enemies have no projectile attacks of their own; they're relegated to contact damage only, which is a great choice that ends up facilitating this more passive style of playing. So describing this as a bullet hell game, while it might appears accurate from the game's aesthetics, is not really all that accurate. This is a more passive, casual experience in which you are mostly tasked with planning rather than taxing your mechanical skill as a player.Personally, I love that. I'm not a huge fan of bullet hell, and roguelikes are often unappealing to me because I dislike their randomness and the lack of any permanent, long-term upgrades most roguelikes eschew in favor of appealing to the crowd which prefers RNG and chance coming together to facilitate a successful run. Vampire Survivors does have a built-in permanent progression system of unlocking stages, player characters, weapons, and permanent passive upgrades. This all serves to dampen what I dislike about roguelikes, and drew me in to Vampire Survivors even further.In the beginning you'll find yourself mostly bewildered as you experiment with new weapons and tactics, but as you grow more familiar with the game you'll begin to gravitate toward specific playstyles, and putting together the pieces and acquiring evolutions becomes intensely addictive and rewarding.If any of this sounds the least bit compelling to you, then take a shot on Vampire Survivors. Although it's in Early Access, I believe the game currently offers more than enough to warrant the $3 USD price tag, and I'm shocked the developer has kept the game at such a low price. It's an absolute steal with at least twice as much value as the current price tag, so there's really nothing to suggest against purchasing this. I'd go even further and urge anyone considering this game to jump on it now before the developer comes to their senses and raises the price.

_childDocuments_.review: Turns out I like playing these types of games.. Like.. A lot. If you’ve never played this type of game before and you don’t know what to expect, I’ll say that it’s like you took the best parts about an rpg, a shoot em up, and a roguelike, then combined those parts together to create the most crack equivalent of a game possible.The massive success of Vampire Survivors has led to the creation of many many clones, both the games that are trying to cash in on the hype, and the games that are actually trying to bring forth their own unique take and stand out. I mean the popularity of Vampire Survivors has essentially birthed its own “survivor-like” genre. I know that Magic Survival came first and is what inspired the creation of Vampire Survivors itself but history is written by the victor which in this case was definitely Vampire Survivors.So for a bit of lore, I’ve played over two dozen different bullet heaven/survivor-like games at this point, and even after playing that many I’d say that Vampire Survivors was still the best experience out of all of them. Some of those games (like Brotato) have come really close (especially since it has mods), and some of them have been complete and utter garbage. But would I say that Vampire Survivors is the perfect version of this type of game? Well.. Not really.. But I would say that it's at least very close to achieving that perfection in my opinion. I’ve played the game patch by patch since version 0.2 (including both of the dlc releases now) and I think what gives Vampire Survivors such an advantage over the others that have come after is its continued development and refinement. Where other games of this kind might have the fundamental features and similar looking weapons/attacks, they never end up feeling as smooth and polished as they do in Vampire Survivors. Plus the music and sound design are super top notch for an indie game. The bar is set extremely high and while I think it’s very easy to create a Survivor's clone, it’s very hard to create one that’s actually anywhere near as good.Overall though I’ll give the game a 9/10 since I’m a bit hesitant to give it a full 10 but Vampire Survivors is nearly the perfect game in this genre (at least in my opinion).

_childDocuments_.review: In Vampire survivors, you take control of one of an increasing number of available characters and try to stay alive for 30 minutes. Between you and that objective stand literally thousands of pixelated monsters who will assail you from every direction. To help you defend against this virtually limitless number of foes, your character starts with one weapon and one booster stat progression (they’re different for each character). When defeated, most enemies will drop experience gems that you have to collect in order to level up. Upon gaining a level, you’re faced with a choice of 3 to 4 options including getting a new item (weapon or stat-boosting trinket) or leveling up an existing one.What sets Vampire Survivor apart from other action roguelikes is that you don’t have control over your weapons. They activate themselves at set intervals that depend on the type of weapon (some basic ones can fire several times a second, while more devastating ones can take much longer to recharge), their levels and other stats. With this defining feature, Vampire Survivors feels like a one-character auto-battler where you still have direct control of their movement. The actual battles may be tense but there’s little skill involved. The meaty decisions occur when you level up and this happens thankfully frequently enough (typically twice a minute).With its pixel graphics and gothic theme, Vampire Survivors looks like a Castlevania spin-off. Even the music would not be out of place in one of the Belmont family’s adventures. The whole presentation is not particularly sophisticated but holds itself together well.While innovative and fun for the most part, some aspects of the game design are annoying. For once, it’s not self-evident how to progress to the next levels. You must dig into the menu showing the unlockables to get it. Later objectives for bonus levels are similarly obscure. Another slight problem is that even though, on average, you level up often enough, there are still occasional stretches of time when all you have to do is move around and let your auto-firing weapons work for you, which is not terribly engaging and can even feel sedate.Still, with more than 100 unlockable items, levels, characters, and synergies between items that makes them evolve into new ones, the content proposition is generous enough to forgive those flaws, especially at that kind of price.

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine if Smash TV and Touhou had a baby and Castlevania was the godfather.  You would get Vampire Survivors.  The simplest way I can describe this game is a roguelike bullet hell where YOU are the bullet hell and everything around you is trying to survive you.  Not to say this game is easy, as it's quite possible to, with a really unfocused build or by playing recklessly, you can still die very easily.  It is very important you learn how your weapons, items, and passives work.  Characters are all interesting and have powerful passives to offer, some more than others, and each character has a starting weapon that you're stuck with.  All characters have the potential to be powerful, though some have an easier time than others.Though let's get to the nitty gritty.  How often will you die?  Oh, you'll die.  You'll die a lot.  But every run grants you coins, which you can use to buy various permanent powerups to aid future runs, like increased might (power), speed, number of projectiles, and health.  I would advise going for increased speed and projectiles as soon as possible and going for the more defensive powerups much later.  Like Smash TV, a good offense IS a good defense.  And a good defense is no offense at all, so ignore the defensive powerups for a while.  On that same token, I would also advise unlocking additional characters as soon as possible since, while the starting character can be good, the whip is not a good starting weapon.  Imelda can be unlocked for a mere 10 coins and she's easily one of the best characters in the game, due to her passive experience boost and starting with the magic wand.  Weapons can evolve in this game through certain weapon and item interactions.  For example, the whip evolves when paired with the hollow heart and the magic wand evolves when paired with the empty tome.  The hollow heart is purely defensive; it raises your maximum health.  The empty tome, however, reduces the cooldown of all weapons, making them attack more often.  The empty tome is one of the best passive items in the game, right now.Weapon evolutions are, effectively, the meta of Vampire Survivors.  If you want to win, you need to evolve your weapons.  This means picking your build, what weapons you want to work with, and focusing on what you need for them.  If you want to use the super powerful version of the Santa Water, you'll need the attractorb.  And in order to get all the passive items, you'll need to unlock them, which means even your failed runs can help you.  For example, if you want the empty tome, you'll need to be carrying six different weapons in a single run.  If you want the hollow heart, you'll need to survive for one minute as any character.  If you want the pummarola, you'll need to survive five minutes as Gennaro.  There is unlockables everywhere and most can be found in the unlockables section on the title screen.  It's often worth just doing runs knowing you're going to die just to get various unlockables.  Like the pentagram weapon is completely worthless, but getting it to a high level does unlock other stuff and evolving it gives a one-time bonus of 500 coins.Speaking of, do not worry about how you spend your coins.  Just spend them, preferably on offense.  You can refund your coins as often as you like, so it's never worth saving up for a big upgrade when you can buy smaller ones to aid you.  You can always refund later for that big upgrade, once you have the coins.  Speaking of, as you unlock things, the prices of your powerups and characters do increase, so buy things you really want first before buying other upgrades and characters.  There is currently a character for every single weapon, so if you have a favorite, you may want to look up how to get that character as soon as possible.For being a relatively mindless mobile game all about moving around and killing monsters, Vampire Survivors is a pretty fun game, especially for the price.  It can be pretty good for just passing time, as most runs last anywhere from five to thirty minutes, depending on your stage.  Not to mention it can be pretty relaxing to just play a game where you get tons of projectiles and rip all your enemies to shreds while they can't do anything about it.  With some characters, this can get especially bonkers.  When I said you can become the bullet hell, I wasn't joking.  So, if you want a game that's just pure nonsense, where your kill count can be pushing four digits just five minutes into a game, Vampire Survivors might be your jam.  At the least, it's a cheap game with a pretty fun, albeit basic, appeal and can be worth a chuckle from time to time, if not the spectacle of holding off hundreds of dudes with a ring of bibles and santa water.Yes, I did say santa water.  It's probably supposed to be saint water, since it's supposed to be holy water, but they called it santa water for some reason.  And I'm okay with that.

_childDocuments_.review: More addicting than fun in the long run but beyond amazing before that tipping point.Roguelike/lite/whatevers that pull off the spinning plates act are always amazing. It's a seemingly simple task that actually requires insane attention to details and balance to remain fun. A select few pull it off and when they do the Overwhelmingly Positive ratings roll in. We all know them, and Vampire Survivors definitely joins the small club. But it's also its own animal.If you break down your gameplay timeline/investment in Vampire Survivors; The first ~10% would be pure delight as you steadily unlock characters and such while learning the game. Reaching new heights. Breaking records. "Completing" a run. Trying new levels and different item rolls. Then the next ~20% is grinding over the only difficulty hump. You hit your one roadblock. You have to adjust your focus to specific unlocks. Do a tiny bit of grinding. Figure out which character fits your style to do it. And then the final ~70% of your timeline is just pure addiction. You've reached the pinnacle already. It's just a matter of sitting through it X amount of times more to unlock the next achievement to unlock the next achievement to unlock the next... You're invincible. There's no challenge left. You're literally just playing to play and get that next dopamine hit from an achievement popping up in the bottom right corner.So while the spinning plates are balanced with care and the game is fun at its core. The only thing that keeps you around is addiction in its purest form. That's not to say your addiction isn't rewarded though. There are new wrinkles for each of those achievements you get. New levels. New bosses with mind bending ideas that seem genuinely "new" even 20hrs into a highly repetitive game. But again, you're more or less invincible. There's no threat to your runs for hours upon hours now. Even from the new stuff. It's just seeing that new stuff that's keeping you going. You aren't playing, you're just watching all the flashing colors and numbers. You cannot stop even though the challenge is gone. You're literally killing time just to see that next "new thing". That's where the ~70% bulk of the game is. Getting to that tipping point is worth it ten times over. The game is amazing. I threw down for the DLC before I reached the tipping point because it is that good and I wanted to support more. But I dunno if I'll even check the DLC content out at all. I'm ready to break the addiction! I think... Maybe just one more hit...Priced accordingly, I have no problems singing this game's praises far and wide. Plus I know most enjoy achievement hunting more than I do and this game has got that. I just wish the challenge/difficulty progression arc was as stretched as the achievement progression arc. Even just a wee bit longer. It coulda really, really been an all timer. But then again if we had the perfect roguelike/lite/whatever game made, there wouldn't be a reason to play any others. Stay safe, wear garlic.Plays great on the Steam Deck! I mean, you only need a joystick after all.

_childDocuments_.review: When a game is five dollars or under most won't expect much of it.  This game is no exception.  When that game surpasses your expectations, early on there is a sort of euphoria. That euphoria pushes you forward to hold witness to those expectations which were blown up, blown up again then nuked from orbit.  The sad part is that with your expectations obliterated at the atomic level once you log five or six hours the euphoria transmogrifies into stagnation.  Consider this game to be a higher quality Little Caesar's Pizza while maintaining the low cost which derives a high value but a hollow feeling when you eat too much of said fast food.You control one of a wide selection of characters.  You only control the characters movement through the planar landscape while all attacks are automatic.  While many offensive skills automatically target an enemy some do rely on your ability to line up attacks which are triggered automatically.  Frag as many enemies as you can then collect the XP that falls on the ground to level up your character.  The collection of XP is a bit of a chore and slows the game down a bit.  Luckily, half way or so through your thirty minute sojourn, there will be so many enemies on screen that pointing your character in any direction results in copious amounts of XP scattered everywhere.  At level up, select one of three to four semi-random skill upgrades.  Skills consist of passive improvements and attack skills.  Once you get the max number of skills then rank each to their max any further level ups result in your choice of a turkey health pack or a small sack of money.  The money is used to purchase new characters and boost skills.  Some skills are unlocked through achievements or taking an action while playing.  Each active skill as an ultimate form which will require you to level it's associated minor skill to max and also select a matching passive skill.  The play field will be flooded with elite enemies by the time you are within your last minute so the ultimate forms are essential.Once you get the hang of things, you can make the game harder.  Once you get a bit bored you can speed up the timer two fold.  Try the bonus stages before the hangover begins.  Once your expectations get nuked you exit the game.  The experience is familiar yet exhilarating for a short time but it's worth the low entry fee.  Here is to hoping the developer of this game got a nice little pay day then tries again with a bit more feeling, experience and do it in 3D.There are some bugs but not too bad, although there was a game breaking bug where my characters main attack just stopped functioning after passing through a portal.  The fix was to quit.  Some enemies will clip through walls but it's not that big of a deal.  Totally worth it for the sugar high.

_childDocuments_.review: There was a time when everyone was playing this game.Most of them would tell you it was like crack, and they just couldn't put the game down.While others high production costs games existed, somehow, this little game had hooked players worldwide, and they just couldn't put it down. I just looked at that phenomenon with some distance, not really caring about it. I had, at the time, others things to do.I saw the game run, it seemed funny, and the amount of absurd power a character could attain amused me enough to check the store page. Game was cheap, so I told myself, why not, right?Jumping in, it was a constant pleasure. First steps are a bit rough, but it takes about 10 hours pretty much go from "Oh god oh god I'm swarmed!" to being an absolute monster. And then it only becomes more crazy. The game is quite easy to break on your knee, but it doesn't means it is exactly easy to achieve, or mindless either. And it many way, it's a good thing, as this game is a big power fantasy where you go from one character throwing a few projectile to some kind of pixeled abomination throwing so many effects on the screen it's almost impossible to get a good grasp of what's happening, but you assume things are dying everywhere.The game doesn't take itself seriously at all, everything is humorous, from the items, to what they do, to the monsters and their bestiary descriptions. The soundtrack is full of great pieces that keep your blood pumping as you go around murdering enemies with a kinder surprise powered up by a spinach.To make things even better, the game receive new content, both free and paying DLCs, making coming back to it a pleasure just to discover new content... And absolutely brutalise it in few hours flat, because you're an absolute brute piloting a caterpillar powered by an addiction for Faberge eggs.Make no mistake, if you wonder why this game has so many clones, it's because it is THE game that came out of nowhere, and was full of greatness the players almost universally loved. This is where it all began, and while it will be imitated, it will probably never be equalled. Many will try to jump on the bandwagon to try to get the Vampire Survivor money, but they will never be able to claim the merit to be original.Cheap, with a lot of content and more added to it, funny, enjoyable and well designed. There is pretty much no reason to not play it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game made me have an addiction problemAt the time of writing this Steam says I played for 145h, I could swear it was like 20 min topsIt's the peak of endorphin generator systemsThe only problem I have with it is that you can't turn yourself down so you can buff your character to the point where it's so fast that it will travel a long distance in a single frame. This makes it basically impossible to collect items. _childDocuments_.review: I'm a simple person. I like survival. I like idle game-style leveling. I like games that mix genres.This game delivers exactly that. _childDocuments_.review: this game is ridiculously addictive. it has just enough gameplay elements to it with the bullet hell dodging, roguelike permadeath, and random item delivery that i don't feel like a doofus watching number go up like with idle/clicker games. learning the rules of the game is inviting and intuitive, you won't get your hand held but it's simple enough to start playing that it's hard to completely mess up and doing things correctly is inherently rewarding so you learn naturally as you play.

_childDocuments_.review: In my Steam library, I have at least 10 great games that I haven't found the time to play yet and I am sure I'd love them - classics like Ori and the Blind Forest, Mark of the Ninja, also AAA titles like MK11 and Doom Eternal. All of those are taking a back seat because of this game.This freaking game. This lovingly crafted 3$ gem. For one, everything is so well balanced that for such a small game, even at 30+ hours of gameplay there's still stuff to do, and runs still feel fun. You wanna unlock all the achievements, you wanna collect all the characters and powerups. The other thing is, it is sprinkled with so many beautiful little touches - the secret characters and stages, the old school game references, the sometimes dumb jokes, the Italian names and puns (for the record I don't know any Italian but still really dig the whole vibe) - it all just feels very homey and nice. Also if you've got it during Early Access (which is still going on as I'm writing this), you get to follow the development of the game and really look forward to the next patch because it's gonna be actual new content.In the end, it is so unpretentious that it just feels like , like it's 2000-something and I just got Abe's Oddysee on a CD or discovered a flash game on Kongregate that I love. I'm not losing hour-long matches to salty 12-year-olds, I'm not farming for resources until 5 AM, and I'm not looking at complex character build charts to follow the latest meta - I'm just playing a video game for myself and enjoying it. And in this moment in video game history, that feels like nothing short of a miracle.

_childDocuments_.review: This might be one of the most addicting games I have ever played. On it's surface it's insanely simple. Just walk around and kill the mobs of enemies as they try to kill you. Your weapon fires automatically, so all you have to do is walk. The strategy comes from what power-ups you grab. Do you grab a whole bunch of weapons to create a swarm of daggers, crosses, and whips, or do you do more defensive with a shield, rotating bibles, and garlic to repel vamps? Eventually if you get far enough you will be basically a whirlwind of death and destruction that nothing can stop...until you are. Add to this a nice upgrade system and tons of unlockable items and characters and you have one of the best games of the year. Also its like 3 dollars! What are you waiting for?!Update: It still kicks ass after 50 hours of gameplay. The DLC is the cherry on top. Get it now.

_childDocuments_.review: Lot of fun for a small price.It's an arcady rogue-lite with an influence from Castlevania and other popular games.There is no complex battle system, just you, moving around, doging enemies and picking new skills/weapons and somehow it still feels complex since you can combine skills to a greater one.

_childDocuments_.review: This game saved my life.I am 27.My ex-wife and I have a daughter together, and adopted our son together. They are now both 4 years old.When we were going through our separation, I found myself lost and miserable. I was self destructive. I got so mad one day from everything spiraling out of my control that I punched some concrete in a moment of overwhelming emotion. That caused me to break my 5th metacarpal in my right hand... my working hand... my games hand.. the hand that I held and carried my children to bed with.. The hand I desperately needed to make sure I could continue to provide.After learning of the severity of my self-inflicted damage, I was borderline suicidal. Keep in mind that just a few months before this, I was the happiest man with no history of depression or anxiety. I have never had fits of rage, or been one to break down and cry, but I was in a low spot that just really buried me from being able to see the light on the other side.Having nothing better to do, I searched for a game I could play, ONE HANDED while I recovered. I somehow stumbled upon this game and read some of the reviews. I decided that it had to be worth a shot... I must admit, I didn't beat the game, or play nearly as long as some of you. In fact, I may have only played this game a day or two.. With that being said, after doing so, I had a new found joy and hope for life. I was able to put behind me the pain and suffering that had been cast over me. I was able to experience other peoples joy and happiness. I was able to see the fruits of my "labor". I relaxed for 5 ♥♥♥♥ing minutes to this music long enough to realize that I was going to be okay.After coming to that realization, I turned the game off, and I went back to work. It hurt my hand like hell but I was motivated. I stopped feeling so damn sorry for myself, and I became the father I needed to be in that moment, not the weak boy I was behaving as.Today, I am close friend with my kids mother. We don't fight, or argue, or say hurtful things to each other. We are parents, and friends.I now have 3 kids. My third child is, wait for it, ALSO 4 YEARS OLD. The woman I am with was going through a very similar situation at the time of my own separation, and we just stumbled in to each others life unexpectedly. We have been in a relationship for a year now, and are very happy together.Moral of the story, you never know what life holds in store for you, and if I would have given up when all the odds were stacked against me, I wouldn't be where I am today. This silly little game helped me realize that.Thank you Vampire Survivors

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun and very simple to play. All of your attacks auto-fire in this game, so you're mainly focused on moving around and clipping enemies for exp to power up your arsenal. Achievements unlock new abilities and playable characters that come with their own unique perks. Cash you collect can be spent on new characters or passive perks that persist across all runs (also freely refundable so you can experiment as often as you want).My runs last anywhere between 5-20 minutes depending on what upgrades the game rolls at me. Surviving into a long run and becoming an OP death machine deleting hundreds of enemy sprites like nothing gives you the good dopamine. And then you accidentally die. And then you go back to the perk shop and think "should I buy another Luck up, or buff my projectile speed? Or maybe raise my HP cap?" And then you start another run to see how that goes. Rinse and repeat.This game is only $3 but I feel like I could have paid $10 or $15 and still get my money's worth.edit: this game should be packed in with every copy of steam like a wii sports

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, but not without its issues.Vampire Survivors is a fun reverse bullet hell game, where the player creates the ''bullet hell'' to defeat endless waves of enemies. Weapon attacks are automatic, and you only have to walk around with WSAD or the Arrow keys, and potentialy use a mouse to select upgrades. Although you can do this with your keyboard as well. Meaning you can play this game with just 1 hand and a few fingers.You have to kite enemies around and collect exp gems to level up. There are a lot of weapons and passive items that allow for a lot of different combinations. Some work together some dont. You try to survive as long as posible, as you upgrade your loadout and enemies get stronger over time. You either die and get some progression in the game, or you achieve specific goals that unlock new items or characters and maps.As much as I love this game, after 60+ hours I can also say there are some massive flaws in it that needlessly pull it down.The first major issue is that although the items you get to choose from when you level up are random, they arent completely random. What I mean by this is that the game creates a ''lootpool'' at the start of a new game, and you randomly get items from  lootpool. This becomes more apparent when you unlock more items in the game, and is a massive issue for a few reasons.First a lot of items dont actualy work together, and there are both weapons and passive items. Weapons need specific conditions to evolve as well as having statistics that can or can not be buffed with other items. Having a set loot pool means you have games that are predetermined to give items that dont work together, and other times you will have items that work together.Second the items in this game have two groups, weapons and passives. You can have loot pools with a single weapon (your starting weapon) and only passive items other than that. Meaning you have no way to put out any damage or make a build that does anything. Adding to this issue is that characters dont all have a good starting item, and some items in the weapon group dont deal damage at all.Third because lootpools are predetermined this hugely prevent replayability. You quickly start to recognize what items are in your lootpool and know what build you  to go with. And worse if the game you started is lost and what games are winnable. Obviously this takes a lot of fun out of the game and its randomness.You can have games where you are level 20+ with a single level 1 weapon and no passive items to boost it.  Or you can have the best build for the situation and not play the game at all, just sitting passively watching enemies die.The only way to bypass this lootpool is by banishing items, however this is not a sollution. Because banishing items remove that item from the lootpool and replaces it with one thats not in the lootpool, you are still not guaranteed to get a different item. And even worse Banishing makes you lose the item/upgrade from that level up. If you have a terrible lootpool thats unwinnable, you can banish all you want but by the time you have banished enough items that dont work together you have already lost since you didnt get any weapons or passive items to make it further in the game.The majority maps that you can play in the game have a set rotation of enemy spawns. And those spawns are not balance to the different weapons and builds that you can get. This means that some maps force you to build for a very specific loadout, mainly AoE loadouts. Because a lot of maps have moments or even the entirety of the time enemy spawns that counter any build thats not AoE focused. Be it with the density of enemies, enemies that fire projectiles, or even a combination of both. A lot of builds just dont work on certain maps, and this hugely takes away from the replayability and fun of the game.Player skill and knowledge does not matter if you build a single target or projectile build for a map where you need AoE builds. You are just forced to either go with AoE builds or lose. Because of this a lot of maps in Vampire Survivors dont have much replayability, since you always have to go with a somewhat similar build. This also ties in the first issue with the predetermined Lootpools.Although the previous two points limit the fun and replayability of the game, this one is more of a minor gripe/issue I have that does not effect actual gameplay much.The game has different enemies, and most just walk slowly towards the player and try to deal damage on contact. There are a handful of enemies that are variations of the normal enemies (not bosses) that have a special ability/attack. Some teleport to the player, some lunge at the player, and others have their movement speed increased when near you. These enemies are almost indistinguishable from the normal enemies, and their abilities are not shown in any way.One moment you can have a bunch of red skeletons slowly move towards you, and another moment a different red skeleton gets mixed in with almost exactly the same color... except this one lunges at the player when they get close.Unless you have realy good eye for detail and remember every single special enemy variation, you are going to take unpreventable damage. And this game being a bullet hell game does not help. Since projectiles and effects obscure vision to enemies and the player a lot.Its not a major issue, but its slightly annoying to me. I would have liked if those enemies have a visual indication that showed that they are different than normal enemies.These issues could have easly been fixed and did not have to be in the game, but unfortunaly they are. If they are a major issue for you then prehaps this is not your type of game. However if you can see past these issues, Vampire survivors is a great game that is certainly worth playing.Did i get the full 60+ hours of fun out of this game? No absolutely not, more like 30-40 hours at this point. But considering the price of the game and the hours i do have fun when playing. I can say its absolutely worth the price.Its not perfect, but then again what game is?

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great game for the price. It's basically Castlevania crossed with the survival version of Dynasty Warriors in a 2D space, except you only move. This game does have some flaws. You really only need to focus on the offensive upgrades, making a handful of the upgrade options essentially useless (but I suppose you could buy them to add some difficulty). With some DLC and more development, this game could evolve into something really fun. However, the gameplay loop would probably remain pretty similar. At $3 it's certainly worth the price.

_childDocuments_.review: Repetitive yet surprisingly enjoyable gameplay of Vampire Survivors is giving old role-playing games with heavily inspired Castlevania vibes. The game literally sucks you in this amazing bullet hell of a game which in my opinion is soon to be one of the classics. Very affordable experience with the dlcs which are great example of passion within developers which we absolutely need nowadays.

_childDocuments_.review: For a game, the price of a sandwich (or overpriced drink) has quite a lot to offer, even if it's simple by design. One of the few early access titles that you can't go wrong with for the price point it's at. If you want a story of any kind, this isn't the game for you, but if you were want to hop in and shoot ♥♥♥♥ on the screen mindlessly, you can't go wrong here. It has more depth to it than you'd think. The game could use more maps \ locations, but I'm sure those will get added as time goes on.

_childDocuments_.review: Obscenely addictive and a great reminder that you don't need next gen graphics or amazing complex and twisting plots to make a fun game. _childDocuments_.review: So, I just "beat" the game in just a little over 9 hours. Solid game, extremely fun to play and fast paced which I loved. Once you beat a level, you unlock "Frenzy" mode or something like that which gives you higher percentages of luck and gold drops and everything is sped up A LOT, which I actually find easier.Currently there are only two levels and in my opinion I find the second level easier and more fun to play than the first. Given the game is still in early access I don't see why the Dev's wouldn't release more maps in the future.Pros:Fun as hell.Fast.Interesting weapon combos where you actually have to plan ahead with your current build.Passive upgrades you can buy with gold dropped from monsters.Multiple characters to unlock with their own strengths and weaknesses.The game is $3.Cons:Only two maps (currently)If you don't plan out your build ahead of time you pretty much know early you aren't beating the map.A little short, but again, I stress the game is in early release, and it's three friggin' dollars.

_childDocuments_.review: For being such a small game, there is so much content. The closest thing I would it plays like is Binding of Isaac. But only one endless room and endless enemies.Your main objective is to find good weapon sets and evolutions and make it to 30 minutes.At the time of review I have 176 hours and 87 achievements.Well worth the money and a great chill game.UPDATE: Coming up on 500 hours, this guy does not stop. The game has become a monster. Mad props to the dev. Constant updates, with new weapons, passsives, upgrades, enemies, relics, characters, secrets and arcanas. It is my go to Chill play game now and I have made a few leaderboard runs. And the dude is not done yet. I have a feeling I will gets another few hundred hours out of this game. Currently %100 achievements and missing 1 secret but I know what to do, just haven't done it yet.UPDATE: Vampire Survivors actually got so big it is spawning clones and kinda of making its own genre. You can say Slay the Spire but VP I think had a much better feel and the most of them are straight up VP with a skin. You cant really say it's classic so fast, but I would say it started a wave of games of his this type. Currently at 542 hrs. Think I will get 1000 for sure.  UPDATE: 1.0 is almost out, it is now a huge and pretty well polished game. So many cool little things now like bestiary, and a random button, And the audio has made a huge jump. I'm so happy I caught on early. Completed everything and still make runs. Its one of the best chill game ever.UPDATE: 700 hours, 100%, and I am still playing. Making new builds, doing challenge runs. I switched my Binding of Isaac addiction for a Vampire Survivor addiction.At least do a few runs a day. One of the best games of all time. Thank you so much Luca.You have made history.UPADATE: New DLC still coming out! IDGAF about Among us but wow, that trailer. I am happy Luca can do stuff that awesome since the popularity. C'mon Konami! We nee d the Castlevannia DLC! ( never gonna happen I know.UPDATE: Well... there is a Contra DLC releasing in the next few days. I already have it paid for and will be completing it for sure. This gives me hope for the Castlevania DLC. At the end of the trailer they showed what looked to be the woods Alucards is running through before he jumps in the castle. I really hope it was an easter egg. I am at 900hrs at the time. I will hit 1000 hours for sure. This has been the best $3 I have ever spent.UPDATE: I just woke up from staying up all night to mostly finish the Contra DLC. It is awesome, really feels more arcade styled with a ending boss. Reminds me of the original NES Contra. Has a lot of reused/remade textures from Contra. They new weapons and evolutions are perfect. Some are 100% Contra. Of course, you can get the spread gun and there are power ups with the wing that do different things. Best thing is the final character is hopefully an easter egg for what I have been wanting. The final character is an obvious nod to Castlevania.1000hr UPDATE: I CALLED IT FROM THE START! There is a Caslevania DLC and is was actually made with Konami. It is so amazing. I dot even have much to say, it is a beautiful work of art. From what I have hear Luca and Konami worked directly on this for more than a year. It is way beyond expectations. Real Castlevania Music, enemies, characters, assets. It pretty much has a Castlevania mode now. It's a castle, you have to unlock door and do mini missions. Real bosses and many of them. It even switches to 2d for a certain fight. As a Castlevania simp. This makes me so happy. I am also so happy for Luca. From a small game to working with Komani. Yes, it cost more than the og game. But it doesn't feel like DLC, it is its own game. I don't know if this is the end, but this is the perfect way to stop. On a super high note. This game went from epic to legendary now. <3

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a fun little game, not one that is small in any real accord. It's simple and you could even just control it with an Atari 2600 Controller if you even wanted to.The meat of the game is maneuvering and utilizing your weapons to succeed, and reaching that goal of 30 minutes ends up being critical to unlocking most of your things, like Characters, maps, weapons, passives, etc. Never play too passive or you'll not level fast enough, and never be too aggressive or you'll just die.There is a lot to say about how much I've enjoyed this game, I love it and it's perfect for what kind of game it is, The Music is amazing, the Visual style is very good, the mechanics are easy to get into, and the difficulty mostly varies based on the map you pick out.Main thing is that Inlaid Library is way too easy to play on, but it's fun overall, it's the perfect map to unlock most of the weapons and characters, It's also a good map to help you learn how to min-max, then you can end up comfortable enough to route what weapons and passives you'll go for.P.S. The Bibles are better than Garlic.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all we should orient you in time and space. The year is 2022 and you are considering a computer game called Vampire Survivors. It's not a very expensive game and appears to have a decent amount of content, even if it is early access. The soundtrack slaps and it has a gothic pixel art design similar to 2D Castlevania, but a random element that makes every playthrough a little different. You purchase the software without hesitation, because you know that you can't buy anything else that is this entertaining for $3.Your faith is strong, your weapons are sharpened, it's time to enter the gauntlet and show these mother ♥♥♥♥♥♥' vampires who is boss. Or maybe you are the vampire, killing everything in Transylvania. Is it Transylvania? I suppose because you have weapons like crosses and garlic, you must be human. It's not really clear to me and I don't care about video games stories anyway. Good thing this game doesn't have one, or a tutorial! So there you are, ready to begin! Press a button, choose the only character and level you can play at the beginning and get to work. Hordes of unholy abominations are going to die by your hand tonight.The game is simple, you move around a 2D plane, kill disgusting hordes of mobs, and collect their gems. Your weapons fire automatically, because you're so bad at videogames you couldn't possibly handle them without help. But don't worry, it's hard enough simply to move around between all the mobs, carefully zipping and scooting, maneuvering yourself into range so one or several of your skills pop those evil dead in the face. When you collect enough gems, you level up, and you choose an upgrade from a random three choices. Keep killing, keep getting swole. When you inevitably get eaten by bats, broccoli boys, or rock n roll witches, your run is over and you are taken to a summary screen that shows statistics like what weapons you used, damage breakdowns, timings, achievements, et cetera. You also will have collected some coins during your run and possibly unlocked the ability to buy some new characters. You can spend the coins between runs on permanent upgrades to your stats so you aren't such a useless baby in the future, and you can also spend coins on unlocking those new characters for future outings. So that's all the stuff you collect and how to use it. The best part about life as a vampire survivor is the constant ramping up of everything. Numbers go up, never down. The screen fills with angrier and angrier mobs and particle effects from your weapons as you destroy the horde. Feedback cues hearkening back to nostalgic 16-bit days fill your ears and eyes as your weapons connect with the dead and you collect their gems. Each vampire survivor has a different starting weapon but you quickly will get several and try to max them out. You also get the choice to upgrade passive stats like armor, luck, health regeneration and so on. Every playthrough is a little different. Try to survive and beat your time. The frantic collection of gems keeps you moving, and there are chests that drop from large mobs that do a lootbox-style animation when you open them up. All vampire survivors appreciate these constant dopamine hits and the rewards contained within. You notice there are no actual microtransactions or keys or actual gambling required though. Why is this part of the game? Is this satire, you wonder? It doesn't matter, you must keep surviving the vampires. Vampire Survivors is easy to play, but if you want to survive like me, it's going to take some skill. Polish your WASD, get your Santa Water and your King Bible ready, and let's ♥♥♥♥♥♥' go.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay I bought this game on sale for $4 and I've got to say, it was worth my money. I've been playing this on a non-gaming laptop as well as on the Steam Deck. It works just fine on the Steam Deck, without toying around with it too hard (I just choose the standard boot option, from a choice of 3 available when you launch the game).This game only *looks* like a twin-stick shooter. In fact, you don't actively do any of the shooting. This game is all about unlockables and challenges. You start with a base set of characters that each have a weapon type. The weapons in this game are automatically deployed based on whatever rules the weapon follows (for example, a basic whip will arc around in front of you, similar to Capcom's Strider arcade game; or some "holy water" will fall from above every X amount of time, create a circle of fire on the floor with Y radius and last for N amount of time on the floor). You can learn each character that you have available, learn their base weapons, and then as you upgrade those, you unlock the ability to acquire those for other characters as well. You accumulate new characters and their base weapons for use in future runs and that's what keeps this game going.So this game resembles a twin-stick shooter in appearance, in that you are on a map which is basically an infinitely-scrollable arena and face monsters along the way that come at you in waves in a way. As you kill, you can collect dropped XP which you use to level up. There's also a currency system for unlocking permanent stat buffs in the main menu, as well as being able to use that cash on a merchant for temporary items during future runs (merchant must be unlocked, as does most of the features of this game).The game opens up a lot over time, going from only a couple of main menu options to unlocking new maps, new modes, a secrets menu, a bestiary, and more. The base-length for a standard run can top out at about 30 minutes, at which point the game generally forces you to die. There are alternate modes you can unlock (like hyper, endless, and more) which switch this up for your liking as well.There's one "secret" objective in the game that basically caused my laptop to struggle (only onboard intel graphics, on an I7 11xxx series processor with 32gb RAM and an nvme SSD), otherwise the game has run just fine on my laptop. The secret involved essentially leaving the map in a trippy "out of reality" kind of teleport which then places you temporarily on a different map, and that entire sequence was too intense for a non-gaming device based on the visuals of that entire sequence. I made it through after a few minutes of extremely choppy gameplay, where then once the map reverted back, my performance went back to normal. I've mostly played using the Xbox 360 wired gamepad for Windows as well. You spend most of the time just using your left analog stick (or moving with the keyboard), while the game otherwise plays itself according to whatever rules are in motion (based on buffs, unlocks, debuffs, etc.).For the price I paid ($4), it's a fun *almost* auto-play game, and being loaded with objectives and achievements is the incentive to keep going, aside from any personal goals you give yourself (like trying to beat a level without upgrades, or with only 1 weapon, etc.).I'd recommend checking out some gameplay videos if you're on the fence, otherwise if you appreciate twin stick-style arena shooters, you will likely enjoy this as well!

_childDocuments_.review: This game saved my lifeI am 27.My ex-wife and I have a daughter together, and adopted our son together. They are now both 4 years old.When we were going through our separation, I found myself lost and miserable. I was self destructive. I got so mad one day from everything spiraling out of my control that I punched some concrete in a moment of overwhelming emotion. That caused me to break my 5th metacarpal in my right hand... my working hard... my games hand.. the hand that I held and carried my children to bed with. The hand I desperately needed to make sure I could continue to provide.After learning of the severity of my self-inflicted damage, I was borderline suicidal. Keep in mind that just a few months before this. I was the happiest man with no history of depression or anxicty. I have never had fits of rage, or been one to break down and cry, but I was In a low spot that just really buried me from being able to see the light on the other sideHaving nothing better to do. I searched for a game I could play, ONE HANDED while recovered. I somehow stumbled upon this game and read some of the reviews. I decided that it had to be worth a shot.... I must admit. I didn't beat the game, or play nearly as long as some of you. In fact. I may have only played this game a day or two. With that being said, after doing so. I had a new found joy and hope for life. I was able to put behind me the pain and suffering that had been cast over me. I was able to experience other peoples joy and happiness. I was able to see the fruits of my "labor". I relaxed for 5 wwwwing minutes to this music long enough to realize that I was going to be okayAfter coming to that realization, I turned the game off, and I went back to work. It hurt my hand like hell but I was motivated. I stopped feeling so damn sorry for myself, and became the father I needed to be in that moment, not the weak boy I was behaving as.

_childDocuments_.review: It is hard for me to explain why I like vampire survivors so much, but I will give it my best try.The core part of the experience is the gameplay. It is mindless and dead simple. Kite enemies, buy auto attacking weapons and enhancements, kill and gather XP. That is it, when you die you try again with more unlocks (which are also achievements which I very much appreciate) and upgrades, then you continue in your standard rogue-lite fashion. I found that I grabbed onto the basics quickly and it was a lot of fun figuring out everything that the game has to offer. But really the best part about this game is that it takes like no brain power to play. I can listen to videos, talk to my friends, hell, I could probably answer complex philosophical questions and still be playing at my peak. It is a time waster, it is easy, and its loop is just a lot of fun. This is why you play the game, if it is not your cup of tea don’t get it.The story… exists? Like kind of, it is there in that you are trying to kill all these monsters and save your friends, but that is kind of it. If you play games only for the story avoid this one.The music and sound design are great. The music is well-composed, thematically fitting, and pretty catchy too. The sound design can get chaotic, but it is pretty dang good. Every attack has a sound and it fits well. In all honesty, though I had the volume off most of the time. The chaotic sound design is over-stimulating for me and I rather have something that actually takes brainpower making sound. Even with that though I think the sound work that this game has is commendable.Graphically this game is pretty good. It is not the cleanest pixel art I have seen and when some of the enemies are increased in size they look a little weird as they just blew them up instead of redoing a sprite a lot of the time, but hey it is distinct and the assets look good. So though it is not my favorite looking game I appreciate what it has to offer.So hopefully that kind of explains my thoughts. I think the overwhelmingly positive reviews are completely fair. And I think this is a must-have game even with the price increase that they did for their full release. It is so simple and fun that I think anyone (besides 2% of people I guess) can enjoy it. I spent 57.4 hours unlocking everything in a game that is worth $5 that is the deal of a lifetime if I have ever seen one.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to keep this straight forward because this game is too.PROS+ Cheap price for the amount of content+ Easy to pick up, rewarding to master+ Controls are intuitive and simple (walk and don't touch bad guys)+ LOTS of content+ Cathartic and relaxing if you aren't gunning for completion+ Sense of power and balancing really helps pace runs and general progress+ MANY characters, all with unique stats and starting weapons+ Really good soundtrack+ Myriad of QoL and customization options make runs feel unique+ Later game options and unlocks allow for even further run building and fun+ Runs are a set time, so can be 'a quick game then back to work' etc+ Developer is very in touch with their community, the discord is great and the game is updated regularly (You WILL perfect this game multiple times as new achievements are added with each update)+ Some great funny moments (*slow clap*)+ A host of 'non game' content in the game like a collection list, unlock list, bestiary and stats.+ Post-game content in the form of small, permanent, per-character, upgrades.CONS- Progress at the start is fast, then you get a long grindy part of progress after 'Randomazzo' is unlocked.SUMMARY AND THOUGHTS= Depending on game play preference, you can tool this to your needs. Like the same weapon? Run that each time and try different characters and passives that scale with that weapon, in a different way.= Testing builds is the most fun I have in this game. Once you unlock Arcanas, builds start getting RIDICULOUSLY fun. Want to have 2 of each your weapons? Specific weapons only, but there's an Arcana for that. Want your projectiles bouncing 3 times more? Arcanas got you covered. You could pick a new theme each day and make a run out of it and still be playing this game months, maybe years later.= For under 5 dollars, what's the big deal with trying it? With SO much content and replay-ability, you'd be crazy to not give it a try.

_childDocuments_.review: Yes, probably. The affordable $4.99 price makes taking a chance on a genre such as this less of a financial commitment, and more of a mental one. This game is in the "Rouge-lite" genre so the entire point is to fail or succeed on the level you select and repeat the process while earning collectibles and unlockables throughout your run with some unlockables persisting to your next run as well as a gold system to unlock other passive buffs for your characters. There is a wide selection of abilities and characters and you'll certainly get your $4.99 worth. It also has a cool little art style and runs surprising well on computers given the almost impossible amount of enemies that can be on your screen at some points. However, the game is too easy. I think it was my third run where I ended up "winning" with me completing the max 30 min level time. After maybe the 10th run I unlocked most abilities and levels which instead of feeling proud I felt almost bored and underwhelmed. Usually in this genre there is a feeling of a hard fought climb to the top of the mountain and it's not easy achieved or duplicated. You can almost achieve success more than failure once you know what you're doing in "Vampire Survivors." This then begins to damper the fun and the only real replayability becomes in experimenting purposefully with different power ups/builds despite them not being a optimal winning strategy, which seems counter intuitive in a Rouge-Lite genre. If you're a die hard fan of this genre looking for a unforgiving challenge and to be tested - "Vampire Survivors" might not be for you given how easy it is to "win" out the gate for anyone experienced in this genre. However, If you want some mindless fun for a few hours and while you distract yourself then for sure give it a go and purchase the game for the price of a cheeseburger.  There are many characters and levels and power ups to unlock and honestly if you fight other Rouge-lites too hard then this might be the perfect game for you.  Enjoy Surviving!

_childDocuments_.review: This game has come a long way since its Early Access days on Steam, with a constant stream of free updates adding depth and content that's simply astonishing. And the best part? It's ridiculously affordable!The gameplay is deceptively simple at first—just move around and attack, easy peasy. But don't be fooled; this game will keep you on your toes as monsters swarm in from all directions. The Castlevania vibes are strong here, with a whip in hand and classic gaming horror creatures to face. Survive for 30 minutes, and you can count that as a victory.But where Vampire Survivors truly shines is in its progression system and weapon variety. Each attempt starts you off with a basic weapon, but don't fret—soon, you'll find yourself wielding a firehose of knives or summoning a colony of bats with garlic's power. The combinations are endless, and you'll be constantly making decisions on which items to use and how to modify your attacks. The satisfaction of creating an unstoppable barrage of firepower is unparalleled.The developer, Poncle, has nailed the balance of unlocks, ensuring you're never overwhelmed but always excited to try something new. The objectives provide direction and encourage experimentation. And when you accomplish them, the feeling of achievement is like a flood of dopamine.The game keeps subverting your expectations, turning everything you thought you knew upside down. It's a wild ride that you won't want to get off. The Xbox version has had some bugs, but they're getting patched, and I'm sure it'll be smooth sailing soon.I have to say, Vampire Survivors has quickly become one of my all-time favorites!
