_childDocuments_.review: Meth < Vampire SurvivorsThe story:I have no clue. I'm sure there's lore, but you don't really have a set objective or conclusion other than surviving a set amount of time. The Gameplay:The game is played from a top-down perspective. You play as one of many characters to choose from at the start of each round. Each character starts with a different ability, amount of health and speed. You walk around avoiding enemies and collecting gems while your collected weapons automatically fire. The gems you collect allow you to level up which in turns allows you to level up your weaponry in order to keep up with the increased health and numbers later enemies have. The concept is so simple, but the execution is incredible! Each round feels unique as you unlock new weapons and characters and you constantly try to survive longer and longer as your base stats increase. Something other reviews don't seem to touch on is the fact that you can play this game one handed. Literally. If you're someone who struggles with tendonitis, or bursitis, or a broken arm, or anything that renders one of your arms out of action, you can play with just the other. The arrow keys, or WASD both work so you can alternate freely. Some pros:- Simple but loveable art style.- Endless replayability.- Plenty of secrets (unlockable content).- Dirt cheap. People pay more for hangovers.- Engaged, thoughtful developers. - Great for injury recoveries.- Great for achievement hunters. Some cons:- None. You can't complain over something with this fair a price/content ratio.Conclusion:This game is absolutely fantastic and I recommend to everyone who wants to try it, even at full price, because it's just so much bang for your buck. Not even including the DLC, which is also entirely justified for it's price.11/10, Will face hordes again :D

_childDocuments_.review: Ever since I can remember I've loved garlic bread - it seems like there is nothing in the world as delicious and as simple. If I was given Garlic Bread to eat for every meal for the rest of my life, I would definitely die happy.Over the years, I've seen Garlic Bread being made in all sorts of ways - using butter and oils - cooking the garlic - using a brush the add on addition butter or oil. And I've come to know that these are all great ideas but you don't always get that amazing garlic bread taste you want. I've tried a few combinations, and found that this is definitely the most delicious.Some Facts: The Garlic Bread we know today is more of an American tradition, however it can be said that the Mediterranean people were the creators of the concept. They were known for dipping foods into hot seasoned oils especially oils that contained garlic.Ingredients: Italian Bread (NOT SLICED) Olive Oil Garlic Butter Oregano SaltQuantity: 2-3 Loafs of Italian Bread 10-15 Tablespoons of Olive Oil 10-15 Cloves of Garlic (Depends on taste and quantity of bread ) 3 - 5 Tablespoons of Butter 2-3 Tablespoons of Oregano (to taste) Salt to TasteI do not count calories or serving sizes. I eat because it enjoy it and I cook because I love it. Total Time to prep and cook: 30-45 MinutesDirections:1. Preheat the toaster or oven to 400 degrees Fahrenheit. Take one piece of bread and cut it horizontally.2. Take a cooking brush and as evenly as possible - spread the oil inside, onto both sides of the bread for that great taste.3. Dice the garlic - Which should be evenly distributed onto the inside of the bread, again onto both sides of the bread.4. Place the bread in to an aluminium foil sheet.5. Place the bread into the oven for 8-10 Minutes at 350 degrees Fahrenheit. This is just to cook the oil and stick the garlic into place.6. Remove the Bread from the oven and place 1 teaspoon of butter onto the bread - the butter should be spaced out evenly so you get that butter taste with each bite. Then season with oregano.7. Place the Bread back into the aluminium foil and then back into the oven for another 10-15 minutes or until the bread it golden-brown on the outside.8. Once the bread is cooked - remove from oven and open the aluminium foil, let it stand for 2-3 minutes so it can cool down a little. Now cut the bread into even vertical pieces.Enjoy your garlic build :)

_childDocuments_.review: The fact I have gotten as much enjoyment and replay value out of a game that cost $2.99 is WILD and honestly feels like a highway robbery. Even with the price increase to $4.99 it's still a damn steal, I've had less fun and fewer hours logged on games that cost triple the price. If you've ever played the stellar mobile game Magic Survival, this is basically a far more fleshed out iteration of it. I'm not sure what genre you would classify this as (I guess a roguelite reverse-bullet hell?), but you basically pick a character out and move around a map while avoiding enemies, trying to kill them with your various auto-firing weapons & abilities, collecting upgrades as you go and try to survive until the timer runs out + maybe even go past the timer and fight some extra baddies. It's a very simple premise on paper, given complexity by the sheer number of characters + weapons + character & weapon upgrades + weapon combinations + maps + etc. Some of the unlockable characters & weapons are unlocked in ways I would never in a million years have discovered on my own, but I enjoyed naturally unlocking all of the content I could until I just couldn't bear it anymore and looked up how to unlock the remaining content. My one gripe with the game is that I wish to god there was an option to turn off chest animations because sometimes you hit a string of opening multi-item chests in a row and you have to sit there and wait for confetti and a light show to stop before you can collect your items, which can halt the flow of combat a bit, but this is such a minute complaint in a game that is otherwise damn-near perfect and that I cannot stop myself from coming back to over and over again just for one more run. 10/10tl;dr - buy it lol

You'll get into a lull once you get further ahead but if you need something to decompress, this is a game for you. You'll get fulfillment out of being able to eventually mow everything down and seeking out each of the objectives nicely put into your achievements category. _childDocuments_.review: 22h 4/10 You need multiple runs, but that is normally in a rogue-lite game There are multiple guides available on the steam guide section, but the most important thing is to know how to evolve items, I'll explain more below No No No Yes No No Not really No NoThis cheap game may not have the best looks, but don't let that turn you away from this amazing game! This one can start slow but is so very addictive and so much fun, the hours flew by while playing this game. It is still in early access and will probably get more achievements, so this review feels somewhat a bit early, but I just want to scream from the roofs how good this game is. A run can start slowly, but if you do things right and have a little bit of luck you can feel so overpowered and that just makes it feel so so good. I hope that the updates this game for sure will get during its early access process will keep that feeling in mind as it is the best. There are a few things that are good to know and keep in mind which will make your progress through the game and getting all the achievements a lot easier:- There is meta progression, you will be able to buy abilities with the coins you get during each run.- You can only have 12 skills in each run, so choose wisely when picking stills each level up.- Try to get your damage skill up as high as possible early on, as that will mostly determine how long you stay alive.- But the most important thing of all is to evolve your weapons! I'll explain that last point a bit more. Almost all weapons can be evolved to a much better version. How you do that is leveling up the weapon to the max level it has, having the support item that it needs (the level of that item doesn't matter), and then kill a boss so you get a chest. Most of the time the evolve weapon will be the reward (and unlocks an achievement the first time you do that for each weapon).  Sometimes it might be wise to leave a chest on the ground if you're very close to the max level of that weapon and just first lvl up till you get that and then go back to that chest to pick it up. Here is the list of the weapons and it support item:Axe + Candelabrador = Death SpiralCross + Clover = Heaven SwordFire Wand + Spinach = HellfireGarlic + Pummarola = Soul EaterKing Bible + Spellbinder = Unholy VespersKnife + Bracer = Thousand EdgeLightning Ring + Duplicator = Thunder LoopMagic Wand + Empty Tome = Holy WandPeachone + Ebony Wings = VandalierPentagram + Crown = Gorgeous MoonSanta Water + Attractorb = La BorraSong of Mana + Skull O'Maniac = MannajjaWhip + Hollow Heart = Bloody TearIn my mind, this is the most important list to keep in mind while playing Vampire Survivors, as the evolved weapons are just so much stronger.The achievements are all very straightforward and none of them is missable due to this being a rogue-lite. The meta progress will help you out getting the achievement easier and another great thing is that you can reset your meta progress to go for different stats without any penalty. This gives you the freedom to experiment with different playstyles without being penalized if it didn't work out for you. TLDR: This game is just amazing! Go give it a try.

_childDocuments_.review: Vampire Survivor is one of those strange games that, looked from the outside, might seem like a low effort project because of the cheap-looking sprites and unpolished graphics in general.But once you start playing it, you realize: "Woah, this is the real deal! How can something so cheap (it costs 2,39€), something still in early access, something not yet fully content complete be this fun and addicting?!".At least that's what I kept telling myself as I kept playing. 46 hours later I am still having a blast with it. The developer keeps adding a ton of things with every new update, obviously as the game is still in early access, and even when they say "oh, sorry but this is a light update" you end up with new areas, new secret bosses, new evolutions, new characters and you feel like the dev is punking you.I am truly amazed by this game, as it is a simple yet well thought out experience at its core that doesn't get bogged down by grinding (you can grind tho if you like).I also appreciate the humor and references in it, which cover a lot of areas, not just other games, but also things like old anime shows or some real people (really easy to get if you're Italian).So yeah, I definitely recommend this to anyone who wants to have some fun leveling up while dodging enemies on the road to become a death machine vomiting projectiles and lasers and axes and crosses and daggers and whatever else to survive the onslaught coming your way.
_childDocuments_.name: Vampire Survivors

_childDocuments_.review: Now I ain't saying this game is good.. I'm just saying yesterday when I got home, I booted up the game for a quick run and spent the whole day playing it and ended up gifting it to three other friends of mine so far. For a 2.40 or so game in early access I've had more fun and spent more time on it than most AAAs games out there.Bonus points for the Castlevania aesthetics and references (of which I grew up with), the sense of humour, the sound effects being on point feeling really satisfying and the music tracks are absolute bangers!A Bestiary would be cool to check the enemy sprites and lore (like in the castlevania games), this wouldn't necessarily affect gameplay (tho it could, like adding bonus damage to enemies you complete the entry for, for example), it would be a nice touch however for that little extra world building and opportunity for humour. Well it's just an idea, certainly not something with a high priority.Looking forward for more updates!!

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely simple pixel graphic game. You fight waves of enemies in a looping arena and choose upgrades as you level up by picking up exp crystals dropped by enemies. All weapons auto fire and aim based on the weapon type. For $2.99, you really can't go wrong. That's not to say this game is without flaws, it's very easy compared to other roguelike games. I find myself quitting every game because I've reached the max number of power ups you can have and only have the option of choosing to heal or add gold. I can't see myself playing this in the long-term because there really isn't much content to unlock, but for the price I paid, I got a good amount of gameplay out of it.

_childDocuments_.review: A dangerous video game that takes advantage of dopamine addiction and power fantasies prevalent among gamers.I used to avoid this game with passion upon the initial release because I thought they ripped graphical assets from Castlevania franchise. After further research, I found out that wasn't really the case.Few months later, I decided to give the game a try for research purposes because I'm an indie developer with a game released on steam as well. I'm a heavy, heavy smoker. I smoke almost every hour whether if I'm gaming or working. However, when I booted this game for the first time, I sat 10 hours straight just playing this game. That's how addictive it is. The fake lootboxes, constant stream of power ups, replayability and simplicity of the gameplay makes the game very, very addicting.Vampire Survivor may seem quite lacking at the first glance, but this is a game I could simply recommend to anyone of any skill level in gaming.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun little Arcade Bullet Hell-ish Action RPG Rouge-lite.The game is quite minimalist, since your only input is 8-directional movement while automatically attacking. However, it's not an incremental/idle game or autobattler, since you have to actively dodge to survive and collect gold to progress. The "Rogue" element here is extra-lite; there is an element of random drops that will have you pursuing certain "builds", and a light progression system of permanent upgrades bought with gold from each run, but that's about it. Each run lasts at most 30 minutes. While I'd call it a Bullet Hell, it's not really a shmup/shoot-em-up - you are simply dodging the swarms of enemies that are spawning, while hoping your build has enough firepower to clear a path for you to dodge through. A few other classes and items eventually become unlocked as you obtain achievements. There are only 2 levels to play.That all said, it is surprisingly fun and original.
_childDocuments_.name: Vampire Survivors

_childDocuments_.review: If you want a very simple yet addicting challenge, I would suggest you try out Vampire Survivors.Coming from someone who normally avoids playing bullet hell-type games, I found Vampire Survivors to be surprisingly really fun. The initial stages of progression you make, unlocking new abilities and characters, panicking because you're 2 minutes til the end but the monsters seem to be inching closer and closer: this is basically what you might expect from this game.The gameplay in a nutshell is you try to survive a progressing onslaught of varying monsters for 30 minutes. The difficulty ramps up every minute and the only way you can overcome the waves is by gaining experience from killing monsters. Every level gained rolls you a random set of 3 to 4 weapons or abilities to choose from, and you improve them by leveling up or finding upgrades in treasure chests that drop from unique monsters. Each character has their own starting weapon and passive, which can alternate your play style, and that's pretty much all there is to say about the game.Oh, and the devs actively update and add new content too so that's a huge plus. Hats off to the devs!

_childDocuments_.name: Vampire Survivors

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot wait for more patches from this game. Solid fun. Would love more ludicrous anything (from maps, to characters, to more item combinations, to even more chest opening music/sounds/rarities). It's great fun. You literally play with WASD (or arrow keys) and that's it! Yet the game isn't "handed" to you. Just because you move fast doesn't mean you can stop death from surrounding you. Just because you hit fast doesn't mean you kill the enemies who are tanky coming towards you. Just because you have an insane beginning doesn't mean you can just "sit still" and let the game play itself. It always keeps you moving (at least for the first 15-20 minutes) and thinking "where are the weakest enemies?" "Where is the boss now?" "What build am I going for if I level up?", etc.Solid game. For how simplistic it looks, it almost feels like a steal at the price it's at right now.
_childDocuments_.name: Vampire Survivors

_childDocuments_.review: I can not stress to you how fun this game is. It feels amazing with all the extra content they have added after early access! With the new characters, maps, items, and even synergies, I cannot say anything else that hasn't been said from others. While it was in early access this was a no brainer for $3, but since the price went up to $5 dollars and you have more than double the game from when it was realeased this is hands down the best $5 you can spend on a game in today's market. Plus, that sound track kicks so hard when you play that you get into it. (Until you cant hear it anymore because of all the projectiles you shoot out.) Easiest recommendation for a game!
_childDocuments_.name: Vampire Survivors

_childDocuments_.review: So much fun to be had from a game with no clicking attack buttons or using abilities, everything just automatically goes as it should and all you have to do is dodge the hordes. Or stand in one spot and do nothing because you have so much AoE that nothing can even get close to you!I would recommend it even while in early access, and normally I don't recommend EA games due to still needing work or no guarantee they will ever be complete. I like how the developers still plan for more content, but even if they stopped work on it I would still highly recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Vampire Survivors

_childDocuments_.review: This is an amazing game with a high amount of depth. This is both it's strength and its weakness. You have to be ok with or better like to min/max, search online for advice and be prepared to be bombarded with information at the beginning. This is in no way a game you play to chill, tension is present for the complete run (30 min) if you make it that far. There are over 20 playable individual characters to play and a weapon-pool that grants access to quite a lot of builds. The different maps are different, from terrain, enemy types to stage items. If you decide to buy this game, get your second monitor ready for research, grab your favorite drink and try to survive.TL;DR: Complex, tense game with high potential for frustration and song of gladness.
_childDocuments_.name: Vampire Survivors

_childDocuments_.review: A nice action roguelike with many playable characters, perma unlocks and many maps. I like how you learn more and more abilities throughout the game and the combo feature is a nice addition to the large amount of weapons (at least for the price). I also like the soundtrack of the game and the pixel art.It's not that much of a challenge, it's more like becoming the challenge itself, just how the game is being advertised. The only downside is that at some point you can't see a thing anymore thanks to the large amount of enemies and projectiles (even more extreme than being shown in the trailer).Another problem I have is the insta kill enemy that spawns after a certain amount of time as a counter for being overpowered. That feels a bit cheap to prevent farming an endless amount of money. So the balancing seems a bit off since I'm overpowered almost every roundBut all in all, the game is a nice time killer, especially for the price

name: Sonic Origins
detailed_description: Feature List About the Game The Blue Blur is back with an expanded multi-game collection of classic Sonic the Hedgehog games - Sonic Origins Plus! Sonic Origins Plus features the four beloved classic titles in Sonic Origins – Sonic the Hedgehog, Sonic 2, Sonic 3 & Knuckles, and Sonic CD with remastered visuals, bonus characters, added modes, challenges, behind-the-scenes content and more while adding significant improvements. This bundle also includes 12 Sonic Game Gear titles, previously released add-on content, playable Knuckles in Sonic CD, and for the first time ever, Amy Rose as a playable character in Sonic the Hedgehog 1, 2, Sonic 3 & Knuckles, and Sonic CD! With more content than ever before, this is the definitive way to experience these classic games! Classic Redefined Explore 4 classic remastered Sonic titles – Sonic the Hedgehog, Sonic 2, Sonic 3 & Knuckles, and Sonic CD in high-definition, with all-new opening and ending animations for each title! Classic and Anniversary Modes Spin Dash your way through numerous zones in Classic mode with the game’s original resolution and limited lives, or the new Anniversary Mode with unlimited lives in revamped widescreen HD. New Unlockables Complete missions and unlock Mirror Mode, new stages, challenges, behind-the-scenes content, a music player, animated shorts, special stages, and more! Game Gear Titles Play 12 classic Sonic Game Gear titles, including hits like Sonic Drift 2, Sonic Spinball, and Tails Adventure! New Playable Characters Play as Sonic, Tails, Knuckles or – for the first time ever – Amy Rose in Sonic the Hedgehog 1, 2, Sonic 3 & Knuckles, and Sonic CD! All-in-One Bundle Sonic Origins Plus includes the Classic Music Pack and Premium Fun Pack, which contain Extreme Missions, Mirror Mode, additional screen borders, new character animations in menus, added music from other Sonic titles, and more!

_childDocuments_.review: If you look through most of the negative reviews or comments, repeated issues along the lines of Sega Sucks.. but never really get into the additional content of the game.. Don't get me wrong, this game has some flaws or bugs. but most games do, even the old one's or The Projects most people are suggesting. it's a very good collection that remasters Sonic 3&Knuckles, Most Issues with genesis emulated titles are gone, as well as thing that actually make the game smoother in most instances. For a Long while it's been Popular On Social media to Bash Products a select amount of people Label as "bad" then because it's in a post that's Never changing people keep seeing it and it becomes an echo chamber of negativity or a Internet version of telephone. it makes a lot of people too scared or too ashamed to try the game or even get bullied when they actually say they like it..Instead of Being Disappointed because of expectations it's better too judge the game for What it is,  A collection that's brings HD remastered versions to all consoles. and Adds Sonic 3&K content and improvements. for all of my friends who have never played these games these are the best and only one's you can buy on any platform now. all older versions had Worse issues. and this adds so much Bonus and Detailed Content including the Sonic Generations styled Mission Mode. which allows you to do New Platforming and objective based challenges. which were never there before. The Content is like Sonic Mega Collection Or sonic Jam (the Title theme is a remix of From Sonic Jam)  but It's more modern.  I feel like this game would definitely be more better seeing how much it want's to be Like Sonic Jam I think the assets used for the title screen would have made an VERY VERY well received Sonic World (Jam) style Hub. and would have made more since as DLC content.. that's something i'm genuinely hoping they add as an option in the future. I Definitely a Blast Over the past month.. Way more playable than anything else I've tried doing. it's only a shame they didn't give Knuckles' Choatics or Sonic 3D Blast Some sort of spotlight.. Other than The DLC music.

_childDocuments_.review: I still feel so bad for the devs who had to make this collection, they were probably crunched to get this game out on time. For God's sakes, I would have been fine waiting a year or two more just for this game to have more than just four old ass Sega Genesis games and unsubstantial bonus content for $49.99 at full price. Even with the Plus content, which is an additional $13.99, It gets worse with just ONE new playable character, 10 poorly emulated Game Gear games, and some DLC packs that some people likely already bought, resold to you at full price with no discounts for already buying it. If you want to play the "definitive" versions of these games, this is not it, this is far from definitive, this is just disgraceful. I can see passion and talent within this collection, and I can see a genuine effort to improve and fix these games to the fullest, Like with Sonic 3 and what Headcanon try doing with that game, as well as the animated cutscenes but it's all bogged down by Crunch time. and horrible business decisions. If you STILL wanna play Origins, please buy it on sale, It just isn't worth buy it at full price.

_childDocuments_.review: Quick disclaimer: Yes, DRM is present.  It's made clear on the store page.  Yes, <insert why DRM is bad>.  If it's enough of an issue for you - and I won't blame you - look into other places to buy the game (console, for instance).  That said, moving onto the actual review...The game is fantastic.  I've seen a lot of hate on the soundtrack and a few other things - if you're a purist, get a Genesis, get the original games, get a Sony PVM and have fun.  If you want a classic experience with some good quality of life improvements, enjoy!That said, there's a few things.  First, yes, the music changed.  On three tracks.  Of all four games.  The tracks known for licensing issues.  Yeah, they don't sound like some of the other renditions of the beta tracks, but they don't sound COMPLETELY terrible.  They're a bit rougher than the other tracks, but they don't sound ENTIRELY out of place.  As someone that grew up playing Sonic 3 and Knuckles on Genesis.... yeah, took a bit of adjustment but it's fine.The next thing, and I'm conflicted on it - is gameplay, specifically how sonic feels and the physics.  Before you roll your eyes - it absolutely feels like a sonic game.  Like, official, not fangame.  But for some reason, and it could just be me, but the gameplay of Sonic 1 and 2 seems a little bit off.  I can't pinpoint it either.  It's not even bad.  Just different.  Sarcasm about being a purist aside, you might notice some differences, as it's using the retro engine.  But it's accurate enough that I enjoyed it.The perks of those coins, whether gained during gameplay or through preorder definitely is a nice QOL improvement.  You don't NEED to use them, but it makes doing a 100% playthrough much, much easier.  All of the emeralds, and such.  Especially because the jank of the Sonic 1 special stage is in full force - while the smoother rotation afforded by the modern remake of the game makes it better, the general physics quirks of the special stage stemming from the original version is there, so... maybe it's just me but I can't stand them lol.Graphics are tweaked here and there, but it's not excessive and overall, the game looks as beautiful as ever, and the widescreen option is great.Whether you're a veteran to the Sonic games or you're looking to get into the series with the games that started it all, Sonic Origins is a solid title.
_childDocuments_.name: Sonic Origins

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking to play the classic Sonic games in both HD and original quality, then this is the game for you! This game is a collection of the original Sonic games which includes Sonic The Hedgehog 1, Sonic & Tails, Sonic 3 & Knuckles, and Sonic CD. It also includes high quality cinematic to improve the story telling for each of the games.As well as all of the above, there are also challenge modes to prove you are the best blue hedgehog in Greenhills.  Once you're done challenging yourself and playing through the story, you can visit the museum to view artwork, cinematic and more!If that still isn't enough, you can purchase the 'Plus' edition for more Sonic games which were released on the Sega Game Gear all the way back in 1990 (34 years ago)!This game is well worth your money and I fully recommend it for any Sonic fan wishing to play the old games again.
_childDocuments_.name: Sonic Origins

_childDocuments_.review: Sonic Origins is definitely a good time but I have mixed feelings of Origins as a compilation product but not to the games themselves. Make no mistake... Sonic 1, 2, CD and 3&K are Masterful timeless classics and always will be and the quality of them here are great especially since all of them are the Retro Engine Remasters. I'm very happy for Sonic 3 being released again after 10 years and further more, Stealth returning to the series to finish what Taxman started with Sonic CD back in 2011 is fantastic and he gave his all for Sonic 3 & Knuckles' return. and so did Jun Senoue with the music both for Origins and the Sonic 3 music replacements ( I think so anyway) and Mission Mode is the Highlight when i comes to added content. There are elements here I absolutely love. My main criticisms is the collection package itself, it feels empty, predictably rushed and lacking of new unlockable content and what was included like most of the art and music has been released countless times before or others has been officially released on Youtube, The Spin off games such as Sonic Spinball and Sonic 3D Blast should of been included, If you're gonna be referencing them Sega, they should of been here. and while I do like the coin feature and classic Mode. I feel they somehow tamper with the games' coding, with glitches where their were never been with the Android releases. I still do recommend the collection and it's a good effort by Sega and Stealth. I definitely seen worse compilations in recent memory but it could of been bigger and better. If it had a few more months for polish.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a blast to the past, and a great game to play to experience the original games in our there glory. Only toke 15hrs to 100% and that's not to long for 4 games but the missions mode made it fun and some where very challenging to do as well. The game also allows you to Cont lost special stages to try and get all the chaos emeralds which helps if your rusty or new to the game. Also for those wishing to play the story mode works for getting the achievement for clearing the game even though the achievement mentions anniversary or classic, so you don't need to reply the game twice to 100%.  With that said they made it so all versions of sonic have his spin dash and/or drop dash which he did not have in the games hes playing in this, which can make some levels easier due to being able to speed up quicker then intended, Also please get this game when it was on sale, it what I did, and I feel like it was worth the money, the original asking price is way to much for how little there is to do in this. _childDocuments_.review: I have been a Sonic fan for a long time. The first time I played a Sonic game was in 2006 with the Sonic Mega Collection Plus on the PS2. Because of that, a lot of my early memories with Sonic have been with the Genesis games. But there was one thing I could never do back then. Actually finish them. Either I had monkeys banging cymbals in my head back then or the games are just that difficult.Years later, probably 2012, I returned to the Mega Collection and learned of the save state feature, which I never knew about back when I first played it. With the save state feature, I was able to experience each classic Sonic game in full. But there was one minor problem. The save states took forever to load. That didn't hold me back from finishing the games and finally seeing those oh so satisfying credits roll by, but it broke the pace of the games to screeching halts. Because of that, I found it hard to return to the Mega Collection simply because the save states took so long to load. That was really it. Occasionally I'd load up a save and replay the final boss of each Genesis game, but it was not satisfying enough. I wanted to play through each game without worrying about lives and continues, without worrying about messing up a special stage, without seeing that dreaded Game Over screen cutting back to the title screen.With all that said, I believe Sonic Origins is the perfect way to experience the original Genesis era Sonic games. You have the widescreen support, no more lives system, the chance to retry special stages at the expense of the unique coins, the choice to play through each campaign as select characters, and the all new animated cutscenes that simply act to bridge the gap between each game. While I have replayed the Genesis games countless times and have had my irks with Origins adding stuff like the drop dash into every game, I don't mind it all that much.What's most important to me is that a new generation of kids will get to experience these games without the frustrating hassles of a retro gaming era so far removed from modern conventions. With this collection, I got to fall in love with each game all over again. And what I like most is that they are all conveniently in one single collection. Sonic 1, CD, 2, and 3&K work wonderfully when paired with each other in a single collection that urges you to play them in order.Oh yeah, this game passive aggressively posits CD as the second game, even though Sonic 2 released first. To be frank, I don't mind it. If it's what the writers at Sonic Team and SEGA want the classic games to be seen as, I'm all for it. The lovely animated cutscenes are done with such care as to give the information from the manuals without overbearingly adding too much lore that contradicts later games.As for my brief thoughts on each game.Sonic 1Absolutely classic. I love it to bits even though it wants to chew you up and spit you out. For the first entry in the entire series, it gets so many of the core mechanics right that it ages gracefully. Being a game from 1991, it becomes insanely unfair as it progresses. Honestly, I love it. And given the infinite lives that Origins throws at you, you can rest well knowing you will never have to be blasted back to the title screen.Sonic CDThis is quite a polarizing game. If you play it like any other Sonic game, you're simply not playing it the intended way. Each level is built to be large and sprawling, encouraging exploration. However that is antithetical to the Classic Sonic experience, since you want to go fast! As the second game in the collection, it challenges you to unlearn what you learned in Sonic 1, and that works really well as a teaching tool for the later games in the collection. The addition of new characters, Amy and Metal Sonic, is also great and makes CD essential playing.Sonic 2Perfection. With more zones than before, a better implemented special stage mechanic and the addition of Tails, Sonic 2 is one of the greatest platformers ever made. Sonic Origins' version of Sonic 2 borrows heavily from the mobile phone remaster of Sonic 2, which means an additional optional zone is playable, and you can have Sonic get a boost from Tails. The best version of an already amazing platformer. I highly encourage you try and win each special stage.Sonic 3 & KnucklesEven more perfection. Not more has to be said. Each zone is iconic, plays really well, and the game does a tremendous job at telling a story with just the in-game sprites and environments. The special stages are at their best, and the music top notch. Wait... the music?!! So yeah, the music in Carnival Night, Ice Cap, and Launch Base are different and vastly inferior to the original music tracks. I wholeheartedly refused to buy this game on console because at least on PC, I can mod the original music back in it's place. That's what I did for my game and I wouldn't have it any other way. Hopefully this review gets dated and an update adds the original tracks to the default experience. Overall though, replaying Sonic 3 had me with a big dumb grin on my face the whole time. I had never played a widescreen version of Sonic 3 before, so to finally be doing it fresh with the other classic games was amazing.I highly recommend this game to anyone that found the original games to be too difficult. It allows you to really appreciate the art in the games at a more relaxed pace, and the changes made are so minimal that you can easily mod the game to remove those minor irks. A very good collection.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: If you've never played any of the original Sonic games on Genesis/Mega Drive and are willing to pay a premium to get a 16:9 remaster that's not as good as the fan-made options you'll probably be okay with this. Otherwise just don't bother (especially if you already have the originals).In a vacuum with no context I think this collection is actually fine? The issue is that they removed the originals when they released this to Steam. I want to give them the benefit of the doubt and assume they just did that because they thought this was going to be the definitive version but that's just not the case in my opinion. I'm glad that we finally have the widescreen mobile remasters of these games on Steam now but there's good reasons why you'd want the Genesis collection versions over this: the major reason being that this lacks workshop support where the old versions had it so you could easily download rom hacks without having to go through the trouble of patching it yourself. You also don't get the roms in a separate folder like you did with the OG versions so you can't use your own emulator if you want to. Not only that but to further rub salt into the wound the "classic" versions available in this version STILL ARE NOT THE ORIGINALS they don't even really try to hide that as there's Hidden Palace in Sonic 2 which is not a thing on the original Genesis version, there's also no slowdown and there's a lot of "bug fixes" in this version, so I'm not sure why you would even bother playing the 4:3 version outside of making a small minority of bosses slightly easier.It's not all bad though, I like that they removed lives as I feel like a big turn off to the originals is that they were really heavily trial and error based and with the small amount of tries you get before a game over I understand why people often dismiss the first 2 games. The 16:9 aspect ratio also really does help with a lot of areas and helps you see hazards way earlier (metropolis zone comes to mind) The animated cut scenes they added are cute and they dumped all the Game Gear games here which is nice. I don't think any of these really make up for the downsides though. Also it has Denuvo lol

_childDocuments_.review: This collection is an excellent base for modding. If you're willing to mod this like I did, you'll have a good time, but you should not need to mod this collection to get these games into an ideal state.Things that are still problematic without mods as of the release of the Plus update:- You can play with a lives counter in 4:3 or with infinite lives and a bonus coin counter in 16:9. These options cannot be changed independently of one another.- Sonic CD's ending is messed up.- Sonic CD's voice lines have been removed.- You can clip (very easily!) out of one of the Sonic 3 bonus stages (the one that plays like the special stage from Sonic 1), which requires a restart of the game to fix.- Sonic 3's music is unbelievably compressed for no reason.- The music for Carnival Night, Ice Cap, and Launch Base are from even earlier builds of the game than the prototype build that leaked years ago and sound significantly worse than the music in that leaked build of the game.- The Super Sonic music in Sonic 3 sounds like something out of Sonic 4. It's not a bad composition by any means but I'd rather the original 4sec loop than something that doesn't even remotely fit the game.- Visual options are still utter nonsense ("anti-aliasing" is a completely meaningless option and I'd rather there be nothing at all than something that shows you didn't have any idea what you were doing). Edit Aug. 24, 2023: the default visual presentation now uses sharp pixels, but this option is still there and it still makes no sense for this game. Note that I do not have the Plus DLC so anything that's wrong with Amy or the Game Gear emulation I can't speak to. Nevertheless, this is too big a list of issues for me to just roll over and accept. Go play these games elsewhere. Your phone might actually be a good choice. There are also numerous fan projects that do a better job than this collection.If most of these issues are ever addressed, I will change my review to a recommended. I really don't need all kinds of fancy bells and whistles, I just need these genuinely great games to be treated with the respect they deserve in what is the only official way to buy them on modern consoles and PC.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, I'd say this is a solid package. 4 great games all in 1 package.(+) Coins & Museum================I really enjoyed the way coins are used (as weird as it is for a Sonic game to have them). I've watched the Sonic CD intro a lot since purchasing this game lol(+) Cutscenes================The new cutscenes are beautifully animated.(-) Price================Is this a great game? Definitely! Is it worth $40? Not really. Unless you really want to play this as soon as possible, I recommend waiting to get this game for a cheaper price. Also consider that there are better, more cost-efficient ways to experience these titles.(-) Sonic 3 & Knuckles Soundtrack================This version of Sonic 3 & Knuckles does not include the original game's Michael Jackson OST. Instead, those tracks have been replaced by new tracks based on the original game's prototype soundtrack. I personally like the original prototypes more than their Sonic Origins counterparts. The new Launch Base Zone theme is still really good (in my opinion) regardless. RIP OG Ice Cap though :c(+) Sonic 3 Boss Fight (Big Arm)================I really liked that they re-added Big Arm (final boss of Sonic 3 standalone) for the Launch Base Act 2 boss fight.(+) Extra Features================I've been enjoying the boss rush and mission modes. The missions aren't much, but they're cool to have. Now as for the boss rush... that's something I've always wanted in a Sonic game. It's amazing to see one finally added to a collection like this. I'm a bit disappointed that they didn't include the minibosses from Sonic 3 & Knuckles, but I guess it's pretty self-explanatory why they didn't do that.(+) Unlimited Lives================You get unlimited lives in anniversary mode. This has made Labyrinth Zone in Sonic 1 a lot less frustrating for me. Also, I was was more willing to experiment with momentum in different stages as a result (especially in Sky Fortress Zone in Sonic 2).(+) Overall Presentation================This is a great package for newcomers overall.

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic collection that goes above and beyond - It's not just a collection of poorly emulated ROMs like some of the other collections out there!! 100% recommended for any fan of 2D platformers. The best part about this particular collection is that it caters to purists who want to play the games how they were originally intended without any of the new features, and players who want enhanced modern versions of these titles. The individual games themselves have not aged, and the remastered versions (Anniversary Editions) play just as well as some of the best modern 2D pixelart games released nowadays. These versions feature new playable characters and new abilities that make the games even better.There's also tons of custom made Missions and unlockables (Movies, Illustrations, Music), as well as Mirror Mode versions of each game.I also really appreciate that this collection doesn't treat you like a baby with a stupid "rewind" feature or special "super easy story mode" difficulties. You've got to actually try to get through these games (though they really aren't that difficult to begin with).My only complaint is that the Steam Achievements are really dumb and easy. I wish it'd reward you for beating every game with every character, beating each of the mirror modes, S-ranking all missions, getting all the unlockables etc. Instead it rewards you for defeating an arbitrary amount of specific enemies (?!), and just S-ranking SOME of the missions. Not that it matters, it'd just make playing through the extra content even more fun if we had better achievements here.If you decide to purchase this collection, I recommend you play through the Mission Mode which is a really misleading name for a mode that allows you to play through all four games back-to-back as though they were one big adventure (which they are!). Ignore the achievements, just play the Mission Mode, then beat the custom missions, and then try out Mirror Modes and different characters.

_childDocuments_.review: - This is an updated review. My opinions have changed since release. Sonic Origins is a hard one to express thoughts on. While there are a lot of things that are done right, there are also a lot of things that are done wrong. Namely, by way of representing the original titles in their entirety. For the average player or newcomer, you'll notice nothing wrong. But if you're familiar with the source material in any meaningful way, you'll immediately notice subtle differences that tarnish the experience. Some of those differences including, but not limited to:Sonic CD missing voice dialogue from Sonic and Amy, the score resets if you restart a level in S3&K, Lack of 3rd jump button, The audio levels in S3&K are all over the place, Sonic 1 & 2 suffer from an air lock when coming out of a roll jump or attempting a drop dash, No centiseconds timers in Sonic 1 & 2, Anniversary mode isn't true to it's name, as it's a cropped version of the Retro Engine and not the original Assembly games. The main menu for Origins also experiences major slow down on certain devices. We can go on, unfortunately.What irked me more than anything, was the removal of the original versions of these games from Steam upon Origins release. While I had bought them years before, it makes it harder for any newcomers to obtain these games. Origins is great, but it does not replace the originals by any means. The originals must be preserved. With all of that said, if you can look past all the little problems, you have an otherwise great collection here. It's still worth the money. It's my hope that SEGA rectifies these problems when Sonic Origins Plus releases.Sonic Origins runs perfectly under Proton on Linux and Steam Deck.Old Review: - This is the definitive way to play the original games. The Retro Engine made these already great games even better. While there are some minor criticisms, It is as a whole, the single greatest presentation these games have ever had.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an interesting collection for many reasons compared to SEGA's past attempts. First off, I'll preface this with the disclaimer that I do think it's a worthwhile purchase, but you should probably wait for a sale if you aren't a huge Sonic fan. The game is receiving updates to fix some bugs, and seemingly to even add new features. The game is only going to get better from here, and it'll get cheaper too, so there's no reason to get hasty with wanting to buy it right away. For example, in 1.0.4, S3&K had new cheat codes added to it that weren't there in previous versions, and fixed probably the most annoying bug in the game.The good:- 16:9 aspect ratio- Brand new story cutscenes- Mission mode- Gallery mode, featuring new concept art we've never seen before- For people who are not great at old arcadey games, the coin system makes the game a lot easier- Drop dash- Brand new remaster of Sonic 3 & Knuckles, which hasn't even received a port in years- The most beautiful remaster of Sonic CD's cutscenes we've ever had- Plenty of new, beautiful sprites for Sonic 3 & Knuckles, improving the presentation significantly, and making stage gimmicks like the Carnival Night Zone Barrel more intuitive- New act transitions for Sonic 3 & Knuckles- Improved S3&K competition mode- As of 1.0.4, new cheat codes for S3&KThe bad:- The high system requirements. This seems to be because of the main menu, which is rendered in real time and requires a modern GPU. This is a collection that was made with consoles in mind first, so the menu is really only an issue in the PC version for low end users. An entire demographic has been left out of playing this collection for a novelty that loses its charm after a few hours of play.- The confusing DLC situation and pricing. Personally I don't really find the DLC to be worth buying, and I think the base game is fine at $39.99. That's about $10 each for 4 amazing games, $8 for 5 games if you count Sonic 3 and Sonic & Knuckles as 2 different games. If you've already played these games and own them in other forms, however, it's going to be muddy as to whether you find that worth the price or not.- The bugs. Personally in my playthrough, I did not encounter a lot of issues. Occasionally there was the odd collision moment, but that happens quite a bit in the original genesis games as well, so it did not bother me that much. There was nothing that actually softlocked me or prevented progress. The only bug I encountered that was genuinely irritating was Tails' AI being broken in Sonic 2, however this was fixed in 1.0.4. - The half-baked Time Attack mode. Like Sonic Mania, there is an online leaderboard for every stage, which is great. However, there is no option to individually play these stages and try for a good time like in Mania, which feels like a huge missed opportunity. The mobile remakes of 1 and 2 had this, and CD even still has its own Time Attack mode in Origins, so it feels like a bit of a glaring oversight to me. The Time Attack mode is made even worse on the PC version, with hackers running rampant ruining it for everyone. It feels like there is little to no point to even trying to compete within the game when so many people are using hacks to ruin the fun for everyone, getting times of 0:0.00. - The sound design. This game has a number of oddities with it's sound. First of all, the music in the Genesis games have been remastered differently from the mobile remasters. The mobile games chose to remaster the music with different hardware, enhancing it from the genesis originals. The results are quite good, but they are not faithful. So, Origins chose the more faithful route, recording the Genesis music off of an actual SEGA Genesis. If you've never played the games on a Genesis or on an emulator with accurate sound emulation, this may sound weird and very wrong to you, but it is actually accurate to the original games. This is a creative decision that is going to be subjective for people. Aside from this, Sonic CD has audio mixing issues, with the volume of the cutscenes being different from the rest of the game. The 2011 remaster introduced looping segments to the stage music, but this version got rid of that and instead the songs stop and start again like the original SEGA CD version, which is a big step back from the 2011 version. Then, in Sonic 3 & Knuckles, that has a redone soundtrack, using the songs found in the old PC version of the game. Whether you like the tracks or not is subjective. Thankfully, the PC version of Origins has a robust modding scene, so you can easily replace these tracks if you don't like them. The one new song that really, really sounds bad, is the new Super theme. It sounds wrong, as it's not even using the instruments from 3&K, the drums are from 2, and the synth sounds wrong. The melody itself is good, and fan remixes have shown you can  make it work, it's just the choice of instruments that make it bad. It's a nice gesture from the team to make a new song for the game, but it just sounds bad. Thankfully, this can also be replaced with mods.All of that out of the way, SEGA has had a bad track record with previous attempts at collections. Old ones used faulty, inaccurate emulators that introduced issues and quirks that weren't in the Genesis originals. This remaster has quirks of it's own, but overall it is the best attempt at a collection SEGA has done so far. Most of the issues can be ironed out with patches, and you can use mods on PC to change bits you don't like, such as the redone soundtrack for S3&K. I do think this collection gets a bit too much flak for what it is. This is far from the worst attempt at a remastered collection out there, many of the flaws are exaggerated because people have this strange bias against Sonic games that they don't have for other franchises. Of course, I am not trying to write off the flaws of this collection, but to act like it is this huge disaster is taking things out of proportion. Sonic fans in general could stand to be more constructive when it comes to their feedback instead of writing everything off as massive flops to farm social media clout and approval from others.

_childDocuments_.review: Well well well, it appears that the internet is yet again too judgeful for a product which didnt deserve all the hate it recieved.....Let me explain to you why i chose to recommend this product despite its past negativity.When i was a kid i grew up playing the old sonic games with a collection called "sonic mega collection plus" (for the PC) which im sure most of you might be familiar with, it contained the original sonic games (except sonic cd which i was really eager to try out) from that point the classic sonic games (my favorites were sonic 1, 2 and 3&k) became my personal favorites and grew on me for the time being, ever since then i havent touched my beloved classics for a decade and unfortunately i handed over my bundle to my cousin which i regret to this day..... (plus computers dont really support CDs anymore so even if i still had it, it would still be useless)Fast forward for the announcement of sonic origins and i was rather thrilled to give it a shot, return back my childhood memories that filled me with joy, thanks to the new sonic movies and my introduction with sonic mania i was finally united with sonic after almost 10 years of not touching a single sonic game. but as you guys may assume i started developing hatred due to the internet's poor reception for the product's release, swearing to never buy it at its current state, i didnt wish to waste my hard earned money on a product filled with gamebreaking bugs.For months ive been debating with myself if i should buy sonic origins whenever i could and decided i would only do it when the game goes on sale, and that is excactly what i did.Let me tell you a bit about the experience i had with each game that was offered in the bundle (by the way i recommend you to get a controller to play the games, keyboard controls are a bit clunky)Sonic 1: the first entry in the series was actually very wierd for me at first, afterall i havent touched it in years,although it is still the slowest sonic game out of all the sonic games on the list, it was still fun but felt exausting clearing 3 stages with no innovation, but hey, it was the first game so i cant blame them.Sonic CD: This game i never tried before and was very eager to finally play it, many would call it "the black sheep" of the series as its generally very different than a normal sonic game, its essentially a sonic 1 upgrade but not fully understandable, i found the level design very odd and not very enjoyable, lets just say i didnt like the game and it made me sick, would never play again but im still happy i tried it and saw how a classic sonic game shouldnt be made.Sonic 2: now we get to the fun part, my second favorite game of this collection, this time sonic gets a new buddy named "tails" which really added flavour to the game and although his controls arent perfect, he is surly a great add on to the game, level design is very good with a sign of a huge progress from sonic 1, utilizing speed more than its previous installment.Sonic 3&K: And the cherry on top, the absolute king and the game that truly finished this collection with a great taste in my mouth is this masterpiece of a game, with the introduction of an actual story in the game, sonic 3&k suddenly gets more depth which would later follow to other games with much more complicated plots like the sonic adventure games which are heavily based on sonic 3&k's story.Plus, with me restoring back the MJ tracks to the game, it made the experience even more enjoyable (no stupid lawsuit will stop me from enjoying these goosebumping tracks >:D)So, what is the overall verdict of the product? Well after thinking about it deeply i came to a conclusion that at its current state, its a totally worth buying!and before you call me biast , heres why i think that way:1) I havent encountered a single bug/glitch as reported by many in the past, it appears that SEGA has indeed fixed the product and its now safe to buy, although i dont promise you that you wont encounter old school bs like bottomless pits and ingame mechanics which are still fairly annoying at times.2) The cutseens done for the game are absolutely gorgeous! the amount of effort and work that have been put to them are mindblowing, and with the introduction of story mode, these cutseens are connecting each and every classic in its place, creating a wonderful story.3) For those that claim that denuvo crushes the game's identity/ruins the game/doesnt allow mods/decreases performances ive got news for you, DO YOU GUY KNOW HOW MANY GAMES RUN ON DENUVO ANTI CHEAT? IF YOU DONT, HERES A FULL LIST OF THEM 4) And for those that miss the MJ tracks of sonic 3&k, just replace the horrible tracks with the tracks here For those that are still wondering if you should buy the bundle or not, it depends if you own previous classic sonic games or not, if you own them in any platform then i wouldnt recommend it, but if you are new to the franchise, looking for a quick escape with the timeless classics of the 90s or just want to add the classic sonic games to your game library, you should give it a go. (And if you worry about the price, just buy the standard edition or wait for a SEGA sale)Do i think this is the best classic sonic game bundle ever released? Of course not! do i condemn SEGA's decision with delisting all of the classic sonic games on steam? Absolutely! But do i think this bundle deserves all the hate it got? Not at all!But at last, Sonic origins is still worthwhile if you fit the categories, otherwise you are just wasting your money with a bundle which will get released a decade later.The classic sonic games will forever have a place deep in my heart as the games that truly defined my childhood and made me the returning sonic fan i am now, its not necessarily the bundle that made me this way, its the games i got to experience once more and keep them where they belong, proudly displayed in my games collection.

_childDocuments_.review: It's everything I always wanted, the mobile versions playable with a controller and with a bunch of extra goodies. What's not to love?Well not a lot, but they are pretty damning.First, what you see in the advertisements is what you get. No widescreen with lives or playable Amy Rose I'm afraid.Second, there's Denuvo. Don't got a good computer? Have fun running this.Third, Sega's tampering of the games because of them being wrapped in Hedgehog Engine 2. Effectively making them non-lightweight games and also getting rid of the menu that CD had. I also believe it is responsible for the input latency I suffered and the slight blur filter they put over the games.It also handles the audio of the games which resulted in the music regressing back to old versions instead of remastered tracks (I'd argue this is a good thing though). Stuff like music speeding up is done internally instead of loading up actual sped-up tracks so they sound wonky.There's also minor stuff like Tails' AI failing to respawn outside of S3&K when too far away so get ready to hear him jump a lot. But using the Up+Jump command to make him fly will help in getting him to respawn proper.Lastly, S3&K is half-baked. It is definitely in the right track to being the best version but the physics here are different so you'll get crazy momentum you wouldn't normally gain in the original game. The music is weird in that you get a mix of Sonic 3 and Sonic & Knuckles tracks and jingles here and there instead of it just being consistent. Oh and the Super Sonic theme they use sticks out like a sore thumb.I think it's serviceable but you aren't missing out on much if you stick to the originals. Did I have a good time though? Yes. They are still the games I love with all the extra benefits they reap from the folks that gave us Mania. But it needs a lot of things to be fixed to be definitive.

_childDocuments_.review: 23/06/23 UPDATE (Sonic's Birthday)So, after a few patches and announcements I want to add the following:Finally, Sega fixed most of the problems with the collection, and gameplay-wise is pretty OK!. Not to mention the mod scene has grown exponentially and we can pretty much restore or fix anything we need.However, I would still advice to get it on discount or as a gift.But there's something else now: We finally got Amy, and... well, she's 11 USD (around $2000 ARS) alongside some 8-bit Sonic titles that are pretty good, but they only gave us the Game Gear versionsFor those who haven't played the Sonic GG titles, these are fine Sonic games, as long as you keep in mind that with it had some hardware limitaitons, so the titles aren't as good as the 16-bit counterpartsThat said, for some of these the game gear version is the worst one. I don't understand why Sega didn't gave us the Master System versions. The SMS had better resolution and screen, with pretty much the same hardware. I don't understand this decisionAt any rate, I would still advice against paying full price for the collection. You can find better fan projects to enjoy the versions of Sonic 1, CD, 2 , 3&K... and even the 8-bit titles:-Sonic 1 Forever / Sonic 2 Absolute-Sonic SMS Remake (S1 and S2 Master System)-Sonic Triple Trouble 16-bit-Sonic 3 A.I.R.**********************************************************************************************************Original Review:Sonic 1, Sonic 2 and Sonic 3 & Knuckles are some of my most beloved games in this franchise (with S3K being my favorite videogame of all the time). Sonic CD is kind of an interesting oddity, but still worth playing. Still, the point is that I know these games VERY well and I have a long history with themDo I think the games are worth playing here? Pretty much! These are good remakes of amazing games. The Widescreen alone makes it a lot more welcoming for new players. Although there are a couple of bugs due to SEGA's incompentence.Is this collection worth it then? No. there are better ways to play all these games.Why? Because Sega rushed things as always, made an incredibly confusing DLC pack for the Deluxe edition, buggy menues, messed with the AI code of Tails, added DENUVO (an anti-piracy software that causes a lot performance issues) and screwed up the possibility of doing more things with the groundwork Christian Whitehead and Headcannon already did.The games are as outstanding as ever, but they did NOTHING with them. They could have given us new in-game cutscenes for zone transitions. They could have re-done the level design for a "hard mode". They could have done a New game+ for each game. They could have added Mighty & Ray on all games and also Amy Rose.The animated cutscenes are breautiful, but they don't add anything new gameplaywise.If you're set on getting this collection, wait for a discount, don't pay full price for it. Or better yet, go play the S1, SCD and S2 mobile versions: these work A LOT BETTER and you could even play them on your pc (google Sonic 1 and Sonic 2 decompilation).And for Sonic 3 & Knuckles, Sonic 3 A.I.R. project is probably the best version of that game ever released, and has the level of quality I was expecting this collection to have.

_childDocuments_.review: Do you like the first four Sonic games? Then this is a great way to play them. Do you not like classic Sonic? Then this probably won't change your mind. It's not anything mind-blowing, but fans will appreciate the new cutscenes and extra presentation and gameplay gubbins. Finally having some way to play Sonic 1 and 2 on something besides mobile (officially anyway) is very good, not to mention having Sonic 3&K playable in widescreen at all. Mission mode is a neat little diversion, story mode seems like a good way to just blitz through all the games in one string, the new Blue Spheres levels are fun if you're into that, and the museum is a nice bonus. I also appreciate the new coins system, as it makes playing special stages less of a headache. For purists, they will like that the original versions are included for preservation's sake (though no way to play Sonic 3 and S&K separately? Bit of a nitpick, but if you're going to include the original roms, might as well add that extra bit, yes?). A lot of people may balk at the "new" music in S3&K, but I enjoy these beta tracks and I'm glad that their existence allows Sega to re-release the game finally. Music is subjective, yadda-yaddaDenuvo sucks but doesn't impact gameplay, and the DLC and pre-order nickle-and-diming sucks but ultimately doesn't take that much away from the core experience. Depending on your priorities, one might also find these games to be too old for the price tag, though I personally think the price was just fine for what I got (four not-unsizeable games with updated presentation and gameplay and a variety of side challenges).It's probably the definitive official versions of the first four Sonic games. They surely cannot get better from here. Please stop re-releasing these games, Sega. Adventure and Advance fans are starving.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to write this review primarily about the Sonic 3 & Knuckles component of Origins, since that's where all my time went.I'm not sure what to say for this one. I've been pretty hyped for Origins, since S3&K is genuinely one of my favorite retro titles and we haven't seen any kind of re-release for it in some time. Unfortunately it seems like we didn't actually get that, and instead we ended up getting something dancing around trying to pretend it's S3&K. As someone who plays through the original on a very regular basis, this port just feels *off*. Sonic does NOT handle smoothly. You seem to stick to some surfaces, mid-air control is nonexistent, some surfaces will send you flying at weird angles, and some gaps will be "fine" one second and then randomly crush you the next. The original genesis Sonic titles were always about fast paced gameplay with extremely tight controls and it feels like NONE of that transitioned over. There seems to be an inconsistent input latency layered on top of everything, as some times Sonic would wait before responding to my jump, while other times I had to purposefully slow down my input of spin dashing because the game would arbitrarily decide to respond to the jump button BEFORE the fact that i was holding down.Maybe the included versions of Sonic 1 / 2 / CD are great (since they use the pre-existing mobile ports), but the attempt at S3&K most certainly is not. I could forgive the $40 pricetag for yet another re-release, the lack of original licensed music, the use of Denuvo, or even the blatant cash grab DLC; But somehow Sega took a nigh perfect game, and found a way to drain the fun out of it. So please don't reward Sega for such a shoddy effort. Just go play Sonic 3 AIR instead.

_childDocuments_.review: I have a ethical responsibility to write a negative review for this compilation. the games look nice in widescreen and it's great to be able to see these on a marketplace. I like being able to waddle over to my computer after a long and exhausting day at work and just hit thoughtlessly hit the "play" button on this and play some old sonic games. The problem is, unless you're absurdly affluent and like throwing money away for no reason, there's no reason to purchase this. As a computer owner there are already ways to play these games in 16:9 on PC for a lot less than 40-45 dollars, and they have less bugs and have way more customization options than this offers. I don't need to tell you this since you've probably already read a bunch of reviews but go check out the decompiled ios/android ports of sonic 1, 2, and CD, and of course, check out either sonic 3 complete or sonic 3 AIR for a far superior experience than what this offers. So basically what you're spending money on here is the compilation goodies and the fact that this natively launches from the steam platform and you can collect achievements for it. The crappy part here is that the achievements are baby stuff. I felt pretty great about having all six chaos emeralds by the end of Spring Yard Zone in Sonic 1, but the game didn't give me any sort of pat on the back or reward for doing so. In fact, the inability to toggle infinite lives off in anniversary mode doubly makes it feel like there's zero incentive for playing these games at a higher level or trying to learn more about them. That sucks!The extras in the museum are sorely lacking. I remember Sonic Jam on the Saturn way back in 1997 having the original commercials for the games from japan and neat stuff like that. The museum offerings here are presented well and some of the art is in unprecedented resolution which is super cool but it's a lot of what you've seen already! It would've been nice to get some developer commentary tracks on levels, or maybe some options to configure custom playlists to enjoy while playing these video games. Yknow, some sort of offering that you can get here and not in other, superior versions of these widescreen ports.I don't need to mention the music, we all know its terrible, but I should mention that there is a mod to restore the original soundtrack already. I don't know if there was any way around this. Michael Jackson's estate is notoriously difficult to work with and probably wanted sega to pay out the ass for a game that came out like thirty years ago. I don't really blame them for not wanting to pony up the money. What I can blame them for is how awful the replacement music sounds. Custom playlists or new compositions from guest composers like Tee Lopes or something could have cool but instead we have Jun Senoue offering the worst-sounding "genesis" remixes of those godawful prototype tracks i've hated for decades. The situation sucks, but it certainly could've been handled in more thoughtful and creative ways. I also think it's cowardly of them to have done their best to hide the soundtrack replacement news until shortly before launch.Ultimately, don't buy this game. I bought it because I'm a stupid idiot and I like buying stuff because it makes me feel better about my dumb life. Go donate 40 dollars to an abortion fund or something and just google "sonic 1 widescreen android pc port" or something like that. Sonic is an anti-fascist and that's more in line with what he would want you to do, if he was real. I don't think he is though. (God I wish he was).

_childDocuments_.review: This is a collection of what many consider to be the best of Sonic the Hedgehog.  The games, for the most part, still hold up well.  The gameplay is still fast, & the cleaned up audio on most titles comes across wonderfully.  The dropping of lives & addition of the spin dash in all games in anniversary mode is a nice touch, as well as getting to play as Tails & Knuckles in most titles.  The coins earned in anniversary mode can also be used to replay special stages in the event of a loss.  The extra modes can also be fun, with mission mode having a selection of challenges, & mirror mode shaking the entire game up for veteran players. This does not feel like the definitive edition.  Sonic 1 & 2 are close to their portable versions, though still missing some things those titles had.  Sonic CD is practically just the Steam version, complete with missing Knuckles as a playable character.  It also uses the original cutscenes, rather than updating them along with all the new ones.  Finally, Sonic 3&K has the most problems, clearing being the odd one out.  It's audio quality is worse, it uses the beta/PC release tracks for stages 4-6, & the collision just feels off on so many points, coming across closer to the original Sonic 3 release.  There are so many small problems here & there that just add up.  As for the rest, the DLC is completely useless & not worth it, adding a ridiculously insulting ability to look at the island in the menu.  Not turn the camera to see around it or view the models, just to look at it. This list was incredibly simple, with the hardest challenge coming from simply beating the games.  No real challenge or meat to them, simply do a missions around each game, & unlock a number of items in the game's museum.  You don't even need to 100% the game to get them. This was a massive disappointment.  The games are all here, & a patch or two could fix some of the problems, but the lack of features to make the games worth playing again for old fans is noticeable.  As for newer fans, these ports have issues that could turn some of them away.  If it goes on sale, & these problems get fixed, then this could change.  As of right now, I really don't feel like it's the best or definitive way to play these games.

I have Sonic 3 on Sega Mega Drive Classics, and the rewind and speed-up features along with the Genesis limitations made it instantly more fun and replayability due to easily accessible mods. And that was like… $5? Sonic 1, 2, and CD on Mobile are like $2 a pop. That’s $11 dollars! Even if you round up every game to $5, that’s $20! And the game is $40!…Or, it used to be.This is the thing that brung me to make a review. With the release of Sonic Origins Plus, the original game’s price lowered down to $30 so Sonic Origins Plus could take the original price of $40. Great, right? More things for the same price, where’s the downside?People who bought the original game, for $40, still have to pay 10 extra dollars if they want to enjoy the “full” experience. That is 50 dollars for $20 and a bunch of Game Gear games, most of the games in question being available in Sonic Adventure DX if they didn’t REMOVE it as a FEATURE.I could buy Sonic Frontiers with $50! I could (have) buy/bought all the Genesis games included in this collection along with Sonic Mania AND THEN SOME with $50! I could buy Sonic Mania, the Encore DLC, AND Sonic Generations for $50. At full price.If you like it, that’s fine. It just didn’t deliver for me personally.

_childDocuments_.review: After pre-ordering this game / collection for 68 AUD and getting every achievement as of now, I can safely say...I would've been better off using Emulators.This was my first time ever beating Sonic 1, 2 and 3&K (and first time getting the good end on CD) and although they are great experiences and I am a big fan of Classic Sonic, this collection pretty much blows, it's only pros being the widescreen gameplay and newly added cutscenes... which SEGA themselves can't even be thanked for considering that was the work of fans. And that's what you're going to begin to really realise, the heavy lifting was done by the fans while the lazy work came from, you guessed it, SEGA.To begin with, the keyboard controls are stupid and I want to sue whoever thought they were a good idea, If I hadn't had myself a controller, I might've sooner refunded the game. Secondly, people may defend this point as the games "staying true to the originals" which I can agree to disagree on but the whole menu's within menu's thing really sucked, having the options all the way at the museum for god-knows-what reason and then examples such as trying to change Sonic CD's Region Soundtrack, which took me longer than it should've, proving the menus really needed touch-ups in the first place. And the Origins menu was so underwhelming without even mentioning you had to PAY EXTRA to rotate and zoom a camera. (And the menu for the Illustrations and Music is Microsoft Powerpoint levels of quality).And the menus within menus leads onto my next point being: Wow, you really just half-assedly threw Christian Whiteheads work into the game with no extra effort. It would've been nice to make some minor improvements here and there but NOPE, apparently they can't do. There's also the missions, very cool idea and a good way to grind Coins... yet every level has these grey bricks just bloody thrown around the place. Normally I'd assume they couldn't change the levels... and yet they can place more enemies and ugly blocks... what is this???Also the mirror mode and boss rush are useless to me and probably to everyone else, the fact they make it an entirely different save/game for have a different Ratio Screen and flipping the world is stupid, just make it customizable. So if you haven't picked it up by now: SEGA does piss all to help in this games creation. Probably just threw this together so they could get more money in their pocket, and they really must love their money because they didn't want to waste a buck on trying to get Sonic 3&K's og soundtrack, I personally do not mind but fans obviously are dissapointed to see this and they must've known this considering they never got CW to port 3&K likely because of this reason up until this point. They claim they "composed new music" to fill in for the songs they couldn't use... when they literally use the unused music instead, yeah ok.Oh and didn't they mention adding an extra playable character or two? "how about we make Knuckles unplayable in CD" Yeah no, this review is long enough as-isNow if you made it through all my whining, here are some parts I DID like about this: Like I stated prior, the new cutscenes, missions and widescreen is so good, these games deserved these and being able to play these games in one neat collections is nice, it's because of this game I get to not only play all 4 games but I get to see all the good endings for myself, and pushing aside the roughness. these games are as fun as they'll always be, especially when played one after another.I like this collection of games, but they are really pushing the definition of a "remaster" and yet they're not the only ones, bad games and remasters seem to be occuring more frequently and it's sad to see SEGA go this direction too.Games like Sonic Mania (and maybe Sonic Generations) are what companies should be doing for their fans to celebrate milestones, but Sonic Origins is what companies think they can get away with nowadays.To conclude: I don't hate this game, I hate SEGA for allowing this great idea to become so terribly underwhelming.
