_childDocuments_.review: I feel like a lot of people really don't seem to understand just what Sonic Origins is....It always felt to me as if it wasn't really intended to be this massive collection of Sonic games like Mega Collection Plus or Gems Collection was. It was never meant to be anything beyond: "Hey, we're bringing the HD Remasters of Sonic 1 and 2 to PC, and here's CD and the never before seen an ACTUAL re-release Sonic 3 & Knuckles, all in glorious widescreen. Remade from the ground up in Sonic Mania's retro engine." Just giving us a nice refreshing take of 4 classic Sonic games packed with some neat things from Sonic's history that should surely reflect it's title as Sonic Origins.This should have been the explanation right? Well not quite. It seems like the higher ups at Sega didn't exactly know themselves how to market this game. As a result it is unclear to us the consumers, casual gamers and Sonic fans alike what this game really is. Couple that with the absolutely terrible price guide and "DLC" additions (which were all later included in the PLUS DLC) and it's very easy to understand why this title's reception is mixed. That being said, what is Sonic Origins. Is it a smash pack of classic Genesis games like the many collections we've seen for decades? Or not.This is a debate that I'm very tired of seeing because all of the people who know are overshadowed by the loud vocal majority that wants Knuckles Chaotix or Sonic 3D Blast to be included in this pack of remastered Sonic games. (I can understand why, Chaotix hasn't had a release at all and is probably the only 32X title worth playing in my humbled opinion.) If Sonic Origins seemed lackluster already, adding these games will honestly make things even worse. "Why is Sonic 1, 2, 3 and CD only in HD, why can't we get other genesis games in HD!?" Sure, if they had competent emulation developers who are able to reverse engineer the code on these old games and then modernize it for today's standards then SURE, games like Sonic 3D Blast or Chaotix would be a no brainer. However it just simply doesn't work like that. As stated previously the titles included in Origins were remade from the ground up. This is not your average Sega Genesis collection and should have been marketed as such!!Don't even get me started on the quality of the remastered games that we got... It just screams corporate meddling. Every game is full of it's own unique flaws and things that we haven't seen in other Retro Engine remakes. Which is another reason why Sonic Origins has a mixed reception but I want to talk about the elephant in the room. The PLUS DLC.I applaud them for listening to that loud majority that wanted more content for this game. I feel like it's especially beneficial to the game's reputation as a whole especially given it's strange launch price, this makes people feel as if they're getting their money's worth. Is what I would say if there wasn't another big elephant in the room, THE DIGITAL DELUXE EDITION. (Which I myself pre-ordered when it was available for purchase.) Do you know what we get in the Digital Deluxe Edition? More coins? - Yes.Music unlocked from the start?  - YesMore Content to unlock in the Art Gallery? - YesPlus DLC? - Ye- No. No?NO!? The game was a whole $15 extra dollars at launch for people who purchased the Digital Deluxe Edition why are those people not being compensated!? We paid $45 DOLLARS FOR THIS GAME. Okay so you give the people what they want, more content but at the same time you're ripping off the people who pre-ordered the Digital Deluxe Edition!? $55 DOLLARS TOTAL!?For a game that's being listed for $29,99!? Come on now. Originally I was content with whatever they offered for this game because I was just happy to see those retro engine ports of Sonic 1 and 2 being playable on more than just mobile phones. I was happy because Sonic 3 and Knuckles was FINALLY getting that treatment as well as being the only title to at this point has NOT seen a re-release since Sonic Mega Collection. If I had known that there was a possibility of this game getting a PLUS update and that THIS kind of strategy would be pulled I would have never pre-ordered it because ALL OF THE PRE-ORDER CONTENT COMES IN THE PLUS DLC! Sega, Sonic Team and their marketing team really dropped the ball on what would have been a decent collection of remastered Sonic games. Is Origins bad? No, not at all. I can tell there was some love put in to all this. While uncredited, part of Mania's dev team helped Sonic Team learn the Retro Engine. But with Orgins and it's troubled backstory, abhorrent marketing and business strategies makes this game just plain bad. Do not buy this title at a high price, wait for it to go on sale. Steam always has really good Sonic The Hedgehog sales and chances are you might even get a game bundled in if you don't have it already. Till then I'll be laying low til the price inevitably drops and I can purchase the plus DLC. (Too bad it's 1 year TOO LATE for me to get a refund.) I'll be playing the BETTER Sonic title that released last year, Sonic Frontiers which GAVE US FREE DLC ON THE SAME DAY THAT IMPROVED THE GAME IN WAYS ORIGINS COULD EVER DREAM OF. Do yourself a favor, wait for a sale. This collection can wait.So for now, this game's recommendation is a no from me.

_childDocuments_.review: I was excited to finally have an easy way to play Sonic & Tails co-op with my friend. That's still possible, but... I can't in good conscience play these versions of the games. Especially Sonic 3K... *man* did they butcher Sonic 3K. The keyboard binding interface is needlessly restrictive (I can't bind the arrow keys to movement? really?), the physics are a little buggy, the music is awfully low quality and just sounds muffled (there's plenty of remastered versions of these amazing tracks, why not just use those?) and the new prototype tracks that they used for the MJ copyright stuff (Carnival Night, Ice Cap, etc.) sound somehow MORE barebones than the prototype tracks already were. I was looking forward to seeing how Sega would update the proto music since I've heard so many fan recreations, but they just.... didn't. They literally just stuck the unfinished tracks in there and called it a day.In fact, "unfinished" pretty much sums up how this compilation made me feel. "Thoughtless", "careless" and "negligent" fit in there somewhere too.This *may* be a viable way to easily play Sonic & Tails co-op in Sonic 2 specifically, but other than that I'd avoid this compilation entirely. For Sonic 3K, check out Sonic 3 A.I.R. instead, it's a way better remaster done by fans.

_childDocuments_.review: You can watch the full coverage of the game here which shows every achievement getting completed. Part 1: Part 2: Part 3: Solid game that is optimized better than the Sega Genesis/Mega Drive Collection or SGMDC for short without mods from the Steam Workshop. Four of the Sega Genesis/MegaDrive/CD Sonic titles are here. Those omitted are Sonic 3D Blast, Sonic Spinball, Sonic 4 Episode 1 + 2 and Sonic Mania. But I would also feel they would be welcomed into this game as a whole package of the *Retro* series. Also I would feel that the Game Gear/NeoGeo games would be a welcomed edition if Sega got the means to put them into Sonic Origins. _childDocuments_.review: Sonic Origins is an interesting throwback into the past, with a few curve balls that either help or hinder the experience. The original Sonic the Hedgehog, Sonic 2, and CD follow very closely with the old Christian Whitehead ports in Anniversary Mode, with some very small elements from more recent titles (such as the Drop Dash from Sonic Mania). Coins are in place of Lives, which do help with certain Special Stages, especially in Sonic the Hedgehog. Sonic 3 & Knuckles is the new port on the block, and while it brings many good changes, such as fixing some sprites and creating new scenes to better connect Sonic 3 and Sonic & Knuckles, there are some small bugs here and there, such as the beginning section of Marble Garden Zone Act 1, and a set piece in Sandopolis Act 2. These errors could be fixed in a future patch to potentially improve the gameplay experience, but aside from that, all of the games play great, and are all very well done ports.Now, down to the more debated aspects of the game: Music and Side Content. There are not many new music tracks to listen to, as many are the original tracks from their respective games. The only new tracks are the Menu music (a remix of the Sonic World theme from Sonic Jam). and the new(-ish) tracks for Sonic 3 & Knuckles's Carnival Night, Ice Cap, Launch Base, Super Sonic, and Credits theme. While the Menu track is somewhat serviceable (I do wish there were more original tracks or remixes for things such as the Museum or Mission modes, as the music can get repetitive), the new tracks for S3&K are a very interesting case. Tracks like Ice Cap and Launch Base are fine replacements to the original Genesis versions, and are very close to the versions present in the Nov. 3 Prototype. Carnival Night and the new Super Sonic theme, however, are either very muted (in Carnival Night's case) or very similar to Sonic the Hedgehog 4's soundtrack (which features poor Genesis soundfont replication). These are featured for only about a good 12 or so minutes (assuming 2 min per Act), so you don't have to wait long until the music comes back to the original tracks we know and love.The extras presented in this game are another mixed bag. The Missions mode is a neat little feature, providing some decently fun challenges that reward some easy Coins for your troubles. They're good tests for understanding how each of the playable characters work, and can be fun to speedrun. The Sound Test option is nice, with the optional DLC providing extra tracks from more Sega Genesis and even 32X games. The Museum option provides both some old artworks that we've seen before, as well as new concept artwork that we've never seen before. This is where you can also view the new cutscenes for the game, that now accompany each game (with CD getting 2 new cutscenes in addition to the originals), with bonuses providing a behind-the-scenes look at the storyboarded versions. S3&K comes a new Blue Spheres mode, which adds new spheres and layouts to test your skill (although it provides no Coins, more of just a bonus experience). While these are serviceable, I would have personally wished for more behind-the-scenes looks at the development of each game, either with more design documents, notes, or even videos of beta versions that we may have never seen before. And as I've said before, some new remixes for some classic tracks would be nice to have as well.With everything said, this is a very serviceable collection of classic games, with only a few small things hindering the overall experience. While some of the exrtas can be a little underwhelming, there's just a small amount enough of new content and insight into the development and history of these games. I would recommend this to anyone who would want to try and play through these games for the first time, or even the second or third time.

_childDocuments_.review: Have you ever heard of a game where the developer had to save its integrity on Twitter and call out the publisher for how rushed, unfinished and buggy the final build of the game is? No? Well, then you're in for a ride.After Sonic 06, Sonic Boom Rise of Lyric, Sonic Forces and Sonic Colors Ultimate, SEGA released another game riddled with bugs and low quality. SEGA rushed this game and didn't want to delay it, because they thought it might be neat to release it on the same day Sonic 1 released, which is a nice homage, but they still don't get that a rushed product is a problem for the devs and the actual buyers. It is like using washing powder for your cake each time, wondering why it tastes bad.Now, before I get into it, I will mention the actual positive side.This game is great in terms of presentation. It is so nice to have the actual islands Sonic ventures on be visualized. They make the Sonic world seem way more connected. Furthermore, the cutscenes are still wonderfully animated. They clearly love the Toei Sonic style, and I wouldn't have it in any other way. While most of the cutscenes shown are only for the opening, others are for the start and ending of the games, which leads into a connected story.The mission mode is also pretty fun. I haven't played all missions yet, but it seems like each mission has its own stage, reminding me of Sonic Generations, and what can I say, they do their job in delivering some extra challenge.The last good thing is that you can retry special stages if you fail. Back then it was quite frustrating, but this way it actually is fun to hunt the Chaos Emeralds/Time Stones.Now, let's slowly dip our toes into the depths.The Sonic CD cutscenes weren't re-animated. I think it would be a nice novelty to keep the original cutscenes in the museum, unfortunately the game uses the old 4:3 cutscenes for the story itself too. That is quite inconsistent and makes it seem like a fan mod.Next is the drop dash, while it's nice to have the drop dash, I just cannot fathom how bad it is in this game. The drop dash in Sonic Origins is more of an instant spin dash rather than the actual drop dash from Mania. Meaning, you lack air control, you cannot redirect Sonic. That is quite frustrating to use. It is nice to have it, but the way they implemented it makes him feel like a car.Now.....the bugs. I would've hoped not to encounter bugs, since I rarely do, but in this game I actually got the most annoying and frustrating bugs possible. If Tails in Sonic 2 is flying whilst you jump into the Special Stage, you'd be able to hear his flying sounds the entire stage's time. Even worse was the fact that I beat Sonic 2's final boss, and when the end screen appeared, I started to realize I was softlocked. I couldn't continue in any way. I was stuck, waited 2 minutes and then just gave up, restarted the game and had to beat the final boss A G A I N. Next is Sonic 3. Sonic 3 is a mess. Next to Sonic changing into the foreground layer, even though during the cutscene he should've been in the background, he also clipped through multiple objects, through layers of the stages, leaving me softlocked a good few times, but they also completely messed with his physics. Sonic in this game is way too fast. He bonks his head against walls he never was intended to hit, ruining the flow of the stage. He also isn't able to reach the heights he used to. I wasn't able to reach, for example, a Special Stage because they messed with Sonic's jump, leading to him not gaining enough height.The DLC for Sonic Origins is such a cash grab. Remember when they tried to monetize Super Sonic in Forces? They literally just put a few missions in here, add an island camera view which should be in the base game, and rip the old models from Generations/Forces, put them in here, stiffly animating them. These extra 5 bucks should've been in the package, even the price is question worthy. Sonic Mania released for half of that and was more of a new game than this is. Hell, I'd even say it makes more sense to buy Sonic Mania and Sonic Generations instead, since you get the best out of both worlds with both being half original/half remake-type games.Also, where is the time attack mode? I mean....for a Sonic game there should be a time attack mode, where you can actually pick the stages and speedrun them individually, just like in Mania.Last, but not least, is a direct question. Where is the new character? You featured Amy so prominently in literally each promotional material, even the ending clearly hints at Amy maybe being playable, but she isn't. It feels like the devs really wanted to make her playable, but realized there wasn't enough time.Sonic Origins might be the 22nd way to play Sonic 2, but it is far from the best. SEGA should learn to stop using Sonic like a GTA free money glitch, 5/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Sonic Origins is, as far as I'm concerned, exactly what it set out to be. A collection of the four-ish games that defined what Sonic is at its core. And as the Sonic films have inspired a new generation of fans, the Blue Blur's history is now more accessible than ever!- Anniversary Mode is a life-saver for fans like myself, who have never had the skill to get far in retro games. Now that I don't have to worry about game-overs, I can properly explore the games without anxiety (or having to look up walkthroughs for Marble Zone.)- The many side-modes and time trial options allow for bite-sized gameplay sessions (which can also serve as training for the core game. Maybe someday I'll beat Classic Mode!)- The museum is a lovely collection of Classic Sonic music, videos and art (including, more surprisingly, every episode of Sonic Mania Adventures, and clips from the Sonic Symphony!) Part of me wishes they included entries from the 90s cartoons and comics... but as a fully Sega-approved collection, it's delightful.To wrap up, I especially recommend the game if, like me, you've been unable to get far in these games in the past. And even if you know these games inside and out, there's enough shakeups in the side-modes to get a fresher experience. In my opinion, Sonic Origins is Way Past Cool.

_childDocuments_.review: - Each game plays as good as their previous incarnations. The controls are as responsive as they should be.- , what more is there to say.- . Sonic 1 and 2 were previously offered in widescreen exclusively on mobile devices, however now they have a new home on proper platforms.-  that do justice to the original source material as well as providing a neat way of tying all of the games together.-  what more is there to say. It doesn't stop pirates, makes the experience worse for the end consumer, and requires an online connection to play.- . For the price the dlc is touted at, they are worthless to buy for anyone other than hardcore enthusiasts. The content they add should be in the game by default anyway, without the extra price.- While I understand Sonic 3's original music cannot be implemented,  in all honestly. However its more perplexing how a decision was made to replace the Super Sonic music with a cover/remix of the original theme.- . You are forced to play the games with drop dash enabled and in the case of Sonic 1, forced to play with spindash, even in the "classic" mode. The only game with decent options is Sonic Cd, and even then, those features were already options from the 2011 pc version. As well, there were missed opportunities to implement features that had even been in previous collections before, such as Sonic Jam's easy modes.- . This isn't much a problem for most casual individuals, but for the keen eyed it can be an annoyance to have a smoothed image on medium to large displays. - . The music throughout the games is muffled and sounds as if a low pass filter had been applied to it. Even at max volume it can be quiet compared to how it was in the originals.- . It frequently drops frames when even above the game's "recommended" requirements.- . The bindings are set to odd configurations with no other default options, forcing players to change them manually if they don't like them.- . You are forced to back out to the menu to change anything. Sonic Mania was the same in this regard but it's still a slight disappointment and inconvenience none the less.- . Your air control is removed in favor of a set arc. Why is this the case, I do not know.- . The variety in them is disappointing, often having mundane and boring objectives. The effort on these missions is clearly lacking, featuring grey blocks in preexisting levels as it's means to create these challenges. It's similar in quality to the extra content found within Sonic Forces, being superficial levels to inflate the game experience.- . This is an even greater disappointment when you realize that some of the images are low quality, especially the "harmony covers" which are taken from a 1996 screensaver and feature heavily compressed versions of said covers.- . The dpad controls for the museum are inverted for some ungodly reason, there is no option to use a mouse and there is no way to easily flip through pages in the manuals without having to exit the full view menu and flip 1 page at a time.

_childDocuments_.review: A new popular trend among videogame publishers seems to be the removal of old games on digital distributions platforms, only to sell them again as part of a “new” collection afterwards – which is exactly what happened with , which launched after SEGA delisted previous version of the included classic  games. As such,  currently remains the only way to play these games on Steam, if you didn’t buy the older versions before. This would be less of a problem if  was worth its surprisingly high asking price of 29,99€ for the base game – but unfortunately, it just feels like a half-hearted cash-grab for fans and newcomers alike.On paper,  includes the first four main Sonic games, three of which originally released on the Sega Genesis () and one on the Sega CD (). However, while one might expect these original games to be emulated as part of the collection,  actually includes the 2011 () and 2013 () Retro Engine remasters by Christian Whitehead instead. As such remasters didn’t exist for  yet, the  team was tasked with creating one for  specifically.For purists, it has to be noted that despite the name, these “remasters” are more than just graphically enhanced versions of the original games, as  now includes the previously scrapped  for example. Notably for a franchise known for its soundtracks, some music tracks from  have also been replaced entirely . Unfortunately,  doesn’t offer the option to play the original games through emulation instead, which means that the actual origins of the series aren’t part of this supposed “Origins” collection - while there is a “classic mode” for each game, it’s essentially just an option for the original 4:3 aspect ratio.One of the new additions to these remasters is the “anniversary mode”, which mainly offers widescreen support as well as unlimited lives. This is also used during the new “story mode” of , which allows you to play through all four included titles consecutively, with new, very short (1-2min) cutscenes serving as a small narrative bridge between the games. Other news features of  include a really basic “Museum” mode featuring sketches, songs, etc to unlock, a “boss rush” (= fight against the game’s bosses in succession) and “mirror” mode (= world is flipped from left to right) for each title, as well as a “mission” mode – sixty standalone 2-3min challenges (e.g. destroy five enemies in a certain time) across the four games with different ranks to achieve. Overall, the new features of  are pretty standard inclusions for these types of anniversary collections and far from substantial enough on their own to warrant a purchase for dedicated fans.Oddly enough,  features a 10,99€ expansion pack (), which does offer the type of content that would make the base game more worthwhile for dedicated fans, such as offering Amy Rose as a playable character in all four games as well as Knuckles in ,  to accommodate his playstyle. Locking content that should’ve been in the lacking base game behind DLC just feels like a rude move, especially after the backlash SEGA already received when it came to the . All in all, as an anniversary collection,  is not offering many arguments for a purchase if you’re a dedicated  fan that already owns the games included in this collection in one way or another.On the flipside, I wouldn’t recommend  to newcomers to the series either - and I can say this especially because  has been my first  game as well. While the included games certainly had a huge impact on popular culture, they haven’t age particularly well in my opinion and might be more of an acquired taste these days. While the early outings of popular  rival Mario for example, such as the original  (1985), have certainly aged as well, I do consider them to be a lot less frustrating than what’s on offer in  – and I certainly wouldn’t have cared about beating them if I wasn’t granted unlimited lives through the “story” mode of this collections.My frustrations mainly stem from three things in particular: For one, while these classic  games want you to reach high speeds as you go through the levels, they also regularly punish you for doing so, mostly by placing obstacles and enemies in a way that are too hard to spot the first time around (e.g. buried enemies). To add to this, during some city zones in particular I periodically had a hard time making out what’s supposed to a non-interactable decorative element and what’s not. Second, the included  games occasionally include gameplay elements which are only used during one level but never properly explained – such as the infamous  during the Carnival Night zone of , an obstacle which needs to be controlled by holding up/down on the d-pad: a mechanic that isn’t hinted at or used anywhere else in the games. And third and final, there’s the boss fights – while I appreciate the game offering a lot of unique boss encounters, some of their hitboxes can be an absolute nightmare when figuring out the weak spots.Combined, these issues made my time with  a much more frustrating experience than I expected – while I quite enjoyed the visuals and music, I never felt quite in control of the flow compared to my time with all of the  platformers for example. That said, I do feel like offering a save state & reload system, similar to the one used in the  collections for example, would’ve been a great help in reducing some of my issues here. Additionally, it might’ve been a good idea to offer a more modernised  experience through the “anniversary” mode with more substantial additions to enhance the overall experience for new players than just widescreen options and unlimited lives. Ideally,  would’ve offered three game options – playing the original games, playing the originals games with slight enhancements (e.g. widescreen, save states) and a substantially modernised version for new players. Instead, there are none of the original games and only “remasters” with small enhancements, satisfying neither fans nor newcomers.Concluding, I’d only recommend  to either dedicated fans of the series who want to own the included games once more or newcomers who are as bullish about getting into a franchise by starting from the beginning as me – just keep in mind that these games are more than 30 years old by now and little is done to accommodate their age.

_childDocuments_.review: Should you buy Sonic Origins?TLDR:No, and you should probably boycott SEGA.First of all.. This game is online only. Which means you cannot play it without an internet connection. No steam deck offline play and no playing Sonic during internet outages, among numerous other things. This is a very anti consumer practise and it needs to be boycotted. This game should be playable offline.Next, Denuvo. Another anti consumer practise that needs to be boycotted... this is nothing but bloatware. 7gb for games that can seriously be no more than a few hundred mb...? How much junk have SEGA added to my system? How much anti cheat spyware crap is in this game? It uses 16gb of ram while in the menus alone, which leads me to complain about the fact the game lags on low end computers. This is where a game like Sonic Mania shines, you can tell it wasn't created as a cash grab by a half baked team, and was instead created by sonic fans such as Christian Whitehead and Stealth.That leads me onto my next complaint. Which is another anti consumer practise and ANOTHER reason to boycott this game (and SEGA as a whole)... When this game was released, SEGA delisted all the original roms, so there is now no easy legal way to obtain the original games on modern tech. This is just pure anti consumer, forcing people to buy the new inferior product, seriously, that's bad practise in every scenario and SEGA have fallen messes in my view, they are no longer a company that I will support if this is the practises they are pushing. Especially with them pushing NFTs on all their new upcoming games. They are here to extract cash at this point, and nothing more. Be aware of this when giving them your money.Now this delisting wouldn't be so bad if the "classic mode" in this game was actually classic mode, you know, the original games in their untouched original format? But guess what... "classic mode" is still the new rebuilt games. All SEGA have done is cut the aspect ratio down to 4:3 and give lives instead of coins.. which means "classic mode" has all the new mechanics (spin dash, drop dash, ect), and it has all the new glitches and errors.. therefore the games do not play the same as the true classic games at all. You would have thought dumping the classic roms in the game instead would have been easier, cheaper, and made more sense. But nope.Next (and this one isn't a big deal for casual players, BUT it is significantly important considering this is supposed to be a definitive collection of the classic games), the games do not play the same as the classics. There are changes in speed, timing and level design, which introduce new problems such as in Sonic 3; where if you reach max speed, you will be thrown into spikes and other obstacles that would never have hit you before on the original game because the level was designed around Sonics correct speed. The Sky Chase Act on  Sonic 2 is another example that really stands out. In this level all the badniks move at all the wrong times compared with the original game. There are also changes to the hitboxes, you can run into objects and be crushed in places where you would never have been crushed before, even when you aren't even within crushing distance. I've never been punished so much for going fast in a Sonic game... this is a serious issue for me, I hate it, and I don't think it can be fixed its a game flaw caused by multiple conflicting issues.I also have to say that the inability to have lives while on anniversary mode is ridiculous. Give us the option to swap those stupid coins for lives and continues, the coins mean nothing. This IS NOT the definitive way to play Sonic. This game is a half hearted cash grab in most respects. Love and care has clearly been taken in some places such as the new cut scenes which are awesome, but it is completely absent in others; such as the horrible music remakes, and severe lack of being able to move during a drop dash (EDIT: Roll lock has finally been fixed), not to mention the DLC cash grabbing.Price and downloadable content? The game is overpriced. It's a blatant cash grab by SEGA and its just not acceptable. They have stripped away parts of the game and then sold it back to the community, and as bad as that is, the DLC is also extremely over priced. £4 for some letterbox backgrounds? £4 for some songs...? Having to PAY TO ZOOM into the islands in the background?? These are all things should have been included by default. Sonic fans are being taken for a ride. £25 - £30 with ALL THE DLC and yes, maybe then you have a price worth paying... but £40 for everything is far too much considering it doesnt even have games such as Sonic Spinball and Knuckles Chaotix in the museum. The price of the DLC for what you get... it's pretty poor and very bad faith. (EDIT: and now to add insult to injury, SEGA are punishing their most loyal fans, pre order and deluxe edition owners of this game are now being charged a second time for DLC they already own if they want to upgrade to Sonic Origins Plus... and the games base price was dropped by £10 which means, if you didnt support SEGA on launch then you'll get more for less. SEGA could not get much more greedy, its pure cash extraction at this stage. The pre order and deluxe edition owners should have received this DLC for less than full price, if not free)Don't get me wrong THERE IS A GOOD GAME HERE. Mission mode is cool, and the new cartoon animations are brilliant, I really do like them! But if thats all you lack, then once again it's just not worth the price tag. There are far superior ways to play these games. The mission mode is little more than a rom hack.The new graphics truly are nice and Sonic 3 looks great, its by far the most noticeable change.Sonic 2 having the infamous Hidden Palace Zone is amazing too and its fantastic to finally have this on our systems, I love that it's finally accessible by default. But again £40 for that level and some mission modes? Sonic fans are being taken for a ride.Final take: Sonic Origins feels so good, yet it feels like its only 75% finished. It's not everything it could have been, and that 25% of lack luster cheapness and DLC cash grabbing isn't acceptable for a game of this magnitude. SEGA are killing their own product yet again with these stupid little things and its just greedy. SEGA really need to change their practises and update the game to its full potential.What has happened to the gaming industry? Its little more than an extortion racket these days, where you buy games broken and in parts and wait for updates on unfinished products, its a joke and this once again leaves a sour taste for the Sonic fan base and drops SEGAs reputation by another ton due to another fumbled release and cash extraction from loyal fans, I will never purchase another game on pre-order or even initial release thanks to the absolute mash of good and bad that this game is, I have yet again had my faith in SEGA (and the gaming industry as a whole) damaged and it's really starting to annoy me.This game has SO MUCH potential, continued support can make so much happen with this title and it could be by far the BEST sonic collection ever created. The menu is nice, the additional things like story mode are awesome! And as I said already, the new cutscenes linking the games together are incredible, it's old skool cool! But without at least adding additional things such as including the stripped out content (DLC) as standard, the game falls short. True DLC should have consisted of additional Sonic game remakes which could be added to the museum in game as time went on. Thats where the extra income for SEGA should have come from. (Not this double dipping they have tried to pull on everyone)Give classic sonic games the glory and respect they deserve and stop screwing around to squeeze money out of people! I'm sure many people would be happy to support SEGA and would happily buy additional museum DLC game remakes.

_childDocuments_.review: This game could've been an even greater, more definitive version of a Classic Sonic Collection. Christian Whitehead, Headcannon, animation studio Neko Productions and their director Tyson Heese clearly cared a great amount for their work on this product, but SEGA decided that a game that works is better than a game that works, and has even more careful, love and detail put into its entire structure and design. The Sonic games remastered by Christian Whitehead and Headcannon and implemeted by SEGA were hastily shoved into the port, being Sonic 1, CD, and 2, are missing minute and major fixes like audio and mechanics. The end result is a solid way to play Sonic 1, CD, 2, and 3&K all together, but it misses the options of Mania like turning on and off certain mechanics like Drop Dash, Super Peel Out, and more playable characters. Digging into the files of the game reveals cut content most definitely dropped because of SEGA's desire for more money, as opposed to a finished, fully cohesive release with attentive patches. It's clear that SEGA did the Challenges too since the quality is okay at best. All the work done by Christian Whitehead, Headcannon, Neko Productions and Tyson Heese is clearly presented with care, concern, appreciation, and love, for Sonic and fans. They have all the ingredients for the greatest Sonic experiences, but SEGA is an unmovable roadblock in this path. Overall, Sonic Origins is a great collection if you just want to experience Classic Sonic games all in one place in a 16:9 screen ratio, but there are so many more additions that could've made this a top tier collection of remasters.Buy this game when it's half off at $20, not at the overpriced selling point of $40.You can always get Sonic 1 Forever, Sonic 2 Absolute, and Sonic 3 A.I.R as a free alternative created by loving fans without the barrier of SEGA.I don't like SEGA's capitalistic, ignorant business practices so I don't recommend this game. Despite all the extra features, get the ROMs for free. If you really want all of the games in one place with extra features, then this collection is worth it on sale. Despite all my criticisms of the game and SEGA, this game is still a decent collection. It just could've been so much more.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought Sonic Origins despite all of the negative attention it was getting. I'm a diehard Sonic fan, so take my review with a huge grain of salt. Disclaimer - I did install 2 mods to enhance my experience, one to fix the blurry textures and the other to restore Sonic 3's original soundtrack. Is Sonic Origins the best way to play these 4 games? No, it really isn't and that's super unfortunate. However, I found myself enjoying it a great deal even though it is far from perfect. It is a very convenient package and the games themselves run fantastic. I played with a wired Saturn controller and did not perceive any input lag. It's a shame because clearly there was SOME love shown in making Sonic Origins, they just didn't go 100% with it. For it to truly be the definitive way to play Sonic, they need to add a lot more content/features such as changing music/options on the fly or adding cheats/debug etc. The museum unlockables are bad. You can google/youtube literally everything that is in there. The museum should have had unlockable Game Gear/Master System games or something more worth while. I really love the new animations before and after every game, although I wish there were extended versions of them you could watch elsewhere. Also, the "Classic" mode of every game is a waste of time. To be clear; THERE IS NO "TRUE" CLASSIC MODE. What you get instead is a 4:3 cropped version of the base game. It's borderline false advertising. I know I was pretty negative, but I'm still going to recommend it albeit with the caveat that it's not worth full retail price as it currently stands.

_childDocuments_.review: Got this for 30 bucks, in my opinion the sweet spot for 4 remaked games. That's it, remaked, not remastered.The reason I say this is I have seen a lot of negative comments regarding lag input. I have played Sonic games all my life and while I'm not a speedrunner, I can tell rather than input lag is physics don't act as what I remember in my muscle. Bosses behave different in the hits, and that's very noticeable, you can't cheese some bosses like in the originals because they changed physics behaviours in some situations. Sum that to the fact I always played in PAL versions and the result is a quite different from what I'm accustomed.I'm not denying there could be input lag, there wouldn't be the decompilations if this wasn't true, but in my case I feel way more the 60 fps and changed physics than unresponsiveness. They are different games than the originals, they wouldn't behave the same even if you use the decompilation mod on them. So yeah, it's a new learning experience for me even if I have played these games all my life and I know them front to back. For instance, you know what a very bad, input lag ridden rendition of these games is? The mega drive/genesis classics before they patched it, and if you want to know how bad it was, try the Switch version which they left unpatched. That is truly straight unplayable.Edit: After clearing all games and all achievements, I stand with what I said. But the biggest change are special stages, the timing in my memory and muscle is absolutely off in special stages compared to regular ones. It took me several tries to finish some of them when I can do them without thinking in the mega drive, the augmented speed of the stage scrolling ♥♥♥♥♥ me up in my perception, but it was fun to get used to them rather than plow through them like I usually do. Sonic 2 special stages are the most changed, not only the speed but the depth and vision range is totally different.The only bad thing I see in this is the mentioned change in some music in Sonic 3, is not only that they sound worse than the originals but they feel really underwhelming compared to the rest of the soundtrack. It really stands out how they were leftovers of prototypes, they could have rearranged them to be on par with the rest. Still, this can be fixed through a mod, something I recommend and is easy to do. Could be worse.I didn't realize it had rankings of everything, included different modes but not special stages. This is something that will make me come back. Overall, the game is much better of what people makes, it's a good rendition but things are different, and you can always go back to emulators or the original consoles if the changes are so negative to you. This is good.

_childDocuments_.review: The classic Sonic games are still some of the best 2D platformers out there, combining speed earned from momentum with exploration across huge, open levels. This collection has all of the best ones in one place, for a decent price. For anyone getting into Sonic, this is where it's at.And as a long time fan of the series, I can confidently say this is the BEST official way to play the classics to date.You get widescreen, better performance, bug fixes, no more limited lives, special stage retries, and playable Amy, But that isn't even scratching the surface of what this collection has to offer. New challenge levels, a huge art gallery, and very pretty cutscenes tying the whole thing together into one big, beautiful package.Now is this collection perfect? No, not really. It's very strange how no attempt was made to add Sonic 3 style save slots to all of these games even after all of these years, to change the game's settings you have to... navigate to an island. All of the features this collection adds are presented in an "all or nothing way", like what if I only want to add the fullscreen without removing limited lives or vice versa? _childDocuments_.review: Sonic is back, but this time as a collection of older titles instead of something brand new. New Sonic games tend to have all sorts of issues, so surely a straight remaster of older ones would not? Well...Sonic Origins is a collection of four games: Sonic the Hedgehog, Sonic the Hedgehog 2, Sonic 3 & Knuckles, and Sonic CD. Each is presented in two formats: Classic Mode, which plays like the games were on their original platforms and then Anniversary Mode, which adds widescreen support and removes lives. Both have their merits, but the widescreen support added by Anniversary Mode absolutely elevates the experience and is easily one of the game’s best features.And yes, the games themselves are great. Fast and fun gameplay with a great mix of platforming, diverse level design with all sorts of interesting stuff to find, and just the right amount of challenge. I’ve always liked how freeform Sonic’s gameplay is and how open the levels were and these four games are no exception.The original game is perhaps the roughest of the bunch, but easily has some of the most memorable stages. The second game is the most difficult of the bunch, but has some of the best music. The third game has the most balanced gameplay of the bunch and honestly might be my favorite. CD is a bit of a weird one, combining some of the good aspects of the others, but I was not a fan of the time travel mechanic and boss fights; it’s probably my least favorite of the bunch.The question is then - do the changes made to these classics make the collection worth it? That’s a bit of an iffy one. On one hand, the package is a bit more expensive than I was expecting for a collection of four old games. With a $40 price tag, I wish the game had included even more classic Sonic games. For starters, Knuckles' Chaotix would have been an excellent addition, but Sonic Chaos, Sonic Triple Trouble, and the Sonic Advance games would have been great too.Quality of life is also an issue. These are old classics ported to modern platforms without the usual features we get with such releases, such as save states or the ability to rewind. I can do without the latter, but save states would have been super cool to have here and that is something that straight emulation does better than this collection.I also was not the biggest fan of whatever filter was used to scale these games up. It looks a bit blurry and nowhere near as crisp as I would have liked - even when messing around with settings like resolution and anti-aliasing (which I recommend you keep disabled). As it stands, it does take some getting used to.The collection does do good in its addition of new game modes though, including boss rush, mirror mode, and a mission mode that adds a bunch of new objectives. Not all of those missions land, but it’s a nice addition regardless. The museum mode is a nice touch too, allowing access to artwork, music, and videos.Perhaps the biggest issue with this collection though is how buggy it is, particularly on the audio front. In every game, I had audio cutting out too early, audio repeatedly playing even when not doing anything, muffled music, and in a few cases - the audio completely bugging out and playing nonstop loud and annoying sounds. And while I have not noticed any collision or physics issues - that also appears to be a common complaint.The collection is obviously a rushed job and you need look no further than the very devs that worked on it stating as such. Apparently there was some sort of disconnect there between the remaster devs and the actual finished product, leading to many strange bugs.I cannot give Sonic Origins a straight positive recommendation, but I also cannot say that it’s entirely negative either - this is why I wish Steam had something in the middle. On one hand, these are some absolutely solid classics and I am glad they are available on modern platforms, but on the other, the collection itself is lacking and there are quite a few technical issues on top of that.Follow my  for more reviews + videos!

The hitboxes are insane. I've died countless times for seemingly no reason. I'm good enough to consider myself nearly perfect at these games and only die when I get cocky. But this port of Sonic 3 is horrendous. Yes, it's fun, but the hitboxes make it to where even if i run into the side of a spike that's pointing upwards or downwards, I'll take damage. I've even ran into one of those barrels and the space between it and the ground was less than a quarter of sonic's size and i ran into the side and instantly died because somehow it registered as a death even though i literally could have been stopped. The gap was so small that even if I rolled, I wouldn't have been able to fit through. Now for the music. The music needs to be the prototype. It sounds absolutely horrible right now. It just sounds like the PC version was converted into soundwaves that the Genesis can produce. The Super Sonic theme sounds like absolute garbage. They butchered the tune and might as well have just left it as the invincibility theme and it would've been 100 times better. In my opinion, they should've used the prototype super sonic theme. _childDocuments_.review: I like this game, a lot actually, BUTThe question being asked is: would you recommend this game to other players? My answer is a big NO.Dropping $40 isn't a big deal to me, but I understand many find that unfair, especially if you're on a budget. My biggest question is why does this even exist?! But before I get into that, I will explain why I bought it. I got it because of the widescreen, achievements, and the ability to easily mix and match mods without having to patch a dedicated rom. That's honestly it. Classic Sonic is a childhood favorite, literally, so this collection has something special for me.Now onto why I could not, and will not recommend this game. It's honestly a waste. It's a waste of money and talent. There are many iterations that exist for each of these games. I grew up with the original cartridges and the Sonic collection on PC many years ago and that did enough for me. The games have been available for pretty much every console ever, and I think you would save money if you just got them individually. Back in 2007 I got the lock-on for only 99 cents online!Honestly, I don't see how this is worth it for anyone, even for those who are new to Sonic. Just get each game one at a time, and see if you enjoy them. Why buy a $40 lifeless collection if you have no idea if you will even like a single game. This collection was clearly for people who already love Sonic, and love the classic games. But here's the thing, if you don't like just one of the included games, instantly the collection becomes a complete rip-off. Personally, I don't like Sonic CD at all, so already I'm screwed, but as I mentioned before, it didn't bother me.This collection is certainly nowhere near perfect. As many have stated, it's filled with bugs that certainly didn't exist in the originals, and there was certainly odd things that occurred that I know didn't happen in the originals. One thing that bothered crap out of me was the jumping felt off. If you were to jump and land and try to jump again the instant you landed, it doesn't register your input. I have no idea what's that's about, but that has costed me rings more than I can care to remember and certainly wasn't an issue I had with the original. As mentioned the physics felt a little weird as well.When this game was announced, I had no idea why people were so hyped up about it. It just looked like a lazy cash grab. Even from the trailer it didn't look special.In conclusion, honestly, do yourself a favor and just get the games individually. Don't waste your time with this piece of crap of a collection. It really has nothing special to offer for anyone.

I'm also really glad they removed lives and added coins instead since I'm pretty bad at the classic games lmao. Outside of the issues I mentioned before, the game runs flawlessly with no frame drops or lag. My biggest issue is with the key-bindings which are absolutely terrible and for some reason, it wouldn't let me change them to how I wanted them. Fortunately, the game is much better controlled with an Xbox controller so I won't be using the keyboard much. Some of the Sonic 3&K music is also vastly inferior due to it being a recreation of the prototype tracks, but the prototype tracks somehow sound so much more finished than the versions used in Origins.Overall, I highly recommend picking this up! _childDocuments_.review: Short version:A heart-warming compilation with minor issues that does not ruin the overall experience.Long version:I am a die-hard Sonic fan that played through all the Sonic titles in Genesis, Gameboy Advance and Nintendo DS as a child/teenager. I also played and loved some of the recent 3D titles on home consoles. Now I finally have the time to try out this compilation myself.Having spent a few hours on the game, I would say there are a lot of things to love and smile at here. Charming animations, fun challenges, a pretty title screen, some interesting twists and modern touches. Yes, the "classic mode" is not exactly the same as what it was in the original Genesis versions. Yes, the music for stages 4~6 in Sonic 3 is different due to copyright reasons. But I think that's okay. It's 99% faithful to the originals with understandable design changes.As for the bugs that people have reported... As far as I am into the game, I have not noticed any bugs except Tails being stuck off-screen, which I don't care very much. Maybe if I go ahead and collect all the Super Emeralds, and maybe if I play through every game with every character, I will discover more of them, but so far I have not run into any bugs that I find annoying... yet. I heard the story about the developers being pushed for impossible deadlines (and hence the bugs). I feel sorry for the developers suffering from poor management, but at the same time I am grateful for what they have delivered as the end product. Let's hope the bugs can be fixed in future patches.If you are a hard-core gamer who is looking for a pixel-perfect replicate of the originals, given the success of Sonic Mania, this compilation may disappoint you. However, if you are a casual gamer, either an old dude like me who wants to re-visit my childhood, or a young fellow who learned about Sonic from the recent movies, I think this compilation is going to be a very pleasing experience.

_childDocuments_.review: This one hurts. So, so much.On paper, You got the guys who did the critically acclaimed ports of Sonic 1, 2, CD, and Sonic ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥' MANIA heading up a collection of the four core titles of classic Sonic. It's on everything and it's easily playable, and with a bunch of nice little extras. Should have been a massive hit with fans, and a must-buy title for anyone.Instead, you get an overpriced, poorly managed collection that still misses features where it's just embarrassing. SEGA were the real ones who headed the collection, and while that doesn't sound strange, essentially it means they were the ones who decided to rip stuff out of the base game to make it DLC, and then hold off content that seemed to be made for the initial launch of the game, for a poorly made DLC pack a year later to... I assume remake the success of Sonic Mania Plus' release?It also means that SEGA decided to just toss in headcannon's ports of 1, 2, and CD in this without putting the effort in to make sure they all work properly. Headcannon technically did the ports, yes, but SEGA was the one who ruined them, same with 3K which was done specifically for this collection by Headcannon. Even with 2.0, there's still a lot of glitches that are present in the game and I can't keep stating this enough, THERE'S NO FULL KEYBOARD SUPPORT. I don't wanna hear "just use a gamepad, bro" when Sonic 3 HAS BEEN ON PC BACK IN THE 90S, it's not unheard of to play Sonic with a keyboard. You literally only need a D-Pad and two buttons, and it's still NOT IN THE GAME. Thankfully, there's Sonic Origins Ultrafix which came out not too long ago, and one of the first things in the trailer is full keyboard support among other nice changes to the game. Thing is, it came out over a year after the game came out. For that time, you got nothing unless you paid for a key rebinder.Because of this, specifically, it just makes the PC version of Origins such a joke. I would love to give SEGA my money for headcannon's versions of the classic titles, but they (SEGA) can't stop messing it up. They delisted the 2011 CD remaster off of Steam for this collection, and it completely stripped the features from that release in this. I wouldn't expect SEGA to do all the little tweaks that fans have done, but when there's such a massive and noticeable gap in quality, I can't help but recommend the fan decomps on PC instead of this collection, since wowee, I can use arrow keys and the enter key in them!I want to like this collection, and it should have been REALLY EASY to not mess up. But somehow, SEGA found a way to do it. Congrats. If you wanted to play the classics on your Switch or PS4 or something, then this collection is fine enough, it's good, even. But on PC, there's much steeper competition with easily accessible fan decomps in 1 Forever, 2 Absolute and 3 AIR, as well as CD Restored which you unfortunately have to track down or pirate since SEGA delisted the 2011 remaster.

_childDocuments_.review: As you can see, the game came out to some "mixed" reception, and I think the opinion of each person largely boils down to what their "relationship" to Sonic is.If you are a series veteran, there's not much to see here. All 4 games here have been available even in widescreen form one way or another (the 2011 remaster of Sonic CD was delisted from Steam just a few days before Origins came out, the ~2013 remaster Sonic 1 & 2 is available on mobile platforms – though you need a tablet with a proper controller to enjoy them, or jump through hoops to run Android apps on PC –, and Sonic 3 already had the fan-remaster called "A.I.R.", again, offering wide screen support), previous compilations like Mega Collection or Sonic Jam had better "museum" content, and "missions" are basically like various small custom ROM hacks.If you are relatively new to – or have an "on and off" relationship with – the Sonic franchise (maybe completing it once or twice over the years, but never getting the good endings etc.), Sonic Origins is a really great way to jump in now:- You can play the game with infinite lives, and even retry special stages, finally putting the chaos emeralds within reach for causals like me. You are still incentivised to explore though: collecting coin TVs (placed where extra life TVs used to be), or getting 100 rings gives you a coin, which you can use to unlock museum content (see below); retrying a special stage also costs 1 coin.- The game saves upon reaching checkpoints, so if you have just 5 minutes to play, you can. (The emulated versions, also delisted now unfortunately, also kind of had this option with save states: but a huge drawback there was that the temptation to "cheese through" the game, by saving e.g. during boss fights, was too high. Now you have the flexibility without taking *too much* of the challenge away.) Some of you might not care about this, but I really hate the fact that I can't play Sonic Mania unless I surely know in advance that I have 20-30 minutes to spare, because it only saves at the end of zones, requiring you to complete both acts in one sitting (which, depending on your age, or your ability to defeat bosses on first try, might be trivial, but for many of us, it isn't).- Missions are actually fun (and more accessible to "casuals" than ROM hacks) and not too hard (which again might be a con for veterans) – they are, in fact, a great way to practice situations you might come across while playing the main games, and they are also efficient coin sources (which, again, you need for retrying special stages).- All games have brand new intro and outro cutscenes, which are really well made. I enjoyed them a lot more than I thought I would!- The only part of the package that's truly disappointing, no matter how you look at it, is the museum mode. It couldn't really be more uninteresting, which is quite a feat considering they had 30+ years of material to gather from. Sonic Jam (the first major compilation of Sonic 1-3) came out like a decade after the first game (maybe even less), and it had a lot more interesting stuff in it.All in all, I'm having a lot of fun with this package despite already owning these games in other forms – but depending on your situation / priorities, you may or may not have the same feeling. I hope the above points will help you determine that.

When you get all 7 chaos emeralds you can become super tails! and when you gain all 7 super emeralds, you can be hyper tails!! (hyper transformation hasnt changed since 3&k but still nice that we have an actual super form for tails) One other nitpick i have with sonic origins is that there is no steam workshop support, anyone who didnt buy Sonic 1-3 on steam before it was removed off of steam, wont be able to play with fantastic mods like sonic classic heroes, sonic 3&k complete, etc.In conclusion, i would say origins is a great way to replay the old 2d sonic games, but the price is definitely more than what id want to pay as these games are all around 25-30 years old. _childDocuments_.review: This collection would still be a bit pricey (and the DLC would still be extremely penny-pinching) if these ports were flawless. Instead you're paying a premium for surprisingly feature-bare and buggy ports. There's little customization for the few features that are there, you can't do something as simple as play with the lives system and widescreen in the same playthrough, one or the other. You can't even say this is for authenticity, you can't ever turn off the spindash in Sonic 1, something even the atrocious Gameboy Advance port lets you do. Bugs are bugs, some are from previous ports, some are brand new. I haven't ran into anything game-breaking but its just so irritating when Tails constantly gets stuck off screen and rapidly spams the jump sound or when the rubble in Marble Garden Zone just doesn't stop falling for the entire stage when the drill robot digs at the beginning.As for added value, you can spend ingame currency to unlock art and music. Remember in Sonic Generations where you could set unlocked music on a per-level basis, including music that doesn't play in the game normally? Nothing like that here! You wouldn't want to play anything over our new awful Sonic 3 replacement tracks! Sit at the sound test! To help collect enough coins to unlocking this riveting content you can play a bunch of original missions developed by the geniuses at Sonic Team. Original may be overselling it since they're mostly obstacle courses of grey, ugly blocks that don't even try to match the tileset plopped over existing levels, you get vapid objectives like kill so many badniks. They have less substance than even Generations' missions and I would not recommend wasting the minor amount of time they would take unless you're really a fan of Sonic Forces' bonus levels. Each game has a mirror mode and a boss rush, exactly as it says on the tin. Though the boss rush has both lives and widescreen enabled, so it's clearly possible for the game to handle it but you're just not allowed to do it. Other than that you have some brand-new cutscenes between games to bridge those gaps. I have nothing negative to say about them, they're pretty and full of character. They were also officially uploaded to Youtube before the game's release, go watch them!Does any of this ruin these great games (and Sonic CD)? Or even mean that this version is bad? No, widescreen is very nice and it's good to see the 1 and 2 ports finally officially off phones, as well as an official port of 3&K. But at this price it's very difficult to recommend a package that's as barebones and flawed as this. I have to praise SEGA's marketing though, revealing the collection as Taxman and Stealth being involved, only to drop that most of the heavy lifting was being done by SEGA's internal teams months later is genius. I'm sure several people would not have preordered if they had known Sonic Team would be within touching distance, such shrewdness should be praised.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, I don't know where the complaints about this game are coming from. I know this game had a rocky launch but I only experienced exactly 1 bug throughout my playthrough of all four games, which strangely happened as soon as I hopped onto THE BARREL (yes, that one) where the game locked up and I had to Alt+F4. The rest of the time the game played perfectly fine. I felt like there was input latency when I first started playing, but in retrospect I'm starting to think it was just me not yet developing a "feel" of the controls. I still reduced the resolution to 1080p and disabled v-sync per Google results just to be sure.Thankfully there is no "life" system in this collection, so you can restart at the last checkpoint as many times as it takes to finish the level. Special Stages are as annoying as ever but thankfully some absolute hero of a developer decided to allow players to retry Special Stages as long as they had the coins (currency earned via collecting 100 rings or completing missions that can be used to purchase artwork, songs, and videos), so unlocking Super/Hyper Sonic is much, much easier to pull off in one playthrough.All in all, not a bad way to experience the Sonic classics. I don't think it's worth full price but if you like the OG Sonic games and this game is on sale, I recommend it.

for sonic like the drop dash or the spin dash (previously an upgrade in sonic jam)various modes including boss rush and mission modenew cutscenes that play at the beginning and end of each game2. the extras are great. probably not as good as they could've been, i mean sonic mega collection on the gamecube had literal games as extras, but origins will suffice. my favourite is the music category. origins features remixes of sonic songs from other games like the smash bros games or other sonic media. 3. coins. coins are replaced with lives, some say this makes the game too easy, but my response would be "would you really want to play labyrinth zone or scrap brain with finite lives again?". coins mainly serve to buy new extras or to retry special stages, a lifesaver for me as the special stages in the older sonic games are frankly pretty terrible, especially sonic 2.=========================the games pretty good, buy it at least for me who wrote a 10 page essay on it.

_childDocuments_.review: I was very excited to see that there was an update that added Amy so I installed the game and then... I found out that I have to buy a "Plus Expansion pack" dlc... but wait a minute, I bought the Deluxe edition for 200 PLN (currency in Poland) and now I have to pay another 50 PLN. So ok I guess... even during the purchase steam warned me that there are items that I already own (I ques it was music and something else from Deluxe edition). Oh well.. so I am paying double it seems.I finished Amy playthrough in Sonic and Knuckles 3. I am not very happy after that playthrough. I was thinking that they might give Amy some interesting story there but it seems that it is a copy paste from Tails story.  Amy is like Sonic but instead of a jump spin dash she has a "hammer run". During that run you have a constant speed despite the terrain. Amy cannot use barriers abilities but instead she has a "hammer spin", which is very similar to Sonic jump ability but with a wider range. Amy can go Super Saiyan but only when she has all super emeralds (just like Tails). During that form she can throw hammers at enemies and of course have all abilities that other super forms have.  To be quite honest I was hoping to have some kind of different play style for Amy. In Sonic Advance (GBA) Amy was playable and required a different approach to the levels. I would love to see something similar here but oh well...It is nice to have access to the game gear games but I think those should be included in base game, or at least in "DELUXE" edition.To sum it up, I cannot recommend this game or its expansion. They tricked me into buying the Deluxe edition on release and now they want even more money... I can see that next year we will have something like "Sonic Origins Plus plus" because they will add Knuckles chaotix and then once again I will have to buy a package that has all previous items for a full price.I will now be careful with buying Sonic Superstars because I have a feeling that they will pull off something similar to Sonic Origins.

_childDocuments_.review: While it's nice to have all these games in 1 collection, it's not hard to organise a ROM folder either. It's great we finally got the 2013 remasters on all platforms, and a remaster for Sonic 3. But it's not worth the asking price. These games are free on mobile, $3 CAD to remove ads, and CD was like $5 before it was delisted just for this collection. In theory it should be at most $20, but it's double that. Where's that extra value coming from? The JPEGs and MP3s you can easily find on the internet? The missions are neat, but that's not $20 worth of content either. Is this value meant to come from the 3D islands? Well you need to cough up another $10 to zoom in on them, so maybe so. Maybe the main menu is worth $30, at least according to Sega.Pricing nonsense aside, one of my other biggest gripes is classic mode. Because it's not classic. Sega's idea of a classic mode is just that you can't drop dash and you play with lives instead of having coins. But the spindash is in Sonic 1, when it sure wasn't on the Genesis. Sonic 2 uses 3D models for the special stages, which is a very nice QoL change, but not classic. And while this is getting very nitpicky, Sonic CD originally had a camera that would pan in front of you so you could see ahead of you, a very nice change for such a chaotic game. 2011 removed this because you could see ahead of you just fine with a 16:9 ratio. But because of Sega's laziness in Origins, now when you play CD in 4:3 the camera doesn't pan. Making it harder than the original.Coins also suffer the same issue Sonic Colours Ultimate did with it's Park Tokens, and that's that they're useless after you buy all the unlockables. Sure you can still use them to retry special stages, but if you've already unlocked everything then you're probably too good to fail the special stages. So they start to stockpile very quick.The Sonic 3 remaster is good. It's unfortunate they couldn't use the original music, but that's the fun part of legal issues. I don't blame Headcannon for any of the issues with Origins. It's all on Sega.Amy is also very janky, and she was clearly made for Mania and she got cut because her sprites use 24 colours, rather than 16 like what the Genesis could actually handle. Some extra Game Gear ROMs don't make this worth *another* $10,Mods are the only thing worth getting this game for, and at the time of writing there isn't really much good mods that aren't just mediocre sprite swaps, or fixing bugs.So I either recommend getting an emulator and some ROMs and ROM hacks, or the RSDK decompilations and mods for those.

_childDocuments_.review: So the game has Denova; blah, blah, yes it's unneeded... but considering I played for 6 hours and never had a instance of slowdown, or stutter; I'd say it's not very threatening, unless you have a ♥♥♥♥ PC.The games are all great, the extra content is fun to unlock. Don't listen to people insisting it's a cheap cash grab. If you're new to Sonic, and wanna see what all the excitement is about; Anniversary Mode is great for easing newer players in; and Classic Mode allows the people who prefer a challenge can go with the Lives and only one try system on Special Stages.With that said and done... this is where the positivity stops. Because from here onwards, things get problematic. The games have a massive amount of new bugs introduced, which were never featured in any other version. Resulting in a strange collection of off, weird and strange occurances. It's because of this, that I recommend this game to newer players who just want to experience these games for the first time... but it's hard to recommend it to players who've played these games for years; as they will undeniably notice the weirdness.Edit: Sonic Origins Plus is a bit of an insult. The game on release was met with a lot of criticism for it's lack of being the best versions of these games (especially since they delisted the more mod friendly original releases), but in addition to that, the original felt a bit like it was falsely advertising new characters in the game (Knuckles in Sonic 1 was the only 'new function' unless you count Tails and Knuckles, or Knuckles and Tails modes). The addition of Amy Rose, was a feature most of us expected or wanted in the vanilla experience, but is now going to be paid DLC. Hopefully there will be a patch to fix the majority of the issues in this version alongside the DLC, or the game itself will begin to feel like the cheap cash grab people called it on release. I still recommend it... but only if you've never played the original games.

_childDocuments_.review: Sonic Origins is a very; polarizing title to say the least. Between it being announced nearly  before it had a release date was quite an interesting move and the  and then on launch; it came out the Headcanon team came out and said they didn’t turn in what was released and weren’t too happy about it. Origins really didn’t have a lot going for it for existing fans; however what this collection was made for and marketed towards, parents who watched the Sonic Movie with their kids and wanted a way to replay classic games from their childhood; Origin was and kinda is perfect for that niche.I’ll cut to the chase; Sonic Origins is a good value in two situations; if you have a Steam Deck or just hate “setting up” emulators or fan ports of these games. However this only effects PC; if you’re on console this is a great value for a game; since there isn’t really any options. So lets talk about like; the game itself now right?Sonic Origins is a collection of 4 Genesis titles (+12  Game Gear games with Plus), under the Retro Engine, developed by Christian Whitehead, a legend in the Sonic space who needs no introduction; they’re all upgraded with full widescreen support in the Anniversary mode or you can keep the og 4:3 in Classic mode; “””new””” playable characters (Amy with Plus) and last but not least the new Story mode that was added to play all 4 games back-to-back in story order. Sonic Origins also comes with tons and tons of goodies that you can unlock with coins you find through out the game and honestly for new and old Sonic fans; it’s always nice seeing them bundle in concept art, music tracks, etc. While it isn’t as cool as Generations was; it’s still a neat touch for them to include  of 90s Sonic art and even new Classic Sonic art.With brand new animated cut-scenes to boot they are by far one of the best parts of this game; they are just usually eye candy to look at, and the Sonic CD intro was upscaled but it looks nice; sure as hell way better than what ever they did to Persona 3 Portables upscaling… sheesh.They all look really nice! I mean to be fair they didn’t change much in this port with the Mobile ports that came out before looked the exact same since they’re using the same engine; but I will say; the anti-aliasing enabled in game can look really weird? Not bad; just strange. They all control as you would expect; nothing really new here other than in all 4 games Sonic now has the Drop Dash. Like it or not it’s here to stay and it doesn’t seem it’s going away anytime soon. Sonic 3 doesn’t benefit that much from it since it was planned to be in it originally anyways, so it feels natural to put back in, Sonic 1 gets a much needed speed up with it, and Sonic 2 just feels even better with how already fast that game is. However; this and I’m not trying to oversell this to you; it  CD apart; since you can just find a semi-flat space in any level and just drop dash back and forth all challenge of finding a spot to Time Travel is just gone; while this makes the game better for a lot of people since it’s even less maze like and faster some people don’t like it and want to be able to disable it (you cannot in any of the games; either in Anniversary or Classic mode.)  but; alas we live in a post-Sonic Mania world and it’s effects will be here forever.Sonic Origins big improvement in the gameplay department I think benefits ‘em all; is the fact you can retry special stages using the coins you collect. In the case of Sonic 2 which stages I personally despise this was a life changing feature to make that game a lot more enjoyable getting all the chaos emeralds; so very very good move devs.By far the biggest downgrade and just lame-o feature is that Sonic 1, CD, and 2 are downgraded to the original Genesis versions; the biggest omission from all of them are multiple save files in each of em; so you can save progress between characters; since in Origins if you wanna change characters and mess around with someone else; you better be ready to restart the entire game! Only Sonic 3 has kept it’s save data system since it’s just already included in the game.As for the 100%? It’s not really that hard. The achievements for the most part are piss easy and you’ll get them as you play and beat each game; the only parts that suck are some of the challenges just kinda are not that fun and will take a lot of grind to get good at and beat the gimmick they’re hittin you with; and getting all the collectibles is something you’ll do while playing the games and doing all the missions.Honestly? The whole part that this collection is good and brings native widescreen and cool collectibles to the table is why it kinda hurts me to not recommend it; at least for PC, if you’re on console it’s a no brainer purchase if you’re a Sonic Fan; but since we’re here on Steam; yeah, it’s just not worth it to the other options you have on a computer, but if you want the easiest, no mods, cross saves for you Steam Deck already set up, to play all the classic Sonic games it really is a no brainer purchase; but I’d recommend saving your dollars for a better Sonic game.  Overall, I just; can’t recommend this for someone that is looking to get the best bang for their buck. If you’re a 100% nerd like me; Sonic 3 A.I.R has tons of achievements; just go for those instead of this.
