_childDocuments_.review: I've been a Sonic the Hedgehog fan ever since the first game released on the Sega Genesis back in the early nineties. I have fond memories of getting Sonic 2 for my birthday one year, and I also remember buying the rental copy of Sonic & Knuckles from my local mom & pop video store. I have a lot of fond memories of Sonic and this collection is an enjoyable way to relive those parts of my youth.There have been numerous Sonic compilations released over the years so what makes Sonic Origins different from the rest? For starters Sonic CD is included here which a lot of those early bundles lacked. There's also a Story Mode where you can start with Sonic 1 and play all of the games through in their canonical order complete with newly animated cutscenes tying each of the games together. Starting with Sonic 1 and going all the way through Sonic 3 & Knuckles collecting all the Chaos Emeralds as you go makes for a great challenge.The games are all in widescreen and built from the engines used by Headcannon for their ports of Sonic 1 and 2. Headcannon was not directly involved with the production of this compilation but their technology was used in Sonic 3 & Knuckles for pathfinding and other technical gobbledygook. You're getting a solid collection of Sonic's classic hits presented in possibly their most definitive editions.There have been some bad things said about the music in Sonic 3 & Knuckles, namely regarding the "Michael Jackson tracks" that had to be removed from the game for licensing reasons. In their place are the original compositions heard in the early prototypes for Sonic 3. They aren't done with a Genesis soundfont however so they sound a bit muddied. I personally would have preferred they use the Genesis originals instead of these weird covers but I'm certain there's a mod that fixes this. There's probably even a mod that puts the Jackson tracks back in the game!My favorite thing about Sonic Origins is the inclusion of the challenges for each of the games. Things like collecting X number of rings or beating a checkpoint within a certain time limit. It provides a nice bonus scenario mode that tests your skills at the classic Sonic games. For all the years I've been playing these games I was still thrown a couple of curveballs that took me numerous tries.Overall Sonic Origins is in my opinion a solid collection of games. Perhaps the asking price is a little steep, but that's nothing a Steam sale can't fix. Definitely mark this one for checking out.

_childDocuments_.review: It's just an ok collection. It's worth the money to have an official way to play these games in a modern format.- First ever remake of Sonic 3 & Knuckles- 4 important games from Sonic's past, ranging from just ok to the best of the best.- Drop Dash was added to each game- Sonic CD's original intro and outros are accounted for and look great- Both Sonic CD OST's are readily available- Widescreen support- Mission Mode provides a nice bite sized challenge- A few of Sonic 3's music tracks were replaced due to copyright issues. The new (or rather, old) music in use here isn't bad, but the instrumentation could've used some work.- Denuvo Anti-Tamper- Sonic CD is still the same cramped game it's always been- Sonic 1 and 2 lock control of your character after a jump from a spindash or dropdash- Sonic 1 and 2's OST was not carried over from the superior Mobile versions- Story Mode offers little reason to play it, as it contains no different content from playing each game seperately. There is also no level select after completing it.- Without mods, the game looks blurry- The DLC is nonsense (I have to pay to pan the camera around the islands? Really?)- Quite a few bugs that are fairly easy to notice.- No online multiplayer support for Sonic 2 or 3- There's not really any difference between S1,2, and CD here and the ones that are on mobile.If you're looking for a more robust way to play these titles, seek out Sonic 1 Forever, Sonic 2 Absolute, Sonic CD Restored, and Sonic 3 AIR, all of which are fanmade versions of these games that contain more quality of life improvements over what's offered in Origins. That said, Origins is still a fairly good way to experience these games and I'm glad it exists.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to say that I did not receive any crashes or performance issues like many others have said. The game ran perfectly fine for me, but when taking a look at task manager I can definitely tell that this game absolutely needs to be optimized.Starting with the positives, I'm a massive fan of the QoL changes. Lives are incredibly outdated and I love being able to play through these games without worrying about having to go all the way back to the beginning of the stage if I die. I'm also thrilled the Drop Dash is here from Mania and that it seems to be getting adopted as a mainstay in Classic Sonic's move set. It really helps keep the pace of the game up. This is also the first time we're getting Sonic 1, 2 and 3&K officially in widescreen. The version of Sonic 2 is also the newer one with the cut zone, previously only available on mobile. I haven't played much of them yet, but I really enjoy the mission mode. I loved that kinda stuff in the Mega Man Legacy Collections and I'm really happy we get something like that here.Unfortunately, the games aren't presented as cleanly as one might expect. There are complaints that the games are "blurry", which I don't think is necessarily the case. I was messing around with the settings and turned off VSync and turned on Anti-aliasing, which made the game SUPER blurry. But the games themselves, playing the game with the default settings, look pretty much like the Genesis games extended into widescreen. They don't really feel HD at all and it's unfortunate that it lacks the crispness I would have expected from a $40 release of games that have already been remastered before. Also, I swear that all of the sound in Sonic 3&K sounds muffled compared to the other games. Maybe it's just me. My ears got used to it.In the end, it's fine. I played through story mode. Knuckles isn't playable in CD for whatever reason, but I'm not a CD fan so that doesn't bother me too bad. None of the unlockables really matter. The new tracks for Sonic 3 are mid. Ice Cap Zone in particular feels drastically different without the original music. Wish they were able to get the rights or whatever, but it is what it is. The games themselves are still pretty solid. Probably not worth the price, especially if you already own the games here.Christian Whitehead absolutely should have been in charge of this project and it should have been $10-$15 cheaper. It is a bit of a disappointing collection, but the games themselves are still very good which is why I'm recommending it. At sale price.ORIGINS PLUS UPDATE:With the release of Origins Plus, the game has dropped in price, released a new character, and emulations of the Game Gear games are available. Amy plays fine. She's basically Sonic with a weaker drop dash and better instashield. The Game Gear games have never been great, but they're nice to have and speaking from experience Tails Adventure is a real gem. As a Deluxe edition owner, I kinda feel like I got screwed because of the pricing. Should have been free, but I can recommend Origins Plus even more now because of the cheaper price and extra content.

_childDocuments_.review: Sigh...After Mania was such a smash hit, I was hoping for Origins to be an utter slam dunk as well. I had a lot of hype going into this. The CW versions of Sonic 1 and 2 on PC, finally. Sonic 3 getting the same treatment FINALLY after Whitehead was denied doing so a decade ago, fancy new intro/outro animations for every single game to provide context for each game's story and a bunch of neat little extras, such as concept art, animatics, extra songs, etc.All of that sounded great, even if I think the price for it is way, way too steep for games that are nearing 3 decades in age. But where does it crumble apart? Behind the scenes is where it crumbles apart.Playing any game in Origins, you can immediately tell corners were cut. The physics, while remarkably close to the original games, still feel slightly off. For example, in Sonic 3's Launch Base Zone, you can't enter the pods if you're standing right next to them because your jump is just ever slightly too high. In Sonic 2, the Aquatic Ruin boss fight becomes weirdly difficult due to the aspect ratio, making it feel more like an oversight. In Sonic 1's Green Hill Zone boss fight, you can effectively cheese the boss by standing under the platforms (which wasn't possible in the original, you still had to dodge).The one thing that gets me though, is the music. Yes, I'm partially talking about the songs in Sonic 3, but I just mean the quality of the songs overall. Again, launching any game aside from CD, you can just hear the compression and crunch of every song. The quality of the songs is astoundingly low quality. It feels like they're using heavily compressed 128 kbps YouTube rips for every single song, and that's genuinely a shame. You don't need to be an audiophile either to hear the low quality, you can just immediately notice it as soon as it transitions from the Origins menu to the game.And of course, Sonic 3's changed music. Contrary to what others may think, I don't hate the replaced tracks. And if you don't know - they replaced the songs with compositions from Sonic 3's November 1993 prototype. Except, for some reason, they based the songs off of the MIDI compositions from the S&K collection on 1997. Zones like Ice Cap and Launch Base sound fine, if anything I think they genuinely recomposed the 1993 proto. ver of Ice Cap and cleaned it up, and it sounds legitimately wonderful, but Carnival Night Zone...god, it sounds awful.And then Sonic 3's Super Sonic theme they added. It's...awful. It sounds like something ripped out of Sonic 4. The baffling bit? They included the Unused Theme in the game's Museum Mode for Sonic 3's soundtrack. Why...couldn't they just...use that? It's just baffling. They can include it in the collection but apparently not use it in the game?I don't wanna keep going. Sonic Origins is a disappointment. I pre-ordered the Digital Deluxe edition by selling my CS:GO knife to buy it, and honestly - I kinda want my knife back now. The animation work done here is incredible and the extras they gave in the game are nice, but none of it makes up for what feels like shoddy ports of mobile games, poor audio quality and just overall lack of polish.I read some behind the scenes stuff on Origins' development, including  and it just saddens me how Sega continues to mistreat its developers and its beloved properties.Shame on you, Sega. Shame on you.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been a huge Sonic fan for two decades now and this collection is perfect. I'll be playing this until Sonic Frontiers comes out. _childDocuments_.review: Honestly, this is just proving that SEGA, after the success of Mania, is just going to start rushing and milking Classic Sonic games now. They've gotten so much flack in the past for their glitchy and rushed 3D games, it seems they'd rather take their time with those games, as seen with Sonic Frontiers being released 5 years later. If they want to get out Sonic games yearly now, it seems they're gonna basically use Blind Squirrel for shoddy remasters (unless Blind Squirrel can get their crap together) and Headcannon for Classic games, with random spin-offs in the off years, and, of course, the mainline 3D games every 4-5 years or so. I haven't even talked about my issues with the game itself and we're already off to a bad start.Back in May 2021, during the Sonic Central, it was announced that they were remastering the first 4/5 (Sonic & Knuckles wasn't announced to be by itself or part of Sonic 3 then), and I met it with a groan (not literally, I was in school and I didn't want to make a scene about a cartoon hedgehog). Don't get me wrong, these aren't bad games, heck, they're some of the best Sonic games out there (not Sonic 1), but I've never been as big for the 2D games as I've been for the 3D games, but I thought they looked good, so I was still a little excited. After that, radio silence for 11 months. Only info we got was that Sonic 3 and Knuckles was going to be wide-screen, which was a no-brainer anyways. Still, I hoped that the game would be good, and that we'd get more games than first shown.Weeks after watching the second Sonic movie with friends, (9/10 movie, if I must add) I began to think about the upcoming Sonic games. Frontiers had 2 trailers, second one being in December 2021, yet Origins didn't even have a proper trailer yet. As I began to wonder for a few days, a trailer came out showing the game. I was excited from what it showed us, and was looking forward to getting the game.Now, we encounter our first issue: price. How much would you pay for 4 remastered Genesis games, including 3 games which were free on mobile? I would personally pay around $20-30, but SEGA let greed go to their heads, and set the price at $40. Plus $5 DLC which should've been part of the main game. Then the next problem, delisting the other versions of these games on Steam. Why? Is it because they didn't want people to get confused? Or is it something more? Is it because you could buy those 4 games for $20 with those other versions? Possibly, but we won't know until someone says something. Then more silence, another trailer at Sonic Central 2022, then they announced they were changing Sonic 3 music (we'll get to that) and then the game came out. And from the get-go, this game was a dumpster fire.Never have I seen a game this divisive in the Sonic fan base. As long as I've been a Sonic fan, opinions have mostly been shared within the fan base: Sonic Mania is a godsend, Sonic Forces is a lazy rushed mess, Sonic 06 is a fundamentally good game ruined by glitches and Sonic's story, and Sonic Adventure 2 is the perfect Sonic game. But this game, I have seen so many fight about this game's quality, it makes Frontiers's discourse look civil. My take: I like Frontiers, I don't like Origins.Let's start with this: these games aren't bad, I mean, 1, 2, and CD are the Taxman ports, of course they're not bad. 3&K was remastered by Headcannon, one of the developers of Sonic Mania. These are all really good games at their core (yes, even CD, I don't think you guys know how to play the game right). They added the drop dash from Mania, added a mission mode, and the main menu has some really cool references to other games like Sonic Jam and Spinball. Museum is cool too, and gives you a lot of never before seen content. Plus there are some really cool cutscenes made by Tyson Hesse for this game exclusively.Positives end here, be warned if you don't like criticism.And to start it off, holy crap, this game is a buggy mess. Holy crap I've seen so many bugs from this game, and mainly from Sonic 3 & Knuckles. I've clipped through walls, been teleported to another position (Angel Island Act 1), seen items bug out, and plenty of other problems. People have also been having a weird bug with Sonic 2 Hidden Palace's boss just not going away after being defeated. I've even seen someone literally skip from Mushroom Hill to Hidden Palace. Sure it's a cool speedrun strat, but it's proving that they don't care about checking for bugs, they just wanted the games to get out as soon as possible. Point 2: Denuvo. End of statement.Then there's a lot of problems with each of these games they didn't fix. Sonic 1 has janky physics that don't work well with the drop dash. Sonic CD doesn't have Knuckles, even though he's in all the other games. Drop dash in Sonic CD makes time travelling too easy and broken. Sonic 2's Tails system is broken, as Tails makes the sound unbearable. Sonic 3 and Knuckles's insta-shield works really weird with the drop dash, making the latter harder to use. The physics of the game feel way off and too fast at certain points. Then they also changed a lot of the songs. Remember Ice Cap, one of the most iconic Sonic songs? They changed it's theme, because copyright. You see, back in 1993, when developing the game, they got Michael Jackson and Brad Buxer to help make some music for this game, which was great because it made such an iconic soundtrack, but also makes it hard for SEGA to rerelease Sonic 3 nowadays. For this game, they decided to get Jun Senoue to remaster some of the songs from the prototype version of Sonic 3. This also applies to Launch Base and Carnival Night, as well as some random songs as well. Don't get me wrong, these aren't bad songs, heck I like the new Super Sonic theme for Sonic 3 & Knuckles, but these changes didn't need to happenThen of course is the crappy DLC that should've been in the main game, and probably were until SEGA stripped it out to sell as DLC because that's something they would honestly do. Also, the blatant lies SEGA made in trailers advertising that new characters would be in this game (there isn't any new characters, unless you count the combo of Knuckles and Tails as a new character, and who does?). I would at least understand if they ported Mighty and Ray from Mania over to this game. What about the Chaotix, since they were in Knuckles Chaotix? But they don't do any of that. Heck, I would just take a sprite changed Sonic to Metal Sonic, I doubt that would be too hard for Sonic Team to do.Here's some of my personal nitpicks: You can't choose which Sonic sprite to use in each game. You can't choose which Sonic ability you want for each game. Sonic can still spindash in Sonic 1 Classic Mode, even though the spindash didn't exist yet. You can't play as Sonic and Tails in Sonic 1 even though you could in the mobile version. The settings menu is hidden away in the museum for no reason. Many songs in the sound test are mixed up, specifically Knuckles Chaotix. The animated cutscenes made by Tyson Hesse are only for the good endings and don't make sense if you got the bad ending. Game looks very blurry for no reason.There's so many other problems I have with this game, but I can't even state every issue with it. One of the biggest problems with this collection is that for someone like me, who has all of the Classic games in the first place, there isn't anything to entice me in this collection. Mission mode is fine and all, but that's the extent of this. If you've never played these games before, or you want this collection for nostalgia, then sure, go ahead and get them. I'm not your boss, do what you want with your life. The whole point of this review is to state that SEGA needs to get their acts together and stop rushing stuff out for the heck of getting it out faster, but I'm honestly not sure how they haven't gotten this message yet.

_childDocuments_.review: This collection is absolute dogsh*t, play the de-compilations or the fan-made ports.-The animations were pointless and honestly a marketing scam (the opening cinematic and trailer marketed it as in-between zones, but it's only when launching the specific game and beating the game, that's it).-These games are unchanged from the mobile ports besides new visual/gameplay bugs that weren't in the remasters (Sonic clipping on-top of Tails' sprite when flying underwater, Tails behind Sonic in Blue Spheres does not jump on the Yellow Spheres, random stutters, etc).-There is no Time Attack despite the mobile ports having them.-The Toei animated cutscenes are upscaled and look beautiful, but the ending is sped-up like it was on Sonic Gems Collection on the GameCube/PS2, a collection that released back in 2005, it is 2022, the 2011 remaster had the correct speed with the sound effects from the JP audio.-Speaking of CD, the audio clips from Sonic and Amy are both gone, now they just either make the Time Stone sfx, or in Amy's case, pure silence, no yelp or giggle.-The bugs from the 2013 Sonic 1 and 2 ports are still present, as well as CD's mobile bugs despite being fixed on the PC/Console releases, AND this is all within a 10 year time span.-Classic mode isn't the original Genesis roms (the ones that got de-listed) DESPITE the game clearly giving the description "Play the game in its original form in 4:3", it's the same game on the Retro engine, but with a border and a life system, which leads to the next issue below.-THERE IS NO OPTION TO TOGGLE LIVES IN WIDESCREEN, CRASH BANDICOOT 4 LETS YOU DO THIS AND ITS A BRAND NEW GAME!!!!!!! Atleast the Mega Man Legacy Collections (35 USD for two seperate packages combined totaling into 10 games) lacked as many problems despite emulating more games across multiple platforms (NES, SNES, PS1, PS3/X360/Wii).I am praying Sonic Frontiers turns out well, because if not I am done with buying games from this cursed franchise. I am okay with sticking to other forms of media.5/10, do better SEGA. P.S. we shouldn't have to rely on the modding communities to fix your broken games.

_childDocuments_.review: As things are, I can't recommend this collection. I've spent way over 2 hours so I'm unable to get a refund, but it's taken me the whole game to reach Sonic & Knuckles only to discover there's a save corruption bug. The first time, I had no idea what had happened, and I thought I'd lost all of the progress made. Thankfully, I'd been backing up my saves to OneDrive due to using the mod manager, and as Cloud Saving was disabled, I was transferring my progress between my PC and laptop manually. OneDrive makes its own backups, so luckily I was able to retrieve one at the end of Sonic 3. Problem is, as soon as you enter Sonic & Knuckles, the game saves, you quit, and once you attempt to load it back up, you're greeted with an error saying there's a problem with the save. In other words - corrupted. It's good I can go back and keep the progress I've made before that happens, but it's still incredibly poor, and God only knows how this slipped through QA.A few others have run into this problem as well and despite reporting bugs to Sega Support, it's anyone's guess if any of the issues will get fixed. :( Because of this save corruption, I'm unable to finish the game, so I feel like it hasn't been money well spent! I've also discovered bugs that shouldn't even be in the games, and they certainly weren't in the original Mega Drive/Genesis versions either! Thank God I own the originals...Apart from this issue, I'm fairly happy with the collection. I certainly think much more could have been added though. And some things shouldn't be the way they are. I've yet to play the Game Gear titles, but even with the inclusion of Amy and Knuckles in Sonic CD, so many new challenges and achievements could have been added. Such wasted potential... Therefore, I don't see the point in going through the games as the other characters. Not any time soon anyway. Perhaps if there were achievements for playing as them...The missions are a nice little diversion, but there are a few that are frustrating and yet have a 3-4 star rating in difficulty when they should be 5! Others feel too simple. Likewise with some of the unlockables - there's some nice stuff there, but I feel the Premium videos could have been much better. The majority consist of test/line-drawing/storyboard animations of the cinematics. Would have been cool to have had some behind-the-scenes documentaries instead.And yes, there's also the issue with the original Sonic 3 music being absent. Thank God for mods, is all I can say! It's ridiculous though that we have to rely on modders and the fan community to fix many of the issues present! Story mode is cool with the inclusion of the new cinematics and how you'll go through each game one after the other. Anniversary modes are essentially the mobile remakes, which can be loaded onto PC for free anyway, so it feels rather cheeky to basically charge for them in this collection.Unless the game is patched and the save corruption bug is fixed, this review will be sitting with a negative rating permanently.

_childDocuments_.review: Sonic Origins is quite a mixed bag of a product, but this collection does more harm than good.To start on the more positive side, the presentation is quite good with each game being represented on their own respective island on the main menu, which is pretty cute. The animated cutscenes produced by Tyson Hesse are outstanding, as well. As for the games included: each version of every game is... good enough, for the most part. Native widescreen support along with unlimited lives are natural additions to help sharpen the experiences of first-time players (like myself) and returning ones.Unfortunately, that's the best I can say about the package as a whole, as the rest of it is quite underwhelming.  There isn't much else to the collection besides that, outside of the museum, which does provide very engaging development artwork, but can otherwise be found online. The Mission Mode is a pathetic addition to the game that hardly contributes anything nor takes advantage of what each game has to offer and instead serves as nothing more than just another game mode. The worst offender for me was the performance: the game simply refused to launch properly most of time and would freeze up to several minutes in other instances.If you'd like to experience Sonic's origins, it'd be best to do so through other methods, as there exist decompilations of each game online that provide way more customizability. This collection simply doesn't do enough that previous releases have.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game as a good excuse to replay the classic Sonic games with some quality of life enhancements. Needless to say it was that HOWEVER, it was not without its fair share of issues. I grew up playing these Sonic games and they will always be a timeless classic and have a place in my heart. The game features 4 games, Sonic 1, 2, 3, and CD. It offers 2 different ways to play the game, classic mode in the original 4:3 aspect or anniversary mode which is in the new wide screen 16:9 aspect and gives the player infinite lives. The anniversary mode gives us new cutscenes as well beautifully animated by Powerhouse Animation Studios and the long time sonic artist Tyson Hesse. As for the game play itself it is the classic games but given enhancements the original games didn't have. Sonic 1 lets you Spindash and use characters like Tails and Knuckles, Sonic 2 lets you fly as Tails unlike the original Sonic 2, and Sonic 3 is in wide screen like never before. Issues I've had with the game range from random crashes or performance issues. Another major issue is in Sonic CD you cannot play as Knuckles. This does not compliment how exploration based Sonic CD is and how explory of a character knuckles is. Another issue that while out of SEGAS control is still an issue is 3 stages from Sonic 3 has music replaced that is not the best sounding. While these issues are/were present, this is still a solid collection. I definitely would refer this to someone if they have never played the classic Sonic games. While the $40 price tag might drive people away, I think with how much things we're improved and added, it seems to be worth it. These games are so replayable and I find myself coming back to them on the regular.

The nostalgia is very high and its good to check all the secrets and extra content they added. I wish the challenges were more creative and that they added more extra content like in old sonic game collections. Adding the other games from that era shouldn't have been too difficult and I guess they limited themselves because of time limits or maybe a "narrative" reasons. The "story mode" has some good animations but everything just left me wanting for more. Sometimes I wish game design was better paid so creatives could dive full in into making remakes or remakes, but that often leads to feature creep and on the other side you get publishers pushing down on game creativity due to weird timelines.As a base its a good game, but thats only because the games it features are able to stand on their own. The idea hits the mark but doesn't keep running with it.

_childDocuments_.review: As a sonic fan for most of my life, I can say this collection is generally pretty great.  Has nice presentation, and a nice amount of collectables and old art from back in the day.No extremely noticeable input lag or performance issues in any of the games they all play fine.  The animated intros and outros are an excellent touch and I really like them.  They are very well done and seem to capture the tone and look of the games very well. Once you install the mod to remove the blur they used to filter the sprites, and substitute it for either the mods options, or reshade filters, the games do look amazing in 4k with the proper filters applied.Only real complaint I have is that the main hub for the game seems to lag pretty bad when transitioning from one thing to the next, and there is a constant fps dip while navigating menus. _childDocuments_.review: Sonic Origins is one of those collections that is very polarizing. For a lot of people, like myself, enjoy this collection because it fixes problems for all of the games (Consistent frame rate for Sonic 2's special stages, the infamous spike glitch from Sonic 1, and some of the hitbox issues from Sonic CD and 3&K), and are also happy to finally get a release of Sonic 3 & Knuckles after so many years of being the definition of a music licensing nightmare. For others, they absolutely hate the collection for changing the music for Sonic 3&Knuckles (even though the needed to do it in order to release this collection at all) and making the games easier by giving a retry function for the special stages (though they agree that it makes Sonic 2's special stages much easier), as well as the ability to turn off lives, and the lack of including Sonic 3D Blast, Dr. Robotnik's Mean Bean Machine, Knuckle's Chaotix, and Sonic Spinball (Though the music from those games are DLC). I can agree that I wish those games were included, but I also understand that they would have to rebuild those games in Christian Whitehead's Retro Engine which would take longer (Spinball and Mean Bean could be easy, the other 2 would need more time). I also like the fact that they added the ability to play without the lives counter. It was just an archaic game mechanic that added artificial difficulty. The ability to retry special stages is also really helpful, especially Sonic 2 with the god awful half pipe. All in all, I can recommend this to people who want to try Sonic 1-3&K. It might not be what purists call the "True Classic Sonic Experience", but it certainly gives more people of various skill levels the ability to experience the little blue hedgehog's roots.

_childDocuments_.review: I've always been a fan of the classic sonic games for multiple reasons. Each game creates a fun adventure with super fast speed and spin dash abilities. What's more they have allowed players to turn super form in any level in the games, with or without sound test or stage select. Also, the games have great music playing within the backgrounds. In addition, the special and bonus stages create mini-games for the players during the adventure, such as slot machines and labyrinth mazes. Furthermore, Sonic CD has incredible time-travel abilities that allow you to literally go to the past and create an amazing future with JP or US soundtracks. Additionally, Anniversary mode allows new players to play with INFINITE LIVES, RETRIES on the SPECIAL STAGES, in widescreen HD. Moreover, Classic mode provides a nostalgic feeling of challenging game-play with limited lives, continues, and opportunities. Plus, the game gear classics create a new 8-bit experience to players who never used a Game Gear before, including racing, pinball, and puzzle games. Finally, Sonic 3&K provides both Hyper forms and Blue Sphere challenges that make the effort worth it. I've always enjoyed the sonic classics, and I hope they will continue bringing more challenges as I take on each story in anniversary, classic, and mirror mode.

_childDocuments_.review: This one really hurts, especially as a long-time fan of the classic Sonic title, and as someone who's been wanting the remastered versions of these games on modern platforms for a decade now. While it's significantly better than the dumpster fire of Sonic Colors Ultimate, this collection is the definition of a mixed bag, and I really can't recommend it, especially at $40.It's not all bad: the new cutscenes are beautiful and charming. Some of the new modes are fun. The addition of the coins to restart Special Stages is a nice quality-of-life tweak along with the unlimited lives. And there are many great additions to Sonic 3 specifically, thanks to the efforts of Headcannon's dev team. At the core these are the same beloved games from the 90s.But for every pro in Sonic Origins, there are at least 10 cons. There are so many downgrades from the previous Retro Engine releases of these games, and Sonic 3 unfortunately was not finished in time. Granted, this has nothing to do with the team; there were very clearly a victim of Sega's crunch. (How this is still a problem after two decades is beyond me.) Here's just a couple of the problems:- Confusingly laid-out menus making navigation a chore. (Sonic CD's music is set to the US soundtrack by default and you need to go into the CD menu to switch it back, for instance)- Buggy implementation of the Drop Dash in Sonic 1/2- Remastered music from previous Retro versions is gone- Misleading classic mode that is just a cropped version of the anniversary versions with lives enabled instead of the actual ROM files- Numerous bugs and glitches, especially at launch. (While Tails's AI in Sonic 2 and some of the mislabeled music in the gallery was fixed, most bugs still remain.) None are game-breaking, but there's enough to become a huge annoyance, especially in Sonic 3's case- Lack of substantial bonus content in the gallery. There's a few new things, but most have already been released in other ways- Texture filtering that cannot be turned off- Need I even mention the hilariously awful replacement zone and Super Sonic music in Sonic 3?This was the easiest slam-dunk possible, and yet it still ended up like this. While I think it's a perfectly solid way to play these games on consoles (if you can find it on a good sale), on PC this collection is redundant, especially with the unnecessary inclusion of Denuvo that Sega loves to shove into their games. And with the old versions of these games now delisted, this is what you're stuck with in terms of "legal" means of playing these games. As much as I'd love to judge this collection on its own merits, the Retro Engine decompilations and Sonic 3 AIR are *much* better options to play the classic Sonic titles now on Windows. You can easily add the new additions from Origins, restore Sonic 3's music, and get so many more QoL tweaks that way, with no invasive DRM.I'm posting this review now with the recent announcement of Sonic Origins Plus which, while having some great additions, REALLY should've been in the base game. Amy really should've been there before, and locking Knuckles in Sonic CD behind DLC is an incredibly scummy move. Not to mention that they're only adding in the Game Gear titles (which you can easily restore into Sonic Adventure DX through the mod installer), when they could easily add in games that have never been re-released like Knuckles' Chaotix or the Saturn version of Sonic 3D Blast. Unless they go back and fix all the problems above and more, this won't be enough to save the collection.Man, these games deserved so much better...

_childDocuments_.review: This game saved my life.I am 42.My ex-wife and I have a daughter together, and adopted our son together. They are now both 4 years old.When we were going through our separation, I found myself lost and miserable. I was self destructive. I got so mad one day from everything spiraling out of my control that I punched some concrete in a moment of overwhelming emotion. That caused me to break my 5th metacarpal in my right hand... my working hand... my games hand.. the hand that I held and carried my children to bed with.. The hand I desperately needed to make sure I could continue to provide.After learning of the severity of my self-inflicted damage, I was borderline suicidal. Keep in mind that just a few months before this, I was the happiest man with no history of depression or anxiety. I have never had fits of rage, or been one to break down and cry, but I was in a low spot that just really buried me from being able to see the light on the other side.Having nothing better to do, I searched for a game I could play, ONE HANDED while I recovered. I somehow stumbled upon this game and read some of the reviews. I decided that it had to be worth a shot... I must admit, I didn't beat the game, or play nearly as long as some of you. In fact, I may have only played this game a day or two.. With that being said, after doing so, I had a new found joy and hope for life. I was able to put behind me the pain and suffering that had been cast over me. I was able to experience other peoples joy and happiness. I was able to see the fruits of my "labor". I relaxed for 5 ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ minutes to this music long enough to realize that I was going to be okay.After coming to that realization, I turned the game off, and I went back to work. It hurt my hand like hell but I was motivated. I stopped feeling so damn sorry for myself, and I became the father I needed to be in that moment, not the weak boy I was behaving as.Today, I am close friend with my kids mother. We don't fight, or argue, or say hurtful things to each other. We are parents, and friends.I now have 3 kids. My third child is, wait for it, ALSO 4 YEARS OLD. The woman I am with was going through a very similar situation at the time of my own separation, and we just stumbled in to each others life unexpectedly. We have been in a relationship for a year now, and are very happy together.Moral of the story, you never know what life holds in store for you, and if I would have given up when all the odds were stacked against me, I wouldn't be where I am today. _childDocuments_.review: *** Note: If you own this game, you need to install the Ultrafix mod. ***I was looking forward to this collection, but the execution is terrible. It has zero respect for the original games.Just looking at Sonic 1, they've changed a lot about how the game works. They included spin dash, even in "classic" mode. Spikes don't work the way they did in the original game. You can't hit Robotnik when he's entering the stage, you just pass through him. The hitboxes for various projectiles are different, right up to the electric balls in the final stage, so veteran players with muscle memory will die in places they wouldn't.These changes were all made intentionally to discreetly "improve" a classic game that these developers have no business modifying. They also delisted all their products that were selling the real version of the original games, so unless you purchased one of those games already, you can now only play this revisionist trash (unless you download a Genesis emulator and ROM for the original Sonic games).The changes they've made to these games show a complete lack of respect for the original work. Each game has a "classic mode" that describes itself as being the original classic game, but it's not true. They couldn't help but modify the original work and then pretend it's unchanged.The original Sonic established Sega as a brand, and it's the only reason they even have a company today. Yet they show it zero respect and make it clear they think they could have done it better, retroactively patching a game over 30 years later with elements of modern game design, even though the current developers had no hand in creating the original.If Sega thinks they can make a better Sonic game than the originals, then they should go do it: make a new game.Don't change the original games and pretend it's still the same game. And definitely don't bury all the real versions of the original games to force people to buy your new updated version. It's all so arrogant.tl;dr: If "classic mode" was the actual original game as advertised, I wouldn't have left a negative review. "Sonic 1 - Classic Mode" should be the same game that was on Genesis. No mechanical alterations. Any changes to the gameplay should obviously be optional and off by default. But they just couldn't help themselves.Edit: If you want this to be playable, look up the "Ultrafix" mod. It fixes every issue I found while trying the game out. I guess I don't need to refund now since the mod exists and I bought the game at 60% off. If you're set on getting this collection, then definitely wait until it's on sale, and make sure you get the Ultrafix mod.

_childDocuments_.review: I've never written a comprehensive Steam review for a game, but then again, I've never been so pissed off by a game, either.Sonic Origins is the biggest letdown imaginable. Before I get into that, though, let's talk about the good parts of the game. The new Anniversary Mode lets you play through all four games with infinite lives. It's pretty well-known that lives, as a mechanic, kind of suck. They're a holdover from the era of arcade games, made to squeeze money out of you back then and to squeeze playtime out of you on consoles. Lives are replaced with Coins, which you can use to retry Special Stages or unlock art/music/video content in the new Museum.The cutscenes before and after every game in Anniversary Mode are, likewise, really cool! They clearly had a lot of heart put into them. Tyson Hesse and Powerhouse knocked them out of the park.The new Mirror Mode lets you play each game in reverse, flipping the screen and changing the game from left-to-right to right-to-left. This is a cool new touch that mixes up the gameplay for veteran players. It's neat.The also-new Mission Mode throws you into courses with set objectives. This is essentially identical to Sonic Generations' missions - you have set objectives (time, rings, etc.) and you're ranked based on how well you complete those objectives. This is... fine.That's the end of the good part of Sonic Origins. Now for the bad.Sonic 1, Sonic CD, and Sonic 2 are almost entirely unchanged from their mobile ports (and Steam port, in CD's case), with a few exceptions that I'll get to later. If you bought and played these earlier ports, though, you might notice something strange about Sonic Origins - namely, at launch, Sonic 1 and 2 on mobile devices were both 3$ a pop, and Sonic CD on Steam was 5$ before it was delisted. Origins is . If you're being  generous and want to bump the other two games' prices up to match CD's  price S3&K similarly, this game should be 20$ maximum. This alone is ridiculous. On top of that, there's a confusing and predatory-feeling bit of DLC that gives you exactly two pieces of meaningful content - 100 Coins (seriously?) and access to harder missions in Mission Mode. Sega's really going out of their way to nickel and dime you on this one.Sega also did a lot of advertising relating to "new playable characters", which is a flat-out lie. Tails and Knuckles have been playable in Sonic 1 since 2013, and Tails has been in CD since 2011. They couldn't even bother adding Knuckles to CD here, which would've been the easiest "new character" to add... but the promotional material and in-game movies focusing on Amy makes me think  who they wanted people to assume was playable. of the aforementioned "few exceptions" to the unchanged ports made the games  overall. Sonic 1 features the addition of the Drop Dash, except you can't turn around in midair after using it and jumping, so you can't chain it the way you can in Mania. Sonic CD has had Sonic and Amy's single, half-second voice lines removed for... some reason; the Drop Dash was added here, too, and it works much closer to Mania's version.CD has also had its entire Steam achievement list nixed in favor of Origins's mediocre "Play the game! Time travel once! Beat Metal Sonic! Beat the game!" ... and that's . Normally, I'd call this a nitpick, but CD's Steam port from  had a better achievement list. Why, Sega. Why.Sonic 2 has Sonic 1's halfassed Drop Dash, as well as at least two minor level layout changes - one in Metropolis 3 that makes a set of spikes borderline unavoidable (seriously!), and one that breaks Wing Fortress's intro. Good job, Sega.Sonic 3 & Knuckles is the most tragic case of all here. Sega contracted Headcannon (of Sonic Mania and Sonic 1+2 Mobile fame) to develop the remaster, which sounds all well and good... until you read  about how Headcannon was treated during development.S3&K's good features include the Drop Dash ( implemented this time, likely since Headcannon actually knows how it ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ works), a bunch of additional rotation sprites for objects like the Marble Garden spinners and Carnival Night's barrels, and a few new flashy level transitions that add a lot of polish and heart to the game. Thanks, Headcannon.S3&K's  not present in the original game are numerous, to say the least. Its music hasn't been remastered at all; the tracks sound like low-quality playbacks of the Genesis tracks. It bears mentioning that this only stands out so much because the other three games  high-quality remastered tracks. The Special Stage music doesn't speed up to match Sonic's speed like it did in the original game, and the new Super Sonic theme is  to listen to, almost as bad as the original.Actually, none of the new music is good. I'm no Michael Jackson purist, either; I played Sonic 3 A.I.R. with all of the prototype tracks enabled, and they all sounded fantastic there. ; the tracks he wrote should've been arranged and programmed into the game by someone who's more familiar with Genesis sound synthesis. The tracks that made it into Origins are watered-down, inferior versions of the original, pre-MJ tracks.Miscellaneous annoying differences from the original S3&K include differing in-game physics (hold down when Marble Garden 1 starts and keep it held - the speed cap behaves differently so you fly into a wall, unlike in the original); the end of Act 1 signposts not falling in the same places, so they don't unearth monitors consistently anymore; a vine in Angel Island 2 forcing you to swing into spikes and take damage; an unnecessary vertical screen lock during Marble Garden 2's falling-ceiling section; and the Super transformation animation not halting you in midair, which cancels it in certain circumstances.I wanted to like this. Sonic 3, in particular, is one of my favorite games of all time; as it stands, though, I can't recommend this garbage fire of a "remaster" to anyone. Sega hasn't learned anything from their previous mistakes, and they've now stained Headcannon's reputation by forcing an unfinished product to meet an unneeded deadline. Mania was delayed on PC to add ♥♥♥♥♥♥ DRM back when it released - why couldn't Sega have done the same here to let Headcannon actually finish and polish their game?This is especially insulting given the runaway success of Sonic Mania. Sega didn't touch that game - they published it, sure, but Christian Whitehead, Headcannon, and PagodaWest were the actual . Sega themselves can't even handle rereleasing the ports previously released by Christian and Headcannon, let alone developing an actual ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Sonic game on their own, as evidenced by the past few years of blunders. It feels like Sega thought they earned some goodwill with Mania, thought "hey, people will probably pay big money for classic Sonic games even if we put zero effort in!", and released this ♥♥♥♥.Zero disrespect for Headcannon, by the way. Their work on Sonic 1, 2, Mania, and this 3&K port had a lot of love put into them - there's plenty of tiny fixes and details peppered into this port that weren't in the original. God bless you, Headcannon, and ♥♥♥♥ you, Sega.Go get a Sonic CD key online or something to play the superior PC port of that game, and go play Sonic 1 Forever, Sonic 2 Absolute, and Sonic 3 A.I.R. for the good PC versions of those. Don't let Sega scam you out of your money for this. I won't be coming back to Origins unless it gets major patches, whether official or unofficial, and major community mods to boot.What a cluster♥♥♥♥.

_childDocuments_.review: Check out screenshot #6. Couldn't even be bothered to make sure the rankings don't spell out "A S S" huh?Another potentially great Sonic game rushed out the door to meet Sonic's anniversary. Again. Another missed opportunity for an "OK" game to be great. Again. All they had to do was ride the wave Sonic Mania created, and the movies have done a lot to help the reputation get better.  It's cool seeing the series get a win every few years, but this isn't one of them.Not quite as bad as the GTA DE Trilogy fiasco, but this one is up there. Glitchy, unpolished, and rushed- with less features than Mania launched with, and a REALLY greedy price model.  And if they really can't use the original tracks from Sonic 3, they should properly communicate why. This was just lazy.Between the modding scene fixes/passion projects, and Whitehead and Headcannon, the fans care more about making a good Sonic game than Sega does. Some of those guys do what you can't or won't do for FREE. I used to love Sega, they tried out a lot of new things stuff, some would say too *many* things hardware-wise, to the point where they were competing with themselves AND competitors. But they always tried new things, they were inventive. They were cool. They cared.Today's Sega mostly tries to emulate past successes (sometimes literally) and does the same goofy, lazy (and now greedy) acts with the Sonic series time and time and time again. It feels like loving and rooting for a sports team that always loses, but your passionate fanbase keeps showing up for your games, loss after loss. Just in the hopes that maybe, just maybe the underdog will make a satisfying comeback. I've personally been waiting 21 years, and these chilli-dogs don't exactly taste like chili anymore.Is it realistically as bad as everyone says? No. The animated cutscenes and extra screen viewing space are really nice. But right now with the bugs, missing content and lack of features it just isn't worth the asking price. I'm waiting for more mod fixes, and, out of sheer curiosity, to see what Sega does about the poor reception. I'm not mad, I'm just disappointed.Hot air rant aside, mods can turn this into something really special. Something we should have gotten to begin with.

_childDocuments_.review: I am a huge Sonic fan. Sonic 3 & Knuckles is still to this day my favourite game of all time. It is hard to give any new comer a proper description of how good atleast this one title in the collection of four really is. We have made almost 30 years of progress in game design but the game still holds up well. I would probably not recommend it to anyone who is not a sonic fan and as such there probably is also no need to even recommend it as sonic fans will or will eventually buy the game. Currently many might feel it is over priced, nothing a special wouldnt fix. What is the fair value? That is up to the buyer.There are a few improvements for S3&K. Sonic now has more subtle animations when it comes to his rotation on the barrels in carnival night zone, probably added due to more storage. Super Sonic also benefits from this as his animations has also been fleshed out such as the rotation on the hydrocity lifts. Flashing sprites are replaced with transparent ones and special stages feels extra smooth.There are noticable flaws in the game. Physics are largely the same but swings in angle island swings you through spikes, the hydrocity air jets pushes you up making it impossible to get a specific 1-up. The special stage at the end of act 2 is unreachable because of the increased frame rate not allowing you to properly clip up the ledge. The large offence is the one everyone has heard about. The Jackson music is missing from Carnival Night, Ice Cap and Launchbase instead replaced by the pc midi and original proto type music. Not speaking of the package as a whole but with a few patches the bugs can be fixed. Sadly the music can't. Other than that I welcome the changes.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're like me and never played the classic sonic games as a kid, this game is perfect for you. I've had such a good time playing through all of these games, and i'm planning on playing through them again. If you're a long time classic sonic fan, you'll find issues with the game, such as lives being removed from the game but most issues are fixed with easily downloadable mods. At the end of the day, these are still the timeless classics wrapped up in a nice package with quality life improvements such as widescreen and a better frame rate. Maybe buy it on a sale if you're unsure.Individual Game Reviews:Sonic The HedgehogThe game to start it all. If I'm honest, I really don't like this game. It's pretty boring thanks to it's level design, and it just makes me want to go play one of the other games in this collection. To make things worse, every zone has 3 acts, so the excruciating pain feels like it lasts an eternity. Also ♥♥♥♥ Labyrinth Zone. Sonic CDThe Black Sheep of the classic Sonic games. This game is weird as all hell, which is evident in it's level design. Sonic CD's level design encourages exploration to destroy generators and Metal Sonic holograms to create a "good future" for that zone. Oh yeah, there's time travel in this game. By passing a "future" or "past" sign and maintaining max speed for a couple of seconds lets Sonic time travel, changing the level's layout a bit and the zones music. This is a really cool concept, and it's a shame it never returned in any capacity. Sonic CD's soundtrack is a true bop and I recommend changing the OST from US soundtrack to JP in the game's main menu. What really holds this game back is most of this games zones are underwhelming, and the only zones I enjoyed were Palmtree Panic, Quartz Quadrant and Stardust Speedway. Also if you don't go out of your way to destroy generators and Metal Sonic holograms you can beat this game in about an hour. Sonic The Hedgehog 2This is what Sonic 1 should have been. They changed zones so that they now have 2 acts instead of 3 which is a more than welcomed change. Sonic 2 also has some of the best level design in any Sonic game ever, and the only zone I didn't enjoy was Metropolis Zone, mostly because it's the only zone in the game for some reason to have 3 acts. Super Sonic makes his first appearance in this game and he feels precise and fun to control. The special stages that you play to get the Chaos Emeralds were surprisingly fun to play, especially because of all the negative things I've heard about them. If you haven't played any of the classic Sonic games before, start here and play Sonic 1 later.Sonic The Hedgehog 3 & KnucklesSonic 3&k is two games put in one, Sonic the Hedgehog 3, and Sonic and Knuckles. Objectively, this is the best game in this collection. It took what Sonic 2 built, and improved on it. The zones in this game are iconic, Angel Island Zone, Ice Cap Zone, Sky Sanctuary Zone, actually, all of them are iconic. This is also the debut of Knuckles, which is cool. The games story is simplistic, yet conveys all it needs to. My only gripe with this game is some zones have dumb gimmicks that get boring after 2 seconds which completely ruin some zones, such as the fan dubbed "barrel of doom" in Carnival Night Zone, and the ghosts in Sandopolis Zone. Returning to Sonic 3&k is Super Sonic, and with it special stages. Although I enjoyed Sonic 2's special stages, Sonic 3&k blow them out the water entirely. Blue Spheres is such a fun mini game that really tests your patience and skill. After beating 7 special stages, you unlock Super Sonic, obviously. But what's unique about Sonic 3&k is you can then upgrade your Chaos Emeralds into Super Emeralds by completing 7 more special stages that are even harder. Doing this unlocks Hyper Sonic, which is just Super Sonic that is more sparkly and has a mid air dash ability. All in all, Sonic 3&k is regarded as the best classic Sonic game, and for good reason. Subjectively, I'd probably put this game equal to Sonic 2, if not a bit higher.

_childDocuments_.review: What should have been a smash-hit celebration of the greatest games of Sonic's history is instead a lackluster collection of ports that are universally worse than even the mobile versions. This is currently one of the worst ways to play Sonic 1-3 or Sonic CD.- The game uses poor sprite scaling (likely linear/bilinear rather than integer) that makes the in-game graphics look blurrier than Mania or any of the mobile remasters. This does not appear to be a problem with any other platforms.- The UI looks astonishingly blurry on high-resolution displays, as if it was created for a 720p  display and then stretched with, again, poor filtering.- The sharp/smooth/CRT filtering options from previous releases have been completely removed.- There is no way to play the games in the widescreen "remastered" mode with the original lives system. You're required to either use the new coins system that removes lives as a mechanic or play in a letterboxed square.- The game does not obey Windows display scaling. Running in a borderless window will cause the game to take up a small chunk of the display.- The game has vsync issues. I get screen tearing issues owing to the game locking to 59fps instead of 60fps.- The music used for Sonic 3's Carnival Night, Ice Cap, and Launch Base zones are sharp downgrades from the prototype versions people thought we were getting. Sega directly stated these would use the original genesis soundchip, but they instead appear to be based on MIDI versions from the mid-90s PC collection. It's rough - Carnival Night in particular sounds like it's from a completely different system, terribly muffled/muddy and with a melody that's almost entirely absent due to poor mixing.- Bugs that were present in the original release of Mania have found their way back in, including bad Tails pathfinding. There are lots of scenarios where Tails will end up stuck on springs off-screen, producing terrible noises.- There are new and exciting physics bugs in Sonic 3 surrounding changing water levels and almost every stage gimmick.- Drop Dash locks your direction in Sonic 1 and Sonic 2, and the way it interacts with slopes in those games makes it basically unusable.- The DLC is a blatant cash grab, and would've just been cute add-ins for any other collection.- The game's encrypted with Denuvo, so while some of this can be fixed by mods (like sound files), expecting anything deeper is a tall order. For the price, the community shouldn't be expected to fix the game's shortcomings.I have a lot of other nitpicks (why are the options are tucked away in the Museum, why can you not change keyboard key binds, and why can you not move with the arrow keys?), but almost every one of these is a dealbreaker. This release is astonishingly buggy and rushed, and until/unless Sega addresses some of the many issues, this is just a worse way to play games you can already play just about anywhere else.I can't believe they want $45 for this.

_childDocuments_.review: After playing all of the games in Sonic Origins, I had to alter my review.  Avoid this game, unless you desperately want the widescreen presentation.  It's presented as the original Sonic games, but it is a buggy mess, and the game physics are definitely different and it frequently breaks things that are supposed to just work.  Can't go fast if the game dunks you into walls instead of that graceful slope designed to catch you. Additionally Sega has delisted secretary Sonic games to make you but this travesty at 4x the price. That said, there are several places you can still get digital copies, and there is a rich fan base that has modded many of the features of this game into other releases.   Personally, I own physical copies of all of these games. If you have a real system and don't mind spending the money, you can get an ossc and cables and hook up your Sega Genesis to a 4k TV and play then as they were intended without some weird corporate shenanigans.  I have hardware to play them in 4k and on the original systems.  To make matters worse, I payed extra to get access to the soundtracks, which are not the original, and are only available in-game.  So basically I payed extra for a sound test that had to be unlocked.In many ways the games are a lot easier here than the originals, and I don't consider that a bad thing.  Having extra player options, essentially, infinite lives, and saves for each stage.  Not to forget the 16x9 aspect, which increases the screen real-estate.  As far as I'm concerned, the game is a money grab and the most cynical re-branding of an original and beloved series.  There are five different editions of this game and they all should have been included as just one edition. Most of the added content is not new. And most of the digital Deluxe edition is a cosmetic change that most players would not know or care if they were missing.

_childDocuments_.review: Post-Plus Release Edit:As someone who bought the extra DLC at original launch, I went ahead and ate the cost of the Plus update too just for convenient access to the Game Gear games.Honestly? I can't say I'm entirely happy with the expansion content here. The Game Gear games are a lot of fun, but I was really hoping we'd get at least a modicum of some kind of bonus included as part of their presentation here -- infinite lives akin to the Origins versions of the core games at the very least -- but no go: these are just straight ports, right down to performance issues akin to the slowdown and audio issues the original hardware was known for.Don't get me wrong, I feel that having them included is nothing but a positive for the collection... but, well, they call the Game Gear version of Sonic 1 a port of the Genesis game. That should really tell you all you need to know about the effort put into their inclusion here.Having said that, let's be real: if you're getting the DLC as an extra, it's probably for the same reason I did: Playable. Retro. Amy. No problems there for me: she's got her hammer, and that's all that matters.Otherwise, my original review for the game stands. A little disappointed? Yeah: save states and being the first really complete collection of the Game Gear games on PC is great, but it really is a bare-minimum inclusion, checking a content box and nothing more. No new unlockable GG-related art, no new unlockable GG related songs, no Origins mode extras for the games... so yeah.Absolutely worth having the collection for the games. Just... don't go in expecting the GG stuff to be anything more than what they already were.Original Review:I mean, I'll be honest... it's good.Now, take this with a grain of salt, because computers are as varied as the people who use them, but personally, I haven't had a single significant issue while playing the games.That said, I'm a casual when it comes to Sonic. I enjoy the games, but I've never ground out perfect finishes in any of them, or gotten all the emeralds, or anything like that. At least, not until this release right here.For someone coming at the Sonic games from the angle of "♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ isn't fun," on a gameplay front this package does a great job of mitigating a lot of the things that tend to be Not Fun (for me) about Sonic. Unlimited lives/no continues helps to soften the blow of some of the frustrating and outright mean level design and enemy placements, and the ability to re-try special stages means you're not punished unnecessarily for not being an expert at a mini-game that, if you miss it, you have to more or less start the entire game over to get a chance at again at worst, or can't practice harder ones until you DO master it at best.Classic Sonic games are short and fun in our memories because we block out the literal dozens of frustrated hours we spent as kiddos memorizing enemy placements, special stage layouts, and hazard routes.This package's presentation of them allows them to be that fun in real life.On the other hand, if you want the classic lives and continues back, or want to be punished for the game eating a jump input during a Blue Spheres minigame, then the classic versions of the games are here. I can't say much more about them, though, because I haven't touched them: I bought the package for the Origins versions specifically.And I haven't been disappointed.Are the games buggy? Yes. They're Sonic games; anyone who tries to claim they weren't buggy *before* this port is completely ignoring every time the Genesis version of 2 will subpixel you into the void or 1 will press you through a wall with a piston.Is the music different in 3? Yes. The new tracks arguably aren't as catchy as the originals, and the whole mix is a little weird, but it's nothing that makes the game unplayable, and if it means 3nK is now free of the noose hanging around its neck from music rights for years, then all the better.Is the package too expensive? Honestly, debatable. Leading up to release my thoughts were an unequivocal "yes," but having played the actual releases, seen the work that's gone into things, experienced the animations and everything else... it's harder to make that judgement. As individual titles, if SEGA has asked me for 8 bucks or so for each of these versions, I would have thought it was 100 percent worth it. Combine that with the bonus materials you have access to, the linked mode where you can play all the games as one continuous experience, and everything else?The value depends on how much you think MUCH more friendly versions of the Sonic games are worth. For me, yes, they're worth it.Is the DLC worth it? Not really. For 5 bucks on top of the normal price for the "deluxe" bundle it's at least less egregious than the 8 if you bought the two packs individually, but overall unless you're the type who loves delving into the sound tests and listening to Sonic music when you're not playing Sonic, or a hardcore fan who needs the hard missions and, let's face it, isn't reading this review because you already bought the whole package? They're skippable. The animations on the menus are fun, but aren't really a value add in any major way.So, Sonic Origins. It's fun. It's functional. Sure, it could be better, but as-is it's (in my opinion) the definitive versions of all 4 games featured in the package, and 100 percent the way I'll choose to play all of these games from this point on.Lots of people are angry at this release for what it isn't, but for what it is, it's solid.

_childDocuments_.review: An absolutely disgraceful collection but I did not expect anything more since it was made "internally at SEGA"CONS:Most important - NO integer scaling, meaning all 4 games look just as blurry as Sonic CD 2011. What was the point of finally releasing the 2013 remasters on consoles if they look worse than when they did on mobile?Mission Mode is comprised of bite-sized, generically-designed levels that would make the most amateur platformers blush. I could tell it was made by Sonic Team cuz the mode features grey X-blocks like Forces and they're EVERYWHERE with no slopes in sightKnuckles isn't playable in CD (a primarily exploration-based game). Don't get me started on Amy - a character that's been promoted since the Archie Mega Drive days as part of Team Sonic. Then in Mania Adventures, then in IDW comics, and now here. So you'd think they would finally make her playable? Lol, you want them to make a NEW sprite-sheet (which they did back in CD 2011 for Tails)? You're asking for too muchNo customizations. After all these years, after fan projects like S1 Forever, S2 Absolute, S3 Complete, S3 A.I.R., OR EVEN Sonic Mania, our boys at SEGA couldn't be bothered to add the most BASIC options between all 4 games like fans do. No peel-out in S3, elemental shields in S1/CD/2, max control, Jam difficulties, can't disable the Drop Dash, no option to use lives/timeouts in Anniversary Mode or collect Tokens in Classic Mode, etc.Island Tour DLC just allows you to zoom-in on each island, not even rotate them. Money well spent. And that "animated characters on island" DLC? All of them are ripped from Gens/ForcesSuper Sonic isn't in S1. Now you might say "What are you talking about, obviously he isn't". Yeah, umm... except some Japanese promo images showed him in Scrap Brain. So I thought "Oh, so he, alongside a 7th Special Stage are in Anniversary Mode, nice bonus". And he isn't. You can only access him using cheats, just like on mobile. Is this a nitpick? Yeah, but maybe they shouldn't have blatantly lie to consumers, then The "Drop Dash" is a pure lie. What do I mean? It's actually a disguised Spin Dash animation that happens for a split-second? Doesn't sound bad, except the AGES version of S1/S2 natively added it to their ROMs. Oh! And in Origins it BARELY moves you after you execute it. Best part? S1/S2 have a fixed jump arc, so if you try to do this move in those games and jump, you won't be able to control yourself mid-air (think Castlevania)The Museum... god, remember those so-called "never-before seen concept arts" they promised? Well I'm here to tell you there are like 6 of them, everything else are Harmony covers and character sheets. The Video section has none of those cool 90s ads, promo videos or even documentaries, just a few pieces of the Sonic Symphony they threw in at the last hour, Origins' cutscenes and every episode of Mania Adventures (and their respective animatics). Both Normal and Premium sections offer very little content, especially if you pre-ordered the game which gives you a 100 Token bonus, you can literally unlock everything in under 2 hours. Not to mention it's complete silence, no remix of History or anything like that, no feeling of nostalgia. Just cynical, corporate silence as you browse what little they offer. Only ""new"" track here is a remix of Sonic World from Jam that plays everywhere except the Museum. ClassyS1/2/CD are straight mobile versions, so they haven't been touched up at all. Meaning the missing rolling SFX in CD hasn't been fixed, and the extended camera is still absentHorrible audio quality. Believe it or not, they REMOVED the remastered OSTs for S1, CD and S2 from mobile. Why? No clue. As for S3&K, y'know... the only new thing here, it isn't given the same treatment so its OST is really muffled, and ON TOP OF THAT, CD's 2 OSTs are super quiet and also in bad quality. How did they screw it up? idk, but it is hilarious Your Score in S3&K resets to 0 if you click the Restart button. This doesn't happen in other gamesThe music DLC (Chaotix, 3D Blast and Spinball) misnamed countless tracks. For example; Chaotix's bad ending theme (Destructive Power) is Door to Summer, while 3D Blast's Invincibility theme is the Menu theme. Incompetent? Very much. Funny? AbsolutelyNo Chaotix island. You might notice how Origins' gallery features stuff from Chaotix, 3D Blast and Spinball, the OSTs from those games they repackaged as DLC at the last minute, as well as the islands from Spinball and 3D Blast in the hub menu and... wait a second... where's the Island of Miracles from Chaotix? You telling me, the island from a game that is the closest to Sonic's gameplay of that era isn't here... but islands from 2 US-made games, one of which is a pinball spin-off made to promote a show that never aired in Japan, are here? Not only is this sorta insulting, I'm like 1000% sure it was supposed to be here as an Options island, they just didn't make a model of it in time, and plastered Options in the Museum of all placesScrewed up physics. Due to S3&K here clearly being made on Mania's engine, it had a lot of ramifications on the game's internal logic. Some stuff is cool like all elemental shields function how they did in Mania, making the bubble shield fun to use. Others... because the game now controls exactly like Mania, there are a LOT of collision/physics bugs that weren't present in the OG gameCD's ending animation. While the restoration team did really well with remastering the original opening, I... have no idea what happened with the ending. It looks like one of those interpolated anime clips. Worst part? It's sped up by 3x and there are no SFXs in the beginning, so it instantly plays the credits theme. The Gallery also plays it off-sync and it doesn't feature the bad ending version. Actually a jokeEven though I'm not one of those people that plays S3 and S&K separately, it's kinda absurd how they initially advertised this collection with those 2 games in mind. Final release? You can't play them separately. Oh wellThe new S3&K tracks. I don't know what sound chip Jun Senoue (same guy who composed S4EI) used but it sure wasn't a Mega Drive one. Tracks sound muffled, quiet and overall don't fit the game. It's especially insulting to CNZ Act 2, its prototype track is EASILY one of my favorite Sonic tunes... and Jun completely butchered it. They should've asked Yuzo Koshiro to recompose them. But you wanna know THE coolest part? Origins is made on Criware, meaning the audio is encrypted, meaning it'll be really hard to mod music in. Just a neat thing, y'know :)Denuvo. No need to explain, you already know the game runs poorly. Countless stuttering tooPROS:Cutscenes look great, but what did you expect from Tyson Hesse and Powerhouse, you knew they'd pull it off with flying colors. However they haven't animated any of the bad endings, meaning if you get one in any of the games, it would still play said game's true endingThe restoration group they hired to scan various pieces for the Museum and clean up the CD opening (not the ending) did a really good jobThe S3&K remaster, despite the collection's flaws, is alright. Nowhere near the level of AIR, which is odd cuz I know Stealth and his crew can do WAY better than this. At least it wasn't done by SEGAClassic games on PC, so your usual "Hope modders will fix it" mentality will continue yet again! You expect SEGA to do all the work? Pfftt, yeah rightNotice how all the collection's positives I listed were outsourced to 3rd parties and not done by SEGA? That should tell you how much they care. In the end you're left with:Sonic 1 (the Spin Dash is still present in the so-called Classic mode)Sonic 2 (with a horrible, downright game-breaking Tails AI)Sonic CD (they use leftover UI from the mobile version I kid you not)and Sonic 3&K (with its muffled, MJ-free OST)Happy 31st Anniversary, Sonic. I can't believe I'm still a fan of your franchise

_childDocuments_.review: Well, you may have noticed some remakes or remasters of Sonic games, like Sonic Origins released recently with some added features, cutscenes and more. But that game has mixed reviews as that game is pretty much similar to Sega Mega Drive Classics on Steam, despite the added cutscenes, achievements and modifications.Why does this game have mixed reviews? Well, it appears to be pricey to have 3 of the original Mega Drive Sonic games merged into one - plus the Sega CD of Sonic CD game, but doesn't have some key improvements. For example, it doesn't appear to have a Classic Scanline screen or to make it look like you are playing on a CRT 1990s TV - like being back in the old school 1990s era. And it doesn't appear to have like HQx2 or xBRZ to smooth those staircase edges nor make Sonic look smoother for gamers who hate eye strains.Don't get me wrong, but the higher frame rates, Museum and Special Missions are ok. However, this game reminds me of the Sonic Mega Collection and Sonic Gems Collection for the GameCube which contains those classic Sonic games for the Mega Drive, Game Gear, Saturn and Arcade. Even the Sonic Mega Collection and Sonic Gems Collection contain some interesting archives and pictures of Sonic the Comic, and Sonic Coin-Op machines some of which were only released in Japan. But those archive collections, achievements and special missions should be only used as bonus features and focus on how to improve the general gameplay for those Sonic Classic games, as well as the remakes.Some gamers don't realise that having VSync on for Sonic Origins causes display lag and we got powerful GFX cards that won't cause screen tearing for playing remade 16-Bit games on an emulator - unless you are using xBRZ at a high factor or that. The Spindash for Sonic 1 segment for Sonic Origins and the Gold Coins used as Lives are ok, but that seems too feeble if you ask me. Also, Sonic 2 had some maps or levels removed as Mega Drive cartridge ROMs had limited storage.

_childDocuments_.review: --Update--They did include the character I was hoping so long for, and it was behind a DLC.
