_childDocuments_.review: Oh god what a let down this was.So first off, the game ran HORRIBLY, mainly suffering ALOT of slowdown whenever the game saved, started a level, came off from the main menu or entering a Special Stage; majority of the time pausing and unpausing would fix the slowdown but around Lava Reef in S3&K the slowdown would happen way more often, maybe it was because of Hyper Sonic? Honestly majority of these issues seem more than likely caused by Denuvo DRM, which from last time it was used in a Classic Sonic title (Sonic Mania) it ran horribly. So I was wishing they'd had some hindsight.The controls in Sonic 1, CD and 2 are all messed up. Main example being that the drop dash is implemented in a way where when you land you don't do the dash immediately and instead it keeps you vulnerable for a frame before doing a SHORT spindash. Alongside this when rolling your controls are locked to just jumping, you are incapable of doing ANY course correction or even changing the direction you're dashing with the Drop Dash.During Sonic CD specifically the sound effects are all sorts of messed up, what comes to mind first for it being the air timer and drowning being pitched up and out of sync. The goal post spinning and other sound effects also end up sounding like they're played through a botched emulator, maybe even an AtGames Mega Drive.In Sonic 3 & Knuckles, the most promising of the games in this batch, the music and sound effects sound really muffled or compressed at times, and the new remixes of the Prototype tracks are flat and out of key at points. And don't get me started on the special stages, I had gotten all 7 Chaos Emeralds by Marble Garden ACT 1, during which I was able to transform into Super Sonic fine. By ACT 2 my Chaos Emeralds had reset to 1 for some reason, in which I had to get all of them AGAIN. And even after that touching a Giant Ring would make me repeat the seventh Blue Spheres stage instead of giving me 50 rings, despite me already having the emeralds. This problem was fixed by Mushroom Hill ACT 1 though due to how the Super Emeralds work. Speaking of the Super Emeralds, using Hyper Sonic is a nightmare. So they never removed his rapidly flashing colour palette or screen clearing flash of white, infact they only made the screen flash worse by adding a hyper quick fade in/out.These experiences were all from one marathon of the Story Mode, and while the new cutscenes and visual additions to S3&K were great and fun, the problems listed above were enough to make my favourite games a miserable experience.Overall this is a pretty bad collection and remaster, bringing bugs and issues to already perfected versions of Sonic 1, CD and 2 (Mobile, IOS/Android) and a decent but buggy remaster of Sonic 3 & Knuckles, which supposedly according to Stealth from Headcannon on Twitter, is not what they handed SEGA fully.If I was to recommend this it'd be hopefully after the game gets patched, as I can see this becoming my main way to play these games if the launch wasn't botched.Instead I'd recommend the Mobile ports of these games and maybe emulating Sonic 3, I would recommend them all from steam but SEGA removed being able to buy the Mega Drive versions of these games a month or two ago to make way for this.Play Sonic 1 Forever, Sonic 2 Absolute, Sonic CD decompilled and Sonic 3 Angel Island Revisited if you want a PC widescreen Sonic experience, all of these require dumps of the payed versions of the games from mobile and a rom back up of Sonic 3, methods for obtaining a rom I cannot give as SEGA's official version of Sonic 3 & Knuckles no longer exists here, which S3AIR used.

_childDocuments_.review: The Good: A great collection of classic games, remade to be faithful while also including nice modern features, such as autosaves on checkpoints, the removal of lives (thank god!) and the ability to retry special stages make this a much more approachable offering for newcomers. With the Plus upgrade the game feels much more complete as a collection and as an Amy fan I'm very happy to see her getting some love. All it really needs is the mod to replace the poorly mixed prototype tracks with something you prefer, then it really feels like the definitive way to revisit these classics. You will get varying mileage out of each game, depending on your taste, but the music, art design and set pieces make for a very memorable romp. Not to mention the lovely new cutscenes book-ending each game which help it all flow together nicely as one package.The Bad: Selling something like characters on the menu islands (and some extra soundtracks in the museum) is really inexcusable in a collection such as this - it really should've just been there with the base game. Luckily for me I refused to buy it, so the Plus upgrade (which includes these 'DLCs') felt less like a robbery, but either way... Plus should've been a free update, especially as it fixes key bugs in the base game. Less of an issue for new time purchasers though, but it's worth highlighting.Conclusion: While I can't condone the business practises behind this release, it really isn't as bad a collection as people make out. I do agree it's missing some of the bells and whistles of the fan made decompilations (which are only legally available to play if you already own the Genesis Classics collection on Steam, as they've delisted it) but it's by no means a dumpster fire. Only you can decide if Sega's business practises

_childDocuments_.review: Initial Reactions for Sonic 3 and knuckles (spoilers)I grew up with the Genesis Games and I even have the damn strategy guide for Sonic 3 when it first came out. I was a huge Sonic Fan and I would still be if this series was just treated with the respect it deserves from its creators. Instead, once again, for the THOUSANDTH time since we've all started playing sonic. "Just barely good enough" is Sega's motto when it comes to these games.The Good-Widescreen-Supposedly scales up to 4K, I have yet to even try that out-Coins are a good incentive to travel throughout the whole game and grab as many rings as possible-Super Sonic is Mapped to the Y Button like in Sonic Mania-Tails Helper Controls are nearly perfect-The camera controls seem to function better than the default controls in Sonic A.I.R, and you can now outrun the screen again. it's quite cool-Ice Cap Act 1 and 2 and Launch Base Act 1 use their prototype music without many changes...And the Bad- The Music does not start or stop correctly in stages. Everything has a strange fade-in and fade-out effect.- Special Stage Controls are tweaked, so if you're used to timing from S3/S3Air you will need to adjust- For that matter it's sort of difficult to use the sound effects from the special stage as a reference point for when you need to turn because of how delayed they are- The Special Stage music never speeds up as you play. So we went from S3 speed up too fast, S3K speeding up slower, and now S3K origins not speeding up at all... why?- Many Sound effects are seemingly added in all over the place for no good reason, It makes some parts feel like I'm watching a flash/youtube fan movie- Instead of letting you fruitlessly attack the first miniboss, they now arbitrarily lock you in place.- The Super Sonic Music is absolutely terrible and I would've rather them played the invincibility theme if it was going to be this bad- The Sonic 3 invincibility music is gone.. BUT they let you listen to it in museum mode for some crazy reason!- Absolutely no gameplay customization options whatsoever as far as I can tell (not surprised...)- Marble Garden's Crushers can now kill you from ALL SIDES rather than you needing to be under them... Ugh!- Marble Garden's swinging spikeball hitboxes are bigger for some reason?- A lot of things break really easily for the experienced players zipping through all the zones: Effects that are supposed to last for moments instead glitch out and last the entire level (For instance Marble Garden Zone when you first encounter the mini boss has debris falling and then it never stops if you run past it).- Carnival Night Act 1 and 2 and Launch Base Act 2 music is god awful which is weird because the prototype music that was recently dug up would've been perfect to use. Either they used the wrong versions or Jun just plain out screwed up.The worst offender of them all-They list and let you listen to the "unused music" for sonic 3 in the museum mode, which the community has already agreed on being probably the prototype super sonic music, but Jun made his own track for the game that screams sonic 4 levels of bad and you cant. turn. it. OFF.I'll update this as I go along but I really hope they fix the music up...Edit: So supposedly the entire game is built up as a modification of Sonic Mania. That's interesting but what's REALLY screwed up is sega took these ports and forced them to run alongside the hedgehog engine that powers their 3D games. They hacked into the sound engine part of the Retro engine that powers the game and... absolutely butchered it.So to break it down for you guys, and please leave a thumbs up if this makes sense...Sega used their 3D game engine to replace the perfect sound that these games had to begin with on the retro engine... and on top of denuvo you are running a 3D game engine at the same time as these 2D engines. This isn't some sort of "Haha technically..." or "Gotcha". This is what's actually happening, does it now make sense why the game runs like ♥♥♥♥?

_childDocuments_.review: The following review also considers the DLC for this game (as of 29th August 2022, should there ever be more).Sonic Origins is ok. Just ok. It does have what I really wanted, which was Sonic 1 and 2 2013 editions on a non-mobile platform, but it's bundled with CD, which...really had no need to be "here", since CD was perfectly fine remaining separate, especially when CD has no additional improvements. (I don't actually care for S3K all that much to be bothered by its inclusion.)The Good:- Mission Mode. Really liked this new spin on tackling levels. The Super Sonic challenge concept was especially really fun. Some of the missions seem extremely textbook given that I am a Sonic veteran, but the appeal to newer players to hone skills is certainly there.- Sonic 1 and 2 (2013) finally coming to non-mobile. It was downright criminal that it took this long. Honestly could have done without drop dash tho, I still don't think drop dash is very good as a concept.- The cutscenes are definitely well done and quite cute.- The fact that they snuck in a Spinball homage as one of the "islands". I'm a sucker for Spinball, so I can't not appreciate that.The Bad:- Denuvo. Unfortunately, SEGA got past the "complaining" phase and compromised only by removing Denuvo from Mania, while Forces still has it and Frontiers is about to. This is basically part of SEGA's host of bad decisions.- Frankly, the way the DLC was presented. You literally have no need for an extra 100 coins. You play all of mission mode once and get S ranks, you're nearly maxed and can buy almost all the unlockables. The missions that were in DLC could easily have been unlockables themselves. Big ball drop here.- I'm not gonna call this personally bad, because I don't mind, but Amy being presented as one of the characters in all the advertising and then not being a playable character. "New playable characters" is straight up false advertising, unless you want to call Knuckles + Tails "new". I can't ignore that as a flaw.- Delisting Sonic 1, 2, 3 and CD for this. Also another bad decision. CD didn't even need to be in this collection, period.- Shoving in drop dash for Sonic 1, 2 and CD. I'll even say it doesn't actually really belong in S3K either. These games did not need a move that the games aren't actually built for a lot of the time. (For the record, Sonic 1 having spindash is more acceptable, especially since it was built in to the mobile release).- CD being ported in with basically no changes. I'm going to call out something specific here: CD still has its own time attack mode built in, but also has the Origins-specific leaderboards, creating an odd redundancy. Oh, and the centisecond timer bug? Still in the game.The Ugly:- Boss Rush. Boss Rush is a nice concept, but it was executed badly, especially outside Sonic 1. There could have even been a time attack mode and a survival mode a la Robotnik's Revenge, or a specially designed boss rush level like Sonic 2 (2013) wanted to do. Huge missed opportunity. Instead, you have many bosses that do need a ring to go fast that have no rings or rings behind you so you have to waste time getting one, in exchange for other levels having rings, such as Final or Death Egg Zone. Very erratic difficulty scale, and it makes for an odd experience.- The leaderboards taking times from your first playthrough (by this I mean taking times from outside the My Data & Ranking section at all), even Super/Hyper times. Big error in judgement by whomever thought this was a good idea. Mania did this right. Even SONIC FOUR did this right. Why make this mistake here?- The coin system being utterly worthless very quickly. This replacing lives in Anniversary Mode was also not a good idea. Doesn't matter if I "have Classic Mode for that". Coins belong in Mario.- The Museum not having its own theme. Also a poor decision.- Mirror Mode. I have very mixed feelings about Mirror Mode, and I want to say it's good, bad, and ugly all at the same time. It's good for a mindfug experience. It's bad for IL runners because it's just an artificial reason for "more levels". It's ugly because no one actually wanted this, considering the time was better spent on other things...Overall, especially after the patch, the game is passable. It's not excellent, and plenty of bad decisions were made. The price isn't "bad" considering the work on cutscenes and the like, but for just the games it was worth halfish.Buy it at half price or less, and unless you also really like the missions, skip the DLC. Right now, save your money for Frontiers IF it turns out to be a good enough game. Try not to support SEGA's bad decision making if you can help yourself.

_childDocuments_.review: The best official versions of these classic Sonic games. Sonic 1 has never felt more fun to play, with the Drop Dash, Spin Dash and an enhanced level select menu which lets you toggle speed caps, number of emeralds, use of Sonic 3 items in Sonic 1 etc). Mirror Mode was especially bizarre and I somehow managed to get lost in a game I've been playing since release. Sonic CD is great, and its what you'd expect if you've played the 2011 version. Toggle to change between JPN and US soundtracks is still present. As of now I'm only half way through Sonic 2 and haven't played 3K yet but this collection is really outstanding. This is the best compilation of Sonic games since Mega Collection. While the latter has more games on offer, I'd argue this is a better deal as you're getting the very best versions of the best 2D Sonic games here. Unfortunately there's a few bugs, such as Sonic CD missing voice samples for Sonic and Amy. I also got stuck in Spring Yard where there was a low ceiling and a spring beneath me so I kept bouncing infinitely. There's also a small amount of slowdown that rarely occurs but nothing major. I'm hoping we get DLC in the form of additional games, such as 3D Blast, Spinball and (hopefully), Chaotix. This is an absolute win for Sonic. Happy Birthday Sonic!

_childDocuments_.review: I'd say Origins a very good collection as well as it runs smooth. I changed all my settings on my laptop to be high performance for the game but it didn't perform well until I actually went into the game and lowered the resolution down two notches. By far my favorite part of Origins is Sonic 3. I hear people complaining about the physics being wrong but I haven't had any issues with those and I think it plays very well. The new frames, sound effects, and added cutscenes create a whole new experience for me personally, You don't realize how smooth the game is until you enter a special stage or a blue orb stage. It's so incredibly smooth that it feels like a modern day sonic installment. My biggest complaint for sonic 3 and Origins in general is definitely the removal of MJ's tracks which include Carnival Night Zone, Launch Base Zone, and my personal favorite Ice Cap Zone. I wound up installing a mod to get all those tracks back because I couldn't stand the alternative themes. (There's also new music for super sonic but I thought it sounded better than the original.)As for the rest of Origins, I say it's all pretty good. Sonic is able to use all of his mania abilities and it felt a little out of place to be spin dashing and drop dashing in sonic 1. In sonic 3 I'm so glad they combined the temporary shield and the drop dash; they compliment each other very well. The extras (with the exception of challenges) feel kind of pointless and I don't really care much about them. Although if you like looking at old boxart, concepts and promotional material be my guest.I'd highly recommend this game to people who've never played these classics and I think it's a great way to jump back into the games for people who grew up with these games like I did.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a HUGE Classic Sonic fan but this collection here is a giant disappointment and I'm gonna give out criticism on why I hate this collection. My main criticism about this collection is the pricing, 55 CAD is too much for four Classic Sonic games, especially when compared to Sonic Mega Collection which cost 20 dollars with 12 games. Sega even decided to delist the four Classic Sonic games on the digital store when the trailer came out and decided to lock some content behind DLCs such as extra missions and some island additions, That is very disgusting since it's a collection of four 30-year-old games. You even can't play as Metal Sonic or Amy Rose despite them being featured in the collection and can't even play as Knuckles in Sonic CD which is just very absurd and a big missed opportunity. Speaking of missed opportunities, It even sucks that Sonic 3D Blast, Sonic Spinball, and Knuckles' Chaotix aren't even in the collection despite them being available as soundtracks by DLC (Classic Music Pack). Sonic 3 and Knuckles is by far the biggest offender here in this collection, asides the glitches and bugs, one of the things about this version that made me upset is the fact there aren't any MJ tracks in this version especially Ice Cap as it's replaced by the earlier music from the beta version of Sonic 3, don't get me wrong for two things, The Sonic 3 Prototype music is very catchy and Jun Senoue is a great composer for the Sonic games, The Prototype music in here sounds awful, especially Carnival Night, therefore, wasting Jun's talents in remixing those beta tracks which is just very sad. It still didn't make sense to remix when they could just port the music from the Prototype version. I pretty much doubt if one of the updates will bring back MJ tracks and I'm not exactly sure why they can't get the MJ music to this version, probably it's the licensing issue. That music changed especially Ice Cap sure did give fans hard times.  While Super and Hyper Sonic finally got their own theme in Sonic 3K instead of using repetitive invincibly music but literally sounds like Sonic 4 music which doesn't feel right for Sonic 3K because of its instruments and it's a shame that it's not using the Unused version (But yet the Unused version music was used in the New Blue Spheres results). Going to Sonic CD in this verison:Remember how the 2011 port of Sonic CD, the music of it uses the unused loops in the Japanese OST but for unknown reasons, they decided to use the music based on the original version of Sonic CD in the Origins version which I also noticed on Day one when the collection was out. The US OST loops weirdly as it's also based on the original version of Sonic CD as well.Going back to Sonic 3 in this collectionAs we got the music out of the way, I even ended up getting those issues in S3K EVEN WITH PATCHES. I ended up getting soft-locked multiple times, the first time I got soft-locked in Carnival Night by a barrel (or should I say Barrel of Doom), and the second time I got soft-locked in the Knuckles Battle in Hidden Palace after defeating him. There have been many glitches in this version especially at Launch.There are still some things wrong with this collection,Classic Mode - Adding Classic mode in this collection sounds like a perfect idea on paper but it's executed poorly as it's just the remastered versions at a 4:3 ratio, Sonic 1 still has the spindash while the original Sonic 1 didn't have a spindash, Sonic 2 in Mystic Caves still takes you to Hidden Palace when falling in the infamous pit, and Sonic 3 still have Sonic and Tails fight Big arms while in the original S3K you don't unless if you play as Knuckles. Couldn't they just have it emulated using the original Sonic versions when using Classic modeAnniversary Mode - Nothing to say much about it but there is another missed opportunity for an option where you can turn on lives.The games (Except for Sonic 3K) don't even have save slots, instead, when about to play the game, a character select will just pop up, even the Mobile ports of Sonic 1 and 2 have file selects. Same thing with the Sonic CD 2011 remake where it even has file selection and options but in Origins, you can only change settings in the title screen (I even noticed it resembles the original Sonic CD selection in Origins)Sonic CD in Origins has voice clips removed, removing "I'm Outta here" and"Yes" voice clips, Classic Sonic being muted is pretty stupid. (If you are wondering, Classic Sonic has gone voiceless since Sonic Generations)In General, This collection is just worthless with big letdowns, This collection is not a definitive way to play classic Sonic games, if you want a better remaster of those Classic Sonic games, I recommend Sonic 1 Forever, Sonic 2 Absolute, Sonic CD 2011, and Sonic 3 AIR. Those remasters are way surpeiorI gotta admit that I really love the little animation cutscenes here, and it feels so nice to finally see Sonic 3 and Knuckles getting a rerelease officially although I'm better off with those fan remasters like Sonic 3 AIR and the original version of the classic Sonic gamesI would rate this collection a 2/10. I recommend not buying Sonic Origins. It's not really worth it.If there's anything I'm forgetting, let me know.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to start this review off by saying that the price of this collection for what's being offered here is too high. Wait for the price to go down in a future sale or just naturally over time if owning this collection isn't the most important thing to you.Additionally, as of the time of this review being written, the game uses Denuvo, and I have noticed some small stutters while playing. It's not impacting performance to the point that it will get you killed during gameplay, or screw up a jump or anything, but it does seem to be on occasion making the visuals on screen slightly less smooth than they really should be.With that out of the way, here are my thoughts on this collection:Personally, I'm overall really happy with what we got here. There are some potential sound balancing issues with some sound effects, such as the crumbling terrain sound in Green Hill Zone sounding a bit on the loud side, but otherwise the games themselves play very well. I do however feel rather dissatisfied by the lack of a toggle option to enable widescreen in classic mode and disable it in anniversary mode.Take note that the versions of the games here are not ports of the Genesis/Mega Drive originals, but rather are ports of the mobile remakes running on the Retro Engine, with exception to Sonic 3&K which was made new for this collection and is also on the Retro Engine. Each of the games has been updated to the most up to date version of the engine.The coins system in anniversary mode is very balanced. Everything that used to give you a 1-up will instead give you a coin, and instead of continues you will get 3 coins. You can retry special stages at the cost of 1 coin per attempt.Update: In retrospect I actually feel like coins are far too easy to obtain between the various game modes, being farmable so easily that you don't even really need to be trying to get them to have more than you could ever need. Just retrying for speedrun times in time attack or redoing missions a lot in mission mode will net you plenty of these things in ridiculously short timespans.The new mission mode is really fun, and is the fastest and easiest way to farm coins. From what I've seen so far, it seems like S ranking a mission will net you 5-10 coins and completing a mission for the first time will net you a bonus, I think 2 coins. Missions are composed of little trials in which you must complete time based objectives. In some cases, that means completing an objective such as collecting X number of rings within, for example, 1 minute. In other cases, you have infinite time to complete the mission but the faster you do it, the higher your rank. Even for missions that limit your time, completing them faster will still reward you with a higher rank.The Museum is very rich in content, and features a number of cool things such as concept art, complete game manuals, OST's, animations, etc. For the unlockable items you spend coins on in the Premium section, it seems as though individual items are very cheap, costing you a mere 5 coins per item. Unlocking everything might be a little on the time consuming side since you need to grind up coins, but it's otherwise very trivial. Outside of the Premium section items are unlocked through game progression rather than by spending coins.Sonic CD in this collection slightly differs from the previous Mobile/Steam release. In addition to running on a more updated version of the engine, it features a title screen that functions more closely to the original release. Tails is unlocked from the start, and Sonic can now use the Drop Dash by default (or at least, he can in anniversary. I haven't tested for it in classic yet). I can confirm that the intro cutscene does in fact include the vocals as well. Unfortunately, Sonic and Amy's voices in-game have been removed for some reason.As for Sonic 3&K, I haven't at the time of this review tested around super extensively, but it does seem to be exactly what you would expect. You might be aware of the legal issues/controversy around the Micheal Jackson/Brad Buxer involvement with the original Genesis/Mega Drive release of the game. A number of music tracks they were involved with were apparently not meant to make it into the final product, but somehow did anyway. This eventually led to a legal issue that stopped SEGA from re-releasing Sonic 3&K for years, and it seems as though they were still unable to obtain the rights to those music tracks. As such, they have been replaced in this collection. The replacements are remastered versions of the Prototype tracks, alternate versions of which were also used in the old PC release of the game. Personally, I think these new versions sound fine but a lot of people seem to not like them. Overall though, this is something to keep in mind. Multiple individuals have made note of how they are making it a priority to mod the Jackson/Buxer tracks back into the game.I'd also like to briefly touch up on the recent delisting of previous versions of these games on Steam. In particular, Sonic 3&K. A fan project by the name of Sonic 3 Angel Island Revisited, or Sonic 3 AIR for short, was able to fully remaster the 3&K experience with a huge number of toggle options and native modding support. In my opinion, it's still the better way to experience the game. To install the game legally, a steam copy of S3&K was required, and was fairly cheap to obtain. However, this is no longer possible, and so even if they manage to continue the project through requiring ownership of Origins or something, the cost of legally installing it will have gone up significantly, which feels like kicking the fanbase while it's down to me. Make of it what you will, however.Overall, I consider this to be worth owning, but as I warned at the start of this review, not for the release price. I will leave it up to you to decide whether you consider it worth it however, and spend your own money however you please.

_childDocuments_.review: It's not as bad as some people make it out to be in their reviews but there are still some glaring issues.The biggest one for me is the image quality, for some reason the games don't look very sharp. It almost looks like like they scaled the game up to half the screen resolution internally, then used interpolation for the rest. I'm not sure if this is what they did but it still doesn't look very great.This is something you can actually fix by installing a mod (which is very easy) but come on, we shouldn't have to rely on mods to get an acceptable image quality.There's also a disgusting lack of customizability. When you play the game in anniversary/story mode you're forced to play with spin dash, drop dash, and infinite lives. Why can't we toggle these off? Why are all these settings are bundled together? Why can't we toggle things off?Drop dash is also another issue because it just feels... wrong. The way they implemented it feels rather inaccurate to Mania in all games except Sonic 3. This wouldn't be a huge issue to me normally because I don't even want to play these games with drop dash, but as I said we cannot really turn it off so... yeah...And of course there's also the issue with the music. I don't just mean the replaced music Sonic 3, there's a much bigger and serious issue going on here.In Sonic CD for example, the tracks have rather weird loop points, and they are clipping! Yes, literally clipping. How did they manage to mess it up when the 2011 CD release had it working perfectly? No idea.Sonic 3 is completely messed up too. The whole soundtrack seems to have a low pass filter applied to it which isn't something present in other games, nor it sounds actually good.And of course, they had to replace some of the music from Sonic 3 with their prototype versions because of legal issues. I love the original prototype tracks, don't get me wrong, but these replacement tracks somehow manage to be much, MUCH worse than those leaked proto tracks which is baffling.And yes, the issues with Sonic 3's music is also something mods can fix but I'm not going to give the game extra points for that.Outside these issues this is a good collection, and without them we would have had something fantastic in our hands. Finally being be able to play these games in widescreen in an official fashion is a blessing, the special stages are SO MUCH better here than in the Genesis originals, the option to be able to retry those is awesome, the entire recreation of Sonic 3&K here is super well done, and the menus are very pretty.I'm really enjoying the mission mode as well, despite it not being anything mindblowing. Same with the gallery I guess, there are some songs and concept art to unlock but it isn't going to hold your attention for too long.And, I mean, in the end, this is a collection if 3 fantastic games (and Sonic 1). Sure, they messed it up a bit but the games themselves are perfectly playable regardless.So... I guess in the end I think the collection is decent, just not $40 decent. It's nowhere near as big of a disaster as Sonic Colors Ultimate, so there's at least that.Also, apparently some people are having performance issues but idk it worked fine on my PC lolEDIT: Slightly updated after playing the game way more, and added some things about mods, but I still stand by most of what I said.

_childDocuments_.review: If you find yourself nostalgic about the good 'ol times and want to fire up your old Classic Sonic games, this game is for you.These games are timeless and replaying them all over again has - if anything - just re-affirmed how great they were and how they can still very much stand on their own.FeaturingCharming new animations which fill in the gaps in between games. You'll find yourself wanting to re-visit from time to time due to how greatly they portrait the characters. Quality of life HUDs, with all the 3D models making the islands feel alive.Mission Mode, with all nice new additions for challenges.Mirror mode to test your wits of how much you know the levels, nothing too fancy but a nice include.Museum where you can see amazing never seen before artwork, play all Sonic Mania Adventures videos, which are on Youtube but doesn't hurt. A wide selection of music from Sonic's history and remixes, along with some other features. Some other points to take in consideration:Physics aren't 1:1 but very close to the real deal, you only notice them if you're very hardcore;Small bugs, most of which have already been addressed, some I can say as from the time of writing this - still exist, but are nothing game breaking.Blur is a thing that you can't disable and mods thankfully fix it - Highly recommend picking it up;Music in Sonic 3K took a toll: Carnival Night, IceCap, Launch Base, alongside Act 1 Music, 1-up have been replaced. I highly recommend getting a mod to bring back the old tracks as the ones chosen here, are worse versions than the respective prototype musics.Plus brings Amy on board, fun to play. Also brings in Game Gear titles which albeit fun, for the price tag it's only worth it if you really find yourself revisiting this title time and again.Overall, with the price decrease, especially if its on sale, I very much recommend the steam version of this game. Mods just bring in soo much quality of life to games that are already timeless neatly packaged under one nice roof.As for users with other consoles, I'll say that albeit it's nice having a physical version of it, the lack of mods would deter me from it. Still, give it a spin without any to see if it's your cup of tea.Personally, with it being available on Steam, I am not looking into purchasing any extra copies, I need my original soundtrack, otherwise it's just not the same for me.

detailed_description: Laika: Aged Through Blood is a western-inspired motorvania set in a post-apocalyptic wasteland. It is the story about a tribe oppressed by occupant forces, and the personal story of a mother coyote warrior who descends on an endless path of vengeance to take back what her people lost. Drive, jump and fight your way through the huge hand-drawn world on your trustworthy motorbike. Race through the wasteland and perform dangerous jumps, shoot enemies in slowmo and reload your gun by performing a backflip! Use skill-based power-ups and persist challenging battles against big bosses ! Vehicular combat on a fast and agile motorbike. A beautiful, hand-painted and post-apocalyptic world. A deep story about a mother-daughter relationship, vengeance and loss. A varied world, epic boss battles and loads of missions. The very first MOTORVANIA!

_childDocuments_.review: GD this game was amazing.Stunning artwork, amazing color palate, beautiful, multi-layered backgrounds, gorgeous South Western American desert scenery, and, best of all, the most incredible and fitting soundtrack to a game that I've ever heard.  The game play is fun, fluid, and very unique... you kill enemies in bullet time, and reloading weapons by doing back flips on your motorcycle was incredibly satisfying.  The bosses were extremely creative, and very few were cake walks.  The story line was deep, with memorable characters, VERY adult subjects, focusing on war, vengeance, survival, a magic curse, and the protagonist being female was done very well, adding a unique element to the tale.Laika is a stunning work of art that you'll be proud to have in your collection, and I'll be immediately checking out anything this studio puts out in the future.Just shy of 30 hours of game play, with a powerful ending that will make you tear up. Treat yourself and buy it now, even if it's not on sale, you won't be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was a revelation for me in terms of a new gaming experience. "Laika: Aged Through Blood" is an atmospheric metroidvania that stands out from others in its genre due to its unique combination of styles and mechanics, as well as its unusual aesthetic. Visually, the game impresses with its hand-drawn graphics, and its brutal violence and frequent scenes of brutality underscore the tense atmosphere of the game world.The main events take place in a post-apocalyptic world where birds have declared their racial superiority over other species and launched a brutal war of extermination. As a result of constant warfare and the depletion of resources, the land has turned into a desert. The other inhabitants of the wasteland hide, gather in small settlements and try to survive. The story follows Laika, a coyote warrior, as she tries to save her settlement from the invaders.The majority of the game is spent riding a motorcycle. You can balance the bike, perform various tricks and block enemy bullets. The combat system is implemented in an interesting and unconventional way: a backflip reloads the weapon, while a front flip gives the ability to ricochet bullets back at enemies. Holding down the fire button activates a slow-motion mode, allowing you to better aim and plan your next moves in battle. The one-shot system, where you and your enemies (except bosses) die with a single hit, keeps the tension high and forces you to be more careful. This set of abilities, along with the proper use of the world's terrain, allows for the effective destruction of enemies, even if it may seem a bit challenging at first. As you progress through the game, however, not only does your character improve, but so does your understanding of the game's mechanics.The game's painterly visual style is very pleasing. Characters, locations and effects are well done and stand out for their originality. The beautiful animated cutscenes are also worth mentioning, although there aren't many of them. The music in the game is wonderful - melancholic and effectively conveys the atmosphere of western post-apocalypse and hopelessness. I particularly enjoyed the mechanic of searching for new music tapes scattered around the world and listening to them on the player while riding a motorbikeNow for the aspects of the game that players may not like. The general description of the quests is well written, but the description of the specific task is often vague, which can make it difficult to complete the quest. For example, a quest may tell you to go to a certain place and find an item, but not give the exact location. This requires careful exploration of the location, which is fine if it is unexplored, but usually these are locations that have been fully explored several times and the item was not there before, or was non-interactive and seen as a decoration. There are also sometimes problems with the detection of interactive items, which can make finding quest items even more difficult. I had a situation where I couldn't find a quest item for a long time, even though I was driving right by it, because it looked like a normal decoration. In addition, quest items can be sold by merchants and are visually indistinguishable from other consumables, making them difficult to find, especially early in the game. The rewards for additional quests are usually small and insignificant.Bosses are not a strong aspect of the game. In fact, their attacks can be quite monotonous. Some bosses follow a pattern: dodge their attacks until the boss exposes his vulnerable spot for a hit. I expected a lot more from the last boss. In general, the bosses in the game are not bad, but they lack variety and complexity.As a result, I liked this game, with its beautiful hand-drawn visuals, great music, interesting story and lore, good and unusual gameplay, and was able to get into it and enjoy it. However, due to some of its features, it may not be suitable for everyone, but those who can accept it will get their share of emotion and enjoyment. I recommend trying the demo version first, which will give you a better understanding of the game. Also, if you buy the game, all your progress from the demo will be transferred to the main game.

_childDocuments_.review: A prime example of the maturation of the indie scene and the creativity it can offer when devs roam away from traditional genre and subject combinations. Laika is short, sweet, and to the point, though perhaps too short overall for what's commonly expected of most games today. It's metroidvania aspects are also somewhat weak, with only three real abilities gating progression, the first two being mostly abandoned once you've used them to deal with the immediate utility-gate. It's also quite linear, and lacks optional exploration and gameplay. However, this is made up for by a very tight, very gripping story packed with emotion and mystery. You find yourself drawn into the tragedies, big and small, afflicting Laika and the people she lives with and meets. And the familiar world Laika inhabits is poked through with oddities. The skeletons of mountain sized creatures clash with modern feeling ruins and odd technology. The implications of a deeply troubled world rife with racial violence that ultimately culminated in a nuclear armageddon so long ago that nobody uses the names of the places they live anymore, just the purposes. And through it all is a distinct supernatural presence. And to accompany all of this is an absolutely first class soundtrack, tailor made to tug at your heartstrings. However, the cutscenes and the music get cut off several times throughout the game, damaging their impact somewhat.To conclude, Laika possesses creative, if simple gameplay, but a fascinating setting, an emotional story, and fantastic music make it worth your time. Like me, you'll probably be looking forward to a possible sequel one day.

_childDocuments_.review: I believe I kept this mostly spoiler free, as in no major reveals that aren't within the first 3-4 hrs of this game.Long story short, this is still an AMAZING GAME! But I give it a 7 / 10. You can read it below.Visuals - 10/10Starting off strong, I have to be honest about the art style. The very first showcase of this game in its trailer had an amazing 2D animation team and that alone captivated me immediately.While historically, and rightfully so, games that have amazing marketing animations rarely translate to the game this one does not disappoint. I can’t exactly explain how or why, but the in game style and the animation just goes SO hard. Every location is breathtaking, every character is so well designed, and the aesthetic is nailed the WHOLE WAY THROUGH. Laika, while it has its faults, is nothing short of an artistic marvel of a game. I would easily take screenshots and make them just static backdrops they’re so amazing. If you are a curator of artistic games, this one should easily make your collection. It gives me that SUPERGIANT GAMES feel, like how Hades is drawn and realized that hits me with really vibrant colors and a captivating use of heavy lineart variation. It is truly worth playing if not just for the sheer beauty of its art team.Sound - 8/10The sound design here, like any platformer, is quite good. They aren’t as complex as say a typical first or third person game would have to add a munch of music and folly to, but what it lacks in sound complexity it makes up for in its soundtrack. Beicoli does an amazing job at filling the role of a musical marvel lost to time, left with nothing but tapes for you to collect on your journey. At first I thought it would hinder the experience, having such a small collection of music at the start of the game, but boy was I wrong. It became a sweet little treat to add to this collection, finding a new music piece here and there to add to the in-game playlist. They fit the atmosphere so well, and while not all of them made my favorites they were a welcome addition to the otherwise barren wastelands. I gave this one an 8/10 because you can only do so much with sound in a scroller in my experience but for what it does it does it very well.Gameplay - 7/10I will admit, I am not a very good platformer gamer. I never really liked the meticulous timing and precise movement they required and that deterred me from a lot of what that genre had to offer. With Laika though, it was genuinely a fun and intriguing system! The first of its kind as noted as a Morovania, a play on metroidvania, where you have to control the orientation of your model, speed and angle all at once which can take a quick minute to get the hang of. It felt unique and relatively challenging at first, but when you did finally get the hang of it it was an amazing experience to master! From last minute parries, to daring flips and near-misses it feels so good for something so innovative for this genre. And while I praise it for what it achieves, I have it knocked down to 7/10 because it left me wanting just a little bit more than what it gave me. The system works mostly flawlessly, with a few minor challenges with how it registers overlapping paths and elevation. But even with that aside with a little learning, I felt a little cheated with the progression of abilities. Namely, the grappling hook. I think it was a missed opportunity to have it merely serve a situational purpose leaving it rarely ever used for things other than to pull a pillar, drag a head, or carry the ONE bomb area. When I saw it in the control menu I thought to myself, this would be so cool to be able to attach to a wall or ceiling and then use it to swing with momentum to reach new areas and such. You can imagine my disappointment afterward. I just think that extra touch could have added so much more not only to the depth of gameplay but also the level design, which is why I had to kick this one down a bit. Otherwise, I had the most fun in the final few hours with the nitro booster which added a whole new strategy to the game that was incredibly enjoyable. Despite it all, what IS here works well but it could have gone the extra mile and really dove into some untapped potential to be an amazingly unique game.Story - 7/10The story, while I am a sucker for the parent-child motif in a narrative, also left me wanting. That isn’t to say I didn’t enjoy it or that it wasn’t good, merely that I just wanted MORE. I wanted more dialogue from Laika and while I understand the idea that she's a short spoken, aggressive, and damaged individual I think it left her a little more underdeveloped than she could be. Things like more history on the blood curse, more about what Maya was like and what she learned before taking the role. Overall just more to really dive into these characters, the lore, and the setting. While environmental storytelling can do some of this, I think it missed a great opportunity for some good dialogue, character growth (or degradation), and some great story beats that could really hit harder on the heartstrings. Halfway through the game we got a good chunk of flashbacks and great information that had me tearing up, but after that there was a lot of missing immersion that could have truly driven this game home. My bias to the trope let me pass this with a 7 of 10, but for most others it’s probably a 6. But again, despite it all I did still enjoy the story. I just really wish there was more to it, or at the very least expanded more on what it has.Atmosphere - 9/10The atmosphere is absolutely amazing. It nails the wasteland vibe PERFECTLY. I love the nitty gritty survival depression they have here. It's consistent and uniform and I praise it for that. Nothing happens where the world or an area feels out of place. The world feels constantly oppressed but also lively with a smidgeon of hope. It reminds me so much of Mad Max and I love it for it. Everything from the need for resources, crafting, the grim uncertainty of its residents, and the wild biomechanical creature mutation stuff all felt right at home in this world and honestly, I want nothing more than to spend MORE time here. It captivates the mind and setting in a way that is both familiar and foreign in its own right.
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: Laika: Aged Through Blood is one of those games that come along once in awhile and does something incredible.An utterly inspired game that feels like every bit was done out of the love of creation, I can feel the love the developers had when making this one. It almost threw me at the beginning, bucked off the bull but I am so glad I climbed back up because the next 16 hours flew by. After getting thrown for a loop about what I was getting into in the opening act and then hitting roadblock after roadblock and dying over and over again in the subsequent level I was close to giving up. That's part of the trick with something wholly unique, there isn't much to pull from, you're learning something completely new. And Laika is a punishing game. One shot and you're dead, but thankfully so is everything else. Learning to control the bike is everything here, once it becomes second nature, you'll be able to approach any challenge and topple it. I front load all of that because the gameplay might frustrate at first but I beg people willing to try to keep going because these characters and this story is so profoundly heart wrenching. The complete package here is entirely worthwhile from the music to the art to the writing. So many tiny little details fill in the world and the story, offering insight to these people and their struggles. So please, give Laika a try, it's difficult and it's different, but it's so good and I'm thankful I kept at it.

_childDocuments_.review: Oh hello, chad who read negative reviews.Imagine this: you are riding along the promenade, the waning sun blankets the great beyond with a reddish tint, the sound and sight of the sea soothing your every senses, you hear the rubber wheel grinding the pavement, reminding of your presence in this world. Some effort is required to navigate the obstacles along the path, but that is fine, rhythmic, even. Nice and lonely, serene and hopeful. This is a very fine evening purchased with your time....except it isn't that fine. It was a bumpy ride, there are a million tiny annoying gameplay things that compound into a somewhat frustrating experience. Detours, retreads, backpedals, blindsides, accidents... all too common. Some segments are great, but many parts of the overall circuit are ultimately lacking. Yet, rear your head beyond the road and you are reminded of the phenomenal wasteland sights, interesting locals who invited you over for dinner to share their somber stories, and that nice bittersweet lady song echoing in the distance. Man, why? Why the finer things in life gotta suck? Why isn't the Lord more forgiving? Am I born with skill issue? This is not fai--Here comes the epiphany: Oh god, they ran out of money! The project is rushed! They are stretched thin! We've been riding in circles for the final hours! The end of the road still got some of that orange barrier lying around! No way! That blows! Curse this money driven world! Another greatness robbed from this plane of existence! Justice for coyote mum and her pup!Please fund a sequel, or an expansion. Buy this game. Endure it or let it sit in your backlog, idc. Give them yo monies.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the best games I've ever played. The music, the art, the gameplay, the story...Gah, just play it! It's HUGE! And cheap even without a sale! Her personality is so strong and her character so well written, I LOVED being in her shoes.What a brilliant, experimental and daring game. I've never seen anything like it before.

_childDocuments_.review: There aren't enough words to express how much I love Laika. This game is the only game that's made me cry so far in my almost a decade of active gaming. This game's music hit me so hard that I teared up listening to just a single song from its soundtrack after finishing it.Loss, life, death, mourning, moving forward, fighting tooth and nail against any odds. It's a soulslike in its depressiveness, but there is genuine hope for the future built within that core of pain.Of course there are pain points. One of the bosses in what I feel is "Act 2" is not communicated how to fight it and ruined an important emotional beat for me. Laika's behavior in "Act 3" is questionable and frustrating, yet also understandable if you squint. A lot of quests are backtracking and fetch quests, but I don't really care.I love this game. I will never not love this game. It has soul, passion, and genuine humanity pumped into every little detail. I'm unsure if I can bring myself to play it again simply because of how good it is.

_childDocuments_.review: Be sure to give the demo a go to see if the gameplay clicks with you before buying.As others have already said, the game is like Trials+Guns+Mad Max esque story. I don't necessarily think the game is bad, I mean I bought it cause it looked fun and there are moments where I was having fun shooting birds and doing flips. It just kind of surprised me with a lot of other things I wasn't expecting and personally found too annoying to continue and finish.First, the world is like a big metroid style map and has quests. Kinda threw me off a bit cause I thought the game would lend itself well to a level based format. I really wasn't expecting to have to do so much back and forth between place to place and it gets tiring very quickly. In other metroidvanias this isn't a huge deal, but in Laika you're doing this on a Trials bike and starts to get annoying very quickly when you bump your head and die when all you're trying to do is drive back to a place you just were.The game offers fast travel but is very quickly undercut by the fact that it's use is tied to a resource. You have to collect wax and craft candles to be able to fast travel and I have no clue why. While playing I saved up some money and wanted to fast travel home to purchase an upgrade only to learn I had 0 candles. I had 30 pieces of wax but because I didn't realize the only place you can make more candles is at home base I was outta luck. I was annoyed and mainly just wondering why a basic game mechanic has to be tied to a resource to begin with. The wax isn't exactly rare, so it just feels like adding an unnecessary step to basic game mechanic. Then there's money and resources. The game uses a similar mechanic to that of Hollow Knight where when you die you lose a portion of your saved up money. If you can get back to the spot where you died you can pick it up again and there will be no loss. Otherwise if you die too much you'll just lose it for good. A mechanic that I think works fine for other games, but that's because there's a margin for error. If I died in Hollow Knight I can try and get back to that spot and have health as a buffer to help me get there through enemies and obstacles. As long as I don't make too many mistakes I can get back. Laika doesn't have health. Bullets, explosions, head hits the ground, those all result in instant death. There's no buffer, you make one mistake and that's it, so if you die in an awkward spot around enemies or difficult terrain you kinda just have to accept you're gonna lose your money.Again, I don't really think the game is bad, it just has some really odd design choices here and there. And at least for me, the annoyances of those choices simply reached a point where I felt the frustration outweighed the fun.

_childDocuments_.review: As stated in the opening load screen for Laika Aged Through Blood I feel it important to put at the top: "Warning this game contains depictions of extreme acts of violence towards children and suicide, and mention of sexual assault, which some players may find distressing."Laika Aged Through Blood is an emotionally devastating story about a Coyote named Laika, one in a long bloodline of women cursed to live. die. repeat, putting this mother of one on the front line of protecting her tribe from the Birds: a group of Zealous Militants who drove the world to nuclear ruin. The game is not shy about graphic violence, from the explosion of gibs when you shoot an enemy to the scenes of physical violence toward children in the pre warning (the disclaimer scenes are thankfully sparingly used and not a common theme you'll witness throughout the game).Beyond the violence is a beautifully desolate world with a phenomenal art style all brought together by an amazing soundtrack of folk music by Spanish singer Beícoli, be sure to check out her work.  The game is a hybrid of a twin stick Metroidvania and motorcycle control and trick games like Trials Fusion which the devs call a "motorvania" in the most satisfying way. Thematically your bike is a huge part of you and will have to master your balance, between angling the undercarriage of your bike to block bullets and using backflips to reload and frontflips to recharge your bullet parries in combat. Whilst retaining the Metroidvania game plan of learning maps, upgrading, backtracking and reasonably challenging bosses.

_childDocuments_.review: Backpedaled on this one pretty bad...The initial impression for Laika is extremely positive, but once the game starts rolling the frustrations start kicking in.First of all Laika is a very good looking game that radiates the passion that went into creating it. The OST is a longshot from my preference, but it's unique in its own way. The artstyle is unique and elaborate. The gameplay is simple (similar to those 2d flash bike games) and makes good use of the few rules it introduces. It's quite neat. The writing is, if very generous, mediocre. It's your average Deviantart-short story in game form; unnuanced "lol quirky xd" characters set in a universe that is thematically over-exploited.Unfortunately the frustration that started to kick in somewhere halfway in the game became a little too much for me. Laika is a pretty good experience, but it doesn't do a good job at being a good game. It communicates itself strikingly poorly and when met with new maps I constantly ran into (literally) geometry I couldn't see or couldn't make out from the background. There are too many overlapping elements, the camera likes to do its own thing making the player character hard to follow (their color scheme is nigh identical to the background). Color palettes are used inconsistently (one such example is the blue hue used for enemies is identical to the checkpoint. I can't begin to count the times I shot the checkpoint thinking it was an enemy when first appearing). Crafting materials that completely go against the grain and pace of the remainder of the design. Enemy corpses that block shots for no apparent reasons. Overlapping elements you have to shoot DURING boss-fights.It's a little too much of the bad for me. The pricepoint is more than fair, but Laika severely suffers not having had enough time to reflect upon itself. It's been a long time since I've seen a game with this blatantly many issues so prominently displayed.

_childDocuments_.review: I played this when it was released last October. I keep coming back to it when I think about what I love about the medium and how it creates these memorable experiences unlike any other kind of media and I wish more people were still talking about this one so I’m writing a review now. Laika manages to marry the short repeatable loops of games like My Friend Pedro or Celeste, where attempt after attempt and failure after failure bring you closer to a satisfying mastery of a 5-10 second feat, with the more contemplative exploration of a metroidvania. Both feel great and act as great counterbalances to each other as you make your way through Laika’s tale. Occasionally, and in boss battles in particular, the camera can get too far from the character and it becomes difficult to tell which way you’re facing. This can cause you to land on your head despite thinking you were about to nail a flawless landing after pulling off a double front flip and laying waste to the bosses weak points. Despite these occasional frustrations I found flipping around in slow motion over and over until I had mastered the moment largely satisfying. Both the exhilarating fights and the relaxing platforming exploration are wonderfully accompanied by the games almost entirely diegetic soundtrack written and performed by real wold artist Beícoli/in fiction artist Beicoli who’s poignant lyrics and haunting vocals beautifully if sometimes heavy handedly reinforce the games themes of parental anxiety about the things we pass (or try not to pass) down to our children and what that means for any one person caught in the middle of generational pulls. I continue to put the soundtrack on regularly as I’m working or driving. Laika’s dying world is beautifully rendered in hand drawn 2D art. Anthropomorphic animals ,friend and foe, populate the wasteland and lend the story just enough abstraction to really land the metaphor without veering into rote melodrama. The game largely strikes a somber tone which is enforced by contrast with its cartoon aesthetic and remains a world I wanted to keep inhabiting. All of these elements come together to tell a very moving and ultimately hopeful story that I have not been able to let go for the past year and change. I whole heartedly recommend you play this one and I eagerly await whatever these devs decide to do next.
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: Wow... Laika: Aged Through Blood Is a remarkable game! The combat in Laika is fast. you can deflect bullets if you time your drift right. But you have to reload the meter for it by doing a front flip and a back flip to reload. So you're shooting, counting bullets, doing flips and making sure you line up your landing all at the same time. You can use the bottom of your motorcycle to block bullets. I mean it's just so much fun.The story is really good with great writing. From the very beginning you want what Laika (your character) wants, vengeance. And I felt with her almost the whole time and teared twice during this play through. I would have felt connected the whole time but the side quest are kinda pointless. They have some fun interactions with characters but they're mostly all fest quest. And the rewards are crafting supplies and at a certain point you already have more than enough. The characters all stand out from each other. But the game takes it away with Laika, Maya (your mother) and Puppy (your daughter). The art style is phenomenal and the music is astonishing by Beicoli. They even put her in the game which I thought was awesome.I highly recommend Laika: Aged Through Blood.
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot recommend this game enough to someone looking for a good story experience. The dark themes presented in this game are handled flawlessly, the wonderful personalities of each character makes for a welcoming world to learn about, and the beautiful yet often menacing locales tell a grim story of the world through fantastic visual design.There are warnings that the game contains disturbing topics, but any scenes of much darker subjects are either are completely optional or there is very little of it in the main story. Most importantly, they are given the proper degree of detachment from normal gameplay to allow their emotional impact to be given the attention it deserves and present proper character development to Laika.The movement and combat can be rather disorienting at first, but as I kept playing I found a beautiful rhythm which made me feel like an absolute badass. The guns feel great but sadly most of them are better used as special tools or are less effective than what you already are given, making the default revolver my most used weapon for the majority of my playtime. The enemies may sometimes be in some annoying places, and I find some behavior of unique enemy types may sometimes be rather inconsistent, which has been the cause of many deaths. I want to also add that the movement is not well designed for a certain location with one area specific mechanic which I will not spoil, but thankfully it is only used once and then forgotten.

_childDocuments_.review: Enjoying the game so far, the gameplay is fun and the story is interestingThe boss battles are neither, as of now ive stopped playing due to how infuriating the bosses are to the point that I have no idea if they were even playtested at all. The bosses are not hard per say, but each fight is incredibly long and drawn out for the simple sake of it and a lack of variety in the bosses themselves does not make the length of the fight fun, each boss has pretty much 2 attacks (some even have 1) , 3 if you are lucky, and each fight can be minutes long. Coupled with 1 hit to die and no checkpoints makes an otherwise good game and absolute slog. Anyone whos played the game can likely guess what boss has caused me to quit playing, and I likely wont pick it back up until some sort of fix is introduced.Also also, the soundtrack is amazing everywhere but the boss battles, which doesnt help alleviate the tedium of playing one for the 15th time

_childDocuments_.review: Laika: Aged Through Blood is a fantastic little indie game that I almost missed. I was browsing the Steam store one day, bored out of my mind when suddenly I came upon this little masterpiece! Brainwash Gang, a company I had not heard of up until this point have done very well with this one.Not only have they stuck to the Metroidvania formula and made a great game to boot, but they have also gone and invented a whole new hybrid of the genre; Motorvania. This certainly made me smirk at the very least. A game where you are for the most part bound to your motorbike. It combines Bullet Hell elements along with those of the Metroidvania genre to create a truly wonderful game play experience, whether you're achievement hunting, searching for secrets, or gunning it for the end of the game, you will have a great time.The plot of the game hooks you in immediately and along with the music really puts you in the shoes, or in this case on the motorbike of the protagonist. It tugs on my heartstrings every time I hear the music even now.

_childDocuments_.review: tldr: this game is certainly not for everyonein part because the plot is incredibly edgy to the point it's almost funny, but it's well written and will be very immersive for anyone into this kind of setupin part because this explores this new "motorvania" approach to gameplay and it really takes some getting used to, some things are unbalanced and at times it feels frustratingbut this game is still a W despite these things because of its worldbuilding, because of its visual decisions, a smooth experience when you do get used to it and upgrade yourself, and because of its music and sceneryi haven't had experience with bike games before, so when picking this game up i was aware it'll take some adjustments to be able to move properlyand i was right, the  and i got confused a lot between things like reloading my weapons vs changing my own direction, but as you go through the game you do develop muscle memory and overtime it grows from a mildly frustrating control fiddle to cool little scenic tricks and a smooth navigation through the map, especially in lategame when you can combine your skills with the new movement abilitiesit does suck that the  is introduced so late in the game, i think, aside from the places intended specifically for it, it could be beneficial for general terrain navigation earlier on for a more comfortable experience, that is the only gameplay-misplaced ability thoughwith far zoom outs of the camera it was  so i kept dying because what i thought was my wheel turned out to be my headthe amount of blood and explosions on screen also sometimes causes frustrating deaths as you cannot see your character behind them and have to guess which way you're positioned toward the groundthough there is an accessibility option to tweak your collision with the ground, i can't comment on it since i decided to challenge myself and see if it gets better overtime - it kind of does? when  in the second half of the game the sprite becomes more readable and you don't lose track of yourself as much, though it still happened every now and again, i'd say in the end it's a problem of visual designi've never had issues with , probably because whenever i saw anything i instantly shot at it and collected everything i saw - and it resulted in always having plenty of things both for fast travel and for spending on new unlocks, i think i only had to venture out specifically to gather missing resources twice throughout the entire game, and it's really easy too, because every resource's location is mentioned in its descriptionthe  aspect felt kind of redundant, essentially it's temporary boons for money or resource collecting, but it doesn't state clearly enough which parts it enhances and without any visual representation of combo multipliers or upped percentages it feels like it's just running in the background doing its own thingit could benefit from more visibility and from always stating which boon does what in the description instead of just a little icon in my inventory, with a description inaccessible anywhere but the cooking stationsthe little  were neat overall, fetch quests from people where we live were the more engaging kind because they make you go out and explore the world and test your memory and attention in the places you've already been, just hidden enough to not find things instantly but not too far off so that it becomes frustartingbut, any quest outside of those usually came down to simply finding one of the snail merchants and they'd always have the thing you need in their inventory, so all of those quests felt like an afterthoughtgotta say i really like the character design in this gamefinally we get women who are ugly huge crooked and weird and cool that waythere were a lot of neat creative decisions hidden in every character, and it's all organic and fitting to the world they're in, and the world has absolutely stunning scenery in every one of its regions, it's really visible what an incredible work was put into its worldbuilding toothe rusty and dusty postapocalyptic-esque overall tone is really well conveyed through the broken down huge machines and sandy hills and mountains, everything feels really big and really worn and ancienti really wish there was more to the , it's essentially only there for a plot point and you can never come back to it after it's done, but it's not bad, i only want more because it looked really cool and there was a lot of  splattered all over itthe songs set the mood in stone, and they go along great as the theme music of the game, though it'd really benefit the game if there was also more actual background music, especially in the early game when you don't yet have the full song ost on your hands and the few songs looping on and on end up tiring, and there are very few zones in the game where there is some background ost to change up the flow and cleanse your palate so the songs would always hit and feel freshoverall i think this game is really good, it has its flops but they're understandable for exploring a new subgenre, and while they do take away from one's experience it still succeeds through everything else, just short of incredible, great kudos to the devs for making this :]

_childDocuments_.review: Its probably one of the games with the most well made story that i had played without the need to make it super long and complicated. Well worth a play.
