_childDocuments_.review: 100%-ed this in less than a week... what a gameI understand that the controls may be frustrating to some people, but to me they're just so insanely clever and intuitive, and the gameplay feels very smooth once you master them. easily my favorite part of the game besides the story. I mean, backflip to reload, bike deflects bullets, using shotgun recoil for a boost? there's a lot of trial and error, but the game is also VERY generous with its checkpoints, meaning you won't have to travel for ages just to get to retry areas you struggle with.I thoroughly enjoyed my experience with this game, even though some parts were a bit of a slog & some of the boss fights are not really made to best utilize the unique control scheme. the story and beautifully animated cutscenes do make up for the less than good parts of the game imo, but that's not something I'm going to get into - you'll have to check it out for yourself!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: No one asked for Bike Souls, but Laika delivered a masterpiece anyway.Story: Darker than my morning coffee. Stands well on its own.Gameplay: simple yet satisfying with backflip-to-reload. Gratuitous flips translate to more style, more bullets, more combos, more loot... and more deaths. If the game is too hard, liberal use of bullet time and cooking will boost your survivability.Art: Very well polished 2D animations and backgrounds. Anything interactable will have stronger borders and saturation than the foreground, which makes the game easy to parse.Music: Grab those cassettes scattered through the map. Well worth the extra bit of exploration.
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: I want to enjoy this game because it seems like it would have a fun story and the gameplay should be fun.However, the developers did not do a proper job of managing the difficulty level. There's no 'Balance' button to keep you from killing yourself in a required backflip or frontflip if you don't manage your movement. Time only slows down during aiming and that's timed with no way to cancel a shot so you can't use it to properly deal with hails of bullets. You only block bullets with your bike which, while it makes sense, will often leave you either getting shot trying to reload or getting crushed with the bike trying to block a bullet.There are areas where five or more birds can get shots at you with ease, they don't need time to aim and are most likely going to hit you. There's no Melee attack so if you fail to kill a bird and get close, you will die.Most of my deaths, and I got 100 in an hour and a half, were from hitting a platform while trying to do a flip or getting shot in one direction while blocking a shot from another.I want to see the creators of the game play and finish the game without using excessive time grinding out to get upgrades. Until then, I'm done.
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: Dark, Bloody and Violent only begins to describe the psychological mess that is Laika: Aged Through Blood. It's not the extreme acts of violence that get me, it's the Coyote mother out for vengeance and her ability to put down anyone who stands in her way.  From the messed up things the Birds do, to the messed up things that Laika's family and community do to her. You'll be stunned by the story only to feel a twinge of cathartic relief as you take out your frustration on the enemy one shot at a time.  Oh and you do back-flips on your motorbike to reload.
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: OH GOD where should i begin with, this fantastic game first and all i finished the game and i liked it a lot, the presentation the music the gameplay was satisfying, and a lot but one thing that i didn't like at all was the ending was fast and the sacrifice of laika was her son mourning her death with the others in the village and thats it, i hope theres going to be more content for this game like a DLC or aa secret ending because the ending left me with more questions rather then asnwer but still i hope this game gets some content because i loved it a LOT.
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: This game... just wow. I wasn't sure if I was going to like the whole shoot-em-up on a motorcycle gameplay, but it ended up being so much fun. But while the gameplay was unique and enjoyable, it was the story that really kept me playing. I'm very much a fan of story-rich games that make you feel something, and boy oh boy, does this game illicit a lot of emotion. It's a dark and gruesome story that does not pull any punches. The devs did a fantastic job of immersing you in deep, melancholic, sometimes painful, emotions while still telling a story of compassion and love underneath it all. This game isn't going to be for everyone, but for the introspective types who love playing through a great story, I highly recommend it. It's definitely become one of my favorites of all time, and I hope the devs keep telling fantastic stories through the video game medium.
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: it was a great game, very fun it brought back those  motorcycle flash games feel with a fun twist.the story is pretty engaging even though laika was wayy too much of an ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ the whole game,its not bad enough to be a deal breaker tho, its more as an bitter person kinda way. the boss fights get wayy too easy at the end as well too specially the last two.. the crab and the final boss... maybe i was using an exploit in the final boss but idk, just holding the dash to enter bullet time unload all the weapons on the boss then getting away with the invincible dash basically one shotted it.felt like a lot of upgrades where crammed in the end of the game as well, and the game for the final parts does overstay its welcome. great experinece overall tho, gonna keep an eye on these developers.
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: The story of a woman making all the wrong decisions and losing everything in the goal of creating a better world for her daughter.I feel like this game would have benefited from being an RPG, or a movie. The story, character, music, setting themes, ETC is immaculate. I wish I could have had more agency there.  The tactile game play is weak, speaking as someone who loves it. (Go play cyclomaniacs 2 if you want to try out a better version of what this game is going for. It's a free flash game.)If you don't like the motorcycle mechanics immediately, you should know they don't get better as the game progresses. The developers needed to gate you off from specific locations for story reasons. So all forms of mobility up until the very end of the game are fixed in a way that hard limits emergent gameplay. As a result every time you unlock something new, you're instantly disapointed about how niche the use for it is. The grapple hook could be replaced with a key card, and the game wouldn't be much different.Inspite of that, I'd still highly recomend this game for basically everything else.
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: A Very fun game with engaging, fast-paced combat, a great story, good music, and a stunning art style. I feel the difficulty is just right: you will find bosses and certain areas take a few tries to conquer. All of the NPCs feel unique and fun to talk to. I genuinely have nothing bad to say about this game. 10/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: Don't wanna mention more about its atmosphere, music or stylish art.Also don't wanna waste more words describing its awesome motor moves and shooting experience.What I want to say is the plot and lines. Occupation army killing civilians(even children) without a care or even just for fun. Who claim themselves as 'saviors', 'future builders' turn out to be nothing more than murderers. Don't all these sound too familiar to you? The game itself creating these plots originally suggesting America, but geometric politics gives us a more  clear subject for this suggestion: Israel.Continuous bombardments and designated accurate airstikes upon freaking EVERYTHING. The young, the old, the weak, the pregnant, the wounded, Israel intentionally strikes them without even the slightest care. Those who choose to stay get killed. Those who choose to leave still get killed on the extraction route designated by Israel itself. Those too sick ,too old, or too wounded who cannot leave shortly get killed. Bloody, even those who come to help the unarmed still get killed. UN buildings and workers, global reporters, local valiant rescuers and doctors all get killed.Friends, 'The birds' isn't a game concept anymore. 'The birds' have already been in our world. Like a disease, like a plague.

_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: great art style and animation, the gameplay and its mechanics is hands down awesome, the story itself (if you can get past some of the really grim stuff thats on display and implies at times) is pretty goods and was pretty intriguing. My only complaint is, please, release the soundtrack on steam because its absolutely beautiful.
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: Impressive story, world building, artstyle and exploration. This emulates the same feeling of taking a long drive to clear you head.The action is great when it works, but the game's main flaw is forcing the player to do a back flip on their motorcycle in order to reload their weapon. There may or may not be mounds nearby for when you need to get up in the air in order to do the back flip. The closest mound might be a long ways back and you'll have to back track just to kill one enemy because you ran out of bullets. It's very rare that I stick with a game with this big of a core issue, but the story really carried the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: Its sincerely just a classic. There is nothing else like it, and what it does, it does good. Some may find some parts a pain, where others don't, and vice versa. Some may have gripes with the story while others fall in love with it. Go in blind. Laugh at what you find funny, get upset and what you hate, take in the world set out for you, rage quit and take a break. Enjoy it for what it is. It really is just a classic through and through.

_childDocuments_.review: Why is there no fast travel point at the "Point of no return"? Why can you not teleport to large fast travel totems from any point in the map, but only when at another totem?Why is the final ending cutscene so short that you´ll miss it if you blink?Why can we not see the impact of our actions after the ending credits (like to see Where We Live and the Characters we helped throughout optional missions)?Why does the game repeatedly start Laika floating in the air during the final boss´ speech and then forces the player to do reload the game multiple times?Why does the exhaust from cooling fans not kill you if you drive through it, but becomes instant death fog if you just as much as graze the aim button? Is it because the game slows down time while aiming, and it then falsely interprets slowed down time?Why does this game leave more questions than answers?Oh, and why do the skydiving BIRDS in the last game segment wear PARACHUTES?
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: Give me Mad Max, but give it a Native American influence with a killer soundtrack and breathtaking hand-drawn landscapes. I haven't had this much fun with a Metroidvania since Hollow Knight. Controls take some getting used to, but when it works, you feel like the coolest thing on the planet.--edit--I've played a bit more, and I'm still going to recommend this, but not as highly. The first 3 hours were polished and fantastic, but almost immediately after that, I ran into some really dissonant game design. Areas shrink and the game morphs into a precision platformer with Happy Wheels physics. Levels feel good only in one direction, which would be fine if there were shortcuts at the end to get you back to the start. Toeing the gas to gently bump your way backwards through a Sonic the Hedgehog level is exactly as much fun as it sounds, but never fear, the enemies all respawn behind you. I'm still playing, and still enjoying, but much less enthused than before.
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: Laika's gameplay is the real selling point. "Excitebike" with guns feels natural yet challenging-- it's hard to master but very rewarding every step of the way. Oftentimes I found myself revisiting old areas just to drive around and shoot things, unmotivated by any questline. I had never done that in a game before! The art direction & theming complete the experience, telling an emotional story about womanhood. The game has some problem points (sometimes lacked readability, control customization like 90% of the way there) but it's otherwise a great game.
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: Finished the game in 14 hours. The game starts off really fun and engaging, you learn more and more about the story, explore the map and learn new game mechanics, but i gotta say after a certain point i felt like the tempo really suffered. Once you have explored a majority of the map the quests kinda make you just ride along the same routes, and the fast travel points are pretty scarce. The good thing is you get to listen to the awesome soundtracks (which i even listened to on spotify on multiple occasions, just because they were so good and stuck in my ear). To fellow ultrawide gamers; the game doesnt support ultrawide so youre stuck with black bars, which kinda makes sense since it would be pretty broken to see further away.All in all, i recommend Laika. Its fun and sometimes just hard enough to get your blood flowing. 20 bucks is a good price for what you get IMO. The storystelling, atmosphere and music are all top notch.
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: So happy I found this in an Iron Pineapple video! Beautiful game, that has a wonderful story and characters, unique gameplay that you can master and an awesome soundtrack that I'll listen to even though I've just beaten this game. There's frustrating moments in here, but if you like souls-games and a bit harder games this is a great one. The weapons are fine, but I finished it basically only playing 3 and not feeling the need to experiment with them as it worked really well. A few parts were there in the end where the polish from the start was missing where I glitched through or into things 2-3 times, but restarting the game fixed all of that. I wish there were a bit more abilities that you get to move around in the levels, but you only get 2 really. The wheelie to go up a track is also sometimes a bit frustrating until you get the hang of it and I had some problems in the beginning seeing if Laika was turned correctly.All of that said: it will be difficult to beat this game for my game of the year, because it's so darn beautiful and the levels are really enjoyable. I would love to have a sequel, It was a great fun to play and really really enjoyable. I really recommend it to anyone that's fine with trials controls and has a soft spot for Souls-likes! You can beat it in ~20 hours, I took a bit longer, grinding and so on because it was just so enjoyable! I'm happy that I live in a time where such games get made!

_childDocuments_.review: Solid gameplay that is simultaneously rewarding and infuriating with it's motorcross style movement, the game always feels good to play. As good as the gameplay is it was the soundtrack, and surprisingly the story that kept me playing. It's an incredibly dark tale from within the first 30 seconds, but by god it's told effectively through it's characters. By the end of a playthrough you'll have a good understanding of the character's motivations, a grip on the combat and controls, and definitely a favorite song. Mine's "The Whisper".There're a number of people who complain about the story and ending. For people who say the game has bad storytelling, I just don't see it. If you show me the sprite for a character we've spoken to I have a good shot at telling you about their character, and how Laika views or interacts with them. For people who complain about the ending,
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really cool game! Contrary to criticism I'm seeing, the gunplay and traversal are all very responsive and fluid, and relies pretty hard on good reaction times and figuring out good rotation. I'd say the block area of your bike is unclear at first since it seems to be slightly smaller than your bike, but other than that I'm finding this very enjoyable so far.There is one caveat in that the speed feels a bit sluggish at times, but I suspect there will be changes to that as I play more and upgrade my weaponry. This is SOMETHING of a metroidvania, after all, so there's bound to be some upgrades.The art is also positively gorgeous, the apocalyptic setting and desperation of the world reminds me heavily of LISA: the Painful RPG, but drawn by a far more accomplished artist. Characters are all memorable designs, ranging from a one-armed man playing guitar with his foot to the wisened old town chief in his wheelchair of bone and car parts.There's also an interesting mechanic where eating/cooking meals gives you timed buffs that do small things like increase combat rewards or combo multipliers.The level design is also fantastic, there's a clear intended flow at all times and some of the platforming challenges it asks are a good challenge. It makes it a point to never ask too much of you, always making it clear where you should be going. If anything, the level design only clashes in how gorgeous it is as you zoom by it. There were several moments where I just wanted to stop mid-combat and appreciate the background I was currently orchestrating a tornado of carnage through, but alas that momentary distraction would be enough to scatter myself to that tumultuous wind.Play this, it's quite good and if you're an artist you'll see a LOT you can learn from. This is a master class in effective use of art!
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: Plays like those old motorcycle flash games but you've also got a gun. It is very difficult at some points as you try to keep your aim, dodge enemy bullets, manage your orientation as you flip to reload, and avoiding hitting your head and dying all while moving at a very fast pace. However, save points are a dime a dozen so you still progress through hundreds of deaths and its very gratifying when you do get past a tough spot. Overall its got great visuals and very satisfying game play, definitely worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start this review off by saying how gorgeous of a game this is. I was immediately roped in by the art style and smooth animation, clearly the devs put in a lot of passion and work into this game. Although admittedly the game may not be for everyone as its unorthodox method of reloading and traversal is certainly something to get used to. I highly encourage you, reader, to download the demo and give it a try! If you like it, you're in for a treat! WHERE WE EXPLAINLAIKA is, as the devs put it, a 'MOTORVANIA!' Haha, It's basically a Metroidvana with a motorcycle, you can expect the same beats as any other metroidvania with this game. Progressing through areas and unlocking new abilities to unlock other areas of the map as the story goes along. The map is littered with resource nodes you can shoot to gather materials to upgrade or craft new weapons which also act as said upgrades for methods of traversal. One thing i really like about this game, like any good Metroidvania, is that you get a LOT of utility out of your weapon since they act both as your methods of killing and in the case of the Shotgun, your doublejump! Even as you unlock new weapons and abilities, your older weapons don't loose any utility, most enemies except for bosses are one shot, so no matter what weapon you use, all will be effective! This game requires a good level of strategic thinking, as you can only reload your weapons by doing a backflip off a ramp or a ledge, meaning if you rush into an engagement without thinking or picking important targets, you'll be out of ammo, or you'll misplace your shots by taking out less threatening enemies! Your bike is your shield, and using it to block fire is always effective, you can even drift and deflect the enemy round back to them! LAIKA has a soulslike mechanic, where once you die, your drop your currency and you'll need to fight back through hoards of enemies to retrieve your lost Viceria, you can craft various food items to give bonuses to the amount of Viceria you collect, or the amount of resources you get, or get a double parry charge, etc etc. A BIIIIIG note should be made on the music and the soundtrack, written and sung by an ingame character named "Beicoli," It really is a wonder to listen to. WHERE WE STORYTELLLaika's story takes place in a post apocalyptic setting, in the lands simply known as "The Wasteland." It's a tale as old as time, a jaded survivor of the wastes who simply wants to keep her friends and family safe and has become an excellent killer by doing exactly that. Laika possesses the curse passed down her mother which makes her immortal, each time she is slain, she rises again from Shrines spread across the Wastes. With her skills gained over the years and this power at her disposal, its up to Laika to defend her village from the onslaught of the Imperialist Birds. Laika's story, while on the more minimal side, is presented excellently and while I would have enjoyed a more worldbuilding, games like these don't require it to tell the story they want to tell. Quirky side characters fill the wastes as this games takes a more comical approach to the seriousness of a Post-Apocalypse setting, you can do sidequests for the villagers in your village and help mend old scars. Laika's story is solid, with a great beginning, middle, and end. I hope that we get another game in this universe, 'PUPPY: SECOND BLOOD?' haha.WHERE WE CAST JUDGEMENTOverall, Laika is a solid experience with satisfying gameplay and a complete story with adorable, funny, and heartstring pulling moments. Mitzfing gives this a 8/10 with a FUN Seal of approval!
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: I keep coming back to the word "singular."  Laika stands completely alone in what it's doing.There's a pretty good Metroidvania in here.  The waypoints are a bit spread out, there were a few points in the midgame where I felt like I was backtracing a bit too much to tick every sidequest and exploration piece, and it's not always clear that you need an upgrade to get to location and that you're just not meant to be able to make that jump right now.It's got Excitebike in its blood.  Am I the age for NES nostalgia?  Absolutely.  It's great.It's got that excellent and fully present soundtrack.  Like something Darren Korb would do for Supergiant, not in its style, but in its exquisite prominence.It's got a protagonist and a world brimming with rage, worry, and sorrow, and yeah, I get feeling that way too.But this game is more than the sum of those parts.  It's brought everything together for, yes, a singular experience.  You should play this game, not only because it's excellent (and it is), but especially because there's nothing else out there like it.
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: Tight controls, and you feel like a god when you string together a good combo of shots, kills, reloads, blocks and deflects. Super killer soundtrack too, and a great story. Some of the level design can be a bit tedious, and there were a few minor camera bugs where you had to reload / suicide to be able to fix, but nothing egregious. I think this game was worth the full price of admission, and I wish the devs the best in their future games.
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic game with a fantastic soundtrack.Be warned: The game can be very difficult.It's the first motor-vania. Balance is of utmost importance ala Trials, but so is making sure every shot is pitch perfect.Laika isn't perfect, there's definitely some rough edges and at times it feels more motor than vania, but it is firing on all cylinders at all times. The gameplay offers a unique spin on traditional platformers and metroidvanias that never feels like it overstays its welcome. In fact the longer you play the game, you get better at controlling the bike, and then pulling off the moves you need for the mechanics (backflips to reload guns, frontflips to reload parries, wheelies, blocking with the bottom of the bike) starts to feel natural.Beyond the gameplay Laika offers a feast for the eyes and ears. The artists did a wonderful job in bringing this post-apocalyptic anthropomorphic world to life. Every character in the game is dripping with visual flair and are well written as well.And the soundtrack. Oh. My. God. Beicoli is absolutely wonderful on every track. She IS the music of the game. I'm no music buff so I can't exactly describe what it is that makes the soundtrack so beautiful, but every single track feels fitting. The OST doesn't waste a single second and as you ride across the wastes, collecting tapes and fulfilling Laika's journey, it is impossible not to jam, cry, and feel pumped with the tracks that Beicoli has produced. I regularly listened to the OST to and from work for a month after finishing the game. I would put Beicoli's OST for Laika among my favorite video games OSTs: (Insert any of Supergiants OSTs), Doom 2016 & Eternal.Laika is a wonderful game and despite some frustrations and a few wonky design choices, it is a game I will remember fondly.
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: I'm 45 minutes in, still playing, and damn I am HOOKED! This is one of the most intense, emotional stories I've encountered in a long time. I'm totally a psych/horror/dystopian/drama fan and holy crap, this game hits the mark in a lot of ways. I've already shed tears, the game-play itself is smooth and fun (challenging and frustrating at times, which is good!) and I'm so sucked into this story I just KNOW there will be more tears! Mix Borderlands, Castlevania, Contra and Redwall and you MIGHT get close to the spirit of this game. x] It's phenomenal!
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: Laika: Aged Through Blood has been one of my favorite games this year, with it's well drawn art style to pull you into it's many interesting locales, fast-paced action that makes you feel like a god once you get a grasp of the controls, and all the characters you meet- and lose along the way, make for a meaningful and sad story that I won't be forgetting for a long time.Not to mention how well it does as a Metroidvainia, with each little choice you take to explore having an impact in some way, be it an upgrade that changes how you roam the Wastelands or a little thought in the back of your head, I at least always felt like it was worth my while. There's much more I could say about this game, but I think it's worth discovering for yourself. Highly recommend in all regards.The only downside to this game is that the soundtrack isn't available for me to purchase by itself yet.
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: Although I'm not the target demographic for the game's story, I still absolutely loved it and everything else in this game. Combat felt awesome when mastered and the world building is just awesome. I loved slowly bringing things together, like puppy's trinket collection or the Wastelanders. However, this game isn't perfect. The bosses (especially the final one) felt very underwhelming and didn't bring a good challenge. I feel that the ending didn't provide enough closure, and could of had at least a longer cut scene or something. I also didn't enjoy seeking the merchant for like 4 different quests. Overall, 9.8/10, could of had some improvements, but overall incredibly good.
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: I was on the fence though most of this but I've just had enough and gave up. After the initial excitement wares off everything becomes so tedious, back tracking + collecting resources feels so unnecessarily time consuming. I usually play games consistently until I beat them but I've gotten so annoyed and fed up that I've taken multiple week breaks from the game, only for me to give up in the last area and just watch the end. It really seems like they focused on story too much as the game play feels lacking. Too many depressing things happen for you to care once your able to predict every story beat like "oh that guys gonna be dead when i get back", "that guys gonna be dead when i get there", or "go to place for good thing but find BaAaD thing happen". No map markers for quests, resources, or anything for that matter.
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to recommend this game, but I couldn't personally get past its flaws. I don't think it's worth playing.Pros:* Real edgelord dialogue, game is very visceral and I don't think the writers felt like they had to hold anything back* Excellent animation, lots of shocking hyperviolence in cutscenes* The motorcycle gimmick is really creative (unfortunately becomes a con later)* Overall art and presentation is solid. Themes and atmosphere is consistent through the entire game.Cons* The movement with the motorcyle is sluggish. It takes seconds to complete a jump, you have limited control in the air, and there's jumps everywhere. Traversing the map was not fun after the first few hours, made worse by...* Too few travel points. Want to get that one item at the corner of the map? It'll take you 7-10 minutes to get there. This, and sluggish movement really don't work well in a metroidvania. Hollow knight also had few fast travel points, but you had so many things to whack and platforming in between areas to mitigate the pain.* Many of the bosses are autoscrollers and those are just not fun. You miss a jump, you start over. The lighthouse boss took me an embarrassingly long time to beat because I kept zoning out, it was so boring.* The music is not bad, but not really in my taste. Early in you have few songs and it was jarring hearing the first 2-3 tracks repeated in early exploration.

_childDocuments_.review: Laika: Aged Through Blood is a mixed bag of an experience, although it's one I would ultimately recommend due to its unique motorbike gameplay.The gameplay: the motorbike is the game's most standout feature, and I would say it delivers in all the ways that matter. Getting used to the controls and reload mechanics has a bit of a learning curve, but once mastered the game is very fluid and fun to control. Both you and the enemies die in a single hit, so the game stays challenging throughout, but riding through an area flawlessly while gunning down all the bad guys as soon as they appear onscreen while doing a backflip on the bike never stops making you feel like a badass.The story: Laika tries to tell a somber and mature story, but frequently stumbles  in ways that makes the script come out as amateurish and even a little cringeworthy at times. When it works it can tug at your heartstrings, but when it doesn't it will leave you scratching your head and wondering just what the writers were thinking. For the most part, the main plot tries to impose a sad and oppressing atmosphere; however, most of the side characters you meet around town and throughout your travels are zany looney toons characters that have exactly one character trait or verbal tick, such as considering everything to be "hilarious!" or being a Karen that complains about absolutely everything, which results in a tonal dissonance that pulls the player out of the experience.The dungeons: All the main dungeons in Laika are very well-designed, featuring plenty of navigational puzzles built around a central mechanic exclusive to that level. They're definitely a highlight of the game.The sidequests: sidequests are almost universally worthless in this game. 9 times out of 10 they consist of fetch quests that will have you travel to levels you've already completed to pick up items you could see on your first visit through the area but were not allowed to interact with originally. Even worse, since every secondary character is a cartoon parody of themselves, almost none of them have any narrative or emotional payoff and they will almost always get brushed aside as a joke that made you waste your time. And to make things even worse, most of the time the rewards consist of useless cooking resources or upgrade materials. I would recommend ignoring most sidequests and sticking to the main story for this game.The music: The OST in this game is fantastic and very atmospheric. One of the central collectibles in Laika are music cassettes which you can then listen to in the overworld while riding your bike. Pretty much all of them are very moody and very atmospheric songs and I was always excited to come across a new piece.The verdict: Laika is a very interesting and unique game you should play if you're a fan of metroidvanias or want to play a game with a unique central mechanic of riding bikes. The main quest is solid, but the side quests are almost universally worthless. The writing tries to be serious and emotional but suffers from a lot of tonal dissonance and come across as amateurish a lot of the time. I would recommend wishlisting Laika and picking it up on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I’ll start this review by saying that Laika: Aged Through Blood is the best game I’ve played in quite a while. This is the first time I’ve felt compelled to pour my heart and soul into a review, and Laika deserves it 100%.This game first caught my eye while I was browsing Spotify, believe it or not. After a few hours of listening to the soundtrack, I knew I had to give it a shot. Music and sound design is a big deal to me, and is one of the main things I look for when selecting games, and Beícoli has created a true masterpiece. From the heartwarming thoughts of wonder in “Playing in the Sun” to the melancholy lyrics of “The Last Tear” to the pangs of regret in “No Return”, this soundtrack will tear your heart to pieces like no other. It complements the narrative of the game so well, matching perfectly with the somber storyline.Speaking of which, I’ll go so far as to say that this game has the best story out of everything I’ve played so far. You’re dropped right into a brutal and equally powerful scene of destruction and loss, and the game doesn’t stop there. This game will make you cry, and its continual onslaught lends particularly well to the perpetual feeling of hopelessness the village's inhabitants express in every interaction. You are the only member of your village that they can spare to fight the bird’s military power, and you owe it to them to make every battle count.The gameplay has also amazed me. Combat and movement are entirely based around your motorcycle. Put it in between you and enemies to block bullets, reload your weapons with a tactical backflip, and parry your bullets right back at the birds with your wheels. Once you’ve gotten the basics down, every encounter is a stylish mix of finesse and vengeance. On top of that, the terrain allows quite a bit of creativity when it comes to pulling off whatever vindictive plan you have in store.Overall, Laika: Aged Through Blood is a true gem of a game, and I’m so glad I had the opportunity to try it. I urge you to treat yourself to what it has in store. I can't recommend it enough.Laika is as heartfelt as it is gut-wrenching, and that’s precisely what makes it so beautiful.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Buy this game, i got it for $15 i would pay $30. Story 10/10, Soundtrack 10/10, Game play 9/10, progression 8/10, Art 10/10I want to start this with a message for the Devs. Great job, holy crap this was an experience. I will be buying more of your games, like right now.This games setting is like a mixture of WW2 and old western. Its story is dark, gory, and sad as are the side quests. there are plenty of light-hearted moments to find, but over all the game was surprisingly deep. I bought this game after seeing a small clip on YouTube and figured it looked fun to mess about in for a few hours. I soon got addicted to the characters and story telling. The soundtrack is one of my favorites and has been added to my Spotify playlists. i rarely feel bad or attached to characters in most games, but this game had me genuinely caring about its world, plights, and characters, and the ending brought a tear to my eyes. the gameplay is pretty fun and simple, once you get over the learning curve, it is deeply satisfying. A perfect combination of difficulty and responsive gameplay, leaves you feeling like a bad a** when you flawlessly clear a group of enemies with out losing momentum. this little 35+ hour game is a recommendation to anyone who likes skill shooters, and good storytelling.

_childDocuments_.review: I love hard games. I've played and beat Celeste, Cuphead, sekiro (platinum), I've SL1'd dark souls 3, blasphemous 1/2, lies of P Ng+, etc. I don't mind playing and replaying sequences over and over again to get it right. But after dying 50 times to the lighthouse boss I find myself not frustrated, but genuinely exhausted and uninterested to make another go. It's a shame because the story is great and there are some fantastic moments in the game. Read the positive reviews if you want to understand why people love it. Death should be an opportunity to learn from your mistakes, but that's not what's occurring here. It simply feels... random. Maybe I get through a 3/4 loop without getting hit by a perfectly aimed projectile, maybe not. Maybe the bubble hits me in a way where I'm properly oriented relative to the ground, maybe not. Maybe I have enough momentum to get up the ramp, maybe not. There's so much variance in each run. And apparently that's not even the most difficult/annoying boss. Perhaps it's better with a keyboard and mouse but I'm playing on the deck. Regardless, I'd appreciate either an (optional) checkpoint system, a way to reload my weapons without needing to do a specific kind of flip, or some kind of life bar/life count system. I want to love this game and experience the story without watching someone else play it on YouTube, but as it stands I'm going to put it down as being "not for me". ♥️

_childDocuments_.review: Game is so very close to being an amazing game but there are a couple of flaws that make this game almost unplayable for me, as well as other problems that affect many people.The game is pretty unique and base gameplay loop is incredibly fun. You ride a motorcycle and it controls very similarly to the Trials games. The unique part is that you have a gun, and you have to turn around in your bike. Turning around is done by holding space, if you just press space you can parry enemy bullets. You shoot by aiming with the mouse, and pressing M1, holding M1 puts you in a bullet time to aim and react better. You reload your weapon, and refresh your parry by doing front and back flips. Yes, you can do it multiple times in a single aerial. Your bike also acts like a shield, turn the bottom of your bike towards enemy projectiles and you won't die. Very cool with tons of potential.The problem a lot of people are having is that they struggle to maintain focus on shooting all enemies, blocking multiple projectiles from different directions, reloading, refreshing parry, and still landing wheels down. People have asked for a mode where landing on your head didn't instantly kill you, and devs have said no. The main thing is that Laika's helmet is a skull, so it's white, but her bike is also white. When focusing not focusing on the bike (or people with poor vision) you can't easily and quickly tell what your angle is. Every end point of the shape Laika makes on her bike is white, so the best some people can do is put two of the white ends down and sometimes they end up on their head. They have tried to implement elements to help identify your positioning in air. The reticle has an arrow that shows the angle your head is at, and the arrow turns red when you are at a poor angle and will die, the ammo counter is in the shape of a revolver, and rotates as you rotate and will turn red at the same poor angles. The bigger issue is that your focus is almost never in the corner of your screen, as there is already an ammo counter on the reticle, the revolver is orange a color very close to red, so the revolver aspect is kinda negligible. If you know anything about the complexities of aiming, you'll probably know that you don't tent to focus on your reticle, but you focus on your target instead. Not only that, but often your attention is completely drawn away from aiming as you still have to block shots from multiple angles.To fix this, I've seen someone suggest a adding a red glow to the border of the whole screen when at a poor angle, which sounds like a good compromise that shouldn't be too difficult to implement, and can be a toggleable option. I'm not sure if I completely agree with a difficulty setting that removes an important part of what makes this game interesting and feel good to play. Not dying when landing poorly is kind of the whole point of Trials, and other similar games that this takes inspiration from, and adding it in can conflict with the artistic direction and intention. On the flip side, I don't think that some players who truly enjoy playing the game should be barred for a simple aspect of important info not being conveyed in a way that makes it quick and easy for them to interpret. Personally, I don't mind how the game currently is in this aspect, but this has been a large point of contention for a lot of players.The problem I have is that I want to play the game fast. Bullet time is a forced aspect, you have to enter it every shot as it automatically start on M1 press, regardless if you wanted to or not. Every time you enter it there is a zoom in effect to kinda help you focus on your shot. The zoom effect can cause shots that were aligned to miss as your angle gets shifted a bit from the zoom. This is further hindered by there being an accuracy penalty for not taking time on your shots. I want to make my shots without bullet time. I think that it plays into the badass feeling that the game seems like it's going for. Being able to full speed make two shots, do a flip, block a shot, and make another shot or two without the game deciding I didn't take enough time to aim so I should miss. I feel like if I can do an encounter without bullet time that I should be able to without relying on RNG to make my shots land, I should. This also affects farming for materials, you gotta shoot ore veins to mine it, but because of the aiming penalties you still gotta take the an extra second to aim your shot, the shot that you are making in a no-threat environment. I find it intrusive and it makes it really hard to continue to play the game. The game has the potential to be an incredibly fast paced experience but needing to stop for a full second to aim a shot that I've already aimed just feels like I need to slow myself down to play at the games speed, but every other aspect of the game tells me that it should be played at a faster pace. I would much rather have a bullet time be assigned to a different binding. It'll allow players to enter it when they feel like they need it, and when they don't need it that can clear the section faster.Honestly, if this one change was made then I could see myself not just playing through the whole game, but also potentially learning to speedrun the game. It genuinely causes me to not play the game, despite every other aspect being amazing. The art design, the music, the general gameplay, it's all great, but this one point I can't get over.

_childDocuments_.review: I can hardly express in words how much I love this game! I never write reviews, but for this game I simply must write one. When I first launched the demo and saw how beautiful the art style was and heard the stunning music I knew I came across something special.It's not just the excellent audiovisual direction that's brilliant about this game, it's the deeply emotional story, the short but sweet animated sequences and of course the gameplay, which is somehow even better than all the other parts of the game!Riding the bike, doing backflips in slow motion while killing enemies all around me by deflecting bullets and shooting them in the face is just pure fun! And it somehow got better and better the further I progressed in the game! The level design, especially in the big tree, felt like an enormous amount of time and thought was put into every centimeter of the game, all the locations are visually distinctive and traversing them is a joy. I even enjoyed that more enemies appeared on the map as I got better equipment and got more skilled in using my abilities, it made sense storywise and created a nicely challenging difficulty curve that, at least for me, fitted perfectly in the sweet spot of not being too easy and boring, but also not being frustratingly difficult.I could praise all the aspects of this game for hours, but I will just say that for me this might be a perfect game. Thank you so much for making this masterpiece, it shows that so much heart and effort was put into it!

_childDocuments_.review: i don't think i've ever really felt truly enchanted with a game like i do with laika; from the incredible soundtrack to the unusual learning curve of the gameplay that soon becomes second nature, from the stories of loss and survival scattered throughout the wasteland, from the beautiful art style and landscapes, i absolutely adored it all and every single minute of this game (even that damn crab boss fight) was utterly *enchanting* to me. i think laika is an enjoyable experience through and through and a unique gameplay concept executed well. i never felt frustrated with the movement and combat once i finally got the hang of it a little after where the demo leaves off, and i wish more games felt like it. part of me wishes there was more, but i also feel that laika paces itself very well and all side content feels important. tldr one of my favorite games of all time!

_childDocuments_.review: Another excellent game that REALLY is sprinting through its third act. Dug the art-style, fantastic animation, haunting (if samey) score, and even its novel gameplay loop. First third I was hooked, even despite the learning curve when it came to the motorcycle. By that middle portion, its indie roots were starting to show, with its side quests offering too little in the way of narrative or gameplay treats for the lengths you go through. Most boil down to fetch quests and the little quips you get as a reward are cute, but so SO lacking when put against the main story beats. Its padding, sad to say.Certain boss fights were also a chore, especially the chicken boss (get that machine gun!!). They were, as a whole, the worst part of the gameplay loop, with basic traversal through the sprawling map being much MUCH more enjoyable.As I said before, ending was sudden and honestly, kinda weak. Not bad mind you, it just felt a bit lacking for the emotional punch it was trying to land. I get that traditional animation is just stupid expensive, but I felt the ending should've gotten a little more than, what, 30 seconds?In the end, great game. Would love to go through this world again if Brainwash decides to put out a sequel. Whatever quibbles I might've had, Laika is a damn good game and I suggest you give it shot.
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: One of, if not THE best game I've played in quite some time.The world is massive and full of little bits to find and uncover; from new weapons to characters you'll either help or massacre. Alot of my play time was just riding about trying to reach a box just out of reach, or find a way into an area that was blocked off. Or trying to help characters about the world with side quests ((Of which there are TONS))The combats a little weird at first, but once you get into it; you'll be pistol whipping, backflipping and boosting your way through hundreds of squishy bird soldiers with a grin as you collect their gibblets for currency!The story unfolds as you explore, do main and side missions and interact with characters throughout. Gradually teaching you more about this world, the people in it and Laika's history as well.. and it is a very sad tale. I genuinely felt sad and sometimes even a little misty at some of the story elements throughout the game.The only downside I'd say is some of the boss fights. They're a little short and a little simple for the most part. Dodge bullet of some sort, shoot obvious target point; repeat. But; that just gives more time for exploring and doing sick shotgun jump backflip reloads as you blow birds heads off before riding off in search of more around the map!I really, really hope we get a sequel some day that follows on from the ending of this game and gives us a little more closure
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: I feel heartbroken about this game. There's something good in here, there's something genuinely as beautiful as harrowing that the game feels like it's getting across, with a particular take on anti-imperialism and actual empathy for its victims that I wanted to see more of - but I can't stand its design decisions. I don't know why they decided the game shouldn't be a linear experience but instead a metroidvania, I can't parse out why it has a million different progression systems - it has multiple different kinds of guns, it has sidequests, it has meals that give temporary buffs, it has resource collection that messes with the pacing. It has a playlist system, where the songs that were once placed perfectly in setpieces, swelling with the emotion of the scene - instead wear themselves out in open stages otherwise devoid of ambience, repeating over and over in a playlist in which they all blend in together with the other collectible tracks. The level of work this game puts into trying to make the player like it less is honestly astounding - there's something beautiful and unique here, but between its mechanical design being as inconfident as it is despite how confident the art design is as well as the simply baffling decisions (as another example - the first two bosses literally wait for you to enter a trigger zone before doing their single attack pattern, letting you take them slowly, easily, and tediously) - it starts to become intensely frustrating. Not because of any difficulty, but because of the way it simply refuses to let the player immerse themselves within the experience. I wish I had the patience to play it to the end, and I wish there was a version of this game that didn't require such patience.

_childDocuments_.review: It took me sometime to force myself to buy it, i knew it could be good or a fun game with pretty art.It broke all my thoughts after the end of the demo and where the game picks up from, alot of love has been put in this project and you can feel it for it's art, gameplay style, characters and tone. But i can't explain with just words on a screen how many things i felt during the story being told through bullets and blood,It takes effort to introduce a character, show how much they appreciate something at the same time you're burning it down.Even more a mother's rage, the only part you're not behind the trigger of a cycling gun chamber, Laika is.And a lot of courage to make the player bond with Puppy, to make them need to sleep and perhaps go check on the little kid every time you go back to upgrade weapons, fetch new quests and dust off again.Every time i shoot i feel the game is alive, impact marks, black and red lines while the bullet flies away and hits, the screen getting more red from the ongoing carnage of the grim biker and it's victims while i hear Coming Home or any of the 20 some bangers made for this game, i can't think of any other artist that could do what Beicoli did.Just go buy it or wait for a sale, go out there and make the wasteland red from their blood and maybe,just maybe, better times come when the blood dries, untill theres nothing left besides bones and shell casings.

_childDocuments_.review: It's like a combination of Excitebike, Mad Max, and Castlevania. And it is beautiful, emotional and very fun. Can be challenging, and you'll die a lot, but it's not at all discouraging. There are many checkpoints, and respawn time is very minimal. I'm not normally very good at coping with games that require you to die frequently, but I don't have any problem with this one.The art is fantastic. The story is mature and emotional and very enjoyable. The music is fitting, reminds me a bit of some of the Low Roar stuff from Death Stranding. Not to mention the fact that you play a tough, battle-hardended, but clearly loving and maternal 'yote mama on a motorbike with guns. For furries, that might be enough reason to get it right there. But for everyone else, the game is actually simply incredible anyway, so you should also get it. =)

_childDocuments_.review: This game checks all the boxes for me. It has a unique system for movement and combat that is very well thought out and has a high skill ceiling (not that it matters for my gameplay). The art and music are incredible. The story is compelling. As far as hard games go, it is probably one of the most fair ones. Deaths are caused by mistakes, and through trial and error. The frequent checkpoints make dying not too frustrating. The whole game is also just incredibly cool. You do backflips to reload and you can deflect bullets with your motorbike. Can't go wrong.

_childDocuments_.review: LAIKA's strongest selling point is definitely the motorcycle. I've played a lot of sidescrollers at this point, and it's highly engaging to have your method of traversal completely shifted in the way LAIKA shifts it. It reminds me, at times, of the way My Friend Pedro twists what "defensive gameplay" looks like; even at an intermediate skill level, good gameplay means becoming one with highly committal and violent STYLISHNESS. But to achieve that, you can't press buttons like you'd normally press them. You gotta press buttons like LAIKA wants you to press them. And that's rewarding to learn.    The levels themselves are quite distinct, and steadily extrapolate on the motorcycle-based movement. Traversing the world quickly, and farming for money + materials, involves an exercise in finding frequent opportunities to safely BACKFLIP (backflipping reloads your gun.) But the developers are aware of the value of those opportunities, and challenge you with tight jump timings, strange terrain, and intimidating enemy placements. Just blindly attempting backflips will get Laika killed, so you need to immerse yourself in the world and determine where to be confident and where to be cautious.    The tone of LAIKA is very somber. A post-apocalyptic story where characters in their different ways embody the pain of what has transpired (more or less, imperialism/colonialism doing their thing to the bitter end). This time, there is only sparing levity to be found through comedy or cuteness; instead, relief from the stressful world of the game is generally provided by beauty. The beauty of finding music that nourishes, of finding places where nature still flourishes (as much as it can in a sundered wasteland), and of connecting with people despite everything. Also the beauty of doing backflips on a dirtbike. LAIKA is unapologetically raw and it may scare some people off, but Brainwash Gang's vision is executed excellently.    Now, where LAIKA suffers most is a presence of bugs + jank, and a lack of overall accessibility.· I've encountered only one bug on the level of a softlock (essentially forced to quit to menu and reload the save), but there are a lot of cases of audio or visual elements continuing when they shouldn't, or dialogue cutting short before you can read it.· Overall presence of QoL (quality of life) features is pretty good, mostly marred by inconsistencies in where keyboard or mouse are useful in navigating menus.· If you have eyesight issues while gaming, LAIKA (at time of review) is probably highly strenuous. This is due to a combination of janky graphical effects (artistically amazing as the game may generally be), a dynamic camera that can make visual elements (like Laika herself) very small and unsteady, and occasional issues with overall color contrast.The devs are actively patching the game to fix issues like these, and I'm loving the game despite them, but they're worth mentioning.    I haven't finished the game yet, and I think it's important for Metroidvanias and open world games in particular to STICK THE LANDING. For the package to feel holistic... and it's doubly important for stories to stick the landing. But, LAIKA has the potential to do so in a big way. I'll check back in here when I finish my ride...    EDIT: I finished LAIKA, and it stuck the landing. It's a good game, thank you Brainwash Gang. <3

_childDocuments_.review: Laika: Aged Through Blood is probably one of my favorite games of all time (also it's better with a controller) It's like Moto X3M as a metroidvania with guns. Both the story and the gameplay are amazing. The traversal is all done on a motorcycle that feels great to control. Just like any other metroidvania, you'll get tools throughout the game that help you get around. One of my favorite tools is the shotgun, which you can use to jump and redirect yourself in midair. Reloading is done through backflipping, and you have a parry which is recharged by doing frontflips. Also, you buy things using your enemies' viscera, which brings up a lot of questions about how viable that is realistically as a currency. Like where and how do you keep your money if it's made of guts that decompose and rot? The story follows Laika, a dog person living in the wasteland who has a daughter and a really ♥♥♥♥♥♥ mom. I think it's a wasteland because fascist birds dropped a big bomb and harvested all the resources. Also I think they might have evolved from humans or something? Anyways, Laika is cursed with the ability to respawn after dying and is thus the protector of her village from the fascist birds as the war begins to ramp up towards its conclusion. It's a pretty sad story that really got me to care about it. Music is also pretty good. Didn't think I'd like it at first, but it kind of grew on me. While riding around, you can find cassette tapes and manually play the songs you've unlocked, which is a really cool implementation on the music. The fictional character that made the music is named Beicoli, who appears in the game and shares a name with the real life artist, who actually made the music for this game in real life.All in all, Brainwash Gang kind of hit the nail on the head with this game, and then kept hammering. Highly recommend. Took about 20 hours to complete (review might say less 'cause it probably didn't count the offline steam deck hours.)
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: Not-quite-a-masterpiece. This game has interesting mechanics and feels fun to play. The music is memorable and a good fit, along with the atmosphere that comes together to tell a story worth experiencing for yourself. It isn't quite on the level of Hollow Knight or Ori, but with a different vibe and a different story, it's definitely worth the play if you enjoyed either of those games. I walked away from this game having thoroughly enjoyed it, but also feeling like if the developers had more to work with, they could have done even better. So I'm hoping they keep building up with stuff like this, more animation, more in-game "stuff" to do/collect, etc.

_childDocuments_.review: To say that I've been tracking this game for years doesn't quite capture it. Undoubtedly, it's THE title I was most eagerly anticipating from Brainwash, and oh, true to form, it's absolutely incredible.From its initial glimpses in trailers, both visually and musically, it promised to be something extraordinary. And after the Steam Next Fest summer demo, there was no room for doubt about its gameplay. But here's the kicker – it surpasses even those high expectations!I've only managed to defeat the initial boss, roughly an hour and a half into the game, but let me assure you, this game is an absolute masterpiece.On the Steam Deck, it runs like a charm, although it's worth noting it surprisingly chews through the battery. If you fiddle with the resolution too swiftly, say, three or four times, it does tend to 'hang,' leaving you with no choice but to shut it down. But, you know, these are just minor hiccups when you consider the marvel that the rest of the game is!

_childDocuments_.review: Laika did not become one of my favourite games but it is a very solid game, still.Pros:* A story is engaging and rather interesting to follow. It's not very unpredictable and does not pose much of a mistery, though* Gameplay is mostly well balanced and soundly made* Graphics is quite good* Decent length* Soundtrack is great, Beícoli really is the best ;)Cons:* Disturbing themes, although presented rather muted, still are present (and are kind of the main point of the game)* Sudden difficulty spikes, some of the fights and specific location parts are much harder than all of the game* Questionable mechanics for loosing in-game money. You need to invest into buying new viscera bags right away, otherwise it'll be a lot of lost viscera and a lot of grind.* Not many choices to make. No consequences will be presented eitherNot here, not there:* Glitching gamepad because of steam gamepad settings enabled by default and game support for gamepad is native. I disabled steam gamepad support in steam's game settings and it went much better afterwards.* Despite the engaging story I didn't feel quite attached to most of secondary characters. But that might be a specific desicion by the authors to relay main character's detachment and inner emptinessAll-in-all, this is a good game and at least stands out with regard to gameplay. Totally worth completing.

_childDocuments_.review: As stated in the description, its a motorvania.You ride a motorcycle throughout a metroidvania map system, shooting bad guys, and doing sick flips.But it is VERY fleshed out. Admittedly, the aiming with controller could be better, but Laika has very solid systems that works well with enemy/boss layouts, the map in general, and just making you feel like an absolute badass.For combat, you really can just go the whole game with the default pistol. The upgrades you get don't increase damage, but this game focuses more on skillfully maneuvering with the motorcycle rather than out damaging your opponents. However it is still fun to use other weapons, and the only "required" weapon you get during the story.Then the story, WHOO BOY IS IT GOOD. It really is a "you have to experience it for yourself" kind of story, but the stories as well as some of the side quests are so heart wrenching. It really does accurately portray the cruelty of the aftermath of war, and the pain it brings.I do recommend this game, but I will warn anyone looking to buy that there are difficult sections in the game, but much of your deaths will be based on your ability to maneuver your bike properly. Have fun!

_childDocuments_.review: If you're going to boldly proclaim that your game is a "TOTALLY NEW SUB-GENRE BRAH", then it needs to have literally nothing wrong with it. That's why everyone clowned on Death Stranding, because despite advertising itself as "the first strand type game" it had numerous design flaws. There are so many needlessly frustrating elements to this game's gameplay that it was honestly a struggle to motivate myself to keep playing.That being said, this game has an AMAZING story. The world, the characters, the presentation, the music, all 10/10, no notes. I kept going because I was genuinely invested in the story and wanted to see how it ended. Then, the ending came, and it sucked. It was a blue-balling, investment-robbing cop-out. All of the cutscenes in the game are way too short for no reason and don't have any time to breathe, but the ending cutscene is literally three seconds long with no dialogue before it boots you into the end credits. I was genuinely invested in what was going to happen, but it turned out to be the most inconclusive, unsatisfying ending I have witnessed in the last five years.This is an ok five-hour linear story stretched into an aggravating twenty-hour metroidvania for no reason. Pass this one up unless it's on sale like it was when I got it.
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: I love everything about this game, the artstyle is incredibly fitting, the combat and the movement are satisfying and, despite it being a difficult game, you will never feel it's difficulty is insurmountable. The story of the game is dark and depressing, yet incredibly satisfying, as any post-apocalyptic game story should be. The main character and side characters are in line with what you would expect from the world like that, yet all of them have their own unique charm to them. Majority of the characters are female and the game certainly has a feminist perspective to it, however it's in absolutely no way forced, pretentious or whatever you'd expect from the recent AAA games. Instead, this feminist perspective focuses on parent-child relations, motherhood and enduring in the world that was lost long ago. At the same time the story represents the only problem I have with the game, it leaves a little chance of there ever being a sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: Story, music, and gameplay are phenomenal, and only gets better as you get more upgrades and gear. This was so good in so many ways, but there are some shortcomings I experienced that frustrated me, which were just enough of an annoyance for me to feel the need to write review.There is a ton of side quests in this game that require you to go back into old areas and not tell you exactly where the thing you need is, like for example there was a sidequest that asked you to find root in a cave in an area where there seemingly are none, and there's even a sidequest where a guy looses his drumsticks and literally has no idea where they are, like you're supposed to scour the entire map looking for these things? On top of that, quest items don't spawn until you activate the quest, so you can't just stumble upon them early and have them in your inventory. The experience of thinking you know where the thing is, driving to where you think the thing is, then having to do the drive all the way back when you realise the thing is not there is a real pain, and useless filler in a game that doesn't need that kind of tedium to artificially increase the average playtime.To make matters worse, at the time of playing there are no guides on the internet for this game. I would say a solid 12 hours of my 18.6 hours on this game is just me backtracking and looking for things. The only saving grace is riding the motorcycle is fun, and when you do find a new area you haven't been to before it's a great feeling.Honestly, despite my frustration I could have easily overlooked this if it weren't for the ending and some missed story beats. Some of the following are nitpicky, some are a big issue imho;- The game starts off so strong but is never able to maintain that vibe, - If you get killed while talking to someone on the walkie-talkie, you just never get to hear that conversation ever again.- Minor gameplay thing, flipping your bike while you're spinning in mid-air stops your spin for some reason- Despite the birds spawning closer to the village as the story goes on, and everyone talking about how they are going to find the village eventually, they never find it. Missed foreshadowing IMHO- There is only one major event that unfolds after falling asleep in your house , and after that nothing interesting ever happens in the village.- There is a clip in the general/cinematic trailer of Laika in a sick solider outfit walking through a city with vendors, and people lying down on the street. This is an area you are immediately teleported to for some exposition, and then immediately teleported out of afterwards. Unfortunate that you can't go back there as it is probably the most interesting area in the game.- - Would absolutely have loved to see more animated cutscenes, the only problem is there are very few tense moments in the game where an animated cutscene could be applied.- Every single area in the game before a boss consists of "Oh, you want to do the cool thing? well, you have to do 3-4 tedious things before you can get to the cool thing!" It should all be cool thing.- Final boss is a bit easier than the boss before it, and isn't even half as cool as the 2nd boss - They never give you an opportunity to learn about the final boss through cutscenes, you never see him ordering an attack or doing anything evil, the moment you meet him is the moment you beat him. In that sense he just feels like a slightly harder enemy that invokes no emotional reaction, unlike finding - Ending was a 20 second cut scene with an immediate cut to the credits and no follow up. ENDING SPOILER: Imagine playing your favourite story-driven game and at the "point-of-no-return" you are immediately brought to the final boss, who is never talked about/you've never met before, kill him fairly easily, then you get a 20 second cutscene and the credits roll. I tried ignoring every shortcoming hoping that the ending would make it all worth it and come back together but it falls short as well. Which is such a shame, cause the story and gameplay had me captivated from the very beginning don't see this getting fixed in the future, would be happy to replay the game and change my review if it does.

_childDocuments_.review: I can't give this an universal PLAY THIS GAME recommendation because the gameplay I think will either delight you or frustrate you. So play the demo and see how you feel about it! If you like it at all - if the game is mechanically interesting, if you like the tone and the presentation of the world and its characters - you will find that the full game features much more of the same, developed richly and with great care.I could write a thousand-word essay why I love this game, but that's not a useful review. Instead, a summary!, both the quieter tracks as well as the many songs with full vocals, which create a gorgeous and thematically dense atmosphere throughout the game. It's extremely clear that the team is acutely aware of their strengths and go to great lengths to foreground the music in this game, with long quiet moments entwined in the gameplay that encourage you to sit and listen.The  is beautiful, detailed, and popping with personality. Background vistas are stunning and desolate. The small details on everything - toys for your kid, the art on casette tapes, the posters in the background, the snippets of personality in your quest journal and on item descriptions - give the impression of a lived-in world with history and feeling. It's not a "super dense lore" approach to storytelling like, say, a Souls game, but I think that's to its credit. It has just enough flavour to give you the sense of a world that these characters inhabit. in this game is fun and has personality. Laika's reluctant and grumpy and not very pleased to have to play the hero when all she wants is to protect her daughter. Is this a very well-established character trope? Yes. Does everyone still love it anyway? Also yes. Smaller characters are a bit more hit-or-miss with their writing but honestly everything works and it tells a great and emotional overall story. Can't complain. is a joy in this game, and I've rarely been happier to just drive from place to place - I only got bored after playing 30+ hours, I think? Every new area you open up has its own unique visual aesthetic, backdrop, etc., but it also has its own personality in how the terrain is designed for you to traverse. This presents constantly new puzzles, so when you're exploring a new area you are kept fully attentive and engaged in trying to understand how to move or spin or flip or jump through this landscape. You'll die a lot, sure. But you'll probably have a lot of fun while doing it. is probably going to be the big dividing factor. The core of it is motorcycle combat, where you're moving, shooting, and doing flips to shield yourself, reload, or refresh your bullet parry charge(s). You die if you take a single hit or land badly. This sounds exacting, and it is, but for better or for worse there's a lot of bloody giblets in the game that make it genuinely difficult to keep track of what's happening sometimes - leading to a small but significant degree of randomness in an encounter which can be frustrating. If you land six perfect shots with three reloads in the air, only to die because at some point one of your shots hit a dead enemy that flew in front of a live enemy (who then shoots you when you land), it's annoying! Or if you're parrying multiple bullets midair but lose track of which direction you're facing (and thus which direction you need to rotate to reload your weapon).The devs have done their best to make a game interface that is both clean and informative (your reticule tells you your relative orientation to the ground, as well as your remaining ammunition) but those are the remaining persistent issues that occasionally crop up. You'll eventually learn to play around them if you try enough! That said, the game makes an excellent effort to minimize frustration - lots of save points, and you lose half your currency on death which you can pick up as long as you don't run out of death-token-bags before recovering it, and even if you lose currency you accrue it so fast while just playing normally that I never needed to farm except when trying to 100% the game.The  of the game might put people off - it is very much post-apocalyptic grungy mad-max gory-dark in its writing. Not everyone likes that, and even as someone who is okay with it, the relentless tragic-ends to various side storylines can verge on rote. I will say I really really liked the story overall, but you could let that one person's tree be okay, at least! Not everything needs to be deathly awful! The  does have a few hiccups, particularly in the second half of the game where things speed up rapidly after a relatively slow, expansive first act. Not really a fatal issue in my opinion, and honestly a super hard thing to fix even in the best of stories/games.The  does risk becoming a bit mundane after a while - enemy types don't change much, and the starting weapon is so mundane-but-effective that I didn't really even upgrade it fully until the endgame. YMMV here, some might find it boring, but for me the evolving terrain layouts kept my brain occupied more than the gunplay per se - the traversal becomes a puzzle on its own, and enemies part of that puzzle and not so much opponents to be defeated.  is also a tad hit or miss.It's a game about a coyote mom on a motorbike with a gun. If that's not enough, a strong story, a world designed around a well-executed and innovative gameplay mechanic, and a stunning soundtrack should sell the case - as long as you're okay with the core gameplay conceit of playing as a coyote on a motorbike, shooting birds and dodging bullets while doing flips. A real diamond of a game.

_childDocuments_.review: If the story or style even mildly interests you, it will deliver beyond all expectations.Laika is a game that reignited what story telling means to me.
