_childDocuments_.review: This game is nice and freshens up the normal sidescroller metroidvania type of game experience with the biker twist, which alone makes it worth the buck for me.BUT you should know beforehand that the game is not really long and has a few design issues which are not really thought through.This review is also more about the bad things then the good cause bad things mark themselves more in your brain then good.  I needed around 20 hours to complete the story and have no open sidequests left, and also collected almost all the things which you do not need to farm a lot for. I guess you could complete it if you only focus on the story in around 10 to 12 hours or even shorter. (could spoil the general story experience a bit) The story is a depressing adventure which is interesting, but after a few hours, you notice that the game really wants to make you feel depressed and sad about the lives the characters live, which will affect you for a few characters, but for most of them not. This is just my experience, but it made the story a bit annoying and predictable for me because I don't really expect anything good happening to the characters I meet , which in conclusion makes you not really invest much emotion in the people you meet. Now to the MC of the story . The story of those characters is really nice . SO AMAZING! The art and music are so nice and really made the experience a lot better. The music was amazing and really matched the style and setting of the game and also made the exploring of the world more enjoyable. The art was also amazing; it wasn't top-notch but almost there. But the combination of the music and art made the atmosphere and feeling of the game insane. It really gave you the feeling of a lone rider who does what must be done, and that's all I wanted from it. I didn't have any crazy bugs or such; the only thing I had was that the game would drop fps to 50 or lower when I was in a menu and streamed the game with Discord at the same time, which was weird but easy to evade. The performance was also stable at 144fps constantly. SO MANY BAD DECISIONS! The game has a few bosses which were just awful to kill, and I know bosses need to be challenging, but these boss fights were one of two things: an easy first try or a frustrating 100 deaths try. This is because you have boss fights which are parkour and frontal boss fights in which you fight the boss with one ramp or so head-on. One of the parkour bosses was nice because it resembled the normal flow of the game, but the other bosses, oh god, help me, they made me hate parkour , because you needed to play everything perfectly or you need to repeat a 10-minute boss fight which could have been easily evaded just through a simple checkpoint. But the frontal bosses are a complete disaster; you literally one-shot EVERY SINGLE ONE if you have certain weapons. You literally need to handicap yourself and don't use other weapons except the starting weapon to make those boss fights last more than a few seconds. But well, that doesn't make the bosses a disaster; it makes them bad, but not more. The real problem lies in the part where they are really annoying to play against if you don't use the overpowered weapons, so you have either the choice to stomp the boss into the floor or every single boss makes you hate the game because of dumb projectiles and tiny platforms. The other thing is that the art is in some situations in your way of seeing yourself. What I mean is that if you, for example, do a , the screen gets almost completely blacked out as an effect, which makes it harder to see coming enemies, resulting in your death and therefore made me not do any of those anymore, which is bad design. The other part where art is in your way is that you really easily lose the overview of your character's direction or where your head is because the colors of your character fade into each other if you are faster or do 360s, which could also be avoided with a bit of outlining. . I really, really want to like it just because of the innovative ideas for a metroidvania, the insane music, art, and world, but the game doesn't really make it easy with the balancing, bosses, annoying mechanics, story, and character relations. I would recommend it, but only if you want to experience a depressing world as a lone biker which grabs you with its art and music with a few twists in the story and if you are ready to overlook a few flaws the game has which make you hate it at some points in its short time.(English is not my first language, so grammar is bad)

_childDocuments_.review: A wholly unique take on metroidvania styled gameplay leaves much to be desired when even the most basic of gameplay actions require an incredible amount of finesse and delicate effort or you suffer instant death. In particular having to remember which direction to rotate your character (which is different depending on which direction your character is facing) just to reload two separate renewable skills that would have been mapped to a button in any other game, and all before you even make it to the first boss is, and I'm going to be clear here, way too much. A simplification of controls and primary gameplay actions would drastically improve the playability of the game, but its clear the developers wanted punishing instant-death hair-pin trigger-based gameplay and this is entirely at odds with the complete unstoppable bada $$ mad-max styled motor bloodsport theme the game has latched onto entirely.

_childDocuments_.review: At first I didn't think the game would be for me. You die with one simple mistake and the game doesn't really mince that. However once I got past the beginning tutorial, the game started to really click with me. Getting a feel for how the bike handles, learning its momentum, blocking bullets with your bike and eventually getting your gun does a bit of time. If you can get past this, it all blends together amazingly while feeling really natural to play.That being said, while I love the darker and grim feeling of the story, it starts to feel kinda sparse after the first few hours. The game is rather on the short side, but I would've loved more interaction or moments in the story for things to grow. Instead it drip feeds you small interactions here and there to progress the story. Though once you reach about roughly the 3/4 mark, the game quickly races to a conclusion, the pacing rushing to resolve what should've felt like a major quest or and then pushing you toward the finale. Despite this what is there is rather nice, its dark and really makes you feel for Laika who remains stoic most of the time but deep down you can tell she's hurt but trying to stay strong for others. If you're a metroidvania fan who is looking for another game to get lost in, you're going to get very disappointed. Despite the marketing, the game doesn't really have much to encourage backtracking. Once you get the shotgun, very little is held back from the player. And what little left is just behind a quest you can do right after getting the shotgun. And the very very very little rest is a lategame upgrade thats locked almost right before the final area. There's not much of the 'Aha!' feeling you get from a usual metroidvania from discovering a way to get back a roadblock that stopped you earlier. There's also not that much reward besides weapon crafting materials which I will get into later. There's not much there to entertain a metroidvania fan. Sidequests give you little else besides a few cute interactions with npcs and a pittance of materials. Even close to the end-game, sidequests are never worth doing besides for seeing character interactions, giving you at most like 3 of a rare resource that you'd need 15 or 30 of for an upgrade, or 6 of a material you might already have well of a 100 in. This sounds harsh but sidequests are never difficult, usually just the standard fetch quest with the very rare combat trial. The interactions while small still give neat insight into a character or have a neat moment between them and Laika.Weapons...are a mixed bag.You will be using the revolver for 99% of the game. Besides for bosses, everything dies in a hit. The revolver is quick, accurate and easy. It will be a staple even into the end game.The shotgun is a vital part of your movement, and in fact some areas are locked off without it. The blast of it will give you a burst of momentum in the opposite direction, boosting you through the air to make tricky jumps or even correct yourself if you mess up a jump. Once unlocked it will always find a place in your arsenal for mobility mostly, and combat secondary.The rest are gimmicky.The machine gun is okay, the sniper rifle is awful and inaccurate, the crossbow requires you to reload it bolt by bolt, and the rocket launcher is impractical and slow with a high chance of killing you.On top of this all, the revolver and shotgun are cheap and easy to upgrade. The rest will require you to grind to do so and will still pale in usefulness.This all sounds rather terrible, right?Not really.The story is sparse but the game is so short that it doesn't feel as if it drags on with what you get from the story and short interactions with quests keeps it refreshing enough.Despite exploration being weak, the handling of the bike, the way you flow with its momentum, and the deadly rhythm of combat makes Laika feel like none other. The story while dark, doesn't dwell in over indulgent edginess. My biggest complaint being mostly "I want more" is kinda rooted in how short the game is, being roughly 10 hours if you focus on the story. Which honestly not that bad all things considered.  If you can stomach some gore and a bit of a rocky start, Laika is a great game

_childDocuments_.review: So .. Laika aged trough blood , I will be short and on point with this one.Pros:* The visuals are Amazing.* The soundtrack is amazing.* The mechanics of the game are interesting.Cons:* The music is buggy and sometimes just not plays so you stuck with some elevator songs.* The mechanics of the game become repetitive really quick and it loses its magic.* The map of the game is riddled with pointless Riddles , which are : " go to this place in map , and look for trash bin , in there , take the item " , zero direction the item or the place of the item has nothing outstanding in it , so it blends nicely with the surroundings.* Many places in the map gives you the illusion that you can go there while its a wall , that you cant go up or even interact with...* The bosses are multi-phase boss , that not only depends on your ability to handle their BS, but also to interact with the surroundings in middle fight , which causes many times going in a wrong corner and dying because simply that and going back to phase one of the boss fight.That's it.

_childDocuments_.review: I really really want to like this game. But it is seriously testing my patience.Laika's opening is really strong. If the entire game was as cool as the opening, I would strongly recommend it. I played for as long as the demo would allow me to, and immediately bought this game. I have always been a fan of metroidvania style games, sinking hundreds of hours into hollow knight alone. Therefore, with how sick and memorable the opening was in this game, and how good the core gameplay loop felt, I decided it was an easy purchase. However, if you are like me and considering purchasing this game after playing the demo, or have been sold it by word of mouth then I urge you to take this review as a caveat.The overall variety is lacking. And not just a little lacking. INCREDIBLY lacking. I have completed the first two major story objectives, and am well on my way to completing the third (more on that later), and I kid you not, there are only four basic enemy types that I have encountered in the overworld, or anywhere else for that matter. No, not four general types of enemy, LITERALLY only four unique enemies. To add insult to injury, all, and I mean ALL of these enemies stand in place, and fire at you. To compare this to a metroidvania with a much more varied sandbox, Hollow Knight has more variety in enemies in the FIRST AREA. You have a mix of enemies that charge you, slash you, and fire projectiles from afar. It's not a ton of variety, and hollow knight will retread enemy concepts in later areas, but in roughly the first seven zones of this game, I have not seen a single enemy other than the aforementioned four.  (I know there are boss fights, but those have their own issues).The lack of variety extends to the zones. While they are all visually distinct, and all offer worthwhile side paths, they really just feel like reskins of each other. Each section of the wastes could have had its own unique challenges to overcome, and unique obstacles to face, but instead you will be doing in each zone roughly what you were doing in the first: Driving up ramps and loops, and shooting bad guys. This could have been helped if it wasn't THE SAME FOUR BAD GUYS copy and pasted throughout the entire overworld. There could have been so much more done with these areas, but sadly, there wasn't. For an example of a game that does this better, Hollow Knight has unique obstacles and enemies in each area, in addition to having visually distinct areas. (There is one exception to this in Laika, which I will talk about later).These problems come to a head when we consider what genre of game this is. This is a metroidvania, where backtracking is often necessary to progress. To Laika's credit, there are lots of reasons to go back to previously traversed areas. There are tons of crafting resources to find throughout each level, each of which unlocks pretty useful and cool upgrades. There are also story items which help you complete quests for various NPC's. I have no problem with the quest system. However, with samey environments (gameplay-wise) and enemies that are LITERALLY all the same, going back to areas that you have already explored with new unlocks to collect their resources becomes a chore, which is sad, because returning to previous areas with new powers is usually a strength of this little genre. Once again, going back to hollow knight, returning to previous areas was awesome, because of their uniqueness, and because there was a sense of getting more powerful. This neatly leads into my next point.Laika Doesn't really have progression. I mean it technically does, but there isn't a very tangible sense of getting stronger. I challenged the Big Tree, what I can assume is meant to be a mid game or end game area, with essentially no upgrades. Basically none. I put a single upgrade into my revolver, and didn't even get another weapon slot. I'm not pretending to be some kind of pro at this game, in fact I'm kinda garbage at it to be completely honest. But I never once felt like there was a challenge I couldn't face with my early game character, or even one where the scales were stacked against me. Once again, going back to Hollow Knight, I remember getting my ass whooped by the Watcher Knights, because I had neglected to get any sword upgrades for this mid game boss. What makes this particularly sad is that after a point in Laika, I just stopped caring about getting upgrades in any way, shape or form, because beyond the usual metroidvania "You need item X to do Y", there was really no need at all to get them. This kneecaps the satisfaction of finding upgrade materials. Why should I care about getting the machine gun or the sniper rifle, when starting revolver can easily clear the entire game. All the doodads you pick up are kinda just meaningless bloat.Despite all this negativity, there are aspects of this game that are incredible. If you can look past all of the issues that I just mentioned, this might be the game for you. The visuals are drop dead gorgeous, in an art style that blends better than any game I have hitherto played beauty and bleakness. The wastelands feel like a living, breathing, yet harsh world. This alone might be enough for people to draw them in. People might like the soundtrack, but I'm personally not too much of a fan. I'm more of a heavy metal aficionado, and therefore blasted 80's hair metal the whole time I was playing, which I felt matched the setting nicely. Music taste is pretty subjective though, so you don't need to listen to my dumbass opinion. The story, while hamfisted at times (to the point where it feels like it's trying to hit you over the head with a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ sledgehammer sometimes) is effective. I like the main character, (not a silent one, but not an annoying one either) and I really felt like I was fighting to make the lives of all the little furry villagers better. I really wanted to help them, to make their cartoon world a better place, but I just couldn't bring myself to slog through more nigh identical gameplay. Anyway, to wrap this up, I have nothing against this game, its developers, its community, or anyone else who might enjoy it. It's just really not my cup of tea in any way, shape, or form. If you want a good metroidvania, there are much better examples in the genre (SOTN, Hollow Knight, Tunic, etc.) I really really want to like this game, but it just feels like it's wasting my time. TL;DR This game suffers from a lack of variety in terms of level design, variety in normal enemies, and an overall lack of progression. While it has excellent visuals and visual storytelling, those for me are not enough to rescue a game from bad gameplay, which I feel like this game has overall. If you have not done so already, go play Hollow Knight instead, as it is a fantastic game (with its own issues, of course).

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to beat the game before writing a review...But frankly I am devastated after the credits rolled.Ok...So I can't stress enough how good this game is. I think it's a game that everyone should play atleast once. The story is dark but so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ good. If you want a good story this is a game for you. Music is amazing. It's still on loop on my spotify it's that good. It's calm, sad sometimes tense and somehow it fits so well with genocide you're committing. I can't explain it, it just works and I adore it.Gameplay is really satisfying. Yes it's hard but that's the point. You'll die a lot, but you'll learn with every death. It's the whole point of the game. Every combat is a puzzle that you need to figure out. Very satisfyingEdit: After 57h and after 30 hours of trying to beat the game without dying... Gameplay just got better. It's tough yes, but it is so satisfying to go through the whole thing memorizing and progression through this game with an outside challenge. Honestly I want a special challenge gamem mode. Pretty please.And the artstyle dear good. This game is a work of art for it's graphics. Backgrounds are just amazing, character designs are really good, and gore is somehow fitting where game just wants you to paint everything with that crimson blood.And every single thing I mentioned works together, creating one of the best experiences of 2023. It's cheap, buy it and enjoy it.

_childDocuments_.review: Laika's greatest strength is honestly in the sound design. The music, the sound effects, and its silence. How it all ties into the heart wrenching story is frankly inspirational. Everytime I hear the soundtrack, I can't help but tear up as I remember another detail about this game's story. Another memory of how it still, after making you think there was nothing left to fight for but one cute puppy, gives you such intense hope for the future.This game is masterful. I can't recommend it enough. It's a challenge, but not such a challenge that you can't push through it with some amount of dedication. If you have any interest in the game, do at least try the demo. It's fantastic.My only hope is that they put out the lyrics for all the game's music because I can't find that anywhere.

_childDocuments_.review: Laika: Aged Through Blood is a unique blend of Trials and Metroidvania, a Motorvania. In a world which games with furry main characters are targeted for lovestruck tweens, this one is a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ dark twist that's grim, distressing, and utterly captivating. You'll find yourself bathed in the blood of enemies as you tear through them with bullets, collecting guts and gore as your currency. This is not a game for the faint-hearted.As someone not particularly keen on Metroidvanias due to a poor sense of direction and a disdain for retracing steps and mundane sidequests, Laika made me love all of that. The seamless integration of sidemissions next to your main objectives, coupled with the thrill of performing tricks on your bike, along with the challenge of equally annoying bosses, makes it a standout for beginners in the Metroidvania genre.Prepare to die—a lot—in mostly in the stupidest ways possible, like falling off your damn bike in a standstill or forgetting to land on your wheels. Thankfully, the developers are generous with their checkpoints, sparing you from tedious retracing. I always have a satisfying sense of accomplishment when I finally land that perfect triple barrel roll onto a wheelie, wiping out a horde of enemies that's more than the amount of bullets my gun can carry.Beicoli's soundtrack complements the barren wasteland setting beautifully. Despite the grim atmosphere, the story is deep and intriguing. Characters leave you wanting more, and the game strikes a perfect balance, keeping the lore mysterious but captivating. You won't get bored; you should definitely give it a shot.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, I have never ever played a game which had a 10/10 soundtrack design, where every piece of music is a masterpiece, yet every other aspect of the game is 6/10 at best (in my opinion at least). My review will mostly build around this summary.-- THE GAMEPLAY --Riding your bike, balancing, trying to shoot accurately, trying to insert some flips into your movement to reload the gun, all this can be overwhelming at first, but you can get the hang of it pretty quickly, and it stays challenging, yet rewarding through the whole game. If this wouldn't be the case, the game would probably be too frustrating, and unplayable. So they did a good job on this part, yet I will still say that the game is only enjoyable around up to the 40% completion mark. The reasons are the following:-- THE NARRATIVE --Again, it starts off amazing. The characters, the story, the vibe; it is rough, unforgiving, realistic and sentimental. They (devs/art director) really give a good glimpse of the feelings and thoughts of this depressed, enervated woman, who's not even trying to do the right thing anymore, just doing something stuff that is expected from her because of her role. With motives so empty and hopeless, it was a great feeling to try to find something pleasant in the game, and I mean in the good sense. I wanted to seek comfort for Laika and he Puppy, which made me kept playing.But here, the 40% barrier shows up again. After that, the characters feel like NPCs in every game ever, giving out the basic "grab that from this area or inspect this in that area" type of quests, which were probably added to revisit areas, giving out more content, which is not a problem, but the backstories for the quests were really uninspired after a while.The thing that I missed the most was the option to choose an outcome, to control the flow of the story in any way. It was so predictable that  Why can't we do it if we choose to? Why does it have to be forced to just swear it to Puppy, but having other quests instead. Even if it's just two cards popping up with two choices, if they would have made the "war with the birds" quests feel like they really affect the safety of Where We live, choosing between that and your family would have been really hard and would have involved the player much better into the story and the hardships of Laika. Towards the end of the game, in some encounters you can either let enemies live or kill them, and I thought they are finally trying to add these options that the player can choose between, but as far as I now, these choices have zero impact on the game whatsoever. I don't know if this wanted to show how it doesn't amtter how you treat people, or how much Lika doesn't care at this point, but I rather felt like a missed opportunity, than an artistic choice.Towards the end of the game, all these just become worse. The characters, the motives, they start to get unpolished, the dialogues are lazy-written and do not carry as much weight, as before, even Laika's character starts to feel off.But the worst experience from the whole game, as already touched by the final boss topic, is the very ending of the game. Of course,  But what comes after you defeat the final boss? -- THE MUSIC --I don't know if these are valid categories for a game review, but I wanted to talk about this topic as well. I have said everything I have found problematic with the game so far. But I wouldn't care this much, nor would I have finished the game at all, if it wasn't for the music it provided. As said by the large cat creature in the game, Beícoli is a genius. And it was a really nice touch to add the music selection and collection as an in-game mechanic, since you will be hearing the songs a lot throughout the game. And to be honest, I had much more fun listening to the songs, trying to understand the lyrics, and trying to put together the backstory based on them, than playing the game itself. I have never analyzed songs to understand the lore in any videogame so far, and the fact that it came naturally, just by how powerful these songs are, made it really enjoyable. Since Laika is not a woman of words, her feelings can mostly be unserstood from these songs, and I really can't express how well these feelings come through. I have probably racked up half of the spotify listens on these tracks at this point.Overall, I wholeheartedly recommend Laika: Aged through Blood. Even with it's flaws, it has a soul you can connect to, and if this is the experience you are looking for, then I am sure this game will have something for you.I'll be looking forward to new projects by this studio, and more importantly, from Beícoli.

_childDocuments_.review: An incredibly good game that overall pulls off an amazing spectacle worthy of a playthrough.++PROS+++ Art, cutscenes are amazing.+++ Soundtrack is an absolute banger, SPECIFICALLY Playing in the Sun which is my song of the year.+ Gameplay is difficult but gets slightly easier over time and manages to be lovely throughout. People will likely complain about the difficulty but it's honestly not that bad at all once you get used to it [And as long as you DON'T use a controller with mouse and keyboard being an infinitely easier and more accurate control method with the autoaim for controller being liable to get you killed]+ Technically tons of content, although the sidequests are pretty bare.+ Kinda loved the anti-war message the game had going. Similarly I loved the Western style of everything.+ Animal people are an interesting decision and I found myself more interested with this then say, human characters. Like the Birds being literal BIRDS led to some real monstrosities you fight, while the friendly NPCs range from adorable to very memoral. [Also I'm biased sue me, but genuienly so many games fail to make human characters diverse enough to warrant remembering, it's going to be pretty hard to forget the western coyotes anytime soon, design wise, as they have no one else to blend into.]--CONS--- Gets a little edgy and very gory. While I'm cool with this and it's literally on the tin [It's not "Aged through Smiles"] but it's not the thing for everyone.- Map is ABSOLUTELY not accurate, or at least wasn't for me at a certain point which makes exploration a massive pain.- Screen transitions can get you killed by enemies you can't react too, or at least it did to me in a handful of areas. Not the biggest complaint but sometimes the camera will pan to let you see a "Cool" thing but then not pan fast enough once you rocket past it.- End game cinematic feels very unfinished and I really wanted a little bit more to feel more closure for the characters I grew to love by the end of it.- Hook upgrade wasn't used for general gameplay and is only used in two areas with it's second outing be FAR less interesting. ??MIXED??? Laika's hitbox can feel so bad at times.? There's a "Boost" for Laika from hitting accelerate twice in a quick succession which I had no idea about until near the end of the game. I don't know if I missed a tutorial or what but it's both entirely pointless and essential in certain bits making certain paths easier than prior.? Vendor - Craft - Upgrade system. Cooking for instance lets you make many different meals with passive gains that last 15 minutes, but overall it's going to be pretty rare to use as you don't always have access to it and you also don't really need it if you're bothering to do side stuff. Crafting upgrades involves bonus viscera sacks, the currency of the game is kept in there and they function as lives, however I didn't know you could upgrade them for a while as they are upgraded at a vendor to the left of your home and is not on screen unless you go all the way over there. The rest of the upgrades just feel like an excuse to heavily limit the weapons you get so you have to grind to level up the fun part of the game. Vendors are also pretty annoying as not all of them are near fast travel points but you have to routinely go back and forth to them to finish sidequests. ? Areas towards the backend of the game feel a little rushed. It wasn't that noticeable to the casual player I think but I noticed.? Combo meter isn't displayed and there is no option for it, at least not that I remember. Missed opportunity given how there's food dishes based on making it last longer.VERDICT: Laika, Aged through Blood is one of my favorites in this genre and for 20 bucks you're getting an INSANELY good deal, however don't expect it to be 100% perfect, you will likely find it to be 1000% enjoyable, especially when you get your combo going and you start pulling off sick moto-tricks by the end of the game. Really fun, memorable and filled with a mix of funny moments but also plenty of gory ones.

_childDocuments_.review: A very moving game with an interesting, if a tad underdeveloped gameplay loop.The art is fantastic, I listen to the music regularly even months later, and the story is deeply tragic (But fantastic!)I think you could split the gameplay into three major areas:- Combat- Exploring- QuestsThe combat I think is quite unique, and I found it pretty enjoyable, however I will note that as you go through the game, you unlock new weapons that do different things, unfortunately most of the time the revolver you start with is almost always the best option, with most other weapons being confined to either beating a specific boss easier or augmenting your movementExploring was nice! There's plenty of world to roam about, and with your growing collection of mixtapes to keep you company, I found myself wanting to drive more often than fast travel (Which while not free, is awfully cheap)Quests are..Where my love wanes a lot. They feel like their only purpose is to provide character progression, and while I'm not strictly against that, the result can bring the game down at times:- You'll find yourself backtracking to areas often. You might explore an entire region on your own! Juuust to get a quest to go find an item you previously couldn't pick up- You're often misdirected, or given extremely vague information. At times I was told to go to a certain region for an item, only to give up, go to the wiki, and find it was in the neighbouring region- Sidequests are never not fetch quests, this led to disappointment. Here's a moment in particular that stuck with me: That all said.. Particularly with the questing. I want to say that this shouldn't turn you away from the game, it has its faults, perhaps those faults were due to limited time, budget, or something else. But the things it does do right, it excels in, and it's not often I can say a game makes me cry just from hearing certain tracks. If you want an experience to remember, this game is it!

_childDocuments_.review: So, I decided to rewrite my review because previous one was kinda messy and wrote almost instantly after game completion. Ok, so this is my first (well actually second if we count previous version of this review) review cuz this game deserves it.  I bought this game with no big expectations because I was looking for new game and conception of metroidvania + motorbike bought me. But man, I didn’t think that this game would be so good. I had so much fun with shotting mechanics in slow-mo, but after a short while I was mainly taken by the story. Only two games in my life made my cry at the end (Laika and Night in the Woods). The funny thing is that after ending of the story I got to the conclusion that am thankful for everything I have (despite that life didn't give me a lot). Truly weird feeling given by computer game.  Pros: - Good mechanic of driving + shooting + slow-mo. Those three elements work perfectly together. - Music, o my good I don’t know where the last time was when I heard soundtrack perfectly fit a world, story and main character. Truly it’s a pleasure for the ears (I will link to two of them at the end if someone would like to try them). - Story, devs made a beautiful fable of mother and child. I was truly amazed how “grounded”, with no big fireworks the story was and how great it works. I miss that kind of stories. Despite of my full love for that game it didn't mean it don't have a flaws. Cons: - Hook could be more useful. - Rewards from side quests (The quests in case of story are good in my opinion). - Telegraphy of enemy bullets. - More teleportation points on the map (But thanks to the soundtrack it didn't bother me.) - More "usefulness" of other weapons. At the end I have two words, one for you reader and one for devs. To you reader if you survive to the end of this revies. Please give yourself a try and download a demo of this game and try it, maybe you will like it and you will buy it, I am sure that you will not regret it. And the word for devs. Thank you for this game. It's truly an amazing coincidence that I had the opportunity to play the namesake of my dead dog, who also looked like her and pass not so long time ago.  Here are those songs:   And now truly at the end (watch out it will be a spoiler form the story).

_childDocuments_.review: This is my favorite piece of art ever. This game is a absolute masterpiece and deserves more recondition.Story:This game's story is so good omg. it wrecked me emotionally, I can't explain what makes it so good without major spoilers. I'd recommend going into this game as blind as possible. Laika's relationship with puppy is so well executed and works perfect as the emotion core of the story.Gameplay:this gameplay is just fun. its a ode to old flash motorcycle games, but with GUNS! its really fluid and satisfying. especially when you get the hang of it and start blasting enemy's without and strategy and coming out unscathed. It feels a lot like hotline Miami 2, where once you get the hang of it you feel like an unstoppable god.Character's:this games central characters are so well written. Laika and Puppy feel like real people, and you slowly becoming more attached toward puppy as the story progresses meshes perfectly with the games pacing and story ITS SO GOOD. My main issue is that a lot of really good side characters get one mission and that's it, or basically no dialogue. Pebble and a Maya are the best (non-spoiler characters, if you play the game you know what character i'm talking about) characters that have so much potential but are severely underutilized. Music:The music is so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ good. it fits the game's theme and world so well. Every song (besides recurring dream) are amazing. Songs like Heartglaze Hope fit the themes of the game so well, and bloody sunset fits the world so well. Than there's the tracks that play during the end of the main missions, Trust Them is pretty good, The Whisper, End Of The Road, I'm Not Gone, and Mother are amazing, and My Destiny is godlike. There are so much gut-wrenching songs in this game, the all feel like a different part of Laika's character turned into absolutely amazing songs. I can't stress how amazing the games ost is, it's my favorite ost in any game, and is up there with Hotline Miami 2 and Chicory's ost's. it soooooooo good.cons:crabverdict:this game is a masterpiece that I could talk about for HOURS. Please go play this game now, you won't regret it :)Also I ship Shaza and Laika like come on they totally ♥♥♥♥

_childDocuments_.review: As a present, I got this game, and the Game is good, although mostly if you follow the main quests.My big grievance with this game is the padding with side quests which mean nothing, and that this game is a motorbike mobility based game in a metroidvania styled map. These two things, the quests and metroidvania with this movement makes the game longer than it should be, and making me want to finish the game already.Some sidequests are literally unfindable if you dont see the "Interact" button or look it up. Its actually really annoying and baffling that a Tree that I have to look for, is completely destroyed so I dont have a clue as to what to look for! But my character knows it seems like...The art is great, especially the animations and cutscenes. Although in some places it gets all over the place with hiding the road, hiding enemies, hiding bullets coming at you through foreground objects as well as the road. Sometimes its a wall, sometimes you can ride through it. Seaport did this the most, and Seaport in general sucks.The bosses however, also suck. They are boring. Creative but boring. The first and second boss were probably the coolest and thematicly in place with the game. But lighthouse boss (waiting around), pyramid boss (single attack), and final boss (Outdamaged) were a big letdown.One final thing I didnt like was the camera not going forward enough. It often gets taken control from me and I absolutely hate it. Cant see where im driving or shooting. Some birds shoot sooner than they are startled and having that extra camera leeway would be great.But it is a, good game. Its fine. Nothing too special. I would prefer it as a chapter based game rather than a metroidvania. The pyramid area is probably my most favourite area of the game because it felt like a level I was traversing. Maybe a bit like a zelda dungeon. Every other area didnt feel good enough as progressing the game, it felt it got easier with more upgrades/guns.

_childDocuments_.review: I received this game as a gift, and given that the themes and art style clicked with me, it seemed easy to give it a go right away and see what was there. I have never in my life, however, bounced harder off a core control scheme/gameplay loop than this one: the sheer act of moving from left to right is tedious and disempowering. Instead of feeling like I am an interesting or cool character in a world that is accordingly hostile, I feel like I'm a balloon tied to a bag of rocks that can't even turn said bag of rocks properly to block what looks and moves like a paper dart being thrown at me in slow motion. The idea of reloading by doing flips is cool, but *mandating* those flips just to be able to even functionally use your gun is beyond infuriating. You get so few bullets in said gun that you will do nothing but reload every few seconds, and this is not fun or interesting to do. The act of dying in a single hit in every single instance, even if your bike is slightly askew when landing, makes me feel like the least powerful and least fun to play character in the world.I have legit never hated a control scheme this much. You can't even just farm materials when you find them: you have to go find a section of slanted ground so you can do your stupid bike air reload flip to go back to shoot the rocks to pick up the stuff they drop. Supposedly this game has a 'souls like' currency system but I never noticed it because the core gameplay was so infuriating I couldn't be bothered to care whether or not I had any kind of 'currency'. You can't even reload your gun when stationary and out of combat, and that one of the stupidest and most unrealistic things I've ever heard in my life. This review is piss-poor but I really cannot convey how mad this game made me, because the setting and premise and storytelling all seem amazing, and right up my alley, but holy cow it has absolutely zero respect for the player's agency or time. What a colossal miss.

Excluding cheaters and master players, the normal time to this point will not be less than 10 hours, conservatively speaking, will be more than 15 hours. So, less than this time and leave a positive review, I'm afraid that they have given up on continuing the game.

_childDocuments_.review: The idea of a bike riding game alas flash games from the long ago was something that already sounded fun.But oh boy Laika is quite the experience.A terribly bittersweet story where some things I expected, others dont, but all of them ended up making me feel melancholic and excited to see it as unfolded.Fantastic soundtrack, each and every single one of the cassettes were a joy to find just to hear whatever tune they had.The art is beautiful, the scenery, the characters (Shaza my beloved) and the presentation was just on point for everything the game try to tell. Now gameplay wise, it was really fun and exciting, the bike gameplay really can carry a lot, but I do have some complains:- The metroidvania aspect feels like it wasnt fully embraced, you wont get much more mobility later than when you started, and when you do, its too late. Pretty much all places are accesible with just your gun and bike, which I think its nice but for a game that proclaims itself as is, I expected more.- I felt like it dragged a bit of its runtime, there was a small time between "midgame to endgame" where I had no side things to do until it was completed, then it continued, by that time I was a tad exhausted with it so I went and tried finishing things up. So overall a bit of weird pacing there.- The optimization is a bit lacking, aswell as settings for it, I would lag with too many (and sometimes just one) particles and animated cutscenes will lag behind aswell which was frustrating (they are few and are AWESOME). I could appreciate some fixing on that side but apart from that it was plenty playable. Now tl;dr I DO recommend LATB, I think it was a nice little interesting experienceIt will last about 20+ hours depending on how you do and/or completeI hope you like Laika as much as I did, and props to everyone involved (PD: I got the recomendation from Pazos god bless him (if you know, you know))
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: Complicated to recommend, but a unique, good game overall.Art style is great, music is very nice, story and characters are memorable and hits hard. Heavy game overall in tone, be ready for that.Gameplay is the part that's a bit off to me, it's not bad but it's really easy to lose track of your orientation and die, camera is a bit janky, exploration and backtracking can feel like a chore and just objectives and other things are hard to find. Exploration isn't great because moving around demands plenty of concentration so, sometimes you just wanna get to a point and it's tiring to do so. Also and this is a nitpick, game is surprisingly hard to keep at steady 170hz even with a 3070 which you wouldn't expect from a 2D platformer, guess there is some rough optimization there.Even with all of that...I think it's worth experiencing. Just lacked polish in some places and a lot of the unlocks and things are basically optional which feels a bit off. But I'll remember it nonetheless, a flawed but memorable game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a complete emotional roller-coaster, you're bound to experience a little bit of everything from start to finish! The gameplay is really fun, even if you don't get the hang of the motorcycle mechanics there's plenty of checkpoints that you don't lose too much progress. The story and music are GODLY, easily some of the most powerful pieces you'll see and hear in any media. There are some minor nitpicks here and there, big one being the lack of replayability for a Metroidvania/Motorvania; one playthrough and you've pretty much got everything covered, but honestly? That one playthrough is all you'll need, it'll knock your socks off and is DEFINITELY worth the price of admission, easily a 10/10 game from me!
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I could recommend this game unreservedly. It's got a compelling story with great characters, a convincing post-apo wasteland setting, excellent presentation and beautiful music. Furthermore, its unique gameplay twists set it apart from the more traditional "metroidvanias", offering a refreshing take on the genre.Alas, this (rather cool) motorbike gimmick proves to be the main thorn in Laika's side. The controls are a bit overwhelming, which results in a lot of clumsy unforced deaths. Combat is quite repetitive, which is further exacerbated by the "die and retry" design. Dying makes all the mobs respawn, which feels needlessly punishing at times. Bosses are a mixed bag, sometimes challenging for the wrong reasons (wonky design, repetitive wait-your-turn-to-attack patterns, etc.).In the end, I really wanted to explore the world and see the story through, so I decided it was worth toughing through the frustrating moments. If you feel you've got the resilience, go for it: rough as it may be, this game is unique.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game, that might not be what you expected when you go to play it.The game has good writing with some interesting characters and what seems like a cool story. I played the demo of this for awhile some time ago. Playing it now with the full version and its good fun again. Now i understand a little more about it to :)It is part Bullet Time, part puzzle, part metrovania, part buggy racing game, part fighting, part platforming,etc...If you are looking for a Tony Hawk or Forza horizon style racing game this is not it. What this is though is a really fun game, with a great art design, cool setting and fun gameplay that has a wide variety of aspects.Sometimes you will be shooting enemies, other times you wil be trying to avoid them and or block them with parts of your Bike,etc.. At first I wasn't sure if this would be the game for me, but once I started to take it for what it offers and not what I was expecting, i started to really enjoy it.Fun game, try it out! I played about 3 hours of the demo to, so its not just the 1 hour steam is showing here on the full game :)Oh yeah and it also runs well on the steam deck to!

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very good 20 hour game, is the short of it.Gameplay is incredibly crisp and I fell in love with it instantly. As many have pointed out, the free demo will very quickly let you will even like it. The demo allows like 2 hours of content, and the save is even loadable by the full game. While playing this game you will feel very damn cool. You will also feel like a massive fool at times. It's amazing when those two feelings are mere seconds apart, because despite having just killed a mob of enemies and successfully reloaded every single weapon, you have face-planted into the ground. Only demerit here with gameplay is the boss fights are a bit... underwhelming? They're not bad, but they are not very hard nor mechanically intense. A bit of a blessing and a curse, as on one hand I wanted a bit more, but on the other I'm also terrible at boss fights in most games. The only boss I had trouble with I figured out was the easiest with a silly cheese strat that made me feel like I was morphing into a cheese wedge.The music is beautiful. The only issue I have with the music is some locations use their own forced... not even soundtrack, but more like ambiance. Considering how long I was in some those areas, it can get kinda dull. However when in areas the cassette player is available, there's a total of like 1 hour of music when they're all unlocked. The music has found its way into my Spotify playlists, it's just beautiful.Visually, game is quite lovely. The artstyle is very pretty, and I at no point thought that something didn't look great. (Note my experience with the demo did have a strange graphical bug, but the full game didn't have it.) The only gripe I have here is the camera. Some places the camera will move to give a specific view of a zone, which is great most the time. However when backtracking, it can result in enemies you can't see. The atmosphere of all the locations is amazing. Characters can also get quite expressive too.Technically the game is quite sound. I got stuck in the ground only twice, and the second time was entirely my fault. I only encountered maybe a handful of bugs, with only one of them I could consistently cause. Besides the one I could cause every single time I wanted it, I encountered 5 gameplay bugs and a harmless UI bug. In total I got stuck in the ground twice, left the camera behind twice, and had the weird progression lock. (I did something very strange and I can easily see how that broke the game, exiting and loading fixed it.) The UI bug is sometimes a quest will be in the logbook twice, but it fixes itself and doesn't cause any instability nor loss of function.Progression wise the game is decent. There are massive jumps in capability spread throughout the game, and they all feel great. Only thing I wish is the game either was like 2 hours longer after reaching peak capability, or gave the capability a bit earlier. A New Game+ might also help this, as I would love to replay the game with all the tools at my disposal to see how cracked it would be. I only went grinding for resources once, but that's because I wanted to do it all at once. Normal gameplay provides an adequate amount of resources, especially if you don't want to upgrade weapons you don't use.Now the story. The story is terrible. No, not the quality, the content. The quality is immaculate, but this game is the only piece of media that's put me on the verge of crying. I will shamelessly admit that there was a point where I had to lie down because I couldn't see from teary eyes. It's a shame that the story will be such a small part of this review, because to me this was pretty big plus. It's terribly great, 10/10.Quests. There's a lot of fetch quests and running around the world. There is a fast travel system, but it isn't convenient all the time. I didn't find that awful as I liked moving through the environment, but I can see how players won't like backtracking and going to places they have been before for simple fetch quests. The rewards are also not great, but eh. I mostly did them for the world building and it making me plan routes through the map.Now, with being only a 20 hour game for doing most of the game's content (I am at time of writing missing just playing more blackjack and cooking more buffs... and dying a lot), the big question is replayability. The story isn't going to hit as hard, but the gameplay will still be crisp. I'm pretty sure runs could be done with a specific playstyle/weapon/goal in mind.I doubt it would ever happen, but if the developers came back to this game I would buy a DLC without any hesitation. A New Game+ would be welcome as well, as I mentioned with being able to play the whole game again with all the bells and whistles. I don't see the need for a boss rush, since the bosses are more of a story telling element than a gameplay one, but I wouldn't be against it as it would probably have wicked speedruns.It's a wonderful game of a coyote mom just trying her best. It's not a perfect game, but the things that make it wonderful easily outshine the bad.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most impactful games I've played in recent years. Laika isn't easy, both in its difficulty and the themes it explores, but its more than worth overcoming its challenges. The gameplay is fun and mechanics don't overstay their welcome. The world tells a story even when the characters aren't talking. And the music is absolutely gorgeous, albeit very melancholy. Spectacular game with an important story to tell.

_childDocuments_.review: For only 12$ and 15 hours of gameplay you will receive:•	full, completed game with nearly no bugs•	very fun and interesting dynamic exploring/shooting bloody game•	large, open, filled world, that is interesting to explore•	most memorable emotional rollercoaster of your life•	probably PTSDIf be serious, the game is perfect in every possible way. Under this cute and well-drawn game hides so much pain, suffering and difficult thoughts that surely not leave you indifferent. Adult topics that were raised is pretty unexpected and unusual, but they amaze with its simplicity and surprises with its depth. This is the first game where you really want to help NPCs and do their side quests because you really want to solve their problems and make their lives a little bit better, not because they give you XP or loot. The most valuable reward from them would be a few lines of dialogue, which would certainly be useful for a better understanding of them and Laika herself. Nearly all of the friendly characters in this game are memorable and leave some warm thoughts about them even if you don’t see them too often or even once...In addition, it is the first game in which children do not annoy, on the contrary they add contrast and more gloominess on the background of adult characters to this dark and unwelcome post-apocalyptic world. Main character`s daughter – Puppy, is an absolute gem of this game. After less than hour of playthrough, you officially become her co-parent along with Laika. You will became emotionally addicted to this innocent little fluffy cuteness and do anything to feel her happy and protected, despite everything.   The game has so many sudden heartbreaking and emotionally tense moments, that nearly the half of the game you will be emotionally devoured and play with teary eyes, trembling hands or just thoughtfully sad. These moments give you enough food for thought about, even after you fully completed the game.Along with emotionally hard and absorbing plot you would listen the angelic Beicoli music that will skyrocket your emotional instability and make all main story moments memorable and unforgettable (also after the end of the game you won't be able to listen some songs without start sobbing after a few notes). This music would lead you through the whole story and supports you in darkest and finest parts of Laika`s journey.The main therapy and emotional respite will be the fast reaction-oriented bloody gameplay with not necessary resource collecting (you can complete the whole game with basic nonupgraded gun) while listening to the Beicoli`s tapes that you collect through the wastelands.The game will have constantly emotional dominance over you. And rest assured you will love every second of this.Laika: Aged Through Blood is like a good psychologist whose shoulder you can cry on, think about your life and move forward. Despite the very depressing message of the game that will haunt you all the time, this game makes you think about very simple but important things that we rarely think about in everyday life. For example, how long have you been in contact with your elderly parents?Gameplay is fun and unique, the story will leave a deep scar on your heart for a while, the music is breathtaking. What else do you need from a game? You definitely won’t find another game like this. This is absolute perfection!
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: I'm gonna write all I thought of it then decide if it's a recommend or not, because this game has me so conflicted. It does exactly as advertised. But there are a few elements that really give me a lot to think about, but that might just be out of scope and I'm thinking ahead of myself, so take all these with a grain of salt.Laika does its job well. I just still can't shake off the feeling a few elements of it didn't really let it shine as bright as it could have, and it's really unfortunate. However, as critical as I am, it's mostly due to the fact that I really did enjoy my time with it. Sure, some portions were frustrating, but ultimately my takeaway is positive. It was clearly made with love, I think everyone can tell that when they are hands on with it. And it shows everywhere. However, even with love behind it some areas can feel either rushed or simply not entirely thought out. It is ultimately a game worth giving a chance to, but if any of the negatives mean a no-go to you, I would also just say follow your gut.

_childDocuments_.review: Where to start?Its a work of art.  A beautiful, yet challenging game.  The art style, the music, both you'll fall in love with.The story is heartbreaking, grim and yet uplifting.  And the gameplay... Once you get used to the controls the game becomes very rewarding. _childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: Going into this game, I didn't have much expectations apart from how I liked the art style. Now, after finishing this.... extraordinary experience, I have some words.1.) The story has been integrated into the game extremely well and is perhaps the best story I've personally experienced in a long while. The characters are well written and have their own goals to the point of them feeling like real people just doing what they can to survive.2.) The gameplay is both hard as nails, and exhilarating. The fact that you *must* do a backflip to reload is such a wonderful (And hate inducing) game mechanic that suits each beautifully crafted level perfectly. 3.) Finally, every, single, location in this experience is both stunningly beautiful, and wonderfully designed. I actively did not fast travel this entire game because of how much fun I had driving around.Is it frustrating? %100. Is it fun? Not all the time! Do I think it's one of the greatest in it's genre?....%100.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed the game. This movement and combat mecanic is a breath of fresh air, even if it can be frustrating at time.It has one big problem. Side quests. Each of them is a fetch quest that without knowing exactly where. They are boring and make the game a few hours too long. You need to ignore them. All of them. They are meaningless. Give no benefits (1 wood anyone?). Have poor indicators which make it take even more time to find what you are looking for.And to make it worse, they really don't mesh with the urgency of the plot.If you are unsure about where to go for a quest (main or side-quest), I highly recommend looking online, the fun is not in circling around like that to find where to press "E".But skipping all those side waste of time. Great game.
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: Short answer; solid thumbs up.Art design, great, music even better, story/ world building/ general aesthetic, better again.The controls and game play are clean and fair, you never die because of bad luck or poor design (keeping in mind I've only beaten a couple of bosses, but based on what I've played so far the design is good).This game will appeal to 'pro gamers' and the casual crowed alike. Rather than have different skill levels to cater to all types of players the developer just allowed for generous respawns and a light death penalty. Better players won't have to respawn as much and worse players (like myself) are free to retry encounters without losing much progress at all.But when you do engage an encounter just right you feel like John Wick on a dirt bike. And again, if you're just looking for a casual experience, if you ♥♥♥♥ up an encounter, the respawns are very generous. But if you think you're good, go ahead and prove it, there is a lot of room here for genuine skill expression.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow. This game was such a nice surprise. Who knew I wanted an action game with light metroidvania elements and Trials controls!? The control scheme is a lot to learn at first, but once it starts clicking it's so satisfying. The art is incredible and the gameplay stays super fun throughout as you face new challenges. The one thing I would say is that if you're going to play this game, there are a few mechanics they don't make super clear. The first is that you use candles to fast travel but they only work at the BIG checkpoints, not the small ones. You have to hold down the interact button to access a menu where you can fast travel or change your loadout. The other thing that I didn't realize for a long time was that in the journal menu the main quest line is the one marked by a skull. I spent way too long chasing down sidequests for not much reward. By the time I finished this I was pretty ready to be done, but still enjoying it. So I'd say focus on the main quests for the most part. This is a fantastic gem that everyone should play. Get it!

_childDocuments_.review: What if Excite Bike was also a metroidvania shooter? This is probably the most interesting metroidvania ever made, certainly the most interesting and original I've played. I love the overall presentation, despite the extremely grim tone. The art is simple but beautiful, the soundtrack is hauntingly atmospheric and heart-wrenching, and the unfortunately rare fully animated clips are amazing to behold. The game plays a bit like old Sonic games, often requiring route memorization of what order to kill enemies in in order to succeed. Respawn points are everywhere tho, so you're normally losing more than 10 seconds per attempt. That said, you can still explore with the weapons to find your own ways of doing things. I was very bad about remembering to use the parry mechanic, and mostly relied on the revolver (pro tip, the machine gun is super great if you continue spinning to reload). I felt it was hard, but forgiving. The narrative is incredibly grim, like anyone you meet could die as a result of you meeting them. If you can deal with that, and be willing to endure some try-try-try-try again gameplay, then I encourage you to try Laika out. Couple bits of criticism tho, the bosses aren't fantastic. I'm not sure what else they could have done with the motorbike-with-gun format but they can come off a lil meh. Also the ending is suuuper brief, sadly.
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: This is just a great game, helps that the soundtrack has been living rent free in my head since I started playing it. There's definitely an adjustment period of getting used to driving the bike while also focusing on shooting and having to decide in bullet time if you have time to block that bullet with your bike while backflipping to reload or if you should burn a bullet parry. I honestly almost never used the fast travel system because travelling the world was just so fun to do and that soundtrack absolutely kills it, almost every track just feels like it belongs regardless of what's happening on screen and that's something that's super hard to nail. I never thought I'd say I loved unloading a full mag of revolver ammo into enemy birds while backflip reloading in bullet time to accoustic guitar and indie vocals but here I am in 2024 getting way too into the world and setting of another indie game that not a single person I know has even heard of before. It's not perfect by any means, I'll straight up say I don't like the level design of the water level and the boss of that zone was just painful but that's by far the lowest point of the game for me and it's about halfway through, also not a fan of the mine level's design of fighting the same boss 4 times but both of those are outliers compared to the levels and fights around them so I'll forgive it.
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: Game-play:I found game-play to be inconsistent at times, but overall it was fine. The only similar game I've played is Ori and the Blind Forest, so I'm not familiar with the style. I found it somewhat easy to play, but hard to master. The bosses weren't very exceptional.Visual style:This game is incredible artistically. As an artist, both digital and traditional; I love the art style and visual design of the game. It certainly creates a unique feeling.Soundtrack:The soundtrack is extremely good, and builds on the atmosphere of the game and it even folds into the story of the game itself. It's also just really nice to listen to (I've used it for road trips and background music for drawing a lot).Characters:This game shines most in its characters. Each character has their own concerns, and not all of them view the player as a noble hero. The interactions Laika has with individuals across the wasteland are varied and interesting. Don't be surprised if you find yourself completing a whole string of side quests just to interact with characters more.I would, and did, recommend this game to friends and strangers. It deserves a lot more attention, and I would absolutely love to see more of this world in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: I would simply love to recommend Laika to anybody. Problem is, it's a game with very good story(which you wouldn't expect from a metroidvania) and very different style of gameplay than most. It's that sort of game where playing the demo is absolutely mandatory if you even think of buying the game. And if you do think you might enjoy it, please get the demo, get familiar with the controls and give it a try. Story is absolutely beautiful, same with soundtrack. Beícoli did absolutely incredible, and it's one of the games that is being carried by the soundtrack and few songs from which will be added to my normally listened songs.So, with the foreword already done let's get to the details. Game where you have a fusion of Trials Evolution, metroidvania and a shooter/platformer at the same time. When you first think of it like that it might seem like an absolute mess of a game. You'd be incredibly surprised how well the elements go together if you get used to the controls even a little bit. It takes a while, but when you do you feel like an absolute badass zooming past enemies, doing flips, comboing shots and weapons together for very cinematic shootouts. Characters you encounter are interesting, varied and each has a story you want to hear. I've been playing games for a big, if not major part of my life and Laika is one of the really few games that made me tear up. Story is really worth experiencing The world is really well done, with some fairly decent storytelling done by the looks of it alone. Although I'd also like to mention that Laika deals with many very... Sensitive topics so treat this as a small warning(?). There are some tedious moments in there, don't get me wrong(for example one of which is that, if you want to 100% the game you need to farm materials for weapon upgrades for example which can deter some players, although I've played through the entire game with almost basic, not upgraded equipment, so it's completely doable). Below I'll post a small pro/con list and a short TLDR:PROS:- Surprisingly good story.- Insanely good soundtrack.- Gameplay gets really fun when you get used to the very specific controls.- Very nicely done cast of characters and world.CONS:- Said specific controls can cause a lot of frustration in early stages so playing through a demo is absolutely mandatory.- Some areas are quite tough and require doing a lot of things at the same time which can build up frustration quite efficiently.(dashing, orienting your bike, shooting 3-4 enemies at the same time etc.)- I did hear about few, very rare glitches bugging some achievements, but developers are more than keen to help you with fixing your save if you get in contact through the official discord for example.TLDR:A game worth trying if you enjoy tougher gameplay or good story. If you enjoy both that's even more of a recommendation from me. It tells the story very nicely, has very good characters, doesn't overstay it's welcome and is just long enough to satisfy with the gameplay, and short enough to not make said gameplay too long for the story it's telling. If you'd ask me personally it's one of those "must play" games if you enjoy single players. It deals with some heavy topics very well. Complete recommendation from me. But it's one of those games you HAVE TO play the demo before you buy as it's really easy to get discouraged by the specific nature of the gameplay. Plus is, said demo is completely free, small to download and might encourage you even more to try this beautiful game.

_childDocuments_.review: I initially found out about this game when it was on a midweek sale, so I played its demo, and since I couldn't stop thinking about it afterwards, I bought the full game shortly after, and frankly, I'm glad I did. From the gameplay, to the soundtrack, to the story - especially the story - this isn't a game you want to miss.In terms of gameplay, this is easily one of the more unique games I played, being a combination of motorbike games and metroidvanias with guns and a hint of Katana ZERO, and it works. That said, the controls do take some getting used to, so don't be surprised if you die from wiping out more often than from getting shot. To explain the Katana ZERO comparison, every enemy - excluding bosses, obviously - dies in one hit, but so do you, so every encounter must be approached like a puzzle if you want to survive. It's also worth mentioning that enemy placements are rather frequent, especially as you progress through the story, so never let your guard down when you're out and about.The soundtrack is easily another highlight for the game, as the cassettes that you can collect throughout the game fits well with the situations you're in, whether it's blasting birds, or simply cruising across the wasteland. The other tracks are nothing to overlook either, for they set the tone of the locations where they play perfectly.The story... oh boy, the story. It's easily one of the darkest stories I've experienced in a game, and I love it for that. The first few minutes alone will set the tone that this is hell on Earth, and nothing will ever get better. Beyond that is a revenge plot featuring a compelling protagonist as she fights to protect what little she has left despite the overwhelming odds.Although the gameplay has a fairly steep learning curve, and the story and overall tone of the game isn't for the faint-hearted, this is one of the most memorable, most unique experiences I've had the honor of playing. Overall, it's a criminally underrated gem of a game, and I highly recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: I have a lot of things to say about this game. More than I can reasonably fit into a Steam review. I would like to preface my review that I seldom play games just for fun. I wholeheartedly believe video games are an art form and an experience. Laika: Aged Through Blood caught my eye because of the art style and seemingly emotional story it had to tell. Laika’s (the main character’s) world is dark and gritty. Death can happen out of nowhere, typical of an apocalypse setting. You play as a woman whose family carries a curse where they cannot die and can act as a medium to the dead. It is because of your condition that you are pulled into being a pawn for your village. Death is far too great a threat in the wastelands, so everyone relies on you to do the dirty work for the village. The story revolves around trying to protect your village from an invasionary force of birds seeking to eradicate the surface dwellers and expand their empire. Surprisingly enough, the main story itself (as in the idea of “go here do task X and then come back and talk to person Y”) is one of the weakest parts of the game for me. Yet, that’s what makes this game so incredible for me.Where the game shines is the atmosphere and characters. The atmosphere is incredible. The aesthetics of the game are incredibly well-drawn and the animations are well-illustrated. But this is only surface-level praise. The designs and themes of the world play important roles. Your tribe is very much inspired by the culture of indigenous American tribes. The invasion force dons military uniforms similar to those of many Cold War Western nations. A lot of the game seems to be an allusion to colonialism. Your tribe rests their dead at a sacred grove, which you find out is being desecrated by the birds for resources. This happens while you try to spread your brother’s ashes in the forest, which evokes your fury. Laika wants every single one of these bird’s brains splattered across the ground- and so do you. It is at sections like this where worldbuilding shines the most. You truly begin to burn with hatred for these birds and everything they do. People keep dying in brutal and cold means. By the latter half of the game, you head over to a town where birds live. Quickly you realise that not all is well in their world either. Dystopian advertisements litter the streets where people are impoverished and broken. It’s a consumerist society that is propped up by the military. I believe this is an accurate depiction of contemporary America. Though the military is out committing acts of violence against different people of the world, their people are suffering. Towards the end of the game, you meet the leader of a resistance movement who explains to you that bird life isn’t glamorous. He is malnourished and poor- living in horrible conditions while the bloated wealthy class continue to live lavishly (sounding more and more like the US). In the aforementioned town, you see a bird that tried to recruit you to a pacifist movement. A movement of birds that couldn’t dodge the draft but instead now refuse to shoot. After this mission, I only started noticing some birds were wearing white bandages on their arms. If you drive up to them- they don’t fire. I immediately felt disgusted with myself. How many of these people have I killed indiscriminately? How many times did Laika perpetuate this cycle of violence? This little detail was so profound that one of the first things I ever did in combat was scan for these birds wearing white. The characters all accomplish their intended purpose. While many of the people in Laika’s village aren’t completely pleasant, you still kind of care about them in a way (some of them, at least). Any time someone dies, you can’t help but feel like it’s your fault. When there’s a chance of a character dying, I felt like rushing to aid them immediately. Your daughter, Puppy, gets lost and I felt like my blood was rushing when I thought she could have been brutally murdered by birds. Even a lot of the less memorable characters had interesting lines and storytelling. Laika’s character development is also particularly remarkable. She doesn’t seem to change all that much throughout the story until the very end, but that’s the point. She’s a woman who does what she has to to protect those she loves. Laika knows this won’t bring her to a bright path, but she believes that what she does now will create a better future for those who follow. Her story stops short, an explosion from a nuke that she detonates with her trusty revolver. Thus, the village is left without a Laika and Puppy is left without a mother. But the message is clear, she sinned and did the hard work so that her daughter wouldn’t have to. I think the game pointed to the fact that Laika wasn’t long for this world for a while yet I still wasn’t willing to come to terms with the ending. The game was phenomenal, but I still had some criticisms. Firstly, the most minor, there were some bugs here and there. Sometimes animations didn’t load or other odd happenings would occur. These are far and few between so don’t worry, the game is very polished. I don’t usually like souls systems in games (in this game, when you die you lose your money just like in Dark Souls). They’re very stressful and just mean that if you die you might just have to end up wasting time on farming more money. This game takes a great approach to this concept by letting you craft more bags that give you more chances to get your money back. So when you die, you’ll lose 50% of your money. If you die again, you lose 50% of what you had at that point. It’s not a perfect system but it didn’t make me want to rip my hair out like Dark Souls did. Sometimes enemies are behind resource containers which take the shot for you and make you waste double the ammunition. Also, you can shoot enemies multiple times. It’s fun to juggle them sometimes but god is it annoying in the early game when they block one of your precious limited bullets. This critique is a bit subjective but I feel like the game rushed to a close. The game was still expanding and then it just abruptly ended. It makes sense for the story, but I wish I could have spent more time with the villagers. Maybe that’s the point? You couldn’t spend enough time with them? I feel like you aren’t given enough time to get attached to the characters to truly weep for them when they pass. It’s certainly tragic when characters die but I didn’t bawl my eyes out like when I played Spiritfarer. They’re around for too short a time for you to truly cry for them (but you feel horrible that your actions got them killed). Lastly, I think the medium ability Laika has wasn’t utilised nearly enough. It was so emotional when she was dragging her brother’s corpse back home, speaking to him and getting his parting thoughts. Those moments were kind of sparse in this game and I think they actually would have been incredibly moving if they were utilised more often (though where they are utilised, it’s often with great impact and depth).Overall, this game is a work of art. I wouldn’t write such a massive review (this is even a shortened version for Steam!) on it if I didn’t find it impactful. Metroidvanias aren’t my type of game so I got annoyed by backtracking a lot, but the fact that I loved this game so much should be enough to show how incredible it was. The music is astounding, it’s one of my favourite video game OSTs of all time. Pair it with the tough and gruelling world Laika lives in and it just adds all that beautiful art to the rest of the game. My final verdict is a 9/10. Every bit of this game was made with love and care and it shows. The only thing keeping me from a 10/10 is that the game started to slightly rush towards the end and the fact that I’m not crazy about Metroidvanias (also that crab boss fight took four years off my lifespan). This game is worth every penny. Please, get it.
