_childDocuments_.review: The idea of a metroidvania with motorcycle ranged combat sounds ridiculous, but it works surprisingly well in Laika: Aged Through Blood. The gameplay (movement+combat) is difficult to adjust to because of how different it is from anything else I've played, and not easy in general, but extremely satisfying once mastered. The art, story, and music are all phenomenal, and I recommend playing Laika for these elements alone. The story of Laika fighting to protect her daughter Puppy is beautiful and captivating. The subtitle "Aged Through Blood" is extremely accurate, and I found the unsubtlety of the violence rather refreshing, actually; almost every game involves lots of killing so I appreciate when games acknowledge the brutalist nature of combat in their games. I beat the game in just over 24 hours with 78% achievements, and I may return in the future to finish them off. I wholeheartedly recommend this game if you like the art style and like metroidvanias with a fun twist, but it is definitely not for everyone. Now for a couple negatives: 1. The bossfights are not very good. There are exactly two bosses that I enjoyed in this game; all the other ones were both boring and frustrating, which is a horrible combination. Dying in one hit works great for most of the game, but most of the bosses have whole phases where you have to wait for it to become vulnerable; if you get hit once you have to go back to the beginning and wait all over again. The bosses I liked had short vulnerability phases and took more shots to kill: it's much more enjoyable to redo a boss if you are doing damage to it often.2. Although the story was great, outside of cutscenes the characters were rather undeveloped: most npcs give you a blatant fetch quest and refuse to talk to you until you give them the item, but once you've completed the quest they either immediately give you a new quest or return to default dialogue. There was several times where I got frustrated because all the npcs were demanding random fetch quests at the same time, all from different areas, and none of them would talk to me except to remind me that I hadn't gotten them their item yet.3. The movement and gun combat were really fun once I got the hang of them, but after 20+ hours of backflipping and one-shotting birds the gameplay started to get repetitive. For the most part, I think the game was well paced and a good length, but it does get boring in parts when there is no story progression and the combat challenges start to look the same. The enemies do get harder as the game progresses, which really helps this problem, but I did consider quitting a couple times because I was bored.4. theres an achievement for dying 1000 times. this is quite possibly the worst achievement idea ive ever seen, and ive played the stanley parable. i refuse to farm deaths for an achievement 🙄TLDR: This game is beautiful and satisfying to play, but the bosses aren't great and it can get monotonous at times. I recommend it overall: the story and artstyle really carry this game.

_childDocuments_.review: It's an excellent metroidvania, and certainly a highlight of the genre, sporting unique movement, refined action gameplay, and an absolutely stellar soundtrack. If you're unsure about whether or not it's for you play through the demo, and if you like it, pick up the whole thing. Absolutely worth it, even at full price.

_childDocuments_.review: Laika's a motorcycle metrovania style game that you can beat in 20 hours. But that twenty hours is one hell of a gripping story in a grim setting with depressing tones mixed with some seeds of hope. It's biggest strengths is the main gameplay itself, the moving story, and the wonderful music you'll listen to and unlock tapes of as you  play through. It's biggest weakness is some of the boss design being fights that drag out for quite a while where death has you refight the boss from the beginning every time you mess up. Thankfully not all of those fights are like this and there's plenty of stages to drive through between the big fights either.I left the game craving much more of the lore and world settiing. It was such a great experience that this review can't do it justice.

_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this game, I really really did. The story, music and artwork are beautiful and stunning. But the game's gameplay, while incredibly innovative, makes me want to tear my hair out. In this game, you use a bike to get around, the bike has alot of utility being able to block and deflect bullets. The problem is compared to a lot of other metroidvanias, Laika: aged through blood only gives you 1 hp and takes away half your currency each time you die. And you are going to die, a lot. A simple backflip to reload your gun could kill you, getting shot by 5 different enemies at once while your gun only has 2 bullet is borderline unfair. To put simply, the gameplay is harsh and unforgiving. The last straw came when I got stuck in the worst save location without any way to backpeddle to a former area. This is a beautiful game with an amazing concept, but the controls and gameplay is just not for everyone.

_childDocuments_.review: To get it out of the way, yes, this game is incredible and well worth the $20 asking price. I almost never write reviews for anything, but this game is an unsung masterpiece with a story so compelling that it kept me wanting more and left me reeling after completion. To memory only one other game has even come close to leaving me feeling this way, that being Undertale. The story is the aspect of the game that kept me hooked, and in a lesser game would be what makes it stand out, but due to how totally unique and masterfully crafted the rest of the game is, I can't say that it alone is what makes the game nor can I say that it is the de facto selling point of the game.Go ahead and skip this paragraph if you want to go in completely blind. I will be touching on the general story of the game and why I think it works so well....Laika is by far the most compelling protagonist in any game I've played in the last few years. And though overarching story describes the tale of a Laika as she battles against impossible odds to destroy a regime of fiercely militaristic, genocidal birds who seek nothing less than total annihilation of all land-dwelling life. Laika is special, however, because she can interact with the land of spirits, allowing her to speak with the dead before they pass on or even to come back from death herself. This is a more-than-sufficient story hook, but is actually the least compelling part of the narrative. What makes the game's story truly shine is in the characters, specifically Laika and her family. Their curse is hereditary, with immortality being passed from mother to daughter once the time comes. Perhaps by necessity, those cursed with undeath, if they even survive the sickness that precedes its inheritance, are raised as soldiers, not children, and are forced to bear children until one daughter grows to replace them. Until them, they are doomed to live out their life as a pawn of war, doing the grunt work that would be otherwise too dangerous for the mortal villagers. Additionally, each life lost and taken for an immortal makes them lose themselves a little bit, and with age memories of past lives twist and turn leaving their memory incoherent scramble of events. This is the curse that Laika bears, and that should she survive, her daughter Puppy will too. Laika lost many daughters before, and not wanting to endure the anguish of losing another child, Laika doesn't name her final daughter. She hopes that this will help her to not grow too attached to her puppy. It doesn't work. Laika never raises Puppy like a tool, as her mother raised her, and tries to keep her happy and insulated from the horrors of the outside world, but Puppy is curious and hyperactive, and due to the deaths of her sisters and best friend, had already lost her innocence. Even still, Puppy is a happy and optimistic child, but not without her misgivings. Death is always on her mind, and she's afraid of dying, and what would happen to Laika if she inherited Laika's immortality. It is through their interactions they love each other very much. Puppy even serves as Laika's moral compass. She is the only person left that gives Laika joy and purpose. The dialogue they share is often sad, sweet, and eloquently-written. In fact, the game's script is to the point and never overly verbose. ... Laika has an incredibly unique combat system, and while awkward at first, it keeps traversal and exploration and engaging. The impact of the weapons is satisfying, and combined with the corpse physics and (frankly comical amount of) spattered blood, the combat becomes incredibly meaty and satisfying as you learn to master it. Checkpoints are spaced apart fairly, and because  save for the rare boss encounter, both Laika and any enemy die in a single hit, combat can become a thrilling but erratic sequence of shooting, flipping, and maneuvering out of the way or even directly into enemy bullet spatter. Even still, learning to shoot, ride, reload and parry in while maintaining proper momentum and rotation of your character, while not too difficult due to future weapon upgrades, high sensitivity and bullet time, is still a bit of a learning curve, and is exacerbated by the fact that the starting revolver has only 2 bullets at level 1, so gunplay against 3 or more enemies takes a bit of practice at the beginning.Characters feature colorful designs, distinctive silhouettes and expressive body language and faces, and the game has crafted a beautiful but bleak post-apocalyptic landscape to explore and fight through. It has a beautifully colorful hand-drawn style that makes the backgrounds pop against the bold-outlined characters, and a masterfully written soundtrack that accentuates the silent beauty of the remainder of the world. The score is filled with plucky acoustics and surprisingly often features vocals from an in-universe singer. When in the wastelands you can collect cassettes and play them at your leisure. By comparison, the larger more story-significant areas and "dungeons", there will instead be an accompanying ambient track. The game is heavily elevated by its exemplary graphical and auditory presentation, and this in tandem with the fiercely emotional narrative was able to on several occasions jerk a tear from my jaded gamer eyes.While I adore this game, it is very flawed. Think of this as bit of a lightning round of gripes. For one, the game has some major issues with its pacing, both narratively and gameplay wise. A lot of my issues with the game's pacing gameplay-wise has to do with the game's at times microscopic instructions as to how or where to get to pivotal areas or questlines. This is combined with a fast travel system a la dark souls one where only a select few checkpoints, often inconveniently placed, are warpable, and with the exception of a particular key item, require consumables to even travel between and ONLY if you are already at another warpable checkpoint to begin. This led me to getting frustrated on occasion, but admittedly traveling the through the desert highways on my bike listening to some nice music was nice after a particularly intense encounter or story beat. The pacing is also a bit scattered narratively, but without getting into spoilers, one character taking her life felt rushed, underdeveloped, and ultimately tasteless. The climax, while good and thematic, felt rushed, sudden, and underdeveloped.Second and thirdly, the sidequests in the game are a cut above horrible. Just about every last one simply means travelling to a place to buy or collect an item for a character with no real useful rewards or satisfying narrative through line or conclusion. Also despite being technically being a metroidvania, your movement options and upgrades are few and far between and underutilized. There is one ability that is used for just one stage and boss or the odd interactable on the overworld, and another, by far the most fun ability in the game, which is used to its full potential but only unlocked in the very end of the game so it never has time to truly shine.My final issue is that almost every single boss in the game (and there are very few), is a frustrating mess in which you have to wait your turn to even hurt it, scripting most battles. Two bosses are autoscrollers, even. One of those is a three-part encounter. This boss design philosophy is confusing and antithetical to the rest of the hectic action of the game. There is only one non-turn based boss, but because of that, both of its healthbars can be depleted in around 15 seconds by a crafty player.It would be great if they weren't issues to begin, but the quality of the game in its entirety is great enough that I am willing to look past these issues. However, factoring them into account, I can't in good conscious give the game anything higher than an 8/10, two huge thumbs up, and a review an ninety minutes in the making.

_childDocuments_.review: My Little Review for Laika: Aged Through Blood :>Overall the game is very good the story is pretty straightforward but its impactful and it stays with you and it really makes it feel like your actions have some consequences (doesn't change the ending or anything), it also just made me cry like three times so if you want some feels yeah.  The gameplay is overall very fun and it feels fluid and it makes you feel cool in general.  The exploration is also fun the world is very pretty and has cool details.  The world also feels very fleshed out and rarely feels empty, although that could also partly be because the map isn't massive.  The fast travel and saving systems are also very nice.  Also this game has the most banger soundtrack ever written it fits the vibe so well and I unironically listen to all the songs outside of playing the game.  The music also comes in form of collectable cassettes you find in game which is very very cool.My main cons of the game are the following: The boss fights can feel a little underwhelming as they aren't too challenging and some are a bit annoying (its not awful but definitely not the highlight of the game) - however a plus to the bosses is the amazing cutscenes that come with them.  There are some bugs, for example I got stuck in a wall while using the dash on two separate occasions, and one time it just didn't put me into a required cutscene or just planned event so I had to leave and rejoin to get it to work.  Also as it is a metroidvania I wish it had more power ups that let you back track and go into areas you couldn't access without them.  There were a couple of them but there's only two meaningful movement upgrades, and they both do the same thing one is just a better version of the other.I fell in love with this game almost immediately because of the beautiful style and I stayed for the story and gameplay. Overall I would totally recommend the game it was a very enjoyable experience and in my opinion the pros heavily outweigh the cons.One more note I might be a little biased because I love metroidvanias and I'm kinda a sucker for post-apocolyptic worlds.I hope someone finds this useful :)
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: Great hook, awesome premise and incredible style, but in the end it doesn't actually do that much with it. Most of the bosses are pretty appalling design wise, they're a slog no matter how hard you find them. It sucks because they're supposed to be narratively significant, but the mechanics just feel tacked on,Narrative itself seems like it has a lot to say, but ends up shrugging all that off. There is a world where it can work, and there are elements that are interesting, but it fails to deliver in a really disappointing way. It's bleak for the sake of it, and the inclusion of SA felt especially tasteless, like it was shoved in last minute. (Its not a dark, depressing, edgy setting without DOMESTIC ABUSE and CSA amiright?)I really wanted to like this game, and I do like some parts. If you're into a fun, sometimes baffling metroidvania with unabashedly furry character designs, give it a shot! But if that's not enough to get you through it alone, give it a pass. Play Echo instead or something

_childDocuments_.review: Okay listen, I feel bad giving this a negative review because the art, music, character designs, world building, etc are all genuinely fantastic... but I would feel worse giving it a disingenuous recommendation after the miserable slog that is the last 30-40% of this game.They just stretched this cool concept of a moto-shooter metroidvania thingy wayyy too thin. The guns aren't distinct enough to feel different. The shotgun is the only real exploration tool you get in the whole game (the hook doesn't count, it's used in like 2 areas and will probably rubber-band your face into the floor). Hitboxes are inconsistent. Platforming feels clunky and frustrating when it's not at high speeds. Cinematic cameras will get you shot by off-screen enemies you otherwise would have seen. There's 6 bosses, and only the first 3 are fun, the rest are you wrestling against the clunky low-speed maneuvering in tight enclosed spaces (slow and confined are definitely what i think of when I think of motorbikes, yep). And the backtracking...dear god the backtracking... seemingly every side quest in this game is either (A) A fetch quest where you backtrack through a whole level to find mundane items like flowers or herbs, or (B) which is somehow even more boring... it just passively completes while you progress the main story.Longest 30 hours of my life.
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: I feel pretty mixed about this game, I LOVE the art, the music, the characters, (some of) the gameplay, but man some parts of this game are ROUGH.I think its a well made game for the most part, its stable, it runs well and has some really fun and unique ideas, but while it has very high highs, it also has some truly low lows. some of the decisions made for the actual gameplay are very questionable and/or frustrating.Like half of this game is a glorified fetch quest, someone asks you to go get something, you go out of your way to get it, you come back and get a crumb of engaging dialogue with an absolutely pitiful amount of rewards, and then they immediately ask for something else. repeat for almost every single side quest. The worst part is that when your initially exploring a new area quest items wont even spawn until an NPC asks for them, so you gotta drag your bike all across the dessert over again for every single quest. It can be incredibly monotonous, again for rewards that are almost always near worthlessThe other major issue I have with this game is the boss fights, I think the first couple are decent enough, but a lot of them have serious issues. These are fights where you have to wait for the enemies weak point to open up before you can damage them, have multiple phases, and you have only one hit point, with NO CHECKPOINTS.you have to restart the entire fight every single time you get by something, or even just land your bike wrong.The actual designs of the bosses are pretty cool, but I started dreading fighting them (The egg and crab can go to hell especially).I've complained a lot about this game, but I don't regret playing it and want to end this off with what I REALLY liked about this game.  I felt like this games overall presentation was overwhelmingly beautiful, from its gorgeous melancholy soundtrack, to its striking art style. The story and characters were also engaging, theres some particular moments that are very shocking and memorable. The gameplay (while still having some major issues) was very inventive and fun for the most part (doing 360s with your bike to reload is VERY cool)You should probably try out the demo before buying the game, should tell if you'll like this game or not.I had a lot of issues with this game, but I also don't think I'll forget about it anytime soon.I wish the best of luck to the devs at brainwash gang, you guys have made some really great and unique stuff!

_childDocuments_.review: one of the marks of an excellent game concept is, upon seeing it, you think "duh! why didnt i think of that?" laika created that thought in my mind throughout the entire game, while managing to execute on those concepts perfectly.first, the gameplay. the concept of "2d run-and-gunning motorbike adventure" is not one i had ever thought of before, but now i wont be surprised if this game spawns an entire genre around it. the concept spawns so many brilliant and obvious in hindsight ideas like doing tricks to reload and putting your bike between you and the enemy to block, integrating the bikes movement into combat. this combined with the fluid controls and the quick respawns made every tiny encounter feel like its own puzzle, letting you combo between your weapons skills and movement to mow down hordes of enemies, all while looking and feeling like an absolute badass. the combat was difficult in places, requiring many many attempts to defeat some groups, but instead of thinking "this is unfair" after dying, i always thought about what went wrong and what to do differently the next time.a game with such brilliant gameplay could be forgiven for having a lackluster story, however laika knocks it out of the park in that front as well. the world of laika draws you in deep, letting you discover everything about what the world is like and how it got that way for yourself instead of outright telling the player. the game has some excellent twists even in its premises that prey on what people who play a lot of games will expect from their stories and plot elements, and pulls these false assumptions out from under you to create creeping realizations that had me taking breaks to process. the stakes are perfectly set, high enough to cause plot tension but not to high as to make the outcome predictable. my only gripe with the story is that the tensional and emotional climax happens at about the 2/3s mark, and is solved rather quickly afterwards. the finale has its own tension and stakes of course, but it isnt able to achieve the edge of my seat trembling that that event about 2/3s in created. perhaps the resolution to that event could have been moved to the finale to keep that anxiety up. the story is still beautiful and heart-wrenching and EXCELLENT as it is, it just sits at excellent rather than perfect for me personally.on top of the excellent plot and gameplay, there are so many more tiny details that make this game feel fleshed out and expertly balanced and overall loved. the little quest and dialogue details that could have been easily left out but add so much to the world and its feel. the cooking system and how it becomes an essential part of the game rather than just an extra boost. the soundtrack being diegetic and tied to optional unlockables, getting excited for each new cassette so you can hear more of the game's absolutely beautiful soundtrack. the fact that quest and item descriptions are narrated by laika herself, giving insight into her thoughts and additional lore that a bog standard description would.every part of this game feels expertly and lovingly crafted in a way you rarely see. i bought this game on sale for 16 dollars, but i would have GLADLY payed the full 20 for such an amazing experience. laika: aged through blood has quickly become one of my top games of all time, and i hope it will be one of yours too.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely fabulous game. Gorgeous, great soundtrack, extremely fun and rewarding mechanics, lovely deep story. I played through the entire game with a controller and that was enjoyable for me, though some may find it too difficult; mouse and keyboard seems significantly easier (you can move the reticule anywhere on the screen and shoot with less calculated accuracy) so I recommend that for anyone getting frustrated. I'm shocked this game is not more popular than it is. Truly a stunning piece of work, thank you to all those who put their time and effort into it.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed this game, there are so many positives, but I find it hard to recommend.  Let me explain.The gameplay, and this may be seen as a deterrent, mostly reminds me of Star Fox Zero.  For those uninitiated to that, let me put it simply; the controls WILL frustrate you.  It is a combination of the Trials motorcycle series, where you crash whenever your rider touches the ground, and a precision twin stick shooter.  Just like in Star Fox Zero, your movement and aiming are independent of each other, and it is extremely difficult to get your brain to put those two things together, especially when you die in a single hit.  Now, there are many checkpoints, and you are given a Shovel Knight-esque way to recover your loot to eliminate any losses, and the game provides you multiple ways to deal with enemies, but there are sections where I died so. many. times. trying to get my bike in the right spot while simultaneously dealing with enemies shooting at you.  Not only that there are foreground obstacles and other visuals to make it difficult to even see your bike, causing needless frustration.This makes it seem like a hard sell, so let me gush over the positives.  When that gameplay works, it feels awesome!  When you nail that difficult section, and deal with the bosses, it always feels satisfying, and you get that beating the dark souls boss moment when you get it right.  I did get better at the game, even though it wasn’t always clear to me at the time.  The story was engaging.  I did side quests for the story over the rewards, that was how much I was engaged.  The devs are unafraid to go there with a post-apocalyptic world, go back and forth with emotions, and portray relatable characters for the context.  If I was cursed with essentially being the gun toting grim reaper on a motorcycle, I would say many would act in the same way.  Also did I mention you get to essentially be a gun toting grim reaper on a motorcycle?The visuals are outstanding.  I loved how the world looks, and how well it connects with the story.  For a post-apocalyptic world they do a great job to make areas visually distinct and full of detail.  The music portrays the world to a bygone era before the apocalypse, but is done well and I enjoyed the contrast.There is a nice development of weapons with upgrades, and skills your bike acquires to expand the gameplay.  However, you acquire most of the upgrades very late in the story, and I can’t imagine doing some of the final segments without the rocket launcher, making them more required than optional.  One piece of advice, you may be tempted to backtrack; don’t.  I got frustrated a couple times on tedious fetch quests that were not worth it, save for ammo upgrades.  Most of the side quests are designed to be around the story area you are in, but if you forget, do not go back until you acquire easy ways to fast travel.  They can be done much more easily near the end game.  Most rewards suck anyways.At the price of 20 bucks and on sale for around 12, it makes for a solid but tempered recommendation.
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: Words cannot describe how amazing this game is.I picked up the demo from my discovery queue because it had a neat animated trailer, and I loved it so much that for the next few days I was thinking solely of getting the full game.Once I did, i fell in love with the game unbelievably fast. I came in expecting a really good game, not a game that would immediately shoot to the very top of my favorite games list.The combat is shockingly smooth, engaging, and fun, the characters and their dialogue know how to get you to care for them more than you ever think you would, and the music is absolutely gorgeous, and despite me being someone that is typically very uninterested in music with lyrics, I fully intend on adding a ton of the songs to my music playlist(s).The game does *not* hold back any punches to get what it needs to get across through you, and there are many moments where I was just left in silence after witnessing what it had to throw. I don't even know what else to say. This game has been an incredible ride. (pun not intended)If you are reading this, do yourself a favor, and give the demo, at the very least, a try.

_childDocuments_.review: Quick Review from a Casual Gamer who just started playing indie games.My overall review on the game is its pretty fun, game goes by pretty quick. I beat most of the game in about 15 hours of game play, both main mission and a majority of side quests. Game play while seemingly repetitive is very satisfying. While its the same thing, the satisfaction of constantly juggling enemies with  a combo while reloading feels great. The story is grim and enticing, and was pretty impactful. I only have two complaints, which are a minor inconvenience, pale in comparison to the overall game. Story felt a little too edgy, characters cussing when the conversation is in a different tone, makes it feel like its out of place and just wants to add more cuss words. You can make a narrative feel dark without so much cursing. And the controls themselves are much better on keyboard and mouse than controller. I wanted this game to be on controller so the gameplay could be more relaxing, but man aiming on the controller is impossible, idk if its just me but mouse and keyboard felt MUCH better.Anyway, solid game 8/10, pick it up its noice.

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't felt my heart sank playing a videogame in a while. There are a few games that have struck that bullseye, namely Oneshot, Undertale, Everhood, and Ori and the Blind Forest/Will of the Wisps, but those were a couple years ago. Brainwash Gang, you sure know how to make a game that's both enjoyable in gameplay and story-wise. I knew, even without paying for the demo, that this was gonna be worth my money, and sure enough it is. Can't recommend it enough.12/10; the extra 2 is how many days it took for me to recover from that ending. Anyone who plays this game has struck diamond.
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful game. Brutal story. Amazing music.I really liked the controls and the traversal. The game feels good to play.Now, it is definitely not for everyone. I loved playing the Trial bike flash games, and Laika feels a bit like them. The map layout is clever, and I really appreciate the novelty of the game.For me it's an 8/10.There is such a discrepancy between the great music during normal gameplay and the somewhat boring music in boss fights. Combined with most of the bosses being kinda underwhelming, it becomes a lacklustre experience. I wish the boss fights felt better. I think the normal combat is fine, though the weapons could have more interesting upgrades.Still a great game nevertheless. Thank you, developers, for a wild ride and a good time.

_childDocuments_.review: This might be the most conflicted I've felt about a 2023 release. Like what a lot of people have already said, the mechanics are tough to wrap your head around with the mixture of Trials/Excitebike traversal and 2D twin-stick shooter combat with one-hit kills. It's incredibly thrilling and satisfying to pull off some of the motorbike bullet-time acrobatics, but this game also gave me two of the most frustrating combat sequences I've had all year. There are unnecessarily difficult mechanics that make some sections just tedious and aggravating. Still, I admire the boldness in the direction that really clicks when you get into a weird stop-and-start flow state a la Hotline Miami. Closest thing that plays like it is Rollerdrome, which I ultimately prefer on a mechanical level, especially with its decision to not punish the player for not landing on your feet. While there's a practical reason for the growing homogeneity of video game control schemes, I can't help but respect a game that bucks that trend and comes up with its own set of controls to create unique moment-to-moment gameplay.It's up there with Alan Wake 2, Hi-Fi Rush, and Season: A Letter to the Future for delivering the best aesthetic experiences in 2023 video games. Just a fantastic cartoony visual style reflected in the memorable character designs, striking background art, and the bombed-out brown and bloody red color palette. The soundtrack is appropriately somber yet has this driving undercurrent of pent-up emotion brought to life by the beautiful breathy reverb-heavy feminine vocals, soft and sometimes relentless percussions, clean plucky melodic guitars, and melancholic keys. It's a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ mood biking through the desert wasteland of your war-torn home country devastated by avian colonizers with evocative place names like "Where the Doom Fell", "Where the Waves Die", and "Where Iron Caresses the Sky". The narrative goes to some real dark places that aren't in any way softened by the cartoon animal characters. It's a game about dealing with the burdens of motherhood and the different ways of surviving and resisting under the brutal cruelty of imperialist forces. The cast goes about dealing with these challenges in very human ways, some of which are selfless and self-serving, all of which are written to be understandable if not relatable. The dialogue in particular is cutting in its raw honesty. It's not without moments of levity, but by and large it tells stories of suffering with a sense of poignancy. All in all, it really is a special kind of game that I have a hard time recommending to just anyone. It's uncompromising in its vision, both in its mechanics and in its narrative. You need to have a ton of patience for its difficulty, and you need to have a strong stomach for its storytelling turns.
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: So much love clearly went into this game and there are so many things that are great. The art (both in the game and cutscenes) is gorgeous. Character design is wonderful. The lore is interesting. The tone gets a little dark in ways that are gratuitous, but I love the western aesthetics so I can overlook some edginess.I love collecting cassettes to expand the soundtrack, its an idea that more games should implement. It's a good incentive for people who love the game (who will enjoy some novelty in the repeating playlist) but easy enough to ignore if you don't care for completionism. The physicality of the cassette player in the menu is also something I love.Despite all there is to love, the game was just not fun to play. It did not take me 15 hours to figure that out (probably 1/2 of that was idling in menus, anyway), I spent a long time trying to push past that feeling because I was legitimately interested in the characters and story and wanted to know what happened. But ultimately the game beat me and I couldn't continue any further.My big gripe with the game is that the combat seems at odds with itself, which often drives players to more conservative, less fun strategies. I suspect when confronted with more enemies than their revolver had bullets, most players left the combat arena to reload because the places to do so in the arena were too dangerous or non-existent. The worst example of this is the .This could have been fixed pretty easily by making enemies slightly less accurate/not always approached at a straight line and then designing combat arenas around building and maintaining speed. Then make up for that loss of difficulty by making enemies more plentiful and let them move (oh yeah, with a few exceptions, enemies in the game are completely stationary). This formula has worked well for other movement shooters (eg Rollerdrome, My Friend Pedro). It's not the only way to solve the problem, but I do think it's the largest problem facing the game.That's the big issue that I feel must be addressed, because it's pervasive and pretty core to the game. Some smaller gripes I also had that did compound that problem:1. The soundtrack is very small and you can't find new tapes fast enough to keep the songs from getting old. It seems they only used a single artist, who is great but that made it worse by leaving the soundtrack with little variety.2. The game features SOO much backtracking. Normally I'd applaud devs for having very limited fast travel, but every time a side quest sent me across the map again, I felt hollow. This problem is exacerbated by the previous two: if combat was more fun or the soundtrack less limited, then going around the map so much would not be so painful.3. The control for turning the bike around was inconsistent, which got me killed in some key moments and led to quite a bit of frustration. 4. The rewards for side-quests were so bad. I did them anyway because I was motivated by the characters, and maybe that speaks for itself. But when they give me like 5 of a common crafting resource, I'd almost feel better receiving no reward.
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: Played the demo version for about an hour and then picked up my save on the proper game. I've beaten first boss now, and give the game high marks on originality, art, audio, and presentation. My main complaint and it's a big one is that the difficulty is just way too high. Would be an easy thumbs up if there was selectable difficult level that offered more health or ammo, but as is you can be doing perfectly and dump your bike and have all progress lost. I don't mind souls like progression at all, but in this game any fall is fatal, and any hit by enemies is fatal, so even basic encounters are taking me a tremendous number of retries.[Update] - They added in an accessibility option that is supposed to make it so you have a small window to adjust after landing on your head so you don't instantly die. Unfortunately it doesn't seem to be working.
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: If you see the weird 2d stuck on a motorcycle platformer and think "that looks awful but everything else looks so good maybe it's not too much and I can just flirt past it " then let me tell you that it is indeed 99% of my playtime. I played to the first boss and the cutscene I was rewarded with after was so short I thought I skipped it. It fact It was literally all shown in one scene of the trailer! The flipping skull? That's it.I don't know why I bought this, I knew I wasn't going to like the platformer and now I feel bad refunding it because the rest of the game (the non-platformer art/animation, the music, the plot, etc) obviously had a lot of care only to be set unfortunately on top of some 2d mobile game. For god's sake there's like 4 buttons to control it.Really unfortunate.
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: First thing to say is this is not a pleasant game. It's very sad, very violent and it's very serious, nasty violence. Give this one a skip if that's not your thing.This is a very impressive game on pretty much every level. The gameplay is fun and fairly original, with a reasonable but not excessive amount of challenge. The story and characters work fantastically well, on both the level of the overarching plot and also at the individual quest level. It's visually powerful and the soundtrack is both unique and atmospheric. It's not even at a very high price point.I can make complaints - the map centre is frustrating to navigate around, the upgrades cost a bit too much given the campaign's playtime, objectives aren't always easy to spot - but really they're nitpicks, and they feel irrelevant even to me making them. The simple fact is it's just a very good offering and well worth your time picking up.
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: I don't see the praise for this overrated turkey. Aiming is randomly inconsistent.  Sometimes I can hit a small object across the map.  Other times I miss a shot with something an inch away with no clear feedback as to what is different between the two cases.  It is hard to tell which direction the bike is travelling especially during boss battles with the screen zoomed out.   I press the button to change direction and about 1/4 of the time it doesn't seem to work. All this leads to a frustrating mess. Story is interesting although a bit over the top.  I like the graphics style and world.  Music is great.  The inconsistencies of the controls and presentation just eventually lead me frustrated and angry.  Thumbs down for me.  Fail.
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: so uh... I hate that there aren't "mixed" reviews but only GOOD or BAD and initially I was conflicted on what to say about this game but overall it was enjoyable enough to earn a YES from me.THE GOOD:- Game felt really good, hard enough with it's innovative gameplay.- I had a blast driving around, Sidequests were also good with bits of lore scattered around them.- Bosses weren't that hard and the last two were even pretty boring.- Music was top tier, probably the best part of the game followed by the Art Style.- Story wise it was really something... made me feel a roallercoaster of emotions, but to be fair i feel like the ending was rushed too much, I'm talking also about the Cutscenes.THE BAD:- Some sections were incredibly frustrating and boring.- you get the "cool Powers" too late in the game to even be able to enjoy them properly.- slow upgrading system, even with buffs your don't earn that much currency.- The Ending... this was the biggest letdown unfortunately, could've been way better without changing anything but adding that "something" that was needed in my opinionif you like Metroidvanias and want to try something different, this game is for you and it's worth it even at full price.
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: I wish more games had this game's storytelling sensibilities. The way the world and the story aren't twisted to serve the player is just, mwah! It really feels like being part of a world that the characters lived in before you arrive. There are things that are reveals, not because Laika just found out, but because everyone but the player already knows and it's uncomfortable to talk about. People avoid mentioning a sore subject, as in real life. To me that's genius.There are storytelling elements we've seen in games before (ready the menu descriptions of everything!) but there's one specific thing that I wish someone thought of sooner. Scripted attempts to make the player feel guilt, a la Spec Ops, is never gonna hit for me again.The game's a masterpiece. I don't think antifascist art has been expressed so clearly in the medium of a video game before.

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot recommend this enough it's absolutely captivated me while I've been playing. For me it just hit all the right notes; engaging gameplay, reasonable challenge, beautiful artstyle, great story and most characters seem well written. _childDocuments_.review: Man, I really wanted to love this one but I just couldn’t get over a few fundamental issues. I loved the music and art, and the relationship between Puppy and Laika seems so earnest. However, I ran into many QoL issues the deeper I got into Laika ATB. There should be a large balance meter visible at all times instead of when aiming with the reticle (the gear in the bottom right is great but the subtle red coloring when off balance is hard to see). Considering how minuscule Laika’s sprite becomes, it’s insane to me that this isn’t an option. It must be a nightmare for colorblind players. Also, this game is really not suited well for Steam Deck. Laika’s sprite just gets way too small to be seen well. It works better on a monitor or TV, but even then sprite size, on screen action, and how easily Laika becomes lost in the background makes it needlessly difficult to see where you are and how to land.The trial and error boss fights are a huge blemish on this game, too. Dying to a bad landing angle or to a stray bullet in the final phase of a boss is infuriating. I never felt like I was improving as I died again and again, and having to repeat boss fight phases over and over just to try something again is pure tedium. There are also mechanics that I just don’t think work well, such as wheelies to get across tightropes or shotgun propulsion. It all feels really random and inconsistent.Level design can be hit or miss, but I did like mastering sections in the moment. Going back across previously explored levels is really tedious, though, and the limited fast travel currency made me quite apprehensive to even fast travel.There’s obviously a lot of care and quality here, but the fundamental issues above made this game so frustrating I couldn’t bring myself to continue it.
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful, bittersweet story about motherhood, loss, sacrifice, and vengeance among many other deep and messy topics it isn't afraid to get into. Throughout your travels you'll come across a number of funny and interesting characters who you’ll love, hate, adore, and make you reflect. The music for this game is so well done and incredibly moving, it really ties the whole game together. I was initially drawn to this game by the art/visuals and they did a fantastic job with them. The characters all look unique and amazing and some of the bosses and levels were very cool visually. I could recommend the game on just these aspects alone. The actual gameplay can be challenging and frustrating in regards to the controls and mechanics, but once you master them it can lead to some pretty satisfying moments. You will die a lot in this game whether it’s due to losing orientation of your bike and slamming poor Laika’s head on the ground, being unable to see a projectile amidst the flying bodies and gore, or simply mistiming a dodge (dying 1000 times is literally one of the achievements). It would've been nice to get more abilities to spruce up the gameplay considering you only really get one and that's towards the end of the game. 9/10 made me cry
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: The core game play loop was okay. I didn't actually do everything because I was more concerned with the story. Though in the process I may have missed some of it. I enjoyed this game but it wasn't a happy game and the core game play is pretty hard to figure out or at least i was for me. There isn't very much else like it though that I'm aware of. I would probably most closely compare it to goodnight punpun. For better or worse. Though I generally value games that make me feel something very highly. I cried a few times throughout. The music is also quite good and available on Beicoli's bandcamp. I think I've listened to the tape songs more than I've played the game. I would generally recommend giving the demo a try if you're on the fence. Its a pretty good indicator of how well you would get along with the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely a non-standard metroidvania, and better for it.The art, the characters, the music, and the overall atmosphere are incredible.The traversal of the map is a cool break from tradition and how it's woven into combat is nice.Fighting is interesting enough, the guns are fun and integration with the movement systems works well.Could probably be more normal enemies, the bosses are overall good though.I had a good time with this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: It's a great game! Metroidvania+motorbike action. Cool gory art style with melancholy music that is too good! The story is okay, it has some kind of message in it, and I think they deliver it pretty well (I guess).Exploring the land with motorbike and shooting enemy mid air while doing backflip or frontflip while maintaining the balance of your bike before landing is just great.The weakest thing about this game is the boss battle in my opinion, the later boss battle feels easy after you got all the upgrade. Hell I beat the final boss just in few second by spamming all my weapon.I feel like the dev kinda hold down a bit on difficulty. The fist half is pretty challenging because you only have 2 bullets in your gun and sometimes the enemy is a way more in a single place. But the more you progress, you upgrade gun and get more gun, make the later game fells easier. If you want more challenge in this game, just use pistol and never upgrade the weapon.Overall it is a bloody cool game!
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: Very good game, though not that much emphasis on the "unlocking traversal options" kind of gameplay. One of those upgrades is also very situational, which is a bit of a shame. In general, it did not feel like a metroidvania to me.Thats not to say that it *doesn't* happen, and the other (still, very few...) upgrades do have a noticeable impact on traversal. Too bad one of them comes just before the end of the game.The core gameplay is still entertaining enough to have carried me to the end, and I did enjoy playing the game a lot.Controlling the motorcycle and gun at the same time, especially considering the reload and parry mechanics makes for a very engaging concept. Sure, one enemy is easy, but a group is harder. Later on, other types of enemies are introduced all of which require a bit more thinking to overcome. It doesn't take long until every encounter turns into a little mind game of its own - Who do I shoot first? Will they manage to take a shot off before they die? If they do, can I block it? Maybe it makes more sense to parry the shot, and save my bullets for someone else?Honestly, the more I played the game the more it reminded me of SUPERHOT.In SUPERHOT, the time-moves-only-when-you-move stuff makes it possible to plan out encounters just as I did for this game.However, unlike SUPERHOT here we only have bullet time, and only if you commit to taking a shot (i.e. while pressing down the trigger), *and* if you take too long to think of a plan, the shot will just go off and you waste a bullet. With the first gun only having two shots, thats a lot.To me, this is an improvement over SUPERHOT: Sure, you have some time to think, but not infinitely so. Thinking fast is rewarded, not least of which because you will probably fall on your face otherwise. Landing with motorcycle on top will kill you, so you more often than not need not only to win the fight, but have time left to land cleanly.Story beats are good but predictable, not much to say here.But the environment and atmosphere are top notch. The additional lore in sidequests also fleshes out the world well.Not going to go into this much more for spoiler reasons.Can definitely recommend getting this and giving it a go. Some caveats though:- Play on mouse and keyboard. The game is horrible on a controller, and I switched almost immediately, to immediate better results.- Getting to 100% is a chore, and I can't recommend it. The necessary items will need to be farmed, which is plain boring. Just play through the game normally, personally I also did all sidequests.
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game. The music is truly wonderful, and the setting is haunting.The difficulty is fair so far, and cooking gives you buffs that can make it easier if you're having issues, but in the end it's still one of those games where you die in one shot, so you're gonna have some frustrating moments, and gratification when you beat a hard boss.The graphic content warning on the store page is most certainly too light - the game starts out showing some pretty graphic gore. Involving a child. Yeah.
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: The stellar music, visuals, and raw gameplay on display in Laika: Aged Through Blood have no business carrying a game  hard in today’s landscape.The immaculate vibes present throughout sections of the game are incredible. The cassette player (how the game conveys background music) has an assortment of music that can be described as nothing short of beautiful – some say it’s repetitive, however I disagree with this statement and posit this enables one to build up a layer of intimacy with the music; the player becomes familiar with what they hear, select favourites, and are encouraged to find more tapes if they start to drag in order to maintain musical diversity/freshness. The music dances between complementing and contrasting the dreary wasteland environment enough to the point where it  has my attention.The gameplay may be tricky at first, but is immensely satisfying to engage with and push the limits-of. As death is of little consequence, you are free to engage with situations at your own pace and in your own time. This allows you to soak in the rich atmosphere and stunning artwork to your heart’s content. Honestly, my initial hesitation of: “Oh it plays like one of those motorbike flash games” put me off to begin with, but once I got into the flow of things, I really saw how it shined above that preconception and how it does enough to be different and interesting. Once I REALLY got into it, I kept catching myself on a rhythm with my guns blaring having a grand old time alongside the soundtrack.The visual design on display is viscerally enchanting. Sheer eye-candy wherever you go – from region-to-region to cutscenes to set-pieces. I just love looking at this game, it’s great. It’s almost  good to the point where some combat settings tend to get cluttered, messy and unreadable with particle effects which may lead to the occasional fumble/death. The music and visuals go hand-in-hand to deliver spectacles and impactful scenes throughout the game.Music, sound effects, gameplay, story, visuals, everything on display is amazing. However, the underwhelming boss fights, bike upgrades, a kinda-shoe-horned parry system and story-mission length (man, some take way too long) pull the game down a few pegs. This game is not without flaws, but this is a good thing, it merely paves for future game titles by honing on what it does best.You should definitely try Laika if you catch it on sale. You'll feel the whole spectrum of emotions. Quite the package.
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't needed to take a midnight walk to ball my eyes out over a game in almost a decade. This game is a one of a kind masterpiece and is a must play even if your not into 2D metroidvanias ( I wasn't but this game ended up really mechanically clicking for me).Just be prepared to cry alot, the story is one to the best Ive seen in decades of gaming but it gets dark and bittersweet.
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: Ended up finishing the game. The core mechanics, visual style and music all held up. The overall game did not add up to the sum of its parts. Any time I played an extended session (which was most times) I could not get over how the traversal of the barren landscape felt like torture. Hold right or left until you get to the turn, and then DON'T MISS IT. I kept returning to my map to make sure I hadn't missed the turn like some horrible Google Maps heavy road trip. That would have already been a little annoying, since swapping routes was rare and easy to mess up, but then there's just birds every other corner you can't even see that will shoot and kill you instantly. This means for long stretches of time you have to mindlessly hold right or left while tense and ready for a bird to pop up out of nowhere so you can shoot it first. This is mostly what your experience will be playing Laika, driving around a wasteland as an immortal Uber Eats driver. That could even be a little more interesting, because then the game would be more built around it, but instead the game has you trying to find objects around the map for a cast of furries that all want a wild boar hide for their stuff. Unfortunately the fetch quests were important to me because the game comes out of the gate with incredible story and conflict, only for the story to fail to expand and end satisfyingly. The long stretches of waiting to arrive somewhere to get a thing for someone end up putting a lot of pressure on the story to be exceptional to be worth all the stressful driving, pressure it cannot live up to. Without the tedious, stressful traveling it would be a fine story, but after the final curtain I found myself wanting more out of it. The traversal wasn't all bad. Some places were challenging without being frustrating, and after multiple visits became fun tricks to smoothly nail without flipping and dying. Unfortunately most of the map you spend most of your time with is not interconnected in a way that makes it convenient, and instead requires roundabout, confusing routes to get to where you need to go. That means instead of revisiting sections of a reasonably sized, compact map with interesting locations you can learn to be excellent at, you will choose to use the paid-not-paid-annoying-fast-travel system. These are rare and allow you to cook, swap weapons, and teleport. Trying to return to your base is awful without a warp, but you'll often  need to travel a long way to get to a warp anyways. Fixing this wouldn't be helpful, since the actual problem is the repetitive and stressful driving you'll constantly be performing. It is boring, unchallenging nothing, and overly challenging at the same time. I finished the game because I hoped the end would make the grind worth it, but it wasn't and I can't go back and get my hours back.
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: Phenomenal art style and soundtrack combined with a story and side-quests that touch upon the dark themes one might expect from a doomed world, but not from a game like this.Do not let the art style fool you. This game is filled with sorrow, and you'll have to drive through it, literally.To note, as there will be some that do not like repetitive gameplay:The game will have you do a lot of backtracking for quests, traders, and region-specific resources, so take that in mind if you are not a fan of that. There is fast travel, but it'll cost you a resource at the beginning of the game, and the fast travel points are scarce and spread out to encourage region exploration.However, this will not be such a big issue as the game will present you with more dangerous encounters as the story progresses, as well as alternative paths once you have the right tools.With that said, I really recommend trying this game out!For me, it hit all the right spots, a bittersweet perfection.
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: Leaving positive review before even finishing the game because Laika fully deserves it - it is a bit difficult for me to put everything into words, but pretty much every aspect of the game works out in the game. Easy to grasp on how to play, easy to get into the story (heavy, shocking - but so well executed), easy to get attached to characters (Puppy...), their stories and motivations....Blah, why even talking! Demo pretty much sums up what the game is about anyway, it costs literally nothing to try it out.
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like it more. its a bit repetitive. 3 hours in and aside from a few kinda fun boss fights, there's just one type of enemy. Some stuff to like, but  not for me, sadly.

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderful art, music and general maternal themes always get to me, very grim but still with an ounce of hope and I love that.Really fun and neat movement, shotgun is a game changer and no new mechanic goes wasted.Art is amazing I cant state that enough, music is amazing and I just can't get over everything, so many good moments with the only flaws I can even think of is some of the boss fights being a bit awkward, but even then I can understand considering the completely new sub-genre they have made with the whole motorvania thing.Bless puppy with all my heart, thank you Brainwash Gang :D I cant state enough how much this game has effected me.
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: Okay I am editing (rewriting) my review. When I was playing in the beginning, some of the mechanics were not clicking with me (when I was just around 3 hours in). Add to that the UI could be really small on steam deck but thats not the game's fault. So when I wrote that review (while still recommending the game), I believe some of those frustrations crept in into the review. However once I got used to the nuances of the gameplay, holy hell this game is AMAZING. I am 20 hours in, and just cant put it down. I was already a fan of the story, art, music, and now that the gameplay has been clicking with me, I find it soothing to ride Where Our Bikes Growl, listening to music and shooting those bastard birds. I LOVE THIS GAME. Go get it. For me its a masterpiece. The mechanics, once you get the hang of them, let you combine traversal and combat moves together and soon you will be in a 'flow state', accessing previously unreachable areas by upgrades and experimentation. The story is beautiful, tinged with a certain sadness but the these 2D characters are just so amazingly written that you WANT them to succeed, even when you fully know that the world they live in is harsh and cruel. Kudos to the game's writers, they really went in and committed to the story, even when sometimes it gets too dark to handle. Laika is such an amazing character, she is stoic and fearsome, but at the same her vulnerability is obvious for anyone who knows her, because not only she's responsible for her village's safety, she's also a mother which keeps the stakes higher than I expected. Again, I am in love with this game <3
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: A phenomenal game that I highly recommend to anyone who likes metroidvanias. If you are curious how it plays, the best I can describe it as is like a cross between those mobile motorcycle games and a bullet hell lite, but with a story I genuinely enjoyed. I didn't really mess around with the cooking aspect much but at one point I crafted every recipe for the achievement, and was just a complete powerhouse for the duration of the effects and made SO much money. So definitely cook more than I did, it is worth it.The Reload system is unique and makes some fights a game of swapping guns lightning fast rather than reloading.At time of writing, I just completed the main story after spending most of my time going after collectibles and being a bit of a completionist. I won't spoil it but I want to say I appreciate the devs for writing a good story.The Soundtrack of this game is a HUGE draw. My wife quite literally bought the game because she got hooked to the soundtrack while I was playing. _childDocuments_.review: Recently I've found a lot of games that make something I am not even remotely interested(mainly any kinds of sports or racing) into things I enjoy. Laika: Aged Through Blood is one of them, and my god this is such a great game. It has an addicting core gameplay loop, a real eye-pleasing artstyle, fantastic soundtracks, and a brutal, gloomy story. All thanks to these elements combined, the game has easily become my favorite and currently the only motorbike that I actually enjoy. Of course it contains some issues that might dwindle the fun. The side quests are just glorified fetch quests, the visual effect sometimes can obscure the protagonist, and the map doesn't away depict correctly, just to name a few. The game is still a wonderful experience to play through.→: The main gimmick of the game is to ride through wasteland doing many stunts, while shooting all your enemies that conveniently just stand still on your path. I gotta hand it to the dev team. They really know how to make riding motorbike through various locations fun and cool. You perform a back-flip in the air to reload the guns and your front-flip to gain charge that allows you to deflect bullet with the bike(don't ask how it makes sense because of video game). Thus, players are encouraged to pull out some cool tricks. Every encounter with the enemies is a mini test to see how you juggle between back-flipping(reloading) and positioning. Time slows down when you hold the trigger, so you have plenty of time to readjust yourself.→: In addition to bike stunts, guns are as important and fun as you shoot them. Your trusty Revolver is jack of trade, able to get everything done with no trouble; Shotgun is the most interesting. Not only does it feel good to shoot, its recoil allows you to do back-flip everywhere you want; Crossbow boasts the highest ammo count and widest spread, easy to deal with multiple targets at once; Machine Gun is great for high combo and visceral(currency) farming because of its high fire rate; Sniper Rifle with magnifying glass gives you the most accurate shot; Rocket Launcher is risky to use, but all so satisfying to shoot back at those rocket launcher wielding a-holes.Another experience I love about Laika: Aged Through Blood is the feel of riding the bike. The thrill of biking-n-gunning is exciting, but the downtime between is equally satisfying. This is where the artstyle and soundtracks come into play. The landscapes are beautiful to behold. Each location has a distinct color scheme. The design of the background silently tells the story of the world, even the name itself is interesting. For example, in Where the Waves Die the background is an abandoned, dried up dam and a barren river. Near the end of the river we can see the bone of giant creatures, making me wonder what happened to this world, what cause the sea to recede so far away, and what would the creature look like when it were alive. The other part of the experience the cassette player. Laika: Aged Through Blood does the background music a bit differently than the usual. Players collect cassettes from different areas, and they are free to choose whichever song they want to play on the bike. Initially I was quite skeptical about this decision. Usually the soundtracks are made to fit in their designated areas, letting the player choose any soundtracks to play may break the immersion. It turns out that my worry is unwarranted. The soundtracks are not only amazing, but they also fit in every area perfectly. →Again, the artsyle and soundtrack are amazing.→I really, REALLY like each character design. I am a hopeless furry after all.→A grim story that depicts the cruelty of war.→Metroidvania style of abilities for more exploration.→Boss fights can be long and tedious, but I think they are good for this kind of gameplay.→: With how little way to upgrade yourself in the game, you can buff yourself temporary through cooking. Mixing up three out of fifteen ingredients to see what the potential outcome might be is a fun mini-game. And the buff you receive is nothing to scoff at, ranging from extra resource and currency gain, more deflect charges, extra ammo, to maximum bike magnet radius and 3x combo starter. These buff can help you overcome a lot of nasty situation in the late game.→: The concept is good, but I feel like the buff you get should be separated from the cooking system, and made into a standalone permanent upgrade system. Things like deflect charges, extra ammo, and magnet radius should be reworked into permanent upgrades either hidden in various areas or become motorbike upgrades you can purchase from the blacksmith. This design might address lacking a sense of progression, and also welcome some more interesting temporary buff like ammo efficiency (a chance to not consume ammo when shooting).The only problem I have towards the game is its side quests. They are not good. Almost every one of them is just a glorified fetch quest that wants you to travel to a specific location to collect a certain object. Other than some dialogues and resources you can get from exploring, there isn't any incentive to do them besides extending your playtime. Funny thing is, you will know which item is the aim of a side quest long before you have access to it. These items like flowers have a thicker outline than other, and it's slightly annoying that you cannot just pick them up and wait for the side quests to pop. It's a shame because I really enjoy the gameplay and I appreciate every opportunity to go out there and explore, if only the side quest were more interesting and rewarding.→The Meathook ability is lackluster. Its need to be more than just hook and pull things. Why not let us hook on to something and swing the bike across the ravine? That ought to fun and frustrating.→Maybe slow down the tutorial at the beginning. You need to give players enough time to practice before introducing new things.→Maybe reduce the blood splattering effect and explosion a little. Often time I find it hard to identify our protagonist due to all the effects triggering at the same time and at the same scene.中文小簡評→第一款我非常有興趣的特技摩托遊戲。→福瑞、劇情黑暗、玩法有趣、畫風美音樂佳，不愛都難啊。→特技摩托加上射擊，後空翻換彈、前空翻讓你可以反彈子彈，這些設計鼓勵玩家秀出酷炫的技倆。→六把槍各司其職，其中散彈槍特別好玩，他的後座力能讓你原地後空翻。→騎著摩托朝著遠方呼嘯而過，欣賞沿途末日廢土的風景，配上極其好聽的音樂，那種自在完全不輸特技摩托的爽感。→身為一位無可救藥的福瑞控，這遊戲的每個角色我都好愛阿。→劇情真的黑暗血腥，那個開場絕對會勾起你的興趣。→類銀河系惡魔成的技能設計與相連的地圖。→Boss戰設計尚可，或許會有點冗長，但配合遊戲玩法完全合理。→烹飪系統是少數你可以加強自己的選項任選三樣食材加再一起，可以煮出多種增益。概念很好，但是我覺得有些增益應該獨立設計成永久升級系統。→支線任務真的不行，大多數都是跑腿撿東西，獎勵不豐富，任務過程也不有趣。→鉤子這項技能很雞肋，應該要設計可以讓玩家盪過峽谷或抓住敵人加速前進。→開場的教學需要再緩點，應該讓玩家多練習幾次再介紹新特色。→噴血特效及爆炸過多，特別是在空中，容易把角色擋住。

_childDocuments_.review: This gets a 'maybe' from me, it has its moments of grace and some beautiful key art and music, but suffers from some truly frustrating and baffling design decisions that only serve to make the whole experience more of a let down.At its heart, the game is a splatformer where you will die many thousands of times due to the somewhat unfair accuracy (and bullet leading) of your enemies, coupled with any single mistake leading to you restarting the whole thing.This isn't necessarily bad, but there are many frustrating elements coupled with this that cause unnecessary frustration. Be it the soulslike bags you leave on death, forcing backtracking to obtain these if you head in the wrong direction (which is often in these very interwoven maps), or your enemies bodies blocking your shots - but not those of other enemies. The latter being quite important given you only have 2 or 3 shots at a time.The game isn't particularly large, but it outstays its welcome with constant and frequent backtracking to locations you have already visited multiple times to find new elements placed there, that you won't know are there until you happen upon them. Despite the maps size, it could still have done with being cut back in sections, especially the ship level that confusingly starts with a 7 minute unskippable cutscene with infrequent dialogue. I'm being critical here and I know, but I really enjoyed the game world and story and pushed through my constant frustrations with it until near the end, but I just can't bring myself to finish the last 5 hours, I'd rather let this one go.If you want to try this one, heavens do keyboard and mouse and not controller, the game is nigh impossible on a controller due to the accuracy needed with such minimal ammo for each weapon.

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't played this game for super long... but I think I can describe it pretty well for new players.  Did you ever have piano lessons when you were little?  You know how they made you play the same stupid song over and over and if you made one mistake you had to start again?  And you just played it over and over and over messing up until you got it right once and the teacher finally released you?  That's Laika.  Taking very imprecise controls, you must, through trial and error, memorize exact sequences of maneuvers and perform them precisely, in order, or you die and have to start over.  In one of the earlier areas you have to drive through a horde of angry, rifle-wielding bird people, and rapidly perform the following sequence of actions with no breaks in near-perfect order if you want to survive: Reflect bullet, front flip off jump to reload reflect, shoot bird, tilt back to block bullet, wait for second shot so your bullet doesn't collide with the bird's, shoot bird, backflip off jump to reload gun, shoot bird, tilt back to block bullet, wait for shot so bullets don't collide, shoot bird, reflect bullet, backflip THEN frontflip both within a single jump, shoot bird, shoot bird, reflect bullet.  Oh... and make sure to go left off the final ledge to reach the checkpoint instead of right like I did because if you go right you get stuck in a pit where you have to kill yourself to escape and your hard-won victory gets turned to ash.    Honestly... it reminds me of an old-style platformer like Mario or Megaman, except it's always on the hardest levels, and you're constantly running on ice.  If you like those kinds of games and you're patient enough you may enjoy Laika.  I mostly play strategy games, and I play Laika when I'm burnt out and I don't want to think, or I'm just bored with the same old same old.  It's challenging, but it's also mostly just tedious repetition.  It DOES feel cool when you finally, after an hour, execute the sequence correctly one time and get to see the next ten feet of the level before you meet more birds...    The artwork is pretty.  I feel like the game is trying to be edgy and hard core, but the fact the it's Happy Wheels with furries, and that I explode blood like I'm a Mortal Kombat fighter every time I tip my nose a little too far forward means that I simply can't take the game seriously.  However, I think that's also the only reason I'm able to enjoy it-if I was taking it seriously I would get too angry because I die every two seconds and I'd have to quit playing.    Conclusion?  I don't know.  I like the game and I'll probably play to the end.  It's nice to play something a little different.  Don't be fooled by the gameplay videos though-it may look awesome, but you're going to feel stupid a lot more than you're going to feel cool, and the cool feeling is very short-lived.  Despite it being a game where you ride a motorcycle, the race goes to the tortoise and not the hare with this one.  Slow, steady, and patient is what carries the day.

_childDocuments_.review: A weird but sorely overlooked game with a gorgeous visual aesthetic, and an equally excellent soundtrack. The story oozes with an overwhelming sense of gloom that, despite its seemingly dissonant style of gameplay with funky motorcycle physics, fits perfectly. It's beautiful, really. The only big downside to the game is that it can be melodramatic at times, where scenes either don't have enough time to breathe or aren't set up in a way that gives you a chance to think over what's being shown to you.The gameplay is challenging yet forgiving, provided the person playing picks up on how its system works, and it has a satisfying puzzle-like loop with the way it combines combat and exploration. Every checkpoint and sequence is a puzzle that must be solved, and approaching it any other way will lead to guaranteed frustration. Mastery of the game's mechanics and being able to properly juggle the systems it throws at you really leads to a genuinely rewarding experience, but I can only imagine how many players are either not familiar with its gameplay style or how many players just aren't willing to understand it.I think this is going to be going way under most people's radar when it really shouldn't. If you've ever liked metroidvanias, enjoy a bit of a puzzle-like challenge, along with a thoughtfully unique experience with gorgeous visuals and music, you NEED to pick this one up.
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: This game tries to do too much. While the core story and mechanics drive the game there are several ancillary things that make the game kind of stumble. You will get upgrades that are maybe useful for one very specific spot but not really anywhere else. The first two weapons you get are the only ones really worth getting and upgrading because the others seem superfluous. Cooking is kinda pointless. There are side quests that just kind of throw in shocking subjects and are over with.But there's a core here that I really like. Laika as a protagonist is cynical about her place in a destroyed world and within her community but little moments of kindness break through and show her as a caring person with an awful lot in life. The mechanics of biking around may get a bit tiring by the end point but there's enough variation and a late stage ability that keep traversal interesting and fun. You'll crash a lot and combat is chaotic to a fault, but generous checkpoints and setpiece moments really carried this game into being one of my favorites of 2023.Also damn that sound track. Everybody's first reaction is "this doesn't match the game" but as it goes on the nuances of the vibe really bring together a unique mixture of aesthetics.

_childDocuments_.review: Come for the gameplay, stay for the music and the story.I must say that I will not be objective during this review because I absolutely loved it, maybe try out the demo before buying it, as the controls may not be for everyone, but if you like what you see in the demo, go for it, because the full game is even better.The story, while not too predominant in the game, mainly some quests, makes you build a "relation" with the people on the village, and you end up helping them not because of the rewards (that are mainly some crafting components) but because you actually want to help them.Moving onto the gameplay, there are 6 weapons and only one of them actually gives you a new ability metroidvania style, later in the game you get 2 abilities more, one situational and one that completely changes the mechanics, so if that is what you are looking for, maybe this game is not for you.The combat is challenging but having frequent save points makes it not frustrating. I must say there's a lot of backtracking in the game but the movement is quite satisfying so it's not really a pain.Lastly, the OST has some of the best songs that I've listened in games, and totally make going through the map a more fun experience, even if you don't like the game, give the music a try.All in all, if you are looking for a new and refreshing experience lasting around 15-20 hours, try the demo and if you like it, go for it.
