_childDocuments_.review: Close to one of the top 10 games I've ever played.  The game is super unique, has an insane utilization of simple controls, makes you actually care about crafting and food, has a very bold plot that feels personal, lots of colorful characters and quests, great visuals, nice little cinematics, and it has a wonderful soundtrack that feels almost contrary to the gameplay but actually transforms a high octane adventure into a contemplative, vibe.  You can absolutely annihilate enemies in this game especially after you've prepared and eaten.  But the game always requires focus and mastery no matter what you're fighting so when you do indulge in those moments it feels like you're a total god.It can be a little rough around the edges, I think they should have made reloads 340 degrees instead of 360 just cuz how some elevations work and there's a couple of camera issues I noticed a few times.  The bosses are not very well done.  There is a little more polish that could have been done in the backtracking, where it can feel like the game is wasting your time, especially if you didn't die so the enemies that you would have backtracked to aren't there.  It felt very friendly with checkpoints, fully aware of how difficult the game can be.  If the bosses were fantastic, this would be a top 3 game of all time for me even with the other issues just because the whole package ends up being so good.

_childDocuments_.review: This game caught me totally off guard with how good it is.  At least for a certain kind of person,  a degenerate like me that takes getting killed personally and will take pleasure in the twenty plus tries it takes to make a perfect run through a section.  The controls are complicated and uncompromising,  it doesn't pull any punches with it's brutal storytelling,  and it asks a lot of you.  It feels like a game that was made with a vision and they stuck to it without worrying about simplifying things for broader appeal.  Once you click with it though,  your hands start doing what they need to without thinking about it and you're in for a treat.  A real masterpiece.

_childDocuments_.review: I had heard about this game from Fireb0rn before it came out and had played the demo. For the controls there is a learning curve, but it was one I enjoyed learning. The main reason why I had bought the game though was the art and message. I love the colors and the music of this game so much, I would've bought it even if there wasn't any game play. It just makes my brain so happy.So if you're into darker stories and learning new mechanics I'd highly recommend this game. If there's any other way to support the artists I'd love to know.

_childDocuments_.review: i finished this game and it's still lingering in my mind, the ost making me miss just riding around on my bike all day.the gameplay is incredibly fun. doing 5 flips and unleashing an entire arsenal of guns on an army of enemies, somber nostalgic music playing as i get completely coated in the blood of my enemies is such a vibe.all the characters felt real and compelling. I did EVERY side quest and i always did them simply because i liked the characters, even forgetting that i get rewarded for my effort. seeing a person in the village i dont know talking about how all their loved ones have died, and their crushing loneliness, go to a friend talking about how glad they are to have known the people they loved brought more joy to me than it shouldve. the story is surprisingly very in depth, and seeing the mc change throughout the game was so interesting. the art is amazing and every area screams about a long gone past with its visuals and detail. whenever you take the last shot on a boss, it perfectly cuts to an animation of the final shot finishing it off.the music is nothing short of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ perfect, calling it just a game ost doesnt do it enough justicemy personal favourite questline had you finding band members across the wastelands (aptly named The Wastelanders) and each one you find adds another layer to the music in the home town.I loved this game more than i ever thought i would, and i hope you do too

_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: This is a near-Hades-caliber game. Do not miss it. It's incredibly powerful. This game has changed how I view games.The character design, the worldbuilding, the atmosphere, all phenomenal.  Furthermore, the pacing of exposition and the way the narrative is handled is just spectacular. As a gamedev and writer myself, it's so refreshing to experience a world without hamfisted, unnatural spoonfeedings of lore. Instead, we're offered glimpses of a world that does not exist to serve or inform the player. It makes exploring the world addictive and makes the emotional, often gut-wrenching revelations about the characters and world feel organic and genuine. At the start, I was also very vocal about bad writing choices they'd made to some friends. And the control scheme is unusual and was initially very frustrating. But honestly, I feel almost ashamed of my initial jaded assumptions, because it has become clear now that every single thing I ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ about in my first hour of playtime was done intentionally and for great effect. Just keep playing this game.I'm going to mourn when I finish this game and can't experience more of these characters' lives any longer.
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: I will say that it is fantastic that we have a 2D Metroidvania that plays uniquely for once in our lives, thanks to the motorcycle and the level design accompanying it. I just don't think that the overall level design and progression suits the backtracking that a Metroidvania calls for; I often dreaded having to go to a location because it meant doing the same jumps, killing the same enemies (or worse!), and doing everything the same while the game-changing power-ups are few and far between to change up the core traversal.I hope this inspires more motorcycle Metroidvanias in the future and tweak the overall design.
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: Laika: Aged Through Blood is a game that lives and dies on it's ability to provide an insane amount of checkpoints to the player in order to lessen frustration, and it falls into a category of games that I would call an 'always on' sort of game.An 'always on' game, to me, is a game that requires concentration or is difficult for long periods of without any real break or pause. Games like Rusted Moss and CrossCode for example fall into this category of game for me. You will die a significant amount of times for the smallest thing, and some of these can feel extremely bad as well. The game provides a TON of checkpoints, though, and as another user pointed out it can feel a bit like Katana Zero where you will restart a section over and over repeatedly until you get your clean run. I don't consider these sorts of things a negative, but a cautionary note for players looking for a more traditional, perhaps relaxed, exploratory Metroidvania experience. With that out of the way. Laika's art, music, animation, and overall design are superb. It is easy to recommend to people as long as they understand what they're getting into. It's a unique experience that's kept me pretty engaged with it's overall visual style and story. Strongly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: Whoever thought mixing exitebike with a metroidvania was not right. Conceptually this is flawed, and even if it was not execution is horrible. Most of the time i had to fight the physics simply to get from A to B and that is without enemies. Fighting is terrible thanks to the reload mechanic, again spin to reload is a conceptually flawed thing Even then, Ghost and Goblins is hard, not because it was a well crafted difficult experience, like dark souls but because its creators lacked the ability and the know how to actually design for difficulty, it all came from poor aerial controls and weak weapons. this is similar, but on purpose.Despite being on a diet of souls like for the past decade or so this games show me that we have yet to grasp how to design for difficulty in mind and the overwhelming positive reviews also show me that we as a consumer still cannot tell the difference between difficulty stemming from poor mechanics and that coming from well crafted design choices.
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: Laika: Aged Through Blood is a game that is hard to call any one thing, but might be best summarized by the name of the first mission: Rage & Sorrow. It's a game in which sorrow and rage pervade even the happiest moments.It's a game about womanhood, and wanting better for the generations that come after us even while we recognize how truly bleak the future seems.It's a game about somehow finding hope in hopelessness.It's one of the most emotionally taxing games I've ever played, and from a pure gameplay perspective I don't think I have ever encountered a game that so perfectly balances challenge and a call for finesse. The game asks you not just to play, but to dance.There is literally nothing else like this game. I have never come across a game so unflinching in what subjects it is willing to approach to achieve its vision.This is one of the best games I have ever played, and one of the most difficult to recommend. It's a hard experience. I strongly recommend paying attention to the content warnings.But if you are up for it, you'll find one of the most engaging pieces of media I have encountered.
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: Steam Deck specific review. This game is a headache. Not overall though, its music is legit incredible along with its atmosphere. Story telling isn't bad either. The actual gameplay design, or ideas, are quite good. It's just the execution and controls that need work. It all feels very clunky or unnatural even 6 hours in. You can "get used" to the controls but getting used to something doesn't excuse the fact that something is heavily flawed.This game expects you to land your bike after performing multiple actions in mid-air. Normally this would be fine, and maybe it is fine on a bigger screen, but it's genuinely annoying on Steam Deck's small screen. The game zooms out during combat, making it hard to see what position your bike is in. Often I feel like I'm failing an encounter not because of a mistake I made, but because the game fails at giving me the right information. I wish I could mess with settings and not zoom out so much. It's controller sensitivity is also wonky, making precise aiming feel not-so-great. However this might also be a Steam Deck specific issue.The one-hit-kill mechanic is probably a love or hate thing. I personally enjoy it. While you can die very easily and with one mistake, enemies also die in one shot. This makes for compelling gameplay and makes you feel like a badass when you finally execute your attacks or parries perfectly. Reminds me of a Ghostrunner. I'll probably complete this game because of the positive things I've mentioned, but I'll continue to roll my eyes at all the design flaws.7/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Do yourself a favor and please play it.This is one of the best experiences i've ever had ever.One of the biggest selling points for me was the story, it is incredible how you connect and feel compassionate with the characters in this game, even if the amount of dialogue with the "secondary" cast isn't super extensive. I especially liked how the game doesn't pull any punches. The story is absolutely brutal, acts of exterme violence are commonplace in this world, and, suprisingly, it is very tastefullly done, never feeling like violence is pushed on the player just for it's shock factor. By the end I felt completely inversted in the main characters story and how it would end. No game ever managed to make me shed a tear except this one, that's why it will always have a place in my heart.This game has some amazing ideas in terms of playability. Almost every single gameplay mechanic has been thought out and is well implemtented, especially the core combat loop, making incredibly fun to fly around keeping in mind your ammunition, parry, and figuring out the perfect time to do a flip to get all your abilities recharged. Also the variety of weapons you aquire througout the game made sure to keep the gameplay interesting.Beícoli, the creator of the sondtrack did an amazing work, making the discovery of casettes one of the biggest motivators for exploring. The soundtrack is superbly crafted to contrast the post-apocalyptic setting.The art style is incredybly well made, making the depressing world feel completely unique and beautiful, as well as keeping all the plethora of characters unique.I'd like to thank the developers for making such an amazing game.

_childDocuments_.review: Strong 8/10, very minor cons with great pros.- The visuals are beautiful, be it the environment, the design of characters, and ESPECIALLY the cutscenes (god I wish there were more of them/that they were slightly longer)- The music is absolutely wonderful, I will listen to it on Youtube, and they absolutely should release a soundtrack on Steam, I'd buy it in a heartbeat.- The over-arching story is good (war against the occupants), but the details of it are VERY good. Dialogue, story beats, character backstories, environmental storytelling, etc...- Gameplay is very enjoyable, flows well from killing to acrobatics with a side of platforming.- Puppy :)- Game felt stuttery, almost laggy at times, despite a beefy computer and simple (yet beautiful) visuals. Still entirely playable though.- Bosses unfortunately are more missing than hitting, and could use a good amount of tweaking (where applicable). - Almost cried several times because story sad :(Would I recommend this game ? Absolutely. Is it perfect ? No, but it's pretty damn good, especially for only 20 bucks. Ifyou think you might like the game, do yourself a favor and pick it.

_childDocuments_.review: I played the demo first, it made me cry. Naturally I had to buy it!Laika: Aged Through Blood is a spectacular game, perhaps not for a general audience. If you enjoy challenging, visually stunning games with heart wrenching stories then It may be for you! I am not talented in platformers, metroidvanias, or even the flash game Happy Wheels, but the story alone followed me even away from the PC. I was obsessed. I wanted to know what would happen to this motorcycle driving coyote mom and her loved ones! Laika is more than just a typical "Badass motorcycle riding woman" trope. Her character has depth and while you'll be carrying out excessive violence on her behalf, she's reluctantly carrying out her role as her tribe's defender. She's just as pained and uncertain of her future, and just wants to live a life of peace as much as any other poor critter out in the wastes.The soundtrack is perfect. You wouldn't think that Soft Folk Pop would be the tracks you'd want playing while doing flips and firing a revolver, but its irrevocably the best fit for this game. The artists even exists in-game, with characters opinions differing on them. Heck, even the respawn mechanic is a canon aspect in-game too. A few notes:The game is Dark: If you are sensitive to certain dark aspects of humanity, just be aware that this game wont shy away from showing you them. That said, you'll find brief moments of beauty and hope within the darkest moments, from amusing moments of childhood innocence and mother/daughter bonding, to bittersweet elegies. Be prepared to die. A lot.  Esepecially early on, encounters are more like puzzles for you to figure out than flowy, on-the-fly vehicular combat. It's a bit frustrating, but by the time you master the controls and mechanics, things will be more smooth. Upgrades are sparse: Some side quests will be essential for story progression, namely Maya, Shaza, and the Hectist's. Do note, some weapons and abilities may be used in clever ways. Also, the game doesn't tell you, but tapping the gas repeatedly can occasionally give your character a speed boost. I wish it was more consistent however.. Some cons:This game really should have a gentler difficulty mode, I'd love to see this story told to even more folks but I'm afraid most will be deterred or unable to see its entirety!Boss fights can be lackluster. A caterpillar Made of Sadness and the Hundered Hungry Beaks were the better two!  I loved how flowy they both were. The others are more stationary and are bullet hells and test your focus a little too much, it can be frustrating.Overall, if you were interested enough to read this entirely, I'd recommend giving it a shot, or at least the demo if it's still up!
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, Laika is a really interesting platformer with its driving, shooting, blocking mechanics. The narrative is overtly, and deliberately dark pretty much at all times but there's some really interesting elements, the main character has a fair amount of depth. And while it doesn't carry to all elements, the game tries to draw at least some of the game mechanics into the narrative itself, such as the character coming back to life.In more depth:Narratively the game really drew me in, exploring new areas was intriguing just to learn more about what was going on. Admittedly the dark tone is perhaps overdone, it almost becomes predictably and comically dark. When everything goes about as bad as can be, the tension in the darkness abates, essentially. The character is a little inconsistant, in that verbally she objects to her role, but is ruthless whenever not in player control. Desires a future without the conflict, yet has no interest in any solution but combat. But that may just be part of her personality. There's a few odd narrative moments. Like randomly pulling off a perfect disguise to a region we never see again, or the ending. I'll try to avoid spoilers, but essentially all hope is lost, then the final villain pulls a cartoonishly supervillain move to ruin their own master plan for no discernable reason. Oddly, I found myself more interested in the lore of my opponents than anything, and felt rather sorry for, most, of the birds by the end.The gameplay is a hard learning curve. In any situation other than your bike you move left and right with A and D, but on your bike pressing those will kill you. By the end, I'd gotten used to it though, but the game punishes any imperfection heavily. Here there are some mixed signals. The game uses a souls-like currency drop system (the currency is the entrails of your enemies, which is quite funny when you consider how many of the merchants like the birds... but accept their body parts as payment) so when you die, you drop half. Die too much as you lose it. This mechanic promotes careful, methodic play. The game otherwise promotes the opposite. You reload with a backflip, you need to build speed to ramp into place, it gives you checkpoints to get back into the action quick when you fail. This seems to promote, rush in guns blazing till you master it, and look good doing it. The screen can get a bit, cluttered and messy during combat though, which being as unforgiving as it is, feels questionable. Once you've become drenched in blood (the game does like its blood) it's hard to tell through the clouds of bird bits if you're going to land on your wheels, or need to do it all again.The soundtrack has some huge hits, all that needs said about that, love the OST... impressive how they managed to make me feel guilty listening to it. Really, the capacity for the game to make everything have dark undertones is impressive.
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: Laika: Aged Through Blood is a really neat concept of a game. A motorbike metroidvania game with guns and a backflip reload mechanic set in a western style anthropomorphic world is an awesome idea!  And while I do think the game struggled to build on top of that base design, overall I had a really good time with the game.The Story: Laika: Aged Through Blood's story is very bleak and dark with light moments of levity. Laika's struggles to deal with her responsibilities and the implications of them are very interesting in concept, but aren't touched on as much as I'd like and the scenes with her family while very emotional, are also a bit sparse in the overall runtime of the game. However, overall, the vibe of the game's story really hit me and I got pretty emotional in a few moments in the game.Graphics: You will almost certainly die a lot to enemies you didn't see or to not realizing you're upside down when you hit the ground as this game can get visually cluttered pretty easily, but I don't think this was often enough to be too much of an issue during my playtime. Beyond that this game is gorgeous. I love the 2d art style of this game. All the characters look so unique and interesting. I just wanted to know everything about how they ended looking the way they did and the same goes for the world around them.Sound: Also a mostly, big plus for me. Loved the music. It matches wonderfully with the lonely, dreary feeling of being on the road. Your mileage may vary on this strongly though as all the tapes are vocal tracks and even for me, towards the end of the game I turned them off occasionally.Gameplay: This game can feel fantastic at points. During boss fights or when the level design just has you keep moving constantly you can get into a groove that clicks real well between riding your back, doing back flips, and deflecting/shooting bullets. Unfortunately, there's only a few boss fights in the game and sometimes it can be a bit confusing where you need to go so you have to bring up the map which ends up breaking up that really nice feeling of just riding through the levels. Also, the game is a bit long for what gameplay is there. It really only has 2 unlockable movement abilities and the second one is gained at practically the end of the game and makes the first mostly pointless. So while Laika does have a lot of metroidvania elements I think going in expected a traditional metroidvania will leave you disappointed. The shooting is hella fun though and I loved spinning my bike to reload my guns. I really wish more games had interesting reload mechanics.Summary: While it struggles a bit to keep things interesting for its full runtime and has some frustrating design elements(traveling merchant, a missing fast travel point) overall I think the cohesive vibe of Laika: Aged Through Blood really pushed me into greatly enjoying my time with the game. So I give it a big old recommend, with the advice that ya try out the demo first to make sure it'll work as well for you.

_childDocuments_.review: I really tried to like this game, but it's not fun to play.The art and story (the little I've experienced) are pretty goodunfortunately the "game" part of the game falls apart very early and completely killed my desire to keep goingit simply doesn't feel good to play, you feel like you're not 100% in control, you get stuck on weird geometries often, the levels are not very intuitive for movementin some situations you cant even tell where you are or what is happening (the foreground/explosions can obscure the character), not a good look for a game where you NEED to be making split second decisions to succeedyou're going to be fighting the camera more than the enemiesYou're not fast driving through the levels, the opposite of what was shown in the trailers basically, way slower and sluggishif you want to explore the level you're going to be stopping every 5 seconds to open the map and check where you are, there is no minimapincredibly bare bones tutorial, I had to LOOK UP the DEFAULT ABILITY to Speed Boost, the game simply does not tell youBosses are miserable as well, feels like tedious wastes of time more than anything elseI had to fight the same boss 4 times I think?  they were all "different fights" but its the exact same boss with the exact same gimmick, very weirdI'm dreading getting through the remaining bosses in this game, which is such a sad way to feel about a metroidvaniasome mind boggling design decisions like, to reload you have to do a backflip, and you can't melee the enemies in any way, not even hit them with the bike apparently? only shootingyou're dead if you're on a flat surface basically, if only there was a way to manually reload without literally jumping through hoops for it, makes the deaths feel VERY cheapoh and you have to manually activate the checkpoints, instead of just driving through them, like you would expect from a game where you're moving very fast through itgood idea for a game but didn't quite get the execution right

_childDocuments_.review: I loved it! The mechanics can be a bit awkward to get used to at first, but you eventually do, and it feels pretty good. Spinning your bike to reload your guns is cool. There are 6 weapons and you can carry 4 at the same time with upgrades, so cycling between them is amazing!Not much enemy variety but enough to make encounters entertaining and a bit challenging depending on the placement and your aim/reaction time. The boss fights could be improved (I hated the damn CRAB) and there were times of frustation where I felt I hadn't hit the ground yet or my bike was blocking a shot but I still got killed, or my bullets didn't hit an enemy that should have.The music is PHENOMENAL and it's one of the 3 greatest strong points of the game, alongside the art and the story. It looks EXTREMELY detailed and has specific animated cutscenes that really stand out when they play. I personally enjoyed the story and its themes very much, it's about motherhood, revenge and love, written with care and while I think the ending could have been expanded a little bit, it has a good closure.I wouldn't mind a sequel that polishes the mechanics and "metroidvania" aspects of the game, offering better interconnectivity between areas and giving your weapons & abilities more specific uses that are not just to unlock a few areas and secrets then never to be used again (like the grapple... so much wasted potential there). The story could easily continue as its narrative has the elements to do so, hopefully the studio does well.8.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: So as far as metroidvanias go, this one is light.  There are like maybe 3 skills that unlock progression, and there's only like weapon/item upgrades.  The game does use a lot of Souls mechanics as well.  But the obvious draws is to it's Trials HD gameplay.  And I was a huge fan of Trials back in the day.  This absolutely made this for me.  I can see how for some people it may eventually get tedious, but that never happened for me.  I'd even forego teleporting just to drive around more.  Specially because as the story progresses, the enemy layout changes too, which is a great touch.  And it feels amazing when you do well in combat.  I've seen some people compare this to Katana Zero, and I can kind of see it.  You get the same kind of endorphin rush when get out of a hectic encounter alive.I do have two nitpicks though.  I did go for all achievements, and the grind to get all the mats to upgrade all the weapons to max was rough.  Like, really rough.  For other completionists out there, I'd highly recommend not doing this.  The other nitpick is I didn't like how the shotgun worked.  You use the shotgun as like a double jump,  but the shotgun blast completely ignores your current momentum.  You could be hauling ass forward, shoot straight down, and you immediately stop moving forward and just go straight up.  And even by the end of the game, I couldn't get used to it.  I'd miss so many jumps because it would delete all your forward momentum, and it just didn't make sense to me.That said, if a light metroidvania, souls-like, Trials HD game sounds good to you, you will most likely have a great time.  I also really enjoyed the dark, gritty story.  Just a great experience from beginning to end.  Even if you are just a Trials fan, I still think this is a high recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: A great concept hampered by patchwork execution.This is more of a mixed recommendation, but I'm going with a thumbs up because the core gameplay is original enough to be worth a look. Combining Trials-style 2D biking with guns, bullet time, parries, air dashes, and backflips to reload your weapons is awesome. Moving Laika around has all the weight and momentum you'd expect of driving a clunky motorcycle around a Mad Max wasteland of the future, but in mastering it, you can chain together a series of actions that make you feel invincible. You're not just fighting the enemies, but the angle of your motorcycle, the speed of your jumps, the rounds left in your weapon, and the number of parries you have left to use. It's a lot to manage at first, which makes success all the more satisfying when you finally get the hang of it.This combined with a stylish aesthetic, some lovely animated vignettes, and a beautifully moody soundtrack are Laika's greatest strengths. It was an ambitious idea to meld this type of gameplay with a metroidvania-style world, something I can honestly say I've never seen done before, and unfortunately... it kind of doesn't work. That's not to the say the concept is inherently flawed, but I was pestered with constant annoyances that made me feel like this was the devs' first crack at an idea that could be done much better with a few revisions.Laika feels like adopts a ton of ideas from other metroidvanias without much concern for how well they fit its gameplay style. The biggest issue I ran into was the exploration. Despite having an open world, this is the kind of game that directs you everywhere with quests, the prerequisites for which don't spawn until you accept a blue checkmark from an NPC. You aren't rewarded for taking the initiative and getting yourself lost in the world, you're directed from point A to point B in a fashion that makes me wonder why this wasn't just a linear action game. There are upgrade and cooking materials to collect if you go a little off the beaten path, but the game's weapon upgrades are more limited by your universal currency than the items you find through exploration, and I never found it necessary to engage with the cooking system at all. While moving along linear paths and fighting enemies feels great, navigating complex environments and backtracking to pick up items that roll away from you often feels like a cumbersome chore.You only get one real movement upgrade all game, and it comes right at the end. This was the only point at which exploration actually felt rewarding to me, as the movement ability is pretty darn fun and completely changes the way you interact with the world. I can only imagine how cool it would've been to get more upgrades that let you fine-tune your mobility and pull off more crazy stuff in combat while simultaneously letting you access new areas. Every time I revisited areas prior to this, I felt like I was punished for trying to explore by hitting dead ends. The game's quests, similarly, feel like fluff that usually involves nothing more than reaching a spot on a map you've already explored before returning to the questgiver.There are some tedious bosses that are poorly designed around the game's movement, but also some fun ones that take advantage of it. Area maps need to be purchased from a vendor, but he almost always shows up right at the beginning of zones, rendering the process largely pointless. You get a bunch of different weapons to play with, but the default pistol is better than all of them in 90% of situations. Enemies are distinct, but the visual noise during combat is sometimes problematic. I could sit here listing minor annoyances that bugged me all day, but I don't want to be overcritical of a game I still enjoyed enough to complete. None of these issues are gamebreaking at the end of the day, they just feel like a big ball of fumbles that stifle Laika's core strengths.Finally, there's the story, which I feel is a fairly mixed bag as well. The pacing is sometimes jarring and intrusive, with too much time spent on too little substance followed by glossing over major developments that demand room to breathe. The main characters are sympathetic, and Laika's relationships with her mother and daughter are engaging ones, but the supporting cast are spread a bit thin, and the game's unsettlingly grimdark tone doesn't feel like it gets explored in any real depth beyond the basic emotional yank of getting upset about bad things happening to people.There's a lot of ambition and passion here, but the execution is rough. It's a whole lot of ideas pulled from similar games without the necessary tweaks to make them fit the unique gameplay style. I feel like with some relatively simple changes, I could've loved Laika, but it wound up being a bit of a 6/10 for me. I hope the devs try something like this again with more focus on polishing up the smaller details in the future, because it has a lot of potential.

_childDocuments_.review: The core idea of line rider meets metroidvania is pretty nifty, particularly when you're doing cool ♥♥♥♥ and just achieving good flow. I think I would've preferred this game if it was more like shovel knight, than a metroidvania though.Game is a little too long for what it is. Boss fights are a notable weak point in this game, as they largely don't do what makes this game fun, which is drive around maps with a motorcycle and having good flow. Also not a huge fan of having to buy upgrades and the cooking mechanic; we should've had more faith in the metroidvania and just littered the map with all these upgrades to be collected, rather than forcing me to farm currency/resources to upgrade things with repetitive/efficient combat routes, and setting other perks behind a timer on a resource that i also have to farm on cooking.Huge missed opportunity in that you get a literal grapple hook, but you can't use it to swing anywhere. What the heck man.Soft reco overall. Alright game with some really frustrating aspects.

_childDocuments_.review: Man, that ending sequence is something special. I would put this up there as one of the best stories in any metroidvania I've played. The wastelands are bleak, the birds who have invaded them cruel, but each night when you return to your home, slip into the bar for some blackjack, stand in front of the band and listen to their music, hand out news and items from the outside to the residents, and finally enter your house and go to sleep beside your daughter, there is a reassuring sense of peace. At least you have this one thing. At least you have her. This propels you to keep fighting, even when some of the game's less polished aspects rear their heads. The most consistent source of annoyance for me was difficulty telling where my character was facing midair. To reload a gun you have to do a backflip, but in the heat of combat, when you are blasting birds below, above, and alongside you, it quickly becomes disorienting. You also get progressively more covered in blood during gunfights, which makes it even more difficult to tell what way you are facing. By the end, muscle memory mostly covered for me, but there were still times when I would land on my head instead of my wheels.The other main annoyance I had while playing, which was really more of a disappointment, was enemy placement. There are some standout sections where it feels like enemies were placed deliberately to create a challenge when clearing them. Most of the time, however, they are just tossed into the room, and you can clear them with ease. There are also countless times where a single enemy appears in front of you, and it's trivial to kill them before they even get a chance to shoot. I didn't mind this because it did keep me on my toes during platforming-heavy sections, but it does feel a little pointless when you can kill half the enemies in the game before they even get a chance to shoot you.Some final positives: The auditory feedback when shooting and reloading is incredibly satisfying. Even though it didn't require much skill, continuously backflipping while spamming out shots to clear entire rooms never got dull. The air dash is also an incredibly fun ability, though it's unfortunate you don't get it until so late into the game. To be fair, it is pretty busted, so having it too early would completely change the combat. Lastly, the music is awesome. There's almost always something playing in the background, and the various tracks have a strong sense of cohesion while still remaining distinct from one another.

_childDocuments_.review: And so after 21 hours of exploring and doing pretty much everything this game can present I'm ready to throw in some thoughts about it.Lets start with overall setting and atmosphere this game tries to achieve. World shown to us as post-apocalyptic wasteland as a result of bomb drop and tries to mix it with some western-like aspects. While traveling around the world you will mostly encounter locations/characters that's are filled with melancholy, emptiness and suffering. But even then there's always a place or two which have a little piece of light to it. And just to clarify even through locations are presented as wastelands they still drawn really well and have unique touches.  adds a lot to this game and might be one of best parts overall. Outside of location/encounter specific background compositions there's like 20 cassettes which work like collectibles and played in general locations while moving around the world. Not only these songs (most of them have vocals) improving overall atmosphere, but they also amazing to listen on its own. (which i strongly recommending to do).Well this subject can be a bit controversial. Personally I liked the way movement and combat system works, but it took some time and even then I was failing here and there because I keep forgetting about something. (I got around 650 deaths by the end)So if someone of you back in the day played games like  or  you might have general idea how moving and balancing your bike works. For everyone else, you have a gas button and while holding it you have to balance your bike left and right, if head hits the floor you gonna die. Mechanic is simple but when you have to keep tracking your position while doing active shooting and reloading (by doing backflip you reload your weapon) you might end up in situations where you keep dying by hitting floor instead of enemy fire. You can block shots with your vehicle/deflect bullets back or even dodge it with shotguns knockback (some accidents might happen with it more often than not). Through the game you might find new weapons, there isn't many but they quite unique from each other and you can switch your guns in middle of fight instead of sticking to one and keep trying to reload it after few shots. Even through when you master this combat system and will be able to do really neat combos, I think it still can be a bit overwhelming experience for many people. So you either gonna love it or be annoyed by it.Game sticks with metroidvania style level design, which means you have some freedom here and there to explore and move around locations but some places will be unreachable until you find an upgrade or locked behind some story events.  sending you into places with pretty interesting stories and their endings can hit you in the feels.  on another hand mostly can be described as a fetch quests, just go back into locations that you visited already and bring something. They can be annoying to do and there's a lot of them, but at least they trying to show you a state of the world and characters that are living in it, and it adds up to the atmosphere which is good.Progression in this game mostly tied to weapon crafting and their upgrades. You might need to gather some resources during your travels and collect a currency from killing your enemies. Bigger combos award you with more currency. And each time you die you might drop half of that currency into a bag that can be recovered. (max amount of bags can be upgraded too)Well I left this aspect for the last since it might be one of main reasons why people like this game. Said story being told about Laika, soldier the protector of her people, also a mother who tries to hide its child from a cruel reality of this world. And while being stoic person, she might have her moments to appreciate stuff around and a wish for a normal life. To make sure the tribe survives, she will be sent on missions to disrupt enemy communications and try to find allies. Through the game she will meet other survivors or victims of these lands. Some might ask for a help, while others just want to be left alone. Even though story is pretty simple on paper, it has some powerful scenes and themes to it.So lets recap it in short: Visuals, Music, Atmosphere, Story.: Combat system in combination with movement can be enjoyable for one player and annoying for another: Too many optional fetch quests.: There's a lot of love was put into this game, with a little problems here and there but mostly good stuff. So game totally worth its money, and should be enjoyable experience for many players.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best indie games I've ever played, definitely worth the price. Looking forward to the sequel!Pros:+Immersive storytelling+Very creative art design (Endless thanks to the team who prepared the detailed background designs)+Excellent music (I added all the songs to my playlist after finishing the game)+Creative core gameplay mechanics (It's a masterpiece to create such a diverse gameplay with such simple gameplay mechanics)+Enjoyable side quests that complete the story+A dark and serious atmosphere that I can't find in many AAA gamesCons: (If i would be a little spoiled):-The motorcycle's NOS feature unlocks very close to the end of the game, it should have unlocked earlier.-It should be a little easier to upgrade weapons and equipment, otherwise the game gets a little boring because you keep doing the same things over and over.-There should have been the ability to play music tapes by selecting them as you wish, or new tapes should have been played as a priority. The game ended before I had a chance to listen to most of the new tapes.-The motorcycle's development is not felt until just before the end of the game. A motorcycle development system similar to weapon developments would have been better.-Moving around the map is a bit exhausting.-Teleportation points are insufficient or their positions are wrong (I never used the teleportation until unlimited teleportation was opened btw)-There could have been exclamation marks on the map showing all main and side quests so as not to miss the entire content.*****Spoiler Alert!********************-Some minor bugs occur after Puppy escapes and Laika brings him home. Laika sometimes dies as if she hit something while driving straight, especially when trying to control the ship.***************+++++ Many thanks to the development team, they have created a high quality work of art. I am looking forward to their new game...

_childDocuments_.review: This game is well done! For a while, I wanted to have a game different and unique from the other games I played. In June of 2023, I saw the teaser for Laika: Aged Through Blood for the first time and I was blown away by just how awesome the game looks. I played the demo just after watching the trailer and it plays great.Before Christmas Eve, I bought the game and started playing it.Pros: The gameplay is so fun.The concept of switching between different guns and riding a motorcycle is great.The setting and designs for the characters have a charm to the theme of the game.The animation of the game plays great.The mission is there to kill some time for certain story events.Music is the best to listen to while riding anywhere.The money of the game is unique. Instead of the usual coins and paper we always have in the real world, it's only the internal organs called viscera that can be used for spending items and food. Some stores are available to buy items and food.Cooking the food can give you a boost (e.g. increased ammo slots, x2+ combo, x2+ resources, etc)Crafting and upgrades can help you throughout the gameplay.The story is enjoyable to watch, but I won't get to the whole story because of spoilers.Cons: The game may be fun but some parts can feel repetitive.After a long play-through, you start to feel bored riding everywhere trying to get from point A to point B. After completing a quest, you can do nothing until the next mission starts.Food and items can be scarce at the time but can respawn for the time being, and the store can replenish the items you bought.Overall: On that note, I'm giving this game a 9.9/10. The game is immersive and I recommend buying this game if you want to have fun and enjoy the journey!

_childDocuments_.review: The recurring themes you'll see in the other negative reviews are that people WANT to enjoy the game, and just can't.Brutal difficulty and overly long tedious gameplay are the general trends, and it's definitely what kills the game.Even many of the positive reviews call out these issues, and just manage to stomach them more in favor of the positive elements.The core controls and mechanics are interesting, and it's a neat theme, with pretty art.Though, ultimately, it's bogged down by trying to be a bigger game than it probably should be, with superfluous mechanics that weaken the experience.You're expected to perform a lot of truly difficult maneuvers for even the most basic of encounters, where even the simplest enemies and jumps feel incredibly threatening.This is not terrible on it's own, and a 'precision' game can certainly be a fine game, but it does get exhausting over time.What really brings it to the level of being a problem, is that there's a currency system in the game, where you drop enormous amounts of resources for every death, and if you die on your attempt to respawn and retrieve them, they're lost.This means that you feel compelled to approach everything very slowly and delicately, which is made all the more painful by a complex reload mechanic that has a high chance of killing you every time you try to reload, you only get two shots between reloads, and can often get into situations where there's no guaranteed safe way to ensure a reload.It all makes for a very miserable experience.There's also crafting, which requires gathering resources, which can only be done by using one of your precious two shots to shoot a resource node, which then necessitates a reload, which again: can easily kill you.It's all just a hodge-podge of mechanics that do not mesh well together, and this is before you even get to the backtracking and repetitiveness.I feel that the minimal change to make a drastic improvement to the game, would be an accessibility option to not drop resources on death, so players could then treat it more like a precision platformer.That atleast would be an easy improvement that could be done with trivial development effort.A more substantial accessibility option would be to give you a health bar with perhaps 3 hitpoints.More holistically, the game would've been better served as a more linear experience without backtracking and crafting / resources, or alternatively a much less punishing and faster-paced exploration game.

_childDocuments_.review: Been devouring this game since it's Next Fest Demo months ago, and it's still amazing, dark af and extremely fun and rewarding. Not done yet, but I'll stay long after credits roll.I will protect Puppy with every fiber of my being.EDIT:Okay so... I've beaten the story. A few big things to mention.1. HUGE ADVICE - Laika's cursor has an arrow that indicates the direction her head is facing. You want to land safe? Point upwards. Additionally, the weapon wheel on the bottom left of your screen will turn blood red if Laika is upside down. Again, want to land on your neck, if it's red, you will. Thereby, when the screen is zoomed out or you're coated in gore, look to either indicator for safety.2. You will get fleeced in Blackjack. No question.3. If you are having difficulty in combat, consider shooting first. Not a joke, shoot from outside of bird aggro range whenever possible.4. Believe it or not, certain birds are non-violent. I won't say which. Do with them what you will.5. The story is very brutal and dark. Catharsis does not come easy.6. Your side quests are for resources and lore on support characters, not the main story. Some side quests (somewhat) trigger main story events. (I hadn't 100% yet, so I may be talking sh*t)7. You will eventually acquire an upgrade that can trivialize the game's platforming difficulty. But you can still easily land on your neck. So if you see something you want, but can't shotgun to get it. Wait and keep progressing, it'll come.So, big thing. I love this game. I loved the demo, obviously the 1st more than the 2nd, but every part of Laika's journey was heart wrenching and amazing. I'm not one for being emotional about anything, but I genuinely felt the story was gripping and painful to watch from the outside, especially being a parent myself. I love Laika, the coyote and the game.Combat: I've noticed a lot of comments that focus on the difficulty of encounters, mostly citing the positioning of enemies and target acquisition. My big piece of advice is consider learning parry timing if you are not confident slapping birds quickly. Parry timing is also dire if your weapons aren't upgraded with improved reload timing. Reducing the spin to reload is paramount to getting combos, thus gaining more viscera, and taking out groups. Rockets can also be dodged but not outrun.I played the game for about 26 hours, and a lot of that time was spent exploring and losing money in Blackjack. I cannot recommend this game enough for it's ease of difficulty, rich and tender story and the gun play. But there will be some getting used to with making flips and jumps.Please, do yourself a favor and give the game a shot. It may not be for everyone, but I feel this game sits with the rest of 2023's outrageously incredible release year. Thanks Braindwash Gang!

_childDocuments_.review: Once I finished the game, I had mixed feelings. It took me a few days mulling it over, because I really wanna like this game, but something was VERY off.	To make it short, the artistic side of this game is GREAT, but the gameplay is lackluster.	So, can I recommend it? Well, if you wanna a cool story with interesting themes, enticing visuals and amazing music to tie it all up together, go for it! You’ll probably enjoy it. But if you’re just looking for a great metroidvania, this is not for you.	So, let me pick apart some things that I liked, and I disliked. For starter, the gameplay. Well, like I said, it felt lackluster. Not because the core of the game is bad, it’s not, in fact I liked the controls and how the motorcycle drives around, I liked the movement, took me a while to get used, it feels weird at the start but once you get used to it, you start being able to do more tricks and risk more, and that’s exactly what I’d want on this type of game. But. There’s only a few bosses (five, in fact). First one is serviceable, it’s simple, but it’s the first boss and should be simple. Second was the best one, I really liked everything about it. Third was annoying at first but then it was fun. Fourth was… boring. It wasn’t interesting, and it needs more. Fifth was an EXTREME letdown, I was able to kill it in like 20-30 seconds and that left a bad taste just before the ending. The enemy variability is boring too, there’s basicly five enemies: pistol, rifle, RPG, machine gun and knife guy. I liked the pacifist guys, which don’t attack you, but I feel this is more tied to story than gameplay. There’s no reason not to shoot them, and it changes nothing (like you can make more pacifist appear if you don’t shoot them or they gonna help you, or maybe if you start killing them, they stop appearing altogether). All enemies go down in a single shot, there’s no minibosses, and most times the placement is boring. At first, you’re learning, everything’s new and interesting, but halfway through the game it’s… ok I guess. There was some interesting placements I really liked (for example once you have to do a wheelie to block two MG guys in a small corridor, that was cool as ♥♥♥♥). Powerups are not great either. The shotgun was weird at first, but suddenly became one of my favorite guns (it blasts you in the opposite direction you shoot) because so much you can do with it. The dash was cool too, I liked it, but you get it really late in game. But damn, it was the best powerup. Then there’s the hook which… Why? All it does is unlocking new areas. I was hoping I could hook into stuff and dangle around or something like that, but nope, you just use it to drag stuff. Boring.	Now, to the artistic side. The story is really nice, and I actually like how most stuff is not super explained. You don’t need to give details about everything to make a story interesting, and my only complaint is how the ending is predictable, but honestly I dunno how I’d fix it, and I dunno if that’s necessarily a bad thing. I really enjoyed the quests, the lil tales, how most NPC act towards each other and you. It felt really believable. The main themes, being duty, sacrifice and child abuse, are super well done. I don’t think enough people talk how Laika herself, being victim of abuse, IS abusive in her own way towards Puppy, being the smothering mother, incapable of letting her child grow up. I really liked the secondary themes: the bone quest for example, how we’re still “nourished” by our ascendants (tying to the whole child abuse thing too!), among others. I see some people talking about Native Americans and imperialism, but I think that’s such a simple reading on the whole situation which is just boring and third grade understanding of the situation and there’s far more deeper in there. The visuals are really nice, it never feels out of place, I liked the designs, I liked the gore, I liked the background, everything is very pleasing to the eye, even the ugly. And all is tied up perfectly with the music. Oh, am I in love with the music. The way you unlock the musics too, I REALLY liked the concept and it made it so much more meaningful. With all that, the artistic side really carries this game. There are places for improvement, for certain, but it's pretty good as it is. I could pick some stuff apart if I really tried and meant to, but I don't think it's necessary or fair.	With all that being said, I HOPE the developers can take all this, and either fix the gameplay side, or if they expand on the game, being DLC or a sequel, can improve on what, in my opnion, dragged an amazing game down.	All that being said, thank you for your time. Appreciate it!
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: Great idea, Terrible execution. When I came across a metroidvania centered around riding a motorcycle, the one thing I was expecting was speed but this game is slower than hollow knight and the bullet time mechanic is to blame. In a game where you have to hit every bullet (since you can't reload or will be very vulnerable while doing so) the developers opted to make the gun very inaccurate unless the player activates the bullet time, which makes the game a series of bullet times where you only have to click the enemy before they get to do anything. The slow pace of the game is further intensified when you account the fact that the bike's have a very low max speed, and the game does not have momentum, once the max velocity is reached, even if going downhill, that's as fast as you will go, which isn't much.Besides slowing the pace of the game and making the combat turn into a cookie clicker, the bullet time has terrible sinergy with the main mechanic of the game, wheeling/fliping the bike, this happens because when the game goes from slowmotion to regular speed the amount of leaning grows a lot causing the player to lose control of the bike, specially since when on slowmotion, your focus is on the enemys your aiming at and not your own bike.My last major critic of the game are the boss fights, they are long segments where for the most time, the player doesn't have anything to do, just watch the motorcycle go through it's path waiting for the next attack from the boss or for his hitbox to appear. What makes it worse is that the game wait's for the final parts of the segment to introduce mechanics never before introduced (as bossfights are very different from your regular gameplay loop) which means that you will have to go through all the boss fight to have a chance to learn what the hell you are supposed to do in a situation you were not prepared for.Other than all that, the art and music are amazing.It appears to me that the motorcicle theme ended up being totally separated from the rest of the game's mechanics, you spin to reload, but it makes you vulnerable if done while in a fight, you can block bullets with your bike but if you try and do it while focused on a fight you will end up crashing your bike on the ground and dying instantly. Very sad, it could have been a great game

_childDocuments_.review: I don't write reviews a lot, if ever really, but this game just hit me like a ton of bricks, I love this game so much. There's is an IMMENSE load of GOOD going for this game, The soundtrack is breath taking and just poignant, The story and themes were well executed, I love how things interact and the movement of the bike is really fun as well as the guns. The visuals are always on point, it's quality ALL THE WAY THROUGHBUT, here are my caveats and nit picks that I think is important to know before buying the game. - This isn't a dark souls game by any means, But it is hard and you will have to get good or die trying. - Sometimes there will be a lot of long times travelling from a place to another place but the soundtrack however makes it really enjoyable. (Spoilers ahead: ) - There's temporary buffs that you can get and playing without them is absolutely a challenge on it's on, if you're more of a casual player don't skip out on them.I don't have a lot more to add, I loved the game, the story made me go through all the emotions, this game is unique and truly just an experience I'd love to see more people do. I know this game is not for everyone, But it sure as hell was for me and I loved it.

_childDocuments_.review: The game isn't bad but it's lacking in many aspects. The gameplay doesn't really evolve much and a lack of meaningful upgrades makes it a bit bland by the end. _childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: An experience beyond words. Can't even do it justice.Utterly gorgeous art, a wonderful, pensive soundtrack, and an emotionally devastating yet genuinely beautiful story all mix with a unique and fun take on metroidvania gameplay that never seems to get old. This game bleeds true passion and soul from every crevice. Every minute I didn't spend playing it, I was thinking about it. Easily in my top 3 games of all time. The kind of game you will feel lucky to have played.
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: Let's begin with the first thing people notice; Yes, the controls are different, you travel on a dirtbike, and have to keep your balance while also using it to shield yourself at times. Is it different? Yes. Is it a terrible idea? No.The game's art style is comic-style that is bright and sharp as a blade, but muted and has a feel that rolls with the theme of the story.After pushing through the frustration and anger, as all souls players will know, I can safely say I do not regret a single moment playing this game. The story is dark and maybe even a little hopeless, but it helps to focus your attention on why you choose to push on; is it for that character you like? Because it's your responsibility? Do it for Puppy?I loved how this game made me work for the story and how I often shed tears reading the dialogue and while the difficulty was frustrating it made the victories and rewards all the more sweeter.I would definitely recommend this game, or even the demo it has to see if it's for you. It'll be challenging, and difficult to adjust to, but if you push through, I think you'll be truly satisfied.
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: A gorgeous symphony of beautiful and affective writing, character design, art-style, music, etc... that is unfortunately held down by it's astonishingly lacking gameplay. The initially intriguing elevator pitch-esque game mechanic of "hill climb racing with a gun" is nowhere near a compelling enough gameplay base to hold the weight an entire metroidvania. It's interesting enough to get you to play a few hours, but I'm 9 hours in writing this and it hasn't innovated on it in a single meaningful way. The movement is not only sluggish and clunky, but it's  Ergo the movement is neither a snappy satisfying system, or a challenging clunky system that must be overcome, it is nothing but a waste of time. I wish this was an animated limited TV series. I want to experience this story and this art and this music, I really truly want to. A well-written story of a innocent mother and child living through a war caused by xenophobic fear is exactly what we need right now. Unfortunately in order to access this story you must crawl a marathon through mud in a downpour. The entirety of the gameplay relies on system that's more shallow than some flash games. Not to mention because of how bland and boring the gameplay is the pacing is  You crawl the marathon, desperately searching for specs of story, going miles between beats. Very upsetting :/I'd love to recommend it, the developers clearly put hard work into this, but you're probably better off just watching someone else play it.
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: The game seemed really good when I first started playing. The story and music were good. The game play was an interesting take on a Metroidvania. It feels like the developers had heart for the game. HOWEVER, it ultimately felt unfinished. A few hours into the game, the game play felt very repetitive. You play on a bike in a Trials-like mechanic and carry a gun with you to shoot enemies in bullet time. Every gun you pick up past the starting pistol is awful to use, so you just play with the same weapon for the whole game. No new combat mechanics are introduced beyond some surface level things needed to get to new areas. The main story isn't very long so they added a bunch of fetch quests in the latter half of the game to pad things out, but it's just re-trotting the same places you've been.The music is usually good. You pick up casettes throughout the game that add new music to the soundtrack. Story sections though force you to listen to more atmospheric music which is mixed way too low and is generally fairly boring. Even some open world sections force you to listen to the atmospheric music instead of the casettes and it kinda kills the vibe.The story and characters are the only things that felt consistently good, but they're not enough to hold up the game as a whole.
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: After playing first few hours I was ready to give this game a great review. Despite being brutally difficult, it felt most fair, and stellar soundtrack, great design and character made me enjoy game a lot. Unfortunately I came to conclusion I can not recommend the game because of horrible level design. Farley early in the game you come to an area (shipwrecks, "Where Water Glistened") which is so frustratingly bad and made me quit the game and never come back. At this level they introduce a new mechanic: wheelie balancing on the ropes, which if finicky and not fun (smallest mistakes make you fall though). But it could have forgiven the bad mechanic and moved on, if not for atrocious level design which made this mechanic 100 times worse: there are a sections which have 3+ level of ropes, and failing on top rope make you fall all the way back to the bottom of the level, forcing you to start all over again. Moreover dying couple of times at different sides of the map because of this mechanics caused me to loose most of hard collected viscera which made the whole exercise even more frustrating. And this is not about difficulty - this is just back design, which devs should fix.To summarize: I still car recommend to buy the game on deep discount to play first few hours, but devs need to fix the levels (or mechanics) before game could be considered fully playable.
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely outstanding! A great spin on classic metroidvanias, with fun unique movement. The bike feels clunky and hard to control at first but once you get the hang of it, it feels heckin' cool and stylish as hell. The soundtrack alone should make you want to play this game, Beicoli knocked it out of the park. And the story as well is just *chefs kiss.* it's nothing too crazy, but it makes you feel the feels. This is a great game that feels like it's empowering women and it does it incredibly well. TLDR: The art, the style, the movement, the ost, and the story are all great and I can't recommend this game enough. One of my new all-time favorite metroidvanias.
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: This game is captivating. The stunning visuals, the music, the story - they all come together to accompany an addictive, satisfying type of gameplay. I haven't been able to put this game down for weeks and when I'm not playing it, I find myself putting the album on repeat, which just gets me even more excited to get back into the game and try not to cry.

_childDocuments_.review: Laika is a great game that fumbles the execution a bit while still managing to be deeply engaging. The game pushes the leeway of the metroidvania to the limit with lots of slow sections, some annoying sidequests which give almost no direction and enough backtracking that it can disincentivise exploration towards the middle of the game as you realise there's not much to find until you reach certain points. The moment to moment gameplay feels great; it's very much got the feeling of one of the easier torture platformer like Celeste or Meat Boy, with encounters that can be difficult to get through but a very quick turn around on retries and usually little punishment for death. Sometimes tracking where your character is facing and which direction you're travelling can be tricky and switching between "layers" to go up ramps can occasionally be finicky however and there's not much enemy variety (although the main variety is in the layouts of enemies and terrain, a machine gun on flat ground feels different to a machine gun under a ramp and so on). The game is great aesthetically and thematically. Despite its often ultraviolent presentation and events, the game feels mature and approaches its topics with an uncommon amount of gravitas and respect. The writers were certainly passionate and interested in what they were doing with the story and nothing feels hokey or phoned in. Some of the more disturbing content is treated as genuinely horrific and it does a good job showing reasonable reactions to it based on the world the characters live in. It all just feels very authentic.My main problem with the game are the boss fights. Other than the first few boss fights, which are generally okay if a little easy and overlong, this game has absolutely some of the worst boss fights in any game I've ever played. I can forgive the simplicity of early bosses as the control scheme is a lot to grasp on its own without a boss to content with, but the later boss fights are bafflingly designed. I never felt fairly challenged; the boss fights feel like they entirely depend on luck and are extremely tedious while also still being very simple. One of them has one (1) attack which it does every 10 seconds or so until you kill it where it fires a projectile in a random half of the arena which splits into randomly bouncing secondary projectiles when shot which then split again. To deal damage to the boss you have to get close enough to hook it then drive away to pull the hook which becomes taut and you need to keep the rope taut for a couple of seconds, then the boss takes damage and the hook detaches. This means that all of your forward acceleration that was being cancelled out is now acting on you so you need to brake IMMEDIATELY as there are bottomless pits on either side of the arena AND a ramp in the middle that will launch you directly into one of them if you drive over it at full acceleration. You need to do this while contending with the random projectiles which involves aiming at them, shooting them and doing a flip on the one ramp to reload (which to remind you will shoot you directly off the arena if you go at full speed). The camera is so zoomed out that it's very hard to tell which way you're facing and your driving direction and you die in one hit. You have to tug the boss FIVE TIMES. Overall it takes about 2 minutes for the boss to do enough cycles to potentially kill it if you hit every possible hook (if you don't pull the hook in time you lose your chance to damage the boss). The other annoying boss is simply extremely tedious along with an RNG attack that pushes you off the ground and flips you to a random facing direction if you get hit by it which makes it unreliable to get hit by; you can get hit five times in a row and land tires down every time and then get hit again and land head down. There are also attacks that kill you no matter where they hit you whereas every other attack in the game has the bike act as a shield. The boss also feels like it takes about three minutes to kill as there's no way to push the phases at all, the boss simply acts on entirely scripted sequences and you just have to avoid it until you get to the end of a sequence. If you die you have to start the entire fight again.Despite that rant, I think the game is genuinely an impressive effort and a lot of fun even though I don't really know who it's for, exactly. Trials meets metroidvania meets twin stick shooter is already a weird combination of genres before getting to the grimdark-hopepunk setting and the gruesome, touching story and the cutesy aesthetic. It all comes together to make an interesting game but it's not for everyone and it skirts close to overstaying its welcome for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: Overall great & challenging game with a fantastic art style, a great soundtrack, and a very intriguing narrative dealing with dark, heavy themes of loss, death, coming of age, etc. It's not perfect and has some questionable choices (mostly in mechanics), but overall it's a really interesting game and I enjoyed my time playing it. Well worth full price and you'll be getting roughly 20 hours out of it if you do all of the quests, and a little longer if you achievement hunt.The aesthetic, artwork, and soundtrack are all top notch. I love expanding the soundtrack by finding new tapes, especially because there's a narrative reason for it. The soundtrack is SO good that even months after completing the game, I find myself listening to it now and then.The game controls decently well, but the floatiness/physics/knockback are all things that take a bit of time to get used to. I recommend just playing the whole game with a KB&M instead of a controller because precision eventually becomes an issue. I played the first half of the game with a controller (the rumble is really satisfying), but switched over to KB&M because of the shipyard, multiple small platforms with death pits, and the rope mechanics being exceptionally hard to deal with on controller.Some mechanics were implemented very well, such as the dash, parry, and shotgun jump. Other mechanics end up being unfun and frustrating, especially the ropes in the shipyard (you "snap" onto them really weird and balancing is a fight, I can't count the number of times I'd get to the end and because of this get quickly flipped over to my death, or would fall off the rope if the angle wasn't perfect and fall to my doom) and the boost having some inconsistencies. The combo counter is not displayed anywhere in the UI, and is only indicated by the screen becoming redder and hazier as you're shooting, which I don't like because it can be unclear if the area you're at is getting you close enough when you're going for the final combo achievement.Combat is enjoyable, but can get repetitive because of the one-hit deaths, the fact that all regular enemies are stationary, and the fact that you will be back tracking a LOT. A Caterpillar Made of Sadness is my favorite of all of the boss fights, taking full advantage of driving fast while navigating terrain and using tricks  The biggest problems with the bosses comes down to the later boss fights really being at odds with the run and gun fun of the rest of the game. I found the strategy that worked best and trivialized some of the subsequent boss fights was simply to take it slow and remain stationary, especially for the  boss that shoots upwards from below you and the  boss that has instant death pits on both sides of the arena platform. The final boss fight has basically no mechanics other than dodging and requires no strategy other than ride up one of the walls and spam as fast as you can, which was quite surprising. The fight felt way too quick and easy since it came directly after the instant death pit boss that could only be damaged during a short time window that followed completing some mechanics with the hook.The story is emotional, hard-hitting, heartstring-tugging, but also very depressing. The lore of the world is absolutely fascinating,  The side quests were a lot of fun, and you will be driven to complete them just by how great all of the characters are, rewards be damned. I do think the game gets a bit too gratuitous at times; the biggest example is the side quest
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: This is such a shining example of how a few try hards on a dev team can be the worst enemies of the entire studio. And as a precursor for this, sekiro is my favorite game of all time. I love difficulty, I love parry mechanics. The music is beautiful. The characters are interesting and well written. Barely know these characters and you already feel invested in them. The art is stunning. But then you're on this flippy ass little bike and die in one hit or if it tips. I'm three hours in, stuck at a room (which I can't turn back from) where there are FIVE enemies shooting at me (all kill me in one hit) (followed by another off screen if I get past these). My gun has 2 bullets. The only way to reload is to do a backflip. So the only way forward is landing both shots, then successfully parry, land ONE shot, PARRY another AFTER the flip is complete, STOP spinning in time to land successfully, then immediately shoot the guy I'm now flying towards. Skill issue my ass, you have a skill issue in game design. This is stupid ♥♥♥♥, and you crippled your game over the desire of a few devs to make it prohibitively difficult not as a hard mode, but as the base game. Because that's the real issue here, it's not that "some people" need an easy mode, its that a small amount of people need a hard mode. Literally just add a one hit kill mode and your game would have made 10x the money and be a beloved, unique indie-vania classic.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't sleep on this game, folks.  It's one of the most incredible experiences I've ever had playing a game.The soundtrack is beyond incredible and the world they've built is...beautiful in its own way.  One of the first areas you hit after leaving your home is 'Where Our Bikes Growl'.  That's the sort of worldbuilding and overview that I *love*.  Some of the best times can be had just driving around and listening to the soundtrack while you're looking at the backdrops.The story is compelling, heartwrenching, and nihilistic at points.  People can be ♥♥♥♥♥♥, people can be tense and angry.  That's what the world has made them.And the gameplay can make YOU feel angry, too.  If you played Excitebike back on the NES, you know how you're flipping and moving your bike.  You also know that going in one direction too much ends up in a splatter.  The bike and reloading mechanics take time to get used to, but as you do so, you start to revel in how smoothly you can do these things.  There still exist places and portions that are utterly frustrating, and I get that this will drive folks away.  But the story is so incredibly WORTH IT, so just keep pushing at it.  You can do it.Take a play through their demo and see if its your game.  If you buy the game afterwards, it saves your progress from the demo.Also, the computer cheats at Blackjack.  I just know it does.

_childDocuments_.review: Got the game as a gift after I'd been looking at it.  gameplay I do quite enjoy it, there is an amount of trial and error involved, but still fun to me.story wise I enjoyed it, ending pace was rushed as i'm sure some people have already said, and I'd say it could have done better in that regard, but otherwise i feel it's solid.

_childDocuments_.review: ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, what a ride.  Never played anything like it.  The story is simple and bleak, but engaging.  The gameplay is just something else, I literally don't even know how to categorize it because if it's part of a genre, it's one I'm not familiar with.  There's a unique and honestly very punishing way of getting around the map, but for the dozens-to-hundreds of times you die, it's at least a really fast respawn with no fanfare, kind of like a good hardcore platformer in that regard, so it's hard to get frustrated as you can get right back into the action.  I thought for a while that the controls were unintuitive and bad, but actually it was me!   was bad!  Got way better over time and had an absolute blast, it just takes you a minute to get accustomed to moving around like this.  Animations were good, music is INCREDIBLE, just a pleasure all the way through.
