_childDocuments_.review: Edit: Grammar. After around 30 hrs playtime, all points in the review still hold trueFirst: Understand that, while this is an arcade racing game, it is by no means easyI have been a big wipeout fan; been playing for decades, so "high speed anti-grav" racing is my shtick. I can handle speed, so long as the controls are RESPONSIVE. WipeOut has its formula down to a T with it's combination of streering and air-brakes.Redout, on the other hand, replaces air-brakes with strafing. In the first game, I absolutely HATED how slippery the ships were. You want to turn left? Well you're going to be moving right for quite some time before the ship finally changes direction. I couldn't stand it, and left the game untouched when I saw that even the best players were crashing into walls (something that you'd never see in top level wipeout).Thankfully, they have toned down this "slipperiness" to the point that the ships finally feel responsive. You turn left, ship turns left. You turn right AND strafe right? Ship turns right harder. None of that slipping in the opposite direction first before actually turning, UNLESS you want to. If you turn in one direction, but strafe in the other, you will accomplish a similar turning style to what Wipeout offers, albeit a little more exagerrated in the direction that you strafe.Controlability aside, the tracks are interesting but mildly forgettable. They are moreso like roller coaster rides, where you're reacting to sudden twists and turns rather than anticipating them. The devs tried to alleviate this by adding "turn signals" that warn when a turn is about to come up. They come in three colors; green means a light turn, orange means a moderate/hard turn, red means hairpin. Or at least, that's what they should mean, but unfortunately each track has different definitions of how hard a turn is. On one track, a orange turn might be considered easy and might only require steering without the need for strafing, where as on another track, an orange turn requires exact timing of your steering/strafing to avoid getting smashed into the wall. On top of this, the turn signals sometimes appear too late, and you'll suddenly be running into a wall because the track took a blind turn that you weren't warned about until too late.I imagine that if you keep playing the game, you'll begin to subconsiously learn the tracks and won't be as dependent on the turn signals anymore, but having them be more accurate/consistent would be a help, especially since there's 72 tracks (if you include the reversed versions). My last complaint is the air maneuverability. Oh my god I can't describe how much I hate jumps. When you're in the air, the steering of the ship no longer has any effect on your trajectory. If you steer left or right, your ship pivots as if you were turning, but you maintain your original trajectory. In order to move in the air, you have to strafe. Got that? Ok, because now you also have to worry about pitching your ship up and down. Ok, sure, but don't forget about ROTATING YOUR SHIP. In practice, this completely juggles the mind because suddenly your main way of turning (steering) basically get's shut off, forcing you to remember that only strafing works now, and that you have to move your left hand to the d-pad to rotate the ship. This LITERAL SPLIT SECOND of hesitation trying to fumble your brain into flight mode is enough to crash your ship. Devs: Please make steering have an actual effect on your ships trajectory. There's no reason it shouldn't.All of these complaints aside, Redout 2 is very fun. It gives that fast paced action of wipeout with it's own unique style. As mentioned in the beginning, the game is hard, and if you're looking for a racing game where you can win every race in 1 or 2 tries, this will not be it. But if you're looking for a challenge, and a game that offers a great sense of racing at breakneck speeds, this is the game for you.

_childDocuments_.review: A good game, in comparison to WipeOut HD. However there are some issues that plaque the gameplay. The Challenges for Time attack and Speed are way too difficult. Those two challenge types require beyond computer level AI perfection to attain. I have had laps where i never touched the wall and was flat out the entire time with boost and still never got close to their times or number values. Mind you, I also have the game set to Zero difficulty, as anything above it, you will place mid field as the AI just blows by you like you are standing still. Best recommendation for the devs is to go back and address these issues, as Wipeout HD wasnt even that difficult on hard mode. What they are asking for is not possible, unless there are cheats I am unaware of. Recommendation is to up the point values you can get while racing for the Speed challenges, and lower the Gold, Silver, and Bronze goals by at least half. 1000 may look cool but if your point ticker doesnt give enough points no matter what you do, it isnt attainable. For Time attack, lower the time goals by at least 10 seconds! When we start out in B series, time attack is possible, but as you go towards the end of the series, even when at max level for the event, there are a few that we arent even 8 seconds close to, and that is on a good performing lap. Times goals are too high and need to be adjusted down.  Lastly, the volcano map and the sky map......I get the need for jump and some of them are fun, but it is super difficult to align on some of these and in some cases you just go right through the track! Not fun. Either add auto align to the game as a non-turn off feature or connect some of these multi jumps into a longer track space so we can land. Further on this but, jumps like 5.0KM/2.14M, seriously?! Lower that value. Granted we may be increasing speed as we levelbut there is not an area on these maps that makes a jump that long. The few places where you think it might be dont even count it. I jump clear from one area to the end of the straight away and that still didnt count! So that tells me the challenge is broken and not registering the jump or there is not a place on the maps requesting that challenge for that type of jump to be possible. Overall good game, but some serious issues on difficulty that make it discouraging to play long term. Not to mention community and seasonal challenges section arent even available and are greyed out! Make it challenging, not impossible. IF these things can be fixed, this would be a solid game in comparison with Wipeout HD and XGRA.

_childDocuments_.review: As a huge fan of the original game, this is basically a letdown across the board. While the first game may feel more amateurish, it had a lot more charm and it actually scratched the itch of pushing the boundaries of speed much better than this sequel ever does. At face value, Redout 2's handling model may feel more immediately controllable than the previous game to people who are familiar to other AG racers, but not a single track ever let me hit the same highs I felt being a speed-demon in the first game. Feeling like I'm constantly fighting to read and stay on track by lazy design "gotcha's" and the like, it's hard to care at all honestly. I spent plenty of a of time to trying to acclimate, memorizing specific tracks for hours and giving it its fairest shake to not put nostalgia on a pedestal. Even with all that time spent trying to recalibrate though, I only ever felt frustrated at best and as if the spirit of the game was completely neutered at worst. With as much as I've invested into the game, it's just not worth trying to like it anymore.EDIT:After some more time playing since my original review, I've only continued to find that there's more frustrating things than there are good in Redout 2. A good amount of my complaints are still problems from my original review, and I reckon most of them could be solved by some patching. The devs aren't hiding or negligent to that fact as far as the communication in their Discord goes, but we're still waiting nonetheless. It doesn't help that it's only gotten more and more annoying to run into these problems as well, to the point of me just alt+F4ing and playing something else as soon as a run gets ruined by one. I won't go over every single bug I've ran into, but I will say that every session has at least one, and every other session recently has ended with one that makes me drop it on the spot. More subjectively, I still prefer Redout 1 for its feel and atmosphere. I admire how much work went into expanding its features and presentation, but not much has stuck with me. Its music is fine aside from being a bit run-of-the-mill, with a few songs that stand out here and there. The visuals are great when they're not making it harder to understand where I'm going, or even where I am on the track. A lot more work has gone into fleshing out the world, with additions such as cut-scenes and voice-overs, which are cute.Mechanically, there's more to manage in every single moment with how boost and health are tied together, and it all synergizes very well in a select few track/gamemode combinations. Level design is much more complex as well, which should be a positive, but feels more like a double edged sword. I'm willing to accept that I won't be great at every track, as every player has their best and worst, but some of these are just so busy design-wise and for such long duration's that there's plenty of races where I feel like there's no time to have a small mental break to reorient myself. With its simpler systems and track design in Redout 1, there were more places on average that gave such a breather, even if just for a second. With Redout 2 placing its fun and balance around maximizing every single little bit of the players health and boost to its limit, performing well becomes exhausting much faster. It's certainly a bigger and more frenetic experience, but I feel it doesn't make it better inherently. I will say, that this is where I'm most divided on Redout 2, because I feel like I could enjoy it. If I were just able to dig in and really grind it out, maybe I'd feel differently. Combined with its inconsistency due to bugs though, it's only made it a terrible experience to try and take it seriously at that level. To add on top of it all, its assortment of game modes is weirdly simplified and bland while everything else has gotten an upgrade. Every mode but one is played basically the same way, and that one unique mode is the one that has drawn ire from a lot of people over its balancing, even after an initial patch or two to try and fix it. That mode isn't as bad now, but it's a sad showing of variety regardless. Another area that's very monotonous is the bonus objective that every campaign race has. I can't think of one that is fun, as most are either stupidly trivial and completed by doing the event at all, or just a variation of "Win even harder". Then there's the objectives that feel broken/unfinished that just beg to be cheesed, such as creating your own jumps to gain Perfect Landings or jump distances, which are annoying at best and never feel good. The system as a whole feels like someone came up with the idea and committed too hard to implement it without any actual substance or care for what makes the overall product engaging. I guess I'm just in for the long haul in seeing if the game improves, because I really do want to like it more. I can't hide that I'm disappointed though, especially since I feel most everything was done with the good intentions of making a more explosive and exciting product. I still have a sore spot for the devs also updating Redout 1 so close to the release of this with an engine upgrade, which has visually ruined and changed how the game looks. So even if I just want to be an old man and play Redout 1 for nostalgia, it's just not the same game I've played for years prior to that patch from several months ago. ORIGINAL:As much as I have enjoyed playing the game so far and will continue to do so, I cannot recommend this to most people currently. I've ran into a few specific tracks in events that have several bugs ruin the experience, such as having the AI randomly teleport 3 kilometres ahead of me, myself teleporting as far as 21 kilometres backwards from a respawn, and falling straight through the track on certain jumps. Even in instances where the teleporting is not the most egregious, it only makes getting bonus trophies that much more finicky when I finally catch up. It's better to restart and hope it doesn't just happen again, with it occurring about 50% of the time. I'm a player that likes to do everything in a clean sweep, so basically having to avoid events with AI in the affected zones just so I can play the game more than restarting it over and over has been very annoying. There's also the difficulty curve the game throws at the player which is pretty brutal. Being an experienced player of the first game, it still took me about 20 minutes of experimenting and then watching someones completion of one of the tutorials to fully grasp the mechanic it was trying to explain. I started to get golds fairly easy then, but it just goes to show how obtuse quite a few things are.Much less importantly, there are a lot of smaller bugs, like the music dropping out or visual fx staying on screen through a restart. I have no doubts that hotfixes and patches will solve all of these problems, big and small, and that the devs will probably continue to keep an ear out on balancing the early-game difficulty, as I think they've already made a few slight adjustments. My biggest issue then is that I feel as the game is currently, it's a bad experience for most players. I hope that the fixes come fast so I can change my review to the positive one it really deserves, since I'm personally still having fun in spite of it all.

_childDocuments_.review: Redout 2 is the perfect example of why lack of QA and good track design can sink even the most fun of ships. Because hands down, when everything goes right, this game is a lot of fun. The sensation of speed is overwhelming in a good way, at times it looks outright gorgeous. It's Redout 1 but better. HOWEVER.This game actively  the player. It advertises itself with Assists and they're cool in principle- until you realize they happily yank you into corners.- they throttle your ship so any kind of time trial goes out the window.- they will pull you off course during jumpsThus, turn off the assists and the game becomes easier - what the hell. Talking about difficulty settings - it does come with a wide variety of them. Which is cool in principle, except they only seem to apply to AI opponents. Which further means that Speed and Time Trials are tuned for the higher difficulties. Which  means as a casual player, you can crash into difficulty cliffs at 2.000 frustrating km/h. So right out the gate, the whole accessibility and difficulty thing is not quite right. They're a trap and the game actively punishes you for foolishly making use of it. So what else is new on the QA front?- Bugs in some tracks where your ship will suddenly stall out (sometimes on flat straights).- Bugs where the AI will teleport 4 km ahead of you.- UI is sluggish, menus nestled into menus nestled into menus into taking way too long to do even the simplest of things. - Restarting a race takes too long for how easy it is to make a mistake. Waiting half a minute on a beefy PC for every mistake is too long.Continuing on then - the track design. This is the real killer for me. In my opinion, good track design is based on the age old premise of: "Easy to learn, difficult to master." Redout 2 however follows the track design of "FU, that's why." Here's how a typical track learning experience looks like here. Look the point is, it's actively player hostile and frustrating. A lot of the track grievances probably come from them using mirrored tracks because some tracks are perfectly fine and only become a nightmare in reverse. Doesn't change that it feels frustrating to learn and get around in. Still, there's an amazing game underneath all of this, so if you look at this and go "cool, this pleases me" - grab the game. I mean it. Go have fun. But if you're like me, you've probably got other games to play that don't actively hate you.

_childDocuments_.review: I think it's important to understand that this is a very different animal to the first Redout. I approached the first game pretty casually and had a great time, while this one is altogether more demanding, and rewarding in its own way. The best way I can put it is that the first felt very much like an arcade racer, while this feels to some extent like a racing sim - the kind you only usually get with real-life vehicles.That said, I think this game excels at what it does. I'm not a fan of racing games in-general, nor of perfectionism and mastering every bend - I prefer to perch myself on the edge of control and improvise, and there's a very good balance of the two here. I'm playing with all the assists turned off (except for a 5% hull limit on boosting, which I recommend), and it surely took some getting used to, but my growth in skill from 1-6 hours, then from 6-12 hours, in incredibly satisfying.Tracks are narrow, long, full of blind twists, turns, and jumps, but once you get over the incredible sensory overload it is totally possible to navigate them blind and come out on top. And when you do, I can comfortably say this game serves up spectacle like nothing else I've ever played. I can't think of many other instances where I've had the feeling of physically wrestling for control in a videogame. At 12 hours in I am constantly surprised by my own proficiency, as moment by moment I do by reflex what I wouldn't imagine was possible at this speed.I had my gripes at first, and I still do: speed events are way too hard, and it's totally unclear how you're supposed to approach them, but I do think they change up the game in an interesting way, forcing you to practice different skills, and it's entirely possible to progress through the career mode while skipping them until you're well-enough practised.It's also marred by a few technical issues - most notably the fact that your vehicle will fly straight through track you should be able to land on after jumps. I've had one or two absolutely egregious examples of this while trying to complete bonus objectives, but overall it's very minor.

_childDocuments_.review: Can't really recommend this one over Redout 1. If not for anything than the music alone. First game is definitely much better in that regard. As for the game itself, it is not the worst, but nowhere near as good as the first. Trophies also seem somewhat busted, or downright impossible in some cases. Those qualify 1st trophies come to mind. I guess I am not robotic precise enough to achieve most of those. The rest are punishingly hard, but achievable with some trickery, or just hurling yourself off the track and and making a mad dash landing on a complete separate part of the track, and hope not to explode. Lot of trial and error trying to find which parts will explode you on contact, and which ones will land you the trophy. Though I feel that you should not need to do such things to get trophies. Feels more like an effort to see how you can break the game than actually achieving something with skill. And yes, the first game had similar shenanigans, but those were very fluid and organic. Redout 2, is like a struggle to overcome bad design or something. Nightmare difficulty is beatable, but I would not suggest anyone to do it. Also the game is pretty much dead. I don't think multiplayer is even an option. And portions of the menu are grayed out. I don't think there will ever be any balancing for the game anytime soon. Or ever. Died fast too. If you like AG racing games, then I would say to stick with Redout 1. Or try something like Ballistic NG. And if you have a PS4 or PS5, there is always Wipeout Omega Collection. Redout 2 I would put on the same level as something like Antigraviator. It just misses the mark.

_childDocuments_.review: First off, just to get it out of the way. If you do not like hardcore racers. Turn around now and find a different game. If your willing to spend the time to turn yourself into neo from the matrix or just enjoy the challenge, welcome to Redout 2. Redout 2 is my first Antigrav racer that I have played and it was a breath of fresh air compared to all the other racers I have played. The visuals are stunning and the feeling of speed is unparalleled in any other racer with absolutely orgasmic soundtracks that really immerse you. Vehicles handle like an absolute dream, and the tracks are very fun and varied. The campaign however is excruciatingly long. And its the only way to unlock new ships, upgrades and cosmetics. Which means your generally ♥♥♥♥ out of luck in multiplayer til you beat it (Unless your a masochist or are fine with the prebuilt loaner ships). The racing itself in this game is extraordinarily fast paced. Which is a turn off for many as they cannot keep up with everything hence the mixed reviews at this time. Especially at the later stages of the game your often going 1500KPH (930MPH), up to 5000+KPH (3100+MPH) in your ship going around very windy, sometimes mind bending tracks. However if you really stick with the game and keep at it, its an excellent way to build up reaction speed and reflexes, hence the "turn you into neo from the matrix" at the start. But once you start building up those reflexes the racing becomes incredibly rewarding and addictive with a very high skill ceiling.I highly, HIGHLY recommend you start off on the easiest difficulty and adjust the assists to your liking when you start off. There is a rewind feature that can be extremely helpful and can really help with frustration, but you get limited uses the higher the difficulty. And despite the lower difficulty the AI can still be a real challenge to beat. Especially considering that one ♥♥♥♥ up, can mean you have gone from 1st with a 3KM lead to now being last with the ships that are now infront of you being 5km ahead. But failure in this game really makes you learn, and problem solve tracks. Making optimal lines, finding the best places to boost stack, and finding your own preferred route.Overall I understand why many people dont enjoy this game and leave negative reviews. This is definitely not a game for everyone, as its essentially the darksouls of racing games. But like darksouls, its just so damn fun when you finally overcome somethin and reach that goal you wanted. I wish more people would give this a try and really put the effort in to learn it. Cause its such a damn fun game that makes you feel a huge adrenaline rush when you get immersed in it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game needs some work in the balancing department(it got it, plz read edit below).Imagine restarting a race time and time again because either A: you crashed into a wall like a dingus, going so fast you can't see from the tears in your eyes after just trying to catch up to the other racers that just flew past you going triple your speed or B: the AI uses their infinite boost and impossible to beat skills to never even let you think about getting 3rd place. On top of all this turn down the difficulty to make it slightly easier and you see yourself grinding a racing game that really shouldn't be a grind and a progression system for the vehicles that gives virtually no player agency. I haven't touched the multi-player mode yet but reading other comments doesn't sound too great. I'd wait to buy this game or if you haven't played an anti-grav racer, get the first game. Hoping these issues get fixed cuz at this point its more frustrating, but yet still fun in moments. I do want this game to see its changes, where it goes and hopefully it will be fantastic!edit: Devs made a wonderful change to the speed challenges and they are way more manageable and fun to do. There was also an overall balancing fix. I changed my review from a thumbs down because the changes were exactly what I and I think many more players were looking for! The game is still grindy and like other go fast racer games the better parts for your ship are behind a wall of try and try and you will eventually(hopefully) succeed. I played some multiplayer as well and going from the level I'm at in the career to multiplayer is like smashing the "Plaid" button, I can f e e l the G's from my seat. Thank you for another awesome Redout experience! looking forward to the rest of the game(there's still lots of options locked behind a coming soon title) ;)

_childDocuments_.review: As a longtime Redout player, this one's a smidge disappointing. It's good, just not what I was looking for.- What do I like?First off, I love how strong strafing feels. It's very, very well-tuned and I find myself wanting this strength of strafing in Redout proper.I think the overheat mechanic is interesting, and the game looks very, very pretty most of the time. Most* of the lore seems pretty neat.Very grounded experience and I would recommend it if you are not a Redout Purist like me.*kind of wish you didnt need to play Space Assault to know whats going on most of the time to be honest.- What do I not like?First off, I REALLY find myself wishing that the physics-based racing design philosophy of the first game was carried over. You have way, WAY more grip on the tracks on this than in Redout and it definitely feels weird having a middlepoint between antigrav racing slip and standard racing grip.The first game's soundtrack was stronger, I feel, with 2's resorting to a lot of noise in some areas. Definitely feels less satisfying to fly along at mach 1 to this game's soundtrack than 1's.Redout's HUD is far stronger than this one's, especially for someone like me that plays games like this to zone out. Yes, this is after the first(?) HUD update. Older one was worse, newer one is better but still doesnt compare to the original.Graphically, I find myself missing the desaturation of the palettes in Redout. 2 has a *theoretically* compelling ship design system, but many of the designs either feel tired and old or allowed themselves to decay out of their old design philosophy(looking at you, Conqueror. You do not look like a muscle car anymore, really).Speaking of which, the cosmetic and upgrade unlocks system is... rather annoying and takes far too long to build up compared to Redout's giving you just about everything out of the gate, with campaign progress to earn cash to buy ships and upgrades being far simpler and honestly far easier and more fun than this game's 'mission to unlock' system.Ship handling feels worse and kind of plasticky compared to the heavier, sturdier Redout's handling, if that makes sense.- SummaryThis game feels like it's better treated as a spinoff of Redout than its own game. Go play the first one and see how it compares to this one, and play the one you prefer. I'll play it because antigrav racing is a bit of a fixation of mine, but I will forever feel the desire for the tracks of this to have just been a massive map pack for Redout proper rather than an entire game.Overall, 5/10. Average, but it definitely feels like a downgrade from the original. Can't in good conscience recommend it over the first one, personally.

_childDocuments_.review: Very addicting special gem!It's not easy, and you will crash and die and be frustrated at first. The ships control differently than most games, other than turning the traditional way, you'll have to manage sideways shifting, pitch, rotation, boosting and ultra boosting.  But once you get over the initially steep learning curve you'll find a satisfying and chonky single player campaign that will see you grow your ship's performance and looks and teach you what you need to know, as you unlock tougher tracks and revisit old ones to complete challenges with your newly buffed ship.The game features a fun turbo system which, explained simply, allows you to always gain speed, at the cost of hp. The line between winning a race and exploding via overheating is thin, and exhilarating.Very addicting, deep just enough, it's fun to learn the many tracks and understand which upgrades, stats and ships are best for every track.Now to the  downside is very little online activity, though the main menu does state a ranked mode "coming soon" which will get players competing online, hopefully.Also some tracks can be visually confusing, with perhaps too many shiny lights and stuff going on in the background, which makes memorising the track a little bit tiring at times.This is a special, intense game for players looking to challenge their reflexes and track memory, until you feel like an unstoppable bullet zig zaging and boosting and drifting through crazy tracks at insane speeds. Very much reccomend for people who wanna go fast and like a good progression system not only in unlockables but also in player knowledge and skill.

_childDocuments_.review: Loved the first game, and am loving this one, too, though this one is really more of a whole new AG racing game than a sequel, so I'll just list the changes from the first and how I feel about them.The physics and handling feel a bit different. I wouldn't say it's any better or worse, but if you've played the first game a lot it might take a little while to get used to. Once you're used to it, it feels great.They changed the boost system from having a boost meter and it stopped you once it was empty. This game instead has a temperature gauge and once you fill that up continuing to boost starts to drain your health. I personally like the new system better because it adds more risk/reward to boosting. You can also set it up to automatically shut your boost off once you reach a certain percent of health if you don't like the added risk of blowing yourself up.They got rid of the active and passive powerups. The active powerups were replaced with just the hyperboost and instead of the passive powerups now you just unlock parts to upgrade your ships as you see fit. Losing the active powerups doesn't bother me because the hyperboost is the one I always used anyway, and I don't know if many people used the other ones much either because all of them used your boost meter so it didn't really make much sense to use any of the others that didn't make you go faster, and I like the upgrades instead of the passives because it lets you do more in tweaking your ship how you like.They got rid of the ship classes. Now each team just has one ship and you move up to higher class races by equipping the performance upgrades. This I like because now if you move back down to redo a lower class race later, instead of just getting downgrades across the board you can pick exactly how you downgrade to match the class rating, allowing you to maximize whichever stats you feel are most important.Instead of money, everything is unlocked as rewards from races. This is my least favorite change, simply due to the fact that ships are also unlocked this way. Unlocking more performance parts as rewards I'm fine with, but having the ships also unlocked this way mean I am almost done with the first class of races and still can't get the ship I want. This also leads to it taking awhile before you get any of the tanky ships, which kind of makes them obsolete as you have to get at least somewhat good at the game before you can use them, and their entire purpose is to help people who aren't so good survive a bit longer while they get the hang of the game.They added turn warnings. This is a great change because, due to going so fast and the turns being so twisty, there's a lot of times where you can't really see what's coming until it's too late. I saw someone point this out and say it indicates how the track designs are bad, but this issue existed in the first game and people who say it didn't have just played the game so much they have the tracks memorized and forget it's a thing. It kind of just happens with this type of game.I've seen people mention a few bugs on some tracks, I haven't experienced them personally but there are enough reports of it I believe they're there. Hopefully those get patched out soon, as that's the only really bad thing with the game.They've also added a new system when you ramp where you have to manually rotate your ship to land properly, and you get a little boost for landing perfectly, and get slowed down a bit if you land poorly. It's a cool mechanic, but also one more thing to worry about for those who don't like having a lot of different things to deal with.

_childDocuments_.review: Speed, blistering, eye-watering, unforgiving speed.  Redout II is by far the superior entry in the Redout series.  I'm going to go as far as to recommend you skip Redout and jump straight to the sequel and then perhaps revisit the original.Having played several hours of Redout, I am far more interested and engaged in Redout II for these reasons.  Redout II has a much more gradual learning curve.  Redout II has a comprehensive training course to help you learn the game and ALL the incredible intricacies of piloting a ship that goes well over 1500 kph.  Throw in improved graphics, better "story", and a slew of other advancements, this is a great game.To describe the game, it's one part F-Zero, one part Xtreme G, and of course, a healthy dose of Wipe Out but unlike XG and WO, no guns, just pure speed and maneuvering This is an excellent game for those who are missing the Anti-Grav racing games.  You have boost, super boost, boost pads, oh and to go even faster, you can combine them! You can't go wrong with a game that has so many incredible features, customizations, and alien tracks.  Grab it, you won't regret it.

_childDocuments_.review: There's an absolute gem here, but it's not quite there yet.The graphics and gamefeel are absolutely phenomenal amd the track layouts are super fun but currently there are a few glaring problems. It's early enough in release that I have no doubt this will be patched soon but as of now this feels like an early access. The difficulty curve is... Once these issues are ironed out I haven't even a shadow of a doubt that this game is going to be pure gold.Edit 2024: The major bug with respawns has now been fixed making the game far more playable, however over a year later and the game still feels incomplete. 3 of the main menu items are still marked as "coming soon". The AI rubber banding is pretty egregious and the game is still plagued with numerous bugs. Sadly the game still feels like an early access. I really REALLY want to love this game, but recommending it in the current state is still difficult.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, first anti-gravity racing game I've played since F-Zero GX. Gorgeous, very fast and very challenging, exactly what I was looking for.There is a lot more inertia than in the aformentioned game but the sensations are really great. It's different, but the sense of speed is crazy. It's also way more difficult than GX (apart from its speedrunning tricks).The ships' customization is a very nice touch and all the parts blend well with the different platforms.I'd have a minor complaint regarding optimization (especially micro-stuttering when you load a track for the 1st time) but apart from that, you should definitely give it a try if you fancy the genre and are looking for a challenge!
_childDocuments_.name: Redout 2

_childDocuments_.review: We don't get many good AG Racing games, let alone great ones.I think Redout 2 knocks it out of the park with its amazing sense of speed and tight controls.I remember getting into the first Redout quite skeptically, and even disliking the controls at first, but it was such a good game that it kept me playing. I eventually understood what an amazing game I had gotten into, and I embraced the challenge and how bad I was at it. It's such a solid game and there is so much great about the first entry that I understand why people inevitably compare it so critically with Redout 2.In my opinion, you have to treat Redout 2 like a completely new game, which is Redout at its core (let that not be mistaken), but is different enough for it to stand out.I have 4 hours so far on my account, but I have 4 more at a friend's before I bought the game for myself. It did take some time to get used to (even after sinking 50+ hours into Redout1) and honestly, for me, a 360 pad is the only way I can actually play this properly. But once you get it, it feels so amazing. If fans of the first Redout were calling it a cross between F-Zero & Wipeout, this one's a pinch more Wipeout - which means the controls are tighter, in the best way possible.I also love the tracks, and I love that they take it to a whole new level with the track design and track length, I like the branching paths, the new jump mechanics.I do think that the tutorial was definitely rushed and a missed opportunity to actually ease people in, and teach them how to play the game, just feels a bit half baked.I've also noticed some glitchyness with some boost pads, and clipping through the map (one time for me so far), but this is all stuff that can be fixed.Is the music a great as in Redout 1? I don't think so, but it also won't hinder an amazing AG Racing experience!People complaining about the speed challenge - don't worry about getting first immediately, keep playing, learning the tracks, enjoy, unlock upgrades, you'll get there eventually, and it will feel amazing mastering a track.Overall to me this game is significantly different from Redout 1, yes, and I will always love Redout 1, but Redout 2 is equally epic in its own right, and I am so hyped for it and for the DLC that is to come. I even ordered a new controller just for this game, cause my dusty 360 pad left shoulder button is no longer responsive.This game is at the very top with the best AG Racing games in existence. If you like AG Racing, just support the devs and let's get more Redout cause this game rocks!+ full disclaimer, I had no idea this game was coming and one day I wake up and a friend is telling me, hey, Redout 2 is out. I got the game on Gamer's Gate cause it was 16% off, and cause I know they're legit. But I got the Season Pass on Steam, and I don't buy games on launch these days.

_childDocuments_.review: It pains me to thumb down this game, because there's so much potential here, but as it stands, it's a complete mess.  It boils down to a combination of bad tracks plus completely screwed up in-air controls.  Every time there's a long jump whether you make it or not is entirely down to chance, and the tracks love having long jumps with gravity pulling in completely random directions.  The devs tried to band-aid over this with a really dumb "Prince of Persia: Sands of Time"-style rewind mechanic, which is itself disastrous in a racing game, because it's completely flow-ruining.  It's unfortunate that the flying controls are so screwed up and take the whole package down with them, because the on-track racing is amazing (and a strict upgrade from the first Redout), but as it stands, it's just a mess.

_childDocuments_.review: Redout 2 is my favorite game, a sequel to Redout which made me fall in love with the anti-gravity racer genre.The goal of the game is to get your ship through insanely twisted racetracks as fast as possible.You need to learn how to land the ship after it is thrown off the track into the air, how to use boosts without overheating, how to handle challenging turns, and so on.It's a challenging skill-based game.Since I like this sort of thing, I have never played on lower than the default - the game calls it "Redout" - difficulty, so I don't know how it is on lower difficulty settings.There are a lot of options to control and lower difficulty, that's all I'll say.I think the gameplay is Redout's strength - there are things to be said about the balance, new player experience, equipment, track design, music, lore, etc., but in the end, I find the racing experience incredibly satisfying.It's why I recommend this game.The game constantly has magical moments where you overcome the opponents at the last few hundred meters of the race, perform perfect landings, survive deadly turns - and the feel of speed is incredible. If you are the type of player who is compatible with what this game offers, I'm confident that this game will give you a lot of joy.Redout 2 is great at what it needs to be.It may require some patience, though - if you're not having the best time after an hour, give it a few more and chances are you'll start feeling a lot better about the game.You'll get used to ship handling, and unlock the game's best racetracks, ships, cosmetics, etc.The game has A LOT of it in the career mode - as of writing this review I've played for 30+ hours and I'm only like 50% done.The events in the career mode might get a bit repetitive - there are 36 race tracks (I won't count reverse versions of them - even though they do make the game more varied) - expect to race in each of them many times.I personally like this, because, hey, more Redout!And the more you play on the tracks, the more you start loving them.It's also a very rewarding career mode - each race rewards the player with ship skins, color palettes, equipment unlocks, and ship unlocks, so you keep getting something new.During the career mode, you are often racing against AI opponents.I have too little experience in this genre to say if AI is good or not, but I do enjoy races against AI opponents a lot, they are quite challenging - and I can't tell if AI is cheating in some way to achieve it, so kudos to the game for that.Because it's a very fast racing game, the satisfaction that comes from graphics is more about level geometry, rather than pretty backgrounds, HD textures, etc.There are many parts of the tracks that feel amazing to blaze through at 1000+ km/h, so I would say that this game has good graphics.They don't feel cheap or old, the game has a modern shine to it.Ranges from 'Okay' to 'LET'S GOOOOOOOO-'.If you like EDM, you're going to like Redout 2's music.Best tracks are reserved for boss races and it really takes them to the next level.Background for the ship manufacturers and tracks is delivered through short cutscenes after they are unlocked and through text descriptions.It sounds a bit silly at times, but it's still welcome.If you have played Redout, here's my opinion about Redout 2 when compared to the original:Everything in Redout 2 feels more intentional if that makes sense.Things that are better:- AI.- Ship-to-ship collisions.- Ship cosmetic customization.- Career mode and progression.Things that are different:- Ship handling.- Ship stat customization.Things that are worse:- Music.- Local splitscreen multiplayer is gone.There are several things that I'm not sure how to categorize. For example, I think I like colors in Redout 1 more, but I'm not sure why, so let's just leave it that.Overall, I think Redout 2 isn't better than Redout 1 in every field, but it is a vast improvement in those that are very important.If you're a fan of the original, you should get Redout 2 - it's a solid sequel.EDIT: 2022 Steam Awards. Redout 2 won't win, but it is my personal winner.

_childDocuments_.review: Its nice, controls are super tight compared to the previous game, and is very fluid and fast once you learn the tracks, the rally style symbols become moot once you learn and imo, do little to help as you start to play.Huge gripe with this game though, there was not really any proper playtesting with anyone outside the development team. Most of the career objectives are all over the place, either incredibly easy or ballbustingly hard (lowered the difficulty on a lot of the times in a patch, but qualification times are still ABSURD). This is a game made for the developers, playtested by the developers, and only truly fully understood and enjoyed by the developers. This comes from obnoxious campaign extra trophies expecting to break the basic rules of the game in strange ways, like fly in a track with no jumps, or do X ammount of perfect jumps in a track with not enough jumps, the things i would expect to find in some obscure youtube video that someone found out they could do in the game after hundreds of hours. To me its the equivalent of making exploits a part of the game, which is fun as easter eggs for rewards, but not to unlock game features.
_childDocuments_.name: Redout 2

_childDocuments_.review: This is a beautiful, exhilaratingly fast and challenging racer with a few baffling flaws in it's campaign and level design.Let's get the good out the way first. -The sense of speed is godly.-Track and ship designs are all beautiful and distinct with all of them feeling unique from one another, and there's an extensive customization system.-Control has been refined from Redout 1's extremely drifty ships that felt like they were on ice, to much tighter, grippier ships that can be learned to master each corner. (Along with the fact that you can better adjust controls natively).So in those respects RO2 is an improvement, but it's a rough gem. -Tracks are often more confusing to navigate with baffling jumps. (One jump has you have to navigate to 2 sideways roads where the road beneath you kills you immediately. And another gives you a surface beneath you to give you the feeling of jumping straight on, before lunching you sideways at a right-side-up track with sideways gravity affecting you in weird ways).-The campaign gives you a linear drip-feed of parts and upgrades per event. (For instance you absolutely KILL it in a race and do everything right, and for all your effort you'd win one new set of flaps for one ship, and maybe a new paint scheme you're passively ok with).-Difficulty is all over the place. There are several events that'll just be too hard on any difficulty other than chill and zero because the AI just has access to faster/better parts than you.-Trophies are all over the place and many feel like they were generated by an AI. (Trophies being secondary objectives each event has for more points/unlocks). I've had a trophy that told me to hit the most BS barely achievable qualifying time (Done through skipping sections of the track and pro-player help),  and a trophy that tells me to fly over a mile in a single jump...on a track that has no jumps and no space to jump too. Right after bending over backwards for that I'd have a trophy tell me to make at least 5 good easy-to-hit landings. On a track with 10 jumps. On a 3 lap race.-Also, the music seems a lot more generic, with a focus away from melodies to just samey beats.But, I stick through all of this because the gameplay is still top notch, and addicting.
_childDocuments_.name: Redout 2

_childDocuments_.review: I never liked racing games, always despised them - i thought they are stupid and with no essence to them. But..... this one is something different. The sense of speed is amazing, tracks are technically challenging at times but overall controls feel very good. There is assist options if you don't want to deal with some elements (like pitch). There are a lot of maps to play around - i played mostly on Arcade mode. Deep career option with events and numerous customization options. A lot of different race ships to choose from - possibility to paint them so you are looking good while kickin ass, soundtrack is good, graphics look solid, no stuttering or lag experienced using 5800X3D with 3070.Overall pros:- variety of race ships to choose from- possibility to customize every ship- career mode with increasing difficulty level- a lot of tracks and their design- doing > Mach 2 - assists if you are casual gamerCons (very subjective):- fun to learn, extremely hard to master- i know you are supposed not to hit barriers but sometimes, they would help being there- you need to ride track a few times to memorize it- strafing & steering might be disorienting at firstOverall i can only recommend this game. Served me a few hours of really high octane entertainment. Me with little to no experience in racing games have fun using just slight assist options so i think this game would fit even racing game newbies. Great game design, soundtrack and ships. Gotta buy it for full price, it is worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely takes me back to the days of F-Zero or Extreme-G.  If you like fast-paced racing games, this is for you.There's a lot of room for skill expression in this game. It takes a while to get a good feel for the controls, especially steering/strafing.  I've read reviews talking about the difficulty, taking the top spot in some of the career challenges (not the races) can be very difficult.  The best recommendation I have is to just keep moving forward, don't worry about getting 1st place or top tier or max completion on every event in order - that's not what the game is designed for.  You'll unlock cars and parts that you can use in different combinations to come back and clear those for the sake of completion.All in all, once you get the hang of it, it's an absolute blast.  I highly recommend it to anyone that enjoys fast-paced racing games.

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun and addicting racing game,the visuals are very pleasing and the game is basically bug free. Well done!I would not touch normal racing games but this one has jumps, boost, boost pads and hyperboost and also requires a lot of skill and concentration which is very gripping!The high number of tracks (72) provides high variety and the feeling of "exploration" will hopefully continue for some more time.*)I can't understand the criticism of some other people for the difficulty level. Yes on time attack I rarely make 1st place, but that is ok - where else would be the challenge? And for races vs AI pilots you can always adjust the difficulty to an appropriate level.I think the funnest thing in this racer are the ridiculous jumps, you can do all kinds of daring stuff while in the air. Drifting and boosting is so much fun. Soundtrack is also great, I love the sound track of the mining complex.Multiplayer works well, no lag at all and it's fun, but it can be hard to find players. It's better to start MP with friends because then you can also choose the tracks (only the HOST can and it is random if you get to be host in regular MP). You CAN select your own gliders, but the option is fairly hidden in the MP garage.The play SP and wait for MP feature is not well implemented, unfortunately - because the SP progress is lost when you get pulled into MP. 90 hours in and still having a lot of fun :DEDIT: *): 40 game hours in and there are still amazing new tracks coming! 72 tracks apparently is really a lot of tracks!EDIT 2: I missed that you can indeed select your gliders in multiplayer, because the "Y" button to show your own gliders in the multiplayer garage is fairly hiddedn in the UI.

I do like however you can now play them in reverse. The speed trials are also horrible!Overall its a great sequel and hope the DLCs add more variety down the line. _childDocuments_.review: Stunning visuals, lovely music and yes, terrifying track design. Redout 2 takes the ethos of the later Redout 1 tracks and naturally bumps them up even more, which is an excellent choice. The usual caveats with Redout apply - the learning curve is more of a cliff. _childDocuments_.name: Redout 2

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately, at the moment (about a week after launch) I can't recommend Redout 2. I think it will be better later, and look forward to improvements and adjustments from the development team.My Issues:- Unforgiving difficulty. This may be a pro to some, but as it stands, the game expects far too much from you too soon. It is tuned for experienced players looking to be challenged right from the start. Simple mistakes even on the easier difficulties penalize the player too harshly due to the very powerful AI rubber-banding. And the difficulty is attached solely to the AI behavior, so any solo events (time trial and Speed) are as hard on the top difficulty as they are on "Chill" and "Zero". The Assists that the game expects you to use as a Beginner only help so much. Even touching a wall will often result in failure on those events.- Unlocking events and additional ships, with often significantly different characteristics is harshly gated: The community has said that the campaign is very doable with the beginning ship, but this depends on my first point. If your particular playing style is anything less than flawless, you will struggle to land even one star on some events until you really focus and get far better at the game. Any desire to change to a different ship is simply not possible.- Progression: The campaign expects you to repeatedly go backward when you have additional parts and that will hopefully allow you to pass previous events more decisively, but it will only take you so far because the events themselves are locked into particular performance ranges. This requires constant tweaking of components to get a ship back into range, which you then have to reset when you go back to higher tier events that expect you to have the better parts installed. This is cumbersome with the UI at times.The tracks are a mix. They're incredibly fast feeling, which is what you want in this type of game, many of them are quite beautiful, and truly fun to race on. It has a neon punch to the face feel that is everything I want in an anti-grav racing game. Some of them are a bit punishing on the heat load, considering the game expect you to use boost the overwhelming majority of the time, while managing overheating/health. Again, mistakes like hitting a wall are truly punishing due to this aspect. But they are really, really fun track layouts. The jumps are...less fun. Some of them are very clearly marked, and you end up loving those, some are around blind corners and you end up dreading those, and the worst ones have very poor indication of where you're expected to land without memorizing each course fully. Expect to crash on them all the time and learn to use the rewind feature.The standouts:- The level of control you have if you want it: It can be a little overwhelming at first, but having the full authority over the flight of your ship is extremely satisfying. Pitch down slopes, pitch up hills, control your flight across jumps. All of it feels great, as long as you can keep up with all of those aspects at once. I can't, but the flight assists work very nicely. - The speed: With a computer that can handle it, this game feels insanely fast. Scenery blurs past you, your focus narrows to the track, and when you are going at the top speed you can, it feels wonderfully real.- Customization: There's a lot of customization available in the campaign, you just have to unlock it all, which goes back to some of my issues, but this one is minor. The aesthetic parts *should* feel like a reward for being good, and they are.- Bit of a minor one, but I really like the tidbits of lore. I just wish it was stored somewhere to read later.

_childDocuments_.review: Redout 2 is an amazing sequel with major improvements on handling, difficulty curve, story telling and builds greatly on the first game. _childDocuments_.name: Redout 2

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: As of my most recent play session, they've fixed the accessibility options applying correctly, and that alone improved my play experience enough for me to *easily* recommend it. The difficulty of the game is still extremely punishing, but now more in line with games like Monster Hunter or Dark Souls- It's not a matter of the game having done something arbitrary or unfair- When I lose places, it's because I touched a wall, not because my craft wasn't pulling the way I needed it to. It's a hard game, but A-G Racers rarely feel better.OLD REVIEW (Pre DLC, near launch): Cannot recommend at this time. Accessibility options are badly bugged, meaning in some levels you're dropped in with no AI assist if you have/need it, goals are rarely fair feeling, weather conditions can sometimes blatantly and fully obscure the upcoming track, and the game feels very openly hostile to non-lifetime AG Race fans. Avoid until patches occur, and even past that, only pick up if you're looking for something excessively challenging.Positively, however, the feeling of speed is unparalleled. When things are going well, and options you need work, the game is a technicolor kaliedoscope of speed. The controls are well defined and well tuned, the ships simply feel like a greased puck on ice when you have no AI assist, and the initial curve of difficulty is very high.
_childDocuments_.name: Redout 2

_childDocuments_.review: The good: Fundamental race changes (removing passive/active abilities) are great, I like the "pure" race experience more than the customized loadouts of Redout 1. This alone pretty much carries the game for me.The neutral: Ship unlocks and upgrades being locked to career (which is most of what I play anyway) means unlocks feel much slower than Redout 1's. Controls are pretty busy on controller, it's kinda trying to be a three-stick game with roll controls being bound to D-pad by default (I moved mine to face buttons but that just changes which thumb has to pull double duty, tried shoulder buttons but that moves other more universal controls like boost etc. away from the index fingers).The bad: Jump penalties feel over-zealous (playing badly seems to trigger a system intended to make you play the track mostly as intended). Texture pop has some 2010 vibes to it. A lot of features feel like they're missing (or in progress), particularly for multiplayer (no boss races, which are one of the main draws for me and some friends in multiplayer).
_childDocuments_.name: Redout 2

_childDocuments_.review: Just like first Redout, it is a great game. It is building on its predecessors driving model, evolving it and adding many improvements.Things I like:  - Rally like turn signs, so you are not completely lost on new tracks, that you didn't race on before.- The new boosting system, which is more flexible than old one, so you get to play with it more and it keeps you on the edge the whole time as you constantly balance speed vs health.- You can stack Hyperboost with normal boost, with boost gate, with landing bonus (yeah, pretty awesome:))- Rewind, so you don't have to restart the whole race, when you make one mistake.- Perfect landing boost is very satisfying and adds another thing to master.- The diffculty options, now range from very easy to very hard.- Collisions with other ships now feel better as well, so you don't get turned around randomly.- You can actually explode right before finish line and still finish the race, if the wreck makes it past the finish line, so you can go pedal to the metal right to the end:)- Speed event isn't binary anymore, you just have a baseline speed, where you start to get points and the faster you go, the faster you get the points. Honestly pretty great merge of Speed and Score events from the first Redout.- Tutorials are nice.- Completely rebindable controls.- Sound effects are more snappy and easier to hear.- tracks with different conditions like low gravity, higher heat, ...Things I don't like (nothing major though):- The very first race seems to have rubber banding, so you get more fun ending, but you know that ruberbanding is never a good thing.- You cannot turn off assists in first tutorials and first race. Honestly I found them annoying, making the ship feel heavy and slugish (maybe some assist tweak for this part?).- Landing grade text comes very late sometimes, when something else is shown instead.- There are no personal bests shown in Career events, so I cannot compare different ship or ingame path results to optimise my run.- Soundtrack is a bit too laid back especially on very first tracks (maybe little volume tweak?).- With controller, there is just too much going on. Default layout is as good as it could be, but there are some compromises, which didn't have to be made on keyboard. Adding option to throttle always on, would free up one finger that is always on trigger otherwise.Few minor bugs:- - EDIT: Both bugs seem to be fixed in 1.1.0All in all, a lot of pretty sweet improvements and only minor annoyances for me, that can be easily fixed.I was sceptical about how they can manage to improve over first one, but honestly, I was blown away, how much more well thought out and executed is stuff in Redout 2.
_childDocuments_.name: Redout 2

_childDocuments_.review: Redout 2's announcment was unexpected, the first trailer hyped me up totally. New tracks, new ship designs, famous artists mixing the soundtrack, music algorithms... I couldn't wait to get my hands on the game. Bought on lauchday, in the first minute. So how's the game? Well...sad to say...but it has problems and flaws...and bugs...and glitches. I like, is the totally redesigned ships, and the new manufacturers. The tracks and the enviroment are astounding. But the good things end here. As a Redout 1 veteran, I've found the game very hard. The new Speed mode is bad, unbeatable and pointless. Time attack races offer only 1 lap. You need to restart the race every time you pass the finish line. There is a Boss and a normal Race mode, which are the same as in the prequel, these are enjoyable. The first game has AWESOME music - perfectly fitted for every location - I loved it so much, I even learnt a few them to play on guitar. They said in the trailer, there will be 'legendary artist', yes, I recognise their style, but somehow the music seems repetetive, boring, not so unique.The ship handling is awful. I get it, you have modules, and you can make loadouts for your playstyle, still the vehicle handling feels sluggish and wonky. Lastly. the 'turbo stacking'. Yes, almost all player were using the turbo boost, and the implemented in this game as a standard ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. You need to use it as often as effective as you can, or the game punishes you - meaning - the unbeatable times. Well, I'm quite disappointed with game so far. (Also..I'm stuck after the B league, I don't have enough stars to progress. Great! ) For the price, maybe it's worth it...but if you a casual AG racer, you'll have a hard time progressing through the game. And absolutely can't reccomend to people who are new to anti-gravity racing.DON'T BUY IT                      yet!
_childDocuments_.name: Redout 2

_childDocuments_.review: Absurdly fast and extremely challenging. The highly anticipated sequel excels at its sense of speed, but don't be fooled by the colorful, vibrant environments and wealth of assist options. Redout 2 lives up as a sequel to the original Redout, tightening the gameplay controls and going all out on the boost management and track memorization.If you're looking for a casual experience, the difficulty options have you covered for a few early races in the singleplayer mode; but with vehicles this fast, there is a very high skill ceiling to be reached to beat the time trials, speed events, career, and most of all, online multiplayer. Coupled with even crazier track designs, surviving a race is feels even more of a feat now than before, and the new rewind mechanic makes those costly slight mistakes much less punishing.While I find a number of things to be desired (multiplayer boss, boss time attack leaderboards, lobby system, in-game chat) I find the fundamentals of the racing mechanics and sense of speed for this title more than exceeded my expectations.You better go play it!( Be sure to check out the Discord community at  )

_childDocuments_.review: Fun, challenging, cathartic gameplay for a reasonable price. Seems like the sort of game Ubisoft would charge £60 for.That being said - the rubber-banding from the AI racers is a bit unbalanced at the moment. Even with a flawless race and a huge lead they can just end up speeding past you towards the end, unless you're boosting constantly.
_childDocuments_.name: Redout 2

_childDocuments_.review: Yes! That's it! That's the sequel we've been waiting for and it's SO GOOD!The sense of speed is still as good as ever, the soundtrack, albeit no longer as original as in the previous game, is still incredibly fun and fitting, the visuals are insane and the new game mechanics at hand really challenge you to master a track! It's fun, it's raw, it's unhinged, it's quite simply great!There are some downsides, mainly the fact that progression seems a bit slow and albeit the customization options are plenty and the vehicles are super fun and unique, it will take you quite some time to unlock them one by one. I would've preferred a money system like in the previous game so you can choose which car you want to unlock. Same goes for cosmetics like ... paintjobs. I really don't think these needed to be gated behind progression, same with the visual upgrades.Another thing I gotta get used to is the difficulty curve. While races are... manageable, time races or speed tests seem incredibly difficult to master and may or may not  require you to come back to them with an upgraded car. I think the first game handled the progression a lot better since you were able to do everything when you first encountered it.The positives, though? My where do I start. It's still the best AG racer out there, the track design is phenomenal and as unique as ever, the cars look and feel really good and the visual style pays homage to the original voxel style. The new upgrade  and customization systems are fun, and I also really like the cutscenes and "lore" we get, even if it's mostly just for flavor. I was worried the sense of speed would be lower or that the music collection would sound too... "generic" , but no. It still very much feels like Redout 1 and for that I love this game.I haven't played Redout Space Assault, but I'm glad you guys gave this gem a sequel. The original one was quite frankly a masterpiece and this one is a worthy follower.Update: The difficulty disparity has been fixed and the difficulty curve is a LOT better now
_childDocuments_.name: Redout 2

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR : This game is great! With very few bugs and great performance "out of the box"the Pros :The gameplay is what matters the most and the manoeuvring feels so smooth. Tracks are well thought out. They give a fair challenge and now with the addition of branching paths with some really hyped moments (little spoiler Cloud Ocean : Mistral has the most insane/epic branching path I've experienced so far). I like how they've implemented the Boss Tracks this time around. No more Portal gates that you can't see on the other side.You can boost on command as much as you're willing to sacrifice ship integrity (I main Asera's ship which is boost hungry) and since i'm finding myself hitting less walls that I used to in my humble beginnings in RedOut, I really like this addition. You can stack your boost on top of your Hyper boost on top of a track boost which is absolutely nuts.The new Visuals are so gorgeous and stay true to the visual identity from the first game while having a more high-fi look.I liked the soundtrack of the first game and find this one good also. I really like that it react to what's happening on screen and enhance your experience (and how it will start playing super soft if you're lowering the difficulty mid-game lol)I used to think that the feeling of speed was lacking a bit compared to the first one but now that I made it to B class, I can assure you that it gets fast AF.To the more negative notes :The Speed Challenges feel so over-tuned for what a casual gamer like me can achieve in the B Class career and with the ship I like to play. In A Class, I've finally unlocked the Conqueror ship which now enables me to get results "more easily" but I'd rather be able to compete with my Asera. In B class I just ended up skipping every speed challenge as they felt like a waste of my time since I could just never get even Bronze.I see where the complaints from the tutorials comes from. It is in fact pretty bad when you want to take a corner a certain way and the only way to get over the time-slow is to input what the game wants you to. Even if it means you scraping the wall along the way. It is quite short though and doing them all gives you a few liveries and the last one gives you a very nice upgrade for late B class/ Early A class.The driving assists feel off to me but I was happy to see that it wasn't very long before you could just deactivate them. The game tries to find a setting suited for you after your first race and if you're already well versed in these types of games, you'll probably find the tuning at or near 0 in most settings. I've come to appreciate the boost safety feature as recommended in another Steam review. Final thoughts :I've played enough of the game to see what it's trying to give as an experience and i'm loving it more and more. I think that it is a really good game that will only get better with a few balancing passes and the usual sneeky bug squashing. Also make yourself a favor and use the Conqueror for Speed Challenges

_childDocuments_.review: This game is actually sick. In my first couple of races I was like "Wow this is so fast!" ...and then I learned how to strafe drift, and use the hull HP as a resource, feather the boost heat, time the hyper boost cooldown just as hull fully recharges, get perfect landings, etc. ...now I'm starting to understand how fast this game can really get. This has been fixed

_childDocuments_.review: A flawed launch, frustrating  difficulty curve and missing QOL features still leave me satisfied, my eyes bleeding and my brain in Adderall mode. It's good, just not quite great.A lot of negative reviews seem to be people expecting to jump into this after RO1 and mop the floor. That's not going to happen.Tutorial sets you against AI whose ships are faster than yours and it's largely a lesson in keeping your cool. It is, however, way to hard and neither teaches you important nuance/skills nor makes you feel good. If not, then at least explain that the competitors have better ships and you need to upgrade your own to get those first places. There is honestly a huge narrative element lost there. But ♥♥♥♥, this is still fun and fast and gorgeous. I'm stoked for a VR mode.
