_childDocuments_.review: I really want to keep this short.I will recommend Redout II, but I am not going to recommend it over the first one, Pacer, or BallisticNG. If you want a good AG racer, get the first Redout.This game is just beautiful and very colorful. It will dazzle you with eye candy. But compared to the first, the experience feels overall hollow. The campaign is no where as deep. If that matters to you...avoid this one.But it is still a good solid AG racer. If you like the racing side of AG racers, and don't need the combat....this is not a bad choice.
_childDocuments_.name: Redout 2

_childDocuments_.review: Literally learning to dance on the edge of Speed and SELF ANNIHILATION!!!Every environment is an amazingly vibrant and lovely dance to learn!Unlike their first game, the boost power is always in your hands! I felt that it was overly restrictive and was longing for extended boost, But here Not only do you have Extreme boost, but also DOUBLE boost, Hell yus!The customizing adds nothing to gameplay(Thank goodness), and A missed opportunity because a lot of it is just a reused and doesn't even look good {Just added cuz it's an already made part.Would have been cool to actual body mods and making an actual different look.O was longing for the deep turns and dexterity of the last games tracks, But it got solved when I got to Neo Tokyo I believe it is. It's literally my favorite Scene because of it. (And I somehow can't remember its actual name...) Might edit that. Oh my final fault with this game was that I wish it had a Recovery strip thing like Extreme-G. Just a little, to reward those who are "Doin it Right" Give some more speed or pull away potential. but it doesn't call for it especially when you are doing it right and Hyperspeeding at almost all times.Anyways. Beautiful and fast F-Zero like.My only gripe with this game is that, the sound for activating regular thrust sounds like an air unit turning on. (When you hear a unit cutting on from outside) It's very lackluster and non-unique. I wish people got wilder with game design sounds, especially when the vehicles or magic is not realistic anyway. Look at kirbys sound design. It's frequently called the best for a reason.
_childDocuments_.name: Redout 2

_childDocuments_.review: I want to keep it short and sweet seeing as there's plenty of reviews that say the same or similar things:Pros:Similar to Redout 1 but with enhanced visuals, music, graphics and more choices with maps, customization and vehicles. Some attempts to push boundaries further than with redout 1 but its more of the same with more polish to it. Sound track is full of absolute slappers. Cons:Jump Designs-I doubted this being that much of an issue when reading reviews before buying but this is a serious issue with the game. Being able to push 2k Mph and maintain certain flow states is amazing but the way some of the native tracks have their jumps designed is atrocious. I thought it might just be people not getting passed some skill gap but there are maps where these jumps and hazards flat out make no sense, esp when you're hitting the jumps damn near perfectly only to find out the landing is almost 45 degrees off axis and now have to do a physics mini game that will at best keep you on the track and at worst remove you from competing in the race entirely. I got the game on discount. Would not recommend buying at full price.
_childDocuments_.name: Redout 2

_childDocuments_.review: At first I was very frustrated with this game because the controls felt weird and I was crashing on the walls on every turn. But I honestly enjoyed many aspects of the game, like the visuals, the ships and the sense of speed which is phenomenal. I started to enjoy the game a lot more when I turned off assist completely and I could fully control my vehicle. After that the game has been a total joy. Hitting those perfect landings is super satisfying and going over 2km/hour is spectacular. I would say this game is difficult but not that difficult as to keep casual players from enjoying it, it just had a rocky start for me, but as time progressed I definitely think this is a great game.
_childDocuments_.name: Redout 2

_childDocuments_.review: I went into this expecting a bitterly challenging, blinding fast racing game and Redout 2 did not disappoint. It's one of those games that pushes you to the limit trying to master it. I really like the time rewind ability, since it lets me see exactly what I did wrong and experiment with different approaches to the more challenging sections.With that said, not all the things that make the game challenging are necessarily positive. The aerial controls are difficult to handle even after 80 hours of practice, and not just because they're slippery. By default, the game wants you to use the D-pad to control your orientation in the air, which requires temporarily leaving the left analogue stick while you rotate your ship. Thankfully, I have macros on the underside of my controller and was able to use those instead, but without them, I'm not sure I'd consider playing the game at all. As it stands, I still struggle with this aspect of the game in a "there's only so much I can do with my hands at once" sort of way.The game also seems to have very high expectations of you, especially on the later time attacks. I know that kind of sounds like "the game's too hard" but that's not...exactly it? I've played a few of these tracks dozens of times, often consecutively. I've got a good loadout for the track, I'm racing well, but I'm consistently getting ~2:09 and the game wants 1:58 somehow. I am genuinely unsure how to shave off those extra eleven seconds. I'm not saying that out of frustration either, I signed up for having to try things over and over again until I get it. I mean I legitimately do not know how to improve.
_childDocuments_.name: Redout 2

_childDocuments_.review: High Skill Ceiling; Fast-Paced; Kick-Ass Soundtrack.Exceptionally satisfying to get good at even against AI racers. My only gripe would be it'll take a while to get to the point where your campaign vehicle matches the performance of the ones provided by Arcade mode. If you want to race against friends, just make sure you're all in agreement on performance score limits.
_childDocuments_.name: Redout 2

_childDocuments_.review: Anti Grav racers have always been on the back burner for me, but picking up Ballistic NG and the Redout Series (Redout 2 is superior over 1 just saying) has been a blessing in disguise. 1. This game has an insane skill gap, but ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ is it a blast once you put some time in and learn the mechanics.2. Career mode is long and grindy but not terribly hard compared to what older reviews say prior to updates(That is where all my hours are sunk into so far and I am maybe half way?). Some refinement on progression would be beneficial (One area Redout 1 was better) but overall is a great experience.3. Visuals are top notch, this game deserves much more recognition but sadly lack of dev support and content and just the niche Anti Grav racer community in general hurts it.All in all, really hoping for some much needed future updates, and hope we can get either a closure to this game with final content, or a new entry beyond that'll be more complete. Still a positive for me as this game is fun as hell.
_childDocuments_.name: Redout 2

_childDocuments_.review: Overall really like this game as someone who played a lot of anti-grav and high-speed racers, but it's not without its problems.The biggest one I find is the flying, because the first couple of times on any track it can be exceptionally difficult to determine where the game wants you to go and you will inevitably blow your ship up either hitting the terrain or trying to land on the wrong portion of the track. There have also been situations I've seen where it appears I'm going to land correctly and instead fall through and blow up. The rewind feature is nice in those situations, but the game also likes to add limitations on when you can use it. It doesn't feel so much that the game expects you to already know the tracks, but it damn well expects you to learn them QUICK.Other than that the game is gorgeous. The strafing and pitching system is so cool, it makes you feel like you're actually piloting these things rather than just driving it. It necessitates the use of a controller which may be a negative in some eyes.Price point is a little steep for what you get, but some hardcore racers may not mind that. Definitely worth picking up during a sale I think.
_childDocuments_.name: Redout 2

_childDocuments_.review: This game, as its predecessor, is a MASTERPIECE. As a fan of the Fzero and Wipeout series, I have to admit I had high expectation for the Redout games, and I was not disappointed! The game is challenging to say the least, soundtrack is amazing and there is even a lore behind the game that can satisfy science fiction enthusiasts!Although I wish we had some weapons to shoot or mess with other racers, Redout 2 (as the previous game) remains a must-have for every AG racing fan, old and new!
_childDocuments_.name: Redout 2

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best racing games on the market, AG or no. If you haven't played, you're missing out.First of all, it's fast. I'm not a huge racer, but when I do race, I want to go fast. Redout 2 scratches that itch like nothing else I've ever touched. The original, while very technical and fun, always felt like I was getting funny readings from my speedometer. Redout 2? On a fast track, with a fast ship, when you hyperboost down one of the straights you're actually going fast.Regarding difficulty: Yes, it is a hard game. It is a bit strange that some events like Speed or the qualification times don't scale. Some of the 4* events are insane (more on that later). However, I've found that every time I put my head down, tweak my ship build, and race again - it's winnable. Progression is rarely gated to perfecting single races - plenty of them genuinely need parts found later to 4*. You can just grind through and get to the next rank then come back later - it makes no difference even if you're achievement hunting. Just takes some patience.The trophies are in some cases annoying. That said, I've ticked them off one by one and there's plenty of proof out there of them being achievable legitimately. Whether or not you want to try and nail a 2km jump off the edge of the track out of a hairpin... I get it if that sounds annoying. It is. But it's so satisfying to nail them.Honestly, my only gripe besides the stutters (seemingly not hardware dependent - I've tried on several rigs) is the music. I can't remember a single track from this game offhand and I still regularly hum the original game's soundtrack to myself. It's good, and it matches the pace well, keeps up the energy, it just doesn't crawl in your brain and stay there like the first games'. Maybe that's a plus if music gets stuck in your head easily, but I do miss the music. Everything else is leagues ahead of the first game and I would consider this a better jumping in point for new players.
_childDocuments_.name: Redout 2

_childDocuments_.review: A true love letter to anti gravity racing, old school full game with DLCs that only add more fun and beautiful tracks. This and Redout (the first game) are a must have for any racing lover. Colors, biomes, sound tracks, ship designs...everything in this game is at the highest level you could imagine.
_childDocuments_.name: Redout 2

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun game, though the controls do require some getting used to. While steering is a lot easier compared to Redout 1, strafing is now also a thing. Besides that, at several areas on many tracks you'll have to fly over gaps, which now also involve rolling, pitching and yawing to the correct area.Don't be afraid to enable some assists to a certain point, the game is definitely worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Redout 2

_childDocuments_.review: I don't often write reviews, but this, this game deserves one.Redout 2 has found it's place in my heart as one of the few recent gaming experiences that actually makes me Genuinely happy to play.For some reason, it supercharges my long lost childhood sense of wonder to race around at 800+ mph through radical locations and blasting that kick-ass soundtrack till my ears bleed.It gives off a "chuck-e cheese arcade racer" vibe, in the best way possible, the kind of game you'd spend ALL of your tokens on cause it was THAT. FUN.The locations in the game are gorgeous, ranging from the Mariana Trench on Earth itself, Tartarus Mines on IO, or even within a field of wreckage just outside of a Black Hole.It's the small things in these levels that really get me, Racing through mars and part of the track goes through water, "WHOA! THERE'S WATER ON MARS?!" Speeding around in the Mariana Trench seeing Beautiful colors and wrecked ships on the seafloor, and being terrified of the ocean the whole time.Blazing around a black hole and having the colors shift is absolutely psychedelic, and the strong gravitational pull of the Black hole pulling your Racer around while you're in the air is freaky.Surfing through the Cloud Ocean and looking down is sick, and the track itself has some really awesome design, since it's all just floating in the sky.Zipping around in the Tartarus Mines is an unforgettable experience, the music gives off such a perfect "Industrial Danger" vibe, and all the machinery and lava everywhere are cool as all hell to look at.The music in this game is something special too, the custom tracks in the game are 1:1 perfect fits to their respective areas. almost as if the music was made first, and then zones and tracks to go with it.Redout 2, I love you, and thank you, for rekindling my childhood sense of wonder, and for a game that makes me happy.and if anti-gravity racing ever becomes real while i'm alive, i'm quitting my job, and camping out to be first in line <3
_childDocuments_.name: Redout 2

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: Ships look way nicer than in R1 (although they still change color based on the track's reflection, just...why)No weaponsUnlocking mods by winning feels more rewarding than just buying them with the money gained from races like in R1Trading your ship's integrity for more boost makes you feel always on the edgeThe possibility to customize an assistant for every single driving aspect is a nice touchThe rewind option (contrary to my purist beliefs) is actually useful, but I feel it was implemented due to the absurd difficulty that is gap clearing (more below)ConsBland music compared to R1, muted after a couple of hoursThe jump perception is awful, most of the times you think you have cleared the gap just to discover you are falling through the pavement. In addition adjusting direction and orientation while mid-jump is frustrating and counterintuitive, and who the hell thought that implementing non-straight jumps when you are going this fast was a good idea??Unlocking new ships is a loooong process: 12 hours in, I've gotten only four.Career mode makes you race the same tracks over and over, that's a way to bloat the gametimeThe tutorial is fragmented to the point that they'll give you useful information when you have already figured it outTracks are very confusing most of the times, due to narrow turns and lighting.Finally, : race tracks feel all the same.No matter the environment, you'll always have the perception of doing the same kind of loops and turns, with an overall feeling of racing inside a mix of a giant pinball machine and the Mario Kart Rainbow Road. No matter the background, it will never actually blend with the actual track you are racing on. I reinstalled R1 because I remembered it not having this problem and man, couldn't have been more right, the comparison is embarassing, it's so much better.I might play it more because ultimately I like fast arcade racing games, but this issue makes my enjoyment of R2 way too low to reccomend it. Get the first one with all the DLCs instead.
_childDocuments_.name: Redout 2

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good racing game that is nothing like Fzero. Sure everything happens in the blink of an eye, you feel the breakneck speed, and you have to stare with such intensity you can't even look at your hud.Sure its exhilarating and takes advantage of modern hardware and high FPS that Fzero fans have desperately wanted forever.BUT WHERE ARE THE SICK F***ING HEAVY METAL LICKS?How am I supposed to get my Fzero fix if there isn't a cranked up guitar righteously shredding that s***? There's not nearly enough. What am I supposed to do? 0/10
_childDocuments_.name: Redout 2

_childDocuments_.review: This game feels severely undercooked, even still.the visual ugprade is welcome, the sound design is still good and the keybinds being configurable is great. I'm in support of the removal of pointless "combat"-perks as well... but... too much changed in the wrong direction.Air control feels . The vehicles change direction like bricks. Even Redout:EH's League 1 ships feel more alive, more agile and more fun to maneuver than these bricks - probably atleast partially due to the way the game handles keyboard inputs now.The titular feature seems  important than in RedOut one.Pitch control basically only matter where the game gives rally style pace notes to 100% signpost it. Even then, ground contact seems almost nonexistant. Impact feels minimal.Ships take ages to unlock, since they're hardlocked behind campaign progress instead of a flexible credit/money system. You're forced into a single ship for like 10 races, before unlocking the second one.There is also no speed league system - just a nonspecific upgrade pool, where any ship can stack upgrades into any 'skill'-category.The ship type or 'brand' just changes the minutiae of the pre-upgrade starting values, as opposed to the core characteristics, but presumably, you can blow out the upgrade budget to make any vehicle to perform like any other...It's a progression system where a flat, fixed car selection pool or open credit store for vehicles would've genuinly been better (see BallisticNG or RO1).Equally, old racing tracks make a comeback, but their race design has changed critically - with almost none of the previous prime setpieces having the same impact.Track design in general is pretty mixed. Some tracks are ace, but some are just downright crap. If I'm shouting "oh fuck off" at every blind jump, every sidewall-less corner, then something in the player teaching & signposting is not right. The fact that this game needed rally style pace notes to begin with is kind of a clue...The track QC is dodgy as well. I barely played 5 hours and have already - clipped through the floor of a track , broken through a sidewall instead of wall bouncing once, and also clipped through the landing of a jump. I'm also not certain if the AI doesn't cheat like hell sometimes. They can be seen barreling past you at mach 2 even while you're coming of a boostpad under active turbo - only to  slow down 50m ahead of you.Give this some more time - assuming developement is still happening - or just play RedOut: Enhanced Edition instead.I certainly need more time get warm with this - but the 5-hour-impression is poor.
_childDocuments_.name: Redout 2

_childDocuments_.review: This is the first time, I write a review, I just want to boost the reviews for this game, because I think it is criminally underrated and I want more anty grav racing games. You know the Anime Redline? I kinda feel like, I'm part of it, if I'm playing this game, especially if I hyperbosst and my ship is faster than 2000kmph and I'm close to exploding. That feeling is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ awesome. (sometimes I got goosebumps from it) I absolutely adore this game. It is not for everyone, yes it is hard, but it gets easier, if you get faster in later leagues. There are also a lot of costumizable assist options, if you want that. The only negative thing for me is that the campaign gets kinda repetetive at times but besides that, it is propably my favourite game alongside Elden Ring out of 2022. Also the difficulty (like in soulsgames) lets you actually be proud of yourself, if you get a close victory. (wich happens a lot) If you like Wipeout or F-Zero, I think this game is for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Redout 2

_childDocuments_.review: I liked Redout 1. A lot. I was absolute ♥♥♥♥ at it, but I loved it. My favorite racing game.REDOUT 2 THO. THIS ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ GAME MADE ME UNDERSTAND HOW TO DRIVE. AND OH BOI. LET ME TELL YOU. IT'S BEEN SO LONG SINCE A GAME HAS MADE ME SCREAM IN EXCITEMENT FROM WINNING. You CANNOT UNDERSTAND how ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ HYPE IT IS to PERFECTLY STRAFE THROUGH 4 CORNERS, seeing a jump incoming... PUSHING THE BUTTON OF BOTH YOUR THRUSTERS, JUMPING THROUGH THE AIR AT 1500KMPH. The music stops (it actually does because dynamic music is a hell of a drug). For 2 seconds, you are piloting a multi-ton metal beast capable of taming gravity... while still being at the mercy of it. And just a fraction of a second later...Impact. Perfect landing. A banging Drum & Bass music drop sounds as soon as you touch the ground. Your 3 adversaries are now behind you. Pull the thrusters to the max, MAKE IT TO THE FINISH LINE WHILE THE MUSIC IS BANGING. THERE ARE, SO, MANY, MOMENTS like this in this game. It absolutely and most certainly sells you the fantasy of being in a mach 1 race for the ages. It is the best racing game i have ever played and it makes me jump from my seat and say HELL YEAH and i dont remember many games in the last 20 years doing that from me. I love it with all my heart and it is a crime to see the reception it has gotten. I stayed out of it because of that same recepcion. But im here to fix my mistakes. BUY THIS GAME. FOR ♥♥♥♥ SAKE!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Redout 2

_childDocuments_.review: F-zero. But the track twists beyond comprehension and the ships are customizable.ungodly good handling model. Cool tracks. Banger soundtrack. And a classic career mode with a long but event restricted unlock system?Cons: bit difficult (dont pick up as ur first racer... im on redout difficulty and even I struggle.) The game is barebones. (Not too noticeable if u like racing/)
_childDocuments_.name: Redout 2

_childDocuments_.review: Game starts very easy (but still very fun), apart from impossible things in the tutorial (that don't  matter for scoring they're here for the tutorial's sake), then suddenly you get bonus challenges so hard you have to almost cheese them, then you get races that are impossible to get first, and you end up feeling good barely making it third.Another huge problem is that the Turn Warning system in the game can be VERY inaccurate, or even straight up missing, making it extra difficult to anticipate turns when you have poor visibility, and you end up generally wingin it as best as you can more than you rely on them.Opponent's racing ships have unlimited boosting and I have caught them boosting WAY beyond what is possible, which could be added to the fact that, just with like most racing games, stats do not matter for the AI.Some issues with frame drop when at high speed with more than 1 racing ship on the screen.I end up regretting this purchase
_childDocuments_.name: Redout 2

_childDocuments_.review: ok so, its a tough game, i have played lots of games before, lots of racing ones and this game is difficult, that being said, its fun because you are flying a projectile that is scrolling through reverse, inverse and twisted racing lanes and it has plenty of playability; by the time im writing this i barely unlocked the top tier or racing, so it has plenty of hours in it to make you happy, buy it its worth it
_childDocuments_.name: Redout 2

_childDocuments_.review: jesus ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ christ FINALLYwho in their right mind thought 50+ hour campaign in a racing game is alright???So obviously - the game is far too long. People usually already don't finish racing game campaigns and I feel that if you make it 50% longer than what other racing games offer, it isn't going to make that statistic go up.The game is alright. It's a very competetive sci-fi racer and it does deliver. All maps are beautiful and most of them are fun to drive on (except Neo Tokio which is just a constant of unexpected turns that will handicap the speed of your vehicle). I feel that this is probably the best sci-fi racer PC gaming has to offer for now. All pointless powerups from Redout 1 were removed and now everyone just has the boost by default (good change). I really like the nitro mechanic which increases the game's competetiveness.The game surely delivers a lot but a huge turn off is still the optimisation which did get better with time but it's still not the best. I think optimisation in a game like this is very important but even considering all flaws I mentioned, I'm not going to downvote the game because it has been downvoted enough already and it really has the potential to become something amazing.
_childDocuments_.name: Redout 2

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely loving this game. Much tighter than the original, control/feedback is unbelievable. Looks amazing on a high refresh display. Needs a little practice but once it clicks its such a thrill, there's nothing else like it out there. A lot of comparisons to Wipeout, but it's a very different racer really. Would recommend turning flight assists on for jumps/flight until you get your head around it.
_childDocuments_.name: Redout 2

_childDocuments_.review: Bought this on the sale but it's truly worth it no matter sake or not. As a Wipeout 2097 fan, looking for similar in an up to date package..found it right here. Look fabulous, runs fabulous and plays fabulous. I play it on my pc with rtx 4080 but I also play it on my Aya Neo Pro and that's where it really feels at home. Bug pat on the back Devs. There's a few minor issues but really nothing that affects game play. If you like futuristic anti gravity  games...this is it.
_childDocuments_.name: Redout 2

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game. Name of the game is high speed, high reward. Just dont be too reckless, lest you burn out on the wrong turnEdit: Its quite unfortunate that we haven't received an update in a year or so. I know that things are being worked on, but a little more of an update on what exactly is going on would be nice. As i've been playing i've noticed a few quirks on some tracks where I've just been shoved to the side for no reason, or it seems like gravity is just ten fold in that spot (not in the black hole ones, ik that's because there's a literal black hole next to me). Also the ship hitboxes could use a tweak. Lunare especially, she really scrapes hard on some tracks that the others don't.One thing I really miss after going back to the first game for a bit is the portals. It was exhilarating to go through one of those and suddenly be on a whole other planet, or in a new area. It also made the boss tracks unique in that instead of looping to each one, it like shuffled each section of the tracks. If there's a way to include those, that would be amazing. It just added a bit of fun to the tracks and just looked cool.Lastly I do have to agree with a lot of people, the soundtrack is a banger, but it just doesn't quite have the same punch as the first and can get a little stale. Still goes hard though.All and all, It's quite a fun game, and a bit unique compared to the first one, but some of the tracks need work. It'd be nice to bring portals back, and I just need some new tracks, both sound and race tracks.
_childDocuments_.name: Redout 2

_childDocuments_.review: This is not for the faint-at-heart. The speeds are fast and the track bites back. I've rage-quit many times. But I'm slowly starting to get the hang of it. Start slow and learn how to read the signs and place your craft on the track well. This is game is challenging but extremely rewarding when done right. If you are a fan of Wipeout or F-Zero. If you're debating whether you try it? You should, well made and nothing like it elsewhere.
_childDocuments_.name: Redout 2

_childDocuments_.review: I know I'm not alone in wanting a neutral button for reviews of games, but this game is both amazing and awful. The campaign is so incredibly padded out that if you make it to S league, you should be given an award for your patience.Tracks are repeated so frequently that trudging through the leagues is undoubtedly a dubious chore. Tracks are beautiful but have some of the jankiest collision. Think you'll land that jump? Sorry, no, you clipped through the geometry and have to start over. But what's the reward for even winning? Oh, it's a flaps that don't change the performance of my ship. Cool. And most races are like that. Not to mention the difficulty of either the A.I. or the challenges of some courses. They're sometimes way over-tuned and a colossal headache for average players.Anyways, the customization is nice but shallow, the rewards for winning races are trivial, and tracks often don't feel fair in a lot of places.I recommend this game if you are interested in AG-Racers but if not, I'd point you towards Ballistic.NG for a much more solid anti-gravity experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Redout 2

_childDocuments_.review: You know that part in Return of the Jedi where they blow up the death star and race out of it and Lando lets out that "Woohoo!". This game does that to me, every single time I play. Also, they've fixed the initial launch difficulty issues, so if you see "It's too hard" in other reviews, know that they adjusted the difficulty significantly and added difficulty settings and even configurable AI control assistance.
_childDocuments_.name: Redout 2

_childDocuments_.review: Pulse-pounding insanely fast and fun. When you hit a double boost and the music screams and the world disappears into a blur, that is when you are hooked. Hit the next turn at 700 mph. The tracks are beautiful and the games plays amazingly on keyboard. I want to keep trying to push just a little more performance out of myself, just a little more control, a little more speed, and then whooff. The release of a completed race and new time. This game is all about that rush. It is hard, ace the tutorial to make sure you have a handle on the way things drive, then go nuts. Try to keep getting those stars and pushing for a little more speed and then soon you will be blasting to over 1000 miles per hour.
_childDocuments_.name: Redout 2

_childDocuments_.review: Ok first I LOVED the first Redout and what worried me? The feeling of speed was not as good as in the previous one... This is not the case, it's fast, sizes of tracks satisfying. The speed feels great and the control over the vehicle is even better than in the previous one.BUT, and that will be a big downside for me, tracks and artistic direction is way less psychedelic and interpreted than before, and it was for me a repulsion argument...way uglier in various ways, modern and texture are dull and souless while it just wasn't the original. Vegetation is sprinkled mindlessly and does not form a big landscape background, rather than a big filler of empty space. I dig the idea to really visit the galaxy and locations of the races, but at the same time I don't care much about cities. Here the tracks are great, but the "show" around is uninteresting and does not blend as seamlessly as in the previous opus. Some will be glad because you get better tracks in general, others (like me) will be disappointed to not choose to play a race for the spectacular experience that it provides...Uninspired tracks, very repetitives in the same planets.... Otherwise, the game is better in teaching you the mechanics of racing, striffing etc... but certain features of the new gameplay were not that necessary for me. I keep thinking about the "tilt" in mind or the recurrent "you need to boost but not maneuver in a jump" kind of new things. I just hate tilting in jump makes me want to die to lower my thumb to do this.The star  unlock progression mechanic is also pure garbage. I finished the first one, beat the last event (few of us did, less than 2%) but I skipped aaaaaaalot of events, here wont be possible.... wich is dumb.Others features are pretty welcome, like the "new"(because it really isn't) super boost.Some technical issues came but didn't ruined my experience, especially cutscenes... and some "stops"... But sttuttering can be super anoying some times.On the con list, no split screen, why? I mean, you did it for the first one why not now? No VR either, which is a shame, bc it's a blast and helped me improve my skills in the first one as the sensations are more accurate...Overall I like it, even I adore the handelability but because of its diffrences (especially for tracks, designs and progression) with the first one, my heart is torn appart... sort of but go fetch the first one :)
_childDocuments_.name: Redout 2

_childDocuments_.review: I was a really big fan of Redout 1, and while Redout 2 inherits most of what made it good, it only made small improvements and sidegrades. I would recommend getting 1 instead if you haven't already and this game interests you.I used to think Redout 2 looked worse than 1; on further inspection that was not a fair assessment, as the graphical quality remains about the same (which is worth criticizing in and of itself for a sequel), but the performance has significantly decreased - I have experienced stuttering and frame drops. What I will criticize is that the tracks in Redout 2 have almost no landmark locations (any ones they do have are just dumb, like the giant robot in neo Tokyo) or anything that is particularly eye-catching or beautiful. I cannot tell the tracks apart in any way, they are all just random pieces of tracks with generic background and no set pieces to set them apart.The high speed AG racing from Redout 1 is still here, and it's still very good (I definitely did have fun in Redout 2), the tracks still have insane twists and turns. They also got into the habit of removing random pieces of guard rail from the track, leading me to fall off a lot.The upgrade system is expanded upon, there are more ships and upgrades to collect, and I like the new boost mechanic where you can sacrifice health to keep boosting, adding a great deal of risk and reward. However I didn't like that you now have to manually aim your ship in a jump, the game is too fast and the control too confusing for me to able to do that. Thankfully there are assist options for jumps, but sometimes they don't work and will just let you crash.I also have to mention the music, Redout 1 had great music, but here except the main menu theme all of them are very boring, a lot are basically a 5 second riff repeating over and over.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Totally recommend.Redout II is like a fine wine – it keeps getting better as it ages. It was a bit rough out of the gate, which was a bit disheartening given the amount of love you could feel was put into making a fitting successor to the original. But now with a few patches added to it, you can tell this one is only going to keep getting better.The good (things I like): Customization: Gone are the tiered bodies and customizations of the original. Redout II really takes customization up a notch and makes it feel like its your ship. Swap out body parts and performance parts as you unlock them to make your ship look and run how you want it. Awesome! Visuals: There was something nice about the angular style of the original, but this just looks pretty. One lap around one of the Fuji tracks is a great showcase of the visual polish, but each locale is stunning in different ways. And its not just the tracks, the ships look amazing too – especially now with all the customization options. Gameplay: The original Redout felt like you were piloting a rocket – steering had the grip-free drifty feeling. Here, it seems the rockets now also have some magnets to keep them somewhat stuck to the tracks, which feels a tiny bit more fun given some of the other things added in. Weather and temperature play a much bigger role – reduced visibility adds some extra challenge, and racing in hot environments makes moderating boost usage more interesting. Additionally, the flight controls allow for some awesome rolls in midair. Line up your landing perfectly, and you get an additional speed boost. Just be careful to adjust vector else you’ll end up flying off away from the track entirely!The not so good (meh):Track design: I get that they wanted to expand on the flight mechanic that was very basic in the original, but blind jumps and weather obscured turns are terrible ways of shoehorning difficulty into otherwise moderately technical tracks. Granted, some people may enjoy that experience, but optional HUD navigation hints would go a long way to improving the overall experience. However, overall, the tracks aren’t bad. Aside from a near 90-degree turn on a certain Neo Tokyo track… Can I get an emergency brake for my rocket? Soundtrack: This is a tough one. The soundtrack isn’t bad, and there are some real bangers, but compared with how awesome most of the soundtrack was for the original, a lot of the music here feels like an afterthought. Race modes: Speed events are neat. Time attack is classic. Races are fun. Boss events are a blast! Last Man Standing and Arena are… alright? The last two are just different rules for regular races, but outside of the obvious rule changes (Last Man = slowest racer DQed each lap, Arena = exploding = instant DQ) they don’t do much else to stand apart from standard races. The extra speed and damage modifiers should be looked at to make them more interesting with each lap.The bad (things I don’t like):Difficulty: Yes, its supposed to be difficult, I get it! But there are still instances where it seems like I’ve done as best as I can with the limitations for certain events, but the AI just seems to be miles ahead. Speed events seem to ramp up in difficulty a bit more nicely now (perhaps even a bit too over-easy), but races seem to go between laughably easy and frustratingly difficult.Performance: Really, this is a minor gripe, but for a racing game, its more than a bit annoying when the game stutters the first time you run a track. This should really be loaded up front. Outside of that, performance in general is great.

_childDocuments_.review: I really, really love this game. The sense of speed has been enhanced since the first game, the controls (generally, barring aerial controls)  feel a lot more fluid, the soundtrack still absolutely slaps. It's a passion project that brings Wipeout, Star Wars Podracer and F-Zero in to the 2020's in a way that no other company has been able to do. It's thrilling, fast paced, challenging as sin, and really really fills a niche that has been missing from games for a long time.Loves:- FAAAAAAASSSSTTTT- The game looks great- The game is long!!! There's plenty to play through- Game mechanics are presented in a virtual training area that lets you put them in to practice before you take them to a "real" race- The ships feel very different from each other- Ships can be visually customised which is a great touch- Soundtrack really does slap (though I do miss what Aram Shahbazians and Nils Holtar brought to Redout 1's soundtrack) and with new environmental incorporation (bass hits on contact with border barriers, hi/lo pass filters on boost and bandpass in the air) the soundtracks feels alive and reactive as much dance music does when DJ'd live.- THE REWIND FEATURE- I play on xbox controller and tapping B lets you rewind if you flung yourself off the course on a harsh corner with no border. It makes the game so much more forgiving- No more weapons- the game is a racer, and has really leaned in to it in this iteration of the game. You might think that makes the game less exciting, but with the new boost system you'll always find yourself with other things to monitor and juggle that make you grateful that you're not being EMP'd every lap. Speaking of boost...- The new boost system that lets you drain your health to boost longer. So dangerous. So satisfying. So clutch. It's the perfect measure of risk/reward- especially when you stack your hyper boost with regular boost. It can drastically change the  outcome of a race in less than a second. Awesome.There are a couple of things I don't like so much:- Currency is no longer a thing. In Redout 1, you played in events and built up currency with which to purchase new ships and upgrade owned ships in career- it made it a rewarding experience to attain your own goals and progress in a way that you found personally fulfilling. In Redout 2 its far more linear. You get given upgrades for completing courses. You will always have access to Lunare before Asera if you follow the upgrade progression etc.- Contracts have been swapped for trophies. Contracts added a lot to the replayability of levels. It also made you feel more in touch with the game world to be approached by the organisations you were in a contract with. (Please note, with 12 hours in the game I should say I have seen contracts YET)- Detailed lore about the companies and universe has been removed from the ship info and put in to sound bytes and simple descriptions throughout career. I loved reading about the organisations that make the in-universe sport possible in Redout 1. It was a beautiful touch that really showcased the love 34BigThings had for the original Redout. - The aerial controls aren't intuitive. They have the capacity to be so, but when you spend so little time in the air it's hard to get used to them inherently. On a controller when you're already controlling your strafe and nose turn via the analog sticks, leaping down to the d pad to suddenly control your rotation for half a second is really jarring in such a fast paced game. By the time your fingers have moved and your brain has caught up with being in the air you're already back on the ground and doing 4 loop-de-loops. In the end I kinda just accepted poor landings and relying on the rewind function.- The world itself is a lot more zany, or at least is presented as such which is more of a personal taste thing than anything else.- The very linear progression applies to cosmetics inclusive of colours. I feel like there should be a far more extensive base selection of colour combos in the game from the start, with less being locked behind career progression. Everyone knows red ones go faster.I got the game in the Christmas sale 2022 on Steam with all the DLC currently available. I'd highly recommend giving this space age racer a shot- especially if you played Redout 1 and are looking to shake off the rust and get back in to the cockpit. The devs seem pretty active, and I'm stoked to see what's next!
_childDocuments_.name: Redout 2

_childDocuments_.review: Coming from Redout 1, after an hour or so of Redout 2 I can safely say: it is very, very good. The ships handle like a dream, there's a handful of control assist options which you can tweak and max out, so your friends can enjoy Europa-esque epileptic tubes and loops.New: Aerial ControlsGeting used to aerial controls takes you a while; back in Redout 1, your ship would just snap into the track; now you have to *roll* and land properly to avoid damaging your ship, and control the pitch so you won't crash face-first into a 90-degree track.New: XeSS and graphicsGraphics are improved across the board, the tracks are brimming with detail and the ship designs are a definite step up from R1. To handle the antialiasing and the performance impact 34BigThings had implemented Intel XeSS, and it gets the job done.New: Boosting and HeatThe old range of weapons, equipment and the energy meter from R1 are replaced with Boost, Hyperboost and Heat. Boosting builds up Heat. Overheating drains your ship Integrity. Hyperboosting can be used after a cooldown in addition to Boost; use both and go nuts.New: Environmental HazardsEvery track contains at least a couple environmental hazards that affect your ship in many ways; you lose traction over dirt, move slower and cool down in the water, and struggle with the gravity near a Black Hole. Yes.New Tracks:Run through the Event Horizon straight into the heart of a Black Hole, Interstellar style. Get suspended in mid-air because you didn't have enough speed to reattach yourself to the track. Become increasingly worried as it's pulling you away.Black Hole smiles at you with eternal malice.New Ships:- WALLACE-RGA new variation of the jack-of-all-trades. ESA-AGR with an emphasis on maneuverability. Turns on a dime.- AKHAL-TECHAwesome speed and acceleration, bit more balanced than SULHA, can take a hit, too. Pleasing Thunder Force aesthetic.- BURAN (dishonorable mention)In Redout 1, the *ussian cinderblock is as unpleasant to look at as it is to drive. Got to give it to 34BigThings, now it's at least manageable and you can change the looks.- BEHEMOTHTartarus mines; a guy piloting LUNARE is sweating profusely, integrity alarm blaring as he watches his last pixel of health.You charge straight through a lake of lava, unphased, sipping a Mai Tai.A SULHA struggles to push you off course. You do not veer off a single degree. Sulha is squished against the next wall, screaming.KOENIG is a turtle. This one is a heatsink that is slowly inching its way toward the finish line.Feel the weight of a ponderous BEHEMOTH.Feel every molecule of air struggle against the sheer volume of your heat-dissipating slowpokium.

_childDocuments_.review: I have to start by saying that I haven't really played a supersonic, anti-grav racer since the likes of PS2 era Wipeout or F-Zero on Gamecube. With that admission in place, Redout II is not for the faint of heart! It is NOT Wipeout with a shiny new paint job and it ain't no F-Zero! I don't mean that negatively at all. Instead of a complete arcade racer, Redout leans more toward the "sim" side (if you can indeed simulate anti-grav racing at 900 MPH). Holding the throttle wife open and bouncing off the walls ain't gonna cut it here. Learning the tracks and the individual machines is key to not being, literally, miles behind.My first suggestion would be to remap the controls so the ground controls more closely resemble aircraft controls. For me personally, they feel more intuitive this way and they're not all switched around when you actually have to fly this damn thing every now and then. And I rarely have to turn on assists and drop the difficulty all the way down but to learn the game, I had to resort to using "Zero" difficulty. I do like how you can turn individual assists (one for each individual control) up or down as needed. As you figure out how to drive, you can ease them back to tweak the challenge as you see fit.I do have to agree with the consensus that the jumps are oddly (and wildly) random. Either it seems like you barely make it with boost or you're flying past the intended landing zone by miles. Speaking of boost, my personal biggest gripe would be that, for whatever reason, it's hard to tell how fas you're going unless you're stack boosting and redlining the heat right on the verge of blowing up. But that eye for speed comes with practice.All in all, Redout II is tough, especially for what you probably think is an arcade racer. But once you get the hang of it, it's exponentially more satisfying. If you want a hypersonic anti-grav racer that you actually have to drive/fly, I've not seen better recently. Recommended!

There is 6 types of acceleration: usual, boost, hyperboost, boosters on track, inertia return landing zones and gravitational. Up to extreme 3600 km/h, and with all of these you can still not hitting any walls.- Tons of customisation, both visual and performance.- Huge variety of different stylistically and technically tracks.- Good optimisation, even for an UE4 game (especially if you tweak engine parameters, this will run on everything).- Amazing dynamic soundtrack.- Huge career mode if you like progression, fully customizable arcade mode for single runs, multiplayer if you want to make sure that your skills are drastically below 'average' player.

_childDocuments_.review: tldr: more than the sum of its parts, parts are good to begin with, the titanfall 2 of racing gamesReally loved the first Redout & have kept picking it up again & again for years, & this one improves on virtually every part of it & fleshes it out into a much more immersive & engaging game overall. the devs find the sweet-spot between arcade & hard sim everywhere it matters -- controls are deep but forgiving; garage is complex & key to performance enough to have to pay attention to your decisions, but simple enough to avoid choice paralysis; career lets you find a balance between pushing your parts to the limit on the way up to the fastest event classes & combing back through for upgrades; the focus on high effects & shaders paired w/ low-poly models looks beautiful & runs great even on older hardware. The controls & the heat/boost system are the best in the AG racing genre; the precise control over understeer/oversteer makes it feel more like DiRT than wipeout, & the resource management involved in boosting (regular boost - always available & raises heat, hyper boost - requires battery to charge & raises heat, braking vents heat, boost types can be stacked) feels like a more active & dynamic version of the fuel & ERS management systems in the F1 games.Re: a lot of the comments on difficulty -- the game does a great job with rewarding the player for learning the system & not ignoring mechanics that seem too complex, not ignoring cars or stats that seem uninteresting to the player's own comfort zone, etc.; for example, you might skip a track because you don't want to deal with a bunch of jumps or hairpins that you can't quite nail & just want to go fast, but you'll eventually need to come back for the points or upgrades, and can tune the car for the track in a way that will let you drift through the hairpins at full throttle without touching the wall, boost to a certain speed you need to hit for a challenge criterion, etc.Unique visuals + immersive controls + high skill + casual-friendliness + fun customization = titanfall 2 of racing games

_childDocuments_.review: This is my first AG racing game, and I ABSOLUTELY love it-Beautiful visuals, even if the environment gets constantly blurred out due to high speeds, the maps are beautiful to look and race at-Sense of speed is unbelievable, easily the best part of the game-Soundtrack is an absolute gem, every song fits perfectly for their respective track-Assists are available if you struggle with a specific aspect of the game, such as boosting, steering, strafing or pitching-Campaign is , and as you progress through it you unlock more ships and upgrades to become faster, it is not required to get perfect scores and 1st place on every race to progress, so you can leave hard races for later-High difficulty, I wouldnt consider this a "bad" aspect, but something to consider before buying, the game has a big learning curve and requires fast reflexes, memorizing the tracks and racing a lot to get better, the AI may not seem very challenging at first, but this can be fixed by increasing their difficulty. As I mentioned, assists exist but I feel the game is more enjoyable when you have most of the control of your ship.-Some of the races require pixel perfect gameplay due to the high point requirements (e.g. speed trails), this is frustrating especially in the earlygame, when you dont own many upgrades for your ship.Overall, this is a very fun game, recommended even if you havent tried out AG racing games before, if you can get it while its on sale, even better.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been putting a ton of hours into this game, and I would recommend this game to my friends. It is an epic arcade racing title comparable to F-Zero and WipeOut on their respective consoles.The game itself is fun to play, which mainly relies upon the player mastering their ability to control their ship in order to pilot it around the circuit as fast as possible. There are several aerospace mechanics (mid air ship manuvering) in the game to master in order to get good at it, though there are assists to allow beginners to pick up the game. The environments are also rather detailed, and diverse between racing venues. The excellent electronica/drum & bass soundtrack also complements the game as well.One bit of criticism I have is the career mode. It does give you some objectives to obtain additional ships, upgrades, and cosmidecs, but that's about it. The track and ship descriptions also provide hints and additional lore, though with all this I'd like to see this expanded into a full fledged story. The tutorial levels are also very handy, but have to be unlocked at certain points during the career mode when ideally the whole library of tutorials should be made available from the start.Overall, it's a great game! If any DLC comes out in the future, I'll be happy to grab it.

_childDocuments_.review: Short: The game has really satisfying racing mechanics, but individual tracks lack identity and Career mode needs tweaks.The intense speed of the game is incredibly satisfying, and once I changed a few controls, it felt really good to have so much freedom of movement. The game also has a great strategic choice between drifting turns and strafing turns, and both playstyles are fun. There is a massive amount of longevity to this game because it has extremely satisfying basic mechanics. There's good variety to the levels and some of the ones that are unlocked later (Origin Black Hole) feel incredible. The campaign is very long, which is nice but problems crop up from time to time. Each mission has a "Trophy" that is unlocked by completing an optional objective and worth an extra progression point. Some of these trophies are fine, like getting 5 perfect landings or finishing at a high speed, but others are more problematic. "Qualify in 1st position" and "Get 3 seconds past Gold" (time trial) are artificially locked behind a very high difficulty and most players will not be able to get them even after several attempts (difficulty has since been rebalanced and this is less of an issue). Others I personally dislike because they dampen the fun of the game. Playing a race is most fun when you're able to set the difficulty so that the AI challenges you, but when the Trophy requires you to lead every lap or win with a kilometer lead, you're incentivized to lower the difficulty to a point where the AI is no longer a challenge. Throughout the game I found myself in an awkward position where I wanted to play on a higher difficulty so that I wasn't just leaving the AI behind all the time, but couldn't because I wouldn't be getting the trophies anymore. One final issue I had was with the abundance of reverse tracks when you first start playing. They make it take a lot longer to learn the tracks, so they probably shouldn't show up until you've raced a track 4-5 times. This wouldn't be as big of an issue if the tracks weren't so much harder to learn than in RO1. There's an "upcoming turn warning" feature now which is nice but it's hard to learn the tracks when all the ones in the same region share some segments and have very few visual differences. The game's progression also feels inconsistent. At the very beginning you get so many upgrades that you can't equip them all without going over. In contrast, Class A has a string of several dozen events that don't give out any ship upgrades, but the difficulty keeps going up to a point where you're barely able to meet the minimum.  Each track region has a 'ship' that is built to suit it nicely, but in many cases you don't unlock the ship until much later, even though the Time Trial Gold time will usually be from it. Because of this, some events are very difficult early on but become easy later with the right ship. There were a few instances where I encountered bugs or the physics felt wonky (particularly when landing after jumps), and hope those will be fixed before long.

_childDocuments_.review: Final Score 4.25/5Verdict: Worthy successor to Wipeout series that brings mature and rewarding racing mechanics, challenging career mode to battle for upgrades, and beautiful graphics,  ------------------------Pro:- Fast, challenging, cool loooking- Responsive controls- Pretty visuals- Awesome soundscape- Thumping dynamic soundtrack- Lasting career mode------------------------Love/Hate: Difficulty - Player reviews around the internet sometime complain about difficulty. I think this is is because of misunderstanding the career mode - you are starting in basic rugged down ship and by playing career mode you unlock "racing modifications", to increase power. Each configuration of ship has speed rating. You will not be immediately winning races with ship rated 208 against ships rated 298.  I like it, as it makes sense to me - I will try to finish 2nd in this race to unlock better rudder unit, so I can be faster on next attempt. Now none of this is explained well in-game, you have to find it out by trial/error. So I understand the confusion, however the game difficulty and career progression is well done by me. Controls - are also new, if you have not played the predecessor. Left stick to turn, rights stick to strafe and control ship yaw - in Wipeout this is was on triggers and left stick respectively. This poses some challenge to master. Make sure to play with assisst if you struggle.Music - If you are into psytrance, dnb and in thumping music, you will like this one. It has interesting dynamic soundtrack model where you can gauge speed by how close to peak techno you are. If not you can always disable music.Announcer lady telling track stories - Not fan of autotune chosen, content is fine but script would deserve a rewrite (english version)------------------------Really bad:- HDR is broken. It does not work. Just do not even try to enable it unless there is a patch with specific fixes.- Control scheme probably could be reworked, maybe the Wipeout scheme is better?- Written description of developers logic behind career mode would honestly be enough (Play races to finish 2nd-3rd, earn upgrades, rerace and win.)

_childDocuments_.review: This is not like the first game, and I strongly recommend playing through the first game first - both for the quality of content and the difficulty curve you will be guaranteed to hit going straight into Redout 2 blind.Redout was an Arcade racer with a progressive campaign that eased you into faster and faster tracks. By the end of mastering the campaign you might not have been the best racer, but you felt accomplished getting each gold medal and a platinum medal or two. You customized abilities and picked a team that suited your play-style, with the more tanky teams being good for less experienced players, as the health pool in the first game was about 1/10th what you are given in Redout 2. It had amazing and unique tracks and event modes, each felt unique and immersive.Redout 2 is an immersive and competitive beast. Coming from the first game, you've had the boost upgrades completely unlocked to the point where you can keep using them until your ship explodes - no more power-ups, meaning the tanky ships are designed to boost for longer with their additional health. From the very first track, you feel like you've been dunked into a difficulty harder than the first game could provide, and that's not necessarily a bad thing, since...You can now put training wheels on your ships in the settings, helping you corner faster and keep your ship from exploding. The tracks themselves now have multiple paths, each environment affects your ships differently, and above it all the music is just as great as the first game.Vertex maps have been redesigned from the first game into actual tutorial levels, showing players ~some~ of the intricacy of the controls, but I feel neglects to show some of the most important tips, like how to drift. (strafe opposite of steer)Another change from the first game is the intricacy of jumps and landing, needing to pitch as you fly. The biggest bug that needs to be fixed is the collision box with the track as you land as you will fall through unless your landing was perfect.

_childDocuments_.review: Truly awesome game, but with a steep learning curve.When I started playing it, I found it too hard.  I got quickly frustrated.  I wasn't even winning the trials.   After a while of almost never winning any speed challenges, I figured I was doing something wrong.  Turns out I was!    I was strafing the wrong way.  When you have some sharp turns to do, you cannot strafe in the same direction you are turning, you need to strafe the opposite way and before you start the turn and then adjust the strafing during the turn.  This changed everything.   I was able to complete the B league and I'm working on the A league now.  This game is very challenging, but it is great.   The first one was only truly challenging in the dlcs and in some specific events.    This one feels more like Wipeout-level challeng.   What a rush you get when you complete a hard event after several tries.   I'm not even in the hardest part yet.   Can't wait to see the insane speed of the last events.  It's a long game too.  I'm close to 90 hours and I'm not even halfway through.    I often need to redo events several times before winning and there are "trophies" in each race that sometimes are really hard to accomplish.  15 perfect landings, dammit!The music is great, but not as good as the first one, I think.   This game looks incredible too, the level designs and the car designs are amazing.   Some tracks need to be fixed (or explained?), sometimes when you jump too far, you go through the racetrack even if you should just land on it.    Some of the time challenges are wrong too (1 in B league and 1 in A league so far).   I finished them with something like a minute and a half faster than gold.  It made no sense (I'm nowhere near that good).   I also sometimes start spinning in circles when I hit the sides in a specific way.  These are small issues that will be possibly be fixed in upcoming patches.I highly recommend the game for any fans of Wipeout and F-Zero out there.

_childDocuments_.review: DON'T LET THE NEGATIVE REVIEW SCARE YOU!Most of those were written at or shortly after launch when the difficulty curve was insanely unfair and the game was a bit buggy. The devs have worked hard to rectify these issues and the game is now much more approachable.That's not to say that it's easy. The controls themselves are their own challenge to newcomers. For the uninformed, simply steering your ship around the track will not do. You have to use both control sticks to control steering, pitch, and strafe. Coupling this with lightning fast speeds, edgeless tracks, blind corners, and learning how and when to boost most effectively makes getting around the track in one piece quite the challenge at first.But rest assured this is one of the most satisfying control schemes to master. As you progress through the (appropriately difficult) campaign you'll progressively upgrade your ship with new parts to help you fly around the track faster. There's not a lot of variety in locations at first, but once you get to where you're racing on the more complex and beautifully designed tracks things really start to heat up.I also have to shout out the AI driving assists. You can adjust how much assistance you want with any aspect of driving. While I recommend using as few of these as possible, I still use the Boost Safety and Air Roll assists after 30 hours.I also cannot recommend the season pass enough. These track designs are some of the best in the business and it's totally worth the money.So yeah, from a veteran arcade racing fan, this is one of my all time favorites. Highly recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is wonderful, I didn't stick with Redout 1 not because I disliked the game, but because I felt late to the party and hardly felt like I understood what I was doing, Redout 2 feels more complex yet I can actually understand what i'm doing and how to go fast, I'm not someone who plays racing games at all, but I dip my toes into a few interesting ones and so far this is by far my favouriteIt has a wonderful sense of speed and tight controls, breezing through a match feels and looks masterful, this game feels like it's less about taking tight corners and more about maintaining and gaining speed, same as Redout 1, the visuals and music are fantastic and I want to specifically mention whatever dynamic music system they have in place is perfect for this game,It isn't perfect however, UI could use some work in some areas, the singleplayer has a daunting amount of content that while has variety, it's not enough for how much they want you to play. Some tutorials being locked behind singleplayer progression which while having good intentions of not flooding the player with information, is a weird choice for players looking to learn, something a difficult game like this will have a lot of, and multiplayer is all matchmaking with no server browser which while isn't bad, is a downgrade in my opinion.Difficulty is something people have talked about, I'm finding it to be easy outside of the speed trials, but I didn't play before the patch that made it all easier, my other complaint is weirdly enough, the lack of rubber-banding, It feels like I get ahead in every race and never interact with the other racers again, rarely any give or take with the lead.I am loving this game, aside from the singleplayer balance it feels more polished than redout 1, On current patch it's still very enjoyable and i don't feel like i'm missing out on the few odd singleplayer missions that seem unreasonable, it's a fantastic pick up and play game that I hope has a good life ahead of it.

_childDocuments_.review: I’ve already written about it extensively in both my Beast Sides and Best B-sides of 2020 features but I still haven’t run out of ways to praise this track. _childDocuments_.review: Yeah if you wanna get max stars then the game is pretty rough.. but that's the whole point of these arcade X00mph futuristic racers. It might not be easily accessible for people new to the genre but as someone that grew up playing Rollcage, Wipeout, Burnout, XGR etc. I can wholeheartedly say that this is it chief.The artstyle isn't anything to write home about but it lends further to the performance and when you're whipping around a corner fast enough to nearly black out then the last thing you should be looking at is the slightly low res sphinx in the far distance.The difficulty... let me start off by saying that I played redout 1 and thoroughly enjoyed it. Only complaint about redout 1 is that the difficulty was inconsistent, at times I would blaze through a course and get gold and others I would be stuck for 30 mins retrying to get the perfect line. Redout 2 on the other hand is far more consistent.. consistent at crushing your balls because ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ this game is unforgiving, that is exactly why this game is so much more enjoyable (imo) than the endless slew of modern racers, I've never restarted a race so many times and still been eager to give it another go just out of sheer determination. Let me tell you about boost management.. because if you're anything like me then you'll get a stiffy from watching the boost meter fall as you rip through the course and then start to eat into your ships own health pool for the first time. Oh you want to mega boost everytime it's off cooldown? yeah no sweat.. just make sure you never touch a wall because you're gonna be riding at 1% health the whole game. You might think this sounds awful but it's actually such a great mechanic imo, think of the possibilities.. having the large health pool is a great fallback for newer players just getting the hang of things but where it really shines is for the more experienced racers, it's a game of chicken to see how far you can push it at all times constantly riding the knifes edge.Conclusion.. if you like a bit of c*** and ball torture and also happen to enjoy racing games in equal measure then this is the game for you.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who has played the first game, I feel that the controls have been changed for the better. Taking out dedicated buttons for air strafing means your right thumb can stay on the right analog stick and allows you to boost whilst navigating turns. The AI assist that can be fine tuned for just about every aspect of using your hovercraft also serves as a great way to ease yourself into the controls and gradually take the training wheels off.Taking out the usable gadget slot, while it decreases variety in gameplay, also serves to better focus this game on racing, especially when almost everyone was using the ultra boost gadget in the first game.Lastly, it feels like Redout 2 rewards players better for masterful driving and boost management. Instead of being limited by how much fuel you have in the tank to boost (hence the low variety of attachments and gadgets used in the first game), you're limited by your craft's structural integrity. This greatly separates those who are constantly crashing into barriers and those who don't, creating a steeper but more satisfying skill curve to master.Couple everything with it's already sick artstyle, framerates and techno OSTs, and this feels like a newer, improved version of an already amazing first game.

_childDocuments_.review: Takes a step in a different direction from the prequel, feeling like it combines Redouts traits with F-Zero GX with its energy boosts tied to your health. That takes patience, and it's fine to condition the player to that.However, the campaign is way. Too. Dang. Long. B League alone curb stomped my head in with the same friggin' tracks over, and over. And over. And over. Then it turned me over to see if I was still breathing--then it dropkicked more of the same set of tracks some more.I couldn't take it anymore and spoiled myself seeing the rest of the zones past that in the free modes. Customization is nice but feels sorta minute with the payoff save for the livery and colors. The tutorial could be introduced a bit better with everything all at once and not really in the bits and pieces format. I found myself questioning some of the newer features that weren't answered until a few successful races later when it was finally addressed - by that point I dismissed the question and moved on hours later.Speed Mode? Holy crackers, does that require S-Tier accuracy. I'm no Blue Falcon and had a blast taking my time getting through R1 and its DLC, some difficulty was there, sure. But this? It's harder than the Speed mode in Redout 1 and gives me the message to skip them for later when unlocking the higher specs for my vehicle. _childDocuments_.review: It's good, but it could have used another round of balancing.Legibility is much improved from Redout 1, with a bright neon line running through the center of the track as well as rally style callouts for turns. Jumps are much more drawn out affairs, giving you time to adjust after takeoff and being more tolerant of speed variations. However as the game progresses and the tracks look more and more like rollercoasters, this shows its limits. The callouts have less than perfect accuracy. There are still a few hills that conceal immediate turns, and many more that hide the straight lines you want  to be boosting on. Your high speed jump will miss its mark because you couldn't tell you'd be falling sideways after this many loops.Despite the experience of the first game, the developers have still not sworn off blinding the player, with clouds occasionally traversing the course and veils of waters blurring your craft's canopy. The loading screen might tell you that low visibility "really brings Redout to the next level", but there's no way you're getting a good idea of the unannounced right-hand turn right after entering the first habitat in Ahti, unless you pull it back a notch and go through it at 30km/h. At least Neptune's pipes are gone.The game is difficult, as many of the other reviews note. Thankfully the game provides 6 different difficulty levels, as well as rewinds that let you undo your mistakes including crashes. It's a shame then that these options only work for races, leaving the other half of the events, ie Time and Speed Trials, unchanged. There's about a 20% difference between what's needed for Bronze and what's needed for Gold, and Gold typically requires a performance that would beat a Master level AI for that single lap. And you'll need golds to progress through the game's second league.Races with a time trial for qualification are even more amusingly off the mark, with the times demanded for first place being higher than what Platinum requires. Narrowing the bracket of target times and scores, letting players use rewinds in these solo trials, and scaling all of that based on difficulty would have completed the laudable inclusion of difficulty levels, but as it stands things were rushed.

_childDocuments_.review: Give this some time, and you'll see it's an outstanding sequel to the first game, whilst leaving a few areas for improvement.The handling is tighter, which suits its more technical track design, and more so the faster you go. And faster, you will have to go, much faster than in the first game. The campaign is brutally HARD, and there needs to be a bit more balance, especially with the 'Speed' challenges. You have to very strategically pick your upgrades and then fly more or less perfectly to be in with a chance of earning some stars on some of these. That's actually a point of contention for me. I was going in expecting to pick my preferred team, and build it up throughout the campaign, but for certain challenges, you really do have to switch it up, swapping out parts to be within the homologation limits. it can get finecky changing your setup so frequently to suit the event.All that said, my biggest gripe with the first Redout was a lack of challenge from the AI. That has been comprehensively remedied here. You will much more often be neck and neck with opponents, boosting past one another and jostling for position, which really adds to the drama.The music is actually for me of a more consistent quality than before, though it's not packed with as many killer highlights as the first. The score is solid and does a great job of getting you pumped up.There is some bugginess at times when landing on tracks, in that it's possible to fly straight through them when you could have sworn you contacted it.  It can be hard to tell at such high speeds and, as others have pointed out, the track can be particularly hard to read when transferring between tracks over long distances, often with a choice of track, along with obstacles to avoid. Moreover, knowing how much extra pitch and boost you'll need to make the gap is largely a matter of trial and error, with certain jumps having some quite counterintuitive physics to them. Once you've learnt the track though, it's much less of an issue. The aesthetic customization is pretty awesome, though it takes a while to unlock things. I'm standing at 15 hours and the vast majority of parts and liveries are still locked. The campaign itself is pretty straightforward, much like the first with a mixture of its different event types across a nice, large range of biomes. I wouldn't bet on the multiplayer being too lively, based on the first game, but you never know.I'm actually going to say this is the superior game to the first, for the overrall experience.Again, be aware this game is hard as nails, but if you give it a chance and focus on strafing and counter-strafing to make it round corners, there's a hell of a thrill to be had here, once again.

_childDocuments_.review: I played Redout 1 and I played a lot of the WipEout games, so I'd consider myself an AG Racing fan.And this one is a mix of emotions.In comparison to Redout 1, I'd say this game is an absolute improvement on almost every level. Unfortunately that doesn't mean it's perfect and it carries over and creates enough issues for me to frequently get frustrated with aspects I feel like aren't my fault as a player.But let's start with the .The amount of blind corners, jumps and open edges is just depressing, and no arrows or pacenotes or rewinds will get you out of that.I love myself some challenging maps, but I want to have a chance at succeeding.Honestly the rest are just nitpicks. I really,  want to love this game but the frequent bad maps make it very hard. I'm still absolutely gonna recommend this game, but it's just such a mixed bag.

_childDocuments_.review: Coming from the perspective of someone who played Redout 1, I would say I much prefer Redout 2  to it. Redout 2 is a lot more technical than Redout 1. It has steep learning curve, even for returning players. If you come from Redout 1 expecting to slip into Redout 2 like a familiar pair of gloves, you'll be in for a rude awakening. However, if you get yourself accustomed to the game, its much more engaging than the original.Redout 2 has taken out most of the powerups from 1, and it's better for it. Most of the powerups were either very situational or very unpleasant to deal with. The only powerup that saw consistent use in the first game; the Turbo Boost, they've taken and incorporated into the main mechanics of 2 as hyperboost. Sparing the details boost management is now much more involved than just doing it whenever you can. It's a tricky system and results in the player having to strategize and adapt depending on the course they're playing on.Now if all this sounds really daunting, don't worry. There have been some very helpful features added to compensate for the higher difficulty level. For one, a very robust assist system has been implemented that automatically tunes itself to your needs from assessing your tutorial performance. The assist system can then be manually customized if you feel unsatisfied with it. If you really have trouble, I'd suggest cranking those up and then turning it off after you get a better sense of how to handle yourself. There is also a rewind feature that allows you to wind back time at will to try again if you make a mistake.Overall, a very enjoyable game. Unlike most modern games, it has a steep learning curve but it tries its best to hold your hand.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an absolute blast!
