_childDocuments_.review: It's more Redout, with a steep curve to get into (a few hours, so keep that in mind) and a more convoluted Career upgrade track. Since I primarily play solo, Career mode is the only thing I'll discuss.At time of review I'm clearing the last bits of the starter B-league.The upgrades to ships now are modular and tied to a point-value used by the career missions. Since the upgrades are rewards for clearing specific missions, you might not have the proper stats to beat an earlier mission.The other part of Career missions are the star-rating, 3-stars on 3rd-2nd-1st and 4th for clearing an objective regardless of placement. These are usually 'go fast', 'beat the top time', 'finish fast' etc., but there are a few ones that are counterintuitive to the way the game is meant to be played (go fast) and some that are a nuisance to get, specifically the Promotion race to A-class, where one jump on the Tartarus track unassisted flew me into the wild unknown many times until I turned on the assist.. and even then it was tricky. It could be fine in a ~2min lap, but this was a 2-lap boss run, so effectively 14 minutes of 'perfect' play in the relative early-game.The customisation has the color schemes and patterns again, but with the upgraded classes swapped for modular upgrades, the cosmetic aspect of ship design has also become modular. You have the base chassis per ship archetype, and unlock modular parts (and schemes and patterns) through the missions as well.The soundtrack is good, but is missing a bit of the original's vibe. It could be part of the new track-blending tech they use for the music, but they lost the stand-outs from the first game.

_childDocuments_.review: At the moment, Mixed.For now i can absolutely not recommend this to Casual players, its baseline difficulty is far too high.While it does have Difficulty settings and Driver Assits, the Difficulty settings only affect how well the AI drive.In Qualifiers, Time Attack, and Speed Gamemodes the Difficulty setting have 0 effect and are very overtuned making even veterans break into a sweat.That'd be not so bad unless almost all of the unlockables be it Liveries, Paint, Upgrades and even Vehicles are locked behind these gamemodes, unlockables you really want if you want to play Multiplayer and i guarantee this will frustrate most of you.Unlockables also locked behind bizarre bonus objectives like landing perfectly 15 times... on a track with no jumps... in a 1lap race.For Veterans however, be prepared for a real challenge.The Tracks are tighter, punishing, more frustrating followed by then adrenaline inducing after practice.The time requirements are tight and even for some of you seemingly unreachable.Eventually after 30 hours i can almost see the light at the end of the tunnel and i am starting to feel more confident playing this game.Be prepared, this is not an easy beast to tame.Other DetailsThe tracks are one outlier, The Boss tracks this time are directly linked, kudos to that, the bad news is that the reversed tracks feel very disorganised in comparison.To the point that in one track, known as Cloud City: Mistral have the AI dying constantly at the reverse.And Tartarus: Ixion where the AI will teleport 4km infront of you if they are forced to respawn at the reverse.Other bugs is where you either fall through a track or worst one, hit an invisible object in the middle of the track and bump back, or more commonly just start spinning like a pulsar, stuck.TL;DR, the game is still in a early state with early release issues, is not reccomended for Casual players, and also Veterans need to be warned that the difficulty curve is way higher.

_childDocuments_.review: ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ this game is way, WAY harder than the first but I love it so far.Redout 2, like the first, will remind you of the days you spent in some sticky gross arcade playing F-Zero AX with the whole two friends that showed up to your birthday. It's a fast paced, chaotic, extremely high skill ceiling game, even more so than the first. It ditched the items from the first game to raise the bar on the boosting and vehicle handling, and honestly I dig it.I've seen some negative reviews regarding the difficulty, and while I don't wholly disagree, I kinda like the challenge? I haven't got too terribly far yet, but it hasn't been too bad, barring a couple exceptions (COUGH speed challenges COUGH).I'm going to defend it though, honestly many games don't bust my ass these days, and I appreciate a game that does.I think the main issue is how woefully unequipped you'll be for those first couple races; AI will have items and you will not, and you start out with an extremely minimal, all rounder ship that really does need those items to compete. The tutorial, especially the very first ones, are simultaneously very barebones and very handholdy, and you may find yourself having to figure stuff out on your own (combining strafing and turning for new players for example) for a while. I think the main issue with the tutorial is that you don't really need to  what it asks you to. During a cornering tutorial I was smashing into walls left and right but it completed all the same. There's a tiered result system (gold, silver, etc) and yet the completion is all the same 1 star.In spite of that, I think as you get over that initial hump the game comes into its own, and it only gets better. I ain't gonna say get gud, but I will say  stick with it a bit more if you struggle. You can clear that hump. Once you do the difficulty feels especially more fair and the reward is so very worth it.The environments are even prettier than the first game, and I thought the first was already stunning. They included more in-depth vehicle customization which I absolutely ADORE, being able to pick apart aesthetics with a goodly amount of pieces and being able to mix and match certain gear gives all ships a bit more wiggle room in terms of versatility than the first game.Still love how the game plays, handling and boosting is very difficult yes, but so very rewarding, and I wish more games were like that.Few bugs I ran into, though they bear mentioning:Some jumps I launch WAY over what's seemingly intended, especially on one Cairo map, and clip straight on through where I should land.I know the AI is cheating on Tartarus. I KNOW THEY ARE. THEY DON'T WHEN I FOLLOW THEM BUT IF I GET AHEAD OF THEM JUST AFTER A LAP  4KM AHEAD. I'M NOT CRAZY.You know what this is. Like F-Zero (especially AX/GX), or WipeOut, this is your cup of tea. Don't mind a bit of ball-busting? You'll be all right. Especially to GX players. That game whooped my ass as a kid. I love a nostalgic ass-kicking. If you're on the fence, give it a couple months to iron out some stuff, particularly in the early game.

_childDocuments_.review: Torn right now. I really wish there was a thumbs in the middle option..I really do enjoy the fast pace style of this game. There's a severe learning and skill curve that makes it hard to get going but rewarding to get better.. The ai is trash and will rubber band and or be forced to catch up to you unrealistically even when you've raced perfectly for 90% of the track. One little bump and all of a sudden, the 2 mile lead you had on ai is instantly lost and they're ahead of you and it just doesn't add up. I hope to see the ai become more realistic and the game can become a bit more rewarding to players that are actually doing well. The multiplayer as of right now is absolutely awful. Not only does matchmaking suck super hard but it often fails, and doesn't properly track the performance of each player. I just finished racing someone online in an un-ranked race and they must have been new because I destroyed them with an over 5 mile lead.. They didn't finished and at the end, it said that I lost.. WTF, okay... stupid.. The graphics, physics, and car customization / unlocking system is pretty cool. I really have enjoyed the actual racing part itself and I've gotten through most of the 3rd league but and can win most of the races but I've gotten to a point now where its just too difficult to progress to be fun.. It needs to be loosened up a bit so that I can actually unlock the parts needed to progress. I'm now stagnating because I cannot unlock more upgraded parts which I need in order to unlock more start on the next races. I'm not complaining about not getting first place or not doing perfectly on a race, I'm complaining because as others have said, its just too poorly optimized and isn't well balanced in terms of unlocks, vehicle power available vs the ai driver difficulty going against you, etc. The other thing that annoys me a lot is the way it looks when you hit a ramp and you need to rotate the car quickly in order to land on the other side of the ramp.. It can be so fast and so hard to even see ahead of the track to know what direction you need to rotate.. I shouldn't have to memorize tracks in order to keep up with that. Its annoying AF.. I wish it would at least indicate which direction you need to rotate. Im not asking for it to be easier, I just want to be able to mentally keep up with the next move needed like it does when it indicates turns, winds, hills, etc as you race.All in all, its the fastest pace racing game I have ever played and its pretty rewarding to get good at. I think in time as they balance out the ai handicaps, unlock parts requirements, make future upgrades a bit more in reach, fix the stupid jump rotations to be more visible before hitting them, and finally, spend some time investing into the multiplayer interface, matchmaking, invite system, and scoring post race, it could be an awesome game. I am hesitant to recommend it right now for the reasons above. I am glad to own it and still play but it can be very annoying at the same time.Cmon devs, pay attention to the common complaints you're getting for Redout 2.. Don't ignore them and then wonder why your game dies in a few months.. Be better than that!

_childDocuments_.review: I'm absolutely sucked into this it's just perfect for me. I love the new risk reward system with how the heat and health bars react to each other on maps you know well you can pretty much be always boosting your shields and heat should never be full otherwise you're just wasting potential speed and once you under stand this the game becomes so much fun and just stupid fast. there is a lot of shortcut potential with the ability to get of the track and boost onto another part of the track I accidentally skipped an entire loop doing that cant wait to see some of you speed runners in time trials. _childDocuments_.review: I would like to preface that I have never played the original Redout game or any anti-gravity racer before, so I cannot give a comparison. However, as someone new entering the genre and franchise I have been blown away by the visuals, the amazing high octane gameplay, and just how fun the game is. The game is challenging but very rewarding especially when you are finally able to make a turn perfectly or beat that time trial that was troubling you before. The game puts you in the deep end, giving you a pretty crappy first car that isnt the best at cornering or strafing. It kind of acts as you training wheels so you can get a feel of the game. I have unlocked 4 cars atm. The game becomes a lot easier when you get the 2nd and 4th car. Makes you feel like a badass going around a massive bend at over 1000km/hr. The are a few issues with the game however. I would say that this game is definitely not for everyone, and the poor design of the tutorials don't help either. For example, there is a mechanic called "Boost stacking" and the way the progression works is that you unlock the tutorial missions as you progress through the game. However, you kind of need to using this mechanic the beat a lot of the missions before you can even unlock the tutorial. The deliver of the tutorials themselves are pretty poor also, It slows down time awkwardly to teach you and it just doesn't work that great. Another issue/bug that I have encountered was on one of the tartarus mines races where some of the AI would teleport 4km ahead of me at the start of the race. luckily I was able to catch up and beat them. Bit of an all over the place review but the bottom line is that the game is very very fun. There is a tone of races to do in the campaign and the game for me is a great mix of challenging and fun. I play on redout difficulty and I havnt had any issues with winning races. I wouldn't recommend this game to someone who is bad at racing games however, there is a bit of a skill filter.

_childDocuments_.review: The previous game, Redout 1 is a fantastic futuristic racing game. Roller coaster tracks requiring you to pitch your craft up and down, beautiful vistas, a complex steering and strafing system, different(or no) gravity on some tracks leading to wild track design with huge jumps or free flying sections, fantastic sense of speed, great electronic soundtrack.Redout 2 has all of that and tries to build on it in three key areas:1. HandlingThe handling is much tighter than in the previous game. It is much easier to avoid the walls and thus tactical grinding or bouncing off the walls is just not the way to go anymore. A good change over all, sacrificing a slight bit of the flavor of the original for an overall tighter experience.2. Skill FloorThe game has a wide range of AI difficulty options. Sadly this doesn't do anything for events without AI as far as I know(time trials and speed events).The game has a tutorial that the predecessor lacked, although it is not great, a bit annoying and weirdly structured (some of it only unlocks once you've already done other campaign races)The game has asssists you can enable in the menu without penalty. If you don't know how to steer, strafe, roll or not blow up from boosting, you can hand it off to AI.The game has a rewind system. A few times per race, depending on the difficulty you can pause the game and go maybe 20 seconds into the past to correct your most recent mistake.3. Skill CeilingYou have two different boosts on three seperate cooldowns(heat, health and hyperboost ability). Boosting with full heat depletes health. You can combine both boosts at the same time for massive speed for massive health costs. Managing these bars cooling down each at their own pace is key.You can control your roll in the air now. You can choose during some jumps where to land and you can adjust your craft accordingly. Also there's a system in place rewarding a perfect landing in pitch and roll with a free speed boost.You can take off of the tracks if you pitch up and boost over a bump in the track, allowing more creativity, but this also influenced track design where some alternate paths can be reached by actually jumping off the track instead of sticking to it. As it stands, it is a pretty great sequel. It's still a bit rough around the edges right now, especially for newcomers I'd imagine. But sticking with this game and improving at it will be very rewarding.I'm personally very happy with this game and having a lot of fun with its challenges. Looking forward to more updates and patches.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall an incredible game, the pinnacle of anti-grav racers and a worthy successor to Redout 1.Pros:* Looks fantastic, nice colourful, shiny graphics and beautiful art design* Runs great on my GTX1070, solid 57-60 FPS on max settings* Blazing fast sense of SPEEEEEEEEEEEEED, playing this game is like an injection of DMT straight to the brain* Overall a hard game. However there is lots of lower difficulty settings and AI assist controls (where the AI will control some things) to help people who want a more chill experience, or people who might be missing fingers etc* The courses are truly crazy, like the world's most epic rollercoaster* A great soundtrack (although I think Redout 1s soundtrack is slightly better)* A huge career mode with 250 events and loads of upgrades for your ship* Tons of cosmetic upgrades as well, colours, liveries etc which you unlock in the career* There is global leaderboards for time attack in arcade mode* Actually has some lore, which is niceNeutral:* A more involved control scheme than most other racers. There is steering, accelerate, brake, boost, hyper boost, boost pads on the track, pitching, strafing and rolling in midair.Cons:* The speed events are currently disproportionately hard, much harder than races. This really needs a balance pass from the devs.* The unlocks in career could stand to be a bit faster paced at the start. Later on you have tons of options to customise your ship, but early on it's too limited.* The difficulty and AI assist options don't unlock until after the first few tutorials* Multiplayer is currently pretty bare bones. You can form a group with friends, and queue for races. But the ranked mode isn't working yet (it's planned), there is no lobbies yet, and no player cards yet.

_childDocuments_.review: Still delivering the fantasy.Like the original Redout, this is hands down the best version of that WipEout / F-Zero experience available today, and terms of concept I think it's an improvement on its' predecessor, stripping out the 'weapons' in favour of a more F-Zero style boost / hull strength balancing act, with the customisation going back into the performance parts you pick.It is however, not for the faint of heart: where the original Redout rewarded you for excellence, Redout II punishes you mercilessly for anything but perfection.  Thankfully, races vs the AI are a little more manageable after a day 1 update, but some of the time-attacks and speed events feel downright impossible without the perfect ship and part selection.All in all? _childDocuments_.review: In short, this game is an improvement over the original in (nearly) every regard.I had plenty of issues with the original. While it could be fun in some regards, I couldn’t recommend it both because it grew stale rather quickly and because of a lot of issues I had with it, many of which are addressed and fixed in this sequel.- The biggest is that ships are no longer extra floaty now. In the first game, even ships with high grip handled like flying bricks and were super-slippery. Now ships are more solidly connected to the tracks and move the direction they’re supposed to and strafing is much more responsive. I admittedly struggled with it at first as I was not expecting it to be as responsive as it was, but I got used to it. Beforehand, it was hard to take even soft turns without bumping the walls, but on that note...- Wall-bouncing is no longer a thing. In the first game, the fastest lap route was not a clean lap, and often bouncing off the walls would be faster than taking the lap clean, odd as that may sound. Now hitting the walls is very punishing and getting a clean lap will be faster, as it should be.- Gone are the useless upgrades and power-ups in favor of a more focused boost mechanic. In the first game, there were plenty of power-ups one could apply to their ship. But, most of them were only useful if you were just starting out, and it would become clear that AP (extra acceleration and speed) and turbo boost were the strongest pairing while all others became obsolete. Now they’ve focused it all down to a simple boosting mechanic instead, with the ability to customize the stats of your craft.- The boosting is quite sophisticated, too. Boosting builds up heat, and boosting while overheating will drain your health. You can use a simple boost, or a super-boost that needs charging. Or combine the two for extra speed. But along with this, the “thrust” stat means boosts are more powerful and heat less, while durability not only means taking more punishment but also that the ship can take more overheating before exploding. This allows even ships with durability as its main selling point to stay competitive in the game, something which wasn’t so much a factor in the first. You’re even rewarded for braking to take turns, too, as braking cools your ship off faster!- Tracks are overall much more intuitively laid out, and there’s even a rally-style warning system to alert you of turns and hazards coming up so you have adequate time to prepare for them. This has helped me out a lot and I wish more AG racers had that! It’s not perfect, though, as some warnings show up too late and some are bugged (there’s one track on Mars that warns of a U-turn that doesn’t exist). Overall, a welcome addition!- AI is much more competitive now. In the original, the AI quickly became obsolete and, once you kinda knew what you were doing, they stopped being much of a challenge unless you really screwed up. Here there’s a constant pressure on you from them, and you really need to get used to abusing the boost system to get ahead.Although that brings in the biggest criticism I have of the game. It. Is. HARD. I’m normally pretty okay with this, and it works really well for the game and the devs’ vision behind it, but right out of the tutorial you get thrown into a race which is extremely punishing and brutal. After that, the game remains challenging, but reasonably so...mostly. Speed events (where you score points by remaining above a set speed) are extremely unforgiving and I struggle to even reach bronze on many of them.Overall, my criticisms pale compared to praises, and overall I feel the game is a massive improvement over the original!

_childDocuments_.review: Good game.Very steep learning curve though. This game's 1st race picks up where the Redout 1's campaign left off (at least without DLC) in terms of difficulty, it feels.There are 5 or 6 different difficulty settings which ought to counteract this, though it baffles me that this only applies to the AI opponents, not the hardcoded scores fore some modes. 2 game modes (time trials, and "Speed" challenges - where you gather points essentially only when hyperboosting) are completely unaffected by the difficulty options. (Devs! Please fix this, scale the scores by the difficulty!)For people returning from Redout 1, please note that the gameplay is focused around a new mechanic, which might not be to your liking necessarily. (More on that later)Gone are the equipment choices from Redout 1. Every car has the magnetic grip module, every car has the hyper boost module. Instead there is a tuning system, similar to many other racing games. Playing the campaign unlocks new tuning parts, transforming your subsonic soap box into a hyper sonic lightning bolt over time.The way you unlock those parts is strictly linear (The same applies to cars & cosmetics). While I like the constant drip-feed of new items, I recognize the blandness and grindy nature of this approach.Gone are also the vehicle classes. Every manufacturer has only 1 car to offer. Based on the installed tuning parts it gets a score - determining on which events it may be used.The main new gimmick of this game is boost stacking. You got 2 different boosts: One which you can use at any time and dose to your liking, and a hyperboost, which charges up until it can be activated. The trick is, that you can use both boosts simultaneously, catapulting you forwarding with absolutely ridiculous speed. What is counter intuitive: Boost stacking is more effective than using both boosts after each other. It gets explained briefly in a tutorial, but in my opinion this has to be taught as one of the 1st things in this game.Gone is the energy bar of the 1st game, instead there is a heat bar. Any kind of boosting heats up your car. At max heat it damages your car, but you can keep boosting as long as you want (and have health to spare)The cars repair quickly when not taking an damage for a few seconds. So where in Redout 1 the focus was on mastering the track, and the boost being a simple button tap when appropriate, in Redout 2 the focus is on mastering the new double boost mechanic. In addition to mastering the track.I was unsure whether I like this. But it grew on me after I got the hang of it after a few hours. However that makes Redout 2 certainly more difficult than the 1st game.Gone is also the awesomeness of the soundtrack, sadly. The music is what I would call "an okay background noise" - its not annoying, just very forgettable :(If you don't mind a considerable challenge, this game is pretty fun. As a casual arcade racer it somewhat fails, stemming from the missing difficulty scaling on ~ 1/3 of all races in the campaign.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been keeping an eye on other opinions of this game, and I'll agree with the consensus that this game is tough - and probably daunting for newcomers to Redout and AG racing games. But I have to say that I love the challenge. This game isn't without its flaws, and I have complaints of my own, but the priority from the developers seems to be replay value - and this game definitely has it if you want it.I have played mostly campaign so far, but even experimenting a bit with the maxed out ships in the Arcade mode has led me to the conclusion that the racing itself is nearly flawless. I think the mid-air/flight controls are a bit frustrating and un-intuitive (rotating your ship with the d-pad??), but the handling and raw speed of this game are just so sublime. To me, it's like F-Zero GX and Wipeout 3 had a nearly perfect baby. No weapons, but if you want a challenging racing game where speed kills, this is it.There is a ton of content in this game, with 36 huge tracks (27 + 9 boss tracks that combine the 3 individual layouts from each location). Each ship has its own suite of visual customizations ranging from minor and hard/impossible to see mid race, to silhouette altering eye candy that you can enjoy if you race with the chase camera. The campaign has a huge amount of events, and incentive to retry them so you can unlock more things. Some unlocks are not great, and I wish there were an easier way of accessing different ships, but I certainly can't accuse the developers of giving me a barebones singleplayer experience.Lastly, I just want to reiterate that this game is not easy to pick up and play. You need to give yourself some time with the controls and you'll be hitting "Restart" often. Try not to get discouraged and push yourself to play better. It's such an intense and fun feeling to hold off another racer as you barrel down to the finish line at 1300 km/h, while the music is blasting along with the beat of your ship's warning alarm and you desperately try to feather the boost so you don't burn up at the last moment.Great game, 9/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Redout 2

_childDocuments_.review: At first I was hesitating to buy RO2, since I already owned RO1 twice, on the Switch and on Steam, and I was not sure, if the game offered anything new justifying its medium price tag. But some reviews comparing it to my favourite anti-gravity racer, I got curious and could not longer resist. I bought the game... and it is wonderful.This games feels like the modern interpretation of F-Zero GX which is largely due to its modified boost-mechanic. Everytime you boost, heat builds up, and when your heat-bar is full, you ship starts to loose energy. But this does not mean, you should stop, in contrary, just like F-Zero, the game requires that you boost so long until your energy is almost depleted (your ship explodes, if you continue to boost) in order to have a chance on the higher difficulty settings (I am playing on Red-Out). If you stop to boost, the heat sinks and if you manage to avoid any damage for a short periode, the your ship starts to repair itself. Note that these are two independent processes, which means, as long as your heat-bar is not full, you can still boost without delaying your repairs, but of course, the faster you are the more difficult it is not to hit a wall. This adds an additional layer of complexity over F-Zero, but thats not all. You have two kinds of boost, a small one, which you can use at every moment, and a big-turbo boost that needs to recharge. You can also use both simultaneously for hyper-speed and extreme heat build up. This risk and reward system is together with the thight controls addicting.Many negative reviews are complaining over the difficulty. Maybe there was a patch, but I had no bigger difficulties in beating the AI-pilots on the level "Red-Out" and I am not an expert player. I could not witness any extraordinary Rubber-Banding, I often finish the race with one kilometer distance, but I also make extensive use of my boosters, always depleting almost all of my energy. Other challenges are more difficult, but I am fine with getting a gold medal only after a few tries, since you can also continue with much easier bronze medal and also because my expectation of an anti-gravity game is to be a hard game. Some people mentioning that the soundtrack is less memorable, and they are right. The different tracks are inferior to the one of its predecessor, if you want to listen to them like to an ordinary music track. But they are superior in supporting the game play, together with the remaining sound design, the warn signals when you overheat or take too much damage, they produce a rush of speed and adrenalin.If you are a fan of F-zero, I recommand this game to you. But you are more in line with WipeOut and you liked RO1 because it was similar to WipeOut, you may not like the new play style. But this is something you will immediately notice in the first two seconds of the game. So maybe you should try it and refund it, if you dont like it.

_childDocuments_.review: Bigger tacks, better tracks, harder tracks, FASTER TRACKS.Redout 2 is most certainly harder than the original if only due to the sheer complexity of the tracks.but that complexity is EXCITING. branches, shortcuts, switches all make for a dynamic racing experience instead of the same track loop over and over. the handing model is much more finely tuned and enjoyable. the graphics are beautiful, especially the lighting and reflections, though you may need to turn graphics down since the game is genuinely difficult to play at too low a frame rate due tot he sheer speed.I have my minor gripes about the upgrade and progression system, as well as the way you unlock liverys and colours schemes. Id prefer a credit system for sure, but that doesn't overall kill the gameplay for me.overall, gets a good 9/10 from me. there's some things that need polishing that may yet come with updates, most of my gripes are minor.

_childDocuments_.review: It's Wipeout but harder. Controls are quite technical and after about halfway through B Class I've gotten a second chassis and it's not bad. Honestly I'm excited to continue playing, but not excited to see where this difficulty goes from here. The AI rubber band themselves from over 1.2KM deficits through really bendy spots that B class shouldn't be able to, and I'm just barely scratching the wins. Another issue connected to this is trying to get the 4th star on most races, with the AI being able to just snap to you at about the 75% point in a race (watched mutiple 800M leads get closed immediately starting at that point) it's really frustrating to try and get 'Win by 500M' or ' Win by 1.0 Sec" when the AI (even with lower or equal vehicles) just gets to keep these stars out of reach until I can come back fully upgraded. I enjoy the little history bits, reminds me of podracer 64 and its little planet facts from the hosts.Theres an ok amount of ships but each has many customizable parts. Customizable in that you can select premade parts, liveries, paint palettes, but I wish you could at least mix&match some of those pieces more.Picked it up because I heard it had a really reasonable solo campaign and so far that is not disappointing (outside of the aforementioned star issue) Would recommend picking up if you're willing to grind and really feel success when you get those corner strafes right. But it may not be quick for all. If you're really unsure, I'd grab it on sale. But if this game can have these small issues cleaned up (as most games attempt to) then I'd say this is happily one of my new favorite racing games.

_childDocuments_.review: Redout 2 straddles this strange line between arcade insanity and technical precision.  This is *not* f-zero or any of the other old sci-,fi racers. Redout has so much crammed into vehicle control that is hard to get a handle on.  To understand this game, we need to talk controls.As with most racers there's accelerate, break, turn left and right.  Instead of the slide or drift mechanics common to arcade racers we have the ability to strafe left or right. I'll get back to this.  We can also pitch the nose of the car up or down to maintain traction and avoid bottoming out on the track.  Finally there's not one but two different boost mechanics. They both generate heat and damage your vehicle, but one is time gated, and they can be stacked for extreme speed.  The game doesn't really explain this and it's required to finish the tutorial.   Finally, we have boost pads on the track like many other arcade games.These mechanics combine to to create a few unique things you have to pay attention to during a race. First is the pitch mechanic that adds just one more thing to think about as the track whips in every direction.  Second is the strafe mechanic. Racing lines have a different meaning when you can strafe to tighten turns or fix heading coming out of one, and when you're having to hit the boost pads. In some instances you can avoid steering entirely. Finally is the dual boost mechanics. Health in redout is a resource. The best drivers will abuse boosting to be within a sliver of life left, and in most cases after stacking a boost you end up entering the following corner with entirely too much speed.In addition to all the control complexity, (and I didn't even touch flight controls) the game also has differ gravity, heat, atmospheric density, and hazards on different tracks, I have confirmed how the atmospheric density works yet, but most of the others do what you expect, including a black hole that changes gravity in different areas of the track.Redout 2 is a fantastic sequel and improves in the gameplay of the original and takes it from being a standard arcade racer to its own unique experience. I can't wait to see how the leaderboards develop over time.

_childDocuments_.review: Different than redout 1, but in a good way i think. The controls are slightly more complex (with the addition of mid-air roll and pitch) and they've let go of the active abilities and ship energy in favor of a more in depth boosting system. Both generating speed and finding ways to maintain it got etched into the core of the game moreso than its predecessor making it far more punishing if you have difficulty with that.However, with the new addition of the "AI assistance" function you can still race without needing to instantly learn how to perfect strafing and mid-air control. Additionally this function can be tinkered to your personal liking letting you play the game however you like, Rookie or Redout Professional alike.Should you not want to grind through the campaign to unlock all of the ship parts, and instead just get right into the multiplayer, the game provides a decent preset garage that can be used from the get-go so you don't have to worry about all the tinkering.Overall:Good game if you like racing games,Great game if you want total control of your vehicle,   The best game if you're like me and love all of these things and all the tinkering the game lets you do.

_childDocuments_.review: After nearly 60 hours of playtime in a 2 week period, I can say this game is very good. Some of the most fun I've had in a racing game, ever. Huge skill ceiling, a meaty campaign with tons of unlockables, and a very solid collection of tracks for 30 dollars. To be more in depth with the track design, its a step up from Redout 1 in nearly every way. They twist, wind, and invert in many fun and unique ways that reward mastery with the new boost system and just how much more grippy the ships are this time around.       Special mention to Neo Calima which is a remix of Calima from Redout 1, Sisyphus being a windy and challenging early game track that features tricky turns and heat management, Mistral for its incredibly unique jump at the end of the track, Ahti for having very fun rotation jumps, Neo Roppongi for its tight and precise turns through the city, all 3 Genesis tracks for having amazing track flow, and Sputnik for being an incredible track set right next to a black hole. Every single zone is unique and varied to have its own style of driving and track design with different environmental modifications to fit each location, like the atmosphere being set to 'Dense' in the Mariana Trench since you race underwater there, causing more drag to be generated losing you speed faster than normal.       Every track can be played backwards too, some of those being even better than the normal version like Mistral, Ixion and Neo Shinagawa. Overall the track design is brilliant and that's more than enough reason to spend hours grinding for top leaderboard spots on your favorite maps.      The soundtrack is also excellent and features some great music that can stand up with Redout 1's superb soundtrack. Big shoutouts to Raging Revolution (Time Attack Mix) which plays in Genesis, Lights Out which plays in Origin Black Hole, and Gaijin's Prooving which plays in Neo Tokyo.        However, the career mode has a crazy high difficulty spike extremely early on in the game that will cause frustration to people that are less experienced. It's not very beginner friendly. What does help though is that if you can push through B League and early A League, the game becomes monumentally easier the further you get. I'm struggling less with the highest league tier on Nightmare compared to B League, the difficulty balancing is awful for the start of career mode. If you are interested in getting the game, I'd recommend joining the Redout discord for tips and advice if you want to get better, especially during the early game.       But overall, once you've really mastered the games mechanics, nearly every track in the game becomes a ton of fun to drive on and it's just pure racing fun. It's just a steep climb at the start of the game that can drive people away from getting to experience that fun.       For me, this game is giving some other games I've played this year a serious run for its money as my GOTY, even in its current unbalanced and rough state. And it's only going to get better as the game gets updates.

_childDocuments_.review: Redout 2 = 1000+ kph Flow State GeneratorI really like the direction they took this sequel. _childDocuments_.review: For most of the review, I’ll be comparing the game to the original Redout. Just like its predecessor, this game is not easy, although I would say that it is definitely easier to pick up. It’s not for everyone, so bear that in mind as you read on.Gone are the days where you have to choose between enhanced grip or speed boost in order to get the bets lap time. Everyone has the exact same abilities: a small boost and a big boost. You are in charge of using them at the right time to maximize your speed.The small boost and big boost increase your heat, which when maximized, causes your ship to overheat and eat into your health. You can use the small boost for as long as you want, until you run out of health. The big boost is on a cooldown, but canceling the big boost reduces its cooldown, allowing you to use it more frequently. If you want to go REALLY fast, you can combo them together, but this further increases the rate at which your ship heats up, and it’s easy to destroy your ship if you’re not careful.The steering mechanics are in theory the same as the original Redout, but in practice feel very different. If I were to compare the two, Redout 2 steering feels more precise, and a bit more responsive than Redout. Redout 2 feels less like you’re piloting a ship and more like a car, as many others have said. Make no mistake, however, because you can still strafe just like before. As with the previous game, strafing is absolutely essential to getting better at the game and earning faster lap times. Pitching your ship into a loop is roughly the same as before; you need to lift your nose up or down in order to avoid scraping and/or maximize speed.Flying seems to be massively improved. Because you have more control overall (even in the air) it makes the portions where you have to fly more enjoyable. Plus, there is an added mechanic where if you land your ship correctly, you get a speed boost. Lastly, there is an assist system that works pretty well. It won’t help you against high difficulty AI, but it can help you on some tricky turns and even show you how you’re supposed to do some of the jumps. You can turn all assist settings up to the max and pretty much just watch the game play itself, albeit with a few wall grinds here an there.The biggest improvement is the inclusion of paste notes! Now, even if you’re new to a map, you’ll at least have a general idea of which direction and how hard to turn.They’ve moved the health and boost away from your ship to the bottom of the screen, making it appear more arcade-like, at the cost having to glance down to check your stats. However, the bars are much brighter and visible, so that’s a plus.You can also see how far ahead/behind you are, with arrows that change color based on how close your opponents are to you.Gorgeous. Stunning. Will the graphics age as well as the low poly scenery in the original Redout? Definitely not. But they managed to achieve a Wipeout-level of polish on most of the surroundings, resulting in more memorable landmarks as you zoom past.The track layouts start out even more tame than in Redout, but quickly evolve into the chaotic twisting and turning mayhem that you know from before. Most of the features you’ve already seen before, like huge loops, spiraling sections of track, and massive jumps. One new addition is divided entryways, where you can choose from 2 different routes. Oh, and the tracks are WAY longer too! Many of them take 1-2 minutes or more to complete a lap!I will say that there are jumps where there is an uncomfortable amount of air time, and portions where even with the paste notes, not knowing exactly how to pitch and steer your ship before going off of a jump presents a huge problem. There are also parts where it it is unclear where or when to land your ship, and in a last ditch attempt, you may be forced to land sideways or upside down.There are six in total, and they’re all great, except Speed. I don’t know why they they didn’t just keep Speed the same as the previous game, but here you can earn more points the faster you go, and there is a time limit instead of a lap limit. It sounds good in practice, but it makes is more frustrating because there’s not a clear target anymore, which makes it harder to gauge how fast you REALLY should be going. Plus, the difficulty scaling on Speed is actually ridiculous -  I have yet to get a gold time for most of the events.There’s not much to say about Race, Arena Race, Last Man Standing, Boss, and Time Attack. They’re all good, with plenty of available difficulty scaling for the AI. The Time Attack levels can be pretty tough, but not as ridiculous as the Speed events.There are double the difficulties from before! One of the biggest complaints in the orignal Redout was that the hardest difficulty wasn’t hard enough. That is definitely no longer the case! I’ve played numerous races using the 3rd highest difficulty (“Redout”) and it’s a decent challenge. Only the most skilled players would be able to win a race against the highest difficulty of “Nightmare” – which is precisely how it should be. Everyone should be able to enjoy the game at whatever level they feel comfortable.The AI also seems to be better at using boost in this game. There are many instances where the AI will actually prepare to use boost directly coming out of a corner instead of waiting another second to use it on a straightaway. One of the main points of using boost is to accelerate back up to a reasonable speed quickly, and seeing the AI use it in this way makes it feel like you’re playing against real people.You can play with friends, or just join a match. When enough people ready up, you start. This makes things simple enough, and is better from the perspective that matchmaking will get you in a game sooner. Apparently there’s going to be competitive in the future, but I can’t help but wonder how they’re going to deal with cheaters – they were definitely rampant in the previous game. Sadly no splitscreen.There are currently a few issues I’ve noticed:-Glaring respawn issues.-Some maps don’t have a barrier going completely around the track, causing you to fly off in that direction forever.- In multiplayer, you sometimes get put into a race after it has already started. Whether or not this is intentional, it’s frustrating to play if you’re already behind.-As already stated, the difficulty of some events (mostly the Speed events) needs to be turned down a notch. I’ll update this review as I play more as well, particularly if the issues get fixed. Like I said earlier, definitely recommend this to anyone who likes challenging AG's! It feels different from Redout, and so I recommend giving it a try even if you haven't played the first one.

_childDocuments_.review: I've never played an anti-gravity racer before. I jumped into this game understanding it'd be extremely difficult. I find it extremely enjoyable and very satisfying. _childDocuments_.review: First of all, I'm very disappointed about how hard this is when you want to compete your opponents in Arcade mode. The mechanics are easy to learn, but I hate the fact that I have to watch constantly to a bar, stopping to overheat the engine. I hate the first career mode, it's impossible to finish beneath 1 minute. Even when I find the fastest line, the vehicle is damn too slow! So, how can I beat this to get futher into the league? _childDocuments_.review: Definitely pick up if you're a fan of any hovercraft racer. They're few and far between, and honestly the genre deserves some AAA quality, which Redout 2 comes close to. It's not indie by any means, bringing a lot of professionalism and polish to the table compared to Redout 1, like great visuals, UI, music & audio, etc. But, it could definitely be bigger in scope like a big budget game (more online play / features, which are coming soon with seasons & ranked play). That being said, if you're just interested in singleplayer/offline, it's NOT short by any means, with tons of events and challenges at different tiers to train you up. It might get a bit grating seeing the first seeing the same few tracks with the fancier ones being held for later in Career mode, but that might be because I'm trying to 100% everything / get every star. If you just play through normally, you'll probably be seeing new tracks all the time.It's also a big step up from the original in gameplay. Redout 1 didn't have items or weapons like a lot of other action racers, but it did have 'Abilities', 'Passives', 'Classes' and flat upgrades you could get with winnings. They've all been removed in favour of swapping out internals of your ship, of which there is now only one for each manufacturer/team (but there's a lot more teams). This only really applies during singleplayer career. In multiplayer, everyone gets to use maxed out ships from the get-go, bringing it down to the skill of the player and the choice of the ship for the map being played (some will definitely be more useful on one map than another). But no matter how you play, keep in mind that Redout 2 is a challenging game, it takes some practice to learn how to swerve around a corner with both turning AND strafing, and avoid walls.Boosting also works differently. Instead of being a limited meter that recharges, you can ALWAYS boost, which fills an 'overheat' gauge instead. Once full, it starts draining your ship health to continue boosting, which provides some fun risk/reward to reach higher speeds, and more caution to avoid bumping walls to start health regen sooner for more boost, rather than worrying about health as some separate isolated thing. E.g. if you're confident with a track, you can keep running your ship within an inch of its life for the best speed, but one mistake could have you respawning!All in all, it might be annoying at first to be bumping into everything, but once you get the hang of it and make a flawless lap with the music pumping and the sound/visual design on the speed, Redout 2 is a blast.And yes, the trailer music is in the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Redout 2

_childDocuments_.review: One of those games where you can feel yourself improving after each race. Very rewarding to play, and lots to master.I noticed the boosting tutorial was over-tuned, and it was nerfed shortly after I conquered it.However, in the brutality of the tutorial, it does teach you a fairly vital part of this game: Using both boosts at the same time (when you are able; between overheating you want your ship to regenerate) and use your health as an extra boost meter. But try not to explode, obviously.Also, feather the brakes on turns, and feel free to let go of the gas as well. I am still improving myself. Again, there's a lot to learn, but so far I'm enjoying my time. The soundtrack is also full of bangers.

I'll try to get that progress again on another time. Ill talk about how the game feels later.) I was doing good against the Ai till seconds before the first lap ended... one of the Ai just flew past me. thought it was cause they had boost, so I thought nothing of it. Later, near the mid, the Ai passed me again, and I went to 2nd place. The other racer passed me and stayed that way till the end netting me a bronze medal. I imagine new players would have a HARD time trying to get into the game: and even when it came to the earlier missions to get used to the controls, I disliked how they slowed time to force you to make the basic moves such as: moving left, moving right, and don't forget, strafing! I'm going to need a lot of time to get used to burning my health to go faster while not smashing myself into the walls. ALSO, I did not mention in the first paragraph, but the boost (it felt more natural to add it here) feels off with regards to regular boosting and hyperboosting. I read around that people had issues with the boosting level since they had to learn to mix hyperboosting and regular boosting to beat it, I simply mixed the two and beat it with silver since I was scraping the walls a lot. During the race, it seemed that there is a delay between hyper boosting and turning off the boost, so I had to restart the race since I came in 4th (which should still give the new players a star or something at this current stage of difficulty. And as much as it is a sequel, I rather liked how the first game had their events and progression: after a few training levels, here: play in all these events to see what you like.) and I even still had issues in the rematch with it not turning off the hyperboost when I want it to. Thankfully, I beat it, but mayhaps I have yet to get a grasp of the mechanics. My first kart from Redout 1 was the Koniog (or however you spelled it) and I used all that extra health to safely get to terms with the game as I had not put lots of time into racing games, let alone anti-grav racers. I like to try new games that seem interesting, and I was glad I got the first game, but after the recent update to the first game, and now how this game feels, its a weird change, but I'll stick with it to see how it goes.Other issues have to be the introductions to tracks have audio issues with the narrator, and some weird visual stuff, but I don't really mind it too much, I overlook lots of stuff, since I'm sure making a game is no walk in the park.I was hooked by the music from the first game, and same here so far as some musical artists worked here too is awesome. however, I'll simply say as a warning, the game feels weird as a veteran, and I imagine perhaps unfair to the new racers. Ill still recommend it, but beware, it has a few "interesting" design choices.(Edit 1) Just got to the second race with Ai (after typing this long-ass thesis) and I will have to reiterate the fact that the Ai a "tad" bit too powerful versus you. I may just be a bad player, but it really feels like the Ai is just better than you and not because they have rubber-banding (you don't) or that the Ai know the maps better than you do, but they seem to have better equipments. *I can't really tell since I don't know all the parts very well*(Edit 2) New patch rolled out, but I guess it helped(?) but I have a slightly better understanding of the boost mechanic now. I am still not familiar with it, but I am welcoming it so far. _childDocuments_.review: This is the first game of its kind where I feel that no matter how insane your speed is, you always have full control of your ship and your gameplay: the main feature of the game is a peculiar control system which lets you accelerate, break and steer as normal, in addition to lateral strafing as well as tilting your ship up and down, while you'll boost throughout the entire races, pushing your vehicle to its absolute limits to get as much speed as you can - literally, since your health is essentially a second boost bar that regenerates over time.You have this sense of high risk high reward that permeates the entire experience, and even in time trials you'll be on your toes, fully focused on everything that's going on without ever feeling overwhelmed by it. It's an absolute blast that I would recommend any fan of the genre, or any fan of racing and speed in general.Just, no matter what experience you have with previous games, when you start your singleplayer career, don't expect to win. The game is NOT designed to be won when you first start, which seems to throw off many, many people who believe the difficulty to be badly balanced.At the start you have a weak, standard ship. Your enemies have upgraded ones, and they'll know the game mechanics better than you, since the tutorial unlocks bit by bit as you progress the first races and won't fill you in on everything you need to know right away. No matter how much experience you have from other games, you'll likely lose.BUT, you'll progress anyway, because unlocking your ship's upgrades, as well as new ships, only requires you to get 1 star out of 4 in events, which, in a normal race, means getting third place out of 4 contenders (max stars only gives you cosmetics). It's something challenging but reasonable, a simple goal you'll have to chase as you learn the game, unlock new tutorials to further understand the game mechanics, and gradually get your vehicle up to speed with the others. In due time, you'll start fighting for second place, and before you know it you'll suddenly be winning, consistently - and it's an incredible feeling of growth and progression, no other game has ever given me.And then, the game will throw you a roadblock, telling you "you need more stars to unlock the next event". And you'll go back to the first races you couldn't win, and this time you'll be competing on even grounds, and finally push your way to victory.It's a beautiful experience all through and through, and it's so sad to see so many people being thrown off because they couldn't get first place right away. Just go with the flow the game guides you through, and you'll have no issue growing to the point where you'll dominate the races you once dreaded.For the rest, this game fixes every single problem I had with the first Redout - the tracks are now much easier to see even at incredible speeds, designed to let you know what kind of turns and twists are coming next, also with the help of little indicators at the top of the screen. "Weapon"-like special abilities are removed, and everything is a pure blooded race now, and thanks to the increased grip of your ship dying from impacting the walls is now a very rare occurrence, which is a big plus considering you'll spend a lot of time on the verge of destruction to push your speed to the max. Every track is truly beautiful, the dynamic music fits the action's pace perfectly, and there's not a single dull moment in the entire experience. And the content, just the singleplayer alone has hundreds of races and unlocks with great replayability due to its progression system encouraging you to return to past events to get more stars. It's incredible, and more game modes and contents are going to come in the future, too.This game is probably the best racing game I've ever played, and it breaks my heart to see so many people bashing it just because it's different from Redout 1 instead of keeping the exact same gameplay. Give it a try and don't be discouraged by its difficulty, as you learn and grow you will not be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright first impressions: A worthy sequel to Redout 1.Some others have said that there are performance issues and some bugs, I've luckily not experienced any and the game runs buttery smooth on highest settings, there will of course be some kinks to iron out after release like with any game but this launch has been flawless for me.I'm so excited to race in a fresh Redout experience again!
_childDocuments_.name: Redout 2

_childDocuments_.review: I shouldn't leave a review only after playing it for 1h, but I saw some negative reviews there and feel the need to post my first impressions right now as the game is released. Obviously I'll come back to update this after playing more. The new system works wonders, truly. You gotta drive and think about how you're gonna use your boost ; just hyperboost, or coupled with normal boost, but then your health will go down faster ? So am I gonna get to 5hp and make sure not to hit a single wall, or play it safer because the upcoming turns are tough ? And then what remaining hp is acceptable ?Do I trigger the hyperboost right as I have it in order to be efficient, or is it really not gonna be worth it because of my health / the curves ahead ?All that while going at 1000km/h :) Some people may not like it, but to me that's actually a very clever way to have two things to think about, that other racing games would do through the usual item system.The weapon system from Redout 1 just did not work (it felt useless) : having the focus on managing your speed and health and getting the curves pitch-perfect is exactly the direction the game needed to take. As for the tutorial difficulty : I literally exploded my car from overheating (one particular rotating straight line is... very exciting to boost in) and still managed to get 1st on my first try. I'm not even that good, as I remember getting owned in Redout 1 multiplayer. And since dificulty (+ assists, although I think it's better without any of those) can be tweaked after that, I wouldn't consider difficulty an issue. As for performance : I run a 2060Super, and am getting 80 fps (so far, I don't know if some future tracks are more demanding) on 1440p with high on settings (except shadow on medium) and epic on antialiasing. So, pretty good I'd say.Cheers!
_childDocuments_.name: Redout 2

_childDocuments_.review: 3 Hours in I think I've a good handle of the mechanics and upgrade system, and even then the AI on easier difficulties is cracked to high hell. In old arcade high speed games (extreme g, jet moto) and as far as I remember, I don't recall racing games being this frustratingly hard. The vehicles feel slidey and non-responsive for these speeds and amount of curves.I would be hard pressed to go through another... what 10-20 hours of crushing defeat thanks to the AI and handling.Visuals and music are really good which makes that much more frustrating as even starting out the AI is annihilating you from making just a couple mistakes.
_childDocuments_.name: Redout 2

_childDocuments_.review: Hold off until there's some balance patches, especially if you're new.Difficulty for some of the early tracks seems extremely overtuned (especially the Speed tracks, which don't seem to get easier when you reduce the game difficulty); just getting a Copper medal on some of the speed tracks requires almost flawless play for two straight laps, including knowledge of ideal boost patterns. I'm fine with gold being unreachable without spending a while practicing, but especially this early in the game it should be fairly easy to land a copper and decently achievable to get a silver. I'm also getting the occasional graphical bug in cockpit view where the camera seems to slip inside of the ship every now and then, usually after a hard landing or similar. Not sure exactly what causes it but it blocks all visibility when it happens, which isn't great in a high speed racer.I like the risk/reward system of using your health pool as additional boost. I am concerned that as the tracks get more technical, the novelty will wear off, since the target numbers for good laps seem to assume that you are burning your health as a resource regularly, and not just for an extra burst of speed at the very end, but for now it's fun.Overall the racing feels great; the problems are mainly the overtuned difficulty (especially the target numbers in time trial and speed events; racer AI became a lot more satisfying when I turned the difficulty down) and the odd bug. Hopefully this gets fixed soon; as is I imagine a lot of new players will bounce off the early wall, and even returning veterans will probably get frustrated that they're having such a tough time so early in the game when they're still just trying to unlock things.
_childDocuments_.name: Redout 2

_childDocuments_.review: It's definitely a different game from Redout 1. And that's not a bad thing either. It's got the soul and essence of the original, but much of it feels cleaner and nicer. It's also far, far more accessible than it's predecessor as well, with a ton of tuning for ai assistance with controls if you should need it. The game is gorgeous, the audioscape is great, and the soundtrack is a banger too. Few games give you the feeling of real speed like the Redout series so expertly manages to do.If you're into hover racers, you really cant go wrong with Redout 2. It's very well fleshed out with tons of customization options and upgrades to tweak and tune your craft that you unlock through the career. While I personally would have preferred a credit/point buy system ala RO1 style, it works well and forces you to get better.
_childDocuments_.name: Redout 2

_childDocuments_.review: Absolute masterclass of a game. The most fun "arcade" racer i haver ever played.The more i play this game the more i prefer the actual gameplay over the first part. Boost and risk management is a lot of fun and there are quite a few visual and sound aids to help you keep track of your health and your overheat status. Would recommend starting the game on pilot and then progressing to redout after grasping the basics. The tracks themselves feel a lot more diverse and challenging. Some of them offer stunning visuals.Also i like the fact that the AI can blow up too if they go too fast or smash into walls all the time.The new turn-indicators are much appreciated.I don't mind not being able to costumize my vehicle in multiplayer when it comes to tuning because usually what ends up happening is that everyone just ends up using the same parts anyway.Disbanding every lobby after every race in casual multiplayer seems kind of uneccessary...maybe atleast let the people play a cup together or something.The soundtrack is absolutely incredible!Overall i would say its a big upgrade over the first redout despite a few crashes i had when opening the costumization menu. The game still needs some polishing in terms of AI and circuit bugs. For example the game respawning you 20km forwards for some reason.But i am not a huge fan of a day 1 season pass. I sure hope that there won't be multiple seasons...i am done with being expected to spend 100 plus euros for every game.Finally for the love of god please do not split the multiplayer into dlc/non-dlc lobbys. Either you make the new maps available for everyone or restrict them to the singleplayer. Whats also possible is that only 1 player in the lobby needs to have the dlc.
_childDocuments_.name: Redout 2

_childDocuments_.review: The tracks are great. The control of the ships feels spot on. The ship upgrade/customization is deeper than the first game. Boosting has a different mechanic than the first game, adding a heat meter and overheat/health damage. Health is readily replentished and hitting the walls is far less punishing to health. You are far more likely to fall off the track than to die by hitting walls. The active modules are no more and there are still NO WEAPONS! :( Overall this game is super fast and smooth and the tracks are all exciting and fun to play. A very welcomed new version of Redout and aside from no combat racing, is hands down the best hover racer out ther for the second time running!
_childDocuments_.name: Redout 2

_childDocuments_.review: Redout 2 hits all the right notes for an antigrav racer for me. Great visuals, great sound design, great OST, absolutely insane sense of speed... honestly, it makes the first Redout look like a tech demo. Everything just meshes better in the aesthetic and gameplay, and i'm loving it. I especially love how they reworked boost, so instead of your boost being a resource that you run out of, it's heat that you build. Use too much of it and you'll damage your ship, but you'll get the highest speed when you push it over the limit. As a result, you're constantly balancing speed while essentially using your health as a resource, and it makes the moment to moment gameplay so satisfying. However, it's not without issues. There is a pretty nasty difficulty curve at the beginning, but it's worth noting that you don't have to get 1st in the tutorial races. The game selects a difficulty rating and assists depending on how you do at them. You can also unlock upgrades without getting first in every race, which makes things a lot better the further in you go. That said, if you aren't experienced with these kinds of games it might be worth waiting for a patch to make it a tad bit more accessible at the start.
_childDocuments_.name: Redout 2

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent, absurdly fast successor to Redout. I still believe it's the only worthy spiritual successor to F-Zero. The soundtrack is even better than the first, which is saying a lot, the ship customization is excellent (before it was just color schemes and a single upgrade per category that you'd never swap out, now you can tune a ship for handling, boost, speed, etc.). Be wary, there are a few obviously day one bugs that will hopefully get patched quick, nearly all involving the ruthless AI. The AI is extremely overpowered right out of the tutorial until you can get several upgrades to your ship, and this is coming from someone that got all the platinum medals in Redout and multiple top-20 leaderboard times. Even if you lower the difficulty, the rubberband is so bad they'll regularly beat you at any difficulty and set world record times, so don't feel bad until you upgrade your ship into the upper 200s. The AI is also bugged on a few of the volcano (mines) tracks, where they will teleport 5-10 km ahead of you lap over lap, making a couple of the races impossible to beat currently.
_childDocuments_.name: Redout 2

_childDocuments_.review: Lots of early complainers that this game is a bit different than Redout 1. Well, its true. It is also true that F Zero X raced differently than F Zero GX, and Wipeout games all had their nuances. Xtreme G2 was not Xtreme G3.Time moves on, and great racing games are hard to come by. This is one of them. I was 8 when I first played F-Zero X, now pushing 30. Many folks didn't even try Redout 1 because "it isn't like Wipeout". Nostalgia is a powerful thing, and would be a shame to miss out on the Redout series because of dedication to one single other game. In Formula 1, the best championship-title level drivers can adapt to any car setup. Are you seeking a challenge, or the same old?They set out to not just update Redout 1, but refine it. Powerups that were questionable have been refined into upgrades, and the boost system is now about how much you can handle. Get it and enjoy the fact that for $30 someone is still dedicated to making great sci-fi racing games, and that there is a community to race online with every weekend.
_childDocuments_.name: Redout 2

_childDocuments_.review: i think most of the negative reviews on this game so far are the result of conveyance issues, so i want to just use this review to try to clear up the two biggest things people aren't understanding:-you can use regular and super boost at the same time. in fact, you absolutely need to be doing this. the boost tutorial doesn't mention it at all and a lot of people are finding themselves much slower than the game expects them to be because they don't know they can do it. hopefully the tutorial gets updated to mention this-you're not supposed to win races in career mode on the first try. i don't know why they structured it like this without really explaining it, but you're supposed to run through and get 3rd places in events so you can unlock enough upgrades to actually try to win them on the second run through, i guess so you get more mileage out of each event? honestly i don't even mind that system but it's kind of baffling to just expect the player to know they're not meant to win. anyway, once you understand those two things, the game's pretty comparable to redout 1 so far, which is my favorite racing game of all time. there are things i think are steps in the wrong direction, like increased emphasis on correct boosting, but the increased ship customizability and the new areas are pretty cool and i'm liking the new tracks so far. don't let the mixed review score scare you, i'm not going to say the negative reviewers are "mad because bad" but i think a lot of them aren't understanding some of redout 2's... kind of alien, unexplained decisions, is all.
_childDocuments_.name: Redout 2

_childDocuments_.review: Changed my review to a negative. I can't recommend this game.I do not have any issues with the difficulty of the game itself, while a lot of players do. I even took the time to make guides to help other people get Gold / Platinum on speed missions.The sheer amount of things that do not work properly such as..1: Terrain issues.. It is common to lose a track because your ship will clip into the floor itself and start spinning.2: The thrust stat being coded in the reverse (The more thrust you have, the less you can boost) This is double frustrating because at some points in the campaign you're forced to add more mods because of the minimum power your ship can have.. So you have to purposely make your ship worse.3: The tedium. You will have to complete several hundred missions to be able to unlock most upgrades. Until then, you're gatekept out of good scores in multiplayer or arcade.4: The arcade ships themselves suck. This kinda ties in with point 3.5: If something happens to the install of your game, you have to start the whole tedium again.I'm too exhausted by this to even think about more negative points.. Just make sure you know what you're getting into, because blackdesert and maplestory felt less tedious to me than this.And i'm not even sure if anything will change because of the massive amount of positive circlejerking that I see that all the above points are positives.
_childDocuments_.name: Redout 2

_childDocuments_.review: I'm an avid fan of F-Zero GX (my best game ever, completed 100% multiple times and won a few tournaments by Nintendo in 2003-2004). I also played quite a lot of Redout.At first, I wasn't sure about the new gameplay.But after a few tracks, it just clicked. The game is incredibly awesome. Everything I didn't like about the first is not there anymore (especially items). Also, the gameplay is much tighter and feels a little bit more like F-Zero GX. You can also customize controls 100%, which is great (I use the same layout of F-Zero GX and it works like a charm).Just remember that the strafe is mandatory, but doesn't work necessarily like F-Zero. Sometimes, you have to strafe the opposite way of the turn so you can drift a bit and then strafe on the other side so you can take the turn properly (feels like pressing both L+R in F-Zero and then strafe on only one side so you peak the turn at 90 degrees). Learning this, you don't have to brake or release the acceleration at all after,Also, hyperboost + regular boost + on track boosts makes your machine go so much faster and it's satisfying. If you find the game too difficult, you can lower the difficulty.In summary, an extremely good evolution of the Redout series. I'm sad to see it has mixed reviews, but oh well.
_childDocuments_.name: Redout 2

_childDocuments_.review: Previously, I stated that I would not recommend this game, especially due to the difficulty. However, after returning to this game, I have found it to be more bearable. First of all, set your game difficulty to pilot at the most, as the default ai will be very difficult, especially to newcomers.I will say though, the progression is a bit tedious. From what I can tell, the intended progression is to pass the events with some stars, then return to the event with the better gear from higher classes to beat them. It has worked for the most part for me, but I find it to be a bit annoying, especially due to how many events there are in the career. While this is not much of a problem for races if you lower the difficulty, it is apparent with the speed and time trial events, which as far as I can tell has the same records to beat across all difficulties. This is made even worse when getting gold in a time trial is mandatory to get the upgrade.Probably my second biggest gripe is the unlock method for customization. What's that? You want that really cool tip for your ship? Good luck finding the event that unlocks it and pray that it isn't behind getting 4 stars in a time trial where you have to beat gold by 3 seconds for the fourth star.
_childDocuments_.name: Redout 2

_childDocuments_.review: I had a bad time with this game on release, but kept it in my library because I'm a fan of future racers. I went back to it now that it's had a few updates and I'm having a much better time. Good:+ I really like the feel of the race crafts. They feel a lot more solid than the original Redout, and there's less "messy racing" since you no longer want to bounce off the walls for optimal times. Ships do lose speed faster though, so less momentum based strategy (+ or - depending on your taste).+ Looks nice, good sense of speed when it gets going. I will say I have performance issues when I use anything but the highest level of AA... not sure what that's about. Nice ship models with aesthetic customisation. + Game is better balanced now. On release it took forever just to make it through the tutorial. + Game is complicated (turning, pitch, strafe, roll, two kinds of boost), which can be rewarding depending on what you're looking for.+ Dynamic music has its moments.+ Is a future racer.Some things that still irk me a little:- Boost strategy really is a big part of it. Not my thing but not a deal breaker. At least you can set the ship to automatically stop boosting at 5% health, not sure if I overlooked that when it came out or if it's new. It should be on by default IMO, I'm not looking at meters while I race.- Jumps can be annoying for a few reason: Unclear landing position, landing obscured by ship, needing to control turning (left stick), pitch and strafe (right stick) and roll (dpad). I only have two thumbs! I guess this encourages you to line up your jumps so that you at least don't have to worry about one of those dimensions, but many of the jumps are blind for the reasons above, so they're annoying when you start learning them.Old Review:I'm a fan of future racers. I love games like Wipeout, F-Zero and Redout 1. I want to like this game, but it is too in love with boost mechanics and bars filling up. I do not want to watch bars while I'm racing.You have a heat bar that is basically your boost bar. If you boost it fills up, if you stop boosting it cools off. If you boost too much you take damage. If you don't take damage for awhile you repair yourself, so in that sense your health is also like a boost meter that just refills differently. There is also a super boost which relies on a battery filling up. Using the super boost also fills your heat meter the same as a regular boost, and you can regular boost and super boost at the same time. So you have two meters strictly related to boosting, and one meter that is both health and auxiliary boosting, and they are all changing all the time. I don't want to micro manage meters while watching high speed racing. There's just too much strategy around boosting. Do I want to trigger all of my boosts at once for ludicrous speed, or portion out my boosts so that I'm constantly boosting? It's really hard to tell which is more effective.There are also boost pads which are fine because at least they don't have an associated meter I have to watch.I am very sad because this isn't exactly a popular genre (RIP Studio Liverpool) and the original Redout was one of my favorites.
_childDocuments_.name: Redout 2
