_childDocuments_.review: Before the patch, my review was summed up like this:-Too high scores for the Speed 180s and Time Attack challenges-Multitude of bugs-Poor progression system for unlocking everything, AND a lot of it is blocking people from playing multiplayer. Thus a lot of people don't play because they literally can't-AI DOES rubberband. and most often then not, they have better upgrades to their ships. No, it's not just "game good, you're bad". No they legit have higher level upgrades, the scoreboards actually show this-Good controls, handling and speed feels good. Double boost system is fun and rewarding and worth it's riskMy review after the patch is summed up like this:-Decent scores to achieve on Speed 180s and Time Attack Challenges. Although some need to be adjusted-Multitude of bugs, random crashes for entering water in some tracks, disgustingly low FPS drops for no reason at all when I wasn't getting that before this patch-Poor progression system for unlocking everything, AND a lot of it is blocking people from playing multiplayer. Thus a lot of people don't play because they literally can't-Haven't done any races other than the challenges post patch, so I can't say anything about the AI. However 34 did say it was tweaked to be easier in the patch notes-Good controls, handling feels good. But they somehow broke the thrust and boost system with the patch and will wait for the DLC patch to fix it.34...REALLY?! Who is going to buy the DLC when the base game isn't even fleshed out or optimized. The progression system makes me want to NOT play, it's so unrewarding and locking mostly every upgrade behind a backwards speed class system is just stupid. The player feels drained, I can get through maybe 2 challenges before I turn off the game because of how bored I am. The game isn't fun with this progression system. Unlocks are fun if you let the player build up to it, this is just based on pure skill, which might work in some other games. However, this literally blocks progress from playing multiplayer. It's either use, pre-built and uncustomizable ship, or don't play multiplayer till you unlock everything.I'm done with this game, and I can't even get a refund because I really tried to love it.Waste of $30. Don't buy it.

_childDocuments_.review: Having gotten over the honeymoon period I can no longer recommend this game.TL;DR the campaign is a slog, non race events are way too hard and frequent, the manner of unlocking everything is very grindy. Tracks lack wow factor a lot of the time, music is a downgrade.It feels both half baked and as if it is trying very hard to be as dissimilar to redout 1 as possible. Tracks in 2 are much longer, but also slower. Technical sections are frequent but there are also few real setpeices. Stuff like tubes and pipe sections are totally absent and while the offerings have plenty of inversions and jumps (most taken at awkward angles that need midair manoeuvring to land) for the most part the game underutilised the possibilities offered from being anti-gravity and having multiple routes. Instead of clear tiers of ship that grow visually more complex redout 2 features a core roster that you upgrade the performance and look of during your career, I like this.However the rate of unlocks is glacially slow, everything being strictly tied to career progression. If you want x part you must win y event to obtain it. This even extends to the ships themselves whereas in 1 you could unlock and upgrade any ship in any order you wanted via an ingame economy. It is incredibly arbitrary and arcade-like now and due to the slow progression often leaves you well behind the curve performance wise. It's only when going back to earlier races with later unlocks do you have some manner of choice over how you build your ship. When going through the game normally you simply bolt on everything you get as you get it since you are so under powered.This even extends to arcade mode, if you choose to use your own garage of prebuilts the AI will not scale down. Then there is the career itself. It is simply bloated. There are fewer event types this time around and some, like arena race, are so neutered as to be barely different from the basic race. You'll be doing the same races, speed trials and time trials in the same few areas again, and again and again. The original redout somewhat had this problem too of classes only using a small selection of tracks until class 4. The difference is the early classes in 1 went by very quickly. Here it feels like a slow, unrewarding slog of the same events over and over with gradually increasing difficulty. Worse still due to the unlock system of 2 you no longer have the luxury of simply skipping certain events you loathe. Doing so can deprive you of cosmetics, parts and even entire ships as opposed to 1. Then there is the difficulty, Redout 1 was not a particularly difficult game. At least in single player. The real challenge was in multiplayer and leaderboards where people compete for fractions of a second. Still the game did recognise when you were truly fast, having hidden platinum trophies for a number of events. But even if you were legitimately terrible at the game you could see and do everything even if it meant farming the few events you could win over and over to afford all the ships. In 2 the skill floor has been massively increased now even qualifying in speed and timetrial events can be incredibly difficult. Part of this is, again, due to the horrendous unlock system leaving you always weak. But the fact the difficulty options only scale AI means these events have a hard limit on how good you must be to progress. This alone would not be a massive issue however non-race events in the campaign practically outnumber the race events. It's a slog when you are gated off from races and upgrades because you don't enjoy the over tuned gimmick events.Finally mechanics, I'm neutral on most of these. Ships in 2 are gripper in general but the tracks are also much narrower and more technical to compensate along with hitting the walls now being more punishing. Powerups are now removed too, not a huge loss as most of them in 1 were useless.In addition to this there is a new boost system. Instead of energy which refuels boosting is now always available but heats your ship up once it is overheated further boosting erodes your health. This will regenerate on it's own after a few seconds of not taking damage. Finally to achieve real speed you need to stack forms of boost. All ships have a hyper boost on a long cooldown, this boost is actually very ineffective on it's own and is designed purely to be stacked with regular boost. I don't mind the boosting system, pushing your car to the edge of exploding for speed is exciting, but your ship also barely maintains it's speed when you do get going. Stacking boosts is also a mandatory technique to remain competitive even against the AI rather than some manner of hidden tech. The sound effects for being low on health and repairing are also obnoxious for how often you will hear them. The bones of a great game are here but the execution is sloppy.

_childDocuments_.review: Positive reviews, PLEASE try to mention at the top of your review that almost all negative reviews are complaining about the difficulty. It's going to shake off new players who may in fact love this game, and are being bogged down by entitled people who want to police how this game should be played despite them being a massive minority.ALL of them are tryhard Redout 1 players who are mad that their new game is harder, and they can't one shot every race with all stars and challenges anymore. The boosting system has been improved alot over the first game, it forces you to chose between safety and being inches away from death constantly just to keep up and it's really really fun trying to balance staying alive with going fast. _childDocuments_.review: I've never bought a game on launch before, that's how much I wanted it, heck I've revisited the page a dozen times just to be one of the first to buy this game!As for the game, it's weird compared to redout 1, but good weird, the kind of weird you get from an unfamiliar rollercoaster ride (and to an extent, waiting for the game was the queue up to it), and hopefully I will get used to it. The powerups are gone, replaced with a boost and superboost, both which work like motorstorm boosting (you fill the boost meter, you explode), except with the healtbar doubling as an emergency boost, giving a kind of f-zero vibe. Also, the game is HARD, it might be due to the differences between redout 1 and 2, but the AI seems impossible to take over in this one, I'm still stuck on the final training race; again, weird, but still good weird, it's been a while since I was challenged by a game properly, and I simply need to get better at boost management. That being said, I still miss the old sounds and HUD, but I'm sure everyone's gripes will be addressed in due time!

name: Lucky's Tale
detailed_description: Lucky Swiftail is a brave fox on a quest to save his best friend Piggy from the monstrously tentacled Glorp. Together, you'll run, jump, and climb your way through a bright, colorful world full of charming characters, boss battles, hundreds of secrets to discover, and exciting 3D platforming action. Lucky’s Tale broke ground as one of the first 3rd person perspective games in virtual reality, showing the world VR can be much more than 1st person experiences. Its pioneering approach to camera, character motion, environment, and gameplay provide a thrilling experience that allows players to freely roam immersive environments that are at once both toy-like and vast in scale. You'll feel as though you've gone inside the world of a nostalgic platformer! Become a hero and save the day in the groundbreaking game that launched a beloved franchise, now remastered for modern VR headsets. NEW in this version : remastered lighting, audio, rendering; optimizations for modern HMDs NEW in this version : refined player movement and an updated character model for Lucky (as seen in New Super Lucky's Tale ) Diverse levels featuring lush swamps, underwater ruins, an active volcano, secret foxholes, boss fights, and more 3rd person perspective camera built for virtual reality and designed for thrilling yet comfortable platforming action Headset tracking for aiming, throwing, finding hidden items; touch controls for interacting with Lucky and menus Additional timed-based and collectathon challenges that reward replays Cute, cuddly, and made for all ages and skill levels

_childDocuments_.review: Lucky's Tale was definitely made for kids primarily. 8-12 year old me would have loved this game, but 32 year old me really likes it too. It's a platformer, we all love them right? It's also not overly easy, I find myself dying occasionally. Maybe not as much as Crash games but probably as much as a Mario game. The level design is pretty amazing, there are no pre rendered backgrounds to add illusion of depth. Everything you see is your level environment. The graphics are highly polished in VR and even a potato can run it. My absolute favorite parts are when you dive into a hole and do a side platforming bit, they are just that extra touch that makes me keep playing. The story is basically non existent, but it's a platformer. There is lots of replayability here too, though I don't think it is that long. I would say wait for a sale but $20 is reasonable, and this genre just works so well in VR. I find myself always searching for the next 3rd person platformer that is actually worth playing. I can't think of that many cons to this game but one major one for me is there really isn't any puzzle solving that is of any depth. I would have liked to have seen mini puzzles that would shake up the monotonous enemy bashing and coin collecting. The voice of lucky is also kind of annoying and childish, but not too bad.Overall I am enjoying it, but I don't think I would have touched this game on flatscreen. VR just makes it really worth playing. I hope they bring Lucky's Tale 2 to VR as well! Would definitely buy it.

_childDocuments_.review: With so many VR games this is an essential for your library.  Excellent production values and worth full price.  It's a platformer, so it plays like Mario.  Hop on enemies to kill them, collect coins for bonus lives, avoid traps, reach checkpoints to replenish your hearts.  The environments are beautiful, stylized, and varied.  Levels start easy but get more difficult as you play.  The music suits each environment perfectly.  It's not a long game, but there is replayability for completionists such as speed runs and finding collectibles.  They recently added achievements if you are a player who needs achievements. _childDocuments_.review: Good VR platformer game. At the time of writing, I haven't played Moss or Trover yet, so I can't compare it to another vr platformer yet, but it was pretty good. The level design looks great, and they've reused models from their New Super Lucky's Tale title, which look very good. Unfortunately, they didn't implement Lucky's dig or slide mechanic from the aforementioned title, but that was expected, as this is a remake of Lucky's first game. Depth perception was a little difficult to master, so I found myself repeatedly falling to my death when trying to jump from enemy to enemy at times. Now that Playful has mastered crafting a great 3D platformer and refined their VR development skills, I'm eager to see what Lucky has in store next.

_childDocuments_.review: Lucky's Tale VR is the third installement of the super-cute true 3D jump'n'run platformer which unites a lot of ideas from other known genre representatives.Difficulty ★★★★☆☆☆☆☆☆ (add 4 stars for gold medal timed trails)First of, this game comes in 3 versions if you buy it in the bundle (release order):* Super Lucky's Tale (SLT)* New Super Lucky's Tale (NSLT)* Lucky's Tale VR (LTVR)While NSLT is a remake of the SLT, TLVR is a complete game of its own and is not directly connected to the story of the first game(s). I think the devs just wanted to test out how Lucky's Tale would perform in VR.The overall game experience is quite good and super-cute, and in some cases can compete with NSLT. The big issue is yet again the difficulty. The devs don't have any sense of making a fair and square challenge, neither in the games before, nor in this one. The overall difficulty of LTVR is easy, unless you try the speed trials. To get the gold medal you have to stay super close to the perfect line and keep running always, and take any hazardous shortcut to compete. But this is when the VR limitations kick in. The game has too much control issues for the task they demand from the players, so getting the gold medals is just very frustrating. * well made VR* super cute game* simple but pretty graphics* good and clear rendering (no blur effects)* good gameplay* lots of levels and challenges* good final boss fight* for my taste the camera is too close (but you can fix this with recentering the camera while leaning forward)* camera panning is aweful for backtravelling sometimes* camera does follow Lucky too slow (especially in vertical maps and timed trials)* the return of the insta-death (I really didn't miss it)* fights could have been more challenging (but this is an issue of all Lucky's games)* Lucky does run on two feeds, but this time at least it looks more natural (in New Super Lucky's Tale it is aweful)* timed trials (gold) are too difficult compared to the rest* the game does get repetitive after some while, there is no progress or and skins to unlock like in the former games* aerial control not very good (unfortunetally the same with the other Lucky's games)* if you die in red coin quest you will be teleported to level beginning (annoying in big levels)* level design not as creative than in (N)SLT* no NPC you can talk like in the former games, it is a pure platformer* enemy can spawn right inside/underneath you and insta-damage you* game uses invisible walls for off-bounds that sometimes you notice to late and die because of it* some objects don't have a hitbox although they look like they should have* no music/sound when you start the game (the volume is set to zero in the options everytime you enter the game)* sometimes the fox shadow is drawn on the ceiling as well* puffer fish does damage you although the needles are already retracted* sometimes you will get no double jump although Lucky connected to the ground properly before (happens often with logs or crates)* hitboxes of enemies are weird* it can happen that the game glitches out and you will get a gold medal for timed trial with a 00:00 timer, yet the game breaks permanently your in-game rewards and Steam achievements along with it. You have to fix this by manually editing your savefile. Common, this totally shouldn't happenI would have really wanted to like this (VR) experience, but two things killed it for me, so thank those devs for the overall negative review:1. insta-deaths: why the hell did the devs went back to the insta deaths? I mean, they knew what stupidity they did otherwise they wouldn't have given you unlimited lifes in the timed trials or removed it in NSLT completely2. timed trials: I really hate to say it, because this kind of a challenge I always waited to get for (N)SLT, now the devs deliver it for the most difficult to control game in their series, but I absolutely have to say it... which lunatic thought that demanding players to chase for a world-record time to get the gold medal with bad aerial control, weird hitboxes and bugged double-jump mechanics would ever be a good idea? I guess we have to wait that they do a 'New' Lucky's Tale VR before we can really enjoy it. On the other hand, just adding VR headset support to NSLT would have been the better option probably than doing a whole own VR title like this.

detailed_description: Digital Deluxe Edition About the Game Don the clothes and weaponry of the elite to become the samurai of legend, Sakamoto Ryoma. The Deluxe Edition both adds challenge to your journey and gives you additional resources to overcome it. The Deluxe Edition includes: Shinsengumi Captain’s Set Ryoma Growth Support Kit Sword Upgrade Materials Kit Gun Upgrade Materials Kit Third Division Armament Expansion Kit The Dragon of Dojima Skin 1860s Kyo is plagued by widespread inequality, and one samurai will change the course of history in his search for justice. Take up the sword of Sakamoto Ryoma and venture to Kyoto to find your father’s killer, clear yourself of a framed murder, and restore your honor. In doing so, you will bring an end to the samurai era and forever change the future of Japan. Draw your blade, load your revolver, and join the revolution in this heated historical adventure that only the creators of Yakuza: Like a Dragon could produce.

_childDocuments_.review: Really disappointing. The only Yakuza game I've played that I just wanted to end so I could be done with it.I've played Yakuza 0-6, enjoyed them, some more than others. This one I did not. I don't know if it's because I just finished Nier Automata, but holy crap does the combat stand out as horrendously bad. Like, Yakuza has never had good combat, but this is really bad. And the story isn't that good either, just a bunch of people using false names so you have to keep track of 15 different new names (because old characters have new names), plus the people they're pretending to be all while a lot of Japanese historical groups you most likely don't know about are warring in the background so it's very confusing to follow. And the "twist" is a total non-shocker. The bad guys of games past are bad guys in this too. What a surprise.This also goes into side quests, nothing of real interest nor note. This entire game honestly felt like a waste of time.

_childDocuments_.review: Good story and good gameplay. Bosses are good for the most part, I felt like some fights leading up to some of the bosses were kinda stupid. For example, being shot by a cannon across the bridge, yes you have cover but its hard to fight the swarm of enemies in front of me while im being shot at by multiple gunmen and cannons. If you want an easier way around it, i'd say just change it to easy mode temporarily. The story was by far the best i've experienced since Yakuza 0, the pacing was good and not too much extra rambling/side quest involvement to the story. Glad I dont have to hear some npc's life story for like 20 minutes just to get back to the main story. The story cutscenes are like either bound to 30 fps and some are 60, it seemed like the promotional ones got about 120 fps compared to the rest. Its not the worst thing in the world but it could be better. The combat remained similar to most yakuza games if not better, the style is like a mix of kiwami 2/6 and yakuza 5 which to me is a perfect combo. One last thing I will say is DO NOT buy the dlc (unless they fix it but they most likely wont) because right now its only one per save. If you delete a save forever you will have to rebuy the dlc, not really optimal at all. RGG please fix this because believe me this is not the smartest move for dlc on your part.Overall, 9/10 close to 10. (If they fix the dlc thing I would gladly give it a 10)I do recommend for anyone looking to pick up a new game, regardless if you've played the yakuza/like a dragon franchise or not.

_childDocuments_.review: I love the Yakuza series, I enjoy the humor of them, and the side stories a great deal.  Like a Dragon: Ishin! delivers on that feeling... unfortunately, it isn't without it's flaws.ProsIf you're a fan of the Yakuza series, you'll probably enjoy most of the game.  It feels very similar, and even the Brawler Style is pretty tried and true to the original series while you're learning the other styles offered.  The storyline has a Yakuza feel, and obviously always a fan of Majima.ConsThe grind.   Oh god, the grind.   I couldn't bring myself to 100% this, there's just way to much to grind out.  Substories are fine, but they added a Bond system that also requires you to grind them.  You also need to grind Ryo to pay for blacksmith to get better weapons.  It's also the only game I can safely say beating the Arena and even the Battle Dungeons doesn't feel like it has any weight.  Just more grind.As for the story, I know people have talked about getting lost unless they know Japanese History, but i'd say that's not a huge thing.  At it's core, it's a samurai revenge story with the tried and true Yakuza elements.   I'd say buy it when it's on sale, but a great chunk of it is Grind and not anything that's particularly fun  (Especially not fond of the battle dungeons, which after a while just felt like damage sponge enemies).6/10

_childDocuments_.review: The good:- Story is top notch. Lots of liberties taken with the real history, of course, but overall feels like it's up there with the best of the franchise- Fitting use of previous characters as model cameos. A few odd ones out, but most are adapted very well, despite technically being new and unrelated characters- "New" combat styles are a lot of fun, very satisfying. Sword-focused bosses feel very different from anything else in the series- Runs VERY well on Steam Deck. Completed the game entirely on the Deck.The bad:- More of a remaster than a remake. Feels very much like the Y5/Y0 era, and not at all like the Y6/Kiwami era.- Porting to Unreal instead of using the Dragon engine is questionable, and came with a lot of drawbacks. Occasional performance hitches and frame drops (thought this was a Deck issue, but seems to be common). - Side stories and filler content are especially lacking compared to the rest of the series- Combat can be very frustrating at times, especially on higher difficulties. Ending sequence in particular has one specific room that's legitimately worse than any boss in the game.- Crafting system is absurdly expensive and grindy - I finished the entire game without engaging with it even once.Overall, very much on-par with the rest of the franchise, and while I would highly recommend it, I definitely would suggest playing on Normal and just playing the main story out. Just be aware that this is VERY much a PS3-era game, and more of a remaster than a remake.

_childDocuments_.review: Its finally here, Ishin is real.In all seriousness this is a great game BUT it have some issues.The gameplay and combat is great like always, since this game is made before 0, you can see 0's DNA in it, like the style switching.Story is excellent as always, as most of Yakuza cast returns to play as an entirely new characters that are based from the era it have, the Bakumatsu. Think of it as a play with the cast playing the different roles they have.Music STILL a certified banger, and they even remixed some themes like   theme from yakuza 5.Content is still top RGG standard, full of variation to entertain yourself in the city of Kyo.Due to its engine change to UE, it suffered with few problems like stuttering on cutscenes and gameplay, which makes it jarring. Graphics wise, it looks great but i prefer the old engine honestly.Another problem is, well you know it, the Bath House which is sucks considering i am really looking forward for it.  Okay that aside, i don't like the trooper system to be implemented in the main game. I just don't like them and the boss using the special skill is just feels really off. I mean sure you can play the game without the troopers but boss still uses them regardless.and minor nitpick from me, is the font choice. I don't really like the font for the game, feels too basic and doesn't fit the setting of the game. Thankfully there are mods for this so i guess that is easily solved.Overall its a great game but not perfect, not my favorite RGG game. But i brought it because i like RGG studios and i want to support them. I am sure they can improve, hopefully. And for RGG studios, don't let the success go over your head.8/10

_childDocuments_.review: I'm gonna be honest. This is a horrible remake of a good game. Ishin has some design choices that make people have vast opinions on it, stuff like  friendship quests with boring objectives, the way the combat is stiffer like the older games  or the story being based off japanese history which some people don't care about.I'm one of the few people who liked those parts of ishin anyway....Though when i say "like" i mean the original ishin, not whatever this ""remake"" is. If you are someone who hasn't played the original ishin or just a newcomer to the series, you might end up liking ishin kiwami.However as someone who's played the original i can easily point out some heavy flaws that make the remake considerably worse in most aspects: Nearly every single boss in the game got some sort of change that decreased or outright prevented the chance of them getting knocked down, ruining certain combos from the original. Unreal engine seems to have nerfed  the grabs, certain bosses slide off while  the others are outright ungrabable in kiwami for no reason.Back blows don't stun bosses as much anymore, they can randomly gain super armor and just ignore your attacks.  Ask any no damage youtuber  and they will say that og ishin has kiwami beat in every aspect combat wise.Combat wise it seems they rebalanced the styles, and by rebalance i mean they nerfed the worst style (brawler) from original ishin and made it even worse, while gunner and wild dancer remain kings.Brawler tanimura parry buff (maxed, gives you combo speed and makes attacks bounce off you.) lasted 9 seconds in ishin and only 3.54 in ishin kiwami for some reason??Even worse is they nerfed brawlers damage to the point where it only exists for certain heat actions, like imagine maxed brawler  tiger drop dealing less damage than 2 sword swings?Certain bosses outright don't do their full combo due to the unreal engine breaking the ai, a certain tutorial boss  for example is a joke (beginning boss is meant to have long combos suprisingly ) but him and his grunts just do like 2 swings and cancel it for no reason.THEY REPLACED A UNIQUE BOSS THEME WITH TOWN BULLY FROM YAKUZA 6 (this happened since they mixed up the ultimate battle and story folder, so  it plays in ultimate battles instead of the story part it's meant to play in like wtf.)on the topic of ultimate battles, og ishin made bosses use their qtes during em, ishin kiwami just makes them go into heat mode and use their ♥♥♥♥♥♥ superpowers. (Which i hate very much since they ruin the mood and are very boring to play against, like imagine having a serious sword fight only for the guy to kamehameha you.) Small gripe, but ultimate battles don't have a  pause at the start so enemies can hit you while the ultimate battle is still fading in.Og ishin has a boss who can throw projectiles (won't spoil) he doesn't spam it too much and uses his melee after hitting you (which stuns you)  or missing (his moves are dependant on that),Kiwami broke that and he just spams projectiles half the time lol!(his ♥♥♥♥♥♥ magic is also a projectile lol, the follow up attack he does after stunning you with a projectile is broken and only works half the time, since unreal can make it randomly miss.)(In og ishin the follow up attack had a green flash because his aura was a unique green, kiwami changed it to orange but the flash is still green because the interns making ishin kiwami ported it and didn't realize that).The giant enemies are spammed everywhere in kiwami, they are unstunnable and can't be heat actioned, truly so "fun" to fight against unless you cheese them.AMON got nerfed. he went from one of the hardest ones in the series to kinda being slightly wimpy since his sword got nerfed and his moveset isn't as fancy. OH and you can stun lock him with certain swords if you want (cough lightning).Graphically: The game was made on Unreal Engine (which makes it a stuttering mess) to make it look more beautiful than original ishin, which is ironic since the game looks like a blurry unfocused mess (where characters look like they are wet and covered in oil) compared to the original ishin, the only positive is that the night lightning looks beautiful but that's about it. Certain fights have their atmosphere kinda bugged or ruined: a certain fight happens in a steamy sauna and the steam is horribly rendered compared to the original. A certain  boss arena has this beautiful atmospheric moonrising overlooking it, kiwami ruins it and dependant on your luck, the moon either doesn't appear or is not correctly shown in the phase transition cutscene due to them incorrectly placing the camera.Another small gripe but a certain boss in og had a badass intro where the music started playing after his name title pops up, kiwami screwed up and the music starts playing before the title even fades in.Certain facial animations for characters are just horrible due to model swaps (yakuza 6, 0 and 7 characters stick out sometimes due to the obvious port). a certain VERY IMPORTANT boss (AGAIN NO SPOILERS) has way worse line delivery in kiwami, they also use his incorrect costume for some reason? Good old recasts. Very minor gripe: They removed a cool post credit scene where ryomas statue is shown (based off the real one.) (Though i understand this since the voice actor in that scene has passed away).The Ishin completion list is notorious for being very grindy, and thankfully... Ishin Kiwami made the grind even worse :D.Grind was increased: chicken racing exploit patched, blacksmith is worse ( Requires Rng), the game is designed to be played with the cards  and your damage is low if you don't use them, even with a heavily maxed sword (unless you use a certain overpowered seal that requires virtue). They totally didn't increase the grind so they could sell you the  paid dlc (exp and crafting packs????). Sega would never do that......Ishin Kiwami obviously has new voice acting, for the most part it's great, but i do love the instances where you literally hear nothing because the voice actor talked quietly, or you hear the mic peaking into your ear, utterly ruining the serious scene.I have more complaints but i genuinely have to write them down somewhere so i don't forget.All in all. I hope emulating stops being buggy and the ishin translation project discord completes it's job so more people can emulate the superior ishin.They really should have just localized it and then just ported it without any of this padding.I feel really bad for the interns or b team that had to port this game  on unreal.if they remake kenzan and ruin it i will cry.

_childDocuments_.review: Finally, a proper samurai action game for PC.  TLDR, if you want a good action game, or you're just a big samurai nerd like me, don't pass up on Ishin!A great hack-n-slash/beat-em-up combat system- Wild Dancer is a blast, Brawler offers all kinds of opportunities, Gunman allows you to safely cheese the crap out of some pesky enemies, and the good ol' fashioned Swordsman style hits hard and feels great.The story itself is kinda messy, but the characters are awesome.  This is my first finished game in the Yakuza franchise, so I'm not familiar with their previous incarnations, but I really came to like this cast of characters.  The long, winding story of revenge and political intrigue ends on a somewhat awkward note IMO, but it's still an enjoyable journey.And then there's the setting.  This is one of the prettiest games I've played in recent years- a gorgeous rendition of 1800s Japan.  I've spent a lot of time just gawking about (in the 27 hours I've spent in the game, I've taken almost 40 screenshots- yay photo mode).  Been wanting more PC games in this kind of setting, and Ishin delivers.Once you're done with the main story, an interesting end-game mode called Bakumatsu Premium Adventure unlocks.  This allows you to continue with your progress so far like most games, but ALSO offers something I've not seen before- the option to make a fresh start, and explore the city free from the main story.  Maybe this is just a regular feature of the Yakuza series, but it's new to me, and seems like an interesting take on post-story exploration.All in all, well worth the price of admission.  Some may balk at $60 for a remake, but as far as I'm concerned, a game hasn't really released until it's released on PC, and Like A Dragon: Ishin! earned its price well before even the halfway point.

_childDocuments_.review: Love this game. It's the same great Yakuza gameplay set in Samurai-era Japan,  with some fun new features. The card system is pretty cool, adding more to the combat and it's optional if that's not your thing. This really is a remaster for good or ill. The game looks great, but some of the npcs look like polished old models from the PS3 era. There is some old styled UI that should have been updated( how you pick items up while roaming, navigating mini game menus, etc. ) but that is my only real complaint. The story so far is great you never know who is on your side. Seeing faces we know and love but not attached to the same characters keeps me on my toes. I really love this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Rating this down not because the game itself is bad (it's actually very fun and im enjoying it so far) but because there are lots of dumb issues and I don't think this game should have been Kiwami'd First off the game is technically a Kiwami (even named that in the jp release) but its more just a UE4 port of the original with some cast changes and some extra substories for 0 and 7(Y:LAD) fanservice. The gameplay itself is entirely the same which makes it incredibly weird to have this good looking game with Yakuza 5 type combat, i'm not saying its bad (I quite like it as I enjoyed 4 and 5 alot) but both Kiwamis have actually done stuff to the combat. Looking at footage of the original it does not even look hugely dated, it was only 1 year before 0 and thats the most popular game in the series that anyone interested in Ishin would have played.There was absolutely no reason this couldn't have been just translated and made a Remaster like 3,4 and 5.Other issues to note:Poor performance, lots of stutters when heat actions happen (apparently a UE4 issue where stuff isnt cached properly) but in general it's not a good PC port. Runs better than Kiwami 2 tho.The lack of legit ultrawide support, the game is unsure if it supports it giving constant bars at the side of the screen but still rendering some text and the karaoke under those bars, hoping for a community fix or a patch on this as this is apparently a UE4 default settings issue (thanks Tim Fornite Sweeney)The game also has one time use microtransactions to get gun and sword parts?? These aren't even good and I don't know why they were added.TL;DRThe game Ishin! itself is fun, game should have been a remaster instead as this isn't a good Kiwami.

_childDocuments_.review: Im not the hardest fan of the yakuza series but after playing a couple of the mainline entries I can tell you this spin off isnt really worth it unless its on sale and your a big fan. To begin the cons -bad preformance-Use of drm. Have to have an internet connection.-pay to win dlc-Story with nothing to write home about-4 styles feel disjointed. Guns are underwhelming and the card system is interesting but not the best and is implemented poorly. It takes up like half the screen. also brawler is just kinda there. _childDocuments_.review: Like a Dragon: Ishin! is a captivating spin-off in the Yakuza series, transporting players to 1860s Japan with a gripping story centered on samurai Sakamoto Ryoma. The game blends historical drama and the series’ signature over-the-top action, offering a mix of versatile combat styles and engaging side activities. The beautifully crafted Kyoto setting, rich in detail and atmosphere, immerses players in the Bakumatsu era, while the dynamic soundtrack enhances both intense and quieter moments. For fans and newcomers alike, Ishin! delivers a refreshing take on the Yakuza formula, combining heart, humor, and history seamlessly.

The dialogue and storytelling is wildly inconsistent, with what is really a very short tale that is dragged out (when so much more could be told within or alongside it) being held together by some very enjoyable set pieces and twists. _childDocuments_.review: Like a Dragon: Ishin! is a fantastic spinoff in the Like a Dragon series. With excellent combat, a great atmosphere, and an interesting setting, Ishin has a lot to love about it. Moreover, the story is unique and not seen too often in video games; your knowledge of Japanese history will determine what you get out of the story, though. However, even though Ishin is a great game, it does have some issues. For example, despite being a remake, Ishin still controls like it came out a decade ago. Furthermore, the switch from the Dragon Engine to Unreal Engine 4 wasn't completely flawless; traversal stutter is more apparent than in previous Like a Dragon games. Still, even though Ishin has some problems, the story, combat, and atmosphere more than make up for its shortcomings. For fans of the Like a Dragon games, I'd highly suggest trying Ishin.

_childDocuments_.review: A treatise on historical storytelling through video games. "Like A Dragon: Ishin" does what few other games have managed to pull off. It tells an engaging and interesting historical narrative, conveys a powerful message, and provides a fun and rewarding experience. If you enjoy "Fall of the Samurai", "Rurouni Kenshin", "Gintama", or "The Last Samurai" then you will likely enjoy this game and time period. I am not normally a fan of JRPGs but I found myself deeply invested in the characters and locations. The combat can become repetitive but it is well worth it to get to the next story or scene. The story itself is a creative retelling of the Boshin War and Meiji Restoration and takes some creative license while still managing to stay true to the historical end result. Take the time to read up on the true events and appreciate the effect that a few individuals can have on a nation's history. With 30 hrs in my first play-through I have only completed 25% of the game. I am satisfied enough to walk away now but could easily be convinced to walk around and attempt to get further toward that 100% mark. This is a must buy for lovers of history, the Samurai, and the JRPG genre.

_childDocuments_.review: - - - Story - - - Excellent main story as usual - it's a traditional tale of revenge told in typical Yakuza/Ryu Ga Gotoku fashion which never get boring. The less known the better. The side quests lack any charm whatsoever; I've actually been skipping almost all of the dialogue which I have never done in the seven Yakuza games I've played. I'm not sure why, but I haven't found any of them interesting at all. I can't put my finger on it, but I just don't really care. We don't get many distinctive characters like Miracle Johnson or Mr. Labido.- - - Performance/visuals - - -Although a patch has been put up to address it, stuttering is still a big problem and has actually got me killed in a fight, which is a big problem when you're playing on Ishin difficulty like I am, where you die after being hit two or three times. The visuals are great, but I do think some of the post-processing effects are quite unpleasant. The texture quality and world geometry all appear to be the same as the PS3 original, with he exception of a few textures that appear to be upscaled in some way or another. Now I understand that the setting does limit the artistic freedom the artists would have had, but the world lacks a sense of depth and clutter - this is not a remaster on the level of Yakuza Kiwami 2, which is what I was hoping for. With all that said, the world is authentically Japan as of the Edo period. It definitely looks the part, but they really haven't pushed any boundaries with this re-release. It's a fun world to explore, and there are some flickers of genuine beauty in some isolated areas of Kyo. This game was updated to run in UE5 and it has some of the best hallmarks of the engine; the modern lighting looks more natural compared to the original. Ambient occlusion looks great, the depth of field effects look great in the cutscenes. One very nice addition is that most of the original Shinsengumi and other characters have been replaced with characters from Yakuza games released after Yakuza Ishin on PS3. As an example it was wonderful to see Hitoshi Ozawa (Awano), Riki Takeuchi (Kuze), and Hideo Nakano (Shibusawa) from Yakuza 0 reprise their roles once again, albeit in a Japan under feudalism - those guys are great actors. Not to disrespect the original PS3 actors as they all performed just as well, but I have more of a connection with the characters that replaced them. The character models in the cutscenes are of a very high quality and look great, however in-game they look about the same as their PS3 counterparts, which is slightly disappointing.To disable the awful motion blur, depth of field and chromatic aberration, paste this code at the end of the engine.ini file. However, I do like the DOF effects in this game, I'm just aware others might not:[SystemSettings]r.MotionBlurQuality=0r.SceneColorFringeQuality=0r.DepthOfFieldQuality=0 - - - Side activities and mini-games - - -All the traditional mini-games you expect from the Yakuza series are here, from casino games to a combat arena, all about the same but in a different era. Utamaruya is the old-school karaoke which is one of my favourites with the excellent soundtrack that uses traditional wind and string instruments. What are unique mini-games are as follows:Nichibuza, a form of traditional dance where a fan is used. There's some lovely choreography and becomes increasingly more difficult, a little bit too difficult for me :)Chicken racing: need I say more?Courtesan visits: you can visit a courtesan and play some fun, innuendo-filled mini-games. The voice actress has a lovely voice.Farming/cooking: at some point in the game you gain access to your own villa out of the way of the hustle and bustle of the city which mirrors Kiryu's Morning Glory Orphanage to some extent - it even comes with Haruka! What you do here is farm and cook what you grow into a surprisingly diverse range of dishes. I don't really find it that stimulating compared to running a cabaret club in Yakuza 0. Plus Haruka is the only best girl. Shinsengumi captain: once you become a captain you can partake in policing activities in the form of missions and management of soldiers. I never enjoyed this mini-game too much because of how limited it was. I don't really have much else to say - it's a repetitive, pseudo-management game that has you retreading the same few maps over and over.I've probably forgotten a load more things to do as there's loads to distract in this game, in typical Yakuza fashion.- - - Combat - - -Bare in mind I am only playing Ishin difficulty which is punishingly hard, so it might differ on easier modes. With that in mind - - It's pretty good, mate. It's typical Yakuza beat 'em up brawling with the interesting addition of... A GUN. Yes, you can shoot people in the face and stab them at the same time! The combat is surprisingly balanced considering you have a katana and a gun, you never feel truly invincible even when you've risen in level and understand the nuances of the combos. Everything is beautifully animated and the Heat actions are as bodacious and over-the-top as you'd like, and fun to look at. It doesn't feel anywhere near as repetitive as other games, and isn't as punishing as Yakuza 4.Like most Yakuza before it, you gain additional abilities for each of the four fighting styles from trainers. You even get an ancient Komaki! There's not much else to say, it's basically the same as the previous games.- - - Crafting - - -Unlike other Yakuza games crafting is essential in Ishin; most games in the series you can completely ignore the crafting side, however you need resources to craft and upgrade your guns and swords at the forge in Ishin. Luckily crafting materials are abundant in the world and you get at least one every time you defeat some delinquents or ronin which are this game's version of yakuza and gang members. You'll find materials on the floor, in wells, in random pots. Certain materials are very rare and you'll have to buy them or earn them playing mini-games. It's quite fun.- - - Soundtrack - - -It would be remiss of me not to mention the soundtrack. The Yakuza music has it's style rooted back in F-Zero GX (developed by Sega) that still carries on with it's composer Hidenori Shoji who, 20 years after GX came out, is still making music in that distinctive style in the Yakuza series. Electronic and rock fused into a soulful and visceral style that really sticks with you, that also complements the often high-octane action and emotions of Yakuza. Ishin is no different in that it has these elements; the addition of traditional instruments like the koto and shakuhachi mixed in with the more high-energy tracks for combat really help that distinctive style to fit into the world.Outside of the heavier, rock/electronic music, the ambient and slower-paced music is beautiful. The wind and string arrangements are soulful and distinct. Though, I would have liked more tracks comprised entirely of instruments like the gottan and shakuhachi, I still appreciate what is included. - - - Conclusion - - -Leaves something to be desired on the visual side of things, and the sub-stories are genuinely dull. However, what you get here is an excellent Yakuza/Like a Dragon story, decent combat and an awful lot to do and explore. Long-time fans will be delighted if they're in it primarily for the main story.I hope my review was helpful.

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr Very good game, some bad systemsThe game itself is classic Yakuza/LaD gameplay but more diverse side content, especially the "Another Life" which lets you farm, cook, and take trade requests with Haruka.The story is very engaging, less confusing than that of some Yakuza titles, and is based on historical events although it takes creative libertiesWhere Ishin struggles the most (aside from the horrendous 100%) is the combat, with -2 styles being mostly useless (Brawler, gun w/o proper gear)-bosses having weird "cheat" properties like not being able to be staggered / being able to instantly turn around when you hit them from behind-combat relying on gear and buffs from seals, making some fights more arduous simply due to dealing not much damage-Personal issue, I dont particularly enjoy the active trooper card mechanic where you press left trigger + a Dpad direction to either get a time-limited buff or do a special attack. The passive abilities associated with the cards are fine, but the active abilities are annoying to juggle and add another entry to the pile of "combat problems caused by the gear system"Despite this, I enjoyed my time with the game but certainly will not be going for 100% / Platinum. MUCH of the content required for 100% is very grindy and not particularly fun (maxing bonds by talking to shopkeepers, having to cook 200 meals, etc.)

_childDocuments_.review: (This part is kinda outdated but I still agree with it, just not how I wrote it) The main redeeming factor of this demake is the new music and the fact it's translated. The enemy AI is horrible, and the devs apparently think that more enemy aggression and hyper armor to the point of it being nearly endless is difficulty. It's not. That's just unfair and unfun. Fun fact, lowering the difficulty to easy makes the bosses operate like actual Yakuza/LaD bosses, with real openings, moments where they aren't constantly attacking, and most of all, they will ACTUALLY GET KNOCKED TO THE FLOOR. WHY DID THEY THINK MAKING BOSSES IMMOVABLE WALLS WAS A FUN WAY TO "INCREASE DIFFICULTY."Edit: I still think I had a good point but I would like to say it in a less aggressive way. Like a Dragon: Ishin! is a solid game. It has a very good story as any game in this series does, the heat actions are even crazier than usual, and the music is great. So why did I give this game a negative review?Because pretty much everything about this remake, the original did first, and in many cases better. Everything about this game is basically just a watered-down version of the original Ishin! from 2014. The combat especially feels much clunkier overall, and you feel borderline pathetic in boss fights. I wouldn't mind this too much if the game was $20 like the other two Kiwami games, but it has the full $60 price, which I think is inexcusable as it is (and seems to be staying, since the balance updates have not addressed any of the bs difficulty issues). At the very least, non-boss encounters are pretty fun, but considering just how many bosses there are in this game (a whole lot), it's sad that this is the case.If you're a fan of this series, I think the game is worth getting on sale. It's a pretty alright experience, I just think it is absolutely not worth the full $60. The story is luckily the one thing that isn't watered-down from the original, though some people may dislike the recasts and that's understandable.TL;DR If you have $60 to spend on a Yakuza/LaD game, get Lost Judgment lol

_childDocuments_.review: This is shaping up to be my favourite Yakuza game, the setting allows the developers to go in to a completely different direction to the Yakuza games, and the final few chapters are my favourite of all the games by far.Everything is refreshing on this game, the visuals and setting, the new systems, the substories and the storyline. Being outside of the Modern Japanese City setting makes exploring this game an absolute treat and though it took me a while to warm up to the older feeling of the game, the fact this game was made after Yakuza 5 made me really impressed given the amount of new content and things it tried to do, and the fact it only came out in Japan made me super surprised they went so far.As long are prepared to adjust back to the Yakuza 5 "style" of gameplay and engine, you will really warmup to this game and if you are a longtime Yakuza fan who has played the rest of the games, you'll feel a really refreshing pace, tone and setting in this game. _childDocuments_.review: This is perhaps one of the weakest entries of the Yakuza series, but frankly, even the worst game of this series is still above whatever passes for "average" nowadays.Also, I know it's supposed to be "like a dragon" instead now, but I don't care about that. It's "Yakuza Ishin."If I had problems with this game, it would be:1) It's too easy. I'd wager this is the easiest Amon fight I ever fought and I've fought them all LJ's (next game I intend to play). I blame War Cry Counter.2) Combat feels very stiff, including wild dancer style. Also worth mentioning, your heat doesn't dissipate over time which... weird. By the end, you're really strong and it's fun, but still, something feels off.3) Menu'ing in this game feels uncooperative. I don't remember so much time being wasted just waiting on the menu to start accepting inputs.4) Time wasting in this game is arguably the worst of the series.also 5) I found myself really not caring about the overarching plot. Yakuza games always have some gut punch to the plot to keep you engaged - and this is true despite the incredible amount of side-content these games have. The stories and character are usually really well written and despite the many many hours of being distracted, you'll be pulled back for more...Maybe it's because I was able to guess the entire plot from the start - and I do mean the very beginning. I blame seeing a certain someone's face, recognizing it and thinking "that's the final boss." hehMaybe because I learned enough about the History of Japan (thanks Bill Wurtz) that I already know what's gonna happen.Maybe it's because... I dunno, I didn't like Ryoma all that much. Can't put my finger on any one reason as to why, but I just didn't like him.Maybe it's the suspension of disbelief that I've created for the Yakuza series isn't enough. I have tremendous difficulty suspending my disbelief even further when I just cut a guy SEVEN times, then impaled the guy while he's on the floor and finally shot him, overkilling his HP bar a few times over... only for him to survive it once the battle is over; meanwhile in the first cutscene of the game, you see people getting slashed once or twice and they're dead. This isn't like in other Yakuza games where pulling out a sword or a gun and murdering the enemies is technically considered "out of character" so you can mentally file it under "ludonarrative dissonance" and move along just fine.I think my favorite thing this game did was the character of Yoshitaka Mine from Yakuza 3 -> appearing as Hijikata Toshizo. They did the character well and picking Mine was really nice.

_childDocuments_.review: Finally after almost 10 years we have Ishin in the west! RGG has delivered yet another BANGER with the kiwami version of Ishin. The game is overall phenomenal and it has potential to be up there with the greats like Yakuza 0 and Lost Judgment. However it does suffer from a couple of small flaws that I think hold it back by just a little bit. 1. CombatThe combat is great and it feels super satisfying. Ishin has 4 fighting styles: Brawler, Swordsman, Gunman and Wild Dancer. With many different fighting styles in the game one is bound to be less popular than the others and that would be swordsman, however in swordsmans case here the style just isn't good at all compared to the other styles and feels really lacking. Brawler and Wild Dancer are good for crowds or for one-on-one fights while gunman is great for crowd control but some use can be found in boss fights as well. Swordsman is only good for boss fights and even then you're just better off using brawler or wild dancer in bosses as they are much faster with better mobility and defense abilities. Swordsman has a slightly bigger damage but it's still really slow even when upgraded and I just never really used it. It was the only style I hadn't maxed out when I reached the final chapter. It looks cool to use? I guess?2. Trooper cardsThe player being able to use trooper cards is not a problem for me as you can just... not use them and call it a day. My slight nitpick about this is how the story bosses are able to use them. If they would use it like once a fight it wouldn't matter at all but sometimes they just decide to spam the special abilities. This happened to me with  boss fight and it felt like a really cheap way to amp up the difficulty. I played the game on legend so usually these abilities just instantly kill you as well especially in the early-mid game when I hadn't crafted good enough gear yet. A "classic mode" would have been nice to experience the game as it was originally intended.3. Bathhouse fight QTE was censored4. The GrindThe game has a pretty agonizing grind when trying to get the right material drops from dungeons as RNG is always involved. I would point out the need for money grinding as well but since the chicken race exploit exists you can completely remove the grind for money with that.5. Unreal Engine stutteringAs the game is on unreal engine the game has some stuttering issues. Doing a new heat action for the first time for example will always result in stuttering. Not really a big issue at the end of the day but worth pointing out I think.All this aside, everything else in the game is absolutely fantastic! Everyone can have their opinions about the cast changes for example but as for me most of them are pretty solid. There's a couple in the OG that I would have liked to return but I think there's nothing wrong with the new cast members. They also created some new music for this remake  and all of the new tracks and remixed tracks sound gorgeous as well.Overall this game is an easy 9/10. If you're a fan of RGG and have not yet played Ishin (Not this one or the original) I highly recommend you play it.Here's hoping one day we get Kenzan and Kurohyō 1 & 2 in the west either in the remastered form or in the kiwami remake form as well as Dead Souls finally making it past the ps3 and getting either a remaster or the kiwami treatment as well

_childDocuments_.review: I love this series in general and I'm glad this finally got released outside of Japan. I wish they had put more care into it vs. launching a game that is objectively worse than the original. There's just enough changes to one of the core gameplay elements to make the entire experience feel worse and the replacement of characters with more familiar ones from other games in the series mostly doesn't work. The model replacement in particular wasn't handled well and there's severe problems with the facial animations in key scenes.I played for over 100 hours. I got all the achievements. I can't say I didn't get my money's worth, but from a story and gameplay perspective, this is easily my least favorite game in the series. If you love Yakuza/Like a Dragon, it's definitely worth playing but temper your expectations.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game and its Yakuza style twist on real historical events, but the gameplay itself does have some pros and cons. I ended up barely using the trooper cards other than to get extra HP, combat healing, and the occasional big damage abilities for the silly giant enemies since the sword and gun combat was very fun.Too many of the substories are just filling up friendship meters, but there are a lot of funny ones, as usual with RGG games. Finding enough crafting materials was never a problem once you unlocked the Trooper minigame dungeons but finding seals to put on your weapons and armor can be a bit grindy, but I would say it's not entirely necessary to go out of your way to get them. I used all crafted weapons throughout the game, and it tended to make the game a little easy anyway, even with mediocre seals.As with all RGG games, there are tons of side activities to do. The karaoke song selection is a bit limited but make sure you sing with Okita at least once. All the usual gambling games are here to help makes tons of money, and then you have Another Life with farming and cooking minigames to relax with Haruka. If you're still short on money, grow tons of Ginseng and sell it at Ebisu and ship orders for Haruka.And lastly, make sure you learn to use Dragonfang Flash and then Dragonfang Beheading as your final move on the last enemy to end encounters in a really cool way.

_childDocuments_.review: After years and years of waiting, we finally got a western localization of Ryu Ga Gotoku: Ishin! in the form of...Ishin Kiwami.Well, to cut a long story short - the main story and everything around it is easily top-tier RGG material if there ever was, but in my opinion the side content is below average.The few actual side stories that are here feel on par with the older PS3 Yakuza games, while the rest are just "Hey, you started a friendship with a person/store!" type of deal.The friendships are a bit of an excessive grind, and are certainly not a fun thing, nor were they ever.In hindsight, they were a bit much even in Judgment, though in that game it was still better handled.As for the mini-games, you have the usual suspects - Karaoke, a dancing minigame (which is actually not nearly as piss easy as what we had in Yakuza 5 and is actually harder on average than 0 - probably closer to the difficulty you can find in the dancing club in Lost Judgment), two of Yakuza 5's minigames (chicken racing betting and an udon ship minigame) with the regular assortment of Japanese board/gambling minigames.As always, your mileage may vary, but I'm sure you'll find something to enjoy there.As for the battle dungeons - well, you either love to grind them or hate to go through them as they go on and on and... ON...Actually, I'd like to shout out the absolute state that is the way the game's balanced and how it hinges on crafting. I don't like it. The sword style just isn't satisfying - almost any enemy that isn't a small fry can block your rush combos with ease while also getting hits on you even though you could've sworn your dodge was well timed or your block should've triggered those sweet, sweet i-frames.What isn't helping is how the crafting system has SO MANY materials that you need to collect, and boy is the game not generous with the ones that count.I'd be lying if I said I recommend playing the game without using mods and/or resource cheats.(Seriously though, I would absolutely DESPISE playing RGG games on a console, where I can't use save editing, install mods or apply specific, pinpoint cheats where they can really count. It's a real shame that some of the best you'll find in gaming has to be bogged down with mindnumbing grinds and questionable design decisions.)Despite all of my complaints, I still recommend the game overall, seeing as all the criticisms above notwithstanding, if you don't find the quality of the side content to be that important or conversely you LIKE grinding the same gameplay loop for crafting materials, then you'll find one of the best main stories in the Like a Dragon franchise here, with combat that can be uneven but still pretty good (bless the Wild Dancer style for letting you run wild on enemies). You'll get much more out of it if you give yourself a crash course on the state of Japan's society and politics circa 1850-1870 beforehand, though.Just, uh, hold fast to your suspension of disbelief, ok?

_childDocuments_.review: This game is tons of fun but it's not the best in the RGG series. To make up for the significantly smaller map and shorter story, this game is filled to the brim with time wasters, a lack of modern QOL design and grind that would make an MMO player throw up their hands in frustration. If this were the only game that I was able to play for the rest of the year I wouldn't mind, but in a world where everything is competing for my attention, it diminishes the fun a bit when you start *feeling* like things have been designed to take longer than necessary. Seriously, no other game I've encountered basically punishes you for levelling up in an RPG. It doesn't help that the game actively obfuscates how to play it, leaving you to the message boards to figure out bypass the levelling roadblock, the blacksmith / crafting weapons, etc etc. Oh, and the bugs. There are bugs.-But for all the above, I still sunk 81hrs into it and I'll probably pop back in after I've played something else for a bit. Combat is fun, the trooper cards are novel and the wacky sidequests kept me laughing. Hell, when I figured out how to fish in the game I think I spent a solid couple hours just doing that one night.-I would absolutely love to see a follow up to this game with a similar setting and combat system, but better balanced, more fleshed out and a bigger map that doesn't feel like a chore. I could see where staying true to the original was tearing at the seams and would love to see what they could do with something built from the ground up for a modern audience on modern machines with significantly less grind for a more organic gaming experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Like a Dragon: Ishin! is up there as one of my favorite games of all time. To finally get a remake of one of the most beloved entries in the series and get it localized for the first time is a real treat. One of the best parts of this game is the combat. Combat is one of the most important aspects in these games, because I know I will spend a good portion of the game engaged in combat. So I was really happy to see the combat done well in Ishin. There are multiple battle styles to switch from with each form having their own unique properties. The Wild Dancer style is possibly one of my favorite combat styles in the whole game, just because how well it flows and how good it is when you master it. All of the other styles are amazing as well. Trooper cards are also an addition to the game. They are fun to use and make things a little easier, but if you want to play through the game traditionally, just don't use the cards. My only complaint with the combat is that it takes a lot of time to level up your battle styles. Even after 40 hours of playing at the time I am reviewing this (this is after completing the main story and doing a bunch of the side content), I am still far from mastering all of the styles and utilizing all of the abilities in the game. Of course, you can easily get experience points from the Shrine, but they take up a lot of Virtue points that would've gone to other useful features as well. Besides that, the combat is one of the best RGG combat systems that I have played in a while. The music is something I love about this game. Most of these songs were from the original Ishin game, but there are some new ones for bosses such as "Soar" and for karaoke songs such as "Baka Mitai". Hearing all of these tracks in game was such a treat with some being remixes of songs in other games. But there are a few nitpicks (spoilers ahead): . Regardless, the music also goes hard in this game. The story was also very good, and I like how the narrative is based on the events that propelled Japan into the Meiji Restoration (the shift away from the Shogun's rule and the restoration of the Emperor). I really love to study Japanese history in my free time, so combining the history behind the Meiji Restoration with the Like a Dragon series made me so excited. If you search up all of the names of the characters in this game, you will actually find people with the same name who actually lived and played a part in this story, including Sakamoto Ryoma. Side content is also very good in this game. The substories are fun as always and some will have you create bonds with the people of Kyoto. The home life side game was also fun and was a great way to make money and take a break from that unravels in Kyoto. It's like Animal Crossing, but just the part where you pay off the debt. I haven't had the chance to try everything in the game, but from what I have experienced so far, it's really good.Finally, I'm really impressed how well Ishin turned out in Unreal 4. I thought we would get dragon engine games from now on, but I'm happy Ishin was not on the dragon engine. I really needed a break from the dragon engine games and all of the things that make it so frustrating to play on. Basically, everything in this game is really good with the exception of some minor nitpicks. I hear people have complained about the frame rate and the PC port in general, but I haven't had any trouble on my end besides a few frame rate drops occasionally (for reference, I played through this game on a Steam Deck). Hopefully more updates will make the PC port better for other players. The only thing that isn't great is the DLC, which many people have complained about since it is only a one-time use and is only tied to one save file. In addition, there is a difficulty setting locked behind the paywall as well. I'm not sure what went through RGG's mind to come up with something like this, but it is my biggest gripe with the game. I would personally not recommend buying the DLC and just get the base game. You're really not missing out on much by not purchasing the DLC unless if extra cosmetics and an extra hard difficulty setting is something you need. Besides all of my criticisms about the game, Like a Dragon: Ishin! will definitely go on the list of favorite games of all time and is my favorite game of 2023 so far. I'm really looking forward to future entries from RGG Studio including the upcoming Like a Dragon Gaiden game later this year and Like a Dragon 8 in 2024. If you are a fan of the series or just wanting to check out a Like a Dragon game from this year, this is definitely a great game to pick up and play.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is generally pretty good.  The combat's a blast, the story has some really great moments, there are some fun new minigames, and the substories in these games never disappoint.  It was pretty fun playing as a character much like Kazuma Kiryu, just in a different time period.However, this game probably has the most scuff since Yakuza 4.  The game is basically a remaster of the original, which I wasn't aware of; I figured it'd be more modern and in-line with the current gen Dragon Engine games.  I didn't mind the blast from the past, but it was unexpected.  The game doesn't seem fully polished for PC, either; I'd get the occasional freeze, stutter, and at the worst of times, a flickering shadow glitch when there were cutscenes in certain buildings.  Not a game breaker, but it was disappointing.  Oh yeah, and the prerendered cutscenes were capped at 30 FPS!  Usually I'm not a snob when it comes to this, but it was pretty jarring when the rest of the game is usually played at 60 frames or higher.Overall, this game is solid.  It's pretty rough around the edges, but generally I'm happy ended up getting a port of this game.  I just hope that if we eventually get Kenzan, it gets the remake treatment instead of just a remaster.  I would GLADLY take more Like a Dragon swordplay!

_childDocuments_.review: Like a Dragon: Ishin! is a spin-off of the Yakuza series that takes place in the Bakumatsu era of Japan. The game has an engaging story, a fun combat system, and a rich open world to explore. However, it also suffers from some major flaws that prevent me from recommending it.First of all, the PC port is poorly optimized and lacks basic features such as shader pre-caching and ultrawide support. The game often stutters and crashes, making it frustrating to play.Secondly, the DLC policy is very unfair and restrictive. The DLC items are tied to one save file instead of one account, meaning that you can’t use them again if you start a new game. Moreover, one of the difficulty levels is locked behind a paywall, which is unacceptable for a full-priced game.Thirdly, the game requires an internet connection at all times to play. This means that you can’t play it offline or on devices like the Steam Deck. It also means that if your internet connection drops while playing, you will lose your progress and have to restart the game.These issues overshadow the positive aspects of the game and make it hard to enjoy. I hope that the developers will fix them in future updates or patches. Until then, I can’t give this game a thumbs up.

_childDocuments_.review: Without spoilers (I ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ hate spoilers, even gameplay related ones, so don't worry), and without a doubt:If you're a Yakuza fan, you should play this. I recommend playing it after finishing every other Yakuza mainline game so far up to and including the reboot (Y7, like a dragon), like I did.This game is a love letter to the entirety of the series.It will keep you smiling and it's awesome.When I started the Yakuza series, the only real thing I knew about Japanese culture was videogames and anime, and everytime I saw anime fans online they disgusted me (maybe I was a bit childish). I kind of grew a hatred for japanese culture without even knowing it. But after playing through all these games, I've really found my peace with japan and their language and their food and their culture, and with this game, I think I'm starting to find their history cool as well :) It's always nice to get a glimpse at the treasure humanity can be, and the Yakuza series always did that really well for me. Sorry, that was probably irrelevant, but buy this game! You might feel the same.If you haven't played any Yakuza games, here's a small story to convince you:I once got Yakuza 0 on a whim for 5 bucks. Since that day, I have spent every real freetime in my life playing through more and more of these games. They're something different, they reminded me what videogames could be, that videogames can be an art form, and full of the developers' love, and that a good videogame can help you learn lessons about life and move your thinking, your heart (and your body with these banger soundtracks).Yakuza Ishin is no exception. I have spent so much time playing these games and I really can't say much but that I don't want to spoil a single bit of this phenomenal experience. If you have any interest in playing tough guys that have a good heart in their chest and fight ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, then this game series might just change your life, and I recommend you just stop reading reviews, buy Yakuza 0 here on steam, and dig into this gold mine that I just so happened to run into one day, you might end up feeling the same as I - that it was one of your best decisions regarding digital media, if not the best.

_childDocuments_.review: Ishin is a pretty solid entry into the I guess its now called "Like a Dragon" franchise now.TLDR the game is basically the entire cast of the various Yakuza games thrown into Feudal Japan. Its pretty fun sometimes recognizing familiar faces but with new personalities including our very own Kiryu...i mean Ryoma...I mean Saito...The world for once isn't Kamaraucho (though it might be where that plot of city ends up for all we know) but the enviroments still stack up pretty well. Most streets and side alleys feel just as lively and alive as they do in the busy city. Though you'll find a few paths that are always conspicuously empty save for maybe a combat encounter...almost like a hidden loading gate which brings me to probably my biggest problem with this game.its old. Like not very old but it is a PS4 era entry and it shows sometimes. I still can't tell if textures have been remastered for this port or not. I have a japanese copy i bought several years ago to play and tbh it seems mostly the same. Theres a few things here that wasn't in that version but most of it seems to be references and bonus material inspired by the other Yakuza titles.Now theres nothing inherently wrong with this in fact i'm glad they did it but what i am NOT happy about is the price point. Full price for a game thats several years old already? translating isn't cheap i'm sure but come on...Now theres another minor issue and thats the fact that the combat of the Yakuza franchise kind of feels goofy here in a setting where fights are frequently decided both historically and cinematically in 1 to 2 hits. The combat isn't bad but you will frequently confuse your razor sharp sword for a butter knife at times.The good parts of Yakuza are fortunately all still here. The story, the over the top violence of HEAT actions, the silly sidestories and the over the top characters are all still present and really carry the experience at times. The troop system they put in place is a interesting twist sure but i'm not a fan as i feel like it really clutters the hud.All in all Like a Dragon Ishin is good, its a fun idea and a fun game and i hope they do more outlandish ideas similar to it with the franchise going forward. It would be fun to see Kiryu and company in a variety of other scenerios and settings.But for this game don't pay the full price as its sort of a rip off.

_childDocuments_.review: As a person who loves the Like A Dragon series to death, Like A Dragon Ishin was one of the games that I most desired to be released internationally and on all platforms. So when it was announced it automatically became my most anticipated release for early 2023. Like A Dragon is the remake of Ryū ga Gotoku Ishin! which was originally released on February 22, 2014, exclusively in Japan, serving as a launch title for the PlayStation 4. Set in the chaotic Bakumatsu (1853–1867) phase of the Late Edo period of Japan, players take on the role of Sakamoto Ryōma, who is distressed resulting from conflicting pressures and uncertainty about one's self and role in society. Being embroiled in the middle of a Tosa coup d'état and bent on finding the murderer who assassinated his father figure, Ryōma burrows himself with a hidden identity in the streets of Kyo and joins the grim Shinsengumi. This remake of Ishin! retains most of the gameplay system from the original game, with the exception of the Trooper Cards, which can now be used optionally in regular combat. In addition, several characters of the game were also recast with new actors, who have previously portrayed other characters in the mainline titles, notably from Yakuza 0, Yakuza 6: The Song of Life, and Yakuza: Like A Dragon. The singing bar (karaoke) minigame features two songs not featured in the original: a new arrangement of the series' fan favourite karaoke track, "Baka Mitai" (ばかみたい, I've Been a Fool), and an entirely new track, "Ichizu Samurai" (い・ち・ず・侍, Truehearted Samurai), alongside the five unique songs featured in the original game. The game's depiction of 19th-century Kyoto A.K.A Kyo is brilliant and the environments are gorgeously rendered in this remake. The combat is super fun and so unique compared to the usual Like A Dragon combat. The Soundtrack is absolutely fire and the remixed songs are absolute bangers. A Solid 10 Out of 10 From Me.

_childDocuments_.review: Like a Dragon: Ishin! is a true Ryu Ga Gotoku studio rollercoaster, putting the Meiji Restoration and RGG characters into a bag with some true soap operaistic elements, then giving it a vigorous shake and making a vaguely historically influenced story extravaganza out of it.And if you don't feel like blazing through the melodrama that is Japan reinventing itself as a nation, you can always go farm potatoes and pet your rescue cats and dogs.10/10.
