_childDocuments_.review: "The core of the game is being eroded by this." - Masayoshi Yokoyama, Ryu Ga Gotoku Studio Head on the Like a Dragon: Ishin (Behind the Scenes of Like a Dragon! – Ep 2: The Road Ahead 8:09)Before I start I want to mention I've refunded the game a fair while ago, so let me know if anything has changed. I'd consider myself a massive RGG Studios fan, I've played every Yakuza/Judgment game available on PC, so it disheartens me to say that this game is the worst the series has been, and I don't mean that with any exaggeration I dislike this game. I will admit I wasn't super excited for this game as I didn't have much of an interest in the original Ryu Ga Gotoku: Ishin! But after playing this remaster (I'll discuss that more later on) I have even less of an interest in doing so. "So what are the flaws?" you may ask, and to put it simply this is a cheap and poorly put together remaster. You might ask why do I keep referring to it as a "remaster" rather than a remake which is what this game is being sold as. Well to put simply half, if not a majority of the original games code, animation, models, and overall gameplay is still in the games files, it was ultimately a port of the original to Unreal Engine 4. With that out of the way I want to point out another glaring issue, the port to Unreal Engine 4. I can make a comparison but I want you to keep in mind it's not as bad, is Grand Theft Auto: Trilogy Remastered. The game overall uses a variety of models, some characters got changed as apart of the cast change, and this can vary on the quality of them as these models come from as early as 2014 with the original Ishin (Ryoma's model is still his original model), or head models that are either from 2020's Yakuza: Like a Dragon (Kondo has Adachi's head), or completely new ones such as Ito (while it uses Hitoshi Ozawa/Kuze's facial scan data from 2015, it seems like they made a new head based off it) and it just becomes a mess in terms of quality as some are higher quality than others. The map and models looks off, as it was completely made in a different engine, and then ported to Unreal Engine 4, except for in cutscenes where they seem to actually be able to take advantage of Unreal Engine, and they do look nice when they work that is. This game would've benefited from a ground up remaster made in the studios own Dragon Engine. The next issue I'll point out is bugs, they are littered throughout this game and they range from minor annoyances to major issues, here are some I would like to note, bosses would sometimes unintentionally teleport throughout the boss fights, cutscenes would start flashing to black and back to normal horribly, sometimes the cutscene camera is inside of a wall preventing the player from seeing what's going on, music would overlap over itself with the second repeat being delayed, the water would sometimes glitch out and cover the screen, and that's just to name a few bugs I've encountered and seen from my friends. I will point out some personal points, I don't consider these as strong and they are up to personal preference. I don't like the trooper card and boss super attack system. The trooper card system from my knowledge was exclusive to the dungeon system, and I think that's fine, but in this game, they are technically unequippable, but they give stat bonuses, that and the cards on the U.I take up too much space, while they make the game less tedious than without them, they should give you choice. I can say the same about the bosses super moves (example: a boss has fire balls come out of his hands), from the same documentary I got my quote from the beginning of my review from, it is mentioned they added these in an attempt to appeal to a wider audience, and I personally agree with Yokoyama on it eroding the core of the game. Despite being a RGG game, they tend to have limits on how silly they'll go, especially in the main game (story). The extracts in Judgment/Lost Judgment which are similar to the trooper cards, are completely optional and you have to go out of your way to use them, so I am completely fine with that. The easiest thing I can compare the boss super attacks to, is the mortal attacks in Judgment/Lost Judgment, but the thing with those is they aren't super silly, they are still relatively grounded. I'd also make another quick point about a thing that bugs me is that they have the original cast of this games model, and as proven by Ryu Ga Gotoku: Online (a Japanese gatcha game), they still are able to use the likeness and voice of the original cast so I don't see why that isn't a toggle especially with the controversy towards the new cast, while I don't personally mind the new cast this is a 80 dollar game. I'll wrap this up with my last point, the price point, and DLC. This game is 92.99 Canadian Dollars for the Digital Deluxe edition, which is absolutely insane. For comparison Resident Evil 4 (2023)'s Deluxe Edition is only 89.99, and that's a ground up remake, and not a port with unnecessary DLC that wasn't in the original. The DLC for this game isn't an issue because it's a "support the devs" option, but because most of it is a predatory EA, Ubisoft type of microtransaction, why do I say that? The DLC can be divided into two things, a DLC for cosmetics (Shinsengumi Captain's Set) which is fine, but it also includes a difficulty mode, which I really don't like but okay. But then you have materials for weapons crafting, and high quality cards, that is an issue, especially the weapons crafting as this game is notorious for grinding. But also another main issue is that these are all ONE TIME USE, so if you get them on the wrong save, or your save gets corrupted, it is gone. This is the most worrying aspect of the game as I can see how it can easily be implemented into Like a Dragon: 8. I want to conclude with, I am genuinely really unhappy with this game, I am hoping that this is a one time thing for RGG, as I feel like every game prior to this has something I really like about it, this doesn't, and it's a shame because everyone has been hyping this game up, and I never was onboard, in a way I'm lucky as I would hate to be a fan of the original Ishin just to be disappointed by this. Personally I hope moving forward, RGG focuses on it's Japanese audience primarily for the decisions they make in their games (in the same documentary I mentioned at the beginning they've mentioned that Sega of America gave them suggestions and they took it.) as it's why we love the games, they move forward using Dragon Engine because they truly made something special with it, it's an inhouse engine that they've improved greatly as shown in Lost Judgment, and I want to continue to see what they can do with it, and also I just hope they drop the predatory DLC, just stick with cosmetics, and story expansions (price them better as well). I still love RGG Studio but I can't recommend this game.TL;DR: Like a Dragon: Ishin! is an overpriced poorly made remaster that calls itself a remake, that has a lot of annoying bugs, a lack of options, and predatory DLC practices.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm happy to see that Like a Dragon: Ishin! has finally been translated and released internationally. I've never played the 2014 Japan-exclusive PS4 game (duh), so I'm even happier that after the first hours I can already tell that it has all components that make for a great Yakuza/Like a Dragon game: suspenseful main story, dozens of fleshed out characters with their own agenda, silly side stories, great soundtrack and satisfying combat.It doesn't improve on the "Yakuza formula", but it doesn't have to - it's a game series that reliably delivers.It's a great spin-off that anybody will enjoy who enjoyed other Yakuza games. For newcomers, this could be a great starting point, provided the setting in 1860s Japan sounds interesting. If it doesn't, it would be better to start somewhere else, e.g. with Yakuza 0 or Yakuza: Like a Dragon. At the same time, there are a few glaring issues that can't be overlooked. The movement outside of combat is clunky and feels very 2014, even on a controller. The story has some pacing issues, after the intro it pretty much slows down to a crawl. On top of that, there are technical issues, that will hopefully be addressed with future patches. Some of those are really unforgivable in 2023: UE4 shader stutter; missing ultra wide screen support (come on, Sega); 30 fps cut scenes (really?).

_childDocuments_.review: A Tale of Two Eras - Like a Dragon Ishin ReviewLike a Dragon Ishin takes the signature Yakuza series and time-travels players to feudal Japan, offering a captivating blend of historical setting and familiar gameplay mechanics. This unique spin-off showcases the franchise's versatility, merging its classic elements with a fresh historical context.Set against the backdrop of 17th century Japan, Like a Dragon Ishin immerses players in the turmoil of the Edo period. The game's portrayal of the era is meticulous, capturing the essence of the time with authentic locations, costumes, and cultural nuances. This historical accuracy adds a layer of depth to the storytelling, making it a compelling experience for history buffs and Yakuza fans alike.The narrative follows the tale of Ryoma Sakamoto, a charismatic figure in Japanese history. Ryoma's journey is engaging and richly developed, weaving personal struggles with grand political intrigue. The writing is as immersive as ever, showcasing the franchise's knack for creating multifaceted characters and emotional storytelling.Combat, a cornerstone of Yakuza games, receives a makeover in Like a Dragon Ishin. Retaining the series' distinct blend of real-time brawling and RPG mechanics, the combat system introduces samurai-era weaponry and techniques. The transition is seamless, offering a satisfying fusion of classic Yakuza gameplay with the flavor of the past.Mini-games and side activities, beloved trademarks of the series, are ingeniously adapted to fit the historical setting. From traditional gambling games to period-specific pastimes, the attention to detail in these diversions is commendable, adding a layer of authenticity to the game's world.Graphically, Like a Dragon Ishin excels in portraying both the urban chaos of old Kyoto and the serene landscapes of the countryside. Character designs and animations continue the franchise's trend of excellence, ensuring that even in this historical context, the characters are brimming with personality.While Like a Dragon Ishin succeeds in many aspects, it's not without its minor hiccups. Some gameplay mechanics might feel slightly repetitive, and occasional glitches can momentarily disrupt immersion. However, these issues are minor in the grand scheme of the game's accomplishments.In summary, Like a Dragon Ishin is a remarkable twist on the beloved Yakuza series. By merging the franchise's iconic gameplay with an impeccably recreated historical setting, the game offers an engaging and immersive experience that stands out within the franchise. It's a must-play for fans of both Yakuza games and Japanese history enthusiasts, delivering a unique blend of action, drama, and cultural exploration.

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr only buy if it's either on sale or you really like the other yakuza games.Ishin Kiwami is a mixed bag of good and bad. It is obvious how much effort RGG put into this remake, however if anything, it feels more like an enhanced port, just on a new engine. Coming off the heels of Lost Judgment, Ishin Kiwami feels like a downgrade in almost every department.While the visuals aren't terrible, at times they look rather disappointing, especially considering that this is the same studio that have made some beautiful looking games. There are times where the game can look rather sloppy, even on the highest graphics settings. At points i'd say it looks worse than Yakuza 0 or even Yakuza 5 During cutscenes the visuals are stellar, which only reinforces how disappointing the rest of the game can look.The cutscenes look great, though they only run at 30fps, despite the fact they are not pre rendered. And even still, the beautiful cutscenes are not prone to problems. Sometimes there is stutter, frame drops or camera jittering, which really takes away from how polished they feel. Considering how the rest of the game runs at at a constant 120fps on the highest settings 1920x1080, I don't think the issues present during the cutscenes are an issue with my hardware. The 30fps cap is not limited to the cutscenes as it is also present in activities such as Karaoke, Buyo Dance and Cho-Han.While visuals are a minor gripe, a much more prolific issue is the technical issues at play. There have been accounts of instability as there is a lack of shader compiling though I haven't experienced this all too much. (whether that be to hardware or having the game on an SSD) An issue I have experienced is very rarely, there are battles that have no music, which just feels really weird and uncomfortable.Combat is refreshing, although a bit underwhelming at times. Gunman is a broken style that turns the game into Devil May Cry 2, even on legendary. Wild dancer is a fun style to use, though not as versatile as Swordsman which is clearly the main style that should be focused on. Brawler is really disappointing and underpowered (even with the loincloth that gives a 90% increase to brawler attacks). To coincide with brawler being a letdown, heat actions feel incredibly weak, weaker than they were in Yakuza 3. Not even from an aspect of damage, but visually, they look very underwhelming and do not pack any sort of punch, which even Yakuza 5 and 0 did, not to mention Kiwami 2 or Judgment. This was probably done to provide more emphasis on the new Trooper Card system.The new Troopers that can be used in combat are a cool addition, if not a bit strange as even on Legendary, it makes boss fights seem pretty trivial (how this fairs on Ishin, I do not know.) It is cool to see some characters such as Ichiban, Nishitani and Makoto as well as the appearance of some guest characters and even animals from the series such as Nugget, Mame and Yama-Oroshi, though these cards can be disabled if one wishes to do so. It is unclear if RGG will keep this new feature in upcoming games or if it was just a one off thing specially made for Ishin Kiwami.The substories are some of the weakest, or even, the worst, the series has seen, as a significant number of them end up being speaking to a person, giving them an item or doing something for them and then unlocking a "friendship" with them, akin to that seen in Judgment, however, unlike Judgment or Kiwami 2, these provide no benefits and only act as underwhelming filler, though not all substories are bad as in some of them we get to see some characters from other games such as Bacchus, Miss Tatsu and Shinji, but that still doesn't detract from how uninspired a portion of them tend to be.Even with all these downsides, Ishin Kiwami is splendid and rather enjoyable, given you've played the other games in the series. The recasting done for Ishin Kiwami is great as well as the return of characters from the original Ishin as we get to see fan favourites such as Mine, Nishiki, Kuze and Ryuji (sans the best part of the shower scene) come back. The story is solid and a well done historical fiction from 1860s Japan with Yakuza characters portraying historical figures.Finally seeing Ishin localised is great with a clear amount of high effort, however significant downsides that do detract from this being one of the better games in the franchise, and if this is a precedent of how Gaiden or Like a Dragon 8 will turn out to be, then I'd be rather worried. RGG's transition to the Unreal Engine has clearly not been smooth, and an important thing to note is that this is the first game without Toshihiro Nagoshi at the helm of the project. Hopefully this is only a small setback for the RGG team and future games will hopefully be stronger and more impressive than the preceding titles. Depending on the success of this game, RGG may hopefully decide to remake or port previous entires that are either region or console locked such as Kurohyou, Fist of the North Star: Lost Paradise or even the infamous Dead Souls (I wouldn't get hopes up for Kenzan considering the nature of the content within.)One day I plan to play the original Ishin to see how Kiwami stands up to it, even if it does have a language barrier to cross.

_childDocuments_.review: Ishin, more than any other game in the Yakuza franchise, is a game for the sickos, and potentially only the sickos. It's the kind of game that provides a rewarding experience first and foremost to those players who have already played every game in the series already, and are deeply invested in the characters and character interactions. By using the faces and voices of major and minor characters across all eight (at the time) main series games, the game does provide a touchstone for players who aren't familiar with the historical narrative being told (and for those who are, given that it takes plenty of liberties with the historical record in its narrative), but the fact remains that, in story and gameplay, Ishin is probably the least accessible game in the franchise, the kind of game where you really need to want to play it specifically.This is a remake of a PS3-era game, ported from its original engine to Unreal Engine 4, and it really does show its age in its animations and combat. The brawler-style Yakuza games very rarely miss in their combat, but Ishin provides a stilted, uncomfortable experience in basically every fight. You have four styles to work with, but one of them is uniformly useless, and two others tend to be situational at best. Most likely, you'll be spending most of your time in the swordsman style, and it makes the combat feel repetitive and not very engaging. Traversal can also be tedious, as the taxi equivalents are few and far between across the surprisingly large map, with a slow standard run speed and a harshly limited sprint. All in all, it makes movement feel unpleasant, which is a shame for a Yakuza game.The games in the series that falter in gameplay tend to make up for it in story, and I do think that Ishin does a decent job of this - even though the story is a historical retelling of the Bakumatsu period, and thus a far cry from being relatable for Western audiences especially, the game deploys its actors in fun, sometimes unexpected ways. Of course, most of the casting is straightforward - Kiryu as protagonist Sakamoto Ryoma, Kazama as a mentor figure, Nishiki as a rival, etc. - but there are a number of characters whose faces and roles in the main Yakuza series make their roles here quite intriguing. Keep an eye out for Mine and Shibusawa in particular, with Zhao and Joongi also creating intrigue in how they're used. Like I said before, it's a great way to help players connect with the characters of a story that would otherwise feel a little too far away from relatability, like watching a stage play.Side content is about as plentiful as you'd expect from one of the PS3-era Yakuza games, with fun spins on staples like karaoke and gambling dens. I personally found myself not really wanting to engage with much of it, given that I was kind of slogging through the game, but I definitely had a lot of fun with karaoke and the Haruka-related minigames, and there's plenty to do to space out the main story. This includes the weird dungeon-crawling side game related to the trooper cards, which I admittedly didn't bother with for a single second because it all seemed exhausting. The trooper cards and equipment upgrades are a huge grind, one that could end up being necessary for making the combat go a lot faster by giving you stronger weapons to work with. It's easily the most griped-about part of this game, which made me glad that I didn't end up really needing to bother with it.On the whole, despite the tone of my review, Ishin is not a bad game - I don't think there's a bad Yakuza game. I do think that you need to understand what you're diving into when you play it, and it's a game whose appeal is much narrower than the mainline games, but if you fall into the demographic who will get a lot out of it, I'd suggest picking it up. Just wait for a sale, and probably make sure you've played all of the main games before this one for the best experience.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is filled with a lot to do, some extremely rewarding tasks, some menial enjoyable tasks, some downright intrusive & not so much fun at all tasks (which is to be expected if you've been playing the entire RGG collection). All in all; this is a great game and a serious 8/10. The reason why I won't give it a 9 or 10/10 is because in my humble opinion, the combat, while incredibly satisfying and visually appealing for the player, leaves much to be desired when coming from the flawlessly capable and snappy combinations and styles from (0). The fighting feels slower (by the frames) and as much as I'd like to attribute that to realism on the developers part, it seems more like they over looked this minute detail in the grand scheme of this game. That high energy slow fighting kind of worked in 4,5 & 6 when you adjust to it and slow down so that the engine could actually render the right moves. Same goes for the story, while I might add the story is incredibly immersive, it also gets incredibly boring and as much as I love the dramatization most of the time in the RGG series, however, with the older characters I found myself almost rushing through the story trying to get somewhere the chapters are kind of strung together like this review, and even the most dramatic parts don't really sit how I feel the developers wanted them to, knowing that in canon the characters were "acting" metaphysically. Besides that and some initial graphical issues upon release, if you're into RGG storytelling and an almost entirely brand new IP using old IP characters consisting of edo period Japanese culture, subculture and socioeconomic turmoil please give this a try it has much to offer as far as actual open world game play & roleplay elements, cutscenes, incredible acting and minigames the majority of my gripes where intentionally critical considering these guys are making some of the greatest games on the market. Still can't wait for the rest of the games to drop, I'll be checking it out for sure. I really can't think of any thing else besides the chicken race glitch that got patched.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty much your Yakuza 3, 4, 5 or 0 set in a 'historic' setting but can be very much enjoyed even if you don't know or dislike history since it's all anime bullshieet anyway where freshly cut or shot down foes get back up their feet like nothing ever happened after suffering fatal wounds. Don't get me wrong though there's quite a few people dieing within it's story as usual but just the overall combat is typical japanese like that. You'll spend a lot of time eating your pain away when hurt which I can't say is unrealistic but it's like those old River City Ransom beat em up games: fight, eat, repeat. A formula all the yakuza games had anyway, so that didn't bother me or anything but do know what you'll find here if you're not familiar with these games or was expecting something else like say a Ghost of Tsushima.The main deal is it's humor and all the substories and minigames that can be done but you could decide to skip a few or even all of these and still have a grand time with a more fluent main story that way (just a harder time completing it on say a hard difficulty without some 'grind' or preparations in unlocked combat skills).That being said I always thought of the Yakuza series as something familiar other then just 'River City Ransom but 3D' but I couldn't quite put my finger on it until now: it's essentially Gintama.You're an oddjob self-exiled ronin instead of a robinhood yakuza this time around that's the main difference and you'll be helping or disrupting all kinds of exploits in and around town all the while having a main goal to figure out who's behind your father's murder. It is however to the player how fast or slow-phased this can be done.The presence of Haruka gave me quite a jumpscare as she is literally what ruined the series for me but the good thing is that she is way more optional this time around and she and her manor can be largely if not completely ignored (A big difference from the dreaded Orphanage of Yakuza 3).Another fellow I didn't quite miss was this Komaki the 'karate kid trainer' guy, he too is there but here's hoping he gets pancaked by a palanquin someday but other then that all the characters are amazing in their own right.It's overall another great edition and perhaps one of my favourite yakuza games so far even but it's not without it's common quirks and shortcomings in both wacky combat or graphics department though considering it's a remake of an older game that finally saw a release and translation one could look past that stuff after giving it a good few hours.There seems to be alot of folks complaining about it's graphics or combat mainly if not the mandatory xbox controller overlay when played with any controller, which I admit has been confusing for me as well especially with all the quick-timed-events in some of the cutscenes and minigames.The only real downside for me personally was that some of the pre-order extras got bugged and cannot be retrieved to this day... because I've got this pre-order edition from a friend I went the extra mile and mailed Sega about it but they point towards Steam and Steam back to Sega in a long story short: I couldn't retrieve these because of playing the US or Canadian version on a EU based Steam account apparently. Now I realise even before this problem occurs that I should not be within the EU but well.. I do hope they might fix it one day but it's not something that prevents me from playing the main game either so it's no gamebreaker. In fact all the free downloadable content doesn't seem to be affected interestingly enough only the pre-order or paid ones are.So there's a lesson in that :P

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who's played all the games in the Yakuza series, I'd recommend skipping this one, unless you get it for half price or less. Here's why I don't think this game measures up to the other ones: is probably the biggest miss. Out of the 4 combat styles, only two of them (sword and sword+gun) are usable overall. The third style, unarmed, deals about 20% of the damage as the other styles, and on harder difficulties, this means you're just pounding away on each random thug for 90+ seconds before they finally go down. The final style, gunman, has so many oddities and bugs that ruin the combat. The biggest one is that when you shoot an enemy in gunman style, there's a 50% chance that they'll start an infinite loop of taunting you, so they just stand there while you spend the next 15 seconds shooting them to death. There are some flashy moves in each style, but you'll find yourself going back to the same two styles over and over again, just so you don't lose every fight.  , which are those comedic side-quests which characterise the Yakuza series, have lost almost all entertainment value due to the implementation of the "friends system". In this game, you meet characters on the street who will ask you for things from your inventory, and then give you some short dialogue to thank you. To maximise the "friend gauge" of that character, you need to give them the same kind of item, and listen to the exact same dialogue about 10-20 more times before that character is complete, and they give you the comedic end of their painfully dragged-out story. It's like being told the setup of a joke, and then being forced to complete 15 identical fetch quests before they tell you the punchline. The huge time delay between the start and end of each substory makes them a lot less funny than in the other Yakuza games.  is alright, but slightly worse than what a fan of the series would typically expect. The main appeal is that they've included a huge cast of returning characters from all the previous Yakuza games, so for example, a longtime fan might get really excited to see how a conversation would play out between Kuze from Yakuza 0 and Mine from Yakuza 3. The game definitely delivers on the ensemble of characters, but the game fails to give enough screen time to anyone. There are times where major characters die off screen.  There are also times where important characters literally disappear from the game, and are never even mentioned again. This alone isn't enough of a reason not to buy the game, but it certainly doesn't help justify the game's $80 CAD price tag.Here are some other issues I had with the game, but couldn't sort into the above three categories:If you're a hardcore Yakuza series fan who would get excited about this game's ensemble cast, I would recommend waiting until the game is at least 50% off before purchasing, since the main story one of the only reasons to get this game. However, with RGG Studio releasing 1-2 Yakuza games every year, it might be best to wait until the next game comes out this November.

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyable game, nice setting, interesting story and a famous Japanese exclusive. Fun mini-games, karaoke is enjoyable as always (baka mitai but with samurai :D), a lot to do and a lot to see.......but the game is grindy AS HELL!!! The opponents can get quire spongy and the bosses can be challenging. They changed the original blacksmith mechanic and now it SUUUUUUUUCKS. You need SOOOOOO much money, time and resources to do anything and god help you if you want to do 100% blacksmith. If you want to put up the work you can make very broken weapons in this game with seals. Managed to make a gun that shoots like a machine-gun, melts armor, had a big chance of doubling the bullets fired and the damaged was limit caped because it was that high . In a room with 40 guys you can obliterate all of them in like 15 seconds. Accidentally i also made a god killing katana that killed all bosses in a few combos. Amon was down in 1 (ONE) combo...4 fighting stances Brawler (useless almost immediately), Swordsman (powerful but slow), Gunman (stay in one spot and kill everything in sight if you have a good gun) and Wild Dancer (absolutely wonderful stance, super agile, quick cuts and gun shots, almost cannot be hit if you move and the most fun i had in a long time with a fighting system).The card system is garbage, it breaks the game. Without those it is a very skill based fighting game, with those you can just power through almost all content. Sure, some full attack animations were funny but it is a whole different game with those. You almost have to use them or at least equip them for the bonus stats and that is a shame.The plot is Yakuza like so the fans know what to expect but new people will enjoy it as well, music was fun and memorable and the game overall is really good but it has its flaws :)Would recommend, just know what you are getting into (i think the blacksmith mechanic, alone, took about 40 hours with the dungeon grind but i was curious how far i could push it so it is not standard time :) )

_childDocuments_.review: An interesting take on Samurai class conflict with all of your favorite Yakuza characters.  There are a lot of returning themes you expect as well as some new ones that really help spice it up.  For example, you gain two types of experience:  one is based on whatever style you have equipped and one is general experience.  When you level up, you get training orbs and style orbs.  Style orbs are specific to that particular style, but training orbs can be used on any style, so you can develop as you wish.Virtue takes place of CP and is hyper useful as it controls several different mini-buffs that don't directly influence combat, but many things happening within the game itself.  You can cook, farm, sing karaoke, dance, fish, and so much more.  This is an amazing and addictive Yakuza experience that's unapologetically Japanese and I absolutely love it.

But the other substories are pretty solid, though the substory radar is a bit hidden since it's a craftable hat this time.Minigames:I really love the minigames in Yakuza and they were solid here.Big Minigames: (2)- - Unique Minigames (Not counting those which are in most other games like Shogi, etc.) : 6- - - - - Conclusion:It's a very solid Yakuza game, it does things a bit differently than the real mainline Yakuza games, but it still is a Yakuza game at heart. _childDocuments_.review: As of posting there is a shader compilation stutter issue. Every time an effect happens for the first time you'll get a stutter, sometimes a big one. Thankfully this isn't the kind of game where new effects are happening all the time, but when it does happen it's extremely annoying.The move to Unreal Engine is devoid of benefits, there's no HDR support, no raytracing (at least give us shadows), no modern features such a move should create. And it looks as good as previous games but not really better, maybe lighting in some areas (at least it doesn't have the generic unreal engine look).Not only is there no HDR support the game forces the setting off if you try to modify the config. I hate that, I wish studios would stop doing that.The worst issue is 30fps cinematics, thats absurd, I can understand a 60fps limit for technical reasons but 30 is an unreasonable compromise to me. I hope that can be fixed cause when you can easily play a game at 120FPS, 30fps REALLY stands out.There's some nitpicks about camera movement where it just feels off for some reason, not very smooth.Another nit pick is the pause screen does not confirm if you want to skip a cut scene. IMO it's otherwise same old Yakuza, I played 13 hours straight today by accident. I love these games and the samurai ♥♥♥♥ is fresh as ♥♥♥♥, I love seeing old characters in a new context and see how things play out. I can fully recommend this despite my issues above. I'm posting my complaints in the hopes they fix these issues but truthfully they don't detract from the game entirely.I hope by launch the shader comp issues and 30fps cut scenes are fixed, and I hope they add HDR support before I finish the game.

_childDocuments_.review: This is from a perspective of a person who played the original on PS3 and PS4 almost a decade ago.The main story is very enjoyable, I personally do not like some of the changes they did for the character models and they did did remove at least one cutscene from the game which was dissapointing. With MSQ they did not have much to improve so I wont talk about that more than I did already.My main problem with this remake is how antiquated the game feels in many aspects. A lot of the small things that were in the original game and were part of the series during the PS3-era are still in the game. Things like only being able to order one food item at a time from a restaurant, only being able to donate one item at a time to a NPC, not having infinite run even at the end of the game and so on. A lot of these small aspects of the game that feel trivial, but when in most parts of the game there are these small aspects that feel more they are wasting your time, it really starts to add up on the frustration. I was hoping that they would iron out a lot of these small things for this remake but they did not. The whole games definitely a 2014 game that just has pretty cutscenese, instead of a proper Kiwami treatment like 1 and 2 got.Combat is still unbalanced as hell. They did nerf the gun style by a little bit, but you can still tear through the msq with a strong gun without having any problems. The OG game was a prototype for stance system that appeared in Yakuza 0 so it was understandable that the system was unbalanced, but for a remake I wish they would have put more effort into making it more balanced. The XP needed to get to higher levels for each stance and limit breaks etc is absolutely insane. I guess I could grind for xp in the arena for tens of hours before I would reach the max level for each stance but there is not much point in that besides achievements.The Economy of the game and crafting also requires "insane" amount of grind if you want to craft the stronger weapons. Recently the easiest way to gain money was patched out so any of the more expensive options require you to grind for money.TLDR; a 10 year old game released with prettier graphics and some QoL improvements which in the end feel half assed, because there are so many things they could have improved. The game itself is not bad by no means, Iam more dissapointed by the remake itself, because with some of the QoL stuff from the newer games, Ishin could have been way more enjoyable experience and that is the point of remakes, bring an older game to modern standards. If I would want to go through two menus and a loading screen every time I want to eat food in a restaurant, I would boot up the PS4-version on my PS5.

_childDocuments_.review: The worst Yakuza experience currently available on Steam. Play literally any other Yakuza game for a fraction of the price, get this if you love the series and it's on at least a 50% sale.My biggest gripe with this game are the combat styles, aside from Wild Dancer (which is actually a great style) this game has a worse combat experience than all of the mainline Yakuza games. Brawler is massively underpowered and basically unusable throughout the game, even if you try to buff it by slotting in the Brawler damage increase seals it still does a fraction of the damage of every other style. Gunman is a single button spam style, it really has no combos and without a Pierce seal on your gun, it is unusable against armored enemies. Swordsman is the worst style I've ever experienced in a Yakuza game. Imagine the Beast style but it does less damage, has less range/aoe, and doesn't have the massive advantage of Beast's omnidirectional block and hugely reduced damage while blocking. It is absolutely miserable. The game has some other pretty serious issues with combat and combat related progression/mechanics. Heat moves in this game are more sparse than other Yakuza entries, for example, you have to level and acquire simple Heat moves you normally have as default for styles, such as the standard downed, grab and near a wall Heat moves. This game is also way more finicky when it comes to activating specific Heat moves with unique activation parameters, and even has enemies you cannot use Heat moves on at all. When you level a style to max you are able to "break your limits" and unlock the same exact leveling tree to progress through again, nothing new or exciting. The game also has a lot of really janky hitboxes, which I think contributes to the sketchiness of the Heat actions, but is also really annoying for combat. The enemy spear and two handed mace hitboxes really stand out.The crafting in the game is solid, although the economy of the game is a bit of a mess, they apparently nerfed the sell value of plates from the original and seem to have gone overboard. Without a ton of grinding (or exploiting) you don't really have the freedom to make many of the high level weapons to either try out different elements or the extra weapon styles, as the game doesn't have the usual activity aimed directly at making you money like most Yakuza games have now. It also effects your ability to enlist new troops as the best pull is a reasonably high sum for only getting 1 troop at a time, but the game gives you very solid troops for free. The Seal system is an absolute mess because the drop rate is hilariously low. When I finished the game having completed 97% of sub stories, every battle dungeon, and had capped out the diligence report for random encounter and sneaks by chapter 7, I had dropped 9 unique seals (I had a varying amount of those 9 but none over 7 total.) I think there are 30 or 32 total unique seals, and they're a powerful way to increase player power. It's very annoying to basically not get to interact with this system unless you use some of the goofy ways people are using to attain them, like spam crafting low level weapons just to disassemble them if they spawn with a seal. I love the Yakuza series and this was a huge disappointment.

_childDocuments_.review: After 64 hours into the game on Hard difficulty I can safely say:- Fix the DLCs being one-time use only. That is unfair and predatory.- Fix the Minigames and Cutscenes being locked at 30FPS. Most PCs out there are capable of handling such, and it's sad to see in 2023.- Rebalance the difficulties. They are not exactly what I'd call "fair". Enemies are plus on basically every attack, some can't even be staggered, and some go as far as being so unrelenting they will hit you as soon as a fight scene starts without giving you a chance to react.- Rebalance styles. Swordsman plays horribly, and I avoid the style like the plague because of how minus it is. You get animation locked on so many moves, because apparently the move speeds up, but the actual mechanic of it isn't, so you're stuck sitting there taking all the hits. Plus, either I'm doing it wrong, or Wild Dancer's quickstep avoids probably like only half the attacks.- Rebalance smithing. Sure, it's meant to be grindy, but when I'm actively avoiding a whole mechanic of the game because it's just that bad to get a hold of? Then something's probably wrong. I would rather run a dungeon 30 times and hope I drop a better weapon, than use the blacksmith. (I avoided doing such by simply going through the story, no spoilers.)I would die for this company but, with how this game is shaping up to be I can't, in good conscience, recommend it to my friends and tell them "Sure, you'll have fun, trust me."I understand wanting to use a different engine and be experimental with it, and I appreciate how you guys have translated basically almost the entire Dragon Engine 1:1, but I'm sad to say it doesn't work. I hope you guys aren't working on having Gaiden and 8 use Unreal Engine too, and if you are, fix these issues while you're ahead. Please, act while you're ahead and do better.If I have any more issues, I will edit this in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: This was such an awesome game! For context, I started playing the Yakuza series just a couple years ago (started with Yakuza 0, then played through the PC remakes of 1-6, then Like a Dragon, and now this), and I have thoroughly enjoyed the series so far. Note that I never played the original version of this (I didn't even realize there  an original release), so this was my first experience with this game.It was really cool seeing the characters I recognize from the original Yakuza series play through this plot in feudal Japan. A small thing I actually  appreciated was that the dialogue boxes included a "show definition" type button when historical Japanese terms were stated: it was a cool learning experience (I don't know a lot about feudal Japan), and it helped me remind myself of key terms the characters kept saying so I wouldn't get lost in the plot. It was a subtle but really nice touch, and I hope they (and other game devs) continue to do so in the future!As far as the game itself, the graphics were solid in my opinion: they were what you would expect from the modern Yakuza games (great scenery, fairly realistic textures, etc.). The non-cutscene character interactions look robotic like the other games, but I think that's fine. The music was also really great. The gameplay was like the other Yakuza games in terms of beat-em-up combat style, but this time, you have 3 combat styles: one where you just use a sword, one where you just use a gun, and one where you use both a sword and a gun simultaneously. I thought this was a nice touch, as there were some enemy types that I preferred fighting ranged, and others that I wanted to get in and fight in close combat.The story was also pretty good; pretty much what you would expect from the Yakuza series (except instead of it being a Yakuza-centric plot, it was a plot about the political system in feudal Japan; similar feeling, though). It was really interesting seeing the interactions between feudal Japan and the British Empire; a really cool historical adventure!Overall, I definitely recommend this game: it's another excellent entry in the Yakuza series :-)

_childDocuments_.review: It hurts me to leave a thumbs down on an RGG LAD game. I absolutely adore this studio I've finished every mainline PC game, and with this I've now finished every spin-off too that's come on PC. (the Judgements are really good, look into them)The biggest gripe I have is that the story constantly loses me. There's this dissonance of the "Guns only kill in cutscenes" narrative that feels especially egregious here. So much so that it repeatedly takes me out of it. Ryoma doesn't like to kill in that recognizable old Kiryu fashion, but... he's using a pistol, and a sword, both being very excellent tools of KILLING. Yet every non-story fight I've gone through feels like I just smashed them with a Boken.And you may think "Yeah, every Yakuza/LAD game is like that.", sure, but there's a difference with a story fight in a Yakuza cutscene brushing off any in-game weapons as Kiryu *actually* using his fists. In Ishin though? Every fight's a sword fight, and they've definitely been shown to be fatal. A tryout almost gets gutted and is told to find a doctor before he bleeds out. Swords are repeatedly established as killing tools in cutscenes, but when a boss-fight ends it repeatedly seems like they've gotten away with just scrapes.Y'know what? That's one point we can look past. It's RGG, playing loose with what's fatal and what isn't is just how they roll and after seven Yakuza mainlines games and the new direction with LAD, I'm usually pretty used to it. And of course there's the fact that LAD Ishin is a remake of the original Ishin, so they couldn't really change the story. Seeing old faces replaced with recognizable faces and voices is pretty neat. I liked all the Y0 callbacks, as that one still remains as my favorite. Feels just a little fanservicey, though.I just wish the combat didn't feel this samey.Brawler is useless as a style compared to the rest, it almost feels present out of obligation to the series. And I get that, but it could've been more useful. What if Brawler came with a disarm out of the box? Which is something the other styles have to unlock. Could be a good cheap source of Bundle Swords for crafting before you get your hands on a lot of cash through Chicken Races.Swordsman is for fighting bosses mainly, though it's useful in any situation. This is the style you'll probably lean on the most out of comfort. It hits hard, has a lot of interesting techniques and in general just feels the tankiest.Gunman is there to mop up mainly as anything remotely threatening can rush you down far too fist. You're either spamming bullets or throwing special ammo repeatedly, which can be a drain on resources. If special ammo stood out a bit better, it'd at least have a fighting chance compared to Swordsman. As it stands though, it's only good to invest in its tree in order to unlock the cannon, which is just too goofy of a weapon to not at least give a try.Wild Dancer combines both weapons, which leads to a fighting style that's fast, low-damage for either weapon, and primarily defends itself through dodges and very narrow parries. It's main use is for dealing with a lot of enemies at one time, since enemy AI loves to attack you in the back while you're using Swordsman.None of it particularly wows me. One of the greatest features of the Yakuza/LAD/Judgement series was that you had plenty of ways to spice up combat. Mainly heat actions and building out a skilltree that organically complements that past few unlocks. In LAD Ishin though, it's a mixture of stat boosts, attack speeds, Heat action unlocks and maybe a couple of actual interesting systems thrown in like a disarm or a combo rush move extension. It's nowhere near as interesting as Yakuza 0, which I will admit to be an unfair comparison.The cards system isn't bad, but it's rather forgettable. Damage skills really don't do as much damage as they ought to (even the overpowered lvl99 ones you get from that free Youtuber DLC), and the damage buffs don't seem to do a whole lot either. The best use I got out of them were the free heals, which took the pressure entirely off of any healing items in my inventory. The system's not a detriment, but for how flashy it looks and predominant a place it takes in the UI, it sure doesn't feel very significant.Ultimately I would say that you can do much, much better than this if you're looking for an RGG game on PC. Both Judgement games are stellar, the mainline Yakuza series maybe gets a little rough at its numerical middle, but feels like a heartwarming epoch when you finally finish Y6. Yakuza LAD is absolutely GOATed, too.LAD Ishin doesn't tarnish my faith in RGG. I'm more than confident that the two new games coming out are going to be beyond stellar, and I honestly can't wait.

_childDocuments_.review: Like a Dragon: Ishin!Wow what a game. It's actually much easier to hate on it and find everything that is wrong with it rather than to focus on the good. Ishin is almost indefensible and I could easily see how people new to the Ryu Ga Gotoku games would totally hate and ♥♥♥♥ all over it. Game is very dated, what was acceptable and cool 5-10 years ago now is not, it's time to move on yet the game is stuck with it's archaic formula. Pretty much all side content is busy work - dungeon - busy work with good rewards only in 3rd dungeon, 2nd life - total trash waste of time with no rewards, as side note it's nice to see Haruka and all but you can't engage with her. Although game says that you can talk to her and bring her gifts or that someone will come to collect 100 RYO for the farm but for me it never triggered, can't talk to Haruka, can't give her gifts nothing,  just cook for her which is so slow and mindbogglingly dumb way to interact, it just sucks. Fishing is there and 1 substory requires you to get a king tuna for the cat, doable but not fun. Graphics also feel very dated, especially when it's not main characters or the expensive brothel, think most generic substory npc's are taken straight from last decade. There are 4 fighting styles - bare fisted but with ability to use special weapons - trash with moderately fast attack speed and like 10 damage, swordmaster with sluggish but strong attacks, gunner, once you get VORTEX gun this is the way to fight, poor mouse though and finally blade dancer style is the way to go fast, strong endless combos and easy to dodge. Game difficulty - easy, not only can you have food that restores gazillion hp but you can also apply medicine in the middle of a fight. There is crafting but it's so basic no point even mention. Some weapons better than others, read fire or lighting swords better than anything else.I've completed game on hard difficulty with 47% completion, which is a lot for Like a Dragon series and while I seen most of the content not a lot of it is a good content mostly busywork.Map design is okay. Annoying that Ryomas name is not Kiryu Kazuma, almost feels like you're playing a different guy however he, himself is still the headstrong bigger than the world character, very charming with awful ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ clothes. Those trousers are ♥♥♥♥.Reflecting upon it no way I would ever be able to recommend this game to anyone who is not already a fan of Yakuza series games, judgement excluding because judgement series is a trash. So this is a hard sell for new players and passable experience for series veterans. Now when game is done, I don't think I'll ever pick it up but I might pickup Yakuza kiwami series as those were brilliant. Also btw the story is trash for anyone who is not Japanese, looks like they needed some patriotic inspiration but as a non Japanese player I can't relate to this crap, not a fan. The villain reveal in the last act is mega cringe, a parody and they even added the over the top evil laugh...yeah ok.So finally it's a pretty bad game, looks like all the good writers have left studio and now interns took their place. Definitely not the way to get fans on board to spawn an epic game series like they did with Yakuza, need way more effort.

_childDocuments_.review: Remember a few years ago when Deus Ex tried to sell single use skill point microtransactions in a single player game and it went so poorly for them they never made another game in the franchise? Well here we have the same thing happening again but they're trying to keep it quiet to avoid the inevitable backlash. Just to be clear, it isn't single use per save. It's one use ever. That alone isn't the reason for a negative review though it certainly puts the game in a bad standing. The fact they also increased the games price after release also doesn't help the game much when talking about the game's value. If you haven't played all the other games in the franchise I would recommend literally any of them over this for the price to content/quality ratio. Also since this is a kinda fan service throwback game a lot of the references to characters will be lost if you haven't played at least the main Yakuza franchise without the spin offs. Then you also have the stuttering and 30fps lock in cutscenes, boring repetitive substories, then incredibly grindy crafting mechanics. Every new action requires the game to render the shader for the animation. (Not too dissimilar to the issues The Callisto Protocol had/has on release) This means the game will stutter every time a new animation is played for the first time. So every heat move, every unique boss battle, every time you use a new weapon with a new glow on it. The game can be running a solid framerate without ever dropping in gameplay but then stutters like crazy for anything new. It basically ruins any interesting boss battle. "Oh they're doing something cool... oh I missed it because the game was stuttering... I can only hope they do it a second time or I'll never know what happened." This also happens in the 30fps cutscenes... so playing it a second time for NG+ you won't have these issues but you also won't have any of the dlc you paid for (including what you got from the deluxe version.) Then the lacklustre substories. At this point I've played pretty much every game in the franchise plus the spin off games and I honestly can't think of any game that had so many boring repetitive substories. So many are just you come across a person, they want an item, you give them an item, wait a minute later and give them the same item again, repeat 10 times and that's a substory complete. There's not even a unique interaction every time you give them something outside of the first interaction and the final item. This is the vast majority of substories. This isn't the maxing out a shop owner either, which feels like it takes a lot more transactions than it does in previous games as well. There are a few unique substories but they feel so rare. This makes the substory from zero about getting toys from the claw machine for the little girl look like a breath of fresh air since you actually have to do something before you return and do the same task again and again. Then the crafting. Honestly playing on hard, just ignore it. The whole mechanic is so grindy for so little reward it isn't worth the effort. It feels like something that's there just for NG+ and the new difficulties that come with it where everything has it's numbers bloated. You can buy weapons very early on that are better than 3/4th's of the swords you can craft. Then you're given weapons through main story battles so you never need to craft anything yourself. It requires so much money to level up the crafting to be able to make something better than what you can already buy elsewhere then the costs to build stuff is crazy. You do get 200 ryo for completing the game which will offset a lot of the costs, hence it feels like a NG+ thing. Also I dread to think how much grinding you would have to do in the battle dungeons to unlock all the materials you would need to craft anything worthwhile. All in all outside of the main quest and the minigames there isn't much in this game to recommend. In previous games the substories were some of the best parts. They were always so crazy and unique almost every time whereas in this they're all so mundane and they feel so copy and pasted in what you have to do. The game has performance issues which we're still waiting on getting fixed. Then the monetisation of the game is questionable at best. If you really want to play the game I would wait until a deep sale, maybe by that point the game will have it's performance patched so its enjoyable to play on the first run not just the second. Also if you do play I'd highly recommend getting a trainer, something like WeMod or something, in order to get what you would get from the paid consumable dlc for free. It would also remove the grinding if you really wanted to craft something for yourself.

_childDocuments_.review: Like a Dragon Ishin! thrusts players into the tumultuous world of 19th-century Japan with its blend of historical drama and thrilling gameplay. As a spin-off of the acclaimed "Yakuza" series, this game delivers the same addictive mix of action, humor, and heartfelt storytelling, set against the backdrop of the Bakumatsu period. With its engaging combat, memorable characters, and attention to detail, Like a Dragon Ishin! offers an unforgettable journey through samurai-era Japan that will delight fans of the series and newcomers alike.
_childDocuments_.name: Like a Dragon: Ishin!

_childDocuments_.review: If you know the Yakuza games, you know what to expect.This game is more of the same with the same characters but translocated into a historical setting.In essence this loosely tackles the historical unit known as the Shinsengumi and the final days of the Bakufu / Tokugawa Shogunate.It is a period where you get to play with both katana and firearm.1) The Gameplay:- Multiple fighting techniques.- Crafting.- A very good cinematic combat system.- You can focus on the main quest or tinker with a lot of side activities, some familiar to Yakuza fans. (singing, dancing, planting a garden, taking care of pets, helping people out recurirngly)- There is a pretty good and indepth rpg system as well when it comes to leveling. Allowing you to flesh out your fighting styles.The story:- The main story much like the Yakuza ones is King. You could just play it for the story and walk away satisfied. As usual there are some plot twists and unexpected events. - The characters are nuanced and interesting.- A lot of history is twisted into the epic plot while adding in a ton of fantasy elements.- The sidestories are whacky but very variable in quality. There is little story here. All in all a strong recommendation for:- Fans of the Yakuza franchise.- Fans of the period.- Fans who like a cinematic storyline with an arcadey fleshed out action system.- People who enjoy a game that offers a lot of optional grind. (most of it to be enjoyed in New Game + probably)

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game expecting a Yakuzah opus situated in feudal Japan. And while there is a lot less humor, it's still quite similar: Lots of side missions, mini-games and stories that give life to the ingame world (the udon minigame is stressful but fun). The cinematics and the story are just as good.But after 10 hours of playing, I have to admit it:The combat system is simply and purely catastrophic.In a serie known for its over-the-top fights, what we have there is below mediocre; The fighting styles rank from useless to barely passable : -Brawler style, useless except for picking up the few tools you can use (then you quickly realize they do less damage than your weapons.)-Swordmaster style, kinda usable against mobs, not really against bosses. Stiff and unresponsive.-Gun style, button-mashing cheese. Game is too hard ? Walk backwards and go pew pew pew.-Wild dancer style, the most useful one (not saying much), At least, allows you to quickly dodge.Another problem shared by all styles : they're all boring to use, even with unlocked skills. Same with the Heat actions : you either go *slash* or *bang*, nothing extraordinary or original. Even Way of the samurai 4 on the PS3 has a more interesting and complete fighting system.Add to that weird pauses when doing actions like picking up items or clicking in the menu and you get a game that's only interesting during cinematics. So you might as well watch a movie.

_childDocuments_.review: So this is the first RGG game that has come out since I played, you know, every one of their other western releases. I like this game.First and foremost: this game feels like a remake that wanted to be faithful to the original game, presenting as an older game with graphical updates. As such it feels less like a full remake than an exceptional remaster (having not played the original myself). It is not as high quality as Yakuza: LAD, or even Judgment/Lost Judgment. I put this first because it was a sentiment I could never quite escape while playing.Second: the grind for money and mats is REAL. It's definitely worth it, especially with your weapons (Futsu-no-Mitama my beloved) but it can be a real slog, even with the chicken racing exploit. My favorite part was the sex minigame.
_childDocuments_.name: Like a Dragon: Ishin!

_childDocuments_.review: I still have this very special connection to Ishin serving as a sort of departures from modernity into a world that stands at a crossroads of what has been and what is. The feudal Japanese setting made it feel special and calming even. This remake of the original Ryu Ga Gotoku: Ishin! enables Westerners to immerse themselves into a beautiful Japanese world that appears familiar to players of the LAD franchise, and due to its 19th century setting, while at the same time feeling distant due to the traditional Japanese customs and difference from those games of the series that are set in modern Japan. The accordance of distance and nearness creates an amazing setting.The combat was fun albeit it had poor hitboxes. Often, Ryoma doesn't even visually touch the enemy for it to count as a hit, or the weapon swing isn't even executed yet, but the hit already connected. Other than that, the combat can feel very fluid and fancy or heavy and methodic.The story was very interesting and full of exciting political intrigue. It felt special to see Kiryu's face actually do some important political ♥♥♥♥ and kill people. Without spoiling too much, you are not looking at a historically 100% accurate depiction of Sakamoto Ryoma's life during the Meiji Restoration, but instead at a fanfiction of a cooler version of Sakamoto Ryoma by a very talented author. The grind, as usual, is terrible, not respectful of the player's time and agonisingly slow.I have played the game for about 75 hours, and have not 100%ed a single of the four fighting styles. If you strive for 100% completion on Steam, don't. The game, like most LAD games, is littered with nonsensical quests, heaps of minigames out of which not all are fun or based on luck, and to complete the Blacksmith you are forced to loot so many more enemies or do so many more missions of the same to collect enough loot to craft everything. Without 100%ing the game, you're looking at a fun experience, with 100%, you are looking at dozens of hours more of doing repetitive, boring and agonising stuff over and over again. ♥♥♥♥ that.TL;DR good game, play the story and then some but stay away from 100%

_childDocuments_.review: I'm 23 hours in and I'm still in Chapter 3 because I keep getting distracted by minigames and substories. Incredible amount of content.Weird that they branded this a remake though. I know it's in Unreal instead of the Dragon Engine, but it uses all of the UI elements, physics, and controls of the games in the Yakuza 0, 5, and Kiwami engine. I'm not complaining because I love the way those games are played, and I never played the Japanese release of the original Ishin, but this really feels like they did the Crisis Core/Metroid Prime method of remastering where they replace all the models with newer ones and add a few new features. It's still worth it though, since we never got the original here and it's absolutely worth playing.

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyed my time with this game. The story is your usual Ryu Ga Gotoku affair with twists and turns sometimes to the point its admittedly hard to follow this time around. The side content is plentiful and the setting is a refreshing departure, we don't see many games explore 1800s Japan. The voice work is as always top tier, zero possible complaints on that front. Yakuza (or I guess like a dragon now) games always set the bar for voice acting and nothing compares with just the incredible voiceover work. Ishin has no English dub for the people who care but why would you play a Yakuza game with a dub?My sole complain with this game is they didn't really do anything for the combat, the combat on this game just feels VERY dated after coming from games like Judgement, which is understandable since this game was made with their older engine years ago.Solid game, easily recommendable if you like Yakuza or find the setting interesting.
_childDocuments_.name: Like a Dragon: Ishin!

_childDocuments_.review: This low budget remake is my least favourite Yakuza game to date. The original was made between Yakuza 5 and 0 so you'd think it'd have some of the best gameplay in the series. Unfortunately, at least in this low budget unreal engine demake, the combat is Yakuza 3 levels of tedious. Every enemy has way too much health and all your styles feel useless and require no skill to use. It even feels like enemy AI has degraded to the point where they'll just stand around and watch you slowly tickle them to death one by one. Group encounters used to involve using throws and positioning to prevent getting ganged up on, even by small groups. Ishin enemies also stay grounded way too long? It's a weird thing to complain about but it makes the game feel cheap when you're doing your sword attacks on an enemy on the ground, not even hitting them, and they still take the damage. The gameplay feels like a cheap Yakuza unity engine rip-off made by one dude in his basement is what I'm trying to say. I could nitpick the gameplay all day long I hate it so much and I haven't even begun to talk about the horrible weapon upgrade system, free influencer DLC or the P2W garbage that you'd expect from an EA game. Even the story, the one element that you'd expect to be consistent is ruined by pandering to new fans of the series. Being a fanservice spinoff, most of the characters in the game are based off of pre-existing characters from the main series. However, for this remake they've changed who some of those characters are. Yakuza 1-5 characters are swapped out with yakuza 0, 6 and 7 characters but the roles that they play in the story are the exact same and they often make no sense. The graphics are a minor downgrade I'd say. Character models and environments are just a bit off, I also had some issues with LOD being really low upon entering a new zone but maybe that's just my computer. The worst offenders are the lighting and the blood effects. These look awful, the lighting is especially bad with large fires and candles. If you're looking for more Yakuza and you have played 1-6 just play those. Or Judgement I'm sure that's leagues better than this low quality remake. Worst part about this remake is that we'll never get the original game in english now. Most disapointing game I've played in years.

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely not the best RGG game, but we should remember that this is a remake of an old game. The plot is decent, but I couldn't help but notice the painful grind and how repetitive the game in that matter is. A lot of substories in which you just have to make cirles around the map and give different characters stuff they want, be it food, healing items, random items, cooked meals, vegetables, and so on. There's more of what to grind, but I wouldn't want to spoil what this game has — when you see it, you'll know it.In general, the game looks nice, but you don't need to be an expert to see a Yakuza 5 Kiwami here. However, the CGI are great here. They also did a good job adding the character models from different games, including the Dragon Engine ones.The DLC's are almost completely useless. You can get some free DLCs, but I used it only once to cheese a fight in a substory, so I don't recommend buying them at all. Only if you want to support the studio, but honestly, this is not something I would buy. There are far better games that show their worth beyond the basic edition.So, I wouldn't recommend buying it at full price. There's almost nothing new in the gameplay mechanics, and the game is not that great to be honest. But being an RGG game, it's still worth playing.

_childDocuments_.review: At the time of writing this, I've put in 37 hours which surprised me.  It absolutely does not feel like I've played for more than a couple hours.  You can't go more than 5 mins without finding something new to grab your interest.  Between the side quests, engaging combat, and mini games there is always something to keep you running around Kyo.  This is the first entry in the Like a Dragon series that I have been able to play at launch without having the thought in the back of my mind that I have more entries to go through.  Maybe that fact is why I am able to let myself get lost in the game and engage with the content available without trying to advance to the next title.The Yakuza series has always had varying combat styles to chose from but they all largely revolved around unarmed combat.  It's refreshing to have combat styles that focus on permanent equipment.  The gunman style is straight broken but it is so cathartic to unload on an enemy that has been giving you issues.  I can't help but laugh after re-enacting the Indiana Jones scene in a hard combat scenario.  I started my first playthrough on Ishin difficulty and oh boy does it go hard.  Most trash mob enemies can kill you in two hits.  Bosses almost always one-shot you.  Don't say I didn't warn you.The story is essentially a who-dun-it revenge story. A colorful cast of characters who have been staples throughout the Yakuza series return but with different names and in feudal japan.  It's easy to find a character that quickly becomes your favorite.  If you've never played a Yakuza (Like a Dragon) game prior to this entry,  you can easily start with this title.  You don't need to know a single thing about the series to follow the plot of this title.  Honestly, you'd be doing yourself a disservice by passing on this game.The twitch content creator troop cards is dumb.  Nyanners and these other random e-celebs stick out so hard in a feudal japan setting.  However, you can completely ignore the content creator trooper cards if you don't download the DLC.Still dumb though.9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Like a Dragon: Ishin!

_childDocuments_.review: The game can be played and enjoyed whether you're a Like a Dragon fan or not. The combat is something unique for the series and it's pretty fun, although I only really got any meaningful use out of 2 of the 4 styles. The RPG elements were...fine. They didn't detract from the experience but they weren't really something that changed the game a whole lot. The story is very good with plenty of drama, plot twists and awesome moments with great set pieces as you'd expect from the series. No spoilers but near the end of the game where you storm a location with Majima is honestly up there with some of the greatest moments in the franchise. RGG knows what we like.The minigames are once again great, karaoke and dancing with this edo period style was fun and just randomly finding the ramen minigame and hearing this game's rendition of Machine Gun Kiss play was so sick.One annoying bit is that to get to Amon you have to collect these collectibles called "memos". You don't need all of them, but still a good bit, and some of them only spawn when you've completed certain substories and depending on what time of day it is and there's 3 of them to choose from so it's really annoying even with CyricZ's guide on the other monitor.Speaking of the substories, they were kinda middling. Some of them are pretty fun, but a lot of them weren't that interesting tbh. Maybe I'm the only one but I don't really have any desire to do more of the substories, they're really not very engaging, especially when they went back to the "no voice acting just make a lot of them" strategy which is not my preferred method.All around though, very good!

_childDocuments_.review: I never got to play the original, as this is a remake, so I can't comment on how well it translated the original content. But, as a long time Yakuza fan, this game is so incredibly fun. Seeing so many Yakuza characters take the place of these samurai was just the icing on top. Playing as Kiryu/Saito/Ryoma is a blast, the combat is at it's best in this entry. Wild Dancer will likely be your favorite as you can basically become a beyblade slashing and shooting everything around you lol. The minigames are great, the side stories are as comical and weird as ever and there's so many things to do on the side that I've spent almost 15 hours just walking around doing random things before I even hit chapter 3 lol. I thoroughly recommend this game to ANY Yakuza fan, and anyone looking to get into the series. And since it's a spinoff title you won't necessarily have to play the others to understand the story, though it'll lose the effect of having said characters play the samurai. Anyways, all around I'd give this a 9/10 rating. Side note though, the DLC is likely largely considered pointless or a scam. They locked the Ishin difficulty behind a DLC, and the extra items you get (like the troops and swords) will trivialize the difficulty of the game as they are all insanely overpowered and takes away some of the fun/challenge of the game. So I would recommend if you get it to only use it on the second playthrough when you're going back through just to have fun. TL;DR Game overall is a 9/10 highly recommend. DLC is meh at best though and they locked the hardest difficulty behind the paywall.

_childDocuments_.review: As always with the Yakuza series, you promise that it will be the last because this is always the same gameplay loop with weird and somewhat broken (but fun) gameplay, the same characters and plot strings with annoying encounters in the street and blurry graphics...but after one or two hours you are just trapped in the game and you cannot leave it until the end !I mean, the overall direction and story (even if the somewhat always the same) are enthralling and the characters (which are also the same archetypes) are so charismatic that you forget everything else. The side quests, not that great in this episode but still good, even if very limited in terms of gameplay builds a great atmosphere and all contribute to the immersion in this period. To sum up the plot and characters, they are really similar to Yakuza 1 which was one of my favorite (plus Majima, here Soji, was a normal character and not a complete clown in this episode).Anyway, the greatest strenght of the game is the same as all games in the series : the pacing which is very wall balanced to make you play a substantial adventure without make you become tired. I would say that Ishin is a bit better than many episodes because it started from zero, without having to carry the weird dramas like Y5,6 etc.The atcivities are various, with many typical ones (karaoke, fishing, shogi...) with some new ones (like chicken racing, farming), not the best in the series and generally average but they help to balance.The fights are not as messy as late PS3-engine games (Y3, Y0, YK) but the styles are really really unbalanced. WIth some ennemies at the end, you can use all of them, but for the most part swordsman is the most effective stance. At the end Sword gameplay is not as intense as brawlers styles of classical episodes but this is less messy. Add it to average boss fights and you get an OK game. The powers added by you infantry (because you are a captain) are a nice addition to help making the fights less bland.FInally, graphics are great for the main characters but blurry for the buildings, etc. The best way to greatly improve it to make them sharp enough is to play with DLDSR (x2.28 makes the game clean, not impressive at all, but sharp enough).To sum up, Ishin is a typical Yakuza games with many flaws in the gameplay and with "unbelievable" plot strings (I mean litterally) but with the same magic that makes you play from the begining to the end, guided by the desire to see what will happen in the next chapter. The only thing that was a bit frustrating in this game, aside from the annoying goons in the street (like in every game, but here it is hard to skip them) was the inability to get enough money and the inability to spend in in meaningful things. You start to earn money at the end with fights while farming gives you almost nothing. Aside from that, if you like Yakuza (even if you promise that it will be the last...I personnaly started with Y1 on PS2 and played all of them since), you will like it for sure.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a fan of RGG you're gonna adore this game.Familiar faces recast in new interesting ways. A return to the old battle style from 0/Kiwami 1 with the added bonus of them perfecting the idea that each style should have its own theme. All the style themes come from the same composition, they're just different parts of the same track, so when you change styles it's a seamless transition from one part of the song to the next. Speaking of music, the old character themes remixed for this game are 10/10 oh my god.There's an in-game gacha for trooper cards, interesting ways to shake up combat but namely they're there to give you a smile seeing your favorite characters from the RGG series as a whole.The story is rock solid minus one strange scene near the ending that you'll just get no explanation for. It's honestly funny but nothing that compromises the story's narrative. It was the most fun I've had in a game in a long while, even if it did come with the occasional "Did you guys even play test this encounter?" gripe. The entire experience is so much fun to a longtime Yakuza fan, and the fanservice is exactly what I want from a spinoff like this. (As a side note for RGG completionists: this is the worst one to 100%. I did the math and you need a minimum of 6200 ryo. If you want to 100% this game, look up the chicken race strat.)
