_childDocuments_.review: This is a mediocre version of a great game. They ported the original engine into Unreal Engine which introduced a lot of jankiness and bugs and general graphics inconsistencies which really bug me after playing the original version previously. I really wish they just ported the original version instead.For the story, it definitely will help to have some knowledge of the Meiji Restoration period otherwise there are a lot of Japanese factions and general terms to keep track of that might get confusing at times.The combat has been changed from the original in ways that make it feel very clunky and slow at times, especially the sword style, and it does amplify some of the annoyances of Yakuza's combat like getting knocked over constantly after getting hit with weapons. The original version did have some issues but this new version introduces annoying mechanics like complete ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ boss super powers (where they have complete melee damage immunity while doing them) and they removed most ways of knocking boss fights down, only a few particular moves can knock them down or you just have to use heat moves (which there is a very limited amount of). You also do barely any damage in a lot of fights against higher tier enemies (mainly in side content like the dungeons) which isn't very satisfying. You're expected to keep upgrading your weapons at the blacksmith but it is very tedious as it requires levelling the blacksmith up (new to this version - makes it EVEN MORE grindy) which is very slow and also requires a lot of money which is pretty slow to earn unless you do chicken racing which is extremely tedious but very profitable.Now for more annoyances with this version in particular:- Don't you love having a cool sword fight with a Shinsengumi captain for him to them put his sword away and start shooting fireballs at you. Sounds really cool doesn't it? Worst change by far- Inconsistent graphics due to porting the original engine to Unreal without modifying models. They seem to have redone textures and character's eyes but this has led to problems such as Hijikata's left eye having an oval-shaped pupil. It feels like there was a lack of care. Hair especially looks terrible. And you can see distant geometry lacks any detail. When paired with realistic lighting it really can look flat a lot of the time.- UI is extremely slow compared to the original game. For example, backing out of the abilities menu takes multiple seconds and if you spam the button you can hear the sound of backing out play multiple times- Shader pre-compilation not enabled which leads to stutters the first time you see effects. This is inexcusable- Some of the character replacements are strange. The character who was Baba from Yakuza 5 is now Zhao from Yakuza: Like a Dragon. This would be fine but this character in particular had Baba's character traits like being kinda shady which fit having Baba's likeness and voice, but now it's just a completely different character. Doesn't really fit with the original intention to me. Also when fighting some of the newly replaced characters, their boss fight themes are just their unchanged theme from their original game. It doesn't really fit having a dubstep sounding song in a game set in the 1800s- Missing multiple health bars. Every boss just has a single red health bar. Pretty sure this was a big complaint with Yakuza 6 which was changed afterwards in Kiwami 2 onwards. This adds to the enemies feeling tanky situation as every hit takes down a tiny slither of their health bar compared to taking down a big chunk of one of many health bars- General lack of polish. Enemy fight intros can sometimes have them facing the wrong way. The transition between multiple phases of some heat moves have a little gap where it shows the regular combat again.- Single use DLC which was not advertised as single use. Many people have used the DLC and then loaded their save and have lost access to it.- Made the main menu a boring image instead of Ryoma on a ship. Why?- They made the dharma tumbler animation faster but you stand still for a second afterwards completely negating the change- Missing little details, such as separate running animations when on stairs- They went way too far with catering to new fans from Yakuza 7. They added wacky stuff to the main story like random giant enemies and added the trooper cards from the dungeons into the rest of the game. While you can ignore the trooper cards, it feels like they rebalanced the game around using them so you feel like you're at a big disadvantage at times, especially when bosses start using the powers from the cards.Don't get me wrong it's a very good game but I hope they put a lot more effort in if they're gonna be using Unreal Engine going forward

_childDocuments_.review: Good game, and outside of some stuttering on DX12 (just use -dx11 launch option), runs very well.Loving the story and characters so far. I've played Y0, Kiwami 1 and 2, Y3, and LAD (aka 7). I don't recognize everyone; there's certainly faces from 4, 5, and 6, but that doesn't matter since this story is entirely separate. I guess it is similar to playing 7 without 4-6, in that regard.So far I'd say the combat is closest to 0, which is a good thing, imo. I enjoyed 0's combat much more than 1 and 2; and ergo I enjoy this a lot too. Very fluid, fun, and a bit mindless. Feels very solid compared to Kiwami 2's engine.Only downside is there aren't a ton of heat actions (for my tastes). I feel like 0 had a bunch, but mostly because you could pick up so much stuff and use them with heat actions. Here, brawler can pick stuff up, but it isn't common, and the heat actions don't have a ton of variety. _childDocuments_.review: Like a Dragon: Ishin is one of the more interesting entries in the Yakuza/Like a Dragon series, and though I had some issues with some of the systems it has, I enjoyed the game overall. The story is based on real historical events in Japan, so I took the time to read the history a bit because the game made me curious about the period.  It was also fun to see characters I loved from the other games play totally different characters.  Compared to the other Yakuza/Like a Dragon games I've played, Ishin has one of the better stories and I liked it more than the story in Yakuza 6 even though they share some plot points.  The minigames are generally good.  There's a fan dancing game that reminds me a lot of the disco one in Y0, though it's a bit easier.  Obviously, there are no arcade games, but the courtesan minigame gives you a shooter to play if you are hankering for one.  I haven't finished all of the Battle Dungeons yet, but I like it more than the other collectible-type games such as Majima Construction in Y2 and Clan Creator in Y6.  The card system is a bit overwhelming at first but it's not too hard to grasp and you can get a lot of nice cards without needing to purchase DLC.The "Harvest Moon" side business is quite addictive, though I wish they would have added more challenges to the Cooking Mamaesque cooking portion.  It's a good early game way to make some money.  The substories are overall not as wacky as the ones you encounter in Y0 and Kiwami 2, but I liked several of them.  I especially enjoyed the Wanted series of substories since they involve ninjas and goofy thieves in Tengu masks.  As for the combat, I loved the sword-based styles the most.  I found Wild Dancer to be even more fun than Breaker since you can chain attacks forever if you get good enough at it.  The Swordsman style starts out kind of slow but over time it becomes extremely powerful and varied.  If you pair Swordsman with a great crafted weapon it can easily carry you through the whole game.  Gunman isn't bad, but it felt a bit simple and situationally useful.  Once I crafted a rapid fire gun, for example, I could just mash the x button and get good results without having to worry about special ammo or trick shots.  Brawler, unfortunately, felt extremely weak and I had to rely on the invincibility frames you get from parrying to score more hits.  Overall, the combat system is heavily affected by the weapons you craft.  The main issue I have about this game is the crafting system. It's a bit complicated but the game does little to explain the system and I had to use guides.  Crafting also requires lot of grinding to get the materials you need, the cash to craft the items (and upgrade the blacksmith), and the seals you need to enhance your weapons and armor.  Unfortunately, the seal system has a lot of RNG, so if you want them all you will have to do a lot of farming and crafting.  Fortunately, the main story didn't seem too hard to beat and one of the best swords in the game isn't as expensive to make as some of the others, so the heavy grind is reserved for players who want 100% completion.  If you're a more casual Yakuza player like me who doesn't need to 100% complete everything, then you should have fun with Ishin.  It's an interesting spinoff and nice change of pace from the main series.

_childDocuments_.review: As a huge fan of the Yakuza/Like a Dragon series and Samurais in general when it was announced that Ishin was getting remade/remastered I was highly looking forward to it.  Luckily the game lived up to my expectations.  If you played other games in the Yakuza/Like a Dragon series you will likely enjoy this game, however I would recommend this game as your first game in the series.  Ishin makes a lot of references and nods to the main series, for example many of the characters themes are remixed in Ishin using traditional Japanese instruments.  If you have not played the other Yakuza games you would not get the references, and these references are some of the most enjoyable parts of the game.  I would recommend playing Yakuza 0 or Yakuza Kiwami 2 if you've never played one of the games in the series before.The main gripe I had with this remake is the squad/card mechanic that felt really shoehorned into the game, and is unfortunately necessary for bosses and certain areas in the game to restore heal and do high DPS.  However annoying it did not ruin the entire game and I would still recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: First thing that I gotta mention is that this game is RICH IN CONTENT! And not just bloat or just existing and going unnoticed like those side activities in Yakuza 5. This game locks you into playing all the minigames and side activities/stories and they are fun mostly. I have never played the fishing minigame this long in any Yakuza game but this one and the farming/cooking minigame just keeps me coming back. 40 hours into the game and I'm still finding new people to "bond" with when I thought I've seen everything at that point. The world of Ishin feels more alive than what I've seen in most Yakuza games. It definitely represents the busy feudal era with its people minding their own businesses buying or selling stuff in the noisy market. Another thing that this game does that other Yakuza games don't is that for some reason, the combat isn't the best part of the game. I played on Legend in my first playthrough (casually without looking up anything about it) and the first 10-12 hours was just a horrible grindfest. Even when I'm finally strong enough in the end game, the combat just feels strange. The bosses can one hit kill you like FromSoft bosses while they tank all your attacks, it's just not fun. I will say though that it does get better once you start upgrading your abilities and gear. The story is what you would expect from a Yakuza game. Rubber bullets, plot twists, betrayal, angry old men arguing, the usual. It's definitely engaging and I always like how in japanese games you start with save a cat then the last mission is kill god. This one is like that too but the last mission is you save Japan. And I wouldn't call this a "remake" more like a "remaster". It's not a Dragon Engine game either. The combat is pretty much the same as the original. The graphics received an upgrade but there are some moments that it looks like Yakuza 0 with graphics mods. One thing that I hate with games these days is that, TAA is forced enabled and when you disable it with a mod or by tweaking the ini file, it looks sharp but bad, it's like you get to see what the game actually looks like. TAA produces these fuzziness in the graphics as it is constantly erasing jaggy edges and it always doesn't look good. I will say that Judgment and Kiwami 2 looks better than this game. I think maybe they should've used the Dragon Engine and revamped the combat and then that would be a "remake". Content is worth the money but if you're unsure, get it on a discount (like I did).

_childDocuments_.review: Currently the main issue with the game is very poor performance. The game stutters constantly, which is not only visually jarring, but can also really mess with you during combat, because a lot of the stutters happen during the fancier animations that of course accompany deadly attacks you would want to be able to avoid, which is not possible when the game freezes up on you. They also somehow managed to make this game look significantly worse than the original which, may I remind you, is an almost decade-old game made for PS4. The character models on their own look good, but the lighting is really off, and a lot of textures and other assets are embarrassing. (I'm told these issues exist but are far less serious on console.)Those issues aside, they did fix the biggest problem with the original's combat, which was that a simple combination of sword attacks could essentially stunlock any boss. Gun and wild dancer (gun + sword style) are a lot more viable now from the start, which leads to way more variety. Things still get pretty simple once you start leveling up the styles, but combat is definitely more engaging.All in all, if they patch this up to remove Denuvo or compile shaders at startup or whatever's causing these constant stutters, it'd be worth getting on a sale. I still would not recommend this be your first Yakuza, because this does not give the best first impression of the series, to say the least.tl;dr - Could be fun if patched up a bit and on a sale, otherwise not really worth your money.(Also, if anyone's questioning the play time - I'm a speedrunner, so I'm probably going to keep messing around with the game regardless. My comments apply to "regular" play.)(Also 2, if publishers get to offer early access for extra money, people paying for that early access should be allowed to post their reviews early.)

_childDocuments_.review: Oh boy, Like a Dragon: Ishin! Kiwami!... lets start first with the gameplay.Ishin Kiwami's (I'm calling the game this since that's what it is in japan.) Combat is very similar to Yakuza 0 and Kiwami 1's combat, using the same style switching combat as those games, however in Ishin's case, it uses the different weapons that you have in your arsenal, those styles being Brawler, Swordsman, Gunman, and Wild Dancer.Brawler is very self explanatory, you use hand to hand combat to defeat your enemies, this style is mainly used as a defense style, as it has a parry mechanic that gives you invincibility for a short time, and you can equip whatever special weapon you have equipped at that moment, its also a very fast style, however the damage do you deal with said damage is not as great, which as I said earlier makes it more of a defensive style than a offense style.In Swordsman, you use a sword (duh), and can dish out slash damage to any foes in your way, you also have the added benefit of being able to block bullets as well, it terms of speed however its a slow style, but makes up for it through charge attacks and the different heat actions you can do, but overall its a decent style.In Gunman, you use a pistol, shooting foes with bullets and special bullets that deal different types of damage. This is one of the more spammable styles, as you can just keep spamming the attack button and sometimes the heavy attack button and pretty much kill anything as long as you keep your distance and they don't have armor.Wild Dancer is my personal favorite, using both the sword and the gun, you can make quick movements and do good crowd control, but with the lower damage, but the style has some of the more stronger (and cooler) heat actions due to them being heat actions that can target multiple at once, making it great for just normal brawling, and has good single target heat actions as well.Now I can't really talk about the combat without mentioning the Trooper Cards, as they went from being just a battle dungeon mechanic in the original game to being able to be used in any type of combat in this remake. Yes, these are broken, especially the very rare ones that represent characters from previous yakuza games, such as the Ichiban card and the Shinada card. However, as people have said, these are entirely optional, you can only use them in the battle dungeons and take them off when you get out of said battle dungeons, that's how I did my playthrough of the game even on Legend, but because of this "new" mechanic, bosses can also use special attacks from Trooper Cards, so it kinda feels forced at times, but again, it's your choice to equip them or not.Now to the story, the story of this game is good, taking place at the end of the Edo Period, you play as Sakamoto Ryoma (not kiryu) and explore the city of Kyo, and other stuff happens when you join the Shinsengumi and get closer to the one that killed Ryoma's father, the story is good but also remember that this isn't one to one to history, more of a original story based on said historical figures, and if you want to read more into them, then be my guest and look into Japanese history!City Exploration is the same as any other game in the franchise, explore, do a couple of minigames, do a couple of substories, and probably fight some ronin on the streets. However, this game also has a really infamous grind with crafting, eventually leading to doing battle dungeons the entire time.Of course this game is a remake, being remade in the Unreal Engine, this game is optimized very well on pc (after the patches that fixed the shader stutters) and with it the game looks pretty at times, this is also the studio's first time using Unreal Engine, and opting out of using the Dragon Engine for this remake. Unfortunate, but I feel like Unreal definitely makes this game setting feel more like that setting because of it.The music in this game is nothing but great, many tracks are remixes of songs from previous games including original songs, especially that final boss song. (Ishin Kiwami also added new remixes for 3 certain bosses, and also gave certain bosses their themes from previous games but not as cool as those remixes and sometimes just needing a why? looking at you Saigo and Katsura fight.)So overall, Ishin Kiwami is a decent Like a Dragon game, however I don't recommend this game at full price, wait for a sale that goes down to maybe 30 bucks, or play it through Game Pass, and don't even look at this game's awful DLC practices, being only able to be used once for a singular save file, and requiring a repurchase after said use. You also don't have to play this game for any canon reasons, as it doesn't really connect to any other Yakuza game in terms of the overall story, treat it as it's own thing.

_childDocuments_.review: The Yakuza game you play when you don't have a new one at the moment.For all intensive purposes, if you're here then you already like the yakuza series and dont know if this will be worth the time, being its own thing.When ishin first released, a little game known as Yakuza 0 was about to come out. so for reference point, anyone whose already played Y0 will notice most features of Ishin are the first iterations of what they found already. depending how deeply you take ishin, this will either make you feel right at home, or leave a lukewarm taste in your mouth as 0 is more or less all these gameplay refinements realized.Most notably the 4 different fighting stances you can use.You're given all 4 over the span of maybe 5 minutes without cutscenes. From what limited resources you have in tutorial land included, unless you just know to prioritize 1 of the 4, the first boss will clap your cheeks. Whereas Y0 gives you 3 over the span of an hour and lets you roam the main city and grind if you want inbetween. Tutorial land doesn't give you anything of note to do that'll keep you there longer than you need to be, as such, you'll rush to the first boss in order for the game to truly begin.Moreover, Ishin can easily be the most grindy game in the series. Even with 2 RPGs and a side game that wants to extend playtime, you will never feel like you're swimming in resources despite all your options. Unless you're playing ishin as a completionist and spending you're time making extensive use of ALL its features, you're going to be lacking in one way or another. it may be financially speaking, it may be statistically speaking, or even simply lacking good equipment.Having done 2 runs myself, once a blind casual run, and again with prior knowledge going out of my way to do even more than previously, it still feels like I could spend another 20 hours just trying to reach a variety of number thresholds before I feel like I can truly curb stomp whatever comes at me. There's simply too many features that revolve around doing repetitive tasks, or being situational and just so happen to do the right thing by accident. one of the biggest contenders for this is earning new moves. normal just upgrade yourself and be done with it, or level up a skill tree then you can learn the move if you find the trainer. in Ishin, you have to be the right level per style, find the master, fulfill the tutorial, then go through the skill tree to be able to unlock the move to actually be able to use it in a fight. leaving you in plenty of moments where you reach the threshold of a number of moves by the 7 hour mark but wont be able to use them till the 25-30 hour mark when you get the skill points to open it.one last example is "strikes of inspiration". depending on your stance you have to just know to setup the right situation to utilize a heat move, and eventually kiryu will have it trigger as it gives you one last QTE you need to land right in order for him to use the move, to then allow you the ability to unlock it, and then use the previously mentioned skill points on the skill tree just to check a box to then finally be able to start using them for real now.I've played ishin on multiple devices, once on xbox with just the base game and no DLC, and once on PC with all the DLC. So with that in mind, which should you get?Any of them. theres not any noteworthy difference between any version. HOWEVER, the DLC for this game is funky. the freebie DLCs' effectively remove a significant portion of the grind for early game and you can get through the story with them alone. that said, you can't even access them in game until you've already been given five across the ass and leave the tutorial land.Meanwhile the deluxe edition DLCs' are half assed. of all the DLC packs included in the deluxe edition, only the shinsengumi captains set is usable across multiple runs. everything else is 1 time use. and I don't mean 1 time use per run like in previous games. I mean 1 time use, period. meaning if you want to reuse any dlc that isn't already free. in particular the ability to use DLC characters like ichiban kasuga, you have to repurchase his pack every time you want to use him on a particular run. its genuinely upsetting.So really, just buy the base game, and snag the free dlc items you can get. you aren't missing anything worthwhile. just experiencing the game in its grindy glory.One last thing of note, Ishin probably has the worst karaoke minigame in the franchise based off what available on modern machines. its got nothing to do with the stylistic choices of feudal japan, but rather I've never found myself genuinely question whether or not my inputs are being read accurately before. the speed of the tracker fluctuates and jumps all over the screen between lines as opposed to a consistent one or two that it bounces back and forth as the notes appear. play any other games karaoke mode, then jump into Ishins' and you'll see what I mean. Its a sad day when a guy has to criticize a karaoke mode in yakuza.final verdict, 7/10TLDR: once the ball gets rolling, its great. However it take a while, and thats not for everyone.

_childDocuments_.review: Like a Dragon Ishin is an exceptional game that offers an incredible story and setting that will transport players to a different era. The game's narrative is beautifully crafted, and it tells the story of the samurai era in a way that will captivate players and keep them engaged throughout the entire experience.One of the most remarkable things about Like a Dragon Ishin is its setting. The game takes place during the Edo period in Japan, and the attention to detail is absolutely stunning. The streets and buildings are meticulously recreated to give players a true sense of what life was like during that time. From the architecture to the clothing, everything feels authentic and adds to the immersion of the game.The story itself is also exceptional. It follows the character of Sakamoto Ryoma, a real-life historical figure who played a significant role in shaping Japan's future. The game presents an alternate history that allows players to see what might have happened if certain events had unfolded differently. The writing is top-notch, and the characters are all well-developed, making the story feel like a compelling drama that players won't want to put down.Overall, Like a Dragon Ishin is an excellent game that delivers an exceptional story and setting that will transport players to a different time and place. The attention to detail and writing make this game an unforgettable experience that anyone should check out. It's truly a masterpiece of gaming and storytelling, and it deserves all the praise it gets.

_childDocuments_.review: This is easily one of the best Yakuza/RGG games made to date. It is a love letter to the entire series, with characters from every game returning, although with a new name. The combat is probably the most different out of the whole series, with sword and gun combat taking a major focus, but it is done very well. The story is also one of the best in the series, making you care about every character you meet. The substories are a bit of a weak point, as they are much more boring and forgettable than the other games in the series, especially games like yakuza 0 and yakuza like a dragon. The mini-games are very strong, however, with the return of the almighty karaoke bar (now a singing bar) and many other fun mini-games like dancing. Overall, an amazing remake and one of RGG studio's finest works.

_childDocuments_.review: Stuttering issues have been fixed.Steam really needs to add a neutral/conditional rating for reviews.I can recommend this if you've played every other Yakuza and Judgement title available on Steam. As it stands, this game is absolutely not worth full price and there's better entries in the series available at a fraction of the cost, as well as the excellent Judgement games that are available for the same price. And that's not even bringing up how this game takes characters from all across the series and re-casts them as historical figures - having prior experience with the entire franchise is essential to enjoying Ishin to the fullest. You're either too deep in the RGG rabbit hole to pass this game up, or it's not worth playing yet.Okay, actual review - this game's an odd psuedo-remake of a 2014 PS3 game. Nearly everything remains intact save for some gameplay and story changes - some characters were swapped out for characters from Yakuza 0, 6 and 7, a famous scene was censored, the equipment upgrading system has been overhauled, and a magical card system that was previously restricted to a side mode was, rather controversially, made accessible in the main game. Said cards give stat bonuses, can be activated for buffs, and - crucially - let you fire ki blasts, chain lightning, levitating energy swords, and a full-on kamehameha.On one hand, this is a game set in late-1800s Japan that generally takes itself pretty seriously - not everyone wants to be able to summon a tiger, bear or volatile chicken during a boss fight. On the other hand, this is a series that has confirmed the existence of aliens, ghosts, deities and more in their universe, and regularly lets you punch them in the face. Meanwhile the series' superbosses can use space lasers, gigantification, teleportation, and pocket dimensions. Personally, I can stomach being able to deal anime damage in a game where my swords can be enchanted with fire, lightning and wind. They did give most of the important bosses some of these attacks, and while some are extremely powerful, they're all generously telegraphed and easily blockable. Getting hit by one is as avoidable as walking off a cliff, at most they just disrupt the pace of the fight.The game's story is great, but takes quite a while to ramp up. The final third of the game is where the story really kicks into high gear - that's not to say that the buildup to it is bad, but I found the side content to often be more engaging. Thankfully Ishin has some of the best side content in the series, and I wasn't left wanting for a good-quality distraction.Ishin's combat system is essentially a prototype version of what Yakuza 0/Kiwami 1 would use - 4 combat styles, each with their own uses, strengths and weaknesses. On a technical level they all feel good, but they lack the same punch, both figuratively and literally. The game really - and I mean REALLY - wants you to use a sword. Your barehanded melee damage pales in comparison to your sword damage, and while this can be compensated for with specific equipment setups, it's still linearly more effective to just build for sword damage. Punching doesn't set people on fire, swords can do that and more. Swords themselves are still fun to use, but aren't nearly as satisfying as simply punching something in other Yakuza games. Guns just... Exist. They have some cool special attacks but as a whole they're underwhelming. If I had to choose between being locked to a single fighting style from literally any other entry in the series, and the 4 styles this game gives you, I'd take the former in a heartbeat.Tl;dr play the other games first and wait for a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I originally played this game using Google Translate after finishing Yakuza 0-7 but stopped at Chapter 3 due to translation issues. I'm so happy that I can finally enjoy this wonderful story and translation officially. Thank you so much for releasing this in the West and catering to your fans. This is easily one of my favorite Ryu Ga Gotoku games from a gameplay perspective but, I think, the story may be even better. The creative liberties taken with the historical fiction create a compelling narrative, memorable characters (even more-so thanks to nostalgia), and teach a lot about Japanese culture as well. As a fan of Rurouni Kenshin, this type of game has been a fantasy of mine since I was a child over 20 years ago and it delivers.I have played for 21 hours so far and I am only on Chapter 4 thanks to all of the side content this game has to offer. I imagine non-completionists may finish this story FAR faster than I will but I want to experience everything. I know that I should be trying to solve the murder mystery but I also have a farm to take care of, food to cook, and people to meet in town who need my help. My favorite aspect of these games are the little moments when you are interrupted by a side plot along the way to something else; these moments mirror life and immerse you in the world. I feel like I am a part of this world when I play; it is hard to put the controller down when you are busy being a real samurai who plays with a gamepad. I found myself in-game last night until 3:00 AM despite having work at 8:00 AM today. Every game made by this studio has that effect on me. When will other studios take inspiration from this series? These games continue to set the standard for what a "good" Action RPG is and I hope to see more Action RPGs from this studio in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR - Not perfect but if you love Yakuza then this game will make you happy. Just don't expect Lost Judgment levels of combat and fluidity, this is a glorified PS3 game.I took a lot of notes during my playthrough, mostly consisting of pros and cons. I will list them and go a little more into detail. Pros: • Combat feels and looks great. All of the animations feel like they had a lot of care put into to them. Each of the 4 styles are so different from each other and each have their strengths and weaknesses, can't say any felt bad to use, except maybe gunslinger which is really only good at long ranges and against non boss enemies. •Music is as usual top tier. Not much to say really except I felt this game had some of the best boss themes is the series. • Great selection of mini games. With this game being set in the late Edo period, there's a lot of opportunity for some unique mini games and I feel this game has a solid set of mini games that fit very well with the series and the time period it is set in.  • Trooper cards are actually pretty fun to use and I would argue almost necessary due to this game being pretty difficult at times. I like many others were worried before the game released if the cards would negatively affect the core game play, and I feel they don't. For probably about the first half of the game, trooper cards mainly consist of just buffs like heals or damage boosts but by around the late game you do get access to some of the more crazy cards. I always just looked at them as another move in my move set and not as a replacement for combat. • Generally the lighting is this game looks fantastic, especially during day time which is an area the Dragon Engine had trouble in. I did encounter some lighting bugs like flickering blood and unlit hair on Ryoma and some NPCS, these bugs were uncommon. • I just loved how colorful this game is. Again not much to say on this I just felt this game made amazing usage of colors throughout the whole game. • The story is good. Not the best the series has to offer but it's engaging. The game leads you to believe it is a very serious story but by the last few chapters it turns into a circus, not a bad circus but it gets pretty damn wacky by the end. Cons: • At launch the PC port was pretty bad, especially with the UE4 shader stuttering. This has since been fixed with Patch 1.03. Although I would still label this port as just serviceable. RGG has definitely made better ports than this.  • I would not under any circumstance attempt to 100% this game. I'd recommend just doing Main and sub stories, mini games, and at most maybe the battle dungeons. If you attempt to get 100% you will hate this game beyond belief, it is not worth it, don't do it, please. • I've always felt the bonds/friendships in this series are kinda boring and a waste of time, luckily most of the games don't have an egregious amount of them. This game has far far too many of them. This also makes trying to 100% a complete and udder chore. • The menus are kind of a pain to use if you're trying to do things fast. None of the menus go as fast you would like them to. With this game also being a RPG sort of, you spend a lot of time in menus, it's just something you have to get used to but you have to take it slow.  • You will be reading and skipping a lot of dialogue in this game and for some stupid reason you have to wait for every little animation to finish before you can skip. Some animations can take up to 6 seconds to finish so you just stare at people walking slowly or people getting up. Very annoying at times. • The camera is generally terrible. It's not as bad as some will lead you to believe but it sure does feel as if its working against you some times. • I only felt this a few times but some of the boss fights are pretty long and have no checkpoints, mix this with incredibly long unskippable qte's and you will get frustrated during certain boss fights when you die at the end and have to do all of that nonsense again. Like a Dragon Ishin is fun, would I say it qualifies as a remake? No, but for everyone now being able to play it for the first time in English, it's pretty tight.

_childDocuments_.review: If you ever played a Yakuza/Like A Dragon game, the beat 'em ups not the turn-based RPGs, then there isn't much new here.That can be good or bad depending on your enjoyment of the other RGG games. Like a Dragon: Ishin! feels lower middle of the road compared to the games in the series I've played. I like the historical period piece the game is going for, and I enjoy seeing Yakuza characters playing different parts like they are actors at the RGG studio.The melee is good, if the same stiff button mashing the series has always been. And like every other game in the series, starts to wear thin with its lack of depth and hundreds if not thousands of opponents fought.  The mini games are a little lackluster. I can't point to any I particularly enjoy. Many of the gambling and gaming staples made the cross over from modern setting of Yakuza to this game. As did fishing, karaoke, dance dance revolution and not entirely unfamiliar courtisan mini games. Perhaps the most interesting mini game here is the cooking ones. Which I found none entirely satisfying to play for very long. And for the life of me I don't know why the develops do a singing rhythm game line by line with the cursor moving at differing speeds. That is beginner trap central.What I did enjoy is much of the charm that found in the series. Little side stories and missions, an convoluted main mission story and like able characters. And I think the game would be an much easier sell if the grinding and padding was cut way back. There's a number of decisions that seem there just to waste the player's time. Several button inputs to pick up a prize ticket or open a jar, forcing the player to return to the same NPC multiple times to do the same action until filling the meter to resolve the substory. None these things hurt the game in isolation, but they had up cause the game to be less satisfying than it otherwise could.Which is why I think the Yakuza/Like A Dragon series has always been niche. I enjoy the quirky fun enough to overlook the fundamental flaws and old fashioned/wasn't fun back then either game design and mechanics of much of it.  So, I do recommend Like a Dragon: Ishin!, but with many caveats. If you don't already like Yakuza games, this game isn't likely to change your mind.

_childDocuments_.review: The review will be split into two parts: The Actual Game and Misc.I've been wanting to get my hands on Ishin for a long time, but was unable due to the fact that there was no english localization. When I heard the news that a remake of Ishin was planned, including english localization, I was more than hyped.The Lore was great, a lot of plot twists and action sequences. I've experienced shock, tension, relief and I immensely enjoyed the game's lore. Acting on the characters was superb.The return to multiple styles is definetly a welcome change. Every style specializes in something else, Sword is for damage, Wild Dancer is for close ranged chip damage, Gunman is for long ranged chip damage, Brawler is defensive (kinda). I also love how the game rewards you with more experience points for things like using various styles, doing moves which are difficult to time and finishing an enemy with a heat action.Also to note is a drastic change in enemy behavior. You cannot combo enemies from behind anymore, they will turn around after 2 hits. Many say that this change is bad, but I think otherwise. My main complaint for Yakuza games in general is that they weren't very hard (I played on Hard). I didn't even utilize combos and had no issues beating most of the bosses. In Ishin however I had to reset 6 times, I actually felt challenged by the game (also played on Hard). Going for the back has been turned from "getting the boss healthbar down by 30%" to "getting a few unblockable hits in". Bosses also give you ample time to react when they break your combo, so you are not punished for going for the back. I like Ishin's combat a lot.This section will tackle side content. The yakuza usuals are here: gambling, karaoke, and most importantly: "Disco" makes it's long awaited return after Yakuza 0. I was happy to play it again. It also has your regular 2 longish side quests and a bunch of wacky and hilarious substories, along with, of course, an Amon fight at the end. -Slight graphical issues from time to time-Weapon smithing is, as of now, completely ridiculous with the prices that are set for certain weapons. -Ryoma sometimes has a very long recoil animation when knocked down-No special indicators for unblockable attacks, which would be welcome-The Penultimate Boss Fight was ass-The UI elements are very slow and janky and you need to wait a while before you can navigate the menus after entering themIt's time to move over to the negative part of the review. I absolutely HATE how they handled specific aspects of this game. I'll go over them quickly:This is absolutely unthinkable, especially for the most expensive RGG game to date. All difficulty levels should be avaliable from the get-go. I can understand things like cosmetic items, in-game boosts, but not a whole difficulty level, cmon now. Also bonus minus points to removing the tradition of unlocking the hardest difficulty by beating the game once.This means that if you redeem the DLC in one savefile and decide to start a fresh new game from the start, . It's a dirty practice, but most importantly, IT'S NOT MENTIONED ANYWHERE AT ALL.I honestly do not know the reason for this, since most if not all of the game is offline. This however makes it impossible to enjoy the game if for whatever reason you don't have internet access. Also if you lose internet connection after not saving, you will lose that progress.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an RGG game, and if you like RGG games, you will enjoy this as well. I certainly did. It is, however, an 8/10 for me, as some imperfections frustrated me while I played.THE GOOD: Graphics were beautiful. I loved the different haori from the deluxe version.I enjoyed the many kinds of fighting styles.The localized writing was excellent as always.Character design was awesome. I like long-hair Kiryu! I also really liked seeing the old faces on new characters.Ryoma is a Redemption Paladin, and the game continues the heartfelt undercurrent that makes Yakuza games great. That said, unlike Kirtu, Ryoma will absolutely kill a fool, even if he gets sad about it afterward.The voice acting was excellent as always. I'm slowly learning Japanese via immersion as I play through the Yakuza series. Kiryu's "Nani?" is embedded in my brain at this point.You can adopt and pet both cats and dogsTHE BADThis game is really grindy. For example, it takes a very long time to earn the materials for a new sword that's not a huge upgrade. But even when you get the mats, you can't make the sword until you've upgraded the blacksmith an unknown number of times. And the ways to upgrade the blacksmith are limited, expensive, and take a lot of time. I gave up on making a new sword and just used the ones I got from bosses. Similarly, whenever you're working on a bond with someone, or healing the stupid amnesiac, or similar, the meters fill at an excruciatingly slow pace.Its origin as a PS3 game shows. There's a lot of running back and forth over the same areas built into most quests, and good lord but you'll be attacked by bandits a million times on the way. It both gives you a lot of information, and yet not enough. I had to go to the internet to learn how to use a special weapon or pay down debt, because the game didn't tell me. The glossary will define the Bakufu or geographic regions, but that's about it. You get introduced to a kajillion people with familiar faces from the old games, but it's difficult to keep track of them all. You get primers early on on the various fighting styles, but so close together that you forget certain functions exist (I'm looking at you, R2 special moves)You spend a lot of waiting for animations to finish. Menus are slow, and even opening the inventory takes a noticeable delay. I'd often like to continue reading the dialogue, but first I have to wait for this guy to shake his head six times, or for that cat to slowly walk around that corner and back. The cooking minigame is fun, but you can only do one dish at a time.Speaking of cooking, it seems like half of the dishes require you to spam a button to heat up the fire, but while there's an accessibility option to circumvent multiple button presses in battle, there's not an option to avoid that in the minigame. I ended up using multiple thumbs and fingers to get my cooking done. Also, I wasn't able to cook everything, because I couldn't find certain kinds of fish and didn't have the patience to go through all the various locations at every time of day to try to find a crawfish. Ryoma can be very stupid during combat. This isn't unique to Isshin, but he seemed extra dense and would often merrily charge into nothing doing a combo while the enemy I started hitting proceeds to wallop me in the back of the head. And again, you have a lot of deadtime waiting to finish combat animations before you can start another/dodge/change stance/whatever.As a soulsborne player, only one fighting style was useful to me. I liked the gun, but it was a peashooter. Barehanded did almost no damage. Sword hits the hardest, but is rigid and misses a lot. Only Wild Dance gave me the combat flexibility I needed to survive in the big fights. But it takes forever, 3-4 slashes then spin away and wait for the enemy to commit to an attack that I can run behind because otherwise he'll guard and/or poise through my attacks to knock me to the ground. Again. I used my trooper skills a lot to get through the gigantic health bars.Some oddness toward the end. There's an important visual reveal where Ryoma plays up that someone's hair has gone white because of his shenanigans! The camera lingers on it and there's a musical sting! But then the next time we see that guy, his hair is black again, and it stays black for the rest of the game. No mention that I heard about why. As an American who doesn't know a ton about Japanese history, the ending got confusing and a little scattered. I needed more explanation of what happened during the Meiji Restoration period, because mostly what you get during the game is that the British were bringing in guns and there is at least one faction that hates foreigners. I would've appreciated more context.Spear guys. Seriously, screw those guys.I really did enjoy this game, and spent a lot of time on Another Life and the minigames (I wish there were more karaoke songs in which Ryoma was lead). I did 90% of the substories, not finishing only grindiest. But these imperfections I mention above really started to wear on me toward the end, and I was really ready to be done by the time the last few chapters rolled around.

_childDocuments_.review: As a hardcore fan of RGG games, I've been waiting for a mere localization of Ishin but when I saw that they're going the extra mile to remake it on a newer engine I was filled joy but still a little hesitant.Hopefully what I feared the most didn't occur(game breaking bugs, visual glitches, performance issues, etc.)We got the same game with even more content and recent lovable characters added to it. Just let me say the soundtracks, minigames, bossfights, story(some parts) of ishin were just brilliant to say the least.However, RGG dropped the ball on some of the new design choices. The stylized aura is now just a simple flame, some small stuff in minigames, the design of some npc characters and the in-game lighting compared to dragon engine games are a bit disappointing.However, these are nothing compared to the stupidest idea of the RGG team since"rubber bullets": The freaking trooper cards and magician bosses. I know there were giant enemies and weird stuff before but bossfights are personal fights and the peak of every RGG game. To see your opponent get a laser beam out of his a$$ is just unacceptable. This sh#t belongs to Amon fights not story ones.Also the enemies take too many hits to die, making it a bit tiresome in most long battles. And f@ck the spear enemies and their hitboxes (you sometimes get hit even ehen you're behind them). Just hitboxes in general, are the worst they've ever been in this title.The ending is really weird, some of the substories are too short and simple and the in door lighting of character models look terrible (for the most part).But thanks to great mini games, soundtracks and iconic characters, I still enjoyed Ishin, which could've been 3 times better if not for the trooper magic BS.I wouldn't recommend this to a newcomer at all, just those who have played previous yakuza games and enjoyed them.

_childDocuments_.review: (Proof read, June 2024)   Kiryu travels back in time to start a rebellion because someone hit a woman. What a chad.All joking aside, I've only played the beginning, and I have no regrets regarding my pre-order.Now that I've finished the story, I'll give this review some value. This game appealed to me on three levels: It's an RGG game, it follows a historical period I study, and Majima. This game was my first RGG pre-order, thus the first Yakuza/Like a Dragon title I've played launch day. The game is great; the story started off a bit slow, but that's typical for most Yakuza games. The story was great; I loved seeing the classic tale of Sakamoto Ryoma being adapted by RGG in such a way as to pay great respect to the man while also telling an independent story. If you're a Yakuza fan, no excuses, get the game!Oh yeah, finally, Haruka's trust doesn't cause mental breakdowns in this game, so yeah, another common RGG win.

_childDocuments_.review: While I REALLY want to recommend "Ishin Kiwami" and I am very happy that it finally came to the west, the advertisement for this game has been quite deceptive. This is not a "Remake" or "Kiwami" as suggested by the Japanese title as well as all the advertisement materials. This is at best a "Remaster" of the original "Ryū ga Gotoku Ishin!" similar to the 2019's Remastered Collection which included enhanced versions of the Yakuza 3, 4, and 5. Although there have been noticeable changes such as recasting many of the characters and adding a few minigames and mechanics, "Ishin Kiwami" looks and plays almost identical to the original game. So, definitely keep that in mind before paying full price for what is essentially a late PS3-era title.

_childDocuments_.review: Like a Dragon: Ishin is another great release from RGG Studio. In the past, changes in platform/engine have had combat that just doesn't feel right (Yakuza 3 & 6), whereas their first entry using Unreal Engine 5 feels amazing to play and is spectacularly beautiful. I thoroughly enjoyed the more in depth sword combat and the revolver with infinite bullets. The story is fantastic and gives a (dramatised) insight into the issues and politics of Bakumatsu Japan. The substories are as hilarious as always and there are a plethora of minigames to enjoy.I did have a few gripes however. I loved the addition of the new characters, but was disappointed when some didn't have Ishin versions of their music but instead played the original track. In addition, the implementation of the relationship system is really boring, as all you need to do is  hand an item to someone and reload the area, just to get the same dialogue 10 times before ending with the "relationship" with a different scene. Furthermore, after 40 hours without crashing, my game closed right as the end credits finished, but before I got a clear save to start Premium Adventure, which was quite disappointing.All in all, I really enjoyed Ishin, and despite comfortably playing other RGG games on hard, it was quite challenging this time around, which was quite fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Ishin stands in a peculiar place, it is both a remake and a remaster at the same time. The added substories, combat balancing, quality of life upgrade and updated visuals are great but the game still feels like pre-Dragon Engine game. Ishin could have benefited a lot from Dragon Engine's fluidity and seamlessness. Nevertheless, Ishin is both an epic tale of Meiji Restoration and a fanservice for long time fans of RGG games.The game still feels great to play though, with the game even severely punishes you if you don't master the fighting styles to their strengths in any given situation. This alone makes Ishin one of the most challenging RGG game. But the added RPG mechanics with equipments, status effects, trooper card surprisingly make for variety of builds and can make for as much an enjoyable experience as without using those mechanics and make for an easier time if it's too difficult for certain players.The best thing about Ishin is how it tells its historical fiction. RGG takes huge loads of Bakumatsu history along with its historical people and spin them for a much more dramatic tale. One that is simultaneously about personal identities and bringing on a change of history. It is personal and grand at the same time along with an ensemble casts whose faces taken from mainline RGG games with diverse personalities and interests. You never really know who to trust or where the story will take you. Witnessing Ryoma's story of vengeance turn into a tale of discovering the truth and forging your own identity in a turbulent times is a remarkable experience. Kyo is also dense with atmosphere and things to do. A lot of substories found in Kyo are loosely based on historical people or historical events which make for a good learning opportunity, some of them also fleshes out certain organization that is just glanced over in the main story. There are however too much of friendship bonds with some of them take too long to progress but most of them still provide different scenarios and quite funny. The other standard substories are great tho, ranging from absurd, funny to genuinely sad. The biggest thing holding Ishin back is the grinding. Blacksmith level, styles level, materials for crafting required grinding and some of them are borderline too much. That said, the player is not forced to grind because the main story also gives you free weapons but playing in harder difficulties makes it harder to ignore the grind, especially how slow the leveling takes past level 70+. Still, Ishin is a great title. An experience that will be greatly enhanced if you are already familiar to Bakumatsu period, knowing when RGG goes off-script from the actual history to tell its own story is extraordinary. As a RGG game, it is one of top tier, even tho it could be better if it's a full remake. As a samurai game, it is still one of the best with believable pre-modern Japan atmosphere, full of details, enjoyable combat, and an engrossing story.

_childDocuments_.review: Our journey of Yakuza games continues, only this time instead of jumping from Yakuza 5 to Yakuza 6 Song of Life, I decided to try out the remake of Ryu Ga Gotoku Ishin, also known as Like a Dragon Ishin!. Chronologically, this game was released in between Yakuza 5 and Yakuza 6, so it fits to play it before Yakuza 6.Like I said, this game is a remake of the 2014 Ryu Ga Gotoku Ishin. It's essentially the same game but with improved graphics, translated (original release was JP only) and some additional content.The story is based off the Bakumatsu era, the final days of the Shogunate period, and the turbulent period of Japan being mixed with western powers. What's interesting is that the character models that the game uses are the same as previous Yakuza games, but they don't have the same name. For example, Kazuma Kiryu is now Sakamoto Ryoma. I'll also mention that 95% if the characters in this game are based of the historical people that existed in real world. The events that happened in this game are based of the real events that happened during this violent period. I won't spoil much of the story, but this has to be one of the best written stories in Yakuza games. I liked the story so much that I got hooked on playing this, which is why I finished it a lot faster than previous games. So the story is well earned A grade.Gameplay is identical to other Yakuza games. You have adventure and combat mode, let's dig into combat mode first because it's the meat and potato of the game. The combat is surprisingly well made, with 4 different ways of fighting. So essentially, we are back to the Kiwami/Yakuza 0 system, which is my favorite combat system, as it adds so much variety to the game. I really liked the combat in this game, especially the crafting system that helps you improve your weapons further. The adventure mode is your typical sidequest hunting, wacky moments left and right, and of course, minigames. Minigames I would say are good, there's a lot of variety of them, from dancing, singing to gambling. There's also "sidestory" system. If you remember the Taxi sidestory in Y5, Hostess Club Management in Yakuza 0 or Majima's construction sidestory in Yakuza Kiwami 2, this is identical to that. Though the minigames and sidestories are great, I do have to say I still liked Kiwami 2 and 0 minigame better. I don't know, the management minigames in both of those games really hooked me. That isn't to say that minigames and sidestories don't deserve a praise in this game.Graphics are I believe done in Unreal Engine 4, and while sometimes they look a bit murky, I think the devs did an excellent job. The game looks visually beautiful.The music is interesting. It has some original music, but because they use character models from the previous games, some of the music is actually identical to... previous games. It's interesting to say the least.Throughout this experience, I would say, Like a dragon: Ishin! is so far, the second best Yakuza game ever made. Now keep in mind, I haven't played Song of Life and later games, yet, but so far, this game gets a well deserved second place. First place is still Yakuza 0.Overall great game, great remake, great story. A fan of Yakuza games should definitely check this game out. Fully recommend it. Now if you will excuse me, Song of Life is next on my list.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a fan of the Like a Dragon / Yakuza series, short story:  buy.Though taking place in a different setting than most of the series and being set so far in the past, Ishin! has no problem at all feeding you a non-stop stream of varied content and things to do in a very busy, jam-packed fun open world.I will get the "meh stuff out of the way first.Combat:  The combat isn't necessarily bad, but feels dated and janky compared to many modern action games.  This is made worse by a frustrating AI that often times seems like it was programmed specifically to make you angry.  The various combat styles are not very well balanced, with the at least 2 of the 4 available not aging particularly well as the game moves forward.  All of this being said, I still would not call the combat anywhere near "bad" since it did keep me relatively engrossed for dozens of hours of gameplay.Story:  The story starts off very, very slow and takes quite a while to pick up steam.  You are given a metric ton of story background early on (thank goodness for the baked-in game glossary you can access at the touch of a button during dialogue) and it can be a lot to process and unpack.  I did not find myself really getting into the story until the final Act, but thankfully the myriad of side content did all the heavy lifting with keeping me entertained the whole time.Other than those two points, the rest of the game is really stellar.  I love the town layout, you are richly rewarded for exploring, chatting with locals and taking on mini games and I foun d myself spending entire hours-long gaming sessions simply goofing around with the optional content.Highly recommend, stellar game and glad we finally get to play a localized version in the US!

_childDocuments_.review: I'll start this review by saying that I agree for the most part about performance and gameplay issues the other negative reviews bring up, but do know that RGG has set itself a damn high bar and transitioning to a new engine is rough to say the least.My "Recommend" will be based on the story of Ishin! itself, and what the remake did to the story by casting new characters. Coming to this game while having played every mainline game before this, I already know all the characters and their personalities. However, placing them in different positions and circumstances REALLY adds depth to each character. Common themes, music, combat styles from the mainline games are re-explored and synthesized and it's just one hell of a series-wide crossover.I'm sure this game to a franchise newcomer will be a good time, but knowing all the characters at play in the story and all the themes re-explored here just adds a whole new layer of meaning to this game that makes every fond RGG fan fangirl.

_childDocuments_.review: I've somewhat enjoyed this one. I wouldn't say this is the best or the worse. I'll keep this review brief because there's not much to say since everything is straightforward.Combat was okay. I like using wild dancer but most of the time, I've been using swordsman for majority of the content. Brawler was kind of a let down and underused. Gunman was mostly for situational scenarios.The story felt short but pretty much straightforward. The introduction of characters was a bit weird and not much more about them since this story is centered on the main character alone which I think is a good thing. This period has history and a lot of backstory to it and the developers kept it short and simple but was a bit overwhelming to grasp. It was easy to pin out what happens in the story since there wasn't much of a suspense, so that was kind of a let down.There is a lot of side-content but when you actually do them, feels a bit lacking and short. Some were interesting and others were meh. The second life isn't that bad nor the best but I would say wasn't rewarding after completing it. To be fair, it would make sense that the story period or setting has to do with the lack of content since there isn't much in the 1800s.Overall, buy this if you're a fan of the yakuza series and it's spin-offs. If you're buying this and never played this type of game, you're better off buying something else because you won't understand. OR, just start playing the series then come back to this. As a fan of the series, this is probably one of their weakest titles.

_childDocuments_.review: Another great Yakuza/RGG entry. Kyo is a very cool place to explore if you're interested in Japanese history and I was surprised by how much effort was put into making the story "historically accurate" (as in hitting all the important beats). If you're already a fan it's a no brainer recommendation. If you're just interested in the Bakumatsu time period I would also still recommend it.- Decent combat system reminiscent of Yakuza 0 and Kiwami 1.- Equipment matters in combat. There's a nice selection of swords and guns with special effects which allows you to make your own build.- Trooper cards can be broken but add variety and a unique flair to the combat.- Engaging main story that can get silly at times but you're probably used to that at this point.- Substories are fun as always.- This remake was made in Unreal Engine 4 instead of the Dragon Engine and it is a bit rough on the technical side. There are shader cache stutters if you don't launch it with DX11 instead of 12, it looks blurry with Anti Aliasing unless you turn on AMD FSR and you have to turn off the motion blur in an .ini file.- Very tedious if you're going for 100% Completion because of the Bond mechanic.- Crafting higher end equipment is VERY expensive. It is so expensive that the only realistic way to get that amount of money is to gamble (chicken races) or grind the Harvest Moon minigame.

_childDocuments_.review: (This review is more for Like a Dragon fans. If you're new to Like a Dragon, go play Yakuza 0.)My favorite part of the Like a Dragon series is the plot and the characters. The endings are always explosive, and I always leave the game blown away. I did not get invested in this game's story. I think the biggest cause of this was the Like a Dragon characters cosplaying as people from 1800s Japan. The setting is really cool, and it's kind of funny watching Kiryu (now Ryoma) and crew navigate 1800s Japan. However, they went for a dead serious story instead of something more lighthearted, which made immersion impossible for me.In terms of substories, there are quite a few filler substories that I wish weren't there (go fetch me "X" 5 times, dull and boring), but aside from those substories are as funny as they always are. Nothing crazy.Gameplay stood up a bit better than the story thankfully . It's pretty standard brawler Like a Dragon gameplay (which I really like), but I was disappointed that all of the interfaces/graphics were the old PS3-era interfaces/graphics and not something more like this company's Dragon Engine. Why this game is not in the Dragon Engine is a mystery to me. 60$ is a high asking price for a remake if you're not putting considerable effort in (I got this 70% off), so keep that in mind if you're more graphically-focused.Also, maybe it's because I played on Legend, but this game did feel a little grindy. Burned through a few podcasts, which I never usually have to do for Like a Dragon games.Even my least favorite Like a Dragon game had a story that I loved, so I'm going have to give that title to this game now. It's my least favorite Like a Dragon game.

_childDocuments_.review: First, a video reviewStream )Ryu Ga Gotoku Studio I'm your biggest fan and a big fan of Russia I like all your games including the plot how cool you make it I passed all parts of Yakuza Judgment Lost Judgment you are the top studio in Japan and I love your country Japan ^^ I want to get your autograph )) he is your most clever man thank you for creating such great games from Yakuza to Like a Dragon: Ishin waiting for 8 part Yakuza) 龍が如くスタジオ 私はあなたの大ファンであり、ロシアの大ファンです 私はあなたがそれを作るどのようにクールなプロットを含むすべてのあなたのゲームが好きです 私はヤクザジャッジメントロストジャッジメントのすべての部分を通過した あなたは日本のトップスタジオであり、私はあなたの国日本を愛しています^ ^ 私はあなたのサインを取得したい )) 彼はあなたの最も賢い男です ヤクザから龍のようにこのような素晴らしいゲームを作成していただき、ありがとうございます。ヤクザから龍が如く、維新、8部作を待ってます。） Like a Dragon: Ishin! is a remake of the PlayStation 4 game Ryu ga Gotoku Ishin, which was released exclusively in Japan. In the Yakuza spin-off, the Sega franchise replaces the colorful world of Kamurocho with the late Edo period in Japan. With a more serious storyline and outdated mechanics, the 2014 re-release does feel like a distant past, especially in combat with erratic hitboxes and a constant cluster of enemies, especially after the modern and more intense gameplay of Yakuza: Like A Dragon, which gives you more room to breathe. Still, if you're a Yakuza fan, it's worth diving into.GameplayWhile Like a Dragon: Ishin! The remake has the same series title as 2020's Yakuza: Like a Dragon, no turn-based RPG mechanics. Instead, it uses the same engine used in Yakuza 0 and Kiwami. Essentially, players are given a choice between four styles of play: Gun, Dancer, Brawler and Swordsman. Each combat style is completely different and can be changed on the fly at the touch of a button. After almost a decade, the multi-combat style engine is still clever because it allows you to strategize depending on the situation.For example, if you're fighting an enemy with a long spear, your Weapon mode will quickly be able to fire from cover at a distance. Surrounded by a group of enemies? No problem. Just use "Dancer" mode to send protagonist Sakamoto Ryomo into a frantic spin with his katana, and fire a barrage of bullets from his pistol. Like a Dragon: Ishin's fights never get boring, and I spent hours improving each path to create my own unique style of play. The game also has an in-depth crafting system that allows you to track down rare materials to create powerful katanas and weapons, including magical ones.The only drawback to the gameplay is that the game's engine can sometimes seem a bit stiff and outdated compared to modern games like Yakuza 6 or Yakuza: Like a Dragon. Even in terms of how your character moves, it's clear that this is a 2014 re-release, not something that has been reworked and improved to today's standards. The animations are clunky, the hitboxes are inconsistent, and the world seems less alive than in recent games. In 6, combat interacts with the world, as you can push enemies into the environment for unique sequences. And in Like a Dragon, the people of Yokohama step in to help you take out the bad guy. Compared to him, Ishin feels a little colder at times.Also, the fight can get a little tedious after being pounced upon for the thousandth time by stray bullies and ronins. As you walk around Kyo looking for side quests, be prepared for enemies chasing you every few steps.Yakuza games have always looked beautiful, and Like a Dragon: Ishin! is no exception. Even though the game came out in 2014, the 2023 spin-off still looks fantastic. Even in the Steam Deck handheld mode, the game runs at 720p and 60 FPS with max settings. On PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X, the game has no problem delivering smooth gameplay while maintaining clean visuals. While the game won't outshine modern AAA games like Horizon: Forbidden West or God of War Ragnarok, Ishin! provides a balanced experience where visual effects don't sacrifice performance.Because the remake replaces the usual grimy concrete Yakuza cities with a late Edo period setting, the game looks amazing in some places. There were moments during the game when I had to interrupt my classes to look at the beautiful nature created by Ryu ga Gotoku Studios to recreate the ancient Japanese era. Ishin's stylish gameplay also never looked better, as every spark of blade and splatter of blood is perfectly captured in the HD graphics of the 2023 remake.Verdict Like a Dragon: Ishin! is an incredible remake, even though it seems dated compared to modern Yakuza games.Although it lacks the magic of the modern Yakuza setting, Like a Dragon: Ishin! still retains the quirky fun that has made the long-running franchise a must-play. While some players may be less thrilled with the 2014 combat system and serious late-Edo period setting, longtime fans won't want to miss this epic Yakuza spin-off.Score: 100000/100000 クールなゲームをありがとうございます。

_childDocuments_.review: Ishin has a phenomenal atmosphere, a gripping story, and is really fantastic as a period piece in the Yakuza/Like a Dragon universe. However, this was all present in the original release of the game on Playstation, and this remaster is not a good port. Cutscenes are locked to 30 FPS, the combat and physics on Unreal Engine don't feel true to the series, and there were some highly questionable practices with the game's DLC (who puts consumable, repurchaseable item packs in a  game?) But by far, the Ishin remake has the worst grind of any game in the series for anybody seeking 100% completion. I have the platinum trophy for every game released on Steam so far, and I have never had an experience as painfully boring and anti-fun as with Ishin. Not only has the price of equipment at the forge been inflated to absolutely ridiculous prices, there is a dizzyingly long list of equipment seals you will never get your hands on without abusing the RNG that determines when they appear. If save scumming is the ONLY viable strategy for completing your game in any reasonable amount of time, something has gone terribly wrong.I love the Yakuza series, and it seems like it will be returning to glory with Gaiden and Infinite Wealth. If you really want to immerse yourself in the world of Ishin, then by all means do so. But I can't recommend it after so much of my time with it was spent completely ignoring that world in favor of endless menu navigation for that final, painful platinum.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who generally loves RGG games flaws and all, I just can't recommend this game whatsoever. Like a Dragon: Ishin! is a mess of a fanservice game with little substance and one of the worst grinds I've ever seen in a single player game. That's what this game serves for explicitly: fanservice. Which would be absolutely fine, I absolutely LOVED Dead Souls myself, but that's because that game wasn't a predictable slog. The game's story gives itself away so fast, and I can't tell if it is because of just lazy writing, or because of the new recast (for Christ's sake why did they decide to make Ryoma's brother Shibusawa). Speaking of Ryoma, he's just such a dull and stupid protagonist. Now I know that this was around the time they started making Kiryu more naive, In 5's case because he was losing everything and 0's was that he was only 20, but BY GOD is Ryoma dumb. Most of the narrative is him just letting his naiveity get in the way of his quest and it's so frustrating to watch. The characters are predictable, If you know how they act in the main game, that's how they act in this one, I don't know how you can make Goda and Akiyama boring, but they managed to. The only character in this game that was any bit interesting was Hijikata, but that is because we haven't seen Mine in a grip and it was interesting seeing him take up a leadership role independent of Daigo (at least to the point I got up to).The combat is just flat out the worst in the series, there's hardly any weight or oomph whatsoever, you can just spam attacks with no reprecussion. Also the gear score system is just awful, it turns the game into a slog and just makes the combat one of many, many, MANY things you have to grind for. Seriously it seems like everything in this game is a grind. Want a new weapon? Grind! Want to do substories? Grind a friendship meter! Want to do the main story? Well you better enjoy starting 10 substories on your path to the next mission marker. It utterly gutted any interest I had with the game whatsoever.There are much better RGG games, much better sword/gunkata games that came out around the same time Ishin! did (both in its 2014 release and the new release). I'm glad this game got released to the west finally and I still would LOVE to see a Kenzan! localization just for the sake of game preservation, but this game wasn't for me whatsoever.

_childDocuments_.review: Spoiler Free ReviewFirst off god bless RGG Studios for not only bringing this game to the west but remaking it on unreal engine the game looks beautiful and is well optimized even for my 1050ti.That being said the game is a 1:1 copy of the original japanese version with only some few changes and nerfs to two of the combat styles.First off if you've played any yakuza game before or even played the original version of Ishin you will see some familiar faces here from previous yakuza games, mainly from yakuza 0. The community has had some mixed receptions of the character recasting, on which im on the side of agreeing with those not in favor of the new set of characters, I prefer the old ones in the original Ishin since the casting made more sense. As for the two styles that got nerfed which is Brawler and Gunman.Very little changed with one of brawlers dodge upgrades becoming now only usable in Brawler only unlike in the original where you can use the dash in all styles, while Gunman has had its fire rate nerfed quite a bit since it was just a tad bit op in the original.Now for the side content, there is a lot that has been added both new and old. The Karaoke minigame is back with a new song that some may recognize from the absolute meme it became, which is Bakamitai. We also have a new farming minigame with Haruka which is honestly a really nice change of pace after fighting some ronins. Overall you will never get bored in this game with the plethora of minigames and substories. Overall i really recommend the game to people who have already played a yakuza game.Also DO NOT BUY the booster pack/upgrade dlc, it is an absolute scam and my only gripe with this game the fact that its only a one time use, and is not even tied to a save file, yes you can only use it once then you'd have to buy it again. Honestly don't know what they were thinking with this, there was some already questionable dlcs at the past like with Lost Judgement where most of the powerups you get from buying the dlc is only a one time use.
