_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: Personally nostalgic for me. A simple story reminding one of simpler times.I appreciate that it is quite close to the source material.Cute, short and sweet. Probably great to play with kids. Could be more engaging, but the simplicity was most likely intentional.Please keep in mind the 'short' part - there's no more than 5 hours of game here.
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: What a beautiful game. I loved watching The Moomins as a child, and Snufkin was my favourite character, so being able to relive it all now is really precious to me. The story is lovely (I especially love the message about protecting nature!), the music is lovely, and the ART IS GORGEOUS! Thank you so much, Developers, for bringing me this childhood dream. 10/10 from me
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: Very true to the source material. Beautiful visuals and soundtrack. Gameplay is pretty basic and simple but it doesn't take away from the atmosphere (gameplay makes sense being music themed and all). The game is the perfect length and doesn't outstay it's welcome. If you like the Moomins or are curious about the Moomin world definitely play this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most visually appealing games I have played. The coloring was done very well. Very colorful yet not too visually stressful. I'm not usually a fan of 3D open-world games, but this one gets a pass because its *looks* 2D. Sound design was also amazing!This game is very user-friendly. You only need a keyboard and the controls are very simple. There's a cool musical component where you can press A to play Sunfkin's harmonica to charm animals. I was a huge fan of that. There are also a ton of puzzles throughout the entire game, but they aren't so hard that you're going to have to look up any solutions.Moomin fans will know that in all the various Moomin media, you never get much of Snufkin's first hand perspective. This game definitely changes that. It was cool to see how he reacts with all the secondary characters. If you're a fan of Moomin you will love this game.One thing I don't love is the system for tracking achievement progress. The progress is counted cumulatively across playthroughs, so you can get the steam achievements without actually fully earning them. For example, there is an achievement for . The game is also still a little buggy. I got soft locked and had to restart because . Overall not perfect, but a really fun and relaxing game.
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: I was expecting a children's game that I would quickly lose interest in, only appreciating the fact that it's based on the Moomins. I'm 37 years old, and I’m happy to have completed this short adventure. Despite its minimalism, the game is very well-made, and it leaves you wanting more. Heck, maybe even someday a bloody action RPG in the world of the Moomins? ;)
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: Game was short, the story was left open for hopefully more free DLC. Really loved the music EXCEPT the parts where someone had to include vocals into the song which made it sound like it was about to break into rapmusic which really killed the vibe. WHO WAS THE GENIUS THAT REALLY NEEDED TO INCLUDE VOCALS IN AN INSTRUMENTAL SOUNDTRACK?!If no more content is added, cant recommed you buy it unless you are a hardcore moomin fan.
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: Although I finished the storyline in approximately 8 hours, I did enjoy every single minute of it. The combination of art design, storyline, music and gameplay allowed me to cozy up at home with Snufkin and the Moomins and escape reality. The pictures are beautiful, the characters cute and like I remember them from my childhood and the music by Sigur Ros provides a sense of calm. The puzzles were entertaining as well. Overall a pretty decent game.. I do hope the developers will come out with some extra content because I feel they could've made this game a little bit bigger.
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: So cute and relaxing. I love the art style, it reminds me of childrens' books illustrations. The game itself is an old-school quest with riddles, not too hard, but challenging enough, so you don't get bored. The main problem I can name are the movement mechanics, which are quite clumsy, and sometimes it is very hard to jump on this exact rock or you simply get stuck because it's inconvenient to pass by an obstacle. But generally, the game is awesome for a cozy evening, couldn't recommend more.
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: This game has truly been a joy to experience. The puzzles are varied and actually fun, it's not constant fetch jobs or things you have to slog through. Beautiful art, music, and characters. It has been such a treat to see Moomin, Snufkin, and friends come to life this way. Buy it full price to support and let them know how much it is loved!
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: I knew a little bit about the characters going into this but not much and was blown away by this gorgeous game. The music, art, and characters just make this such a charming experience. I played it through once on stream and then replayed it again all cozy on the couch so I could really immerse myself in the story. Highly recommend this beautiful and cozy game.
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: As a lifelong fan of Moomins I really appreciated the authentic feel of this creation. The music is wonderful, the art is perfect, the puzzles some are super simple, but no matter- I enjoyed them anyway :D I smiled the whole time I played this. If you're a Moomin fan, this is a must-have in your collection of games.
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: An adorable game bringing the spirit of Tove Jansson's beloved and genius children's book series. With beautiful watercolour art, sweet music, well-known and lloved characters and all kind of kooky creatures, the game has an easy and enjoyable mecahnics of doing little tasks of goodness and teaches us the important lessons, like cops are both useless and cruel, nature cannot be owned and private property should be torn down so everyone can roam freely. <3
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: Worthwhile buy for me when on sale! A lovely game about belonging, nature, music and friendship. I don't know too much about the Moomin universe, but now I'm curious to learn more about my favorite characters from the game. Gameplay and quests have enough variety to avoid being tedious. Get this game to experience its art, whimsy and storytelling.
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: The game sort of presents itself as being more musical than it actually is, which was what suckered me into playing it in the first place. The game is definitely not for me, and it took several attempts to power through. Keeping the review positive though, because there's nothing "bad" about it per say, it just needs to be stated that this game is aimed towards a younger audience despite the property being much older than said audience.
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: The game offers an incredible story and an engaging experience that truly immerses you in its world. While there are occasional stutters in the movement mechanics, these minor issues don't overshadow the overall quality of the gameplay. It's a must-play for anyone who appreciates a well-crafted narrative in their games.
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: The game is nice and relaxing. If you're looking for a laid-back game, this is it! I'm bad at directions so I got lost several times trying to find my way to where I needed to be. However it didn't take long to finish the game so I was okay replaying it to complete all the achievements. So don't feel rushed playing this game. Take time to enjoy the scenery, the graphic, the music, the character design, etc.! I feel fond of Snufkin, Moomin, and other characters more than ever after finishing the first run.
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: As a person who grew up watching Moomin shows (In Estonia), I have to say that this made me so nostalgic. I used to be a huge Moomin fan so this game really was a dream come true. It's very cozy and fun to play. I'm only halfway through while writing this review but you can bet that I'll finish it quickly. (I wish it had my language but I'm used to everyone forgetting about us so it's fine. I enjoy this game just the same). Get it!
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun and cute game! Took me 5.5 hours to beat it on my first try, and I did not get every single achievement. The art and sound are amazing, and it's such a heartfelt addition to the moomin family story. The plot of the game is similar to Snufkin's role in Farlig Midsommar, but it is completely different otherwise. I really liked it!
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: Bought this for my MIL to try play while recovering from an operation as she is a huge lover of Moomins. She has never played computer games but had a go and unfortunately the learning curve was a bit too steep even with the simple controls and calm game pace. However, the game is spectacular visually and the soundscape is absolutely divine, the environment cute, heartfelt, lovely, characters quirky. I have never read the Moomins but I enjoyed myself so much getting familiar with the characters and environment through this game. I feel that the controls and gameplay are simple enough to try for a non-game-player, even though it didn't work out in our case. This game feels like a warm hug from a friend to me (and I bet it's even more so if you already have a warm past with the Moomins), love it <3
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very peaceful to play. I did go through and get all the achievements in the game. If you are the kind of person who enjoys more variety while playing something or want a more challenging game. You might not like this particular game. For me I found it over time kind of boring. Nothing really new or super exciting after a bit of playing. However it is a cute story, with simple game mechanics, and comfortably corky characters. If you want to just relax, explore a large world with weird little creatures, and save the forest this is the game for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game all about atmosphere. The artstyle, the sound design and the nostalgia the game presents hit me like a truck and although the gameplay is nothing special or innovative, my experience is still positive. I DO believe that you need to have some relation to Moomin in order for this game to resonate with you. The environment and characters are charming by themselves but require a bit of context in order to fully appreciate their behaviour. I also played the game in my native language (Swedish) due to that all my previous contact with the Moomin-universe has been in Swedish. Sadly, the writing feels very tame, with very little wit compared to how Tove Jansson portrayed the characters in her books.In this game you play as Snufkin, a boy who travels to and from Moominvalley every spring when the moomins come out of hibernation. This season, however, he finds that Moominvalley has changed. The river no longer flows, there are parks and rules put up all over the place and Moomin is nowhere to be found. You control Snufkin as he runs, jumps, interacts with and plays music to the different characters and creatures of Moominvalley. There are simple puzzles, stealth-sections and gathering quests. The game is about four hours long and provides tons of charm along the way.+ Lovely artstyle+ Great sound-design- Repetetive and shallow gameplay- Sub-par writingAll in all, I would recommend this game, but it might be a little too expensive for what you get. I would buy it on a sale, it is a joyful little experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: It is the cozy game of the cozy games! If you are such Mummitrolls fan as me, you will love it! I liked that even stressful moments are more challenging than stressful, which is very nice for a relaxing evening! Very happy I got it!If you are a sidequest person, there will be enough for you. However, even with completing all of those I think they game will not take much more than 10 hours total, which is a bit sad. But this is a problem of most cozy games.
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed the art style and the music for this game. It's charming and using different instruments to play for the various scenarios was intuitive. The art style was very unique looking and charming in its own way. I had some issues with moving the character with a Mouse & Keyboard but luckily enough, I could switch to a controller. I would recommend using a controller if you want to play the game. I did have some issues with the frame rate or the game stuttering when you are trying to move the character to go downwards. It wasn't a huge issue but something to be aware of.
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: Giving this a positive review because why wouldn't I? It's a very cute game and I love the vistas, and who doesn't want to harass police officers as Snufkin? However, it's a pretty short game, taking me only 4.2hrs to finish it once. I replayed it twice to get all achievements but each time felt like a drag. The map did little to prevent me from getting lost a lot on my first run, and I assume most people only play it once. I also could not figure out how to switch off the tutorial. (BTW there's a Hemulen Painter to the south of the Hemulen Bug Collecter who I missed completely and apparently other people missed him too.)
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely adored this game. It was a cozy game with a strong message on having respect for nature. The music is great and the visuals are phenomenal. The only issue I personally had was certain mechanics in which you place a boulder down, it's quite hard to get it to sit exactly where you are facing, but other than that, this is a game i'd highly reccommend for anyone who is looking for a cozy RPG with beautiful visuals and music.
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: I thought nothing would scare me as much as The Groke, but a bunch of rowdy kids were enough to send my heart out into the stratosphere. 10/10Super cute game, and I will probably come back to try and get all the achievements one day. I recommend it to people who like Moomin, the art style, and music. The atmosphere is superb, and all the little tasks are simple enough that you want to complete them all. I would not mind getting more side quests. The play style/puzzles are very simple and suitable for children. Adults might find it a bit too easy if they go in expecting too much. I played the game in Swedish and was delighted with how much the writing reminded me of Tove Jansson. You can really feel the love for Moomin in the writing, themes, and story. I hope the other language options exude just as much of that love.At one point on the map a log completely breaks, which means that you can not make it back to that part of the map without taking the long way around. It makes sense in the story, but since I like checking the map for missed items/action events, and in general just experiencing the beautiful backgrounds and art, it was a shame that it took so much time to get around on that part of the map. (Very understandable though.) When chased it took a little while to get a hang of how to move certain items and what way to move them, which almost made me worry that I had bugged something, but I figured it out after many many tries. All in all a very fun little gem.
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: Snufkin was a super cute game! The mechanics are very easy to figure out, the puzzles were pretty easy and not frustrating at all. Really liked that we can change the keyboard controls to make it more suitable for personal playing styles. The music was very cute, art style was consistent and not distracting, very pleasing to look at, really enjoyed the overall story. Fun quick little game to play!
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: I had looked forward to this game since it's announcement, and I can honestly say that the wait was worth it. - Not only have the dev team managed to really bring out the feeling of what moominvalley is like, the characters are also spot on! Wonderful game, short, but non the less a wonderful created game which I'll be playing over and over again
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good game that can be recommended, although if you're planning on buying this you should note that:- It's a short game- It's not a challenging game- Not much replay value eitherIn short, it's a kids game. But that doesn't mean you couldn't enjoy it. I bought this to get something chill and pretty to play for vacation that's all about the V I B E S, and for that itch it works pretty well. Moomin world works in a video game really nicely, and the game is really beautiful. The art and the music work fantastically. It just makes you wish they'd gone a bit harder on creating a game that would give you a bit of a challenge, at least an optional one. Still, it's really fun to play through, just know what you're getting if buying this.
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: I adore this game. I was already a fan of Moominvalley from the show so I was nervous that the game might not live up to the humor and animated magic I remembered.I've never been so happy to be wrong.The game was lovely from start to finish!The watercolor-esque graphics are beautiful, the music is soothing, and the dialogue made me giggle more than once.The puzzles are just enough to be challenging without being frustrating or obtuse.And you can't go wrong with ecopolitical anarchy! Restoring nature feels satisfying and brought a smile every time without getting overly repetitive.Would love to be able to play it again for the first time if I could!
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: I was so hyped for this Game for so long before release and I'm so glad it turned out to be as wonderful as it looked.I grew up in the 90s reading and watching The Moomins and they mean the world to me.This game is so unbelievably beautiful and true to the art and writing of Tove Jansson.I genuinely believe she would be so happy to see this and proud of the team behind it.I highly recommend this game if you love the Moomins as it will genuinely make you so happy and you will love it.The game managed to make me cry happy tears because of how wonderful it is.It would also make a wonderful entry point for someone new to the Moomins.All in all one of the best games I've ever played.You should definitely get it!Thank you to the team!
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: Ok. Where do I start?I haven't actually played this game myself. However I have watched my ten year old daughter finish the game closely followed by her thirteen year old brother. They both give the game great reviews.One thing we all agree on is that the hand-painted graphics perfectly fit the game and really attribute to the cozy atmosphere you also get from the books. We played through the game first in Swedish and then in English and they were both great experiences.There are some really exciting moments where you need to sneak and play the stealth game which had my daughter on the edge of her seat the whole time. My son really enjoyed trying to find everything and 100% the game during his playthrough. Near the end of the game it takes an interesting turn which my daughter liked very much.The only criticism my kids have is that they thought they were about to finish the game several times and then the game went on. This happened several times during their playthroughs and led to some anticlimactic moments, but in the end they thought the game mechanics and the story were really good. However, they only wanted to play through the game once and they don't see a lot of replayability. The game took them about four hours each to finish.
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: It's very much a kids game (for better or worse depending on, y'know, age.): as such, it can be a bit slow, simple and handholdy. But this doesn't really matter when it's got the atmosphere so perfectly right. And it really does.The story feels both like an actual Moomins tale and a whistle stop tour of the characters- in a good way. The art and music are exceptional- especially the art. It's a truly beautiful game, as you can no doubt see. Running around the island, seeing the sights, playing tunes for the creatures that inhabit it, and tearing down the police presence getting in the way of all that; it's all good fun, all so fitting for how a world like this should be explored, and makes for a great Moomins experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: Very cute game. The art style reminds me of the picture books of my childhood and the soundtrack is nice and relaxing. Snufkin meets up with what feels like every character in moomin valley and it is quite nice to see them all, even if it's just a minor appearance. The game could be summed up as "Snufkin commits vandalism" and that fact alone had me chuckling several times while playing. All in all, an enjoyable 4 hour experience. Worth the money, imo
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: Loved the artwork, music, and mechanics. I really appreciated how much the studio paid attention to details and created a story faithful to the Moomin lore. The controls were a little awkward but it wasn't a big problem with custom keybinds. I was taken away by how good the game was at this price point! I highly recommend this game to fellow Moomin fans.
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: In Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley, you go on a search for your pal Moomintroll and try to bring life back to Moominvalley.The game offers a beautifully drawn and relaxing play through with a good story line and side quests. The game itself isn't too difficult, but there are some missable achievements. If you miss them that's ok because the game has repeat play value.
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: A very sweet and fun game to play while talking with friends where it's easy to laugh and joke about all of the funny and sweet situations the developers put you through. Visuals are stunning, music is beautiful, I love Moomin Valley, and I love the way this game understands the characterization of all of our beloved characters!
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: Very very very sweet and well dedigned game, I enjoyed it very much. Imho I think maybe was a bit too short, wish we could just explore the valley after the final scene and to see the valley resored with all the water. Also, developers, please, please fix all the bugs! There is an issue with the zoom in in the Barometer scene and in thefinal stretch of the final park, where there are a lot of policemen and you need to hid in the bushes at the bottom of the park, the screen moves down and Moomin cant walk fast enough, made me get caught like 10 time, fix it please!
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: A great simple fun kind of game. Well enjoyed. The final part of the last mission before you run through the final gates, while you hide in the plant gardens the screen no longer centers on Moomin/Snufkin so u have to blind run as you head to the upper part of the screen. Otherwise no other camera problems experienced in the game with centering on your character
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: Very cute and entertaining game. I honestly have a hard time sitting through most games because I lose interest in what's going on, but Snufkin: Melody of Moominvally has an intriguing story that makes you want to see it to the end. Including plenty of quests to keep you busy, and truly gorgeous artwork!
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: not too familiar with Moomin other than knowing that it's a thing, but this won me over easily all the same. the visuals, music, and story are all beautiful as hell. it's utterly endearing when it comes to its characters, humor, quest design, exploration, and general mechanics too. sometimes there are moments of minor jank, but this is too delightful to care.
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fantastic, it's extremely charming and cool, but at a certain place in the story there is a bug that freezes my screen during a cutscene. This makes it so I can't move and have exit the game to fix it. It resets to a checkpoint before the glitch so I can't progress the story. If anyone has a fix I will change the review but until i hear a solution I can't recommend it
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: I SUPER DUPER LOVE THIS GAME. It makes me feel so nostalgic while playing. Many characters known from the books gradually appears and are in their roles with interesting, charming, and lovely motions and stories; I said lots of "awww so cute" every time they were introduced. The graphic is fabulous and aesthetic with very beautiful, calm, and pleasant musics. Also, the voices of every characters are so so cute (again) and fascinated especially Toffle (I have a crush on his naive and child-like voice. Love love love this guy). Hope there will be more updated stories for this game and game development from other stories or even from the books.
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: FANTASTIC GAME!! I absolutely LOVE Moomins, grew up with them. I can feel that devs had the same childhood. It is perfect game for moomin-lovers. I saw ideas that devs had during the process about how the Snufkin should look like and what should be the style of the game. I think they made the best choice!!  I am SO happy that this game exists. Also you can stare at the sky through flowers and look at the sea. 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: This game is SO HOLESOME! Enjoyable for/with kids, but also as an adult who loves beautiful handmade art, music and lovable characters. In around 5 hours we tear down parks and zoos, because nature is beautiful as is. In a way, the game says "dont mindlessly listed to authorities and help nature thrive". I love it!
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: So beautifully made! I've been playing a lot of games and most of them with far more action than this, but due to depression and other stuff I haven't felt like playing in a long, long time. This was perfect to make me start again. This combines the games we used to play as kids with the nostalgia of characters we grew up with. There's some tricky puzzles but there's no way on Earth you won't figure them out, so you will always feel like you've accomplished something. No one dies, the game autosaves and you just know there's gonna be a happy ending. The perfect game for when you just don't have the energy or mindset for something heavy but still want to solve mysteries and feel all fuzzy inside :)Also: SNUFKIN!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderful game for kids or adults that have nostalgia for the world of Moomin. You have to read a bit, so you might need to help kids who can't read yet.The game is a bit short (I played for 8 hours), and tells a good story. It was really nice to meet so many Moomin characters. I was smiling throughout9/10 (because it could have been longer)I will definitely recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: An absolutely stunning little game that very obviously has a lot of love put into it!I finished my playthrough in less than 5 hours and with only 2 missed achievements, so it's absolutely possible to get all achievements in your first blind go.I do miss that there was more of the game, because what I got is wonderful.Metal gear Moominvalley/10, we love an eco-terrorist
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: This game was beyond charming. My knowledge of Moomins was very minimal, I just knew it always intrigued me and drew me in, and I regret that I didn't jump into playing it until this week. Despite it being a relatively short game to 100%, achievements and all, there wasn't a moment I didn't enjoy (though there is a chase scene that had my heart racing, admittedly) and I am officially irrevocably enamored with the world and characters of Moominvalley. You will absolutely find a character (or more) to love (Little My is my soulmate) in the way Snufkin and Moomintroll love one another and you won't be disappointed by the art, music, or charm along the way.
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: Step into the enchanting world of Moominvalley and reunite with beloved characters in "Snufkin Melody of Moominvalley." This game offers a refreshing dose of nostalgia as you wander through the familiar landscapes and encounter the iconic faces from the Moomin stories. The storyline itself is a delightful and well-crafted tale that will surely bring a smile to your face. The visual aesthetics are simply stunning, adding to the immersive experience.I wholeheartedly recommend this game to both longtime fans of the Moomin stories and newcomers alike. It's a charming journey that captures the essence of the beloved tales, making it a must-play for anyone seeking a delightful adventure.
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: Spoiler Free review: Honestly when I saw the other reviews on this game I was concerned because the average game-time I was seeing was 2 hours.I've been a huge Moomin fan for several years and this game truly is a great addition to the franchise.Everyone is incredibly true to their characters, the artstyle is very similar to the books, and the overall story and gameplay is a lot of fun and it's a brand new story whilst tying in others into the mix to give it that nostalgic moomin charm.This game almost made me cry when I finished it, It's such a lovely game.If you're a moomin fan or just someone who likes cozy games- I absolutely recommend trying this game out.it's so worth it.(This next part is a spoiler)Also- I find it funny how dirty snufkin is when ruining ms fillyjonk's clothing- one swipe and just so much filfth comes off the guy.
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: If you are a fan of Moomin and his friends then you would definitely enjoy this game. It's got a beautiful artstyle, relaxing soundtrack and some nice humor sprinkled throughout the game.And even if you are not familiar with the franchise, you will still end up walking away with a nice and relaxing game you can enjoy for a few hours.Most definitely a strong recommendation from me.
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: A cozy game in the theme of Moominvalley (if you have no seen the animated series, I highly recommend it as it provides more background into the returning characters, but is hardly essential to play the game). Overall, I was never stressed, even during the various park stealth sequences and one chase scene. Music was calming and quests were cute.My only regret, one area becomes locked off after returning from it, and by the end I had 2 achievements I felt could have been completed had I simply been allowed to return there. TBH, I was shocked I hadn't naturally completed both achievements just by playing the game, as I felt I was very thorough in every area.Oh, and no matter how much inspiration I collected I could never reach level 8. It insisted on denying me the final sliver of progress, even after collecting tons more inspiration. On the plus side, those players collecting inspiration have solid leeway and can afford to miss bushes/ferns/dandelions/mushrooms/flowers/clams without risk of being locked out of areas or achievements.Overall, despite my minor gripes, a fun game to play.
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game - highly recommend.  Very fun, not very long, and it isn't hard to do all the things.  The only thing I didn't like is the theme song - it's incredibly annoying and sounds very sad for no reason.  Also the credits can't be skipped or sped up and that awful song plays the entire time.  It's basically just one word repeated over and over but I don't know what it is because it isn't in English - I'm not sure if that makes it more annoying or if it'd be more annoying to hear a word I understood over and over - either way, annoying lol
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: I've been a Moomins psycho for several years now and when I found out the game was being made, I was beyond excited. Now that it's finally here and I've played/finished it, I'd like to acknowledge the superb work you've done. First of all, the drawings are extremely beautiful (resembling the cartoon version from the 90s), the universe is faithfully transcribed and wandering around Moominvalley brought me a lot of joy. The watercolor work is also truly amazing! The story is relatively simple but Snufkin as an eco-terrorist is absolutely brilliant, the vibe is immaculate. The musics are nice and even if they’re looped, it doesn't become annoying after a few hours of play. I loved finding and seeing so many characters from the Moomins books/comics; from the Hattifatteners to Ninny, the Muskrat and even the Island Ghost...! The mechanics of the game itself with the instruments and the levels/inspiration to gather are well thought out, my game went as smooth as possible with absolutely no bugs. The huge plus for me would be for The Groke, a terribly underrated character (but one of the best in my opinion and in the entire Moomins universe)! The little detail of “she” made me very happy. She also has a place of honor in this game and I really appreciated it. I enjoyed following the progress of the game's development and I loved playing it, I highly recommend it to all “cozy gamers” and even more to all the fans of The Moomins universe and of Tove Jansson‘s work! A huge thank you and congratulations to the entire Hyper Games team, you have done an excellent job and paid a very faithful homage to the original works!
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: Good game! Story is fun but short. I would have liked to explore the valley more but now I have to restart the story if I want to get all achievements and see everything. For some reason I cannot go back when the game asks if I like to finish the story or do something else. Some sort of DLC would be great!Really worthy for 20€ game!
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: Indeed, it's a good game, but unfortunately, my experience turned sour after the final task. After the credits rolled, I couldn't proceed with any unfinished tasks. The game forces me to redo the same task. I would have to start the game from scratch just to be able to complete all the tasks, making sure not to tackle the final one until then....
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10 would recommend for a mental health day play through. This game is a beautifully animated escape from the real world. I impulsively bought it one weekend when I needed a game purely for escapism, and didn't want anything too stressful. Visuals and story are adorable, soundtrack featuring Sigur Ros is super chill, my only complaint is that I completed in 5 hours and I wished I could have gone back and played through more after finishing the main story. Would love to see more Moomin games in the future!
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: Super cozy game that isnt too easy, made me think a fair share of times! Lovely graphics and familiar characters and stories. The map is a tad difficult to understand sometimes, and the pointer is not always helpful. Would love to be able to put waypoints to follow on the map outside of the tasks.Recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this game a lot. I started watching the Moomins last year, and I became a fan. I read all the original newspaper strips and watched the famours 90's animated adaptation, and this game is a faithful adaptation of the tone, rebellious commentary, and sweetness of Tove Jansson's works. Loved every bit of it. Let´s fill Moominvalley with crime!
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: This is a beautiful cozy game in the truest meaning of the word.You play as Snufkin and do little tasks that you find in the woods.You don't have to kill somebody, you don't drive, craft, buy or sell anything.You just walk through the woods and you are nice to each other.It's like a personal therapy session, but cheaper. Highly recommendable!
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: "Respect existenceor expect resistance"- Snufkin (probably)Very short but extremely adorable and wholesome title.Im surprised how well the moomin vibe and artstyle translates into the game. Graphics are on-point. Music is great. Story is pretty simple but it fits the source material. Game mechanics are basic and puzzles are really easy, but it's clear that the main focus of developer team was to make the game accessible to all ages and to do justice to Tove Janssen legacy. And they've succeeded.If you're a nostalgic, millenial sucker like me or if you have kids, it's worth checking out.
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: Game easy enough for children so can be played by everyone. Very nostalgic for adults.Cons (for me): No dub, you only have written text. It is quite short for what people would expect from game nowadays. Not sure if you'll like if if you're adult and not Moomins fan. Also, note that if you don't finish all side quests, you will not be able to come back and finish them without starting game from saves earlier in the game (or I haven't found a way to do it haha).  Pros: Moomins, Snufkin and Little My ;) Really cute graphics faithful to original. Engaging story that again fits original story and character design by Tove. Beautiful soundtrack. No bugs (at least I didn't found any...). Overall it's clear it was made by people who know and love Moomins.Hope to see more Moomins games in the future, hopefully longer ones.
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: I've loved Moomin my whole life. Played one Moomin game as a child over and OVER again and I didn't know how much I've longed for a Moomin game as an adult, until I started it and felt full of Moomin love. If you like me love Snufkin, Moomin and all the other Moomin characthers  let your inner child loose and  have a great time in Moominvalley. Mumin <3
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: I'm usually not one for for calm or peaceful games. But when I saw they made a moomin valley game I decided to give it a chance. This game is beautiful and very well made, even if the story is simple It's still fun to experience. Not to mention this game has such good replay ability. I would recommend this game anyone who wants a beautifully made calming game.
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: Lovely art style, calm and soothing soundtrack, simple gameplay. Defintely gets my recommendation if you're looking for a game to chill with.Played the whole game through on a Steamdeck, what a great way to experience it!Although not very long, its an experience worth having, especially if you like Moomin.

_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: Have not yet finished playing but I don't think i'm going to wait to write how amazing this game is! nostaligia hit pretty hard, the art direction is ✨fabulous✨, the story follows the vibe of the show and it's always fun seeing the references the games does to the original sources!will definitly play it again to take off the signs from the valley and fill it with crime!
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: Such a soothing game and a lovely experience. It is delightful to see how much the makers have put an effort to capture the essence of Moomin and their love for it,  and it really shines through in every aspect of the game. Loved every moment of it and so many memories and moments of childhood came up when playing through it. A must play for any Moomin fan!
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: Melody of Moominvalley was such a joy to experience. It took me some time to actually sit down and play it, However when I was able to play it it was such a blast! Being placed in the world of Moominvalley was very cozy and getting to see many of my favorite characters was definitely a highlight. On the side of gameplay, despite not being much of a PC gamer I found it very easy to navigate and manage the puzzles and exploration around Moominvalley. _childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: i was gifted the game so keep that in mind, but genuinely this game was so much fun to play! i played it all in one playthrough because i was enjoying it so much (about 5 hours of gameplay for me). i'm usually not much of a puzzle person but this game was just the right amount of challenge where i didn't get frustrated (which can happen kind of easily for me!) the characters were personable & charming and the story was really enjoyable to slowly work through. i highly recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: An absolute must if you've grown up loving the Moomins.The artwork is beautiful and true to Tove Jansson's style, while keeping it clean and simple as dynamic game sprites. The music is simple and effective. The plot is clear and simple. There are some lovely little side quests to keep you busy and the dialogue has been written well, keeping the characterisations true to the books. It's not a long game, or particularly deep, but there are puzzles and lots of whistle-stop-tour cameos. I hope there're more of these in the pipeline!
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: Mooninvalley is a very sweet, cozy and charming game. Fans of the saga and especially the old animated 90s series or the books will like it, as both the artstyle and the stories seems like a perfect blend of the two. You’ll get to explore Moominvalley and meet most of the characters from the universe. Pretty good dialogue. The controls are also easy and intuitive. I personally like that they didn’t hold back on Snufkin’s anarchism. He will destroy signs and even pick apart whole damn parks, and the anti-authoritarianism is treated like it’s heroic and not vandalism. For a game aimed towards children, I find that especially endearing in a way. The Groke scenes are also quite scary, and will appeal to those who remember it from the TV series. The relationship between Moomin and Snufkin are also exactly made in a way so you can interpret it how you see fit. (I see them as best friends personally.)Only drawback is that it’s not a very difficult game, but I guess it goes more for being chill and almost meditative. It’s critiqued for being a bit short, but I think the length is alright. It’s a game anyone can play. It has a very nice end and animated sequences too.
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent! The art, the obvious care and love for the original source work, though the game seems to mostly draw from the 2019 series in both story and art style (at least so far as I have seen). Gameplay is fun and relaxing. Especially love the sound design ( the simple joy of realizing that your music echoes gently when played inside a cave is something I will relish with childlike delight with every cave system I come across!) There are portions where I am slightly  annoyed as Snufkin gets stuck behind a some tall bushes for a few moments and I am unable to move him or when its obvious that I have to proceed in a certain direction but I have difficulty doing so as the game will not respond or I have to target my jumps from a specific somewhat off angle to reach a rocky platform (however this could entirely be caused by my running this game on an older laptop and it overheating). Even if this isn't an isolated experience it is still hugely minor compared to how relaxing, beautiful and enjoyable the game is overall. Hugely recommend, especially to existing fans of the franchise, but still very enjoyable as a starting point for those getting to know the many beloved characters of Moominvalley for the first time. <3
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: A great retelling of the beloved Moomin series.The control options on PC should still be improved, to be honest. I had to adjust it based on my own preferences. I still enjoyed most of the story and I'll replay it in the future if I ever need a break again.Recommended to people for all ages. Love Tove's work.
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: i've been going through a really rough bout of depression. i'm on meds for it, but i was told they won't kick in for a few weeks. on a whim, when i couldn't find anything enjoyable to do, i decided to boot up this game.i haven't felt this happy and at peace in months. this is an absolutely breathtaking game, and it scratches the part of my brain that always itches for moomins content. it being entirely centered around snufkin is super fun too. it's beautiful, it's silly, it made me laugh in many places. the relationships between the characters hit just right, in a way that i think introduces them perfectly even for newcomers to the moomins scene. i think tove would be proud to see how far her silly little guys have come.
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: The art is amazing and beautiful. The storyline is adorable and fitting with the universe. It's not too difficult so as to distract from the story or the art, and it has some lovely puzzles too. It takes an hour or three to finish, which is the perfect little bite-sized game. _childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this game so much!I love the Moomins and it felt so nostalgic and happy to explore that world. The dialogue and characters were perfect and the storytelling was very in line with existing Moomin stories. The music was wonderful, and I teared up when I heard The Nothing Song because it also features in the ending of one of my favorite movies, Vanilla Sky ❤️ The hand-drawn visuals were gorgeous and the gameplay was very fun and relaxing. _childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely gorgeous...I've been a huge fan of Moomins for my entire life and this game was like playing through a storybook. Tove Jansson herself would be proud!PROS / CONS+ Art-style is absolutely beautiful.+ Progression feels natural.+ Music is pleasant to listen to.+ Entertaining dialogue.+ Side-quests are well incorporated to the story.+/- While I understand the artistic choice, I still missed proper voice acting.- A bit too short, it's over very soon.Please support this game, it deserves your money!
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: The puzzles were easy enough so that I could see myself replaying this in the future with the younger folks in my family. Love the artstyle, music was great also!As for the cons, there was one single typo I spotted, some minor glitches or problems with the policemen AI and sometimes the NPC's instruments or background/cutscene noises would become overwhelmingly loud.Regardless of that, it's an easy 10/10 for me and I would recommend the game to anyone who loves Moomins.
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: I've waited for this game since it the development was first announced and it was everything I wanted and more from a moominvalley game, I absolutely loved it and my younger self would be screaming from joy. I fully enjoyed it, the music was lovely, the entire game was soothing. I loved this game so much
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: I had a lot more fun than I was expecting! There were so. many. sidequests. And I enjoyed doing them all! The game is a little rough around the edges sometimes with hitboxes not working the way you expect, and there being some "hidden" sidequests (i mean the sidequests that very minor characters mention to you and you get achievements for, but aren't added to your quest list [e.g. the spider one at the very start of the game]). And sometimes if you already have the required items for a quest you actually have to walk away then come back to it for the prompt to relinquish your items to appear.Not game-breaking stuff, just a little tedious.Oh, and the soundtrack and ambient noises are very pleasing. Some background music even changes as you progress further in the game (even Snufkin's playing get more energetic) which is a really great touch! If filling Moomin Valley with crime (the good kind) is your fantasy, this game is a must-have!
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: This game is absolutely enchanting. I loved the story and meeting all the characters, esp. my favourite THE GROKE! The graphics made me randomly stop at times just to enjoy the beauty of them. Same with music, I'd stop at certain locations for longer just to listen to it for a while. I cross my fingers for more Moomin games to come out. The devs did an amazing job!
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: Very good but not perfect, if there is one thing that would raise my score of this game it would have been more variation in the gameplay since there's pretty much only the instruments and the world puzzles. Everything else like the visuals, sounds, the world and all of the characters are really cozy and great. _childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the cosiest games I've ever played, and easily a new favourite of mine. The art style is beautiful, capturing the spirit of Moomins while still having its own unique take on it, the world is wonderful and much more explorable than I was expecting with rewarding sights, collectibles, and achievements, and the writing is amazing, particularly for Snuffkin and Little My. I played the whole game in Norwegian, a thing I very rarely do partly because it's seldom an option and partly because the few times it is an option it doesn't tend to be very good, and it completely blew me away with its wit, humour, and heart. If you have any sort of nostalgia to Moomins whatsoever, or are simply a fan of cosy ecoterrorism and wanderlust, this is absolutely a must-play.
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: I am maybe in the second chapter of this game so far, and it really captures the feel of the world Tove created (the Moominworld? Moominverse?). The graphics somehow manage to be peaceful and dynamic at the same time, and evoke watercolor on paper. I absolutely love the aesthetic.The choice for limited voice acting fits well, with characters' speech bubbles being accompanied by an appropriately-toned "Hmm?" or "Hehe!" I initially thought this seemed like an odd choice, but after having played for a few hours, I now feel that the gentle flow/ambiance of the game might actually be somewhat disturbed if all the lines were fully voiced.The process of unlocking new areas/obtaining items that help you to unlock new areas feels gently intuitive. Exploring each new area is pretty relaxing, in my opinion.This part is particularly subjective, but as someone with (very) poor controller skills, I like that the game is not set up to punish me for having the reflexes of an elderly sloth. And finally, the soundtrack is lovely and gives a feeling of whimsy - and what else would you expect to find in Moominvalley? Some of the tracks include Sigur Ros, which is perfect!Overall, I would say this game was certainly worth the wait. The hard work that the team put into this is on full display, and it comes across as something done by exactly the sort of people I would want making a Snufkin game: people who genuinely like the source material. This game is so well done, and I'm so happy to be playing it!EDIT: I have finished the game and stand by everything I have previously said here. It's a fairly short little tale but I had a good time!
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: It's a game. About going against the authority. About compassion. About seeing the good in everyone without any exceptions. It's a heartfelt, passionate and wery welcome gift to Moomin fans, to the Moomin world, to us, players. A light yet deep story packed in a fairly simplistic gameplay seems like it was written by Tove herself, yet it's original. Playing through this game was like reading through Moomin book: a charming and a light adventure with a fair lesson at the end. Overall, it's 10 / 10. I am deeply in love with this game just after three hours it took me to finish it.
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: Nothing too special and sadly very short (around 3 hours to complete.) The art, environments, characters, quips, dialogue, are all extremely on brand and entertaining enough, so Moomin fans will most likely get their money's worth and what's wanted out of it. But, think of it less like buying a typical video game, and more of buying an animated interactive comic/storybook with light puzzle and fetch quest elements that don't really require too much thought. It was nice and relaxing just to roam around Moominvalley, even if it was a tad bit too linear and railroaded. Definitely one of it's biggest strengths in that regard and has a ton of lovely art, aesthetics, atmosphere, and vibes, but as a game experience it seems to be just fine and just okay. Might be hard to recommend if you're not already into Moomin, but if you're reading this chances you already are. So if you're a Moomin fan who thinks this has potential to be a good time, it's likely you'll have a good time.

_childDocuments_.review: Every single detail of this game has been so carefully and lovingly crafted.The visuals still leave me in awe; from the storybook style to the animations filled with personality, it is a feast for the eyes. Tove Jansson was known for her use of colour in her art, and clearly the team did their research because the colours are simply divine.The music is fittingly atmospheric in every scene and just a delight to listen to (so glad the deluxe version includes the soundtrack!). They evoke emotions ranging from relaxing to upbeat, from pensive to mischievous; the latter of which is wonderfully conveyed in the track "Oh, great... Woodies", that maintains a sense of silliness without ever becoming annoying. The sound design is perfect in my opinion, with satisfying sound effects and funny voices that contribute to making a truly immersive world.The writing carries with it the Moomins' signature comedy and queerness, and the story emphasises a balance of togetherness and community, with independence and solitude (the latter experienced through quiet gameplay moments of finding "resting spots" where you can bask in nature's beauty).The gameplay isn't incredibly difficult but still challenging enough to be engaging, and has enough variety to keep it interesting. I like that the slow-paced exploration is interspersed with the blood-pumping chase sequence and park stealth missions. Progressing the game unlocks new areas and characters to interact with which was GREAT motivation for me.This was overall an incredibly enjoyable and emotional experience; I would 100% recommend to fellow Moomin fans as it's such a great new way of entering the world of Moominvalley, and I feel as though those new to the franchise will also get a lot out of it - you must experience the artistry on display here!!I know a lot of players have expressed disappointment over the length of the game, and that they wish there was more, and I have to agree - despite the content available being perfect, I did feel as though there could have been MORE. More opportunities to use the skills we're taught, more character interactions, etc. Obviously I don't think this would have been possible with the time restraints/game dev as a whole (so impressive that they achieved what they did in, what, 4 years?!), but I do wonder what we could've gotten in a world where they had a bigger budget and deadline... ah well, as far as complaints go, "we want more" is at least better than "we want less", eh? 😆 And I'm ultimately very glad they went with quality over quantity.

_childDocuments_.review: Even if you didn’t read the stories or watch any of the adaptations, it seems almost impossible to not be aware of the Moomins and their visual designs, both created by the Finnish writer and illustrator Tove Jansson. Yet, there haven’t been that many videogame adaptations of the series and those that existed seem to have been exclusive to either Finnish or Japanese market. As such, Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley might be the first videogame adaptation of Moomins to release internationally and on several modern platforms. It is a very very simple game, but also a very very charming one.If you are somehow not aware of Moomins at all, the series are centered around a cast of different fairy tale-like creatures that are somewhat based on the North European mythology. The cast of characters is pretty large, but at the center of it all are a family of Moomintrolls who live a simple life in the Moominvalley, going on simple adventures and finding new friends. The mood and overall tone of the stories is different from what one would find in, say A. A. Milne’s Winnie-the-Pooh stories, as more characters can be very pragmatic or sarcastic and more parallels with real world can be drawn, but the feel of the world isn’t entirely dissimilar. As such, Moomins are very much intended for the kids first and foremost, but they can be enjoyed by people of all ages.The game nails this intended audience feel quite well. The story of Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley is very simple in its criticism of meaningless “progress” and industrialisation, of bureaucracy for the sake of bureaucracy and every dangerous and scary situation is just part of an adventure on the way to an end, where everything will definitely work out. And the delivery of this type of story is very good, while also succeeding at introducing the world of Moomins and its many cute characters to the players.Gameplay-wise, it also hits an interesting balance of being engaging and potentially challenging, without being obtuse or difficult for kids but also completely uninteresting for experienced players. As a whole, the world of the game is presented as a giant open map that gradually opens up in an almost metroidvania-like fashion and as you explore you will be finding characters to help (with quests dedicated to that) and some optional activities to do. Most of the time you just explore the world with a top down view and solve simple puzzles that often involve playing different instruments. But occasionally you get simple, but still interesting stealth sections, during which Snufkin engages in simple acts of eco terrorism and sabotage by removing the “do not” signs and destroying tasteless statues.It’s all presented in a really wonderful art style with a pleasant soundtrack that is both surprising and somewhat disappointing. For one, the soundscape of the game is genuinely great and the tunes are very good on their own. And occasionally a Sigur Rós song might start playing, as they’ve co-written a couple of instrumental compositions for the soundtrack. Yet, despite the game’s relatively short length, the amount of music is surprisingly limited, so you will be listening to the same simple tunes very often and there’s just not enough variety to them. Given the tone of the music, it reminded me of the fantastic Chicory: A Colorful Tale that did a far better job at creating a similar mood through music.In a way, that’s been my general feeling about the game. What it does it does quite well, sometimes great even. But at the same time, it never tries to go higher than just being good, like there’s no huge ambition behind the project. No fault in it, really, as what Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley does it does really well and I’m glad I’ve played through the game. But it is no more than “very nice” and “very pleasing”, which is a tiny bit of a shame.

_childDocuments_.review: Lovely game. My daughter of 4 loves it, and I'm enjoying it too. It looks great visually, obviously inspired by the books, which we are reading currently. Music is chill. Runs amazing on the Steam Deck. I'm sick of games for children that are of low quality because you can get away with it. This is obviously not such a game, it seems to be made with love, passion, and skill.The game is just perfect for my daughters abilities. She gets a bit scared when she needs to handle police, so I often have to take over then, but she'll get there. The penalty for getting caught is non-existent. She got VERY scared when we had to run from the Groke, but in a fun way that she will remember and that we talk about together.My single critique is the lack of voice-over. I really get how much of a cost-saving measure it likely was to not include it, and the little funny sounds when speaking with characters are very cute, but it is a hassle to have to read aloud every time. At least there's translation into our native language of Danish, so I don't have to translate on the fly.That being said, I can only recommend this for any kids that enjoy the Moomin world. And parents too.
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: As a finn and a child of the 90s, I do have nostalgia for Moomins and a bias towards this game. I want this to be good with all my heart. However, even with all of my bias, I do feel this game merits objective praise, from adhering to the style of Tove Jansson in art direction making it stand out, music that is inspired by but not copying the previous iterations of moomins and the relaxed pace of the gameplay complimenting the shorter length (as compared to other titles with infinite gameplay or longer narratives). I have seen criticism regarding the length and gameplay of the game, but in my opinion, it is better this way. Why?You feel like being a part of a Moomin adventure.Not some epic narrative to rescue the world or navigating intricate web of politics or a ''AAAA'' pirate action-RPG-cash-in.Just a story of an Snufkin returning to the valley after a long winter absence and finding it changed for the worse and Moomin has gone missing. And we have to fix it by filling the valley with crime, anarchy and friendship.Just another good adventure in moominvalley. Do play it for the feeling of visiting Moominvalley and know that you are always welcome back, just as you are.
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: I love Moomin and I love Snufkin, this game has amazing art style, relaxing music and stays true to its source, also nice to see and play games developed by a studio from your  own country (Norway).The only thing "negative" I have to say about the game is that it was a bit short, I would've hoped that it was longer, I finished it in around 3 hours, keep in mind that this was me trying to be a completionist, there are a couple of things I missed. The time was well spent and I don't necessarily hold it against the game, however I think thats something people should be aware of when buying the game.I also wish we'd be able to free roam after finishing the main story/game, just walk around and chill, finish up sidequests if you still haven't completed them all and find whatever you've missed. When finishing the game and pressing "continue" on the main menu it puts you back right before activating the last cutscene and ending the game, without the possibility to return to the normal free roam part. Hopefully there would be a possibility for the developers to add an epilogue update of some kind that allows this.All in all great game, I really hope the game wins an award for its art style as it 100% deserves it.
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: This game is absolutely stunning, and an overall lovely experience, and I highly recommend it! 9/10!Longer version:The artstyle and the soundtrack were both top tier; I kept getting distracted at the places where Snufkin could lie down and you got a pretty view. Atmosphere wise, this game was a perfect game to play while drinking tea and having scented candles lit. Very cozy, very lovely!The gameplay was fun; the puzzles and parks not being too easy while also never being hard enough that I felt stuck. (Except for the one place, but I'll get to that after I'm done with all the praise.)I especially loved the section with the woodies; it was both a fun little puzzle section, plus Snufkin's dialogue during was hilarious. And I was very happy in general to see that the woodies got to feature in the game, since a lot of people tend to forget about them existing.Snufkin and Little My's banter during the game definitely gave me massive sibling vibes, which is perfect since they  siblings (another thing people tend to forget), so seeing their interactions reflect that made me very happy!Now... For the one thing I didn't enjoy in the game.As cute as it was that , the fact that it changed the gameplay drastically for the last "level"/park of the game was just plain frustrating. Up until then, the gameplay was firmly established, each park stepping it up in terms of difficulty, clearly building up towards the final stage. I sort of get what they were going for, , but there are so many other things they could have done instead to achieve the same thing. If it hadn't been for the fact that I knew it was the last stage, I would have quit the game then, simply because of the intense frustration I felt at But other than the stumble at the end, the game truly was a lovely experience, and I will sing its praises to anyone who tries to talk to me for the rest of the year!
