_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley has been on my wishlist since the very first announcements. I'm a huge Moomin fan, and was so excited to see what the game would hold after playing the demo too. The illustrations are beautiful, amazing! Truly captured the essence of Moominvalley for me. The characters are very fun to engage with, and the basic storyline is strong.  I feel like the developers did such a good job with shaping the game to be true to the softness and quirkiness of the Moomins, but missed some more sidequests or a more in-depth storyline. For an adult, it wasn't very challenging, but pleasant nontheless. I have to admit I was a little disappointed to have finished it so quickly. I can still go back for some achievements of course, and I will, but I've put a little over 4 hours of active play time in the game and it was done.  I'd reccommend it if you're a fan of the Moomins and looking to explore Moominvalley in a different way, or if gorgeous artstyles are your thing, as long as you keep in mind the story itself is over before you know it (which also says a lot about the enjoyments I did get even thogh it was short)!
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: This game is absolutely stunning! The beautiful art and music makes it a true pleasure to revisit Moominvalley as an adult, and the quests are fun and offer just the right amount of challenge. Pulling out the Park Keeper's signs and knocking over statues was oddly satisfying! The story is creatively written and executed, and the overall feel of the game is very cozy and relaxing. Loved it!
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: I bought the game during the first day it was available. It is so nice and cozy that I want to replay it right now, even though I just finished itThe game is new, so, of course, there are some bags, but they do not make the game impossible to finish (mostly they are about "freezing in the bushes" for several seconds)The Moominvalley is full of adorable creatures which are there not only for a picture, but for some quests too! Although the main plot is not very long, there are a lot of side quests to enjoy!Ps: the game is not to make you brain work. It is quite simple and relaxingAnd yes, I am not crying, it's just nostalgia
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: Gorgeous game, perfectly capturing the Moomin-vibe we adore. The puzzles are very calming to solve, not hard at all. However I was very sad that there were no gameplay after the story ends and I couldn't even figure out how to bring Moominmama's flowers back to life. Even though the main story is well rounded and complete, some closure was certainly missing in my opinion. I would've appreciated more side missions, overall the game left me with an "incomplete" feel. 10/10 for music, artstyle and loyalty to the original but sad face for not being able to go back to the valley after it ends.
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely wonderful game!! The moomins have a special place in my heart, and the art, music, story and gameplay are perfect and brought me a lot of comfort and joy. Even if you're not a moomin fan, I totally recommend this game. Who knows, maybe you'll discover a new world that you'll fall in love with :)
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: This was a delightful game with fun puzzles! I love the art style and colours, especially since you can control the contrast. Getting to see so many of the Moomin characters was a treat too and all the characters felt like themselves and the writing was on par and matched Tove's writing (at least from my perspective). I can't wait to play again and find all the pages for Moominpapa and see what else I need to boost my stamina.Controls took a sec to get used to as well, but nothing that made the game too difficult, even in the Groke section all you needed was movement and the S key. There was only one spot where I got stuck, on Hattifattener Island when you first get the drum and move the frog, it was a bit tricky to maneuver for the game to let me jump on the next rock but, I was able to get over after I took a break from the game. 10/10 :D
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: Played trough the whole game right away, what an experience! Have been waiting for this since the demo. So adventures and relaxing to play, but still you have to use your brain! Really emotional to see the good relationship between two best friend, Mummi and Snusmumrikken! Best game i have ever played, not kidding. And also brought back my good childhood feeling and memories when i saw Mummitrollet as a kid. i was always called Lille My as a kid since i was much like her, so good to see they still made her as sassy and sarcastic as she always was! Hope theres a sequel, maybe we can see them in in other seasons of the year? Developers, please do! REALLY recommend this game both for adults and kids! 11/10!
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: If you’re a fan of the Moomins and if you spent your time in the Moominvalley as a child, this is a game for you. It’s been a while since we’ve gotten a Moomin game that wasn’t a mobile game. Now, the game is short, about 4 to 5 hours if you explore thoroughly and its 20€ which might be a tad expensive for the amount of content the game has, but if you’re willing to overlook these things, I think you will really enjoy the time you put into the game. I know I did. Some things are just worth it. The characters are faithful to Tove Jansson’s creations, the art style is absolutely beautiful and the cozy vibes are there. Overall, well done Hyper Games.
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: What a beautiful game.  One of the best games I've played. Soundtrack, art direction, characters, story, gameplay, everything is perfect. I watched the show when I was a kid and while playing this game I got brought back to those times. I haven't cried like this in years, of course these were happy tears. Thank you for creating this beautiful game. This is art.
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most beautiful games I've played in a long time, I've been watching the development for a long time and was so excited it finally released! So much so I played it 100% style (minus a hiccup I had at the beginning but that gives me an excuse to play it again lol!). If you want a nice, wholesome game to play then this is the best one that I will now and forever recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: The best licenced game I've ever laid my eyes on. It perfectly captures the charm, magic and wit of Moomins and draws inspiration from different books to create a plot that works in a videogame format. The art style is beautifully and faithfully styled after Tove Jansson's watercolor illustrations, and while I wasn't crazy about the DMCA-threat opening song the rest of the soundtrack and sound design was wonderfully atmsopheric. I also like that the settings have a streaming safe music mode.In terms of gameplay Snufkin was larger than I expected! I'd say it's a 3-5 hour playthrough depending on how quick you are and how much time you spend blowing dandelions and staring at the sky. I enjoyed how the gameplay was structured to have slightly different-feeling sections, including the boss fight equivalents all having a bit of a different twist of their own. Overall There was more variety in the gameplay than I had expected beforehand! Lastly, the Finnish translation of the game was very good, big props for that.A highly enjoyable, atmospheric game to brighten anyone's day, especially a Moomin fan's!
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely wonderful. Brought back a lot of childhood nostalgia. The Artbook was also beautiful. I would love to get the gazing spots as animated backgrounds for my desktop or Opera GX browser.As a child I used to watch the cartoon in estonian so seeing the english names was slightly odd. If an estonian translation comes out I might replay it (for the third time) and recommend it to my young neices and nephews.Thank you to everyone who worked on this game <3
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: As a Moomin fan, this game is great. The game borrows a lot from it's source material even down to story concepts, which makes it feel like i'm treading familiar ground through a different lens.For someone only getting into Moomin through this game, i'd say that the characters may feel a little underbaked without prior knowledge of who they are.The game has simple gameplay concepts, but it makes the most of what it has, and never truly ditches a concept that's been introduced, which i can appreciate.A few gripes are a weird glitch with NPCs jittering like they were teleporting around at a certain point in the endgame and the lack of a post-game where continuing after finishing the game just leads you to the game's final moments. Returning to certain areas of the game is also impossible after you've left them.Because of that, the game may very well require a second playtrough if you decide to earn 100% completion.All in all, the game is still exactly what i looked for, a mostly chill game that allows you to sit back, explore, take things at your own pace, enjoy the visuals and listen to the great soundtrack.
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great game with a amazing story that really reminds me of the real moomin books and storys. good side quests to but would like more of them. i was dissapointed of that it didn't become open world after you finish the story that would be a awesome add on or dlc for the game. random encounters would also be great.i bought the deluxe but i would like more side content for the next updates. i really recomend it for story game fans and moonin fans! :)
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: oh my goodness, I cannot put into words how much joy this gave me. You just have to play it to know. It amazing, the art, the music, the storyline and extras, all absolute gold. I spent half my time enjoying the drum and just banging on it around anything and everything the moment I got it. Please why is this game so good, it has every and no right to be all at the same time.
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful game and wonderful story! I loved watching Moomin so much and  Snufkin was my fave character. So I was super excited when I found out there was a game being made based on Moomin starring Snufkin! I excitedly waited for this game and I was not disappointed! The story was well written and all the characters felt exactly how I remembered them. Everything about the game was charming, the humor was silly, the art was amazing, the music was soothing and beautiful, and all the characters were just so fun to talk and interact with. The gameplay wasn’t too difficult but wasn’t super duper easy. There were a few times were I struggled moving Snufkin (because he got stuck in odd ways) but I mostly blame it on user error and May have just been my keyboard acting strangely. Otherwise I loved this game so much! Thank you for making such a wonderful game of characters I absolutely adore 💕
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: So overall I enjoyed the game but I was surprised how short it was. Nice for Moomin fans tho.+the graphic design+the vibe+some funny and cute dialogs+being quite faithful to the books and the TV series-short, it took me 3 hours to finish-considering that, it is a bit pricy for me-the tasks were very simple, they didn't involve much thinking or agility-because of that the game was sometimes boring and repetitive
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: I started watching the moomin anime from the 90's for the first time a couple of weeks ago and I immediately became a fan of these beloved characters and the world they live in. When I found out about the existence of this game I just knew I had to play it... and it was everything I imagined it would be. I absolutely loved it!! It made me laugh and cry a little (I'm very sensitive lol), also it was fun to notice the similarities and changes in comparison to the 90's anime. The only negative thing I can think of is that I wish it was longer... I'll definitely play it again but it would be amazing if a DLC with additional content came out sometime in the future. I really hope this game gets the recognition it deserves!!
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: Nothing too deep gameplay-wise here, but an enjoyable romp through the Moominverse. Probably more aimed towards a younger audience, but if you're an adult who enjoys Moomin you'll appreciate this title. Expect to put in about 3-4 hours.While I enjoy the "stealth" missions advertised in the trailer, I wish there were maybe a few more. The music  instruments I feel could been more varied both in number and in use, but otherwise perhaps a good starter game for a young audience, though with no voice acting will require reading skills to play.
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: Such an amazing experience, i never expected a game to be full of life. The ambiance is soothing, the visual are stellar its like the moomin books came to life before me. the characters were so well written and the story was so heartwarming. id recommend this game to any long time moomin fan or anyone looking for a nice relaxing charming game to play to take their mind off everything.
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: This was an incredible game. I've been a huge fan of the Moomins for a long time and have been following this game for a while and it totally delivered on my expectations. It was actually longer than I had anticipated. Overall, it was a beautiful experience and felt true to the original stories. Will absolutely be playing it again.
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: Been a huge fan on the Moomin series for so long and Snufkin is my absolute favorite character so I've been excited for this game since it was announced! Love the story, the gameplay, the characters, and I'm very impressed at how similar the art is to Tove Janssons while still being it's own thing. Such a lovely game and I hope they make more games set in Moominvalley in the future!
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: Short and sweet.    Honestly, just a beautiful experience full of the life and charm of the 90s cartoon.  Snuffkin himself is a care-free vagabond who returns home to moominvalley and discovers that one man's selfish vision of the valley is suffocating it.  You'll solve quick puzzles and explore the valley all while helping its denizens along the way.
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: A work of art! some of the stills I wish I could have as a screensaver. It allows in game breaks with sights, multiple plot lines with various characters, and I had a lot of fun with the variety of mechanisms Snuffkin can use. My favourite feature would definitely be how you can click on a quest site on the map and there will be a black pointer finger that will point to the direction of the site. I wish I could use that feature for certain areas on the map regardless of whether it is a quest site but who knows maybe that would be included on an update! 10/10 best gaming binge ever
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: The Moomin franchise has always been extremely close to my heart, and this game absolutely does it justice with its beautiful art, heartwarming story and engaging gameplay. I swear I found myself smiling the entire time while playing, and I had to force myself to stop playing so I could go about my daily business! 100/10 would recommend!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: I sacraficed a butterfly to a spider.Got to vandalize public property. (ACAB)I made a public official lose their home and job at the same time.I disturbed wild fauna and flora by banging a drum so hard, the plants died and birds went insane.Rode across a small body of water on a sea monsters head.Recommended.In all seriousness, this is a well done game with a wonderful atmosphere and a faithful adaptation of the original world and characters of Tove Jansson.
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderful music and visuals, a cozy little playable storybook. If that is what you're looking for, this is exactly it. My only qualms are its short length (I am missing 3 achievements but otherwise beat the game in under 4 hours) and the movement. Mouse clicking to move feels a little strange and sometimes I'd get stuck on a wall. Aside from that, a perfect experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful, charming game I can't recommend enough. A breezy but engaging adventure through a gorgeously rendered version of this world, delivered in a way that left me warm and fuzzy all over, a teary smile as the credits came to a close. Completely worth your time and money, especially if you need to get away from things for a little while.
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: A very wholesome and comfy game. In my opinion, it's more of an experience than a game, as its main points are the music, the clever dialogue and the beautiful artstyle & environment. These points all combined create a magical atmosphere in which you are immersed into the wonderful Moominvalley as you make your way through the nifty storyline.The gameplay mostly consists of easily solvable puzzles, but are enjoyable nonetheless -  at times quite reminiscent of the puzzles from the game 'The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time'. Took me about 5 hours to complete the game in an unhurried pace.
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely stunning looking game. It really is the moomins comics come to life. I don't know who thought giving Snufkin more than one instrument was a good idea, as if he's powerful enough.  I love how the lights hit the ambient at night and that you can  Overall a relaxing, warm and funny experience, encompassing many characteristics that make the Moomins special. Thank you <3
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: I really really liked the game, the art, the muisic and story were just wonderful! But it was so short, I wish for more moments between Snuffkin and Moomin  and for more areas to explore. Also would be great if cut-scenes for  were different each time. Big thanks to the devs for the game, hope to see more!
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: Adored this little game on the release date!! It’s a sweet little adventure, with a longer playtime than I was expecting! Theres a main story, but also plenty of side quests to accomplish as you explore. I had a delight after realizing the flute synced up with the band musi and just played along with them. The only downside is that the quests can sometimes be a little confusing on what your meant to do (the butterfly catching quest and the watercolor one I couldn’t figure out), but other than that? Wonderful. Stunning game. I recommend the DLC just on cute little aesthetics alone
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: Snufkin and the Finnish Hippos are here to remind you to commit Ecoterrorism today! The art style and audio design was fantastic. I really enjoyed this game from start to finish and all the little side quests fitted in nicely with the overall story. Obviously best instrument was the drum, because who can forget the iconic meme of "First I bang my drum, then I bang your mom" Classic. Loved it! Try it today!
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: Completing this game took me 4.5 hours with unlocking 62% of the achievements, is it little? For me, it's too little; I feel a bit unsatisfied. I understand that I might not be the target audience for this game due to my age, but I enjoyed playing it a lot, and I wish there was more. Musically, it's fantastic; unfortunately, I played with the streaming option on, so I didn't hear all songs or musical motifs were used. A big plus for the overall experience, and a big minus for the length of the game. Because of that, I feel like I overpaid a bit; this feeling wasn't there with Stray, even though it was also a relatively short game
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: this game in mutiple ways is a masterpiece. from the music to the art style, the details and just the overall vibes makes this game an amazing expierence. as a long time lover of moomin and as someone whos been waiting for this since the trailers first dropped i highly encourage you to pick up this game. get some of your favorite snacks, a hot cup of your drink of choice and get cozy. 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: Overall impression: great game and I highly recommend it. I grew up with a lot of mumin so I'm very nostalgic for it and I think it has everything I love about it. The artwork is amazing, the music fits perfectly, and getting inspiration for helping others and playing music for wildlife to me is the spirit of it all. Of course I cant say for sure, but I think Tove would be proud. You've all put in so much work and it did not disappoint. Two very minor things I would recommend is a custom cursor for the aesthetics but the default one can get a little lost in the artwork sometimes and I hope this would make it more accessible. Second is that I also noticed that movement stopped if the cursor hit the edge of the screen and continuing movement would be a great QOL change. Some of the side quests not showing on the map wasn't bad for a first play through, but would be nice for 100% completion runs. Everything else I've already seen mentioned like the ability to go back after the end to explore (I really want to see Muminmammas garden in bloom)
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: First of all -  what a wonderful and wholesome game! This was a nostalgic trip for myself and  you can absolutely notice the love behind this title and how the devs kept the charm of the world of the moomins.  Some activities could be repetitive but overall who can says no to being chaotic,  kicking down signs etc. haha.  Cannot wait to replay with the copy righted music since as a creator you had to turn them off and 100% the game of course!
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: This was an absolute, truly lovely, treat of a game. so wonderfully wholesome and cute to the core, that I couldn't help but smile with childlike imagination the entire time playing; and I don't even have the nostalgia of having watched or read the moomin books and shows as a kid. The gameplay is based on exploration of a beautiful world with the perfect amount of side tasks and just the right amount of freedom of exploration to find shortcuts and loops through areas for efficient map design. The game does have a few small stealth encounters, but theyre very short and very easy. Just a little, mark to mix up the otherwise walking simulator. But not difficult enough to break into the general wholesome exploration of a beautifully designed and drawn world, meeting lovely characters on a journey.Also, theres so much more exploring than I even realised. I was pretty confident I was at 100% by the time i hit the final cutscene and found I missed several sidequests still. Giving the game enough replayability for completionists, without so many that you start to dread exploring the map.
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: “I would save your life eight times a day if only I could.”– Snorkmaiden (Comet In Moominland, 1946)“I had now found my first friend, and so my life was truly begun.”– Moominpappa (The Exploits of Moominpappa, 1950) Wonderful artstyle and soundtrack, not completely finished with the story yet but I'm enjoying it so far. <3

_childDocuments_.review: Let`s save Moomin and fill Moominvalley with CRIME and MISCHIEFAbsolutely fantastic art style, I am here for all the cozy vibes and I can see myself replaying this many times, as I love Mumin so much. It fills me with nostalgia, it´s full of hidden jokes, you meet all your favorite characters from the books and you can flatten the ferns with your drum! Loved it, 10/10, thank you to the developers for an amazing game.

_childDocuments_.review: A few games can be called "Masterpieces". THIS is 1 of them.Incredible art, fantastic music, ABSOLUTELY AMAIZING STORY so far!A game for children AND adults, exactly like the original Tv-series.very very VERY special thanks to the developers for bringing us an amaizing Moomins game and honoring the Moomins creators vision. Heres hoping it will be 1 of many to come!"Masterful Piece Of Art"PS. Im DEFINETLY not Finnish!

_childDocuments_.review:
Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley is a musical adventure game in which Snufkin needs to restore the harmony of Moominvalley, after a series of grotesque parks has appeared and ruined the valley's natural balance. 

The game is an ambient and wholesome experience for both kids and adults, and combines open world-mechanics with puzzles, stealth and melodic elements.

name: Nine Sols
detailed_description: Nine Sols is a lore rich, hand-drawn 2D action-platformer featuring Sekiro-inspired deflection focused combat. Embark on a journey of Asian fantasy, explore the land once home to an ancient alien race, and follow a vengeful hero’s quest to slay the 9 Sols, formidable rulers of this forsaken realm. Story In New Kunlun, hero Yi has awakened the 9 rulers of this forsaken realm. To defeat the 9 Sols in the deserted city. “Becomes one with the way of Tao…” New Kunlun, the Solarian’s last sanctuary, has remained quiet for centuries. Inside this vast realm, the ancient gods left mortals with a promised land that is forever protected by the sacred rituals, yet the truth of this world remains unknown to most. Everything changes when Yi, a long forgotten hero from the past, is awoken by a human child. Follow Yi on his vengeful quest against the 9 Sols, formidable rulers of this forsaken realm, and obliterate any obstacles blocking your way in Sekiro-lite style combat. Explore in unique “Taopunk” setting that blends cyberpunk elements with Taoism and far eastern mythology. Unravel the mysteries of an ancient alien race and learn about the fate of mankind. Features 2D Sekiro-lite Combat: Slash, deflect, charge into enemies and blow them up with the Taoist talisman! Each fight combines fast, brutal action sequences with classic platforming mechanics. Intriguing Boss Fight: Ready yourself to fight the vicious ancient guardians and gruesome creatures. Be patient and utilize every move in your arsenal, mix up with Yi’s godly bow to defeat these larger than life figures. Taopunk Setting: When cyberpunk clashes with Taoism, melding sci-fi elements with eastern mythology/fantasy, the experimental genre of Taopunk was born. Exploration: Traverse in the interconnected regions of New Kunlun. Discover secrets, piece together the story behind Yi’s revenge. Aids from inhabitants: Meet interesting NPCs of this world and interact with them to receive upgrades, gain new abilities, and discover useful technology. Hand-drawn Environments/Animations and Manga: Nine Sols is filled with meticulous hand-crafted, anime style landscapes, sprite based hand-drawn animations, blending with Japanese manga inspired cutscenes. Red Candle Games From the creators of award-winning psychological horror games Detention and Devotion, comes Red Candle Game’s latest title Nine Sols. The studio aims to deliver a stylized action platformer that’s cohesive and complementary to its lore-rich narrative. It’s an ongoing, most ambitious project from this indie studio.

_childDocuments_.review: Platforming with a nice fighting system posing a fair challenge.Endgame requires the player to learn a certain playstyle, creating a learning curve over the whole game. The game is incredibly fun! There is scary bits though, so be wary of this. In general the ambience and music enhance this games experience and I heavily recommend playing with those on.
_childDocuments_.name: Nine Sols

_childDocuments_.review: A crazy good title, I am delighted by how much I have continued to think about the game's story. While I remember thinking   the themes were simplistic, there's a point near the ending where I realized that simplicity is sometimes very effective in creating a deeply satisfying narrative. Areas fully explore a boss' personality before fighting them, and after you explore their memories making each memorable and dynamic. The central hub has a number of characters who's interactions I find deeply compelling. All of this to say the game holds your attention in both its game play and story, all densely packed in a vibrant world waiting to be experienced.
_childDocuments_.name: Nine Sols

_childDocuments_.review: This game is AMAZING. the story and plot makes it all the more interesting, and i honestly think the gore makes it just a bit more unique. im not with gore, i kinda dislike it as a whole, but with this games cartoony style, makes the gore so unexpected, which gives this quite the unique experience. Mixed with these emotions givin from all these characters, truly mix in with it all. If you have time, and you enjoy difficulty, with a game kinda like hollow knight. PLAY THIS GAME. 10. out of 10.
_childDocuments_.name: Nine Sols

_childDocuments_.review: Nine Sols is genuinely the best feeling game I have ever played combat-wise, the music is phenomenal, the art is utterly gorgeous, and the bosses are some of the best I have ever experienced. I cannot praise this game enough, if you enjoy metroidvanias, or 2d platformers, or sekiro-style parrying, you will love this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Nine Sols

_childDocuments_.review: I see a lot of people comparing this to games like Dead Cells. That game in true Rogue-like fashion is all about single runs starting over if you get to the end or you die. The best comparisons I can give you would be Hollow Knight and the two Blasphemous games. If you're a fan of side scrollers, games that require patience, skill and repeatedly dying while you figure out boss mechanics akin to Dark Souls, Elden Ring etc, then you're going to LOVE this game.I only have 4 hours in it so far, but since I started it, its been hard to put down. There's a great story, interactions with NPC's that also drive the narrative forward in meaningful ways. The art style and animations are just fantastic. Gives lots of Hollow Knight and Ori vibes 100%. I'm not sure if the art in the game is all hand-drawn, but wouldn't surprise me if it was. You'll see what I mean.The combat so far has been pretty tight. You get abilities and weapons just like any typical adventure game. To unlock them you have to level up and/or progress through the story. Just like Hollow Knight, DS etc, when you die (and you will die in this game many times, I promise) you drop your EXP and can retrieve them, but if you die on the way you lose them. They treat this more typical though unlike in HK that you don't have to fight a clone of yourself to get them back. Just pick them up off the ground and you're Gucci.  You have a Jade system that's very similar to HK in that they're used to amplify things such as combat, dodging, currency acquisition and so on, but require the proper nodes to equip. I've tried playing it with both a controller as I usually play these games as well as Keyboard & Mouse and I can say that their controls on KB/M are actually quite good. You can tell this meant to be played with a controller, but its nice to see they put in the effort for us KB/M folks. You can remap all the keys to suit your needs, so if you aren't down with the sticks, you'll be just fine.If you've got this far, stop reading this, drop the $30 (which I think they could have easily asked $40 and been fine) and go enjoy this game. Don't know how many hours its meant to be for a standard play through, but I wouldn't be shocked if you get at least 25-30 hours, more if you're a completionist like me :-D*UPDATE*14hrs played and the game gets better and better, story really starts to unfold as you progress and its 100% worth your time to do the side quests not only for upgrades to health etc, but if you're enjoying the story, you get lots of dialogue and pieces filled in to Yi's background. Also, after reading the description on the store page, they're on point with the references to Sekiro. The dodge, parry, punish mechanics are definitely inspired by that game.

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun game with great combat.Took me a while to really get hooked but I got really into it at around the 3rd boss.The combat is extremely satisfying once you get a grasp of it and fans of Sekiro will definitely enjoy it.The story is really interesting and there is lots of lore to find.If you care about getting every achievement you should know that there are 2 missable and 2 mutually exclusive ones (one takes about 30min to get while the other requires almost a full playthrough).If you are sensitive to gore or disturbing imagery this is not the game for you and you should listen to the content warning the game shows you at the start (gore doesn't appear outside of bossfight comics and the opening cinematic as far as I remember).The game has a single jumpscare that is pretty easy to avoid if you struggle with stuff like that (appears in the room that loops when you enter it for the first time).Minor criticism:A key part of the combat is only explained once and you are pretty screwed if you didn't get it initially and might have to look up how to use it (or I am just particularly stupid).NPCs also only tell you their sidequests once and then never mention them again until completion.Doing multiple things in a sequence like reading multiple log entries or talking to an NPC and giving them an item can be a little frustrating because you get kicked out of the menu after each individual action.The negative points are just minor gripes I have that you might not care about,  I'd rate the game around a 9/10.

_childDocuments_.review: HIGHLY recommend this game. Definitely one of my favorite games of all time. Everything about this game is exciting, captivating, challenging but digestible, and above all beautiful. If you want a game that similar to Hollow Knight, Blasphemous, Katana Zero, or another platformer with great graphics and an outstanding story that really all just comes together at the end, then this is for you.Incredible art. Hand-drawn everything that makes the game feel intimate and it truly matches the soundtrack, too. Boss fights were always so fun to look at (however stress-inducing the fights were lol) because of the way various attacks were animated/drawn. Amazing soundtrack. Background music, boss fight music, and sound effects were all on point. I especially enjoy the songs for the Lady Ethereal boss fight and the end credits once you've beaten the final boss.Great story. There were a lot of points where I thought there may be plot holes, just for that to not be the case a couple of hours of gameplay later. Everything came together at the end and new developments in the story really just kept me coming back.As I said earlier, challenging but digestible gameplay. If you've played Hollow Knight, for reference, this game is easier than that. However, it's not so easy that it's not worth playing. The number one skill you need to have in this game (aside from parrying which is a HUGE must) is patience. Minions, bosses, parkour challenges, or whatever obstacle you face will require patience to learn the mechanics or the timing or the patterns. Sometimes you may encounter fights that seem impossible for a gamer that doesn't have much time to play games, but trust me when I say that you just have to keep coming back. You WILL get through whatever part you're on. And you're going to want to get through it because of how amazing the rest of the game is. Furthermore, after beating all the optional mini-bosses, finishing all the side quests, and collecting all the treasure, I finished the game in 36 hours which is not terribly long to completely play-through a game.Small, but not really spoiler, spoilers below:There are two endings to this game: Normal and True ending. I completed the true ending in Standard mode and really enjoyed how the story was wrapped up. I'll definitely be playing again (in Story mode which just emphasizes the story more and makes boss fights easier) to collect some of the achievements that I didn't get in the last run and to experience the normal ending. I expect the True ending to be more fulfilling, though.PLAY THIS GAME!!!

_childDocuments_.review: Parry people to death, best sekiro outside of sekiro that I've seen.Granted, there are problems - you have to skip way too many dialogues on subsequent playthroughs.The progression of the Bow arrow types is nonsensical - the first arrow you get deals great damage, travels instantly, pierces through enemies and stuns bosses out of their attacks. Wonderful!Then you get a new arrow type, an exploding arrow that stops at the first enemy it hits and does three explosions. Why would I even want to use it? And then you get another upgrade, a homing arrow that has long travel time and doesn't stun anyone. Again, why would anyone want to use it? The progression should have been the other way around, start with the useless homing arrow, get the great and wonderful Cloud Piercer last because it is the best one.

_childDocuments_.review: To be honest I was not quite sure what I was expecting besides all the chatter of it being a sekiro cross metroid vibe. I must say that I am a few hours in and it has been a wonderful journey. I am playing this title on my Steam Deck (as an fyi) runs perfectly, no issues or hastles so far.Pros:- Incredible artwork style that is really beautiful- Storyline: Fantastic story that keeps revealing more and more of the hidden underbelly and lore behind the Sols and the leaders on this planet. It is not the most super unique story but it is well told and has kept me engrossed to want to see what happens next.-Characters: The characters are fun and memorable. I enjoy coming across new ones with their silly saying and quirkyness that adds to the wonderful artstyle making it feel like I am in an anime. Again it is not ground breaking writing but the characters are charming and sweet. -Gameplay: The gameplay is fun, a lot of fun. Parrying still takes a bit getting used to but as you progress and new abilities are afforded to you it really makes you feel like a badass ninja when the blocking and combos hit just right. The platforming is fun and with the help of a little butterfly/bird thing you are able to open passage ways and entrances that have hidden closed entry ways. So far the platforming has not been too difficult which is fine with me. Some areas can be a little tough but nothing like games like Celeste. Character upggrades are fun and the homebase point of relax and recover before heading out again is fun and interactive as every time you return the NPC's have something more to say and more of the story to divulge making the area more lively and engaging. The bosses have been epic, I have only fought 3 of them but man they were fun. I haven't synced up with the Steam Deck for a day or so, at time of writing I am perhaps 5-6 hours in. I am stoked that there is so much more to still do. It is just such a rare thing to get such a lovely game with a good balance of story, characters and gameplay. I never write reviews but this has been too great to not give kudos to the devs behind this. Will update the review as I progress.

_childDocuments_.review: if you can get past the yapping, and there is a visual novels worth of it, this is one of the best metroidvanias on the platform currently. the developers have created this wonderful aesthetic of bold colors and eastern mythology and religious inspirations leading to a world look affectionately called "Taopunk". combat is extremely fluid. the parry and talisman bombs allows for a push and pull form of combat where you'll take a defensive stance and push your advantage, and the bosses ensure you do not forget that. They are challenging but ultimately not super hard once your in the flow, the only boss i struggled with was due to me not realizing the flow of the fight. once i did, it took only 2 or 3 tries at most. The final boss, without spoilers, is a narratively and mechanically perfect bossfight.the narrative i take nitpicks with. the overarching plot is really good but theres alot of dialogue. unskippable visual novel dialogue. the characters are fun and mostly likable, and the overarching villian of the plot is the perfect example of the protagonist and antagonist having similar views, and horribly opposite solutions for the problem that put them at odds. peak game 10/10 would true ending again (i havent done it yet)

_childDocuments_.review: Starting off this review by saying, if you don't like parry mechanics, or, have difficulties with games that have a notable skill ceiling.  Then this game may not be for you, or I simply recommend playing it in story mode.  Only play standard mode if you want a challenge, and are willing to deal with everything this game wants to throw at you.That aside, Nine Sols is a masterpiece in my own humble opinion.  It is not perfection, but I don't feel that is necessary.  I may be an outlier in this, but I never once encountered a bug or glitch that damaged my enjoyment of the game, and that is so rare with many modern games, that it was refreshing to say the least.  Red Candle clearly put a lot of thought, effort, and love into this game, and it shows with how seamlessly everything works together.  The art is amazing, beautifully combining aesthetics, themes, and presentation in a way that oozes with emotion from the natural areas to the heavy technological ones.  Nothing feels out of place from my personal experience, though I'm sure there are small details I missed.The combat is difficult, probably too difficult for the average player, but once again story mode makes it not feel overbearing.  I personally played through on standard from start to beginning, so my opinion or understanding of the two different modes may be somewhat biased.  However, if you feel up to the challenge, standard mode is very a rewarding payoff to some of the most stylish and nearly seamless combat flow I've experienced.  Overcoming the difficulty curve is much like solving a puzzle, and seeing your effort play out in smooth style that I don't get from many games.  Making a mistake and figuring out how to conquer it feels too good not to emphasis.This game does make heavy use of parry mechanics though, so I can see that dissuading a lot of people from wanting to try the game.  However, if you're willing to put aside that concern, and really give the game a chance, you might find yourself surprised by what there is on offer.  The game has a very notable Hollow Knight feel to it, while retaining its own identity, and trying things from a fresh and solid perspective that just works.  If I could buy it again, I would, and I already plan to gift the game to friends I know would love it.  I normally wouldn't say this, but AAA games have a lot to learn from indie games like this, it's not even comparable.  I'm not one to lightly credit a game as phenomenal, but Nine Sols has earned it with absolute fairness.If you're hesitant about the game, I wouldn't recommend it unless you want to challenge yourself, and are willing to reconsider what mechanics are make or break for you.  If the combat mechanics of the game still bother you, then don't buy.  However if you are willing to step out of that comfort zone, then you might fall in love with Nine Sols the same way I did.Absolutely at the top of my list of top tier games, and fulfills some things I've always wanted out of a game, including some things I didn't know I wanted.

_childDocuments_.review: Nine Sols is a Sekiro-inspired metroidvania set in a tao-punk world developed by Red Candle, and was my most anticipated game of all time. I picked it up immediately after it released and it has since become one of my favorite games of this year due to its fun combat and engaging story, along with a brilliant setting with a unique aesthetic.Visually, the game's presentation is quite unique. The world the game is set in is hand-drawn and digitally animated, with in-game sprites using relatively thin line-art and bold use of colors. Each character is wonderfully drawn and well-realized, with enough detail in the sprites to give an impression of what they are and what role they serve in the universe. The only problem with the visuals is that there are some animations for the enemies that use tweening, and these animations can look quite odd in comparison to the rest of the game's enemies, which use hand-drawn animations, though it's mostly a personal nitpick.The sound design is really good. Attacks are telegraphed quite well thanks to the merging of visual and audio feedback, making the deflection system quite understandable and easy to master. The sound of perfect deflections especially have a meaty bang, making them feel satisfying and powerful.The music of the game is one of the highlights for me. The soundtrack perfectly blends cyberpunk with Taiwanese styling, giving it a unique soundscape. A personal favorite of mine is the song "Last Man Standing" due to it's high energy. Sound and visuals work together to create a unique atmosphere of cyberpunk mixed with Taoist imagery, the very core of what Red Candle calls Tao-punk.The gameplay is quite simple. Most of the gameplay is split between exploration, combat, and platforming. As a metroidvania, Nine Sols is well designed in all three avenues.The exploration is one of the first things Nine Sols gets right. Despite being quite linear, Nine Sols' exploration isn't compromised entirely. Off the beaten path, there are treasures and unique encounters to find, and the game encourages exploration due to its blending of narrative into its gameplay. Whether it be finding artifacts, Jin, or snippets of story, Nine Sols gives reason to explore, and the atmosphere of every environment is brilliant enough to warrant slowing down.One of my main concerns before launch was how the emphasis on combat would hinder the platforming of Nine Sols, but thankfully, the game's platforming isn't entirely compromised. A couple of sections in the game emphasize the platforming, and the game's precise controls make these sections quite fun to traverse, doubly so since a lot of Yi's abilities that he gains are platforming focused.Combat takes center stage, and Yi's combat toolkit is relatively simple. Yi can parry, swing his virtual sword, and shoot different kinds of arrows with the Azure bow. Parrying is quite simple; Yi will extend his arm to deflect an attack. Imprecise parries will give Yi internal damage, which is represented with a red bar and heals over time, or can even heal with precise parries (once the player has sufficient skill points). Precise parries don't damage Yi at all, but are more difficult to pull off. Thankfully the window for parrying is quite forgiving, and parrying rewards Yi with a Qi charge. Qi charges are expended when attaching a talisman to the enemy, encouraging a far more aggressive playstyle, and certain abilities gained improve Yi's combat effectiveness, such as adding in new kinds of parries for specific kinds of attacks.One feature in combat I neglected to mention is the Jade system. Jades act like the charms of Hollow Knight, but each jade is far more balanced in that they have an upside and a trade-off, like increasing the speed of Yi's attack but having Yi also take some internal damage in return, or increasing the health gained from Yi's healing pipes but having the health recover over time and stop when attacked. The Jade system is well-designed, and some Jades even encourage incredibly risky playstyles.The deflection system would've gone stale quickly if the game didn't mix things up as it goes on, and thankfully, Nine Sols has a lot of cool ideas for its gameplay, taking advantage of a slightly more linear structure by having unique setpieces that don't overstay their welcome and are long enough to feel fresh and satisfying. Boss fights in the game act as the climax to a section, and each fight is fun and frantic. The fights heavily emphasize reaction and taking advantage of windows between attacks. They're hard enough that they feel like immense challenges and are incredibly satisfying and rewarding when beaten. More importantly, they never feel stale; they all require Yi to still maneuver around the battlefield, and every death feels like the fault of the player and not the game.Story takes center stage in Nine Sols. The story follows Yi, a Solarian who seeks revenge on the Sols after being betrayed and presumably killed. Yi is found by a child named Shuanshaun, who eventually follows him to an area called the Four Seasons Pavilion, the game's hub area and Yi's resting spot. What makes the story so memorable for me is the characters. Every character has their own motivations and worldviews, and they even have their own journey and growth. Shuanshuan especially has some of the best moments in the game, especially after gifting him some artifacts scattered throughout the game's world. At times, the story gets really dark, so the moments where Yi is gifting to Shuanshuan act as a reprieve and allow time for reflection. It even culminates to one of the most spectacular endings I've had to experience in a video game.Nine Sols is a wonderfully crafted experience that I will no doubt come back to over and over. It had every chance of failure caused by mechanics that could've gone stale, but Nine Sols is effortlessly brilliant in its structure and unique setpieces. The story is beautiful and bleak, a mixture of dark and lightheartedness, and its presentation is unique and appealing. It's a niche experience; the metroidvania genre is its own niche, and games inspired by Sekiro aren't super common. But it's an experience I found enthralling and frenetic, and an unforgettable one at that.

_childDocuments_.review: In a year that has seen nothing but example after example of AAA and publishers despising you as a consumer, leave it to a small indie team to hit a home run so hard it sends the ball intercontinental. This is the new high water mark for this genre, not only is this the best game I've played so far this year, it might flat out be the best game I've played in years; there's no doubt in my mind that it's the best metroidvania game in a long time and I mean no hyperbole when I say that.The music, the instantly iconic art style, the aesthetic, the writing, the world, the combat mechanics, performance, UI, the movement mechanics, the lore, the characters, the flow all of it is just A+ after A+ after A+ to the point where it's kind of unbelievable. Everything flows so well into the next, every area is a new delight for new enemies, new music, new ideas, a chance to learn more and see more. Everything compliments each-other, ideas fit together so seamlessly it's unbelievable this team hasn't ever made a game in this genre.I intend to update this with more thoughts as I get further through it but I might literally die if I don't get out how good this game is, if I can convince one person to buy it, it was worth it, go into it with as little context as possible and let the developers take you on their journey.---After finally completing the True ending my feelings have absolutely not changed, in fact they have grown stronger. The game is a beautiful, touching, satisfying masterwork, and it leaves on a wonderful, haunting note that shakes you after the credits role in the same way a great book does.At no point does the game stop being fun, does the story stop being intriguing, do the characters stop being compelling. The final boss of the true ending is a brutal endurance fight that expects mastery of the combat system to beat, you can see for yourself the discrepancy between the achievements for proof of that, but the note it leaves on is absolutely worth the effort.Nine Sols is easily one of the best games I've played in years, maybe in my life. My only regret is I can't travel back to help kickstart this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I am here for the same reason you likely are; I saw metroidvania, I saw souls-like, I immediately thought of Hollow Knight. As a TL;DR for this massive review: if you're thinking of buying this game to scratch your silksong itch, do it. It's not as good as Hollow Knight, but it's pretty high up there. Though if you do buy it, give it until the fourth Sol before you decide if you want to keep playing. I know you won't be able to refund it, but this game has a very poor start in my opinion that needs time to grow on you.Having just now beaten the game, I can safely say that this game is absolutely worth the $30 price. I was very on the fence seeing an indie game priced that high, but after things kept popping up on the game for me, I finally gave in and paid the full price. I was expecting a much shorter game, or a game that is poorly inflated with excess content, but instead I was blown away by the sheer quality and size of this game. It was rarely too much; the only overwhelming thing for me was the parts of the game where I spend 40 minutes getting through the massive queue of character interactions i had built up. However, this game is NOT for everyone. If you are bad at or dislike parry mechanics, this game is not for you. If you dislike excessively difficult games, this game is not for you. If you don't like taking on the same boss 20 or 30 times before you finally beat it, this game is not for you. If you are someone who absolutely despises games filled with character interactions at every turn, this game might not be for you. It fills a very particular niche, and for people who enjoy all this stuff, it is a genuinely amazing experience that I couldn't recommend more, especially once you master the mechanics. However, if you buy this game, you should absolutely give it a lot more than a few areas before you decide whether or not you want to keep going. The game gets much better as you keep playing, and i only fell in love with it halfway through. With that out of the way, let's get into:Starting off strong, this game's combat is one of the most satisfying and fun combat systems I've ever played. Its much higher complexity makes it so that performing well and proving your mastery of the system becomes far more satisfying than a simple combat system like Hollow Knight. The enemies also complement this system near perfectly, mostly being designed with the system in mind. That may sound like an obvious thing, but it's surprising how many games make enemies that are made without thinking about how they would function with the combat system. Even some enemies in this game feel more like they were simply made and forced into the combat system, but those are few and far between. The way you fly around in late game combat from consecutive parries is incredibly fun and being able to take advantage of a perfect opening to deal massive damage just feels amazing. The shining jewel of this game is easily the boss fights. For clarification, when I say boss, I am referring to any fight with a health bar on the bottom of the screen that is either a sol or has some sort of comic intro or defeat scene. There are very few that I consider bad, and my absolute favorite boss in this game is an experience I will never forget. The fights can be done with such perfect, fluid motions that often when I lose, I am just in awe at how fun the fight really is, I am excited to take it on again just because it was so damn fun and exhilarating to play. I've also often found that people's favorite bosses are incredibly varying, which is a testament to how fun nearly every boss in this game is.The story of this game is honestly pretty good overall, I enjoy getting to learn the answers to a lot of the questions I have about the game, but it is definitely a weaker part of the game. I do love the interactions I get to have with my allies as well, they are often funny and cute, or are a nice progression of that character's story. Lastly, the level design is very good, the theming of the areas feel perfect and I love nearly every gimmick that the areas present me with. I'm not great at analyzing the greatness of level design, so I don't have much to really say beyond this, but trust me when I say it's very well done.To start this section off, I would like to say: Red Candle Games, if you ever make another game like this, please do not ever make a group fight boss again. The two that are in the game currently, being Goumang and Kanghui, are easily the worst fights in the entire game. Goumang is an Ornstein and Smough style duo fight, facing off against an agile and rapidly attacking smaller enemy and a slow but powerful large enemy. However, unlike Ornstein and Smough, the Goumang fight does not pair well with each other. The large enemy often uses wide unblockable attacks that take your priority while the smaller one peppers you during this, aiming to catch you when there is literally nothing you can do, or throwing a projectile at you that feels like it was made to just piss you off in the worst way. It's a shame, because Goumang herself has such an amazing character design for a one-phase fight where she sits and watches you fight the most BS pair of enemies in the game. Kanghui on the other hand just feels fundamentally awful. He sits, stuck in place, summoning a horde of enemies for you to take on where it feels like every enemy is simultaneously the priority, making for a fight where you will deal with ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ constantly changing situations where you can do nothing.With that out of the way, I also will say that this game has one of the weakest starts I've ever seen in an actually good game. It sets up a story, only to end that story within the first 30 minutes or so, then makes you wait around for the first few areas while it sets up its actual story. The combat system at its most basic form also doesn't quite make for the kind of moments that i love this game for, you are just learning the basics. The first boss isn't all that interesting, one of the early minibosses I came across felt like it had insane expectations from a new player like me, the second boss is Goumang, and at that point I was struggling to keep playing. I managed to push through, despite the fourth sol, Jiequan, being a package of everything I hate, and eventually I fell in love with the game while I was fighting him.The story is highly predictable, which took away from a lot of my enjoyment of the story by the end as i could see the twists a mile away. But the gameplay had already snagged me by then, so i was in it to finish the game just for the fun of it. The minibosses are the exact opposite of the main bosses in the game. Some of them can be fun, but by the end of the game they are way harder and way more ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ than the actual bosses, and even some of the early ones put awful expectations on new players. The final one I fought was easily the worst, it felt designed to actively ignore the combat system, throwing attacks at you during attacks, giving you very little time to react, etc.Lastly, the design of the enemies gets a lot worse near the end of the game. Once you beat the 5th sol, it starts to feel like some of the newer enemies are, instead of testing your prowess with the combat system, trying to find ways to ignore the system entirely. Making attacks impossible to react to, demanding focus when you're fighting a enemy that needs that focus, or even throwing in contact damage out of nowhere on an enemy they put in groups. It dampens down the ending sections of the games, but the bosses are just so fun that it keeps me going, plus not all the enemies at this point are that awful.Though despite these bad parts, I think the game is such a fun and even unforgettable experience at certain points that it is well worth experiencing it if you think you'll enjoy its niche.

_childDocuments_.review: Nine Sols is a spectacular platformer game that admittedly took a little bit of time for me to get the hang of, but once you get the hang of timing parries and everything clicks, the combat becomes spectacularly satisfying when dealing with both bosses  and high numbers of low-level enemies. From a narrative standpoint, the protagonist is one of the more compelling ones of gaming, whose journey of vengeance slowly transforms to one of redemption as he forms bonds with the characters around him. From an appearances perspective, the art style is unmatched, reminding me somewhat of Thunder Lotus Studio's Spiritfarer with an Eastern slant, with everything from the characters to the stages exuding both traditional Chinese aesthetics and sleek cyberpunk features. Altogether, I was totally satisfied with this game, and I highly recommend for anyone who's a fan of platformers, unique visual styles and Chinese culture (even with fun Easter eggs of character names that reflect Chinese mythological counterparts). 10/10, no notes. Just don't give up on the first or second bosses and you'll be fineEDIT: Plus boss rush mode added!!!

_childDocuments_.review: Did you like Hollow Knight? Did you ever wish it was brighter, harder and Taopunk? Do you prefer to play as a cat instead of a bug? Did you ever wish that Souls games have two modes, one "Standard" and one "Story"? If your answers were mostly yes, then this game's for you. Nine Sols puts the "Sekiro" in the 2D souls-borne/metroidvania franchise. Your primary defense mechanic is a parry, which also gives you charges to blast foes. Glancing blows are a thing, and will count as mitigated DoT effects. Dodging is your secondary defense mechanic without being rendered useless. Both of these have their own advanced uses when you combine them with other basic mechanics like jumping or other ways of upgrading your character. It's simple as an idea, but it branches out brilliantly. Which brings us to boss fights, which are designed to man-handle you in a manner similar to Sekiro. I won't spoil but they're tough. The first Sol boss is a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ skillcheck in the same way FromSoft skillchecks you with their first boss of each game. After that, the game keeps giving you clear upgrade paths that feel appropriate for each stage of the game you're in. I cannot underscore how smooth progression feels.Hollow Knight has a more interconnected world, while Nine Sols feels more linear; however, I'm feeling that this is intentional. The game drops you to the bottom of the map and then you're climbing upwards, as if you're exploring a tree. Which incidentally is also where your game points as your final destination. At the same time, it builds, with both mandatory and extra areas, on the platforming legacy HK and its spawns have built - but does so with creative twists that make Nine Sols stand tall next to its predescesors.It boasts an obscure but precisely implemented theme which governs story, atmosphere and overall aesthetic: Taopunk. If you haven't played the game, you can't imagine it, but once you get in you'll know exactly what I mean. I wish this theme was explored more often in stories.The story is so far is cohesive, with well-fleshed out characters that feel real, whether they are cats or not. It revolves around the main character's relationship with a little kid... and you know how these stories go. Also, no spoils. The cutscenes are comic-strips which make you think the story could be told in that medium as well if the company really wanted so.Overall, it's staying in my favorites folder. You can nitpick it and find minor flaws, but the overall experience is a 10/10. I wish they give us the option to replay bosses, or even a pantheon feature where we fight extra difficult versions of bosses. If a DLC comes out for this game, it'll need to include this feature. What a fantastic game you put together Red Candle, congratulations. I'm definitely keeping an eye on that company.

The bosses are super well designed and every boss and area feels unique and the game experiments with a lot of different things for each area, which makes the game really fresh to play. I would definitely recommend this game to everyone who find it even a little bit interesting, and for people who have played Hollow Knight.

_childDocuments_.review: If you are a parry-combat fan and enjoy the difficulty of hard, but fair boss fights, then this will be a 10/10 game for you.Combat is crisp and reactive. Every parry or attack connect is backed by strong sound effects. Most of the enemy attacks are well telegraphed both by audio and visual cues. Bosses can be quite challenging (the last one took me about ~2hr to defeat, others ~30m or less) and I got my ass beat many times. Fortunately, on almost all occasions, the game communicated with me clearly what I had ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up and it was easy to find a solution/react faster on my future attempts.Worth nothing that exploration and platforming are well-made, but not the focus of this game. To my surprise, the story was not half-bad and featured some great animated sequences. Both the characters and main theme were well-crafted and managed to deliver a emotional and satisfying conclusion to the plot.As a huge fan of Sekiro, I enjoyed this immensely. Playtime: ~20 hrs for 100%TL;DR - If parrying activates your neurons, buy this ASAP.

_childDocuments_.review: Very early into the game as of writing this, but I can't imagine it gets much better. The game looks cool and flashy, but after a while you realize that's all it has going for it. Combat is extremely simple, with it just being quick time events into holding down the talisman button. You don't really get much options for movement either, so the loop is, use your free invincibility to wait for an easily parry-able move, parry, attach a talisman, repeat. Now, that could be a fine enough loop for combat, but with the game trying a lot on its visual style some moves are simply just harder to parry, and thats even if the hitboxes line up with the moves at all. There are very minimal i-frames if any when hit, so there's been a good few times where because of the layout of the arena or environment, you just get combo'd and die instantly. I want to talk about the exploration and map, but there isn't really much to talk about. Mostly uninteresting layouts and easily noticeable secrets. Maybe i'm just not used to noticing everything yet, but the artstyle and design of the different areas just feels really same-y and bland. semisolid platforms look really similar to regular fully-solid platforms, so you'll just jump is place trying to go through platforms a lot and not be able to flow through areas that well. Overall, the game just feels kinda rough, which is understandable considering my knowledge of the developers, but I can't find myself to recommend this game at the time.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an excellent metroidvania. It's Hollow Knight x Sekiro. The combat is fast, expressive, and very satisfying. The traversal and platforming don't really reinvent much, but they're competently made. The narrative really surprised me with how well written and emotional it was.Honestly, the only real con to this game is the awful map. It's barely functional enough to figure your way around. Most metroidvanias live and die by the map. Red Candle, for some reason, split the full detailed world map into non-detailed chunks. When you view each "area" up close, you get to see the parts of the current area that you've explored, but the transition points between these areas are just arrows with no labels or easy way to see where you're going. There's no way to put your own markers on the map to remember where you need to come back or where you've been. Some parts of the map are these doors that go into back rooms, which don't have any maps, and they also aren't marked in any way when they're "done".The rest of the game is EXCELLENT, and I still recommend it. The entire package, minus the map system, is honestly a masterpiece. I hope Red Candle puts some more work into the map so that people with less patience than me can still enjoy the game.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR game is great at its price if a bit shortI'm really not a fan of parry focused combat systems in general but the rest of the game still managed to keep me around for the full playtime. The story and world building kept me interested from beginning to end. I got more attached to the characters than I expected within such a short time. The environments were beautiful and varied. Animation was stellar. Art was more gruesome than expected from the cover, and better for it. Only real issue I had with the game was the difficulty spike on the final boss. I actually quite liked the fight itself, but why is one boss taking up 4 hours of my playtime on a 29 hour long game. Other bosses took me around 5-30 min with their difficulty seemingly more tied to their lore than their placement in game progression.I also feel if you came to this game straight off the back of Hollow Knight you may find yourself somewhat dissatisfied with the depth of the exploration. There were only a few real puzzles and nothing heavily hidden away to discover. You get basically everything with just your first walk through each zone and some short backtracks when you get a new tool to explore with. I don't personally count this against the game and enjoyed it for what it was, just a comparison I thought of near the end.

_childDocuments_.review: Not a perfect game, but one with lots of heart put into it. If harder games tend to make you rage, I wouldn't recommend, however if you're up for a learning experience, pick this one up! The highlights include obviously the gameplay, and less obviously the story. The gameplay is punishing at first but gradually more satisfying as you go on and fall into the beat of battles. Excluding a singular boss that keeps on spawning mobs over and over, low point of the game for me, every boss fight is incredible! As for the story, I would've never thought I'd grow as attached as I did to this cast, especially Yi and Shuanshuan's relationship, very touching moments! I admitedly haven't played that many metroidvania so it's hard to say how good it is for the genre, especially when it's a much lighter experience on exploration compared to genre staples, but I'll confidently say I had as much fun playing Nine Sols as I did Hollow Knight!

_childDocuments_.review: High highs and low lows. Went in with very high expectations seeing 95%+ score.:Story, characters and world-building are surprisingly interesting. Combat and traversal can feel really satisfying. Finding secrets and optional mini-bosses is fun. Some bosses are very creative and surprising.:Exploration: Pretty quickly levels start feeling samey and not that fun to explore. Loading screens for every single room you enter, for some reason. Backtracking can feel a bit tedious, even later-obtained fast travel forces you to go to the home base first, then to your destination (+2 loading screens). Map is clunky to use.Combat: You take a lot of damage from bosses. It can be frustrating to learn their moves or attack patterns if you die within seconds. Why do you die withing seconds? You can get stun-locked into multiple hits, then into spikes/fire/aoe hazards, and just die if you get hit once (there is a skill that you can unlock later to help with this, but it's pretty mandatory and should be there by default). There are 0 iframes after getting hit, so bosses or enemies in general can one-shot you with multiple damage sources at the same time (bomb clusters for example). Fighting multiple enemies at the same time is definitely not something this combat system was designed for, so it's just frustrating more often than not. Healing is too slow for how fast some bosses move or teleport around the arena imo. Overall just a bunch of small flaws with combat that add up to an unnecessarily frustrating experience.Edit after finishing the game: Many hitboxes are atrocious. Unskippable cutscenes. Bosses get very confused when you stand close to them/behind them. They start jumping and attacking backwards, or just doing a 180 in the middle of attack animations. Unbounded counter is a clunky mechanic. This game demands a lot of precision from you, but doesn't provide much of it in return.:There is plenty to love in this game, but two core things for me, exploration and combat, just had one too many frustrating quirks.

_childDocuments_.review: This game took me by surprise: I didn't expect it, moreover, I didn't know about its existence. How happy I was when I found it! Now, after finishing it, I can finally say that this, gentlemen, is one of the best Metroidvania games I have ever played. To be fair, in my opinion, this game shares first place in the league together with Hollow Knight. I loved it so much—the combat, the mechanics, and especially the story. However, I do think it was a bad decision not to let the player choose between skipping the dialogue and not skipping it.I played the game at 60 FPS on medium settings on my Steam Deck, and believe me, this game was made for this device. It looks wonderful, the controls feel very responsive, and I wouldn't be lying if I said that I craved the very this kind of experience as a kid.My favorite boss is Lady Ethereal. By this point, I had mastered a decent level of the parry mechanic, and it felt like the fight was choreographed—it looked so beautiful. All the bosses are extremely well done, needless to say, but there is a special place in my heart specifically for this Lady. _childDocuments_.review: Incredible game. It's easily a 9/10 for me.Praises:1. The art and soundtrack are AMAZING. Truly nuts how good the atmosphere of this game is. The big tree, the transmutation zone, the dream scapes – these are memorable environments. The boss music is next level. The manga panels during key moments are such a creative touch to the story. I'm really glad that there is a story mode, because I know so many people who I want to recommend this game to based on the aesthetics of it, who aren't into hard games. 2. The combat system is so neat. The game bills itself as Sekiro-like combat, and I understand why they do that, but I think the devs are selling the game short in some of the innovations they have in the parry system. The unbounded counter is a really great evolution of the parry system, and the talisman system is a great and natural way to make parries beneficial without ripping off Sekiro's posture system. Yes, it's clearly inspired in many ways, but it's a very unique system and not just a Sekiro-like.3. The lore of the game is so good. I know people criticize it for lore dumping, and there certainly is a lot of lore dumping through NPC dialog. But the amount of lore that characters drop in endless conversations is only a small fraction of the total lore. There's so much about New Kunlun and Penglai society that is assumed and hiding in plain sight, things that are known to the characters but not to the player, that nobody says and that you have to piece together yourself. The story itself is good, but the standout is of course the worldbuilding. "Taopunk" is not actually how I would describe it. I feel like the Taoist themes are a bit over-marketed relative to what the game actually has. But it absolutely is a unique kind of sci-fi, and a very compelling one.Criticisms:1. The lack of invincibility even 0.01 seconds after taking a hit can lead to some pretty frustrating deaths in mob fights. 2. The jades are mostly not that great. Not nearly as cool as the Hollow Knight charms from which they take inspiration. 3. The lack of a universal fast travel system until the midgame can lead to some dull running around the map, until the midgame when they give you the ability to fast travel between every save point. (Tbf, Hollow Knight never gives you this.)
