_childDocuments_.review: I’m writing this for my fellow weenie hut gamers. My metroidvania loving, Dark Souls hating pals who were drawn to this game because there’s a little kitty in it. A little kitty with a magic, glowy sword and a propensity for tearing the guts out of things. What could be better?! I’ll tell you: a game that doesn’t make you want to stab yourself with said magic sword.That was why, despite falling in love with the character/world design and animations as soon as I saw the trailer for this game, I was skeptical. I’ve gotten better at video games in the past several years. Hollow Knight pushed me to do so. You know what else it pushed me to do? Give up the game for over a year, and put it down for the second time just before the final boss (I like exploring in games, not bashing my head against a wall). I heard this game was hard, and while I could best Ender Lilies, I’m under no delusions that I am a Big Girl Gamer. I love video games, but some of them are just too ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ brutal for me, and I want to have FUN while playing them.Then, by the grace of kitty gamer Jesus, Nine Sols blessed me with a gift: story mode. Story mode that you can switch to whenever you want! I didn’t want use it at first, but knowing that it was an option got me to take the plunge. So I did! I started Nine Sols, and my dodge-loving ass immediately had a hard time with the focus on parrying. But it was fine. The world was beautiful, the story had a strong hook, and I was a fuzzy little guy.I don’t know where exactly I was when I turned on story mode. I know I was being repeatedly stabbed in the face by a robot with a massive sword, but honestly, that describes a lot of my experience with Nine Sols so far. I immediately performed better. I could actually parry, where I was just rushing in with blind desperation before. Not all the time, but it was PROGRESS. I’ve seen a lot of talk about the dropping everything at death mechanic (which unfortunately you can’t turn off) giving people a heightened feeling of tension. Maybe it does, but in my case, it just makes me feel hopeless. That not only isn’t fun, but makes me perform FAR WORSE. If I could have turned the soulslike death mode off, I would have stuck with the original difficulty. As that wasn’t an option, story mode was a great alternative.There was another problem, though. After curb stomping the enemy that had given me so much trouble, I found that story mode was TOO easy. Therein lies the beauty of ~DIFFICULTY CUSTOMIZATION~! In Nine Sols, you can change how much damage you take, and how much damage you do. I set the damage I do back to its original value, and halved the damage I take, which is perfect for me. Fights aren’t a cakewalk, and I still die quite a bit, but I’m HAVING FUN. I’m exploring the beautiful world, seeing the story, kicking ass and having mine kicked in return. You can even bring back items to give to your own pet humans!You can look at other reviews for a more detailed breakdown of what you can expect from this game. The purpose of my review is to let people know that, if you’re drawn to this game, but are put off by the talk of intense difficulty, drowning in a sea of Git Gud, that isn’t the impassable barrier it is in most hardcore games. Red Candle Games has a place for us weenie hut gamers. It’s on a dying planet, full of robots who are ready to stab your face.

_childDocuments_.review: Of all games I have ever played in my 25+ years of living, few have resonated with me as deeply and quickly as Nine Sols has. This game is the best game of 2024 and it's not even close. Everything in this game is perfect, from the beautiful hand-drawn art, to the heartfelt story, to the fantastic fast paced combat.This game has the best combat I have ever seen in a game, feeling akin to games such as Hollow Knight and Dead Cells while taking a more defensive and patient approach to the souls-like metroidvania combat system.The game's story is confusing at first, but slowly begins to make sense over time, revealing a deep and enticing story filled with tragedies, sacrifice, and vengance. Without spoiling too much, the game follows Yi as he takes revenge on his former coworkers in an attempt to stop the project he concieved and helped make from destroying the world.The game's heavy emphasis on parries and counters make it feel unique yet familiar, with the best comparison I can come up with being bosses in Soulsborne games. The abilities are all intuitive and fun to use, with some being simple and common in other games, such as double jump and air dash. while others like the Tai Chi Kick and (spoilers) Unbounded Counter make the aforementioned combat exponentally better and more fun.UPDATESince my initial posting of this review, there have been two things I will quickly mention. first, the true ending brought me to tears. Second, this game has been nominated for several categories in the Steam Game Awards, so I humbly request that if this game interests you, vote for it in at least one category.Overall, this game deserves far more praise than it gets. I truly believe this is one of the best games of all time, and is more than deserving of a 10/10 from me. If you enjoy metroidvanias, this is a must have.

_childDocuments_.review: This is Red Candle's third game, but their first foray into the genre, which makes it even more impressive how realised of a vision Nine Sols is. The combat  is inspired by Sekiro but hardly dwells on it; parrying attacks is not how you defend, but also how you unlock your most powerful attack through the talisman system. The same core idea of parrying instead of i-frame dodging is moved to 2D and developed in a vastly different direction, making for an extremely engaging and reactive combat system.Combine that with an intriguing exploration that gives you quite a few mobility options right out the gate (preventing early game slog) and you get an absolutely essental Metroidvania. The strongest point, however, is the story. The game doesn't try to be obtuse and hide vital information in item descriptions or vague environmental clues; the story DOES open itself more and more as the game goes, but you never feel intentionally left in the dark. There are quite a bit of subplots and themes realised - all done with very few moving parts and just only a several core characters that are well written and more complex than they seem. The only downside is that after a VERY strong opening, the game leads you through two of its perhaps most boring zones with an industrial theme and (comparatively) little character. Thankfully, the following locations really bring out the promised "Taopunk" vibe in full force.It's also worth mentioning that the game has a few difficulty jumps. About 20% of my total playtime is due to attempting the same two bosses. The game is quite demanding at times, so  good reaction time is a must.

_childDocuments_.review: Bosses/player damage are way to overtuned to the point where it does not provide much challenge, but rather just adds unnecessary tedium. I think of those kind of games I liked the Messenger approach the most where you can at least control the tempo of the fight if you played aggressively enough (and in most of games with this kind of battle of attrition fights tbh). Here the tempo of the fight again is so overtuned that you have to go through very long chains of parries and animations until you have a reliable action window. This game is essentially a korean MMO of metroidvanias - high precision, high grind, but very very very very low skill ceiling.This, with the lack of the quick restart button and multiple phases makes the whole fights a "high risk low rewards" case. Am I supposed to grind for levels? Should I search for the tao fruits before facerolling bosses? Is it a megaman style combat where I'm missing something essential that will give me an advantage vs certain boss? Dunno, game puts no effort into explaining what it wants from me (I suppose its just a 'git gut' situation), and I dont want to bother either, I am so so so incredibly bored.Core game is much better outside of the bossfights, but it's not even metroidvania, you can only choose between first two bosses, and the rest of locations and fights are complete in a linear fashion, no optional upgrades, everything is linear and railroaded.Vibes and design: This game is a winner.The rest:Exploration and core play: Hollow knight wins hands downChallenge approach: Blasphemous wins hands downBossfights: Messenger, Hollow Knight, Ender Lilies, pretty much everything wins hands down (I would not even mention Rabi Ribi / TEVI that are like godlike piece of art compared to this: . It's not even such a high bar to pass tbh.Parrying mechanics: Grime wins hands down and the Final Performance boss fight is how I would prefer this kind of boss fights to be implemented:  So like 3/10 I guess?

_childDocuments_.review: "Heroes are forged in Agony" ... I Hardly ever write a review but ... I just fell so in love with this game that I forgot what reality feels like for a few days. The Gameplay is the best part for me as it genuinely explores Taoism and the philosophy of non doing, you can sense this in the fights, if you approach it in like any other beat em up or metroidvania or action game for that matter and simply do combos or button mash, you will get your ass kicked and most probably won't even win against the first boss, the key here is the art of being calm and keen observation and parrying opponents moves are so very well executed that it just clicks whenever you get a perfect parry. If you want to just experience the story and not want to deal with all this, there is an alternative mode as well called the story mode, but if you choose the standard mode, prepare to be ready to parry and be more observant and defensive. All in All, one of the best games I've ever had the pleasure of playing, Thanks to Red Candle. you have found a lifelong patron! and I will be following your works closely and hopefully there are more DLCs or other franchises like this.

_childDocuments_.review: Extraordinary game. Nuanced character writing facilitated by an excellent English localisation, A complex, haunting, and detailed world and story revealed by character conversations and lore from items with interesting designs, a confident, unique and beautiful art style, some of my favourite music in a game ever. Thoughtful exploration of the ways systems and leaders can fail. A morally ambiguous protagonist on a quest for vengeance against antagonists with sympathetic motivations who are nonetheless deeply contemptible.Enemy attacks are well telegraphed, and satisfying to parry. The difficulty is very high, but it feels fair to me. My skills and reflexes are not great, but I've found persistence to be rewarding in learning enemy attack patterns. When I die (which is frequently) it feels like my fault, not the game's. So far (about midway through), the game has consistently added new abilities that keep combat feeling complex and fresh. Changing my strategy with equippables and combat styles has resulted in significantly different gameplay experiences, sometimes providing the edge to get through a particular boss fight I was stuck on. I generally prefer 3d soulslikes over 2d because I find it is difficult to make movement, exploration and combat feel as nuanced in 2d, with only a few exceptions- this game and hollow knight are some of the only 2d soulslikes that feel rich and rewarding in the way fromsoft's games do. Making parry-based combat feel good and responsive is so hard, and it's amazing to me (as with hollow knight) that a fairly small team managed to make it feel so good.Issues I have with the game - There is a story mode, but I do still want a challange, so I wish there were more granular difficulty settings, e.g adjusting the parry window or slightly lengthening the duration the unbounded counter can be held. This is very minor as every time I've gotten stuck, I've been able to eventually move past the bottleneck after learning the boss. Very minor, rare grammar mistakes in the English localisation - this is extremely infrequent and doesn't detract from the overall excellent localisation. Fast travel unlocks late, which is fairly annoying, but fine once you eventually get it. It might have been nice to know early that I would get fast travel later, and I would have put off backtracking. The xp and skill based system is a little weird- I got the maximum number of skill points from killing enemies fairly early, and the remaining skill points can only be obtained through finding special items. Maxing out normal xp in this way feels demotivating, and I wish there was a way to respec, as a particular skill that would be really helpful on the current boss I'm fighting is fully locked off from me- I can't grind for it to help with the fight. Sekiro also had this issue, and solved it by allowing additional xp to be spent on very expensive damage upgrades- something like that would be cool. Linearity - so far the game is pretty linear. This is totally fine, but I wish that when I was stuck on a boss, there was a little more opportunity to go explore somewhere else and get stronger before coming back to it.  Also - I love Shuanshuan. I'd die to protect Shuanshuan. Great job red candle you made a perfect little guy.

_childDocuments_.review: Nine sols is a metroidvania, souls like game.The game is 2d and everything is beautifully hand drawn. I played this game twice; one on standard mode for the true experience, and one in story mode for a more casual experience. Standard mode; it's how the game was meant to be played, you will be put to the test in skill and a lot of trial and error. But when you push through, the game feels very rewarding when doing every thing just right.Story mode: It lets you tweak how you want to play the game, so for anyone who isn't too good at souls like games like myself you can slightly adjust "some" things in the game to enjoy the story and exploration more. Which is very nice.The games main story was incredible, and the side stories to certain characters had a lot going for them as well. Nothing felt unfinished and everything ended with a satisfying conclusion. Also,I will say this too, go for those collectibles as you play, their are some great moments that come up from finding items.The combat in this game is tough, From the bosses to the small enemies, this game will not go easy on you. It's center of focus is to parry your opponents next move to gain an upper hand in the fight. At first, its a little tricky to get right, but man does it feel satisfying when you can pull off a perfect parry and attack. I will also say, the fights in this game are insanely fun and very challenging. Bosses are so unique and bring such a thrill to this game. The music in this game is something i couldn't get enough of, especially certain boss themes; their music went hard at times. The characters; i loved every single one of them. Their stories slowly being unraveled as the game pressed on just left me wanting to know more. It was that good. Nine sols gets a thumbs up from me without a doubt. It deserves its "overwhelming positive" reviews. The game is fantastic. If you like games that have a challenge to them with a good story, definitely pick this one up.

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished my first playthrough on Standard Mode, and I have to say that Nine Sols has quickly become one of my favourite games of the last several years at least. Yes, it's hard, but the difficulty never feels contrived or unnecessary. The deflection-based combat is incredibly satisfying. The main boss fights are fantastic, as you learn to parry, counter, and dodge every attack in a beautiful rhythmic dance. Notably, the final boss does present a HUGE (but completely fair) difficulty spike right at the end of the game. Nothing before it even comes close to the challenge it presents. It took me dozens of attempts over several days to beat it, but I was ultimately successful. I was never bored or overly frustrated during this process, because I could see my progress as every phase got easier over time, as I slowly mastered every move and combo in the boss's arsenal. Finally beating that boss was more satisfying than any other boss I've beat in recent memory. Much like Sekiro, you have to master the game's mechanics to be successful. You can't go respec into a broken build or farm levels. and you will likely max out your power progression well before the final boss. There is a good amount of variety available with the Jade and Spell Style options. There seem to be lots of viable loadouts, so I suggest just going with whatever works for you. Story-wise, I really enjoyed the narrative and truly cared about the characters. You can tell that the developers put a ton of thought and passion into the game's world and narrative. Overall, I have very few complaints and wholeheartedly recommend Nine Sols.

_childDocuments_.review: Nine sols is an amazing metroidvania game with sekiro inspired combat. Everyone who enjoys metroidvanias  should definitely give this a try! _childDocuments_.review: This is an excellent, story driven metroidvania with tight, satisfying, clean combat and a dark and enthralling narrative.Story:The story hits hard at the beginning, continues to wallop you in the middle, and hits hard at the end. Many stories of an otherworldly type have a silent, dumb, naive, or amnesiac protagonist that has little context of what's going on around them, as a mechanism to explain the world to the player. This story has a protagonist with strong personality that is highly knowledgeable of the world around them, which allows for a large amount of mystery and intrigue as they react to the events of the game. You're constantly encountering snippets of information that tell you more about the world while drawing you in by raising more questions. This builds up into a satisfying payoff by the end where pretty much all of your questions are answered in a satisfying way.These snippets come in the form of environmental storytelling, written logs, well written graphic novel style dialogues, dramatic comic strips, and short but beautiful, artistic in-engine sequences. The narrative itself is extremely dark, thought provoking, and grey. It's very much front and centre, supplementing the brilliant gameplay, despite the gameplay being strong enough to do the talking for itself.The moment to moment narrative beats are tied strongly to the game's villains - the nine Sols. These characters are interesting, varied, and strongly characterised. The conditions under which you meet them is highly varied and non-formulaic, while also matching their individual characteristics. Insidious ones may trap you, flippant ones may not even be interested in your activities, etc... The boss fights are thematically appropriate and very cool.Gameplay:The game has hard combat and interesting platforming. It mixes tight parry-timing based melee combat with interesting traversal mechanics. It has a story mode for people who struggle more with this type of combat and want an easier experience. The combat feels punchy, elegant, and fluid. There's quite a lot of enemy variety and environmental hazards / constraints that keep it fresh throughout the game. There are a lot of set pieces such as getting locked in and assaulted, doing difficult platforming while under continuous sniper fire, having to be stealthy, or carrying out intricate platforming where the world around you is continuously phasing in and out of reality XDThe core combat is simple to learn and difficult to master, with a grindable, XP based progression system that enhances your core abilities and damage, exploration based upgrades that enhance your health, healing, and crowd control special abilities, and exploration based items of which you can only equip a few at a time that modify your abilities - like the charms from Hollow Knight.There's a lot of story and gameplay incentive to explore the world. The world is also filled with shortcuts that you can unlock after pretty much every major piece of platforming, which avoids frustration. There's also a fast travel system that slowly unlocks for you which is a great quality of life feature.Every zone is thematically unique, often rich in highly disturbing environmental story telling, and characterised by unique platforming or combat mechanics that always feel appropriate to the environment and Sol - such as traps, snipers, lava flows that must be avoided, respawning enemies, disappearing floors, etc...The bosses are hard, varied, and make you feel like a master of the game once you're on your 15th attempt and are dancing around their nuanced attack patterns like a boss. There's no ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ in the boss fights. They're very well balanced such that there is always a pattern or sequence of moves you can do to dish out damage while avoiding taking any, though actually doing so requires looking for the pattern and engaging with the game mechanics. They're also not as difficult as equivalent bosses in a game like Sekiro, which strongly inspires the combat style as the developers state.Overall:A very stylish, thoughtful, and enthralling game where I always wanted to learn more about the narrative and was perfectly happy to chop through thousands of dudes with my hands to do so. Would absolutely recommend to metroidvania fans, fans of good story in general and sci-fi in particular, people who liked Hollow Knight, people who are interested in east Asian culture (the Taiwanese developer used Taiwanese and Chinese artistic cues for the visuals, audio, music, and theming rather than western references leading to a very unique style for a game of this high a production value), and to souls-like enjoyers looking for their next challenge.

_childDocuments_.review: While your first impression of this game might be that it's a metroidvania it doesn't really suffer from the common occurrences like getting lost or not knowing where to go, or having to backtrack once you get more movement powers.The parry system is fun and done in a way that I think is more accessible to people that might not be used to playing timing centric games. A delayed/late parry will cause some internal/temporary damage to your character while a perfect parry will block all of the damage for example, so even if you're unfamiliar with an enemy or boss you can still make it through on imperfect parries alone. The game also offers a fair bit of customization with how you play and approach the combat with items you find and skills you can unlock.One of my biggest gripes with the game was fixed in a later patch, so if you're reading this review now you won't need to suffer through not having a detailed map before finding the areas chip as that is now unlocked from the start.

_childDocuments_.review: Good game.The bosses are easily the highlight of this. Regular combat is fine, but more strategically interesting than action-interesting. But the bosses, man. You'll go into one and die in five seconds, and the second time you'll survive six. But the thirtieth time you'll perfect-parry every attack like that scene from The Matrix and when you reach phase 2 you'll realise you're still at full health. That's a feeling nothing can compare to. One of the bosses, after beating, I was yelling at his corpse to get up and give me a phase 3. They're good fights!The setting/story is the other big draw. At the start it's just edgy which is fun in its own way, but it gets very emotionally deep as it goes on. And not just in word-dumps, the game pulls off a few tricks to make you grow to love the mascot kid just as much as the main character does. Well enough that it's my favourite hub area in any game I've played.I won't deny — with some of the bosses, after thirty deaths you might need something to keep you going, and that's when the game's aesthetics really deliver. The screenshots should make it clear the game looks pretty good to begin with, but the animations, designs, and the perfect-parry sound effect really keep things good. Especially the last one — much of the game's style is focused in your own actions. Parrying attacks, the cool-guys-don't-look-at-explosions talisman (which is your main source of damage!), the time-slow when you pull out your bow... everything's optimised for style, in a way that doesn't get old. You'll keep doing things because they feel cool to do, and that translates to having fun with the game.Plus there's a great end-credits song, which is always free points.Of course this isn't just a boss rush with story. It's a metroidvania. The exploring parts are... good. They're good! Unfortunately that's all they are, a 7/10 as opposed to the 9-10 of the previous points. You won't grow bored doing them, and the movement upgrades tick the boxes. But you'll rarely get excited finding something tucked away, the area unlocks are pretty linear and you don't get the fun of peeking into an area you can't visit yet, and there's nowhere that ever requires much of your platforming skills. The area gimmicks are good at least. This part doesn't detract from the game, but it's not why you'd play it.Negative points: not many, the game is a polished product. Lightning round: loading screens are too common, it's annoying you can't fast-travel between nodes and have to hop back to your hub then go back out, the mapping system has too many intermediate steps, can be easy to lose track of where you're supposed to go especially in the earlygame, a couple of bosses are easier and only took a few tries when I wish they'd take more. And no boss rush, seriously weird oversight. Let's hope for it coming in an update.All in all this is my current GOTY candidate for the year. And not because it lacks competition.

_childDocuments_.review: An absolutely amazing experience. Playing style-wise, it is Ori/Hollow Knight+ Sekiro, but this is not to eclipse its originality of the art and combat design, storytelling, and world-building: Unique style of 2D hand-drawn arts, challenging but fun combat with the offer of different styles of fighting, portraying an intriguing world infused  with futurism and Taoism elements, and an absolutely beautiful storytelling which brought tears to my eyes. My only negative comment was about the map and quest navigation in the game as I felt lost a couple of times during the game. Even if the quasi-open-world experiencing is what it is aiming for, if there is a place or a log that shows all the past conversations with NPCs so that I can check what are the hints that I have missed, that would be great. _childDocuments_.review: Nine Sols has the best combat out of any metroidvania I've played, and is comparable to Hollow Knight in terms of being one of the best metroidvanias I've played period. The characters are great, the artstyle is beautiful, and everything feels snappy and responsive.It's also really, really, really hard. As in "I just finished Elden Ring and the minibosses in the first few areas of Nine Sols are harder than most of the bosses in that game" hard. The game demands incredibly quick reactions and good pattern recognition from the first area, and appears to only get more difficult from there. Fighting two enemies at once is difficult, and any more than two is generally instant death. Even if you love parrying in games (I do!) you're going to get your ♥♥♥♥ pushed in more than once.If you love metroidvanias you'll probably love this game, but you have to know what you're getting into. No shame in turning the difficulty down.

_childDocuments_.review: 4.5 hours flew by before I realized it. Once you feel like you've got a handle on the combat, they throw in a new mechanic that freshens it up. They've got their own unique combat style that intensifies as the fight goes on. If that scares you, then the story mode is an alternative that's less demanding. The music is enjoyable, story captivating, and searching for secrets is rewarding. Also you start off with a grappling hook. So, I'd recommend.edit: I just finished the game. I only have one critique, but I would still recommend the game. My issue is the boss fight design. It seems like the first boss and the last boss are the hardest experience, and all the others are less demanding and fluff.         I ended up giving up and doing story mode for the last boss because the rest of the game doesn't prepare you for it. _childDocuments_.review: A tense, brutal challenge that manages to avoid ever feeling too "unfair" or "rage-inducing" (if you come at it with a patient mindset, that is).  The world is gorgeous, mysterious and a treasure to explore, although there is less returning to earlier areas for progression than I expected for a Metroidvania--plenty of chances to do that for optional content, though, so it balances out. The skill tree and jade system are both good (if unoriginal) ideas, but the former often feels too number-crunchy and niche while a number of jades feel useless. Perhaps they could have been folded into one system keeping the best of both? Either way, this is one of my favorites of the year so far, and I am absolutely gonna be playing it again and going for the True Ending soon.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a relatively good metroidvania, so I wish I could recommend it as I had it on my wishlist since the earliest demo. But, the below combat notes were annoying enough that it made me really not enjoy playing the last third of it, finishing it just to put it down.- Double Jump comes really late in my opinion, but this isn't that big of a deal- The red move counter feels terrible in my opinion. As a hold for 1 second and release mechanic, you're constantly worried about holding it long enough if a red attack comes at you quickly. Something like "attack with parry held down" would feel way better as you know the move is going off, not guessing right before a devastating attack would hit you if you held it long enough or not. - Enemy attack animations where a sword or claw ends slightly behind them registers for a fraction of a second post-attack as if you're walking into the pointy end for fun if you get too close behind them after their attack. - Dodging through enemies doesn't always work, especially on bosses, if you're more than a pixel away. I'm guessing it calculates if you would move more than halfway through their hitbox, and bosses just have bigger hitboxes or something. - Enemies can ready a swing, and even if you dodge through right before the attack, they'll spin 180 instantly when unleashing it. If they spun after the first attack of a chain, I'd get it, but getting hit by the first move by trying to dodge through them is very annoying. - If there are tiny iframes when hit, I can't tell. I've gotten insta comboed by small enemies and bosses alike, especially if there are lasers I get knocked back into like the theater duo boss.

_childDocuments_.review: I really really wanted to like this game but no matter how much I throw myself at it hoping it’ll click I can't help but find myself getting increasingly aggravated by just kind of annoying game design that does nothing but punish the player for being bad at the game. I'm more than fine dying in an encounter a 100 times over because I'm still bad at the game, I'm fine with that because I want to get better and beat that encounter, what I'm not fine with is every time I die having to walk back through sometimes several screens worth of enemies and traps just to get back to the point where I died. Not only does this just kill any drive I have to play and kill any momentum I had because of it I'm constantly at risk of losing jin and money slowing me down even more. There's a lot of other little things I personally really didn't like whether it's the game taking close to ten hours to give me a fast travel, lots of enemies feeling like sponges, the map having next to no useful markers, lots of little pointless cutscenes or the lack of I frames when hit for a lot of attacks that should really have them but the short of it is I just really didn't enjoy this game unfortunately which really ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ sucks because the game has some absolutely beautiful art and the lore and story seemed super interesting. in all honesty it's another game I wish I could leave an “in the middle” review for because I can tell there's a fantastic game under these issues I have I just personally couldn't get past those issues. _childDocuments_.review: One of the best metroidvania I've played in years. Now before you buy this keep in mind that the combat in this game is not like hollow knight or messenger or most metroidvania. The combat relies HEAVILY on the parry system so if you're not a fan of sekiro or lies of P refrain from buying this. Parry is your best friend and dodging is the friend that you talk to once in a while. One of my favourite aspect about this game is that the bosses fights are immaculate. The music is kinda nice too.Long live apemen.
_childDocuments_.name: Nine Sols

_childDocuments_.review: Most fun I've had with a metroidvania since Hollow Knight. The main gimmick Nine Sols have that elevates it from its contemporaries is the parry-centric combat. There are two types of parry ala Sekiro, if you time your parry perfectly, you take no damage, if you slightly mistimed it, you'll take some recoverable damage, though you can't die from imperfect parry. Both types of parrying give a resource called Qi, which is where things get fun. You can use Qi to dash forward and put a bomb on your opponents that explodes after a short delay, and if you have the right upgrade you can hold down the Qi button to do even more damage. The experience of perfectly parrying every single enemy's attacks, dashing past them, and then walking away while they get blown to bits is pure dopamine, no matter how many times you do it. Aside from this, the game is also incredibly well animated and has a pretty unique aesthetic that combines cyberpunk with traditional Taoist symbolism, aptly named Taopunk. Nine Sols' weakest point is probably the metroidvania elements. The game is fairly linear despite how interconnected each zone is, and while the zones themselves are good, there aren't a lot of them. Rewards for exploration kind of suck too, early and midgame it’s mostly just cash, with all the good upgrades being back loaded into the last half. It should go without saying that the combat more than makes up for these deficits, however.
_childDocuments_.name: Nine Sols

_childDocuments_.review: Overall a really great metroidvania, the combat is amazing and the parry system works well. It is very story focused but the story is good, but the endings were a bit of a let down. All the main bosses were really unique and fun to fight. The side characters were great and each area felt distinct. The artstyle is top notch and the same goes for the soundtrack. I loved the home area and how it changed throughout the game.Enemy variety was kind of lacking, there's like ten enemy types with minor variations of them. There were a few bosses that were definitely way harder than the rest of the game especially the final boss. Probably my biggest gripe with the game is that you can only parry the direction you are looking unless you are in the air, this made some attacks feel really cheap and I didn't even realize this was a mechanic until the end of the game. I thought some hitboxes were broken but it was because of this mechanic that I thought that.It's definitely up there with the greatest metroidvanias but with a few minor issues8.7/10
_childDocuments_.name: Nine Sols

_childDocuments_.review: I am delighted to give Nine Sols my strongest possible recommendation to anyone. As a fan of Sekiro and Hollow Knight, Nine Sols so perfectly takes inspiration from both of those to make a truly wonderful game. I have not yet completed the story as of writing this, but being the majority of the way through I feel now is as good a time as any to leave a review. All of the boss fights (to this point) are uniquely challenging and memorable, the OST and art design are absolutely gorgeous, and the combat is so buttery smooth. The parry mechanic is the bread and butter of this game, and you will be punished over and over again until you've mastered it. The parry mechanic is more forgiving than Lies of P, but only slightly more punishing than Sekiro via the internal damage mechanic (temporary damage taken from missing a parry, but can be recovered by perfect parrying, unlike NG Lies of P). This game perfectly fits the needs of both the Hollow Knight and Sekiro communities who are in desperate need of a sequel.
_childDocuments_.name: Nine Sols

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game. I don't understand the bad reviews suggesting that the combat is unpolished and wonky when it is clearly not true. I have never felt cheaped out by the game. Almost every death I took was deserved. Some of those boss fights are among the most satisfying, coming from this genre, even more so than hollow knights. The exploration feels satisfying while having great level design in general. Now, the only nitpick I have with it is that for the most part it's pretty linear. I personally enjoy that more than looking around the same areas for hours trying to find the way to go. Hollow knight in comparison had a way more complex and incredible map layout while also having multiple ways to play the game. While Nine Sols lacks a bit in that sense it makes up heavily for it with its combat and also its story. Music  is amazing too, everyone loves that in a video game.Also, the Old boy homage was the highlight for me! I had a big grin the whole way through, haha!Played on standard mode. Finished the game at about 85%.
_childDocuments_.name: Nine Sols

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a fan of 2D indie games like Hollow Knight, Dead Cells, and other Metroidvania's, but also like Souls-like games, this is for you. Very block/timing focused, very challenging. Combat is very satisfying, upgrades come in at a good pace and game never slows down enough to get dull. Music is great. Story is dark, interesting, and has a good mystery that still hasn't fully shown itself 13 hours in so far, looking forward to completing this. Also runs perfectly on the Steam Deck.Only complaint is that UI elements occasionally fail to communicate exactly where you need to be going. Many times I backtracked or wandered around the map aimlessly. Not sure if it's things that are lost in translation, but some sort of log with objectives would help a ton with this game. Make sure to keep an eye out for the '!' on the map, always check for those.
_childDocuments_.name: Nine Sols

_childDocuments_.review: Came here from the beautiful artstyle and interesting setting, stayed for the amazing gameplay, characters, and compelling story.This is my 2nd Metroidvania that I've ever played, and it's outstanding on all levels. It became one of my favorite indie games of all time and one of the best games I've played in 2024.The combat is fast-paced, smooth, and satisfying to master. Every ability that the game gives you is viable in any way in terms of exploration and combat. Some of the jades can be hit and miss in terms of viability, but it allows for room for experimentation with how you want to build your character.The bosses are very well designed in terms of visuals, mechanics, and personality/lore. The story, without any spoilers, is really good, and the pacing is well laid out. It kept me hooked from the beginning to the end.I know that the difficulty can be really hard sometimes, but if you look for openings for attacks, utilize your abilities, and practice the parry mechanic, you can overcome it! If you're really having a hard time, there is a story mode difficulty in which you can adjust the amount of damage you want to deal or how much damage resistance you want on yourself. I highly recommend this game, if you are a huge fan of metroidvanias/games that are challenging but yet satisfying to beat (similar to FromSoft's games and Hollow Knight) or just everyone who wants to try something new!Side Note: As of this right now RCG is now added Boss Replay/Boss Rush game mode and ported the game to consoles and added to XBOX PC Game Pass lineup. I highly recommend to all of the console or game pass people out there to try this game!

_childDocuments_.review: I just played four hours of this metroidvania game.I am very impressed!It seemed obvious from the very beginning that the game would be able to deliver quality graphics in a hand drawn style, which it absolutely does. Very early in the game, expectations of a traditional metroidvania story setup are subverted by unexpected plot twists, leading into quite captivating world building and story content that is good for the genre. Then it turns out that the gameplay is pretty great. The combat system is a soulslike system with great rewards for people willing to learn the parry system, but you can get by with ambushing, brute forcing, dodging, and applying special skills in various situations as well. I do not parry in the Dark Souls games and never loved Sekiro due to the focus on unforgivingly difficult parrying, but I tend to parry in this game due to good telegraphing of enemy attacks and good balancing of the risks and rewards of parrying. Exploration has been open ended and often quite tense in the best possible way, due to sparse placement of respawning points, in a way that reminded me of the original Demon's Souls.The only problem with the game I could point to is an interface issue that should be fixable. When browsing shop lists, the information shown for the selected item inexplicably lags behind when you move up or down the list, for no good reason. The game is not verified for Steam Deck, but works great on my Steam Deck OLED, although I could easily increase the sub HD default resolution to 72op while maintaining a perfectly solid frame rate.I am looking forward to making serious progress in the game during our national holiday in Sweden in one more day, but I can already easily recommend the game for fans of the metroidvania genre.

_childDocuments_.review: Nine Sols is an amazing game that leaves an impression that few games can. The story will draw you in emotionally and keep you hooked all the way to the end like a wild roller coaster. I sometimes struggle to find game lore interesting, but Nine Sols is a major exception. Nine Sols weaves story and lore together in a way that compels the player to seek information not immediately presented to them and the knowledge gained each time feels rewarding. The payoff of this combination is a high-stakes tale in a world that feels like it lives and breathes right in front of you.The gameplay can be demanding and requires developing some careful coordination and muscle memory, but will never present unreasonable challenges. The moments when you do start to understand an enemy's attack patterns and overcome those challenges is highly rewarding. You will feel like you can suddenly see and understand the numbers in The Matrix tear your foes down. 10/10 without a doubt and I am hungry for more.

_childDocuments_.review: Post 100% Edit: It's a rough slow burn, but its a nice gem. Post Ending Edit: The ending boss require you to have a really damaging build, preferrably all skills unlocked and most of the charms collected, because if you won't - you'll be stuck with whatever you have on you. Expect to get really bruised if you try to push yourself in this game, despite looking like Hollow Knight and wearing Sekiro inspiration on its sleeves it does not reserve itself to give you the breather room or options to deal with the enemies. ➕ Cute character designs➕ Really swift gameplay and story introduction➕ Interesting Blocking late parry trade system akin to Street Fighter chip damage style➕ Varied gameplay set pieces and enemy encounters🟣 There is not much room to actually enjoy its difficulty, its hard. It's not mechanically difficult but gameplay limiting difficult, you are tight on money, tight on XP and resources and you don't really have that many options when approaching enemies🟣 Despite being crowdfunded and having a 2+ years of development it lacks a bit of polish here and there, some animations feel unfinished (Edit: some animations got patched actually), some item descriptions need better translations and some cutscenes could really use a Skip or Cancel option (e.g. the Hacking sequences are not cancellable nor safe to use, it could really use some of that Cancel button magic).🟣 No beastiary or lore codex for its world. No quest logs ☹️🟣 The story is serviceable, but a bit rushed with its reveals.➖ A lot of the enemies feel like concrete slabs compared to your damage output, even if you follow the game's way of [Parry - Place Charge on the Enemy - Explode it], it will take a while to kill enemies. The player damage scaling crawls really really slow, and some bosses having Two or Three phases (some bosses can regenerate health indefinitely!) and one hit kill strings just make you feel miserable. First 2-3 hours of this game is pure torture, the game really pushes you to your knees before providing you story based upgrades (e.g. a Charged Attack or an Airdash).➖ Despite touting sekiro mechanics, i am not aware if there's a way to attack enemies poise. Your parry attacks won't stun enemies nor deplete their poise. The only way to stun enemies is to either break their shield with a charge attack or with a Remote Charge (by wearing a certain Talisman/Charm). I dont think the devs should have pushed their game marketing into Sekiro territory.➖ Most of the Skills and Talismans (The Charm system) are reduntant and don't really offer any difference to the gameplay style, most of them provide your character with some stat boosts for a really high price usage requirement and nothing much else.If you are not a fan of High Risk - Low Reward hard games, then your best bet to enjoy this game is to either cheese it by farming gold and XP to buy upgrades or to employ cheap safe tactics of dealing damage. Trying to take risk through the game by using dash i-frames or constantly parrying enemy attacks is not worth it - majority of the enemies and bosses have long attack patterns, regenerating health, lack of stun stagger windows, multiple phases and third party environment assisting their bloodlust towards you, don't push your nerves.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best metroidvanias ever made. Almost every encounter and boss was difficult, but fair and forgiving. Nine Sols didn't just borrow Sekiro's combat, but also Sekiro's design philosophy; every boss seemed like an impossible mountain to overcome, but the grueling process of learning the patterns led to near-flawless victories at the end. There is only one playstyle, with upgrades to different aspects here and there. The game demands mastery of it. You simply have to get good. What really surprised me was the quality of the story and storytelling. Much like Sekiro, the story is about the end of age and those who'd cling to it, wrapped not in Buddhism but in Taoism, something I knew nothing about before the game. Thankfully it explains everything you need to know without hiding necessary in text logs or item descriptions. The protagonist is flawed, fleshed out, and his character arc is great enough to drive the story. I was engaged the whole way through his revenge-plot-turned-redemption, tying into the Tao and the nature of self-improvement. How one can achieve immortality through selflessness and the love of those to remember us by.Hollow Knight weeps to be honest.
_childDocuments_.name: Nine Sols

_childDocuments_.review: Like I'm sure a lot of people did, I came to this game looking for a metroidvania fix while I waited for Silksong to come out. Initially, I was coming to the game looking for an experience similar to Hollow Knight. There are two similarities: the metroidvania map exploration format, and the fact that you're playing as someone shorter than everyone else. If you're looking for a game to compare it to, you'd find a comfortable comparison in Sekiro, but a slightly more apt likening might be Lies of P. Both have mechanics centered around deflecting attacks in tempo with your enemies, but Lies of P allows for weaving dodging more easily into the mix. Similarly, Nine Sols challenges you to navigate your own way through the patterns of enemy attacks. Establish your own rhythms, find what works for you. There's a lot of different approaches to every enemy and boss, so one can really feel free to develop a combat style within the combat style the game sets out with. The game is extremely well paced. Exploration is the key to increasing your power, as long as I adequately looked around I never felt the need to grind at any point during my play through. Each new area, like any good metroidvania, forces you to learn new tricks and develop your skillset to meet new challenges. Each area feels different, even if there are some repeated enemy designs. For me, the primary highlight comes from the bosses. The bosses in this game are AMAZING. It may take a few attempts, but once everything clicks from their moveset to the range of their attacks every fight begins to feel like a dance. There's this amazing flow and impact each attack has, I just can't quite put into words how good the boss fights in this game feel. Some are better than others of course, but none really stuck out to me as bad. I loved the experience this game provided. The music, the atmosphere, the story, I really had a fantastic time. I came looking for something to tide me over until Silksong came out, and I ended up finding one of my new favorite games.

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic Metroidvania for people that like good, difficult combat. While the music, art, and especially setting are wonderfully polished and unique, the story is good, and there is solid platforming and collectibles... the combat is the real selling point. If you loved Sekiro this game is pretty much a 2D version of it, with its own unique mechanics, but ultimately a heavy focus on timed parries and taking advantage of openings. Heavily Hollow Knight inspired (like most modern Metroidvanias), but it brings enough unique ideas and polish to the table that I can honestly say I hold it in the same high regard.Be warned the game is fairly difficult and there is a noticeable difficulty spike, especially for the final boss, but it isn't done in a frustrating way, and certainly feels rewarding to complete.

_childDocuments_.review: First time I've ever wanted to review a game, writing a few hours after letting the ending sink in. This was actually the first metroidvania I've sat down and completed in it's entirety (and will be going for 100% achievements soon). A phenomenal game start to finish, the combat mechanics and platforming do more than enough to make the experience enjoyable for the entire playthrough, it left me wanting to go back and start another playthrough immediately! The game is fairly difficult (the final boss especially), but if you can deal with a bit of trial and error in true metroidvania/soulslike fashion, then you'll enjoy the experience. I only have a few minor things I want to see added to the game. While I'd love dlc to get more out of this game and it's world, the base game is amazing as is and doesn't *need* anything added to it, as the gameplay and story are very well fleshed out. All I think it really needs to be perfect to me, is the ability to reload to certain story checkpoints to rematch specific bosses or complete quests/achievements you may have missed or messed up, and a boss rush mode to refight these amazing bosses easier (which they have shown interest in adding a boss rush mode after their focus on porting is done from what I've heard!)The atmosphere is extremely unique and beautiful, and the soundtrack was amazing (instantly added multiple songs to my personal spotify video game ost playlist). You can feel how much heart and soul the devs and artists involved in this game's creation put into it. Cannot recommend this gorgeous work of art enough. 100% recommend, easily one of my new favorite games of all time!

_childDocuments_.review: This is an excellent piece of art, with some really fun ideas and good world building / story telling, that I think is ultimately flawed by some questionable design decisions that might be from it being the devs first metroidvania / action game.The art, soundtrack, lore, and responsiveness are all top notch. Exploration is mostly fun, although even when fast travel is fully unlocked it's a little annoying (you have to teleport twice essentially). A lot of the boss fights are quite well done, and most of the enemies are interesting and distinct, with only a few rooms where the encounter design is seemingly intentionally annoying (requiring a specific technique or thing to cheese it safely).All that said, the game has a weird amount of "autoscroller" style time gates. From literal ones (where if you die, you have to redo the whole thing), to more figurative ones which are much more frequent. Boss fights in the later 1/3 of the game are especially guilty of this. Bosses turn into HP sponges, with 2-3 health bars and a new phase for each, and after 1 or 2 attempts you're probably clearing the first health bar with no notable drain on resources, which means it just turns into a time sink. That's because the dangerous attacks are unique to phase 2 (or more often, 3) and often require VERY specific timings or things to counter them, which you have to learn through trial and error, and I very rarely lost because I was out of health potions but more often because you just get chain attacked from failing to figure out how to counter one giant attack into another random dangerous attack. The later bosses also have a tendency to have 2 or 3 moves which have very different reactions required, but have similar (or identical) tells, which means you have to react during the second part of the windup animation. Again, these are often incredibly dangerous attacks that even with the max health for the time, can lead to you dying before you have a window to heal. Invulnerability frames from getting hit do exist but it's a fraction of a second. Unfortunately the final boss is the worst of them all - they do not react to a number of your tools the way all previous bosses have, the parry timings are intentionally all over the place, and several of the attacks require a very exact sequence of actions by you to survive. The boss also has a preposterous amount of HP given how few attack windows you have, and given you can't create windows with this boss like you can with some of the previous ones.If you struggle with the standard difficulty, I strongly recommend changing it to story mode - reducing incoming damage a little can help you learn the boss fights significantly faster, and boosting your own damage can mitigate a lot of the wasted time in the first 1-2 phases of the fights. And the game as a whole is worth it. But the default difficulty is significantly harder than Sekiro for a good chunk of the game, and actually harder than anything I can remember trying this hard with. Most boss fights do not have a cheese, like many harder Soulslikes, they have things you HAVE to do just to survive - there is no easy way out. I hope they make another metroidvania, and I hope they use this experience to refine it. The autoscrollery feeling in a lot of the later parts of the game (where you just have to go at the speed the game says, no exception) along with multiple multi-stage boss fights with unique, life-ending new attacks at every step, feel like they could be removed and replaced with something more interesting (more fights instead of super long, trial-and-error ones, for one thing). But the game gives you the tools (in the difficulty settings) to power through and experience the game, so it still gets a recommend for me.

_childDocuments_.review: Holy, this game is crazy good. _childDocuments_.review: Nine Sols could have delivered a gripping, combat-driven adventure, but it gets bogged down in relentless, clunky storytelling that interrupts gameplay at every turn. From the very start, you’re forced through a tedious opening ceremony where “gameplay” consists of holding a direction key—only to then watch a cutscene. This sets the tone for the experience, with lengthy, poorly translated dialogue between uninteresting characters making it impossible to get into any real flow. And if I’m forced to read it, I’m going to judge it. Verdict? It’s bad and far too verbose, bafflingly considered a “highlight” by some.Once you finally get to the combat, there’s potential here, albeit marred by limited feedback. You’ve got a basic three-hit combo, where only the third strike really counts in terms of damage, forcing you to time attacks carefully as enemies won't flinch. Parrying and exploding talismans add some nice layers, and as you progress, additional abilities make combat slightly deeper and introduce new ways to counter enemies. But just as combat starts to feel engaging, the game pumps the brakes to throw more dialogue at you. In the end, the few moments of decent gameplay aren’t enough to make up for the interruptions that spoil the experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolute peak. Love this game. It gave me an unforgettable experience. But I want to mention some great and not sides of the game. Pros:1) very aesthetic and interesting visual design. Cyberpunk themes with Chinese painting style are making unique combination. Personally, I love this choice. It may not suit for everyone, but if you love this, your eyes will be pleased.2) soundtrack and sound design are great. Tracks are suit for the situations, some tracks are so memorable, that I listened them separately.3) very challenging combat. You have a large arsenal of abilities, that give you a lot of choices in battle. Especially it shines on bosses. Different styles are valid, you can play only with parries or make you build only with charged attacks. Also, absence of invincibility creates more intense combat. You can just get off after getting a hit, you need to react to other attacks. Sometimes it creates very butthurt situations, but overall I prefer that choice more.4) narrative is also great. Personally, it was heartbreaking at times and I really cared for the characters. Their dynamics are trustful and interesting.Cons:1) metroidvania aspect of the game is decent, but sometimes it creates not very pleasing situations. In the beginning, when you not have teleport between nodes yet. If you find a node, you can teleport through to the main hub. After, you can teleport only to that specific node, from which you almost traveled to your main hub. Personally, I didn't have that much problem, but for some people it can be not okay. Also, game is pretty linear, idk, mission system could be more suitable for that type of game. Exploring metroidvania world can be more pleasing to hear than just run through missions, but the second option could allow replaying it with different play styles. In metroidvania, if you finished a boss, you can try another playstyle on it only on the second play through. Devs said, that they are working on boss rush now, so this problem is going to be solved.2) i very much love the combat, but it still has some flaws. Absence of invincibility frames really create more intense combat, but sometimes you can find yourself in a situation, where you get hit by one enemy, immediately get hit by another and fall into damageable area and just die. After practice those situations will be minimal, but for some people it can be very annoying. On bosses can be similar, but mostly on first tries, where you don't know all boss attacks and can get several hits in a row and just die. With that being sad, if you what some challenge, it will be not that problem for you. All that I said can be fixed with your skill, so don't find that much of a problem3) bosses are hard and it is good. But if you want to play more aggressive, you need to practice more with bosses, and it may cause more tries. idk, there is some contradiction in game, where you have very aggressive and proactive abilities to play with, but bosses will punish you for using them pretty hard. Personally, I was missing some more room to play proactive. And you still can do it in this game, but it is much harder, than just play reactively. With that being sad, i absolutely recommend this game if you look for an intense combat game with aesthetically pleasing visual and great narrative. If you play sekiro, you may also love this game as well. All that problems, that I found in this game, are minor and not that fundamental.

_childDocuments_.review: An amazing game that deserves far more attention than it got.Nine Sols has by far the most satisfying combat system I've experienced in a 2D platformer, with a rather flexible parry system that doesn't strictly railroad you into a single play style. It's always a joy to perfectly parry every single hit of an enemy's combo, then proceeds to slap a talisman on them and watch as they explodes with your back turned against them.Boss fights are also fantastic, each having a unique flavor to their designs and gimmick which makes them exhilarating to learn. while not being so difficult to demand complete mastery of the mechanics to an exhausting degree , ensuring that the average player doesn't get brick-walled by a particular encounter for too long.The story is also really enjoyable with a very compelling protagonist in Yi, who is a breathe of fresh air compared to its contemporaries in a similar genre, who are either silent blank slates or lack any distinct personality. While not a chatterbox himself, Yi is a character with a clear agenda and pre-established relationships who is also capable of surprising cruelty. His core motivations is a mystery and progressing the game is as much as uncovering more about the lore as it is to learning more about him as a character and his role in the whole thing. Watching him develop as he bonds with the resident neanderthal,  boosting his max Health by getting drunk, listening to messages from his sister, are all facets that adds to Yi as a character.The titular Nine Sols who serves as the game's main bosses also have fleshed out personalities, backstories and goals, misguided as they may be, that adds more layers to the narrative and helps makes them distinct from one another. More than just one-note bosses, they're characters who opposes Yi for their own reasons.Overall, a must-play for anyone who likes games. It's not too long (took me 24 in-game hours) to overstay its welcome and not too difficult . It has a compelling narrative and some of the best combat system in a 2D platformer.

_childDocuments_.review: Story mode reviewDo not let anyone tell you playing this on story mode is too easy. If you get enjoyment out of certain settings that the developers put in the game so more people could enjoy it then that's money well spent.The story mode setting makes this game a lot more accessible. Selecting this difficulty allows you to adjust two multipliers in the pause menu under gameplay. Damage dealt and injury. Both of these have a very wide range. You can deal more damage ranging from 100% to 1000% and you can take less damage ranging from 1% to 100%. So you can make this game as hard or as easy as you want which is a brilliant idea for a game like this. You can pause the game at any time and change these settings on the fly and tune them until you get it just right. Also worth noting that if you start the game on standard mode you can switch to story mode at any moment and unlock these settings. But you can not switch back to standard mode if playing on story mode.As for the game itself? It's excellent. Combat is fast and satisfying. Exploration feels rewarding, traversing the map is fun and the controls are great. The art style is lovely, the dialogue is well written and the characters are interesting with some great designs. Character upgrades are also paced very well. Every time I got something new it felt right and kept me interested. Always looking forward to the next skill or movement upgrade.This is easily my favorite Metroidvania since Hollow Knight and one of my favorite games of 2024. I've taken down 4 main bosses so far and I can't wait to continue. If you're interested in this game but feel like the combat style is a little intimidating I encourage you to give it a shot on story mode and make the appropriate adjustments until it works for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Rock solid metroidvania with a great combat system. It feels like a hybrid of Sekiro and Hollow Knight, but with much more of an emphasis on combat over exploration than Hollow Knight. The game has an absolutely gorgeous art style and slick animations. Story is pretty solid. Only real criticism of it is that there is far too much expository dialogue that gets dumped on you at times. The map has relatively varied and interesting biomes. This game doesn't require a whole lot of backtracking although the lack of fast travel until the halfway point is annoying (I thought we evolved past that after Dark Souls did). Side quests in this game are also interesting and the characters are worth interacting with to learn more about them and the lore of world. The pacing of the game is a bit...odd. The beginning few hours are brutal while trying to learn the game and get used to the parry mechanics. Then, the middle of the game almost feels too easy while the late game feels like a significant difficulty spike. It would've been nice for a more linear growth to the challenge. Also too, this game has a point of no return that is obvious and the game hard saves before you cross it so you can reload your save after finishing the game to clean up quests and etc. That's something more games need.The combat system is excellent...mostly. It heavily borrows from Sekiro in it's parry-centric combat and it feels great to pull off subsequent perfect parries. And, it's not too punishing for slightly mistiming the parries. However, the one thing that to me feels like a design oversight is the lack of recovery frames upon being hit by enemies. If you get hit, then not only do you flinch or get thrown backwards at times, but you also can repeatedly get hit by bosses. This isn't very noticeable until you hit the later game bosses where the difficulty and enemy damage output has significantly ramped up. I can't tell you how many times I got juggled to death like I was playing Tekken online. For me personally, recovery frames are borderline mandatory for these types of games so it's disappointing that they are absent here. It doesn't ruin the experience by any means, but it adds unnecessary frustration and the lack of them feels like a massive oversight.Bosses are a standout in this game. Excellent designs, interesting move-sets, and beautiful scores. The later game bosses are on par and even exceed some Sekiro bosses in terms of challenge and balance. This game nails the feeling of a dance between the player and a boss. If you love that, then this is a must play. My ONLY criticism is this game LOVES multi-phase, multi-health bar bosses, and I have never been a huge fan of that. This game tries to have each phase teach you different things about the boss and build upon each other, but going through already mastered phases (and health bars) to learn the next phase adds a level of tedium to otherwise excellent fights. This is especially apparent with the three phase final boss for the true ending. It's a great fight, but it's a slog getting through the first two phases every single time and the boss itself is  overtuned (grapple does too much damage, some wonky hitboxes, borderline insta-kill, juggle combos, and a third phase that doesn't add enough to justify it's existence IMO). Overall, this is a really good game, but it is VERY challenging so if you're not one who enjoys the git gud process then I would steer clear.

_childDocuments_.review: Finished on normal ending, though I've seen the majority of the game's content.To get right into it: if you're absolutely starving for more in the vein of Hollow Knight, this game stacks right up to it and sometimes even exceeds it.If Hollow Knight is metroidvania Dark Souls, Nine Sols is metroidvania Sekiro. It's more than just a surface-level comparison; the combat mechanics, aesthetic theming, and boss design clearly takes a massive amount of influence from that game. Where Sekiro has a large focus on Buddhist imagery and ideas, Nine Sols incorporates Taoism to the same degree.The setting and background story of Nine Sols is phenomenal, I love its fusion of spiritualism and technology. While the Flash-like animations of characters might be off-putting, it's outweighed by how stunningly gorgeous the environments are. I especially love the areas where Red Candle shows off their expertise in disturbing horror imagery.With the occasional exception of annoying encounters with a lot of enemies, overall the combat and boss fight design in this game is top-notch. The various parry abilities all look and feel incredibly cool when you pull them off. The main nine bosses, especially in the second half, are tough as nails and don't leave any room for cheesing or shortcuts. You need to learn their mechanics to succeed, but it feels ultra satisfying every time you nail the execution on them.The soundtrack is an eclectic mix of traditional eastern music and electronica. On the whole it's good, and occasionally you get some really stellar standout tracks for the boss fights.The world is a joy to move around in and explore, but it's often a little more linear than Hollow Knight. Less Super Metroid, more Metroid Fusion. I didn't mind since it's paced out so well, I had a hard time putting it down on account of how much fun I was having with the level design.What a story, too. It's a smart blend of the broad strokes operating in massive scales, while the majority of time is spent with the small but well-written cast of characters. The friendlies in your hub are all really charming, and the way each boss has their backstory teased out is really engrossing. Big kudos to the translation work here, it all reads totally naturally for the English version.While the last few hours can be a bit of a slog, otherwise this is easily a contender for the top games of 2024. Red Candle, despite their horror background, have confidently nailed the souls-y metroidvania style with style and grace. If you're into this genre, I cannot recommend Nine Sols enough.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely gorgeous and brilliant. The combat is SUPER fluid and satisfying, the upgrades are paced out nicely, and the story is insane. I personally love the blend of bright and vibrant and colorful, and dark and gory and grotesque. The difficulty ramps up a lot through the game as you learn new techniques, but never feels impossible (except for the final boss, who is SO GOOD). It's always just challenging you a bit more and requiring you to implement the new moves you just learned into your repertoire. It really does scratch that Hollow Knight itch, while also doing its own thing. I do wish there were more platforming challenges, there was one point where I thought I was required to do some pretty difficult platforming and was proud when I'd finally done it, but found out later I'd accidentally broke sequence and the area opens up much more easily later. But I personally would've loved a little bit more difficult platforming. Past that, I really can't complain about the game. If you enjoyed Hollow Knight, Ori, or even Sekiro, give this game a try. Also this is the company that had their game removed from Steam due to their Winnie the Pooh reference, so they deserve ALL our love.

_childDocuments_.review: I've seen a lot of people comparing this to Hollow Knight, and while I see where they're coming from, I ultimately disagree. With obvious exception of the jade system being similar to HK's charm system, Nine Sols is a distinct take on the Soulslike-inspired Metroidvania.For starters, the actual Metroidvania part of the mix is downplayed. While it does have the expected progression of "obtain new abilities to unlock paths in previous areas", most of this game's abilities are handed to you along the main path rather than being something you have to actively seek out. Likewise, exploration has less focus here. There's generally only one or two areas to visit at any given time, and you often get direction about where to go next. Though this is typically just a general idea of which region to visit rather then a waypoint. I found the amount of freedom fine, but some bigger exploration fans might not enjoy it.There's also the fact of the story of having much bigger focus than in other MVs. I found it somewhat refreshing that the protagonist Yi has a distinct personality and dialogue, as well as established relationships with other characters. Rather than being vague monsters with maybe some cryptic lore, all the bosses have strong characterisation and backstories too. I was also surprised how much I enjoyed the relationship between Yi and Shuanshuan, the child Yi takes care of. That kind of thing could've been trite but I found it compelling here, particularly with touches like having Shuanshuan's drawings show up around the home base as you form a bond.Of course, there's still a strong Soulslike influence in the combat. I'm generally not a fan of the corpse run mechanic, but it's pretty inoffensive here. The levels are designed in a way where you're constantly opening shortcuts, so you can usually get back to where you died easily. Even with a couple big losses from failing to make it back, I had more than enough money/XP to get everything by the end. The boss difficulty was tuned a little high for my liking, with many taking dozens of attempts. There's a high level of trial and error: combat is less about reflexes, and more about learning the exact parry timings for each attack. That said, it is very satisying when you master each attack to pull off a victory, and I ultimately did enjoy fighting my way through the challenges Nine Sols presents.

_childDocuments_.review: By far the best Metroidvania I've played in a very long time and absolutely deserves more attention!! This is my first time ever writing a steam review for anything just to get this game's score up and hopefully encourage more people to give it a chance, that's just how much of a good time i had with it.The story as well as the gameplay start out a little difficult to get into (especially if you, like me, have little experience with parry-based combat) but once they finally click in your head they really click! the combat becomes so much more fun and dynamic once you allow yourself the time and patience to absorb it, which is a very good testament to games which reward pure player skill and dedication rather than meandering fluff. It's one of the very few games i ever felt the desire to 100% and exploring its little secrets and bonuses never felt like a chore but rather a natural part of the experience that i was fully engaged with.Coming back to the story, while it admittedly starts out a little confusing and i'd get lost at some points it does feel very satisfying to see your questions answered and earlier bits eventually pay off by the end, developing Yi and Shuanshuan's relationship specially was a nice way to get the player invested in these characters even when you know so little about them at first, so once everything's tied together by the end the conclusion to Yi's character arc really pays off.The visuals are absolutely breathtaking and as a side note i wish this game had come with a downloadable art book along with the deluxe bundle, i'd absolutely be willing to support it further...Overall it's a massive recommend and while i understand parry-based mechanics aren't for everyone, and it's certainly a difficult game, i hope more people are able to look past their preconceptions and are able to give it a chance :)

_childDocuments_.review: I went into this game having decently high expectations given what I had seen of it and today, after having beaten it, I think it's one of my favorite games now. Which is saying a lot considering how many games I've played. I don't know if I'll write an entire essay on why this game is so incredible, what I will say is something which surprised me a lot; pretty much every aspect of this game, to me, was either good or better, nothing about it frustrated me. It takes a lot of effort and knowledge to be able to pull that off, especially with something that took me a little me almost 40 hours to beat. The art and story are what really drew me in, and then stuff like the combat is so fun, I don't know how they did it. What I do know is now I can't rest until I get everyone I know to play this. Some stuff I used to consider being some of my favorite games looks dim in the brilliance of Nine Sols. The game is good. Play it.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't know... Steam really needs neutral rating.This would be a good game for me if not all of the frustrating mechanisms, which honestly feel more like Dark Souls cargo cult instead of something which is actually well thought.Where's the fun in unavoidable stunlocks in some cases?Where's the fun in having to backtrack half a map to a boss?Where's the fun in barring essential game mechanics behind unlocks early on, which is especially punishing towards new players? (swift rise)Where's the fun in random encounters where game requires you to perform two mutually exclusive actions at once? (fengs, unbounded counter + two parries at once)Where's the fun in having all these health/damage upgrades if any boss can two-shot you regardless of how much you get, and you generally don't get back to fighting early enemies?But probably the biggest gripe is that boss fights are unwinnable without dying first to learn their attack patterns. By itself it is not bad, except that the game has all the bosses have multiple phases, which means that every time something unpredictable happens in phase2, to learn it you just need to repeat phase1 over and over again.I am quite sure that the game would be sub-10hrs of content if not for these artifical time drainers, and that's really a shame, because story is great, combat flow is great by itself, visuals and music are top notch, and overall feel and responsiveness is just pure joy? EDIT: whatever, after finishing the game, I decided it is a bit better than it is bad, so overall worth it. There are definitely lows and highs in the experience, and overall most of the lows are in earlier parts of the game where player is barred from some essential mechanics. Later when full kit is available it is way more enjoyable.
