_childDocuments_.review: "South of the Circle," set against the mid-Cold War era of 1958-1964, opens with a plane crash that foreshadows a fate already scripted. The game boasts a top-tier narrative, though its gameplay—limited to choices that ultimately don't alter the story—may divide opinion, resembling more a cinematic experience than a traditional game. To me, a game can be a vessel for storytelling, and in this light, "South of the Circle" shines brilliantly.The narrative unfolds through the protagonist's memories, which, like anyone's, are fallible and colored by personal values. The recurring interrogation scenes with the professor highlight this, as the protagonist repeatedly revisits his past, grappling with whether he stood up for Clara out of conviction or if it’s a reflection of his regret over betrayals.The player's choices seem inconsequential, underscoring the theme of individual helplessness against the sweep of historical currents. "South of the Circle" poignantly explores the inescapable societal forces that shape our inner shadows, silently steering our thoughts and actions. The predetermined ending, symbolizes the inescapable pull of the era, casting us onto the jagged rocks of tragedy and pain, revealing the subtle societal influences that quietly mold our identity and choices.
_childDocuments_.name: South of the Circle

_childDocuments_.review: The game plays out like a Film with time lapse of the present and past revealing parts of the story being told. You play as Peter, a shy/timid man who is a professor at Cambridge University. He is stuck in Antarctica trying to find rescue. as you try to find rescue you keep having flashbacks of Peter's life when he was at the university. Which led him to meet Clara. she's brave but also dismayed. The flashbacks story unfolds with Peter trying to write a paper for the university.(which isn't going well) Also the cold war is starting to kick off with protests of nuclear disarmament, possible threats from Russia. while at the same time discovering love. The gameplay is simple: you walk around and you click on objects to interact with this is also how you select the optional dialog. although you have optional dialog like offer games, These don't change the outcome of the story. But it doesn't take away from the feeling of being invested in the characters. And that comes down to the writing of the characters and the dialogue that goes on with them. There is a sense of realism and life in the different characters. which is really accomplished by the voice acting. The graphic design is very well blended with shapes, colors and shadows. The soundtrack is very much in tune with the mood of the story. all of this works very well together. to make a solid game. Now the biggest downside to this game is how the ending unfolds. Which I can't cover without containing spoilers.
_childDocuments_.name: South of the Circle

_childDocuments_.review: A love story against the backdrop of nuclear non-proliferation/disarmament? Hi, yes, it's me.Ok, so maybe this game is a bit of an easy sell for me, but South of the Circle is a beautifully stylized story-rich interactive novel. I say novel because it is less of a game and more a QTE narration of the love story between the two main characters during the Cold War. If you think the game looks pretty and the premise/storyline looks interesting, and you don't mind a more laidback experience, then this is a fabulous title to pick up. If you're looking for something heavily action-oriented, you will likely be disappointed. My only complaints about the game are that the QTEs don't seem to have a huge (any?) impact on the end of the game (though they do affect the immediate dialogue) and occasionally the camera angle veers into an awkward spot (though this normally only lasts a few seconds). The game took ~3 hours to finish and an extra hour to grab the two achievements I missed on my first playthrough.
_childDocuments_.name: South of the Circle

_childDocuments_.review: The game's pretty story-oriented. For the pricing the game is pretty good in terms of story, audio, and graphics but the ending was kind of lackluster. This game is more of a movie than a game even with the minor interactions and "choices" you get. It'd take you at least 3 hours to finish it. I'd say give it a try if you're into story games, if not then don't bother.
_childDocuments_.name: South of the Circle

_childDocuments_.review: This game has interesting thematic elements. The sound design is excellent. I even like the minimalist style. But it's irredeemably clunky in the way it switches from story element to story element. I hate being forced to control a character for 30 seconds with only one possible progression option. I'd rather watch a movie which is liable to be edited better or work in C story and other narrative elements. I can see people, especially narrative crafters, enjoying it as a study, but the lack of traditional gameplay is glaring.
_childDocuments_.name: South of the Circle

_childDocuments_.review: : 3/5South of the Circle is a charming and well-told narrative experience rather than actually interactive game.: 4/5While I had some reservations about how the player interacts in the story, it was solid and definitely an order of magnitude more interesting than usual video game narratives. The characters are well thought out and the plot is interesting, using the back drop of the cold war to tell a character drama and mystery through the eyes of completely normal people. I really liked how the story touched me several times, especially by the end, when the conflict welled up between the main character's past and present.The pacing is too slow however, and an hour could definitely have been cut off while preserving the intended narrative.: 1/5 There is little gameplay to be found at all here, and what there is is rather just an excuse for the story to be sold on the Steam storefront instead of shown on a video site. It also felt very much like that the few decisions the player makes have little impact on the narrative, though they do change how some characters react to each other - this was at least satisfying to some degree. Sometimes it was impossible to tell what the characters were gonna say with the choices presented, and I would sometimes feel angry that the main character tells a completely different line than I intended when selecting a 'feeling'.: 5/5The game has a beautiful coherent artstyle, and a soundtrack of very high quality, hitting the precise notes to enhance the story at any moment. My only shortcomings with the presentation is a large number of instances where characters clip uncomely through the terrain and objects, and the faces of the characters were, while loyal to the artstyle, a bit too faint and don't convey emotions very well.
_childDocuments_.name: South of the Circle

_childDocuments_.review: The cinematic work put into this game is masterful. Everyone involved with the voice acting, writing, music, and visuals did a stellar job, and all of there were blended in such a way that they all shine rivaling blockbuster movies, but playing to the strengths of a narrative experience. My advice would be to set aside four hours to play the game three of which will be playing the last will be just sitting there after.
_childDocuments_.name: South of the Circle

_childDocuments_.review: Rating: 6/10South of the Circle is a journey that pulls you in from the get-go, thanks to its captivating story and breathtaking soundtrack. The voice acting adds layers of depth to the characters, making you truly feel immersed in the experience. But as the tale unfolds, you can't help but feel a twinge of disappointment. The story, while intriguing, ultimately feels like it's missing something, leaving you wishing for more meaningful choices and a more satisfying conclusion. The narrative's cinematic qualities and stellar soundtrack make it seem like it would have flourished on the big screen, but alas, this is the only medium it can be experienced in. Still, there's no denying the unique charm of the game. It's flawed, yes, but it's also undeniably captivating. If you're willing to overlook its shortcomings, there's a lot to love here.
_childDocuments_.name: South of the Circle

_childDocuments_.review: I loved the visual style of the game and the "behind the scenes" design prototypes. But the game itself was more of a frustrating experience. No matter how you act, the outcome is the same and the story develops very slowly through constant jumps into memories. The most annoying element is probably the slow and clumsy movement, especially since you don't have any option to explore the environment and just need to keep pushing the button to move from point A to point B.I hope the developers will create a game in this visual style with a more interactive gameplay and more "open", explorable world. This one has a creative potential, but falls short as a game and as a visual novel.
_childDocuments_.name: South of the Circle

_childDocuments_.review: Classy, classy, classy.If you are bored with the shallowness of mainstream games this is the game for you.Powerful baggage of different kinds of emotions. Minimalistic yet stunning visuals. Beautiful music. Great performance by the actors doing the voices. If this was a movie, in the years when cinema mattered, Oscar-quality.
_childDocuments_.name: South of the Circle

_childDocuments_.review: I wasn't sure what to expect when I bought this game, but I've been pleasantly surprised.The writing, dialogue, and voice acting are all excellent. The art style reminds me of an old cartoon strip with a modern twist, which is really appealing. The only thing that slightly bothers me is the eyes—they're a bit too undefined and could use some color. They come across as a little creepy, though that might just be my personal preference.The writing, settings, and dialogue fit the era perfectly. It took me a minute to get the hang of the dialogue choices, but once I did, it felt intuitive. The vehicle controls, however, are a bit of a nightmare. If you've driven the Mako in Mass Effect 1, you'll know what I mean—it's like that, but worse.I haven't finished the game yet, but I'm really enjoying it. If you're looking for a relaxing day with a good story in an interactive novel format, this game is both engaging and calming to play.
_childDocuments_.name: South of the Circle

_childDocuments_.review: South of the Circle is actually a very intriguing and absorbing game, I didn't expect that.The developers were clearly inspired by "Firewatch" and "What Remains of Edith Finch" and for some reason I thought this game would be like Firewatch but in Antarctica. I forgot the trailers promising us a story about relationships and careers, set in 1960's cold-war Britain. The voice acting is great and the story is well-written. It was like actually watching a movie!Yes this Interactive Fiction is a typical walking simulator with minimal player agency but it is far from a simple FMV.Your choices do matter, but only in the context of the relationship.This is not a multiple-choice game with branching paths and endings, come on now.It all serves to immerse you and to deliver a gut punch in the ending.It is a beautiful game, the minimalist art style was competently used to give us an inoffensive 3D picture and convey the story well.Even the snowy regions did not flashbang blind me with all that white, unlike other games (like planet Hoth in SWTOR).This game is asking you to feel through it, asks what you would do.Stand by your convictions and principles or sooner or later break down after being chipped away at by friends, society and culture.I was steadfast in my beliefs and morals, yet the ending shows that it is not about us and this is not how the story went.Peter and Clara's relationship was beautiful to observe.If you did not understand the ending, it might feel like female schizophrenic gas-lighting. Short and beautiful game, with a bit confusing and cannibalizing liberal/feminist message about the cold-war 1960s.
_childDocuments_.name: South of the Circle

_childDocuments_.review: Everything about this game was beautiful. Magnificent. Gorgeous. Spectacular. Nobody half-assed a single element in this game. Everything from the music, the voice acting, graphics, scene transitions, pacing and plot, there was passion behind this. I can't believe I haven't heard of this game any sooner. The gameplay is similar to telltale, however that's not an actual issue. It doesn't let you choose which line to say, rather what emotion that comes out of you. At first it was hard to understand, but the more I was talking, the more I understood what each symbol meant. And even if you choose something different than someone else, everything just flows perfectly. ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ fa-nominal job everyone did.Pros- Music makes a scene 10x better when used correctly, and in no instance was music misused at all. Even the changes in music, either mid scene or transitioning, was a joy to hearVoice acting- top tier in my opinion. It felt real with the breathing and the breaks the voice actors took.Camera- In no scene did the camera feel out of place. For example, in the plane when the Russian and Floyd are talking, the focus is on them since Peter is sleeping. It's those little details that makes something so powerful yet surreal at the same timeSetting- Every set wasn't fully detailed like an arkham game for example, but it didn't need to be. From the snowy mountains to a city in the UK, it didn't need a whole bunch of details in the first place.Cons-I can't really say anything bad about the game. I mean 2 things that bugged me was the movement and the decision making.The movement I had to jerk a bit but it wasn't to the point where it was annoyingAnd the decision making. Again I liked that it wasn't sentences, however it did stump me here and there. But to get around that, just look at the timing and see when one option comes into play so quickly versus when another one does 1-2 seconds later.Overall: ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ play this game if you want a rich story. I nearly shed at the middle. Fantastic job 11 Bit Studios. Fantastic job.
_childDocuments_.name: South of the Circle

_childDocuments_.review: A fairly decent story for a game and the art style is nice but there is no game in this. All of your choices in conversation seem inconsequential and the few times you get to move in the world there is literally a single path to follow. It might as well have been a TV series. The character movement through the landscape is, although clearly motion captured, occasionally shonky with limbs passing through objects. This could have been a stylish chose-your-own adventure but sadly its a single linear story that is slowed down by waiting for a button press after every sentence. Very disappointing.
_childDocuments_.name: South of the Circle

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, we all know what this is and what to expect: This is an animated movie where you occasionally click on the screen so you feel a bit more connected to the narrative. Call it "walking sim", call it "narrative experience" - whatever.I like to play these games occasionally, there are some interesting settings games like these explore and if you take them for what they are (=narrative experiences) they can be quite charming. The problem with this one is the ending. I don't mind downer endings (hi there, "Know by Heart") , I don't mind bitter sweet endings, I don't mind ambiguous endings (hello there, Pathologic) but this one is just muddled. In the last 2 minutes the narration pulls the rug from under you and tries to explain the twist in a sentence or two plus it leaves the rest completely unresolved. I loved the narration, the presentation, the music and the story but those last 2 minutes really left a sour taste, not because it did not give me what I wanted but because it felt so rushed, muddled and overall unfulfilling. If you want to experience a game that does the narration part better, try "Know by Heart" by Icepick Lodge. Any devs who want to dabble in this genre: A clean execution on well trodden paths is better than trying to risk everything for some narrative cleverness to make your work "stand out".
_childDocuments_.name: South of the Circle

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, I know it sounds unhinged, but you don't play this game for the gameplay, that is pretty basic and unremarkable. You click and hold circles, and you move around, don't get it if you don't like narrative games. This is a game you play for its story, and it's definitely worth it. You're following the same character in two different times in his life, alternating between scenes almost seamlessly. The different timelines have very different moods and settings and you don't have time to get "tired" of it before you switch to the other. They do join at the end too. Visuals are good, great voice acting, nice music, can be completed in about 3-4 hours with all achievements too. Yes, the ending is a bit odd, but if you give it some thought, it makes sense. Anyway, worth it!
_childDocuments_.name: South of the Circle

_childDocuments_.review: Finally found a new one! Kind of calm, mature, narrative game with fascinating story and extremely well voice acting. Genuinely I don't care anymore whether the story branches out to 10 different endings based on my choices. If not, well.. I still enjoy the ride and feel engaged deciding for the character. 'South of the Circle'  was a gem for me after playing mediocre games for so long.
_childDocuments_.name: South of the Circle

_childDocuments_.review: Promising start but ultimately underwhelming. It was a nice concept, and I kept playing to see how the story panned out. The interaction is a bare minimum which is great if you just want to focus on the story. 6.5-7 out of 10. Recommend with reservations.The story in itself is quite simple, a bit predictable but certainly emotional. It could have really gone places but felt like it only scratched the surface of the characters and their relationships. And then all the choices you make don't seem to matter at all. Then at the end you are suddenly thrown an unreliable narrator twist which could have added a lot of depth and become a bigger feature in the game, but instead it just funnels everything back to the story the creator wanted to tell.    So the choices I made did not matter and it turns out the character behaved differently to the character path I thought I was shaping. And it crumbles down right at the end. Ultimately an unsatisfying way to finish the story, and quite rushed. Which was a shame because there was a lot of potential and a really nice concept but just never really delivered and then took over the story at the end so all your character choices meant nothing. Technically a few gliches throughout the playthrough. File verification/validation helped some. Other times character got stuck on a screen with no camera movement or any place to go - just pointless clicking everywhere. Quitting and reloading reset it and it progressed fine and presented a different path so no idea what happened.
_childDocuments_.name: South of the Circle

_childDocuments_.review: Another outstanding game from State of Play. They're out here again with an amazing presentation for their games. I knew that they could do visuals and animations well having played Lume and Lumino City, they're previous games. But here the acting just elevates the presentation and story to just incredible levels. The combination of the voice acting, body language, and what little facial animation there is just works. It worked so well.Speaking of the story, it's absolutely lovely. It just sits with me and how it ended. At first I was puzzled and a little frustrated by the open nature of the ending. But after reflecting on it and basically spoiling myself online with the other choices, I think I love it. I liked that it dealt with themes of memory, love, and suspicion. And all of that was told well by the great pacing, dialogue, and actor performances. I really love how well this game told it's story.A few quick positive notes. I like the choice system they made here. The story itself is fairly linear. There is only one plot. But you can influence the moments in between by choosing the emotion of the lead. Doing that just adds a nice personal touch to the story telling and changes up some of the emotional impact of the scene. Another fun note is that the soundtrack is beautiful. Glad it's in my library now.Overall, I love this game. And I hope for more storytelling like this in more games.EDIT: I forgot to add that there is an e-book of the game's script as DLC for this. Provides a nice bit of context to that ending and the story as a whole
_childDocuments_.name: South of the Circle

_childDocuments_.review: No matter what you want, no matter how good you choose to be. Like real life, it does not matter. In the end you just experience on reality or at least what reality remembers about you. To accept your choices or at least the things you thought you chose.Is this a good game? I don't know. Like plenty of other reviewers said already, you don't have a choice, it's already chosen. The story already happened and it tells you a story on how it is. Not on how you thought your character remembered it.
_childDocuments_.name: South of the Circle

_childDocuments_.review: The game is very story rich and emotional, to bad none of your choices matter, whatever you pick will be made into a set path that was met with a VERY dissapointing end. Do not buy if you like a "choice matters game" it felt kinda like getting an amazing looking cake, then discover its just filled entirely with cornflakes on the inside once you got towards the end...
_childDocuments_.name: South of the Circle

_childDocuments_.review: It's a visual novel with 2-3 options in dialogues, choices do not matter, regardless of decisive or unconfident answer the dialogue only varies in 1-2 lines and eventually, it leads to the same ending. I don't take it as an interaction game, the ending gives hope but still fogged, the idea is more clear.Playing this game reminds me of A Lion's Song by Mi'pu'mi Games and the Movie The Theory of Everything. All present a period in the last century in which women are looked down even in institutions of higher education. Their talent is not appreciated or respected and their names are to be removed if a report wants to be published or taken properly. What hits me is the man in the game actually insists on keeping the girl's name as a co-author, regardless of all the opposite voices, knowing he might lose in the effort he has put in the past 3 years. However at a certain point the girl said I thought you were different from other men and they broke up. Misunderstanding or fact, this game talks about unfair treatment of a woman  like (1) the girl gets the chance for higher education and care from her father only because his brother died in an accident (2) women get higher education but people only care how fast they type (3) once they get pregnant they might lose job. There's been progress in women's rights over the past decade but still much to be done.Player is constantly jumping between time, the places remind the same but you'll meet different times and people. Come to think about it after beating the game, it might be the guilt, or the regret the man kept in mind when he's desperate and in the last few hours. The ending is interesting as it seems all are tricked by their own country, all about politics and it is never clean. If you look today it's still the same. It's an okay game, can be slow sometimes, not much highlights but alright for the time and price.
_childDocuments_.name: South of the Circle

_childDocuments_.review: This game could very well have been significantly shorter, but that's my only grief with it. It's beautiful, well written, the voice acting is awesome, the animations are super cool, the music hooks you and the whole thing is incredibly polished. One of the really cool recent narrative experiences, together with titles such as Before your Eyes and Hindsight. Highly recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: South of the Circle

_childDocuments_.review: Not much of a game, since it's lacking a "playing" aspect but a very good interactive movie with beautiful graphics,really good animation and a quite good story, although I did not appreciate much the symbols used to denote the feelings/choices in dialogue.Well worth it's price. I'd give it 6/10 coffee mugs.
_childDocuments_.name: South of the Circle

_childDocuments_.review: South of the Circle is a profoundly engaging interactive narrative set in the Cold War era. I admire the game's narrative structure, particularly its adept unfolding of the story, seamlessly transitioning between past and present scenes. It features intriguing, ambivalent characters and delves into profoundly human questions surrounding memories, opportunism, the power of life choices, patriarchal inequality, academic complexities, and, of course, love. If you enjoy this type of game, then this is definitely for you. I had a truly great time with it!
_childDocuments_.name: South of the Circle

_childDocuments_.review: South of the Circle takes players stands out within the visual novel genre with its distinctive art style and captivating music. Overall, the game offers an experience that is both enchanting and, at times, a touch perplexing.One of the standout features of South of the Circle is its simplistic yet incredibly unique graphics. The game dares to veer away from the conventional visuals seen in its contemporaries, opting for a style that is refreshingly minimalist. However, at times, this distinctive approach might feel engulfed by negative space, leaving players yearning for more substance in certain scenes.The true masterpiece lies within the game's musical score, which is nothing short of a roller coaster of emotions and seamlessly ties scenes together. The harmonious blend of the soundtrack is easily the most enthralling element of the narrative.Unfortunately, the weight of story choices doesn't translate into meaningful consequences. This could be a source of disappointment for those seeking a more impactful decision-making process. Furthermore, the ending leaves players with a sense of vagueness and dissatisfaction, a lingering feeling that contrasts with the otherwise positive impression the game leaves.Despite these minor drawbacks, South of the Circle remains a small gem within the story-telling genre. Its innovative approach to visuals, combined with its emotionally evocative music, creates an ambiance that is both rare and captivating.
_childDocuments_.name: South of the Circle

_childDocuments_.review: The cinemtagraphy is some of the best I have seen in a game. I would consider it more of a lightly interactive film than a game, but as a film, it was artisitcally breathtaking. The voice acting, script, and overall creative vision were incredible. The story about sexism in higher education was powerful. However, it did not seem like my choices that I made in the story had an impact on the trajectory or ending of the game, which was a big dissapoinment. I am glad I played through it, even if I felt like it would be better suited for a short film format.
_childDocuments_.name: South of the Circle

_childDocuments_.review: You are a climate scientist, studying clouds. This story flips back and forth across time, forcing you to face childhood demons and adulthood choices alike. This game is not about clouds, nor climate change. Hope that created some curiosity without giving any of the game away.A story about how men define themselves, no, how they let their work, define them. And place it first, before love itself. How they are so stupid to place love of their country above even love for the only woman who noticed them. Yep, it's a graphic novel, and this one lets you make choices of a sort, choices which all in the end may well come undone. International politics and a secrecy act destroys as much as it protects, lies. No, the Russians, are not coming, it was all a lie. Travel from Cambridge to the arctic circle, in a rather more deadly game that appears at the surface.Reminded me a little of The 39 Steps in it's plot and pacing, and Firewatch in the artwork, and pretty much every walking sim in the gameplay. A very well told story, not remarkable, just well told.If you enjoy this story, you have to check out this list of similar stories
_childDocuments_.name: South of the Circle

_childDocuments_.review: Pro: Very nice storyCon: Your choices do NOT matter at all.The moral of the story is pretty much that all men are misogynistic jerks. Even the ones who seem nice. You can try time choose all the nicer/better responses, but the game will throw it all out in the end, making the choice the developers wanted.Literally none of your choices matter in the end.Beautiful story with an ending that leaves a bad taste in my mouth that gets worse the more I think about it. Save yourself the $$.
_childDocuments_.name: South of the Circle

_childDocuments_.review: After Stray, South of the Circle was my 2nd surprise of the summer: excellent storyline, very gripping from start to finish, superb artistic paste... easy gameplay to learn (given the type of game it's not very difficult)But what a narrative slap! Too bad the choices have only a few branches in the scenario / to be done urgently in around 4 hours / go for it. The soundtrack is also very very good!
_childDocuments_.name: South of the Circle

_childDocuments_.review: A great game, though it's more an interactable movie then anything else. Genuinely one of the most fun and greatest stories I've seen in a while, and the effort put into this shows. Theirs one scene where you HAVE to use the mouse to progress, but beyond that, everything worked quite seemlessly. I generally like the asthetic and the story was one I loved, especially in how it references your interactions. Relatively short taking maybe 3-4 hours to beat, but genuinely one of the most engrossing stories I've had in ages.sidenote: offline play isn't counted torwards the total hours spent for some reason.
_childDocuments_.name: South of the Circle

_childDocuments_.review: The problem with this game that it's not a game at all. Game implies interactivity. This game is not interactive, it's like animation film. It reduces the possible richness of input to primitive signals. Am I monkey to press Y when the game asks to press Y? At first I got engaged in the story, but after some time I started to notice red flags until I start feeling disgust to this game. If my actions doesn't change the game why should I react at all? And if I would not react why should I play it at all?The only thing which was good in the game was art. The story had a propagandistic flavor which tried to mix modern political agenda with cold war tension, but in unconvincing manner like people who tell you about a war living in comfort.
_childDocuments_.name: South of the Circle

_childDocuments_.review: When I started playing, I thought it is a walking sim. Linear, story-driven, get bits and pieces of story line from surroundings. No, it's not. Surroundings are empty (except first found item being a story spoiler). Then I thought it is an interactive movie. Choices, different routes, charters. No, it's not. Visual style is anti-movie, no details, no facial expressions, no scene depth. Then I realized that it is a book. Not an interactive book. Just a linear audio book with crappy illustrations.This "game" has zero gameplay. I've completed it in 3,5 hours. One hour of this time is main character walking (or driving) forward with nothing happening. Other 2,5 hours actors reading their lines. And sometimes player needs to push some buttons so the "game" can tell when player falls asleep.Maybe the story itself is thrilling and engaging? No, it's not. The romance between "strong female character" and sissy (main character) is predictable to the last bit. The other part is a "fight for your life" trip in the snow. And it's awful. Two men crash on a plane in Antarctic. Pilot broke his leg, so another one (main character) needs to bring help. He speaks with the pilot several times offering to get back to him, but pilot refuses. He does not need food, shelter or warmth. Once MC encounters a map. A paper map with a ship printed on it. And two adult men seriously discuss that this ship is their salvation. A picture of ship printed on a paper map. Really?Won't go deep into politics. Cold war bogus. Free democracies, evil soviets. Evil like in Red Alert, but not so funny.Spoilers ahead. Don't buy. Waste of time.
_childDocuments_.name: South of the Circle

_childDocuments_.review: The art-style, the music, the voice casting were all perfect.I enjoyed the whole ride but the tension and plot twist at the last chapter really made it work. The atmosphere was on a constant high and I absolutely love all the voices of the characters.I only wished the ending would be more understandable and if your choices would matter. Every choice you made in the game get kinda waved away in ONE scene at the end so you will still get that same ending and you cannot change that.Great game with an emotional touch. Worth the price!!
_childDocuments_.name: South of the Circle

_childDocuments_.review: thought i'll give it a second chance but maybe i just like being dissapointed by the same things multiple times hihiprobably music is the best part of this game, but even it is really mid. im sad because it looks good but is soooo boring... i wanted some dark, political plot twists and what i got is talking abt clouds, main characters with no personality, illusionary choices and so eye-rolling romance ehh
_childDocuments_.name: South of the Circle

_childDocuments_.review: A point-and-click narrative game during the Cold War where you follow the struggles and past of Peter, a academic who has crashed in Antartica. The achievements revolve around missable collectibles and finishing the story. There are guides that show the location of the missables and you can finish the game in 1 playthrough. Estimated time is 2-4 hours.The game has great voice acting, characters and a very interesting story. It falls a bit flat as you are given choices but they don't really matter or impact the game in any sense. It could best be described as a more cinematic experience and if you keep that in mind I think you will greatly enjoy the game. The price however feels a bit steep for its length and I would recommend to buy it on sale. If you're an achievement hunter, feel free to check out my curator for more reviews!
_childDocuments_.name: South of the Circle

_childDocuments_.review: South of the Circle is an emotional narrative adventure with a deep mature cinematic story. A short, linear indie title with beautiful, artistic audiovisuals and sensational voice over. It is not a classic game, but definitely more of an immersive experience. I’m glad that South of the Circle is very well priced, and I think it’s worth giving it a chance if you like similar titles.How does South of the Circle work on Steam Deck? Simply great. Nearly perfect 60FPS at 1280×720 with low power consumption (10-12W). The game has full gamepad support.
_childDocuments_.name: South of the Circle

_childDocuments_.review: mediocre story with one of the worst gameplay I've ever seen. I would mach rather watch this story unfold in an animation form or a short movie. At least it would've have quality animations and consistent collisions. In the current version, it has the worst walking simulation part there is. The animations janky as hell. The collisions are filled with bugs.6/10 story0/10 gameplay
_childDocuments_.name: South of the Circle

_childDocuments_.review: This game takes about 4 hours to complete.If you're the sort of person who loves literary novels and/or games that are really more movies where you occasionally have to push buttons, you'll love this "narrative experience".  This game is visually striking, has wonderful music, is very well voice-acted, and has an engaging story.  There's a bit of wonkiness with the models sometimes, but I didn't encounter any bugs more serious than minor visual glitches.  But...it's really not much of a game.  There are no puzzles to solve, no real choices to make, no resources to manage, nothing that makes it a game.Given 11bit's other offerings and the look of the game, I was expecting something where the point was to make difficult choices that had deep impacts on gameplay and/or the progression of the story.  But in this game, your choices are more illusory: you can choose whether to respond fearfully or angrily to someone else's demands, for example, or whether to introduce yourself by your first name or your title, but it doesn't seem to do a whole lot to change the overarching narrative or even the immediate conversation (I have done only one playthrough, ).  I was enjoying the game until I figured out that nothing I was doing was really changing anything--it is engaging visually, narratively, and musically.  I don't think this one is for me, but I think the people it is for will like it.
_childDocuments_.name: South of the Circle

_childDocuments_.review: What a fantastic experience! I'm already a massive fan of the people that make this game, so I'm not surprised in the least to see something like this come from them. The story and voice acting are absolutely brilliant, I enjoy the subtle touches you add to the story. So happy to give you my money, keep making amazing games.

_childDocuments_.review: South of the Circle is an interactive story game, where you make decisions in an intricate story that switches between two times in one man's life. The story is interesting and engaging, and the choices range from small, insignificant talking points, to large, very difficult decisions about love and war with seemingly very high stakes.Unfortunately, those very decisions are where the game fell short for my playthrough specifically. The story itself has some requirements on what happens, which limit what outcomes can come from your decisions. The game leads up to a large decision near the end of the game, where I personally made an honest decision that went contrary to the game's story. This ended with a section that felt unfair and forced the outcome I explicitly chose not to make. While this made sense in the context of the story, it felt like I was robbed of some agency and as though my decisions never really mattered.Nonetheless, the story that the game gave is still super interesting and unique, and poses questions that were extremely interesting to consider and watch play out. While I do believe that this story makes the game well worth playing, the shortcomings in the decision tree made the emotional impact fall flat at the climax of the story, making it not quite worth full price in my opinion. Others may make different decisions than I did, and therefore may be significantly more emotionally engaged at the end, so your opinion may very well be quite different from my own.

_childDocuments_.review: South of the Circle was a very compelling adventure to play. Its story is very interesting, very well constructed. _childDocuments_.review: "It could be ours, though. This beautiful thing. If you wanted it to be."An absolutely captivating little narrative experience. If you're one who has issues with games not having enough proper GAmEpLaY to warrant their existence then steer far away from this. You're in for the ride and making only slight emotional adjustments to the dialogue and intentions. This is not a choose your own adventure type thing nor are you making choices and affecting events much. It's a lightly interactive narrative experience, and a wonderfully carefully crafted one. Gorgeous use of music and camera angles and editing, this has some of the best cuts and scene transitions since Virginia and Sifu. Perfectly naturalistic dialogue and delivery, the characters are believable and human and I found myself engaged on both narrative levels. If you were bored (or angry) with games like Firewatch or Virginia or Oxenfree, then no, this is definitely not for you. But if you get swept up in narratives in video games, it's a lovely and mature and surprisingly delicate experience. Go in blind. Let it surprise you.8/10

_childDocuments_.review: "South of the Circle" is a barely interactive walking sim/visual novel with a plot about having a nice Antarctic plane crash and getting some amnesia and then discovering what kind of person that you are, I guess.  Problematically there's arguably less to this than older walking sims, the plot isn't that gripping, and there's not much remaining of interest to gamers.At least this is sincerely and genuinely made, it's not an asset flip and it's not a construction kit hack job, so there's elements of quality to this that put it far away from the shovelware bins. The problem here, chiefly, is that you can get the entire experience of the game just by watching a play through on Youtube.  Why pay money for that?On the upside, the game does feature customisable controls and resolution, so at least some of the basic, minimum requirements have been met.  Unfortunately there's a number of other technical defects and shortcomings which contribute to the game being difficult to recommend to gamers.The game features low-polygon "retro" assets with shader effects to blend them into a cartoony looking illustration style instead of doing their job properly and texturing the game assets, making this look like a barely functional 3D game from the early 2000s.  This visual style is a method that lazy devs often use when they have a lack of interest/capability to create highly detailed, high poly models and instead use shader effects to disguise that shortcoming under the name of "art".  It looks passable, but only in a "just good enough" sense.  Given the pricing for this game, you'd expect better.The game is just incredibly shallow from both an interaction and a game design sense... narrative is good, arguably vital, but it needs to be backed up with solid gameplay.  Otherwise we're just competing with Youtube and Netflix, and that isn't why we're here.The game never really caught on with the millions of gamers on Steam, with a very low peak player count close to launch, and then just a handful of players launching this game every couple of days.  This is undoubtedly caused by factors such as those raised in this review.  It's always helpful with buying decisions to consider how popular and successful the product is, and unfortunately while this did accumulate a few participation trophy reviews, overall, people just aren't using it.So, should you buy this game?  Is this one of the best of the 100,000+ games on Steam?"South of the Circle" has the preposterous price of $13 USD, for which you could easily get any number of older AAA games.  Given the defects and quality issues with the game, coupled with the unrealistic price, this is impossible to recommend.For comparison, the $13 asking price for this game could get you games like "Hunt: Showdown", "Phantasmophobia" or "Resident Evil Village".  Quality, professionally made games like those are frequently on sale cheaper than this.

_childDocuments_.review: Better have an incredible controller for this one, boys! Gonna need a finely calibrated joystick for solving the intricate puzzles and as many buttons as possible for all the fighting combos. The final boss was a smoker. Be prepared to grind to survive as well. For real though, I thought the saving grace of this game would be the story but instead its woke drivel. Tired old progressive arguments with mundane characters with zero charisma. Is Antarctica cold btw? It must not be, or Peter doesn't think so because he never once pulls the hood up on his jacket. He also never wears his goggles. The entire time. He doesn't shut the door to plane at the intro. Guess he'd rather his pilot died of exposure. Plenty of tools to use as weapons or to hike with in the first base and yet he doesn't exploit anything to survive. No food or water. His father was right, he's useless. Dude can't row a boat. I honestly could care less about the guy. Tried to sabotage him in any way possible but there is no struggle in the game. You cannot fail. There's no purpose. I came to realise that its not a game at all. You simply watch a story and make a few pointless dialogue choices that have little to no bearing on what happens. There is nowhere to explore. Nothing to do except turn a radio knob. The most exciting part is getting to hit a button when he's aiming down the sights of a rifle and hit some targets, yet they found a way to ruin that. I tried to at least crash his car but he refused to leave his lane. Dear God I know weak men like this actually exist but I don't care to play as them in a fictional video game that is meant to entertain me. Its not even a good story. Cliche and woke. I'm struggling to finish it. Not even worth it if it was free. Don't waste your time.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a sucker for some historical settings and was naturally drawn towards this game. While I went in with expectations of a simple story, the game unfolds in many ways with interesting commentary on the Cold War, recognition and status in academia, the notion of masculinity and patriotism above all else, and the role of women in all of this. This is delivered through great acting and natural dialogue that grounds the characters. The gameplay is light and the art direction is simplistic but is used well, especially in transitions.My only major gripe is the unsatisfying and inconsequential ending. There is an explanation for the direction of the ending, but it is not one I agree with wholeheartedly. It also leaves on an open-ended note, which feels like the characters' conclusion was ripped away from me. An epilogue would've been just enough to tie up the loose ends.
_childDocuments_.name: South of the Circle

_childDocuments_.review: I am not exactly sure how I feel about the ending and the way that the choices you make throughout the game plays out. In such a game with the minimal amount of gameplay, the choices are the most we can interact with the work. Therefore the way those choices were handled was not my favorite for this game. Anyway, I like seeing such narrative games and this one, for the most part, is really good and does get an idea across. So a recommendation it is.
_childDocuments_.name: South of the Circle

_childDocuments_.review: *WARNING FOR SPOILERS*One of those cases where it's so close to greatness and falls just shy of it to the point where you almost get angry at the game for not nailing the landing. The majority of the story is SO good: engrossing, tightly and subtly written, full of characters you root for and hate and come to love. The larger themes are so fantastic: red scare suspicion giving way to humanistic collaobration, women integrating into upper levels of education in a way that illustrates exactly how difficult so much of that fight was, the struggle between science and war and how often war wins out. The transitions between the present and the past are so seamless and beautiful I had to pause to catch my breath a few times. I was pounding my desk several times trying to get Peter to get back up, get moving, survive. Survive. And yet. That ending. That ending retroactively nearly ruins the experience.That said. I'm still very glad I played it. The writing outside that ending is some of the strongest I've found in games. The environments and the music are so beautiful. And Clara? I loved her to death. If this was a feature film instead of a game, I have a feeling it'd have been deeply loved. Extra note: play it with a controller. Using mouse and keyboard could be pretty wonky with camera angle changes.

_childDocuments_.review: On one side of things, it is a gorgeous visual spectacle and a marvel of design and passion from the developers. On the other, it is a weak, strangely jumbled movie that passes as a game because it has buttons you click sometimes. Nothing more than a visual novel. While this isn't a bad thing, and I often find myself gravitating towards those kinds of releases, here are some issues I had with the game as a whole. I am an absolute glutton when it comes to video game soundtracks however, and absolutely loved the compositions and score by Ed Critchley. The score beautifully supported and uplifted the game, and you can tell that a lot of love was put into making sure the music was an accurate reflection of the scale and scope of the game.The voice acting was brilliant as well. The cast was clearly chosen with care and it reflects in the overall feel of the game. Even though most of this game is good, and I enjoyed my experience, I would say the only reason to pick this game up would be if it was on sale, like I did. I'm not sure the roughly 3 hour run-time of the entire game warrants a 13 US dollar price tag. Pick this game up if you'd like to experience it for yourself - I'd rate it a 6.5/10.
_childDocuments_.name: South of the Circle

_childDocuments_.review: The story is well paced and feels done by an expert even if it seems simple at first, I found myself being impressed by the games ability to tie themes together and build mysteries and twists, even if I saw some and blindsided by others. The soundtrack was brilliant especially the music but even the ambience was perfect. I'm not a musician so I can't say why it's good but its excellent in all the right ways, helping solidify this feeling of uneasiness, desperation and surrealness of what is happening.This game is amazing at storytelling but it's clear weakness is the gameplay. Not to bad but it is mainly making minor choices in the story "cutscenes" to keep you on it or walking to another point for a cutscene, short enough though and its usually to give you time to think about whats happening. To reiterate not bad but keep in mind if you want to play it.
_childDocuments_.name: South of the Circle

_childDocuments_.review: This is a narrative focused game and if you want to play this game you are not going to see much game play.This is more like a great indie movie, I don't use great often in my reviews so I will try to explain why I used that word. I said there is almost no game play but there is one mechanic that helps you to pay attention to what is happening, you have icons that symbolize your feelings in the situation.It isn't vital to the story's outcome or your decision matter thing, the emotions icons are a great tool because the story really pulled me in. The voice acting is great, the sound design is great,the visuals do a good job in the overall feel of an indie movie and the story is for a majority well written and structured.Some sections don't hit as hard and some are a bit boring but these are really minor complaints.When I finished this game I felt like I left the small movie theater. Great stuff if you like these type of narrative experiences.
_childDocuments_.name: South of the Circle

_childDocuments_.review: Man, what a story! This is one of those titles that embody the fact that games have finally "grown up". It's a realistic thriller that has research breakthroughs (depicted very respectfully), reflections on the place of women in the mid-XX century society, international espionage, unlikely friendships built at gunpoint, and, obviously, survival in the Antarctic with all the mental problems it entails. The voice acting is wonderful, and wonderfully British at that, too.Just great overall, play it if you haven't! Other people seem to dislike the ending; I won't spoil it here but, well, to me it just looked like another plot twist that tied some of the strings together and was quite in character with the rest of the game. Give this one a shot, I'm sure you won't regret it.
_childDocuments_.name: South of the Circle

_childDocuments_.review: Sound Design and Visual Style of this game is gorgeous, No contesting that. The Story is fairly interesting, with a unique graphic style that complements the story.(Best to experience for yourself)This game is relatively short, a good 3-4 hours you could complete it. Quite easy to gain all achievements.Give it a chance, you wont be disappointed.  Cheers.
_childDocuments_.name: South of the Circle

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very "qualified recommend".  As in, this really isn't for everyone.  It's beautifully done, and does contain quite the story.  So for that, I do give compliments.  But, by far this isn't for everyone.  It's not a "game", it's more an experience.  If you want an experience and a story, then feel free to try this.  Though warning, it's really a One and Done.  If you're looking for a proper Game, there's other items from this Studio's library.
_childDocuments_.name: South of the Circle

_childDocuments_.review: I can't stop feel the unfulfillment of the idea that interactive narrative is to prepare a few options and different screenplays, then hand the rail lever to players. It's never the right way to make players aware of the weight of story creation and have fun from it, when the writers give it away themselves.Through a thorny path, this game tried to answer the question, what my choices mean to the story and to my heart. When they were all negated, I can surprisingly feel they are closer to the character, and to myself, and connected us. Isn't it just like the beautiful scenery of Scottish highland, though ephemeral before the storm.It's cruel and cunning, but I love it.
_childDocuments_.name: South of the Circle

_childDocuments_.review: It was a great experience playing the game: thrilling story, beautiful art, and fascinating narrative techniques. It just happened that I didn't play this game until I had watched the movie  a week ago, even though it had been downloaded several months ago. This has made the game even more compelling, as I had some background knowledge from the movie and some researches that I did for the movie. I would recommend anyone who wants to play the game to also watch the movie, and I assure you that you'll have a better understanding of the game after watching it.
_childDocuments_.name: South of the Circle

_childDocuments_.review: If you want an interactive drama with a cold war aesthetic, this is a game for you. I love the story, acting, and music although the ending left me a bit confused. I did experience a couple bugs where the game struggled to register my inputs, I watched a playthrough and that is not supposed to happen. It has the 'we wanted to make a movie' vibes. Overall a very pleasant experience despite the subject matter. Trigger warning: violence, emotional abuse, misogyny
_childDocuments_.name: South of the Circle

_childDocuments_.review: South of the Circle, an artistically vibrant narrative-based game, deals with the maladies of the academic milieu amidst the 60's Cold War paranoia. It features a wonderful pastel palette and minimalist style but be forewarned that player input is also kept on the minimal side.The Good:Beautiful graphics and visual styleBrilliant voice acting and soundtrackInnovative way of steering conversations with emotions instead of repliesCompelling premise for the storyAtmospheric and creepy settingsGreat way of telling the story, with the past and present weaved togetherThe Bad:The game gives an impression that your choices matter when they don’tDisappointing and hastily put-together endingMany plot holes and loose threads ruin an otherwise good storyLack of puzzles makes it less of a challenge.
_childDocuments_.name: South of the Circle

_childDocuments_.review: This is certainly one of the most "interesting" games that I have played, whether for good or bad. A part of me almost didn't recommend this game because it really is a mixed bag. The main protagonist is sometimes likable and sometimes a complete jerk, some of the commentary of the game is excellent while other parts of its commentary border on stupidity. I liked the overall shifting of timelines that the game made for its sense of confusion, but I also think that it was used to also cut some corners. The choices that the game offers are cool, but there is also ultimately a set path, and this game would of benefited from having multiple endings, and speaking of which, the ending, is so obtuse, and although I enjoyed the journey that the game makes you go through, the journey as part of the plot could of also been completely avoided. Overall though, I still somewhat liked the game despite the fact that I also feel that this is a mixed bag. I will give this game a 6/10, and I'll give this a recommendation, because this game is certainly "memorable" whether for good or bad, or maybe, somewhere in the middle.
_childDocuments_.name: South of the Circle

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful, emotional experience . Clara's Scottish accent is absolutely adorable . The negative reviewers who complained about their choices not having much impact on the story or the ending should have read the description of the game. Not only it doesn't promise that,  but actually states quote "The story focuses on promises made in between career and true love, where our choices burdened by our past seem to be illusory". But actually the story we get to relive through it is much more than that.
_childDocuments_.name: South of the Circle

_childDocuments_.review: a very short narrative-driven walking game. and yes, choices in this game don't matter, key moments will always play the same. at times, i did wish that the dialogue choices were given to the players instead of using the confusing icons, but eventually, i grew fond of it because it did reflect the character's emotions well.
_childDocuments_.name: South of the Circle

_childDocuments_.review: South of the Circle is a great visual story game. It's more like a movie than a game but I really didn't mind it. Beautiful artstyle, complelling story and amazing soundtrack made me so immersed that I finished the game in one go. So if you're a player who likes a great story then this game is for you! ;)
_childDocuments_.name: South of the Circle

_childDocuments_.review: A really nice ambientation. The soundtrack fit the game scenes. So far it's present a good plot mixing the present moment and past/future (I didn't end the game yet so is difficult to know if the cut scenes is related to the past or to the future of the character)Looks so nice until now, with 30 minutes of game I realy recommend this title.Note: 8 / 10
_childDocuments_.name: South of the Circle

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, I think it's perfectly okay to make a cinematic videogame, with a single plot line where there's no player choice, just a great experience and narrative. If you smash buttons and the things happening on screen seem to correspond to it, I call it a videogame. But that's not exactly the case; There's not much you can do interactively wise. Most of the time your agency as a player is more in the way of the story than driving it. But that's a perfectly fine design choice for a game with a narrow focus on the narrative; it's just that I would have loved to lose myself in the whiteness of the Antarctic with just a map and a compass.In the End it's a great narrative game, with a delightful artstyle that avoids the damned hyper realism prevaling in this medium.
_childDocuments_.name: South of the Circle

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent narrative game with an outstanding story. The aesthetic is lovely and the voice acting is very well performed. I almost played it in one go (had to take a break at some point) but I was so invested in the story that it was hard for me to tune out. If you love story telling and adventure, this game is made for you.
_childDocuments_.name: South of the Circle

_childDocuments_.review: A fun little story, told in a very cinematic way. The visuals are great and the music is amazing. Gameplaywise it's a walking simulator in the purest sense, there's no real, impactful gameplay, but I thought it was fun nontheless. If your local cinema disappoints you, spend the money for a movie ticket on this game instead!
_childDocuments_.name: South of the Circle

_childDocuments_.review: South of the circle: 8/10I was immersed as soon as the story began. That's what this virtually is, a point and click story.  So why 2 points away from 10/10? I had several glitches where the next story wouldn't load and my character just walked back to where he had begun without me having any control and I was really confused by the plot where the female character just randomly started storming off and yelling... none of my choices mattered in the end. However the graphics, story transition and music, mechanics were great. I wouldn't recommend this game if you are someone who doesn't like a story that jumps back and forth in time. Nor to someone who is sensitive to subjects such as war, nuclear or otherwise, family issues or to those who are light sensitive.
_childDocuments_.name: South of the Circle

_childDocuments_.review: Although this game only takes about 3 hours to play, and choice is so limited, it's more like a movie than a game, it's still a fantastic purchase that I can recommend to anyone interested. The art style, music, and voice acting are all top notch, and the ways in which flashbacks are interspersed throughout the main story is one of the game's most charming aspects.Works great on Deck.
_childDocuments_.name: South of the Circle

_childDocuments_.review: I'm usually always interested in these 'artsy' looking indies, but am almost always turned away by the price when it comes time to buy them.  I felt like this was in the sweet spot at launch so I bought it on a whim not knowing anything about it.This game has fantastic writing, performances, music, but is all totally eclipsed by the game's stellar art direction.If you're looking for a nice interactive story to unwind with, I recommend checking this out.  For all the folks complaining  then you kind of missed the point.
_childDocuments_.name: South of the Circle

_childDocuments_.review: Pro's:- Heartfelt story- Good pacing and unique style- Amazing atmosphere and soundtrack.Con's:- Lackluster animation- Buggy terrain (items floating in the air, clipping through rocks)- Speech options are not very clear. You can chose an emotion and intention, but not the actual words.- i didn't feel my choices made an impact in the end. Will have to play a second time to be sure.7/10Good for a enjoyable 3.something hours.
_childDocuments_.name: South of the Circle

_childDocuments_.review: I got this game because I tend to like narrative games and the art style looked neat and I ended up SO drawn into this story. I didn't really have an idea of what it was about and by the end I was so captivated in the tale it told.Pros:- Amazing story telling with amazing voice actors to express it- the art style was absoLUTELY brilliant- The pacing was very well doneCons:- The choices didn't really feel as impactful as I had hoped- There is a little glitching sometimes in the character models which can take you out of the moment- Some scenes can be a lil too real (May need a TW for some folks)Overall, It was such a good story I don't think you should pass up the opportunity to experience it yourself. I give it 10/10 flashbacks.
_childDocuments_.name: South of the Circle

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR I can easily recommend this game but I want to highlight some issues for improvement:- Zero Video options. Setting the resolution and V-Sync would be nice.- The game doesn't hide your mouse cursor, so you have to tuck it away manually when using a gamepad- The first prompt in the game looks like a radial gamepad-thumbstick selection between words. I paniced because it seemed like KB+M wouldn't work. Had to restart so I could catch the conversation again.- Clipping issues are common and are distracting in a game with this visual style- Sometimes you won't be allowed to pause the game until your next input prompt- Ambient audio continues to play when pausing the game- Why is there is a small white circle in the top-left corner of the screen during the entire game?
_childDocuments_.name: South of the Circle

_childDocuments_.review:
Antarctica, 1964.

A crashed aircraft, tail to the sky.

Cambridge academic Peter stumbles from the wreckage in search of help, fighting the cold. As his attempts to escape the ice grow more desperate, the lines between his past and present begin to blur.

A love story between colleagues Peter and Clara, set against the backdrop of the Cold War, South of the Circle is a narrative adventure game about memory, survival, and the consequences of not dealing with the past.
_childDocuments_.name: South of the Circle

name: Wildfrost
detailed_description: Feature List Build your perfect deck unique to you! Recruit cute card companions, elemental items and equip powerful charms to aid in your fight against the Wildfrost Choose your Leader from a variety of tribes, each with different playstyles and stats Master a dynamic ‘counter’ system to put your strategic skills to the test Expand and develop the hub town of Snowdwell between runs Unlock new cards, events, customisation options and more! Endless replayability with daily runs and challenges! About the Game The sun has frozen over... The world has succumbed to the Wildfrost. Now only Snowdwell and its survivors stand as the last bastion against an eternal winter... Build up a deck of powerful card companions and elemental items, as you battle to banish the frost once and for all! Perfect your card battling and deck-building skills, and set out on a quest to bring an end to The Wildfrost! Begin each journey with your chosen tribe Leader, each gifted with different randomised skills and stats, before mapping out your chosen path into the unforgiving frosty landscape. Rescue and recruit frozen companions you find along the way, unearth lost treasures, and spend your hard-earned blings with travelling merchants. The decisions you make and routes you take during each run will help craft a powerful deck, unique to you each time you play. Collect a huge array of cute, but mighty card companions, as well as handy items and clunker cards to aid you in battle. Experiment with different elemental card combinations to find your winning formula. Your companion cards aren’t just disposable minions for dealing out damage; upgrade and customise your favourites by adding wobbly charms to enhance their powers, making your deck a powerful (and adorable) force to be reckoned with! Plan ahead with the help of a dynamic counter system to map out your next move and fend off frosty foes. While Wildfrost battles are turn-based, cards don’t attack every turn. Instead they have a ‘counter’ which counts down the amount of turns until they’re ready to automatically make their move! By keeping an eye on enemy monsters’ counters, you can plot ahead your perfect play. Buff your companions? Stall an enemy attack? Or maybe count down your own timer to wreak havoc fast! It’s up to you to strategically turn the tide in your favour. Need a rest? Take shelter in the cosy town of Snowdwell. Here survivors have gathered to keep warm using the power of the Luminice, a giant shard of hot ice. As you progress after each run you’ll be able to return and gradually help expand the hub town itself, constructing buildings such as a Pet Shop, Inventors Hut and more! These new areas will unlock fun and useful new things to use during your adventures, with new cards, tribes, cosmetics, challenges to complete, and events to encounter. Think you’ve defeated the Frost Guardian? Even after you’ve beaten back the frost, Wildfrost offers endless replayability, with daily runs and challenges! Test your skills and improve your score!
