_childDocuments_.review: I think the game is just bare bones for what it is.It is a hybrid visual novel / escape room simulator, but the visual novel part is very simple and there isn't much there to latch onto. The characters are quirky and remind me a bit of the game Psychonauts but they feel like they should've been fleshed out way more. I would have liked to have seen a stronger/longer story, more students to interact with, the ability to explore the campus in 3D, secrets to discover / bonus puzzles to unlock and solve. Anything really to add to the depth of the game, because at the moment it's only a few hours of game play.The puzzles themselves are fun because the timed element adds a bit of pressure, although most of the puzzles you will find you have almost double the amount of time you need if not more to solve them, which begs the question: why include a timer in the first place? As far as quantity and quality, there are roughly 10 puzzles and they are pretty easy to solve, I've found much more difficult puzzles in Escape Room Simulator and the We Were Here series respectively.If you want to play multiplayer escape rooms, play Escape Room Simulator or We Were Here series with a friend. If you're looking for a rewarding, puzzle based visual novel, try playing Paradise Killer. All that being said, it's worth it if the game goes on a deep cut to spend a few hours solving puzzles. I hope the devs use this as a baseline to make a more fleshed out game in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: This game is actually really good. The puzzles are clever, the setting interesting, didn't come across any bugs or glitches.However, the whole games is completely ruined by implementing a timer into every mission. Instead of enjoying yourself while taking your time to figure out the interesting puzzles, you always have the feeling you're under pressure and in a hurry, which gives a totally hectic vibe to everything.I hate it.Therefore I cannot recommend this game. If you're not bothered by that, go ahead and buy it, it would actually be awesome if not for this godawful timer.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: I loved the idea of this game, an escape room type game with a story that hooked me when I first started to play. Sadly, the game is mostly gameplay and little story, with the story elements being shallow and unoriginal. What's the problem with the game being mostly gameplay? The issue is the gameplay is a dumbed down version of escape simulator with levels feeling like basic comunity levels. The worst part is the game is only a few hours long with no replayability since the whole game is just ten short levels. It's a slap in the face to play repackaged escape simulator levels for $20 WITH AVAILABLE DLC that costs almost as much as the game.TLDR: Game is too short with no replay value, a boring story, and levels feel like re packaged escape simulator levels.

_childDocuments_.review: Game worked mostly fine until we reached the Rival Room. At this point it turned into a race against the clock to not desync and disconnect. Even if one of us stood completely still we couldn't really make it past the weight section before it disconnected. The furthest we got without a disconnect was the spinning shapes. Can't recommend this game for online play until this has been fixed.Game is otherwise a very simple and linear escape room game. Enjoyable until its not.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is way too short for the price tag.the puzzles are usually pretty good, but there are points where i spent way too long trying to figure out what was the interact-able that i was missing to solve the puzzle. and there was only one puzzle that i would say was bad  and it was used twice. the sentry puzzle i feel was not clear and no other puzzle had the same type of solution to it.overall its an alright game with a story that you can predict from the start, with standard puzzles that are visually good. i just wish it had more game play.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun solo or with a friend. Engaging and humorous story-line and intuitive interface. The art style is nice, and the music suits each environment. You'll enjoy the characters and the voice acting as well. Only issue I had was during online multiplayer mode where as you finish an area the game freezes. I believe they're working on that, as the dev has requested log files from affected players on their Discord server. I do highly recommend the game, however if you plan on playing online with friends you may want to check first to verify they've sorted out the glitches.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: It's just not good enough for what it is.Currently there's only about 12 rooms to escape, which for me has taken under 4 hours. The developer has launched the game as a basically unheard of studio with no other games on Steam, at $30 AUD, and already has 2 DLC packs planned at the cost of DOUBLING the price of the base game. This is NOT a $60 game, and this just reeks of cut content to milk the game for more money, rather than adding to something down the line.The rooms give you an excessively long time to solve them. 95% of the 'puzzles' are utterly brainless, to the degree that I barely had to think to already have the answer in. Most codes to locks etc feel like they're directly above the lock. There's only one or two points in any of the rooms that gave me any sort of pause to think about them. Despite the difficulty rating going up as you progress, the rooms feel no harder, and I'm annoyed I didn't refund before the 2 hour cutoff, as I expected 'harder' puzzles that never came. Without any aid I scored the highest A+ grade on every room without effort.There's very little agency in solving things, and no way to overthink anything. For instance, there's a puzzle involving finding pieces to recreate some art, but when you go to place any of the pieces you find, they all just drop on the table in the right place at the right angle. Rather than at least having the interesting interaction of trying to line things up and find the right perspective to view them, everything is just plonked in place for you, brain off. Any object in the room will either be key to a puzzle, or interacting with it will basically have the dialogue popup say "nothing useful here!" which removes the fun or working out what's relevant and what's extraneous detail The game is set up in a manner which largely forces you to solve A to access B, solve B to access C, solve C to access D. There's only one or two rooms which feel like they have any form of open-endedness to the order you go about solving them.In terms of visuals, the art style is lacking. It's heavily Danganronpa-inspired, which means large, chunky cartoon aesthetics in the environment, with 2D VN style drawings for dialogue. Not a fan of the character designs at all. The headmaster looks so haggard that all she reminds me of is Yzma, and one of the janitor's eyes is halfway down his head. Characters are very one dimensional, especially your 'rival' who is the most generic 'I hate you because I'm your rival, and I think I'm better than you' character ever written.Many players are experiencing graphical glitches, I personally had a section of a room where textures were strobing through a solid wall from outside. Most of the achievements are being reported as bugged for various users.The game has co-op, but as there are only 12 rooms and all are exceedingly easy, I have no desire to play the game through again with someone else, and I'm glad I didn't as it would have just slowed both of us down by needing to fiddle to manage an inventory that isn't shared between you.All in all, I would not recommend buying this game, and I certainly would not have bought it full price if I'd realised ahead of time that I'd be supporting the scummy practice of releasing a buggy game with half the content cut at the price of a full game.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: Playing this co-op with a friend so my review is based on that experience.The co-op feels really janky and glued on feature, especially in the world map, but in the escapes it's ok, there is a split screen option, where you can see both your and the other players view, so there really isn't much need to have any notes on puzzles if your friend is looking some instruction else where in the room. But this split screen feature also kinda removes any real reason to communicate heavily and for that sort of thing I'd go for the "We were here" series.Playing co-op also probably cuts down the required time to complete each escape by significant amount of time since most of the rooms are non-linear so both can do their own thing.The setting menu is bare minimum but I'd really like to have more options for mouse, it feels like there is mouse acceleration on and when you zoom in on a puzzle, it's like going into CS:GO sniper sensitivity and realllly have to drag the cursor over to get anything done. This is my main issue with the game.Also at least in co-op mode, the game screen gets stuck sometimes after getting thru a room and need to restart the game.Overall I'd probably enjoy this most as a single player experience and don't feel this is that well suited for co-op
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic little game that I only wish was longer. Each room is challenging without being frustrating, and the story line was definitely worth paying attention to. I will definitely be grabbing the DLC for this one, I thoroughly enjoyed this game. I'd replay it, but I already know the answers!! Might still replay it though lol

_childDocuments_.review: ★★★★☆ - Great 6 hours (Completed Base Game)	- First-person escape room puzzle game cross with visual novel.	- Engaging puzzle mechanics that progressively challenge players keep gameplay fresh and prevent monotony.	- Some puzzles may require a hint or two, but overall difficulty is well-balanced for a satisfying experience.	- There is a timer for each Escape Room that keeps pressure on the player but is quite generous in the time it gives you.	- Hogwarts-esk storyline that unfolds through interactive dialogue and in-game cutscenes.	- Characters are well-developed with their own personalities and give depth to the puzzles.	- Unfortunately is missing full voice acting which would add to the immersion of the story.  	- Plot twists keep players invested in uncovering the mystery behind the Escape Academy.	- Visually appealing with detailed environments and character designs.	- Graphics contribute to the overall atmosphere and make exploration enjoyable.- Make sure to explore each environment thoroughly before starting to solve the puzzles, as hidden clues are essential for progress.- Using Pin in-game for certain items and Notes in the Steam Overlay (or a physical notebook) when working on puzzles is important for Puzzle Solving without having to constantly backtrack.

_childDocuments_.review: Purebred escape room offering very fresh and interesting gameplay. And this applies to both single game and game in the company with a friend. Cooperative overcoming challenges here is one of the factors, but the main trump card is the fact that all rooms have a countdown timer. Its presence is a very risky factor, because such spurring always works on 2 fronts - on the one hand, it injects adrenaline into the blood and provokes the brain to work extremely intensively, but on the other hand, it requires designers to be as efficient as possible in building locations and puzzles. The amount of time here is very tight, the player has no time to yawn, so immediately set yourself up for an intense pace of passing. The plot is funny and light, it plays rather a background role here, everything is geared towards solving puzzles.The level of puzzles is pleasantly surprising, if some require minimal effort to solve, then most will make you sweat furiously. Many rooms have a complex structure, which makes the action unpredictable and intense. I can’t say that absolutely all the puzzles turned out to be successful (as in any game of the genre), some had to be passed by brute force. The solution of some did not seem elegant to me, although I understood the idea of ​​​​the creators, especially for some of the puzzles in the last room, but most of the tests here are simply lovely. Smart decisions, assertive dynamism and timely presentation of not always obvious clues. Angular visual style is not for everyone, of course, but does not interfere with enjoying what is happening. It is noticeable that the authors feel very confident in the element of secrets and puzzles, skillfully juggling various mechanics and offering interesting solutions. It turned out to be very competent, exciting and moderately difficult, what more could lovers of high-quality puzzles want, we definitely recommend it.

You play about 10 puzzles with different levels of difficulty and there is a non engaging story line. Constantly crashed on loading, couldn't do more than two rooms in a row without it crashing on us on both sides. I enjoyed the game but the amount of bugs we encountered was just too much for me to rate this positively unfortunately and it seems the reviews on the DLC are the same so I'll be passing on that. Also, it's a really short game. We beat the whole thing and got most of the achievements in under 4 hours from beginning to end and I feel like it needed more to feel worth it especially given how buggy it is. Also, in terms of story there was no real feeling of a progression of time. I was surprised to find out this was all in a year in game time when it felt like the first week still. It just wasn't dense enough to feel like a full year. I wish there was just a way to feel like time had actually passed in the game. Love the art style though, that was amazing.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: Really great and fun game, although pretty short. I got this in the Humble Bundle so it didn't bother me how short it was. If I wanted to play more of this kind of thing with a friend, I would consider getting the DLC. The vast majority of the puzzles were basically well made and almost none of them had me resorting to guessing. Those that I did guess on were then almost always because I wanted to try and go faster, not because of moon logic.Warning for others: I'm (mildly) red-green colorblind so that may be why, but there are a number of puzzles that were made harder than they were probably intended to be because they relied on color. On at least 2 instances I could not differentiate between 2 colors that were important to see the difference between (once a light blue and white, another time a yellow vs bright green) and another time colors that would likely be bright and distinct normally were obscured to just the point where they all appeared muddy and difficult to distinguish for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: The puzzles flow really well. Some are a bit obvious, but most of them do get the noggin going, while not being overly complicated. Obviously a lot more fun if you can play it with a friend.Remote play together is possible, which is a nice option to save some money, but one of the aspect where the game shines is the ability to switch between split screen and full screen if your friend has his own copy of the game.Alternating between exploring in full screen and then sharing information in split screen to open locks etc. was such a refreshing and pleasant dynamic for an Escape Room game, I wish the other games in this genre would adopt this mechanic. The PvP is interesting, but the puzzles are recycled in the different game modes of a specific map, so the novelty quickly wears off.Still, it was a free update so this is a nice addition to the game.A few words on the weak points of the game :Despite these points, the game is very enjoyable, and I would recommend it to every Escapist Enthusiast.It falls on the short side though (5 hours on average to complete the base game), so do get it on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Escape Academy was a nice co-op puzzle game to play with my partner. There is currently a loading issue bug, which results in a long initial start up and there was a game breaking bug in the arena level towards the end of the game, we had to restart that level once. Also the Escape Academy theme song in the menu is bad, but it's starting to grow on me.I'm looking forward to trying the season pass levels later when the price is lower during a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: Do you like puzzle games? How about escape rooms?Want an entire game built around completing a few, fairly high-quality and well designed escape rooms?Do you want to do those puzzles either solo or even in co-op?!Then Escape Academy might be right up your alley. Although a bit on the short side, It's a very fun, well polished game with great, high-quality puzzles.I never would have thought to try Escape Academy if not for the most recent Steam Next Fest, which had an Escape Academy demo up featuring its first 2 levels as playable. I got to say from the moment I started playing that demo I was hooked, and I do not regret picking this up and completing it day one.Escape Academy may not be unique in its premise - many developers have tried their hand at creating similar titles, and you can find many puzzle and escape room games on the market these days - but Escape Academy might be one of my favorites in terms of its puzzle quality, ease of use, and overall aesthetic. There were a few things here and there I wished was a little different, but overall Escape Academy is a great game to experience and I would definitely recommend picking it up.Below may be a few things you might find interesting to know more about before purchasing.I completed Escape Academy in roughly 4-5 hours including repeating the first two levels I had previously played in the demo version. There are 12 levels in total (including the tutorial level) in the base game, as well as a short interlude level before the finale and the occasional short dialogue section between levels. Each level is timed, taking around 15-30 minutes to complete at the expected pace on your first run through the game.Every level can also be repeated at any time as many times as you want, however replayability does suffer somewhat as each level appears to only have one solution, causing future attempts to be easily speedran.All of this ends up revealing Escape Academy to be a well put together, if fairly short, game. Some may find the length worrying, but for the current price of $20 it definitely feels well worth the cost in my opinion.There does appear to be more content coming down the pipeline fairly soon though, with 10 more levels coming in future DLCs alongside a few other updates, so this fear might not be that big of an issue pretty soon!A common issue some games face, especially in puzzle or point-and-click adventure titles, are the convoluted actions and  extreme leaps in logic ('moon logic') required by the player to parse in order to occasionally solve puzzles or even to just advance further into the game (i.e. combining objects that makes no sense to be combined, and then using said object on something that makes no sense in using said item on!). Puzzle games can feel extremely frustrating if there isn't a clear goal as to what needs to be achieved, if the puzzle being solved lacks a sort of internal logic to its solution, or if its concealing necessary information from the player.Luckily, Escape Academy doesn't succumb to any of those pitfalls. The levels in Escape Academy all feel very straightforward in what they are asking for you to accomplish, with each puzzle acting as a logical stepping stone to completing said levels; at no point did I ever feel like I was hitting my head against a wall or feeling like a puzzle made absolutely no sense. Every level and puzzle in Escape Academy felt like they had a logical thread to them that helped put you into a bit of a 'flow' state.And although Escape Academy is fairly straightforward in its puzzle and level design, that isn't to say its bad or necessarily easy. There were quite a few individual puzzles I remember finding notable as I played through the game, both for their surprising difficulty, and for their complexity. I still recall how in the level, 'The Breakout', how I continually over-complicated one of the final puzzles before finally getting that big 'ah hah!' moment, or how even though the final puzzle of the level, 'The Lab Rat', was fairly straight forward, it was a long and complex process that left me nerve-wrackingly close to running out the clock.And even then the puzzles and levels are fun regardless, with a wide variety of environments and themes to help each level stand out. (Big shout out to 'The Rival Room', definitely my favorite level in the game)Escape Academy also has a surprisingly robust hint system for those players that need a bit of a hand. Although I did not need to use it during my initial playthrough, I did go back through to see how well the hint system stood up against some of the more abstract/difficult puzzles. Escape Academy definitely surprised me with how good the hints were at providing a small but helpful nudge without spoiling many solutions.I have to be honest, I really love the aesthetic and setting. A secret, prestigious academy for escape artists to refine their trade? Where every lesson is its own escape room with crazy puzzles, all taught by a fun cast of eccentric professors? Sign me up! It really ticks a bunch of similar boxes to similarly popular school-based things like Harry Potter/etc.Unfortunately though, the story, while fun, is fairly bare bones and really only acts as a bit of a segue between levels to provide context to the situation. While there are a few small side conversations you can have with various characters to help flesh them out, these tend to be fairly short with only a few sentences at best.It's a bit of a shame. The game is set up in such a way that each level provides you with a medal/badge upon completion, with you needing 10 badges total to graduate and finish the game. With how everything is laid out, it really feels like the game was supposed to have more of these smaller conversations placed around the game world to flesh out the characters a bit more, intermixed with a few small puzzles here and there to split up the time between the major badge-obtaining moments. I know this game isn't trying to be anything close to something as big and complex as an RPG, but this was definitely an area that felt a bit incomplete: the characters and world are fun! Let me see and interact more with them between all my puzzle solving!Overall though, great game! Can't wait to see more!

_childDocuments_.review: I played this with my friend and it was really fun until we got to the Rival Room. The game then totally broke and nothing worked after we got to the weight puzzle. Then only one of us touched the weights and we were able to get through, but the rotating room puzzle completely broke.We restarted the game twice and restarted Steam, and it still broke when we tried it, so we can't complete the game. _childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderful game to play with your partner or a friend with even natively implemented splitscreen. I love to play it with my girlfriend - the world needs more of such great content! <3The given timeframe for solving a puzzle is mostly appropriate. But you can extend the given time, if you are to slow. You'll receive school notes at the end of a puzzle, which depends on the amount of needed time extentions and and needed advices.Bought the season pass already to have more fun with the game! :)
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: This is a pretty good good, if somewhat short escape room puzzle game. The puzzles are good quality, requiring a decent amount of intuition and observation to suss out the answers without being too obscure or too obvious. They don't hold your hand. Plus, in true escape room style, these come with a time limit. As I said, the main game is pretty short, I finished in four hours. There are a few level pack DLCs which I haven't tried yet though. As with most of my games, this was a Steam Sale purchase, and I would recommend the same for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: I'd leave a neutral review if I could.Overall, I enjoyed the game, the escape rooms and puzzles were decent fun, albeit definitely on the easier side. The story is barely there but we're here for the escape rooms anyway so I didn't mind.For the asking price the game is a bit too short (around 4-6 hours) and barebones in my opinion, and the game doesn't feel well optimized, there's an annoying stuttering issue even though the graphics are pretty basic. None of the graphics presets or resolution changes the fact and the game feels smoother with a mouse than a gamepad for some reason, so it seems like some issue with the game itself. It was borderline unplayable on my monitor, but I could tolerate it on my TV and finish the game. Oh and don't get the game if you get motion sickness easily.There's an obvious comparison to be made with Escape Simulator, and both have their strengths. Simulator has a decent level editor while Academy doesn't, but has split-screen multiplayer, larger levels and in my opinion, a better UI. Simulator also only has 3 (4 with the DLC) themes while most escape rooms in Academy feel unique.There's no replayability here because every puzzle has a set answer. You CAN replay levels but you'll probably only do that to get the achievement for getting an A+ in every level. Because you already know the answers and can even skip most puzzles completely.I'd wait for a sale or get it on gamepass. but I'm still eager for more content.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely buggy. Constant crashes, and when playing co-op the game would frequently de-sync causing puzzles to become unsolvable and force a restart.Even absent the bugs, this is a fairly average puzzle game that compares unfavorably to others in the same genre. Worth playing only if you've exhausted Steam's roster of puzzle games and after they've fixed the bugs.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: I had a lot of fun with this game :D I really enjoyed playing it with my partner. We play a lot of puzzle esc games together, and this game was set up in an unexpected way that we both loved. We're about to buy the expansion packs for the game :D I really liked that an option was included to toggle the split screen on and off, as I get motion sick very easily. The only problem we encountered was that there was an issue with lagging between our two characters during a particular puzzle in a later level. The puzzle wouldn't move forward for my partner as the game registered me as standing on a platform blocking the puzzle, but I was standing directly behind him/ as far away from the puzzle as I possibly could be. The developers did mention that they patched this issue in a recent review though :D <3 Overall, really loved the game, would highly recommend :))
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent game !- The game has a story, so it is really nice because these kind of games usually don't have a story. - Regarding the difficulty, the game isn't hard. Only the last level has the maximum difficult. I don't like when rooms are too hard, so that's why I put this in "pros" but if you like very hard levels, you will find 1 or none.- I prefered these rooms way more than the Escape Simulator ones. I find that they're much more 'alive', whereas in many Escape Simulator rooms (apart from the latest DLC additions) I've had the feeling that they lack life. You're never alone in these rooms : there is always someone who is there or a computer which speaks to you or someone who speaks to you. I also didn't have at all the impression to make random moves (trying to click on random buttons for example) whereas sometimes in Escape Simulator that was the case.I also find the inventory system better than Escape Simulator because it is less complex and you can't drop items. You don't have 10 or 15 items in your inventory as it usually is the case in Escape Simulator. And because you don't drop your items, the rooms stay clean, whereas in Escape Simulator they can quickly become a mess.- There are less rooms than in Escape Simulator.- Escape Simulator has a VR mode. That's not the case for this one.- There is no workshop in Escape Academy.- You can't bind your own keybinds.- Graphics settings are too limited. You can't change your FPS limit for example.Everything I said is subject to change if Escape Academy still receives updates !
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best puzzle games I have played in a long time. I've always been a fan of escape rooms and puzzle games, so this is perfect for me. The puzzles are intuitive but also challenging at times, especially with the threat of a timer in most puzzles, and it is just so satisfying to figure out the answers on my own. The times I did need hints, they were helpful without giving the whole answer on a plate, and other than impacting the score at the end, which is only useful for the achievements, it didn't punish the player at all for using them.The story was compelling and interesting, and I enjoyed navigating the twists and turns while at the Escape Academy. The characters were fun and interesting, and I wish I could have spent more time with them so I could really get to know them better. The world is very interesting and I want to see what more the devs do with this setting. There is a promise of two future DLCs and a free update, so I am looking forwards to what they have planned next.The only major flaw I see is how short the game is. It only takes about six hours if you're going for all of the achievements. On top of that, the replayability is nonexistent, because you've already solved all of the puzzles, so it's only worth it to go back if you're hunting for achievements. I would love to play much much more of this game, because I think it is such a fun concept and it's well-executed. Since I can't get any of my friends to do an escape room with me, at least I got to enjoy these ones. I highly recommend it if you're looking for a fun escape room game to play though.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: For $20, Not worth it. Completed the game in 4 hours without feeling like there was any real challenge. Also, for the DLC to be $15 for 10 more levels in the next year seems like too much money invested for what i can only imagine to be another 4 hours of game play. If you have not played escape simulator, I recommend buying that instead as it has more game play for the money and does not divert any time from escape rooms for a half baked story. Ton more escape rooms in the base game and with community rooms being made so often that there is no shortage of new rooms to play. TLDR: If you are choosing between escape room games, go with escape simulator

_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: I purchased this game for myself and my wife after we got through all of the content in Escape Simulator. This game is good, but not as fun as ES. The rooms are simpler in some ways, more complex and larger in others. After our third level, my wife decided she didn't care for it, and I later decided to start over and finish on my own. I found the game to be a good challenge and the levels were fun. The attempt at a story is nice, which is something that is missing from ES. There are a ton of really bad puns in this game, which in a way are funny.The game is unfortunately quite short. I did a play through several months after stopping my initial playthrough (replaying three levels, one of which is the intro) and it only took me between four and five hours. The asking price is a bit steep for the short experience. However, if you really like escape rooms or this type of puzzle game, it might be worth the asking price. If you are on the fence, just wait for a sale and it'll be worth it. And I see that there is some DLC planned. I will definitely play it.The split screen option was cool, and would make for online play to be much smoother. This is a feature that is certainly missing from ES. Definitely better to play in the same room with someone, but if you can't, this is a good option. Nice touch.One issue. I had the graphics set to ultra and experienced some lag and performance issues. I had to drop down to the setting below this. I have a very good computer and I find it hard to believe that I can't play the game on it's max settings.Update:Updating my review for the season pass. The two DLC are fun and quite challenging. Felt harder than the original game, but it's been a while, so hard to compare. But my escapes came down to the wire on a few. Took me 7.4 hours for both, so still quite a bit expensive for what you get, but I had an escape room itch that needed to be scratched. Worth it on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: This is an escape game where you have to solve puzzles to escape. However, it wasn't a hit with me. The puzzles were fine but nothing too groundbreaking (I was only taken by surprise once or twice). The game is kind of janky and restricted, which shows. The drawings are pretty  good but the 3D environments (which is where you'll be actually playing) are not good at all. The game does have an overarching story, though, so if you really want a videogame escape game with that, you could pick this game up.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: This game is such a blast, especially with a friend. The puzzles are just the right level of difficult, with some being easier than others. It definitely felt like a good challenge and I loved the twist on the escape room genre. The puzzle designs are gorgeous and really creative too. I especially love the stained glass window badges you collect and the fact that items from each escape classroom appear in your room as you complete each one. Only criticism is the game is definitely a little short and probably not super replayable but the tournament of puzzles is a good add on, I preferred to play with a friend rather than against them though.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: So... here's the thing, I really liked the game.  It was a fun, thematic, story-driven escape game.  I figured I'd like it and I did.  The problem is that it's just so short.  I think you can get a lot more play time from more puzzles and such with other games for the $20 price tag.  Maybe if you can get it for $5 - $10 then I'd definitely recommend it.  Also, it has no replayability.  Once you learn the puzzle, that's it.  I guess you could challenge yourself to speedrun it if you're into that sort of thing but that's about the only replay value this offers.  If you're new to this genre of games, check out The Room series instead.Oh, and one other thing, I'm not sure what the point of co-op is.  IRL escape rooms are great for groups and teams, but these puzzles aren't nearly that complex.  I played the whole thing solo in about 5 hours, and if you had two people working on these, I imagine you'd get more value out of renting a movie.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: It's no secret that I really, really like this game. The only thing I don't like is that it's so short.I went in expecting just a puzzle game, and ended up with a full fledged story, main character, villain and everything, And without giving anything away, this is one of the few instances I felt the villain felt threatening to both the main character and the player, so yeah, wish there had been more game to enjoy.As for the puzzles, I like them, but I would put them under "The Room" series level in complexity and agility. However, I'm glad to inform they're not "Deponia" type: you can get yourself out of every single puzzle by yourself, or at most, with one or two hints.However, I'll say, when I saw the main character I was expecting some sort of nice, laid back story, not everything the poor guy goes through. Like, seriously, I would need therapy after going to that school XD.If you like puzzle and point and click games, this one is for you. You won't regret it.

The puzzles are generally pretty easy if you've played escape rooms before, but I found the time pressure made it much more intense and engaging. I think they did a really good job on the variety of the puzzles and the theme that tied it all together. Overall, a bunch of fun and well worth the money if you like this kind of thing like me.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: I do recommend this game, but not at full price. I would say I found the experience average, with some puzzles being very frustrating (I refused to use hints until the final room). It felt like I would hit a brick wall and often times the answer would turn out to be really simple, but because the developer would have a different mindset to the player, the puzzle really wouldn't feel simple. A few frustrations aside, the game is enjoyable and worth trying if you are into puzzle games.If you liked this review, check out my

_childDocuments_.review: It's way shorter than I expected. Seems like 3 hours is all I needed. Tbh I left the game open to have a bathroom break. At the same time there are a handful of solutions that do not make sense or are misleading where there environment sets you up to focus on a different (incorrect) solution to the puzzle. All by all if you want a puzzle game that is not actually challenging, this is a good choice. But that's about it.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: This a great and fantastic game that I recommend everyone to play. Though, I wanna comment on the recent Tournament of Puzzles DLC. I'm going to be honest, I was pretty disappointed to find out in what would probably be their final DLC for the game, was a PvP mode. I thought, "Who asked for a PvP mode? Why PvP?". Not only is player retention simply not there for it, the mainline gameplay is far much superior in every way. As noted by the devs, the environments in the Tournaments of Puzzles are truly some of the biggest and coolest looking stuff I've seen from the game. While its a cool addition to the game, the resources and time used to make it should've been saved for another mainline DLC (even for a sequel I would say). This mainline DLC (had it existed), would've truly been THE ONE. Even Bigger and cooler looking environments, with some of the most fun, interactive, and thematic puzzles to date. Hope it doesn't end here. I would love to see more of Escape Academy from Coin Crew Games.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: 5/10 Puzzle Solving/Escape Room 4 - 7 Hours 3/10Escape Academy is an escape room based puzzle game with features about 10 missions of varying length (most missions take around 15 - 30 minutes each). There really isn't much else to say about it. There is a huge array of puzzles with some really creative environments and logic thrown in with the only problem is that most puzzles boil down to either being far too easy, or just simply brute forcing until you get them.The only thing I really want to talk about are the problems I experienced. The intro sound (before the main menu) is unbearably loud and the volume controls don't change this. I played this game co-op with a friend and at the end of each mission the game soft locked and I was unable to go to the main menu, or anywhere and I had to force close the game each time, i'd say this happened to me for all but 2 missions. The game also put my monitors refresh rate to 67hz, but there are also no FPS settings in the menu and the game constantly felt like it was stuttering and dropping frames. My monitor is 177hz and this title didn't register in GeForce Experience so it didn't have any settings to optimise.If you haven't played Escape Simulator i'd highly recommend that over this (it also features custom maps). I think this game is good, but the problems I had playing it outweigh the actual gaming experience.

_childDocuments_.review: This was a great electronic escape room experience.  My spouse and I both got it and played through together, which was really nice to be able to do. The game did tend to freeze on us after completing a mission, but it was after our progress was saved at least.  Just meant we had to kill it and restart a session a few times in the course of beating it.  Still, a really fun game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was an amazing find, a gem of puzzle/escape room games. _childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: An unobtrusive puzzle game called Escape Academy is an interesting surprise in this genre. The puzzle sets are reminiscent of The Room series, which itself is inspired by escape room games that can be found in every major city. In this game, you become a student at an academy specializing in evasion. You learn to adapt to the situation, use objects and solve various ciphers around you to open locks and doors.Graphically, the game has a comic feel. You won't enjoy big panoramas, but you'll still be pleased enough. The main goal of the developers was to create that comic atmosphere where you become the main hero of the academy. And as it usually happens in similarly tuned scenarios, you also have your rival here, who teases you while playing.Puzzle sets (or escape rooms if you prefer) are marked by difficulty and you usually know in advance how much time you have to solve them. In case you get stuck, there is no need to "google". The game has its own "hints" system, which is quite helpful.Control is not very intuitive (that is, as far as PC is concerned). Working with the inventory, entering characters and picking up some items is a bit clumsy and if you are pressed for time they delay your progress quite a bit. But what the creators succeeded in doing is pinning various notes, in case you are solving a cipher.The game has a Season Pass available, which will add more content and we will probably be able to look forward to the continuation of the story. The latter is not a strong point, but the final twist has its charm.My rating: 8.6/10
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: Fun, fairly short game. Most of the puzzles weren't too difficult for me, but there were a couple that stumped me for a while. My sense of difficulty is also a bit skewed since I've played a lot of games in this genre before, so people that don't have as much experience would probably think it's harder. They also made the puzzles have a good sense of tension. There were multiple levels where I definitely was aware of the time counting down. Overall definitely recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: The game is absolutely wonderful.The story is existent (which is already a relative upgrade over most most other games in the genre), the art direction is nice and consistent, and above all - the puzzles are brilliant. There wasn't even a single puzzle where I felt I had to guess, nor did I feel that puzzles were obvious or easy.A great, balanced journey, that I enjoyed finishing in a few hours.Highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: I can't speak as to this game being a co-op experience, but as a single player I enjoyed it very much. It took me 9 hours to complete all the rooms with an A+ score, but you can finish the game without ever gaining a single A+ score.This game takes you through a series of escape rooms, all of which have a valid reason for granting you only a limited time to complete it successfully. This adds a bit of spice to the task of figuring out how to solve all the puzzles in each room. In reality though, for players who do not enjoy time pressure, once your time runs out you can just get extra time which only results in a lower grade (it is an academy, after all) for completing each room.The story, characters, and everything else was fine, and I didn't experience any bugs during my playtime. And while I saw a twist coming in the story, it wasn't exactly what I anticipated.All in all a comfortable recommendation for players who enjoy puzzle solving.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderful 2-player online escape room game that I think surpasses even "We Were Here". In "We Were Here", many of the puzzles rely heavily on the fact that you can't see each others' screens, forcing you to clumsily describe obscure scenes. Escape Academy, on the other hand, is the complete opposite - you see your teammate's screen at  times, even when playing online!  This was a bit annoying because you're forced to play on half a screen. However, it's also fairly convenient because you can easily share clues without having to vocalize them.The puzzles in this game feel much more like actual escape-room puzzles. There is a hint system, but we never needed to use it because all the puzzles are fair and straightforward.  In fact they are a bit on the easy side, but not so much that the game is boring.There is the semblance of a storyline, but it's pretty bare-bones. Don't come in expecting Danganronpa.  The game has 11 (and a half) escape rooms, with about 4.5 hours of content.  There's not really any replay value - once you beat it, you're done.We encountered numerous bugs, but fortunately none of them were game-breaking.  We had two crashes, but both occurred in the overworld, so we didn't lose any progress. There were also multiple times when the puzzles desynced. Fortunately even then, either player can solve the puzzle, and it will still count for both of them. Two achievements are broken as of this writing.Overall I think this is the best multiplayer escape room game of . I think it's worth the $20 asking price, and it's easily worth the $0 if you already own PC Gamepass.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: What a weird, wonderful, creative game. Had a blast playing the base game with a friend, all of the puzzles were satisfyingly challenging and felt great to crack. The game really captures the feeling of escape rooms, frantically running around at the start and shouting out everything you see in a confusion until it all starts to piece together.  We only got truly stumped at 2-3 points throughout, and the game's generous hint system makes sure you're never stuck for long. Each room has a time limit, but the limits are high enough that we never felt truly pressured by them (and I don't consider myself particularly good at puzzles).Beat the base game in 5.5 hours which might put some people off with the $20 price tag, but every second of gameplay was so lovingly and intricately crafted that it felt entirely fair, especially if you pick the game up on one of its frequent sales. I was already excited to dive into the DLCs, and then they drop a big free content update just for the hell of it? Great game, great devs, and if you look at this game and think you'll enjoy it, you absolutely will.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: This game absolutely shines in its puzzle writing. The game may be short (like under 10 hours in total if you count all the DLC in it) but the puzzles are absolutely fantastic. None of them feel unfair and solving them always made me feel accomplished.What makes this game stand out among other escape puzzle games is the story. It's full of camp but it adds some very enjoyable context to everything that's going on in each puzzle.If you like escape rooms or puzzles at all, this is a solid recommendation.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: Escape Academy is a great example of how mixing genres can sometimes just turn out meh, but you still enjoy your time. To put it succinctly: a Harry Potter style "year of school" story works best when the story is long so you feel the passage of time, but escape room puzzles are dense in design so there aren't enough to fill out that whole year well.There are something like 8-10 fun and well-crafted puzzle rooms at the core of the game. Since they're where the real gameplay is at, their good design is enough for me to recommend it. They also introduce 6+ unique characters that would be fun to get to know, but you interact with each only like 3 times, severely limiting the scope of the "academy" aspect to the game. So I'd say get this game if you're interested in puzzles, not if you're fiending for a great story.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: Starting with the bad.-The dialog is boring and useless, the story basically tells itself through the environment anyways. -The timers feel immersion breaking / out of place and could be replaced with in-world visuals, the room filling up with water is a good example. -There's no support for widescreen resolutions ie: 1920 x 1200, had to play in 1920 x 1080. The controls are a bit finicky and the movement feels like it has acceleration or something as if its designed to be played with a controller. -The game suggests you use a pen and paper in real life even though there are methods to pin puzzle objects to your screen and an in- game notepad I feel would serve as a better solution.-Failing the timer on a puzzle forces you to either take a lesser grade by adding time or quitting straight to the main menu even though you could mid puzzle, just leave the puzzle and easily re-enter to reset it, kinda confusing there isn't a restart button for puzzles.-I hate the water jug puzzle that seemingly needs to be in every adventure puzzle game or escape room. I'm on the fence of whether this is homage to the genre or just a lazy thing to insert. Either way if you've done it 20 years ago you know the exact solution and it just feels like its in the way.Now the good parts.-The visuals style and themes are well done. -The puzzles are fun with some challenge but not so esoteric that you feel the need to brute force or look up guides.-None of the puzzles feel like they're repeating themes / scenarios or puzzle mechanics.-Didn't run into any bugs.-For $20 I feel a 5-6hr game is worth it but I could understand it being an issue for a lot of users when there is a sea of quality games on steam at that price point or lower with many times that amount of content. I did find myself wanting more at the end but not because it was too short but because it was so good.In short if you're a fan of the genre of escape room type games I highly recommend it, not that you really have much of a choice in this genre for recent releases.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: The base game is pretty fun, if a little oversimplified. We never really got stuck on anything.I do like the system of showing a puzzle summary at the end of the level, to show you what you might have missed out on because your partner did a particular bit.What is not fun, however, is the tournament of puzzles 'DLC'. We played one of each before concluding they were too repetitive and the adversarial format wasn't fun. If one player falls behind there's no real way to catch up so unless you're equally talented at the various puzzles the matches will often end in curbstomps.Nevertheless the base game will give you a few hours of coop fun so I can recommend this.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderful game that plays a lot like an escape room. Most of the puzzles are something that could be in the real world, only a handful are "video game" puzzles. All of the clues are pretty well presented and follow along directly to their puzzle. My only gripe is the last puzzle which felt more like a word puzzle than an escape room.

_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly a bit dissapointing to me, it had some fun puzzles but a few others leaned on math problems too much for my taste of escape rooms ( feels cheap imo when the best puzzle you can think of is giving the player a math problem to solve ) but besides personal preferences, i would say the biggest problem of the game is it seems like it was supposed to be a 1 player game.Interactions get fairly whacky when 2 players are trying to do the same puzzles and sometimes some boxes would open just for my friend even if i was the one to put the code in. There also were so many bugs that required us to restart the game, mostly when we both would press Enter to skip the dialogue at the same time.On sale the game is fine but was a very sour experience for us compared to escape simulator and the we were here series.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: If you're familiar with other escape/puzzle games, you'll be very disappointed with this one. It's just sooo easy and short. I don't know why people recommended this, but if you are an experienced escapist, look for another game.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: My friend picked this game up for him and I as we both love escape room type games. It is a very fun and easy game, the puzzles are challenging but not overly hard. Some are more challenging than others and (probably my own fault) the answer wasn't always immidiently obvious and took some time to find but it was never so bad that we needed to use hints. And getting the achievements are very easy if you know what you're doing. Came for the puzzles, stayed for the rat
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: Very good (and very quick) puzzle game. I wish it had more of a meta wrapped around the puzzling, maybe something with actually going to school and classes and interacting with other students. I played solo and it was really easy. I think playing co-op would be way too easy for any experienced puzzlers.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: A solid entry in the "escape room" genre, with an upcoming, optional "versus" mode.Pros:* Excellent puzzle quality.* Good music and voice acting.Cons:* I find math puzzles to be tedious in puzzle games - guess what this has several instances of?Meh:* I hate timers on puzzle games - guess what this game has, on almost every level?* I especially hate timers on puzzle games w/ a "screw around with the puzzle until you solve it" type minigames - guess what this has a few instances of?TL;DR: If don't like puzzles, avoid.  If you don't mind the timer, 8/10 - else, 6/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: In terms of co-op puzzlers, this one is not great in terms of puzzles, but it tries to have fun characters and story and that's where the game undoes it's own progress. A boring and sometimes outright annoying cast; the devs should just have forgot the story entirely. But you know, I still played it and had fun with my friend.HOWEVER, then there's this Tournament of Puzzles thing and OH MY GOD SHUT UP COACH. Everything that was bad in the main game is WORSE here. The only fun thing is the power up box and I know I was just trolling my friend at one point. You can run into the same puzzles MULTIPLE TIMES in one round and it's not impossible to get the same randomized SOLUTION more than once as well. This is a puzzle game sin, and just to make sure I left this review the Coach Yoach character just SCREAMS IN YOUR EAR anytime anyone does anything, and his voice lines don't even take the context of the match into play. Do not bother, go play We Were Here or Escape Simulator or anything else you can find. There's nothing memorable here, and the writing and characters will erase any good memories it could have left.

Being able to see though the other players eyes made for a great Quality of Life feature. The game did bug out sometimes after escaping a room, and we'd both have to reboot the game. _childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: If you want to play this game singleplayer, this isn't the review for you.Very often in multiplayer, puzzle elements will become desynchronised, meaning that a moving piece could show up entirely different on the other player's gameplay. This means that the intended and only correct solution will work for one person, but the other will not be able to progress because inputs work differently on their personal version of the puzzle element.In other words, if you want to play this multiplayer, get ready to face a lot of broken puzzles.

Tried re-booting the game several times and nothing loaded. Looking online and this has been a problem since they have released this game and they still haven't fixed it.. really pathetic on their part...
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: I really wish this game wasn't as hard as it is. If the premise is a puzzle game but timed, just make the puzzles and when we figure out the solution let us finish the level. Too many of these single points where you are gonna need either pause all action and figure out this one thing or you are just gonna fail this one run, not that it really matters cause you can just replay the level and get back there, which, kindof makes the timed aspect redundant. I feel like, if its gonna be timed, I should be able to figure it out within one run, maybe not where I can still complete the run but where I dont have to replay the run multiple times more. And the annoying voiceovers that just repeats constantly isnt making it easier. Shame really, some levels were really rewarding and more engaging cause of the timer. Just for an example, the restaurant level, figured it all out, beat the buzzer with one minute, first try.Any level with the stupid red, white, blue shapes, forget it.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: It starts off charming enough, but the difficulty of the puzzles scale at an uneven rate. Some puzzles are easier than the game indicates, others are harder than the game indicates. Oh, and if you were hoping to be a perfectionist and want to get A+ on all of the puzzles, don't bother using hints. If you take too long on a puzzle, just quit out of it and try again. This part has allegedly been fixed in a very recent (as of this edit) quality of life update which makes replayable levels track the best grade you've gotten. Whether or not this affects the Honor Roll and Overachiever achievements has yet to be seen.All in all, you have a game that has uneven difficulty, a lackluster ending, and is too short of a game to justify paying $20 for it, let alone the additional $15 you would have to spend to invest in a season pass. Most people would say to wait for this game to be on sale instead of paying the game for full price, but after playing through all of it, this feels more like a demo instead of a fully-fledged game.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: At first, I loved this game. The Island DLC, great. The time one, eh, got kinda not co-op and more head to head. This tournament thing? Sucks. We couldn't even finish it because I got stuck, and the other person was light years ahead. THAT IS NOT FUN. THAT IS NOT THE GAME I PAID FOR. Honestly, don't want to play anymore. It's ruined.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: The puzzles were a lot of fun, if not a bit too easy. The puzzles were very well designed, and this is a great escape room game to play with a friend. I did have a bit of trouble with desync in one of the levels, but I still can't figure out if it was on our end, or if it was on the game's end. It did happen several times in a row on the same level until we brute forced our way through it, but it only happened on that level so who knows.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: Attempts to cover up weak but time consuming puzzles with a timer to make it "difficult." They're not actually difficult to solve, just difficult to finish within the time limit, creating an artificial sense of urgency. I love puzzle games and I've played many of them. This one is by far the worst. Puzzle games should be challenging, but fun, and leave you with a sense of accomplishment when you solve them, not frustrating and a bunch of time-consuming busy work transcribing information. It's generally not hard to figure out  to do in this game, it just takes forever to do it. And I hate timers - all they do is stress me out and ruin the fun. I tried to ignore the timer, but it's difficult, especially when the game stops you when you hit the time limit with a big YOU FAILED message before allowing you to continue. Overall, just an annoying experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

Was excited for the dlc, but it costs $10 for what is probably only a few hours of content. Cannot recommend unless it's on sale for like $5.

_childDocuments_.review: okay so first of all, the games content is fun, the riddles are fun to solve and its not just a tiny room like in "escape simulator". its definately worth playing if you like escape rooms and dont care about the surrounded quality. the content is fine!BUT....1) when you play with friends, you are forced to be in a vertical split screen mode, with an annoying limited view, as there is no FOV slider available. and when using remote play, everyone but the host has a huge ping.2) compared to the other game, this one here has a campaign and not just levels to choose from. though the story or "visual novel" is bland and boring.3) the graphics are horrible and you cant customize anything, not even pick your character. 4) the movement is a bit clunkyfor 6 hours of content its 2 bucks more expensive than the other game, but offers a roadmap with new content being added in the next year/s. though it might cost extra. meanwhile in escape simulator you can play community maps, made by users. so, in the end it depends on how much you care about those negative things...
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: Some of the puzzles just straight up didn't make sense and had to be brute forced to solve them, very short game and imo not worth the price tag. The split screen online co-op made it too easy as well, it should just be your view so that your partner can describe what they see instead of you being able to see both views. Would not recommend this game to anyone, spend your money on the We Were Here series instead or play some Escape Room Simulator as it has so much more worthwhile content.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: The game plays very well and has some visually interesting levels. But the story line is essentially a non existent generic story with a less than impressive twist. Additionally the game is incredibly short; I finished the entire game within three hours. For a 20$ price tag/ you can get games that will give you 100+ hours
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

Find a item in one puzzle and use it outside the so called test area to solve a game wide puzzle or anything. And with the time you can not experiment as much as you would like. _childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: I got this in The Great Escape Room Bundle from Humble Bundle. It has been the least interesting of the games I have played so far. The veneer of a story just highlights how arbitrary most of the puzzles are, rather than having something thematically tied to the escape room. Some of the puzzles make sense for where they are (garden), but the more common "figure out a sequence of numbers or shapes" just seems out of place or random. This game had a higher frequency of "what do you even want from me?" and "I know what you want, but the interface is too opaque for me to see how to give you the answer" than competing games.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: Played this in online co-op with my wife.  It was very fun, had a good level of challenge but all the puzzles made sense and were possible to figure out.  We did have a minor issue where one of us would randomly get disconnected which would end the session and we'd lose all progress on the escape room, but luckily this only happened twice so it wasn't enough of a deal breaker
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: All in all, escape academy is a very satisfying escape game. The levels were very well done and i loved all except one or two that didn't vibe with me.Almost all levels are build in a way that you don't necessarily need a partner but profit greatly from playing it with one. The story is also surprisingly goodl, both me and my friend thought it was very basic and predictable but the twist we expected never happened and we were surprised by the turn the story took eventually.It took us ~5 hours to complete the base game.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: Fun escape room game with a story to play through. I did the base game in around 5.5 hours. Base game has a good variety of puzzles and didn't repeat stuff, but some of the DLC has repeating puzzles. They should have used the same puzzle type and changed how to solve it, made some of the rooms really easy after you did the earlier ones since you didn't have to figure out some of the repeated puzzles.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: Played this game with my significant other and we both really enjoyed it. There were a few puzzles I didn't enjoy, mainly because they felt like more traditional puzzles than escape room style puzzles (Mainly the 2nd and 3rd puzzles in the Rival Room, and some at the very end) but the majority of them were really fun.I always love a game that has local coop as an option. And for online coop I liked the ability to toggle split screen view with the press of a button, it really reduced frustration to be able to easily see what your partner is looking at.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: I actually received Escape Academy for free from an Epic Games giveaway, but I loved it so much that I bought it on Steam to add to my collection. I played the entire story campaign with a friend through local co-op with Parsec, and it was a really fun and memorable experience.The puzzles are really creative, with just the right difficulty, neither too simple nor too complicated. The gameplay experience was smooth with minimal visual bugs and zero crashes so far. The storyline is interesting and does add an element of mystery to the story.In summary, this game is absolutely worth it and you will easily get 10+ hours out of the story mode alone, while being an absolute blast to crack puzzles, especially in co-op mode.UPDATE: My buddy and I freaking love the new Tournament of Puzzles! PVP definitely adds more adrenaline to the puzzle solving experience than just a timer. This game is a no-brainer at this point; trust me, you'll have no regrets!
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: An escape room game designed as a school where you learn to be an escape artist. Drawn art style is interesting and nice but the 3D modeling is kinda meh. Puzzles aren't super hard, but because each one has a time limit, the pressure can sometimes make you miss a clue. There are definitely a few head scratchers. The storyline and characters are for the most part interesting. Only the dlc anti-escape island was a little lackluster compared to the others.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: This was my first time doing any escape rooms (real life or video game), and I had fun. I like how the rooms feel immersive. I found all the puzzles to be doable without hints, but there were a few rooms that felt stingy on the time limit for a solo player. Thankfully you can extend the timer, so whatever.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: i am obsessed with escape rooms irl, and this game perfectly captures the essence of an escape room online. as soon as i finished the main campaign, i immediately bought all the DLC to get more content. the puzzles are challenging and fun, the story is awesome, and i just couldn't get enough !!!! can't wait for more updates, this is probably my favourite game i've played in a long time!
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: Absolute blast of a game with some solid replayability. I enjoyed the story parts and almost all of the puzzles - if they involved math or turning a room, they have my wrath, but that may be personal - and while the characters were mostly one-note, they were a pretty cool note.
