_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: The art style and character illustrations are great. There's a good variety of escape rooms and the puzzle designs are often really interesting. I did not initially think I would enjoy there being levels with time limits but I think it enhances the experience and adds a fun sense of urgency to the gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: This game shows that a puzzle game in a visual novel format works. The puzzles are fun and engaging while the story from the main game and dlcs are enjoyable. This team did a great job making this game. I played this game solo and the puzzles were fun, I assume that doing it with a friend will be just as enjoyable.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: I can not stress enough how amazing this game is. I hate spending money on games, and I have 0 regrets about giving escape academy my money for every DLC they make. I'm hoping for a 2nd game as there simply isn't a better escape room game on the market. The plot line, easy game play and puzzles are all well done.10/10 gameits like halo 2 and halo 3 met and had a baby, also go play animal well.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: An interesting story based puzzle game, with escape rooms themed to various areas of this school for Escape Artists. I wish there was more interaction with the characters, or even the ability to customize my character based on the few times it's 3rd person, but overall the unique storyline, voices, and cool characters make for a fun twist on Escape Room video games.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyable escape-style game, inspired me to also get Escape Simulator (they look very alike but not the same team!)This one felt very creative with calming/pleasing visuals, and the level and puzzle design were a treat. Puzzles not too difficult, but some can be a bit twisty.Great to play with another person side-by-side, as well as enjoying some of the vs. modes in couch co-op.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: Forgot to write review back in the day butThis game is **amazing** for long distance (or short distance) couples! Each mission is about 20 to 45 minutes and we had loads of fun figuring everything out, doing about 1 to 2 missions each session and following the story!A small downside however was that we couldnt select which charachter (the girl of the guy) we were or atleast couldn't figure out how to change that.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: Clever and varying puzzles, nice story and atmosphere.It is not optimized to play online multiplayer, it lags and stutters. I assume it works better in local co-opFor the developers I would recommend checking the control scheme that Escape Simulator uses. That is the best I have seen so far. Easier to use items, show each other stuff etc. The movement is perfect in that game.Still enjoyed this one and will most likely pick up the DLC in the future
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: Escape academy is a really fun coop game. It was fun to go through the levels and i liked the story for what it was. i think there is quite a lack of content though, we had completed the game around 10 hours including the dlc and the new update sounds cool but i like escape rooms for the puzzles and collaboration not the competitiveness. so pvp content doesn't really fit the genre for me personally, Though we did test it out once and it was fun for what it was at the time.  I think the game would do well with community maps just for more content.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: The puzzles are extremely fun and interesting. With only a few frustrating ones and most of those are in the DLC. The story is incredibly charming. It's light enough to not get in the way, but involved enough to actually feel like a part of the experience. I thought I'd hate the timer but honestly I really liked solving all these puzzles under the gun. If you like first-person puzzlers, this one's up there with some of the best.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: Hands-down one of the best escape room games on Steam. The art design is beautiful, the puzzles are clever and intuitive, the timer adds a level of tension that a lot of other escape room games don't have, and it's all wrapped up in a surprisingly good story that kept me engaged from start to finish. 10/10, hope they wind up putting out more DLC in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: Great game with many levels that offer a good challenge. Only downside would be 100% the base game and having missing achievements because they are tied to the DLC. Was going to get them in the future anyways, but I believe those achievements should be paired with the DLC and no with the base game. Playing with a friend is the best way to go!
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: Had a fun time!Desync issues caused myself and the friend I was playing with to have some solid confusion a couple times, but thankfully it didn't happen in the Rival Room like some of the other reviews I read before buying the game said.The puzzles are relatively simple as escape rooms go and there's a lot of signposting if you pay attention, so it's not a huge challenge if you're looking for that (though the fact that they put "blissfully approachable" as a featured quote in the trailer should tip you off to that before you buy). The story is pretty decent. I enjoyed it, nothing groundbreaking, but I wasn't really expecting a crazy story from this. If you like the pitch in the trailer, that's pretty much the story you're getting.The game doesn't have a strong co-op focus. All the puzzles are completable solo, and they don't change for co-op sessions (though I will admit, having the key on one end of the split-screen and the puzzle on the other did make things go a little nicer)Price-wise, I think it's pretty reasonable. it's not super long as games go for $20, but considering going to a real-life escape room is about double the price per person for one room, I don't mind it too much. It has gone on sale relatively regularly though, so if $20 is hard to stomach, you can pick it up for a little less if you're patient.Haven't yet tried the DLCs and I'm not sure if I will, but we'll see.Also you can pet the digital dog and non-digital rat.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, this is my favourite puzzle co-op game so far!The story is intriguing, the characters are interesting (my favourite is definitely Professor Bonilla), the puzzles are fun - even the hard ones -, and the visuals are stylized, colourful, and pretty! I wish this game was longer. I still have to play the DLCs, but I'm looking forward to more content surrounding the Escape Academy universe! I'd love to know more about the characters as well, including more about their backgrounds.I played this with a friend and we had a LOT of fun! We really wished the game didn't end.Thank you Skull for the amazing gift!
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing!The puzzles are great, and there is an option for multiplayer too, so you can solve them with a friend.The lore pulled me in and I couldn't stop playing.And the game is updated regularly! The developers are always releasing new DLCs!This is a must play game for anyone who likes puzzles and a good story,
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun!  All the rooms are challenging, but not too hard.  There is a hint option if you get stuck, and if you run out of time, you can always continue and get more time.  I bought the bundle because I heard the game was good, and I'm glad I did.  I love escape room games, and this is definitely the best one I have ever played so far.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: Delightful escape room game - definitely the best of its kind that I've played so far, with fun characters and writing, and puzzles that I could see used in a real escape room (even the ones that get a bit more deadly than a real escape room could be). If you like enjoy puzzles and/or escape rooms, you'll love this
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: It's a love letter to puzzle lovers and logical thinkers and i'm only writing this so we can get a third DLC.You don't need to recite Shakespeare, you don't need to know the average distance to the moon and you don't need to know the airspeed velocity of an European swallow - Everything you need to solve the puzzles is cleverly tucked away in the environment and your only task is to throw your raw brainpower at it.  If that doesn't sell you on it then it also scratches that itch you've always had to join a secret society and alsoexperience a less traumatic academic career.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of escape rooms, this game is fantastic! The puzzles and rooms are very creative. Beyond that, I think one aspect that makes this game stand out from other escape games is that it is not just a collection of themed rooms but has an overarching narrative that is clever and creative with a really fun cast of characters. I love how you get escape puzzles and also a great story! I would highly recommend this game for puzzle/escape fans.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: A fun point and click adventure! The story is just there and I wouldn't have missed it, (it's not bad, just unnecessary imho for this  game) but it's really just a back drop for the puzzles anyway. The environments are beautifully crafted and there's plenty of puzzles that will have you really thinking to get through them (those hints are quite helpful sometimes.) while also giving you enough moderate to easy ones to keep the progress going and to avoid undue frustration.If you like puzzles and point and click games, this one is a gem!
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: This is an extremely fun game with the only negative being that it is very short. Expect that the base game and both DLC will take 10 hours or less, even with a couple of level restarts trying for A+. I would recommend picking it up on a bit of a sale, as the base price is steep for what you are getting.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: Great game with great puzzles, fun and challenging without frustrating the player. With a bit of logic and attention, it's possible to go through the game in no time. The cons are the relative short time of game, which I felt it could be a bit longer, and the buggy multiplayer, ocasionally desyncing me and my friend games. Apart from that, pretty solid game.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: This is a surprisingly unique experience to some of the other escape room games I've played. Not necessarily because of the puzzles themselves, but just in terms of gameplay. For each room there is a countdown timer, and because of that, I found the puzzles to be much simpler and more visually clear on what you need to do. I actually liked this, even though I found a lot of the puzzles easy, there was still a thrill you get from having the pressure of a timer. I actually found the biggest hindrance was just getting stuck in my own head and over-complicating things, since that's what I'm used to in escape room games that give you infinite time to solve. My only complaint is that I wish there had been more! I was really interested in the characters of the academy and would like to know more about them. Here's to hoping for a sequel?Also Turmeric the rat is the greatest thing that has ever happened to me in any escape room game ever I love her so much.I give it:Down with AI/10
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: A fun escape room game. Played it local co-op with my gf, and it worked fine. It had some stutter issues tho, and it made me a bit motion sick. The game itself is fun. A good variation of puzzles that are logical and not over-complicated. The hint-system is nice to use if you are stuck. Story is basic, but it fits good enough with the gameplay, and the puzzle rooms makes sense.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: Fine puzzles and time pressure like real escape rooms. Most of them are not hard to solve (which means if you are looking for a real challenge you may want to avoid this game). There are some funny interactions between characters but not much. The first DLC is fine too (although still not challenging enough IMO)
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: Great escape room game with fun characters and challenging puzzles. The one aspect I didn't like is a small usability thing: the game has a split screen multiplayer mode, but for some reason you can open that split screen view on Network play - as a matter of fact it's open by default, forcing you to press 'Z' to close it whenever a level starts. Being able to see what your partner sees is a huge advantage, since communication is half the fun of an escape room. However, this is not a big enough issue to take away from the fantastic game play.10/10!
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: JUST downloaded this game last night for the first time because me and a friend wanted a new co-op game to play. We're over an hour from each other but still only a state away, and we started having some issues while playing. We've made it through the entire game without problems and playing together online up until the arena level where we're competing against our rival, and it's working only up until the rotating cube puzzle. When we get there, my friend is doing the puzzle because she knows what's going on, and we almost immediately go out of sync.We both realize, we log out and go back in, restarting the level from the very beginning and it happens again but so much worse. It's gotten so out of sync for both of us, my timer at the top of the screen is still counting down from 22:00 and her's is at 17:00. When I view her screen in the split screen mode, her character is glitching off the map and it's doing the same puzzle we finished 5 minutes ago. It seems like we're not the first people to have had issues with this portion of the game either, and if things were different I would be writing a completely different review.If the bug gets fixed it would be greatly appreciated. We both have genuinely enjoyed the game so far and we've almost finished it up to this point!
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: I'm glad I found this game because I love puzzles and have played Escape Simulator and many other puzzle games. Got this on sale for $13 and definitely worth it. Played solo and enjoyed the story. For someone who has experience in escape rooms and puzzles, you'll find yourself enjoying the slight challenge of solving the rooms. For others, you may be relying on the hints a lot. I used the hint feature twice and after seeing it, would be like "oh duh it was right in front of me." The rooms have timers (about 20min) but I liked that aspect and never went over time (although I would pause to think sometimes). Dialog with characters are short and rooms have multiple layers to extend game play. After you finish a room the game kinda walks you through the puzzles so you understand.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: This game is absolutely amazing. If you like puzzles, strategy, and escape rooms, this game is perfect for you. You can play multiplayer or single player. Either way, this is super fun. I absolutely loved this game, me and a friend played it along with the two DLC's and are invested for any others that will come out in the future. 10 out of 10. I want to commend the makers of this game because this is a beautiful and masterpiece of a game. This brought me so much joy and gave me so much fun to do. I think this is VERY underrated. This game deserves to be known much more than it is. Amazing game. Love it.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: Have you seen that Escape Room horror/thriller movie? This game is if that movie was good. The puzzles are fun, actual puzzles. There are time limits but they're reasonable and you can get hints if you need them. Much more fun with two players, but possible with one. The story can get a little bonkers at times but it's really fun and entertaining. The character design is pretty good too.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: Let me be up front, I DID get this game on sale.I liked most of the puzzles.  Often my biggest hang-ups where when I over complicated something.  There were a few that I'm still not fully sure how I solved.  The hint system is mostly fine.The 'pin item' system needs adjusting.  More often than not, the item I pinned sat over the area I needed to be interacting with and made it a giant pain, forcing me to waste time copying things down that I shouldn't have to.  I did attempt to move the item to a different corner with no success so if this IS a thing, I couldn't get it to work.While I don't mind the timer, not a fan of the maps where there's a lot 'go go go' and 'hurry up' kind of dialog from other characters or just the noise of the environment.  I get it's supposed to be 'high pressure' for some of these but it makes thinking very difficult.The story was fine.  Nothing earth shattering but I play enough Escape Rooms without a ton of story so that didn't bother me.Overall, I enjoyed the game.  Though I understand the hesitancy for the price.  If you're really not sure, play the demo and at least at the time of writing this, it's on Game Pass.  But yeah, had a good time.I will just add I have NOT tried to do any of the multiplayer stuff yet.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: It was good.The gameplay follows an escape-the-room style. The controls for it make a lot of sense, they work very well and nothing was broken or made difficult by the controls, they worked the way they should for this type of game. The puzzles themselves are well designed, and none of them are too challenging they can all be done without anything too absurd needed to solve them and there is no outside knowledge needed, although it did help me with a few of the puzzles to get the answer easier. There are also hints available that are very helpful without giving the whole thing away although it will sometimes give you hints for things you’re not working on and thus it can be frustrating if you didn’t need help with that aspect. The environments and the general rooms themselves are pretty interesting, the one on the ship, in particular, is well-designed and has a lot of fun. There is a mechanic where the player is able to pin items they’ve gathered to the screen to make it easier to see them(as if the player had the object in their hands or next to them and can look at it without needing to navigate a menu) while this is helpful at minimizing unnecessary menu navigation and feels more akin to reality, the pinned items would sometimes be in the way of the puzzle the player was trying to solve. The game is pretty short however, it took me just over 5 hours to 100% it.The story follows the protagonist joining Escape Academy, dedicated to teaching people how to be master escapists. There are a good number of characters the player meets which have the impression of a personality but so little time is spent with most of them it doesn’t manifest into anything beyond the surface level that the player sees. There isn’t an overarching story per-say, more just smaller stories that do lead to a conclusion but those story beats are interesting and keep the player engaged, and what little is known about the characters is interesting. It has more of a story than I’d expect from an escape-the-room game and as such it does stand out a bit even if the story itself isn’t all too deep.The graphics have a cartoonish look to them but are well-designed. The rooms feature a good amount of color that makes them pop and stand apart from each other, much different from a single mansion or room-style game and it works well, the characters are also well designed and each has a very unique look that shows off that little bit of personality that they have. The puzzles also look great and they don’t have anything that makes them hard to understand.The soundtrack Isn’t very noticeable, it’s there but it doesn’t do anything not that it feels like it needs one.Escape Academy is a solid game, the gameplay works for the most part and it has a solid story, there are a few annoyances and the game is lacking in depth from the story and characters but overall it’s a very solid escape-the-room game.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fun game, there are some things that bothered me, but overall a good experience. This things that bothered me aren't all directly related to the gameplay, so that's always a plus. The good - Some of the puzzles were challenging. SOME of them. Most of them aren't too challenging, I would say somebody over 13 years old would be able to solve most of the puzzles. So they're mostly a little easy for me, but there were a couple that had me stumped and required a walkthrough, that's okay. The art style is great, it's similar to other games but it's got it's own charm with the texture in the 2D characters, the 3D models could use some refining but it's a cute style that works well with handheld systems. The 3D models remind me of Danganronpa, or the phoenix wright games. The game was a fair length, I do wish it was longer. I did get the season pass and already completed the DLC that's currently available (the island is the only one) and I'm looking forward to the future DLC. It cost about $40CAD though, and for 17 hours with little replayability, it's not super impressive with the length.The things that bugged me - There are steam achievements that are reliant on playing multiplayer. That always bugs me, I can never find people to play these sorts of games with so finding somebody to play and earn achievements with would be nearly impossible for me. Maybe I'm just a loner, but it's annoying. I love gathering achievements, and I can't with multiplayer ones. The difficulty of the puzzles did annoy me a little, many of them were too simple for me. I do escape rooms in real life sometimes though, so maybe I just have more practice than what they were expecting from their targeted audience, but I do wish there was more of a challenge with the levels that were marked more challenging than others. It didn't seem like there was much of a difference between the level 1 challenge vs. the level 5. The length was different, since there were more puzzles, but the difficulty wasn't much different.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: Was fun, a little short but not too challenging or too easy. Most of the escapes were at least thought provoking and there was a good variety in challenges and styles. Biggest flaws are the fairly silly story, the low replay value inherently and the score system, which probably should be a first time clear sort of detail. Once you know the answer, the puzzle is pretty much solved. There is even an achievement that has you use this fact to pass in a short amount of time. Game was also weirdly buggy in multiplayer6.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: It's a nice game, it can be quite tricky sometimes but in general nice for some casual gaming session. The main issue that ruins it for me is the fact that while playing online coop, the keeps crashing every 2 missions. It's very annoying and it's hard to maintain the sessions going because of the frustration. If that gets fixed, would absolutely recommend, otherwise be advised the game could crash causing some progression to be lost...
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: This was a lovely play through with a friend.  The story is unique and fun while the puzzles are just the right level of challenging.  That being said there were some problematic moments with online co-op game play where the game froze from time to time and we each had to relaunch.  Truth be told it was a minor inconvenience for a VERY fun escape game experience.  Perhaps best as a sale game purchase if you're looking for bang for your buck.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: It’s a solid game, it’s fun and it requires thinking from the player. It is not always easy, but it is also not unsolvable. The co-op mode is an extension that is a lot of fun. However, I had a technical problem at the end where I ran backwards without stopping. Even after several restarts and reinstallation of the game, the problem was not fixed. 7.5/10

_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: Feels true to the escape room style. It plays pretty quick (I finished in about 6 hours), but the puzzles are all well thought out. Each "room" has a unique theme. There are lots of puns peppered around each room which gave me a laugh. It has good colorblind support too. I have trouble with color-based puzzles but once I enabled colorblind assist, each color was labeled. It helped save me a lot of time trying to focus on the colors.I hope the developers make more of these games. I have not tried the DLC yet.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: We had lots of fun playing this in a split-screen couch setting. Most puzzles, while generally fairly easy to solve, gave the proper escape room experience. A few too many of them were faster to brute force than to solve, which should not be the case in an escape room. I also didn't appreciate that some puzzles requires you to think like a native English speaker. I consider myself fluent in English, but I don't think in English, and this was an obstacle in some parts of this game. The overall story is cute and not too pretentious. I didn't experience any significant bugs. I had to restart the game once because there was no audio, but I think that was it. Overall I definitely recommend it as an escape room co-op video game.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic puzzle game. The format is based off of escape rooms so you're trapped in an area and have a time limit to solve the puzzle. The art style is amazing and is perfectly toned with the dialogue and story to help the game overall feel cohesive. I really enjoyed the choice in puzzles everything felt fair. There was only maybe one time that I said "how was I supposed to figure this out?" This is not a dig at the difficulty it simply means the clues were intentional and could not be misleading which i find happens a lot in other games. The puzzles are also very linear. One solution will lead to another puzzle with in turn will unlock something else once solved. I also found that when Items were obtainable you pretty much instantly knew what they were for. This game was like the perfect balance for someone who wants a challenge, but isn't trying to go through mental gymnastics. If you're someone who dislikes math or writing down clues I was able to complete the game without using a notepad, although it was recommended to use one. Overall I'd rate the difficulty 6/10. The game has it's own difficulty rating for each puzzle, but I found it to be inaccurate. All of the puzzles were of similar difficulty.If you like escape rooms this game is a must. I have played escape simulator and I liked this game better. It is definitely worth it for full price. I plan to buy both dlcs.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: This game is awesome! I had a hard time pulling myself away.The puzzles are no joke. I definitely needed the extra time on some (or even the occasional google for help). The hints system feels limited.Cute story, cute art, and it was a great experience to get "in the zone" and work through the environment. You certainly deserve to feel some pride for beating levels.I highly recommend the DLC if you enjoyed the main game, as well
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: Escape Academy feels like it has the foundation of a good game - the visual design is distinct, the cast is fairly memorable, and, of course, the puzzles are thoughtfully crafted and logically solvable, which is ultimately the most important thing about this kind of game. The sticking point for me, though, was the stunning amount of jank, particularly in online co-op - I played through the entire game in co-op, and frequently ran into desync issues that basically made true cooperative play break down frequently, the only saving grace being that I was physically in the same room as my co-op partner as we played on different machines. There are other prominent bugs as well - the game frequently hangs either at startup or when attempting to exit to the main menu, necessitating a force-close of the game, and during my last play session, controller support seemed to completely fail, forcing me to remap keyboard controls onto my controller on the fly in Steam Input.Like I said, there's the foundation and framework for a great game here, but I think the technical issues will make me hesitant to recommend it for a while, even at the rather fair price of 20 bucks. Until those issues are definitively fixed - and online becomes a lot more stable - I would say to wait for a sale, a good one, before plunging in.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: Puzzles are mostly easy, and the graphics are fine enough. The movement glides, and all in all its a good game. Storyline is cute but predictable. What is not good is the glitchy crashing that happens at least once per session that I play it online with a friend. Would recommend. Would wait for it to go on sale though. :)
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: The price tag is a bit steep considering the amount of content, but there are some really fun puzzles in here if you can get it on sale, or have some money to throw around.  I played it solo and had a great time.  Be warned, though, its performance is quite poor; I found that my framerate was wildly unstable on a reasonably powerful rig, sometimes dipping as low as the low 40s, but considering this game doesn't particularly care about twitch reflex, it's not something that wound up bothering me all that much.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game with friend! First game I finish at 100% in 4 hours.The game felt sometimes too easy (always scored A+ and never failed any test), but I'm used to this kind of enigmas.A mode, allowing to change the difficulty and randomizing the enigmas answer could improve the replayability.The game crashed a few times, stayed stuck between screen at the end of some dialogues.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: Note: I played the whole game single player.This is a very enjoyable escape room game. The "escapes" are all part of a larger plot and they flow well, making a sensible story with plenty of twists. The characters are enjoyable and endearing and the graphics are endearing. This game has lots of small details that really add to it, such as the humorous flavor text you get when inspecting non-puzzle-related items, the way your dorm room collects memorabilia from the puzzles, and the interactive elements around campus (I especially like eating everything in the cafeteria).Although the graphics are nothing special, they have style and are more dynamic and interactive than many escape-style games I have played. The level layouts have great variety.The puzzles are not too hard. I felt pressure from the time limits but rarely came anywhere close to not solving an escape in time. But you definitely have to think. Random guessing/clicking will not work!Give the demo a try. If you like it you will probably enjoy the game because it gives a very good sense of the style, humor, and types of puzzles.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: Found the game to be pretty enjoyable co-op experience, when things are working smoothly. We unfortunately had a number of issues where the Host and the partner had puzzles displaying different settings, causing some puzzles not to solve, and only one player able to progress to the next area because of this. If the bugs can be sorted out it's a recommendation with a friend,
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun game! A bit short, but not annoyingly so. Fun characters, interesting world building, good puzzles, very fun with a friend.We did run into one desync issue with one the Pipe Dream puzzle in the last level, where our tiles weren't lined up but that was due to us messing with the board at the same time, causing the issue.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best escape games on steam. It got some bugs that occur, when multiple players use something at the same time or enter codes at the same time. Despite this and some other loading issues the game is really well made. It got some nice puzzles and the difficulities are just right. Def would recommend :)
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the better Escape Room games I played this year.It is not without flaws.You can get stuck in the scenery, sometimes the púzzles are a bit obtuse, and the menu system is not great. There are a few missing quality of life features. Like there is no option to restart a room from a menu or just leave the room. You have to quit to the main menu and reinitialize your session with the friend you are playing with. That is just a bit annoying.The story is quite nice and the art style is really clear. That is one game I happily recommend for online co-op even if not everything is smooth.Score: 7/9
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: The game itself is somewhat fun but majority of the puzzles are too easy. Completing the entire game in 3.5h with majority of the puzzles done on A+ without much effort.. And on top of that, having to restart the game 6 or 7 times because it kept crashing in Co-op. There's not much re-playability either, puzzles are so simple you remember them. We played through the game a couple of times to clean up achievments and even so, landing on around 6.5h since two were bugged for 17€ isn't something I can recommend unless you're a die-hard puzzle gamer (game itself isn't that bad, just too easy and too short)
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: An amazingly immersive game with well-balanced and various puzzles. Clues are well crafted and the timer gives you fire under your feet feeling - just like real life escape rooms.  The duration of the game is just enough but at the same time leaves you craving for more.  Season Pass purchase is a no brainer. Hoping and waiting for even more future DLC updates.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: This is a pretty good game in single-player and a really good game in co-op mode. It's great being able to play with a partner and collaborate. It also helps avoid getting stuck, hitting your head against a wall, because your partner will think about things a little differently to you. A fun way to spend a day. Took my wife and I five hours to finish.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: The difficulty of the puzzles was challenging, but they all had their own sense of internal logic so once you began to learn that it got easier. The puzzles actually made sense too. I wasn't a huge fan of either of the two art styles (one for 3d, one for 2d) but that's just me. My partner and I are couch gamers and we really appreciated how fluid it felt to have two people playing splitscreen. There are so few local co-op games, so thanks for including that feature!
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: I would love to buy the new DLC for Escape Academy. I was only allowed to play the first mission. Now I'm unable to open the game. I get a black screen with the lock emblem circling but the game is clocking hours as if i'm playing. The Puzzle that I was able to play seemed cool like a game I could really get into, but not being able to play this game seems like a waste of money.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: Puzzles are incredibly creative and the sense of accomplishment accompanying "a-ha!" moments is so satisfying. Designed to make or break your relationship in co-op play, but I cannot recommend it enough for game night. Just good old fashioned fun that requires unlocking your brainpower more than anything else.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: Escape Academy is an excellent addition to the escape-room simulation genre, along with Escape Simulator.The rooms are distinct, the puzzles are well designed ( the now cliché  puzzle!), and manage to give a lot of a-ha moments throughout the experience.Playing local multiplayer helps with puzzles that are split across areas by offering separate perspectives, and you're even rewarded with a different experience when playing together in one of the rooms, so it's worth it!I highly recommend this one - it even has a well-written and suitably absurd story with twists and surprises.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: I played it with a friend. And overall it was a great game. The pro's:- Very good artwork- Very good story (But it has a very strange and sudden stop)- Very easy to play with a friendThe con's:-Puzzles don't have much in common with each other (skills you learn from puzzles don't get used by other puzzles)- The game only has 10 puzzles in total ( it will take around 4-6 hours to complete it.)I recommend waiting for a sale and then buying it.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: I was completely obsessed with this game! I am an escape room lover in real life and after playing through many of the Escape Simulator rooms, I was looking for a game exactly like this one! It did not disappoint! I loved the story, and the rooms were all so wonderfully themed! I am already excited about any DLC that might come out for this amazing game. If you like escape rooms even a little bit, this is a no brainer.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun game, perfect for either co-op or singleplayer. Took about 5hrs to finish with a friend and encountered 0 bugs during the playthrough. I really like the ability to toggle split screen to view friends screen. The story is okay - but the puzzles were great, definitely making you think outside the box. The puzzles have many different interactables, but only some contribute to solving the puzzle. The only thing I would change is to make it so most of the notes contribute in someway, maybe even throwing the player off
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: This game had everything I like to see in an Escape Game: Relatively variety, Fun Stakes, and puzzles that just make sense. I only found myself stumped maybe one or two times because of how fluid each level felt. I felt like these levels had almost a puzzle chain that did not make the game a search game. The only downside to this game is that it's just too dang short. I beat this game in less than 3 hours, and 20 dollars is not worth 3 hours of gameplay. Buy this game, but only when it's on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: Played this game with my partner and boy howdy was it a blast. Puzzles weren’t too infuriatingly difficult that we got at each other’s throats, but weren’t too easy and we actually had struggles on some. My only wish is that it was longer because these were some really fun puzzles! Can’t wait for the dlc!
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: This game isn't bad. It needs some fixes. Some very good puzzles, but there could be some more challenging ones. A few too many bugged puzzles in multiplayer, where the host and other player see 2 different game states.Some levels are clearly designed for a single player experience e.g. doing UV light sort of effects where there's only 1 piece of equipment making them visible to the team... the other person is forced to sit and watch.if it were an early access game, I think I could look past the above issues.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: I dont think ive written a review for a game before but I had to for this. This game is well worth the money. Took me about 6 hours to complete. Puzzles were well constructed and the story was great! Finished the game and immediately went to see when the next DLCs were coming out. Really home the devs keep this one going.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: I got into Escape games w/ online co-op during the pandemic and finished quite a few titles already. This game stuck out to me with great art direction and well designed puzzles. The difficultly may lean on the easier side for experienced players, but you'll never encounter a puzzle that will completely stump or aggravate you if this is your first escape game. Definitely recommended with a second player.it is a bit short so I'm looking forward to upcoming seasons to rectify this!
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: Satisfying puzzles, beginner friendly design choices, and great use of applying escape room concepts using gimmicks that could not be used in actual escape rooms make for a very entertaining time with this game.the characters are also enjoyable and add to the experience overall.I am not personally familiar with escape rooms in general, but I could still enjoy the experience provided by this game immensely. I definitely recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: This is lovely little game, I write this having just completed it solo, so you can see it took me about 4 hours to finish. The puzzles are good and flow well, they're not massively difficult but they will get you thinking enough that you get that nice little shot of dopamine when you get it right. Something you often find with puzzle games is that there are a few really good puzzles a bunch of mediocre ones and usually one or two that are infuriatingly obtuse and I'm happy to say that this isn't the case here, I never found myself solving a puzzle by accident or getting the solution and being annoyed about how I was supposed to work it out.The story is nice, I liked that it gave a sense of light humour to the setting but didn't go out of it's way to take over the focus of the game, I found myself happily going into the optional extra story bits for the short conversations with and between characters, the only thing I found odd is that there seems to only be two students at this academy but that never really distracted me from the game.When all is said and done I think the best comment I can make is that I'm going to pick up the season pass as I'm excited to play the new rooms that will be coming.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: Get out a pen and paper folks, Your gonna need to take some notes. Maybe Scribble down some number from a wall! This game is a great buy and a great play! The puzzles are not SUPER hard but are not easy. They are a good mix in the middle.  There a handfull of puzzles and a great story line headed your way when you sign up for ESCAPE ACADEMY! It is a great coop game, I had a blast playing with my friend! I would defintly recommend to grab a buddy and a pen a paper jump in discord and go pass the test!
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: I love the puzzles in this game, I dont know how it compares to actual escape rooms but there is the right mix of challenge, a few of the puzzles its more find all the bits then the solution is obvious but thats the nature of these. I do wish there was an untimed mode however, I have never been a fan of timed things.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: This was a great time, the puzzles are so nicely designed that you couldn't brute force them and needed to use your surroundings to solve. But not too hard that it caused your brain to melt and hate certain puzzles. Probably some of my favourite puzzles in an Escape Room game. I cannot wait for more!!! The story line was also cute, just wish I could change my avatar and gender. Other than that 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a big fan of this game. It's not very long (probably about 10 hours max at launch) and doesn't have a ton of replay-ability, but it's a lot of fun on your first playthrough and it's great to speedrun if you're into that sort of thing. Really nice aesthetics and a fun story combined with lots of interesting puzzles makes this an easy recommendation from me, but you might want to try and catch a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: Good game to play, excited for new updates and seems like a game they can continue to drop new levels as they come up. A quicker play for the price, but still enjoyable and quality. Neat idea if they could add some level creator to this, but highly recommend putting on the wishlist at the very least to snag this at some point
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: Charming art style, comfortable difficulty level. I never felt like I was in over my head in solving the puzzles, but never felt like any were too difficult either. the completion noises are also highly satisfying. I played it alone and felt that the story and puzzles were smooth, even though I'm pretty sure this game was intended to be co-op. 9/10 can't wait for more updates and puzzles.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoy puzzles so this game was right up my alley.  The puzzles felt unique and varied between the different zones.  The biggest let-down for me was how short the game was (12 puzzles at release).I do not regret getting this game; I had a lot of fun with it.  The roadmap makes me hopeful for more challenging content in the future, but it may not be worth it right now until more content is released for some users.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: A fun co-op escape room game, with a low barrier of entry.• Predominantly solid puzzle design (starts off a bit too easy, but hits flow on the second half of the game)• Cool character designs• Ability to see your partner's screen takes some of the guess work out of puzzles• Some really unique puzzles when the game lets itself expand upon its premise (Ship Level for Example)• Well designed levels - clear visibility and easy to interact with things• Extremely short (Under 4 hours), with 0 replayability for $20• Absolutely awful and distracting soundtrack • A generally "meh" and predictable story that the game makes you spend a decent chunk of time onOverall, worth playing, but also maybe better to wait for a sale to get a decent value out of it.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: This will be the first game I felt strongly enough about to leave a review. I'd first like to say that my girlfriend and I are avid escapists. We love traveling all over to challenge ourselves with escape rooms. It has been a long time since I found a game that brought so much joy in our life that we could play together. I don't understand people speaking about the "replayability" of this game. It's an escape room. Once you figure it out you don't go back and do it again after you know all the puzzles. We did have two instances of our screens showing puzzles solved on her (host) screen but not appearing solved on my screen. (The specific scenes for devs to check out would be the glowing pipe puzzle on the last level and the last statue puzzle in the courtyard/tagging level). While this game can probably be completed in a night, I would recommend spacing them out to prolong the enjoyment. Thank you again devs for allowing us to make some great memories and we both look forward to the upcoming DLC.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: Gotta say I refunded the game on other gaming platform  because of the same issue as others with online split screen forced upon the players, but after the fix with the option to turn it off the game is actually up there when it comes to a good escape coop game. Just a little thing that would probably be nice for people is making the split screen as an option instead of just bound button, so you don't have to turn it off every level, other than that the game is pretty fun, good atmosphere, great idea of implementing escape into the story and puzzles are so far pretty nice, maybe little easier for people that have some experience with escape games, but surely can recommend for both new players and veteran escapees.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: YOU CAN PET THE DOG!!!This game is so fun! Very innovative take on a puzzle game, with a nice story line to go along with it. Some of the puzzles I've been able to figure out with great timing, while others have been more challenging for me. There's a great range of puzzle types within the game, and the environment/art assets are beautifully made. I can't recommend this game enough if you enjoy puzzle games, want to support indie game studios, and enjoy lovely art.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: Escape academy is a short game, but very fun. Puzzles are well designed without being overly intricate or needlessly complex. It's a great game for for anyone who loves a good puzzle. There is also a story mixed in with the puzzles that helps give the game a little extra zest. It's a little expensive for how short it is, maybe pick it up on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: *After replaying the game in a much more finished state, I decided my old review wasn't sufficient any longer, and have written a new one.*Overall, my impression of the game has changed since it first came out, but not my recommendation. I would still not recommend it, for several reasons. First, some of the puzzles are still not exactly straight forward, but not in the way you would expect for a well constructed puzzle game, they aren't hard because the puzzles themselves are, some of them are hard just because how the solution is come to and implemented can be a bit sloppy. They largely fixed this in the DLC, but that brings us to another problem.Second, and this one is a big issue for me, the game is more or less not complete without the DLC, or at least, is not worth the price. 20$ for a game thats kind of half baked and can be beaten in just over the time that qualifies for a Steam refund is a lot when there are games out there that are half the price and offer high replayability and hundreds of hours of potential game play for your first playthrough alone. This game doesn't really offer that much replayability (not that uncommon for a puzzle game), the only way I would really find value in replaying it is to play the new DLC packs. At a usual price of 10$ each, you're suddenly looking at a 40$ price tag in order to get a full game, which again, given the games that are available on Steam, is not my first choice.Don't get me wrong, the game went in a much better direction than it started off in; and I have found some moments of enjoyment. But it's just not a good value when it lacks replayability and getting a decent length game costs extra; so I still can't recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: I have done a lot of in person escape rooms and Escape Academy captures the escape room experience perfectly. The puzzles are fun and balanced, you can tell how much love and dedication went into developing this game. I would absolutely recommend for anyone interested in escape rooms. No previous escape room experience needed but those out there that have experience will still have a ton of fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: This was a fun game! The puzzles aren't too hard, but still challenging. I also really like the overall aesthetic of this game, I think it's pretty. And the sound effect that plays after managing to figure out a part of the puzzle is super satisfying. I did encounter a couple of problems in the library and quad levels, but nothing that couldn't be fixed with a restart.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: It's solid, but not amazing. If you've played Escape Simulator, this is a small step down but still enjoyable. It's a lot more fun in co-op, but still doable as a solo experience. I think the main thing going against it is that it feels like they could have just waited another few months and just had it launch as a bigger game at a slightly higher price tag on release. This isn't the kind of game I see most people coming back to most of the time, and it would be a shame if the DLC greatly improves on the base of the game only to go ignored.TLDR: Play with a friend, story is average, difficulty is medium, maybe wait for some DLC before picking up.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this game, but my feelings on it are very mixed.Really fun game with some very enjoyable gameplay. The puzzles in the escape rooms are almost always satisfying without ever feeling too easy. One or two puzzles every now and then feel a bit obtuse and there were some situations where I lost a lot of time because I hadn't clicked on one of the many unassuming objects in a given room. But overall, they were extremely fun.The characters are very enjoyable and it's a shame you don't hear more from them. The trailers for the game had me expecting a lot more interactions between them and the player, and I was disappointed when the credits rolled and I felt as if I hadn't really gotten to know them that well. The writing got a good amount of laughs out of me. It's a very similar game in tone to stuff like Psychonauts or Portal which are both games I think are hilarious.As you can see by my playtime (3 hours), it's a very short game. I think most playthroughs would take a bit longer than mine, but the dissonance between this time and the game's price isn't something to ignore. I think $20 is a fair asking price for this game, and I would recommend buying it. However, as the game has just released and the DLC is not out yet, I strongly suggest you DO NOT buy the season pass. I know it's for content coming in the future, but spending $40 for 3 or 4 hours of gameplay left me feeling kind of robbed. And despite seeing how apparently the DLC doubles the amount of escape rooms, I'm still not sure it's a fair asking price for a game this short. I should note, though, that I only played the single player content.Overall, I would recommend this game to anyone who likes escape room-type point and clicks. I think due to its personality, charm, and story, it's a better experience overall than other games on Steam of this genre like Escape Simulator. But as it currently stands, $40 is highway robbery for a game this short and this barebones. tl;dr Don't buy the DLC just yet. It's a short game well worth the $20 asking price for the base game.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun and solid escape room game with lots of satisfying and clever puzzles. Feels very authentic to the vibe of a real escape room, just with some extra video-gamey flair. The designers used the virtual medium to great effect. The story is nothing special, but it's clearly not the main focus, so I can forgive it for that. I only have a few complaints, and all fairly minor at that:- I would appreciate some kind of way to view the "report cards" you receive at the end of every level. Being able to keep track of your best times and ranks would be helpful not only for checking your progress on certain achievements, but would also be fun to show off to your friends.- The admittedly-few bits of 3D character animation feel very limp and lifeless in my opinion. There could have been a bit more polish put into it.- While the puzzles are normally very well-designed and clearly playtested throroughly, there is one puzzle in particular with an instruction that I'm fairly certain was just downright wrong and misleading. (Spoiler tagged for the sake of others who have not reached this point in the game) - The game is a bit buggy on its initial release. Notably, the cursor and some of the campus map interactables seem to appear on the loading screen at the end of a level, though you can't click on them. There's also a couple bugged achievements. I was able to get every achievement except for "Overachiever" and "Study Buddies," neither of which triggered despite me fulfilling their conditions. I even attempted to fulfil the conditions on multiple save files, but to no avail. I've seen some other people report that other achievements would not trigger for them, even though I was able to get them just fine, so it seems that some issues may vary between users for whatever reason.Despite these small gripes, I would say this is overall a very well-put-together game that I have no serious issues with. Like many others, I was a little upset by how short it was, but I know there is an upcoming content update and DLCs that hope to remedy this, so I'm excited to see what those have in store. I'm very glad to see my excitement for it was not misplaced.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: A fun and charming puzzle game that is challenging enough to make you feel smart without leaving you frustrated or feeling cheated. The characters are vibrant, the puns are plentiful, and the art and style are top notch. The puzzles all make sense with no leaps of logic or red herrings, something that can frustrate with real life escape rooms. The coming updates and DLC are the cherry on top of a delightful gameplay experience. Highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: Super cute and fun game.All of the puzzles make are well thought out and they were only a couple that we got stuck on for a while but when you understand the solution they make sense. Sometimes if you hit a roadblock it helps to double check what items you or your partner have. Overall super fun game and i'm eagerly awaiting the dlc. ^_^
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: Would recommend if you love escape games! Most of the escape rooms are rated 3/5 until you reach the final escape room and its suddenly 5/5. Would appreciate if there was a auto save function, because I have wonky internet so I kept dc-ing in the final room and we had to speed run that game.Favourite part of the story line was,Can't wait for the DLC! and hopefully new updates for year two.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: Overall Escape Academy was a very satisfying experience that's worth the $20 cover charge (or ~4 hrs if you've already got Gamepass).While I wish the difficulty was significantly higher at most points, the pacing is well done with a lighthearted concept and delivery that distracts from the simplistic puzzles. The levels are fun and creative, and manage to hit a wide array of settings while still working within the boundaries of the plot.Note that at the time of writing this review, many of the achievements on Steam are currently bugged for some players. This including the Chatterbox and the Study Buddies achievements.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: As somebody who loves escape game genres as a whole, this one was really entertaining. I picked it up and played it to help distract from a bad time, and when I finally finished it and closed stuff down for the night--oops, it was 2 AM!There are some instances of hints or tools possibly being a bit out of the way, for example in the  However, in that same mission  because I pretty much was able to guess the correct answer  So make of that what you will. Most later instances of using the hint feature were because I continued to play despite getting tired, and we all know how sleepiness makes the brain kinda foggy--But that's just it! I enjoyed the game so much, I played on despite that. Very tempted to show this to my partners so we can fumble around in multiplayer and I can show them it, as we've been having fun with other multiplayer escape room games as well.In summary, very good, challenging but not overly so, and definitely worth the price, I'd say. Consider me somebody definitely eyeing that season pass when it's a bit closer to the release for the first bit of content!
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly this is a enjoyable game! It is and is not a puzzle game if that makes sense? Its escape rooms which are puzzles but feels like not at times as well but I digress. Took me around 4 hours to solve everything. I played the game alone. I enjoyed many of the puzzles while others did frustrate me but that's puzzles! The hint system is usually pretty good and the timer does add to the experience. If you enjoy puzzle games I would say try this out if you think its a little pricey for 4 hours then maybe wait for a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: I definitely recommend this game! It has a variety of challenging puzzles, entertaining and at times tense gameplay, interesting characters and plot, and a wonderful art style.The levels are all unique and atmospheric with a multitude of different puzzle mechanics to keep things interesting. The rooms vary in difficulty but (sometimes with the help of hints) are passible for someone with little background in escape room type games. Overall a great game to play either by yourself or with a friend!
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

_childDocuments_.review: You've just arrived at Escape Academy, a school where promising students train to become the ultimate Escape Room Master. Play over a dozen masterfully hand crafted rooms, designed by experienced experts in the field of REAL LIFE escape rooms. Experience the entirety of Escape Academy alone in single player OR through two player co-operative play. Available in local or online splitscreen. Explore the campus of Escape Academy and get to know the faculty, a colorful cast of characters, each an expert in the art of Escape. And some with secrets yet to be uncovered...
_childDocuments_.name: Escape Academy

name: Little Goody Two Shoes
detailed_description: Dreaming Maidens: Pocket Mirror x Little Goody Two Shoes In these narrative-driven horror adventure games, you will find yourself using your wits to solve puzzles and explore rich environments full of charm and wonder. Your choices will determine your fate - try to discover as many endings as you can to uncover the truths to mysteries long forgotten! This bundle contains: Pocket Mirror ~ GoldenerTraum: a modern RPG puzzle horror game that will have you playing as a young girl who, deprived of her memories, finds herself embarking on a dreamy and frightening journey of self-discovery. Little Goody Two Shoes: a fairy tale horror adventure game with a dark twist. Follow Elise, an ambitious girl determined to become rich, as she attempts to escape her humble life and finds herself getting more than she bargained for… Little Goody Two Shoes Deluxe Edition Take Little Goody Two Shoes’ music anywhere you go with the Deluxe Edition! This bundle contains: Little Goody Two Shoes - a fairy tale horror adventure game with a dark twist. Follow Elise, an ambitious girl determined to become rich and escape her humble life in the village of Kieferberg. Official Soundtrack - The official soundtrack for Little Goody Two Shoes features 64 all-original tracks from the main game, including 3 unreleased bonus tracks. PLAY THE DEMO NOW! Try the demo today and enjoy the starting section of the game, where you explore Kieferberg and its mysteries, romance its bachelorettes and get a taste of the terrors of the Witching Hour... About the Game There once was Elise , a vibrant and ambitious young lass with a big dream – becoming filthy rich. In spite of this, the stars didn’t seem to have reserved our protagonist much fortune in life. Elise, who came from humble beginnings, had no choice but to spend her days away assisting her fellow neighbours with menial tasks to make a living. One day, Elise discovers a pair of beautiful shiny red shoes buried in her backyard – what a surprise! Bewitched, Elise embarks on a fearful journey that pulls her closer and closer into the heart of the mysterious Woods! Will Elise risk it all for the sake of a dream come true, or settle for her humble day-to-day life? The ending of this tale is yours to write… Little Goody Two Shoes is a horror narrative adventure game, set in a hand-painted fairy tale environment. There are 10 possible endings to fit your choices and actions in the game. But there’s more than meets the eye here, as you must also manage multiple aspects of Elise’s life in the village to stay alive. Remember, all decisions matter in this story! During the day, you will need to strengthen Elise’s bonds with her fellow villagers and work to make a living by playing fun minigames. But once the moon rises, make sure to keep Elise fed, healthy and sane in the multiple encounters with deadly foes as she makes her way further into the Woods. Kieferberg is a small and devout village, which means Elise will need to carefully navigate her relationships with the villagers to avoid arousing suspicion of witchcraft and be left to die in the Woods as punishment. At night, Elise can roam around the Woodlands, a mystical and phantasmagorical realm where enigmas and deadly enemies await as she tries to uncover its secrets. Through a limited day and night cycle Elise will need to carefully manage her needs if she wants to stay alive to finish her tale. Get struck by Cupid’s arrow and fall in love with the charming bachelorettes of Kieferberg. In this all-female cast of romanceable characters, unlock dreamy date scenes and storylines for each of them.
about_the_game: There once was Elise , a vibrant and ambitious young lass with a big dream – becoming filthy rich. In spite of this, the stars didn’t seem to have reserved our protagonist much fortune in life. Elise, who came from humble beginnings, had no choice but to spend her days away assisting her fellow neighbours with menial tasks to make a living. One day, Elise discovers a pair of beautiful shiny red shoes buried in her backyard – what a surprise! Bewitched, Elise embarks on a fearful journey that pulls her closer and closer into the heart of the mysterious Woods! Will Elise risk it all for the sake of a dream come true, or settle for her humble day-to-day life? The ending of this tale is yours to write… Little Goody Two Shoes is a horror narrative adventure game, set in a hand-painted fairy tale environment. There are 10 possible endings to fit your choices and actions in the game. But there’s more than meets the eye here, as you must also manage multiple aspects of Elise’s life in the village to stay alive. Remember, all decisions matter in this story! During the day, you will need to strengthen Elise’s bonds with her fellow villagers and work to make a living by playing fun minigames. But once the moon rises, make sure to keep Elise fed, healthy and sane in the multiple encounters with deadly foes as she makes her way further into the Woods. Kieferberg is a small and devout village, which means Elise will need to carefully navigate her relationships with the villagers to avoid arousing suspicion of witchcraft and be left to die in the Woods as punishment. At night, Elise can roam around the Woodlands, a mystical and phantasmagorical realm where enigmas and deadly enemies await as she tries to uncover its secrets. Through a limited day and night cycle Elise will need to carefully manage her needs if she wants to stay alive to finish her tale. Get struck by Cupid’s arrow and fall in love with the charming bachelorettes of Kieferberg. In this all-female cast of romanceable characters, unlock dreamy date scenes and storylines for each of them.
short_description: Venture into the woods as you play Little Goody Two Shoes, a phantasmagorical horror narrative adventure where all your decisions matter!

_childDocuments_.review: No game has stirred such conflicting feelings in me and shown me how limiting Steam's thumbs-up/thumbs-down recommendation system is. With that out of the way, I want to give this game its merits. The audiovisual presentation is second to none, matching 90's anime aesthetics with storybook illustrations to bring an unquestionably beautiful fairytale to life. The story manages to keep you on the edge of your seat—how far will Elise go to achieve her wish? What is she willing to sacrifice? In that sense, it manages to make you want to play further to find out. It is a pity, then, that the overall gameplay is absolutely miserable to go through. Don't get me wrong, here and then I do not dislike some difficulty in my games, but some sections made me wonder if anyone outside of the development team actually beta tested it.The day sections are fine. The minigames have a bit of a learning curve, and Kiss the Rat might require fiddling with the max FPS, but overall, it is fine. However, the Witching Hour segments. Never have I hated getting through a dungeon as much as I had during my time in the "Berry Forest" (Thursday and Friday's dungeon). I am sure whoever designed a certain dungeon absolutely loved getting lost in dark caves in Pokémon without Flash. Very sure of it. Oh, and also add lighting fast enemies, guess-based segments, and sometimes even lag if you've got a low end device. I dread playing through it again for other endings. No NG+ either. I don't expect to get what the developers did in Pocket Mirror for such a feature (I don't think it would work very well), but I'd like at least a "Story" difficulty that could tone down it all a bit?Look, I still recommend at least giving it a try, if only because it is quite rare to see an indie title with such production value and passion poured into it. Again, the music and art assets have a level to them that is mostly unparalleled, and Kieferberg truly feels alive. It is quite a shame, then, that the gameplay balance seems to have been an afterthought. Which, y'know, you'd think it would be important and all given it is a game first and foremost.
