_childDocuments_.review: A game clearly made by a bunch of artists and writers who utterly lack the game design skill to actually pull off what they wanted to do. As a lover of adventure games I’m not a stranger to encountering adventure games like this, ones that add mechanics that just drag the experience down because the devs just did not have a good grasp of them at all or were too afraid that their work is not “gamey” enough so they felt the need to shoehorn them in. Little Goody Two Shoes is a life-sim/yuri VN frankensteined together poorly with an RPGmaker horror game and those elements are at complete odds with each other. The aesthetics and atmosphere are phenomenal, merging 90’s shoujo and Grimms’ fairy tales wonderfully. The writing is solid enough too as the main cast of ladies are likable and the mystery is engaging enough. The life sim elements are mostly fine, most of the job mini-games are alright though I’m not a fan of the rat one. The game does a bit of a bad job of pushing the player to overly fear raising suspicion though as it’s usually not hard to avoid or at least drop it down; I can easily see someone screwing themselves if they invested too much stamina and money in bringing Rozenmarine to work with them at all because it’s just not worth it, the villagers can be easily assuaged with the right responses. The night time horror segments is where the game completely goes to ♥♥♥♥ though.This game really shows how it’s essentially a bad 2000’s RPGmaker horror game just with an actual budget as the nighttime segments are jank as hell with puzzles mostly relying on trial and error. One night has you run away from a boss who will instantly kill you and the game can’t really handle the chase sequence that well; spike blocks will fall too fast to dodge within a fair window unless you know they’re coming and the second segment seems like sometimes you’ll just get randomly killed even when you’re running full speed. The puzzles gets worse as the game goes on as Thursday has you play floor is lava with phantoms that are attracted to sound, but the camera tends to be too zoomed in to see them effectively at times so you’re probably going to walk your ass into a few of them because the game gives you very little visual or audio cues that they’re coming. Apparently some of the segments were even more obtuse and ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ before they patched them and that’s just galling to me. The breaking point for me was on Friday where you had to go in complete darkness because turning on your lantern gets you instantly killed by statues. It’s absolutely abysmal puzzle design to the point where I’m baffled the devs thought it was a good idea. It’s not clever or challenging like good adventure game puzzles should, it genuinely feels like a troll. Thankfully somebody on Steam told me the solution so I went back and beat it but man did it still suck. The endings are also unsatisfying because they seem kind of at odds with each other and don’t really give a true conclusion if you take them into account. Just a wet fart of an ending to top of a game that was unraveling as it went along.This game just utterly frustrates me because this game could have been great but its ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ design decisions prevent it from being such. The game isn’t completely unsalvageable, a couple patches and overhauling the Friday puzzle to not be so awful and it’d be at a decent enough quality. Gonna be blunt and say they really need to hire a person who actually knows good adventure game design if they want to make keeping games like this. This is definitely the kind of game that you should probably watch an LP of. I’m usually the kind of guy who will readily defend games that have merely serviceable gameplay but great everything else, but Little Goody Two Shoe’s gameplay is too annoying for me to heartily endorse experiencing yourself.

_childDocuments_.review: An RPG Maker horror game without the limitations of being confined to the RPG Maker engine.Fantastic art and soundtrack, but gameplay itself is quite clunky unfortunately.Daytime segments are incredibly dull and long. But you need to pay attention and do well, because this is how you earn money and resources are limited. You'll be spending a lot of money to not starve to death, to not go insane in caves and when picking up the game's collectible "golden maidens". If you have enough left over, you may buy things an NPC requests and healing. Whenever you talk to people you also need to pick the more polite option (2 options, so always 50% chance!) or you may be branded a witch. You should also pick one or two of three girls and always spend time with them, or risk getting an incomplete ending. "Bad" endings are easy to get once you understand how endings work, which is simple to grasp once you've gotten to the end.Nighttime segments are the meat here. They have obstacles that are either too easy or too hard, and nothing in-between. A lot of times you'll face instant death due to parts needing a trial and error approach - where failure is just death. Sometimes requiring a few tries before grasping what it is the game expects from you. Even though you have health points and healing items! But when an attack doesn't kill you, it usually does very little damage. Free health items are available to find in the world to help you out. So death either comes instantly, or... never.Game length of a first run is 12 or so hours, more if you talk to absolutely everyone and try your best to find collectibles and then despair when you miss one, they don't carry over between playthroughs!Replay value is kind of bad. The only new thing for you will be 2 more interesting endings per girl you didn't have enough resources to spend time with. And they're somewhat similar to each other. You sadly cannot skip the overwhelming majority of cutscenes or dialogues, which is a huge issue. If the game is feeling extremely generous, it may offer you a button press to speed up the game during some (very limited!) conversations. Not looking forward to the achievement cleanup of a 2nd and possibly 3rd replay.1st time through the mystery and diverse nighttime sequences carry the game, but would not recommend playing more than once!

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this game, but there are too many design issues.Boss areas are unforgiving until you learn the mechanics.  This may take reloading a few times.  However loading is slow, and you have to reply the events up to the boss scene which may take up to 5 minutes; only for you to fail again.  Literally the first boss will insta-kill you if you don't move immediately after the long CS is over.  No retry option that puts you at the start of the fight/trial either; continue just reloads last save.On top of that you can't skip previously seen text.  If you load for any reason you have to go through all the text and scenes again which gets quite annoying when retrying a segment or replaying.Even worse then that, is how easy it is to softlock your save by missing a single event.  Game takes place over a week with certain times of the day; but you have to do certain things at certain times to avoid a bad ending.  Most of these are easy to find, but some aren't.  If you happen to miss one, you have to restart the entire game as all that awaits you is a bad end.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is bad. And that's a shame because I really wanted to like it.The first and biggest problem with this game is the controls. They SUCK. Like, they suck on a legendary WTF level. The game only gives you two sets of predefined keybinds to  control the game and they're both something you'll need to adapt to. And I just want to ask, why? Why not just give us some standard keybind options so we could pick the controls we wanted? You even give us a settings screen where we can choose our keybinds.... from two predefined options. Just.... why? It's not like this game needs complex controls, you could probably implement the basic controls in RPGMaker, so why go out of your way to make this so complicated? I don't know.Moving along, one thing the game absolutely excels at is its visuals. So many of the "nightmare" scenes are striking, otherworldly, and frightening even despite the lower-res environments. A lot of this stuff would be right at home in Puella Madoka Magicka or Alice in Wonderland and that's really something that should be admired.The gameplay feels awkward. The game feels like a lot of different ideas were put together that didn't add up to a cohesive whole.Your days will go as follows: Go to town to make money by playing frustrating mini-games, maybe date one or more of your waifus, and then go home where a 'nightmare' sequence occurs which will drag you into some very creative and creepy surroundings. The nightmare sequences are very well done but they're also very challenging. They usually end in a chase sequence of some kind, and the chase sequences feel very unfair. You can't look very far ahead of yourself during the chase and that makes it hard to avoid obstacles. Sometimes obstacles just fall in front of you but you won't know that until they're already on top of you. Plus the folks chasing you move very fast and you have limited time to move around obstacles. Eventually, through a combination of blind luck and memorization, you'll manage to escape.The "work" mini-games where you make money are pretty punishing as well. Your timing has to be exact, and the terrible keybind setup doesn't help. You'll get through these minigames with B's and C's because the game doesn't force you to pass them, it just gives you less money if you don't. And you'll need money because of the game's "hunger system." Every 'hour' that goes by in the day (there are six in total) consumes a unit of hunger. If you run out of all six units of food for your character, you die. Not eventually, or after a while, you die right on the spot. Why? What's the point? I understand needing to keep your character fed and healthy but is your character so fragile that she can't even skip a meal without keeling over? Why is this so punishing? Oh, and there is NO automatic refill for hunger when you wake up in the morning. You'll need to work for and buy every loaf of bread you eat. Sometimes, if you get caught up in a story sequence that causes two 'hours' to pass in rapid succession, you'll die of hunger with no opportunity to eat any of the bread in your bag.The hours zoom by every day and you feel much more under the clock than even most farming sims like Harvest Moon.The story is kind of hit-and-miss. It definitely has potential. The biggest problem with the story is its characters. They don't feel very well fleshed out, and your list of waifus feels mostly like stereotypes with fairly predictable revelations coming out about them later in the game. The worst character by far is the MC, who is either a tsundere or a flat-out b****. Tsunderes do not make good protagonists because they're so aggravating. They can be fantastic side characters but after a few hours with Elise, I really wanted to slap her. She comes across as a selfish, spoiled girl with a deluded sense of her own importance. This actually ties into the story, but it doesn't make her any more fun to be around. The voice-acted sound effects are very repetitive and annoying. If I hear Elise say 'What in the Lord's name' one more time...The story is actually intriguing, dealing as it does with witchcraft, Faustian bargains, and the like but I just don't have the stamina to get through it. The game's difficulty is sharp, and it feels artificially punishing.What's worse is that you can see that there is a really good game under all this, the framework is there and it's fighting to break free from under all these mystifyingly bad design decisions.It's clear that some real talent went into this product, especially in the visuals, but unfortunately, the whole is not greater than the sum of its parts.I'm intrigued by the story but I'm going to get the rest of it on a youtube let's play.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't get confused. This isn't a horror game. There may be some creepy things every once in a while, but scary, this game is not. It's more of a Thriller. A long story that you slowly unfold the answers to the longer you play. So if horror is what you are looking for, I would advise against this. HOWEVER, this is a good thriller that is DRIPPING in atmosphere and style. The developers knew what kind of look they wanted this game to have from the get go, and they commit. To summarize, this is a thriller puzzle game that is deeply drenched with a specific aesthetic. And if that it was you want, you most certainly will get that here.Make sure to use all your save slots.

_childDocuments_.review: Though I have a lot of problems with this game, as a game, such as pacing, polish, movement, and how puzzles are communicated, I can't help but think of this game as a masterpiece. Though the dialogue/VA can be a bit wonky, it has it's own charm. Everything from the sound design, the sprite work, original art, music, attention to detail... it's all incredible. Game is also incredible at making you feel like ♥♥♥♥ with how tragic and gut-wrenching its endings tend to be. There are happy endings, only 3 of them (one for each romance partner) out of 10ish total endings. The rest are all soul-crushing and left me feeling like trash for hours afterwards from the ones I got. Use your save slots if you plan on playing this, leave yourself outs for if you mess something up... Special props to positive depictions of lgbt themes, appropriation of religious culture, small town death, and so on. I very much look forward both playing the other two romance paths (Rozen is a sweetheart,) as well as the games predecessor and sequel, Pocket Mirror. Here's hoping this studio can go on to get the recognition it deserves.

_childDocuments_.review: As a massive shiller of Pocket Mirror to my friends, I'm pleased to report that I enjoyed Little Goody Two Shoes for same reasons why I liked AstralShift's first game. I liked atmosphere, art, music and presentation BUT there are several things that prevent me from recommending this game to everyone, namely: - The apple does not fall far from its RPG Maker ancestor, puzzles are still as unintuitive and will require a lot of patience from the player. I personally didn't hate it much, in fact, I was quite happy there are still games out there that don't spoon-feed the already-obvious solution by having main character constantly scream "pull da lever and maybe box will move!!" at the player, but I can easily see why other people will find this aspect infuriating. - The game is in a really weird state in terms of game's plot. If you have prior knowledge of PM's story, even before playing LGTS you already know how the direction this game's plot is going to take, but, even if you are not familiar with PM, the story here is fairly straightforward and doesn't pull too many punches. It is serviceable, but doesn't leave much room for interpretation. Some people will argue that's a great thing, since PM's story was nearly indigestible without a YouTube guide, but I still found the plot of it to be very interesting, it was really engaging to learn about the main character, her family and the characters surrounding the PM protagonist. LGTS introduces new characters but...- ...but these new characters are just OK. The game does not give enough time to get to know these three new characters (even with dedicated dates) and they have incredibly low impact on the story. During first playthrough I've almost completely ignored Freya, making so that she was only relevant in one single scene. In contrast, her dad appeared more in various dialogues throughout the game, managing to become a more fleshed out character compared to his own daughter. While playing you will also have to save scum a lot to pick correct rizz options, so be warned. The game still got me yiiking out as I enjoyed other aspects a lot, but for everyone else it might easily fall into "not my thing" category which is completely understandable. If you are unsure about buying LGTS, I can easily recommend playing Pocket Mirror Classic which you can get on itch.io for free (you can go with the Steam release version, but frankly I don't think it makes that much of a difference, unless you want to support AstralShift's work) and make your choice off of your experience with it. If you liked Pocket Mirror, you will probably Little Goody Two Shoes too.

_childDocuments_.review: this game is an absolute masterpiece. there is something so nostalgic about 80’s/90’s anime style married with 1930’s hand-painted animation style… it’s so enchanting and warm; i felt like i was sailor moon stepping into the snow white or pinocchio universe. the mini-game visuals are also stunning, resembling those antique arcade games we all know and love.i enjoyed the time progression within the game, giving you the choice of what you’d like to accomplish during each period of the day, whether it be the chore minigames with corresponding arcade visuals or romancing your favorite anime girls. the witching hour was very alice in wonderland-esque, with its whimsical character design, spooky theme, and overall eeriness, which left me intrigued to discover what was happening within the story.the story itself was intriguing and fun to explore. i found myself even more curious after each night, eager to uncover the secrets that lie within kieferberg. there are musical cutscenes peppered throughout the story as well, adding another element of whimsy to the entire experience. i also found the music to be quirky and distinctive, creating an immersive atmosphere!there are multiple endings, ten in total, that offer loads of different stories and options for replayability.it also played extremely well on my steam deck!i would recommend this game to anyone looking for something with an intriguing, spooky narrative and variety in its gameplay mechanics. and if you’re also an enjoyer of all things vintage and antique, you’ll absolutely ADORE the ode to retro anime and early western animation! <3

_childDocuments_.review: The art is gorgeous and the game nails the aesthetic it's going for, but I wouldn't suggest buying the game in its current state. It feels like the developers prioritized style over gameplay, unfortunately. The controls aren't very responsive, especially if you're playing with a controller or Steam Deck—expect a lot of input delay/lag. One of my biggest frustrations is that the game only lets you skip text in certain scenes. You die a lot in this game, so having to go through lengthy cutscenes with no option to skip through them after each death gets really grating. Additionally, while some of the witch hour puzzles are interesting (and they're always great visually), many of them are more frustrating than challenging. I enjoy difficult games, but the difficult moments in this game felt cheap ways to make you die easily rather than a satisfying kind of difficulty. An autosave feature in the witch hour would've helped a lot, at least so you're thrown back into the action right away rather than having to re-do puzzles and click through a bunch of dialogue again.I was very close to just giving up and watching the rest of the game on YouTube towards the end, but stuck through it because I was enjoying the story and characters. I love the older shoujo anime art style, media with queer representation, horror games, time+resource management, and basically everything this game is on paper, so you'd think I would've loved this game. Unfortunately, it fell flat in too many areas, but I think it'd be great if the developers patch some of the more glaring issues.

_childDocuments_.review: Gameplay-wise, you freely move around town and talk to characters in each time period, with working or going on a date passing the time. Working involves playing a short minigame, performance determines how much you earn and they can be fun. The final segment of each day has some light adventure game puzzling and possibly evading hostile monsters. These segments are decently challenging and have a lot of interesting things to see.The characters (that you are supposed to like) are fun to interact with and the love interests especially so. The dates are definite highlights since they give a deeper insight into Elise and the love interest's character, along with just being really heartwarming to witness. The plot is also interesting, and there are a number of endings to achieve depending on your choices, with the good ones all feeling like a great reward and fitting close to the tale (though I would have liked to see the Kieferberg plot thread expanded on more). Coupled with the gorgeous art and fantastic music, it's a pleasure to witness from start to finish. I strongly recommend it, moreso if you're into yuri.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is honestly fun as hell and let me tell you why, as well as one gripe I have!Pros:- Beautiful 90s anime artstyle (Card Captors, Sailor moon.. the nostalgia enthralls me)- Classic RPG maker vibes (nostalgia overload) [Same verse as Pocket Mirror *dies of nostalgia bliss]- Fun suspicion elements (Mystery is my favorite genre so I love this)- Horrifying/Small village cozy OSTs. If someone you know hears one track, they'll be shocked it's a horror/cozy game. Lovely vocals as well!- Top tier voice acting! I genuinely cannot picture the dub or sub sounding any different. The VA nails Elise's snootiness, and did you know she voices her in JP and the theme? Sick!- Romance options, where I feel like I have plenty of time to get to know each girl before choosing one! It's super hard to pick a girl.Cons (few and one will be fixed 100%):- 4 hours in, in the first event in the woods, after saving, it wouldn't let me leave the menu. The menu actually allows you to see what buttons are being pressed and none of them would let me exit. I highly doubt they'll keep this in the game and it only happened once.- The puzzle in this area felt kind of unnecessarily vague, as someone who loves puzzles, and looks forward to them whenever I play a Mystery game. I even hate hints about these and don't care if it takes me 30+ mins. This one made me wish I just knew the answer tho I won't lie. Haha   * To avoid spoilers, I'll simply tell you that I was using a candle for something, to lure something, they took away the candles in the second part, but kept the same thing required to lure,after I finally figured out how to progress and were basically like "you're on your own" with drawings on the ground that further served to confuse me. I figured it it all out, but I did get admittedly frustrated.But overall I think the game has the perfect atmosphere and I'm as hyped as I can be about a game. If you love RPG Maker games, I believe the world and characters, as far as I've progressed, are really something special. I wouldn't be surprised if this set a new bar for the genre, and I like figuring out what mysteries the world holds. Definitely worth the price I'd say!Note: If the bug is fixed, and the puzzles from here are the right amount of difficult, I'll remove all cons because I really believe in this game's potential. It is seriously more fun than I'm describing.

_childDocuments_.review: F*** the , all my homies hate the .  Spoilers ahead. For real though, it's a 10/10 for every other part of the game. My only gripe with the serpent's grove for thursday and friday night is that the safe spaces against the visages are too few and far between, with the visages being too numerous! I dont mind a little evasion in my dungeons but this just ends up with me having to stand on a little island for stretches of time, all to be bullied back onto that space whenever i get smacked by a visage. The process then repeats until i see the end screen and start over. I had no issue with fail states until that part of the game, which I think needs serious revisions. The suffering continues on friday, with the weeping angels. I understand the idea behind the challenge, but the grace period of you turning on the lantern to gain your bearings and the angels rushing you is much too short. On the other hand, just fumbling your way through the dark isnt an option either, with the thorns taking a chunk out of you every time you try to use the walls as guide. My recommendation for this is to do away with the thorn walls altogether for this portion of the dungeon, and it would be drastically improved. I understand that the design approaches for levels and puzzles comes directly from the norms of designing for rpgmaker, which I have no issues with! But i sincerely urge the devs to rethink this approach when it comes to the serpents grove. Elise's movement isn't divided into tiles, and so presents a difficulty when attempting to traverse through collisions that take a life every time.  The crows grove was great! No notes! Which is why its so disappointing to have to hit a wall in the next area. The writing is also top notch! The dialogue and character writing is extremely likeable and compelling, though i do think that the endings do feel just a bit narratively discordant to Elise as a character. I feel that LGTS's position as a sequel does limit its narrative impact somewhat, with player agency ultimately dismissed with the existence of a canon tie in with pocket mirror. Of course, one could dismiss the connection entirely, but I personally like to take in overarching narratives as a whole, and hesitate to ignore whole swathes of story outright because of a shaky tie in. All in all, it's an impressive showing from AstralShift, with incredible production value in its art direction, music and strength of its writing. Super duper polished with undeniable rough spots, but it's nothing that cant be fixed in future patches. PS the minigames are awesome and the wooden cabinet is the cutest thing ive ever seen

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this game and I really do believe it is worth playing, with a few 'but's. I don't regret playing it, and I think it is worth full price if only for the art and music alone. But I do think, if you're on the fence about getting it, getting it on sale would definitely be a safer option to avoid being disappointed.Aesthetically, it is a beautiful game. I love the mixed media and styles. Using almost jarringly different art mediums for certain situations made certain moments more memorable. Like others have said, if you were a fan of the art and music direction for Madoka Magica, this game is for you. The story is interesting, and it and the art/music are the only reason I kept playing. (very mild gameplay spoilers ahead)Horror game? Maybe, not in the traditional 'horror game' approach. There were some horror elements, but the game does not go out of its way to try and purposely try and be frightening more than it does by being uncanny and occasionally uncomfortable. I can really only think of one 'jumpscare', so if you avoid games due to those, I don't think you'd really experience it here. Gameplay wise, it wasn't bad for an 8 hour game, but it wasn't my favorite- and it was enough that I don't plan to replay it for any of the other endings. I wasn't a huge fan of the day to day gameplay loop of mini game > talk to someone > minigame > end of the day event. I wish I could fast forward through 'cutscenes' and not just general dialogue, especially in later parts where I had to keep restarting. I didn't end up having to look up any guides, but I found myself frustrated several times with a few challenges, and a particular 'lagoon' puzzle didn't really make sense with how I finally solved it. My favorite parts of the game didn't really last long.(vague story spoilers ahead)Story wise, I was invested. I didn't know what to expect going into the game blind, but I did really enjoy the direction it went in. I really only felt disappointed towards the end during the 'Him' section, some things happened without any build up, but somehow it was just very underwhelming with how much build up there was for 'Him' throughout the entire game. It is possible, since I only experienced 2 endings and this game has like 10(?) endings, that some are better than others.

_childDocuments_.review: What a sensory delight! The art style is nostalgic, magical, romantic, and surprising. The music shifts with the story, following you as you move through strenuous village life, to building tension and dread in occult mystery. Our protagonist Elise is an 18/19-year-old young woman, trying to survive on her own for the first time, after her grandmother passes away. She feels overburdened, and underappreciated, running herself ragged to survive off small amounts of food.She lives in a small, isolated, old Catholic town, full of devoutly religious and superstitious villagers. Quick to defer blame of any arising problem, the townspeople frequently lay their sights on Elise to take the fall. Her fiery attitude only adds to their suspicion, so choosing the right thing to say to calm their nerves is crucial. During the day, Elise works a number of odd jobs around town, which you play as an 8-bit arcade style mini game. The aesthetic and accompanying music make it so much fun!After work, you can choose to go on a date. At the beginning of the game, you decide between three ladies to pursue: Freya; the artsy farm girl and childhood friend, Lebcuchen; the woman of God, and Rosenmarine; the quirky traveler who shows up in your barn. Each day, you meet your sweetheart in a cozy location, and get to know her through tender sunset conversations. The contrast between the stress of the day, the horrors of the night, and the dates' liberating respite of gentleness can't be understated. The yuri side story of blossoming love between Elise and her friend is darling and genuine. I chose Freya as my "favorite girl," and the way she manages to soften Elise's testy exterior is truly charming. Little Goody Two Shoes is primarily a haunting adventure, but I would adore playing a slice-of-life game where we get to see more interaction between the girls. At night, you venture into the elusive woods, following a mystery you find yourself wrapped up in. You gain knowledge from unnerving creatures, who put you through fate-testing trials. Each night consists of exploring a section of the woods, and trying to make it through by solving puzzles, and avoiding monsters. You are given many chances to save, alongside many chances to die. The witching hour levels are challenging, but not maddeningly so.I am at the final stage of the game, and really don't want it to end! It's been a joy playing, and I can't wait to see what this studio comes out with next.

_childDocuments_.review: From the area design, to artwork, to music, to mini games and other fun mechanics — it is so well crafted. Despite the horror elements, it felt cozy and comfortable all the way. You are offered save points at every turn, and the locations are so beautiful, that it doesn’t even feel punishing.The endings are many, and vary significantly — although, you can get almost all of them in one go without a full replay, if you are attentive enough, of course. I managed to finish it in the spawn of about three evenings, and all 14 hours were a blast. Each little place in the village has its own secrets, and wandering around sometimes rewards you with a side-quest or a trinket you can sell. Or even more (but that would be a spoiler). All villagers are unique — not only due to their backstories and personalities, but also literally, since there are no copy pasted NPS’, they each have their own model. Same goes for the tree romance options. All of the girls severely differ from each other by personality, have their own quests/artworks, and offer their own endings. The only reason I won’t replay this (I managed to get 5/10 endings in one go) is the lack of fast travel — all the running and hopping from place to place gets a little bit tedious. What’s also worth mentioning is the lack of a full voiceover — you only get to hear exclamations, sighs, cut out sample phrases, and they all repeat a lot, which also gets boring after a while. Overall, though — amazing.

_childDocuments_.review: Little Goody Two Shoes is one of the best/most fun RPGs I've played in a LONG time. The art style is gorgeous (very reminiscent of classic 90s shoujo anime), the minigames are fun, the romanceable characters are adorable, and there are some genuinely creepy/unsettling moments to drive home the game's central conceit of how far you're willing to go to achieve your dreams. There are ten endings, and each has the potential to break your heart, lift your spirits, or make you go "WTF". While I wouldn't go so far to say that EVERY choice matters, how you play the game can affect what ending(s) you'll get and how you feel after you're done. This was a joy to play; highly recommended. (People who photosensitive disorders should be aware of rapidly flashing screens if you run out of health, and skipping dialogue has the background fast forward like a VHS. People with low vision should be aware that one level requires you to navigate through almost complete darkness to progress through the game. Make sure the game is safe and accessible for you to play before purchasing.)

_childDocuments_.review: The art is fantastic and the dialogue is all very enjoyable but there's a few things I have gripes with, mainly in regards to it having multiple endings. The game tells you to make sure you save often to avoid backtracking but it's designed in a way to force you to backtrack through almost the entire game if you're hungry for more dialog.  Overall my opinions of this game were fantastic with a first playthrough, with almost nothing to complain about, but attempting any subsequent playthroughs will surely sour your experience of the game. I'd love to see this addressed in the future, in addition to maybe a fast travel option included upon getting one of the endings. _childDocuments_.review: 9,5/10Once upon a time, there was an old lady who lived in her cabin in the forest, close to the small and peaceful village of Kieferberg, the lady lived her days somewhat lonely, living alone, until one day walking through the forest, she found a basket, where inside There was a baby, a girl who the lady adopted and named her Elise, and from that day on she raised the little girl. And so the years passed in the no longer empty cabin, with Elise growing up and filling the house with happiness, while the two had fun and learned new things together while all time smiling. ^^But unfortunately, one day age took its toll, and the old lady who took care of Elise came to the end of her life, leaving the now grown-up young Elise to have to fend for herself in order to support herself, having to fend for herself by doing domestic work for villagers in exchange for coins to buy food. Time passed and this new routine displeased Elise more and more, filling her with dreams of a life full of riches and luxury, without ever needing to work again and far away from the small village, something unfortunately impossible for the young woman, or was it what she thought, until the night she found an unexpected visitor inside her chicken coop. ^^+ A game with a very interesting story that manages to balance cuteness, romance and horror, as well as several secrets and things to discover.+ Three different options of girls for romance and each with their own charms to discover each of they routes.+ A total of ten different endings, including good and bad endings for each of the girls we can relate to.+ Interesting puzzles that fit well with the narrative during the more "peaceful" hours.+ The jobs to get money, despite only being four options, they managed to turn them all into fun minigames.+ The arts are incredibly beautiful, both in terms of the characters and events in the story, and in the pixelated part of the world, it is simply impeccable, truly beautiful.+ The soundtrack songs are also incredible, and perfectly match each part of the game, including some sung songs.- Unfortunately, the dialogue is only partially voiced, with the vast majority only having a voice at the beginning of the sentences.- Not having the New Game+ option, I think it would be interesting to continue with the money and items that were not used.The night everything began to change, when Elise ends up meeting a girl from outside the village called Rozenmarine, who despite a somewhat "friendly" beginning, starts to live with Elise. From this point on, our journey begins, guiding the young protagonist throughout her days, deciding what she has to do at each stage of the day, after all, Elise has to worry about her health, hunger and sanity, all three of which they are reduced for different reasons and will cause an abrupt end if they reach zero, and they can all be recovered with the help of items, but this requires money, which the villagers will not give for free. ^^But our protagonist's day isn't just about work, as there is always time for romance, after all, not only Rozenmarine, the traveling girl who is always willing to help Elise with anything, but also the kind and friendly peasant Freya and the smiling and always worried about the other Lebkuchen nun, all three very willing to help and get to know Elise much better and who knows win the protagonist's heart. And help is something that our protagonist will need, because without any warning one night, Elise begins to have strange dreams, about a being who claims to be able to make all of the young woman's dreams come true, but this will not be for free, and only if Elise obtain certain tributes for him within a week, in increasingly sinister and dangerous places where one mistake could be fatal, leading the question, how far is Elise willing to go, to fulfill her desires, and after all, what are the young woman's true desires. ^^My biggest, most sincere and true compliments to the AstralShift studio from Portugal in this part, I can't think of anything else to say about the art other than it being beautiful and wonderful in every part, from both the most bucolic and the sinister sceneries, to the characters and especially the art of the romance scenes, they are all impeccable and beautiful. As for the soundtrack too, I have nothing but praise, I liked the songs and I think they managed to combine the songs used very well with the parts of the story in which we hear them, as well as some incredible sung songs. ^^Little Goody Two Shoes was an excellent surprise, I already knew that the artistic part would be incredible having had contact with the previous game from the same studio, Pocket Mirror ~ GoldenerTraum, which I confess I still need to complete, but I had no idea I had so much fun with this game from start to finish, I was always wanting to explore and learn more about this story, that I sincerely congratulate the creators. Until the moment I write this review I have only done the route of one of the three girls, but here I say that I will soon do the others and I leave my most sincere recommendation for this game, which really pleased me, as it is not only beautiful, but also fun, with an interesting story and characters, three beautiful girls to meet and fall in love with and I'm sure that like me, you won't even watch the hours go by while playing. ^^

_childDocuments_.review: Great game!! Looks absolutely gorgeous, the story really hooks you in, the music is very pleasing, and the voice acting is lovely (Freya Phoebe i love you). There's a nice attention to details, I've spent all of my time looking through every nook and cranny of each map, trying to find every new bits of dialogue I can get. There's a good amount of content, worth more than 30 hours if you take your time reading through it all. If you're an RPG Maker horror game lover like me, this will definitely be for you, even more considering this is a prequel to Pocket Mirror (which you should play as well!). There's multiple endings I'm still going through. I love the dates with the girls and their interactions, always accompanied by some beautiful artwork. If there's one thing AstralShift knows how to do, it's gorgeous art :) And of course, having played through Pocket Mirror a few years ago (and once more when the remaster came out), I was so excited to learn more about the lore!As for the negatives, the game has a few bugs here and there (for some reason, I kept getting softlocked by some text not appearing at the well until an in-game day passed and it finally fixed itself...). Another issue is the pace, especially during the Witching Hours. it sometimes took me a moment to understand a mechanic, causing me to die repeatedly and having to go through cutscenes/dialogues again and again. You can skip dialogue sometimes but not always, and it can be a bit repetitive.Otherwise, I found the minigames and puzzles to be well-balanced. The amount of items and currency you get while doing tasks was more than enough for me to survive the entire playthrough without running out of food/healing items. I was a bit stuck at times which led to me looking at a guide, but I'm attributing it to a skill issue on my part (I'm not much of a pro gamer...). Otherwise, I felt the game was really fair and I don't see it impossible to find all the endings by yourself without having to look them up, which is really nice.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a gorgeous game that hearkens back to late 80's-early 90's style anime, complete with VHS noise and fast forward filters.  In the gameplay sense, you're trying to keep ahead of your food, health, suspicion, and sanity loss.  To make things difficult, you are almost broke most of the time.  To make things weird, you're having dreams and visions of things that may or may not be there--the ones that are there tend to hurt.     The story is eerie and compelling enough to keep players curious, and the branching paths (10 endings, not counting standard game overs) make for a significant amount of play, even if you'll be retreading territory sometimes.  Simplified, this game could be defined as resource management with some puzzle dungeons, but they are neither too difficult nor too easy.  Some things may not occur to you right away, so save and experiment.     As of 10 hours in I've completed one playthru and gotten a single ending, but I'm still looking because I was rather unsatisfied by my first ending--not through fault of the game, but rather because there were things I did not address in my first run through.     Fair gameplay, perfectly adequate writing, and glorious presentation.

_childDocuments_.review: honestly?? 10/10 game. Reminiscent of stories like Puella Magi Madoka Magica and Revolutionary Girl Utena with its somewhat surrealistic portrayal of navigating girlhood, Little Goody Two Shoes does a stunning job at capturing the joyful whimsy of an old fairy tale while navigating the horrors, stresses and our protagonist Elise faces day and night.Now that that's out the way the game is simply gorgeous, backgrounds, animations, sprites and even things like the HUD and menu screen are so thoughtfully designed to be reminiscent of old fairy tale illustrations with intricate borders and detailed patterns, painted backgrounds and still life style portraits for in game items. Its beautiful. The charm of the art style being inspired by 90s anime almost just feels like the icing on the cake honestly. Like i said 10/10 game, the music is full of whimsy and the characters are great, heads up tho Mibby has an expensive appetite.
_childDocuments_.name: Little Goody Two Shoes

_childDocuments_.review: How this game does not yet have a massive cult following is beyond me. This is the best horror I have played in ages. The art is breathtaking. The music is unique and forboding. The characters all have you doubting and overthinking while you yourself aren't quite ever sure of what to do and where to go. You're never really safe and playing this game without consideration of your actions makes everything spiral in a beautiful way.This is easily one of my favorite games of all time now already. I am going to 100% this and I am going to revisit it for years and years to come.If you like horror at all or you were, much like me, one of those kids that was way fascinated with those old RPG Maker horror games then you absolutely need to get this.
_childDocuments_.name: Little Goody Two Shoes

_childDocuments_.review: Throughout my entire playthrough I was just completely blown away by the surprisingly nuanced writing, beautiful music, consistently incredible art direction! The art perfectly blend the looks of retro anime, old RPGs (rpg-maker or otherwise), and european fairy tales into a unique visual identity full of personality. In addition, occasionally unusual art mediums are utilized in relation to a certain story element which I will not spoil here, but it certainly enhances that unique visual identity.As for the writing, the themes, motifs, and overall message are just a modern fairy tale to the very core of it's essence.My main fear going in was that the romantic elements might be a bit too "dating sim" for me, but I'm glad to say that just like the rest of the game, that element was handled with great care! Each romantic opportunity ended up being something I would look forward to, since they always felt like meaningful character explorations. And even on the few lighter interactions, Elise still has great chemistry with all 3 of the romance options, which keeps the writing of the events investing. I could ramble for hours about how much I loved this game. I'd say it might be one of my favorite video games now. If you like mysterious narratives, spooky old fairy tales, retro anime, gay people, and/or witchcraft, you should play this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Little Goody Two Shoes

_childDocuments_.review: Gorgeous, distinctive art style as well as an absolute banger of a soundtrack really carry this game to the top of the 'Hidden Gems' pile. If you like puzzle-oriented gameplay with a healthy dash of dating-sim features and, of course, a bit of horror, then this is for you.I will note, though, that this game is technically a prequel to the developer's other game, Pocket Mirror. Considering this is a story-based game with multiple endings, that information may or may not colour your perception of how much your choices matter. Still, would recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Little Goody Two Shoes

_childDocuments_.review: To put it into one sentence: Little Goody Two Shoes is amazing.Style, atmosphere, dialogue, variety, alternate endings and secrets, it has all you need from a horror game. The story goes surprisingly deep, the romances are very genuine and the way you engage with the game can differ wildly by what you prioritize. It is one of those tricky old-school inspired horror RPGs where you can make mistakes that will hurt you far down the line, but it also has the modern sense to guide the player just enough to feel they have proper agency in the outcomes.The village of Kieferberg feels incredibly alive with all the villagers soon becoming well known to you and being involved in constant events that shake their faith and stir suspicion amongst their own. It could be that their superstitions will escalate into doom for the protagonist, or perhaps she can instead become the backbone and hero of the town.Elise is a protagonist with big dreams and the courage to face the trials in her way to that happy ending. Her relationship to most of the village is strained and she clearly wishes to leave it behind and spread her wings, but it's never that easy. Every wish has a price.In this game you will explore Elise's past and decide her future and both may not be as clear as they seem. Maybe you will not feel like investigating the truth and just focus on your tasks, perhaps you will do anything to reach the miracle promised by the mysterious being or perhaps the love Elise shares with the three girls closest to her is its own reward? No matter how bad or how good things turn out... There is always a choice.
_childDocuments_.name: Little Goody Two Shoes

_childDocuments_.review: I love, love, LOVE this game. It's aesthetically gorgeous of course, that's a given. But the way the still art style is blended with the pixel sprites and used to better the story are what really stand out. The gameplay itself is also fun, but I would be lying if I said I didn't have to check for ways to solve a couple of the puzzles. The story is engrossing and the various options make for a good replay value in and of themselves.It isn't without issues, however. The controls can be laggy, which can be frustrating for the sort of gameplay involved. My biggest issue with the game is the save and reload system. For a game where you die a lot, sometimes you have to reload and replay several minutes of dialogue over and over. It would be solved if the game just autosaved right before every puzzle or gave you the option to start from the beginning of the puzzle. Alas, we'll just have to wait and see if that's fixed in a later update (though I doubt it).Overall, this is still a great game and is in my top 5 for the year.

_childDocuments_.review: I feel bad giving a bad review after having played for approx. 2.5 hours, I know it's not a lot. As a matter of fact, I gave up in the woodlands. There was something wrong with the moths at some point,  they just didn't want to follow me even though I had the lantern equipped. Doesn't work if I reload my save, so the game is broken. That's always nice huh ? I really wanted to enjoy this game, this is honestly, without hesitating, the most gorgeous 2D game I've ever seen. Even Ori doesn't compare in my opinion, I really like the in-game art style, how the environment beautifully set up, the village looks incredible. But the game itself is just really, really bad. I don't even know where to start. The minigames : I just don't understand. I have no problem with gathering eggs or with cutting logs with an axe, but does it really have to take place inside some ♥♥♥♥♥♥ gameboy / arcade machine 2D game format ?  You can't implement it directly into the game with the gorgeous graphics ? I don't understand what value it brings to the game. It's totally boring, there is absolutely zero fun. I just don't get it.And then there are these weird phases with a top-down view. There is something that I immediately noticed : the graphics just don't look that good in this perspective. Just like in the woodlands with the moths as explained previously, or inside the castle. It's really hard to put the finger on exactly why it doesn't work. But these moments in the game aren't really pleasant in any aspect. And it's not really scary or unsettling either.There is also the slow pace of the game : why everything has to be so slow ? Why the game has to reload a scene before and after a dialogue ? Same with the transitions between the scenes : they should be faster. I really don't understand all these loading screens. They are displayed on screen for a micro-second before disappearing and starting the next screen, but the fade-in / fade-out effects makes the whole thing so slow. And there are a lot of cuts.I really wanted to love this game. Elise is actually a pretty cool character. It really could have been better. I just feel the concept of the game itself is too flawed and not really interesting. The gameplay is just boring.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game for a first playthrough, but frustrating for repeated playthroughs should you want the other endings too. Here's the reasons:You cannot skip certain cutscenes and dialogues. This is already an issue in the first playthrough, so speedrunning the game for a different ending becomes a chore.There are 10 endings for this game, which is a lot, but if you miss some key item while playing the game, you are locked out of most of the endings. Be prepared to save a lot and pay attention to things.These are not related to the reasons, but I hate how some in-game tips misleads you into thinking they'll be a great help. Bringing a friend to do chores only helps for getting the S-rank achievement, because getting her to do it with you consumes 2 extra bread, which assuming you get S-rank in the chore you're doing, only nets you 40 coins profit as you earn 60 coins for S-rank, and 2 breads = 20 coins. Not to mention you do have to make sure you have 4 satiation bars ready before doing so, because anything below will simply lead you to game over after you are finished with the thing. There's a NPC that you have to bribe her every day in order to avoid raising suspicion, but her demands gets more expensive as the week progresses, and you can simply clear all the suspicion she brought to you by choosing the right words when talking to the townfolks. It's better to save the money for yourself than to bribe her.All of this makes me not want to do another playthrough and instead watch the other endings on youtube instead. Still, I'd recommend you to play the game for yourself, and if you're more willing than me, get the other endings too.

_childDocuments_.review: I think I'm less than halfway through but writing a review feels right about now.There is so much sentimental value here, so I hope to not gush too much. But it can't be helped, I'm going to anyway! Little Goody Two Shoes is very close to perfect. The visuals, the style, the artwork, even the menus and game over screens are brimming with an artistic vision that is well realized.All the heroines have a readily apparent uniqueness to their personalities and the hints toward their back stories make each moment intriguing. The storyline flows well, pacing is great, and I was immediately pulled in. It could be difficult sometimes to select which character I was most interested in during the peaceful and whimsical daytime sequences. Save files are abundant and multiple endings are present, so I can imagine replaying this over and over again and trying to achieve all of the endings.Nighttime sequences introduce a whole new style of gameplay. The horror element takes a while to start up, but much attention is paid toward level design. The bosses are memorable, the chase scenes can be deadly, and the tension is decent. I felt like a few areas were harsh so far as checkpoints, but I was able to squeeze by every single one and advance nicely. None are too frustrating yet.Overall, this is a game that is almost peerless insofar as style and atmosphere. It is one that I look forward to returning to. I highly recommend checking out the lengthy demo if you are interested. It does well at introducing all that is charming about Little Goody Two Shoes.Thank you to my friend, Matt, for this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Little Goody Two Shoes is mostly reading. There are gameplay elements, such as playing minigames to make money, managing your hunger throughout the day, and avoiding murder in nightmare-like Witching Hour sections. But Little Goody Two Shoes is predominantly a game about being in a town that believes a witch is causing different supernatural events each day. (And they aren’t entirely wrong — your dealings with demonic, supernatural entities throughout the game are the root of the issues.) So I think you get the most out of the game by running around town and seeing what everyone has to say (then talking to them again to hear Elise’s thoughts on them), even if it feels tedious.Though I feel like the townsfolk are relatively one-note. The town’s overall reactions to the New Suspicious Event of the Day are interesting, but the moment-to-moment conversations started to feel repetitive. Some people believe there’s a witch and will always basically say “It’s the witch’s doing!” while those that don’t believe will always just say “Let’s calm down”. A few of the townsfolk (excluding the relationship options who are obviously good) stood out, but most fall into either of the previously-mentioned camps. The main character, Elise, has a strong personality, but you do have to be willing to raise your Suspicion to really see her funny rude side.The Steam description mentions that this is a game where your choices matter. While this game does have a lot of endings, I didn’t feel like the game had sweeping branching paths that let you avoid the Witching Hour stuff. But I do think this approach was interesting. It makes it clear that this game is the story about Elise wanting her wish. By having Elise and her wish drive the plot forward instead of the player and THEIR wishes, it gives Elise more agency and thus more character. Giving the player choices that don’t stop Elise only makes this idea more powerful.Though I could be completely wrong and I just missed the choices that DO completely divert the story. But at the end of the day I like this idea.While I think the game is mostly about the townsfolk, the Witching Hour sections are certainly the meat of the game. You get one every night, so they’re plentiful and always there to look forward to. The game obviously looks beautiful enough everywhere, but the creative and creepy environments in these sections really do look (and even feel) amazing. As far as the gameplay in them goes…it’s nothing groundbreaking thanks to Elise’s limited movement, but it’s still engaging. Only one and a half nights had mechanics that I found more annoying than whimsical.A lot of the things pertaining to the supernatural in this game are written in riddles. As an idiot who is never good with this stuff, I feel like I maybe missed a lot of what makes people obsess over this game. It also makes it hard to tell if me thinking that the “lore” part of this game felt underdeveloped is true, or if it all just went over my head. It’s not confusing enough that you won’t understand what’s happening, at least. I’d be remiss to not mention the soundtrack. With a whopping 64 songs that are either fun, funny, beautiful, or cool, the music was something I was conscious of throughout the whole game.Overall, I think Little Goody Two Shoes is good, but its writing needed more direction to make the characters really stand out and shine. You could choose to not talk to anyone and just focus on the main plot points (and Witching Hours) to sidestep this issue (at the risk of throwing the baby out with the bath water). But I think it’s an unavoidable issue in the game’s important Relationships anyways. The game would probably also feel very short; my playthrough where I talked to everyone all the time was ~13 hours. Still, if the general witch-hunting premise and Nightmare sections sound interesting to you, the game is certainly a nice little treat regardless!

_childDocuments_.review: It's been awhile since I've been this hooked on an indie game like this. I absolutely love everything about this game (and the fact that it's sapphic is a huge win for me and all the lesbians). The art style is a love letter to early-late 90's manga art, and the game play is reminiscent of many horror RPG maker games (such as IB, Mad Father and The Witch's House), which I loved in my teens. I think this combination was a genius idea on Astral Shift's part. The nostalgia I felt accompanied by the hauntingly beautiful soundtrack was just a few of the highlights in this game.:: :I personally think that the positives heavily outweigh any negatives in this game. I've played through around 5 endings (?) so far, while romancing Rozenmarine. It can be somewhat tedious to get all endings or achievements, as there will be some parts of the game you can't skip, namely the puzzles (or dialogue). I've seen some complaints about too much dialogue, but coming from someone who plays Genshin, I think the dialogue amount is completely fine and relevant to all aspects of the story. All in all, I really, really love this game and I hope to see more from Astral Shift in the future!!!! And... please release some merch I will buy everything.

_childDocuments_.review: Finally 100% the game so now i can write this review confidently.I've been waiting for this to release for some time and I love this game so much, the art is stunning, the music is BANGING and the story is great! The multiple endings are all pretty good as well and what's great about this is that you don't have to play pocket mirror first so newcomers can hop in and enjoy the game! There are also a few bugs like getting hit right as a cut scene plays that just makes the game confused and freezes it.Another point I would like to suggest is (even though it might not make sense story-wise) please add more free sanity items either in Kieferberg or in the witching hour. _childDocuments_.review: Wonderful, wonderful, gorgeous game. The demo charmed me instantly and it only got worse for me after the final release, completely absorbing my brain for 11 days straight. Now I only regret how fast i went through it, because there's nothing else left for me to explore, while I still want to come back and see if there's anything I haven't seen yet. _childDocuments_.review: This game is both amazing and frustrating so I will list reasons why for both.  - The atmosphere and art style is a unique blend of 90's anime and European folklore. You can see the influence of characters like Asuka from Evangelion, Tomoyo from Cardcaptor Sakura, and art styles like Slayers, Utena, etc. Everything is gorgeous, from the CG characters that have a copic-like quality to them, to the pixel art, and especially the art style during the witching hours. There are times where I want to pause the game just to stare at the characters or environment. - The soundtrack is beautiful, a mix of anime-like pop with folksy accordion. The animated scenes that accompany the songs feel fun and perfect. - The game itself really leans into classic RPGs in that it gives you very little guidance. You can easily miss something and not realize it until later when unfortunately it's too late and you just lost hours of gameplay. I am actually writing this after a second playthrough where I hardlocked myself out of the endings I was trying to get. It feels a bit ridiculous that you need to be so so cautious when saving to the point that you should have a separate save file every day just in case. - You cannot skip cutscenes. I feel like there is nothing more enraging than dying after trying hard against a boss only to be sent back to the last save and have to watch the fight cutscene again. I think this may have been done on purpose to envoke the feeling of 90's RPGs when the same thing would happen. Unfortunately it just makes me upset because you have to die multiple times to learn how to win each fight.Overall this is the most conflicted I've felt about a game in a while. Because I absolutely love it and think people should play it but some aspects are so irritating to me that I am going to have to take a break for a few days before starting over. It seems someone has made a 100% guide, which I will be following the third time around as to not make the same mistakes again.

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic game with a beautiful art style, engaging plot, charming characters and an amazing soundtrack to boot (or... to shoes?) I loved slowly getting to know all the members of the town, having Elise interact with the three main girls in adorable ways, planning my time and managing my resources in satisfying ways, and slowly learning more about the mystery of the witch. I don't have much horror rpg genre experience, since I'm usually not a big fan of horror, but this was a lot of fun to play through regardless!My only real criticisms are that I wish cutscenes I've already watched could be skipped entirely instead of just fast-forwarded (in some cases, fast forwarding isn't even allowed), since it makes the process of replaying for different endings more tedious. This as well as the ability to rewind to earlier parts of the day / week. I got around the need for this by keeping a bunch of manual saves, but it would be a nice QoL feature to have rewinding be built-in. Ultimately though, the game has enough going for it that I don't mind these minor annoyances. I'm still working my way through the other endings, since I've only gotten one so far, but for just 20 bucks this game is very much worth it! Looking forward to checking out Pocket Mirror afterwards!

_childDocuments_.review: A beautifully lovingly crafted game reminiscent of 90s anime. The visuals and overall presentation are striking and so full of life and charm. It uses multiple art styles to get across different feelings, pixel art for cute little mini games, storybook for cut scenes and more surreal and darker styles and looks that clash with the established cute art for the darker underbelly. The music is fantastic. Everything from the little tunes talking to towns folk and doing chores to the foreboding tracks while exploring and trying to achieve your goal. The story is and writing is very nice. The characters are very fun, especially the four main girls, but the towns folk are very nice to talk and feel very developed by the end. Muffy and Mr. Gustav are highlights. I wont talk to much about the writing or story as you need to see it yourself but it is pretty good and well told. While not required, as this game takes place before hand and stands on its own, it would be beneficial to play Pocket Mirror for a wider narrative. I recommend Pocket Mirror its very good. Game play wise you'll be doing a few things. At day you'll be talking to towns folk, doing chores to get money so you can buy food, dating sim gay girl stuff, that sort of thing. At night you'll be doing puzzles and.... well it wouldn't be fun if I went into depth with it now would it? Overall its an amazing game 100% worth playing 10/10 will wear shoes again.

_childDocuments_.review: Follow Elise and find out about the “fated” night and how it all lead to the upcoming Events that will deliver a relative dark story with no real “happy” end and will she find out if its really possible to get a 2nd chance on a happy life or what really happened, who she really is? And what about the price for it all?The game will offer you from animated pieces of anime style and beautiful designed/cutiefied scenes which are like a moving picture book. It also offers you dazing cg’s for various interactions.While you got a drawn like overworld in I would say 2.5D which offers breathtaking views over a vast landscape you perhaps will try to reach~But don’t let the sight fool you beneath the cute and beautiful lays a dark/abstract construct which adds a new layer to your story.Solve puzzles with near to no hints, die, survive, carve for hunger, lose your sanity overall welcome to a gameplay that will teach you to mange Elise’s Hunger, Health and Romance while of course grinding some money to pay for those things too via simple to heavy Minigames~Ahem besides that the gameplay offers you a relatively big map to explore the deep dark secrets of Kiefernberg, while you can trade, talk with various villagers, do tasks and much more. But always remember you are just a “fragile” girl in this world~Delve into a very fitting thematic music with some bits of voice acting and then also enjoy the animated pieces with full singing in japanese, which feel like sung with heart.The Game offers you 10 endings, 6 of which are related to your romance, 3 that seal your fate and 1 that lets you know why this all is happening to you. The Lore from the endings but also from the characters, interactions and findables is quite big and will immerse you even further.The game needs around 8 hours if your optimistic and don’t try to find out about everything, if you try to search, find,.. it will take you about 12 to 16 hours. (for one ending or perhaps “more”)This Game still hooks me and got me pondering about what is really real in this story and why we are fated as Elise with such a fate which seems to loop and to a degree seems like a story that never really ends~ So yeah uhm I would not have thought the game would hook me that much, its been quite a while since that last happened, so all I would like to still say is make sure to bring a lot of time and take the time to really immerse yourself into this story, its really worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is basically perfect. Every aspect of the art-style is incredible, including the UI, menus, levels, characters, and cutscenes. The story and writing is extremely well done and intense at times, and the characters are all unique and interesting. The puzzles are also pretty good, though the game is not abundant with them. I could barely call it a complaint, more of a minor annoyance, but if I had to think of anything wrong with the game, it would be the dialogue options, as they're the main mechanic of either raising or lowering the town's suspicion against you. It's usually unclear which option is good or bad, resulting in what feels like more of a coin flip. This isn't a very big issue at all (and might even be intentional) because managing suspicion is super easy, and you'd have to be pretty unlucky to get it too high.If you're even slightly interested in this game I very highly recommend you try it out!!!!

_childDocuments_.review: Little Goody Two Shoes is a jrpg inspired by fairy tales such as Snow White, Cinderella, Alice In Wonderland, The Wizard of Oz, etcIts about a poor orphan girl Elise who dreams of fortune. She lives in a village of witch-fearing people. And Elise must be careful of her actions lest she gets accused of being one.One day she finds ruby slippers and is approached by a mysterious figure promising Elise her greatest desire. However this will come at a cost. Its up to you to decide if you are willing to pay it. The game has multiple endings. And which one you get will depend on your actions, dialogue, the tasks you do, etcTasks are done via mini-games.There are survival elements to the game; you need to make sure you eat to keep your strength up.You are given multiple save slots which you should take full advantage of in case you mess up.There are 3 girls you can romance, this will also determine your ending.

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished this game! I think all in all it's an interesting and compelling experience, though I think it's weighed down in places by some things that could be improved with QOL updates. In particular, if you want to get all of the endings, you have to plan ahead, which isn't too much of a problem, but if you want to get all of the character-specific endings, you essentially have to do three separate playthroughs. This wouldn't be much of an issue if the "skip" button actually skipped scenes rather than acting as a fast forward. That ended up making the process of getting the last 4 endings after I had already gotten 6 in my first playthrough more difficult than I believe it had to be. On the note of more difficult than it had to be - the only parts in which I was deeply frustrated and not in a fun way were with the boss sequences, especially with their instant-kill conditions. I also think that some of the puzzles aren't the most intuitive, but I was able to do all of them without any guides. Back to the positive notes, I think this game is a fun time with an interesting narrative and compelling characters. My favorite was Lebkuchen, but I feel that each of the girls, especially Elise as our protagonist, had a lot of fun and charm to them, which made me want to see all of the endings. The lore is fascinating and compelling (especially since I chose to play Pocket Mirror first before checking this one out!) and the puzzles, while a bit obtuse at times, still make Sense and rarely ever detracted from the experience. It was also fun to get all of the achievements! It goes without saying that the production value of this game is a stand-out aspect of it, from the lovely musical moments and charming voice acting to the ways in which all of the art direction comes together, especially the mixed media segments. If you are open to some light frustration with the puzzle and boss design, and willing to take the time to do enough playthroughs to at least see the endings you want to see, then I recommend this game for any fan of dark fantasy horror adventures. I'm excited to see what AstralShift works on next!

_childDocuments_.review: Little Goody Two Shoes is a fine example of a game that manages to be style over substance, while still being, for the most part, good. The majority of my praise for the game comes down to its mood, aesthetics, pacing, and presentation. As you can see right off the bat from the trailer, it takes very heavy stylistic inspiration from late 80s to early 90s anime, and where it does embrace those, it does so with gusto. The cheerful Japanese vocal tracks for not only the intro but two animated musical sequences in the game expertly recall the distinct charm and style of their inspirations, calling to mind European-inspired children's anime like "Grimm's Fairytale Classics". However, once you get into the game itself, this aesthetic is (potentially disappointingly) not maintained constantly. While it's still used for backgrounds and certain animations and effects, the main game sprites are much more recognizably modern, but drawn in a cute and appealing chibi-esque style that's still quite endearing. Aside from the handful of cinematics, though, the real show-stealers are the nightly trips into the mysterious woods, which take a highly abstract mixed-media approach that's unapologetically inspired by Mahou Shoujo Madoka Magica, a clear inspiration in the story too. Down to the beautifully hand-drawn UI elements, everything about the presentation is just a feast.Unfortunately, the primary gameplay loop is very poorly supported. The game advertises itself as one in which "all your decisions matter". Anyone who's ever bought a video game before knows how typically hollow that promise is, and that rule holds here. The game is obstinately linear. While the protagonist, Elise, has the option to build and deepen relationships with several cute-as-a-button girls, who have their own varying dialogue for certain key parts of the game, virtually everything that has any bearing on the direction of the plot is based on a handful of very late-game decisions. If you know what criteria are needed, it's quite easy to set yourself up to see all ten endings (and a few ending-esque alternative game-over sequences) on a single save. The primary gameplay outside of the puzzle-oriented forest dungeons is mostly just talking to random townsfolk and playing a handful of minigames for cash.That cash is used to purchase recovery items to keep Elise fed, healthy, and sane, but except for health (which is often better restored by just reverting to a save after getting chewed up by the forest's various phantasmagoria), they're really quite easy to maintain. The biggest risk for running out of hunger is simply forgetting when you advance to the next phase of the day, but the game considerately reminds you of this with an obnoxious audio and visual effect that makes that impossible to overlook. There is a grand total of about one side quest that's more than just a quick A-to-B fetch quest and has any bearing on any sort of story progression. The Suspicion mechanic seemed extremely interesting at first, but most suspicion-raising conversations either present you with options so seemingly identical that it may as well be a coin toss, or so obvious that they might as well be named "Raise Suspicion" and "Lower Suspicion".The writing's a little clumsy in spots. It struggles a bit with repeating itself, especially in terms of vocabulary. Some recurring phrases come up with an outright weird level of consistency. Every single character will always describe getting chewed-out as "getting an earful". Talking at length about anything is "wittering". Every character, regardless of age or even humanity, refers to others as "lad" or "lass". It creates occasionally jarring issues with character voice, and really does not help in differentiating even the relatively small cast of still largely interchangeable villagers.However, Elise herself is delightful. She's headstrong and absolutely certain of what she's owed, palpably gritting her teeth when forced to play nice by the player to avoid ending up abandoned in the woods by the superstitious townsfolk. While her prospective love interests can feel a little bland, she's prickly and dissatisfied and powerfully motivated with a level of resentment and ambition that perfectly fit her place in the shoes of the dark fairytale heroine - though some of what catches her off-guard about the story will be things that the player sees coming from miles off.The story is, at least to a point, another strong point. The problem is that it starts on such a promising curve of steady escalation of tension, then just suddenly throttles off. Up to roughly the halfway point, the story progressively gets more intense, as dark omens and inexplicable tragedies pile up, all building towards the increasingly portentous big day of the festival at the end of the week. Paranoia grows, awful things happen, and it starts to feel like it should be getting harder and harder to evade suspicion. But then things oddly just... get better for a while. It remains trivially easy to keep suspicion at zero, and the steady accumulation of dread flatlines.Despite a weak core gameplay loop and the disappointing plateau of a plot that should have ratcheted the drama up to a horrific climax, though, I found the whole experience of LGTS still remarkably enjoyable. The excellent soundtrack and visuals enrich the whole game in a level of dark fantasy splendor that's really worth recommending on its own. It's not something I expect many players would want to revisit just for the fun of the gameplay, but the cycle of the lovely but troubled pastoral setting and the otherworldly mysterious woods comes together into something bewitchingly beautiful.

_childDocuments_.review: Little Goody Two Shoes is a storytelling game that take place as a prequel to Pocket Mirror (also an absolutely amazing game) where you play as Elise, the girl who is stuck in a daily life that she desperately wishes to escape. If you like thinking that every decision you make in this game is the wrong choice, then you should buy it. If you don't like complex puzzle solving, very vast themes to other medias and various historical stories, then I'd suggest waiting or just watching a playthrough. I cannot recommend this game enough and if you play it you will probably love it as much as I have already.

_childDocuments_.review: This game looks great, plays nice and I'm amazed how high effort it all is!A well made RPG Maker-Style horror-ish game with an old-school anime style where everyone just accuses you of everything bad that happens in the town. Not very scary, but it has an interesting story and some likable, shoujo-like characters that you can even romance (and they're all girls). In the day you can go romance some girls and work for some money so you buy food to not die of hunger - this money also helps you prepare a little bit for every night that comes later, buying health items or sanity potions to stay sane. It's not a very hard game, so far I haven't really felt like I have to care too much about the hunger bar or the sanity bar. In fact I don't think these mechanics are challenging at all and I wish there was a harder mode (maybe this changes later).Anyways, I recommend it!
