_childDocuments_.review: First off, let me say that this thumbs up is purely on a 'get it on sale' kinda mindset. If there was a 'maybe' option for reviewing, this would probably be one of those games.  - The art style is amazing and fits the weird fairy tail book mixed with 80s-90s anime. - The music was enjoyable for the 8 hours I had with this game. - The story was pretty neat, except for a few bumps I had with other sections I'll get to. - The trek from Elise's home to town gets annoying when you get to do it 2 times a day. A fast travel system would have been nice. Luckily, the game is short enough that I can pass it off. - The puzzles in the game are alright, nothing to write home about. Then again, there was one that was rather clever, but that might have been my dumb ass not knowing. - ♥♥♥♥ kiss the rat. - The dating system is dumb and forces you to pick one girl at the very start. Pick the wrong girl, you can't date anyone else. The moment you go on a date with someone, the other two are no longer options. Speaking of which, if you don't get all 6 hearts  Personally, I picked a girl, dated her once, didn't like her, but couldn't pick anyone else after that... but I'd already gotten through 3 days of the week before realizing this... - The survival elements are just... really poorly implemented. Food, after the 2nd/3rd day is so plentiful as all the games you have to play during the week are easy as hell (Except for the dumb chicken game which controls like ass and kiss the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ rat.) and usually net you 60 gp. Hell, even matches, which again, you are supposed to be careful with end up being tossed at you like candy, the same goes for healing items. The only part of this system that even remotely was trouble was the suspicion system, but even that is easily deal with by stuffing Muffy's Mouth with sweets. - The choices in dialog sometimes make 0 sense or sometimes are the exact opposite of what they mean. When dating, you get a heart upon saying the right thing to your girl. Often times, the two answers are 'say bad thing' or 'say other bad thing', with one of them progressing your love hearts. The worst of it, for example, is a boss later in the game where failing to pick the right answer means instant death and you get to restart the boss battle! I had to redo the boss battle 3 times because each dumb question had answers akin to meaningless words. One such answer "I'm scared." turns into Elise saying 'I love her!' ...  WHY NOT JUST SAY THAT IN THE DAMN ANSWER YOU SHOWED ME?! Isn't the point of a dialog game is to have some kind of player interaction that they can judge the outcome on?! This happens many times throughout the story, but not nearly as egregious as this single boss fight.  - You can't date Muffy! Give me my little sweets goblin!
_childDocuments_.name: Little Goody Two Shoes

_childDocuments_.review: Oof. I really wanted to go into this game and absolutely love it but now that I've completed it, I really wish I could give a neutral review, because I can't fully recommend this game. Visuals:The game is incredibly stunning. I often found myself just standing around an area, admiring the surroundings. That said, the sprites can be a little too detailed and maximalist for my liking, and the artworks for the men look very strange. I also wish that cgs would be displayed on the entire screen, instead of a small window.Audio:The music is very pretty and the sound design was fitting. The game is partially voiced, however it's pretty aparent early on that they did not record a lot of voicelines so they tend to repeat a lot. Some of the voice lines also seem randomly a lot louder than the others.Story/Writing:The plot is okay. It's a pretty standard fairytale kind of story, nothing groundbreaking or unexpected really. The characters are fine, though I never really warmed up to Elise's personality, personally. The writing ranges from very good to eh. For the most part the writing feels appropriate for the pseudo time period but I'm not sure why Elise says "for goodness sake!" every other sentence (hyperbole).Gameplay:The gameplay, oh god the gameplay. This is the main reason I was close to giving this game a negative review. The gameplay is basically split into 2 sections: Town and Woodlands. The town gameplay is during the day; You'll talk to villagers, hang out with the love interest of your choice and do minigames to earn money. I don't really have a problem with the town gameplay, I just wish the minigames were optional and didn't determine how much money you have throughout your playthrough. In LGTS you need money to buy items that are essential to continuing your playthrough. You basically have a stamina bar that automatically decreases over the course of the day and needs to be filled up again by buying food. If the stamina bar is empty, you automatically die, so having enough money is essential. Problem is, some of the minigames absolutely suck (Looking at you, kiss the rat) Thankfully, you're never actually forced to play kiss-the-rat and the other minigames are tolerable, but it's not my favortie part of the game. I was good enough at them to never run into a money problem, but I've heard from other players who got basically softlocked because they struggled with the minigames. But my bigger fish to fry is the woodland gameplay. On most nights you enter the woodlands where you have to face a multitude of different puzzles while evading enemies. Most of these puzzles are complete bullsh*t trial and error with no explanation what you need to do. And even after you figure it out, they're honestly just not fun to get through. Sometimes a boss fight is also after a long unskippable cutscene, so you have to waste 5 minutes of spamming the spacebar every time you die. And I also love that one puzzle where you're lost in a giant dark room with no clue what to do while running away from enemies. Did I say one puzzle? I meant multiple. Honestly the puzzles all kind of feel the same, which only makes this worse.Also I'm not sure where to put this, but there are multiple game breaking bugs in this game A YEAR after release. he most egrecious example of this, is getting locked out of the shop on the final day. If you forgot to buy food before this, you're literally just insta dead, hope your last save wasn't too long before that.Lastly Endings:I'll keep this as spoiler-free as possible but if you still want to play this game I'd probably skip this part regardless. Basically, the endings are kinda disappointing. Especially the good endings don't really feel earned. I expected a bit more after 11 hours of playthrough... But they're also not terrible. I really like that they give you a little picture to go with it, and I also like the variety of endings you can get. That said, I've only played 5/10 endings, because those were all the endings I was able to get after my playthrough and god knows I am not playing through this game again any time soon.Overall I'd score the game:9/10 Visuals8/10 Audio7/10 Writing3/10 Gameplay5/10 EndingsFor a total of 6.4/10. I recommend it if you're an rpgmaker-like fan who is used to suffering through badly designed puzzles to experience the story. (I say this as a big rpgmaker fan and I will probably return for more playthroughs of this game... one day.)

_childDocuments_.review: This game released on Halloween, hadn't had time to dive in just yet but it was actually one of my most anticipated game of this year ever since Elise took over Square Enix's twitter last year, or was it the one before? Either way I'm happy to say it hasn't disappointed. The game is part investigation and mystery, part Social Management, and part economy management. It's set in a small German town during the middle ages(?). The game has a delightfully Clampy art style with a mix of Disney in its background and paralax art, all that accompanied by an enchanting soundtrack that always perfectly suits the mood of the scene happening on screen. I spent last evening playing it with my girlfriend, it's super cosy despite its horror and mysterious elements, and really can't wait to play some more. We're both excited to see where the already mysterious clues and rumours about the woodland witch lead us. The main character, Elise, is immediately endearing and fun to play as, and it's one of the few games I can think of where the character is explicitly a lesbian which is fun and cool to see. Also this game has set the new record for crying speed runs as it made both me and my girlfriend cry about 60 seconds into it.Edit: We played a session or two more since the review, we're deeper into the game now and the spooky elements have started showing up. Super compelling and great, can't wait to continue.Edit 2: We have since finished the game. One of my favorite games now honestly, just what a vibe and great story. Fantastic characters as well, loved it to bits and put Astral Shift on the map for me as one of the best devs out there. 10/10 Lebkuchen forever.

_childDocuments_.review: An amazing phantasmagorical adventure with a fantastic visual style and OST. The story is amazing, as is the romance. _childDocuments_.review: This is a primarily narrative-driven linear game, with choices that allow you to get different endings. The time- and resource-management aspects are largely overstated, as you never really have to sacrifice an event for another (there's even a guide to be able to get every ending on a single save file). As such the difficulty of this game is pretty relaxed, with random spikes that I can see causing trouble for some players.If you're worried about the horror aspects, this game uses horror mostly for aesthetics and tension. Maybe I was just too busy admiring the gorgeous visuals to get truly scared by anything.Speaking of which, if the visuals or soundtrack appeal to you at all, I would definitely recommend this game on just those elements alone. I stopped in many places just to admire the visuals and listen to the soundtrack, and I'm sure the music will be stuck in my head for a long time.A tiny oddity I noticed is that the game has language support for Japanese and English, but both options use the same (English?) voice actors, just speaking different languages. Japanese seems to be the least jarring, since there's cutscenes that have singing in Japanese, I just found it interesting (also, the "voice-acting" option refers to dialogue grunts, there is no full voice-acting in the game).The story wasn't anything outstanding, but it provided a nice mystery, and rewarded me enough for paying attention to lore and such. I was assuming I'd learn about the townspeople in even greater detail, but considering the scope of the game I guess it wouldn't make sense. That said, the characterization I did get was something I enjoyed greatly, enough to bother hunting around every hour of the day just to see how people are reacting to current events. Knowing afterwards that this game is a prequel to the studio's other game puts things into more context as well.A small detail I enjoyed that I haven't seen any other game do is conversations smoothly recognizing that your character knows some information. For example, a conversation will go something like this: And if you haven't spoken to anyone before then they'll explain. This happens within other contexts so smoothly that it took me a bit to even recognize this.With all that said, by far the worst aspect of the game has to be the save-system. The game has no auto-save whatsoever, and game-overs will always restart at your latest save. This means constantly having to save at times you expect story progression to take up time, and often having to re-read dialogue after game-overs. The game has a fast-forward button, but unfortunately it doesn't seem to work for big story cutscenes, when you'd most need it (perhaps something to do with actors having to move around the screen and such?).Hopefully they can improve the saving and fast-forwarding in a future patch. At the very least a bandaid fix for specific segments where continuing after a game-over puts you right where you left off.

_childDocuments_.review: After playing through this game, figured it's time to put my two cents in towards this game.  90s Anime Aesthetic mixed in with the dark elements of a typical Grimm fairytale methinks (and also a prequel to Pocket Mirror, but I haven't played it yet), this was different but also enjoyable for me.Game follows Elise, a girl in a village who dreams of something more, she wants to one day leave the village of Kieferberg & live a royal life.  After an encounter with a traveling girl named Rozenmarie & some strange happenings which culminates in finding Ruby Red Shoes buried in her garden, Elise finds herself on the path to that dream, but the price may be heavy to pay...This game takes place In & around the Village of Kieferberg and different hours of each day for a span of a week.  From here, you manage your day accordingly before braving the mysteries of those who would grant Elise's wish.  During the day, you "work" by playing certain mini-games to earn money to buy what's needed to survive & during the "Witching Hours" is where you encounter the challenges.You must make choices to manage yourself over the course of the week game time & that means keeping yourself alive 4 different ways.  The basic one is Life Bar, which you can lose during your treks in the forest like any normal adventure game.  The other 3 are Food, Sanity & Suspicion.  Food you have to keep an eye on because you'll need it after every phase of activity each day, more if you employ Rozenmarie to help with your jobs.  Sanity, in my gameplay, is mostly lost when you interact with Golden Maidens & finally Suspicion always plays a part in your Village interactions.  With all the strange things going on, the people will be on edge & think you may be a Witch, so everything you do and say will be judged, but if manage your choices well, you can make it through the week.  Basically you work during the day, chat around to learn the state of the village each day & pursue romantic relationships with Rozenmarie, Freya or Lebkuchen.Exploring the forest during the witching hours varies with each night & you'll be navigating through each area & solving puzzles while a light is shined on the mysterious past of Elise & how it ties to her situation.  Many of the puzzles are basic but can be challenging if you don't know the info of where to look.  For a while, I was lost on the Moonphase puzzle for example because I didn't bother to examine places that at least made solving a but clearer.Despite the appearance of this game, it does have vibes of Dark Mystery & Horror.  In fact a good majority of the ten endings are bad endings(  ).  In fact, when it comes to everything surrounding the Witches' worlds, it just literally screamed Puella Magi Madoka Magica Witches & the areas are sort of a reflection on that style & thought it was something.All in all, it's a great game.  Kept me entertained, had some good & bad surprises, so try not to read a guide before at least playing it blind first time.  At best you'll enjoy it better that way obviously.  One major issue I had is that when I did fail in parts of Witching Hour & I chose to continue, I couldn't fast forward through cutscenes just to get to the point where I try again on the point where I died.  Some conversations I can Fast Forward thru & some I couldn't whereas I had to hit the button on my controller repeatedly just to speed through the scene & try again.  Aside from that, it's a good game to consider.

_childDocuments_.review: I looked forward to this game for years and even backed it on Patreon, but it turned into a disappointment. The worst issue in my opinion is the controls - it's a struggle to just pick up something from the floor or interacting with the right object (it always thinks I want to look at something else). However, there were many other things getting on my nerves. The graphics look very beautiful in the screenshots, but once you actually play the game you get the feeling the UI and environments were designed BEFORE testing and optimising the layouts (a deadly sin in my opinion). It's difficult to tell what's decoration and what can be interacted with, so this game's solution is to make speech bubbles with icons flash over the objects now and then. It feels like a quick fix rather than intentional design.As someone who followed the development of the project for a long time, I feel like the concept was a really good idea but that the final game wasn't quite what I imagined. Of course, projects always change over time, and perhaps I just had too high expectations, but something just doesn't feel right.On a positive note, I really like the soundtrack, so I got something out of my purchase and maybe the game will be updated in the future to adress some of the issues.

_childDocuments_.review: Elise's journey to achieve her dream of gaining riches and leaving Kiferberg behind was a joy to play. The village interactions during the day were always kept interesting due to Elise's sharp personality and the personalities of her friends. Likewise, the "maid of all work" aspect of completing jobs effectively put the player in her Elise's shoes. Days definitely had an urgency to earn money and balance my hunger, sanity, and suspicion resources to avoid an early demise.Presentation wise the entire package is fantastic. The soundtrack is beautiful (so many good songs), and the pixel art + 90s anime art style is striking and filled with creative touches particularly in the night scenes. The story itself was enjoyable the entire way through. The main downside is that besides the ending, the relationships you decide to pursue don't change the core story. Rozenmarine, Lebkuchen, and Freya were all absolutely adorable and a joy to interact with, so it is a shame that this aspect was not done better. In the end, one of my favourite games of 2023

_childDocuments_.review: It's got some issues for sure, an antiquated save system, the protagonist being who they are (wonderful, but also so frustratingly in denial that she often can't see two feet in front of herself), and the survival bars which went from an interesting mechanic to an exercise in "go buy bread so the game doesn't softlock you", but with all that aside this is honestly still a real gem.The lovely german fairy tale aesthetic, the classic anime art that's melded several times over with other unique styles, the super well written music, even the character designs are all wonderful, and they all work together to form something that's truly unique. On top of that, there really aren't many other games I've played that have so mastered that feeling of falling out of normality into something so horrifying and alluring in equal measure that you can't help but be tempted to dive yet deeper into its depths.If any of that sounds cool to you, and you like RPGMaker esque games, then absolutely give it a go! I for one am quite excited to see where these devs go from here.

_childDocuments_.review: Little Goody Two Shoes is a story game that mixes the elements of both an RPG and a visual novel. Generally speaking, I am not a fan of RPGs (Final Fantasy, Octopath Traveller, etc.) so when I first saw the trailer for this game I was sceptical that I would enjoy it. Luckily they offered a demo and I was pleasantly surprised to see that this game does not play like an RPG. I would say that it leans more towards being a story and visual novel game, only borrowing how you navigate the world from an RPG. The incessant grinding of an RPG is thankfully not included in this game. If you’re curious if this play-style is up your alley, I recommend giving the demo a try.I have very few critiques for this game. It is exceptionally well made. Most throw this game into the category of “RPG-Maker-like” though I would say that it goes above and beyond what that engine typically has to offer (for reference this game is made in Unity). Immediately I noticed just how beautifully detailed all of the artwork was in this game. The design effort put into the world you navigate really shows. Despite only having several points to visit on the map, it paints a vivid picture of the world Elise lives in as you get caught up in watching the story unfold. On a technical side, you don’t navigate the fixed grid RPG-Maker requires, plus there are several extra features and polish such as, mini-games and animations that you won’t find in games from that engine.The writing for this story is also well laid out. To avoid any spoilers the most I will say is that the town of Kieferberg and Elise’s goals are shrouded in just enough mystery to keep you wondering what is going to happen next the entire time. It is quite similar to a good mystery book that you can’t seem to put down, but you also have the element of wondering if the actions you are taking are the “right” ones as time progresses. Even after you complete the game for the first time, as advertised, there are 10 main endings. Getting to an ending takes about 12 hours. However after finding one ending, I found that the world & story was so well built that I wanted to unravel the rest of the mystery of this adventure and took the time to complete all endings. I can say that although some endings are weaker than others, overall I really enjoyed navigating around the land of Little Goody Two Shoes and interacting with all the colourful characters to ultimately uncover the mystery this game sets up and experience the emotional endings it has to offer.Technically speaking, I found very few QA issues and only one hard lock that can be fixed by reloading the most recent save. All of which already appear to be reported on the Steam bug posting page for this game at the time of writing. My critiques are: - I wish that there were more mini-games. These were always fun to try and high score throughout the days but it would have been nice to see a few more for variety. - Some of the endings I found the deciding choices to be less intricate and more binary than I thought they would be. I will refrain from further detail to avoid spoilers. That being said, the endings themselves make up for this complaint.In whole, this game gets a strong recommendation from me if you are looking for a story game that you navigate like an RPG. It has beautiful artwork, an interesting story, great voice acting (Same VAs in both JP & EN) and an enjoyable “game play loop” with great controls.

_childDocuments_.review: Little Goody Two Shoes is a beautiful game. It nails the feel it's going for perfectly. I saw another reviewer list as a negative that they got sick of looking at the art/that it all started to blend together eventually, but I can't even begin to imagine that, myself; I spent most of my time with this game marveling at just how pretty it looks and sounds. It's incredible. I'm jealous.Art aside, though, as someone who played this game after being unfortunately disappointed by Pocket Mirror (AstralShift's previous outing, which this game is technically a prequel to, although you don't need to play it to play this or vice versa), I found it an improvement in nearly every aspect; it's obvious to me that AstralShift made good use of the time they had to improve at their craft. The story is easier to follow and paced much better, the puzzles are less obtuse, the gameplay is a lot more thought out, not least of all since it's not held back by RPG Maker...I had a few minor hiccups (dialogue options coming off differently than I thought they would, some gameplay sections got a little frustrating), but they didn't even come close to ruining the experience for me. I loved this game from front to back, and the ending left me hollow inside (there are good endings, too! That's the only reason I'm consolable!). Highly highly recommend it. I'm a big fan of the general aesthetic and vibe of this game, and it has roots in RPG Horror, so it was right up my alley. This game is for the gays and they refused to let us down.

_childDocuments_.review: Iconic game. This game is clearly drawn from the lineage of enigmatic and spooky RPG maker classics, which is a trend very close to my heart. If you love Yume Nikki or Ib, this could be a good one to check out. It's one of those games that's probably more fun to go in blind, because (spoilers) this is a charming, folksy game that turns out to have sinister undertones. Little Goody Two Shoes pulls this off with flying colours, due mostly to the absolutely lush glory of the art. You can tell they put a ridiculous amount of effort into even the tiniest aspects here - the inventory screen, the time passing sign, the "Do you want to save" confirmation. Every single piece is ornately hand crafted and illustrated, so that you're constantly discovering new beautiful little bits off artistry.As the game spirals into its more sinister and unhinged moments, that art progressively goes off the rails with it. We get wild combinations of pixel art, lush hand-drawn animation, 90's anime VHS vibes, even some nightmarish claymation. It all manages to fit together, it's all gorgeous, and this relentless pace of constantly seeing new wild beautiful ♥♥♥♥ is a major motivator that pushes you through this game.The game loop is really crisp too: in some ways it kind of feels like Pathologic for beginners. You have to manage various resources of hunger, money, matches, time, and (as you break away and explore the hidden places) your sanity and health. The game starts you off in this folksly fairytale town, but as events progress the people in the town grow more and more suspicious, and you have to juggle their suspicion as well. It's simple but it starts to really ratchet up the stress and tension as the game goes on and you have to make stressful choices - do you sacrifice some food to stop someone from gossiping and raising your suspicion meter? Can you afford to explore that hidden area when your sanity is dipping low?There are quirks and issues here. At times the game gets a little too hard for its own good - meaning you might have to reload over and over again to see a section through. This isn't the kind of game that feels satisfying in - it's not like Super Meat Boy or anything. Your main motivation here is the story, atmosphere and art, so having to reload a bunch just feels like a frustrating road block rather than a satisfying test of skill.The endings also in my eye are a little unsatisfying. There are 10 different endings, so you're intended to play through at least a few times to get a bunch of them. Each ending basically resolves a single subplot of the game, and everything else that came up is left unresolved. This makes each one feel a little lacking to me, personally. I ended up feeling like I wanted one really solid ending where all the separate plotlines came to a head at once.Anyway, if you like cutesy games that turn out to be spooky, RPG maker classics, old folk tale influences, this is a great pick.

Some people in the forums say this game can softlock you, or the like.It cannot. However, you can lose the chance to reach good endings if you're not paying attention. _childDocuments_.review: I’m not sure what we can do to convince you to play this that the phrase ‘Yuri Phantasmagorical Horror’ doesn’t already cover but Little Goody Two Shoes is fantastic throughout. The game is beautiful and the art , the characters and the twisting narrative are all so well refined that even as you the player can see what the road ahead might look like you feel compelled to assist Elise in her naivety anyway. Her struggle is very relatable yet so obviously foolish. All said and done though when Elise finally catches up to you the player and realizes things are not as they seem the choice ultimately lies with you. And make no mistake if you make sure she finishes the job you will be reminded every step of the way that was YOUR choice with a sequence that is equal parts as brilliant as it is confronting.We played to get all the endings and even knowing what was coming for some of the bad ones did not make things any easier, the narrative is just that well paced and has plenty of creative ways to twist the knife in your back [which you helped to put there]. Thankfully the good endings and many of the date sequences produce so much wholesome yuri goodness that it all balances out.The day to day time management mechanics are also very satisfying and while the minigames that represent your work can feel incredibly frustrating at first I think that contributes to your Empathy for Elise, her life truly does kind of suck but perhaps not enough to justify what follows…We’ve probably already said to much, please, please play this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Rabbit hole game. The art is really the most fascinating aspect of the game. And by looking at the credit roll you can see why... number of people on art is way more than those who are on programming, and it is clear that most of the programming went into tech art. It has the classic bishojo anime feel, while also having the dark fairy tale style as the rabbit hole goes deeper (I can only describe that as similar to how Majo is presented in Madoka - fairy tale, but with madness). It captures its sources of inspirations accurately and is executed with a stunning finesse.The writing is OK, but to be honest, as how the game presents its mechanisms, I was initially hoping for a much deeper rabbit hole. In the end it turned out to be... not that deep. I think it has just reached my "averagely deep" standard. Puzzles and minigames are sadly, a little mundane to my taste. It has that "let there be puzzle, and there's puzzle" feel, as the puzzle mechanisms are not exactly strongly tied to the story.  Anyway, enjoyable, fine yuri content, but don't expect it to be a deep rabbit hole game if you are familiar with rabbit hole games already.

_childDocuments_.review: The game runs well on Steam Deck!You don't need to know the plot of Pocket Mirror to play this one fyi. The games do link so you might want to know who the big bad of the prior game is, or that Elise Couple of tips and tricks in no order:- If you don't like eating noises or have misophonia, Elise makes a horrible crunch sound when she eats anything, which doesn't mute if you turn voice acting off. Turn off sfx to mute the sound or just lower the volume before eating or drinking if it bothers you.- If you want to cheat and give yourself lots of money to avoid the mini game grind:- If you struggle with button mashing  on Steam Deck.- The game doesn't really tell you this but you need to find Muffy to give her the food bribes. Elise will get a little bubble of her and her pink hair above Elise's head when Muffy is near. I usually find her hiding near a tree in the village centre.- Lebkuchen gives you bread in the evening which is nice, not sure if that's just because I'm dating her though.- Do all the story events you can on Wednesday and Thursday evening. Apparently missing them can cause you to not have access to certain areas later. I'd especially recommend on Thursday finding time to  I'm not sure if the game will let me go back and do this later on because My thoughts:It's a crime we can't date Welma the Innkeeper! But I'll settle for Lebkuchen :)I enjoyed this game about 70% of the way. It is beautiful and the devs have really nailed that 90s anime aesthetic. I loved the little dates with your waifus. The music is top notch. Resource management can get annoying but if you use my cheat above it's not an issue.It's all the sections with instant death and limited save points that annoyed me. The game gets especially tedious towards the end due to this. You'll have to replay sections because you didn't go exactly the right way or anticipate a block in your path at the right time.I didn't love Pocket Mirror but I really enjoyed this one. _childDocuments_.review: Very appealing art with phenomenal hand painted environments, leading-class soundtrack and high contrast between the fairy tale joyful day and grim, cruel and nightmarish nith makes all this game excceptionnal atmosphere. Truly, this is probably one of the most beautilful, if not THE most beautiful, 2D game I played. The oniric nightly settings feel like suspended in the time and at the same time calm and scary.All this art serves a very interesting and grim, yet sometimes cryptic (which goes well with the overall narrative) story. We see the slow and unavoidable stream of events triggered by Elise desire. From a gameplay standpoint, the alternation between "cozy" day where you recover from night (by earning money, dating, etc.) while avoiding being suspicious and investigating (optional quest) and the puzzle/action dangerious night is kinda addictive. However, the game can be unecessarily annoying at times with some "messy" gameplay (generally because of very crappy hitboxes) and long reloads to replay crappy parts. The game feels also a bit cryptic at the start and you might just fail/being locked because there is many things to do and all of them are very shortly explained. Plus some mechanics are less important that the game makes you think (suspicion for instance is not thretening), therefore there is a lot of cognitive load in this game (hunger, sanity, suspicion, health, relationship meter, money, do not miss some conversation with people you barely identify,...) but once you get a grasp of the gameplay balance, it becomes less a burden. This point can be really negative because I cannot imagine a world where I would retry the whole game if I failed to make many saves (one pice of advices : MAKE MULTIPLE SAVES) because the walking between screens is kinda slow and repetitive + the night aciton/puzzle are also interesting once but clunky as hell. This is truly a game of one playthrough unless you are a masochist... Therefore, even if the game has multiple endings, I will not replay it. That is why I followed some guides to do not miss anything (as well as the side quest leading to another ending). I watched some endings on YT too.To sum up : Little Goody Twi Shoes is a great experience with phenomenal art, grim story and a great contast between night and day which make it a great tale on its own. However, even if the gameplay ideas and the whole concept is appealing, the overall clunkiness (bad hitboxes, backtracking multiple times between screens, some slow and repetitive parts) make it a one-playthrough game. A really memorable experience...but once.

_childDocuments_.review: Gorgeous game. Unfortunately that's all it has going for it.For as much as it wants to boast that your choices matter, it loves nothing more than forcing you to make story-set choices as well as use up your precious time you might have wanted to spend to craft your own path healthily or manage your stats that the game itself burdens you with heavily. The game tries to combine difficult management with story telling rpg with path forging multiple-ending rpg with difficult horror puzzle rpg and it shows it is held together with spit and sticks. I cannot for the life of me understand the purpose of this game other than flavor, vibe, and sensory-pleasing design. When I work hard for money to buy my food I cannot enjoy the satisfaction of earning my stats before more of my resources, be them food, sanity, time, or health, are immediately cut down twice as much as I have earned. Being on only one food or one health or one sanity is horribly punishing as it ruins the entire gameplay experience, with constant unending filtering of your gameplay that ruins the one thing this game had going for it, and that is its visuals and sounds and music. The low resource filters should be warnings. They should not be on all the time, I cannot enjoy my time playing with constant whispering and wooshing and cackling in my ears, serving as further punishment for not being on top of your stats despite how difficult it is. The way to make money, the minigames, are also oddly unbalanced in how much they reward you for your effort each? I have no idea why that is a thing it would be so easy to just make them all give relatively similar monetary rewards for relatively similar difficult tasks regarding the effort put into succeeding in them.I cannot figure out the point of this game. Am I supposed to play it for the story? The gameplay? The visual design? They get in each other's way. I cannot enjoy the story or vibes due to the extremely merciless management gameplay, I cannot enjoy the hard management gameplay because the story locks me out of making choices with set events, I cannot enjoy the art because the game punishes for not being on top of the management by ruining the art....What am I doing here? I should just play something else that actually has a clear purpose and rewards me for playing or for succeeding.I wish I could recommend this game due to its flavor which I love. I'm a very nostalgic person so when I saw early internet horror rpg with old european folk vibes and old anime aesthetic I knew I had to buy and play it, but god was I disappointed. It breaks my heart that I cannot recommend it. :( This game let me down ngl. That's just how I experienced it anyway. I guess I'd recommend it for like, people with lots of patience and very little to do? But uh, in that case maybe you should pick up a more healthy and productive hobby instead.

_childDocuments_.review: Love the art design, the cutscenes and the minigames but unfortunately the general gameplay is so badly designed that I refunded the game.Here's a list of my gripes after 2h of playtime (contains minor spoilers I guess):- The very first riddle in the game is already borderline BS. You're in a huge room full of stuff (including several bookshelves) and find a note asking you "not to look for knowledge, but for a golden glow" (or something to that effect). Well, the solution is checking out the ONE bookshelf (out of many) that has a very faint (and hard to see) golden glow around it. I'm sorry but that's just dumb. So I'm not supposed to look for knowledge but the solution is checking out one specific bookshelf anyway? WHAT? That note could have been worded way better, like MAYBE pushing me towards checking out the bookshelves instead of making them seem unimportant??- I died after a lengthy cutscene because I forgot to eat before the time block and the game didn't give me an opportunity to do so (because it forced me into a cutscene right at the start of the time block and then forcefully advanced time). So I just starved to death right there in the town square, surrounded by people, with bread in my pockets. So I had to reload a save and that cost me about 15-20 minutes. Wow. I should also mention that a good chunk of that lenghty cutscene was unskippable. Wow x2.- The last straw was when I encountered a monster in a cave. The monster just one-shot me (even though my life bar was 4/5 filled) and I had to load my old save again. At that point I called it quits. The game is just too hostile for me (and not the fun and engaging kind of hostile like Don't Starve).I'll probably watch a playthrough on Youtube or something but I can't be bothered to suffer through the game myself. I get the impression that it wasn't tested enough because several flaws could and should have been ironed out (like being forced to starve to death after a forced cutscene).3/10 - Very disappointed

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to enjoy this game. It had the potential soundtrack, animation, storytelling, gameplay mechanics, and personality but there’s something’s that starts off small and become increasingly problematic later. Wilma names are spelled differently too whether she’s inside the store or outside the store. The game doesn’t explain if there’s two of her or if she has any family. Then the real issue arose for first combat; should warn players to save right before, the first time, to avoid restarting their game all because you died from one blow in the crossroad cave. The game isn’t helpful. If the player is going to go to the windmill, warn them for grape juice or sanity before entering. My issue is with the woods trials. I shouldn’t have to google in order to play this game. I don’t like to feel like I’m cheating but I also don’t need a game to hold my hand. Common sense would be to judge the player into thought by persuasion. Persuade me to walk closer and closer to the moths. Same with the crows. I had to google why I was getting pecked at, couldn’t make it through the woods because Elise would tell me to talk to the one crow and then the crow wouldn’t hint me anything! And for goodness sake! give us some aid! There is a major boss run and the crow’s lair had zero mushrooms nor bandages but plenty enemies than the last night. When you think you’ve found something they give you more flipping matches and grape juice that doesn’t help you escape the woods. What I have to look forward to right now is going back to a previous save, treading lightly to the end, and having Google on stand by for the remainder of this game. That’s my pov of the game.. pretty but not very fun. 3/5.

_childDocuments_.review: Art and music, gorgeous. Story and characters, predictable but compelling. Gameplay, awful. The time, food and sanity management system is tedious and just pull your attention away from the story and horror. The mini games are too simplistic to be enjoyable in the long run, and this especially bad since playing them is essentially unless you want to starve to death or go insane since you need to be making money at least twice a day if you want items to stave off falling into negative stats. Then there are the horror sequences, these involve dodging enemies whilst keeping your lantern constantly lit, because if you don't your sanity drops every second. Oh, your lantern also goes out everytime you're hit and enemies are heat seeking missiles and you have a limited amount of uses for your lantern. Any semblance of horror just turns into frustration when all you're doing is getting staggered and ripped apart. Frankly this game deserved a much better gameplay loop, because clearly a lot of passion was put into it, but the style just doesn't have the needed substance.

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful, well-realized game. It carries a similar spirit to the first game Pocket Mirror, but goes far beyond it in presentation. The aesthetics of the game are its strongest point, and makes a good case for minimalism not necessarily being the best route. Beyond that, it is also an enjoyable story in its own right. The game takes place in and around the village of Kieferberg, across the span of a week, with each day divided up into different time frames. Each day carries the story forward with new events in the village, while you also have to work for money in order to afford food and other items. The game has light survival mechanics, with multiple things like hunger or sanity to consider, but these are not too difficult to maintain. Every night, you travel into the dangerous woodland near the village. It's here the game is most similar to Pocket Mirror, with puzzles and supernatural events aplenty. You are tasked with acquiring a set of items before the end of the week, in order to make a wish to an entity residing in the woods. While doing this, you have to avoid suspicion from the villagers, and avoid being accused of witchcraft. An important part of the game is going on dates to build your relationship with a character of choice, and eventually fall in love with them. Getting your wish is dependent on bringing your love with you at the end of the week, so it is important to commit to this mechanic. Overall, I really enjoyed the game. It is an unusually beautiful game, with even the menus and UI being wonderful to look at. Recommended if you would like to try a game with roots in RPG Maker-type games, but which has grown into something much more.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good game, it's got awesome art and a pretty good storyline. I'm a sucker for witch stories, and found this one especially interesting. There were just enough people in the village that it felt alive, without feeling like there were too many characters to get to know. And I appreciated the whole suspicion mechanic and the entire game feeling like a witchhunt. I just have a few issues with the story and some minor nitpicks that made the game a lot more annoying for me.I only have a few problems. One, is that overall the endings were somewhat... empty. I got three so far, both with rozenmarine and failing to do the gifts in the right order (whoops). But except for while I believe is the Canon ending (ending 01), the other two felt very dissappointing. There was so much buildup and this whole journey, and then just an unsatisfyingly vague conclusion. I'll finish a few more endings as I also got the Freya romance during my route, although super sad I missed lebcukhen, I'll have to watch those endings online.I think my other problem with the story is how oblivious Elise is. I also had just a couple problems with the gameplay. Somethings things are supper well explained, like how Missy works (you have to find her at specifics times and can just not run into her if you rush to do something. I also didn't love how annoying effects were at low hunger/sanity. For the longest time I did not get the die from hunger or die from sanity achievements because I couldn't stand having a third if not more of my screen taken up. Also, I appreciate the voice lines, but sometimes they just happen way too much and get annoying to hear "Rosamarine!" for the 5th time in a conversation. Lastly, the most annoying thing I had is that every dating session has a choice and there is a right and wrong one, and if you get it wrong, you simply don't get a heart. I don't know how many I missed because I didn't realize this until I was looking at my locket lategame and noticed that it was rather empty. Like, if you spend the time, at least have some indicator or make it known that it's going to happen. I think I would've gotten Rozenmarine up to 7 hearts, but by the time I realize it I think I had just done too much content to go back.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: A genre-bending narrative adventure that will appeal to fans of creepy anime, visual novels, or anyone who appreciates exploring branching narratives.I wrapped up spooky season this year with this little title after watching a YouTube video about it, and it absolutely hit the spot. Although it was crafted by a Portuguese developer, it takes its visual and thematic cues from horror anime like Madoka Magica, going so far as to feature VHS-style visual aberrations and optional Japanese voiceover. It plays most similarly to a visual novel, but has 16-bit era exploration and mini games, and just a bit of dating simulator baked in.Presented in storybook motif, you'll follow the humdrum life of Elise, a poor peasant girl who lives alone and works as a day laborer in a small Alpine village. Found as an infant in the woods by her now-deceased grandmother, Elise longs for a life of ease & opulence. Things quickly escalate after she finds a mysterious witchy traveler in her house, and before long she's drawn into a supernatural struggle between forces beyond her reckoning.The story takes place over a week, with each day split into six discrete time periods during which you'll decide which work or relationships to pursue. When you take on a job, it's presented as one of four triptych-styled arcade machine minigames, and your performance dictates how much money you'll be awarded. The games are short, fun, and feature beautiful pixel art and chiptunes. You'll need to get good at these, as your budget will be strained to buy enough goods to keep your hunger, health, and sanity meters filled.You'll also have romantic options, though there are only three potential partners. Spending time with them will prevent you from earning income, but deepen your connection. Each girl has a distinct anime-trope personality, and it was rewarding to see them each open up over the course of the game. The romantic aspect is sweet, fairly chaste, and gives the story more emotional weight.The narrative here is largely on-rails, with only a few significant branches, but it's competently written if not ground-breaking. There are ten endings, and while it is  to achieve them all in a single playthrough, you’d need to follow a walkthrough and explicitly ruin the tale. I recommend following your romantic interests and exploring as you see fit, then playing through again if you want to see more. The game is less than ten hours long, and sports a fast-forward feature that makes repeat runs pretty speedy.Little Goody Two Shoes didn't blow me away, but it was a pretty enjoyable escapade with a mix of creepy and sweet vibes. Pick it up if you're looking for a bite-sized fantasy tale to give you mild scoops.

_childDocuments_.review: Somewhat mixed review, but you can trust me here.A. I'm pretty picky about what games I like.B. I've played every iteration of the story.WHAT YOU MIGHT LIKE:-Aesthetically, this is the most beautiful game I've ever played by a LONG-SHOT! It combines the look of early technicolor Disney animation (think Snow White), shoujo animation of the 90s, elements of medieval illuminated manuscript, paper-cut-out-style artwork, and traditional Austro-German craftsmanship.-A solid story with solid dialogue.-Fantastic atmosphere.-Fun mini-games.-Great themes that make you think. An interesting & fantastical take on the unwritten history of lesbianism, and the ways that a person reacts to marginalization; subtly written, too.-A good length!WHAT DOESN'T LAND:-For the first time, I wish a game was more repetitive. The tasks and mechanics and challenges that the game asks of the player don't have any continuity with each other from where I sit. The rules and goals of the game change too often.-The game also feels strangely a bit empty. So many beautiful places and things in the game are not to be used or explored-- a locked room in the house can never be opened, despite the locked door being one of the most traditional stores of intrigue in gaming as a whole. The protagonist refers to things she wants to accomplish-- she wants to grow crops in the backyard, or chop down a stump on the lawn-- which got me excited to do some farming or little tasks. (I know, there are too many farming sims... but it seemed fun this time, ok!?) Some parts of this game feel unfinished. So many Chekhov's guns that never go off. Two of four mini-games come back as boss battles; two never come up again.-The endings are mostly fine. Not disappointing. Just fine. No real twists.-Felt there wasn't much player agency. I wasn't bored-- you're not just watching the story take place-- but there isn't much space for creative decision-making.-Resource management is too easy, in my opinion.Overall, though, a memorable and great game!

_childDocuments_.review: How could one ever skip a game that takes much of its artistic inspiration from CLAMP's work from the 90s and 2000s? But even ignoring all that, there's a beautiful story full of mysteries to be unravaled here.The story follows the character of Elise, who, at first, may seem an arrogant, stubborn, snotty little brat, but after a few minutes of gameplay in her shoes (ha), you'll see she's every reason to be who she is. Luckily for her, she has three support pillars in Freya, Lebkuchen and Rozenmarine. Each one of them who can (and should!) be romanced. Each of the romantic scenes is a treat, even if brief, and the best part of each of the game days by far. While not spending time with your sweetheart, you'll pass the time doing Elise's job as maid-of-all-work: chopping wood, collecting apples and so on for her neighbors in order to acquire money which can be traded for items that can regenerate your health, and hunger and sanity meters. These are done in simple but charmful minigames that never felt old for me.At the dead of each night, Elise will explore dungeons full of puzzles and enemies to avoided, since Elise has no way to fight them. Some of these are not too problematic, others... well, they are my only caveat for this game. They are extremely frustrating putting it mildly, which may make some people think twice about replaying the game in order to go through the other romance routes or for completionism's sake.Still, not a purchase I regret in the slightest!

_childDocuments_.review: "Little Goody Two Shoes," is a captivating blend of horror, adventure, and life simulation. Set in the quaint village of Kieferberg, players step into the shoes of Elise, a young woman yearning for wealth and a life beyond her humble beginnings.Pros:- Stunning Visuals: The game boasts a '90s anime-inspired art style, with detailed pixel art and atmospheric lighting that bring the world to life. - Engaging Narrative: A rich storyline intertwines elements of horror and romance, keeping players invested in Elise's journey and the mysteries of Kieferberg. - Diverse Gameplay Mechanics: Seamlessly blends life simulation, puzzle-solving, and exploration, offering a varied and immersive experience. Cons:-  Inconsistent Day-Night Pacing: The day-night cycle can disrupt flow, sometimes making story events feel too rushed or prolonged.- Occasional Objective Confusion: Some interactions lack clarity, causing brief moments of confusion about objectives or motivations.- Restrictive Resource Management: The inventory system can feel limited, making it challenging to balance Elise’s tasks with free exploration.In conclusion, "Little Goody Two Shoes" delivers an exquisitely crafted experience that’s perfect for fans of dark fantasy and story-driven games, merging fairytale horror with a nostalgic, immersive world.Score: 10 out of 10 ruby slippers—perfectly fitted for a dreamer’s dark journey.

_childDocuments_.review: tldr; lgts is an outstanding title and is absolutely worth your time if you love rpg maker style horror games, lesbian romance, and 90s anime aesthetics.little goody two shoes takes concepts tried and refined over the years of rpg maker horror popularity and brings them to truly lovely heights here. in honor of its 1st anniversary, i'm finally taking the time to review it - this is one of those games i loved enough to purchase and play on multiple platforms, so needless to say it's become a favorite over the past year.it's been said so many times but it really cannot be understated how visually beautiful this game is - the sprites, backgrounds, and illustrations are all beautiful, and that's not even to mention the gorgeously animated scenes. the use of multiple art styles and mediums is not only visually pleasing but also serves to heighten the atmosphere the game attempts (and succeeds in my opinion) to create. also, the music is just absolutely stunning, and the vocal tracks are a real highlight.while the story and characters are not new territory, the way they're handled is caring and elegant. elise is one of the most interesting protagonists i've encountered in quite some time, and her explicit and exclusive attraction to women is both refreshing and important to me. she's deeply flawed in many ways, which only serves to make her more intriguing. her interactions and relationships with the three love interests are all lovely, and i think the writers struck a fantastic balance between romance, horror, and tragedy. not to mention the individual love interests themselves are all well-written and fascinating characters - you're bound to find at least one of the girls interesting enough to learn more.gameplay has never been and will never be the primary highlight of the genre, but it doesn't need to be. mind you the game still plays just fine, and fans of rpg maker horror games will understand the gameplay loop of the witching hour segments with ease. puzzles and chase sequences are par for the course but still interesting enough. the mini-games throughout the day aren't particularly challenging to do decently at, but may prove tough to get higher ranks if they aren't your speed. luckily, you don't need to do particularly well in order to make it through the game. the extra money provided by high ranks is really only necessary when pursuing certain endings. those not used to the style of gameplay may find some of these elements frustrating, but a little bit of patience will get you through.all in all, little goody two shoes is a well-told narrative wrapped in a beautifully-executed presentation. the game lives or dies by its story, characters, and aesthetics, and it puts every ounce of energy into delivering on all fronts. i truly hope to see more from astralshift building off of this format.

_childDocuments_.review: I usually don't write Steam reviews on account of being kind of shy about my feelings on games, but I didn't want to keep quiet on this one because it became a new favorite almost instantly for me. I did two playthroughs in one week, and I'm still intent on playing it a third time (partially for the achievement I'm missing, but also because it's a really fun, tense game).Everything about the game is beautiful: the shoujo-style sprites and CGs (I got so much nostalgia for the shoujo manga I read when I was younger), the UI, the pixel art, the locations (the Bedewed Forest of Berries stands out to me as the most gorgeous of all), so on, so forth. It's a visual marvel as well as an auditory one. I love the music to death and I'm guilty of looping Ruby Red Shoes and Ruby Slippers Mirage over and over again on my walks to class. It's such a pretty game in general and all of the artists involved did a wonderful job!As for the story, it hinges on a simple, traditional premise: a girl is offered the chance to have her wish granted, and she must go through a journey to see it through. It's obviously more convoluted than that, but that's what it is at its core; it reads a lot like a warped version of Wizard of Oz, where Dorothy wants to leave Kansas forever instead of return home, and Oz happens to be from the depths of hell. It does an excellent job of presenting a mangled fairy tale to you, and it hooked me almost immediately. I understand that some people may see it as having a slow start (considering the core of the story isn't immediately/quickly presented in favor of slower introductions to the characters and world), but I didn't personally have an issue with it. I love the macabre whimsy of it. Oh, and the cast of characters may not tick every box for some, but I genuinely love all three love interests- Freya very much is my favorite, though-, and I even grew pretty attached to some of the sprite-less side characters. If you're playing through, I genuinely recommend talking to every villager if you can! It makes the community feel more alive.The one major problem I have with the game is clarity; I get that the point of a puzzle is to puzzle you, but some of the sections are agitating to figure out. I spent a long time in the Bedewed Forest just trying to figure out the moon puzzle, and it's only on my second playthrough that I even managed to understand just what the solution was. Maybe it's a skill issue, but it stood out as genuinely frustrating both times. It's fun in theory, just a little agitating in execution; I think a clearer presentation of what to do would've made a huge difference. The puzzles in the Ceramic Grove of Wheat were a lot easier to work with.All in all, I have a deep love for this game and had a wonderful time playing it (and I'm going to have a great time playing it again), and I'm willing to recommend it to anyone who will listen. It's a beautiful marriage of my personal favorite elements of a game, and so while I know I have a bit of a bias, I still think it's worth picking up. It's been a hot minute since a game's gotten a genuine visceral reaction from me, so I haven't shut up about it since I picked it up.To sum it up: game good, art good, fun time, Freya best romance option. 9/10 cannot recommend enough

_childDocuments_.review: Little Goody Two Shoes is basically a simple indie game concept that succeeds in presentation aspects because it was likely flooded with money from publisher Square-Enix. It looks like a PS1 JRPG, but it's not an RPG. The original game this is based off of was made in RPG Maker, so there's a tendency to want to associate the term. It's more of a text-heavy narrative adventure with sim and horror aspects.The game starts off with a beautiful hand-drawn cutscene that hearkens back to the early days of CD Rom-based games. The story is pretty interesting, as it draws from classic tales like Cinderella and Wizard of Oz while also being its own unique thing, along with using traditional archetypes you see in traditional storytelling. The main character, Elisa, is unfortunately not really very well fleshed out. At the very least she has a spunky personality, but her motivations are not clear. Her desire to leave her life of servitude would make more sense if, I don't know, she was living a life of servitude. She does chores, but she gets paid for them, and nobody is forcing her to do them. It's like the Cinderella story was cut and paste in there without really considering how all the pieces fit together.There aren't a lot of maps, as you are mostly going into the woods and nearby town, but the game is broken up into several days that each have their own section. During each of these segments the characters and events are different, so each part of the game is like a different stage that is set for the player to explore. Between the minigames, discussion branches, secrets needed for endings and relationships there's enough variety to keep the player from getting bored. You also have to manage Elisa's different status bars, from her health to her tendency to go crazy and even more nebulous things like townspeople suspicions.I guess because Elisa is supposedly a witch the townspeople become suspicious of her so you have to choose the correct dialogue box to proceed. You also have to manage her hunger by eating food. The food bar is a bit extreme as if it goes empty she dies immediately. If she's hungry in the afternoon and she doesn't eat by dusk she's dead. It's a little extreme, especially since there's an option to use two bread to make a minigame easier. If you agree to do this you can win the minigame, but if your hunger bar is less than 80% full she will die immediately after. It's pretty terribly implemented but I guess they had to find a way to make the game hard.The "witching hour" sequences are the best part of the game. They're like mini dungeons with varied and clever puzzles. There's one where you have to figure out clues based on moon cycles and another one where you are controlling two characters at once while trying to avoid damage. If you are trying to 100% complete the game you will need to keep multiple save files because one mistake can mess up your run. The game gives a surplus of healing items if you look for them, but there are still tons of instadeaths. I kind of like that the game is hard and at times cryptic because it gives the player things to figure out.Aside from the character hunger bar being broken, the only other thing wrong with the game is the "relationships" aspect. Basically you build relationships with one of three characters to essentially set up the ending you are going to achieve. The only issue is that it's very shallow. Each interaction has you picking one of two options. It's not even clear what the correct option is so if you pick the wrong one you have to reload and select the other one. It would be better if these sequences were more tied to game play in terms of maybe a minigame, fetch quest or something of the sort. Instead you have to sit through banal dialogue of characters randomly falling in love for no apparent reason.The game has ten endings, but most of them are very short. There is one lengthy ending that gets repeated for all three characters, I would say it's the "bad" ending but it's also probably the canonically correct ending as it just makes the most sense based on the protagonist's decisions throughout the game. It's a must-play for fans of PS1-era Square games due to the graphics, sound design and music. This game made me super nostalgic. It's hard to believe it was made by a Portugese game company because it feels like an authentic JRPG. There's a lot of polish. There are just so many little details like unique crow animations the day after a crow level is completed, wind blowing leaves in the foreground, mixed media in the cutscenes (Live action pictures, anime drawings, cartoon drawings, etc.). It's really just phenomenally done and this is honestly one of the most beautiful looking games I've ever played. It is overall a great game and I am so happy that indie games with this level of detail are being selected and bankrolled by huge publishers like Square Enix.

_childDocuments_.review: where do i even begin???? this game is absolutely fantastic. it is an underrated gem in the rpgmaker horror world and its such a shame more people do not talk about this game!!the art is in multiple mediums, and great care was taken to the visual elements of this game. the graphics, pixel art, and sprites are absolutely stunning. there is great music as well! the characters are all so charming and cute. as far as gameplay goes, i will admit some puzzles were a bit convoluted. as long as you pay attention to the dialogue during puzzle segments, you should be fine. small details count! the game is very good at reminding you where to go if you ever get lost. i easily got the "true ending" on my first playthrough with no guides and without looking anything up.if you like sapphic witches, horror elements, and rich storytelling then this game is for you! i highly recommend this prequel game. and if you want more content in this world, i also recommend to check out the sequel partner game: pocket mirror!!

_childDocuments_.review: I first picked up this game on its release date last year since it looked right up my alley, as it has two of my favourite things: Yuri and Horror. I only ended up playing the game for a bit before getting absolutely overwhelmed with all the things I needed to keep track of, like making sure I had all the items for Muffy so she wouldn't raise my suspicion level, completing all the side quests to get free items, and making sure I did the jobs (some of the mini-games are an absolute pain) correctly to have enough money to buy bread and healing items (and some items for Muffy as well) for witching hour. On top of that, I had to take Rozenmarine with me to the jobs because if I left her alone for too long, she would start blabbing and raise my suspicion level.Having all that thrown at me at once really made me not want to play the game, so I ended up putting it on hold. Since it's spooky season again, I decided to pick the game back up, give it another chance, and play it no matter how overwhelming it got—and it worked. After playing for a while, I eventually got used to all the mechanics and finally experienced the great story, amazingly written characters, beautiful art style, and the soundtrack that truly blesses the ears, along with all the spooky horror elements I would have otherwise missed out on.As a huge Madoka Magica fan, seeing the game take inspiration from the show was a huge plus for me. Everything from the dungeon art style being similar to a witch's labyrinth, to the use of Germanic runes, to certain lore elements—like when Elise got the snake's curse being similar to the witch's kiss. This game would have been a solid 10/10 for me if it wasn't for the elephant in the room: some of the puzzles were badly designed.A couple of the puzzles were very poorly structured, leaving me confused much of the time. The game also isn’t great at giving hints about what you're supposed to do, which is a huge downside. In one puzzle (I'm looking at you, Moon Lagoon puzzle), I still don’t know exactly what I did to get past that part. I wandered around for a while, clicked a few things, and somehow managed to beat it. Instead of feeling excited about doing the puzzles (as I'm a huge puzzle game fan), I found myself absolutely dreading the witching hour because of those annoying, confusing, and not-very-fun challenges.In conclusion, I really did enjoy the game overall, despite one of its core mechanics not being very good. I’d say it’s definitely worth giving a proper try. You can absolutely see and feel the passion and love the team put into it. The dungeon design might be frustrating, but the characters, the Yuri romance, the art style, the soundtrack, and even the spooky atmosphere and elements all make up for it.

_childDocuments_.review: A compelling narrative, nuanced writing, and an amazing mixed-media art-style that includes 90's shoujo aesthetic resulted in this game being a surprise favorite of mine. The bright pastoral European setting balances out with the folk horror elements perfectly, and the soundtrack if full of banger after banger that heighten the atmosphere, whether it be cozy or creepy. I could listen to the Kieferburg night-time theme all day. This game is art for art's sake, and I recommend it to anyone who is looking for that type of unique gaming experience.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very beautiful and heartfelt tale, with quite the selection of memorable scenes. I loved the character interactions and sense of mystery, the music was fantastic, and the graphics were so polished and wonderful. For a horror game, it does what it means to very well, and I'm very happy I gave this game a try.I played this three times, in order to get full completion, and after the first run and a half, it did become a bit tedious for the lack of quality of life functions... My finger ached a bit from having to hit shift constantly throughout the game, but I suppose they were going for slow-burn authenticity with how the travel and skips were, keeping the emotional nature of the game, so I can let it slide.There were also a couple of buggy areas and some control functionality that caused some issues, but for an indie work like this, it's been wonderful and I'm happy for what it turned out to be, even if I'd prefer if there were fixes and some warning that there would be missable content the next go-around. (I found out the hard way that Rozenmarine had an invitation on Monday that you had to manually check for at the house... This cost me an entire extra playthrough despite me having all the rest of the checks needed to finish the achievements in full.)Very cute game, overall, and will be remembering this one for a while to come!

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game and I'm sure you will too if you are a fan of RPG maker horror games (I think this is a step up though, at least from the older/outdated ones).There are some puzzles that are a little obtuse but the positives definitely outweigh the negatives. Beautiful visuals and soundtrack and a fantastic story that ties in wonderfully with Pocket Mirror.Side note: This game is a prequel to Pocket Mirror (for the uninformed) and I definitely believe that, if you are intending to play that game too, that you should play it before Little Goody Two Shoes because an ending in this game has a MASSIVE spoiler for Pocket Mirror. (I also think that was how the games were intended to be played, after all Pocket Mirror did come out first.)I know Pocket Mirror's story is pretty confusing but LGTS isn't going to make it any clearer even though some people say it will (and besides, just because something comes first in a timeline doesn't mean you are meant to consume it first—that is the point of a prequel, I think.)Anyway, Little Goody Two Shoes and Pocket Mirror are great games but play PM first!

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the best looking 2D games I've ever played. It pretty much just straight up might be, because I can't think of anything better! The artwork is immaculate representation of 90s style updated in high resolution. Even if this style doesn't float your boat, the art direction all across the game is extremely strong. The character designs are on point, the background art captures the fairytale feeling, the scene CGs show how fragile yet lively the cast is. You can tell this game was made with so much love and care for the setting and the characters!The music is also phenomenal, solidifying every beautiful and emotional scene. Everything else was a cherry on top. Does the game have much gameplay? Eh, not really, but it doesn't need it, because the art and music carry everything. Its as interactive as it needs to be to be just immersive enough to enable the music and art pull you so much deeper.At its core this is a cinematic interactive novel from the perspective of Elise as she struggles to make ends meet, and then is given a carrot on a stick to perhaps finally attain her dreams. Most of this storytelling is done visually and musically, but the meat of it is in the character dialogue with the townsfolk as the events of the story unfold, where you can lose yourself for hours. There is also lesbian romance and witchcraft so that's awesome. My favorite romance was I don't quite remember how I stumbled upon this gem, but I'm very much looking forward to future games by  Astral Shift!

_childDocuments_.review: Little Goody Two Shoes is the second half of the Pocket Mirror experience for me, and having played the original and waited for so long to experience this, I can say every second of wait was worth it.Every frame of this game is legitimately beautiful, and I would print all of them on my wall if I had the chance.The story is captivating, well constructed and... disturbing. It's even more disturbing if you played Pocket Mirror, considering the payoff of understanding PM well, is knowing exactly what's going to happen here. And the payoff is one of the most incredible scenes in a game, in my opinion.The characters are awesome! Rozen was the one I knew from the beginning, so I hold a special spot for her. She's really really interesting to read further! Leb is pretty, she's fun and overall super caring, and Freya... Freya has my favorite scene in the game... let's leave it at that!10/10!

_childDocuments_.review: I'm gonna be real, this game does not have the greatest replay value, besides the new cg's when you date a new love interest most of the game stays the same so I'd play it once and then watch a YouTube video on the rest. The gameplay is alright, it's not bad but it's nothing incredibly memorable. Though a complaint that I will make that I wish they'd consider is trying to eliminate the need to re-watch cutscenes over and over depending on where you die for certain parts, it wasn't as much of an issue as it was in Pocket Mirror for me but it was still noticeable. The ending is a tad predictable and they don't do much with it to surprise you to keep you engaged for the end. That said I still like the ending for what it is. overall the game is solid and I give it a... 6/10. Now that my complaints are out of the way, I'll move on to what I like.now personally if you are a huge fan of art and atmosphere, what I've always loved about Astral Shift is that this is where they shine, the worlds they create are absolutely full of whimsy and overall I do not find a lot of games with this type of feel so I love it SO MUCH. As someone who grew up with Pocket Mirror it was fascinating to see how they executed the prequel. The characters themselves are really well made and are fun to watch when it comes to their interactions as well. At least on the first playthrough I definitely think the experience is worth it. The voice acting is phenomenal as usual. There is also a good chunk of BEAUTIFULLY made animations and songs within this game that I will watch on repeat. _childDocuments_.review: I love me some lesbians!Aside from that, this game honestly has a lot of care put into the design and art of the game. Everything is well crafted and you can really feel the love for this game. There are fun & short animated cut scenes that happen through out the game. A big one being the opening to the game. I genuinely love the style of the game and the designs of the interfaces. Lots of work and care went into those and it shows! I like the fact that even though I don't know the main cast very well, I feel like I do. When you talk to one of the love interests, you can see how much they care for Elise. It makes me compelled to date them. It feels a lot better than farming sim interactions I get. I really like the task list they give me. As some one who struggles with free roaming games, it helps out a ton. It shows you exactly what you can do in each time block of the game and what to look forward to in case you forget. For example, in the morning someone will set up a date for the evening. It will show up on my task list labeled for later today and when it is evening, it gives me a little notification. It helps a lot!If you enjoy yuri, some rpg horror, mystery, and the art & design of the game, I highly recommend picking it up! If you're really scared to, try the demo or watching someones first play through to look into the game. I love the art and charm, so that keeps me hooked! Plus right now I am in love with Lebkuchen ^_^ I get excited to see her everyday!!

_childDocuments_.review: I came into this game with out much context or knowledge. It's one of most creative and artistically fulfilling games I've ever played. Of course, the art may not be for everyone, so take my praise with a grain of salt since art is subjective, blah blah.The game itself is very fun too, with a lot of interesting puzzles, intriguing story, amazing soundtrack. I'm someone who is very easily frustrated with games because I'm very stupid and have to look stuff up. This game does a good job of balancing the gameplay and the lore so that you don't get a one-to-one to do list, but you're given enough hints that you can probably figure it out in a decent amount of time.My only grips with the game is that it has a few bugs(?) and have hitboxes that can be fairly unclear. Kiss the Rat is the biggest example of this where it's difficult to time as you don't get a clear hitbox for Elise's range.This game is a 9/10. I will be grinding the endings with my buddy who I've gifted the game after my third day of playing. Thank you yuri horror jesus.
