_childDocuments_.review: I had a lot of fun playing this, the art direction is impeccable and the sheer immersion in the world you get from something so simple as a menu, or a loading screen is ridiculously good. The vision is clear, and I absoloutley loved the visuals, music and themes of the game. However. Around the Friday mark there's a rather harsh, untelegraphed difficulty spike. The puzzles, are thankfully rather intuitive however I think there are some tricky ones that could've used a little more subtle hints- there are some elements I really couldn't figure out without a guide (and i'm a puzzle games girlie at heart) so that part was frustrating. The writing and characterisation has it's moments, but the ending of the story seems to leaves more questions than answers- the 'canon' love interest of the three available in particular suffers from being overdone in her characterisation, to the point of annoyance, making it hard to gravitate towards her. The suspicion meter is played up to be important, but seems to hold little bearing. Everything about Muffy is frustrating.Overall this is a beautifully accessible and lovingly made game, but it's got it's quirks. The scares were good, the nightmare levels nailed the feeling they were going for. But come in with a guide, and be patient.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is extremely good in lots of aspects: the graphics are gorgeous, the story is really interesting and the artstyle makes it even better by giving horrific and gory vibes! It truly nails that sort of eerie atmosphere, especially with all the various dialogues and NPCs interactions you can trigger. There are also enough saves that you won't lose much even if you get a 'game over' and have to start over, which is a huge plus for me.HOWEVER, by the gods, the game has a huge issue with movement and hitbox, especially during night times. The graphics, as I said are beautifully drawn and I really am impressed by the amount of details added, but it also makes the environment heavy, messy and difficult to navigate at times. For example; you'll have spikes that hurt you if you ever BRUSH them. It's not even 'fully touch them and you get hit' type of hitbox; it's a 'if the tip of you dress ever brushes on ONE pixel of a spike' type of hitbox. Also sometimes, the screen will violently shake because something is falling on the ground, which makes it even harder to see what's going on as you're getting chased by a monster that can oneshot you. Some of the puzzles are also... not great. And you can easily miss some if you're not careful enough. At least, you should have enough items to keep a good health bar but still very annoying if you end up getting hit multiple times in a row.I won't say that it was so bad that I gave up playing, but it did make me so frustrated I had to close the game and come back another day as I had to redo the same phase over 15 times before succeeding (I only managed to get it right because I ended up having the whole sequence memorized by heart). It does show that the game truly has potential: I wanted to know what was going to happen next, the characters are lovable and the story IS really good, which is why I kept on trying. But it is good to know that unless you have a very keen eye, you'll probably die a few times on several occasions to stupid things. I also do not recommend playing with a controller; the game was clearly conceived for keyboard and is better played with one unless you have really good minute movement reflexes. (Also if you're a fellow AZERTY keyboard player: be sure to switch to QWERTY beforehand by changing the keyboard language to ENG because you won't be able to change the controls in the game.)

_childDocuments_.review: If you want this game for the visuals, you will not be disappointed. Each date with your romantic interest has one, sometimes even two, detailed art pieces. Even a couple optional conversations in the game have an art piece, which blew my mind. The backgrounds themselves are handcrafted. Each art style, from the mini-games to the stop-motion in the songs, shows how much love was put into this game. It is a visual treat that never stops giving. That reason alone is enough to get the game, in my opinion. My only major critique in the art aspect is the absence of a gallery of all the art, the songs, or even of the endings. The fact I point this out is less of a negative but more of a testament to how beautiful the art is. PLEASE add a gallery.As for gameplay, it is pretty straightforward. The systems are simple and work together well. The game design is crafted to keep you from getting frustrated but gives you the room to figure things out on your own. On my first playthrough, I only had to consult the internet once, but even then I could've figured out where to go if I gave it a couple more minutes. Save points are plentiful and there is a lot of telegraphing in dialogue and visual cues that tell you what you need to do and where to go next. If you explore even a little, you are rewarded with matches and health items. Most of your deaths will be due to not understanding mechanics or not paying attention.My only gripe with the gameplay is that the camera in the Bedewed Forest of Berries sometimes allowed enemies to get cheap hits (since the camera would focus on a point of interest and hide the enemies nearby, even when I moved away from the point of interest). I thought it was worth noting since I don't imagine this choice was made intentionally to raise difficulty. Still, the plentiful health items offset this frustration for me. Generally, I think this game is beginner-friendly to those who simply want to experience the story, as long as you pay attention to the dialogue.As for the writing, I really liked it. On my first playthrough, I got the bad ending with Freya in full (not the ones related to missing key items) and that's still honestly my favorite one, even though the good endings are also nice. The character-writing is the best part. I love the dates with Freya, Lebkuchen and Rozenmarine, and the conversations around town help bring substance to various characters. The writing made me feel genuinely bad for getting the bad endings. I have Dim Delusion on my Spotify playlist now.All in all, one of my favorite games I played this year. Highly recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: If you were a queer person who spent their time online obsessed with RPG Horror Maker Games, Shoujo Manga and anime of the 70s and 90s, and the yuri and feminine themes of all of those pieces of media, then Boy Howdy do I have the game for you!!I have historically been very bad with horror, but this game had so many things up my specific niches, I was determined to push past said fear. I've been pleasantly surprised at how kind the game is in it's horror segments! Even the more frustrating parts will have a save point directly beforehand to help ease the frustration of that moment. I do highly recommend making use of different save slots though; this is a game where it's biggest challenge can come from it's resource and time management, especially if your'e itching to get as many achievements/endings in one run as possible.Sometimes the plot could lose me at points; not helped when I was trying to juggle so many events, overcome my anxiety at the horror segments, and figure out if I was getting all the right things for the ''''true'''' ending (spoilers: there is no singular True Ending). The characters are endearing, and even now I couldn't tell you who my favorite girl to pursue was: I love them all and I want happiness for them! I do appreciate the themes of female ambition, and how that ties into each of the girls, including Elise.The game is gorgeous, though on occasion it can be so focused on it's aesthetics that it's hard to tell what you as a player can have a hard time telling what directions you can go in and what counts as an entrance/exit. Sometimes the visuals seem to clash with the story (it's strange to hear Elise's cynicism about such an idyllic town, and That Sure Is a Girly Dress for someone who has been working and barely scraping by for 8 years Elise), but if you keep in mind it's meant to be treated more as a fairy tale, I think that dissonance is easy enough to get used to. It feels like the team really went all out in including a variety of aesthetics they liked into one pot, and it's such a delight.

_childDocuments_.review: I came into this from having played Pocket Mirror Goldenertraum first (and seeing absolutely everything the game had to offer), so that's an influence here to note. Also, I highly highly hiiiiiighly recommend playing Pocket Mirror before this if you intend to play both.It's hard for me to say "recommend" but I don't really want to say "don't recommend". This game was a disappointment in many ways. I'll start with the "negatives":I get why the intended ending is what it is, but it did not make it any less desirable. And the alter ending, while more desirable, just felt like a real tonal shift and lacked the proper sort of transition into it. And Elise is no ????. Elise is not really the most enjoyable of protagonists. I know this is by design, but I don't really get endeared to someone like her. The witching Hours(aka the puzzles) are like 50% good, 50% not good. I really enjoyed the water one, the final one was hardly a "puzzle" and was like the first one, which was basically just "don't die". This is disappointing coming from Pocket Mirror and all the really fun and interesting puzzles/chase sequences. The sim life stuff normally should feel like a nice break from the nightmare, but it actually ends up feeling like too much. There really needed to be more nightmare integration into things. But the minigames were nice, even Kiss the Rat, no matter how terrible I was at it XD Onto the postives, on that note!:The music is really fantastic, much like Pocket Mirror. Though I felt the sim life music was not as easy to continually listen to in ambience as the tracks on Pocket Mirror. Still, many wonderful tracks. The sound direction is also great, just like Pocket Mirror. I don't know if this is something they did better with an update, of which there were apparently many, but the water witching hour you could hear the enemies quite well and which direction they were coming from. Doesn't mean I died any less to them x_x Headphones make all the difference, just like they did in Pocket mIrror.The visuals are amazing, and bleed into so much, especially the minigames. Though the retro look may be a turn off for some, it replicates that era quite well! it really is a visual masterpiece! So much style in everything, from the character designs, to the backgrounds, and even the UI! Truly well implemented!Onto the not as good, but not as bad either:The dates are nice enough, and I felt myself regretting some that I didn't pursue the other girls much. Maybe some day I'll work up the endurance to do another playthrough to see their full stories. Though, the girl I went with, it felt lacking with how things ended. it was a nice enough ending, but felt like they weren't addressing the real issues. The bad endings felt more in character. I'm really not sure how to feel about this game, outside I enjoyed Pocket Mirror Goldenertraum better. I really really recommend that game! But it's not like I don't recommend this game. It's great how a yuri dating sim can be a thing (but I'm really not a fan of routes design...) and to be combined with horror is also fantastic! But there are things holding it back. I'm looking forward to whatever Astral Shift does next, but I'm more cautious about things than I was after I finished Pocket Mirror Goldenertraum. Still, I think these devs have a lot of promise. I just hope next time they don't dilude the horror aspect too much with life sim things

_childDocuments_.review: I simply can't recommend Little Goody Two Shoes enough.I loved the story, design, and game play enough to replay this , putting in a whopping 50 hours to get all 10 endings and all 40 achievements. (Typically, you can play once to get almost all of the achievements except for one of them, so only two play-throughs are required - but I wanted my first play-through to be blind and thus I missed a few things.) The art is so cute, the characters' personalities varied and realistic, and there's a dark psychological/literal undertone to the story that is rewarding to follow. The puzzles and mini-games can be frustrating, but are almost always fun, and never too hard as to gate-keep less skilled/puzzle-oriented players. I spent the majority of my first play-through exploring EVERYTHING. The town & woods are gorgeously designed, with interesting perspectives and beautiful art -- complete with hidden items and secrets scattered about. There's also so much optional extra dialogue you can read to gather more insight into the story, the town, and the people within Little Goody Two Shoes. Literally every time cycle gives you more dialogue to explore (by time cycle, I mean dawn, morning, noon, dusk, evening of EACH and EVERY day!) - and even though the game is technically only a game week long, this week is so story rich that you feel like you've been living in the town of Kieferberg for years.If you like , with several (10) endings dependent upon your chosen path, please check this game out. I'm looking forward to playing the sequel, Pocket Mirror, next. ❤️

_childDocuments_.review: This game has really great visuals and a lot of variety on the soundtrack.  The writing is decent as well, and if you are a yuri fan, that's a pretty strong draw as well; you're in control if it ends badly, so if you like a bit of tragedy you can sample that flavor alongside the happy endings.The life simulation aspects are pretty underbaked/simple to deal with, especially if you play it the intended way and prioritize having romantic encounters with only one of the girls. You can completely ignore the sanity mechanic if you simply do not pick up the collectibles that drain it, and stay out of the optional areas that make it act as a timer.  The hunger mechanic is easily beaten as well, especially if you have a good reaction time and can get the max money out of the job minigames every time.  And it when it comes to your health, I would say the game is quite generous in giving you healing items for free as well.  All that said, I would rather these aspects be too easy than too hard, so it's a decent attempt at a first foray into these mechanics.The puzzles are not particularly difficult, apparently they had updated the game at some point with additional hints Elise can give the player as well, so as long as your at least decent at figuring out what a game wants you to do, you shouldn't have any issues progressing through the game.  Nothing is particularly ambiguous and I very rarely got stuck, and when I did it was simply because visibility was poor and I walked past something important.  Though inevitably due to its RPGMaker roots, occasionally you'll have to die here or there to figure out how something works.This game can slingshot between teeth rottingly sweet and "make your heart sink" dread, and I enjoyed both sides of it.  It is possible to get every ending in a single playthrough, but I think it's an easier time and a better experience to just focus on one girl at first.  It isn't a large amount of content, but if you have a favorite, you'll miss scenes involving that girl if you don't focus only on them.  After the initial playthrough, then go through it trying to get as many as possible if you're a completionist.  I do wish there was a full-on "skip to next decision" button, instead of the speed up text one that this game has.  It also only works on certain scenes (not including some of the longer end-game scenes, so it was a bit annoying when I was hunting all the endings).  I used an autoclicker to advance the text as quickly as possible.  Another little complaint I have is that the menus sometimes have strange delays, but I chock this up to Unity as a few unity games I've played have had this problem.Overall, I enjoyed my time with Little Goody Two Shoes, even the angsty bad endings added to the characters for me, and as I was playing I couldn't wait to see what was coming up next, cause I knew it was going to be a visual/auditory treat (even if the inevitability of what comes next causes me dread).

I sometimes was so annoyed I had to take a break and just get away from the game for a while before I could attempt another chase sequence or puzzle.Also annoying is a certain bug which happens on the last day, which makes it impossible to buy items even though you'd have enough money to do so. Hopefully the developers are going to fix this shop bug, as it keeps me from actually finishing the game.If the bug gets fixed and I'll finish this game properly I'll update this review.

_childDocuments_.review: Little goody two shoes had quickly risen to being one of my favorite RPGs. Taking the same style and story that a classic jrpg game usually has and giving it a whole new format. The game is one of if not the prettiest inde games I’ve ever played and just feels so fresh. The ‘retro’ sprites with the hand drawn backgrounds, dynamic lighting, and 80s anime esc character portraits gives it a truly unique style. Like if the Brothers Grimm met Sailor Moon. Without getting into spoilers, the story is very interesting, and had me truly invested in some of the characters and the mystery which surrounds Kieferberg. I think the game is worth playing just for the visuals and music alone, but the story makes it all the more worth it. Specifically Golden Phantasmagoria, such a unique and beautiful track.The only issues I had with the game were some puzzles I thought were a bit annoying, those being the mirrored movement and moon puzzles, you’ll know if you’ve played the game. Those felt a bit unfair and frustrating.Still, I’m so glad I played this game, it was so good I bought the connected game (Pocket Mirror,) and proceeded to beat it the next game. Please, if you’re a fan of good stories, mystery, horror, RPGs, adventure, life sims, I think most people can find something to love about this game, and I’m ecstatic to see what AstralShift comes out with next!

_childDocuments_.review: I aldready played and enjoyed Poket Mirror so I was well aware of AstralShift's ability to craft frightening yet beautiful worlds but Little Goody Two Shoes exceeded my expectation, you can see it from the trailer: this game is gorgeous. This game nails the fairy tale vibe, it has great pixelart, painterly landscapes, vintage anime styled characters, great animations, great soundtrack, all sorts of cool additions like songs or old anime like interludes, it's just very high quality and well put together overall.As for gameplay, it reinvents the rpg maker formula, adding some cool minigames and a bit of resource management like hunger or sanity, which I found balanced and never frustrating. The rpg maker formula carries some problems though, while the game brings some new quality of life changes, it still has the flaw of having to be played more times to get all the endings, which of course can get a little tiring. That being said the game is getting patches and the devs are listening to user feedback so it wouldn't surprise me if they fixed this or other small issues.Overall I enjoyed Little Goody Two Shoes quite a lot, I was completely engrossed in the story, the setting and the characters, I'd say this game definitely isn't getting the attention it deserves and the same goes for AstralShift, I wish them the best of luck and I'm already looking forward to their next project!

_childDocuments_.review: This game has gorgeous hand-drawn German-fairy-tale-inspired art with character design inspired by '90s/'00s anime (e.g., Rozen Maiden), yuri (!!!), amazing music and a spooky vibe. _childDocuments_.review: Little Goody Two Shoes: A Fearful Dance with DiversityRating: ★★★★☆Little Goody Two Shoes emerges as a groundbreaking horror game that fearlessly delves into the unexplored realm of queer representation, making strides in the gaming industry's ongoing pursuit of diversity and inclusion. Developed by a visionary team, this game weaves a chilling narrative around a cast of queer characters, challenging traditional norms while delivering a compelling and immersive horror experience.The game's central strength lies in its commitment to portraying queer characters authentically. Little Goody Two Shoes doesn't merely tokenize these characters but seamlessly integrates them into the narrative, allowing players to connect with their struggles, aspirations, and fears. In an industry that has historically struggled with diversity, the game serves as a beacon of progress, highlighting the importance of reflecting the rich tapestry of human experiences.The narrative unfolds in a haunted Victorian mansion, where players take on the role of a protagonist who must confront not only the supernatural but also their own insecurities and prejudices. The horror elements are heightened by the atmospheric storytelling, with the mansion's creaking floorboards and flickering lights adding layers of suspense. Little Goody Two Shoes masterfully utilizes its horror backdrop to explore the characters' inner demons, offering a unique blend of psychological horror and queer storytelling.The immersive gameplay further contributes to the game's success. From the eerie sound design to the meticulously crafted environments, every element is designed to pull players into the unsettling world of Little Goody Two Shoes. The tension builds steadily, keeping players on the edge of their seats as they navigate the haunted mansion and uncover the secrets within.What sets Little Goody Two Shoes apart is its ability to create an emotional connection between players and the characters. Through diary entries, audio logs, and haunting visuals, the game invites players to empathize with the diverse cast, fostering a sense of understanding and acceptance. The decision to explore queer narratives within the horror genre not only breaks new ground but also challenges players to confront their own fears and biases.While the game excels in its storytelling and representation, it does face some challenges in pacing, occasionally sacrificing the horror elements for character development. However, these moments of respite allow for a deeper engagement with the narrative, ultimately enhancing the overall experience.In conclusion, Little Goody Two Shoes stands as a testament to the evolving landscape of gaming, where diversity and inclusion are not only acknowledged but celebrated. Its seamless integration of queer characters into a horror narrative is a bold step forward for the industry, demonstrating that games can be both socially progressive and spine-chillingly entertaining. As the gaming community continues to demand more diverse stories, Little Goody Two Shoes leads the way, offering an immersive and thought-provoking experience that lingers long after the final scare.

_childDocuments_.review: The visual style is just great. I get serious good vibes playing this one. Graphics fit the whole way from start to finish and are pleasing to watch. Lots of good, fun details across the board here.Also thank you to the devs for giving most of the characters more than one pose for the talking parts.Just the right amount of spooks and weirdness with just the right amount of character development.The story is not as brutal as Pocket Mirror, but it has some heavy tie-ins to it.What will you expect with this game?1. Heavy on story.2. No combat, just dodging things.3. Four Minigames4. Lots of exploring and a few puzzles5. JRPG style movement6. Lots of good composed characters7. Ten Endings and a bunch of different game overs.Seriously, if I were to make a game with a main character with a flaw, this one is just great. Elise is a "maid of work" who has been doing odd jobs almost every day and she WANTS to be rich and greedy and such. This is a great way to work a character flaw in.The animation is beautiful. It reminds me heavily of a good 90s style. It's hard to explain but it's really really good. It's just charming to watch. There are full motion videos too.Soundtracks I almost never mention about in reviews, but this one is just so delightful to listen to. It reminds me of that one NIS game called Rhapsody. Music fits with the scenarios going on just great.Also note to devs: I enjoyed the uniqueness and the details of the moon puzzles :DI have a couple of trivial downsides I want to mention. None of these are major1. Fast forwarding dialogue OR skipping doesn't work in some parts. The end sequence is unskippable but the secondary credits are, for instance.2. A fast travel would be nice in some minor cases while searching. It's not required but it would be a nice QOL for a few specific things. It's not too tiring though to travel so it's no big deal.3. I would like to lower the audio on the near insanity effect. When you get low on sanity it just annoys the hell out of you. Sort of like Legend of Zelda while at low hearts. This can be alleviated by always making sure to have sanity restore items. :D4. Some of the dialogue choices feel a little vague to what happens. On my playthrough I had a 50% chance to get the response I was looking to say. But even the ones that I was unsure of that had a good event went in an odd direction O_O;; This might just be the method of storytelling. Either way it was not grammar errors. Luckily, save points are plentiful.5. When you have a "Friend" help you with work, it costs 2 stamina (bread) icons. And then when the time changes you lose a third. So if you only have 3 you automatically get a game over :D I would have said to pay your "Friend" with bread or not allow you to choose her unless you had 4 or 5 stamina.

_childDocuments_.review: I honestly have no idea how this game flew under my radar. The game is truly amazing, both in its obviously fantastic visuals and its game play. I went in kind of expecting yuri bait at the endings but you do get closure at the end of  all of Elise's tale's. I felt the only one that wasn't quite as satisfying was Rozenmarine's, but I feel she served a different purpose in the game than a romance candidate anyways so personally I didn't have an issue with it. Leb good ending is my favorite, she is best girl.The mini games were very fun. They looked easy at first but their difficulty is deceiving. I struggled the first few times on all of them except the apple collecting one, which is by far the easiest of the bunch. The fact that they weren't just filler content or useless sidepieces in the game was a plus as well, as you have to do them to earn money so you do not starve or die from sanity loss.The dungeon puzzles themselves were fine. The only ones I thought weren't that good was Thursday and Friday night's puzzles. They were a little frustrating, not because of difficulty but because (and you might be able to relate to this feeling if youve already played it) the directions were not very clear. I dont know if this game was translated from another language or not but sometimes the dialogue felt that way. And in a game where you are supposed to figure a lot of things out by yourself, it can sometimes lend the only directions you are given to be even less helpful. This game can be very unforgiving too, I died to random stuff many times that i just didnt expect you to be able to die from, or just because I thought it would be more forgiving with its hitboxes,timing, etc. It is definitely a trial and error type deal, and thats fine. It was a lot of fun learning the puzzles and figuring things out myself, but Thursday, and Friday especially, were definitely more frustrating than anything and it felt as if they dragged on too long.Overall I think the game is amazing. It really exceeded my expectations in every way. Its so easy for smaller story given games like this to be trash since so many of them just get pumped out like they are being made in a factory or smthn but this really is a diamond in the rough and I hope that Pocket Mirror is just as good since ill be playing that one next. I got this game on sale so if you are even a little interested I say go for it, especially if you like yuri. It will not disappoint.

_childDocuments_.review: bursting with incredible charm down to the gorgeous 90's shoujo aesthetic art direction and animation, cute and colorful characters and designs and super intriguing storytelling and well-done horror, the worst of the horror being not witches or the creepy death-filled forest but the fear of the seemingly friendly villagers you grew up with willing to turn on you in a second if you're not careful. also! girls loving girls the only reason i can't give this a full 5 stars is just because of how cumbersome the gameplay can get at times. with no fast travel and the running animation barely being any faster than walking combined with how many times you have to go to the exact same places all over the village multiple times a day it gets tiring fast, both mentally and physically with holding down the trigger button to run for actual hours. this could be fixed with just being a toggle instead. you can also VERY easily lock yourself out of completing the game in multiple ways. i don't mean just the food and time-passing system which is totally manageable if you're paying attention, but also being able to easily skip over obtaining key items to complete the actual story if you don't follow exactly what to do in the exact order. if you don't happen to have a save file for before you're supposed to obtain it, you're screwed and need to start the entire game over. you shouldn't be allowed to go to the next day without it.in the later witching hour segments, hints on what to do to proceed and how to survive can get incredibly vague and near directionless, which can be irritating at best to downright infuriating at worst. in the wednesday witching hour, you are told to run through the various mazes to get to someone as fast as possible, what they do NOT tell you is to stop at a couple of floor panels on the right at the end of each maze to stop said someone from falling to their death and killing you instantly too. in the thursday witching hour you are told that monsters will instantly kill you if you have your light on, thus you think you're forced to stumble around in the dark trying to find the exit while being stabbed repeatedly by things you can't see. what they DON'T tell you is that the monsters will kill you if you have your lights on ONLY IF YOU'RE MOVING. something this simple could have saved people hours of headaches. all that aside, i adored this game and i am looking forward to more games by this developer in the future! absolutely playing pocket watch next

_childDocuments_.review: Hmm... let's jump right into it:  this game has fantastic art.  Absolutely stellar!  The music too, is golden.  Super charming.  Wonderful!  Every day of the week brings the same world alive in new ways...  In these categories it's perfect...Now onto the characters and the story...  Pretty intriguing.  I had an enjoyable time getting to know the colorful and fearful townsfolk of Kieferberg, and after the previous game, Pocket Mirror, I wanted to learn more of the backstory of that universe.  However... the amount of time getting to know the romance interests of the game were somewhat limited after the unforgettable strange events in Pocket Mirror.  This wasn't the bare minimum, but don't expect anything too deep.  I did enjoy the interactions, but perhaps due to the gameplay mechanics, it was mostly a matter of attending occasional events and guessing a vague choice; rather than something unfolding more naturally over a longer period of time or unexpectedly with Elise.  (Do note I've only pursued one character at this point.  I would like to see the rest, but without some kind of gimmick like a New Game+ with extra content, I find it hard to justify repeating everything once more unless a lot changes... And doubt it will, except at some key points.)As for the day gameplay mechanics... It's probably the biggest weakpoint for me.  While there's nothing that wrong with it... after a couple days of gameplay you'll know what to expect at its core.  There will be much running around town, a few of the same minigames, talking to everyone if you so choose; and if you're like me and really want to exhaust all that can be done, you'll spend each day running *everywhere you can go in the world,* each time period,  of each day, to see if there are any changes in each... gorgeous area...  It doesn't take that long, but the time adds up running in circles...The game even features a perfectly executed fast forward feature for most conversations... If only that feature would just work while running around the world too... you'd save so much time on replay!  (There is no fast travel...)  But I should mention if you just want to pursue the main objective, there isn't much of an issue, as the map lists objectives and you generally know where to go.As for the night mechanics... I have no issues with that!  No spoiler!Finally without getting into the endings, I just wish there was a little bit more as everything reached conclusion fairly quickly at the end...  It was great, but now it's over!Would I recommend it?  Yes!  It's a pretty safe bet if you like what you see on the store page.  You're in for a strange tale full of troubling mystery and chores xD  Did I mention the art and music??? Magnificent!
_childDocuments_.name: Little Goody Two Shoes

_childDocuments_.review: - The visuals. The art style goes from pixels to shoujo anime to cutesy child-like drawings, and it's all great to look at.- The OST. Lots of catchy, good sounding pieces, especially the vocal songs.- The gameplay. Minigames are simple and fun, romantic dates give you insight to Elise and her love interests, and witching hour segments provide variety to the game in enemy encounters, puzzles, and atmosphere.- The setting. Kieferberg is an interesting locale, and the townsfolk provide depth to the town and the story as it unfolds. Speaking of which...- Your romantic interests. All three girls have a different feel to their personalities. There are some similarities when it comes to their conflicts and motivations, but they deliver both in their own ways that makes you connect with and like them.- The endings. The endings feel "complete" and give closure to the story. But - The tone of the endings.  But that's not a knock on the game. Bad endings can be good if they execute storytelling well, and this game does that. The good endings provide closure as well, which were developed through your romantic dates. But if you don't like bad endings, regardless of whether they're well-written or not, you may not like this game.Personally I liked the most of the endings, some won't due to the points above.- The suspicion mechanic. Don't know how to feel about this one. It does feel easy to make it a non-factor by bribing Muffers and choosing the obvious dialogue option when talking to townsfolk. But it makes sense to have it in the game due to the story. Maybe there could have been more penalties and challenges for having a low suspicion rating? - The UI feels unresponsive at times. You'll select an item you want to use, press the confirm button to give you the option to eat, place, etc., and it takes at least half a second to actually display the item's options. Also, there's a second of delay when you start a conversation with NPCs and when you go through the minigames' start menu and controls display.- The morning, afternoon, and dusk cycles throughout the days can feel a bit repetitive. You go through each one by playing 2 available minigames out of 4, or by going on a date with a love interest if available. There could have been a few more different minigames to reduce the repetitiveness.- 50/50 dialogue options. Without spoiling too much, there are certain dialogue options that weigh heavy on your progress. Some options feel vague on what the outcome will be. Hope you saved before an important decision, because if you choose wrong, you'll have to backtrack.- Give us a "Gallery" to view romantic date CGs and the endings. There's a lot of great art and people would like a quick option to view endings without having to load from the save files and go through travelling and dialogue.- Make the UI faster to respond to our inputs. See the negatives above. Patched in 12/15/23. Thank you, devs!Overall, I recommend Little Goody Two Shoes if you like games with great art and music. The world is interesting to explore, and though it can feel repetitive at times, the gameplay is fun and engaging.

_childDocuments_.review: The visuals- Gorgeous. That's probably the first or second thing you noticed if you looked at the screenshots. Aside from the obvious things like character sprites and backgrounds, the UI is so artful that it makes me angry when I see the menus in other games. I won't go on about the visuals too much because you can already see this game in action, but look at Elise. Look at her poofy dress with little grapes embroidered into the apron, and her big hair that swishes from side to side as she runs, and all her silly expressions. How can you not love her? Also, shoutout to the fantastic CG's that always made me feel some sort of way.The sound- It's also great, even if it doesn't stand out at quite the same level. In particular, the music is perfectly on point for setting the mood, and there's a lot of variety. The cute chip-tune style BGMs that play during the minigames are maybe my favorite, but there's a lot of competition. Incidentally, I won't say any more, but if you want to see a bombastic spontaneous musical number then you are in for a ****ing TREAT.The gameplay- Fun, eclectic, a little flawed. It's hard to pin down the genre if you don't just say "horror." It's a dating sim, a puzzle game, an action game, a resource management game, and there's even some minigames to round things out. Eclectic. The puzzle/action sequences that make up about half of this game will have you doing things that definitely recall this series' RPG Maker roots. You'll be chased around the screen, navigate mazes while avoiding hazards, and hunt for items. My only complaint is that some of the puzzles can feel a little bit obtuse. I can't say whether this is a "git gud" situation or not, but I found a couple of them tested my patience. The other half, the "domestic" sequences, are mostly about making sure Elise is making enough money to feed herself, keeping small town busybodies from lynching her, and romancing cute girls with all the time she has left over. Working is represented through cute minigames, of which there are four representing different chores. Your performance will be reflected in your letter rank and accompanying payment. You will need that money to buy food, because every segment of time that passes has a cost to Elise's hunger meter. Your other important meter in this game segment is the "Suspicion" meter. As you might guess, you want this meter to stay low. Things will happen as the game progresses, and it is the player's job to make sure Elise doesn't draw any undue attention to herself. If it gets too high, there are consequences. Aside from that and other story shenanigans, Elise will spend her time with any of the three girls which are seemingly already head over heels for her. The "date" segments consist of visual novel style scenes between Elise and the girls. Once in each scene, you'll have a dialogue choice that will determine how well the date ends up going. Each successive date advances the story between them. The game does not force you to focus on any individual, but given time constraints you will not be able to see all the scenes with all the girls in one play through. No, I didn't learn that first hand. What kind of person do you think I am? It's Freya, always Freya.The story- I don't want to spoil anything, so I'll just say I haven't seen a game nail "slow burn horror" this well in a long time. Everything up to this point has probably made the game sound quite silly and strange- and it often is! But under that silliness there is something unnerving and sinister. The story is not especially complex, nor is it full of dramatic twists, but I believe it is better for it. The horror in this game is obvious and always slowly encroaching, like an inevitability. To be honest, I didn't go in expecting to be genuinely spooked by this game, but I was very pleasantly surprised!TL;DR- Game is so beautiful, game is so cute, game is so spooky, game is so girls

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to rate several individual parts that make up this game, then one overall review.    Soundtrack= 4.5/5 (One: ear torture, five: pure beauty)  Great sound, especially for nighttime and witching hour bits (redacted because of spoilers)    Visuals/ Art= 5/5 (One: eye cancer, five: eye candy) Visuals can be merry when they want to be, and can be grim when they want to be. Level design is top tier and the retro-anime style is very well done.     Storytelling/Character writing= 4.5/5 (One: unbearably boring, five: ATLA tier) The story was fairly good, and the characters were excellently written.     Gameplay= 4/5 (One; unplayable, five; engaging and fun) Unfortunately, sometimes the answers for puzzles are sort of unreasonable, and there is one point in the game where you can get permanently locked out of the ending. Additionally, the minigames for the tasks are either way too easy, or just rage-y. However, it is still super fun to play.      Overall= 4.5/5, worth playing and good to get even if there is no sale.

I'm not really into yuri but the three girls and the dates were cute. Freya feels really irrelevant compared to Lebkuchen and Rozenmarine which is a shame. I didn't really like the nighttime sections. They are where the game becomes more like a normal rpgmaker horror game, with puzzles and chase sequences. _childDocuments_.review: I loved Pocket Mirror for many reasons, but the one that stood out was because it gave me an introduction to classical music, a genre I now hold very dear (there was a disc in the game which played Ravel's "Pava pour une infante defunte," the first time I'd actually listened to a classical piece unto itself). No matter how many disparate genres I'd experience since then, I couldn't forget this game because of this one point.That was more than seven years ago. Since then, I have played triple-A games of all kinds (Witcher 3, RDR2, Cyberpunk, Skyrim, Elden Ring, and so on), and while initially wowed by these games, I garnered a certain fatigue with every new "top-tier company" story. Specifically, an emergent routine of "I will have to wait a few hours (if not forever) before anything remotely entertaining happens because this 'big universe' wants to build itself", and such. The stories themselves were often based in more common interactions of the sort one might find in meeting a stranger on the street (as opposed to more philosophically nuanced themes). This isn't to say that, for instance, Witcher 3 (which is one of my favorite games) isn't socially relevant or adroit, just that it is (in a very Radovidian sense) a world viewed through the eyes of a pawn, as opposed to the eyes of a king (the latter of which appealed more to me personally).Few games had given me the same ethereal sublimity and charm I found in Pocket Mirror. Besides the triple-As I mentioned earlier, I've engaged with countless visual novels, RPG Maker games, souls-likes and such. Unfortunately, none of them ever struck me the way Pocket Mirror did, and I had perhaps subconsciously accepted that I could no longer find sensual novelty the way I did with Pocket Mirror.That was until I played Little Goody Two Shoes. I haven't the slightest idea how the story is going to evolve after I write this review (though I can somewhat confidently assert I'm in the early stages of the game). But this game to me is just refreshing. Everything about it feels new in some way; the controls very clean for a 2D RPG, the world crafted so clearly lived in, the music so delectable, the graphics so charming, the minigames so engaging. In short, I am entranced by this game. AstralShift have somehow reinforced in me the hope that games today don't have to just be graphics-monsters with middling stories or strong one-off concepts; they can be immaculate, mechanically interesting, and thematically nuanced, all in one box.I just want to reify: I do not know how this game will proceed from this point; the curious thing is, I don't care. This game could end(s) in the most disappointing way possible, but the ecstasy, the rejuvenation I feel in this moment, supplants any vituperation I could possibly have in future.

_childDocuments_.review: Stunningly gorgeous game. You can feel the attention to aesthetic detail in every facet of the game's design, from the UI, environment art, and character sprites, to the music and sound design. I was surprised to find out the dev team wasn't Japanese since they went out of their way to create several animated musical sequences for the game in the style of anime openings that are all written and sung in Japanese.Wish I could sing the same praises of the gameplay. The main gameplay loop has you managing your time and money during the day in a way that's loosely reminiscent of a dating sim, while at night the game returns to a more established RPG Maker horror adventure game formula where you collect items and complete various puzzles and other trials while avoiding environmental hazards. It's an interesting choice, and surprisingly punishing if you don't earn enough money to spend on food and healing items (you will be taking *a lot* of damage in the later Witching Hour sections and you'll also have a sanity meter to manage). The game does a good job of pointing you in the right direction without outright holding your hand and isn't afraid to let you fail which I appreciate, at least when it comes to story events and big narrative decisions. However, the game really tested my patience at certain points during the Witching Hour segments (dying 10+ times in a row to trial-and-error insta-death ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ is not fun) and about halfway through the game I was quite bored with the villager interactions and minigames, which is where you're going to be spending most of your time outside of cutscenes. It's serviceable gameplay, but the story and immaculate vibes are good enough to elevate the experience into something worthwhile.TL;DR, if you like RPG maker horror games or other types of narrative-focused anime games, it's worth buying, especially if you're into yuri

Nonetheless, it had a lot of charm and you should at least try out the demo before purchasing.I really hope Astral shift learns from their mistakes with tedious gameplay and focuses more on storytelling in their next title.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm currently in the middle of this game, and I LOVE it so far. I'm very bad when it comes to horror games, I often freeze up and am too scared to even try. However I think this game is balanced enough so that I can still get through the 'scary' stuff. I really enjoy how it doesn't rely too heavily on jumpscares, rather the scariness of the atmosphere and the mysteriousness of what's to come/what's going on. I love RPGs, and it not having combat and just being puzzle and story based was a pleasant surprise. (Idk why I expected there to be combat? I just associate games like this with turn based RPGs) Either way I really enjoy puzzle games, and having a spooky story along side it is very nice. The only thing that *could* be bad for others is some of the puzzles are really trial and error. (One REALLY in particular, but I won't spoil it). If you get frustrated with not having clear directions of what to do, I'd say that's something to look out for. I personally enjoy having to figure out what exactly to do myself, and it adds the scary factor to it. It also feels a whole lot better when I overcome the challenge, and some of the challenges are really creative and unique!And as for the romance, I'm kind of in between on it. Since this is my first play through I'm not sure how much romancing certain people has an effect on the story. I do enjoy that I don't have to work hard to earn the character I like's affection. (FREYA MY BELOVED <3) ALSO THE MUSIC!?!?!?? I LOVELOVELOVE THE MUSIC! They way they can capture scenes with just the music alone is so good. One of the daytime music tracks really reminds me of The Secret Life of Arrietty. so pretty BUT YEAH! THIS IS MY FIRST ACTUAL REVIEW ON A GAME, I saw that it only had like 250ish so i wanted to contribute if it means more people buy this game. Please buy this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I've bought this game after watching a vtuber enjoy it and I gotta say it's so far been really well worth it.The art is incredible, 90s anime style portraits, handpainted backgrounds mixed with pixel art, animations in the middle, calling back to old Grimm Brothers fairy tales and also some other references to popular culture.There's pretty nice girl's love, which is very cute, fun minigames that I wish I could play just for the sake of playing them. _childDocuments_.review: This game is delicious, though with some mild-to-moderate annoyances, though not *quite* enough to bring down it being one of my favorites this year. Let's line up the good--the art style is fantastic, the music is wonderful, the animations are satisfying, and the story is 90% compelling, with some ehhh tropey events (by no means a bad thing by itself) and some... I guess this varies person to person, but some of the endings are lukewarm when it comes to satisfaction. This review will refrain from particular details and spoilers.So, beginning with the gameplay, it's not so bad. Getting money is predicated by doing well in cute little mini-games, which are all good (I hate the egg one though, for goodness' sake) and besides that, gameplay consists of running around and talking to people, followed by puzzle-based dungeons. The environments of the dungeons are beautiful, but the puzzles are, to me, pretty hit or miss. To note--I am not big on puzzles, and even then I only needed to consult a guide for one early game puzzle, so It's by no means a "hard" game so much as some of the puzzles are "annoying."The biggest offender is the water zone, which despite easily being my favorite dungeon... it's puzzles are BS I don't like them the worst. Alright? Alright. Honestly, don't be afraid to take a look at a guide, because the puzzles are in the end a sidejob to the game's spectacular art and animation, alongside it's story.So the story--it's pretty good, though to an extent it suffers from the dating-sim issue of "hey so there are multiple romance choices... but there's also the one you are *supposed* to pick." As in, sure, you can choose any of the three romance interests (or be a good maid and work all day everyday) but there is still a partner who gives you the most insight and lore into the universe, at least by my reckoning, which can be mildly disappointing.I played the English dub, and it's good, so I also suspect the Japanese dub is just as good, so pick whatever it'll be fine. I guess for a tl:dr:Don't be afraid to look at a guide, talk to literally everyone, save before every romantic date. The people with exclamation points are important, and the people will the letter give you loot (do make sure to pay attention to the dialogue, though.) I will fight anyone who doesn't think Freya is the best. Thanks.

_childDocuments_.review: Little Goody Two Shoes is an RPG Horror game unalike any I've played before.As a big consumer of rpg horror, most of them fixed around a fairy tale theme try to subvert the original formula of fairy tales, in ways that often feel very two dimensional and flat. Little Goody Two Shoes embraces the iconic fairy tale formula for what it is while having a completely unique and fleshed out voice of it's own. While playing, I constantly waited for the other shoe to drop, and subvert it in some kind of way or another, but it never did.Little Goody Two Shoes unique personality, unique style, unique ui, and fully fleshed out world left a strong impression on me. I've never seen such polishing to the formula until now. After completing a couple of the endings, I feel like I am no longer the same person who started the game.If you're a horror rpg fan don't miss out on a life changing experience like this.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't usually care to post reviews for games, but I'll make an exception hereTL;DR: It's an incredibly charming game, that despite lack of some of QoL features and uncomplicated gameplay, provides an impressive narrative experience. It feels like a carefully crafted labour of love, and feels like it has its own soul, which is not something I am able to say about many games that have been released recently.I bought the game blind, based on the tags, description and the screenshots on the showcase. In fact, I only became aware of it a few days after release, after Steam helpfully recommended it to me. Truth to be told, I became quite smitten with it after playing it merely for an hour or so, and the opinion has not changed after I've completed my playthrough.Gameplay-wise, LGTS is not terribly challenging. The minigames are rather forgiving, I find, even for a person with rather poor reflexes like me. Puzzles, likewise, are very solvable if you apply yourself to them - I haven't had to look up anything on the internet (I'm looking at you, Flowers). The management aspects might be rather constraining before you figure out what you'll need, but it's not an insurmountable challenge.But the raw gameplay I'd consider just a diversion from what is a wonderful narrative experience. The world is carefully crafted, from the artwork, to the little details like the layout of the town being identifiable from the viewpoint on the hill your home is located on. Speaking of artwork - gorgeous, I love the '90s anime aesthetic! It has a lot of charm to it, and I never felt like any character, creature or object were out of place with the way everything was drawn. And the soundtrack, too, will stay in my head for many days. It sets the mood very well, and is wonderful to listen to in its own right. I don't quite feel like my words can do either of those justice, to be frank.The characters I found rather believable, especially given the constraints of a Girls' Love story, and I liked how their backgrounds informed their interactions with you and each other. The dialogue was written in a way that I find authentic to the setting, and coupled with all the things above it allowed me to easily immerse myself in it. I have to confess I have grown rather attached, and while I'm a quite sentimental person, that has to count for something. Another matter - the protagonist feels like a real person, with their own goals, perspectives and motivations. It sounds like a trivial thing, but I have found it lacking in the past.If I were to complain about something, my expectations about the endgame were a little different. I expected the Witch,  and Father Hans being a bit more proactive on the last day, and having a bit more choice with how to proceed, based on your previous actions. But I can't say I'm very disappointed with what we got instead, even though it's quite a bit more mundane.It wouldn't hurt to have a day or two more to acquaint ourselves with the LIs, either, although I understand that LGTS is not as fixated on romance as some other games.Overall, I'm a little lost for words. I have read through this review a couple of times, and I'm not terribly satisfied with what I had written - it doesn't feel like it really reflects how I felt about the game. Regardless, I hope that it will offer some insight for someone who's on the fence. And if folks from AstralShift read it, I hope it will make their day a little bit better. Your efforts are appreciated.

_childDocuments_.review: i've gotten about half of my total time on the game (as of writing this) in the last like 3 days.so, visually, loved it, every render of each character felt like it really captured that very early anime look, which they nailed perfectly, the pixel art was great, the animations were incredibly smooth, everything looked amazing, don't even get me started on that animation that plays when you boot up the game.story wise, i got a little lost at times, mainly cause i'm severely stupid, but overall loved the story, despite getting one of the bad endings for my first play through (i'm gonna shoot for all the endings in the game.). It's absolutely a slow burn story, only revealing more of the story, and the town, and what's going on if you actively go around talking to NPC's, and that will also change some the the dialog, they'll ask if you know whats going on, and if you didn't talk to anyone something different will be said rather than if you did.and the music, holy hell it's amazing, it has no right to be so damn good. I bought the game like two days after it came out, and ended up getting the soundtrack for free, i would absolutely recommend buying it and letting it play if you're busy writing, or at your computer for several hours for some reason or another.and now some complaints..some of the puzzles were a little vague, and this i ended up having to look up a walk through for a few parts. One of the last sections of the game, you can't use your lantern. Call me stupid but it took me ages to find my way through, and the boss of that bit, also was a little annoying, having to select certain answers on a very short timer, and instantly dying and having to go back to your last save if you choose the wrong one.and muffy. i hated muffy. she's got a cute design, but when I'm already running low on money due to trying to keep my hunger up and buy health items for the night, it's annoying when she ends up requesting one of the more expensive items you can purchase. and the thing is, if you don't do what she wants, she'll make your life harder in game, possibly changing the ending you get.overall though, i loved the game, i highly recommend it if you like slow burn stories and having to plan out ahead of time a bitsolid 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: Coming off the heels of Pocket Mirror GoldenerTraum earlier this year, I was very excited to see that LGTS would be releasing so soon after it. I quite enjoyed my time with Pocket Mirror, it wasn't my favorite RPG horror game, but it did have a lot of what I was looking for from the genre, so it quenched my thirst for a time.That being said, Little Goody Two Shoes is LEAGUES better than Pocket Mirror ever was. I had only found out recently that PM's story was written on the fly as the developed the game, and while that method can work in some situations, I don't think it quite worked for Pocket Mirror. It did, however, do wonders for Little Goody Two Shoes.Somehow, the lore they crafted specifically for Pocket Mirror works a million times better in LGTS. Rather than being drip fed Elise's story in Pocket Mirror, you get to play out her journey—see everything she went through, and it's just so good.The overall gameplay is a huge step up as well. There's a whole life sim aspect during the day, with people to talk to, mysteries to solve, and minigames to play. During the night is when the game most closely uh...mirrors Pocket Mirror. It's you usual RPG horror game—something I'm quite fond of—with puzzles, enemies to avoid, and things to collect. It's still a formula I quite enjoy, even long after the RPG horror craze has passed. But there was one "puzzle" in the crow woods that I just ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ LOATHED. There were these shaking trees and birds that would pop out and peck you if you did the wrong thing. But I never figured out what the "right thing" was no matter what I tried. So I just ended up bolting through and tanked the damage. Terrible. I hated it. Thankfully that's the only part about the game I genuinely did not like.The game isn't really all that scary (barring the serpent woods), but what I felt beyond that was this deep-seated dread. I knew what happened in Pocket Mirror, I knew what was coming, and yet I was powerless to stop it. I just had to sit and watch as Elise ventured further and further into the woods... Okay well there's some alternate good endings as well, but we all know what the true ending is.The addition of the dating subplot is actually ingenious. You get to know these girls, really understand them—all while you watch their romance blossom. But you still know what's coming. You know what you'll have to do. It really gets you to care about each and every one of them, to really savor every moment you get with them.Also can I just add how funny it is that there are no male suitors? Like, that kinda ♥♥♥♥ never happens outside of yuri VNs or lesbian dating sims. Elise is a LESBIAN and there's nothing you can do about it.Little Goody Two Shoes is a wonderful return to the classic RPG horror genre, with some modern touch-ups, a fantastic story, wonderful characters, GORGEOUS artwork, and a killer soundtrack—anime opening included! (More games should do that.) Absolutely recommend to those who love horror games, lesbians, or Pocket Mirror. Hell, even if you haven't played Pocket Mirror, it works very well as a standalone title.

_childDocuments_.review: Little Goody Two Shoes is a gem. I wasn't sure if the gameplay was for me, so I tried the demo first. I was captivated. All the art, all the menus, all the tiny UI elements are rendered in a beautiful 90s anime style. There are several viewpoints where you can see a glimpse of the rural landscape, with hills and mountains, and a lonely white castle in the distance. I immediately felt peaceful and at home.If the art was the thing that made me start the game, the story was what kept me returning. The premise is simple: a country lass desiring a better life, and a way to achieve just that *for a price*. All narrated as in a VN. The gameplay itself is simple yet rich: you have to keep Elise well fed, sane and unsuspected throughout the 6 day phases. Doing that will cost resources you have to earn by completing minigames. Meanwhile, there are secrets to find by exploring. The puzzles are easy to understand, but nonetheless I needed several attempts for a few of them, just to get the timings right.I was totally immersed in Kieferberg and Elise's story, so I will totally do a second a run to unlock more endings. By the way, if you are a fan of Madoka Magica, you will like this game. The art screams Gekidan Ino Curry and the OST is majestic (I still have the devilish march playing in my head). It is a story of wishes, and hope and despair. (Freya best girl btw)

But even if you know the story, some surprises are going on in this game.Oh Lebkuchen, grant me redemption.

_childDocuments_.review: Good god this has to be my game of the year personally. Little Goody Two Shoes retains the RPGMaker game experience while also having beautiful art, enchanting music, and even more. (Playing Pocket Mirror for context is optional and doesn't diminish enjoyment if you don't but I highly suggest playing the remaster anyway.)QOL stuff that has become standard with more modern RPGMaker and RPG games have been added, such as the ability to speed up dialogue by holding shift, auto mode for textboxes, and even text speed options. Saves are near crucial points and paired along with 20 save slots so you can space them out however you'd like. And the devs added a spot to reread tutorials in case you accidentally skipped one is given to you at the beginning of the game. While there are some frustrating points with puzzles, the answers are very much facepalm moments once you figure out the answers. The characters I personally love RPGMaker games and I want to say this to the people who are going to play this game and aren't familiar with the territory of these kinds of games.  expect to get absolutely everything first try. Your first playthrough, is supposed to be a blind experience. Play it through once (or even twice) before going for completion.

_childDocuments_.review:
Set in the mysterious Kieferberg Village, Little Goody Two Shoes is a homage to the original PlayStation and early PlayStation 2 RPGs and is centered around Elise, an ambitious girl determined to become rich and escape her humble life.

Players will step into Elise's shoes and soon find themselves immersed in a 90s inspired horror role-playing adventure game. Gameplay elements such as "Sustenance," "Reputation & Suspicion," and "Exploration & Narrative" will guide players to complete their daily tasks by day and uncover the woodland's darkest secrets by night.

Players will also have the ability to set their own paths to navigate through the wicked woods, solve puzzles and build meaningful relationships in this nostalgic gaming experience.

name: SUPER CRAZY RHYTHM CASTLE
detailed_description: It’s Super Crazy Rhythm Castle, the chaotic rhythm adventure! A puzzling co-op mashup unlike anything you've ever heard – work together to think outside the box while keeping your combo. Solo, or with a band of up to three friends … … Can you conquer the castle? An unforgettable journey with a light heart and a tapping foot. You’ll become one with the music and the madness. Unlikely heroes, approach Rhythm Castle! Inside, the unhinged King Ferdinand awaits, ready to defend his crown and ruin your day. Overcome his twisted challenges and beat him in his own game. Throw beans into an ancient summoning ritual. Shut down a giant eggplant DJ. Cover tiny meat people in gravy for reasons that we promise will become clear. All while keeping the beat! With over 30 tracks – plus a few hidden extras – tune in for earworm rock, hip hop, dubstep, and plenty more. Chaotic cooperative gameplay that’s fun and accessible. Not a pro at rhythm games? Each player can play their music in three-button or four-button mode – or hop out to focus on puzzling while your buddy covers the music! Whether you go solo or sync up with friends, get ready to embrace the madness and take on the challenges of Rhythm Castle. From musical escape room to elevator arcade, you’ll need to think outside the beat to stay ahead of the king’s mischief. Juggle music play with tricky tasks and blasting action to solve each level! Gunning for a gold medal? Unlock & play every song in the Music Lab. No nonsense, just pure rhythm! From the twisted mind behind Super Crazy Guitar Maniac Deluxe, the flash game sensation. The rhythm lives on in Super Crazy Rhythm Castle! This game installs the following third-party software: Epic Online Services - Used when PC crossplay is enabled for match making between Epic and Steam users. If the PC crossplay option is kept off then the game does not rely on Epic Online Services, and it can be uninstalled.
about_the_game: It’s Super Crazy Rhythm Castle, the chaotic rhythm adventure! A puzzling co-op mashup unlike anything you've ever heard – work together to think outside the box while keeping your combo. Solo, or with a band of up to three friends … … Can you conquer the castle? An unforgettable journey with a light heart and a tapping foot. You’ll become one with the music and the madness. Unlikely heroes, approach Rhythm Castle! Inside, the unhinged King Ferdinand awaits, ready to defend his crown and ruin your day. Overcome his twisted challenges and beat him in his own game. Throw beans into an ancient summoning ritual. Shut down a giant eggplant DJ. Cover tiny meat people in gravy for reasons that we promise will become clear. All while keeping the beat! With over 30 tracks – plus a few hidden extras – tune in for earworm rock, hip hop, dubstep, and plenty more. Chaotic cooperative gameplay that’s fun and accessible. Not a pro at rhythm games? Each player can play their music in three-button or four-button mode – or hop out to focus on puzzling while your buddy covers the music! Whether you go solo or sync up with friends, get ready to embrace the madness and take on the challenges of Rhythm Castle. From musical escape room to elevator arcade, you’ll need to think outside the beat to stay ahead of the king’s mischief. Juggle music play with tricky tasks and blasting action to solve each level! Gunning for a gold medal? Unlock & play every song in the Music Lab. No nonsense, just pure rhythm! From the twisted mind behind Super Crazy Guitar Maniac Deluxe, the flash game sensation. The rhythm lives on in Super Crazy Rhythm Castle! This game installs the following third-party software: Epic Online Services - Used when PC crossplay is enabled for match making between Epic and Steam users. If the PC crossplay option is kept off then the game does not rely on Epic Online Services, and it can be uninstalled.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wish Steam allowed for a "mixed" option. Don't get me wrong, I absolutely love this game, but it's very hard to recommend this game outright.Super Crazy Rhythm Castle is a mix between the party, rhythm, puzzle, and action genres. It's a truly unique take on rhythm games, but the rhythm portion is not the sole focus, and if you come in expecting a more traditional experience like Guitar Hero, Osu!, DDR, or Beat Saber, you will be in for a surprise. There does exist a more traditional rhythm game mode within the game, but it is very simple and does not include any kind of "training" features you would find from other games in the genre. This mode is also locked behind some progression, so by the time you reach it, I would say you would know whether or not you will enjoy the game.Niche. Love or hate. These two phrases succinctly sum up this game. It's in a niche of a niche all its own and you will either love it or hate it, there is no in between. Try the demo, watch some playthroughs, this is not a game you "get" at a glance, you have to experience it to some degree to really get what it's about and the first few levels will give you a good idea.If you're an achievement hunter, this game is of moderate difficulty if you're decent at rhythm games, with some key exceptions. This game is tailored for the casual experience more than anything, so some of the levels are incredibly frustrating and will make you question many of the design decisions made with this game if you're aiming to "complete" it rather than just "beat" it. Level 14.... These issues are much less pronounced to unnoticable if you're not a neurotic e-trophy goblin like me.It may seem like I'm complaining more than anything, but I do love this game. It has great art, a bunch of really appealing and well made characters, enjoyable dialouge , a great and varied soundtrack, and a good deal of the gameplay is fun, even if some of it was intentionally designed to frustrate you.Overall "recommend", I had lots of fun, its a great game, but really play the demo before you buy. It's unique, but it's not for everyone.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is honestly such a joy to play. It's goofy, chaotic, fun, almost every single song has some kinda beat you can bob your head to, the characters are silly...Frankly, this is just a really good rhythm game that's played best with friends. The minigames are especially difficult, because you can't rely solely on playing the rhythm part of the game to make it through; you gotta hotswap between doing rhythm and doing something else, which I find to be really engaging.This game isn't for everyone because of this, and that's okay. SCRC is a wonderfully chaotic and delightful little game that appeals to a lot of players, especially groups who like rhythm games, but some people might not like because of it being a bit too difficult.I'm just glad to see Second Impact make a game after roughly 8+ years of waiting that is THIS GOOD, to be honest. I grew up with SCGMD4 as my gateway drug to rhythm games, and I've grown a deep passion for games like this because of it.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played this game a few times with others, but I went solo to get all the achievements (including the PRO medals).There was a lot of times I thought about stopping, and several I wondered if I would actually recommend the game.The actual mechanics are pretty neat. The overall design of the levels is really quite entertaining, the music is good, the visuals are appealing. There's even a story... like, an actual one.If you aren't worried about getting three stars the levels are actually pretty fun. The game garage has catchy tunes with unique lighting effects, and there's a lot of small details in each main level which indicate the player's status — it just takes some time to look around and figure out each thing.There are some frustrations, though.- BALANCE. The game is balanced so there is no room for error. It is more punishing than necessary, and this is a *major* detraction from the enjoyment. It's not enough to play well. There's a lot of things happening at once, and most levels have a gimmick of some sort, which can be hard to spot or even understand. Levels usually require failing a level to understand the mechanics, because there is not enough time to both experiment and succeed in the same run.- CONTROLS. The keyboard defaults are hard to remember, and the controller gets extremely uncomfortable — legitimately hurt my hand joints to play several of the faster levels.- PUZZLES. There's many adventure-game-adjacent puzzles outside the music levels, which don't always have obvious solutions. Since it's not possible to review the descriptions on items after they're in your possession, any clues that were in there are lost to time. Also, at this time, there is almost zero guidance online: if you are struggling with a level, you are absolutely on your own (unless you can read Japanese, which sometimes uncovers a couple of Youtube videos).- REPETITION. There's no way to skip cut scenes. You can speed up to get through dialogue more quickly, and sometimes this helps uncover objectives that weren't clear the first time, but generally speaking the lack of a skip slows the pace and creates frustration when a group is struggling. Also, there's no checkpoints when a level has multiple stages within it — if a mistake is made late in the level, restarting means going back to the very beginning of the first area and listening to ALL the banter again.If you experience a great deal of joint pain, struggle with an inundation of visuals, or find repetition frustrating then this game may not be a good fit. However, if your main draw is unique rhythm gaming, good music, and a colorful game — this is an excellent choice.I legitimately hope to see more from this franchise in the future. DLC, sequels, etc. This is worth supporting.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't think I've ever written a review before, but this game deserves it. I've never played a whole ton of rhythm games before, but this one grabbed my attention. A rhythm game with witty writing, a clear and present story that doesn't overstay it's welcome and is just the right amount of funny and absurd, and a WILD art style that is so incredibly varied and inconsistent that it's always a joy to look at and discover new areas. The music choices though? Top, f*cking, tier. There's such a wild range of genres and artists, and the music always fits to the level you're playing. Oh but if you're thinking it's just a regular old rhythm game, get f*cking ready because you better be ready to multitask/use teamwork to beat all the levels. If you liked Overcooked or Moving out, imagine playing that, while also having to keep the house you're playing in lit by powering it by playing a rhythm game off to the side. Also imagine if you will that the rhythm game is easy to start, but actually difficult later on. Like, I played with a person that's played rhythm games for a long time, and the Pro level songs in this game kicked his as$. If you want a game to play with your friends, or just an incredible rhythm game, please for the love of f*ck play this game. The devs deserve so much support and money for all of the work that obviously went into this game. Play it

_childDocuments_.review: I purchased this title completely expecting to play Piano Tiles on PC (now co-op!) but the rhythm game aspect is not even the bulk of the fun part of the game, as enjoyable as it is by itself.Each level is a variation of attempting to complete fun yet panic inducing mini games all while you and your friend/s struggle with trying not to miss any notes. Some levels you can get by with a low hit percentage as long as you do well in the mini game, while some levels are 90% or go home. Either way the game makes sure to have each one bring a different challenge to overcome accompanied with a banger of a soundtrack. Most levels are a hit in terms of how creative and fun they are, and the ones that kinda fall short are still worth a replay to get that three stars.It is very accessible as well, offering a "Regular" difficulty option if someone in your group chooses to. Even though this splits the music board into two variations if someone else picks "Pro", I didn't find this to be distracting.Bought this at 50% off and is worth every cent.
