_childDocuments_.review: For years now, Square-Enix has been trying to make a good A tier original IP game. The games they've released have mostly been middling mediocrity. But finally, they've released a game that I'd actually call "decently good".  First things first though, is actually set expectations, because in usual fashion, SE's marketing did an absolutely terrible job. Harvestella is a JRPG first, and a farming simulator in a somewhat distant second. Neither are particularly deep, but the JRPG portion is a proper (A)RPG with a full job system, dungeon diving, and overarching story that is surprisingly compelling, while the farming portion is just the player plopping a few veggies & fruits in an expandable (but still limited) area, and tending to 2 specific types of  animals, all this so that you can have ingredients to cook food that you'll use as supporting items for the aforementioned dungeon diving. The audio for the game is...interesting. The music is pretty good, kinda reminiscent of Nier Automata's. The voice acting, by contrast, is almost non-existent. If the simplistic farming hinted at it, the lack of VA exposes the fact that this game had a low budget to work with. The story does lose a lot of it's impact when the only times you'll ever hear a character talk is in random grunts and shouts. Ofc, that's likely leading you to the question: "If it's that obviously low-budget, then why is it priced like a marquee game?", and the answer to that leads to why, I think, Square-Enix has been unable to make their lower-tier efforts stick: pricing misalignment. This game, like a lot of others in their catalogue, is way overpriced for how underbudgeted, and how unproven, it is. This game would be a FAR EASIER pill to swallow if were somewhere closer to 40$/€ base price than within spitting distance of AAA pricing that it is now.   But I'm digressing there. the TL;DR for this review is: Low-budget JRPG with simple farming sim bolted in, compelling story but overpriced, rec'd when on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR:  A soulless Rune Factory wannabe that's mechanically very basic. Only get it if there's huge discount >70% or get Rune Factory instead.The action part is super basic; you can't customize your stats, the only thing equip-able is your jobs (skill sets) and accessories. There's no weapon crafting and customization, and the same goes with your armour. As your party members, the only thing you can do is upgrade their weapon. That's it. They don't receive EXP, they just automatically have the same level as you. Fighting enemy is just tapping one button, with the occasional skills & evasion (only in some jobs). Oh, and don't forget to eat because stamina won't regenerate on empty stomach.As for the farming part, just imaging Harvest Moon in the early days, but worse, especially the animal part and the equipment. You can only get a chicken coop and a barn, and you need to purchase said two types of animals from a merchant. Unlike Rune Factory where you can capture almost any monster, this feels very basic and not fun. As for the farming equipment, there's no upgrade. You can only level up your farming skills, but only through grind quests after you unlock the required characters. This is just a blatant way of extending play time.Crafting is very basic. There's only two crafting: item crafting which use items gathered from exploration and cooking, which is use your farmed crops and gathered materials. Most of the times, you craft items to help exploration (e.g. fixing bridge), and some damage items.As others said, the action and farming part feels like independent of each other. Farming is just for making money and getting ingredients for your food, which is basically your potion. Exploration is OK. Nothing special, nothing bad.Then, the graphic, audio, and story is what you expect from a 3rd party game that's also released on Switch: graphic feels like PS2 era with fancy effects, audio is of typical budget JRPGs, and story is filled with all sorts of common tropes and character types of anime world, that's heavily sugar coated so the game is playable by kids.All in all, this game is a soulless husk of a chimera of two game genres, that's filled with the most boring flavour that you can find.

For the actual review, scroll down to the /rant the actual game review starts there.I've seen this game get a lot of heat, some things I think are not really compelling reasons to thumbs down the game, other things are absolutely valid. Here's the deal, if you're not a trans-phobe, or someone who takes offense that you can select non-binary as an option for gender, some of the bad reviews are based around that bs... because, apparently, a feature that has been in tons of video games for decades, is all of a sudden important for  modern games as some bs to "counter alt left agenda". So, basically, if you're obsessed with adding "politics" aka, formalized judgmental fascist hate that has no basis in reason, logic or the things I was taught to abide by growing up (manners and courtesy and to not criticize others who are different... yeah, the stuff that's ACTUALLY old school), then, point blank, don't buy this game, it's not like selecting gender and voice are the core components of the game, but if a simple character selection screen or the fact that relationships aren't tethered to "gender norms" (relationship mechanics are also not the main focus of the game, seriously... the stuff I mentioned are little pockets off to the side)... if you're that much of a thin-skinned snowflake, then so be it, go get offended in your little parroting hate groups and try to rebuild fascism because you're too feeble to exist in a world with people... the rest of us actually don't have such tender sensibilities and don't go out of our way to GAF what other people have goin' on below the clothes... because we're not obsessive creeps... /rantThat said, the game, the review, these two things are more important in the end, they should be more important than some weak willed person who hates others because they can't be arsed to spare a neuron to care about their own life and how they comport themselves (because, ya know, accountability for personal actions isn't important as long as these weaklings find fabricated and unrealistic faults in others)...So, here's the deal, this game doesn't really break new ground as much, it has components of a few games, but, it does have, imo, an original mix of those things. This isn't a full on replication of Stardew Valley as others might suggest, not in my opinion at least. You do farm, you start with a basic field and are told that you need to use that as a main way of generating income, however, crops are limited pretty heavily at first. Is this a bad thing? Depends. For me? No, no it isn't, it has just enough farm work to annoy the crap out of me like working on an actual small farm that only had an acre of field and about 20 cattle and 20 chickens did when I was a kid. That's not bad per se, as, though I hated chores like any other kid growing up, and hated more that we relied on the farm to actually eat, I don't mind that annoyance in video games. Time is active, and aside from it pausing during scenes, it is a component you really need to be mindful of. If I had a criticism for the game, it's the time component is a bit too aggressive, imo. Seriously, even with fields that have crops that continue producing yield, a greater portion of the morning gets taken up by cooking meals and crafting bombs, etc. You don't want to skip farming because, especially early, farming does actually bring home the bacon... I might be being a bit literal with that metaphor... That said, as you progress, like with other games in the genre, you can unlock more points of interest, I won't draw a Stardew valley comparison as much because the game reminds me more of the Harvest Moon that was on Wiii, imo. Here's the deal, though, there are other ways to get money, and, more effective ways to boot, you want to always be producing crops because you can use them to cook dishes which makes the adventuring aspect doable. Why? Cooking a meal and having some basic juices available early on is the difference between clearing a level and passing out to wake up at home with a doctors fee subtracted (admittedly that's very Stardew Valley). Dying doesn't actually kill you or lose your stuff, but, it hits you in the wallet and, early on, that's a big deal because even the most basic upgrade to your house is $2k (the kitchen, which in turn is how you cook). This game factors in costs too, the starting area has a ton of crops you could conceivably buy, but, some seeds are worth the price, others are a flagrant rip off, it's up to you to figure out what to buy where. Keep in mind that seasons are a thing, and, furthermore, crops take different amounts of time to grow. One reason that's extremely important, and one reason that I'm re-emphasizing the time progression being just a tad too aggressive, is that, unlike other games in the genre, if you plant a crop that, say, grows in spring and summer and continues producing yield instead of being a 1 off, you will not be able to let that crop stay from season to season because of another mechanic in the game, Quietus. What is Quietus? IDK, not that far in to get the story explanation, but, it wipes everything except crop yielding trees in between 30 day seasons, so, if you wait til day 30 of spring and drop a crop that produces yield in 2 days, you've just wasted your seeds. Does this change later on? IDK, not that far, but, I think reviews are best as you're playing the early to mid game, so, from that angle, I guess I'll find out. This mechanic, though annoying, is, imo, a fresh take on the genre, and, when quietus hits, you get the ability to take a break from the farming and do other things, like explore a mystery dungeon that appears only on quietus, etc. Dungeons/combat/leveling: There are a decent amount of dungeons early on, small world, but, each dungeon has at least 3 parts, most have more. Combat is basic but functional, spam your specials and spam normal attack in the meantime. It sort of reminds me of FF XII but without the gambit system. You have 2 others you can have run with you in combat, they don't need micromanaging, the only thing you can upgrade on them is their loyalty for passive bonuses/their specials, and what level their weapon is. Skills and jobs are tied to meeting new companions, you can switch between 3 at a time, bring repair kits and bombs when you get them. Death is the standard "pass out and doctor revives you for a fee at home" affair, leveling is JP reliant and linear, no min-maxing theorycrafting here. Enemies require different tactics, but not too in depth. Combat/leveling/Dungeons are functional without micromanaging (given that micromanaging your farm takes time, this is a good thing). You get a weapon that levels up with money/items ala FF VIII, and 2 accessory slots. Spells are tied to jobs. Is it worth it? I think the game is worth it, I've played for the past bit of hours you see consecutively and haven't got past Spring of the first year yet. So, time spent versus amount of gameplay is less than a dollar an hour. It's not for everyone though, and the side-quests are usually wholesome if that gets under your skin.  I'd have bought this for full price. Oh, no Denuvo is also a +

_childDocuments_.review: As of posting (will update):  At Mid-Summer of the first year.  Almost 30 hours in.TLDR; This game is what I wanted Rune Factory 5 to be.The game is a mix of Stardew Valley, Rune Factory and Final Fantasy with its job systems (also story) and being able to change them on the fly along with leveling them up individual and unlocking stuff.  The farm can be upgraded multiple times, with a lot of things to work towards.  Also have differing farms (from what I understand), such as a water farm and cave farm you unlock further down the road.  Doing fairy quests (a fairy represents each season), you are able to unlock things similar to the community center in Stardew, but the rewards are arguably much more important to focus on (and easier to do) as they unlock magic and other things, which essentially act as tool upgrades and the ability to make various equipment and items for the farm (such as fermenting barrels and such).  The Final Fantasy portion is, of course, the JRPG aspect as you can see by the artwork it borrows heavily from old paint-like portraits and has a traditional JRPG and early FF storyline where you unlock jobs, level up and get job points from using said jobs.  They also change the clothes of your character as well as other benefits.  You are able to swap between three at a time during battle.  This has an element of strategy with the game's break system and how enemies are weak to certain elements or weapons that each job possesses.  You are also able to have two additional party members follow you around in areas where there are monsters to fight.Some of the dungeons (areas with monsters to fight and to travel through) are annoying as you have to dungeon crawl to get specific items to unlock an obvious path forward, and having to back track to said path once you have said items.  Not all have been like this, but enough to make me take a break for a short time out of exasperation.  There are shortcut points that you can travel directly to when you enter a dungeon once you unlock them, saving you time.  There are also mounts that help save you time when on the world map.To elaborate on saving time, the game has a time of day system similar to Stardew.  You wake up at 6AM (after the tutorial) and you collapse at about 2 AM (the game simply says you are "Very Tired" at 12 AM and the time of day switches to "Early Morning" without a time.  Though in the next two in game hours or so the edges of the screen black out until your character themselves go unconscious and will have to be brought back to your bed and be charged a doctor's fee.  The fee is minor and not a percentage of your wealth, but you do start the next day at 12PM instead of 6 AM.There are plenty of teleport features to avoid this, including an easy-to-get but takes-up-a-slot bell that sends you directly home.  As well as each waypoint offering the same service.  To date, I've not run out of time while making it back because of the options they give to the players.Seasons offer new crops, similar to other farming games.  But they do their best to make sure you don't use reharvestable crops by making them have limited offerings at low prices compared to others.  They're mainly for cooking as a whole.  One-time crops are usually the go-to to make money.  Though rewards for the crops are typically fairly low, which makes the farming aspect last long as you make money to upgrade everything while also trying to save some for more seeds.  It's at a fair balance as a whole -- not too quick, even for someone that min/maxes every day.Will update when I finish the game / beat the post game.The combat and graphics are probably what you'd expect out of a game that is also on switch.  Many of the towns look nice, but some far-off background locations look bad.  In some cases, just some grass and trees.  Though areas that are prominent that you can visit in the distance look good, such as the Seaslight (the giant crystal in the background).In whole, the game to me is better than base Stardew Valley without any mods and it is fun to have actual characters and parties and jobs and a real storyline to follow.  Also to make use of your farm on your journey as an adventurer and, to a lesser extent, a hero to people.  It is also everything I would have wanted Rune Factory 5 to be.  So as a whole, I'd say it is better than both of those games if you're looking for something similar but with different twists.

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this game, but it is contingent upon a couple of things - I think you need a fan of the aesthetic of this kind of game, which I can only describe as "the Squeenix aesthetic" - and you need to be willing to work with a very 6/10 experience.  A bit above middling, but not by much.  For my part, I found it scratched an itch, but it won't be a game I come back to.  Definitely wait for a sale.This game tries to be a farming sim, relationship sim, JRPG, and action-hack-n-slash game all in one package, and it does none of these things particularly poorly, but also not particularly well.I don't really have organized thoughts on this game, so we're doin' bullet points:*The UI is optimized for controller and is super awkward for mouse and keyboard.  Highly recommend hooking up a controller if you're playing this on PC.*The story is weapons grade anime bildungsroman, with a complete cast of all the stereotypes and cliches: a hero's journey for your protagonist, a redemption arc for a main character, and all of the party characters generally figuring out who they are and how they fit into the world.  I find it cringy but tolerable, but if you care about stories on a technical level, this game's story will annoy you greatly.*Character creation is very limited.  Putting aside the fact that it took me until I started a second game to figure out that one of the models is actually intended to be a bishonen man and not a chunkier woman, you can pick name, hair color, gender, eye color, and combat voice.  That's it.*I can't really tell if the story "choices" affect game play or even the story at all and that's due to the fact that I've redone several dialog trees, leading me into my next point...*During the cutscenes prior to fighting bosses, you have to make dialog choices.  This means these cutscenes are unskippable and so you do not want to die during a boss fight. Not usually an issue, as this game is not terribly difficult, but an autosave as combat starts would be a huge quality-of-life improvement.*Combat is extremely simple and while I appreciate being able to move around, if I'm going to get hit regardless of where I'm standing for anything except AOE attacks, the combat should've just been turn-based.
_childDocuments_.name: HARVESTELLA

_childDocuments_.review: I want to like this game so much as it really is a neat subgenre of the Harvest Moon games but after playing for a dozen hours or so, I've noticed one glaringly obvious flaw that has become really bothersome and that is the lack of a event skip or fast forward button on the cutscenes. There are lots of side quests to the games credit, but to its detriment is that they are all unskippable text slogs at an already agonizingly slow pace. Going through several of these quest events and realizing this, I'm just getting more and more mad. What's even worse is Square doesn't care enough to add this simple QOL feature that's present in most games since 20 years ago and the game has been out for a while now. There are very little updates in general. With that in mind, this game should be avoided like the plague, it's not worth the inconvenience it poses to you as the player.

_childDocuments_.review: I rarely leave reviews, but felt I had to give a good review having now played for the first 15 days of the game. _childDocuments_.review: so after some trailers and watching the gameplay for this game i was genuinely excited to play harvestella but after 10 hours i can honestly say that this game is not it the combat was just lacking and i can actually say this about almost everything in this game dialogue story everything just felt mid at best plus the stamina\hunger system is just a big no even after i played the game with cheats and mods to better the gameplay it just felt meh even the core of the game which is the farming felt unpolished and just for lack of better words MEH i could honestly only compliment the art and the music but most of the time even that felt mid in conclusion i really don't recommend this game its unbalanced unpolished and doesn't really know what it wants to be either go full farming sim and invest more in the hunger bar survival mechanic or go full action adventure and invest in the combat more or just go full on l turn base (could have been a lot better in my opinion) but sadly this game tries to be both and just fails immensely for lacking any real identity of what it wants to be my final score for this disappointment of a game is a 3 out of 10

_childDocuments_.review: I thought long and hard about if I would or would not recommend the game and finally leaned towards No. I think I would sum Harvestella up as being a solid Okay/10: all the different aspects of the game are shallow, so you can get tired of it quickly. I got it on sale and it's been keeping me busy, but there's nothing to write home about here. There are no crop levels, fishing levels, and the combat skilltrees don't feel particularly meaningful. There's no real way to mitigate damage, so you're discouraged from playing any of the frontline classes. An overwhelming amount of the game is a walking simulator where you talk to one character in one spot and then run to another spot to talk to them again, which is especially heinous in a game where you need to eat to slowly regain the stamina spent doing so. They just didn't really seem decisive on what they wanted out of this game. It's alright for a while, and then loses its luster.

_childDocuments_.review: I'd like to start by saying this: do not go for this game if your main goal is to play a farming sim like Story of Seasons or even Rune Factory. This game features elements of farming sims, like farming or crafting or cooking, but - at its core - it is a JRPG.The game has pretty scenery, a fitting and imho really good  soundtrack, compelling characters and interesting quests, as well as a seemingly simple, yet fun job and battle system, especially for boss fights. Fighting is rather fast-paced I'd say; nothing too tactical, but it still does require quite a lot of moving and dodging around certain battle mechanics. So far my only criticism is the very little voice acting. There's a few battle lines and everyday talk at your farm (like good morning, welcome home, etc.), but that's about it. I wish the character quests were fully voiced at least... :(If you're looking for a casual and relaxing game, I think there are definitely better and cheaper choices out there. If you enjoy JRPGs however, definitely try this one out! In particular, I think anyone who played Fantasian and liked that aesthetic will definitely appreciate Harvestella.

_childDocuments_.review: I waited to buy this on sale thinking that the initial price tag (£49.99) was a bit steep for a farming sim with some JRPG elements... I was wrong. This game is worth every penny and I ended up absolutely loving nearly everything about it.Harvestella is a mix between Final Fantasy, Xenoblade Chronicles, Nier:Automata, Rune Factory, and so many more.For me, this was my favorite game of 2022 and I heartily recommend it to anyone. If you want a cozy game with a great story and interesting characters, this is it.This game has a clear vision and the team executes that idea perfectly and I love that about it. The graphics are intentional, and whilst it may looked a little dated in the way in renders textures at times - it's completely forgiven by the art direction and framing. At times I paused during dialogue just to take it all in. Truly fantastic art direction throughout, and in the latter half of the game this really kicks into high gear.I feel the team did so much with relatively few resources, and if the price was £39.99 standard they would have been lauded for their amazing work rather receiving just above average scores. Nevertheless, I think the game is fantastic and I dearly hope they continue this series. I really appreciate that it's a 'lesser' title by Square Enix, we need more like these in the vein of the original Bravely Default etc. To me this is an instant classic and I'm extremely grateful that this game produced and released exactly as the developers intended, it's honestly magical.At times I was extremely touched by the side quests, and the main plot. There are moments where I had to put my controller down and think about what was happening, how characters felt, and how I wanted to respond. Toward the end things do get quite complex and spending this time to consider things really pays off. Not rushing through this game is the best way to play it, I think. I had not been this impressed with a games story since the semi-reboot of God of War.For any future title in this series I hope the combat does get improved slightly as I'd really appreciate a way to dodge or block enemy attacks.What a wonderful experience this has been!

_childDocuments_.review: I honestly have no idea why so many people are complaining about this game. I would definitely count myself as a part of the "intended demographic" and I have loved it so far. There seems to be so much more story for me to get through after ten hours, and so many new characters for me to meet. Sure, the farming aspect is definitely overshadowed by the game's JRPG elements, but I feel like players should be aware of that going in. It is most comparable to the Rune Factory series, another set of games I absolutely love. If you are a fan of Rune Factory, then Harvestella should be right up your alley. Do not go into this game expecting Stardew Valley or Harvest Moon. It is very much a JRPG first and a farming simulator second, like Rune Factory.I also think the visuals are stunning. I see a lot of people complaining about optimization but it fits the style of a JRPG perfectly to me. The game is vibrant, runs perfectly on my 4K monitor, and is so enchanting.I hope that the consensus here changes from mixed to at least mostly positive. I am so happy with Harvestella so far. Also... CUCUMBLE! What an incredibly cute name for a cucumber...

_childDocuments_.review: The game is good so far. While it is quite similar to Rune Factory, there are some aspects of it that aren't quite as complex, and others that I think it does better. The farming is simple Story of Seasons/Rune Factory fare.When using a tool or planting seeds, your character is locked in the direction they're facing, and you can move forward/back/left/right making it a lot easier to interact with your farm.The combat is super simple so far. There's a number of jobs to unlock though, and each job has a number of active and passive skills to unlock. I only have two jobs so far though, so I can't say for certain how deep the combat gets.The graphics are pretty standard PS4 level graphics, and the PC version doesn't seem to have any settings you can change. The game does run at high frame rates, with zero stutter though.Overall, I'd say it's a good game, but definitely not $60 good. If you're on the fence about the price, I'd wait for a sale and get it for $40-$50 or less.

_childDocuments_.review: In no particular order, except for the first one, I do not recommend this game as it stands for these reasons:Horrible character customization.Lazy writing (especially the random events in dungeons).Not open-world in the slightest. Lots of invisible walls. Feels very restrictive and ruins immersion.Map design is extremely simplistic.Character's job clothes and combat sounds are bad (female mage looks and sounds terrible).Dumb response choices (your character is a clueless idiot) that barely change any dialogue anyway.No clothing, accessories, or hairstyles to unlock. Yes, you're really stuck with that weird ass cut the entire game as far as I can tell.Jobs so far aside from Warrior are just a copycat of other characters you meet with what should be their own unique combat style. And they're boring.I personally don't care about having more voice acting, but I would like to get a feel for what a character sounds like when you first meet them as opposed to later when you go out and adventure with them, for example.The map designs, again, are a joke. Basically 3 different things you need to do, either spend an hour repairing a swimming pool ladder (why the hell are these in forests?), repair a wooden bridge, or blow up random debris, all just for shortcuts or access to mediocre loot.Treasure chest locations make no sense and never reward you with much.No gathering points or animations, just invisible stuff you pick up off the ground.Fishing is just "wait and press A, congrats you got it".The tools look totally impractical for their purpose. The watering can is just a shower head. The hoe is a hammer-looking thing for some reason.Character writing is shallow.All the important characters have way better hair than the MC.Speaking of the MC, males and females wear the exact same outfit down to the thigh high boots. Lmao.The game's pacing is weird. I don't know if there's a time limit for anything quest-related, nor do I know when the seasons end (how many days in a season? Do my crops wither and die in the next?)The FEAR monsters are literally just oversized versions of the regular ones which is cheesy, I hate reskins/recycling assets.I paid $63 and some change for this game, which would've been a good Nintendo 3DS title about 7 years ago. I love JRPGs and farming sims. I love Harvest Moon/SoS, Rune Factory, and FF games. This does not deliver. That being said, I'm still going to play it a bit longer to see if I can possibly get more of my money's worth, which sadly I doubt. I'll probably be back in another 10-20 hours of playtime to just add new things I found that suck to this list.Edit:My impression of this game did not improve. I really hoped it would. I'm halfway done with the main story and I just can't take the awful writing anymore. Maybe if I could skip the incredibly boring and pointless dialogue and cutscenes, but I can't. Seriously, I didn't have high expectations at all going into this. I didn't even get it for a story, and it's so bad I can't pick it up again. There are a few other things that didn't sit right with me that I forgot to mention, like no blocking and dodging in combat, but all you really need to know is this game is worth a quarter of its price at best and having to sit through the story will make you want to shoot yourself. I will add I've noticed a lot of positive reviewers saying things along the line of, "you need to realize this is an RPG first with some farming elements on the side". Yeah, I expected that too. But I don't blame someone else for expecting more harvesting when the title of the game is literally Harvestella.

_childDocuments_.review: I will update this review as I play more of the story and do more of the character and side story quests. Right now my recommendation is more of a 'I am enjoying it/I am not enjoying it' kind of thing, and until I have the full picture it's going to remain that way. There is a huge, huge discrepancy in my thought process for this review that I want to cover first and foremost, and that is:A little bit weird considering if you check the game's store page currently tagged "Farming Sim" and the blurb even calls it a "life sim", but I believe this game is an RPG first, farming sim second. Especially, consideringEdit: After completing main story, you can propose to any character and have them live with you on the farm.As such, I will be reviewing this like it is an ARPG with farming sim elements to supplement its economy and item crafting, rather than a farming sim with ARPG elements to keep you playing and engaged with the story like in Rune Factory. It may seem like I'm splitting hairs here but defining what main genre this game is  shifts my expectations and what the critical features of the game are.So, I will be reviewing the game based on these core aspects: Travel, Combat, and Story.This section covers the stuff you'll be doing in between quests, i.e. the downtime segments, and progressing through the physical map inside dungeons. I literally don't know what to call this grouping so I just called it 'Travel'. It's ... ok. Farming stuff is passable but it's got a more 'self-sufficient adventurer's farm for recovery and crafting" feel than "profiting by shipping 10 trillion level 10 Turnips every 4 days" feelI want to say first that this game puts its WORST foot forward in the first chapter, where most people who come from farming sims know you can put off story and do whatever you want unless you want to unlock a character or something. You SHOULD NOT do that here, as the first Chapter locks you into days that start at 10AM and the game will constantly bug you about going to bed at 7-9PM because this Chapter is secretly the tutorial Chapter. Once you complete it, days will start at 6AM and it will no longer bug you about sleeping. It's really stupid and is possibly the worst first impression that I've ever seen.The way time progresses in towns and on the field I am ok with. However, the overworld time progression is the killer here.Time progresses really fast as you move on the overworld map, so you feel strapped for time throughout much of the early game. Once you unlock the Toukaku and the Airship, it improves considerably though the latter is tied to story progression.The town and dungeon layouts are good, but this is SE so ofc they would. What is the bane of my existence however are the fact that there are repairable ladders that use up one hour of in game time if you do repair them, though they usually create a shortcut. Note that you can only repair them from the place you want to get up to, so you have to take the long way around to actually build the damn thing, eating more of your time. Makes repeat visit that you will (inevitably) need to make shorter, but at the same time the time cost forces you to revisit often BECAUSE you're running out your time, of which there is an OHKO for hitting 12AM w/o sleeping. Oh yeah and crafting uses up time (~20-40 mins per craft), so preparing to take on a dungeon that day actually cuts into your time to take on the dungeon.The only positives I can think of regarding the time progression is that it actually forces me to plan ahead with my time a little, getting into that feel of being a self-sufficient adventurer who needs to split their time up appropriately to be best prepared for the challenges ahead and is slowly but surely 'solving' a dungeon. It's not really a game feel I'm used to in games like these, which let you run as fast as you want with time as your only constraint. Some quests don't advance time, but other do as part of the story which isn't telegraphed when you enter them.I've never played any of the ARPG FF games other than XIV, but I can clearly say the combat is similar to XIV. Attacks follow similar rules where you have to be out of range before they cast to not get hit, or at least that's how I felt when backing off from a living plant who was swinging only to get hit from like a meter away. You pretty much have to tank hits as they come and avoid getting hit by the ones that make the floor turn a different color to warn you not to step in there for a couple of seconds. The dash is dogwater since you can't cancel into it from attacks and I have a feeling there's no invulnerability on it. Can't say for sure cause they former part makes it really hard to test the latter part in a relevant combat setting.The job switching function is actually useful since enemies have different weaknesses, and some bosses have multiple weaknesses that you want to swap around to jobs they're weak to for easy double breaks. Jobs collect Job Points so long as they're equipped, so you can power level weaker ones using ones you've already fleshed out. I've collected all but two, and they all feel pretty unique from one another, at the cost of a few feeling too strong (Woglinde has HP regen + ATK buff skill, for example).The bosses are ... unique? I went from fighting a generic plant mini-boss to a FFXIV raid boss in one dungeon so ... yeah. Actually felt really nice to fight them since the camera appropriately panned out for specific attacks and positions so I could actually see things. There is a big issue though with some of the mini-bosses and regular bosses where they'll immediately basic attack as soon as you load in, hitting you before you can retaliate. Since HP doesn't restore between floors, this is really annoying since you're just getting hit for free because the game decided so.Also, your character levels up between days, which furthers my suspicion that you're supposed to have 'grind and prepare' days and 'explore the dungeon' days to find the most enjoyment out of this game.The story is ... really good. Surprisingly good. The side quests have a lot of character to them and the main story doesn't hold back either. They all tie into this theme of fighting for a better future even when there appears to be only handful of solutions that all aren't ideal. It's pretty generic for a JRPG, and I can create a 100+ row exel sheet with all the games and books that share the same theme, but this game explores it in a way that makes it feel more fleshed out. It's not just in the main storyline and interactions with the focus characters, but in the sidequests and relationship stories as well. The final decision in one of the chapters has a really good set of dialogue you can get if you try to literally walk away and the hit 'No' on the choice confirmation the game tries to force you to make, which ordinarily you'd assume would take you back to the choice menu. It caught me off guard and was an interesting twist on something I took for granted about game dialogue options. There are also some interesting details. After Chapter 8, Aria disappears from the title screen splash.I do want to point out there is some weird dialogue, specifically after 2 choice answers. It's like they tried to account for both in the same response and it comes off as stilted, but it's a little uncommon to see.
_childDocuments_.name: HARVESTELLA

_childDocuments_.review: Probably one of the rare few games that hybridize RPG and Farm Sim in a great manner that is highly efficient.The storyline is worthwhile, the gameplay is good, and the farm mechanics while not detailed, are still well designed. The combat can be occasionally challenging, especially in the latter part of the game if the player doesn't keep up with leveling up, getting good accessories, and upgrading weapons, but it is very rewarding, especially since a lot of the major parts of the story require fighting powerful foes. The game is probably one of the best attempts at copying the incredible success of Rune Factory games, and I think that this game proves that RPGs and Farm Sims were truly meant to be mixed together.
_childDocuments_.name: HARVESTELLA

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game. It's got wit, it's funny and can be sad. The story line is what I would expect from a game made by Square Enix. I love the battle system and leveling style. It takes all my favorite elements like fighting, farming, cooking and friendship and puts it neatly into one great package. The only con for me is the fact I have no interest whatsoever with the playing the "pronoun" game. I don't want pronouns shoved in my face in a game because I go to games to get away from the ridiculousness of the world. I don't want to see it in a game too. Otherwise, it's a great game and I would highly recommend it to fans of Square Enix and RPGer's alike!
_childDocuments_.name: HARVESTELLA

_childDocuments_.review: Harvestella is a game that is easy to love.  The level of familiarity from games previously played will leave you in a comfortable space.  It is Square/Enix's execution upon their own familiar territory, with making engaging stories with relatable and lovable characters.  Though there has been much to fear with the influx of games that the company has been putting out, it is extremely evident that this game is a labor of love and the developers have spent a great deal of time getting it right.  All the tedious prospects from similar games are shoved to the side for an extremely engaging and robust experience.  You grow crops, you meet neighbors, you go on quest for ingredients and materials and you do all this through a great setting.  The graphics are charming and remind me also of games previously released (Bravely series).  If you love farming simulators and also a little bit of story I absolutely recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: HARVESTELLA

_childDocuments_.review: Harvestella, jack of all trades, master of none.the game has everything you'd expect from a farming/life sim with action rpg elements.However, farming is a bit lackluster as is combat, however the story and graphics make up for that easily.i wouldn't say this is worth the £50/$60 they want for it but not picking it up when it's on offer for £25/$30 would  be enough of reason to buy it based on price for value.Many believe that you don't have an evade/dodge option by the way, this is not the case, each job you get has that unlocked in th skill tree for that job (yeah you read that right, there's a job and skill system!)Add in the fact there's multiple endings and 2 hidden classes/job plus other endgame content and at least 1 hidden dungeon only accesible during the 1 day in between the seasons and you have plenty to explore!Lack of voice acting really isn't an issue in the game - i'm not sure why people expect this in a life/farming sim with slight ARPG elements. You at least still get some voicing in combat and minor other places.Over all, Harvestella is a great 1st entry into something that could become an amazing series and i sincerely hope they use this is a learning experience and build upon it to deliver us an even better sequel.
_childDocuments_.name: HARVESTELLA

_childDocuments_.review: Don't come into this game thinking it's a farming sim. It's definitely an RPG with farming elements. However, that being said, I love this game. The landscape, character art, and music are all amazing. I feel the character models lack a little, but they're okay. The Lalafell feet get me. It's easy an 80+ hour game if you do all the side quests, build up your farm, do all the relationship quests... I'm at 60 hours and just now finished the MQ, and most of the side quests.
_childDocuments_.name: HARVESTELLA

_childDocuments_.review: Note: I've played more than 25 hours but mainly on steamdeck and it's messed up my total time.Havestella was my vote for game of the year and honestly wasn't what I would've originally expected. I went into it thinking "Oooo a Square Enix take on Harvest Moon? Sign me up." because I'm an absolute sucker for any farming sim games ever. _childDocuments_.review: For players who are new to JRPG's, you could consider this a mix of Stardew Valley and Final Fantasy 14. For those who are lovers of the genre, you may consider this a mix of Rune Factory, the Atelier series, and Final Fantasy 15, with hints of older FF titles.Pros: + The story, absolutely magical and it just keeps giving. It is all around sweet. I like to think of the main character as friend to all children.+ The game play loop feels satisfying.+ Well Thought out GameplayCons: (Nothing big)+ Could use subtitles for battle dialog (Most of it is just hyahs and such, but occasionally it will warn you when you are in areas that are too dangerous for you)+ I can tell it was a port from a switch game only because there is an annoying pixel width strip around the edge of the screen when it fades to black during dialog.Addressing other comments:There is not a lot of voice acting... And that's okay in my book. It gives a really nice old school JRPG vibe while delivering us all the advances in gaming we could expect. This is clearly a well thought out game that deserves better than other reviews are giving it. If you are new to JRPG's, it may take a bit to get used to, but the story as I have played so far is well worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: While this game looks cool, and it seems like it would be amazing given how its published by Square Enix.. but after playing for a bit.. i can say that its rough. very rough. _childDocuments_.review: tldr: I do not feel this is a good representation of what the designers were attempting and would regrettably suggest you look elsewhere for a new game or research further to make sure this is the type of game you want.  Read on if you want more details.     The combat is very shallow.  It's real time, but you can't really dodge or chain together attacks in any meaningful way.  You spend all your of time just absorbing damage and walking out of damage areas.  Bosses have the barest minimal of strategy, but it's easy enough to overpower with just minor healing.  There are multiple jobs, with 3 at a time being equipable.  These, like the other skills, do not chain together fluidly, all animations must complete before you can use a skill or change jobs.  The jobs do not have any unique resources  (like energy, mana, rage, etc) just the generic stamina that decreases from doing anything.  There is only one attack button, a run button that can be upgraded to a short dash with no invulnerability frames, and your use item key.  There are no blocks, no combos with your party members, no dodges, no interrupts, nothing at all increase complexity.  There are two item slots but these are the most basic attempts at an item system.  There are magic attack/defense, physical attack/defense, and then just specific element damage reduction.  The two spiciest things I found were one that granted a small buff to hp and one that granted better chance to resist poison (how much better it did not say).  There was nothing that helped certain skills or schools of skills or granted passive effects that might alter how you approached combat.  You could easily just ignore these entirely and suffer no real detriment.  I can't imagine this was what the developers wanted to do with their combat system.    The farming isn't connected well to the rest of the systems.  You just need food to heal and later on it's important because you're always running out of stamina.  There are seasons, and new areas on the farm unlock through the story and are purchased from a vendor in town.  Seeds have to purchased or found.  You do not get any seeds back from harvest or any way to generate some by using some of the harvest.  Food can give some beneficial effects but it's not really large or interesting.  There is no exp or other stat growth connected to the farm that I found in my time with the game.  I found the entire system to be under developed.    The story parts (quests, character stories) are very obvious and not well told.  This is one of those titles that has you make a character but then tells you how your character feels and offers you non-options for dialogue.  I didn't expect or need choice, but I'd prefer that options weren't offered in that case.  If your story is better told without input from the player, then just let the story play out and don't offer fake choices.  I'm not sure what audience this story was written towards.  Often very obvious setups are explained to the player like we're in kindergarten, but then there's overwrought tragedies and just fumbling attempts at comedy.  There is also a lot of dialogue and it can not be skipped.  To compound those issues, Harvestella is also one of these titles that animations must complete before dialogue can move forward.  It's likely why they didn't have a skip, but I'm surprised they didn't at least have a fast forward.  So when you've got the gist of the situation in the first 5 seconds (and you will) you will be forced to slowly wade through each and every dialogue box.  This needed a rewrite to both shorten it and punch it up.     There were no crashes and the performance was fine.  I would say that there are far, far too many load screens.  I can not imagine why they'd need so many load screens.  Not even the Switch, which has lower specs than competing platforms, should have required this many.  They load a building, not a large one, and if there is another room in the building, regardless of size, they need another load screen.  Not sure if they just didn't want to animate doors or there was perspective issues.  It was extremely tedious to explore due to this.    Lastly just a quick mention on the music.  It's very generic JRPG fantasy stuff.  It's not something I particularly like, but it's not poorly made.  The issue here is that there's not nearly enough.  Right when a "tragic" event is about to occur the music is volume is dropped and then in the next dialogue box the tragic music plays.  Same for the happy music or comedy music.  Note I said, the tragic music, because it's always the same track.  If you're doing quests you'll hear these dozens of times in very short order.  Worse, after the event is done, it'll reset to beginning of the track that's was supposed to be playing in the area.  So if the music for the event didn't change the area's music, it'll just reset the track beginning.  It's not a big deal, but it's irritating, particularly in the tavern with Emo's song since it's extremely obvious when the track resets.      I can only guess the designers did not get the time or funding to really explore the concept they were attempting because this feels like an early draft of the concept.    In conclusion, as the end user I can only rate what I purchased and regrettably I think you'd be better off looking in to a different game.  I hope the developers get another shot and are better able to execute their vision.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is absolutely great. It has all of the aspects of a jrpg rolled into a farming sim. I think most of the negative comments are about the price, but given the sheer amount of content available, its definitely worth it. If you are only playing for two hours you won't see it, but after playing for 13 hours straight and comparing achievements to progress, you can see that there is so much more to go. There are a plethora of side quests to keep it fresh, a large quantity of areas that I haven't even begun to explore, and I haven't even gotten out of the first SEASON yet. If you are a JRPG fan, if you are a farming sim fan and enjoy the daily/monthly time cycle, enjoy cultivating relationships, you will definitely enjoy this game. It is NOT Final Fantasy 7 remake level graphics, but it is a huge step above most other farming sims graphics. The great thing is that this runs well on a Steam Deck, which I think was their aim. Don't sleep on this one because of the mixed reviews from people being cheap and trying to get refunds.

_childDocuments_.review: Hey guys, I wanted to give yall my share and view of the game. (and no im am not through the main storyline but still at year 1)I play with K+M not with a controller and its not that bad (note I have a mmorpg mouse so I have numbers from 1-12 on the side of it so it depends if you have numbers on the side)•SE's approach to a farming sim is with Harvestella well done with little flaws.For me who is having experiences in playing titles like Harvest Moon, Story of Seasons, Stardew and oc. Final Fantasy titles such as ff7(old), ff14 etc. and some Jrpgs from the "Tales of... series" and yes I mentioned them because it feels like this game is kind of a mix of all of em. Strongy the Final Fantasy part is the biggest thing that comes into my mind regarding some things:•The battlesystem is a mix of FF's traditional 3 party member system that you have in most of the single player and FF14. (but its pretty normal on difficulty)BUT why ff14? well for starters evading normal attacks is more difficult than any soulslike game since there is hardly an evasive system in here more like a mmorpg (for me it felt heavily like ff14 as mentioned before) you fight do auto attacks some skills change classes do the same and evade whatever effect is on the ground (you can still evade normal attacks with some classes dash or just by being range its just damn difficult).• So the battle system would need lil improvements that it is for a better experience since I can imagine that this would be a throw off for some ppl.I like the Story so far in the game also strong FF/anime style like you have character progression with your party members and also with the npc's you are have sidequests with. It feels like theres a lot more depth to the World than it would without them (also they give good opportunities for backtracking stuff)•The Time a day passes by in the game is imo a lil too quick (like in other games its not perfect but it works you just have to be quicker) I wish I had sometimes more time for a day than there is (because sometimes it feels like I have to dedicate the entire time during the day for things like fishing since this also takes a lot of time or gathering mats lvling up classes etc.)•The World design is awesome you have your regionals like villages and farm and traveling the overworld is like the overworld in FF7 (old) as far as I like it i strongy wish sometimes it should be more Open world instead of the Tales of design likes (like jumping up and down from a ledge that saves some time instead of running a whole way back with the little time one has at a day).•The Farming in this game and its progression towards what you can do on your farm at the beginning of the game and a lil later on is made in some ways unique for example you have to progress the Main story to unlock certain abilities that helps  you spending less stamina and time on the farm (also unlocks some stuff you need later on and some stuff widen the farm that you can use).•There are no Tool upgrades for your dayli farm stumm like plowing watering hammersmashin stuff but instead you gain abilities that are optained by simply doing your stuff (you will find out when you play it dont rlly want to spoil anything).•So yeah in all I love the mix up in Harvestella that they put in. It is Playable on a rate of 8.5-9.0 simply because some stuff that I mentioned in the Text are some stuff that I personally liked to be improved/made better. Nontheless I will continue playing it and have my fun with cuz IT REALLY IS FUN! and I hope this imo review is of help for and that you maybe giving it a try It is definitly worth it. (but maybe not on a 60 bucks price worth)

_childDocuments_.review: I'm really not sure what to make of this game. There are some extremely odd things about it and some really satisfying things. I, personally, really enjoy the art style and the music, but can definitely see how that might not be received well by others. It very much feels like a Squenix game, so it was super familiar territory for me.Something that may be an annoyance to people that aren't super familiar with farming games is that this follows the same sort of progression reward/gaining levels that Stardew does. You don't get your level as you achieve it, but you get all your progress at night after going to sleep. This didn't bother me as I have played some games that I really love that use the same system. It's just something to consider. I like most of the mechanics though and the story, though weird, has captivated my interest enough that I want to keep playing.Pros:- Non-binary gender option- Combat is okay- Art & Music- The meal system -> as long as you have food in your belly, stamina recovers slowly- The way mechanics unlock and unfold the longer you playCons:- Lack of any real character customization- Clunky actions for the farming portion- Price- Each game day is way too short- Long tutorial, slow startMeh:- Long cutscenes- Very weird story. Not bad, just weird.There are definitely some things that could be improved, but overall I think the game is a decent buy. It will be a much better value if you wait for a sale, though.
_childDocuments_.name: HARVESTELLA

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. If you're into JRPGs and not so much into farming, this is the game for you. There's no pressure in progressing the story and doing side things like quests and companion progression since nothing is time-locked. You don't have really to do much to increase relationship with characters since you just need to visit and watch their stories. This is a good point for me because in other farm games, you had to gift people stuff every single day which is kind of a chore. The farming is like your typical farming game stuff though. Plant stuff in correct season, water everyday, harvest then sell. As you keep working on your farm, you do get stuff that makes everything easier so it's rewarding to farm. You also get to process stuff for money which is always fun for any game. LOLThe combat isn't that complex but in comparison to other farming games such as Rune Factory or Stardew Valley, this one's flashier and also gives you something to work on because of skill trees. The allocation of farming/combat playtime feels a bit closer to playing to Sakuna: Of Rice and Ruin which I also recommend if you enjoy this one.

Also, couldn't have even bothered to subtitle the few voiced lines? Also the main story was predictable. The only interesting storyline belonged to one of the companions in my opinion . Was not worth anywhere near 60 bucks. Sucks for me for being too much a Square fangirl I guess.

_childDocuments_.review: If Final Fantasy (heavy influenced by 14) were a Rune Factory/Stardew Valley game. I absolutely love this game. It reminds me honestly a lot of XIV (it's clear some models and animations were taken from it (the children you first see are LALAS AHHHH) and the clothing design heavily reminds me of it) and I think that's what adds to the charm on top of a decent story and of course farming, crafting and fishing till your hearts content. My only gripe is you have to sleep at midnight, but you get used to it quickly. Dungeons you have to take slowly and I honestly like it. It's linear as most games of this type are, but the job system you can swap between in battle adds a unique twist thats very FF in nature as you start off as the fighter and unlock from there. It seems more balanced between spending time farming/fishing and exploring the dungeons/areas. I appreciate the balance quite a bit. Character Customization as many people have noted, isn't there, but it also doesnt bother me. Reminds me of the Pokemon games, simple grab and go. It doesn't really effect the game itself. The Non-Binary option is a wonderful addition that makes this NB Chimera so happy. It's such a small but notable change. The game itself runs smoothly and I have no technical issues yet. Graphics are gorgeous for simple design choices. So far its a solid 9/10.

_childDocuments_.review: I really like this game's story and battle mechanics. The story is interesting and has well written characters; it also is very geared towards helping kids and others out. The battle mechanics are fun but staying caught up with the levels and gear usually is a grind for me(I don't remember if I chose a difficulty at this point but if I did it'd be easy). There are also farming mechanics, which can help you pay for things or make food to help in your journey. It can be a grind at first but later in the game it gets easier(I won't say how because spoilers). The animals that you can take care of are adorable(to me), and you can pet them too.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is surprisingly addicting! It starts off feeling like a Rune Factory Lite without relationship mechanics but it really opens up the more you play it and the more you unlock. _childDocuments_.review: More JRPG than farming sim. In fact, at times the farm felt like a money sink because turning crops into meals isn't profitable and you need to keep your ingredients around to craft food for combat, so you spend all your money on seeds and only occasionally feel secure enough to sell those crops for money without hampering your cooking potential.Judging it mostly as an RPG with a time limit each day, I had fun with the game and the story while it was around, the dungeons are paced well against the time limit of each day, the bosses are pretty cool, and so on. So if you're looking for a decent JRPG with ways to take breaks when you feel like it, it's a pretty good game for that. Though I got pretty bored of the farming by the time I was finished with the story (which was before the first year ended for me), so come for the rpg more than the farming.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't really write reviews, but like a lot of people, I think this game gets unfair reviews, especially from people who have played it for 3 hours or less. This is by far no time to be able to assess anything about this game, because a lot of things are only unlocked bit by bit, as with many life simulations. So why do they say the game isn't worth the money?It is a pity that there is no real synchro. But that alone is no justification for rejecting a game entirely. The soundtrack and story is good, not world class but definitely not bad either. The graphics are nice to look at and the characters have deep and interesting stories. It's a mixture of a JRPG, Rune Factory, Stardew Valley, Bravely Default and feels like a little Octopath Traveler.At the moment I'm still having a lot of fun. And I just hope that people won't be put off by the reviews and will give the game a chance. I'm sure you won't regret it.
_childDocuments_.name: HARVESTELLA

_childDocuments_.review: I will preface this by saying that if you have this game on PC, PLAY WITH A CONTROLLER!I'm usually married to keyboard and mouse, but made an exception for this one because I wasn't having fun with combat. An XBOX controller made everything so much better.As a big fan of Rune Factory games, Harvestella was exactly the kind of game I've been itching to play.It's beautiful, and offers similar playstyle to Rune Factory games.I loved that you don't have to be on top of talking to every single NPC every single day and that your relationships to your allies progress naturally with time. Just make sure you check your mailbox. In Rune Factory it can get overwhelming having to find, talk to, and gift all the romanceable NPCs every day. Here it's much simpler and to me it's a good thing. Although sometimes the days go by very quickly, especially once your farm is much larger and higher maintenance, there are ways to mitigate and plan for getting things done. I found myself enjoying management elements to this game that were probably not intended, but I enjoy figuring out ways to get things done efficiently [in games, NOT irl xD]I liked that the dungeon maps had good layouts for multiple visits, where you are rewarded for reaching a certain point and making a shortcut back [always have repair kits on hand!]. Not being able to clear out a dungeon fully in one go might not be to some people's tastes, but for me it helped me enjoy each map for an extended period of time before moving on, which is nice and makes them more memorable.The story was definitely interesting. I don't think it's skippable, but I haven't tried. I enjoy story-based games with cut-scenes. The game overall was a healthy mix between fantasy/nature and tech/mech stuff. Usually I don't enjoy the latter, but here it worked for me. The job class system was extremely enjoyable and no matter what your preferred combat style, there's definitely one or more classes you'll enjoy. I liked Woglinde, Avenger, and Mage a lot, but definitely mixed it up here and there with some of the melee ones as well. I liked figuring out which teammates to mix and match for their party bonuses depending on what I was going for in each dungeon.There's plenty here for completionist lovers. From cooking/crafting, to Fairy orders, to filling your encyclopedia and fishing up all the species you can find. There's not much to do after endgame besides achievement hunting, but I can see myself replaying it for fun or just piling up money and supplies if I feel like just farming in a pretty game.I'm pretty happy with Square Enix's take on a farming RPG. I hope they make more. Rune Factory games take too long between releases. Would be nice to have more good ones more often.Something I would have liked Harvestella to have is maybe furniture and allowing you to decorate your loft yourself. I was initially excited at the prospect until I realized it's just for trophies. This alone would make for a lot more gameplay and helping to have more things to do once you finish the story. But I think I got a decent amount of hours out of it regardless, so it's less a complaint and more a suggestion that would have made it even better.ALSO, Woolums and Cluffowls are cute, BUT WHY CAN'T I HAVE A CHOCOBO FARM??Jokes aside, the Totokaku is such a cute mount, would have loved to be able to use him on the farm/dungeons and not just in the overworld. Running around collecting things or fighting monsters on him would have been lots of fun xDThanks for letting us pet him!!
_childDocuments_.name: HARVESTELLA

_childDocuments_.review: I've already played over 50 hours of Harvestella and have loved it, but there are some things I found disappointing.  I wanted to get closer to completing the game before leaving a review but I like taking my time to enjoy the game and purposely play it slow. I'll update once I finish instead. At this point I'm about halfway I'd guess.First and foremost, the price. I hesitated to play for so long after seeing so many negative reviews beside the price tag. After playing, I'm shocked so many people hated it. It's definitely a mesh between action RPG/farming. I'm not surprised it didn't do either perfectly, but I thought it was still well done. The keys chosen for fighting actions feel extremely awkward so I struggle in battle. Fighting itself just feels very off until you've done it for awhile, but coming back to it after an absence is rougher. I would say to wait for a sale, the game is amazing but there were certain things I thought would happen/would be available that were not and it disappointed me. Why is it worth it? The game itself is gorgeous, you can see the edges of some environment models, but overall the world is beautiful to just look at it. Your home is cozy, magical, and the story premise starts off simple and builds up. Is the story dramatic? Well, yes, and I enjoyed that. While fighting can be awkward to begin with, the farming feels much smoother. The world is interesting, although the NPCs definitely give recycled NPC energy after the first town. The fighting areas in game are interesting and so are the enemies. Despite having seasons and a plot line, the game allows you to move at your pace. If you want to rush and do everything in a year or two you could. Or, you could take 3 years to finish Chapter 3 - although you may miss out on some developments that allow you access to certain seeds/tools until you complete it. I thought the characters and their story lines were interesting, I don't know much about the MC at this point except...well, you know, 'amnesia'. There are plenty of job upgrades (you can switch among them at save points so your battle style can change), farm upgrades, items to find, recipes to find, and farm developments to keep you busy. The companions are interesting and my initial meeting with a certain character who is your first mini boss was hilarious in my opinion. Also, I hate fishing mini-games usually so I enjoyed the minimal effort this game requires to fish. I truly looked forward to playing this game.Where was I disappointed? Honestly, overall the ability to personalize anything is low. To begin with your character model has two options, and I can see how some people were upset that the options were so limited. You do not have any option for a super muscular hero, and with the exception of only a handful of characters in-game I just kinda went forward imagining that was how this world worked - everyone had big hips and narrow shoulders. However, I could see how someone who wanted either an MC or a single love interest option that was more muscular could be disappointed. You can change your race, hair or eye color, but I felt some of the hair colors didn't highlight as well as the generic blonde. Outside of that - the house can be upgraded, but from what I can tell nothing actually changes physically. So, it's beautiful, but it always looks that way. The farm, the animal areas, and most areas do not change except for a handful of  developments that open more areas. So, if decorating your house or watching it grow is important - that's not gonna happen. Most disappointing was an attic area - I thought it would be the space you could 'personalize' but instead it's like a vague award spot that's never explained. There are seasons, Quietus is interesting, and your farm shows off each season but some places don't really change with the seasons and it's slightly off-putting but understandable as certain towns are associated with seasons...so I'm not sure how best it could have been handled. There are no festivals/holidays, although it could be explained with the serious plot. Last, some farming sims/RPGs include extensive love interest plot lines - from what I've heard this does not. The characters are well-developed and your companions do have personal quests, but don't expect a romantic plot line to follow the main plot - this is more of an epilogue development.Overall, loved the game. The music is amazing, graphics are amazing, and I found the game engaging. However, the ability to personalize nearly everything is limited/non-existent, battle controls make me feel like a flailing octopus, and the farming sim element is more to support your team in battles instead of developing your homestead.
_childDocuments_.name: HARVESTELLA

_childDocuments_.review: Ultimately the game isn't terrible, it does have its charm and can hold your attention well. Some of the arcs with the NPCs you can interact with are well written. There are a lot of side quests though that are built around people just not communicating with each other and getting you involved to fix everything, such as a group of kids where one is about to move and is being distant. Their friends notice and think they did something wrong and try to fix it (with your help) and only make it worse until after more stages the truth comes out and everything is good as new.The art and environment of the game looks good and I find it pleasing to explore, however you often have to run through the areas many times for supplies so it gets a bit old. The farming element isn't bad, I wish the crops that repeatedly bear produce wouldn't die before the end of the season, it appears they will die 15-20days after being planted unless it's a fruit tree or vine.The economy of the game is fairly slow to start, the majority of your crops will only sell a little more then the price of the seed and even if you produce something from it, the value doesn't increase by much more especially if it's not a unique item. My biggest issue with the game is the combat, it's definitely a bigger part of the game, equal to if not more relevant to the farming aspect. With it being Square Enix, you'd think this side of the game would be well done. However there are no real defensive maneuvers to avoid attacks and even if you try to sprint around between enemy attacks, most enemies have unavoidable attacks regardless of range. Additionally if you try to focus on being range and let your companions front line, the enemies will try to reach you but if they get caught on your frontline for too long they will reset and the aggro tethering is a very short distance as well. Ultimately in my opinion this game is enjoyable but I wouldn't say it's worth the $60 price, maybe for half off then it's worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: HARVESTELLA

_childDocuments_.review: I played the demo and was not a fan, so I kind of forgot about the game again. A few days after release I was seeing more and more positive experiences from people with the game, so I decided to give it a try.What can I say, it is somehow exactly what I need right now. The game feels very chill to play, I love the farming (especially  the watering!) and I love that it is not super in depth like RF with soil stats and all that. The game opens up much more right after the demo ends, in chapter 3. The story is fun so far, side quests are entertaining and emotional, the characters have personality and I just enjoy how much stuff you can unlock in this game, makes it fun to work towards things, even if it's just an upgrade for a current machine you have.It is hard to know if you will like the game without playing it, and the demo is not a good representation, since many annoying things have been fixed in the full release, but I am glad I decided to try it.
_childDocuments_.name: HARVESTELLA

Why? Because we were playing the game all the time.
