_childDocuments_.name: HARVESTELLA

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, lets start out with this, the game isn't bad. It's not great either.The graphics are decent enough, the story line seems decent enough, but then we get to the save functions and controls, those are absolute crap and a real pain to try and change around, especially with a controller. If you can't easily save your game with out having to look around for several minutes, or you can't easily re assign controller mapping then it's a no go in my book, especially with the price tag. To be honest I just think this game is a port to be a money grab, and with minimal effort put into porting it over. If you're going to get it then I would say wait for a sale, it's not currently worth the price tag put on it with the basic functions being such a pain in the back side.
_childDocuments_.name: HARVESTELLA

_childDocuments_.review: Graphics 11/10 - Pretty unique, similar to Bravely Default.Story 6.5/10 - It's fine but I wouldn't recommend it for the story.Questing 5/10 - 60% of the quest have cookie-cutter stories, 40% are fun, unique and emotional to some extend.Gameplay 4/10 - For combat, you only smash Attack until the enemy is dead, you can't dodge attacks or stagger the enemy, and there's a lot of animation locks. Becomes barable on the mid-game around Lv25 - 30. You have to take lots of heals.Price - I'd only recommend buying it on sale.Time to complete - Around 40 to 60hrs if you read the dialogue. Side quests included.You can marry any side character after you beat the game. (You must wait a few days after beating the game).My thoughts: Honestly, I would pay 45€ at most for a game where you simply mash buttons till the enemy is dead. The class change is a neat but with the lack of fluidity it feels so lackluster. Most of the "issues" the game have are features most farming games with combat have- however, a more polished combat would've really hit everyone's expectations on the bright side. In this day and age, it's combat system makes a parallel between what people would want on JRPG vs what people experienced back in the day of Harvest Moon and Rune Factory, making it's gameplay have very mixed reviews and thoughts.
_childDocuments_.name: HARVESTELLA

_childDocuments_.review: OK I needed to update this review after finishing this.If this came out during 2007-2011 era of gaming it would have been an A+ Gem. or if it was an indie title for $30.Story is wild but characters are solid. "Romancing" in this is an option but it feels kind of tacked on. "Tacked on" describes this game pretty well actually.If you are looking for a farming/life sim like Rune factory or Stardew, don't look here.This an old school RPG that uses farming as part of the grind rather than getting money and Gear from combat. The farming itself is enjoyable but not for everyone.The game is a 6/10 with an awesome idea but poorly executed. It just falls short of so much..barely animated cut scenes, hardly any voice acting, basic combat, basic economy. But i had fun and played the crap out of it so I will rate is positively, just wish it was... more.
_childDocuments_.name: HARVESTELLA

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic blend of AJRPG and farming sim - if you like both of those genres, you're gonna love this. I really wish there was full VA, but the farming content is quite diverse and gets deeper and more complex the further you go. The action combat can be difficult if you don't prepare, but a smart player will set aside part of their farm to grow things not for money, but to use as healing and buff items for fights. In this way, it does something with the farming sim genre no other game has - make you actually think about what you are growing in terms of it's usefulness, instead of how much it's worth. 8.5/10 Great music, story seems good so far, farming has depth and nuance, and the world is beautiful.
_childDocuments_.name: HARVESTELLA

_childDocuments_.review: Medium overall score at best, no way to skip convo.A shadow of rune factory or Harvest moon at best.The story concept is pretty good but is about the only saving grace this games got.Job system is okay: if you have played Final Fantasy Tactics, Final Fantasy 5 or heck even Final Fantasy X-2 with its dress sphere you know what it does, you can change between 3 classes in fight and use the skills of the class to fight. Your companions are stuck in one class. Aria is Martial Artist, Ayle is a Spearman, Durthina is a Caster and so on, while you can switch around. However the actual combat mechanic is clunky, and honestly boring, I think I would have had 10 times more fun if it was turned based and flashy fighting than this crayon drawn action combat... and we know they can do better, FF7R 1 and 2 is infintivly better and smoother and their Tactical RPGs and Classic Turn Based RPGS of the past have always been solid if not great.My take is that they tried to make a farming sim with relationship and friendships with villiagers from the local town and even other towns but didn't commit enough to it. The Farm is how you grow resources for food and gain money, thats it. but it is placed so far on the back burner that all you do is water crops go out kick monster behind and rince and repeat with a bad fighting mechanic and bad farming mechanic and a abyssmal slow releationship growth.If they had made the farming, upgrading the farm and so on more enganging this would get a thumbs up.If they had made the combat better and more fun, be it a cleaner and smoother Action RPG or a classic Turn based one then this would get a thumbs up.If they had made exploring more important than it is, then heck it would most likly enough to squeese into a thumbs up.Because the story is actually good, or at least I like it a lot. But it simply isnt enough, and as saving is a chore in this game and loading can make you have to listen to the same convo yet again, then urk... yeah.A good exsample of Square Enix taking multiple concepts, and instead of making it properly in each aspect they make it halfbaked in each and hope it is good enough.If you are really in need of a RPG with farming fix you can do worse, but honestly you can do much better as well.
_childDocuments_.name: HARVESTELLA

_childDocuments_.review: Square-Enix's first modern foray into the Farming/Life genre, Harvestella provides a chill, charming and enjoyable experience for any fan of Harvest Moon, Rune Factory, or Stardew Valley.  That said, this is a JRPG take on the farming sim genre, so keep that in mind.  You start with a small farm plot that has to be upgraded/unlocked.   Your affection level with other characters is not progressed through daily interactions and gifts, but rather by completing their sidequest-storylines, and only significant plot characters have these affection level ranks.  And the sidequests.  Oh boy thar be sidequests.The Good:Visually, the environments are absolutely stunning.   These combined with music that has no right to be this good just amplifies the chill.The combat is fun, and provides a good bit of challenge.  I often find myself having to pull back in combat and find a second to eat a snack and regain health.The Bad:The character animations have a tendency to be somewhat rigid and stiff, especially while performing farming actions.  Voice acting is sparse, and many characters look somewhat similar.The Ugly:There has been some small amount of controversy about Harvestella since the demo dropped, due to it's character creation.   Harvestella allows you to pick Male, Female, or Non-binary.   A male character can pick a female body type.   If this bothers you, this isn't your game.  Despite what has been said, nothing is being forced on you.
_childDocuments_.name: HARVESTELLA

_childDocuments_.review: Okay so this game isn't RF, don't expect it to be. Instead its a heavily story bound game with lots of (unskipable)  dialogue. The farming aspect is a bit lackluster but its there and is enjoyable. The combat in the game doesn't feel difficult at all, as long as you have food to heal you and for stamina purposes. As expected from a Square Enix game it looks great and sounds great. Overall i'd say the game is worth a play if you enjoy RPGs. People who complain about the price should just wait to buy the game on discount otherwise I think its fine to charge 60 for it. I sincerely hope that this game continues to get some QOL updates because as it is now there is not enough options for the PC settings in this game, such as allowing 144 FPS or even just allowing us to tweak graphic performance.
_childDocuments_.name: HARVESTELLA

_childDocuments_.review: Square marketed this as a farming sim. It's not. It's a cinematic heavy JRPG with some farming elements. The control scheme for m&k is one of the least intuitive schemes I've ever seen. The main thing this game has going for it is that it's really pretty, but so are basically all of the other FF games at this point. If you want to play FF with farming, get into FFXIV online. There's a farm in there somewhere, and you'll spend just about as much time on it as you would on the one in this game.
_childDocuments_.name: HARVESTELLA

_childDocuments_.review: So this review is coming from an older gamer who grew up on older FF, Harvest Moon and Rune Factory games. This game has a big big feel of Crystal Chronicles with farming. An old-school RPG feel with farm sim stuff attached. So far I am enjoying it. And from what I've experienced, it DOES put the RPG aspect BEFORE the farming sim. But that's completely fine with me because I have been enjoying the story and combat. It doesn't have voice acting, but I am used to that, as well as limited character customization. The music is BY FAR the best part.I would recommend this game only to people who grew up on Rune Factory and similar games. If you don't like old school RPGs or farm sims, this game isn't for you. Hopefully there will be a few QoL updates soon, as that's my only gripe with it. (Time moves too fast, need a better shipping value interface, etc) Will probably update this more as I move through the game.EDIT 18 HOURS IN: Still recommend the game, and I'm loving the story/world building even more. When I mentioned before about Crystal Chronicles, I meant that in the sense of the world building. The races, the magics, the old-school jrpg feel, the story. THAT is what's really drawing me in. The game isn't anything like Harvest Moon or Rune Factory because the game is its OWN thing. Do not come into the game expecting a clone of either of those.There's a few drawbacks I would like to point out. Some of the interfaces should be looked over. Like I should be able to see the value of the product I have already sold. Or there should be a book I can check to see what the values of the items are. And if it's already in the game I have not found it yet. I have been using spreadsheets made by other people to see what's worth selling, which shouldn't be the case.I really really love the feel and style of the classes but I genuinely wish there was a DEDICATED dodge button. I don't mind that it uses stamina, I just wanna be able to properly dodge, not a dash.Some of the animations are stiff but that genuinely doesn't bother me, I've seen worse. Just pointing it out.I do feel like some of the side quests drag out. The stories are cute, but near the end of the quests I'm feeling like it's more of a chore than anything. I want to feel invested, not just doing a quest for some rewards. That being said, some of the quests catch me off guard about how sad they are. Good writing, mediocre execution.Honestly my biggest complaint is time. I know they said they "fixed" the time management between the demo and release but days still feel too short. I would love an extra 2-3 hours in a day period, especially giving how fishing works. I would love to be able to enjoy this beautiful world at a leisurely pace.Have not finished the main story but still enjoying the world building. I'm a sucker for some of the themes in the game and hope to see more. The Conellus are so cute!My genuine feel is that the negative reviews don't give this game a chance. It is NOT a "Final Fantasy Harvest Moon/Rune Factory" game. It's something it's own! And my advice is to simply try it out and see if you'll also enjoy it!
_childDocuments_.name: HARVESTELLA

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoy the Rune Factory series this game is basically that. Its your typical farming simulator with rpg mechanics and final fantasy-esque plot. What I like about this one though is that the farming part of the game isn't all-encompassing. If you prefer your life sim games with alittle more rpg action and leaning into story progression more then I'd say its pretty solid.
_childDocuments_.name: HARVESTELLA

_childDocuments_.review: A Honest opinion.Like other's when spending 80 on a game you check out videos, peoples comments everything. Being physically disabled gaming takes mind off pain and lets face it we all have a reason why we play video games.But for me and 2 kids in university for 80.00 I want to know it is worth it. Every game that has farming etc everyone always says look another stardew valley copy etc.  Yes it may feel like stardew with some aspects but its not. I really love the achievement aspect . You have to do or catch so many things to work towards unlocking something special. One of the great things about this game is you don't have to carry items to cook or craft. Just put items in your chests and when at crafting machines in the house it takes from your storage. I cant tell you how many games i have spent rushing back and forth from chest to chest. First off the graphics are great , not mind blown but they are great,The story line flows and having extra quests on top of it also is a huge bonus. You are not limited to doing one thing. Want to fish fish want to cook cook. Fishing lets face it every-game that has fishing people hate the fact trying to match up certain things to be able to even get the fish. I love the mechanics that its easy to fish if you watch the bobber and one click. No match up between the lines. Yes I found 80.00 high but time flew this weekend  I enjoyed  it a lot and comparing other games that were 80.00this actually was better then some of them,  just a suggestion. What I find is worth 80 others may not and vice versa.Now for the bad part the things I feel need to change.1. Time goes by to fast 3 seconds is 10 min in game so the option to make the game play slower would benefit both those who take their time and those who wish to move fast. I feel rushed at times esp farming and cooking.2. You do quests for the doctor but yet each time you get treated the price goes up higher and higher .I understand the doctors quests give coin but that coin is basically just paying for your death.So def please lower this as right now if i am over the time or die it costs me 1k to be healed. 3. Have some human dialogue. I was shocked a company like this hardly had any at all in this game. May not seem relevant but it makes the game flow and feel more exciting. 4. Please change the character creation. The character creation looks like other games that only cost 20.00 or lower. People take pride in making their characters and every little detail people spend hours and hours to choose 1. This game has huge potential and I really cant wait for it to hit console.
_childDocuments_.name: HARVESTELLA

_childDocuments_.review: At 3 hours in I cannot recommend this game.  It feels like Square Enix was working on a JRPG and then someone from marketing made them throw in farming and other life sim mechanics as an after thought. The result feels unfinished.  The environment is very pretty most of the time, and it's so strange to see barely 2D characters with so little skin texture against a beautifully rendered tree. It's like parts of the team didn't finish in time, or didn't care as much as whoever did the environment and music. Some of the dialogue is also really cringe,  Considering the price point and that this is coming from a big studio, I just don't understand how they're calling this a finished product. The music is gorgeous, and that's the only thing keeping me playing at this point.  I'm only 3 hours in and I just feel irritated, hopefully as the story progresses it will get better.  Selecting the non-binary option just makes you choose between the two gendered body types....that isn't a non-binary option. I also take issue with the fact that every female character is wearing heels.  Have you ever seen a doctor wear heels? Or a fighter? No, because that doesn't make any sense for what those occupations require. Yikes.  Just...yikes.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't normally write reviews, but I feel with this one it's important to have a more balanced score than is currently showing. I haven't had any issues that diminish my enjoyment of this game. I'm completely hooked and absolutely love it.I wish there were more graphics options, better ultrawide support, and sure, more character customization. Based on the keybindings and menu layout/options it's pretty clear it was designed for Switch, but it doesn't matter. It's gorgeously stylized and runs beautifully on PC. I play with a controller and haven't had any problems.I'm 36 hours into it as I'm writing it and I can't put it down. The core gameplay loop is very satisfying and I've yet to feel like I'm hitting any barriers or stagnant points in the progression. In fact, quite the opposite, the game continues to open up and surprise me with depth I wasn't expecting. I would've been happy if the game had continued with the level of content it had established already so every time there was a new crafting recipe or farm tier unlocked it was a pleasant surprise that left me feeling spoiled with things to explore.It doesn't shatter any ground set by Final Fantasy for the JRPG or Stardew/Rune Factory for the Life Sim or Farming+RPG genres, but it does it very very well. I'm enjoying this far more than I enjoyed Rune Factory 5, and even slightly more than Rune Factory 4 Special due to the more engaging story/characters/combat.For anyone concerned that it's more JRPG than Farming Sim there's no pressure to progress the main story. At no point aside from the opening and maybe a day or two mid-game have I been forced to dive into the main story if I wanted to just take time and farm through the seasons and upgrade my farm. Progressing the main story does help you grow your farm, but it's also very natural to do a bit of both without feeling like you're sacrificing one or the other.The day length is very forgiving. Often I'll have a few hours extra which is the best time to craft and cook for the next day, so I agree with their choice to have those actions cost time. Quests generally don't progress the clock.Please please if you're on the fence give it a try. I know it isn't for everyone, but it definitely deserves more praise than it's currently getting and I'd hate to see people miss out on a surprisingly rich game.
_childDocuments_.name: HARVESTELLA

_childDocuments_.review: 17 hours into the game, Main story 3A done, about to do 3B, in summer month for reference.So I'm obviously not done yet but I have been having a really good time playing so I wanted to give my feedback 17 hours into the game. This could change as I progress to better or worse, who knows.Summary first = I love the game so far. Not the best game out there, but its really enjoyable. Anyone that enjoys (enjoyed) rune factory, harvest moon, and square RPGs would probably enjoy this title. You get a little of all of it here. In terms of farming, its not as good as stardew valley, but as a package I love it. The 60 dollar price tag can be an issue for some, and so for them I would say wait for a sale, and then pick it up. But for me it was worth it.Music = 9/10 Really great music, I plan on buying the OST if I can. I'm hearing elements of Nier and other Square games which I love, and so far every song has been good if not great. Not much else to say hereArt style = 9/10 Beautiful. The graphics might not be the best, but for me style and environment is king. I would rather have a good looking 16 bit game than a crappy looking top tier graphics style. That said, the art style is amazing. The glowing crystal effects, the characters, the trees, water, everything looks good and cohesive. Artistically beautiful to me who was disappointing in Rune Factory 5s generic style. Playing on steam deck and it looks great, same as when I played it on my PC. I imagine the switch version is not as great.Character Customization = 4/10. This in my opinion is one of the weakest parts of the game. You can choose gender identity from male, female, or non-binary, and then character model (not tied to previous selection) with some skin and eye colors. The Issue I have is lack of further customization, like hair style, maybe some accessories, some more body edits like height or weight or whatever. Maybe we unlock something later on, but the lack of options is sort of disappointing in a game like this. That said, I love the artstyle and how most characters in the game look.Farming Gameplay = 8/10 So far I like the farming. It appears to be a good time balance between farming and combat (at least how I am playing) and tasks like watering is actually pleasant. I'm not dying for a watering can upgrade because its kind of fun to just hold down the button and strafe through the crops. There are upgrades (like farm quality, farm size, harvesting more than 1 plant at a time, hammer, tilling etc.) so it feels like you are progressing your farm as you play. One of my concerns is using farm plots for processing items like feed makers and such, but I see at least another large plot I don't have access to yet, so space might not be a long term concern. Animals are fairly simple, I would have liked a way to interact with them beyond petting (at least the chicken type monster) so they could be a bit more enhanced. But overall farming is fun and never feels like I have to choose between farming and fighting due to the many easy ways to get stamina foodCrafting x/10 = Not really sure how to score this but its a simple crafting system that makes sense. You get areas to cook or craft, you buy recipes or earn them from quests and other tasks, and you gather ingredients from foraging, farming, fishing, and fighting. My only regret is not saving 3-4 plants from spring to help me cook some food in summer, as you can turn in food for gil/rewards at the inns later. There is always a couple simple recipes you can make from things you find in the farm/easy areas to gaurantee you can craft at least the basic food, and you can easily craft an item to teleport you home, which is great for time management/exploring without fear of staying out too late.Fighting 8/10 = It gets better as you progress. My major complaint is I like games that reward you for timely dodges, iframes, things like that. You CAN time attacks and avoid attacks, but sometimes its just easier to take the hit and heal inbetween if necessary. There is a neat job system (always love job systems in square games) where you can swap between 3 jobs in combat, and they give different damage types/status/attack styles. Party members, while automated, are nice and make combat a bit more involved, since it appears each party member has a job you can choose from, so you can choose specific damage types to help out in certain areas. Also avoiding stronger monsters and coming back for them later is extremely satisfyingFishing 5/10 = Don't look for anything insane gameplay wise here. I'm not sure about if time/weather/season affects fishing, but so far its fairly simple. Press B when lure is underwater and you get the fish. It's a good activity to do if you have time left in the day for either money or ingredients. This isn't a hard rule, but ingredient fish mostly seem to hang out in the ocean, and money fish tend to hang out in ponds/rivers. Story/dialogue 7/10 = There is a lot of story, a lot of dialogue. The characters can be really charming and there are fun interactions, but sometimes I wanna get back to farming/fighting as soon as possible. That said, this is a story game, so you gotta know that going in. You can ignore it if you wish and speed past dialogue since there are quest markers, but I don't recommend that since it's a large part of the game. Main complaint is I wish there was voice acting.
_childDocuments_.name: HARVESTELLA

_childDocuments_.review: - Performance and stability; this game would run on a hot potato. I never had any frame-dips, no long load-times and no bugs.  From start to finish it was all around smooth.- Playstyles; Instead of being stuck with a single class you instead equip 3 classes (from a selection of 12) and switch between them mid-combat at will. Casters, melee fighters, ranged weaponry. or a combination of them. That coupled with a decent skill tree per class does add some fun to it.- Story; okay so at the start most players will think "Generic story". While that's true the story does evolve with some decent twists. While a few twists will be made somewhat obvious it's still legit fun to unfold.- Farming; Make no mistake. This is an RPG with light farming and not a farming sim with RPG elements. The farming isn't nearly as in-depth as what you'd find in something like Stardew Valley but it's decent enough that it doesn't feel like a neglected mechanic.- Presentation; Okay so the graphics aren't what you'd expect from Square Enix. There's a lack of detail in character models and a bit of a generic feel in terms of the anime-esque aesthetic. But the scenery, attack animations and enemies all look fairly distinct and well-done.- Sadness; For real. Every character in the game has a sad backstory. Friends, enemies, quest givers. The problem is that they force it so hard that when something genuinely sad happens it does feel like it's lacking impact because all this game knows is sadness.- Plot-holes; While I did enjoy the story there's definitely some glaring pot-holes. I'm not gonna spoil them for obvious reasons but it doesn't feel like the story was picked over with a fine comb- Scale; the story itself effects an entire planet so you'd think there'd be a vast amount of areas you can explore. It's actually really small in scale (there's only a handful of towns you can visit). While I do think smaller scare works in some games I do not feel like it works here.- Character creation; okay this is just flat-out bad. Basically just a handful of presets. The problem is that even if you choose to play as a male you'll always look feminine. Since there's no way to change your outfit you're stuck with this negatively distinct look.- Combat; Reminiscent of the old PSO games with it being slow and telegraphed. The problem is there's no real dodge, animation cancel or block so you're gonna face-tank often. Combat could be better but it could be so much worse.The good outweighs the bad here imo.

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished 100% this game with some guides for the harder collectibles. Honestly I had a blast the whole way through. It may not have the deepest farming or combat, but I found the game challenging and engaging the whole way through. Main Story- Has what you'd expect from a Square Enix published JRPG with a few novel twists here and thereSide quests- If you don't enjoy trekking from one map to another in support of a story they might not be for you, but the in game rewards are sure worth it. Each side quest is novel and enjoyable, some play out as you'd expect but others have a bittersweet twist, all had a story I genuinely enjoyedCharacters- There's no courting like you'll find in Stardew, SoS, or RF but the personal character events you unlock help you get to know the characters just as well if not better. There's also great skits (like Tales of games) you can view when eating a meal at a save point which greatly helped in fleshing out the personalities and stories of the characters that can join your party (I recommend trying to find Brakka's hard tack skit saga)Visual Design- The color balance and design of each area was unique, pleasant, and thematically appropriate. The core cast has a good variety that expresses their personalities well. Combat- There's no dodge cancelling or blocking, so the challenge is placing your character in the right spot to kite enemies while balancing skill cool-downs. Sufficiently fluid and enjoyable, cross skill passives make kitting out your character fun to plan around. Farming- Farming is pretty simple, no star values or fertilizer or seed making, the items your ship are either HQ or normal, two types of animals and limited farm upgrades. the actual task is making the most out of your farm land and the minimal profits you make while farming to craft items for adventuring and keeping your farm afloat. It's likely you'll reach endgame before you have too much leeway in cash. I liked this aspect but it may not be for everyone. Music- Sidequests pull from a small list that can get repetitive, although, each dungeon and boss has their own theme. I did like every track in the game, some even have a NeiR: Automata feel to them that heightened the tone of a world on the precipice of death. Overall 8.5/10 would recommend, the game sets a great foundation for a new IP I could absolutely see SE cultivate with some time and care.

_childDocuments_.review: This game tries to do many things, and just fails at all of them, which is puzzling since 2022 is almost over and there's a wealth of other games they could have used as reference to make a better game. Pros: Side Quests : Probably the only thing I think this game does better than most other (J)RPGs out there. Side Quests have actual stories to them, with cutscenes, character development, etc. instead of the usual "kill 10 rats". Cons:Combat : Dodging does not exist, and I mean that literally, the action of "dodging" is not existent in this action RPG. This means that you will constantly be drinking juices or eating food to keep your health back up. Enemies are also more likely to be hitting you over your party members, and many of your actions root you into position so there is no "flow" to the combat, you just have to take the hits and carry enough food to help you through. This also leads to the only support job being pretty useless, and there is also no "Healer" job (as far as I could find). Farming/Resource Management: It's just a grind. It's not a leisure activity, it's the only way to generate income (outside of quests) and get ingredients needed for drinks and food that are mandatory if you wish to survive going to the dungeons and fighting bosses. The ability to make drinks and food must also be unlocked/purchased, they are not given to you from the get-go. Time Limits/Action Costs: You have 18 hours in-game time to do everything you need to do, so everything is a bit of a race, like exploring dungeons.  Almost everything in the game costs time. From cooking food, making juice, going from one city to another, even investigating mysterious points in a dungeon (which either drops items or punishes you with debuffs or monsters spawn). It's annoying. Really disappointed in this game, and I just cannot recommend it, especially not at that price of a AAA game. If you really want this game, wait for a 50% off sale or something better.

_childDocuments_.review: Notice that most every negative review has less than 2 hours - intent to return or not. With only 4 hours, I can confidently call a lot of them liars. Any review that says there is no dodge mechanic is actively wrong, or outright liars. There is one. The problem here is that the tutorial is pretty slow. That's a reasonable criticism to make. Assuming the tutorial reflects the entire game, is another. Not feeling the game is worth going deep in is a fine problem. But there is so much more to the game even with barely any more time, like the Break system.There's at least 12 Jobs with their own skill trees, abilities, and so on. Combat is very basic to start but will very obviously expand with time. Being able to swap Jobs mid fight is the key to this. The controls even on a controller take a bit to get used to, but it's not impossible. This was definitely a game made with controllers in mind - but unfortunately no robust button remapping.That's a good criticism too. Re-mapping keys is messy, and definitely an afterthought. But game seemed better to be on controller even if full remapping was available. KBM is superior for a lot of games, this doesn't seem one of them. And the graphics options very much are lacking. However, aside from pre-rendered cutscenes looking extremely fuzzy on a higher resolution (I run 2k), the game still looks amazing. Visually stunning so far. The story also has me very interested so far. There is a lack of VA and character customization, but I honestly didn't even think too much about it beyond adding my own VA. I was too interested in seeing how everything was going to fit together. There's a lot of disparate pieces but they will have to fit together.Oh, and stamina? The game doesn't make you a slave to it. They make replenishing stamina super easy, and seems like it will be a very important mechanic in late game.Or down the line this will become a negative review. But I am VERY much enjoying the game even in the early stages. I hope that doesn't change, as i was looking forward to this game since the announcement. Got my code for free, but I am not about to pretend to enjoy a game.

_childDocuments_.review: Spent 40 hours on it, and was bored for the vast majority of it. The game itself looks like an upscaled 3DS game. It is pretty ugly all throughout. The story is very slow and boring. The party member side story quests are very slow and play out like they didn't have enough story for them, so they really had to stretch what they had. The farming and RPG are very badly integrated together, so you really have to choose do you want to farm or do you want to go through the story, so it feels like two separate games. That being said, the combat is slow, simple, and unsatisfying. It is basically a rotation of using your abilities on one class, switching classes, spending your abilities, switch to your third class, spend abilities, and then go to your first class, if it is off cooldown, and spend your abilities, if they are off cooldown. The farming and crafting are very slow and unprofitable, so it seems like a but of a waste. It takes so much to buy enough seeds to fill up a farm. Also feels like it is mostly supposed to be not fully utilized until late to end game, especially with the lvl 2 refining equipment needing so many crops to make, say, flour or jam.

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely love this game; however, I can see where some of the mixed reviews are coming in. Ultimately, this is a really charming JRPG (reminiscent of JRPGs from the Squaresoft era) with some very dark themes and farming sim elements tacked onto it. The majority of the game was battling and running quests with the farming elements feeling tedious and misplaced sometimes. The story was absolutely out of control, epic, and went "full anime" as I like to say - where it went totally off the walls in the best way possible (at least for those who are anime fans). Like a lot of anime, the story started light and charming and went to a very dark, dramatic, and complicated place. This game is way too dark and battle heavy for me to recommend to anyone looking for a relaxing farming sim. Also in true JRPG style, it can get pretty grindy if you are trying to get all the achievements. If you are into Rune Factory and older JRPGS (FF7 and earlier, Xenogears, Chrono Tigger etc.) I would highly recommend this game, even if you aren't super into farming sims. It transported me back in time, reminding me of the RPGs I grew up on and loved as a child and would obsessively play through over summer break. The farming elements support the battling system and are crucial to give you buffs, heals and stamina. Even though the battling system is a lot simpler than the ones you would find in more traditional JRPGs, they're still a bit much for anyone looking for a relaxing farming sim. For several bosses I was like oh ♥♥♥♥ I actually have to prepare, pay attention and think about this which is not something people looking for a farming sim typically want. Old school JRPG fans: GET THIS GAME, you'll love it! I think if you are coming from a pure farming sim background and expect something like Stardew Valley, Harvest Moon etc. it's going to be a disappointment. Actually, you'll probably hate it. This game is severely mis-marketed. I would even put a bit of a TW on this game (suicide) as it had some VERY dark story elements. Unlike the idyllic environment that those games immerse you in, the story in Harvestella is already fairly dark and apocalyptic (in true Final Fantasy style). It doesn't have the satisfying dopamine inducing grind that a lot of farming sims have. There's more farming than I expected, but gameplay focuses heavily on RPG elements with extensive dialog, story, and battles. The farming sim elements feel tacked on and even tedious at times, and not that enjoyable. It's like they copied the farming elements from Harvest Moon on a very limited scale (you can build machines to create more things like turning eggs to mayonnaise etc.). The expansion on your farm is very linear and you unlock block like sections of it so you can farm more. You cannot rearrange your house, customize your house or any buildings on your farm. The design and art that went into it is phenomenal though, so it's a bit of a disappointment that they missed the mark here. Your farm is beautiful and gives off such a chill cottage core vibe. It feels like they didn't do a lot of research into the farming sim market, or played any farming sim games much themselves.Hope this helps you make a decision to play this or not. As someone into dark story elements and JRPGs I sure as hell enjoyed it.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: The intro to this game is very dull and cutscene heavy. Game starts opening up a lot about 3-4 hours in and is starting to get really fun. Game lacks Life sim parts of Farm sims and replaces it with JRPG style quests. Combat is very simple so far and food items are required due to lack of defensive options.Personally this game is hitting a lot of checkmarks for me so I am enjoying it despite these faults.If you are playing this game expecting Harvest Moon or Stardew Valley with a Final Fantasy coat of paint, you are probably going to be disappointed. The impression I've gotten from this game is that it is a JRPG first and a Farming Sim second. I personally love both JRPGs and Farm Sims so I am really enjoying what I see and I see a lot of potential in what this game might have in store for me next.The game starts off VERY slow, the first few days have you starting the day late and essentially only being able to progress the story. It takes about an hour and a half to get to the first dungeon if you take your time and then you still won't be able to do much other than explore said dungeon. There are also a lot of cut-scenes that could be intriguing or incredibly dull depending on how much you enjoy standard JRPG stories. Oddly enough you can't even manually save until you reach the mid point of the first dungeon about 2 hours into the playthrough, Though there is auto saves each night. The combat is alright, but since this is really early in a JRPG, it is incredibly simplistic. There aren't any defensive options (so far as of 5 hours in) other than a basic dash, so you'll probably be taking a lot of damage from monsters. Healing items are a must if you plan on delving deeper into dungeons. If I hadn't been paying attention to the pre-release materials and seen that there is more to this game, I probably would have dropped the game here.However, once you reach Chapter 3, the game starts opening up. You start getting quests from the people in the town. The Main Quest is split into 3 distinct sub quests that require you to investigate parts of the world in different directions. You start unlocking more classes and getting more skills for combat. You get more stuff to do on your farm and from what I can tell from the images on the store page, there is a lot more that I have to unlock here. It looks like the Farm sim part of Farm sims is probably going to be more important as I progress, though the Life sim part of Farm sims seems to be practically non existent and is instead replaced with standard JRPG style questing.

_childDocuments_.review: It's so rough around the edges in some really odd spots. The lack of voice acting (except contextual things the characters say when you're out and about) is glaring coming from a company as major as squenix. The farming feels...okay, I guess? It oddly feels very tacked-on and shallow so far.My biggest complaint, however, is the combat, which was supposed to be a big selling point of this game. It feels incredibly lackluster: combos have very long ending lag, you can't use skills as part of a combo, the skills so far seem to be just a single attack with a really long cooldown. Worst of all, there doesn't seem to be any defensive options; combat is mainly trading blows with enemies as there isn't any dodge or block and the long ending lag to your combo means that enemies will often hit you before you can do anything. I'm just puzzled as to how the developers envisioned the combat. Another complaint I have is the stamina: it runs out far too quickly and it's way too annoying to try and keep your stomach full so it can slowly regen.Ultimately, I expected this to be a like a more polished Rune Factory with more focus on combat and less on farming. What I got was a game with worse versions of both. Even the polish falters in many places: although they put an option in the menu, they didn't even bother to swap the confirm and cancel buttons by default (something usually done with every JP game in the west). If they ever patch the combat so it's not a complete slog I think I can come around on this one but until then, I'd say it's not worth the full $60. Maybe $20, and that's only if you're okay with awful combat.EDIT: I forgot to mention, you get a dash that feels like it should be used as a dodge of sorts, but it's almost completely useless in that regard, as it is also affected by the ending delay issue. If anything, it makes trying to run more cumbersome.

_childDocuments_.review: On first impressions I'm left feeling rather disappointed. The character customisation/creation is awful, really surprised by this as you can only choose variations of the same character with the same hairstyle. I was also disappointed that there is no voice acting in the game, it lacks immersion from the get go. Most SE games have fabulous VA.Game days are way too short, I barely have time to do anything before Im being told to go home to bed, lol for a 50 year old lady it's a bit like being a kid again.I went to the town and things are pretty quiet there with very few items to interact with, usually in farming type games you can chop every tree and grab every flower. In this game there are tiny markers that in random spots that you click on and give you some type of material. There are chests to loot, I've found a couple, again no costumes or gear changes just some crafting mats.I'm thinking SE you really need to up your game to compete with some of the amazing Farming RPGS out there. The only reason I'm not looking for a refund is Im pinning my hopes on the story and immersion improving.If you are on the fence at this point Id say this is a 30 euro game, not a 60 euro game.Im going to keep playing and updating this review as I progress. Ill definitely change my recommendation if it improves greatly.(70 or so hours later)Ok so having completed the game and upgraded as far as I can be bothered, Ill just add to the above response, none of which I would change based on my complete play through.The biggest issue with this game is expectation, I bought the game and paid the €60 price tag on the expectation I was going to be able to play a relaxing lifestyle farming sim with roleplay, customisation and story elements.What I got was a JPRG fighting game, great story and loads of little side-quests with no customisation AT ALL. Upgrading is the thing in this game, you can upgrade everything from farm gear to weapons and skills. That in itself is OK for me but the grind of the dungeons got very old very quickly,  rushing from save point to save point and needing to replay the same levels over and over if you didn't get to unlock that ladder or repair that bridge. At one point, in the Castle I was ready to throw in the towel,I'm glad I didn't, things got easier and the ending was worth waiting for. I was however glad to get to the end as the lack of customisation options for my character and my farm just made everything feel really old really quickly. I wont recommend this game as a modern farming sim at the price it sells for; because it just cant complete with the likes of Disney Dream light Valley and Grow Song of the Evertree. Both of which were much cheaper but much more enjoyable for me.If you like fighting JRPG games in which your character looks and feels far less heroic and attractive than every other character in the game including the Robot companion then go for it, its a sweet story and will keep you busy f you like a bit of grind.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game, after being so disappointed with Rune Factory 5, but this game is nearly as bad. The characters are bland and cliche, the NPCs have no personality, most are just named "old woman" or "traveler" generic descriptions to make it clear they're not important. Even the store owners are just "Renovator" and "Smith." It's clear they put no effort in to trying to make the town feel alive. The named characters aren't much better, either. They're very one-dimensional, within a few lines of dialogue, you know exactly what kind of character they are, and that's all they'll ever be. The game constantly railroads you, preventing you from visiting any locations that aren't your quest objective, and locking NPCs in to set dialogue until you complete the objective. There's no friendship or relations to build except by following the railroad of the story. I wanted to enjoy this game, and kept giving it more chances, hoping that if I just got a little further in the storyline, that things would liven up and the training wheels would come off, but by chapter 3 the tutorial should be over, and there should be some kind of player autonomy. There is not. It's just one disappointment after another.

_childDocuments_.review: Summary:It's Final Fantasy lite, that has all the annoying mini-games replaced with farming-lite.+++ AtmosphereThe environments are really pretty, and the music tracks are really beautiful, and honestly are some of the best music tracks I've heard. The world does feel like it's a lived-in place, and the NPCs are well written. This is the game's strongest aspect by far. It's very much a feel-good-game.+ StoryIt's very dramatic and in part over the top Final Fantasy -type story, and it's good. It has some heavy handed but well laid environmental and stay-positive messages.+ CharactersThey are all like-able and well written and have distinctive personalities. The character specific events are fun and you do feel like you get to know each other a bit. Unfortunately the promised romance stumbles in the end.+/- CombatIt's fun-ish, but outside boss battles, it's very... MMO-ish, where dodging or blocking isn't a thing. You just face-tank hits, and compensate your lack of levels with spamming healing items. Not great honestly, but at least it is flashy at times.- Voice ActingIt's good (I played with JP voices) when it's there, which it isn't most of the time. The dialogue is not voiced. The only things that are voiced are greeting lines, combat shouts, and the monologues of bigger boss battles. It has the same amount of voice acting as Morrowind. This game would have really benefited from being a fully voiced game.-- RomanceIt's only lip service. If you've played Rune Factory 4 and 5, throw those ideas out of the window. This game has the relationship depth of vanilla Skyrim, and it's very squeamish about even having characters say that they love each other, as if out of fear that declaration(s) of love would give the game an adult rating. If Anything, THIS should have been the focus of the game more than the farming aspects, because game already is 95% adventuring, discoveries, character interactions and <5% farming life.If there ever is going to be a Harvestella 2, I hope they focus way more on this aspect, because there clearly was a LOT of potential here, considering how much time and effort was spent in fleshing out the characters.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay so I've made it through the game, nearly completing all the optional stuff. So how is it? Well, TLDR first; It's worth a play through, but only on sale. I think the story is nice, though it's writing is a little bland. I really liked the various nods/references(whether on purpose or not) to other games like Nier, FFXIV, Bravely Default, Elden Ring(yes, that's what I said XD) and it's other more obvious inspirations (Rune Factory, Secret of Mana, though I have yet to play those. The music is really nice, though I wish it varied or turned off sometimes haha, but those dungeon/boss beats slap pretty hard. The gameplay is a pretty satisfying loop, though it's slow at first. The farming element kind of just becomes a means to an end for potions/upgrades, and the limited features don't really allow much customization or "aesthetic", the farming has a frustrating slowness to some of the mechanics(plowing, placing or breaking things etc) which I wouldn't complain about if it at least all three tools had the same coverage squares lol. Kind of hard to explain, but overall it's still fun, and it gives you a reason to progress/farm outside as you go through the story. The story... is pretty nice. I'm a huge Nier/ffxiv fan so I felt like this really had the same soul as those games. I wish the writing was a bit better, and I wish there were more casual bonding moments similar to bravely default, as it felt really scarce. I really loved feeling represented and allowed to choose my pronouns, and it felt amazing going through the game. Honestly, my only gripe is how this game felt a little unfinished or empty. I wish there was just a liiiittle more, I feel like it has a great core, but just kinda missing the spice. I would still say this game is not worth 90$(CAD), and would probably wait until it goes on sale, but if it had a little more to it(more voice acting, more farm customization, character customization) then I could justify the price.Also... please, oh please if devs read this... fix the faeries voices... why does it trigger on every. single. action I make on the farm lol I wanted to strangle the faerie every time she goes "SHUPATSUUUUUU" LOLIn the end, yes, I'd say it's a good game. My expectations were a bit high for a 90$ game. Do some research, try the demo first. It's good, but I think it's a game you'll either like or hate lol

_childDocuments_.review: The game is weirdly much better than the sum of its parts, most of which seem like shallow copies of other games that it used as inspiration.  The story actually ended up being pretty decent, despite having one of the worst beginnings I think I've ever experienced (was the game made by Ubisoft? lol).  The key is that the different systems do a pretty good job feeding into each other, so the shallowness of the individual game play loops is offset by the interplay between them.  The game has the day timer similar to Stardew, so you sort of have a time (and energy) limit to your daily activities, but the level design is excellent, with dungeons that sort of loop back on themselves, with shortcuts constantly opening up so that your next trip to the dungeon allows you to easily progress further.If you're looking for an action JRPG with a solid shake of Stardew Valley mixed in, you could do a lot worse. It has a nice, almost soothing, daily game play loop that is somewhat satisfying.  7 out of 10

_childDocuments_.review: A very comfy and beautiful game for your daily wind-down.I often feel pressured when a game uses limited time per day, but not in Harvestella.So far there has been no punishment for taking things slow and not progressing the story or clearing dungeons.Story and exploration start off very linear and branch out in Chapter 3. At this point you'll unlock a lot more crafting and cooking recipes, new areas and materials.I really enjoy the rich environments and gorgeous character designs.Their fashion draws many inspirations from similar JRPG entries from Square Enix while still being unique.Character customization is limited to the starting screen and your currently equipped Job. I suspect that this will not change over he course of the game.Sound design is nothing special but the amazing soundtrack makes up for that.Just like with the character designs the soundtrack incorporates many elements from previous popular SE games.tldr: If you like a slow paced fusion of Harvest Moon, Final Fantasy and Nier elements, you'll probably enjoy Harvestella.

_childDocuments_.review: I cant very well say, after 67 hours of playtime, this is a great title from Square Enix. Wish I could give it a middling score. Cutting right to the chase, the level design is TERRIBLE; too many same-y colors in levels make managing your way through them impossible without getting "lost". And this doesn't include the MANY times you will have to sleep and then come back because the "day" isn't long enough. Levels also have ridiculously unnecessary puzzles that make the actual chapters far too long. Its padded for no reason at all besides just to make the games length longer. Onto the story. Typical convoluted Square story with META, META, META--the likes of Christopher Nolan and M. Night Shamalan had an illegitimate child levels of M E T A. Now, if you're a weirdo and LIKE that kinda ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ then go for it. The story will satisfy that 4th dimensional itch of what is real and what isn't, "is this a dream or is this a reality?". But if you're someone who HATES that kind of stuff, AVOID THIS GAME. Because you won't be playing it for the lackluster, confusing dungeons or the character building (which there isn't any beyond being able to cuff your favorite character after completing ALL of their quests. Which also, garners you nothing--no special moments, no special armor, buffs, etc.--NOTHING.) All in all, if you enjoy a crazy Square Enix meta-story--play this game. If you like difficulty for no reason, but the bosses are easy as ♥♥♥♥ and are unfulfilling--play this game. Otherwise, it's just not worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: A 'Final Fantasy' FARMING game? Count me in. Or - so I thought. There's so much disappointment, I can't believe I bought it even half off. It's less about the farming, and more about following some crack typical JRPG storyline while dungeon crawling through areas that make this feel like I'm playing on a 3DS. Seriously, the controls are horrible. (I haven't tried it on a controller, but I heard it's better?)It's so frustrating standing right in front of a prompt and pushing the button over and over again only for nothing to happen. Turn the camera a little to the left, nothing, a little to the right, nothing, back to the left - ah, there it goes. It's like the commands just don't respond at all at the most random times.There's a classic job system, but I'm still confused as to why we need such an in depth class system for a 'farming' game. And you only get a few materials over and over and over again from exploring.And don't even try character customization (there isn't any.) I picked male at first, but was incredibly off put by the fact that it's literally the same design as the female, only a different stance. What?? Female it is.And worst of all: the farming. Since the game is on a 'timed' day cycle, everything you do takes time. And you have to be back home by like 7-8pm. It takes you until about noon to just throw some seeds down and try to get the game to register your watering commands. Then you can't harvest them for a few days, to be turned in for money that you don't get until the next day. The rest of your time is supposed to be spent dungeon crawling through a storyline. So, five minutes of planting, half an hour of JRPG stuff.I imagine that it might be rewarding later on, but I've played for at least four hours straight and can hardly do anything but water seeds and slash the same three enemy designs over and over. Maybe without the pressure of the time/day cycle going by so fast and the controls working better, it wouldn't be so frustrating.

_childDocuments_.review: Entertaining, but lacking in detail.Harvestella is an ARPG/farming simulation combo that sounds bizarre, but works out fairly well. Players take on the role of an amnesiac traveler who is thrust into a new life of managing a farm, slaying monsters, and uncovering their lost memories.Harvestella's farming mechanics are decent. There are four major seasons, a variety of crops that can be grown, and a few different environments that further add to farming variety. Animal husbandry features are minimal, but a vast number of cooking and crafting recipes encourage growing as many different types as possible, rewarding players with new discoveries, although a lack of winter crop variety slows down the game considerably during that season.Your character can learn a variety of combat jobs and equip up to three at a time while exploring dungeons. Each job comes with unique movesets and passive abilities to customize your playstyle the way you want. An elemental weakness/resistance system further encourages you to experiment with class combinations, rewarding you with special moves from your comrades if you manage to target bosses' weaknesses enough. ARPG fans may be displeased to hear that the player cannot block or dodge attacks in Harvestella; spacing yourself from an enemy's swing or telegraph can sometimes allow you to avoid a hit, but many attacks are completely undodgeable, requiring players to eat food and drink that they've prepared in advanced to heal during battles. Additionally, some jobs don't explain their attacks with much detail, and other jobs are downright underpowered, which creates an overall clunky combat experience.The narrative starts out extremely slow with a run-of-the-mill amnesiac JRPG plot, though there are some plot twists later in the story that keep things interesting and somewhat unique. The major characters of the story aren't particularly interesting, however; although each character has their own extensive sidequest chain dedicated to their own development, these quests are usually little more than sophomoric monologues that force character development rather than letting the characters grow organically.But perhaps the biggest issue with Harvestella is that there is a lack of fine details that are so important to making RPG experiences immersive. In cutscenes, characters regularly handle objects that are invisible. Dialogue choices exist, but they have no impact on anything and most of the time, the choices are two different ways of phrasing the exact same thing. All cutscenes are unskippable, which can make the banal writing of the sidequests become too tiresome to bother with after only a few hours of this 50 hour RPG. Translation errors abound, including both improper word choice and spelling/grammar mistakes. The culmination of all of these forgotten details create an experience that feels phoned-in.I did enjoy my time with Harvestella, but I acknowledge that it has numerous issues that might turn off many fans of ARPGs or farming simulators. That being said, it has a bit more crunch to it than your average casual game, and its mechanics are fairly simplistic at their core, so I would recommend this game for both casual gamers and kids.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't let the negative reviews fool you, this game is fantastic!The music is wonderful, the visuals are cozy and sweet, and honestly I find this the perfect balance of JRPG and farm sim. The farming systems may not be as deep as something like Rune Factory, but I find that this is a benefit rather than a hindrance given how much importance is put on questing. As much as I love RF games, sometimes I get overwhelmed with how much time each aspect of farming and dungeon crawling demands - I'm not having this issue with Harvestella! Also the side quests are so endearing. It's definitely more of a JRPG than pure farm sim, but I do think that care was taken to make farming fun, even if it's simple. The story starts off a little slow, but once you get to Chapter Three, things start to get interesting and the game loop really opens up! My only complaint is that playing using a controller doesn't allow you to remap the controller buttons, so using the B button on an Xbox Controller to confirm things was something strange to get used to. If you are playing using a PS controller though, there is a mod on Nexus which changes the interface to a PS layout. Anyway, get this if you're looking for a relaxing, cozy JRPG with farm and crafting mechanics. The beginning may feel a little slow, as it takes its time with set up, but it's well worth it!

_childDocuments_.review: Is this game worth playing?  Yes, it is.  Is it worth $60?  Only you can decide that.  I have no regrets.I also had very few expectations. I didn't do any research about the game beyond that, and bought it the day it released because they were all excited about it.  I was pretty skeptical of it actually being what I would imagine a combination of those two games to be like, so I wasn't disappointed when it wound up being its own thing.  If you WERE expecting a true hybrid of Final Fantasy and Stardew Valley, you WILL be disappointed!But, if you're willing to take it for what it is - a somewhat traditional JRPG with a pretty decent story (so far) and some farming and ranching stuff thrown on, then you won't be let down.  The graphics aren't the best or most vibrant, and the controls are kinda really bad at times (the game is technically a PC port of a Nintendo Switch title, explaining a lot of the graphical and control limitations) but they do the job without getting in your way too much.  The combat is... lackluster at best.  The controls don't help it any in that regard.  I just settled into playing as a mage and flinging spells from the rear ranks while the rest of my party does the whole melee thing. I know I threw in a lot of negatives there, but the game is still good, in my opinion.  I'm enjoying myself and it's a good change of pace for me right now.  The farm you live on in the game is actually quite large and I haven't unlocked the vast majority of it, 23 hours in (I may just be bad/slow, don't know).

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start this review off by saying that this is not a farming sim, regardless of what the game says.This is an action RPG and visual novel with some farming sim elements taped to it for... Reasons. I genuinely do not understand why. The farming is not very deep or engaging, and mostly exists just to fill your pockets with cash and ingredients for cooking.Now, with this in mind...This may genuinely be one of the most engaging games I've ever played story-wise, and it genuinely brought me to tears multiple times. The story follows your main character as he, she, or they wake up in a town in what appears to be the middle ages with no memories. From there, you start an adventure to uncover the mystery of your own memory loss, and the story of another girl who arrives shortly after you do. From there, you meet an expanded cast of party members who all have their own stories that all revolve in one way or another around grief.Grief is a constant undercurrent through the story, from the main character stories, social link style events, and even the sidequests. It takes a more adult approach to this than most games I've seen that tackle the theme, but I understand that's not something that everyone is in a place for.That's a lot of words about the story, but not much on the gameplay. This mostly revolves around exploring a series of dungeons, and fighting hordes of enemies while switching between the different classes you unlock as you find different party members. It's... Fine? The combat was okay, and the dungeons were interesting, but honestly a lot of the gameplay mostly felt like an afterthought that I had to put up with to get to the next story beat. This is a game that lives or dies on its story, and your willingness to put up with a mediocre hack-and-slash/farming sim hybrid to access it. If you like other Square Enix games that are heavy on the story, like Final Fantasy or Bravely Default, this might be worth a check. Same if you liked games like Persona, SMT, Metaphor Refantazio, or Rune Factory. But if you're looking for something like Stardew Valley with a deep farming system that you can sink your teeth in, or high-octane combat to push you to your limits... Look elsewhere.

_childDocuments_.review: To start off my review, I think it's important to mention the nature of hybrid games. Naturally, focusing on two different elements means less time can be given to each one. In this sense, Harvestella will not be the best RPG or best farming sim you've ever played. However, it combines the two distinct elements to create an extremely harmonious game with hours of enjoyment. I've seen many reviews complain about the lack of dodging, and how you're forced to rely on food to survive tough encounters. This is not only natural, as the game is a farming sim AND an RPG, but it's extremely satisfying. By forcing players to use food to survive, those that invested in their farm will have an advantage in combat by having much higher quality food with buffs/heals/stam. The combat in this game is also important to farming, as certain types of materials cannot be food except through combat. The combat system in Harvestella has much more depth than anything rune factory or stardew valley managed, as certain foods can even increase the amount of damage you deal of a certain type, provide poison damage, remove debuffs and more. The classes all feel unique, and despite not having many skills to use, you are expected to swap jobs frequent to "break" bosses to deal bonus damage. The focus is not on "mages" having access to every element, but rather each class having access to a select few and finding out the right combination of classes for each boss. There are even different types of physical damage, (wave, crush, slash etc) so melee classes can still contribute to breaking enemies. The farming is easy to adapt to, and does not feel "janky" after you've been playing for awhile. Locking the character is even helpful after you unlock a few faerie abilities to help speed the process up. The farming is extremely relaxing and rewarding, as I'm always looking for different things to make using the assortment of ingredients I've found. I love that there are so many different types of plants that can be grown in more than just one season, as it helps prevent me from locking myself out of recipes in a given season. It's not as forgiving to make ever plant grow in every season, but it's still much more flexible than most games. There's always some farm innovation to work towards as well with different "makers" as we call them, or unlocking caves to grow certain things in. The farm itself is also massive, and can be explored further as the game progresses.  The cooking in Harvestella completely dominates every other farming sim game I've played. I rarely ever cooked in Stardew, but cooking is not only enjoyable, but rewarding in Harvestella. Bringing dishes to the different town inns rewards a huge amount of money, and finding new ingredients as I progress is always exciting, as it means I can likely create a new dish. Finally, the social aspect of the game is much better than what people give it credit for. It's no Persona, but doing sidequests is not only enjoyable for the dialogue (the characters are interesting and well-written) but it also improves them as characters through secret abilities, party buffs and who knows what else. The sidequests are all well-written and interesting as well. The music for each area is also breathtaking, despite each area having a different sound to it. There's not a single track that doesn't feel like it belongs. To conclude, Harvestella is not the best RPG or best farming sim ever made. It's a beautiful, hybrid game that has brought the gaming spark back to my life, which has been gone for a long time. It's implemented all of the aspects of each genre in a cohesive way, so the game never feels boring. I would highly recommend giving it a shot on the switch demo, but I would also recommend buying it. It might be expensive, but there's plenty of enjoyable content for the price tag.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Mediocre game with great graphics and poor gameplay and horrible execution of critical mechanics. Visually this game is wonderful, and I'd have loved it if they had chosen one way to go and develop it into a well thought out game instead of trying to ride this awkward middle ground of farming sim dungeon crawler. But mechanically it's just bad.As a story it's decently good, interesting (if not completely cliche and predictable with the end plot twist), but as a Harvest Moon/Story of Seasons/Rune Factory knock off, it's a poor entrant. The farming portion of the game is just so lack luster with exceedingly poor returns, giving players no reason to grow crops outside of what they'd need in the moment for crafting the cheapest healing food and what you'd need for Food Turn In quests. And with no way of purchasing out of season fruits/veg and no gifting system for npcs you aren't encouraged to craft anything more than you as a player would need as crafted items hardly ever sale for more than their base components and yet eat into your in game time when crafted anyway. Giving only 2 farm animal options, a chicken and a goat/cow, and no way to really care for them other than put feed in silo and 'petting' them, and no way of getting access to them if it rains or during Quietus only enforces how half assed the farming portion of the game was. As far as the battle system goes. It's bad. They try to use FOEs as obstacles in dungeons but those just end up being slight annoyances you can ignore them for the most part as they are tied to a small portion of the map. The class system feels bare bones and thrown in as a second thought to give you a reason to grow closer with the other major characters in game. The actual battles itself are also painfully tedious. Caster/ranged classes have no option to dash dodge and each cast/shot takes a good chunk of stamina despite their painfully frail lack of any form of defense while Melee classes are forced to take unavoidable auto attack damage from enemies. Skills are on long cool down periods BUT ALSO eat deeply into the stamina bar with each use, and some skills feel absolutely useless, especially the Woglinde class skills. With no true healer or tank class available, you have to carry stacks and stacks of food and juices just to make small amounts of progress in current dungeons to get to the next monolight so you can quick travel back home and spend 2 in game days restocking on those vital healing items just to spend less than 12 in game hours picking your way through to get further the dungeon. It's a constant struggle with time in the story required dungeons vs revisiting older areas to try and gather materials you can't grow on your farm because they're required for repair kits or bombs or sprinklers or feed makers. The 'customization' part of the game is also pretty pointless, only giving you fences that require in game time to make and no real way to consolidate your maker machines into an aesthetically pleasing hut or side garden, you end up with either machines sprinkled through your farm jarringly or a hideous amalgamation of all your machines in one designated spot.

_childDocuments_.review: Harvestella is a decent RPG combined with well thought out life sim mechanics, but containing a major design flaw in that while there are plenty of people who enjoy both RPGs and life sims, most people do not reach for both simultaneously. Someone looking to enjoy an RPG will find the life sim mechanics needed to progress tedious and break up the narrative, while people looking to unwind with a good life sim will find themselves thrown into battles they weren't in the mood for.  All in all, I think it was a fun ride worth experiencing; just become the irate farmer on your way to fight god with a basket of veggies so you can get back to harvesting.

_childDocuments_.review: If you have played Rune Factory/Harvest Moon or the Atelier series you know what to expect from the gameplay loop: You have a home base where you farm and craft, and you explore other dungeons and towns via a world map. (Time progresses in real-time, unless you are in an extended story event.) At first, the combat feels light, but as you progress and gain more classes and skills, you will find that there is in fact some decent depth to the gameplay. The interface is very clean as well. Overall, it runs great on the Deck, but it stutters for several frames any time it buffers any new effects or loads in a new model. This only happens, for instance, when first switching classes or using abilities, but its enough to hurt enjoyment of an otherwise flawless experience. (The game uses Unreal Engine, so its likely the developer's lack of experience with it, and this could be patched later.)Do yourself a favor and play this game - and crank up the music!!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is like if Final Fantasy, Monster Hunter World, and Edge of Eternity were spliced together in a laboratory.My wife’s boyfriend says it’s like if Final Fantasy and Rune Factory had a baby.Harvestella surpassed my expectations. Picked the game up on a Steam sale, and ended up pumping almost 150 hours into it, even with its apparent flaws, Square Enix cooked something special here.They wrongfully advertised this game as a farming sim when in reality it's full blown crazy JRPG where you start growing carrots and then you're facing an existential threat to humanity complete with enough sci-fi beats to make X-files sweat! I greatly enjoyed it and it was one of my unexpected games of the year. The plot/ lore/ writing is unexpectedly good and less cliche than your typical JRPG, and the job system is fun if flawed. I really did not expect NieR:Automata meets Shadowbringers but that's what we got! It's a game you have to play to understand why someone would like it. If you describe the game it sounds like a whatever game, but once you play you feel how truly amazing it is. One of those games that's greater than the sum of its parts, and does a lot with a small budget. Does it hit everything right? Of course not, the limited budget shows: Enemy variety is poor, very limited voice acting, the RPG aspects are somewhat shallow, and there's not a load of depth to the farming or combat which is very xenoblade-like, yet its still retains a fairly addicting gameplay loop,  just enough to hook you until the story goes off the wall and grips you all the way, like seriously, this is one of Square Enix’s best JRPG stories without a doubt, and in their advertised farming sim game!As someone who spends their time playing either JRPGs or Farm Sims, this is a perfect balance between the two. IMO it's a perfect entry for anyone who has never dipped their toe into the opposite genre. It is such a cozy game with a crazy strong atmosphere and you will be longing to go back to play it when you have to go to work. I sometimes forgot I wasn’t playing NIER as I played it. I appreciated that the overall tone was slightly less depressing, but the story and sidequest were quite similar. Even the port town felt like the same place as in the original NIER game.The story took me by surprise in such a good way, and I was even impressed by the great writing in the side character stories and quests. They actually have depth thanks to some very good side character stories that really flesh them out, even random NPCS, yes those random ass NPCS staples in RPG’s, are memorable because their sidequests are actually heartfelt stories, not just go find my 10 pelts.Loved the characters, loved the plot, loved the world. Did feel like everything could have used more size and depth but hey, it wasn’t a big budget game, and I’d rather be left wanting more than left wishing it hadn’t overstayed its welcome.But the music, man. That music. That is where my expectations were blown out of the water. It’s so frickin good. And honestly, the soundtrack is beyond everything that got published during the last years. I purchased the soundtrack to keep listening to it while driving. Amazing game. Little things here and there I wish were improved or expanded upon, but the complete bats**t direction the plot devolved into was so notoriously Square Enix. It's a shame that it got a bad rep due to flawed marketing & review bombing by as***les.Unfortunately it was review bombed pretty early by people angry at how the male character model looked, how they expected the customization would be what one generally sees in a life sim but not JRPG, the demo being too fast (although they adjusted time for the actual release), and then some were just mad at the completely avoidable nonbinary option which made them go into troll-y conspiracy theories on the Steam forums. Real Solid game, truly. Definitely one of my favorite's I've played recently, with warts and all, the games ambition really made it stand out to me. Don’t miss this gem if you are into JRPGs. You can easily spend more than 100 hours with it. I recommend it even at full price.9/10
