_childDocuments_.review: I got this game on sale for 30$, and overall I would say it was worth the price if you like games in the same genre such as rune factory or if the mashup of "final fantasy + farming sim" appeals to you as it does to me. I think at the full price of $50-60 it would be a bit harder to justify, primarily due to its overall simplicity and lack of depth of its core features.Additionally, while I personally don't consider it enough of a deal-breaker to warrant a negative review- I would actually *not recommend* this game for children of religious families. Several themes, so-called 'protagonist' companions, and many lines of dialog clearly stray from what is required by the fantasy narrative into full-on anti-religious bigotry. The game world includes a religious cult clearly modeled after the catholic church, which are depicted as evil, oppressive, simple-minded, and superstitious. All of these instances become especially notable in stark contrast with the inclusion of beings of supernatural origin, such as magical fairies, in the game; This is a strong indicator that the writers purposefully decided to overlook the presence of their own supernatural elements in game, and cherry-pick their disdain towards the more real-world religious elements (i.e. implying people are stupid for thinking god exists, while literally standing right next to magical fairies and a unicorn.) I almost always overlook these types of themes in games, especially eastern ones, but had to highlight it this time because it was so pervasive. Being respectful of others doesn't just include the color of their skin.Moving on, pros and cons:PROS:+++ 2D Artwork is excellent, UI is good. 3D environmental visuals and shaders look really good stylistically, even though it was made to run on that overpriced potato console the nintendo switch.+++ Music is really good, I would think some FF music enthusiasts would happily purchase the OST.++ The style of the overworld map could be the new gold standard for similar games in my book.++ combination of final fantasy elements with a farming game work out very nicely.++ The game's core strength is in its variety of features and its presentation. + The story & character arcs are 'decent' I would say, but not great. The initial mystery and intrigue of the game world is soiled a bit by a lackluster and unoriginal 'reveal'. Not bad, but they could've done a lot better.  + story and farm progression is well-paced and doesn't pressure you much. getting knocked out in combat is not punishing at all. Several quality of life elements such as easy teleport points all combine into a very casual enjoyable experience.Cons--- Anti-Religious themes and dialog far exceed the levels required to meet the narrative into what is clearly promoting bigotry and disdain for religious peoples outside of the game itself.-- Absolutely *none* of the core features have any depth: combat, class system, crafting, fishing, farming, animals, quests, npcs, relationships. None of it has any depth or complexity. -- Romance options are non-existent. The ability to court and marry your favorite npc character(s) is a pretty big draw for fans of the genre and it's not present here. - All cutscenes are non-skippable, and there are a lot. This will be a big deal for less patient people.- The game gives you 3 fake gender choices for your character: male, female, and non-binary. Every option looks female. - This is a nintendo switch game. All of the 3d models are hyper simplified to run on decade-old hardware. Visually, the worst part of the game is the 3d character models; specifically the NPC townsfolk. This gets overshadowed slightly by the quality of 2d portraits, but I can't help but think a game by square enix asking for 50$ on the regular could have afforded to make some genshin-level character models for the pc release and not reused the same 5 townsfolk npc models for every single quest.

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR better than expected, but its not stardew valley or rune factory. Its final fantasy farmingIll get the elephant in the room out of the way first, the non-binary option in the character select screen is completely useless, except for a line near the end that if i say it would massively spoil the plot of the game. TBH i would say the writing of the game fits the male avatar a lot better than the female avatar, and i get the sense that the character customization was shoehorned in 2 months before launch. If they just stuck with the male avatar and gave him a bit more personality, i would rate this game about.4% higher than i will since the bulk of the writing and other characters REALLY carry the game.The writing and the story is really good, and it feels like it belongs in a fully fledged Final Fantasy game than a FF/farm game, but it does really fit well within the confines of the gameplay. the supporting cast have a persona- like story path where you hang out with them for story beats, support them with choices, and when you complete each story beat, they grow stronger, which is an intensive to go thru the story. most side quests are generally 3 quests deep that spans roughly 3-4 in game days, so you dont have to rush to get them done all in one day. and they do reward free seeds for the farm, which really helps in the early game. i never expected so many gut punch and depressing stories in a farming sim, but it makes the stories that have a happy ending and the overall plot feel much more impact fullThe gameplay is not turn based like older FF, but is more of a hack-n-slash with a few special moves mixed with avoiding telegraphed attacks. You do have a stamina meter that you need to keep an eye on if you want to dodge or use special attacks, and if your character is hungry, you dont regen stamina. you can keep your character full by making meals in the kitchen (when you unlock it) at the farm with the ingredients you find/grow. you also can make drinks that act like healing potions with the fruits and veggies you find/grow as well, so you dont buy potions, you grow them.The farming part starts off slow in the beginning, like all other farm sims do, but thru the story, side quests, mining, fishing, and growing crops, you can expand the farm slowly with the money you earn. you have to be careful near the end of the month through, since each season is one month long, and if you still have crops in the field when the games "quietus" event comes, the crops will die. you also have to make machines for the farm to process the ingredients you grow to make food, which usually takes a day to completeThe quietus day usually comes at the end of the month,. and usually opens up a dungeon on the farm where you can get crafting materials for machines and your weapons, and gives a bit more xp than normal dungeons, so its important to go as far as you can in the dungeon during quietusThe farming aspect does feed into the questing aspect, which in turn, feeds into the farming aspect, which makes a satisfying loop of trying to get farm work done and enough supplies to go dungeoning that day, which in turns makes each check point in the dungeon more satisfying.Overall, a pretty solid game, great story, really damn good writing, and satisfying game loop. though if your looking for a farm sim like SDV, you will be disappointed. id give it a 8.8/10. id enjoyed my time with it but i dont blame you if you wait for a sale, since there is alot of great games coming out this season

_childDocuments_.review: Let me clear up the huge misconception:THIS IS NOT A FARMING SIM LIKE STARDEW VALLEY.THIS IS A JRPG.If you come into the game with the mindset of a JRPG, this is a good game. I'll be honest that reading through the description I thought it would be heavier on the farming aspect, but this is primarily a JRPG.I have played pretty much all the farming sims like Harvest Moon, Story of Seasons, Rune Factory, Stardew Valley, My Time At Portia/Sandrock, etc.. I would say Stardew Valley is heaviest on the farming aspects with a sprinkle of combat and quests. Rune Factory I would put in the middle with a pretty decent farming system but also very heavy on the story, quests, and combat. Harvestella is heaviest on the story, questing, and combat, with farming being more of a side thing you do.As for the main complaints I have seen:NO CHARACTER CUSTOMIZATION!There is almost no character customization, which is pretty typical for most JRPGs. I'm surprised they even let you do any customization. If you want to insert yourself and make your own character, this game is not for you. Doesn't seem to be any way to change your clothes too besides switching classes in combat. I don't mind this as I'm used to it, but I know this is a turn off for some people.THERE'S NOT ENOUGH TIME!I have not had any issues with time coming from other standard farming games with time systems. There is plenty to do in one day and there are so many ways to fast travel that it makes me wonder if people played more than a few hours. You get ways to fast travel a few hours in and it is very easy to craft an item that will take you home from anywhere. Stamina is super easy to get back with even the most basic of foods. I think people are confused and think you're supposed to clear dungeons in one go - that's not the case. You should be spending multiple days, that's why there's shortcuts you unlock along the way in dungeons.FARMING IS TOO SIMPLE!As I mentioned before, this is a JRPG first.THE GAME IS TOO EXPENSIVE!This is the only main complaint I agree with. As this is a Switch game, I was surprised to see it priced at $60 like a AAA title. While this is clearly a labor of love and worth more than a $20 indie game, this does not feel like a full AAA release. I would say it would be fairly priced at $40. If you love JRPG's, then this is still a good buy at $60, but if you're on the fence I would wait for a sale.I recommend getting this game if you like JRPG's, but do not buy it expecting a Stardew Valley type game.

_childDocuments_.review: I’m recommending this game, but with some big reservations.  I’d give it a neutral review if I could. It does a lot of things right, but it screams “low budget” in some pretty obvious ways.First, it’s a JRPG + life sim, but it doesn’t do either particularly well.  This game could have been a chance to appeal to both JRPG lovers and sim lovers, but instead I’d recommend it only for the niche audience that likes both.  The systems are fun and addictive, but overall pretty shallow.  For example, the character customization and growth is weak for an RPG, and the relationship system is weak for a life sim.The combat leaves a lot to be desired as well.  It’s not terrible, but limited dodge/movement, no blocking, and 0 cooldown on healing items means that the intended way to approach tough fights is to just spam chug drinks to heal your way through them.  This is made more obvious by the fact that your NPC allies seem incapable of moving out of telegraphed AoE attacks, so you’ll spend most tough fights just healing them.  Despite all this, the job and break systems are enjoyable enough for the combat to be addictive despite its flaws.  It’s fun to explore the job systems and try out different classes for different enemies.The generic NPCs and side quests are probably the game’s weakest point.  Pretty much every sidequest requires you to talk to X number of people in town, go to a location (which ends in a fight 90% of the time), then travel back to the location where you picked up the quest to complete it.  The NPC models are also unapologetically recycled like crazy, so get used to seeing the same models everywhere in the game.  The writing can be entertaining for some of the quests, but the reused models and lack of voice acting ultimately makes them feel flat.The farming is probably the element I enjoyed most despite its simplicity.  Planting, watering, and harvesting can be done relatively quickly, and the farm animals are adorable.  It’s rewarding to see your farm capabilities grow as you gather each of the faerie NPCs, and all of the processing stations give you some variety regarding which products and crops you can grow.Ultimately it could have been a great game if it had a higher budget or was in development longer, but it’s overall a fine game that will appeal mostly to players that like both JRPGs and farming sims.  If you like only one of these genres, I’d probably stay away.

_childDocuments_.review: This game definitely scratches the farming sim itch for me and the story ain't half bad either. Took about 60 hours to complete the story and planning to put more in to get all the achievements.Pros:- Looks very nice and runs great on PC. Played the demo on Switch and I prefer having graphic fidelity + good frame rate over it being portable.- Extensive story with a good variety of dungeons, reminiscent of Rune Factory games.- The music is bloody amazing! I loved all the remixes they made of the main theme.- Decent farming sim, with a good selection of crops- Enjoyed some of the character side quests- Variety of classes for combat- Don't need to grind too much for items/moneyCons- Story dungeons does start to drag near the end, grinding the story to a standstill at points (especially chapter 6-7).- Combat is very simplistic and doesn't really offer as much free movement as I would've liked.- The time system feels a bit too fast but you eventually get used to it- Sprinting taking up stamina, which forces you to eat constantly (some may enjoy this type of mechanic but I just found it irritating when trying to get through dungeons)- Side quests got repetitive very fast and most of them were forgettable.- While I do like the majority of the character quests, I would've preferred they shortened it because some of the scenarios didn't really progress the character development/story.Overall I enjoyed the game a lot as a farming sim and RPG hybrid, with it being one of the more polished Square Enix titles I've played. It really feels like a blend of Rune Factory (farming sim), Xenoblade (Story) and Nier (music) while doing it all to various degrees of success. The story could definitely be pushed further as it feels like a pretty standard JRPG plot and the combat could use some tuning to make it feel smoother, but ultimately, it was an experience that was worth its price tag.

_childDocuments_.review: Not much to really to add that hasn't already been said. This is a JRPG with farming elements and not the other way around. I was interested and bought it for that reason since pure farming sim games tend to lose my interest after awhile. I think the part I am surprisingly enjoying the most is the time management aspect. Time always flowing (except when paused) so you're constantly trying to squeeze as much in out of every day. Arrive in town at 7am but shops open at 8? Better fish for a few minutes to earn a tiny bit of money while you wait. Just arrived at a broken bridge that takes an hour to build and it's 10pm? Build it, teleport back home, and have a new path ready to explore the next day.One minor complaint is the beginning of the game is short on save points (you only save when you sleep). This means if you want to wake up, tend to your farm, and then save, you can't. Not until you unlock the save points later (an hour or two... maybe more?) into the story. Kinda made beginning a bit more frustrating since you get all your money, levels, and new crops/etc when you wake up. Really makes the first couple of hours of game play a "just one more day" kinda feel.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a genius-level excellent experience, but it does a really bad job of letting you see that for the first maybe 10-12 hours. It's all about the atmosphere, and once you're in, it feels incredible.It's also definitely a JRPG with heavy farming sim elements more than it anything else.I would put money on this being a Final Fantasy spin-off that, one-third of the way through development, they turned into a farming game instead.- Combat is low-effort and intended to be easy, not being able to dodge or block standard attacks feels bad initially, but it works as a balancing mechanism to make the economy of food vs hunger and healing items matter. If you want good combat, this isn't it, but the combat *works* to make the whole game feel better.- Farming takes a long, long time to open up to where there's any degree of freedom, but when you have everything unlocked it's satisfying to do everything daily. There is some automation, but it's definitely Rune Factory more than it is Stardew Valley. It's a lot more about self-sufficiency and supporting your adventures through money and food than it is becoming a God-tier farmer.- Days feel very short to begin with, but that's to keep the stamina use of sprinting an active decision, and to make upgrading your mount feel good.. After a while, with upgrades and food, they feel pretty long.- The "plot" is annoyingly mysterious at first, but is mostly cliched set-dressing. The real strength, as with any Final Fantasy-esque title, is in how the characters interact. Townspeople and party members feel real and intelligent, suffer unique problems, and the resolution of these across dozens and dozens of quests is easily one of the most emotionally satisfying experiences I've had in a videogame, outside of playing Nier or FFXIV.- There are so, so many quests. So, so much dialogue, and it's all at least pretty engaging.- The negatives, like lack of voice acting and character customisation, are real and unfortunate. It clearly has too much dialogue to voice act without costing an insane amount to make across languages, but the lower budget of this game clearly isn't represented in its pricing. At $40, this game would be an absolute steal as a JRPG.- There are parts of how it looks that reminds you this is a Switch game with a lazy port. However, on art direction, it carries.- The overall 'balance' of gameplay has been engaging and varied in a way that it's hard to recognise until you realise that it's stolen almost 25 hours of your time over 2 days. This game is like crack.If you like JRPG dialogue, and you like farming, and you like listening to S-tier music and vibing in S-tier environments, this game is for you, and you'll love it to pieces, like I do. If you want hyper engaging combat or super-deep economy mechanics, give it a pass. The worst part is that, sometimes, you might think you're playing an Idea Factory game because of how it looks, but when it comes to the overall experience, this is a fantastic piece of work that's worth your time and money.

_childDocuments_.review: Part baby-sitter the rest Agony Aunt, and you are given a farm.Lost your memory along with quite a few others that you will meet,( but has nothing to do with the same thing).Questing in this game is the worst i have ever experienced in any game ever. you just go around sorting out peoples problems while listening to their life stories, or you will be caring for children as you lead them into dangerous dungeons to play with them or to help sort out the kids problems with each other, Enemy magic attacks can not be avoided and will deal 1/3 thrd of your hp, so is best to let your group take agro, which is not always possible (mostly not) Because your team will not attack even while being attacked and will only attack after you deal damage to the enemy fist, and take the agro instantly.Friendship quests often get stuck in a loop and quest dialogue choices dont matter at all.This is the first game i have ever wished for a quest to finish or to say " please no more" to myself. The rest of the game could be quite good,  Such as the dungeon crawling, If only you had more than a five minute day, After 12 midnight  you will collapse and return home to pay the medic bill for that collapse, only to try and get back to where you was b4 that happened, and try to get there b4 midnight again, You will have to run past the mobs if you can in a desperate run against the 5 mins that the day will last (ok a little longer but not much), if you cant make it in time then you need to teleport home and run back the next day.The farming is OK and it also has that 'destroy crops day' that some others have in their game, Here its called "the quiet" where as its a storm on others. either way the NEED to destroy the players crops are real here too for some mad 'annoy-the-player' obsession idk.Anyway, this game could be rescued if the days where 4x longer and they removed that crop destroyer all together. or even give us more than 5 days warning considering some crops take longer.Well if final fantasy where turned into a farming sim, This is not it. This game would just destroy that legacy.SRY i can NOT recommend this game as a game, but more of a boring  "Agony-aunt" sim, with a farm.

_childDocuments_.review: Managing time, stamina, and food, with combat and map-travel was kind of interesting from a micro-management perspective but overall, the game was a watered-down experience where you're neither interested in the farming nor the story. It's not bad, but it's not good either.Do not get this game expecting a farming sim: this game is more JRPG than anything else. The farming is shallow, and it interferes with the JRPG half of the game and leads to a game that doesn't excel in anything. It takes forever to get to the meat of the main story because of the time & stamina system. It's difficult to make money (especially in the beginning of the game) outside of sidequests, but the sidequests are beyond tedious. They have you run to a house, read a 3-5 minute unskippable cutscene, then manually run to just outside the house/to another house in the same map, read another cutscene, and then manually run back inside the house; loop until the final cutscene. Most other JRPGs at least have you kill 30 chickens to break up the monotony. The sidequest stories started off interesting but themes quickly started repeating themselves, and they eventually test your patience since you're running like a headless chicken from one end of the map to the end to read bland anime sidestories. The combat is a simple mash-run-mash loop with class affinities and a couple skills mixed in. I never enjoyed playing the game, but I never hated it either. It's just...bland.

That said, I do have a few minor gripes. See my original review below for those.----ORIGINAL REVIEW----Well, despite having basically zero graphics options, the game runs well and looks good. But come on Square! You did this with FF7 remake too! Providing options is essential in PC gaming for game preservation and allowing the game to run well on various configurations.No mouse support in menus other than clicking the button to accept/cancel things. In actual gameplay, thankfully, the camera is controlled by the mouse and it actually feels good to play on mouse and keyboard. No ultrawide support, unfortunately. Music is beautiful. Voice acting would have been nice...there is none here. No way to skip cutscenes. Despite these relatively minor gripes the game does seem fun. Runs well on Steam Deck. Easy 60fps with 3-4 hours of battery.

_childDocuments_.review: So many of the negative reviews I am seeing as of 11/5/22 only have around 1 or 2 hours into the game. So I want to give some of my insights after around 8 hours of play.First thing of note is that if you are expecting a game that is MOSTLY about farming, this may not be what you are looking for. The farming in this game is a means to an end. The main draw of this game will be the story, resource management, and time management. You will spend much more time out fighting monsters, or listening to NPC lore than you will actually on your farm. This game is much closer to Tales of Arise than it is Stardew Valley. Now if you like Tales of Arise, you will most likely really like this game.The days are short, and you don't have much energy to work with so managing your time is the biggest part of the game. You will not make it to the end of most zones in one go. You open shortcuts and paths that make your next attempt at an area much quicker. You also need to make sure you bring enough supplies.That brings me to the farming portion of the game. As I said before, the farming is a means to an end. You will farm for money to fund your adventures, and for food to make into meals to sustain you on said adventures. The combat is not super in depth, and is mostly about grinding and preparation. You take a lot of unavoidable damage. Going into a dungeon without good meals in your pocket will force you to turn around very quickly.Those are the main points, but there are a few other small points to consider.Good:The sound track is very good.Most things in the game are fairly simple, so its a good game to relax with.The story is interesting enough to make you want to keep going.The game runs very well. (at least on my rig)Bad:The character customization is bare bones. i.e. you only get to pick gender, skin color, and eye color.The game uses a standard Nintendo control scheme, so Confirm is B and Back is A, and so on.Most things being very simple can sometimes be a detriment, like the combat for example.Most of the time you only get 2 dialog choices, and one of them is usually really dumb.To wrap things up, I am genuinely enjoying my time with the game, and feel like it was worth the price I payed for it. ($60)Its not going to be a life changing experience by any means, but if you like JRPGs, and want to farm occasionally, I would recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow so like I don't understand that day 1 review bombs especially the ones comparing this game to Rune Factory in terms of customization when you couldn't edit your character at all in RunefactoryThat being said this game is very pleasant. If you are coming in this expecting a straight farm game like stardew you will be dissappointed.This is a classic Square Enix JRPG with farming *elements*However you are not locked behind the msq with time gates or anything. You can pace the game however you like and focus on farming before heading out and progressing the main story.This game is very addicting and honestly very good. So yes, I recommend this game esp lovers of square enix titles such as bravely default and octopath traveler.

_childDocuments_.review: Some of the OST in this game are life changing. The first time you're hit with that Quietus OST and look out above the cliff, it really engraves this eerie sense of calm in your mind. It is and probably always will be in my top 5 in terms of musical composition and atmosphere. The game's story is really good towards the end, giving you that feeling when you first played through  and keeps you guessing all the way to the very end.My only gripe with it being that it does start off very slow and somewhat childish aside, it was a pleasant story to experience. The combat, although kind of basic, was decently fun and the skills made each class feel impactful. Here my only real con was the fact that I don't think the farming sim tag does this game any favors, since that was the main reason for me to avoid playing it sooner. This game is more of a solid JRPG with farming as an extra to chill inbetween questing. Being able to farm and cook is a nice touch, sure, but even without that this game would have been great. For anyone who likes JRPGs with a touch of emotion, this game is a must play. Hope to someday be able to play something similiar with a more mature tone. That is about the only thing I can think of that could top a game like this.

_childDocuments_.review: Do you like Harvest Moon & Animal Crossing? Well too bad this game is more like a FF light than any of those actually.TLDR: Harvestella is a fun little diamond in the rough that despite it's short comings as a smaller scale game it makes up for in being a charming RPG take on traditional "farming" games of it's genre. 8.5/10()Harvestella is a very charming game. The art style is very reminscent of FF games and specifically I felt strong vibes from Bravely Default for a more recent and similar (in scale) comparison.Combat is a simple action based system, a bit clunky compared to what you can get from other games, but it does a great job at keeping things interesting enough throughout the length of the game with options for combat reminding me a bit of FFXIII's 'roles' at times being able to swap between them.The dungeons while not immensely challenging keep you going for a while if you do not wish to rush on through and the boss fights are enough to finish in one attempt, but with mechanics to keep you engaged for several if you mess up a bit.The farming is straight forward and scales with the story of the game somewhat, so don't expect to farm out everything quickly.()

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr I can recommend it on sale (currently at the 9 hour mark). It takes a few hours for the game to open up some of it's potential, but so far it's really good. I have a few gripes that some other people have stated (limited voice acting, lack of reliable dodge mechanic on combat, shaky & sluggish start), but 9 hours in, and it's very fun. Farming is just a sped-up version of what you get out of Harvest Moon and Rune Factory since many crops only take around 3 or 4 days to grow, with some just being overnight. Combat doesn't feel overly hack-slash thanks to the Job system, but you take a ton of damage constantly thanks to the dash mechanic being underwhelming, and sluggish imo. To deal with that, however, you can manufacture food and items from the crops you quickly grow into consumables that restore health, stamina, and your food gauge. It balances itself out if you actually take the time to farm.As for the intro, the first few hours to the game drag; it feels like they didn't know how they wanted to start it, which leads to basically an awkward exposition dump, and an hour-ish long tutorial of different things. Not at all helped by the lack of voice acting in dialogue. It feels weird to not have just little snips of voice acting through out dialogue, and instead have the voiced companions speak here and there in the dungeons. It just strikes me as such a weird decision as of how to include voice acting in the game; it feels barely there. As usual tho, the music in Square Enix games does not miss, so that's a plus. So far though, the lack of VA work has been my biggest gripe, which is a very good thing in this case; most everything else in the game is either enjoyable, or generally doesn't bother me...aside from the price.In my eyes, you CAN NOT justify this game to me as a full $60 (as of review time). Get it on sale when it's discounted, even by 10% if you feel like it; it's a good game, don't get me wrong, but this game is $50 max. So far, it just lacks a little bit more QOL to justify a full game price imo. All in all though, good game so far (as of time of review).

_childDocuments_.review: Due to Steams newer policy to only allow 2 hours of gameplay before making the game unrefundable, I put in one hour into the game. To be honest, 1 hour isn't USUALLY enough to try a game out. But in this case it is. There is no dodge mechanic, the game in the beginning kinda feels cheap, there is no voice acting (edit: I found voice acting, once. Talking to an old granny blacksmith. And it was only a goodbye and hello), jumping is pointless as there is nowhere to really jump to, the fighting is SUPER basic, Gathering is as easy as clicking with no animation to show that you have harvested anything (mining, lumbering, etc), & worst off most the townspeople are just npcs. _childDocuments_.review: TLDR: A great JRPG that seamlessly incorporates farming mechanics into the genre, but starts slow and feels strangely tight on budget for its starting 60$ price tag.Personally, I loved this game; my own enjoyment was above 4/5 stars, but I think its really something where your mileage is going to wildly vary. I definitely didn't love it at first, mostly because I went through every single townfolk quest ASAP, which is where the game's worst parts show; low number of character animations, NPC models, lack of voiced dialogue, and lots of reused music. I still found myself excited to keep playing though, egged on by new recipes to make, plants to farm, characters to meet, all that. The slowest part of the game is also when you're recruiting your party, and each new member additionally brings a new job for you to use. I'm sure people aren't clamoring for another JRPG that starts slow and feels great by the end, but I'll spend the rest of this review explaining why this game was good, I promise.I alluded to this earlier, but the farming is a consistent high point in the game. Its simple, of course, but still gratifying; everything you do on the farm feeds into combat, like how you make all your own items to use during combat.I liked the cast, and all of the 2D art and character designs are fantastic. I mentioned the townfolk quests earlier, but all of the character quests were great- much more interesting storylines that also teach you about the game's world, and are also just in shorter, more digestible conversations than the townfolk dialogues. Overall, the game was pretty, though sometimes the seemingly low budget shines through. The music was another high point for me, even despite tracks getting reused often. I don't have many games I've played to compare this game's combat to, but I didn't feel any particular way about it. I'll take any JRPG where enemy encounters are seamlessly integrated into the world you're exploring, but perhaps that's a low bar nowadays.The story goes places. The game is presented as typical fantasy, but I should warn you that it veers into sci-fi a fair amount. I was drawn in by it, and found it uplifting at times; it's pretty anime, though, and I could see some people reading it as trite.At the end of the day, I'm going to reccomend this to JRPG fans, especially those who have played life sims before as well or just enjoy some simple pleasures. I don't think this game stands as some staple, but it does feel a little bit like an underappreciated title, and it's had good sales in the past.
_childDocuments_.name: HARVESTELLA

_childDocuments_.review: What this is: A really fun JRPG with farming elements.What this is not: A farming life sim with fantasy elements.If you're expecting a Rune Factory rip off, you may be disappointed, but this game isn't trying to be that and it holds up on its own, with a very unique and enjoyable take on the farming sim genre.The farming element is minimal and simple: it's your primary source of money and not particularly time consuming, as you don't really need to actively maintain your farm outside of watering your crops, which is quite fast.The day/night cycle is also short, but it's not a problem, as it primarily exists to break the gameplay into bite-sized segments and provide an avenue for advancing the story. The dungeons are designed with this time limit in mind and work out well, often pressing you to go just a little further to find the next shortcut before heading home.Combat is interesting, with the job system providing a lot of flavor. It seems like it's action-based, but those elements are minimal, feeling similar to turn-based combat, but in real time. Neither you nor the enemies can avoid most attacks and there's no stagger, so most encounters come down to numbers and strategic use of abilities and items.Overall, this is a very enjoyable game that succeeds in breaking the mold and bringing the RPG aspect to the forefront.
_childDocuments_.name: HARVESTELLA

_childDocuments_.review: First and foremost- don't come into this game if all you want is a farming/life sim. You'll be disappointed.What this is is a JRPG with Farming Sim elements. It has a lot of the hallmarks- farming, unlocking new areas through quest/tool/house progression, a fishing minigame... but when push comes to shove most of your time is spent doing a series of story based JRPG style quests. This isn't a bad thing by any stretch, but certain QOL elements and even main gameplay features of a farming sim are missing. Take relationship building; similar to Tale of Two Towns or Trio of Towns- there are multiple different towns, each with different people who you can befriend. However; only key people. Unlike a normal life sim where you can befriend everyone, the befriending here happens through a series of side quests- which slowly level up the love of specific party members. Much more similar to an RPG. Normal people, even the shopkeepers who sometimes seem like they'd be interesting to get and know just... don't talk to you outside of work. Ever.Farming is interesting, but instead of having one massive field from the get go- you only have a very very small field that you need to upgrade. Unlocking new paths doesn't require a single tool upgrade, but a craftable item. Point is this game certainly has its issues. BUT.If you take the game as a full picture of what it is, so far I really like what I see. After a slow build up similar to most JRPGs, the gameplay reveals itself as quick but still relatively deep. Quest lines/Side quests- even with non-friendable characters last over multiple (up to three) separate sub quests. The rewards for said quests all seem relevant and useful (mostly due to how little money you will find yourself with for a long time; but you still make progress.), I found myself engaged most of today with playing the game, and while it wasn't exactly what I expected I look forward to what else is to come.Please read this review, make your purchase choice accordingly. It is an expensive game, no doubt, and I do think it could do with a QOL/PC relevant patch; but so long as you love both JRPGs and Farming Sims in equal measure and wouldn't be disappointed by any balance of either? you should do well with this game.Edit: Played a bit more now. Still stand by my initial review. Must say while the farming doesn't get any deeper; once you start unlocking Faerie tasks it does make it even faster. I think my biggest problem with this game right now is some of the side stories giving really bad "messages"; and me getting more than fed up with the illusion of choice. I know it is a mainstay staple of most JRPGs like this, but just once I do wish they'd make a game like this with a few more branching pathways.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm only about 7 hours in but considering how criminally underreviewed this game is I'm gonna give it a go. If something later significantly changes the game I'll revise my review, though I have heard the game has a lot more going for it later.This is sort of Square Enix's take on a Rune Factory game. It almost feels like an inverse scenario. Where Rune Factory feels like a farming game with a side of action RPG mechanics this game feels like an Action RPG with farming attached to it. For better or worse the farming isn't at all mechanically complicated, and maybe something akin to the original Harvest Moon in its depth. I think this works to the game's benefit because the dungeons and side quests are going to be the majority of your play time. The farming is also very intuitive compared to some Story of Seasons or Rune Factory games, and you'll likely finish your farming and get to town well before any stores open, at least where I am. I saw a few reviews about this but I actually like the idea of a shipping box within the confines of a game like this, I think it's a good way to naturally regulate the game economy, because nearly every rpg has an egregiously bad economy, either it's too easy to make too much money or the merchants have no value whatsoever. Putting a timer and space limit to cash gain kinda makes the shops feel more special. I also think the time economy fits well with this sort of game, though it has been patched to be much more forgiving so it could have been worse in its pre-release state.The combat is simple and easy to comprehend, basically you have a basic attack and a few skill cooldowns, and you juggle job classes to keep the pressure on until those cooldowns reset. Enemies all have multiple weaknesses and you expose those weaknesses to make them more vulnerable to your normal attacks. At least where I am, nothing mindblowing, but pleasant enough with just enough thought involved where you aren't going to sleep. The character animations while they attack and farm are really nice, and are rounded out by little subtle animations such as a small lurch forward when coming to a sudden stop, but weirdly enough during most of the npc dialogue they move extremely robotically, to the point where it's distracting. On that note, this game is very nice looking in my opinion, but is designed to run on a switch. It has pretty good art direction and all of the locations so far are fantastical and have pretty striking colour palettes. The story seems a lot more involved than something like story of seasons or rune factory, and more along the lines of something you'd get from a mainline final fantasy. Even aesthetically it feels like a reimagining of one of the pre-ps1 final fantasies or crystal chronicles, which I don't think is a bad thing. All that being said, I'm not far enough to give an overview about how I feel about the story. The characters and dialogue are all pleasant enough though.The music so far is all good. I love all the town and battle music so far. I think the guy who did God Eater did it. I haven't gotten into any butt rock, but I'm hopeful I'll get some eventually.The game also runs really well on modest systems, and I love when games don't take up much drive space, it's more motivation to keep them installed and poke back into them, and this feels like a game that would benefit from that.Some points I'll take off (that may be nullified by skills and such gained through progression):There is no scene skip to my knowledge. you can't even really speed up dialogue at all. This is a pain if you have to restart a cutscene.The value of a vegetable isn't accessible through the item description. It may be in the encyclopedia but it makes it a little harder to suss out how much I need to ship to get to a target amount of money.Not very much character customization at all. I like that you can specify pronouns and change hair and skin colour but there isn't much past that. Granted, that's more than Rune Factory generally lets you do. I know that's probably not changing in a patch but I would like at least to be able to wear my class outfits outside of dungeons. I think just that would add a little bit more of a personal touch.

_childDocuments_.review: Its definitely pricey if you value it by game hours, but it has one of the best ludonarrative experiences I've had in a while. Its writing for characters is standard for square enix games and the slow burn of story as MULTIPLE PARTS OF THE GAME was slowly foreshadowing and building up to a very VERY intense reveal was just really refreshing for people who paid attention. Culminating in a final battle with real emotional weight as this game finally pulls back the blinds to show you the real underlying message of the game. An underlying message that really is iconic of square enix titles, calming nostalgia of previous titles and a firm moral (not just ethical) outlook. Game is good despite its flaws, and best described as an RPG with lifesim elements tagged on. For detailed review, continue reading.This review contains no plot spoilers.I can best describe the gameplay loop as economy-exploration management. Everything costs money, stamina recovery requires food. Food requires items. Everything costs time. Multiple forms of damage CANNOT be blocked or dodged, therefore hp and stamina recovery items are needed. In its base, the game splits the farming and rpg elements as if they were mutually exclusive...You farm to get money, to farm more. But when you explore, you burn through items and food, meaning you need more money. So there is an underlying economy of action, where you try to differing level of efficiency balance these aspects. But it does help to slow the pace down, along with the faster timespeed actually means you aren't blasting through dungeons in a single in-game day.This gives you time to focus on the slower aspects of the game. Taking in the scenery, doing all the side quests and character bonding moments. Crafting gear and upgrades, planning your farm layout. But this is where it begins to show its issues. You can only build on the farm plot, processing machines take up farming space, you have limited decoration options (practically only different types of fences), your farm is massive but with very little to do (which makes me assume there was cut content in some areas). In essence, the "space for play" is a lot less than other life-sim centric games like story of seasons, stardew valley, rune factory.This is why the game is more RPG than life-sim. Especially when story characters have VERY LIMITED daily routines, there is no gift giving, no birthday calendar, no town events, etc... From a gameplay perspective this was very disappointing to me because I was expecting a Rune Factory made by Square Enix. Instead I got a ARPG Bravely Default with light farming elements.But did I play through to the end? Yes. Did I enjoy my time? ALSO YES. The story really is what saves the game. Apart from nice graphics, art, a gorgeous musical arrangement, and multiple endings.I can very vividly remember multiple quests. Sister Claire's quest chain and Cherie/Lyn's quest chain, just to name a few. That's to show how varied the writing is, and usually its because side quests do have surprising weight to them at times. A simple fetch quest can turn into an intervention for a lost soul, or just be meme-worthy content. It really does vary, and this is where the main marketing point which partially confused the life-sim fans. This is where the life-sim comes, where you find out about the lives of the people that live alongside Quietus (which is also very seldom mentioned in quest lines) - since people see Quietus as a change in seasons much like a winter coldsnap and just live through it.Most negative reviews I'd reckon would come from the lacking life-sim aspects. Yes, can confirm there is a marriage like option. Not sure if you have kids, and it does allow for any-sex partners. But its not a major concern, as what really feels lacking is the post-game life-together moments. As once you get to post-game there really isn't much to do. And the LACK of life-sim elements to flesh out the day-to-day really starts to hit you. There really is just adventuring and finding all collectibles and post-game dungeon. As compared to Rune Factory, which the developers HAD EXPERIENCE IN, there was a lot less content to justify playing past ending Quietus. Which really is a shame because after such a beautiful ending you kind of wanted to see the world grow past it, explore the remaining story elements and dangling plot threads, do more for the towns etc...That's why the full price really hurts. Because at that price I was expecting Rune Factory AND MORE. But I got an expensive but well-written game storybook that lacks post-game support for longer playtimes. I really do hope that there is post-launch support and expanded content WITHOUT PAID DLC. Because right now it feels overpriced. Only buy at full price if you want to tell square enix to make more games like this, but even now it still feels like a cash grab at times as I really felt that they had the capacity to make this game even better...

_childDocuments_.review: Requested a refund.Start the game, you get to choose your gender:Male => only female body shapesFemale=> only female body shapesNon binary => only female body shapesfrom a pure dev perspective, it's just outright laziness.Now you want to reflect progressive and inclusive movements in your games? Last I heard, gender is not the only component to identity, it's one part of it.If you want to be inclusive and go beyond a lame attempt at it just to create a buzz then just let people fully customise their characters however they want.You have several games where you give a lot more customisation options, but for this one you just decided to slap 3 genders labels to look cool and you jut stopped a labels, this is just a big farce and an actual insult, don't treat identity matters so lightly.I personally will absolutely not settle for "oh look at Square Enix, it's lame but they tried, that's nice".Next time, let people that have these matters at heart handle it, or get advice or whatever, you have the money to do it right.Finally SE, gender is a complex concept nowadays, that extends way beyond body shape and gender labels.Look at Blizzard and World of Warcraft, they dropped gender choice altogether, giving straight away body type choices.It is the perfect approach? Not sure, but it felt a bit more thought through.I used to be a Square Soft fan, things were never the same since after ff10.Most of their recent titles just left me feeling meh, convoluted stories, flexing tech muscles, generic combats systems, forgettable characters, bland worlds. The fragile human touch seems gone. It's a machine under pressure, not a team of passionate people anymore.Harvestella is a big no for me, if you get me angry after 10 seconds, what else will frustrate me later?And for 60 EUR? no Thanks.

_childDocuments_.review: Harvestella is a life-simulation RPG where, as the protagonist, you wake up in Nemea town during the season of death known as Quietus. Now that it has passed, you will lead a life of self-sufficiency by growing crops, cooking, and crafting to get by. All of this will help you enhance your skills in real-time battles where switching jobs during combat is key to overcoming them. Will you be able to overcome threats that arise and figure out the truth behind this world's creation?Harvestella is another JRPG from Square Enix that focuses more on living a normal life as a farmer rather than fighting. While the farming and life aspects do exist and can help, this game is first and foremost an action RPG. I find it to be quite enjoyable even though the combat system is less detailed than other real-time systems found in other games. But will this be a game you can enjoy on the Steam Deck?I can happily say the answer is yes! Harvestella is able to run out of the box at 60 FPS and it felt incredible. Playing this in my hands with the Deck's gamepad felt like a perfect fit. I did notice a couple spots where battery would drain more, but these were far and few (mostly in town). To mitigate this, I set a TDP of 9. This did drop frames to 58-59 in some areas, but I wouldn't have been able to tell if I didn't see the framerate bar.I did notice that setting the framerate cap/refresh rate down to 50 also helped save even more battery and keep the game feeling buttery smooth. Bringing it down saved about 3W, which added about 30 min to an hour of overall battery life while bringing temps down by 4c-5c. For a minor change like this to help and still keep the game feeling smooth is definitely recommended.There are some pre-rendered cutscenes that don't run correctly, so using Proton GE 7-43 (we have a guide to Proton GE on our website) fixed that. Otherwise, I experienced no issues at all!It also appears that some objects in Harvestella don't produce shadows, which makes looking at certain scenes feel off. The biggest one for me is the farm in the beginning. The rocks don't have any shadows and because of that, feel like they don't belong and were just models placed in the scene. It isn't the end of the world, but it is definitely noticeable.Harvestella is another example of Square Enix absolutely crushing it with Steam Deck support. The game is a good time, but what makes it even better is the near-perfect performance on the Deck. Since the only thing that needs to change is Proton GE, this game gets a perfect 5 star rating, but doesn't quite hit Best on Deck. Luckily, Harvestella is still a great game to play on the Deck, but due to needing Proton GE, which doesn't come pre-installed on the device, we can't give it our coveted badge.

_childDocuments_.review: (Note: I am not finished with the game yet, so this is just based on my experience so far.)Although this game was not on the scale that I was expecting, I was pleasantly surprised by how much I was enjoying it. There were a lot of mixed reviews when this game launched, and I definitely agree with some of the complaints, but I think that some of the simplicity in this game is not all that bad. Pros:- The game is absolutely beautiful-- from the environment to the music to the character art.- The story is surprisingly interesting as well. It may be a little generic, but it's definitely got me paying attention. I haven't skipped through any of the content so far.- The side quests are interesting on their own as well. They're not related to the main story per se, but they definitely tug at some heart strings.- I love that there are so many jobs to choose from and that it's easy to swap back and forth from one to another. - Game runs smoothly on PC and I don't have any issues with character movement or abilities.- The boss fights have been very interesting so far! An example of some battle mechanics that I ran into reminded me of things that I experienced in a Heavensward dungeon from FFXIV. - Although the material gathering is very simple, it honestly reminded me of how gathering in the Tales games.Cons- There is barely any voice acting in the game. You'll hear bits and pieces of voice acting in the game, but there is none in important cut scenes. It's probably one of the biggest disappointments for me.- There is barely any customization aside from what you're able to do in character creation. Your outfit changes depending on the class you're playing, but that's about all there is, which really sucks.- Character models look very outdated and don't fit how detailed the background and environment are. Kind of reminds me of old FF/Square games, which is like...okay, but I feel like it could have been WAY better. - The price tag for the game is honestly quite high. I feel like if way more voice acting was added and the character models matched how much detail they put into the environment art, then $60 USD could be justified. I'd definitely wait for a sale or something.

_childDocuments_.review: Harvestella is a hard sell. It's lighter on farming and customization content than the games that clearly inspired it, and the combat is so bare-bones as to feel wildly incomplete, but there is a fantastic backbone here for something greater down the line. Farming is largely background noise to the many sidequests and meaty main story, all of which vary wildly in terms of entertainment. Some quests are genuinely well-written and touching, while others are humdrum time-wasters, but thankfully the former generally tend to outweigh the latter. The main quest is a mess of half-realized characters and ideas pinned against a surprisingly excellent world. The locations don't stray far from the usual four elements, a JRPG staple that apparently just won't die, but I like the general town designs and the backdrops make for some terrific art design, though admittedly that's in the distance and rarely up close.Coming off playing Rune Factory 4 last year, the combat and skill systems are a complete joke and the worst part of this game. The enemies are brain-dead, the combat has no weight to it, and the rudimentary skill trees are bare branches, at best. I do like the passive bonuses you get from your party members' side quests, most of which are solidly entertaining.It doesn't do enough to push the genre forward to rank it higher than Rune Factory or Stardew Valley, but there's definitely fun to be had here if you liked those games. I did, and I'm entertained enough by Harvestella to recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Plenty of bugs. For example, in Echo of the Bulla (Map), there is a bridge that is in JP text when using the EN translation. There are the semi-bugs/continuity errors such as of a party member running off and if you return to town right away, that party member will be wandering around town (but if you return to the dungeon, the party member will still be in a rush and ahead of you in the cutscenes). Similarly, the quests that pop up upon doing so will also treat you as having already been through the area.In a later map, if you return right away after an event, Jumping off certain areas can result in the minimap not updating, thus showing the wrong minimap. Combat is meh. Could use plenty of QoL such as making it easier to swap targets mid-combo (the enemy has to physically enter your combo area for physical attacks, for example, and the attack will fizzle if in the middle of magic charge and the target dies). Your AI allies can be rather dense as they won't attack if you have not attacked for a few seconds even if being attacked. FEAR enemies are mainly tough because they have a very short leash, some will literally despawn while fighting them. Otherwise, they are actually absurdly easy (but time and stamina consuming) to kill if you know how to deal with their attacks (there is a trick to beating one as soon as you find one, but it does require you to be at relatively full stamina and be fairly early in the day).Farming is okay, but very basic and feels more like it was just an extra part of the game. Two mechanics from farming games though...My biggest two annoyances are the stamina and time mechanics. Time is very fast here and stamina is fairly low even with being able to recover stamina with food. Almost everything consumes stamina. The dungeons are clearly meant to be cleared in short bursts of running to the next shortcut and then ending the run about there.I personally hate the fishing minigame due to how heavy RNG is.The art and music is beautiful as expected of a square game. Only issue is that events such as talking with an NPC will often reset the music, causing it to break when you enter and exit a conversation or in some cases, after a new line.As for the story... it is kind of annoying. . Outside of that, this is basically your typical storyline that Square often uses . Not much in terms of surprises since the 'twists' are given away fairly early on for the most part. Your choices don't matter for the most part as the same things seem to happen with only small variations in the text and/or the how/why.
_childDocuments_.name: HARVESTELLA

_childDocuments_.review: I was a little apprehensive about this game with it being a completely new game from SE but it turned quite good. Clearly this game doesn't have the same depth as Rune Factory when it comes to the farming and crafting but that could come in a sequel and what is there is quite sufficient to last the whole game. What needs to be understood is this is a game in which you are supposed to reach the end in a reasonable amount of time, not some endless farming game. The story is quite decent and is definitely one of the strong points. The characters are pretty cool and each have their own questline. The music is also pretty great as you might expect from SE. The one dark point which I saw in many other reviews is combat. Indeed for an action game being unable to dodge and/or guard is really disappointing.So to sum up Harvestella IS a good game and worth the money (although I got it on sale at 35). If they could add some depth to the gameplay and improve the combat to make it more dynamic and responsive it could be a great game.

_childDocuments_.review: For those who wanted a super animated, over the top Final Fantasy or Nier game, this is not your game.For those who wanted a comfy, nostalgic game that reminds you of the days when you played on the PS2 or PS1 and enjoyed story and character arcs, this is for you.It has the job classes. The cute stories. The heartwarming positive enforcement. And the puzzles you're looking for. This is the game for the person who just wants the comfy gameplay that doesn't ask for much beyond learning your class and farming.I give it a 9.5/10.It'd get a ten if I could marry.

_childDocuments_.review: I understand why most games don't have demos. No one wants a team to waste resources and time that could be spent on the game itself to put together a demo. Unfortunately, HARVESTELLA is a shining example of why we still need demos to be made. Instead of having an opportunity to get a feel for whether or not you like the game early on, HARVESTELLA puts you on very slow rails and funnels you through a long intake to get to all of the elements of gameplay in a way that feels like it's intentionally built to block people from returning the game if you don't like it. By the time I realized this game did not speak to me, it was too late and I had played the game for way too long to realize it. This would have been fine if it had felt like I'd spent that amount of time playing the game, but it did not. Imagine the introduction we could have had instead if the game had not been designed with this in mind. I played it for longer to give it a chance, but even now that I'm approaching the second ending I can't bring myself to keep playing this. It just bores me too much.It just felt very deliberate to me, so I'd say to anyone uncertain enough to check the reviews: just don't risk it. Even with a nearly half price sale (iirc) I feel like I got ripped off for what I walked away with.Personally, HARVESTELLA feels like a game where developers looked at aspects people like in the recent farm sim craze, and balled it together without care at making either the farming or the combat feel good to play. Because it just doesn't. It's sad, because while the concept of using magic or technology while farming are not unique, it always has the potential of being refreshing to see. For me, the gameplay itself just felt tedious and empty, sorry. I was really hopeful for this game, but it just never delivered the same satisfaction as other games in the genre.I also think something was lost in the translation of the character arcs. There are definitely themes for the companion characters that feel like there was something creative there, but the execution of the dialogue and cutscenes just feel like they fall flat. Overall, there are better farm sims, and there are better combat games, and in trying to be both it feels like HARVESTELLA has failed.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a beautifully designed, intricate, and mysterious world that's ready for players to explore. I'm really enjoying it, with a few major caveats that I hope will be corrected in patches - mainly the controls are laggy and will not trigger, or will trigger only with a delay.FYI - The game does not feel particularly open or sandbox-y, all of the areas are accessible through specific paths and there's not a lot of ability to climb over or around obstacles, though this is mitigated by a transportation system. There are some awkward gating mechanics to keep you from exploring too early (literally the intro has giant translucent gated off areas) and the story can kind of step on immersion quite a bit.Despite all that, the world and story are imaginative, beautiful and fun, so I would recommend getting it - though you might want to wait for a few patches and a sale.Pros: -Really beautiful world design-The storyline is intriguing and unpredictable, I'm very interested to see where it will go-The character designs are great-The music is very atmosphericCons:-This is the biggest: the controls were definitely not designed for PC and they are super laggy. While you can customize them, it's somewhat hard, due to how they're set up. The right and left click particularly seem to be reluctant to trigger when farming or gathering which is immensely frustrating.-You can't gather at your own pace, there are limited harvestable nodes that appear each day.-Almost immediately, a long dungeon quest kicks off that is Super Urgent to complete, and locks out other areas - but it takes days to complete, and considering you've recruited companions who just seem to wait in the dungeon for you to come, it feels extremely fake and un-immersive-Only a few of the village NPCs have lines or interactions, the rest are flat and nameless - this is not the type of game where you befriend them all-The farming, crafting, building seem to take a bit more of a backseat to the plot than I expected.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Not currently worth $60. I'd say worth $35 at most at this point. Wait for sale or for fixes/features. It honestly feels more of an rpg with farming on the side. Square Enix isn't exactly known for adding features to single player games, so this game may never get better.The main features that need fixing/adding first:- The atrocious character creation. Choosing a gender is pointless as each only have the same options, a male and female body type and four skin colors. Except the male body type still looks like a school girl, especially with a long ponytail sticking out the side of his (her?its?) head. And there are no options to change hairstyle. - There's no option to skip dialogue, which make side-quests that much more annoying.- There's not enough to do/ not enough customization on your farm. It feels like basically a plant-water-fight sim. The coops are in a predetermined location as well. The monotony gets boring quicker than combat in FF12.- The faerie voice acting is creepy as heck. Every time I leave the farm or use a tool powerup, the terrible voice acting rears it's head (every single time, not even just every once in a while). Here are some more pros and cons.Pros:- You don't need to fill up your watering "can." That's nice.- There is no annoying minigame for fishing. Let's hope they keep it that way.- You can craft from items in your storage, which is just a nice quality of life feature- Great artwork and lighting- You can save often enough to not be much of a pain to stop abruptlyCons:- Terrible voice acting. Even from the first time you hear it, it sounds robotic and amateur.- The dialog choices they give you are virtually useless and have no meaningful impact at all except to be annoying.- You can't skip cutscenes or dialogue.- You need stamina to fight, and you can actually enter a boss fight without any stamina (they are NOT escapeable).- The auto-targeting will randomly switch to a further away monster for no explicit reason.- And when you do switch targets, your whole party switches with you. So if you want to save time on attacks, forget it.- The jumping feature is also virtually useless, except for getting around small useless hurtles around town that shouldn't be there in the first place. Otherwise, there is no other reason/need to jump at all. - Your party can't path very well, and many times you will find yourself fighting alone because of that.- Some crops practically give you no profit at all, such as the carrop (spelled correctly) that buys for 105 (or 95) and sells for about 115 o.O  ... It's good for making health drinks I guess, but I prefer foods as drinks do NOT increase your hunger meter. And just for context, most upgrades will cost in the thousands, so a 10 profit is laughable at best. I don't buy carrops, I just sell the ones I get from quests/mail. - And the cucumbie takes roughly 10-12 days before you make ANY profit off it.- Combat is bland. You just do your singular primary attack ALL the time and occasionally do 1 of 3 or 4 other attacks when they are off cooldown. - You take way too much damage, and the only equipable defense you can get is two ring slots. So if you want to conserve healing supplies, you have to be a mage full time and attack from a distance while your party soaks up all the damage.- It is pretty monotonous. There is not near as much to do as with games such as stardew valley. I get bored playing this game real fast. No customization. No mining (except picking up items in monster locations). Pretty much nothing except plant-water-fight-repeat. It actually feels more like a regular rpg with farming on the side. And the combat isn't anywhere near as satisfying as a normal final fantasy game.

_childDocuments_.review: Harvestella is a great game well-worth playing--so long as you know what you're getting into.I'd almost call this my favorite farming sim, but this is honestly more of an action RPG with a farming sim attached. If you love story-heavy games and can find joy in the mechanics of a simple ARPG, I'd highly recommend it! Sadly, the demo is only on Switch, but I'd recommend getting a feel for if you'd enjoy this kind of game first (whether playing the Switch demo or checking out some early gameplay).I've personally put 140+ hours into the game (I played through the whole game and 100% it on switch first). And I don't regret a second of it. Something about the story and characters really pulls me in, and the music is phenomenal.As for my trans friends out there: oh my god does this game make me feel so good and seen. Like, I can choose whichever body and voice I want, but the very first choice is what my pronouns are. The euphoria I felt finally being able to play as a non-binary person in a farming game (without mods) is immense. And your chosen pronouns don't show up too much (that I noticed), but it feels so good when I see a character refer to me as them.If you choose to play Harvestella, I'd definitely recommend playing this version. It plays much better on PC (and if you have a good PC, it looks great at 120 FPS). And the game thankfully has an option to switch up the select/cancel formatting for controller (the default controls make circle on a PS controller select). I'm not certain how the keyboard/mouse controls are, but it feels very good to play with a controller.Again, please, please, PLEASE be certain you know what you're walking into when you buy this game. And if it interests you, don't pass this game up!

The only thing that changes are your "pronouns". You can change your hair and eye color. Otherwise, you play a female character. In the first hour, you get to play about a total of 10 minutes. I haven't gotten much further at this point. I am pretty disappointed in it so far. Maybe I'll check it out again in the future, but I have no desire to right now.

_childDocuments_.review: Simply put, I feel like this game is poorly marketed. But it is a lovely letter to classic JRPG's and that includes Harvest Moon. But go in expecting a JRPG with farming content and not a farming sim with JRPG elements. The farming sim element is good, but so many other games do it better, but this is a lot more story focused and you'd reserve your farming portions of the game (most of the time) to the start of your day. But it does feel like there's pieces to this game from multiple JRPG's without nostalgia baiting. You can definitely tell what games influenced this.The plus points: - Great story with some interesting twists, some you can see coming some you might not. (though at time of writing I've not finished it, but 5 chapters in)- Compelling characters (IMO)- Decent gameplay- Good side content- Decent farming, though not competitive to any other game's farming. - Great soundtrack- Good sense of nostalgia without being nostalgia baited or bland. - It has a job system- World Map with a mount, a submarine and an airship and with some parts to explore. It's small, but heyThe negatives: - Some see it as a negative, though I disagree that it is one, but it's barely voice acted. For a £50 you might expect something fully voice acted. For me, it meant it felt more like the era of JRPG's I loved the most and I feel like it'd probably have had mediocre voice acting if it was fully voiced, but I figure put here as it might put some people off- It's straight up a Switch port to PC, there's no attempts to improve (or even alter) the graphics on PC. - The target cursors don't line up correctly on a 21:9 monitor- Battle controls can sometimes be clunky, you can get animation locked into an AOE. - Character customisation, it's hard to even call it that, You can only affect name, gender, body-type and different colours (skin/hair/eyes).For me when I was trying to decide to buy the game it was a question about what I would be willing to pay. For me? I think it's worth it because I am getting the enjoyment and hours out of it for a £50 game. However, it lacks some qualities I think I'd come to expect a £50 to game to have except maybe on the Switch. But overall it's a charming game that I found compelling and would happily recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: HARVESTELLA

_childDocuments_.review: This game is like a great mix of a AAA game and indie game combined. You and your companions raid different areas in an action rpg style. You only can level up when you the day has ended and you rest in bed. Besides the fighting areas, you'll tend to your farm, mostly to make great meals to eat during combat which give you different perks. Or creating different things at the work bench, like bombs and stuff to enter otherwise blocked off zones. My biggest problem with this game is it wears out it's welcome. I've played almost 60 hours!!!! When I was at 40 hours i was wondering when I was going to wrap it up.. then I got the bad ending and I pushed forward to the good ending. I just think a game like this should of wrapped about between 30 and 40 hours. Other than that, this is a solid game.
_childDocuments_.name: HARVESTELLA

_childDocuments_.review: The game isn't bad. It's just hard to recommend with other games that do what it does better. The fact that it definitely looks like a Switch game doesn't really help (although the art direction is good).The farm sim comes secondary here, and is really only a means to make money and food for yourself, so if you're looking primarily for that, you're better served elsewhere.The adventuring, meanwhile, is frustratingly limited by the in-game passage of time. Yeah, you can grab teleports and build shortcuts to get back to where you were in most cases, but you're still cut off for sleep. Eventually I found myself starting to ignore parts of my farm because I didn't want to source more seeds... I just wanted to get back to the dungeon I was working on.Combat itself feels... rigid. You have to learn how long your animation locks are in order to not stand in telegraphed boss attacks. Otherwise it's just a matter of swapping jobs, pushing your buttons, and carrying enough healing items.There's a decent story buried there too, but even that I feel like has a lot of concepts that are just borrowed from other games at this point. I say this even after progressing into .All of that said, if you have tons of patience and don't mind your grind being broken up like I do, this might be worth your time. I just don't think it is for most people I know.
_childDocuments_.name: HARVESTELLA

_childDocuments_.review: Pro'sGreat music scorePlenty of content Nice storyAcceptable graphicsTime managementLGBTQ+ representationController supportCon'sTerrible combat systemJob system isn't goodWeak character creationFishing sometimes takes too longFEAR monsters reset too easilyExtremely limited character voicingWorld map feels tinyHarvestella is another prime example of why Steam needs to overhaul its reviewing system,  this game isn't  bad by any means and is quite playable, and even fun but its got problems that are unfortunately core issues that are fundamental to the games design which, unfortunately are unfixable but if a sequel is made,  I hope the feedback is taken into consideration and improvements are made, because Harvestella is definitely a worthy addition in the Harvest Moon/Rune Factory style of games. Harvestella could have been a classic if it had more time to grow,  better combat and more personal touches like different clothing, more important characters which have birthdays or mini-events at certain times basically combining some of the interesting fluff content from games like Harvest Moon/Stardew Valley with the combat system of Rune Factory, would have definitely helped this game.GameplayHarvestella to me,  feels more like Rune Factory Frontier than any other life/harvest simulation game I've played and that isn't exactly a bad thing really,  however that being said it does have significant issues which hold the game back from truly shining which is the combat,  it's just bad.   Sure you have the job system which could have been great, the issue is that most jobs are basically there to counter monster immunities and if you have the wrong 3 jobs equipped, the fights get increasing more annoying and fighting FEARS?  Forget it,  because they not only easily reset they hit extremely hard and the dodging/evade system in this game is useless and broken,  almost all monsters basic attacks are nearly undodgable and have little or no warnings they are about to attack which means you are almost always taking damage and require you to take food to heal, especially on tougher FEAR battles or end of chapter bosses.Graphics and sound are roughly about average for 2022, the graphics are not blistering eye candy level but they get the job done, they almost reminds me of mid PS3 era graphics,  and the sound effects are average too,  the music though is definitely above average with some really good catchy tunes.   Plenty of side content to complete, most of it usually rewarding with crops and a bit of money.   The farming side of the game introduces the time management aspects since you have limited time, do you spend your day farming/gathering materials, do you catch up on finishing quests and/or side content?  Do you head to the dungeon to farm job points?  You have limited time each day and deciding how to plan out your day.Overall,  Harvestella is above average for sure, its not perfect at all and rough around the edges in places but the foundation for a sequel with everything improved across the board is there.  I especially like the inclusion of a Non-Binary gender,  the representation is appreciated and kudos for the developer for including it as an option.Hopefully with some updates and patches, Harvestella can become a farming life sim that can rival the established and greats in this genre, right now - it's promising.
