_childDocuments_.review: The short version of this review is that I absolutely love this game.  I am fairly sure I am basically at the end of the story now, but I think I'm at a good point to be able to talk about it.First off,  as many others have said, this is a JRPG with effectively a farming game side activity.  The farming never really plays an important part.  It's pretty nicely implemented, and I enjoyed it, but it's not "important".  At some level, the farming is just a way to get materials and ingredients for making healing items, money, and misc items.  That said, it is pleasant and a nice thing to do on the side when you need a break from whatever else is going on in the story.Now -- I find the stories to be wonderful.  Most of them hit me in the feels the same way Final Fantasy 14's stories do, to the point where I wonder if it's some of the same writers.  The main story has a lot of interesting twists and turns and gets pretty intense and heavy as it goes on, in proper Square Enix rpg fashion.  It really does remind me a lot of a Final Fantasy game in that sense.Side stories are not typically your 'go kill x monsters' fare.  In fact a lot of them are literally go to a place, talk for a bit, go on about your business until you hear from the person to meet them for the next part.  I found it to be a good way of storytelling and giving you a lot of back story without making you do a lot of repetitive tasks.Non-main quests are .. well they're a mix.  None of them are frustratingly repetitive or boring, and some of them are also still just 'go talk to this person and come back', but they are generally all cute and give good rewards.  And as someone else mentioned, there is actually a surprisingly large skew towards "helping kids" in those stories.  I enjoyed those quests, but even I noticed how many were like that.All relationship stuff is done through quests, and to my knowledge there's no marriage or anything like that.  I am fairly positive that after I am done with the epilogue that there won't be much else to do and I'll probably call it at that point.  But I've enjoyed every minute of it and I hope to see some expansions or something at some point to bring me back in.One last thing regarding the combat -- one thing that stood out to me about the combat is it felt a lot like playing FF14 (or really any other mmorpg tbh) -- meaning it had the typical tropes of tells on the floor to show you where an attack is going to go -- "get out of the red" kind of feel for most battles.  I found that to be interesting in a single player game.  I felt right at home so to speak as a fan of FF14.I found Harvestella to be a wonderful experience and I would absolutely recommend it, but go into it knowing it's more JRPG than Farming Sim.  =)Edit: I just completed the rest of the story and went a bit further and I wanted to correct something above.  You can indeed marry.  (I haven't tried it but it's an option)

_childDocuments_.review: A great Harvest Moon type game with ARPG elements. I've been a huge farming sim fan since the original Harvest Moon came out on SNES and I have to say I enjoy the relaxed nature in this game. I don't ever feel like I'm fighting the clock. I love games like this that give you a choice. Will I fish all day today and make some good money, Will I work on the farm? Should I explore and forage to create some decent food so I can explore a dungeon further? There is a lot to do here. The story so far is a step up from similar style games. While not groundbreaking, there is a plot and I'm interested in seeing it to the end. Combat is very fun, and I would say the best in the genre. There is a ton of depth so far in the skill trees and I'm only scratching the surface so far. I know a lot of people see the Square Enix tag and are expecting AAA quality and you're not going to get that here. This probably had 1/10000 of the budget a Final Fantasy has but I have to say so far overall this game already is one of my favs in the ever growing farming sim genre that has exploded over the years since Star Dew Valley hit the scene. TLDR, if you can overlook the character customization and are itching for some farm sim fun with a sprinkle of Square Enix, you're going to like this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly I really like it, it feels both similar and different to games like Rune Factory.Early thoughts :- Time feels fine, I don't feel rushed to do anything, I've seen a lot of people complaining about travel time but it's been improved since the demo and fast travel from other areas to your home is a thing, and mounts are a thing to increase overland travel. Not sure if mounts work when you're not on the map- Feels a bit less social than games like RF/Stardew/Story of Seasons but I kinda like that cos gifting everyone and talking to everyone each day is a chore. It seems like relationship progression in this game is through side quests with the character. Not sure if romance is a thing.- Combat is pretty fun, probably the best of all the farm/life sims I've played but not as good as an actual action game. You can unlock 12 jobs in total I think, and equip 3 at a time which you can switch between when exploring- Farming feels decent, no boring stuff like refilling watering can. Tool progression seems to be linked to the faerie job things you unlock after completing chapter 2?, when you complete a certain amount of tasks they give you stuff, like in my case I got a charge hoe move to till 3 sections of land in one go, not seen anything about crafting tool upgrades- Story seems interesting so far- There are mounts but I don't have one yet cos I'm a broke scrub, the first one looks like a cute fluffy jackalope which I need- Fishing seems like decent income when you have time to burn- It doesn't look like the farm itself is very customisable but I might be wrong. It looks like the areas where you'll keep the equivalent of chickens and cows/goats are fixed, but I think they're upgradeable- Same for house, not sure whether it can be customised yet- Graphics in general are really nice for a farm/life sim but I do not like the character's running animation (I play female) when in combat areas and all the female characters are built weird, super spindly arms and rather large posteriorsI don't think I'm gonna get bored of the game any time soon anyway, but I'm not sure how long the story is and I don't know if there's an "endgame."

_childDocuments_.review: I really like farm sim games. Even before buying this game, i read in the reviews that I should (despite the name) not expect a real farm sim game, but instead a game that has some farming elements, but that is about combat and storytelling. I was fine with that. However, when trying the game out, my impression is that yes, it's not a farming game; but the combat and storytelling are also not good. Thoughts:- The game is from the controls very obviously a console game. The controls are clunky and extremely un-intuitive on pc.- Farming is extremely simple and just a chore.- Story consists of lenghty cut-scenes that you can't skip or really speed up, and which I found boring.- You spend a large amount of time running through the world, to do the same 2-3 things every day (for example: always pick up a plant at a certain spot). You are limited by stamina, so after running all the way, you can only complete a few actions and then have to run all the way back.In total, in my playtime, a typical ingame-day consisted of the following: I get out of the house. Want to do a boring farming-score, but get interrupted by a cut-scene which I can't skip which is boring and does not advance the storyline - the impression is "the developers thought there should be a cut-scene here, but they had no ideas for actual dialogue". (Often, the cut-scenes are basically characters muttering to themselves.) Then I run to a forst to pick up one herb. I am out of stamina - i go to the city to do stuff, but find that there is nothing to do. I go to bed. Next morning I wake up, same thing (including the senseless cut-scene). Run all the way to the resource, pick it up, run back again, still nothing to do here?! -> Yup, nothing to do. Off to bed it is then. Repeating that 10 times. Uninstalling. Finally, writing this review.If the above sounds gripping and exciting to you, or if you really, really enjoy generic console-RPGs, buy all means, buy this game. If you (like me) are used to actually good PC games with some depth (be it in the mechanics or the story), better buy a different game instead.

_childDocuments_.review: The protagonist wakes up amid the mysterious phenomenon known as Quietus, in which toxic dust fills the air and threatens the lives of humankind, but is unable to remember who they were or how they got there. (Cliché, but at least there’s a far more interesting reason for the amnesia than usual.) A whole bunch of other WTF stuff happens and the protagonist has no choice but to try to figure it all out if they’re ever going to have any kind of “normal” life.      • I didn’t personally confirm this, but according to others, the game doesn’t play well via keyboard.      •  involves: JRPG-style main story and sidequests, JRPG combat, farming, fishing, gathering/mining (mechanically the same), animal caretaking, collecting, crafting, and cooking.     •  is real-time action-oriented, but slow-paced compared to others. HP and stamina gauges to maintain. No random encounters; enemies are on the field and can be avoided by dashing. Only story-related enemies lock party into an isolated grid. Player has no direct control over party members. Party members cannot heal, so that is solely the responsibility of the player. If party members are defeated, they revive themselves after a bit of time passes. No “Game Overs”; if the player is defeated, they appear back at their home with the local doctor lecturing them about being careful. Player can switch job classes during battle to have access to different abilities and elemental attacks.     • There is no difficulty setting, so ? Probably not. That’s just my opinion though. General fights are easy enough, but some of the bosses can be fairly hectic. A more casual gamer might need to level up significantly in order to survive boss fights. Optional bosses can be very time-consuming.    •  is available post-main story. There are eight human main characters that are conveniently all single and available for the protagonist to romance. The player can only romance one character; sorry, my fellow polyams. After the partnership commences, that character moves in with the protagonist. It is not particularly romantic and is definitely not a focus of the game.    • 3 possible . 2 bad endings & one good/true ending.    • Lots of mysteries to figure out.     • Extremely addicting. Messed up my sleep schedule. Had dreams about it.    • Upon completing parts of the main story, faeries come to the protagonist’s farm, and I like their system of unlocking things that improve the gameplay.     • I really appreciate items being clearly marked in their descriptions as “used in crafting/cooking” or “to be shipped for money.” Otherwise, I hoard everything not knowing it won’t be useful later in the game. (An exception being juices and jams. For some reason, they’re labeled as items to sell, but some juices/jams are needed for a few recipes.)    • Items/ingredients don’t need to be in direct inventory for crafting/cooking or when going to the smith/builder. Items/ingredients can be taken from storage. Super convenient.    • I like the “secret” thing you can do during Quietus (when the player can’t do much of anything). Spoiler:     • Very pretty settings throughout the game. An autumn themed forest, a cherry blossom town, a beautiful beach town, and a frosty winter town. The water is pretty.    • Lovely, beautiful music.     • The confirmation button on the controller can be changed in settings. As this game was also released for the Switch, I’m glad they put in this option, because using what I consider the “cancel button” for confirming is odd. Every game on the Switch uses “A” for confirm, which is where “O” is on a PS4 (or 5) controller. That’s the cancel button.    • Criticisms of organized religion and blind faith.    • Philosophical narratives on what it is to be human and the worth of humanity’s salvation/preservation.    • Character creation is disappointing. Very limited. (Though, at least there’s a non-binary option for pronouns.)    • Even though the sprinklers hover in the air, you can’t plant seeds directly beneath them.    • Several instances of “repair bridge” prompts being left in Japanese. That’s sloppy work for a AAA company.    • I encountered a bug with the jumping ability. I don’t know the trigger, but at one point my character couldn’t jump like she was supposed to. Had to restart the game to fix it.    • While there are a decent amount of NPCs with darker skin, not a single one of the main characters is dark-skinned. There are eight human main characters and couldn’t even get a token.    • While there are random NPCs that are referred to as “they/them,” none of the main characters or even important side characters are non-binary. I always find this situation weird when devs give the player the option to be non-binary for their character, because it means they’ve acknowledged the existence of trans people, but are still unwilling to put them further into their story.    • During the “Return to Sender” sidequest, an NPC refers to Castle Lewis as the Castle of Illusion even though people outside of the main characters don’t know that’s its true name.     • Illogical and asinine decisions/reactions from grown-a$$ adult characters. This happens repeatedly throughout the game in sidequests and even by some of the main characters. It’s different when little kids make unwise decisions due to their inexperience and naivety, but grown-a$$ adults doing completely nonsensical or downright dumba$$ things is a weak excuse to further a plot point. The most common example is an adult character running off into a dungeon by themselves for whatever reason despite having no fighting skills; it’s like they have no sense of self-preservation whatsoever and that’s horribly unrealistic. What you need to take away from this review:  The most common reason for negative reviews for this game was people b!tching about wanting one genre and not the other. You have to be a fan of both JRPGs and farming sims or you won’t have a good time with this game. Understandably, people get cautious about getting hybrid games because a lot of times they're poorly designed. I feel like this is  an example of that. I feel both genres were integrated very well for this game. Everything unfolds at steady pace for more casual gamers to adjust to JRPG elements, if they’re unfamiliar. The only issue might be the difficulty of combat, but otherwise, I definitely recommend this game to people who enjoy both genres.

_childDocuments_.review: Despite a slow start, not quite being the farming sim on the box, and clear budgetary constraints, Harvestella manages to be more than the sum of its parts, making for one of the most unique, moving and interesting JRPG experiences I’ve had in recent memory. If you like stuff like Nier/Automata’s worldview and environmental ‘feel’, with writing that feels like it could at times be by Yoko Taro crossed with Kojima, phenomenally atmospheric music with elaborate battle themes, Persona-style social links, Xenoblade-esque extensive intertwining character side quests, Virtue’s Last Reward/999-style asides and exposition, 13 Sentinels-style  sci-fi themes, Rune Factory-lite farming mechanics, hack and slash dungeon crawling with pretty decent light puzzle mechanics, please give this a shot, or at least wishlist it for a sale. It’s the sort of game which would have probably been lauded as a truly one of kind 3DS or PS2 era title. Unfortunately, the $60 price tag and being a Switch port (and square seemingly just not sending out review codes) I suspect led to a lot of people glossing over it, and the direct comparisons to farm/sim contemporaries don’t really do it a lot of favors especially early on. After completion I would have easily paid $60 had I not been apprehensive about the quality, but for most the $40 price point is probably better.Just a really genuinely special game with some rough edges and a lot of heart.

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic JRPG + Farming Sim. Coming from FFXIV and Stardew-like games, I wasn't sure if I'd like a game like this. However, it's absolutely amazing. Please, do not let the *mixed* reviews bug you, almost none of them are from people who have gotten past the tutorial chapters.The game really opens up after Chapter 2-3, and my pesonal to-do list in the game is a mile long. :DSome of the pros:+ Love love love the characters thus far. They feel pretty fleshed out and real, once you get to know them. Dialogue is a bit cheesy sometimes but I don't mind it.+ The sidequests with townsfolk are pretty enjoyable. A comfy mix of humor and Trauma, along with decent rewards for doing so.+ Big fan of certain QoL things, like being able to pull crafting/cooking materials directly from your storage instead of needing them on your person, or not having to stand still while watering crops. Makes the farming/crafting aspect feel a lot more fluid.+ The classes are fun and I can see the FF bleeding into the class flavor. Haven't had a chance to play everything, but I really like the Mage and the Pilgrim.+ The collectible systems really start to pop up as you complete Chapter 3. Very Happy. Dopamine go brr.+ The simple fishing minigame is a nice break from the hell of Stardew fishing. Put the rod in, wait, pull it in and get a fish. Is it basically just a loot box? Yes, but it's chill gameplay. + The world map is explorable and also has little secrets! I won't spoil but there is more there than just the big stuff, but that comes later. :)+ The actual farmsim part is on par with Stardew. Not sure what the in-game will look like, but the plants, season rotations, daily maintenance, sprinklers, etc., are on-par with other games in that vein.+ The music is stellar. Every bit as awesome as one would expect. + I like the character art in dialogue.Now, the cons:- Not much character customization. Hair color, eye color, and gender [male, female, nb]. I'm personally okay with the options, but you may want more.- Your outfit is fixed. Apparently this is normal in many JRPG games [and other SE games]. Hopefully they add this in some capacity later? Each job/class *does* have different outfits, but you always revert to the default when you're not in combat areas [like dungeons]. This can be a bit jarring when you first start.- I think menus and inventory management could use a bit more love, but it's not *super* lacking. Definitely something that I think will improve with time, provided the game receives updates after launch.- The combat can feel a bit samey sometimes, but the boss fights are very cool and very much feel like ff encounters (down to the aoe markers, lol).Overall, I very much recommend this game. I find it worth the $60 price tag, but ymmv. Worst case, wait until a Winter sale and grab it then, you won't be disappointed. <3

_childDocuments_.review: Its a cozy JRPG with some farming attached to it. The focus is on the rpg side more so than the farming side.Stories for NPCs are told via sidequest and so far i have enjoyed them all. Most of them are chain quests actually. The farming aspect is more on the simple side but at least i was never pressed for time or have i ever run out of stamina. The main story so far is very well told and the music is really good! Personally i love the art direction however it is a switch game and it shows. considering the time i invested and still going to invest i feel it was worth the money. There is a lot of content for players available if one gets past the first 2 or 3 hours. I think ppl that liked older harvest moon games or prefer a more story focused title with sim elemants will enjoy what harvestalla has to offer.Edit after 30ish hours:If you are over the age of 30 and crave a good old fashioned JRPG think 90s early 20s, this is it. Seriously, the story is so well done, the side quests are so well done, the characters are so well done. This is by far the most Jrpg or the Jrpgs that i played in the last 3-4 years. Think of the farming as a fun side activity that you can spend hours with (such as chocobo breeding) or just spend enough time to get money and health potions (drinks). Its really is the JRPG side where the game really really shines.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't normally make reviews before finishing the game, but there has been a lot of negativity in some reviews and in the discussions, so I wanted to give you an idea of why I am so addicted to Harvestella.Background: I like JRPGs and Farming sims, but I can be rather critical of poor ones, which seem to float around more recently.Pros:+Great balance between quests, adventure, and farming+The story (even small characters) really shines+The world thus far oozes with personality+Well stylized art+Fantastic sound track+Pretty well thought out character progressionCons:-Mediocre Switch port (lack of quality settings, graphical limitations, controls)-Combat is rather simplistic (though still good for farming sims)-Farm is not fully customizable "Cons" I have read people say that I don't think are issues:~Can't manually save until a couple days in (saving at night early on is more than sufficient)~Lack of character customization (Never super appealed to me and I'm used to Harvest Moon/ Story of Seasons, with no options)~Mediocre game for 60$ (Console games go for 60$ for over a decade, if you can't afford games, wait for a sale)Overall, the simple yet rich story from all of the characters really gives this game a charm. Mechanically, it isn't perfect. The combat gets kinda spammy and some of the animations take too long, but the FFXIV AOE circle dodging is fun. The combat is better than Rune Factory imho. The farming is also solid and the events with the main characters are what I always wanted from a farming sim. Basically, this game isn't perfect, but it is a beautiful, well written, and fun farming adventure.

_childDocuments_.review: The game feels dated, and not in a nostalgic sense. It's like someone took a game from the PS3 era and added some modern polish to it. The music and art direction are top notch because SQUEENIX, but the gameplay loop lacks depth. Also very slow to start up in terms of progress.Sure, as I got further, some of the inconveniences (i.e. lack of Stamina) are addressed by mechanics introduced later. However, the pacing for this was slower than I'd like. Story elements being slowly introduced are one thing but walling off in-game mechanics that feel almost essential behind hours of gameplay/cut scenes/dialogue? It makes it hard to set a goal and can turn a good portion of players away.Regardless, something about this game keeps me coming back. Is it the hot doctor lady? The yet-to-be-explained story beats? The game definitely has that "Final Fantasy" aesthetic to it.

_childDocuments_.review: I will say that this game is not worth $60, buy it when it is on sale. I absolutely love this game though. The high points is the music and the story. _childDocuments_.review: So, very early impressions, but here are my thoughts for anyone who is thinking about buying now...TLDR: Good game, it appears to have been developed primarily by Live Wire, not SE (Live Wire is a more indie team, 11-50 employees, solid track record though) so don't expect a triple-A title. If you're not a hardcore fan of JRPGs and farming/life-sim type games, wait for a sale ($30 would be reasonable value imo).For any who want details, so far, this feels like a very good game, best production values I've seen in farm/life sim games, and its most directly comparable to Runefactory. The game looks great, the music is great, and the combat is probably the best I've experienced in the genre. Unfortunately, the game has very little voice acting, not sure I've heard anything outside of combat/exploration, and I'm unimpressed with the English voice over. I'm still early into the story, but I like what I've seen so far, its more typical of a JRPG than a farming life sim (disclaimer: I'm a fan of that). So, we've gotten a well developed fantasy world with lore, factions, and interesting party characters. Unfortunately, the more minor NPC's are generally underdeveloped compared to something like Runefactory or Stardew (nameless npcs, reused models, no backstorys, etc). I'd say Harvestella builds a more interesting world, and Stardew builds a more interesting community, imo.As for the farming gameplay, I'm still making up my mind on that. At this point it feels workable, nothing special compared to something like Stardew, but deeper than what I saw in Rune Factory 5. I'm not far into the game, so I'm very open to my opinion changing.It's also overpriced at $60, Square Enix and farm/life sim fans like myself will probably get $60 worth out of it, but for anyone else, I'd say wait for it to go on sale for like $30/40. Don't expect a triple-A title with this one, it wasn't actually developed by SE, but by Live Wire, an indie dev known for Ender lilies. That said, this game feels more like a double-A title (SE may have pitched in on development), but still has probably the best overall production values and writing I've seen in the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: So I've put a good 30 hours into this game and honestly, it's nothing special? I love games like Harvest Moon and Stardew Valley, and I love Final Fantasy, but this attempt at making a hybrid just comes off flat. It feels like two mediocre games merged into one, except even they are quite simple.The farming side is basic. Just two animals you can add to your farm, basic upgrades and crops you can unlock. It feels separate from the RPG side except for the food you can craft that can heal you or provide buffs in combat, but even that could be replaced with basic potions. The JRPG side has a generic storyline with generic characters and terrible writing. There are job classes, but these are again basic with just a few special moves. The combat itself is a button mash. The side characters and 'romance' questions are boring. The farming and JRPG side just don't complement each other at all.The whole game feels cheap and rushed. Parts of the game haven't even been translated properly. There's no animations for actions like mining. I really WANTED to like this game, but 30 hours in, I can't be bothered to see it through to completion. If you're really curious about this one, now's the time to try it while it's on sale. It's not worth full price.

_childDocuments_.review: I need a 'Maybe' option to go with the Yes/No on recommendations. I like this game, but I'm not gonna lie - I did expect more, somehow. - You will have a slow start - every farming sim I have ever played is a slow start. So it takes time to get more seeds, expand your farm's capabilities, etc. Some upgrades are tied very much to the main storyline, so getting that upgrade on watering, or the ability to destroy those larger rocks? Painfully slow. - Character creation seems very limited. I'm not sure anything would change with the gender selection, TBH.- The intricate cutscenes you usually get from Square aren't here. Ditto voice acting.- Developing character relationships - again, just not quite the depth you'd want, very scripted. It feels like it leans a bit more towards visual novel, but less options.But... I am enjoying working my way through the storyline, trying to figure out the secrets behind the Seaslight, Quietus, etc. I've got the three Seaslights done, waiting to see what's next as there's been a fair but of foreshadowing. And typically, I pick up farming sims as pleasant timewasters - they're usually kind of relaxed, low-key, repetitive. It has got that chill, stress-relieving aspect. And the artwork is pretty.So my overall opinion? It's not bad, but it is limited, and they could have done better. If you want a farming sim with a mysterious backstory, go ahead. If you're after the sort of JRPG that wows you with its intricate gameplay, don't pick this one. And either way? Maybe wait for the price to go down. I would be more put out if this game hadn't been a Christmas gift.

_childDocuments_.review: Comment the first:  Play this game with a controller, not M&K. If you're not used to Switch controls, there's an option to switch cancel/confirm, and it will fix the issue you will otherwise have. If you are a fan of slice of life / farming / japanese rpgs (all 3. you must like all 3.), you will probably love this game. I love this game. This is not Harvest Moon, Stardew Valley, or Rune Factory. It is in the same genre as those games, but it is definitely its own beast. Does spending about a half hour doing a quest that's mostly just talking to people (in which you reconcile a father and his teenage daughter after a fight over what she's going to do with her life) sound like a good time? (This quest does not exist; it is an example and about on the same level as a fair number of quests.) To me? Yes, yes, yes, yes, yes it does. But I recognize not everyone shares that opinion. The farming loop is good; the mechanics of farming itself aren't tedious. Combat is action-RPG, you don't control your party members, player skill comes in in choosing the proper job/ability for the enemy in front of you. A couple of the boss fights are pretty novel, but the mechanics are easy to figure out. The puzzles are easy but not braindead. The story is better than anything I've played in the genre, by far hands down no question, but it isn't as good as your pure-RPG with a story focus might be. It's good, I love it, but it's pretty cliche and a lot of the story time is padded out with REALLY mundane slice of life stuff (which I enjoy). If "love and the power of friendship saves the world" isn't your jam, give it a pass. If you're looking for cozy and heartwarming and good-cry (my first tears appeared at about the twenty minute mark), you will disappear into this game and nobody will ever see you again.If you enjoy the genre, it's a good entry, especially given you get like a PARTY and choices in combat and actual abilities instead of just swinging a sword. And an RPG story, even if it's not SE's best storytellers (which imnsho are those behind Endwalker, so if you hate THAT take my opinion here with a grain of salt). I mean it's a farming game what do you want.

_childDocuments_.review: I am about half way through Harvestella. When I first saw this game, I saw what looked like a fresh jrpg gaming experience so bought it almost immediately. I saw the mixed reviews others gave too. Personally I think this game is a gem. It is a classic japan gaming experience that has used time elements very well. The graphics are older school but it is lovely to look at. The gaming experience is top notch. It is a game with a combination of RPG and Farming type elements, with a world map you can actually ride a mount around on!Like other games there is the main quest line and  about 36 side quests from what I read. You must do the side quests they are stories within themselves and have had me sobbing at the stories that unfold. The game tends to be gentle in nature it is not hardcore. The rpg elements are minimal to tie in with the farming elements which are minimal too. So not difficult to master. Even though the character customization is simplified too, I dont know why anyone would want a different character to play with while playing this game, as the one given is  perfect :) I like the combat in this game it is fun and easy to master. The creatures in this game you fight are awesome and original looking by the way. The game has a day/night time element which has been done superbly in my opinion. There is 30 days that last about 20-30 minutes per day depending on what your doing. Then there is 4 different seasons (120 days) that affect what you farm and the fourth one which is winter, I have a funny feeling I cant grow normal crops due to it being winter. It will be a fun challenge to try survive without my usual crops and i like this element in games very much. Also each 30 day ends with a natural phenomenum called the quietus. This is a period where you cant function in the world properly so you have to stay housebound while it passes. You have to remember to stop farming during this period or you lose all your crops. Its like a lockdown like coronavirus lockdown was in our lives but in the game. I knew Harvestella was going to be a great game and I wasnt wrong. Even if the graphics are not superior this is a classic of a game that everyone should play. The farming is fun and not intrusive and you dont have a gigantic farm to manage so its nice to work with. Its like a toned down final fantasy game with farming as well. A new concept for me and im definitely enjoying it. The game is meant to be between 40-80 hours to complete everything unless your a speed gamer!

_childDocuments_.review: (((TL,DR: Most negative reviewers didn't get far enough to even know what they're reviewing. If you like farming/RPG hybrids like rune factory, harvest moon, or stardew, this game will probably be for you, but you're going to want a controller.)))Let's get this out of the way first. Most of the negative reviews are coming from people who couldn't wait more than 3 hours worth of playtime to complain about why it wasn't good enough. Until you complete chapter 2 (Which most negative reviewers probably didn't) The game will have you go to bed at 10pm, and hold your hand to a small extent, to which it will let go and let you stay out late into the night afterwards.Yes, the game isn't perfect, it's not a perfect Farming sim, and it's not a perfect Arpg. But the combat can be mildly challenging and also decent fun if you switch up your classes mid combat to take advantage of element types. The farming is fun, and does get better as the story progresses and you unlock the task book which will grant things like food processors, automated sprinklers, and higher levels of tool efficiency related skills. I've seen quite a few complaints about how the farming is lacking QOL features of other farming games, and as a Harvest Moon/ Rune Factory veteran I honestly don't know what they're on about as it's much more fluid than either title's previous entries from the get go. It's a simple system that works, and is fast and efficient as you don't want to invest too much time into your farm (although with latter farm expansions, you could spend the majority of an in game day tending to it)I won't try to defend the abysmal player character select choices or lack thereof, but the characters you meet along your journey are slightly above mediocre, they have stories and relationship levels, and although I'm still unsure if this game has any level of actual romance to it, the game DOES give you flirty options and some characters flirt back. Still too early on for me to know though. REGARDLESS: Even just being  "Okay." These characters are leaps and bounds more in depth than traditional farming sim games. I have enjoyed my time with a few select characters so far, and was interested enough to visit some characters further to learn more about them. The story as a whole (So far) Is not amazing, but interesting enough for me to want to learn more.I have played almost every major Japanese made/ inspired farming game in the last 20 years, and most are often very low budget, or are early access garbage. Rune Factory 5 left a particularly bad taste in my mouth. And while this game is not perfect, it hurts to see a game in this genre get so many negative reviews when it is obviously a step in the right direction and a decently well made one. you're not going to find farming sims that look, play, or sound as nice as this every day, and I'm sure some of the negatives to this game could easily be reworked in an update or mod.

_childDocuments_.review:
In a vibrant and colourful world, players will tend their crops, befriend the townsfolk, overcome threats, discover the origins of the world and the truth behind the calamity along the way. The story begins when the player wakes up in the middle of "Quietus," a calamity that comes with each change of season and threatens all life. "Quietus" A season of death that comes at the turn of each season. Crops wither and the dust of death prevents people from even walking outside. It is said that the duration of Quietus is getting longer each year.

"World"
Players will be able to explore the various cities and dungeons of the world: "Nemea Town," where cherry blossoms bloom all year round, "Seaside Town Shatolla," with a lively bar scene, "Lethe Village," with its beautiful colors of the four seasons, and the snow-covered "Holy Capital Argene." In order for players to reach the "Seaslight," the four giant crystals that govern the seasons, they must cross a beautiful yet rugged path.

_childDocuments_.review: I played this game in full on Game-pass at launch. What can I say that hasn't been said? Hi Fi Rush is an absolute gem. It's not just a rhythm game with a banger soundtrack, responsive combat, and an incredible world with interesting game mechanics and easter eggs, It is a game that can make you fallback in love with gaming. We all know the issues inherent to the game industry, even now this review comes as a result of many people losing their jobs and the great studio behind this game being shut down. It seems like outside of a few gems, no game comes out untouched by bureaucracy, controversy, and corporate greed. Hi Fi Rush is a platformer that reminds you of your early days playing games, it is joyful and fun. It is a bit difficult but rewarding. The ragtag band of characters in here are fantastic and lead you through a fun story that touches on corporations hungry for profit at the expense of everyone else (sound familiar?).I highly recommend this game to anyone with an interest in platforms or rhythm games or just action games in general. The team behind it deserved better but hopefully this game's legacy will live on.

_childDocuments_.review: Hitting all the right buttons at the right time in the right rhythm, Hi-FI Rush is a love letter to japanese rhythm games, pop-punk of the 00's, beat 'em ups' and platformers. Like a breath of fresh air in the heavy dusty air of flopped triple-A on top of flopped triple-A, it drops in at a very humble 30 euros like that cool careless friend of yours that's always late but makes all conversations feel velvet smooth effortlessly.Most of all it feels minty fresh to play a game that doesn't take itself too seriously and has fun with its characters instead of trying to engage in deep thematics and theatrics to strike a cord. The story line does not reinvent the wheel, but you can feel that the developers had a blast incorporating the characters into the gameplay and did so very meticulously.Favorite part: Hearing The Progidy's iconic "Invaders Must Die" rev up as you smash into the evil corporate tower of Vandelay and start beating the crap out of hordes of cafeteria robots to the beat. A feeling i can only describe as maniacal smiling and intense goosebumps.Don't sleep on the fun. Plug in your stereo, kick up your feet and grip your joy pad tightly as this game absorbs you into the video game equivalent of mid-00's Avril Lavigne and No doubt.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is the music video you have in your head made real.Despite being a rhythm game, it's incredibly friendly to those that may not keep the beat as well. Rather than punish you for being off rhythm, it rewards you for being on rhythm. And it does everything it can to keep you on the beat. From the distinct music to the pulsing UI and environment to the toggleable rhythm assist bar. It wants you to get in the zone and stay there.Naturally for a rhythm game, the music is vital, and the song choices are phenomenal. Each track is perfectly suited for the level and keeps you pumped and keeping time while you fight. Even the Streamer-Friendly replacement songs are still faithful and just as good if not arguably better than the original.While the characters and story aren't deep, they don't need to be. They're still interesting, charming, funny, and over the top like a Saturday Morning Cartoon. It knows exactly what it wants to be, and it goes all the way with it, which leads to some genuinely funny moments.There is so much polish and detail put into this game that I can't even get it all out off the top of my head. _childDocuments_.review: Verdict: My favorite game this year so far. I'm happy this genre blend (Rhythm-Action) is going on a roll lately, although it is a pretty niche genre,but for me Hi-Fi Rush solved the biggest issue on the rhythm side: Example of active punishment is breaking or off-putting sound when you miss, like the standard rhythm game.Sure, you will still have some sort of a punishment in form of final score rank at the end or progress block for certain sections, but there is an accessibility option for that progress blocker (Easy/Normal only) and I appreciated that.Some way this game could improve if there will be a sequel (fingers crossed):1. SoundtrackWhile I do think the overall soundtrack, both OST and licensed are  (I even bought the OST), it lacks the iconic OST for the game (e.g Devil Trigger/Bury The Light from DMC5). Working with a higher caliber composer hopefully will be a huge improvement. More banger soundtracks are always welcomed!2. PlatformingJumping as Chai takes time to get used to, because it's more on the bouncy side. I basically just double jump and/or Jump-Dash to pass between platform.More magnet-grapple platforming is also pretty good for me.3. Option to lock-on targetsIn this game, magnet grapple to the robot is basically your "target lock-on". In the sequel I hope there will be an option to manually lock on the target.4. Misc: Achievements or "speedrun side"Not all of the dialogue/setpiece are skipable. This will be quite tiring if you are planning to 100% this game, because you basically have to finish this game at least 5x to 100% it.Extra credit if the achievements clears faster if you do the harder difficulty first (e.g if you achieved something on Hard, it also applies to Normal and Easy)PS: I think the game will ultimately benefit on the replayability factor if this is improved, because action game emphasize more on replayability to make better score.From the The Game Awards side, I would love to see this game nominated for Best Action and Art Direction!

_childDocuments_.review: HEY~ HEY~ HEY~ CHAI!Is this game for real? A triple-A title, that is neither a remaster nor remake, released in 2023, technically polished day one, no micro transactions, no battle/season passes, and zero marketing hype?! I must have stumbled into a time machine taking me back to the PS2 era of games. No, I'm not dreaming! Hi-Fi Rush is real and it fully deserves all the love and attention in this modern gaming world of excessive monetization.Hi-Fi Rush knows what kind of game it's supposed to be. The characters are charming and don't take themselves too seriously, the cutscenes are snappy and to the point, the cell-shaded animesque visuals are pretty.Between fights, the action is broken up by very light platforming and puzzle segments that, once again, test the player's sense of rhythm. This is my only real complaint because Chai's jumps and air dash are too stiff and heavy for some of the precise platforming required so it can be frustrating when you frequently misjudge the distance needed to clear. Thankfully, they don't overstay their welcomes and are nice palate cleansers before you jump into the next high tempo brawl.If you're still on the fence, try the game out on Xbox Game Pass then support the devs even more by purchasing a copy here. This game will make you feel like a kid and is worth being on a bucket list for games. It may have only released in January but its already a strong early contender for GOTY.I give this an: 808/10

_childDocuments_.review: When people say games have gotten worse over the past decade or so, it's because we stopped getting games like this.Everything from the visual style, the choice of music (both copyrighted and music made for the game!), the combat, the short sections of different gameplay entirely, seriously everything about this game, save a few very minor gripes (mainly the platforming at times) is pure good game design.The story is super simple and fairly predictable, but that's okay! I realize that most games we're accustomed to have super complex or dark stories to tell, and there is nothing wrong with that! But wow, is it refreshing to play a game where you can just go with the flow of both the story and the gameplay. I also think it's worth noting that I haven't played a singleplayer game that made me genuinely laugh this much in years.The gameplay is DMC meets BPM, or Metal Hellsinger. If you're like me, that probably already sold you on it, but if you're not very musically inclined that's fine too! While the rhythm is an integral part of the game, playing to the beat only really gives you benefits, you don't really get punished for, say, attacking or jumping off beat. In fact, the game will do everything in its power to MAKE everything you do sync up, even if you know you hit a button off beat. The majority of the combat encounters are fun, although they can tend to feel a bit repetitive when you have 2 or more encounters nearly immediately in a row, but that doesn't happen often enough to really detract from the game as a whole. The bosses, on the other hand, are the absolute peak of this game, in my opinion. Each one has unique music chosen specifically for that fight that succeed on so many levels: They are just good tracks, they match each boss perfectly, especially the songs made for the "streamer mode," some of the songs even give insight into the personality of the boss you're fighting, it's just awesome. If I could add one feature to this game, it would be an option to skip straight to the bosses upon replaying a level, I just love every boss fight so much!At $30 USD this game is a steal, great value for your money in my opinion. This game was somehow able to recapture the feeling of coming home after a long day and being super excited to keep playing that new game you got, a feeling which I haven't truly had in years. If this is the best thing to come out of 2023, then I think I'd be alright with that. The only thing that could be better for the time being, is having more Hi-Fi Rush content from Tango.

_childDocuments_.review: There aren't a lot of games that I can say that I've genuinely loved. Super Metroid, Mega Man X, Wind Waker. Some of the more typical titles that, while are exemplary in their own regard, are almost -expected- to succeed because of their pedigree. And, largely, they did. Some of them stick out in my mind for more personal reasons, but honestly? I felt involved from start to finish. Well, largely anyways. Some parts in Wind Waker I wasn't but that's neither here nor there. Even the newst God of War game, while great, didn't have me fully engrossed in the game.Hi-Fi Rush did.From start to finish, every beat that hit my ears I was entranced with this game. It is gorgeous, stylized, incredibly polished, and engaging in every way. The first few levels take a bit to give you your entire toolkit, BUT, and I would really like to stress this when I say this, you never really feel like you're missing out, and more importantly, the game doesn't make you feel like it's dragging its heels. A little overlong but not in excess, and to be honest I didn't really care. I was too busy grooving and shuffling to the beat and smiling from ear to ear.And that's what makes me so happy, so overly joyful about this game.  I was having FUN. Not just in playing it, but in watching it and listening to it and EXPERIENCING it. The animation is top notch and it does things that should be standard in character animation and presentation from here on out. For being a game that completely came out of nowhere, it is a treat and a joy to experience.Now, I will say that from start to finish, it is at best, an 8 hour game, not counting post game content.  And some of you might scoff at that and think that you "deserve" more time from this game for what you spend.I say you're wrong. For being a short experience, there is an unbelievable amount of polish, and every aspect of the game flows smoothly into the next, transitioning seamlessly as some of the cutscenes do and it is nothing short of masterful.  It is a game that knows EXACTLY what it's about and the amount of love and care and FOCUS that has gone into it is genuinely spectacular.Honestly, I could ramble on for longer, probably write a treatise on why this game is worth your time, but I won't. I'll simply cap this off by say that you should absolutely give Hi-Fi Rush shot and get down with the rhythm in your own time. I promise it's worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely amazing game full of soul and creativity, it's no wonder this game hit every other out of the park when it released in the same time frame.As someone who doesn't usually play rhythm games, this one is the one I REALLY love and am currently in the process of 100%ing, even despite the bethesda publisher tag, the actual devs deserve the money.Hi-Fi is a rhythm based combo game, there's scores, combos, good music and the world reacts to it. There really isn't anything else like it on the market and I could go on way passed Steam's limit to praise how everything feels great in the game, so instead I'll just mark some very minor things I had an issue with.1. There were some cases where, despite varying the times to make sure, for some reason beat-hits were just not triggering midfight, I have no idea what was going on since during fights I ended up testing and they always acted as if I missed them. I haven't had this issue for awhile though and I know it wasn't a skill issue since I was hitting the beat-hits out of battles consistently fine.2. Visual clutter can get a bit much, there's a minor bug where the end-hit effects will lock in and follow you around which can sometimes obscure enemies, another thing is certain partner attacks do alot of effects and can ALSO obscure enemies and important info. These are both(yes even the bug) usually due to the player's actions but the bug should probably be fixed at least.3. Some annoying boss attacks. I won't spoil much but there's 2 bosses, one early and one late, that have certain attacks that I felt we're frustrating for different reasons. One of them straight up prevents you from getting close or else you get damaged, what makes it frustrating is they sometimes stay in this mode for random amounts of times, sometimes too long and you're left there bleeding score meter and time. The other boss has attacks that have random variants that cause an additional lock-on laser, if you're attentive you could dodge/parry these, but it felt very inconsistent and sometimes he'd put these lock-on lasers out of sight. Combine that with visual clutter and sound clutter if you're doing anything big and you could get hit in the back completely unfairly.Despite these main issues and some VERYSUPERMINOR ones, the game is a fantastic awesome game. Easy 9.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: A true masterpiece of a game. The charm, the fun, the comedy, and the sheer quality of this game never lets up for me. Going into this I expected to find a pretty generic and cookie cutter hack and slash game with gimmicky rhythm mechanics, but immediately after seeing the premise for the game of Chai having an iPod fused into his chest. I was hooked. Everything after was just so much fun. FUN in a video game. Crazy. I haven't had this much FUN in a video game in a while now, so I am extremely happy to find one that fills me with so much joy when I play it. It is just so satisfying while also being genuinely challenging, a real hard line to walk, but one that is executed very well here. Story wise it's very simple, but for me that doesn't matter because of the strengths of the characters and their interactions. After finishing the game their is also so much more to see as you hone in on specific play styles and improve your combat capabilities. Overall, Hi-Fi Rush is not only my GOTY for 2023, but a game I will use as a future base line to how I evaluate games in the future. It has so much going for it, but most of all it feels like a truly passionate project that the people who created it, truly wanted to make. I find this game very inspiring and gives me some valued hope for the future of gaming.Plus the soundtrack RIPS!

_childDocuments_.review: It is so difficult to review this game. It's a weird mix, that may not work for everyone, but will work very well for others.GOOD STUFF: Extremely good.BAD STUFF: Extremely bad.Among all the serious world saving games that make a seasoned veteran gamer approaching 30 mostly indifferent towards the newest boring oh-so-epic universe that needs saving, HI-FI RUSH is a colorful, out of the blue game that is like no other. It's charm comes from it's genuenely good, albeit childish humour, it's surprising ability to constantly pleasantly surprise you with gameplay and(!) story twists, and it's highly varied storytelling method that constantly jumps between in-engine 3D animation that goes on during gameplay, 3D inengine animation cutscenes, 2D cartoon style animation cutscenes, 2D animated comic book page style cutscenes, is just such a joy to experience and it's so fluidly and creatively mixed there is really nothing else like it. Imagine this:You take Spiderman: Into the Spiderverse (and the following movies in both animation style, theme, and vibes) into Shrek, then put them both into Ghost in the Shell, then mix in a little of actual physical comic book you hold in your hands. It is incredibly lighthearted while dealing with very serious topics that are thought provoking and serve as rich discussion material such as the role of marketing trying to take control of your life, the role you play in supporting this machine, the somewhat stereotypical cyberpunk evil corporation theme, even some family tragedy (which could've been handled a little better at the end though), and somehow HI-FI RUSH is the most life celebrating, funny, all positive vibes and fun game I possibly ever played. Excellent writing, good humour, creativity in boss design, great music, fluid gameplay, it's all there. And not only you can pet the cat, later you can even dress it up.It's... *chef's kiss".Imagine you take Devil May Cry or Metal Gear Solid as action games, and make a slightly watered down version of them that makes it more accessible for everyone, but the depth you lost (which is not much, the the game is absolutely worthy to stand among those titans) is made up with RPG elements you may be familiar with from NieR Automata. The good kind of RPG elements: no loot, no gear grinding (pun intended, you'll see), no leveling, none of the crap that doesn't belong to a good action game but plagues the genre anyway. It's *cheff's kiss*. While it may appear so, this is no casual game on higher difficulties: invincibility frames matter, and the game is openly talking about these kind of tech-stuff on character chipset customization (passives) and combo descriptions, however, on easy difficulty it is also very accessible to anybody! Your first playthrough you won't be able to afford unlocking every move which also sort of adds a little "build" building feel to the game, and it's a positive element that you can also sell combos and special moves that you may not like so you won't acciendly spend your hard earned special move meter on those. I mean, the 3 games I compared it to: those are masterpieces competing for the throne of action games, also they are my most beloved games I think very highly of, so HI-FI RUSH earning a positive comparison with those for gameplay and content richness (see below) is the highest praise I can possibly describe this game with.However, this is also a musical, rythm based game and much of your success will depend on getting in sync with the music and the animations of various enemies in form of QTE's, which... can be hard to deal with.This game has a lot rythm elements to it like many musical games do: shoot on rythm otherwise you do no damage in Hellsinger, or your stage is being created from your music in Audiosurf. It has a lot in common with those, except the action gameplay is only rewarding you with additional score and AoE effects on your attacks if you stay in rythm. However, it adds QTEs. If you've played every game in existence that has QTEs and you combine them all together, this game is towering above that abomination with how many QTEs it has, and it's so extremely annoying if you are bad at it that it's frustrating beyond to the point wher kills the joy and positive vibes and experience but turns it outright POISONOUS. That's a word I don't use lightly. You get this hard earned victory in a bossfight, but no! Enter: weirdly timed QTE where the game throws at you 5-20 or even more QTE button press prompts, that not only you have to press before they disappear, you have to wait a little and press the button with perfect timing(!), timing can vary(!), and the pop ups are randomly thrown all around the screen(!) and may god have mercy on your soul if you play this on a big TV like I do. You miss out on entire cutscenes, in fact a very large number of otherwise so well coreographed cutscenes that are important for the flow such as the final showdown with a boss, even the final boss. This is spammed everywhere: elite enemies execution, phase switching in boss battles, simple "break the wall" buttons... imagine retrying the same very hard QTE 40 times over in the middle of a bossfight and you lose a little health every time, locked into replaying this animation 40 times! 40!! It's poison that I felt slowly turn my fun and joy into physically hurting sorrow. Honestly, it's a game killer if you can't get your head around this, and it's possible, but not easy at all and requires dedication from you.13,5 hours. Levels vary between 20-60(!) minutes+ 4 difficulty levels (normal highly advised for veterans of the genre even, it gets really hard later on if you start on hard!)+ Additional 2 unlockable difficulty levels (one where low combo score - if you let it drop - kills you, and one where missing even a single beat kills you)+ Unlockable secret levels (after first playthrough)+ Arena mode (after first playthrough), which sadly has a very strict timer that is incredibly disheartening to play this, it should be far more forgiving, and actually requires a patch that stops the timer when your big special move "cutscene" animations play out, because otherwise you are just not supposed to use them and that feels very bad when you face this situation.+ Challanges that reward ingame currency, and also enrich your home base (there is one!) graffiti wall!+ A character customizer opens up that let's you mix and match indepth customize Chai, the main character, and also all friendly NPCs with full costumes.+ There are little side objectives in some missions. For example, a birdpoop cleaning robot is very annoyed with the nearby pigeons, so you have find them all hidden nearby and get rid of them, and who knows, maybe you get something of value in exchange!+ All of this is supported by Achievements!+ None+ Ingame currency not purchasable.+ There is a huge difference between games designed to be grindy to unlock stuff, and a game well designed to be highly replayable but also keep offering unlockable stuff for quite some time during that. This is the latter, so when I say there is no grind, remember this when you feel like you can't buy all combos during first playthrough.+ FREE 30€! At full price is half price of an AAA game, and this is very much one that puts those to shame.+ Flawless KB+M support+ Flawless X360, X1 controller supports (friend gets Xbox button prompts using Dualshock though)+ No crashes, rock solid 60 fps on an old config.+ Photo Mode!- 3D inengine cutscenes can desync image and audio. Set "cutscene quality" to speed over quality (not much difference).

_childDocuments_.review: Hi-Fi Rush is a proper joy to play all the way through, no strings attached . It is a *damn* fun game, that wears its genre and medium with pride - it is a videogame-ass videogame that feels like developers from the PS2 and GameCube era were plucked from the past and made to make a game today. Which is at least half-true, as Tango Gameworks is comprised of ex-Clover and PlatinumGames employees. One of the finest Character Action games out there, the combo depth is insane. Chai practically plays like Nero from DMC4/5, and Tango's DNA comes through strong. Never gets too overwhelming though, game does a very good job teaching its mechanics without being too handholdy. Game trickles plenty of new and exciting things over its runtime, and it all blends very well together. Enemy variety is good, no one battle feels the same. Minor complaints: the lack of a "reset camera behind player" button can get annoying in platforming segments. The lack of a dedicated lock-on button is annoying (especially for Devil May Cry and Bayonetta veterans), but there aren't any directional inputs and the auto lock on swing feels pretty accurate, so you can get by without one. It feels a little too easy to maintain an S combo rating and not as satisfying as you'd hope - double and triple S ratings would be appreciated, or make the S combo rank harder to hit and maintain. The lack of a taunt button isn't really an issue, but having one would be pretty on brand for this game, and especially for Chai :)Slightly more major complaint: Higher difficulties aren't meaningfully different from lower difficulties, just tighter rhythm timing, higher enemy HP, and enemies do more damage. Wave compositions and enemy behavior isn't any different, and boss movesets remain the same, so replays on different difficulties can get repetitive.That aside, Hi-Fi Rush is a fantastic game, and we need more of it, and of AA cheaper games in general. Must play.

_childDocuments_.review: Hi-Fi Rush: A Rhythmic Solid Beatdown Rating: 8.5/10Hi-Fi Rush is that indie game that pops up out of nowhere and suddenly becomes the next big thing. It's a stylish, rhythm-based action game that's a breath of fresh air in a genre often dominated by gritty realism. Think of it as a more colorful and linear, but less edgy Sunset Overdrive.The Good Stuff (+):+ Visual Symphony (+): Hi-Fi Rush is a feast for the eyes. The vibrant colors and stylish animation create a visually stunning experience. It's like playing a music video game.+ Musical Mayhem (+): The soundtrack is a perfect blend of catchy tunes and intense beats. It's like playing a video game with headphones on, except you won't want to take them off.+ Easy-to-Learn, Harder-to-Master (+): The combat system is accessible to newcomers but offers plenty of depth for experienced players. It's like learning a new dance move, but with more violence.+ Charming Characters (+): The characters are quirky and memorable. It's a cast of misfits that you can't help but love, even if they're a bit generic.+ Creative Combat (+): The boss fights are a highlight, with unique mechanics and challenging patterns. It's like playing a rhythm-based rhythm game, but with more explosions.The Not-So-Good Stuff (-):- Generic Storyline (-): The story is as predictable as a superhero movie. It's a familiar tale of a hero fighting a corporation, but the charming characters make it enjoyable.- Short and Sweet (+/-): The game's length is a double-edged sword. It's a nice change of pace from the endless grind of AAA titles, but it leaves you wanting more.- Overrated? (+/-): Hi-Fi Rush is a solid to good game, but it might be a bit overrated. It's like that indie darling that everyone loves, but you're not sure why. Certain things stand out but I don't think it'll make a top games ever list.The Verdict:Hi-Fi Rush is a fun and stylish game that's worth checking out. It's a breath of fresh air in a genre often dominated by gritty realism. While the story is a bit generic and the game could have been longer, the unique combat system and charming characters make it a satisfying experience. It's like that indie game that everyone raves about, but you're not sure if it's really that special.

_childDocuments_.review: I still can't quite believe it, but Hi-Fi Rush somehow managed to  fuse Hack-and-Slash and Rhythm games into one perfect gem of an experience. It's all just so much fun, and manages to fit together absolutely seamlessly. I'm amazed how much thought went into the design of everything, from the artstyle, to the game mechanics, to the plot, to the sound design. Everything in service of creating a cohesive, yet enjoyable world to spend a little time in. It's one of the few games I've ever immediately decided to replay after finishing it, (partially for achievements, partially for exploring the in-cutscene costumes and easter-eggs), although I didn't end up replaying it  as many times as the Wall of Fame would have me do.That said, I've replayed the second level boss fight at least ten times. There's something about it that just gets me pumped and feels really satisfying. The music is absolutely rocking the mood, and elevates a relatively fun fight into an absolutely excellent one. I could really feel the beat and sync with the moves.On the other hand, the level 8 boss fight is not nearly as fun. I mean, the music is still fantastic, and the first two stages make for decent fights, but the diving move in the third stage is completely ridiculous, and iust causes the fight to become a massive slog, at least for me.The characters in HFR are all well-developed and fun, and the costume feature (unlocked after beating the game) only underlines their distinct personalities. Also, the voice actors deserve a raise, because they did an incredible job bringing them to life. Overall, I recommend giving Hi-Fi Rush a shot. It's a real breath of fresh air in the AAA scene by virtue of being a 10/10 game, apart from a little nitpicking.

_childDocuments_.review: This is easily one of my favorite games of all time. The characters are so upbeat and positive to match the bright and beautiful color palette of the world they live in, on top of a compelling story and top notch writing to boot. The combat flows incredibly, especially for someone very familiar with Character Action/Spectacle Fighter type games (for those familiar, it feels very akin to something like Devil May Cry 3 more than a Bayonetta, to its own positive effect). The system of attacking, dodging, and parrying to the beat is incredibly well realized with some fantastic music to get you in the spirit of the game's attitude, and the game never outstays its welcome, which may imply it's short (and, at about 8 hours or so, it is, to be clear), but truly just means it tells the story it wants to tell and never feels like it's wasting the players' time with nonsense that doesn't benefit it.I write this review now because Tango Gameworks, the creators of this game, The Evil Within 1 &2, and Ghostwire: Tokyo, have been shut down by the corporate monsters at Microsoft, seemingly for no other reason than to help pay back the company after the Activision-Blizzard Acquisition. Microsoft is absolutely abhorrent for putting these wonderful people out of a job and for robbing the player base of more games like these. I advise you to purchase this game while you still can; the game features licensed tracks, and I wouldn't put it past Microsoft to simply delist this game instead of renewing the licenses (though, if the case is that they keep the game up but patch the game to remove the licensed songs, as much as that would be terrible, the copyright free music that the devs kindly added for Streamers is arguably as good as the prerecorded music and reacts better to the game. Your milelage may vary). To those at Tango, thank you for an incredible game. I hope your next endeavors bring you as much happiness and passion as can be felt throughout the entirety of this game.

Yes, not every joke is a hit, but I'm honestly surprised by how often the humor and good vibes stuck around.The time I spent in Hi-Fi Rush can't be replaced by any other game, and I have a hard time finding a gripe to cling to. I had fun, and its awfully sad just how many games fail to deliver on that very same prospect. Hi-Fi rush entertains, respects your time, and perhaps most importantly - cannot easily be replaced.As story-based / action combat hybrid games go? 9/10 - A full point missing, simply because you can often feel the game's scope pushing back against the fantasy of it all. _childDocuments_.review: Honestly, I don't know how an Action/Rhythm game could do it better.  Had this one in my backlog for a while and finally decided to play it.  - The characters are cheesy and fun.  - The gameplay/combat is absolutely phenomenal. - Combat rewards you for using  of your combos and mechanics, but you can keep it simple if you want. - After every battle, you get some feedback on your performance and points to boot like an arcade game would. - The Story isn't the most ambitious thing ever, but complements these characters well.  - The transitions between gameplay and cutscenes and vice versa are very smooth. - Brilliant aesthetic. A cell-shaded, comic book inspired, cyberpunk world... that literally moves with the beat! - Training Room allows you to practice combos and "git gud" at your leisure. - The special attacks are awesome and flow really well in the heat of battle. - Extensive upgrade system. I had nowhere NEAR enough cash to purchase everything by the end of the campaign. - Collectible powerups (health boost, etc) scattered throughout the levels to reward exploring. - Post game allows you to not only replay all the levels/bosses but allows deeper exploration with all your new upgrades and continue the story after the credits roll. - Tons of showmanship. Stronger enemies will get angry and challenge you to a 1v1 duel where, if you win, you can insta-kill them. These moments are pretty hype with unique animations and fanfare. - Respectable difficulty - I died a handful of times... but more often than not, I THOUGHT I was about to die and pulled through. Very satisfying. - Optional mini quests scattered throughout the levels reward you for exploring and interacting with the world. - Some of the later bosses have certain combo attacks that move OFF beat. When the entire game thus far has been ON beat, despite being telegraphed, this can be quite jarring. - Platforming doesn't feel great. I'm not entirely sure why, but it often didn't feel clear WHERE I was gonna land. Retractable platforms would often pull themselves out from under my feet before I could finish if Ididn't stop and wait for them to reset first. Breaking up the flow. - Levels can be kinda long. I had a few instances when finishing a level took almost an hour. I often felt like I needed to put the game down after a level due to burnout. - Tutorials feel a bit heavy early on.I can't claim to be an expert on Rhythm games, not usually my thing, but this was an exceptional experience. I love it when games reward me for learning combos and engaging with the deeper systems. The music was poised to perfectly compliment the gameplay and not distract from it... a delicate balance! I even found myself liking the protagonist in a "Oh my god, he's such an idiot... ha ha... I love him!" kind of way. All in all, 10/10. I don't believe there's a game that does what Hi Fi RUSH does better.

_childDocuments_.review: Hi-Fi Rush is my dream game, and I don't say that lightly. Ever since I got into character action games as a teenager, I had always imagined a game that blended the high-octane energy and combat of a character action game with rhythm elements. For the past 10 or so years, I genuinely never thought I'd see something like that happen unless I myself went out and tried to make it. I'm genuinely so happy I was wrong. Hi-Fi Rush is everything I imagined that game would be and more. It has the style, substance, and above all it's the most enjoyable experience I've had playing a game in years. With mechanics that are quick and easy to learn, but it's also very intricate with the amount of combos you can string together so it'll take time to feel like you've mastered everything (even for someone with experience in both character action and rhythm games, that being said DMC players will feel right at home playing this game). John Johanas and his team made an incredible game that is clearly filled with so much love and passion that I can't help but recommend it to everyone.

_childDocuments_.review: Gameplay: The gameplay is great. Even when the novelty wears off, it's been a very enjoyable game with some fun bosses to fight against. It's definitely a rhythm game. Story:The story itself is pretty standard. Rather predictable and all that, but honestly it doesn't take itself too seriously either. It's good at establishing the feeling of hype, regardless, so the cutscenes that follow, compliments the game and bosses well. Characters: This is probably the first "horrendously stupid protagonist who still somehow gets stuff done anyway" that I actually liked. Peoples' reactions are generally rather funny.Music: It's pretty well-done. I'm not a huge music person so I can't really say much more than that. The songs that were made/selected in this game were really fun. If you're a streamer, there's an option to have non-copyrighted music for the licensed songs. Misc:I beat the story in about 16 hours according to Steam. I was playing on Hard. The game has definite replay value, though. It's a good thing though in my opinion; it doesn't overstay its welcome, unlike a lot of other games nowadays. Other reviews says "it's a PS2 game made in 2023" and that's a really good way to put it. However, it's minus the jankiness a lot of old games would have. And there's a surprising amount of accessibility and customization features to the game, too. If you want the game to function as a single-button rhythm game, there's an option for that. I really can't think of any better way to make the game. Highly recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: I have finished this game clocking in 16 hours (including a few hours spent in the training room), and needless to say it is probably one of the best games I've ever played in my life, it has an extremely strong sense of creative style, design, humor, combat feel, and of course, the most impressive thing is the music. The music is terrific, easily the best rhythm combat game that ever released, the selections are all amazing, there were no misses, only wonderful, catchy, rhythmic tracks you rocked your head to as you were kicking ass with the fun combos you can do. Despite the cliche tropes and power of friendship ending, I believe this was the perfect approach to such a stylistic and funny game like this, the dialogue and humor is top notch, the character expressions are so well animated it's like you're engrossed watching a nostalgic cartoon you look back fondly on from your childhood, it's phenomenally animated. Now let's talk about the best system in the game; the combat. The combat system is DMC-style rhythmic beat-em-up.It's perfect, it's smooth, it's just fun. the combos are all fun to link together, the bosses in this game especially are very unique and fun, I loved all of them (maybe for the sole exception of Mimosa, I found her boss design to be a bit weird and not too rhythmic but that's just a nitpick). The game kept introducing new mechanics every now and then, just at the moment when I'm like "Hmm... is there more to the game or is that it?" the game introduces a new mechanic that keeps me preoccupied that further developed the combat system to make it easier to combo, and also enhancing the enemy encounters with more mechanics to use like parrying, magnet links, counters, battery farming, partner combo links, special attacks and my favorite one being the unique parrying/dodging sequence that tough enemies have after you break their posture, it's always fun to perfectly parry those. The level design is amazing, it's fairly linear but has a few secret areas you can find to get more gears, graffiti, or even key items to help you gain more health or reverb, I liked finding those Z-Shield and fire doors you had to go back to after beating the game to find more hidden things in them, it was a cool reward for remembering where they were, oh, and of course the hidden doors too that get unlocked have fun challenges in them. My only complaint is that the platforming isn't as smooth sailing as the combat; due to Chai's double jump not having forward momentum, it makes some jumps awkward, and more often than not using dodge mid-air isn't that viable either due to it launching you too far. The developer team managed to mix and match the colorful cartoony 3D overworld design with the 2D comics every now and then, the art is amazing and so creative it blows my mind how they were able to design such a   world. The audio score in particular is beyond perfect, heck, the environment is quite   beating to the rhythm, everything flows so well in this game, it deserves all the love it gets and more.As for the characters themselves, I love all of them, our heroes are all lovable and the voice actors are extremely talented. the character designs are all top-notch, I love Peppermint's and Kale's designs, I'm glad there is also LGBTQ+ and POC rep in this game too. This game got robbed of it's GOTY and it should've gotten at least a nominee, it's a completely original game that I believe has barely any faults, it's a perfect game. I'm looking forward to Hi-Fi Rush 2, I'd buy it in a heartbeat no matter the price. If anyone reads this and you're unsure; just buy it, trust me, it's going to be one of the best games you've played ever.Make sure to
