_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Amazing art style, soundtrack, intuitive gameplay, great cast, great combat, and a healthy helping of replay value. Very well worth full price at $30, since I would even pay $60 for this game. I avoided spoilers since you should go buy it.Hi-Fi Rush is one of those games that comes around every now and again that comes out of left field and subsequently becomes a smash hit. It's a game that immediately captivates you and thrusts you into a bright, colorful, and interesting world while exposing you to some of the tightest combat we've seen in a good while out of character action games. The soundtrack is a banger all around, the characters are great, the story while a bit cliche is interesting and captivating, and as an icing on the cake, this game will age very well in years to come. Story is simple. Your character, Chai, is a wannabe rockstar who signs up to receive robotic enhancements as a test subject for the Armstrong program which is provided by international tech mega-corporation Vandelay Robotic Solutions. During the initial surgery your music player is embedded in your chest, causing the world to sync to the music, and causing you to be labelled a defect and subsequently hunted down by Vandelay. After your first few bouts you're greeted by your first companions, Peppermint the tech wizard and brains of the operation, and 808 the robot cat. Peppermint tells you that there's something fishy with an AI program being developed by Vandelay, and having nowhere else to go, you agree to help with taking down Vandelay by securing the 6 passwords from the 6 company bosses. The narrative is predictable and basically follows any other similar story script to a T, but that's not always a bad thing, and it executes this very well.The cast of characters is witty, well voice acted, well designed, lovable, and none are insufferable or excessively cringey. Sure, the game has it's moments but the humor in game is basically all tongue-in-cheek, in good taste, and doesn't overstay its welcome. You'll have companions you actually care about, NPCs that are interesting and sometimes funny, and villains you just love to hate, which is more than can be said about a lot of other games released in years past. There is not a single character who came off as insufferable, and you can tell the voice talent put a lot of work into making these characters shine, as well as the animators and artists who brought these vibrant characters to life.Actual gameplay is very tight, responsive, and satisfying. It plays like any other CAG where you fight in arenas connected by platforming and traversal sections. Immediately you notice the game is in sync with the music as well, everything in this game follows the rhythm which makes platforming easy, predictable, and never feeling like the game is pulling a fast one on the player. There are many combos you can purchase from the in game shop (not real money) to diversify your combat and aim for those big scores, special attacks with a wide variety of effects and uses, your companions that assist you in their own unique ways, passive upgrades in the form of chips with a variety of effects. Combat follows the same rules as platforming, which makes combat feel fair, predictable, and challenging without cheap difficulty spikes. The pacing in this game is some of the best I've experienced; right when I was wishing I could do X, I would be introduced to doing X. This gameplay loop is fun, exciting, and even when you beat the game it begs to be played again if you want to 100% the game.This game immediately captivates with its comic book art style, incredible animation for both 3D and 2D cutscenes, the world that lives and breathes the rhythm of the music, and everything full of color and life. Even bits of the infrastructure is gettin its groove on, as well as your very nice and non-intrusive HUD, your own idle animations, and 808 as she sits as a floating, blinking metronome. If that's a bit of a tall order for you, you can opt to have a metronome displayed on the bottom of the screen for easy reference. All non-intrusive and easy to flip on and off.If you stuck around, hopefully your next action is to click Add to Cart and start playing one of the best games of 2023.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't normally do reviews prior to beating a game, but I'll make an exception here. Hi-Fi Rush is good. Straight up good. Gameplay is Devil-May Cry meets Rhythm Game (more so than dmc5's light rhythm mechanic) with bits of jrpg storytelling mixed with classic level design you would expect to find in playstation titles like Ratchet and Clank. The core combat is extremely solid, exactly what you would expect from a hack-slash action title like a devil may cry title, where matching your attacks to the beat of soundtrack powers up and speeds up your attack animations. While for some it may be hard to get the rhythm mechanic down at first (I notoriously struggle with them) the game makes every effort to make it as easy for you as possible, from enemies attacks also timing to the rhythm (allowing you to make so slick parries and dodges once you get the beat down) to visualizing the beat throughout the level design. Certain parts of the level are ALWAYS moving to the beat of the sountrack, the protagonist snaps to the music, there are visual and audio cues when you nail the timing, you even have the option to enable a visual representation of the beat at the bottom of screen for ease of use if necessary. Now just that alone would not have sold me on the game. But it absolutely OOZES style as well. From your main weapon being a guitar, to the anime and jrpg inspired design, the beautiful color palette and a wonderfully done fully voiced dub. I don't think there is a single line of dialogue that isn't dubbed, and all of it was cast extremely well. It feels extremely fresh and nostalgic at the same time.

_childDocuments_.review: Even if it's not perfect by any stretch, hi fi rush is a fun little rhythm action game reminiscent of combo action games like DMC and the like.The art style is a super pretty comic book style that runs as smooth as butter in gameplay, while cutscenes offer that gorgeous purposefully-low-framerate style that just makes everything pop in the most amazing way.The game is a combo action game, meaning plenty of smacking enemies all over the place with memorised combos for high scores, or alternatively using the same 2 combos over and over again and still getting an S rank.The game isn't very challenging even on hard mode, but the bosses are half difficulty spike and half bullsh!t spike. As long as you can keep the beat and mash dodge/parry, you can deal with anything the game throws at you.The writing is really marvel/borderlands, meaning that everyone is the snarky ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and there's plenty of "explain the joke as it happens" cringe. Thankfully it's not totally insufferable here, and a lot of the humor actually lands. The characters are all archetypes, but they're entertaining enough, although as a footnote a lot of the actors sound really bored with the material.The biggest flaws with the gameplay are threefold:1: The jumping is absolutely atrocious. It rockets you straight up into the air and gives you little to no distance, even with an aerial dash. Trying to do fast paced platforming (or hell, even slow paced platforming) with it is a complete and total nightmare.2: There are so many particle effects being vomited onto the screen at any given time that enemy telegraphs might as well be invisible. Trying to pick out that one tiny split-second star sticker that tells you you're about to be flattened and react to it is like trying to pick out a specific rainbow pebble in a fishtank.3: Some enemy attacks have to be parried in order to kill them, but the timing for the parry sequence doesn't gel with the stage's actual beat, and basically requires you to tune out the music for a moment to get it right.What's most disappointing though is that the music in this rhythm game isn't very memorable. Only a couple songs in the whole soundtrack really stuck out to me, and of those one was a song I've heard before, and one was a remix of a song I've heard before. Compared to other rhythm games I've played recently where the soundtrack was just bangers on top of bangers, a lot of the tracks in hi fi rush are just atmospheric grunge-rock fluff that all blends together into a smoothie of denim and stupid haircuts. Despite all that though, it's an enjoyable little romp at a decent price, especially for bethesda. It's worth it if you want a game to relax with for a few hours that's actually upbeat and colorful for a change.

_childDocuments_.review: I tried this game on a whim the day it came out on Xbox Game Pass...and was completely blown away. _childDocuments_.review: Hi-Fi Rush is one of, if not the best new game released by a big studio I've played in nearly 10 years. It's a rhythm hack-and-slash game with aesthetics and writing that reminds me of videogames and cartoons from the pre-2010s, and that statement may be an insult coming from some, but from me it's one of the highest compliments I can give anything in the entertainment space.i felt like this could have come out in like 2003-2005 on the PS2 and it would have fit right in. The fact it came out in 2023 shows me that the old-school style not only still works, but is still remembered fondly by at least someone in the industry who knows how to recreate it. And words cannot describe how thankful I am for that.The story is pretty dang good for what it is. It's not trying to be this super-serious story like Last of Us, God of War, CoD, etc., instead it goes for a more goofy cartoony and honestly just fun style that has really felt like a lost art form for the better part of 10 years. Like, I've seen plenty of games and films attempt it since 2013, but very few of them hit the nail on the head as they instead go for some new style of cartoony that... most of the time just feels bland and boring in comparison. This game feels very much alive and kicking. And by the way, the soundtrack is awesome and if there's any chance of that getting a store page on Steam, I need to know about it immediately.The gameplay is also pretty dang smooth. Like maybe Devil May Cry smooth. The fact that I can screw up the timing and still play is a godsend for an action-focused game such as this, and there are a few cases where I wish other action-rhythm games did the same. And thankfully, there's still an incentive to try to match the beat as doing so will cause enemies to sometimes drop health pickups or energy pickups during combat, which is a great counterbalance to removing the punishment for being off-beat.Now, when I played I only encountered one or two bugs, the main one I found was on the first level when you take the second "shortcut" the camera became stuck in place while my character was not, so I had to back out to the main menu and restart from last checkpoint to progress. It worked fine since then.Hi-Fi Rush is a masterpiece, a modern classic, and definitely a contender for my GOTY 2023. I never could have expected a magnificent game like this to come out when every other company just pushes out the same boring overdone hyper-realistic hyper-linear hyper-monetized overly-politicized creatively-bankrupt criminally-underpolished crap to add to the monotonous gray hodgepodge that is currently the AAA game industry. The industry should take some notes from Hi-Fi Rush, honestly.

_childDocuments_.review: So I did not expect a Game of the Year contender to come this early. This game is easily one of the best game I played in a a long time. _childDocuments_.review: Entertaining rhythmic beat-em-up. Art direction is very refreshing and more reminiscent of an indie title than a big release. Visual and sound design are on point throughout the game and leave no part feeling unpolished. Very pleasing to look at, with huge, colorful, and detailed landscapes and backdrops that make the world feel coherent and large.That being said, the writing makes High School Musical seem profound; the characters are very flat and uninspiring, their dialogue consists of displaying their single personality trait with no meaningful interaction between characters. I will say, however, that the voice acting is very well done. No matter the simplistic character design, the voice actors make each character feel believable and engaging (even though there is little substance behind it).My biggest gripe with the game, however, is an array of small gameplay issues that kept bugging me throughout my playthrough:- The level design is oppressively linear. Levels feel like a bunch of different sections glued together which are so cinematic they feel like quick-time event sequences at times (there *are* QTE sequences in the game, too). The moments you are left to explore on your own were most enjoyable, but they invariably proved unrewarding and boiled down to traversing the level.- The combat has you stuck in an arena until you clear out all enemies -- I was expecting it to be more like musical Dark Souls. In crowded arenas, your combos take too many beats to land and most of the time you're dodging or parrying.- The first 3 hours of the game are a tutorial with constant starts and stops. You don't unlock all your mechanics until practically the end of the game. Most your mechanics feel like gimmicks made to artificially stall your level progress. For instance, - The QTE/repeat-the-rhythm parry sequences feel unsynced to the beat (I'm not sure). When you first hear the rhythm, it starts on the start of the bar -- however, when you're supposed to repeat it, it starts whenever the approach circle reaches the center of the screen, which is never on the first beat and it's hard to time on which beat it actually hits just by looking at it.- Platforming feels really stiff- Bosses' unique mechanics are not immediately obvious, and it takes a while before you grow accustom to their moveset.I also wish there'd have been sections with songs in other meters than 4/4, but that would probably require reworking combat entirely to make it enjoyable.Ultimately, while the rhythm aspect makes it unique, the game ends up feeling like a licensed game. By the end third of the game, playing felt tedious. All in all, it's pleasing eye- and ear-candy, but mediocre in all other regards.

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10 - Absolutely amazing game.Playing this really takes me back to the good'ol Playstation era full of adventure jumping games I played as a kid. _childDocuments_.review: Alright, I never leave reviews but if a rhythm game has this problem I can't let it go.There's no LAG CALIBRATION. For video or audio. For those who don't understand the problem: Video/Audio Lag is the amount of extra time to get the frame/audio the game feeds to the computer at that moment. If its 10ms, that means the frame/audio the game anticipates will be shown/played now will instead be shown 10 milliseconds later. THIS CAN BE A DEAL-BREAKER FOR YOU.If your lag is high, for video OR audio, you wont hit the rhythm. You'll instead hit offbeat and miss several things throughout the game. The timing on some things are pretty loose, but others are strict down to the tenth of a second (on normal) which is more manageable then you think. Lag makes those moments nearly unhittable. Meanwhile the platforming isn't great, but I rarely play any platforming games so don't take my word for it.Otherwise the rest of the game is splendid. 1 major nitpick and one minor one. Highly recommended to anyone with 0 lag.P.S. _childDocuments_.review: Hi-Fi Rush is a Masterpiece in video games. Every byte oozes charm, polish and bravado. This is the best Gamecube game that Capcom Never made. Created by industry veterans and published by Bethesda of all companies. Tango games consists of industry veterans of and founded by Shinki Makami, who worked on: Resident Evil, Devil May Cry, Viewtiful Joe & Disney's Aladdin (snes).Every single aspect of this game is tied to the beat. Your attacks animate to the beat, they do more damage with perfect timing, and eventually like Neo, you wont even need to see an enemy to parry them. In combat, your combos become Guitar Solo's. You find yourself attacking, moving and feeling the beat as you unleash your S rank combos. Your normal attacks are power chords, your parries are rests in the song, and your buddy attacks are big riffs.Characters are lovable and well animated with the grandeur and bombast of a Studio Trigger Anime. I constantly found myself with a dumb smile on my face as it all synced together. I cannot recommend Hi-Fi Rush enough. It deserves to be played by every fan of Action Platformers.

_childDocuments_.review: After finally achieving the golden guitar from completing every challenge Hi-Fi Rush has to offer, words cannot describe how much I've fallen in love with this gem of a game.The visuals are aesthetically pleasing and I absolutely adore the comic book style the game takes on. The character writing in this game is cheesy but in a fun way and each of them are designed in such a way that both their personalities and appearances pop out. Even talking to every NPC in each level is worth it just from listening to their fluff dialogue. The humor in this game is corny but charming, and I can never get tired of it. And finally, the combat system. Granted, if you're not a seasoned action gamer nor musically gifted, even on Easy mode, there will be moments where this game does kick your ass. But once you get the hang of attacking in sync with the beat as well as parrying, the game itself becomes a lot more fun. Still challenging as it does keep you on your toes, but that's what makes it an overall engaging and gratifying experience.There is, however, one gripe I do have with this game, and that's the platforming. A lot of times, it feels as though I have to double jump across every little platform to make sure I don't fall because Chai has very little momentum jumping forward and tends to fall down very quickly. This might be because his rate of falling is also in sync with the music, which does feel a bit counter-intuitive to make his fall sync up with a single beat as opposed to two and thus makes it feel clunky. But really, that's about my only issue. Everything else about this game is fantastic.Hi-Fi Rush gets a definite 9.5/10 from me, 10/10 if Tango spruces up the platforming. Highly recommend playing this masterpiece.

_childDocuments_.review: If you like action games and you love music (especially rock), this game is a no-brainer.The combat is very satisfying and one thing in particular that I liked about it was how it's easy enough for anyone to learn and enjoy, but complex enough to make sure it never feels monotonous. Sometimes spectacle fighters can feel intimidating with the amount of practice it takes to be both really good and stylish with combos, but I think Hi-Fi Rush does a wonderful job of making you feel bad-ass even if you just mash random buttons.The story isn't anything amazing, but it's not bad by any means. This is a lighthearted game with a cast of silly characters that crack goofy jokes, so it's honestly a nice alternative to the plethora of darker and more mature games out there.The replayability is great. There's collectibles to find even after you've beaten the game, special gamemodes, many achievements, and 5 different difficulty levels. You might find yourself replaying the game simply because it's such good fun.Visuals are fun and poppy; if you love comic-book aesthetics, you'll love the art and animation.I'd say Hi-Fi Rush is worth the full $30 price, it's a very well-made game and I can tell it was crafted by people who have a genuine passion for making games that are, above all else, simply great fun.If you don't smile within the first hour of playing this game, you have no soul.

_childDocuments_.review: Hi-Fi Rush is one of the few genuine masterpieces to come out of the AAA space in the last decade. It's impossible to put into words how fantastic this game is, even on a level that eclipses the game itself. To get the obvious out of the way, the music, visuals, and combat are all spectacular. I'm honestly shocked how well Tango nailed the spectacle fighter genre on their first go, while also infusing it with something entirely new to that genre. Sure games like BPM, COTND, and Metal Hellsinger exist, but Hi-Fi Rush's beat is  beautifully interwoven with the game in every aspect of design, something that the aforementioned games couldn't nail. The world *breathes* to the beat, and the rhythm can come almost as naturally as breathing for those who are willing to let the combat click. Not only that, but I am also extremely surprised Tango pulled off such a beautifully designed and stylized world, especially considering their past works. The game is wonderfully animated, the worlds are richly detailed, and  the characters really do shine with how lovingly the cutscenes were animated. But I think what really shines from this game is how, for the first time in ages, can I feel the soul of the development team in this game. Take it from someone who is currently working in a AAA studio, most of the AAA games, regardless of quality, are almost polished to a fault. They feel almost inhuman, with so many people coming and going to a project, they come out feeling like something made in a machine. But even ignoring the heartwrenching (in a "ive been there" way) credits song, I can really just feel this games dev cycle. A pitched passion project thats been workshopped for ages, constantly fearing cancellation, with budget cuts and arguments with the finance team in droves. Injokes and dumb ideas becoming implemented parts of the game, while cut content was turned into a joke rather than flogged back as DLC. But at the end of the day, despite all of the troubles, this feels like a passion project fully realized, that everyone is proud to stand behind. I know all this "soul of the game" ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ makes it sound like I'm high out of my mind, but I really do mean it. Hi Fi Rush is a masterpiece, not only because its a great game, but its a great game with a soul.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're reading this because you've already bought and been playing the game, this is yet another GLOWING review (shocker). But for the uninitiated, HIFI RUSH is an high octane rhythm action plat former with more personality than you can imagine, and while I could write a 10 page essay on why that's the case, let's stick to the basics, because honestly, you need to be spending less time reading reviews and more time buying and playing this game.Soundtrack is at the core of this game, and it is no slouch. The game feels so satisfying with it's indie rock aesthetic tracks. And they are catchy while also being musically fitting to continuously play through the game. If licensed music is a huge turn off because you like to record or Stream, HIFI RUSH has you covered with fully in house free-use banger tracks that replace the licensed tracks that would otherwise get your content in trouble. It's such an immense undertaking for a small attention to detail, and you will find this a common theme in this game.The Story and Characters are simple, but it's fun, humor filled, and you may find yourself cheering on the cast as you progress through the games story. There's plot twists you won't expect, and other cliches and tropes that may make you roll your eyes while still smiling because damn it, it's still executed so well despite how cheesy it might seem. The whole cast is lovable, and the villains you not only love to hate, but provide comedic and serious moments that make not a second of this game feel boring as you traverse their respective levels and fights.The game play takes the premise of any good rhythm game and multiplies the satisfaction by tenfold. It's simple, but can very quickly get complex and if you don't take your time to find the groove you will struggle. Combos feel exciting and impacting, with just the right amount of variety in moves that the more you learn the more situations you can handle and keep your flow going. However, it never feels overwhelming because the game cleverly introduces you to all its mechanics as you progress through the whole story, giving you time to learn the mechanics and prepare yourself for new ones to challenge you.The level design is SCARY GOOD. The game manages to feel accessible to everyone while still proving to be a challenge to overcome as each stage gives you new obstacles, enemies, and interactions you've yet to come across in your journey. This makes HIFI RUSH never feel repetitive or stale as it's constantly giving you new challenges and obstacles, or even building upon older game mechanics for fresh new interactions. HIFI RUSH's level design never makes you go "Oh great, time to do X for the tenth time in a row." Achieving this was absolutely one of the most applaud-able aspects of the game.Finally, for now, lets touch on the animation and art style. HIFI RUSH takes heavy inspiration from the current Renaissance happening in western animation studios, whereby 3D rendering pipelines are changed to include elements of 2D animation, onomatopoeia, movement lines, and using frame rate to emphasize movement. By combining traditional animation with 3D rendering, HIFI RUSH creates an aesthetic of a Cell-Shaded, indie rock music video printed on comic pages. The cut scenes are gorgeous and blend so smoothly between game play and animation that it keeps you constantly immersed in the world that's been created.I've seen some real gem games come out before, many games I'd still give glowing recommendations for the level of heart and soul put into them. HIFI RUSH is a once in a decade gaming experience, topping off even some of the greatest most charming games out there. The level of polish and detail in HIFI RUSH would lead me to believe even the studio janitor gave it their all cleaning the places that contributed in making this game. It's practically criminal that an game this well developed from start to end is only 30 dollars. I'd happily pay 90 dollars for this easily. I could go on and on and on about how stellar this game is, and everything in this review barely scratches the surface on how much FUN it is to play this game. But it's time to close the set out on this review.If you're one of the few that found this review and used it to decide whether you should pull the trigger on this game. Here's your decision. Get this game. You won't regret a single second of it. Great Job Tango Gameworks, your passion paid off immensely.

Even for special units that need to you hit them with a particular ally before you can damage them didn't need any special attention because cycling through all my allies would eventually hit them anyway...The graphics were too flashy (probably due to me spamming my ally summons) but it just adds to the lack of thought process required to play.The story was nothing special (I just beat Atomic Heart and its basically the same thing).The dialog was 'quippy' but overall nothing special (way better then Atomic Heart).The audio wasn't bad but it wasn't memorable at all, just these generic rock tracks through out, which is a bit unfortunate for a music game.Weirdly they had Nine Inch Nails and Zwan playing at the end of the game. _childDocuments_.review: It's Ratchet and Clank meets rhythm combat, to the extent that you're collecting gears from items you smash and most enemies are robots. I had to double check that this was a Bethesda Softworks IP, developed by Tango Gameworks (ZeniMax > Xbox Game Studios), what a weird and neat game to spawn from a developer known for gritty DOOM-and-gloom games.It's fantastic, while short. The game lives up to being a fun combat rhythm game. The immense attention to detail in the world and the characters, literally everything moves and fights to the beat of the music. Matching the beat during combat is really satisfying and rewarding, but at the same time punishes you for slipping off-beat. Combat happens in controlled cells that are very obvious allowing you to explore the level freely between the combat areas. Tons of secrets and hidden areas to explore, easter-eggs and comedic side-commentary from worker droids.My gripes with the game revolve around hard to complete button combos, can't really tell if you got it right. Perfectly timed enemy attacks every time you try to finish your combo. Some levels have hard to track beats or the beat is kinda lame, the track used in the final two levels was by far the best. Some combos will launch you up and over the object you're trying to attack. Some of the QTE's will drive you mad even though they're just some side objective. About half of the boss fights felt strategic using block and solid attack timing, others were just button mashing like the final boss.Note: If you're having trouble with timing, try disabling the low-latency option. As weird as it sounds I was more used to regular latency on my controller so the low-latency setting was messing me up.

_childDocuments_.review: One of those games that's just damn fun. I've always thought a rhythm hack and slash would be awesome, and this is just exactly that. Having dodges, parries, and combos all to the beat of the music is hella satisfying, especially if you're a gamer and a musician like myself. Is super fun and can be quite challenging at times, and some of the fights involve pretty complex rhythms and such that you have to deal with. My biggest complaint is just that it's a little short - I got 11 hours - but usually when that's the worst thing about a game it means it's pretty damn good. Plus, there's quite a bit of after-game content I've yet to try out. Gameplay is definitely the best part of this, as the combat is super well done, but there are a lot of other amazing aspects of the game - the artstyle is awesome, mostly taking on a comic book look, even occasionally switching to 2D animation for some of the cutscenes (with some cool transitions). The story is super fun and charming, and all the characters are unique and well played, with some pretty solid character development and such. Overall, I definitely recommend, especially on sale as it is as of writing this - but I still recommend at full price, as it's not too expensive to begin with. Just overall a very well polished, solid game that does exactly what it set out to do and more. And just in general, hella fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Hi-Fi RUSH is one of the most fun games to release in recent memory. When this game shadow-dropped with a single day's notice in January of this year, I was instantly intrigued by its voice cast. When I saw gameplay of it, I was instantly sold. I've wanted a specatcle action game in the style of BPM: Bullets Per Minute and Metal: Helsinger for as long as I can remember, and Hi-Fi RUSH underpromises and overdelivers. With action coming straight out of Nero's toolkit in Devil May Cry 5 and puzzle-platforming that reminded me quite pleasantly of Super Mario Galaxy, HFR starts with a bang and never dips in quality even once across its 10-hour runtime. The rhythmic aspect of the game meant that every single enemy attack was easily predictable, and though I was worried this would lead to a lack of difficulty, it throws so many enemies and mechanics at you at once that it still feels as frenetic as its contemporaries. The cartoony artstyle and lighthearted charm blend with a combination of original and licensed music to give Hi-Fi RUSH a unique style, and though the plot is rather by-the-numbers, the characters are so varied and likeable that I never felt bored with it. The biggest surprise for me was how anti-corporate this game published by Microsoft was. There is plenty of post-game content to pad the gameplay when the story is done, and though I didn't engage with it, I am glad to see it here. Chock-full of content and quite fairly priced, Hi-Fi RUSH is not a game to be missed out on. 8.5/10.

You deserved better than Microsoft.Original post:A gem that came out of nowhere that both reminds you of the great games from the 2000s and is a giant breath of fresh air among current big games.+ An amazing core gameplay loop where combat feels incredibly satisifying and stylish.+ A fun mashup of spectactle fighter and rythm games, where EVERYTHING follows the beat.+ Combat is "easy to learn, hard to master". Does not punish you for not hitting on beat, but rewards you with more stylish and flair if you do hit on beat. While there are a lot of helpful tools that assist, I still had a challenge to consistently land on beat.+ Gameplay that evolves during the story, with both varied enemy types and the ocassional gameplay-style shift that still matches the rythm.+ Awesome soundtrack where both the licensed songs and the originals make you pumped.+ Amazingly animated and colorful artsyle that would totally be your favorite animated series if was one.+ Kickass, hilarious and heartwarming feel-good story. A straight-forward story told really well.+ Loveable heroes that you root foor and charismatic villains that are both fun to watch and satisifying to defeat.+ Suprisingly strong satire of tech and games-industry when you look for it in the story and the levels.- Some levels can be a bit too long, although that is felt more on the second playthrough than the first playthrough. Mileage can therefore vary.I have a hard time to find fault with this game without sound nitpicking. I strongly recommend this game, and I really hope we see more games like this in the future. I'm already hungry for a sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: Use this game to test gameplay literacy among your friends: if they suck, never listen to their opinions ever again. Even better, remove them from your friend list immediately: why would you hang out with such losers anyway?Joking aside (or not), Hi-Fi Rush is an action game that uses music to encourage players to synchronize movements and attacks to the beat. It might feel weird at first, but soon enough you will start to get the feel of the beats, chaining together dashes and attacks seamlessly. There is nothing quite like it. What sets this game apart is not just its gameplay, but the way it marries that with its cell-shading visual style, which is basically unmatched as of now. Together with charming characters and excellent animation work, it really elevates the entire experience.GOTY material.

Tango Gameworks managed to make a game that made me buy it twice because I enjoyed it the first time, and I wanted to enjoy it the way I was supposed to my second time. _childDocuments_.review: Honestly one of the freshest experiences I've had loading up a new game in years. The first boss fight had me about the same as the scene in ratatouille where the guy is blasted back to his childhood after taking 1 bite of the food. Everything was very expressive and had a whimsical tone with a comic book artstyle i enjoyed a lot.Absolutely loved playing this game, and i'll see if I can try and get around to 100% it. I could talk about all that I liked but this review would be insanely long. Just to name a few, Korsica would definitely be mentioned multiple times in that essay. Every time she was on screen I was having a blast. 808 the robot cat is named after the Roland TR-808 drum machine and all the sounds she makes are from the sound effects of that machine. Phenomenal tidbits like this were in a lot of places.A few things fell a bit short for me but I want to stress these did NOT impact my overall view of the game by the end. Just worth noting.- Movement was janky sometimes, if you jumped off a ledge toward a magnet hook and got closer than it wanted you'll lose the prompt to snap to it and fall which I thought was strange. Momentum didn't carry with some heavy attack moves which means i'd stop dead in my tracks trying to slide a big hit into something and miss.- The game railroads you with QTEs and for me on a PS4 controller looking at mandatory Xbox button prompts it was rough at some points (this was recently patched as an adjustable setting but before I had this option it was a pretty big dent on my enjoyment.)- Combat could stand to be more flexible. I felt like a lot of sections grinded to a halt to make you do things a certain way before you were allowed to keep going, rather than just pace it better. With that, a handful of enemies REALLY want you to kill them "the right way" and it felt a little stiff at times. Also some enemies kept walking out of my super move(s) so that was pretty cool.- There are very brief sections you can play as characters other than the MC and they both happen at the end. I really wish they didn't do it that way! I wish we had more of these opportunities. It was a great idea that was cut short once I learned it was on the table at all.Overall though, keep the first things I said about this game in mind above all else. This game was really enjoyable!

_childDocuments_.review: Hi-Fi Rush was a game that immediately caught my eye when I saw screenshots the day it got announced. The art style, gameplay, and everything seemed right up my alley, but I wasn't sure *how* up my alley this was.Getting the hang of fighting to the beat of the banger tracks in the background took a little bit to get used to, but when I got it *it stuck*. Fights are really fun and feel so rewarding when you pull off insane combos and specials. The only gripe I have about combat is that it feels like it takes *so long* to get out of combat. You have to wait for the results of the fight to go away before you can leave the area. It really isn't that long but I'd love it if it was more seamless so you can get right back to what you're supposed to do after the fight.That's literally my only dislike with this game.Minus the length. It's super short and for once, I want a game to be longer. Yeah, there's post-story shenanigans, but I'd love to see this game expand more during the main story. I want to learn more about the characters, the world they're in, and everything like that. I want more interactions because ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, these characters deserve it. They're all crafted really well and they have really nice development throughout the story. Their designs are *chefs kiss* as well. OH and the humor?! It doesn't feel childish at all! It's super funny and the dialogue had me cackling pretty much the whole time.I can't forget to talk about the music.♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. The music is amazing. There's a mix of Bethesda originals and songs you'd hear on the radio, and let me tell you, it's amazing. The soundtrack is diverse in a really hard-to-explain way. Overall, I give this game a solid 9.9/10 (deducting that .1 because of the not-seamless-post-fight-♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥)

_childDocuments_.review: Originally, I left a joke review, but this game is genuinely amazing and I recommend it at full price.It's a character-action rhythm game. It takes aspects of Devil May Cry (and many of Platinum Game's titles) and combines it with a rhythm-based combat system, something that you would see in Guitar Hero. The story was simple, but very enjoyable. The characters were fantastic thanks to the hilarious and charming dialogue. It isn't Shakespeare, but it gets the job done. I seriously played through this whole thing with a wide smile on my face.The boss fights were incredible. And the music gets you pumped. Nine Inch Nails does that. There is also some fantastic original music.Overall, it reminded me of a past where I could go into a GameStop or Blockbuster and buy a game for my PlayStation 2, expecting it to be just fun. Nothing more. No delayed patches to finish the game. It's sad to see those times gone, but at least we get occasional gems like this game that remind us creativity in the gaming industry isn't dead. Thank you, Tango Gameworks. You made me have a Ratatouille critic moment. This might be the most bug-free Bethesda game to date, because I never saw any bugs in my 12 hours of gameplay. Just incredible.Oh, and there's JoJo references. Actual references. GOTY.

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't finished it yet, but this might seriously be one of the greatest games of all time.Funny, Charming, Stunning art and animation, rich with detail and most of all♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ fun as hell.Hi-Fi Rush is basically a Hack N' Slash/Character Action Game, similar to a classic God of War, a Devil May Cry, or a Bayonetta.The twist is that the entire gameplay loop is on-beat to the incredible BGM they have playing constantly. Everything from combat, to platforming, to puzzle solving, to opening treasure chests and even QTEs. It's all synced with the tunes in the background.The combat is the main draw here, and every attack, dodge, and parry string better together and do more damage if you keep the beat, incentivizing you to feel the music in everything you do. Furthermore, even if you miss, the action will still happen, and it will always finish ON beat. This really helps to get your groove back if your timing is off. If you complete a full combo on-beat, (Or perform the final hit of your combo on-beat) you get a special "Beat Hit" that does an additional finisher on your enemy.You might think that this musical gimmick comes at the cost of depth, but it doesn't. Everything is here. Pause Combos, Light-Heavy-Light Combos, Aerial Raves, Projectiles, Parries, Dodges, Enemy Enrage Mechanics, Long Range Grabs, it's ALL here just as you would expect in any DMC or Bayonetta game.  These mechanics are married so well together and it's so satisfying to pull off a long string with no mess ups.I'm playing this game on a subpar machine with a fairly outdated GPU, but it still runs for me at a smooth 60+ FPS, with the only issue I've been having is that some cutscenes get slightly desynced from the audio track, which can be slightly distracting, especially since they went through the trouble of matching the animations so well to the audio.The art style is heavily based on anime (Getting a lot of Studio TRIGGER vibes from this game) complete with Japanese Katakana SFX text popping up occasionally and one character that is almost literally right out of JoJo's. However, you can also definitely see a lot of western comic book and animation influence in the art style as well, think something like Invincible or Ben10. Just like the seemingly disparate Action/Music genres, the art meets perfectly in the middle of Eastern and Western, and it looks really great.The animation is where this game really shines the most in my eyes. Even if you're not a fan of this art style, and prefer your games to be more realistic, watching any cutscenes from this game you have to just admit that these characters are incredibly expressive and bursting will personality. From their facial expressions to their body language at any given time, you can tell that no expense was spared to bring them to life as fully as possible.The English voice acting is superb, breathing even further life into them. If that's not enough, there are tons of language options to choose from so you can always listen to it in your preferred language. This game came out of nowhere and stole my heart. If you like action games like Devil May Cry, rhythm games, rock and roll, anime, and even a little dash of Persona in there for good measure, you're gonna love this game.Hi Fi Rush has so much love and passion behind it. You can see it in every moment. (Literally.) Please play this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Hi-Fi RUSH

_childDocuments_.review: In 2023, a game like Hi-Fi Rush is a miracle. No marketing, no microtransactions, and nothing to judge the game on but the quality of the game itself. It was games like this in the early 2000s that made me fall in love with video games, and my feelings towards this one are no different. I dove in skeptical of the hype, and came out a true believer.It's worth noting that I played entirely on the Steam Deck, mostly docked, and experienced no technical issues whatsoever. Hi-Fi Rush's story is pretty straight forward and you get into the action from the second you pick up the controller. There's never really a lull—the story doesn't stop for the entire 15-18 hours you're playing the game. If nothing else, the writing is efficient. It takes you where you need to go and shows you what it needs to show you in order to tell the story that wants to be told.Personally, I enjoyed it a lot! It's cheesy and hammy and a little cliché but it's fun, and that's what matters. The voice acting isn't over-the-top and I found myself invested in all of the characters by the end. There's a lot of sequel potential with this one too.This game is definitely Devil May Cry meets your favorite rhythm game and it's a match made in heaven. Even if you don't have rhythm, the game has accessibility options and various difficulties to make sure that everyone can enjoy it equally. I consider myself to have rhythm, but I don't have very good mechanical control to make combo-heavy action games easy for me. I played on the Hard difficulty and still had a blast. I used a lot of continues so my stage ratings were usually poor, but that's okay. I found that the increased challenge let me appreciate the combat more and ultimately made me better—even if I had to redo some encounters and bosses so much that my thumb cramped up.The only thing that I hesitantly wish for is a more precise—or at least visually apparent—targeting system. There's no real way to manually control which enemy you're locked onto, which makes some encounters difficult to safely navigate and can ultimately lead to fatal errors. There's not much to say about the music. It was perfect. The mixup of classic songs with songs recorded by the game was a great choice (although scary for licensing in the future). The game takes a similar approach to Nier: Automata where the songs change based on your environment and gameplay, an obvious choice for a game so heavily focused on music from both a gameplay and thematic point-of-view. The UI in this game is cute and completely serviceable. It's not without its shortcomings though. The game tries to educate you on how to equip certain items fairly early in the game, but you don't actually have enough money to really experiment at that point, so I found myself unable to figure it out later on when I actually had more money to experiment. It's easy, so it didn't take long to find, but I distinctly remember being confused for about 5 minutes. (Hint: You can only equip items in the shop, and you want the Left Trigger button on shop screens where you can buy equippable items).It's incredible that Tango Gameworks decided to shadowdrop Hi-Fi Rush without any sort of marketing, but that confidence was well-placed: this is an incredible game. It takes modern game design and marries it with the best of the more experimental gaming eras. At $30, this game is a steal and everyone with access should play it.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. Reminds me a bit of Ratchet and Clank, maybe due to the gears collectibles and platforming aspects. Incorporates rhythm and action really well, a genre I hope developers continue to explore. Combat is fun and expressive. You can unlock a good amount of combos, but I don't think there were too much. I found in the heat of battle I'd end up reusing the same ones but that's simply a skill issue on my part.  The enemies are interesting and varied (sometimes annoying - looking at the bird robot). The boss fights are pretty interesting, and the later ones definitely kicked my ass (in a good way!), although my initial playthrough was on Hard so not sure how that would change on the lower difficulty. The art is vibrant, feels like I'm playing in a Saturday cartoon (with the occasional anime influence). The story gets a bit cheesy at points, but the dialogue is well written and hilarious. I especially loved all the random robot dialogue throughout the levels. There seems to be a decent amount of post game content that I haven't gotten to yet as well as a ton of secrets to find throughout the levels if you're into that sort of thing. If you like action games at all, have even the slightest interest in rhythm games, and like laughing, big recommend from me. Interested to see if there are any plans for more Hi-Fi Rush in the future or even anything inspired by it.

_childDocuments_.review: Downloaded the game through Xbox game pass and not even 30 seconds into the tutorial stage I had to pause and come buy it on Steam."30 seconds? That's nowhere NEAR enough time!" you say. But let me tell ya, this game is so damn polished you can see your reflection in it. Tango Gameworks has made a world where every ounce of visual and auditory detail is just  in style. I knew that with this much attention given to the detail of the world around you, the rest of the game must surely be the same way, so yea that's how I knew at just 30 seconds that I was in for a treat.6 hours later, I'm extremely delighted to say that my faith was not misplaced at all. The gameplay is a blast, the music is hype, the visuals are charming, the characters are fun, the voice acting is great, and the humor is Borderlands 1 and 2 level of hilarious. I could go on and on about what exactly I love about each of those aspects but this review is long enough already and frankly I just want to get back to the game!The year has only just begun but IMO it's already an extremely strong contender for GotY 2023.--------I had started writing a much more in-depth review but I clicked that "allow comments" on the side not realizing it would delete it all without saving T-T So instead, I'm just going to share an anecdote that I think sums up my experience best:The game encourages you to sync all of your button presses to the beat and rewards your good timing by playing a little "hey!" or cymbal crash sound effect. These extra audio stabs fit the background music so well and are so satisfying to hear that even outside of combat I find myself "hey!"ing and crashing along. As a result, I fall to my death a . Not because the platforming is especially difficult, but because I just  ending a phrase of music with a dash-induced set of cymbal crashes and if that dash so happens then to send me flying off a ledge then fly off the ledge I must, health be damned!

_childDocuments_.review: Most overrated,overhyped chaotic mess. I was expecting skill based game,not a game where the most of the encounters are just a total chaos. You just can't be focused in one moment on rhytm,combos,dodging, parrying around 360° radius, ememies shooting at you, melee attacks, on enemies running around like crazy, and using special moves to breach enemies shields. _childDocuments_.review: Through densely inspired skatecore aesthetics, HFR is a combo-oriented hack n slash with enough campy writing to stay in your memory past its completion.Where HFR suffers most is that it attempts to coast so hard on its visual and thematic style, that it ends up with often flat and near-insufferable character dynamics. Chai is exactly who you expect him to be- a jabbering protagonist who bickers with the female lead despite being stronger together. These tropes are not explored, subverted or even seemingly acknowledged. The characters are simply action figures with a little button to say something that their personality would say in response to any moment. The Rhythm combat is also underexplored- All music stays within one genre, and it fails to even give that longevity. All rhythm is stuck to basic 4/4 timing, save for the occasional doubletime or QTE. You are never inputting combos like a lead guitarist, only like a rhythm guitarist. For the first 10 hours of the game, you barely have the resources for more than a few combos which means the combat is crazy repetitive up until late game.With all that said, it hits its stride after the middle point of the game and without elaborating much it's the exact type of game the world needs more of. Short, contained stories with a unique central mechanic and a clearly invested creative team who takes the time to add charm to every level- props that bob and weave with the rhythm, seamless transitions between cutscenes and gameplay, and a willingness to not drag out levels longer than needed.

_childDocuments_.review: Everything about this game hits right. Hi-Fi Rush is similar to Devil May Cry with the combat and score for each encounter. The game has an in-depth combat system which has a rhythm that you can take advantage of to get extra damage. The combat is expressive and there is tons of moves you can add to Chai. You can add chips which change how your partners function, like faster cooldowns or double damage. It's got a unique charm to it and while I didn't play for the story I was surprised how well it was put together. The bosses have their gimmicks and they are all enjoyable.There is a surprising amount of post-game content including in-game currency to unlock music for your hideout and unlocking costumes for the characters you meet throughout the story. While I didn't play it, there is an entirely new mode which functions like a rouge-like where you advance a tower with buffs/powerups which you obtain on that run. I fully recommend this game, even if you only plan to play through it once.

_childDocuments_.review: An absolute delight from start the finish.Featuring great style, and refreshing blend of action and rhythm gameplay, I have a fair bit to mention here.Starting off with the+++Positives+++EVERYTHING, is tied to the beat and rhythm of the game!Character animations, platforming, combat, the option to go off-beat exists but it's nowhere near as rewarding or efficient.It's also surprisingly easy to get into, having enough destructible objects laying around means you're practising attacks in some form, and stretches of land mean you're most likely dashing in rhythm to go from point A to point B faster.Besides rankings and slower animations, there's no real downside in messing up the beat too much either, it's very friendly but rewarding to master.The style of this game is just a delight.Striking comic book aesthetics to accompany a goofy adventure with fun characters, followed with humour that actually gets a good chuckle out of me quite often, it's just fun!The music, while pretty good, actually goes a step further with streamer mode.Streamer mode gets rid of any licensed songs and replaces them with new OST, and in a lot of cases I think these songs work way better.And at half the cost of a standard AAA game, I have no reason to say you shouldn't buy this at full price.Game's a bargain as is, lasting roughly 10+ hours, and it's mostly just all quality stuff.Now onto the---Negatives---The enemies covered in armour are anti-fun.They require an ability to get rid off their armour, but usually it takes multiple hits to get rid of it before you can actually deal any damage.The problem is that this ability without any upgrades, is kinda a bit long, and once you get rid off the the armour, the enemies themselves are usually nothing special.Not bad, just not great either.Having the option to replay stages after beating them would've also been nice, but you have to beat the game to do this.I get why, as there is some post-game content, and new side areas you couldn't get to your first time through, but all the same I would still like to be able to go back.And finally, my last complaint is related to one of the last few stages so this'll be a minor spoiler but not enough to make me say "avoid this".>>>Conclusion<<<Hi-Fi Rush is a game that I found to be an absolute delight and one I'd highly recommend to others.Even if you don't think you'd like rhythm games, I still recommend you keep an eye on this, the game really does do a good job of getting you into things.Just a whole lot of fun and well worth your money.

_childDocuments_.review: Ah yes, Devil may Dance!As a woman beater myself I can really relate to Chai as he beats women twice. Very cool character.Wait, what?!This is one of those rare games that deserves a 10/10. It is faultless. Everything works as intended as is fun. It is so well polished. Best rhythm game ever.Took me about 10 hours to beat it. Initially I thought it was a neat concept but kinda simple. However, the more I played it the more I enjoyed it. The second half of the game had me smiling non-stop. The game feels oddly nostalgic, like it feels like an old PS2 game in the best way. It took me back to the days of me playing PS2 games when I was younger. I found the characters charming, the combat was pretty good, I loved the music, and the bosses were great. There wasn't really a point in my run where I felt like I was having a bad time. I'm surprised such a high profile dev literally released a PS2 game in 2023 and I mean that as a good thing. Just the entire design of the game is old-school PS2 era. That whole "insert Sonic meme saying I want shorter games with worse graphics and I'm not kidding." It's hyper focused on delivering fun gameplay without bogging things down with an open world. And the cel shading and smooth animation makes the whole game pop. A lot of attention to detail as well.Some of the boss fights and set-pieces are incredibly creative and exciting. I was struggling to stay on rhythm initially but as I started to vibe with the music I naturally started to stay on beat. The rhythm based combat was super cool, it reminded me a bit of the old days playing Rock Band and Guitar Hero but as combat instead. It took me a little while to feel comfortable with, but once I came to terms with how enemies will only hit you on the beat, juggling parries in with my regular combat started to feel a lot more natural. The soundtrack was great, with 2 Nine Inch Nails songs and the level that used Whirring by The Joy Formidable was amazing the way it used the build up to the end of that song as the ending to beat the boss, oh man, so great! The voice acting is an absolute treat. Robbie Daymond does a great job making Chai a Peter Parker-type everyman and Erica Lindbeck does her usual thing but it works well for Peppermint.Also, as someone who works with disabled people, it was so amazing seeing how this game has such great representation of disability. Hi-Fi Rush's cast is predominantly filled with disabled characters. Like Chai for example, he uses a prosthetic arm because (as confirmed by the creators) he didn't have full function of his arm. Peppermint also uses a prosthetic leg, Korsica and Roquefort are basically on life support, etc.  It's not all in your face about it and made to fit naturally into the plot. It just feels natural, which is rare in media. I think part of the reason it feels so natural is that in the game world it feels… normal. And That it's normal and okay to be disabled. Which is something I really loved, it's not focused on extensively, it focuses on the characters themselves, rarely ever the disability. They're fully fleshed characters who happen to have disabilities! I'm super thankful for this game.I'm almost in disbelief at how great it was to just play, like "Wait a minute, we could have games be this fun on a moment to moment basis?" I've always appreciated Insomniac for putting gameplay first and just making something a joy to play. Then this comes along and does that with presentation and a theme that clicks for me even more.I cannot recommend this enough to everyone, it's been awhile since I've seen something be surrounded by so much positivity in gaming discussions and it's great to see. Also realistic graphics or not, this might be the best looking game I've ever played.  Gotta say, this could easily be a $60 release with all the content and its quality. It's an absolute steal for $30. 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: Do you like Action Games like DMC, Bayonetta, Ninja Gaiden, Astral Chain, all those?  Do you also like rock music and pumping rhythms?  How about colorful cartoony Jet Set Radio style graphics?  Big on tongue-in-cheek 4th wall obliterating dialogue?  Most importantly, do you want Phil "I'm bad at my job" Spencer to shove it for attempting to shutter Tango Gameworks for seemingly no reason?If yes to any or all of those, buy this.It's genuinely one of the most fun and creative games of recent years-- Character Action Gameplay and Rhythm Games aren't something you'd assume would mesh well, but they work EXTREMELY well here.  The combat is fluid, a little hard to get into if you're not a Rhythm Adept but once you get into the groove it becomes so fun to just style on enemies.  The bosses are really creative with how they play around with the more lyrical tracks, too.The story is kinda barebones, a rather cliche "big corporation is evil and tries to make money in a comedically evil way, go stop them" story, but the writing does a REALLY good job carrying that skeleton of a story and making it something greater.  It's funny, it's a sh*tpost of a script and right when you think things are gonna get serious it still has the time to crack a joke (which makes the more cathartic opening of a certain late-game stage hit way harder).Mix all of that with the bright and vibrant artstyle and you have a game that feels like it was ripped straight out of that mid 2000s experimental PS2/Xbox title age.  It's just a fun, fun game to play all around, so give it a shot.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is the embodiment of you playing video games after middle school when you were a kid and then had the omega brain idea of creating a character action game with your favorite songs as the background theme.Fantastic battle-rhythm combo system, awesome visuals and level pacing, a plot not too convoluted but engaging enough to follow through, characters that are unique while not wearing you down with extreme tropes, it's hard NOT to find an aspect of the game that isn't appealing to anyone who saw a THIRTY-DOLLAR video game made in the year 2023. The game does an incredible job teaching you the mechanics throughout the story, and mastering combos and new moves, while may take some time, feel so satisfying, especially as the soundtrack and crowd starts rocking out harder to your style meter.Exploration feels great as well, finding secrets and power ups to help you rock out harder during the more difficult combat sequences that ramp up later in the game. That and having silly NPC interactions makes traversing through each level a fun experience, and barely feels like you're just wasting time going from Point A to Point B.My only honest complaint is when the action gets way too crazy, it's hard to keep with all the mechanics that can occur (musical ques from enemies, visual blips to attack, etc.), but the game gives you just enough room for recovery and to reassess the room, allowing you to get back onto the beat and back into combos. Whether you're a fan of the classic PS2 character action games, you love NIN, or if you're looking for a lovable gang of doofs to do sick smoking style combos with, Hi-Fi Rush offers a grand experience at a ridiculously affordable $30. Would highly recommend to anyone, and would also recommend petting 808 at any given chance.

_childDocuments_.review: Hi Fi rush is a very good game. Its such a creative idea to combine just frames with actual music rhythm. The flow of combat being dictated by the beat combined with dmc-esque combos makes a great game play loop. Boss sequences use the rhythm excellently.The level design is great with surprisingly good platforming, which is also tied to the beat. In my eyes this surpasses similar titles like dmc5 in this regard, if only for the elegance of keeping with the theme of rhythm. I enjoy the writing for the most part. Its rare in these sorts of games to actually get competent character development over the course of the game. The satirical corporate humor is good too. My only complaint is that there is a lot 4th wall break and lamp-shading that is kinda funny at first but gets tiresome at times. My first play through I saw minimal bugs. No crashes. I occasionally got a bug where an attack wouldn't come out but it was too the beat so it still comboed. I think it happened like twice. I have accidentally caused a certain bosses grab to occur but not actually grab me (got stuck to them while they were moving, I eventually broke free). Also during cutscenes, occasionally animations would trigger when they shouldn't. But these are the only bugs I've encountered and for the most part they didn't take away from the experience (that boss grab wasn't great)I love action games where combat mastery is a key part and this game definitely scratches that itch.

_childDocuments_.review: I typically don't write reviews, but...Tango Gameworks's Hi-Fi Rush is a game with a fantastic concept and excellent execution, especially considering its complexity. Essentially, through Hi-Fi Rush, Tango Gameworks effectively explores the scenario of "What if Devil May Cry was a rhythm game?" Like Devil May Cry (of which I am also a huge fan), Hi-Fi Rush is a hack-and-slash game, but its approach to gameplay is unique due to its rhythm-based mechanics, which are integral to the overall experience. The combat centers around executing light and heavy attacks and various combos in time with the music, making listening to the music an active component of the gameplay and enhancing the overall immersion. The soundtrack consists of both licensed and license-free tracks of excellent quality, akin to an alternative/indie rock album. This genre of music complements the happy-go-lucky vibe and bright anime cell-shaded graphical style presented in the game, proving that graphical fidelity in video games isn’t what truly matters. This is something that the triple-A gaming industry, for the most part, doesn’t seem to understand.While the combat in Hi-Fi Rush may take some getting used to, its skill curve and complex mechanics are far easier to master than those of Devil May Cry. Though I could compile a long list comparing the two games at a mechanical level, there are two main aspects that highlight how Hi-Fi Rush is much more accessible compared to Devil May Cry. First, Hi-Fi Rush uses an auto-targeting system, unlike Devil May Cry's manual lock-on targeting system. Second, Hi-Fi Rush’s version of the Devil May Cry style meter, referred to as the Rhythm meter, primarily builds up based on landing combos with good timing, rather than simply executing as many varied combos as quickly as possible, as seen in the Devil May Cry series. What makes Hi-Fi Rush’s Rhythm meter even more accessible is the game's consistent beat, which strikes a perfect balance. The beat is fast enough to maintain the fast-paced flow integral to real-time action combat systems but not so fast that your hands begin to hurt and fatigue after a while—an issue I encounter with the Devil May Cry combat system (a game that generally plays as fast as you and rewards your self-inputted fast gameplay). Overall, Hi-Fi Rush’s combat and gameplay are fluid and polished. More importantly, all of its inner workings and complexities, centered around its blend with music and rhythm game mechanics (which must have taken forever to get right), contribute to a fun gameplay experience.Narratively speaking, Hi-Fi Rush isn’t anything remarkable. It tells a relatively basic, straightforward story that complements the level design. This isn’t a bad thing, as narratives across all mediums don’t need to be complex or thought-provoking to be good. The characters serve their purpose; they aren’t terribly complex, nor do they need to be, given that the narrative itself is written to accommodate this. Protagonist Chai, in particular, is a great character. While he’s written to be annoying, you can’t help but like him, which is exacerbated by Robbie Daymond’s excellent voice performance. Daymond is known for roles such as Goro Akechi in Persona 5 Royal (Atlus), Megumi Fushiguro in Jujutsu Kaisen (MAPPA), Prompto Argentum in Final Fantasy XV (Square Enix), and Lloyd Bannings in The Legend of Heroes series (Nihon Falcom). On a personal level, Chai resonated with me because he represents my close attachment to music, specifically my evolving love for rock music. Chai is a character that represents individuals like me, who at one point didn’t know how to play an instrument but still had a profoundly deep understanding of music. In particular, there is a cutscene towards the end of the game that effectively emphasizes this.As a writer, what I appreciate most about Hi-Fi Rush narratively is its dialogue. The game has a comedic structure similar to movies like Deadpool (Marvel Entertainment) and video games like Sunset Overdrive (Insomniac Games), both of which are effective in their endeavors. This aspect of Hi-Fi Rush is particularly impressive since it’s typically very difficult to write a script with this type of comedic structure that doesn’t feel cringe-worthy. In contrast, Square Enix’s game Forspoken is an example of how to mess this up, resulting in a script that is wholly cringe-worthy.As I finish writing this, a sense of sadness washes over me as I confront the realization that Xbox has shut down Tango Gameworks without any known sensible reason. The creative minds at Tango Gameworks produced one of the best games Xbox had published in many years. Consequently, Hi-Fi Rush, with all its amazing innovations, will never see a sequel, as without Tango Gameworks, there is no possibility of one. Hi-Fi Rush was clearly created by developers who were deeply passionate about crafting the best and most enjoyable gaming experience, rather than focusing solely on monetization. This dedication is sadly rare in the triple-A gaming industry, where companies with vast financial resources often refuse to take creative risks due to an extreme and at times unreasonable fear of financial loss. Hi-Fi Rush serves as a symbol in the triple-A industry of what it means to create something with passion, with the end goal of producing the best product rather than merely the most profitable one. While Hi-Fi Rush isn’t the best game I've ever played, I deeply appreciate it for what it is and what it stands for. And in an industry where the triple-A space often refuses to innovate, Hi-Fi Rush is more than enough for me.- PC OPTIMIZATION -☑️ Amazingly Optimized🔲 Meets the PC port performance standard🔲 The Port has some issues🔲 PC port is in an Unacceptable State🔲 Unplayable- WORTH BUYING @ FULL PRICE -☑️ Yes🔲 Its Free🔲 Wait for sale🔲 NoENGINE: Unreal Engine 4GRADE: B+/A-

_childDocuments_.review: A fairly standard character action game or whatever they're called with light/heavy attacks, combos, and a letter-based grading scale, but with rhythm mechanics. You do more damage and get other benefits if you're on beat with inputs, and moves for you and your enemies are always on beat. Not a ton of depth, but elevated by the music integration, support characters and varied enemies. The combat is challenging without being frustrating, and fighting on beat feels very rewarding. Overall has a nice 'in the zone' feeling that I really like.Writing isn't brilliant but it feels like a genuine attempt at making a fun script; the characters are likable and fun despite being rather two dimensional. Some good humor, especially the physical humor, but some pretty corny jokes. They (arguably) venture pretty closely into summer animated film quality at some points, but the game has so few jokes it's moving through both verbally and visually that it doesn't bother me. Plus, it feels sincere rather than snarky, like the director is just a cornball, so it's fine.I think the visuals and music are good too, but that's subjective. Has some licensed music that scenes were built around, but also "streamer mode" tracks made by an in-house band or something that sound like slightly different versions of the licensed stuff. TL;DR: A solid feel-good game with a neat gimmick. Korsica is best girl.

_childDocuments_.review: Stylish combat, great cutscenes & lip syncing, flashy environments, and a unique gameplay mechanic that never gets old. Hi-Fi RUSH is a pleasant surprise in an age of live service, MTX, battle pass driven AAA games.This offers a really fun single player experience for a fraction of the cost. The "hit enemies to do more damage on the beat" is quite hard to master at first, however the environment moves with the playing music to help you keep track of it (there's also an on screen indicator that you can toggle on/off which is really useful when you're getting the hang of it) and once you know what you're doing, you can pull off some impressive combos. The boss battles are also great!The art style is really nice, the characters & enemies are really well designed, and the environments are popping with colour. I've not experienced any bugs - performance is also rock solid (60 fps on high settings with a 1070 + ultrawide).What an incredibly well made game - would strongly recommend!

_childDocuments_.review: Hi-fi Rush Full ReviewScore- 9/10-ProsGreat characters, story, and soundtrackBeautiful art styleExcellent combat that gets better as the game goes onAverage 15 hours to beat the base game-ConsYou can't skip cut scenes after viewing them leading you to watch the whole scene from the start annoying during boss battlesChallenges and powers can't be set or changed in the levelFinal Notes: Hi-Fi Rush is precisely what it looks like and an exciting rhythm game with the humor to match its art style. If they did come out with a sequel I just hope they add the ability to skip the cut scenes and make it more accessible to view /set abilities and challenges in the level not only at the shop and hideout.
_childDocuments_.name: Hi-Fi RUSH

_childDocuments_.review: Hi-Fi Rush is a stylish, energetic, joyous blast of a video game. This surprise hit from Tango Gameworks takes on the concept of a rhythm spectacle fighter and masterfully executes it. It's just plain fun to pull off flashy moves to demolish your foes, all in sync with the music. The only con I have is the platforming can be annoying at times, but that's a very minor flaw. Otherwise, this is one of those games with so much passion and creativity poured into every part of it that it's extremely hard not to love.The game is also very newbie-friendly. Combos aren't very long or complex, there are many visual indicators to help you sync with the rhythm, and you aren't punished for being off-beat, instead you're rewarded for good timing. This is greatly appreciated, as I am not very good at rhythm games or spectacle fighters, yet it was easy for me to get into a groove with Hi-Fi Rush.
_childDocuments_.name: Hi-Fi RUSH

_childDocuments_.review: This is what gaming used to be.You get the full game, with unlockable extras and goodies by doing challenges. Not once does the game ask you for more money. Its a complete product, made with lots of heart and passion. It plays wonderfully, a spectacle fighter + rhythm game is a brilliant combo, excellent soundtrack, loved the characters and the writing is the type of cheesy and goofy stuff that just makes you feel good inside.This game is worth every single cent.

_childDocuments_.review: I am terrible at anything musically related but I still had fun playing through the first time (took 15 hours to beat it and I died around 5 times to the final boss). I didn't like that i was getting C's and B's on normal difficulty so I kept playing and practicing. Replayed on hard and did the post game challenges and I'm getting A and S ranks on everything now including the challenges. Once you get the rhythm timing down, the game is very generous with its ranking system. You only need to land 70% of button presses with the rhythm to get an A rank in Just Timing which is one of 3 things that affect your battle rank. Taking damage has a very small effect on your score but it's not noticeable 95% of the time unless you straightup die and have to restart from checkpoint.After you beat the game you unlock the challenges doors that were locked during the first playthrough, level select, character customization shop, and the Rhythm Tower mode which is this game's version of the "Bloody Palace" from the Devil May Cry games.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR; An amazing rhythm-platformer that's clearly a work of talent and love for the genre. It's accessible, satisfying and most importantly fun.Hi-Fi Rush is really an instant classic. Its platforming has all the classic elements of the genre, integrated brilliantly with rhythm-based movement. The combat is also inspired by the classic beat-em-ups but with its own twists and of course music sync. And speaking of music, the soundtrack is really a treat, both the original tracks and the guest artists' work is top notch and will keep you vibing for the rest of your day. Without any spoilers, they've done some really clever work blending the various tracks with the encounters, and especially boss fights.I think what really resonated with me about this game is how it manages to invoke games and comics/anime from your childhood, with its cute little story and vibrant characters, it manages to strike a chord (pun intended) of nostalgia. It really is refreshing to see a studio make something like this, definitely try it out!
_childDocuments_.name: Hi-Fi RUSH

_childDocuments_.review: Hi-Fi Rush is an experience like no other, with an outstanding sound track and satisfying movement. Along with a great story, Hi-Fi Rush is something unique, while it may be a rhythm game at heart, it is so much more than that, from platforming to fighting, it has so much more than an OSU! but feeling the music is critical to mastering the game. Tango Gameworks has done something no other developer could ever dream of, while its so sad to see them disbanded by Microsoft. If you wish to pickup Hi-Fi Rush, which I would highly recommend you doing, I urge you to use a 3rd party key reseller as a way to stick it to the man if you know what I mean. Hi-Fi Rush has so much to offer and was definitely worth my time and the money I spent.

_childDocuments_.review: This was a game that made me feel something I hadn't felt since my childhood: genuine glee after finding a completely unexpected game that quickly became one of my favorite pieces of media that I would praise it to every person I could about just how good it was.This was the best game I played under the Bethesda umbrella in many years. And this is the last game I'm buying from the  Bethesda umbrella for foreseeable years, as I don't know how long it will take for me to stop feeling this seething indignation.I will still continue to support studios such as Obsidian under Microsoft, but only because I feel the worst I could do was give Microsoft a reason to go "See?! We were right to close studios like these. Now let's quadruple down on live services."And to Tango, you are absolute legends.
